name: Cricket 24
detailed_description: Cricket 24 is the culmination of a decade of Cricket video game development and includes teams from every corner of the globe. Players will be able to take on major cricket nations including Australia and England in the official Ashes, West Indies, New Zealand, Ireland and more, plus for the first time ever, professional Indian T20 teams, all set in over 50 detailed official stadiums. Cricket 24 is the most complete video game simulation of cricket seen to date. Cricket 24: Building the most realistic cricket video game ever! - The Ashes: Cricket 24 will feature the biggest rivalry in cricket, The Ashes. Detailed cutscenes immerse the player in the moment as the Ashes tour progresses. Feel a part of the team with press conferences and team training sessions. Unique commentary allows for complete Ashes immersion. Experience The Ashes playing as a single player, or as Australia or England. - Official Licenses: over 300 players with full photogrammetry. Major Cricket Nations including Australia, England, West Indies, New Zealand and Ireland plus more. The biggest tournaments including The Ashes, the KFC BBL and Weber WBBL, The Hundred, the Caribbean Premier League plus a number of professional Indian T20 teams, along with more than 50 highly detailed official stadiums. - Career Mode: follow the journey of your player from club cricketer to the international stage, developing your skills and growing your fan base as you hone your craft to become the next big thing in cricket. Cricket 24 gives more control to the player in determining their destiny, becoming a short-form hero, focusing on the Test team, or trying to balance both on your way to cricketing stardom. - All new fielding: a complete overhaul of the fielding systems to provide the most realistic and responsive fielding controls ever seen in a cricket video game. - Cross Platform: fully cross platform, play online against your friends and the world’s best players regardless of platform. Create and share custom content across different platforms including stadiums, players, teams and more with the academy.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve purchased and played every installment of Big Ant’s cricket game series and unfortunately, as much as I wanted to like Cricket 24, it’s plagued with a lot of the same issues we’ve seen since Cricket 19. This review is a message to the BigAnt team, you can and should do a lot better than this. This game is essentially a repackaged version of 22 with very minor improvements to things like the menus, music, and having licensed teams which are all great additions but when it comes to core gameplay, there’s little to look forward to.Fielding is atrocious. They might have made improvements but in my first couple of games I had fielders running parallel to the ball, fielders standing outside the boundary rope before the ball even got to them, fielders kicking the ball over the boundary. This is absurd. And again, this was my SECOND match in the game, so if you actually tested the game before release, this should’ve been so easy to catch (no pun intended).Commentary: it’s ridiculously bad. Hit a shot for 6 “poor shot!”, score 20 runs in an over “batters were kept quiet that over”. Like come on guys, how can your system not check “if runs scored > 6, do not use any low scoring commentary”. Like again, these are just the basics.Bowling feels arduous, you can hit perfect lines and lengths all day, deliver tons of variations, and it feels like playing to a random number generator where hopefully one of them gets you a wicket, otherwise you’ll be sitting there for 50+ overs or simulating. Batting however, does deserve praise, it’s pretty enjoyable and I do feel punished when I have a lapse in concentration but otherwise in control.If you’re looking for a fresh game from Cricket 22, this isn’t it. Skip.For BigAnt, I’m all for you guys having minor regular releases with incremental improvements, but you absolutely cannot pull an EA Games FIFA on us when you haven’t gotten core gameplay out of buggy, just bizarre mistakes mode. If fielding continues to be a joke and the commentary is blatantly wrong, this isn’t even a finished game in my opinion, you’re missing your foundation and basics.Your success with Don Bradman came by listening to the community and wanting to make the best game out there. Please take your time and do it properly, heck if you need a kickstarter because you’re still an indie studio making the only legitimate cricket game out there, we’re behind you. But please don’t drop releases like this that quite frankly cheat a community when the basics are still very raw. I’m excited for the next proper iteration, but for now, this isn’t it.

_childDocuments_.review: My review for Cricket 24 focuses on why I don't recommend it for those who already own Cricket 22:1. While Cricket 24 does offer some improvements over its predecessor, it largely feels like a rehash of Cricket 22 without significant enhancements to justify its price point.2. The developers seem to have prioritized licensing deals over meaningful gameplay changes, neglecting several areas that could have been improved upon.3. It's concerning that there hasn't been a patch for the game in over two months, indicating a lack of ongoing support, possibly due to the studio spreading itself thin with numerous projects.4. The development studio needs to prioritize quality over quantity. They're churning out too many games simultaneously, resulting in rushed releases and missed opportunities for refinement.5. Better communication from the developers is essential. Providing roadmaps for updates, as they did with AFL this year, would instill confidence in players about the future of Cricket 24.Now, for some specific feedback on potential improvements:1. Allow players to select the entire touring squad of 16 as the captain, with detailed information on each player's form, fatigue, and recent performance stats.2. Implement options for communication between batting partners at the end of an over, such as telling them either slow down just block we are going for a draw or getting to the end of day, smash it out of the park we need to win, get a single get me on strike 3. Enhance the blocking mechanics. When its the end of the over have the option to go to your partner and tell them either slow down just block we are going for a draw or getting to the end of day, smash it out of the park we need to win, get a single get me on strike 4. When blocking the ball make it go further and before running allowing us to tap a button that says no run or waiting, have different type of no's 5. Introduce more pressure in career mode, especially when playing for national teams like Australia, by setting performance benchmarks for players to maintain their place in the squad. such as you have to score past 50 runs to stay in the team or they will drop you, take a certain amount of wickets, have more pressure on you getting dropped and knowing if you are6.Improve the AI to deliver a more realistic and challenging gameplay experience.7. Allow players to choose the starting year in career mode for added customization.8. Introduce more injuries into the game, as they're currently too rare to have a meaningful impact on gameplay.9. Implement the option for players to change helmets after being hit, adding realism to the game.10. Incorporate Ultra Edge technology into replays and offer camera movement in hotspot views for a more immersive experience.11. Add the feature for batters to emerge from the change rooms when coming in to bat, adding to the realism of the game.12. Include a variety of celebration options for centuries, allowing players to choose their preferred style.13. Provide more control over AI bowling rotations, allowing players to dictate bowling spells and strategies for their team.By addressing these points, Cricket 24 could offer a more compelling experience and justify its place in the cricket gaming market.

_childDocuments_.review: Prepare for a detailed review that will include numerous suggestions. Although there have been improvements in different areas, Cricket 24 still has significant issues. I cannot recommend purchasing it in its current state. However, the latest patches showed significant improvement and hopefully soon it will reach a stage worthy of its price.Pros:- The game surpasses its predecessors in terms of smoothness.- First slip catches can now be observed.- Dismissals show higher variations compared to previous iterations.- Watching batters execute certain shots is a visually pleasing spectacle.- Two new bowling styles for seam bowlers and two for off spinners have been added, along with a new batting style.- Licensing has been granted for 8 IPL teams, besides PSL and several associate nations, and a remarkable 50 new stadiums.- They have heeded my previous suggestion to expand the range of career mode teams available for selection.  - The skin details for ‘create a player’ have been improved. Without a doubt, the created players in this game outshine those in Cricket 22.- The ambiance is improved by the sound of the crowd.- Additional field setting.Cons:- Spinners! The developers are struggling to balance the spinners’ power with their ability to turn the ball.- The presence of a superhuman wicketkeeper undermines the realism. - The stumping needs to be fine-tuned.- The fielding performance has not met the expected standard.- Adam Gilchrist has been selected as a new commentator, although I had hoped for Danny Morrison or Ian Bishop. The commentary is just as bad as before. - The T20 match simulation remains untouched. Playing as a lower order batter, I am devoid of both the batting and the sense of realism.- There is no rule for foreign players in a lineup, breaking the realism.- The lineup is lacking dynamism as a whole. Any changes to the batting order or the use of a Nightwatchman will not occur. The utilisation of bench players is neglected by AI.- Left-hand seam bowlers go around the wicket during the power play, while right hand off spinners go over the wicket. The order should be reversed for both.- No new delivery types were introduced for arcade controls, like reverse swing or carom ball. The opportunity to bowl leg breaks as an off-spinner or off breaks as a leg-spinner is also not available. These mysterious spinners are a requirement for the game. - The visual representation of the generated players is still unappealing. There are female cricketers with a bald head. The issue can be resolved by granting us permission to change the visuals and names of all club players. One possible approach is to pre-generate a group of players in the academy and use their appearance when starting the career.- The consideration of allowing headbands, such as the one worn by Stuart Broad, and hijabs, similar to a female player from Scotland, should be given in the academy.- The absence of in-game communication poses challenges for batters and captains in evaluating match situations and adjusting strategies, and resulting in an ordinary AI.- There should be a revision to the speed standards for fast bowlers in career mode club cricket. A genuine fast bowler should be a rarity in club cricket. (For a fast-medium pacer, the speed proficiency should generate medium pace speed, around 125-130 kph, for the first three stars. The fourth star should be around 135 kph and the fifth star should give 145 kph. For Fast it should give 135 kph up to three stars and 145 kph for fourth and 150+ kph for the fifth star.)- Similarly, a speed proficiency for spinners would be needed. Rashid Khan, for instance, is a fast spinner known for his bowling speed of around 100 kph. On the other hand, the left arm spinners from Bangladesh have a bowling speed below 88 kph. Moreover, we saw Kuldeep Yadav’s remarkable improvement as a wicket-taking bowler, marked by his enhanced speed.- Apart from the IPL teams, the licenses offer no valuable contributions to the game, and there are numerous missing faces. Players from different countries make up the rosters of associate nations.- Please add two or three bowling styles utilised by the primary bowlers from the top 10 nations. The presence of a style akin to that of Muralitharan, Harbhajan, or Shoaib Akhtar does not account for the current bowlers. As a Bangladeshi, I would love to see Shakib and Mustafizur’s action as both are licensed. - I know the licensed Bangladesh national team or BPL may not be included. But please include a separate fictional NCL, BPL, BCL and DPL. Starting my club career, my dream is to get selected on DPL for List A cricket and NCL for FC cricket. Then I want to play for franchise-based BPL for T20 and BCL for a more competitive FC experience. The career mode’s gaps can be rectified, by adding the aforementioned suggestions. To conclude, I do not recommend the purchase of this iteration to those who already own Cricket 22 or 19, as I am the owner of all cricket games produced by Big Ant Studios. If you have other past titles, you can purchase it for the upgrades and the positive direction it is moving in with recent patches.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could say this game is worth your money and that it's finally the cricket game we all want, but it's not even close. TLDR: Pretty much no improvement in any areas over prior games, and some areas that are worse, ends up being a slog sometimes, not worth your money, if you want to play a cricket game get one of the prior ones.GOOD:Graphics seem improved although not much, the bowling feels a bit better but has a lot of issues which I'll mention later. More teams is always good and the amount of facial scans they have was a pleasant surprise, especially how many English counties have been done. BAD:As per usual with big ant the fielding is janky and feels awful, players will still take absolute blinders, before then proceeding to consistently forget the ball is going towards them and just letting roll past them. The bowling still feels way too random set ups rarely seem to actually affect the batter, and batters will frequently feel like the best players in world even though they're a number 10, plus even when they get out it makes no sense, I've had more batters outside edge in swingers than out swingers, as well a had more batters beaten on the inside edge by out swingers than in swingers, it makes no sense. Pace feels like it has no affect, the AI treats a ball bowled at 80mph the same as one at 98mph, it makes being a fast bowler feel boring. To add insult to injury, the only good part of the previous games, the batting, is worse, sweep shots (using arcade batting) don't work half the time instead your player will play some weird clip to leg-side where they played sweeps in the previous game. Playing spin is now awkward as hell because sometimes your player will block to leg-side when you aim in to off if the ball turned quite a bit, missing the ball and getting you bowled. Commentary is bad still, just this time the dialogue rarely even matched what just happened in-game, and on the topic of sound, in my opinion the bats sound worse than in prior games, that one is just a personal one.And last but not least, player ratings, the default ratings for most players feel completely wrong, with test batters having 25 defence, this results in some international players not even making the first class teams, which just makes the teams you play against at that level fell really generic and dull.If you really want to play a cricket game, save your money and get one of the older ones they are just as good if not better.

_childDocuments_.review: Ah, Big Ant. I love you guys. As an Aussie, I'm proud of our local team that managed to turn my favorite sport into a yearly title, despite a rocky start in the 2010s.When it comes to sports games, I tend to wait 2-3 years between pickups of a given title, partly due to cost and partly because these games don't fundamentally change year to year. A lot has been added since I last looked at this title. There's a well-developed women's competitive scene, more leagues like the PSL and The Hundred, and even a customizable grassroots start to the career mode. I can't express how much I loved recreating my beloved Glenelg team in great detail and winning the SA Shield with my favorite club mates.Despite the other reviews I see here, I think these additions would be enough for most fans as long as you kept the same solid cricket game underneath. Well...I have three main gripes with this game: the menus, the immersion-breaking commentary, and the AI/gameplay.Firstly, who designed the menus? They're not intuitive to a console controller's button mapping, despite the game recommending one. There's also a severe lack of confirmation screens, leading to me progressing through them when I wasn't finished with the last screen and no way to go back. This shows a severe lack of testing by people who weren't familiar with the game's quirks during development. It just lacks polish.As far as the commentary goes, there's lots of good stuff here. Cricket being what it is, there's plenty of solid talent and content to draw from, provided you can get the rights to it—which you've done. It's always nice to hear Church's reaction as I smack another on-drive into the carpark. But that lack of testing rears its ugly head again. I can't count how many times Gilly has said, "and that couldn't beat the fielder," only to have the ball roll away for 4 because the fielder didn't so much as get a toe on it. Or, more egregiously, Alli will start talking about fielding strategy for the closing overs of a T20 game when I've just finished the last delivery and the match is over. Combined with an animation of the batsman squaring up for his next shot, the poor execution of when these are coded to go off breaks the immersion and shows a lack of care for the final product.And then there's the gameplay itself. You have two options for a sports or racing game. One option is to go simulation: add as many realistic elements as you can and make the game engaging through mastery, allowing the player to be fulfilled by challenging and beating the game on its terms. But here, the batting is less nuanced than it's been in the past, and the AI is far too easy to manipulate, particularly when it comes to fielding. It's just not strategically engaging.Okay, so your other option is to go more arcade and/or make it a power fantasy for the player. But to realize this game design, you have to congratulate them and make a big deal of every milestone. When their team's in the final, focus on that. Recognize when their career character hits big milestones like 5,000 or 10,000 test runs. But you failed to capitalize on those moments. I didn't even realize my Strikers were in the final of the BBL until we were raising the cup. Hell, even a dynamic trophy cabinet in the back of menu screens would've made it feel more worth progressing through the career mode. Instead, the game feels hollow; there's no sense of accomplishment to it.If you love cricket, if the game's on sale, if you haven't grabbed one of these titles in the last 3 years, then go ahead and pick up this game. It's a solid sports game. It'll scratch that itch, it did for me. I love Big Ant, and I wish I could support them more. But like a fast medium bowler, with a game like this, you just have to focus on your line and length. Unfortunately, they've pitched this a little loose, and it probably deserves to be smacked away to the boundary.

_childDocuments_.review: Being Dutch and therefor probably 1 of the very few people that plays this game in my country, the lack of Dutch players and the Netherlands not being in the T20 World Cup mode despite them being in the last one and the upcoming one is a big fail for me. There are also some BIG issues with how players behave. When the batsman hits the ball straight ahead the bowler never tries to stop the ball even when it rolls right by him. When the batsman hits the wicket on the other side it's not given as an out. Batsmen will swing at the air in the completely wrong place. Short balls are impossible to hit because the batsman will never raise his bat high enough no matter what shot you are telling him to make. Taking wickets seems to be completely at random and has nothing to do with how well you bowl or what bowling style you use. Fielders will let high balls bounce before they grab them even when they are right underneath the ball and it should be an easy wicket. Fielders also start running well after the ball has been struck so they usually are too late to stop a ball from getting to the boundary. Fielders also have no clue where the boundary is and will grab the ball and then casually walk over the boundary with it. There doesn't seem to be any animations for fielders to throw a ball back before they step over the rope. The commentary is repetitive and at times completely wrong. Run outs are impossible when you are fielding. The fielder will throw the ball way too slow to actually hit the wicket in time or even worse, will throw the ball at some random fielder somewhere else entirely. I have played for over 20 hours now and had ZERO run outs. I also had Steve Smith going out because he stepped over the line well after the ball had been caught by the WK and you have 0 input possibilities to make him stay behind the line. I even yelled: WHAT ARE YOU DOING and he just walked away from the wicket and was run out. LBW is never called by the umpire unless you review it. Now there are positives. The customization is extensive in Career mode. Kits, gear, name and logo of your team, player names, everything can be made as you want it. I obviously chose to play in the Dutch league where random Dutch cities suddenly have cricket teams they don't have in real life and they even play first class cricket which is completely absurd but I can forgive that. The fact that the Netherlands is even in this game should be noted as a plus. The number of licensed teams, players and competitions is pretty good but the IPL being not fully licensed would be a problem for a lot of Indian cricket fans no doubt. The developers seem to be capitalizing on the absence of competition in the cricket gaming market, rather than focusing on genuine innovation or responsive updates.The support and development team appear unresponsive to community feedback, contrary to the expectations set by their previous updates with Cricket 22. This is a stark contrast to smaller studios like Embark, developers of "The Finals," who actively engage with their community and rapidly address player concerns.Cricket 24 might appeal to die-hard fans of the sport who will play regardless of quality, but I advise casual players to steer clear. _childDocuments_.review: The best cricket game out there by far. An absolute treat for cricket enthusiasts. Great game in retrospect now. Incorporates a lot of realistic aspects of cricket. A pleasure to play. Later versions have a high bar to match since expecting quite a bit of fine tuning and additions to later versions. But I am definitely strongly in favour of BigAnt working on more versions. Great Job Guys. Things which were improved since last review - 1) Keeper catches to edges while playing spin were nerfed, which was awesome since it was way too overpowered.2) Massive improvement in ball and game physics as compared to Cricket 22. 3) Defensive shots to spin are much better now since earlier, front foot defence was absolutely useless due to the batter playing down the wrong direction but it's mostly improved now with prompt response time by the developer team too. Props to the team.Scope for improvement - Not sure how much of this can be incorporated but have to call it out since I love this game and would love to see it progress.1) Batting to spin involves a lot of backfoot defence even to full deliveries. Playing the front foot defence even with the correct direction makes the batter play down the wrong line. This needs to be corrected. 2) Some of the assisted shots are quite weird. Backfoot pull/hook to a pace bowler plays for head level bounce even when the ball is not coming high. Sometimes even hits the stumps. Backfoot glance should be played to some of these deliveries. Backfoot glance off the chest is limited to only those deliveries that slide down leg side.3) Sometimes the batter passes through the stumps. This is a major negative and nerfs the gameplay experience.4) Keeper collects to spin have been improved but still a little off. Sometimes keeper collects in front of the stumps and sometimes even in front of the batter.5) Shots off the shoulder of the bat have quite a bit of power if timed well. This is unrealistic. Shots off the shoulder should be very weak.6) Fielder throws need to be looked at. Sometimes, fielder looks at one end and throws to the other to affect a direct hit.7) Not the biggest factor but the commentary is not great. Not very accurate to what is actually happening. For eg -  For a defence which is ideally timed when picked up by the bowler/fielder, the commentator says "definitely stopped 4 runs there". Suggestions - Again, not sure how much of this can be incorporated but would love to see these since I love this game and would love to see it progress.1) For career mode, if you could introduce a version of social media, similar to the ones they have in NBA 2k and/or a version of sports news calling out top performers across the world like they have/used to have in EA sports Fifa series, it would be a massive enhancement in gameplay experience. A feature that could do wonders for the game.2) Celebrations to wickets/milestones can be improved (a very minor point).3) World Test Championship needs to be introduced in Career mode. A big miss at the moment in career mode.4) Instead of Bowler/Keeper diving and throwing themselves to collect fielder throws, you could have backing up by fielders past the bowler/keeper i.e. backup fielders would also track throws and position themselves to collect stray throws.Note: This is a must try for cricket enthusiast. I do not mean to condescend. Love this game. I only want to see this game grow in popularity. Thanks,Nice Guy

_childDocuments_.review: Well I dont normally write reviews and this is my first so here we go. First of all the game looks pretty good although there has been some little bugs I have noticed and one that made me smile was when a fielder threw the ball to the bowler, the bowler caught it even though he had his back to it, must have eyes in the back of his head yeah. :) Players running through each other happens enough to be mentioned here, Some of the commentating brings out some comments of my own, like "that was very good bowling not giving the batters much opportunity".... even though I just hit 5 sixes off that over! Some of the comments dont describe accurately what just happened like saying there was no run from the hit when I just ran my arse off to get 2 from it. Commentators contradicting each other eg. short balls - one commentator says that "he can only bowl 2 of them in an over" the next minute another commentator is saying they can only bowl one an over. There are a few more but you get the idea. They dont effect play but they are bugs none the less and if anything quite humorous in a way the developers probably should address. The biggest bug for me is when I play Country Club in Career mode, when the slips or keeper catch the ball from edges from yorkers the batter is not given out. The commentators say "edge, or thick edge through to the keeper" or similar and the graphics show a clean catch, play continues normally. Even after manual appeals.These are bugs that... er bug me, and I hope they are addressed in the near future. Oh yeah another one the devs probably should look at, when playing and I have only done this in Career mode, I presume it would be the same in any other mode, when I get out all I have to do is click out of Career mode, dont save then go back into Career mode and the game starts on the previous over. My highest score so far using this is about 360! I promise myself I wont do it when I get picked for the Australian test side ;-) It does get a bit repeticious but thats the nature of cricket and I find myself clicking through replays and cut scenes. All in all a good fum game and if you are into cricket you should try this game.Congrats to the devs, just have a look at a few more bugs eh.Well I am a few more hours in and edges off yorkers in the Ashes tests also not given out. So not  much point bowling blue yorkers because caught edges wont see the batsman dismissed.The game can be a bit difficult or clunky to play with PC Keyboard specially fielding, and I find it hard to use all the bowling and batting keys, but hey I am still learning and getting some good scores. Have not tried the game at its hardest yet.Also that little trick about clicking out of game not saving and going back into the game, eventually the green health bar on the batter will wind down to nothing and you are automatically retired hurt, but not before using this to your great advantage.still having fun....

_childDocuments_.review: Although I'm recommending this game, I do want to point out not one or two but lots of concerns regarding the game. However, I was very optimistic about this one because of all the hype that was created around it. 1: The fielding is horrible from fielder not able to judge the ball near the boundary line to every throw being thrown at the stumps 2: The slip fielding in this game is useless 90% of the snicks will go at the speed of light towards the boundary. 3: You can't have a full stadium of crowds even at full crowd the stadium is 40% full.4: At away games the crowd will cheer for the opposing team lol? 5: Commentary is really off sometimes I'd play a defensive shot and Gilchrist will be waffling how the fielder saved it from the boundary.6: Career mode should be much much better and something like Ultimate team from FC24 or similar to that style should be integrated in future games. So that we have something to build and have motivation to play more. This review isn't about the game being negative or that one shouldn't buy but these issues are the ones that i expected Big ant to fix after sometime which they didn't and it is to make the game more successful in future launches. Plus I have spent almost 150 hours on this game so I really do enjoy playing it but the bugs have really started to bug me off (No pun intended) If BA decided to charge 80$ for a game which replicates 2k style career mode and FC24 Ultimate team I'll be the first one to buy

_childDocuments_.review: As the Cricketing season buzzes with excitement, Big Ant Studio presents its latest offering, Cricket 24. This game, while thrilling and detailed, stands under the looming shadows of its predecessor, Cricket 22, echoing many of its strengths and weaknesses.Having crafted four predecessors, Big Ant Studio’s approach towards creating a cricket game is seasoned. Their dedication to delivering a game that’s engaging and lasts a considerable amount of time is commendable. Unlike many sports game adaptations which require players to find joy amidst obvious flaws, Cricket 24 offers a smoother experience.* Game Features and Licenses:-  Cricket 24 unfolds as a vast game encompassing a plethora of features. From globally renowned tournaments like The   Ashes to the rapid T20 leagues, the game has it all. This edition also steps into the colossal Indian cricket market with   some, albeit not all, IPL teams. The availability of character and team creation tools allows players to bring their   imagination to life.* Career Mode – A Step Back?:-  Cricket 22 introduced players to an intriguing career mode teeming with narrative elements and training minigames.   Cricket 24, rather disappointingly, has chosen to trim this feature rather than expand it, creating a void for players who   loved the narrative gameplay.*On-Field Gameplay:-  The on-field gameplay is a testament to Big Ant Studio’s expertise. Batting stands out as a joyous experience, allowing   players to choose between arcade and simulation modes. Bowling, although detailed, loses its charm due to a sense of   detachment from the real-life spontaneity of the sport. The AI, particularly while bowling, often makes the gameplay feel   predetermined, stripping it of the excitement that real cricket offers. This makes matches against AI less challenging and   somewhat predictable, contrary to playing with a real opponent.*Visuals and Aesthetics:-  One of the standout features of Cricket 24 is its visual representation. From the intricate player models, thanks to the   photogrammetry process, to the expansive stadiums, the game offers a visual treat. However, the movement of players   lacks the natural fluidity observed in real-life athletes. Despite this, the overall visuals, including the player kits and   broadcast-quality camera angles, enhance the gaming experience. *MY IN GAME EXPERIENCE REGARDING CRICKET 24:-    As far as gameplay goes, Cricket 24 is great fun. With different bowling and batting styles to entertain, it has a level of     depth that will appeal to both newcomers and existing fans of the series.     Cricket 24 has some flaws and bugs that needs to be fixed especially in the Fielding department and will be fixed as the     developers are constantly listening to the Cricket Community giving patches which is improving the gameplay day by day     making it more flexible and quite enjoyable too...    POSITIVES:-* Control options to suit newcomers and experienced players* International licensing including men’s and women’s leagues* Licensed player appearances and kit attention to detailNEGATIVES:-* Some new gameplay mechanics are not fully polished* The game can be prone to occasional bugs* The presentation is somewhat lacking in my opinionFINAL NOTE:-Cricket 24, while commendable in its vastness and core gameplay, seems to have missed the mark in capturing the essence of a full-fledged cricket match.Big Ant Studios are a team known for their dedication to constant improvement, and we may see these things fixed through patches and updates in coming weeks, months.As Big Ant Studios continues its journey, there is hope that they will dive deeper into the nuances of cricket, bringing to life the ebbs and flows of the game that make it so revered globally. Until then, Cricket 24 offers a fun, immersive experience, even if it doesn’t bowl a perfect yorker.Last But not the least I would like to thank specially Kapcha42 and CP (Community Pro) for recommending this great game and Hoping that future patches and updates will make the game more versatile and enjoyable...Thank You Big Ant Studios for these masterpiece of a game hope you guys will not stop developing Cricket simulation game in future times.My Rating Regarding Cricket 24:- 7.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Cricket 24: A Masterpiece Unveiled in 2023Cricket enthusiasts, your long-awaited dream has come true with Cricket 24. This game, announced months ago, has finally arrived, and it's a true game-changer. Let's dive into why this game is an absolute must-buy.The Menu and UI: Cricket 24's new menu sound, background music, and UI are a visual treat. It's a promising start, and we can anticipate more exciting changes down the line.New Commentary Package: The addition of fresh commentary lines is a game-changer. It's a massive upgrade that transforms the gaming experience, and Gillie's commentary is a standout.IPL Inclusion: The inclusion of IPL with all eight major teams is a monumental step. This alone makes Cricket 24 a significant upgrade. Those who clamored for IPL in the game are getting their wish granted.Licensed International Teams: Pakistan and PSL are now part of the game, a testament to the developer's massive efforts. More nations are on the horizon, promising an even broader cricketing experience.Visual Brilliance: Cricket 24's visuals are top-notch. Player models are sharper, grass is more vibrant, and the ball physics are incredibly realistic. The game truly brings the stadiums to life.Lighting Effects: Day and night matches are finely tuned for a lifelike experience. If you have an OLED TV, the game's magic is even more pronounced.Player Motions: Player movements are more realistic and fluid, immersing you in the action. The attention to detail in player motions is now becomes hallmark of BA's games.New and Improved Shots: Two new batting styles and a host of new shots within existing styles are a delightful surprise. Style #7 is a particular favorite, adding to the game's allure.Here's why this game is a must-buy for users who still plays Cricket 19 :——————************———————Prepare to be blown away by the wealth of new features in Cricket 24. This game has raised the bar with innovative additions that redefine the cricket gaming experience. Let's explore these thrilling enhancements:New Batting Style: Introducing the seventh batting style, a tribute to the legendary Sir Sachin Tendulkar. This style is a game-changer, allowing players to emulate the master himself.Revamped Bowling Styles: Cricket 24 unveils four new bowling styles, featuring the blistering pace of Shoaib Akhtar and Trent Boult for the speedsters, and the magical spin of Muttiah Muralitharan and the crafty Harbhajan Singh for the spinners. These bowling styles offer a fresh and challenging dimension to the game.Licensed Player Appearances: Expect lifelike player avatars, particularly from the IPL teams, where players bear a striking resemblance to their real-life counterparts. It's an impressive level of detail that enhances the immersive experience.Dynamic Batting Moves: The game has perfected pull shots and backfoot defense, providing players with even more control over their shots. Hitting boundaries or defending skillfully has never felt more satisfying.Responsive Fielders: Fielders in Cricket 24 are more agile and proactive than ever before, a substantial improvement from Cricket 22. However, there's room for further enhancements in future updates to make fielding even more realistic and less robotic.Balanced Fielding: Gone are the days of the "GOD-like" short cover fielder. Now, even a slight mistimed shot may find its way in front of the fielder, adding an element of unpredictability.Frontfoot Defensive Mastery: Batsmen showcase beautiful frontfoot defense moves, leaning forward to reach the ball. This provides a more authentic cricketing experience, although introducing a random element to this skill is a thoughtful suggestion.Expanded Arsenal of Shots: Cricket 24 introduces a variety of new cricketing shots, including the late Square Cut, Sachin's Classical Straight Drive, Joe Root's innovative Ramp Shot (Reverse Scoop shot), and a range of Cover Drives and Slogging shots, similar to those of Surya Kumar Yadav. It's a small but impactful touch that adds to the realism.Pre-match Huddle: Witness players huddling up before the start of the match, a detail that adds authenticity to the game's atmosphere and showcases the team spirit of cricket.In conclusion, Cricket 24 isn't just a game; it's a love letter to cricket fans. It's the embodiment of dedication, innovation, and authenticity, and it promises to deliver an unmatched cricketing experience. If you're a cricket enthusiast, this game is more than a purchase; it's an investment in the love and passion you hold for the sport. Get ready to be captivated, challenged, and thrilled like never before with Cricket 24.Note - Let me be clear, this is not a paid review. _childDocuments_.review: Rating: ★★★★☆ (4/5)As someone with over 400 hours in Cricket 24, I’ve had the chance to explore nearly every aspect of this game, and overall, it’s an impressive cricket simulation with a few notable strengths and areas for improvement.Gameplay & MechanicsCricket 24 offers one of the most authentic cricketing experiences available on PC. The depth of mechanics for both batting and bowling is well-designed, providing a realistic challenge that captures the essence of the sport. Batting has a satisfying feel, with proper timing and shot selection being crucial, while bowling comes with a decent level of complexity, rewarding strategic placement and understanding the batter's weaknesses.However, the learning curve can be steep for newcomers, and it might take a while to truly master all aspects of the game. Once you do, though, the gameplay becomes a highly rewarding experience.Graphics & PresentationThe visuals in Cricket 24 are solid. Player models and stadiums look detailed, and the overall presentation has improved from its predecessors. Weather effects, lighting, and field conditions add to the immersion, especially when playing longer formats like Test matches. While the animations for players have gotten better, there are still occasional glitches or robotic movements, but nothing too distracting.Career ModeThis is where I’ve spent a significant chunk of my time. The Career Mode is one of the game’s highlights. Starting as a rookie and working your way up to international cricket is a thrilling experience. The ability to choose between different leagues and formats adds variety, though I’d love to see more depth in the interactions and storyline elements. Improvements in player dynamics or adding a personal touch could elevate the career experience even further.Multiplayer & AIThe online multiplayer offers a lot of fun for those looking for real competition, but there are occasional issues with matchmaking and lag. When it works, the thrill of playing against a skilled human opponent can't be beaten, but technical issues can sometimes detract from the experience. The AI, on the other hand, is fairly competent, although it can be frustrating at times, especially with field placements and decision-making.Game Modes & CustomizationWith a wide range of game modes, including Test matches, T20s, and tournaments, there’s enough content to keep you engaged for hundreds of hours. The customization options for teams, players, and even leagues give players the freedom to create their ideal cricketing world. This is a big plus for those who like to modify and tailor the game to their liking.Bugs & IssuesLike any sports game, Cricket 24 isn’t without its bugs. Over my playtime, I’ve encountered a few crashes and minor glitches, particularly with replays and player models. The developers have been active with updates, which is a positive sign, but there’s still room for optimization, especially in terms of loading times and server stability in multiplayer matches.ConclusionAfter 438 hours, I can confidently say that Cricket 24 is a must-play for any cricket enthusiast. While a few areas could be polished, the game’s core mechanics, immersive gameplay, and variety of modes make it worth the investment. Whether you’re playing solo in Career Mode or competing against others online, there’s enough here to keep you coming back for more.

_childDocuments_.review: A Roller coaster Ride: Cricket 24 Review(Bought it again after it got somewhat fixed and writing a fresh review)Cricket 24 is the latest addition to the virtual cricketing arena, promising an immersive experience for fans of the sport. While the game boasts several positive aspects, it falls short in certain areas, leaving room for improvement.Positives:-->Photo symmetry of the Players:Cricket 24 excels in bringing the players to life with exceptional photo symmetry. The attention to detail in replicating the physical features and expressions of real-life cricketers adds a layer of authenticity to the gaming experience.-->Improved Batting and Bowling:The game has made significant strides in refining the batting and bowling mechanics. The controls feel more intuitive, providing players with a greater sense of control and skill when facing deliveries or sending down a crucial over.-->Official Licences:Cricket 24 has successfully secured official licenses, enhancing the realism by featuring authentic team names, player likenesses, and tournament branding. This adds a level of immersion that is sure to please cricket purists.Negatives:-->Drops in the Frame rate:Unfortunately, Cricket 24 suffers from occasional drops in frame rate, impacting the overall smoothness of the game play. These inconsistencies can be jarring and affect the overall gaming experience.-->Inaccurate Ball Hitting Direction:The radar fails to accurately depict the direction in which the ball is hit. This discrepancy can lead to confusion and frustration among players, especially when strategic decisions hinge on reliable information.-->Run out Issues:Despite being comfortably inside the crease, players often find themselves victims of runouts. This persistent issue disrupts the flow of the game and needs urgent attention through updates.-->Subpar Fielding:The fielding mechanics in Cricket 24 leave much to be desired. Players report instances of awkward movements, delayed responses, and missed opportunities that detract from the realism the game aims to achieve.-->Bad Animations:The game suffers from substandard animations that can detract from the overall gaming experience. Unnatural movements and glitches in the animation sequences may impact the visual appeal and immersion of Cricket 24.-->Below Par Commentary:Cricket 24 disappoints with lackluster commentary. There are instances where a remarkable bowling performance is attributed to the wrong player, undermining the immersive quality of the in-game commentary.-->Numerous Bugs:The game is plagued by a multitude of bugs that hinder the overall experience. These range from minor glitches to more significant issues, and addressing them is crucial for players to enjoy the game without constant interruptions.-->Review System Issues:When reviewing a decision, the replay often goes missing, leaving players clueless about what has happened. The direct transition to the big screen without proper replay analysis is a flaw that needs immediate attention.-->Slow-motion Replay Dysfunction:The slow-motion replay feature in Cricket 24 is plagued by functionality issues. Instead of providing a detailed view, it consistently plays the video at 3x speed, rendering the feature ineffective for reviewing critical moments accurately.In conclusion, Cricket 24 offers a mixed bag of delights and disappointments. While the game's positive aspects contribute to an enjoyable experience, the negatives, such as frame rate drops, bad animations, and persistent bugs, need urgent attention to elevate Cricket 24 to the level of excellence expected by avid cricket gaming enthusiasts.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to go ahead and say it... this game sucks. It's priced like a AAA title but plays like something your 17-year-old computer-engineering cousin might make as a hobby. This game would be fairly priced closer to $10-12, as there is some entertainment value, but from a game development aspect it's almost like they forgot to actually finish it. Almost every aspect of the game is embarrassing if you're a professional developer, you cannot  show even one over of gameplay to someone and not have to apologize for at least 12 mistakes. The commentators are watching a completely different game, and not a single thing they say has anything to do with what's actually going on. Which lends itself to the actual problem, which is that clearly no one at the studio played this game before releasing it. Testing? What testing? Why would anyone waste time on testing? This is a game that is about 20% developed, and after all the post-release patches it is at about 25%. If I were a game developer, I would not want to attach my name to this game - it's a great resume for how to not make it in gaming, and when considering that it costs as much as Game of the Year titles, it's quite sickening. The game is largely unplayable without customized gameplay setting changes due to the fact that almost every ball faced will be edged to the keeper and caught on medium-and-higher difficulty. There is no attention paid to quality-of-life improvements, such as the ability to save your squad from one match to another amidst a tournament, the amount of times you have to rebuild the entire lineup is a waste of precious time. Most other games have learned from game developers before them and added at least the minimum workable UI that is expected in a next-gen game, but this one seems to start from scratch and attempt to rebuild the wheel from a very early 2000s game design that they've improved on only minimally. This game misses all the crucial dimensions to immerse one into a true cricket match, and after 27 hours of playing the game I still don't have that cricket thrill and feel and seems like I'm mostly just playing Stick Cricket with 3D graphics. After 3 lackluster and lazy attempts this is largely still the same poor quality cricket game that it has been, and it's probably time to hang it up and let someone more competent take a shot. I can give them a pass on the fact that they don't have enough licensed content to make this game feel authentic, given that the community has done a decent job at bridging that gap (despite the lackluster tools available), and seeing as how no licensor would ever want their brand being tarnished by such a poorly designed and poorly developed game, but even that is a big factor contributing to the failure of this game to present a respectable standard. If you can get t his game for free, it's worth a play or two after considerable customization and manual setup to make it even somewhat enjoyable. For any price >$0 it starts to exponentially become not worth it. To say I'm disappointed is clearly an understatement, to say I would recommend this game, an outright lie.

_childDocuments_.review: Having spent considerable time with Cricket 24, I find myself both impressed and frustrated. On the positive side, I absolutely love how realistic the player movements are this year. The fluidity in batting, bowling, and fielding is remarkably lifelike. Passing the ball around the field feels natural and adds a layer of enjoyment that keeps me engaged in each match.As a career mode enthusiast, I'm thrilled that they've scanned most of the players I wanted to see. This attention to detail enhances the authenticity of the game, making team management and player development over multiple seasons genuinely satisfying. It's not every day that a sports game captures the essence of so many players so well, and it's a feature that keeps me coming back for more.However, there are significant issues that dampen my overall experience. A major concern is the workaround that many players have discovered for the AI opponents. This exploit undermines the challenge and excitement of facing off against computer-controlled teams. It feels like a shortcut that detracts from the skill and strategy the game should encourage.Another aspect that frustrates me is how heavily scripted the gameplay feels at times. There are moments when outcomes seem predetermined, regardless of my input or strategy. This scripting diminishes the sense of control and immersion, making some matches feel unfair or unrewarding.I also can't help but feel that EA has us scammed each year with the high price tag, yet they continue to get away with it. While there are improvements, they often seem incremental rather than substantial. It raises questions about the value for money, especially when the game doesn't address longstanding issues that players have pointed out. In conclusion, Cricket 24 offers a mix of highs and lows for me. The realistic movements and extensive player scans greatly enhance the gameplay, particularly in career mode, which is where I spend most of my time. However, the exploitable AI, scripted moments, and questionable pricing strategy leave much to be desired. While I appreciate the strides made in certain areas, I hope future installments will address these shortcomings to deliver a more balanced and fulfilling cricketing experience.

_childDocuments_.review: SUBJECT: SUGGESTION: Enhancing Realism in Cricket 22 & 24: Implement Dynamic Wicketkeeper Positioning Based on forward Batsman Movement Specially to fast bowlers.In real-world cricket, when a batsman steps significantly outside the crease, wicketkeepers often adjust their positioning closer to the stumps to create opportunities for stumping. However, in Cricket 22 and Cricket 24, this critical dynamic is missing. Wicketkeepers fail to adapt their positioning (especially in the case of fast bowlers), even when the batsman advances, leading to unrealistic gameplay. As a result, batsmen can confidently step down the pitch, even against fast bowlers, sometimes advancing halfway, and hit the ball without facing any real risk of being stumped. This undermines the realism of the game, allowing players to take exaggerated liberties that compromise the competitive balance and tactical depth.This issue affects all formats—Tests, T20s, and ODIs—and addressing it is crucial for improving the game's authenticity. Implementing a feature where wicketkeepers dynamically adjust their positioning based on the batsman’s movements, even for faster bowlers, would significantly enhance the gameplay experience and align it more closely with real-world cricket.I have played Cricket 22 and 24 on Switch, steam deck and computer and the problem remains the same across the platform.

_childDocuments_.review: Cricket 24 is the latest installment in the popular cricket video game series, and it delivers a solid experience for cricket enthusiasts. Here’s an overview of the game:GameplayCricket 24 offers a comprehensive cricketing experience with a wide range of game modes, including Test matches, T20s, and One-Day Internationals. The controls are intuitive, catering to both casual players and hardcore fans. The shot selection feels more fluid, and the improved AI provides a more realistic challenge, making the gameplay feel dynamic and engaging.Graphics and PresentationThe visuals in Cricket 24 have seen a noticeable upgrade. Player models are more detailed, and stadiums are recreated with impressive accuracy, capturing the atmosphere of real-world cricket venues. However, while the graphics are good, they still fall short compared to other contemporary sports games. Some animations can feel a bit stiff, and player likenesses are hit or miss.Content and FeaturesOne of the highlights of Cricket 24 is the extensive licensing, which includes teams, players, and tournaments from around the world. The career mode is deeper and more immersive than in previous editions, allowing players to build a career from the ground up. The inclusion of women's cricket is a welcome addition, reflecting the growing popularity of the sport across genders.MultiplayerThe online multiplayer experience is generally smooth, with a variety of match types to choose from. However, connectivity issues and occasional lag can disrupt the experience. The community features, like tournaments and leagues, add to the game's replayability, offering something for both competitive and casual players.Sound and CommentaryThe commentary in Cricket 24 is decent, with a good variety of lines that add to the realism of the game. However, it can become repetitive after extended play sessions. The sound effects, such as the crack of the bat and crowd noise, are well done and enhance the overall atmosphere.Overall ImpressionCricket 24 is a worthy addition to the series, offering enough new features and improvements to satisfy both long-time fans and newcomers. While it may not be a perfect game, particularly in terms of graphics and occasional online issues, it still provides an enjoyable and immersive cricket experience. If you're a fan of cricket, this game is definitely worth picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: **Cricket 24: A Promising Delivery with Some Dropped Catches**Cricket 24 steps up to the crease as the latest installment in Big Ant Studios' cricket franchise, and while it delivers some impressive shots, it also suffers from a few unforced errors.**The Good:*** **Authenticity:** Cricket 24 captures the essence of the sport with realistic gameplay, player animations, and detailed stadiums. Batting feels smooth and responsive, while bowling offers a wide variety of deliveries to outfox opponents.* **Licenses:** The game boasts an extensive roster of officially licensed teams and players, including The Ashes and major domestic leagues. This adds a layer of immersion for fans who want to play with their favorite cricketers.* **Customization:** Cricket 24 offers a deep level of customization, from creating your own players and teams to tweaking gameplay settings to your liking.* **Graphics:** The game looks great, with improved visuals and lighting compared to previous installments.**The Bad:*** **Bugs:** The game suffers from a number of bugs and glitches, ranging from minor graphical issues to game-breaking crashes. Big Ant Studios has been working on patches, but there are still several issues that need to be addressed.* **AI:** The AI can be inconsistent, sometimes making questionable decisions or bowling unrealistic deliveries.* **Career Mode:** The career mode feels underwhelming and lacks the depth and progression of other sports games.**Overall:**Cricket 24 is a promising cricket game with a solid foundation, but it's hampered by bugs and some questionable AI decisions. Big Ant Studios has a history of improving their games post-launch, so it's possible that Cricket 24 will become a much better game with future updates.If you're a die-hard cricket fan who can overlook the current flaws, you'll still find plenty to enjoy in Cricket 24. However, if you're looking for a polished and refined cricket experience, you may want to wait for future patches or consider other options.**Recommendation:**If you're willing to be patient and wait for updates, Cricket 24 has the potential to be a great cricket game. If you're looking for a game to play right now, you may want to consider other options or wait for a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this is a fun game to play and is comprehensive in terms of the number of real-life or close-to-real life tournaments it contains such as the World Cup, Ashes, IPL, BBL, etc. It is also comprehensive in terms of the fact that it has women's cricket with many of these same real-life or close-to-real life tournaments. Big Ant did a good job of incorporating Women's Indian Premier League or WPL in this - only it is called something different with the team names being slightly different. That is understandable considering they probably did not get the license to use the real team names or the real name of the league itself.Having said this and having played many other cricket games before such as EA Sports Cricket, Codemasters's Ashes, etc., I have to say it is disappointing how many bugs there are in this game. The AI fielders in your team are morons who will just stand by and watch a ball go through when it is right near them. There is also something severely wrong with the calendar in career mode. Even though you have plenty of days, the training or rest times are locked for no valid reason. It happens quite commonly.The commentary is beyond terrible - it is too repetitive with Atherton, Gilchrist, Mitchell, etc. saying the same thing over and over again. This is one place EA Sports won back in the day, which sometimes had the Commentators recite great moments in the history of cricket or cricket statistics. There is none of that in this. What's more - there are also bugs in the Commentary with Alison Mitchell regularly talking about what is in store for the next team coming to bat when that team has already batted its last innings or a better getting out after a half-century and not moving on when he/she never even got a half-century. I should also note there should not be commentary, particularly from great cricket legends like Gilchrist and Atherton, in minor tournaments such as Canada Cricket League or very low level cricket leagues in any of the major cricketing nations. It is ridiculous to have anyone believe that they would provide commentary in such leagues.There is also no sync between what is happening on the field and what the commentators say - most of the times it is either irrelevant or simply moronic (e.g. batters would get 12 runs in an over in a Test match and commentators will say the bowler kept in tight. 12 runs in one over in a Test match is NOT tight!). And what is with the "they, their, and them" neuter-gender pronouns. This is where I draw the line on liberalism. It sounds so odd and terrible. If Big Ant was expecting a hats off on political correctness, I am sorry, they are not getting it. You clearly call the men's career mode "men's career mode" and the women's career mode "women's career mode." So, just use "he, his, him" for the men and "she, her" for the women. It sounds beyond odd to rigidly apply political correctness in the manner they did. Unless some gamer is overly sensitive, they are not going to be offended by use of "he, his, him" for men or "she, her" for women. The only other reason I can think of for this "they, their, them" is laziness - the programmers did not want to waste time for creating a separate "he, his, him" or "she, her" for the men's and women's games separately. If that is the reason, well... Big Ant has won the award for laziness.There are other noticeable errors or areas of the game that are simply lacking making me wonder if Big Ant put any effort into this at all. For example, the user-created player's earnings are not accessible for buying equipment or training to improve skills, the training is an endless cycle which does not result in improved skills for your player if even if the player completes it successfully, there is simply no way I have found to increase the player's skills. How did Big Ant miss this? This the same company that created AO Tennis, where all of these things are possible for the user-created player (although that game was beyond boring). There could have also been a way to allow the player to create international teams of their own, such as for example, a US or Canada women's cricket team. This last part is not a bug or an inexcusable oversight, but others I mentioned here clearly are.Again, that doesn't take away the fact the game is fun to play. But the above bugs and lameness and be putting off to gamers. In summary, I would give this game "5" for fun, but only  a "2" over all, maybe 2.5. Big Ant has a long way to go to improve this game. As to the price of the game - yeah, it is pricey and I would not pay the full price. I bought it at a discount when it was offered. Wait for the discount. I wish there was a third option for this as opposed to recommended versus not recommended. If there had been one, I would have chosen that - something like "neutral."Addendum: this comment needs to be added; leaving out the five-time IPL champions, Chennai Super Kings was not only really noticeable, but also just a big downer.

_childDocuments_.review: I love cricket, I love big ant, I love video games. But this game still has me rubbed the wrong way, Yes it looks fantastic, so real and so great. However it plays very poorly, there is something innately unfun about Cricket 24's game play. The realism barrier is immediately broken, and doesn't feel balanced compared to Cricket 22, the commentary is dumb at the best of times, when a defensive block is sent straight to the bowler and the commentator announces an amazing stop for 4, or when the ball sails into the keepers gloves and the commentator goes, I have no idea what they are appealing for, it feels annoying and ruins the big moments. Fielding is also incredible overpowered, AI fielders can make every single type of physically impossible catch, apart from dollies that kids would catch when you're bowling of course. Not to mention every single fielder has the fastest rocket arm in the world. Bowling also is completely unchanged, working for a wicket feels tedious and stupid, especially when hard work and toil rewards an edge, dropped, and the next ball the batter finds their footwork and smashes it over your head for 6. Batting however for me is the biggest let down, so many new shots, 360 cricket, and yet you find yourself getting out to impossible catches, getting bairstowed while spamming the no run button or pressing the special shots trigger just for your player to play a cover drive and get bowled. It makes no sense, and is such a let down especially when a non-360 game such as cricket 22 felt better to bat in. No part of me understands why this game was released when it was, it feels so unpolished and unfinished, which is such a disservice to the incredible work we all know Big Ant do, just look at the game! Why was this game pushed out of the door when it wasn't ready, It needs so much fixing, and after that it needs more content. Especially around the bone dry Career Mode. Overall disappointing but still probably the best cricket game out there, marginally.

name: Black Myth: Wukong
detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition The Black Myth: Wukong Digital Deluxe Edition includes: - Black Myth: Wukong Full Game - Weapon: Bronzecloud Staff - Equipment: Folk Opera Mask, Folk Opera Almsgiving Armor, Folk Opera Leather Bracers, and Folk Opera Buskins - Curio: Wind Chimes - Selected Digital Soundtrack ※ The included weapon, equipment, and curio can be claimed from the Trailblazer's Gift menu at the Keeper's Shrine (Respawn Point) during the early stages of the game. ※ Selected Digital Soundtrack allows you to listen to multiple selected musical tracks from the game by activating the Music Library function on the game's title screen. We highly recommend that you first experience these pieces as you journey through the game as the Destined One, then return here to relive them to your heart's content. About the Game Black Myth: Wukong is an action RPG rooted in Chinese mythology. The story is based on Journey to the West, one of the Four Great Classical Novels of Chinese literature. You shall set out as the Destined One to venture into the challenges and marvels ahead, to uncover the obscured truth beneath the veil of a glorious legend from the past. • Explore a Land of Vast Wonders 'A world unseen, where wonders gleam, And with each stride, a new scene streams.' Enter a fascinating realm filled with the wonders and discoveries of ancient Chinese mythology! As the Destined One, you shall traverse an array of breathtaking and distinctive landscapes from the classic tale, composing an epic of adventure that is seen anew. • Confront Mighty Foes, Old and New 'Heroic Monkey, might and fame, Adversaries rise, to test his name.' One of the major highlights of Journey to the West is its diverse cast of adversaries, each with their unique strengths. As the Destined One, you will encounter powerful foes and worthy rivals throughout your journey. Fearlessly engage them in epic battles where surrender is not an option. • Temper Your Mastery of Varied Spells 'Spells unbound, talents in play, Unleashed abilities seize the day.' Spells, transformations, and magic vessels of all manifestations, in which some counteract while others amplify, have long been iconic combat elements of Chinese mythology. As the Destined One, aside from mastering various staff techniques, you can also freely combine different spells, abilities, weapons, and equipment to find a winning strategy that best suits your combat style. • Discover Heartfelt Tales Behind Every Facade 'Within all souls, both wild and tame, There thrives a tale of life's fierce flame.' Beneath the ferocity and craftiness of your foes lies an engaging tapestry of their origins, personalities, and motivations waiting to be revealed. As the Destined One, you will uncover the stories behind a variety of characters, delving beyond your battles with them to taste the love, hate, greed, and fury they once held and still carry within.

_childDocuments_.review: When Black Myth: Wukong dropped, I was very skeptical. I grew up as a huge DBZ fan but had no idea that Wukong was a source of inspiration. Honestly, the game looked like another try-hard, wanna-be souls-like that was simply cashing in on an iconic character. Boy, was I wrong.I started seeing gameplay videos flooding youtube and tiktok. While certainly a very similar feeling to the Souls series when it comes to boss fights, it feels very unique and refreshing in its own way. Combat is top notch, the controls are tight, and the the skill tree is both dense and rewarding. While the core gameplay is comprised of mainly bouncing between boss battles with a few (and I mean, very few) enemies, the "open world" feels very good to explore. Each time I tuck into a corner or press forward just a little further to see, I'm often rewarded with a hidden chest. There's a robust crafting system, brewing, spells and transformations galore. Respeccing your character is not only free of charge, but encouraged to try new strategies for each boss. I think my favorite part is there's no lost progress upon death. You always maintain your progress, making death feel more like a minor setback than a soul-crushing experience. Pun fully intended. As a mid-30's gamer, I will not get into games that don't respect my time and this one does so beautifully. But while Black Myth Wukong ticks all of these boxes to make a great game, it's story is what truly captivates me. Rarely do I care about the lore behind bosses, but each of these seem to be hand crafted with great detail and I find myself reading their entries after each boss battle. Learning more of their story is almost as good as the loot. It's a strange, perplexing, and difficult journey and I look forward to more beautifully crafted cut scenes after each chapter. There's only one downside to the game that I can really bring up: You have to git gud. There's no running away and overleveling like Elden Ring. There's no ridiculous OP weapons or summons that will hard carry you through encounters. Often times it's just you, the boss, and all of your abilities on cooldown. There are times that some fights seem ridiculous, but I can honestly say it never feels unfair when I die. The game makes you get up close and learn the dance of each boss. Really gets your blood pumping and once you finally down that boss after multiple attempts, the feeling is euphoric. Because YOU did it. So if that's the only negative, then it's one I'll gladly accept. Getting stuck in the Water Temple for weeks made me appreciate that piece of the Triforce. Downing Ruby and Emerald Weapon after weeks of grinding and min-maxing were moments of monumental bliss. I've got a feeling that Black Myth Wukong has a few achievements like this waiting for me at the end, and I'm looking forward to every second of it. Go buy this game. I'll update this review upon completion, but there's a high chance this will be my favorite release this year. UPDATE EDIT:100 hours in and I've completed the game 100%. All 81 achievements. Currently on NG+3 and still loving it, although I've decided to put it down for now. The sheer enjoyment this game has brought me has made it my personal GOTY. I loved it enough to beat it 3 different times and get all the achievemnets and not once did I ever think "Aw man, I've gotta log in to do X, Y, Z..." Through all the trials and tribulations, I have persevered. And it has been the experience I've needed for a long time. P.S. Screw you Developers. How dare you make me actually shed a manly tear over a spider and a pig.

The only memorable music is from a character in Act 2, which you'll know right away.6/10 Wait for a sale, I got my copy for "free" with my 4070 RTX. _childDocuments_.review: Started very well, got bad very quickly. It IS a souls like indeed, don't get confused by the marketing and what many people are saying. If you're planning to buy the game and don't like souls level hardships, unfairness and rage-inducing gimmicks, maybe redirect your budget on something else.Have I become the only gamer who doesn't find endless trial & error and grinding a massive boss' healthbar for 10 entire minutes fun? Is there anyone else who feels much more rewarded by beating a boss in just one or two attempts after an engaging, focused and fair fight that forces you to play well and use all the mechanics that the games has to offer, but doesn't force you to learn the boss patterns by heart through endless repetition and a dozen unfair deaths, just to finally beat him because you finally had some luck?Chapter 1 is perfect at doing what I just described and I enjoyed it a lot. Difficulty was well balanced there, fights were engaging, challenging and fun without ever getting frustrating. But in chapter 2, suddenly, it becomes a proper souls like with a massive difficulty spike, bosses with endless health bars that barely take any damage but have endless combos that can destroy yours, camera issues that become your enemy more than the enemy himself. I was halfway through chapter 3 and got to the Pagoda Prison boss, that's where I uninstalled the game. After beating a stupid massive dragon in a totally random way (because the fight itself is purely random) and having to go through the most annoying level design ever in the prison, here we are with another huge, annoying boss with an almost invulnerable health bar... no, thanks.Moreover, exploration gets so damn confusing from chapter 2 and a lot of rage-inducing elements are copy-pasted from Dark Souls and randomly introduced. To make it even worse, the environments are just not at all impressive. Chapter 2 is just red rocks everywhere, chapter 3 is just snow everywhere (excluding the prison, that's awfully confusing to navigate and definitely not fun to explore). Everything gets repetitive, frustrating, infuriating and uninteresting very quickly, and it's a real shame because the combat system is very fun to use in fair fights, the design of the enemies is really inspired, the general atmosphere of Chinese mithology is fascinating, but that is not enough. A game needs to be fun in the first place and this one stopped to be after less than 20% of its length.I feel like From Software has ruined the action genre as every action game nowadays borrows the WORST souls-like elements just to follow this damn trend. I'm sooo sick of it.P.S. I market the product as received for free because I got a free code with my Nvidia graphics card. I didn't receive the product from the software house directly.
