_childDocuments_.review: It's impressive what they've achieved with the gameplay of this game. I can't recall experiencing similar mechanics in any other game; it's completely innovative. The game is incredibly fun, with gameplay that's simple and easy to understand, yet it’s built on solid foundations that allow the gameplay to evolve into more complex combinations using the same basic mechanics. It's an elegant and well-constructed gameplay experience.On the other hand, the story so far is fascinating. The art is beautiful, but we're constantly encountering more and more breathtaking landscapes. I'm eager to see the battles that will unfold later in the campaign. I highly recommend this game. I'm enjoying it on the Steam Deck, and I believe it’s exceptionally well-suited for portable play.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: (also played the demo for 2.5 hours)At first I was pretty compelled by the story and unique music. The direction definitely feels modern, and the social commentary is a nice touch. The combat can be pretty difficult and engaging. However, these encounters quickly become repetitive and feel more as if they were a hindrance to the RPG aspect of the game.I do not enjoy being forced to change gameplay styles each chapter in these fights. Not because the characters you switch to, with differing skill trees, are weaker or stronger, nor because the enemies change (which is not enough), but because the new characters are less exciting. Companions in the past have the move sets and occasionally the same culture of your future protagonists, so you're already used to them, and you're also used to the setting and quirks of their group. The differing combat trees don't feel rewarding, just tedious. Companions so far were more engaging than your character, but they're momentary. The item system has good RPG mechanics, but the items in combat feel about as boring as the rest of your characters moves. While the game has fantasy aspects, your character's gameplay is grounded down to a boring, historical viewpoint of weaponry. As the game got through the later chapters, the quality of the story definitely started to dip, NPCs felt repetitive with earlier conversations, music - once excitingly fresh - now became stale. I loved the demo and exploring a new world, but now it feels like a chore. Unfortunately I can't recommend the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I had a great time playing this game!Great visuals and beautiful music. The story is on a heavy side, but I enjoyed it and find it very compelling. I felt invested in the characters. I love playing through different arcs that converge in the end.The battle mechanics are really cool. It's both dynamic and strategic at the same time.The skill trees really give depth to each characters and allow you to pick different play-styles.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I knew I would enjoy playing this game when I first got to play with its "we-go" tactics system and found a wide array of ways to handle any given encounter.I knew I would find the game endearing when I made a donkey mad at me and I watched a character sprite waddle across the screen with no walking animation.I knew this game would be something  when it delivered a sudden, raw gut punch, and then just kept going. No lengthy cutscene, no musical swells, just tragedy striking in the midst of sudden chaos. There was no time for gravitas or reflection, everything kept moving and before I knew it the moment was gone and so were so many of those who had once surrounded me.And then a different, also very frustrated looking donkey joined my party.This might sound like tonal whiplash, and in some ways it is, but I promise that all of the rapid changes in tone are handled with incredible care. The sudden swings in mood are built to reflect life, how quickly a moment of joy can be brought down by tragedy only to be brought back up again by connecting with others who have experienced the same pain. More specifically, it's a story about how colonial atrocities exacerbate the already tough ups and downs of life for those who are forced to experience them. It is about those who survive and have to find ways to keep living not just as things change, but as things are ripped away from them by colonial greed.If you are a tactics nerd, there is a lot to love here gameplay-wise. And I do love it's gameplay! But that isn't why I'm hooked. I'm hooked because I have felt the pain of wanting desperately to tell someone how much they mean to me, only to throw up a middle finger and a smile and hope they can read between the lines. I'm hooked because I've had moments of ecstasy and joy be suddenly interrupted by the death of a loved one, only to have my subsequent sobs interrupted by laughter at a cat (or in the game's case, a donkey) doing some stupid ♥♥♥♥. I'm hooked because I feel humanity emanating from every element of this game's design, plot, and characters, and it , but it only hurts because the game made me care so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ much.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is SO. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. GOOD.* But I hate the ghosts that move during your turn SO MUCH. This would easily be a 9 or 10/10 game without that. With that, I really don't think I could recommend it to anyone who's interested in tactical turn based combat. It's not really turn based a LOT of the time.I have no other complains about this game, the writing is on point, the graphics are so full of charm, but this one mechanic with ghosts that chase you during your turn, giving you no time to actually plan and think, absolutelly tanks the experience for me to a degree that I even find hard to put into words. It's like someone took a ♥♥♥♥ on the Mona Lisa.I cannot stress how much I detest the ghost mechanic. It works thematically but much to the detriment of every other aspect of the gameplay.I really, really, really wish the devs would give you an option to disable it, it kills the vibe of a turn based tactical game for me.There's also a serious issue with some of the stage hazards only impacting the player and not the enemies. One of the examples of this are the mushrooms that grow during a fight taking up space in the arena and if you step on it, you're damaged. However, enemies are not affected by it for some reason...? And then ranged enemies can just stand there shooting at you indefinitely, and if you're playing one of the melee characters, well, you're ♥♥♥♥♥♥. If you're low on health, it's an automatic loss, and a very anti-climatic one at that.tl;dr: Great game, but one or two mechanics really bring the game down for me. No turn-based game, especially one this hard, should put their players on a timer to take their turn. The real time mechanics make me anxious and as a result make me not want to play the game, much less recommend it to friends who would otherwise enjoy it for sure.*Edit: I played more of the game, I've beaten act III and defeated the seemingly infinite waves of guards in the arena for the achievement, and I'm unfortunately going to change my rating.For every single thing I loved in acts I and II, there are three things I absolutely hate about Itzae's campaign, from the inconsistent hitboxes of shielded enemies, to her horribly limited moveset, to how illogical some of the karmic rewards are, and just how god awful it is to interact with the ghost and fungus mechanics with a melee character. Again, I loved acts I and II, except for one or two mechanics as explained above, but after finishing act III, I don't think I want to play this anymore, much less recommend it to anyone else in its current state.Edit 2: I saw the dev's response about assist mode, and for that reason alone I'm changing my review to positive. I still think there are a lot of flaws with the combat, mostly in act 3 and regarding Itzae's kit, but disabling ghosts must help immensely with it, even though now it's a bit too late for me.  I guess the final review is: "Positive, as long as you disable the ghost mechanic from the get go".That is if you're lucky enough to figure out that 'Assist Mode' allows you to do that, which isn't exactly intuitive. You have to first enable it to then see what the options are, and I would never have known it unless the developers explicitly told me.Edit 3, and likely final edit: Disabling the mechanic works, but now playing through act 4 I see a lot of enemies that have skills to specifically summon these ghosts. Now they just summon the ghost and it dies immediately. It makes some fights a joke. These enemies don't attack or move instead, they just stand there and summon a ghost that then dies on the spot.It's... a poorly implemented band-aid at best, but it's still better than nothing.I still recommend the game, but it's not nearly as good as I thought it was when playing acts 1 and 2. It's still worth your time though, and I look forward to see what these devs make in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: "Arco" stands out as a gem in the indie gaming landscape, offering a captivating experience with its striking pixel graphics, enchanting music, a multi-layered story, and immersive gameplay.  The pixel graphics in "Arco" are nothing short of impressive. The sprites and backgrounds have a very chunky aesthetic, but this works in its favor.  Its easy to tell what characters are who and the locales are varied and gorgeous.  The game boasts vibrant and meticulously crafted environments.  They are richly detailed, with charming character designs and smooth animations that breathe life into its Meso-Americanish pixelated world. This retro-inspired art style feels both nostalgic yet fresh, creating a visual experience that is both engaging and delightful.Complementing the visuals is a soundtrack that elevates the overall experience. There are appropriate ambient sounds and beautiful spanish guitar (some of the sound effects reminded me of those used in the adventure "Roadwarden".  Actually to be honest, as I am playing this game, I am reminded of "Roadwarden" in many ways even though Arco is a different genre of adventure...and that is quite a compliment!) .The music in "Arco" is beautiful and atmospheric, with each track meticulously composed to enhance the game's emotional and narrative depth. The controls are responsive and intuitive, allowing for fluid movement and precise actions. The game's design encourages exploration and creativity, with challenging battles that keep players invested. All of the battles are conducted as a mix between an "active time battle" system...though they also have a turn based strategy element.  It works quite well and each fight is exciting and rewarding!  There is a very challenging element to its gameplay as well, because you have to conserve your money and items, because you can not gain infinite experience (at least thus far in my adventure)...so you want to do the very best you can with what you have.   Also, there are choices that you must make in your adventure that may strengthen you, but also curse you in battle.  These curses come in the shape of little ghosties that chase you around the screen while you fight...even as you try to decide what to do.  It adds yet another exciting element to the battles you face.Overall, "Arco" is an experience that is greater than the sum of its graphics, music, story, and gameplay.  I'm about 8 hours in as I write this review and I am hooked.  The way I see it, Arco is already a uniquely memorable experience is resonating with me, and I feel will also resonate with fans of retro-inspired games and newcomers alike. "Arco" offers a well-rounded and immersive adventure that is well worth playing.  SO PLAY IT NOW...or a ghostie will get you while you sleep ;)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Brad from Lisa the Painful, but he's mexican, must assemble the avengers to defeat spanish Hitler and end colonialism forever.Honestly the game is very fun, the combat is novel and smooth, the story is very touching and there's clearly a ton of work put in every aspect of the game. It reminds me a lot of skyrim, or red dead redemption, in that it's a semi open world with a lot of stuff to do with a focus on story (though this is more finite in scope and more heavily story driven). I do have a sore point with the game, and it's actually a positive thing for a lot of people. The game has a ton Easter eggs and alternative endings, which causes the same issue as most games of its kind, where to replay the game to see most of the endings (or even the full content itself) you'll inevitably replay through a lot of the same story beats, which is kind of annoying. Granted the game does a great job of having variety throughout its story, so you'll certainly see a lot of new stuff on a new playthrough. That being said you'll probably need to look up info online to see all there is to see, again there's lots of easter eggs. I personally can't be bothered, and well that left me feeling like I didn't get the full experience, but that's just me. Can't really begrudge the game for it, since that's just the nature of the genre, but still worth mentioning.I liked the story a lot, but it definitely will be more touching to you if you've suffered at the hands of colonialism or racism. I haven't, as a privileged white lady, though it isn't hard to see that the themes in the game will certainly resonate well with a lot of folks in the prior camp. It's also very respectful of central american and indigenous culture, again I'm white so I'm ignorant on that, but it's not hard to see where the writing's heart is and where the inspiration comes from. It's nice, adds a nice vibe to the game, and I think it's a very novel story to tell.Smooth, fun, engaging at every turn, packed to the brim with extra content, and an emotional and sensitive journey (in a similar vein to Lisa the Painful), I'd easily recommend it to anyone who loves story driven rpgs, or even folks who are fans of say skyrim or red dead redemption, since the core game loop has a similar vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: crazy underrrated game, definitely a hidden gem for me. Really liked the story, characters and turned-based combat system. You can have so much variety in your play style, which I really didn't expect. Pixel art and the art style in general is also very pleasant to look at. Price tag is a little bit high and I encountered a few bugs here and there, especially after loading a save file but other than that - solid
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know where to begin; this is fantastic game!  (Minor spoilers in this)Story: it's heavily Central/South American inspired and with an emphasis on the effects of colonization. Each major act has a different viewpoint that is compelling to follow. I don't want to spoil much, but each character in the game has a unique but meaningful motivation that makes me want to go back explore each nook and cranny of their story to find the wonderful tidbits of their experience. There are branching paths that you might have to backtrack for (that the game will let you do) or major branches that encourage larger replays, and I'm on board for all of this.Gameplay: It's turn based with a twist: each turn plays out in about 1-3 seconds of real time when you finish deciding your actions. It's challenging to figure out the optimal turns to move your character(s) to keep them alive, but also defeat the enemies. The skill trees for each character are largely unique and provide a challenge to play as them solo, but really shine when the characters come together. Music: Top notch. Very emotional and moving in the dramatic sections of the story and it really gets pumping in the battles. Never gets repetitive, even when you're replaying the battle over and over to perfect the outcome. Visuals: I'm a sucker for pixel art, and this is the pinnacle. I love how it's simultaneously detailed, but simplistic. You can see multitudes in the portrait and avatar designs, and the world/background designs are gorgeous. Overall: This is a fantastic game. I don't like giving a numeric score as it really diminishes from the experience, but over all this is a most solid recommend. The story made be feel some strong emotions and really satisfied the gameplay itch. I really hope more folks get to experience this.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic 8-10 hour experience. Combat makes you feel cool and feels really smooth, very innovative. Outside of the combat, the story is the other main focus, and is executed really well. The world is so cool in concept, and as an archeologist with some Andean and Mayan/Mexica experience I felt it leaned on actual history just the right amount while still creating its own fleshed-out world. I really appreciated the playable characters, all 4 are really unique and endearing in their own ways. I paid full price and it's definitely worth it, but on sale this game is a no-brainer pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Played through a bit of act 2. Got to a settlement and bought a shovel. Figure if it's gonna be worth 15 gold, it'll be pretty useful. They wouldn't make something that expensive single use, right? I get to the first point in the game where I can use it, and wouldn't you know it, breaks immediately. Well, might as well walk down this long corridor, I think, hey, what could possibly go wrong?I'm following a dark path I may never recover from. All I can ask is you stare into the void with me, please buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I do not often leave written reviews but this game needs to be heard. Set in a sort of magical realist Latin America, it follow the travels of our heroes across beautifully pixelated landscapes and a compelling revenge story. The real standouts are the soundtrack – which is sensational – and the tactical battle system. Battling is pretty unique – a sort of mash up of KOTOR and Into the Breach – where action is paused even few moments for everyone to take and execute and action and then restart so you can see results of that action and then plan your next move. HIGHLY RECOMMEND. Be cool and buy and play this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Always wanted a game with these mechanics, and the story/art is very charming.. game clearly has potential.However the game is extremely buggy and the mechanics are not well implemented, leading to very frustrating situations where the entire fight goes wrong because the enemy ignores stun, or attacks even tho they had no attack indicator, or the melee attack prioritizes an irrelevant target, or you fall off a cliff because the dash indicator is incredibly unreliable... etc etc.Looking forward to revisiting this when the bugs are ironed out / game has been improved in general.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is probably one of the best looking games I have ever played, even though the characters are one pixel! The backgrounds are absolutely beautiful mexican inspired landscapes with a pinch of magic and wonder sprinkled in. The gameplay is separated in exploring these wonderfull locationss through quests, even though some of the quests are of the fetch variety, and combat scenarios. The combat in Arco is one of the most unique I have ever played. It's a turn based affair with a twist, every action plays out at the same time. You select whatever action you want to use: attack, dodge, move, teleport and a lot more based off of those principles BUT you have to keep in mind all of the enemy actions: bullets flying over your head, enemys trying to separate your head from your body with a shovel, towering warriors trying to punch your lights out...it never gets boring or repetitive in part to you receiving experience to use in a skill tree that lets you learn new moves and level up your health and magia. Lastly I want to mention the music. The music brings the whole package together. It is an absolutely perfect soundtrack to go along with the pixelated backgrounds and it gives heart to the plot points. Arco is one of the best games of the year and I couldn't recommend it enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Meh. Like many others I bought this game thanks of the developers crying pretty convincingly about how no one wants to buy new games anymore, but there's nothing remarkable going on here. Arco tries hard to be a proper story-based RPG, but the story is based on thin, trope-y characters and quippy geek humor. There are ASCII smileys - lots of them.The combat system is decent, but not robust enough to carry the game on its own, especially since the structure of the game doesn't really allow you to just ignore the writing and focus on the gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this game after the dev stated that "nobody buys this game :(". I have played the demo fully and bought the game. However, the combat simply stops being fun. Right after the demo ends you get a new character who is melee only. This, and the ghost mechanic makes combat tedious and irritating. _childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: It's definitely a pretty game, with a beautiful setting. It's just... dull.There's no story. They made the meta-choice to simply rely on tropes. It's like playing a lifeless bag of game storytelling, devoid of anything. Characters are frequently inhumanly obtuse. Motivations make sense for them, but not for players. (They burned down a characters village; I get why  wants vengeance, but why should the player share his single-mindedness?) Simplistic stereotypes abound. Dialogue is dull and long.I think this was a stylistic choice by the devs, but I think it was the wrong one. It just makes progression feel so... uninteresting. The third act character does the same thing and goes the same places as the second-act character, without anything new learned in the plot. There's some interesting ambient storytelling if you pay attention, but the dialogue ends up being about fetch quests and killing rats-in-basement stuff.The gameplay is okay, but seriously suffers from two things: 1) the lack of difficulty options and 2) overuse of combat. For #1, it means you'll either find it too easy or too hard. For #2, it means you'll fight dozens trivially easy battles, with the interesting scenarios -- the "real" game -- just here and there. The gameplay really shines when you have interesting characters with you; environmental objects to take advantage of; initially insurmountable odds. But as it is, there's just an uneven run that (for me) felt like a lot of busy work with occasional spikes of difficulty -- but that never really forced me to pay much attention to the game's systems. You're never really pushed, and there's no "Hard" mode to do so.Presentation-wise, the environments and map looks great but that's mostly it. The character portraits are cramped and small; the music is a bit abrasive; the sound design isn't particularly good.So overall, I liked wandering around the map, looking for secrets. But I found the gameplay inconsistent, and the main story of vengeance against the Red Company to be the worst part. In a world with a magic tree, evil curses, skeleton mages, hidden Mesoamerican ruins, caves in mountains, monks on hill, troglodytes with spears -- somehow going wild west is just immensely underwhelming with such boring characters and dialogue.I know I'm not the only one that feels this way, since only 20% of players have finished act III. I don't regret paying money for such gorgeous landscapes and the joy of picking option A or B at random events. But I can't really see myself finishing out the game.

_childDocuments_.review: You only need to get about 20 minutes into this game to run into the narrative that the "pale" people are the anti-nature, greedy, cruel etc. etc. evil people. I was interested, now I'm not, I get enough of that from Hollywood etc.

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, worth the money, but!Can't recommend it due to a big number of fights, strange character progression, equipment and it's usage.From my perspective the game has a narrative that states "capitalism is bad, we need to preserve and nurture old ways" where all "red" guys are bad, they corrupt the land and exploit people, meh.Last chapters have too many fights so I turned on assist mode and used dynamite for all fights (sic), gameplay doesn't evolve into a something tangible.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this, but combat is a slog and could have been designed much more elegantly and enjoyably — as the interminably long and boring combat tutorial at the very beginning makes pretty clear. A game (particularly: A good game) should be able teach you how to play it through gameplay, not through a long built-in lecture. I would have figured the fact that the developers (and publisher?) felt a long exposition of how to play was necessary would have served as an early warning sign of marketing issues, but somehow they didn't arrive at that conclusion. As a result, sales are what they are, and I hope everyone involved has learned from it. I know some of those involved with the game's development have adopted an attitude that "does this sell?" should be the only mindset, but that's a logical leap that isn't supported here. The issue isn't that the game can't sell, it's that not enough care was paid to HOW people play games today when determining what needed to be done to make this vision sell. Short answer? Show, don't tell: Craft combat to make it not require a tutorial through growing complexity and lessons.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a sleeper hit for me.got it for the amazing pixel art visuals but played through it because the combat is fun and challenging and the story captivated me.The writing and dialogues feel natural and the characters and protagonists come to life. to top it off, the music is beatiful.All in all, if you like pixelart, a good RPG and story, combined with a new kind of tunrbased / realtime combat and like awseome music, this ist a must for you.Especially for a game that doesnt even cost 20 bucks.Thanks to the dev team for this awesome experience!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm only in act three (started over with ) but I've already fallen deeply in love with everything about this game. The pixel art is beautiful, the music is enchanting, the characters and story are heartbreaking in the best way. I've been recommending it to all my friends and I can't shut up about it on social media.
