_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is art. It's worth the money. I'll have some negative feedback that I do believe is worth mentioning in a sec, but really, wow. The writing feels very real and genuine, the story actually gripped me (which is good, I'll circle back to this later), and the art style while seemingly simple is actually surprisingly gorgeous. More than once I arrived to a new screen in the game and audibly said "oh wow" or something. Really impressive stuff here. Please, despite what I'm about to say, you should buy it. I love this game and it's so much better than so much of what is out there...Now, the complaints: Unfortunately my main complaint basically boils down to "a lot of the gameplay". I wasn't lying before, this IS worth buying. With some effort, I began to enjoy the combat, but it makes a pretty rough start by being very difficult right from the tutorial. It's not even difficult so much as it is shockingly precise which can make battles feel like problems of memorisation, not skill or strategy. I had many battles where I was just doing the exact same things, over and over, just to get to that one part of the fight that I wasn't sure how to handle yet only to once again lose there and have to do it alllll again. The main issue, I think, is that while I normally love having lots of upgrades for characters in a game, in this game (it at least seems like) it's impossible to buy every upgrade for each character in one run. Certainly I finished each of the first section for each character with MANY upgrades still remaining to be bought. The thing is, the game is very tough and XP is very limited so at the start of the game I really regretted what I had purchased for my character and felt stuck with lackluster abilities and strategies that didn't mesh well for a few fights before I could finally buy a power that helped in a big way. It's hard to know what to buy, especially early on. Hint, ranged options are extremely useful... As mentioned above, thankfully the story and art is so incredible that I have actually pushed through and played almost the entire game even with some pretty major frustrations with the combat. It's a real shame that I'm not always loving the combat, though, because I really like the idea and I'm pretty sure it's original: the way you plan your moves and then see everyone's moves happen at once is a really nice blend of moment to moment combat and strategy, and when you (finally) get any of the characters to a point where you feel like you have a solid option for most circumstances, it's actually extremely satisfying to engage in the combat. The problem is that each character suffers from the issue I mentioned: they're really underpowered at the start of the game and it's hard to know at first what to buy to actually get them to work. By the time I started the third part of the story I felt a bit more at home and was able to build out in a more functional way but wow it was a tough start!I think the game either needs more XP per battle/event and/or an easy way to respec (sorry if it is there and I missed that!), but ultimately, I think it's just a product of a combat system that's slightly too complex. I think, for most characters, a few of the upgrades could just be dropped. They don't seem nearly as useful as the cost/opportunity cost would require.However, again, despite more than a couple "damn it, how many tries is it going to take to win this fight?!?" moments, I'm still a huge fan of this game. I think it strikes a great balance between being serious and funny, it tackles really difficult subject matter in a way that is (mostly) very fair and real, and it definitely made me feel things in a way that games usually don't. I don't want to say anything cus, well, spoilers... But I was genuinely really sad and felt like my choices had mattered at a few points. Definitely a game that gets "morality systems" right, none of this basic black and white BS and/or your actions having no effect on the world. Finally, I had one really awful glitch that showed up twice: in two separate boss battles, the music just started to stutter, repeating the same half-second of audio at max volume infinitely. It was very grating. The first time it happened I just gave up and started the fight over but the second time I was over halfway through a very very difficult boss battle and felt like I had a chance of winning so I suffered through all the way til my victory. Thankfully, that fixed the issue as well, which is great (I was worried I was going to have to do the whole long-ass fight over!) but it was still really frustrating and has made it tough to return to the game.Overall, I think this needs a little more polish, a slight rebalance of combat abilities (literally just one extra move available at the start of each character could fix the majority of this issue) and it will be a 10/10 experience. Again, despite what I've said, this is better than most of what is out there right now. It's still worth a buy, even if only for the story/art, but with some help online and/or some grit, you'll also find the combat very engaging and cool (in time). I'm happy with my purchase.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a beautiful and fun game that shows the craft and care developers put in every aspect of it.In terms of gameplay, the game is a turn based combat with some small twists: positioning is very important, but also quick choices. Here’s a really great twist: the choices in your game can spawn “guilt” during combat, which always moves even while you evaluate your turn. It is fun, novel and exciting! I don’t play too many turn based combat games but that made it so more engaging.The game also brings RPG elements. As I mentioned you make choices and those impact the game in subtle and small ways. I don’t think it branches that much but gives some replayability and lets you build your characters your own way.It is somewhat unforgiving, specially at the beginning when you are still learning the gameplay, but over time it does get you in the flow. stick to it!Finally, the story is a classic western revenge one but with the twist of placing the action in a weird anachronistic amalgamation of Latin American cultures. Combined with the fantastic pixel art and amazing music it is incredible. I love it. It is one of those games where it looks like simple parts but make up for a fantastic package.Thanks to the developers for putting so much care on every aspect of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A refreshing tactical game, with excellent backdraw. I enjoyed the story, but the combat run out of steam at hour 5, since it doesnt provide any additional mechanics to play around with. The progression of the story was more interesting than gameplay progression, and at hour 7 I just went to watch a story playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Taking the time to leave a review on here because this game was really good! I really liked the flow of combat - even though it's tactical and turn-based, it's also fast. You can take some time to plan while you have it, but the inclusion of the ghosts ensures that you're periodically forced to think on your feet. Plus, the emphasis on positioning keeps you moving around the battlefield which makes each encounter feel very dynamic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Really impressive how they're able to create a powerful sense of place and atmosphere using such a minimalized, low-res pixel style. Between the writing, the music, and the art, they create a rich world. But they manage to do it with minimal text, without over explaining the backstory.The gameplay is very clever and unique. It can be frustrating at times, but the ability to immediately replay lost battles and work out the puzzle in each one is satisfying in a way similar to Into the Breach. While I don't find it to be the most addicting strategy gameplay, the different characters and branching skill trees allows the player to try different approaches and personalize their playstyle.Very solid game!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game, very polished. Grammar could use a little work, but it doesn't sour the experience in the slightest. The story is great through the end and Act 4 absolutely clears the rest of the game. The humor is dry and on the nose, and every (main) character is likeable. The world is believable and the ending is pretty much perfect. 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: In Arco, you shift across 3 different perspectives and follow the story of 4 protagonists - various natives of the land this game is set in - and the effect of western colonisation on their home. While the story itself is a little lackluster, the game truly shines when it comes to its main focus and what it does best: the innovative combat system. The combat in Arco is tactical turn based - with the player being given unlimited time to decide how to move your characters to avoid enemy attacks, what attacks to use on which enemy, and so on - with a twist: depending on your choices during the game, you may accumulate "guilt" which spawns ghosts which can hurt you during the "deciding" phase of your turn, suddenly forcing you to decide on your actions quickly and adjusting them to avoid these ghosts. This natural time pressure really helped put pressure on the player without there being a restraining timer and keeps the combat fresh and fast paced. Last but not least, the music is really good, especially the ones with lyrics at the end of each chapter.Arco is a hidden gem that I would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is unlike anything I have experienced. Beautifully rendered in pixelart, Arco's visuals will charm and amaze you. So much thought and effort has been invested to produce a gripping story with rich characters and deep lore... the soundtrack alone is worth it! The mechanics are great too, allowing for a versatile play-style. I like being challenged, and this game rewards you for improving tactics and strategy in combat. My favourite thing about Arco is playing as multiple characters with unique yet complimentary skill-trees. There are many secrets and hidden treasures to find and choices to make that are worth revisiting. I've put in over 30 hours into this gem, and I've barely scratched the surface. If you like fresh takes on turn-based combat, I highly recommend it!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely perfect Lite RPG, I love the 8 bit graphics, and the gameplay /story are way above what you would expect, every battle is fun and not too long, good mix of strategy involved so you don’t get bored of repetitive battles like most games nowadays. Overall it was a great story and game that I couldn’t put down, I hope this team keeps producing games like this, I’d but y them all
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is delightful on so many levels - the turn-based mechanic, the story and setting, the cheerfully classic video game aesthetic. It is clearly a work of love by the creators, which shines through on every level. One thing I especially love is the lack of penalty for dying - you can just retry as many times as you want, which allows you to play with different approaches and mechanics. The game has a soul, both on the story level as well as the game-design level. Easy to enjoy multiple playthroughs as well. I'd recommend it to anyone who likes video games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Fresh approach to turn based strategy giving you a sense of urgency which is usually absent in the genre. The art is great and music inspiring, both supporting an amazing story of revenge. The dialogue is great and i wish i didn't skip so much of it at the beginning of the game not knowing what to expect.This is again proof that you can't trust AAA games anymore for any sense of creativity. Enjoyment resides in indie titles.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: What a banger game.- Incredibly intense combat like you've never seen before (this sometimes borders as a negative because Arco's combat demands your PERMANENT attention, someone talking to you for 2 seconds WILL cause you to die and restart the encounter)- superb art style, merging cute characters and animations, excellent use of color and well designed environments- great OST and voice songs- poignant story - well written and sometimes very funny dialoguejust go and play this, one of the best games this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyed the game a lot. Each main character has its feats and feels diverse enough.Gameplay is fun and the game felt fair and not punishing.Some decisions had unexpected twists which was welcomed.Loved the pixel art styleKinda hated the ghosts as they can be really annoying when playing with more than one character at a time or sometimes I just wanted to play when doing other stuff but I couldn't due to this feature. Encountered some minor bugs but nothing actually game-breaking:- Never received some achievements for finished quests- Finished fights re-triggered after loading a save file- Some NPCs disapeared or re-appeared (when they shouldn't be there).Finished the game in 23 hours which felt long enough and makes the game easily replayable.It has enough content for more than one playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a beautiful game in a unique setting with fun (yet challenging) combat mechanics. There seems to be lots of choices, secrets, and storylines for each of the characters, who are all realistically written and compelling to play as. Both the music and the art are very evocative of the setting. Highly recommended to those who enjoy RPGs, narrative-driven games, and donkeys.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. The setting and narrative were both great. The game also starts off pretty slow, but it picks up in chapter 3.I wasn't quite convinced by the combat, not automatically healing to full at the end of combat and moves having long cooldowns both regularly led to drawn out fights where you circle strafe for ages waiting for stuff to come off cooldown.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: What a wonderful game from start to finish. It is a tactics game where you have (nearly) perfect information about. You know what your opponent will do next turn and need to react.The best part is the story, art, and music all weaving together. I could not stop but was reluctant to finish because I enjoyed it so much.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Good game. Fun combat. Good story. Engaging. Some of the menus could use more work to make them clearer. When I pause in combat can I not resume without starting the fight over!?!? Sometimes it feels like combat doesn’t present all of the information that it should. It might look like I’ll hit an enemy with an attack but the distance falls short. With clearer UI this game could be an all timer.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I really enjoyed Arco.  The lower resolution yet beautiful pixel art, the excellent score, the interesting take on turn based combat, and the story make this game a great value at the price point.The combat in Arco is turn based but feels significantly more active because of the bullet mechanics with their projected paths being visible when pressing space.  Coordinating your parties movements and attacks around the most active threat on the map is really satisfying.  The playable characters have many different play styles available due to the large level up tech tree.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game was a lot of fun. The combat was very unique and engaging. It can be hard, but it's not too much of a setback when you die. The guilt mechanic was really cool, though I didn't fully realize the effect until a 2nd play through.I rarely play through a game twice, but I'd definitely recommend playing once with low guilt and again with high guilt (e.g., being a bad person). There's a lot of changes and branching choices that make the 2nd play through not feel repetitive. The setting, characters, and art style were all good. Played well on the Steam Deck. Occasionally ran into some bugs, such as un-formatted text, a single crash, and a single instance where performance tanked. While it would be good for these to be fixed, it didn't detract from the experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: First of all: Play this game blind. I mean, no spoilers. Okay, seriously. This game is so great that I HAD to review it. If you're like me, you'd buy the game for the innovative combat system. Turn-based when picking actions, and real-time upon execution. The game gives you a plethora of abilities to unlock and switch before combat, giving you freedom on how you approach the encounters.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing game. I think it's an example of a near perfect indie game. The gameplay is new and feels fantastic, the pacing between story, exploration and combat is great, the story is engaging, the combat is simple yet exciting... Add a little exploration and rewards and you have a fantastic game.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: If you like turn based games, you owe it to yourself to play this Gem. Heck, even if you don't usually vibe with turn based stuff, you may still like this unique combat system that blends skill point resource management, positioning and a little play it your own way, as every character and a few different styles you could venture down. The story alone carried me through many late nights, before I realised it was 2am, or I forgot to start making dinner because I got so engrossed in the characters and their quests for vengeance and closure. It felt like choices I was making, actually mattered, as they did have repercussions, both in world, and mechanically with the guilt system.It's not a long game, but really it doesn't need to be. I really loved learning about the customs and traditions of the world, inspired by (or straight up from, lost on me due to my cultural ignorance) Meso-American living. I really enjoyed my time with this game, and I wish the developers all the best and hope that they return to this world in the future. I look forward to re-playing it again, trying for the other ending and achievement hunting. But not right away, and this is one of those games that I feel you need to let settle in after you've completed the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.Art - 10/10, like the style and everything looks completeCombat - 9/10, really enjoy the way turns work and the skills each character has, but some attacks' hitboxes              feel wrong.Exploration - 9/10, love how often you can find stuff by just walking around each area, but I wish there was              fast travel for trips longer than 3 map areas.Music - 10/10, listen to it. The songs that play at the end of each chapter set the perfect tone for the              endings I got.Story - 9/10, the guilt (not morality) system is cool, the side quests offer some extra characterization based              on how you deal with them. I love that the game doesn't punish you for doing things that your              character doesn't know are wrong. The main storyline(s) are interesting, but I'm not done with it yet.              I might change this part if the ending is really good or disappointing. TL,DR: fantastic game, if I knew what I was in for I'd have been willing to pay $60
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible indie game, loved it. Visually it uses a more minimal pixel art style but with enough detail presented to give characters personality. The battles are a fun take on turn based gameplay. They offer a challenge, but are mostly short with an easy way to restart at anytime, which invited some fun risk taking. The story was compelling, interesting and grim. There was a surprising number of choices presented throughout the story that at least seemed impactful. A few in particular made me interested in a second play-through to see what would've changed.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I had my doubts in the first part of the prologue, this screamed "style over substance" story game, but soon I saw this title merged both a unique setting, art direction and well written story, with a completely new type of gameplay that I really want to see more of. I would love them to expand upon this formula somehow, someday, maybe even a fantasy "oregon trail" style game, I also love that the game doesn't push any "forgiveness" angle for the sneering imperialists, sometimes you just gotta torch the bad guys!Awesome game, loved it all around.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Great art style. The story has been very engaging so far. The music is fantastic — this is one of the few games where I don't have a podcast on in the background because the music does such a good job of keeping you in the world.Combat is challenging but not impossible, it requires tailoring the skills you take in to each encounter which is great — you can't just sit on the same set of skills all game so you don't feel like you are wasting any skillbuys, you will use it all eventually.I wasn't sure what "blends turn-based and real-time combat" would look like, but after playing it that's exactly how I would describe it. It's hard to get a feel for until you play (or maybe watch some I guess), but I really enjoy the blend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: 3/4 of the playthrough was on steamdeck. If you're on the fence about this one, try the demo. It plays through the first act and gives a pretty good example of what you can expect. Graphics are low-fi and strategy gameplay is satisfying. Lots of fun ethical decisions to be made and a really satisfying and sad tale of vengeance. Would highly recommend this if you enjoy the demo. Can't wait to see what else this dev group comes up with. Great job!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: One of those very rare gems that anyone interested in video games should check out.I'm not gonna go into detail about all the good things about it, because it is almost everything.Only a few nitpicky-ish issues to point out:- Sound seems to bug out sometimes and produce a weird constant bzzzzzt sound when there are too many audio sources playing at once.- Melee range of enemies (and yourself) is very unclear for most abilities. You'll be hit a lot due to that.- Ending seems somewhat rushed, especially the ending slides. Itzae's ending for a minor choice at very beginning makes zero sense and is just flatout disappointing.- The UI can be buggy, especially that oddly tucked away repeat fight button in the top left.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished yet, but so far, I'm in love. I obviously knew that it was going to be very pretty, and it is. I wasn't expecting it to be that nicely written, sad and nostalgic, but very funny at times. The gameplay is also great, and just my cup of tea. I really anjoy the ghost mechanic, it feels right at home with the story. Can't wait to play more and finish the story. <3
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I remember seeing this game at the Latin American Games Showcase and thinking it looked really cool. I remember the characters fighting a bear and the combat looking kinda funky. I was curious.A month or so passes. I finally get the game... and I was in love. There is so much love and care put into the game, and by such a small team as well. The pixel art is wonderful, the art pieces of the landscapes are stunning, the characters are fantastic all around, and the combat is really damn cool. This just feels like a deep, real Mexican/Latin American story to me. And I feel like we don't get many of those in games. At least not until recently.Please buy and play this game. Support the team behind this game. Support Latino games and devs. Itzae was my favorite by the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very fun. The combat never gets boring. The first real character you get is a archer, and before you grab all the skills in the skill tree, the game jumps to the next character so it never gets boring. Other characters vary from being melee, support and more. The game locks you out of many options after getting one so you can only choose one path. This creates interesting decisions that are very fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I don't think this review is enough to express my satisfaction. I just finished my first playthrough and the journey was unexpectedly quite emotional, it was an AMAZING gaming experience. Loooooove the story telling, I adore the writing very very very much. 10/10 and would 100% cry again for this masterpiece. Plot aside, the turn-based combat system is really delightful and refreshing.I like how the game is pretty progressive on the level difficulty, it lets you learn from solo ranged combat, melee, then tactical strategies with more different types of character teamed up, which provides different play styles with the abilities of your choices, makes the game less repetitive. It would get easier once you're familiar with the positioning and abilities, and It feels SO good when you managed to defeat everyone without getting any damaged. You are also given different options in the dialogues sometimes, which you could get different outcomes, and sometimes it could be a little punishing (well well well, if it isn't the consequence of my own actions.) but never too frustrating as in the worst scenario, you can just run a save.IMO, The best thing in this game is probably the ART. like, CAN WE TALK ABOUIT HOW GOOD IS THE PIXEL ART IN THIS GAME?! Breathtaking. Incredible. Fascinating, Wow. And the music? ABSOLUTELY FANTASTIC, DIVINE. So good that sometimes I had to take a good moment to appreciate the view and ambience. I also wanna talk about how it was serene and peace at the start of Act 2 , but then it brought tears and emotions when I went back there after I completed the game. Beside the emotional parts, the combat music would 100% make you feel like a badass that you won't think you are in danger, but your enemies are. There's still some bugs here and there, but so far those I experienced weren't really bothersome, and I'm sure the devs are working on fixing them. Beside that, it is a game I would highly recommend, nods and big double thumbs up.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: About 6/7 hours in and I absolutely adore this game.  Love the art style with its bright sunny vistas and the evocative music is superb.  Just a real feel-good game, even though the battles can be complex there is no penalty and it's easy to just re-try and attempt a different approach.  Must confess I turned the ghosts off though as I found them too stressful and they made the battles too panicky, but good that they're there if you want more  challenge.  There's heartfelt story in here too but tonally does seem a bit off at times, not sure it feels natural for the characters to often swear in what is generally some very gentle pithy dialogue.  But love the game overall so eager to find out where the adventure goes next and would've happily paid double.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: It's a decent experience with a novel but frustrating combat system. There's a lot of QoL I'm still looking for but my most significant gripe is just with some sudden difficulty spikes. The combat is an acquired taste as you have to adapt to many details not being on your side. On the other hand, the brutality makes murdering the colonizing dogs more satisfying. The setting is a refreshing one that I've rarely seen and the pixel aesthetic is very pretty.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: First off, this game has a super generous 2 hour demo, and progress (and achievements!) carry over to the main game. It's a really unique tactical combat system with a combination of real-time and turn-based mechanics. The writing is snappy but also really strong at quickly allowing you to understand characters and their personalities and motivations. Overall, after 2 chapters, I highly recommend this.Months removed, this is still my goty. A terrific, impactful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry, which is not easy to achieve in this medium, especially considering the art style the team chose. Arco is a masterclass in storytelling that could very well have been directed by someone like Alejandro González Iñárritu in cinema. It also boasts well-thought-out and polished gameplay mechanics, along with an award-worthy soundtrack.I hope this "hidden gem" stops being a secret soon because it deserves all the accolades that may come its way.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Love the game! Fantastic art style, fun turn based combat and a good story. Doesn't drag on too long but doesn't feel overly short. All games don't have to be 100+ hour epics, and I like that they didn't make anything feel padded or filler. That, combined with there being a lot of choices and branching will make me revisit the game again in the future for another playthrough.Great game for the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I got surprised by this game in every sense. I was expecting a narrative heavy rpg with a solid history and somewhat easy and fast combat that would give approximately 5 to 8 hours of playing, however the game is rather challenging while being fluid and fun, the music is gorgeous, the history makes you dive heavy in emotions and although I think a bit cliche, it still is very engaging. The only flaws I see in the game are QoL improvements related to keyboard shortcuts and messy UI.Very fun, beautiful artwork and I hope the low numbers don't stop this people from making games because I'm already excited to see what they do next.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't finished this game yet but I am having a blast, the setting and characters are interesting. As well the combat is unique and interesting.I just finished and I absolutely love this game, just finished my first run which ended up as low guilt and had a blast, probably going to play a no guilt run later. The combat is really interesting especially with how enemies spawn in letting you set up to kill them the moment they spawn, ambush is also interesting either losing or getting a turn. It was also fun making an absurd amount of money in act 4 with sifting through sand with water or in act 3 with fishing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a beautiful story of grief, pain, community, and, ultimately, revenge that unfolds through breathtaking mesoamerican fantasy environments. The hybrid turn-based tactical combat is catchy and addictive and remains challenging through the entire game. Hidden story paths, secret areas, and divergent character builds encourage multiple play-throughs of the story, which takes about 10-12 hours to complete. Incredible music, charming character writing. A very satisfying indie experience that I highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't write reviews but this game is absolutely amazing and apparently it hasn't sold well, so I'd like to help. Arco has the best turn based battle system I've ever seen (no joke), it is simple and satisfying but it has depth and it never got old for me, and being able to choose you skills is also really fun. I'd love to see a multiplayer version or an endless like mode even if I don't think it will happen. The atmosphere and theme is also fantastic and with that music is just such an amazing combo, it might have simple graphics but it still looks sooooo good! Also I really enjoyed the story and I love the characters, especially my guy Tizo :)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: beautiful game lots of care and detail put into the atmosphere and the style. the combat is novel but definitely a little rough around the edges. there's a lot of ambiguity in the timing of attacks and the pathfinding can get a little wonky if you're not careful. it's still very fun but there were some moments where i'd have to restart a fight because the actions i chose did something other than what i was used to them doing normally. again though, very worth your while!!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazingly fun, bought it at full price and have 0 regrets. The story is amazing, it's keeping me on the edge of my seat. The world map and combat mechanics are very good, the loop keeps you engaged and having fun while being fed the story. The graphics are simple but very flavorful, the music is awesome. Play this game, seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: If I were to choose one word that perfectly describes Arco, I would say "heartfelt".This little game contains so much pure intention. It shows in the wonderful music, pixel art visuals, snappy and interesting dialogue, and a deeply moving story.The combat is the most unique aspect of the game by far, it's kind of like turn-based top-down Superhot, with a surprising amount of complexity stemming from enemy variety, and most of all - unlockable skills, which give a lot of freedom of how you want to tackle upcoming encounters. Said freedom extends beyond combat though, as almost every interaction presents the player with multiple choices which can truly impact what happens next in the journey.I found the setting shockingly captivating, it weaved quirky fantasy themes and nature anomalies into quite a grounded narrative.It made me cry multiple times AND contains a couple species of funny goblin creatures, two rare qualities found only in a few games.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is nearly flawless. It's firing on all cylinders from start to finish. The story is compelling enough on its own. (I'd gladly watch a movie of just the story) The music is perfect. It has such sweet sorrowful lows and super catchy and heavy highs. There's a high skill ceiling for it's mechanics, yet it introduces them slowly enough that it never feels overwhelming. The UI is so clear and usable that navigating menus feels as easy and natural as breathing. The graphics work so well to convey information that I sometimes forgot how simple they are. Like some of these people are made up of like 6 pixels but I get so immersed that I'm no longer seeing that, I'm seeing what the game wants me to see. This game deserves everyone's attention. I can't possibly recommend it enough. Perfect 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: The game looks nice. The story seems to be interesting. The combat system is unique. Skills make sense and feel good. There is much to appreciate here, which is why i give this a "neutral" recommendation.On the negative side: I lost motivation to continue playing.You basically have a more or less linear path though various screens. Each offers some short conversions, shops that don't want to buy most of my stuff and combat opportunities. The combat can by quite challenging. A little too challenging for my taste. I always lack money to heal myself. And when you started to get used and a little attached to your character and it's progression ... it's switched for another one.As said the story seems to be interesting. Even meaningful with the reference to south american history. It's just not told very compelling (for me).
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I was very kindly gifted a code for Arco and immediately I'm struck by how beautiful the game is.  I love the pixel art style and the soundtrack is calming.  I'm loving the combat mechanics, the character interactions are beautiful and there's just this overwhelming feeling of love that seeps out of Arco.  You can tell that it was made with passion and it really shows.  I am really excited to play more and I can't wait to see how the story unfolds.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: effin newcomersthe game play is really good- the demons always mess me up which i find a cool twist because you can have a strategy, and then a demon shows up and you get all panicked and emotional and you kinda have to figure out how to master that to keep momentum.i also like that the cookies made me feel better.i almost feel like im on the journey with the character given the history...not just playing a character, but dealing with sh*t with the character.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A fantastic game that marries a decision-based, regret-filled story of revenge and wrongdoing with a clever quasi-real-time combat system that rewards careful planning and bold moves. It's not the biggest game--the progression trees aren't really that deep, and enemy variety is fine but not amazing--but the framing of the stories and the way the larger narrative progresses keeps you invested the whole way through. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco clicked after about two hours and haven’t stopped thinking about it since.The combat is fluid and unique. You really do start to feel like Neo dodging projectiles and weaving in and out of attacks, utilizing each characters toolkit for specific enemies. The real-time blending into the pause phase is a fantastic concept executed really well. You can even fundamentally change how combat feels with the pressure put into the pause phase.The art direction is stunningly focused. The pixelated backgrounds look like art pieces. The portraits display real character and personality. The real winner to me, however, is the soundtrack. This game has once again reminded me of just how much an amazing soundtrack can elevate a game - there’s a battle at the end of Act IV where it all comes together and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ man it was great.There is so much more to say about this game, like how my second playthrough is completely different thanks to rewarding and branching exploration, or the world building, or the character writing, than can be written here. Arco is a criminally underrated gem with a truly fresh take on the genre. It may go down as one of the all times greats for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Solid, unique tactical gameplay, excellent upgrade system that lets you feel strong without giving you sawdust tier meaningless treadmill upgrades that RPGs usually do. Incredible music, phenomenal pixel art, and a very satisfying revenge story as expected from a western-inspired tale. All of that in a game with good pacing that doesn't overstay it's welcome.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: that was incredibly good. absolutely worth the money. loved the gameplay and the story. if you're in the mood for an excellent role-playing game and the feeling that only a handful of games can give you - to be immersed in another world. look no further.even if you're not a role-player and don't like pixel graphics, you should check out the game. it's really great.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough, I absolutely love this game. The visuals are stunning, the combat mechanics are super addictive and fun specially since you can always try a new strategy or skill to get over a challenge. The narrative really hit me at different points both for good feelings and bad and made me like and have a connection with the characters, the music and audio design is right on the dot to boost the aesthetic of the game even further. Loved seeing a lot of mexican culture references too, of course.In general every aspect of this game stands by itself amazingly and then combines to make a wonderful games, congratulations to everyone involved.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful. A lot of soul poured into this one - it has great atmosphere, very natural dialogues and an interesting, western-like story. The gameplay is very enjoyable and the focus is exactly there - to have fun from the gameplay, not getting punished on every step. It's not easy - but it keeps it interesting, but not frustrating. A great little gem of a game <3
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Action is an interesting take on turn-based combat mixed with bullet hell and strategy RPG elements. Each character has a bunch of really cool moves they can unlock by spending experience points on a skill tree, and it's fun coming up with strategies incorporating the unique skills of each party member. The writing is gritty and emotional but also humorous and endearing, all elevated by a beautiful visual presentation and soundtrack which made for a thoroughly engrossing experience that was hard to put down.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game was incredible. The story and the artwork were incredible. On top of that, the central mechanic, the controlled tactics game was really well built. It felt like a tactical version of controlling a MOBA character, which is great for someone like me who really struggles with speed and precision. The turn based nature was great. Cannot recommend this highly enough!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Game is awesome from start to finishThe scenery was jawdropping and the musci ohenomenalI really enjoyed the combat system, one thing is the transition from rpg segments to combat felt a bit weird as it opens the menu up to srt uo and fight, but you get used to it and doesnt break the pace muchI also found "weird" that most combats you are outnumbered and very few you have multiple characters to control, which is a shame, because the combat gets more and more interesting the more characters you control as it allows you more strategic freedom this is notably shown in the later chapters where its easier to have a party of multiple characters like the chapter about Chio and her brotherIm not always into stories in games but this one I was invested from start to finish and the options it gives you either matter in the Guilt meter or to affect the story in some wayIt doesnt take much time to finish but I can see this game having more content down the line, I hope they do soOverall fun game, amazing combat and story, cant wait to see more content down the line
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A brilliant mix of Fallout, Nuclear Throne and SUPERHOT that tells a profound story from a unique anti-colonial perspective that we desperately need to see more in games. I'm only a few hours in, but already I'm sensing that this is something really special. The art is astonishing, the writing is really beautiful, the soundtrack full of solemn ambient tunes and biting guitar riffs in equal measure. It also has an absolutely electric combat system that, while taking a little while to get used to, results in encounters where you either feel like you survived by the skin of your teeth, or that you're the hardest bastard to ever walk the earth, teleporting away from bullets and flinging arrows with pinpoint precision like you're Legolas. Games like these deserve to sell in the millions.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: i have yet to finish the story, but gameplay alone is carrying this title hardcore. having every unit's turns occur simultaneously is a simple yet super innovative twist on turn-based combat. and just when you're getting comfortable with the flow, a ghost appears to force you to think quickly and remind you that even when time is paused, you're not safe.the dialogue is endearing and kept short and sweet. no conversation ever overstays its welcome. this combined with the instantaneously responsive UI keeps the game moving at a brisk pace, ensuring you're never kept away from another combat situation for too long.the low-res artwork is cute, and there is no shortage of pixel vistas to stare at during your adventure. this game just seems to be doing everything right, and while it hasnt blown me away or anything, it's very good and as long as the story holds up it will remain as such.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a gorgeous game. The beautiful pixel art landscapes were what first drew me to play it. Little did I know there would also be creative turn-based (but somehow still real-time) combat and well-written branching dialogue choices. Now every time I jump on I get to enjoy this trifecta of brilliance. Couldn’t recommend this one enough and can’t wait to play more.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely excellent. Arco’s ability to craft so much deep story in such few pixels is outstanding. It’s thrilling and moving and beautiful, and that’s all before the gameplay where the combat puzzles provide the player with such a varied and simplified toolset making every battle feel interesting and unique and customizable. This game is lovely and thoughtful and has got an unbelievable soundtrack. Awesome game
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game! I enjoyed every minute of play and was actively looking forward to every session.The worldbuilding and narrative structure were very exciting and even made me shed a tear or two.The atmosphere delivered through landscape pixelart and music were beautiful. Makes you fall in love with the setting. I'd love some of these as postcards or prints.The combat system feels very unique. Scratched the same itch as "Into The Breach" with some interesting twists. I would have enjoyed a few more fights that require you to reequip your character, but other than that it always felt exciting and some of the bossfights were quite challenging.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write a review, so know that I am spending valuable minutes telling you this:This game is good. It doesn't overstay it's welcome and has an engaging and interesting story. The gameplay is cool and something I haven't experienced before, and the combo's you can achieve is satisfying and fun. Give the demo a try, you'll do what I did when you're done - say "buuuuut I want to know what happens next" and then buy the game and not regret it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I love its unique twist to time-based strategy combat.. something that's usually very slow and complex it's implemented in a unique, simple yet very deep way. I need to keep playing to get a full sense of the narrative elements but I believe it's already one of my favorite concepts in games this year, and will certainly keep playing (and probably replaying!)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game kicks so much ass. I started it with some trepidation, as I’m not the most tactical-minded person, but it’s an elegant system full of depth and customization that lets you figure out your best ways forward. Yeah it’s tough but by the time I’ve solved a particularly tough encounter, I’m usually able to do it while barely getting hit. To me that speaks to how each encounter is thoughtfully assembled and meant to test the elasticity of your thinking. All that and the best soundtrack of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is worth a play though, you can feel the love and passion the devs had for the game when making this. It is fun, with a great story, and even with how simplistic the art is there is still a lot of depth that goes into the world. For sure one of my favorite games of 2024. Sad to see it hasn't gotten the love is deserves yet but I hope that does change.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: (current playtime: 11 hours)Honestly, would recommend. It's a fresh take on a tactical RPG, with no levelling stats, and basically optional grind. The bulk of the game's progression is via skills you use in combat.Still though, even though the later skills are good, they still require skill and forethought to use. The story is quite good, had me pretty enraptured when I played it. I gotta do a few more playthroughs to catch everything, but for a first, full playthrough, I thought it was pretty good.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: The story and the art style are really interesting and will likely keep me coming back. Nice little ability system and simple, easy-to-learn combat mechanics.The way controller buttons are labeled in the UI is a bit confusing, though, and can be rather frustrating when it results in unintentional actions during combat. Not quite enough for me to say "not recommended" but I do hope that gets addressed soon. Other than that, it's a nice little casual RPG.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, this game is actually amazing! The expression "hidden gem" tends to be used a lot but this game is actually a hidden gem. It is fun, it is original, it is polished and I can't stress this enough - IT IS FUN.There is zero ambiguity about the combat. You get all the info you need and turns happen simultaniously. Making a good move or a good plan and seeing it unfold before your eyes in real time is incredibly satisfying.I already completed it once and I am starting my second playthrough. The funny thing about it is that I'm not even a big turn-based fan but Arco's simultaneous turn based system is so good that sometimes I even found myself restarting fights just as I was about to win because I wanted to see if I could do it better/differently. I love experimenting with all the skills and items that the game puts at your disposal. This is one of those cases where I enjoy the gameplay for it's own sake.It is sad to see it fly under the radar so much but to the devs I say that you guys have to believe in yourselves. Many interesting and original concepts had slower take offs in the past and the small numbers are not reflective of the game's quality. What you have created here is a formula that can span multiple games, all wildly different from one another while relying on the same ideas. I also say this for selfish reasons as I want to see more games like this in the future. I can only imagine what you guys can do once you start polishing this gem.The setting and art direction are also quite beautiful and interesting as well.  Mezoamerican/wild-west fantasy is not something you see everyday and just like with the gameplay, I hope I get to see more stuff like this instead of the same old european fantasy. I am a fan of it but at this point the medium is oversaturated so this new world was a breath of fresh air.The story is good. It is nothing ground breaking but it doesn't need to be. It is dark when it wants to be dark, it is over the top when it wants to be over the top, it is funny and lighthearted when it wants to be just that. The dialogues are short and to the point when they don't have much to say but take their time when they need to. They aren't very on the nose either so whoever wrote it clearly put in the effort to make the characters believable. Intentionality and sincerity are more important than originality when it comes to story-telling and this game has those things in spades.The music is beyond beautiful. It is absolutely amazing and I say so as I am listening to it right now. There are no bad songs here. They only range from good to absolutely amazing. Lagrimas de Cal, El Gallo, Whale Fanatics, Voices of the Past and the menu song are my favourites.Some critiques:1. The skill tree keeps the stats and the skills separate and some players might get tricked into getting a lot of skills before investing in magia, which I think, makes the fights slower than they need to be. In the future, weaving skills and magia together or making magia grow automatically would be better, I think, as it would make the combat a little bit more fast paced.2. Either I need glasses or the skill buttons are too small. I missclicked a few times mid combat and it was frustrating.3. Some issues with playtime registration. I did not play offline or anything like that and I should have more hours. I think it has something to do with the fact that instead of desktop shortcuts, I pin my games to the taskbar.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent blend of turn-based and real-time tactical gameplay that should be getting more attention. The anti-colonial narrative is a welcome twist on classic Western revenge narratives that's worth experiencing at least once, and the characters are endearing (if a bit one-dimensional), but the gameplay is what's likely to bring you back for multiple playthroughs.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a magnificently thought out game. It's mechanics are deep and allow for a variety of playstyles. It is very rewarding to attempt different builds of the 4 main characters learning synergies between their abilities. The guilt mechanic is a fantastic application of mild pressure on choices and the ease of retrying a fight is SO very welcomed. You can restart any combat at will, edit your loadout of gear and abilites or even back out of a fight entirely without having to go through the trouble of reloading saves etc. This game FLOWS and it SHOWS.Hats off to the Arco team. You filled this pixel world with life and danger and consequence. Revenge, its motives, and its costs are all painted in a bloody swathe across the narrative. Hold on to your tamales amigos, you're going to need the HP to survive this unmissable experience.10/10 A true gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco slaps - the flow of combat is very satisfying, and the characters I've played so far in the story feel unique and interesting. What took me by surprise, however, is how cool the narrative is. Not only are you fighting against creatures, monsters and colonisers, you also really feel the emotional weight of your journey. Definitely recommend picking this up!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I was pulled in by the incredible "turn based action game" style combat and got impressed by everything the game has to offer.The music is incredible throughout the game and each type of enemy has its own encounter theme.The characters are likeable, there are secrets to find, and the story is excellent. My game of the year so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: i'm about 6 hours in and really enjoying Arco.  the setting and story are compelling, the art and music are excellent, and combat is one of the few simultaneous systems i've enjoyed.  there's enough information to form strategies and respond to changes, but a subtle pressure system keeps you from getting stale.  it's not flawless (dodging should actually dodge everything!), but it makes for satisfying and varied combat.excellent work all around!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I don't write reviews often, but this game deserves more attention than it is getting. It is a rare gem.I have enjoyed many games, and there's some I would say I have enjoyed more than Arco, but I have not had a game appeal to me in this way since I was a kid.This game is original, the mechanics feel fresh and fun, the story has a ton of heart, the world has this magical-realist quality to it that is so compelling, the soundtrack kicks ass, and it is so refreshing to see a game from a more Indigenous perspective. _childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome turn based strategy, a fresh take on the genre backed up with a compelling story and interesting characters. _childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: We're all used to indie games that taken themselves way too seriously. Arco's biggest flaw is the opposite, it doesn't take itself seriously enough.This starts with the trailer, a soft voice over making the game sound like a quaint indie title. Then a second trailer that has cartoon animations and doesn't show a lick of gameplay til halfway through.  What I played in the demo is not at all what I expected after watching the overly sentimental trailer and I bought the game immediately after reaching the end of it. Gamers are burned out on "Look at us we're a small indie developer, please support our game" style marketing that tries to pander to their sympathy.Arco doesn't need pity, and it doesn't need to hide behind cartoons. It has deep and fascinating combat mechanics that are very unique from anything I've played before (mechanics that aren't mentioned til 30 seconds into the trailer?). The turned-based combats blends nicely with the soft real-time elements to force you to make quick decisions when you'd really beg for more time to think. Your decision making process changes vastly as you level up and gain new abilities or switch characters completely, adding to the challenge and complexity of "keeping up" with an ever-changing battlefield.The story is also great. The only thing that holds it back is the use of emojis in dialog text. I don't know why this decision was made. The writing is plenty good enough to carry the characters on it's own. It doesn't make them endearing to throw text faces into their dialog. Again the developers should've taken their game more seriously. Despite both these issues I loved playing through this indie title, it was worth every penny. They should remove the emoji's in an update and we could consider this a work of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just a couple of hours in, but this is already becoming one of my favorite games of 2024! With beautiful pixel art, innovative turn-based combat and a gorgeous soundtrack to boot, I want to thank you for this wonderful experience! Arco deserves your attention! I really hope Franek, Cahill, Bibiki, Fáyer continue to make more games like this in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a beautiful game written and animated so wonderfully that I wanted to pursue it's exploration and rich story. I want it to succeed and be sustainable. But I found the turned based combat to work against the unfolding narrative for the sake of chasing a into the breach like experience, without the snappy reload. It's so beautiful, and so frustrating.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Serious contender for game of the year. This game fires on all cylinders and just doesn't stop. The beautiful pixel landscapes, the music (from the adrenaline-pumping battle tracks to the gorgeous vocals to the ambient tones), the amazing characters and how their stories interweave, the resonant yet witty writing, the fast-paced tactical combat that grips you but also makes you really think... I'm going to be thinking about this game for years. You owe it to yourself to play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal game, with a unique combat system that feels very fresh, fair but not broken levelling and skill trees that let you sway the direction of each characters fighting style, and an engaging and fun story. The dialogue and characters are half of the charm in this game, and stepping into the shoes of the story makes this game a real gem.Theres so many choices in this game that can lock off or open up different pathways for each chapter, I plan on going back in to find more.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Really unique turn-based combat! A lot of the gameplay is very refreshing, and I looooove the pixel landscapes. The detailed pixel work in this game looks so lovely and goes great with some of the more tranquil soundtracks. I think the overall story writing for this game is quite fun, and characters like Itzae and Chio quickly became my favorite : ] I ran into a few issues here and there, a little lagging after playing for a few hours and often miss-clicking battle inputs. I sort of wish there was a way to increase the size of the buttons as an accessibility setting, as they are rather small. I'm also not crazy about some of the more "modern sounding" dialogue, and sometimes I wish the characters could express their emotions visually a little better.All of that being said, this is an awesome game with some really good stuff inside. _childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Like probably in my top ten for story games. I was wanting to play a game with this battle system so bad for a while but didn't know where to look. Then this popped up. Also the story was great too, not to mention the art. The only things that need fixing are some of the crashes. I had like 5 happen to me over the course of the game and while they weren't bad, they just kinda annoying. Also there was some balancing issues, like a fight with just one character is much harder, so it made the final act very easy. The hardest fight was definitely the boss in act IV, because of this. My last gripe was that the ghosts should have been used more often outside of act I, because I didn't see many, even after going down the secret path in Act II. _childDocuments_.review: Really enjoying this game (just finished Act Three on the writing of this review).The graphics and soundtrack (while sometimes a touch repetitive) is very good at setting the mood, and the storyworld is both tragic and fascinating to explore. _childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: What a treat!Very good writing, engaging characters and world-building.The whole experience has a very adventurous feel, you constantly set out into unknown land, stumbling upon adventures and into situations as you go along.I really enjoyed the fighting mechanics. You change perspective with every chapter until the last, throwing you into the shoes of a person, unknown to you, that has a different background and acts on different motivation, than the previous protagonist.The narrative has branching paths, which adds to the replayability. _childDocuments_.review: This game isn't for me, so I am refunding it. I do think it's well-made, so I am giving it a positive review to help out the devs.That said, I do have things I want to say.First: I really don't like how big the skyboxes are in the overworld. Basically, so much of the screen is taken on a pretty background that you can't go to. All you can do is stare at it. This makes the characters look so small on screen and over only the bottom part of the screen. The main character is like 5 pixels tall and most of that is made up of the llama they are riding.
