The story itself wants me to feel invested in characters that look so small. This might be a me thing, but the story didn't grab me in the hour I played.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: ARCO should be a genre mess, trying to blend turn-based tactics RPGs with the bullet hell. How do you blend slow, methodical, turn-based combat with the frenetic, screen-filling attacks that define the bullet hell? Somehow, it works phenomenally well. Part of it is down to the game's impressive map design. There is a huge variety in map types. In an ancient ruin, I had to navigate fighting multiple enemies on a map so small there was barely room to dodge; in an abandoned temple, I had a long, thin map with multiple environmental hazards; in a forest, I had to deal with a big open space full of rapidly-spawning enemies chasing me away from key areas. Enemy attacks have a good amount of variation too -- bandits might wield a shotgun, forcing you to avoid large area spray attacks, or a rifle, forcing you to try to outpredict a shot that is too fast to dodge, while bugs leap suddenly across the map or explode after dying, forcing you to get in and out quickly.I also want to shout out the 'grief' mechanic. Rather than morality, the game has an invisible system that tracks grief. The more bad times you see and do, the more likely you are to be 'haunted', a ghostly presence joining the battles. Unlike the enemies, however, the ghost only moves while you're on the turn-menu, drawing closer the longer it takes you to make decisions. It's an evocative mechanic I've never seen executed quite this well, and it ties in beautifully to the game's themes of losing your people, culture, and heritage to a colonizing force.Solid writing, great art design, and shockingly engaging genre-bending dynamics all combine to make ARCO a genuine treasure.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: It's so awesome. It's got everything I like: adventure, collecting resources, funny little dialogue flourishes, some battles where you gotta think a little (have some fights where I have multiple do-overs but its still pretty fun), and multiple character stories that seem to tie in together a little (I'm still making my way through Chapter 2 at this point). And it's all done in a minimalist pixel style that still offers a gorgeous amount of detail. highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Really enchanting so far. The story's a relatable but seldom seen Western from the perspective of the folks who lived there first.I was surprised to hear the strumming guitars and HD music but it's an effective and memorable soundtrack.The combat resembles Transistor or Parasite Eve. A Semi-turn based type of RPG where it's satisfying to think out moves or rush through encounters trying to get to the same point to make a slight change in order to win.I am loving it so far and am very glad I bought it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The art style is gorgeous (especially on steam deck), the music is fantastic, and the story is very compelling. There's a lot of depth here: secrets everywhere and a lot of choice in the paths you take in the game. The combat is fantastic once it clicks, it took me a bit of time to get accustomed to it but it's really engaging, especially as you progress and get more abilities. It can be pretty difficult but it's doable, and it's very rewarding to take down a particularly challenging boss.One of the best indie games I've played in 2024, highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Novel mechanics added to a turn based battler. Maintaining a balance of offence and space management while managing your energy resource. Takes a little bit to get the hang of it, and luckily the devs have baked in retrying battles to help master every encounter.Wonderful pixel art, with a fun mix of abstraction and higher resolution environments.Beautiful music.interesting dynamic choices that modify how you move on the map, interact with characters, suffer consequences or reap rewards.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: It's can be hard for games to tackle serious topics. But I'm always glad if developers (truly) try.If you're sincere about it, towing the line between being respectful to the contents of your story and still making a game that feels somewhat original and not just like you're ticking of some boxes is a challenge. The audiovisual presentation is an additional point to consider, since it can make or break the combination between gameplay and narrative flow.Arco tells a story of settler-colonialism wrapped in a tale of personal revenge. Or the other way around. It's up to you which you weigh more after you have played the game. In a fast switching campaign system between tightly designed and engaging fights and dialogue based narrative parts, it takes you on a journey through mostly basic, but still aesthetically pleasing pixelart set pieces. Some of your choices will have an impact on your experience. Because it doesn't linger too much at any one point of its story, there are some emotional gut punches in this game that I didn't expect hitting as hard as they did when I first started playing. Much of that I assume comes thanks to the excellent soundtrack and direction. Direction, Arco's strongest feature in my opinion.Because in the end, while all of its parts are good, individually, with maybe the exception of the soundtrack, they're nothing to rave endlessly about. I write this because I think you shouldn't expect a combat system that revolutionises anything, or a story so filled with twists that you'll never know what's coming for you. No, what you can expect is to be absorbed in this game because it feels like it's very personal to the people that made it and they paid a lot of attention to all of its parts fitting in just the right places. Thus, at no point it feels like the setting (colonialism) is just a vehicle for the story of revenge, nor does one overshadow the other and the combat feels fresh by moving on with upgrades to your characters and new items at just the right pace.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely fun little casual-but-still-challenging turn-based tactical adventure through a reality-adjacent-but-inspired-by-real-world-cultures desert-themed world. My only complaint is that I wish it was longer. Though that's not a very fair complaint given its very reasonably price. Maybe I'll just have to replay it... 8/10  classic RPG loop of explore a richly realized world, fight (not grind) bad guys, consume items to keep up -- all with the added layer of point crawl between stages intuitive point and click or WASD. Couldn’t be simpler. pixel art that is somehow roughly rendered yet intuitive and accessible. I enjoyed the boxy aesthetic.Sound design: unobtrusive; didn't make the game, nor did it detract I found no bugs and it should run on a potato employs tried and true tropes while avoiding being tired or overdone. The narrative follows three distinct tales of loss woven together through a mutual goal of vengeance against an evil robber baron surprisingly good. It is as unpretentious as it is effective. The characters are multidimensional, the plot is old but new, and the dialogue is snappy and natural – often interjecting well-needed levity.  Very engaging. It definitely has the “just one more turn” thing going for it. It makes you want to see each combat through to completion, explore every crevice of each scenic map, and see what will happen next in the story.  Low to moderate. You can’t complete all the skill trees in one playthrough, so you may want to try rerunning with other builds. However, the story is static, and you’ll know the twists before they come, so you can optimally prepare for them. (Although this point might be a positive for the power gamers among us.)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Great pixel art made me download the Demo, and awesome and unique combat made me buy the game before I finished the Demo.Combat is really refreshing, and makes for some cool combinations, ghosts that haunt you in combat are also a cool idea, and since you know on which turn they spawn, aren't much of a hassle.I've seen people say that the combat is hard: I'd disagree a little. First fight with 3 gunslingers is kinda hard, since they have fast projectiles, but once you get the the gist of it, you will finish the fight fast and all other will be easier. You just need to wait until the semi-turn-based combat clicks in your head.Primarily playing on SteamDeck, only gripe is that the game has letterboxing effect on a 16:10 screen. Hope it's not a constraint of pixel art design and will be addressed soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: While I only have 1.9hrs at the time of writing this, I actually spent 3.2 hours in the demo.Truth be told I wasn't expecting to like Arco. I've never been a fan of turn-based combat as I find it quite stale. But with Arco, it feels more like action and the world just pauses while you make your move. Everything is still in motion, it just halts momentarily. Positioning is just as important as the abilities/items you use, making it strategic as well. I don't have enough good things to say about its combat.. it's just so damn satisfying. I find myself actively looking for fights instead of trying to avoid them like I do in other games.I also loved unlocking new skills, reworking my loadout to try new strategies. The sound design when things land, or when items are used, the fluid sprite animations, the feedback, it all just comes together beautifully.As I mentioned, I spent 3.2 hours in the demo - it's quite long, and if you decide to buy all your progress is saved, and achievements you earnt will be unlocked on steam. There's nothing stopping you from trying it out to see if it's your cup of tea.I was convinced well before I even finished the demo.I know I mostly talked about the combat, but that's what really drew me in. There's also a vast story there, beautiful pixelart landscapes, and gorgeous music that comes with it.Try it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: If this game looks even remotely interesting to you, you need to play it. You like intense games that blend strategy and quick action? Play it. You like guitars? Play it. You like llamas? Play it. This game takes the beauty and wonder of South America and runs wild with it through it's majestic pixel art. There's no fat, all the quests are good because the combat is robust enough to be consistently fun and engaging while still being expanded upon as the game goes on. In spite of the challenge it provided, I never had to grind or got stuck on any fights for too long. Dialogue is surprisingly satisfying to read somehow which, in my opinion, has to be the greatest technical triumph of this game cuz i have no idea how that did that.Game dev industry, idk what to tell you guys. Just make better games like Arco. The world is starved for more llama based content. Some people may not know that that's what they want, but it's what they need
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful graphics, crisp audio, and fluid game play. Not only is Franek one of my biggest art inspirations, they're simply pristine at what they do, and so is everyone on this dev team. I couldn't recommend this game more, I'm not one to like turn-based combat, but this game handles it so perfectly and treats like the fragile genre it is.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Story 7/10Combat 8/10Graphics 10/10Great world lore with some funny jokes here and there, but the main narrative is pretty uninteresting and linear.The combat system is really good, fun and satisfying and the fights are challenging, but it becomes repetitive because a lot of fights have the same ennemies (gunners).Graphics are excellent, makes me think of a pixel art version of absolver set in a desert landscape. The movements are fluids and theres multiple well made cutscene trough out the whole game.Really like this game, 8/10 would recommend it to fans of turn base strategy fighting games
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: One of the few games I've actually finished in the last year or so. Really original and new world, pretty cool storyline, but most of all - a great combat system that mixes frozen synapse with superhot and makes it turnbased. Literally every fight was enjoyable. I also love the fact that the game doesn't waste my time. Movement is very fast, locations aren't big, travel is very fast, menu and UI are very fast and easy to use. It was kinda addicting, I think I've finished it in 2-3 days cause I liked it so much.A perfect game for the Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible game from start to finish. It has a unique mix of real time and turn based combat, and it's simple to pick up without sacrificing depth. Every character has a great number of build options and the encounters are varied enough to keep you trying new things to get an edge. Also has a very neat mechanic that has your choices in the story affect combat but having your characters guilt manifest as ghosts that creep towards you not while time is moving in combat, but when it's stopped and you're making your choices.And speaking of the story, I enjoyed every last minute of it. It has a fantasy/western setting resembling Central/South America with a very diverse array of cultures and creatures. It also has a great deal of environmental storytelling making the world feel huge and full of wonder without needing to tell you everything that's out there. The cast is comprised of many great characters with a surprising amount of depth, each with their own motivations and flaws. The game also gives you choices that really feel like they matter, making you think carefully when something comes up no matter how insignificant it may seem at a glance. The actual overarching narrative itself was really well put together as well, a good revenge story where you play as indigenous people of various cultures fighting against colonizers.Personally I think its a masterpiece, and I hope it eventually gets the recognition it deserves. Now that I've finished and given my thoughts, I'm gonna hop right back in to see what other choices and discoveries await me in the beautiful world of Arco.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: What a ride. Ironically I found this game by reading an article about how it wasn't selling well despite fantastic reviews. I have a feeling this game will eventually get the recognition it deserves. It's a modern Oregon Trail with fantastic combat, engaging dialog, and an endearing art style. It was the perfect length for the price, even though I wanted there to be more when I was done. An endless mode would have been a fantastic addition (maybe in a patch!).
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Still on my playthrough, but wanted to leave a positive review for what I've seen so far.The combat is a cool mix of turn-based and real-time, and I found an ability set very early that I really like for the characters I've played so far. The art, music and especially the backgrounds of each area are so good at setting the mood and giving a sense of scale. I'm looking forward to seeing the rest of the story!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game last night; according to my playtime it took me about 13 hours, which sounds about right (and falls within the 10-15 hour playtime that the developer mentions).I enjoyed Arco a lot.  It's got a fun way of storytelling that reminds me a tiny bit of Live-a-Live, and the gameplay feels like the best parts of Into the Breach.  Customizing your characters is fun, and I'm pretty sure there's multiple ways to break the game with the tools you're given - hot tip, the "weaken" debuff makes enemies TAKE MORE damage, not deal less, which took me a minute to figure out.  Also: the variety of uses all the items have are fantastic.  Being able to use things in combat for different effects and then also be able to use them during the various small events you run into is one of my favorite things to see in a game, and it's here in spades.  I'm going to be playing through it again to try a guilty run (my first run I tried my best to be a good fella), as well as make a few different choices just to see what happens.If you like strategic battles, solid writing, fun exploration, and absolutely lovely pixel art, I'd at least give the demo a try.  I paid 18 bucks for Arco and I feel like I definitely got my money's worth, but I can't speak for anyone else.  Anyways, time to get back to .
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Everything in this game is just perfect, 10/10 experience. Combat, the story, dialogues, freaking awesome music, beautiful and unique pixel art. Decisions you'll make are important and impact the story. I've played it for 10 hours and I had only 1 small bug in one fight where ranged enemies were not doing anything while shooting, but it was just for one fight and I have no idea why it was like that. It seemed like they were shooting to the ground and their projectiles collider with the ground instantly.Overall I can highly recommend this game. Very unique and fantastic one. Every single minute was well worth the price.The only thing I would change or remove are the ghosts appearing from time to time. They are perfectly fine when you're playing as single character, but when controlling 2-3 characters then it's becomming an issue. Especially in crowded locations where you don't have time to even move all of your characters to the locations where they will be safe from both ghosts and projectiles. However I'm also aware that by removing them the game would lose the "evil path" playstyle.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Fun combat with a nice atmosphere, and a satisfying level up system where you get new skills frequently. Arco has a compelling world, which despite having poor dialogue has lovely locations in a sort of fantasy Wild West with cool pixelart and immersive music. The combat is quite hard but satisfying. Out of combat you explore the map point by point, unlocking new locations, making choices which feel impactful, and managing your resources. There is lots of optional content to uncover. I enjoyed Arco and I think this original-feeling battle system is it's big strength. The only changes I would make is tone down the ghosts which can get very frustrating, make PC mouse and keyboard interface in combat feel more fluid (specifically the command icons), and make Crabs a bit more readable in terms of how to damage them. Overall I recommend this charming game and its priced very fairly for a fun 13 hour game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool game. The combat mechanics are are unique, as it's a mashup of turn-based and real-time combat where moves are executed simultaneously. I haven't yet finished the game, but it looks like choices really matters in terms how the story will play out, so I will most likely play again with different choices and see what happens.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing art style and soundtrack. There have been some places where I stayed to keep looking the background while the music was playing.The combat is great and force you to think how to approach each combat to success without being extremely complex. The skill trees allow you to play in different ways.The story is great, and often you will wonder what happened if you choose a different path, offering replayability.Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A very interesting game so far, the gameplay mechanic is quite ingenious and fun. This is exactly the kind of game I like to see from the indie crowd! Love the ghost mechanic that throws a monkey wrench into what you're trying to do at all times, fun fun fun!I can see myself putting in a good 50+ hours on this in the long run. The story has been intriguing so far, and I hope it leads to something thought provoking in the end, but on game mechanics alone this is worth the asking price!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves all the love it is getting and more. I have been exploring single player and indie games for the past year and a bit and this one is a huge stand out for me. The story is amazingly well written, choices feel real, combat is super fresh and fast paced even though it's a turn based combat system, and the music is amazing. I am not someone who enjoys Turn based combat, I generally find it boring, but this game does it so well Every action feels punchy, satisfying and impactful. Edit: Just finished my first play through and after starting my second and finding a secret I am even more i lovePlease if you are even a little interested in this game buy it. The devs have made an amazing game and deserve all the love and support out there. I's at act 3 and can't wait to see how the story progresses. I plan on doing more play throughs trying to find and solve the secrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: One of the first thoughts I had about Arco was "This is a great game, but I don't think I'm good enough to match it." The truth is, I wasn't. It took time for me to get a handle on the battle system, but several failures, frustrations, retries, and skipped battles, I now get the satisfaction of winning battles on my own on the first try most of the time. Things that I've learned that I'm applying to my second playthrough:1. Stick to one "attack style" per character. Some will specialize in range, some will specialize in melee combat, others are best with more "creative" options. The game does not reward generalists. 2. The game also does not reward "holding on to your stuff until later". If the game gives you battle items, they're meant to be spent in short order. There's no big boss battle where you'll be glad you held on to that rock from the first few minutes of the act.3. Attacks that spray in a cone can hit an enemy with more than one projectile. You wouldn't believe how long it took me to learn this.  4. Buy the tools and wander everywhere you can on the screen.5. There's currently a bug in the first temple that will allow you to repeat battles over and over again for extra experience. Find it and exploit it until it's patched out. The music is phenomenal, the pixel art is beautiful, the story is engaging and memorable... and the battle system is both brutal and forgiving, allowing for experimentation and encouraging creativity. Excellent game overall, I've looked forward to playing it after work all day today and looking forward to my second playthrough this week.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is amazing. I finished it in 2 days since I couldn't put it down. It took me 9 hours to finish it, and it is the perfect length for this game in my opinion. The story is interesting and compelling throughout the entire game. The gameplay is suprisingly engaging and challenging for being turn-based. The art, while simplistic, is perfect for this game and the audio is very good as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Loved this game. The aesthetic is a gorgeous love letter to (mostly) Latin America. The characters are vibrant and endearing without being stereotypically noble or flawless - in other words, they feel very human and lived in. Whether you're idling with the acoustic and the soft vocals of the title screen, or rocking out to the battle music, the soundtrack is jammed full of bangers, too.The combat system is the real seller, simple on the surface with a surprising amount of depth. It's fluid and quick but allows for a comfortable amount of tactics without getting bogged down in it a la XCOM, for example (and I love XCOM!). It feels so rewarding when you find a build that comes together, too. Chio surprised me by starting as my least favorite character to play, relying on her brother to do all the damage, then completely 180ing into a death dealing machine once I got her build online. Even after my first playthrough, I can imagine a bunch of fun build paths I didn't try, including stuff like full tank Itzae or an Item abuser. The action order can be a teeny bit frustrating at times -- it's not always clear which attacks proc before others, or what frame an ability activates on -- but it's a pretty minor issue, and one I don't have a great solution for without breaking immersion by just showing the frame data.I'd say you'll probably get 1-2 playthroughs. There's not a TON of replayability but you'll almost certainly miss things the first time through, and the second round could be a fun one for experimenting.Awesome game, highly recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I've only played this game for about two hours, but if you like indie games, tales of vengeance, and want stories about indigenous people in a fictional but not too different world to our own? You've come to the right place. This game has turn based combat but your moves play out in real time. Let me explain. You have to shoot an arrow where you think the enemies are going to go, or you're going to miss. The same way that you can curve your movement and dodge out of the way of a bullet you know will whizz past you but you need to be closer to be in range for your next attack. You use various skills as you try to avoid melee and ranged attacks (cool feature where you can tell "bullet time" where bullets and arrows are going to fly next). This game is unique and has a certain character to it where I can tell a lot of love was put in it. Other than the combat music being a bit repetitive, this game is beautiful. If you like supporting indie devs, this is a must buy as I picked it up from seeing it wasn't getting noticed from gaming articles. Otherwise? This game feels like it's a once over it's done, but I'm recommending it as a solid 7.5/10 thus far with no regrets on a purchase. I like that the game was harder than I was expecting. I am a little annoyed that certain moves aren't all that helpful when XP is scarce. I wish there was an opportunity for a respec in traits because I definitely wanted melee and quickshot abilities ASAP instead of waiting for distant lobbed shots and learning how to dodge. A little annoying, but I'll live. Always support indie devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I really recommend this game. The creator said that despite positive reviews, it hasn't sold that well, which is a damn shame because there is a lot I love about this game.First of all, meso-american settings are few and far between because god knows we'd all rather have the same generic european fantasy setting instead. Big win for the latinos. The characters and stories are really cool, the artstyle is fantastic, and most of all, the combat is super unique and fun, and I hope more games come out with that kind of combat system.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful, poignant story surrounds a tight tactical machine. Mechanically plays like elements of Into the Breach, Sword and Sworcery and Valkyria Chronicles.Around 10 hours of gameplay, many hidden optional paths to take, multiple ways of building characters and parties. Could for sure get a second playthrough out of me.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: So far, so good! I'm not always the biggest fan of regular turn-based tactics games (e.g. XCOM), but the free movement and sort of real-time aspect the combat in this game has makes it feel totally different from a "classical" tactics game. Fights are also quick (which is often my biggest annoyance with tactics games), usually around 5 minutes or so, including restarts.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This is a really great game.  Beautiful contemplative scenery behind a tricky and sometimes grim rpg.  The gameplay is very satisfying.  The fights are often difficult but you can try them as often as you need to so it never feels unfair.  There's not a lot of opportunity for grinding xp and items which makes getting those things feel precious and makes each victory sweet.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Game is good. Finished it once, it's about 15-20h(I idled a lot), but I can tell there is a lot of content still in the game that you'd have to see on other playthroughs. There are some ~decisions~ that pass over through multiple acts and affect how you progress through the game, so that's pretty awesome.There's a little bit of jank, but it's nothing too bad that really affects the game. Movement on maps is a bit weird, targetting some map icons(I was playing on controller) can be finicky sometimes, and there were several times where I had to restart the game because the audio broke. Either it would play static for the background music or stop completely.Despite what other reviews say, the combat system is fine. It's similar to Crosscode, except it forces a pause after every round. You just need to learn the timings for attacks and travel time of projectiles, which doesn't take very long if you pay attention. If the dev wanted to make this easy mode, they could add a countdown or timing bar above enemies' heads for their attacks.I do have to say that the end of Act 4 boss was kind of bad. It wasn't hard at all, just tedious. There's absolutely no threat of dying if you just run in circles until the adds die, but the boss itself makes it tough to use melee, so you're stuck with ranged and depending on which character you have, that can take a long time.The story is good, I like how it all came together over the different acts, even though it's kinda cliche and has been done a million times. This is a pretty unique way to present it and each character has a fitting story. The ending was a little bit abrupt for me, I felt like there could have been a bit more after the post-final-fight final fight, but I can't say I'm disappointed.Overall? I'd say 8/10, lacks some polish but still shines.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I have only completed the first two acts so far, but I can tell you this game is incredible. Great music, innovative combat, well done theming, interesting characters, amazing setting. this game is gonna go down as one of the great indie games of this year. Id rather this game be a classic than a cult classic, so if you're considering buying this game or know anyone who would, you wont regret it. play this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A surprisingly deep and story rich game with beautiful pixel art graphics, nice progression trees and great turn based mechanics. I really like how the various characters are introduced and progress throughout the story, both from a story perspective as well as from a gameplay perspective, as each character has very unique traits.Hoping for a sequel!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game so much, i just got to act V but it is a masterpiece. refreshing in it's art style and game play. the tech tree is a diverse but not overwhelming letting you have a choice to how you want to play your character. the music is an amazing, such a beautiful soundtrack to accompany a beautiful game every track sets the mood for battles and scenes perfectly. the way the world is build is so full only for a 2D game it makes the world feel very real and you start to feel bad for what the antagonist is to villages in the area.  it has already jumped to my favorite games list and i haven't even finished it. 10/10 great job panic
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game. For how simple the game plays, the story that is packed into it is so much more than i could have hoped for. The combat system isnt super challenging but very fun and the big fights will make you think a little bit about skill and gear choices. Apart from a few bugs (that werent game breaking but definitely noticeable) everything functions and feels great. Overall the gameplay will keep your attention through what turned out to be an awesome, super in depth, emotional roller coaster of revenge. All of that at a great price!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game so far. I picked it up expecting to try it for 30 min and played for 8 hours straight.The combination of the innovative combat, compelling story, and the absurdly high character/pixel ratio keeps pulling me in. The combat deserves a special mention -- the subtle blending of turn-based and real-time combat makes it one of the most fluid strategy-based systems I've every played. There's enough skills, items, environments, and enemies to keep encounters feeling fresh, but never so many options that it feels overwhelming.Also, there's llamas, many and majestic.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful, it's satisfying, fun, and well worth your time (and money). I could not recommend this game enough. So if you are reading this, just go play this game. The rest of this review isn't as important as you playing Arco.The strategy in this game matches the depth of giants like Into the breach while also carrying a story that moved me in a way that I was not prepared for. I could not put this game down, and am so glad I gave it a try. Just give it a try, finish the first act, follow the story, enjoy yourself, strategize for way too long on one turn, repeat a fight over and over, until it all just is done flawlessly, or don't, play it however you want and have fun. This game is awesome
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game! I recommend it to anyone who wants an innovative take on tactics, one that's much more action focused that a traditional turn based system or anyone who is interested in a melancholy "weird west" story. Highlights for me:1. The combat system2. The soundtrack3. The final act4. The jokesThings I didn't really love1. Ghosts2. The guilt/morality systemSometimes I felt that the story telling and the combat system were at odds and it wasn't always clear to me what actions would trigger "guilt", sometimes it felt like a classic RPG about killing and looting and other times I felt like I was scolded for relatively benign actions. That feeling of uncertainty around the outcomes of my choices combined with how many secrets there are in the game makes me think that this game is meant to be played more than once.Don't let any of that discourage you, this is an excellent game. I'd be happy to play a combat arena version of the tactics system and I'd be happy to relive this story again one day and even if I don't think the combat and story are in full congruence I have no qualms recommending this game to everyone (get the soundtrack too!)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is a fantastic game. It’s a rare example of a game I had reasonably high expectations for that were actually exceeded.  The combat is a little tricky to wrap your head around at first, but by the time it matters you’ll have no trouble with it because the game does a great job of teaching you incrementally without it feeling like a tutorial you have to get through.  It’s fun, rewarding, and perfectly balanced.  The only thing that tripped me up for half the game was terrain effects. You really have to pay attention to them, as some trigger from tiny pixels.  You always have time to scope out the map and see what you’re in for, and you’ll learn what’s worth taking advantage of and what’s worth avoiding.  But the battles are very fun, so I’d often just jump in and run through a deadly path without realizing it.  Fortunately the game is very forgiving and you can just try again.While I don’t think the story is going to feel incredibly new or unique to anyone, it’s still emotionally engaging and the world building is fantastic.  I really enjoyed learning about everyone and their way of life, how they approach the rapidly changing world, and cope with hardship.  The Tuag twins were my favorite to play. They were such a good team with fun skills that combined really well.The game isn’t easy but I would not call it difficult either.  If you lose, you’ll learn from it and get through eventually.  I think the final boss could’ve been a bit harder, as I don’t think winning on my first try really matched the challenge of the other bosses, but it was an epic and chaotic fight.  The ending tied everything together really nicely, too.I think the only thing that disappointed me about Arco is that there was nothing post-game.  It might’ve been hard to make that work, but I can think of DLC opportunities so I’ll be keeping my eye out for that.  I just finished Arco a few days ago, but I think I’ll play it again soon.  I wouldn’t say it’s too short—it was the perfect length—but I just played it non stop until I finished. Now I miss it.  I can’t wait to see what these developers do next.  Arco is the best game I’ve played this year.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game, love the art, love the story, love the combat system, love all the little secrets.Franek is one of my favourite pixel artists and his work here is astonishing.Never thought that the story will be so damn beautiful and complex. Ending of act IV caught me unguarded.Combat system is surprisingly deep and I want to try it with different builds.Definitely will try to find all of the secrets.Please play it. It's amazing.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely a "hidden" gem!Pacing feels good, written narrative is surprisingly interesting to follow and the general mood of the game is relaxing and captivating at the same time. Even though the combat is turn-based, there are certain aspects that force you to make quick decisions in some encounters, so the game strikes a nice balance between calculating your actions and having to think on your feet.Backtracking sometimes feels like a chore, even though longer distances are travelled automatically. It would be nice if we could skip going through each screen again, though there is a certain atmospheric mood to traveling with the animals, so perhaps the slow travel can almost be justified.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I played the demo, enjoyed the gameplay and thought "I'll probably skip the dialogue as usual" and boy was I wrong. The story is very enticing, I found myself playing not only because I enjoyed the gameplay, which is fun on it's own, but also because I wanted to know what happens next.Also, i've only done one run so far, but it seems like the game has branching paths and some moral choices aren't presented as moral choices,the game simply asks you "what do you want to do?" and you must deal with the consequences. It feels so much better than the mass effect approach of "good or bad decision"
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Criminally underplayed. Ever since Flamberge was abandoned, I've been waiting for this kind of tactical gameplay again. It's charming as hell and has very cool combat, with an excellent soundtrack. If you're a fan of simultaneous action turn-based tactical games, you should really give this a try.Edit: The story and characters just keep getting better. The world is unique and engaging with a sort of understated mythical feel to it. The dialogue is entertaining and genuinely funny at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Really refreshing to play a game with an original combat system, and I think it lands well! The ghosts help give it almost a blend of turn based and real time combat feel. The vibe of the game is perfect with the music really helping the imagination fill in the pixel art visuals. I haven't finished the story to see where it goes, but it has me intrigued in act 3. I really think, especially at the price point, the game is worth giving a go.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the greatest indies Ive played recently. I am not someone who is typically interested in turn based rpgs and while Ive followed the artist for their pixel art for most of this games development I was hesitant to buy it due to its price and my typical interests. However after just over 2.5 hours of play I can promise this game is worth the purchase and more. And according to the dev, thats about how much the free demo is. give it a try I promise it wont be a waste of time. art direction: Incrediblemusic: wonderfulStory: still early but the world feels very deep due to the random interactions and how they impact your play. More of world building aspect but it feels good to walk around and interact.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: The combat drew me in because it reminded me of similar tactics seen in into the breach and FTL with telegraphed enemy moves and time freezes, but wow... the story ended me. The writing and dialogue is concise  but uses every word to pack a punch and really get you attached to the world. All I can say is I hope we see move projects like this from the devs. Absolute proof that writing and game mechanics are all you need for an absolute banger. this game punches WAY above its price tag and easily in my top 5 games of all time on story quality alone.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun little tactics rpg with beautiful pixel art, an interesting setting, choices that matter without feeling like the end of the world, and a weird little combat system with just enough timing mechanics sprinkled in to make turn based combat feel fresh. Just watching your characters ride llamas around the gorgeous landscape is a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is an action RPG with a deep story and multiple intertwined mechanics. The trailer is very detailed and does an excellent job introducing it, so check it out to help your buying decision. Here are my three thoughts:1. There is a LOT of story, and it's delivered through short conversations and action scenes. Very "show, don't tell".2. Combat is complex and challenging. Think Slay the Spire meets action. The designers did a great job adding elements like dodging into a turn-based game. It's also quite hard, which I found delightful.3. Your story decisions matter. No spoilers, but whatever you do and how you communicate with characters influence where the game goes.I greatly enjoyed the game and wholeheartedly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Great gameplay, really cool skill trees.Interesting setting, interesting characters. The story itself is a little hit or miss. The whole "journey of revenge" thing felt a little over played imo, but it hit best in Act 4 and 5 for me (act 4 was my fav). Also it's uh. Really heavy. For almost the entire thing. So I found that a bit hard to play through when I wasn't always in the mood for heavy. There's also lighter funnier bits that I enjoyed, but they feel pretty far and few in between.Honestly, I really want a roguelike version of this game were you slap together your rag-tag crew of 2-3 ppl and go take on the big bad ala sts map traversal. Would happily pay another $10 for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Cute art, fantastic OST, nice story and fresh gameplay, was really enjoyable throughout and it has a pretty unique personality. Would've liked a bit of a longer closure but I'm probably too spoiled there. Took ~12h for me but don't make the same mistake of hoarding items and cash as I have.Seems potentially fairly replayable, might give it a shot.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco is intriguing so far!I'm only in the middle of Act III, but I'm enjoying Arco immensely. The soundtrack is fantastic, the writing and world building grabs your interest, and the combat is a refreshing take on a turn-based RPG system. The guilt system is neat and I should probably stop killing folks because the sins of my actions weigh heavy on my characters' minds!Will update my review when I finishEdit: I finished Arco and I loved it. It's story and characters were fascinating all the way to the end! Some fights were pretty tough but the game encourages you to change your skills and items when failing, so it was enjoyable to solve. If you're looking for a fresh turn-based RPG experience, Arco is for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Engaging story and thought provoking choices that actually feel like they mean something. The turn based combat feels different but in a good way. its a very fresh and fun way to manage fights. Please give this a try if you're interested, the writing is fun and the world building is great and easy to understand and get into. Play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I'm partway through Act III, but this is one of the best indie games I've played in a while. The combat is satisfying, and may take a little bit to figure out (the amount of time i dodge rolled bullets that hadn't been fired yet, only to die to them is embarrassing) but when you get a feel for it is truly fluid. It's a perfect combination of turn based and real time, which did had me sceptical but now is something I'd love to see in more games!! So if that is worrying you, just go for it - I had a blast  Aside from that, the story and writing is incredibly compelling, and I'm a big fan of the humour. The soundtrack WILL NOT EXIT MY HEAD IT GOES SO HARD. Not to mention the art and character designs, its incredible (i am just a sucker for pixel art tho).Only encountered small 1 bug, and has been said it will be patched. So the polish is extremely highOverall, highly recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Feels wonderfully unique to play — in many ways it reminds me of a modernized take on CRPGS like Fallout 2. Their take on turn-based combat is pretty inventive! NPCs and player characters share plan and execution phases, but certain things like projectiles take multiple turns to complete so you have to do a bit more planning ahead than you might expect. The systems feel good so far (somewhat into Act 2), and the story has felt compelling enough to make me want to explore and talk to characters outside of just progression-oriented dialogue.It’s a special game, and I really hope more folks pick it up!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: The combat system is totally unique, and I love the art and setting. I think there are a few wrinkles that could be ironed out- some areas are a little odd to explore if you enter from the east for the first time, for example. Despite some rough edges, the passion at the core really shines through! Highly recommend :)
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm two hours into my second playthrough and this Game is Just pure Magic, Getting to 1000+Gold was also fun while abusing the Trader lmao.Awesome Game, amazing Music, Neat Story, effective Skilltrees with enough variety (pls more gun abilities DEVS PLS <3), Choices U are allowed to make are cute and Spice it Up Sometimes, straight Up banger Game.Thank you for this Gem
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A game so nice I finished it in two days, realized I'd been so excited to see everything that I'd inadvertently skipped a lot of side stuff, and so immediately started it up again. It's incredible to me how fresh, exciting, and dynamic it feels even while playing it for an immediate second go around. The fighting is a fun, turn-based strategy style that I'm not good at by nature but really enjoy the challenge of; I can't speak for how someone with actual skills at that may enjoy it, but I love it. I could recognize a genuine improvement arc in myself--not just my characters--as I played the game and really began to learn, understand it, and get more clever about how to use the mechanics, which I really enjoyed. But what to say about the story? I love the story. A lot. The characters are endearing, the world is enchanting, it feels full of love and potential and passion. This is a kind-hearted game with something important to say. I'm trained as a history teacher and did my senior thesis (and most of my undergrad/grad research in general) on the intersection between ecological disruption and european-style imperialism. Arco deals with this topic in a way that is engaging and impactful, and offers players the rare opportunity to explore it through a strictly indigenous perspective. It's rare to find fiction on this topic that doesn't inevitably crumple to a white savior complex or stumbling over itself to assuage a white audience's guilt. The protagonists all experience this world and react to it in their own ways, having unique stories that eventually are woven together by common threads. The themes of guilt and grief tied into the revenge plots are phenomenal, giving the player incentive to think about what they do before they do it and also feel the weight of their character's conscience as they barrel through the world. The senses of love, grief, hope, loss, family, and anger all bleeding through the story are something really special to me. It's a game I wish I could reach into and touch. It's a sentimental experience with a fantastic gameplay loop that makes it equal parts introspective and exciting. The art style is both adorable and breath taking, a combination that's hard to nail. The music is so good my friends listening to me play kept asking for the song names (and thankfully, the soundtrack is already up on spotify! <3) This is a game that feels cared for. I want more of this world. I want more South American fantasy in general. I love spending time with this game and these characters. I really hope to see more from these devs!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is immaculate. It's just the perfect mixture of "difficult but fair". It's not perfect, there are some typos, there are some quirks...but you'll be enthralled by the surprising depth of the story, the compelling character narratives....it's really, really great. I'm 30+ hours in the game and that's only on my first play through heading towards the 5th chapter.....and I feel like I might even give it another go after that to see how the story changes.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where the makers put their heart and soul into it, and knew what they were doing. This game is among the best RPGs I've ever played and certainly earned a place at the table of greatest pixely combat RPGs ever.The story is dark and immersive but the visuals are cute and pleasing that creates a juxtaposition unlike any game I've ever seen.Everything is so fighty and detailed and i love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This is an RPG with a nice atmosphere. The battle system is a bit unconventional but that's something I enjoy here except for battles with more than one character to control. Those are a bit stressful and at least until now for me not worth the hassle. I also didn't find out how to heal my companions, so they tend to immediately go down. Anyway, get it, play it and see for yourself.Edit: You can switch to the other characters in the inventory screen by clicking on their names.I finished it. Wow, what an atmosphere this game has. Play it, fall into it, fall in love with the story! Buy this!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A couple hours in this game is phenomenal. Tight, refined Battle mechanics. Clever storytelling both in raw prose and in interactive structuring. It feels like the game is flirting with the player, training them to embrace the story with their heart rather than raw mechanical expectations. Great stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game with rewarding turn based combat mechanics and exploration. I'm engrossed in the narrative of the game as well, one has to be careful of the choices they make in the game because the actually have appropriate consequences. Can't recommend this enough to anyone who's into tactics or turn based strategy games, it's well worth your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco really caught me off guard in the best way possible. I was expecting a fairly casual play-through but ended up getting hooked by the story. The dialogue options feel incredibly meaningful, and there are plenty of secrets to discover that keep you wanting more.The music is another standout—these tracks are just beautiful and really set the mood for the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible atmospheric experience with an open, beat by beat tactical combat system that feels as if it could be expanded upon indefinitely.  Expect hypothetical sequels and mods of this game to keep you engaged for hours post credits.  Special shout-out goes to the color palette and musical score for matching the mood spectacularly.Has some stuttering and bugs in the late game, but nothing that will ruin your experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I find this game super unique for its kind. I'm kind of really enjoying it so far. I love where its going. If I had to nitpick and complain about something, I am SO ANNOYED at the fact that when you are picking movements, it allows you to run right off a cliff. In the game if you want to move the option will grey out if you try to move to somewhere that you cant. BUT if you pick a place too far past a cliff it will drop you right off. If its too far or if you can prove past it, grey it out.OTHERWISE, pretty sick game so far. I'm liking it.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Arco gives me the feeling of returning to the original fallout games in the best way possible. The combat and the world are really interesting, and the writing is light touch and ever so slightly memey in a way that works for the game. The optional route I've stumbled on is insane- I have no idea where the story is going, but things have gotten out of hand in a fascinating way and I'm along for the ride.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous pixel art and music, an emotional story, a compelling combat system and many secrets to discover - what more could you want? I'd wholeheartedly recommed this game if any of these points seem interesting to you.The game can drag a little bit towards the end with the amount of combats and some less exciting story phases, but it doesn't overstay its welcome by any means. I took ~2 hours of break time and then dived right into a replay to search for more secrets, experiment with different skill builds and explore how other story choices play out.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game will get you tearing up pretty early. The gameplay is fun, but story is even more fun! I'm on chapter 3 and Oh man, I did absolutely everything I was not supposed to do. The game, doesn't punish you too severely for making those dreadful choices. Has it's own humor and very sad parts. The game so far is outstanding!
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This is a special game - Excellent game play mechanics, music, story, and heart. It is difficult, each encounter being a puzzle to solve but the restart button is free and generous. I failed many battles many times but I was always close so I tried again. The ending really affected me , I'm sure I'll play again some day and make different choices.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute gem. Stunning pixel art, gorgeous music, addictive fighting and a story that gives you the same righteous anger as the protagonists.Do not play this game without headphones. There’s no voice acting but the music is not to be missedThere are still glitches and optimizations that need to be made, this game is not perfect and may crash occasionally. Still, it is absolutely worth every second you play
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good. I could gush about semi-coherently for hours if someone let me. However, I must restrain myself.Arco is a game about revenge set in a Mesoamerican-inspired fantasy world. Even though it sits squarely in the Western genre, the world of Arco still feels unique. This great setting is boosted by the wonderful art and music, which is simplified while still feeling real and visceral. All the characters you meet feel like real people, and the cultures are not stereotypes or "planets of funny hats". The devs could have stopped with this. I would be happy for a game with such an awesome world, even if its gameplay was mediocre. But the gameplay isn't mediocre. The gameplay is AWESOME. The turn-based tactical combat hits the right balance between simple enough to grasp but complex enough to have fun playing with. You will never feel as much like an action hero as when you dodge between bullets and punching someone in the face. Each ability has a clear-cut, unique role to play, and you can customize your skills to your play style. Want to shower the enemy with a hail of arrows? You can do that. Want to get up close and personal with the enemy? You can do that too.Finally, the story is very well-written. I would highly suggest going into it blind. You will not be dissappointed.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: So far so very good!My favorite thing about Arco is how blisteringly fast its combat is compared to most TBS/tactics games or JRPGs. I get the impression the developers respect my time, not only in that the game progresses quickly, BUT ALSO because it's so fast, Arco can ratchet up the challenge for free (and it does so). Failing a mission in FFT or Battle for Wesnoth can be exhausting or frustrating. But ARCO expects you to die like Dark Souls and Hollow Knight expect you to die. Fights are short and brutal, and you can retry them instantly without condescension.If that sounds scary, well, it also seems the greatest difficulties in this game are optional, self-imposed. You're given ample opportunity to prepare yourself for mandatory story fights, via the RPG mechanics in the game.Also the music and sound design help you settle into into Arco's rhythmic and moody combat. It's very satisfying.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Came for the pixel art, stayed for the gameplay. I've been following the development of ARCO for months now and, despite knowing almost nothing about its gameplay or story, I was planning to buy it on release mainly because of the art style. Was not dissappointed at all: graphics are beatiful, animations are fluid and sounds, music and VFX turn this into a very solid game.The biggest surprise came with the gameplay, the combat system and the story. Challenging but fair turn based combat with a twist - I am still on the second chapter and I already discovered several ways to approach every battle. The plot of the game is very mature, your choices affect the outcome in certain parts of the story, you definitely root for ARCO's characters...Will update this review as I finish the game but so far I cannot stress how good this game is. Very much recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: A new spin on turn based strategy with nostalgic pixel art and a breezy story about revenge and retribution. It's a lot of fun and easy to pick up. There are plenty of choices you can make and I'm curious to see how they affect the story and replayability. There are also various builds for each character, so you should have enough to explore and try out for a second playthrough.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: I was initially drawn to this game by its captivating pixel art and strategic combat. However, my heart was taken away with the music, the writing, and the story. Arco is an adventure brimming with wonder and depth, where each character’s journey feels profoundly real. The struggles they face and the evocative sounds of this world linger long after you close the game. Both the narrative and the combat system shine as they tread on unfamiliar territories, remixing ideas from tactical RPG's but making choices both in combat and out, really change the course of the game.I've played the game from start to finish, I've enjoyed every fight and story arc. The combat is hard yet once you get the hang of it (also very easy to restart lost fights) you feel like coordinating a western standoff in real time. Don't miss this game if you like tactical combat. Few games have tied mechanics like this, and you will be happily surprised.This indie gem is a treasure, offering a full game experience that resonates on a deeply emotional and aesthetic level. My sincere congratulations to the team for creating something that feels genuinely fresh.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

_childDocuments_.review: Enter the breathtaking world of Arco, a dynamic tactical RPG where your decisions shape the story. Three tales forged in bloodshed, laced with magic, and united by revenge.
_childDocuments_.name: Arco

name: Thank Goodness You're Here!
short_description: Thank Goodness You're Here! is an absurd comedy slapformer set in the bizarre Northern English town of Barnsworth. As a traveling salesman, take the time to see the sights and meet the locals, who are very eager to give you a series of increasingly odd jobs…

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to come right out and say this straight away: Thank Goodness You're Here is one of the funniest games I've ever played. I can't remember the last time I laughed out loud *this* often doing anything. The visuals are endlessly charming, the voice acting is perfection, the music is great and it's just so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ funny.Now - big asterisk - I am English. Half Northern, half Midlander. Much of what's funny about Thank Goodness is based in very specific references and vibes from Northern English culture from the last forty or so years. I may have been bordering on tears seeing a shop called "Price Shaggers" and the hilariously named products contained within, but I do wonder if this game might just make an American's head explode. That's what I love most about Thank Goodness though. It absolutely refuses to compromise in its depiction of the Yorkshire essence. It may only be a small subset of gamers who can fully enjoy the game, but by god will that group of people love it. It's obvious just how much love is in the developers for this county, dialect and cultural reference point. Despite some often grotesque or unflattering imagery, it never feels mean-spirited. Instead, Thank Goodness depicts a people and place with honesty and a wry humour that is more respectful than if they'd avoided anything potentially offensive. It's akin to when your best mate takes the piss out of you. From the outside, it looks cruel, but between the two of you, it's the truest expression of affection.The game is definitely on the shorter side, only taking me two hours (and I was really dragging my feet trying to see everything) but it's so jam-packed with jokes, weird dialogue and unique animations that I could have sworn it was more like four or five hours. The gameplay itself is fairly rote and is just there to facilitate as many jokes as possible, and the structure of the game can feel aimless as you loop through the same four or five areas over and over. Each return visit does see the area changed, with background characters advancing jokes or new sub-areas to explore, but it can be a little discouraging to go through the same bits over and over. Ultimately though, the devs turn this flaw into part of its big meta-joke on the relentless busywork that's prolific in so many games, so it's hard to really criticise the game for a flaw that can't really be remedied without losing so much of what makes it special.If you've ever lived above the middle of England, it's basically law that you have to play Thank Goodness You're Here!. A shining example of surrealist comedy that manages some surprisingly emotionally affective moments, this is a sublime experience that I can do nothing but recommend. I can't wait to forget as much of it as possible so I can play it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: In the , Deus Ex creator Warren Spector famously stated that his dream project would be a game taking place entirely within a single, expertly crafted city block, where you`d go aroud interacting with its people and their stories.In , a stranger will relentlessly offer you sausages through a fence hole in Coal Supper`s "" - a game where you assume the role a lil' british goblin-manchild, who goes about solving the problems of the jolly townsfolk of Barnsworth entirely by means of slap.It is beautiful, it is aggressively Northern England and it just might be the funniest game I`ve played. Buy this.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Usually, I'll review with deadpan one-liners, but for this absolute gem, I'm going to stuff a bit more meat in the pie. I first caught the reveal trailer on Friday morning and spent the whole day itching to get back home to play it.I live abroad now but grew up in England—alright, the south, but still—this game made me incredibly nostalgic for the warm vibes of the old stomping grounds. As a kid, I lived for the British absurdist comedies of the 2000s—The IT Crowd, The Mighty Boosh, and Garth Marenghi's Darkplace—and Thank Goodness You're Here captured that spice and had me laughing out loud again and again.With that said, I don't want to alienate or imply that anyone who didn't have the same childhood wouldn't find this a joy. The devs even diegetically added the option of having 'English' subtitles as opposed to 'Dialect'. The absurd running jokes in a cozy Yorkshire town really were the milk in the tea. Speaking of, it's absolutely recommended to mash a Yorkshire brew on the side to top it all off, so pop the kettle on and I'll go through some spoiler-free stuff in the meantime:You control a nameless businessman with, for the most part, three inputs: move, jump, and slap. The slap, hilarious as it is, doubles up as how you interact with the world. In this sense, it's a simple, relaxing break if you're coming from fast-paced action games, and a great next play if you're used to point and click, visual novels, and the like. Perfect to kick back and play from the sofa with a controller.The art style and feel of the game are reminiscent of 90s/00s British comics and illustrated books, you know, the kind where there's a bunch of stuff happening in one massive picture, and the thrill comes from scanning your eyes over the entire page to catch everything. With punchy and quirky animations adding to the charm, this is spot on. A genuine joy to play.Though it's around 2-4 hours for a single playthrough, the shorter time shouldn't put you off. They've packed so much personality into this that it’s well worth it. I wrapped it up in a couple of nights, so it’s ideal if you enjoy shorter experiences. I found myself wanting to knock on every door and check every corner for smaller gags, and I'm pretty sure there's more for me to go back and find on a second playthrough. I wasn't disappointed with what I'd found so far. It's tempting to give examples, but please just check it out yourselves.Oh yeah, Matt Berry's in it as well.Thank you, James, Will, and the rest of the team at Coal Supper! I had a lot of fun <3
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I usually don't bother writing reviews for games because I'm just an average Joe who plays games and I don't have anything insightful to say. However, Thank Goodness You're Here has probably been the best $20 I've spent on a game in a long time. It has a great art style, great humor, and good music and really makes me want to explore this little town that is filled to the brim with personality from top to bottom. PLEASE do not watch anything about this game before going in, just dive in and have a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a huge person on watching people play games, and if they seem good or funny enough, trying them out myself. I didn't make it a full five minutes into someone's gameplay when I desperately wanted to try this game out for myself and I'm so glad I did. As someone who was born in America, some of the english language or words were extremely funny, especially out of context. I had no idea what some of the people said but I didn't need to!This game is a perfect mix of funny and weird and it's right on the border where I loved it. Some of the scenes left me speechless in a good way. I was actually surprised at how much effort went into this game, there was quite a lot of interactions that changed over time and it made it so much funnier. My favorite were the two neighbors with the trashcan, that was gold!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: What a strange and original production. It's very funny and very British (especially the accents), satirising elements of "culture" we don't see in American games, like Greggs pasty shops, Victorian chimney-sweeps, and chavs at the chippie. It's also extremely surreal, recalling quirky Brit media like '90s TV news parody "The Day Today" or David Firth's darkly weird "Salad Fingers".Gameplay is somewhat linear, and easy throughout — you explore different sections of the town and occasionally do a platforming or collect-'em-up section — and replay value will be very limited. You could plough through it in a few hours if you were so inclined, but then you'd miss a lot of hidden treats and eavesdropping on the townsfolk's wacky conversations. I saw it as more of an interactive short film, and a very entertaining one.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Thank Goodness You're Here is a pretty short comedy game, but what it lacks in length it more than makes up for in humor. The gameplay is very basic and boils down to "hit all the things until something progresses", but every single thing you hit will either make you giggle or piss your pants laughing. It takes 2-3 hrs to beat, but I plan on replaying once or twice and inviting my friends to watch and experience the humor. As an example, it starts out with some random question that I assume someone from Northern England would understand, and when you say "What?" it turns on subtitles with translations.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: 100% yes. Fun jokes, great voice, music, animation and awesome stories to follow. If you take it slow, you can enjoy different scenes as time goes by- the neighbors with their bins, the lady with the driving instructor, the burnt steak etc. Best part, is that there is no hint but the game is made in a way that certain paths are blocked at specific scenes to help you understanding where you need to go, plus the dialogues will let you know roughly what you need to go. Bought this game when it's on sale- it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I understand what I just played.Thank Goodness You're Here is an interactive cartoon where you play a silent gentleman trying to see a Mayor about a business proposal. Since the mayor's in a meeting, you can either wait quietly for him to finish, or explore the town. Exploring the town opens you up to a world of linear requests that take you from one whacky scenario to the next across a very British, very insulated little community.There is very little challenge here; when I was stuck I just kept meandering until I found an open path. But the joy of the game isn't really in the challenge, it's in just seeing and hearing the people interact. Your character helps move things along with them but I almost get the feeling that they would do their own thing without you. It's not a bad thing, mind you. But, considering the $20 price tag, there will be some people who find it too expensive for what you get.I paid $17 for it but I think it's more worth $15 when you take into account the animation and voice acting involved. It is a very short experience--three hours for me with a few moments where I didn't know what to do. With that in mind, my recommendation is to wait for it to go on sale.I wouldn't skip the experience, though; it is an entertaining one. I should also point out that although it is animated, it is not for children. There is a lot of language and inuendo in the game and at one point, you do see a man who is naked from the waist down. It's not a huge deal, but I thought I'd point it out.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A very silly game about everyday life in Britain, much like the main character, it's very short and sweet, running around 2.5 hours for a first playthrough, it's a fully linear affair with a few easy puzzles. Plenty of laughs to be found, but your mileage may vary as the brand of humour presented won't be for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: What a gem. It's short, but worth the full price. It's quirky, strange, and hilarious. It's unlike anything I've played, it's one of the most original games I've had the pleasure of trying. I wish I could play it for the first time again.As long as you're okay with weirdness, do give it a try. It's absolutely perfect in what it does, and it's bound to make you laugh.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely funny, doesn't punch down, cute cartoon stylings and great dialogue that has quietly become something that gets quoted around the house.The game itself is pretty much linear, so don't expect a huge world to explore with multiple different challenges available at the same time. Took about 2.5 hours of play time to complete, and I think that's okay value - plus someone else in the household also got their own playthrough from the start which made the overall value for money higher.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: All I could think of ever since I've played the demo was: Slap slap slap —Slap slap slap Slap slap slap Must. Slap. Everything. Every. Thing.(and everyone, for that matter)All. The. Time.A first look:That being said, this game is hilarious. It's funny, absurd, weird, fascinating and above all creative. Thank the lord for subtitles, too, because I would be a tad lost sometimes without them; I love the accents. It's stellar voice work, and I'm here for it. The play on words you often come across is glorious, too. I'm still laughing over tits—the birds, of course. Someone will have to explain 'threepence' to me, though. I should stalk my UK friend this evening…My only pet peeve, but that is more on me than the game, is that I'm so eager to explore and discover everything that I sometimes rush through too fast and miss some conversations. When I turn back to tune in, the conversation stops or is without subtitles. Yet it didn't pass by me that there are fun little details like things written on the wall or ground, the employee of the month pictures above the window at the very beginning, the market stalls,… Accompanied by cartoonesque visuals and great music, it just comes together. Everything feels right, which leads to a real vibe while playing, and I love that. I'm just laid-back exploring and slapping, lots and lots of slapping. I… I just can't help it. I'm not even ashamed of it!So, it's a big yes for me, with a big thumbs up and a smile. You can tell how much dedication, love, labour, etc, that went into this game.I even would like to ask when "thank goodness you're still here" will be released. I would love to see more of this odd 'slapformer', which I didn't know I needed so badly in my life!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I love the hundred-hour epic as much as the next guy but short games are good too. _childDocuments_.review: My guess would be around 4 to 5 hours if you know what to do. Or if you follow a guide it might be shorter as you won't miss out on an achievement, so you don't have to replay the game.  2/10 1,1 but probably 2,1... why the decimal number you ask... because there is an ending you can reach within under 20 minutes.  not yet. , but it is still missing a few achievements.  No Yes, many! No No No No No No difficulty option NoWhat the heck did I just play? I expected something funny and strange.. but I wasn't prepared for this amount of strangeness going on in this game. To be upfront, my rating for this game might be a bit lower than some others because it turned out the humor in this game wasn't my style. There were funny moments, but also quite a lot of moments that didn't do anything to me. In Thank Goodness You're Here! you play as a little guy who goes to visit the small town Barnsworth. The reason why... I'm not exactly sure. Your boss asks you to go there and don't miss the bus. So the good employee you're... you jump out of the window to not miss the bus! There you have an appointment with the Major, but he is busy the moment you arrive. So you have a choice... wait for the appointment, or explore the town. If you choose to explore the town.. you'll enter the wildest fever dream you'll have without having a fever or without dreaming. You'll make multiple runs through town to help out the people, or sometimes make their life miserable. The story on its own is wild and I would recommend playing the first playthrough without a guide and using a second playthrough to mop up the missing achievements. At this moment achievements don't unlock if you start a new playthrough directly after your first one. You have to restart the game for the achievements to work on a second or third playthrough. Thank Goodness You're Here! has many missable achievements. a whole bunch you'll just unlock out or curiosity and some by just following the story, but there are many where you have to do something specific. Like: listening to two potatoes talking before you chop them down to make fries or find all the singing mice. I think that the main story can be beaten in 1,5/2 hours, so a second playthrough to mop up what you missed isn't the worst. I hope that someone will end up writing a complete achievement guide. I tried to make a start but wasn't sure about everything and also had no clue about a few of them, so I gave up writing one. I'm looking forward to coming back to this game after a guide is available to mop up those last few achievements I'm missing. I give Thank Goodness You're Here! 3 out of 5 stars.
