_childDocuments_.review: Lovely, weird, and very funny. A strange puzzle game that doesn't follow any particular loop, where the fun is in discovering what the hell is it you're supposed to be doing next. Sort of a metroidvania in how often you have to backtrack, but this never feels boring as backtracking always reveals a new puzzle element, as well as some silly new quirk to the world or characters in it. Production values are top notch. It feels like you're playing a real TV cartoon, one I would definitely watch outside of the game. The lighthearted presentation misdirects from some hilariously dark moments. And one of the voices is Matt Berry! It's on the short side, but feels like a complete experience and leaves you wanting more. Good stuff!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly funny, well-thought out game. Engaging and hilarious throughout, every small detail will at the very least make you chuckle. I would definitely play a sequel, I only wish it was longer than 3 hours. One of those rare games where paying 10 bobs for 3 hours feels worth it, wanting more comes from not wanting the game to end rather than feeling like there wasn't enough of it
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A pleasant surprise and full of English country charm! I have had some great little laughs and smirks from cheeky jokes here and there. :) My only gripe is I frequently encounter a bug where the audio on cut scenes will lag behind and doesn't sync up leading to many a scene run for 30 seconds to a minute without any audio.  I hope this is addressed in a future update.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: "Thank Goodness You're Here" is an intriguing mix of stylistically fun visuals and classic British humour that makes it a unique experience. The game captures a whimsical, almost cartoonish charm that keeps you visually entertained. The humour, distinctly British, is a refreshing touch that adds a layer of wit and charm to the overall experience.However, the game does have its drawbacks. The gameplay is quite linear, which can make it feel restrictive at times. The game mechanics are limited, offering little variety or depth in terms of interactive options. Additionally, there are moments when the game seems to miss the point or fall short of its potential, leaving you wanting more. It sometimes feels like a game that my mum would find funny, which might not appeal to all age groups or tastes.In summary, while "Thank Goodness You're Here" has its entertaining moments and stylistic appeal, it might not fully satisfy those looking for a more engaging and varied gaming experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A visually appealing game with hilarious bits even though I didn't get all the context of its humor. A good (although short) comedy game for its price with my concern only on the subtitles. Sometimes they are delayed and there are times they wont even show up at all, and its hard to understand what they're saying as I'm not a native English speaker. Overall, you could clearly see that they've crafted this game with love and effort.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good! I really loved The Good Time Garden and this an amazing game that expands on the vibes of that game. The best way I can describe Thank Goodness You're Here! is dream logic. It's not challenging and there isn't exactly puzzles in the way I thought there would be. However atmosphere and characters are perfection, and while simple the gameplay is super fun. The voice acting is also top notch.Took about 2.5 hours to complete, around another 2 to leisurely get the remaining achievements. Worth the price and I look forward to showing it to people I know.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Love, love love this game, been patiently waiting since the demo!! Absolutely hilarious, the British humour is spot on, was laughing out loud so many times!Aside from the humour, the art style and voice acting is amazing! The tasks you do along the way are all so different, it never feels repetitive. I love how the more you progress through the game the scenes change throughout the town making it even more exciting to keep exploring and find what's new! I didn't want it to end 10/10!!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Well I cured a milk shy guy bathing with a cow, destroyed a mans home and mental stability, became an unwilling participant in a fertiliser inspired activity, used buttery nubs to free a man I went on to bully, set up some displays and made the fishmonger maybe the happiest man around, kicked a man with only beans to his name, got fed some sausages, slapped some things and made the sale. All in a few hours work.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, ok. I’m gonna be that guy. This will be my first review on Steam in my mountain of games I can’t seem to finish!What an absolute treat of a game! I loved running around and slapping literally EVERYTHING. I slapped a guy in the tush and he said “oh, that’s queer!”. Maybe to you!!The music is so fitting, the slapstick comedy isn’t too overwhelmingly cheesy, the graphics remind me of a colorful comic, and the cut scenes will leave you believing you’re watching a Saturday morning cartoon. I LOL’d so much in this game, and as a 41 year old father and husband who works with the general public and absolutely HATES people, I needed a good laugh. (And I don’t laugh at video games)Took me 3 hours to “beat”, but I am going to go back and get all the achievements. I promise you’ll have a blast fetching meat and slapping jiggly booties in this unforgettable quest!10 oot uv ♥♥♥♥♥ 10
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Well worth the price for three hours of laughs. I played this game for some friends and we were cracking up at how ridiculous this game is, the gameplay and story are so thoroughly enjoyable I didn't even realize it only took three hours to play through. Playing through a second time to get the achievements
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been excited about this game since I played the Demo. I did NOT regret buying and got entertained throughout the whole game so much that I played it through in one sitting, which is rare. The humor is great, the wordplay is exquisite, and the game's symbolism in so many ways is DAZZLING. I WANT MORE! I NEED MORE! I'm looking forward to more games or even parts? DLC's? Whichever it might be. I'll happily play and cackle away. #blushingincluded I 100% recommend it to everybody who is into weird humor and fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Stop reading this review, AND BUY THE GAME NOW!!! The gameplay is refreshingly simple and focused...yet somehow manages to also be heavily nuanced. the humor falls somewhere between Misadventures of Flapjack, Blackadder, and Only Fools and Horses. The town stands out as its own unique and multilayered character. simply fantastic.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: It's extremely charming! It was something I looked forward for ever since I saw a trailer and demo for it. It plunges you in a world that is very lively with no exactly clear direction or map so you'd have to explore every inch and encounter funny characters along the way. I do think it is a bit short as you can finish it in one sitting and even faster if you blitz to your objective. Even so, such a unique experience to play in the real life small British town of Barnsworth and its accurate depictions, yup. Assimilation into meat and all.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't laughed this hard in any video game ever. I actually hurt my arm from so much laughter.I absolutely love this games art style so much. The music is also fantastic. I loved every second of this game and the characters are all fantastic. If you want a good laugh or had a crappy day I would really recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Very much an 'experience' game, which will most likely already tell you if it's something you're into or not - more like an animated comedy sketch show in game form. Beat it in 2.3 hours, with nothing really challenging about it. However, those 2.3 were some of the funniest I've had with a game, effortlessly fun and joyful in a way many games are not. Really well written, some great long form gags, a great way to spend an evening.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly, possibly, the funniest game i've ever played. I am genuinely upset at the fact i know i missed content in this game, and am ready to replay it from stem-to-stern to see the rest. More british than monty python, and a time capsule of weird, surreal humor mixed with deeply down-to-earth britishness. Worth your money, worth your time. Poke everything. Avoid the plot as long as you can, poke every object, try every direction. It's always worth it. I'll be watching Coal Supper with eagerness. I can't wait for their next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This is possibly the funniest game I've ever played.  It's like a cross between Monty Python and Regular Show, but interactive.  Basically it's an adventure game with platforming elements.  You can move, jump, and slap things, and that'all you need to do.  It's only a few hours long, but that's a plus because none of the jokes ever get tedious.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A charming little game that's less bout the gameplay itself (which does include very simple little puzzles), and more about exploration, navigation, and soaking in the overall experience. Gets quite surreal, some swearing, and overall reminded me of late night Channel 4 animations. Good fun, but can be completed in one sitting in around 2 hours.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: As a lad from Yorkshire and one from a small village very slyly mention in the game this was everything and more I wanted from a game with a Yorkshire setting. Everything is overly exaggerated but even then there is a bit of truth inside it to how people talk to how they act.What a lovely game and so much fun, it flows smoothly and you never feel like you missed anything.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Being from Yorkshire, I don’t think I’ve ever related more to a video game than I have with Thank Goodness You’re Here! Coal Supper‘s love letter to Yorkshire, if you will. I also can’t remember the last time I finished a game laughing. That said, you absolutely don't have to be from Yorkshire, or even Britain for that matter, to appreciate all this game has to offer. If it has already peaked your interest - buy it! In short: tha thought it wa ‘reyt bloody good!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Stumbled across this on my front page, played the trailer out of curiosity....3 hours later I was watching the end credits roll. One of the best games I've played in a long time. Brilliantly funny, simple to play, and well worth the asking price, short though it is.An absolute gem that deserves recognition.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: My only complaint is that there are not enough starts to award this game. Lovely slice-of-life depiction of an ordinary town near Machester, full of ordinary Machester-type people. Confirmed by our official British correspondent Angel Taiils, confirmed as being 100% lore-accurate to "♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Manchester innit"must play. GG's well made game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a little bummed that this game only took around 2.5 hours to completely finish, so unless you want to go back and get all the achievements then don't expect much.  However, the comedy is very odd and British, the artwork is cute, and the game is worth playing for sure, just know how much you're getting for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 experience. Charming visuals, excellent comedy and really captures the spirit of t'North.As soon as I saw the first trailer I was extremely excited for this game. This seemed like the exact brand of absurd yet distinctly British humour that is almost impossible to find anywhere outside the works of David Firth. I was not disappointed.+++++ Humour+ Art style+ Animations+ Voice acting+ Authentically British+  Rewards your effort and engagement with plenty of extra gags and humorous conversations to discover- Very occasional stutter (potentially a problem with my PC and won't affect your enjoyment of the game, but happened often enough to mention)- Not really a game as much as an interactive sketch show (not an issue for me but may be for some)
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay isnt anything too special, but the presentation, comedy, and voice acting makes everything a lot of fun. The comedic timing is top-notch. Bunch of odd and hilarious towns people to help. It's not very long and can be finished in one sitting(took me arund 2 hours to complete)If you like weird/surreal comedy, and British people, then I can recommend this 100%. Oh and it also has Matt Berry in it, that alone makes this worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Oh, thank goodness you're here! There is a game on Steam that you have not furiously violated your vision spheres with and it is about time you rectified that problem at your earliest convenience! Yes sir! You must slap your little hand everywhere and jump on everything! Make everything right AND wrong! No in between! If what you are doing seems normal, YOU ARE PLAYING IT WRONG!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I found the game to be pretty enjoyable. I really loved all the small jokes sprinkled throughout the game and I just found it enjoyable to find all the little details throughout. The comedy in the game is pretty good as well and you don't have to be British to understand it. The total playtime for a full playthrough does feel short at around 2.5 hours but I also feel that it's a fairly good amount of time and doesn't overstay its welcome.Some of the issues I have with the game that I would love to be addressed.- bug where once you complete the game and stopped watching the credits makes it so that no achievements can be earned.- the ability to skip cutscenes and the end credits but maybe only make it available once you've beaten the game (and not when you've sat in the office for 15 minutes)- I would also like to see a soundtrack release for this game. I don't know if that would be possible with some of the licensed music but I think it would be cool to have either way.Any other issues I have with the game are minor.Also as a side note, I really loved the Easter egg of the Playdate. As an enthusiast of the Playdate it's always fun to see it show up or be talked about.I'd say that this game is worth picking up if you're interested in it. I don't imagine it coming down all that much in price in the near future (just look at Untitled Goose game as evidence) so I would say if you want it, buy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Take equal parts Rick and Morty, Adventure Time and Wallace and Gromit, throw them in a blender and make it ridiculously, deliciously British, and out pops Thank Goodness You're Here.This may only be a 2-3 hour experience, but it's astonishingly creative. These devs are funny, funny people, with some incredibly weird ideas, almost every single one of which fully lands. I wouldn't hesitate to call Thank Goodness You're Here the funniest game I've ever played, genuinely. It's such a joy that I played through it twice in a day. The second playthrough was even better than the first, as it was easier to keep track of the different character's plotlines and appreciate them more.So really, if you like British humor even a *little bit*, this game is utterly essential. The only caveat to point out is that gameplay takes a back seat, with each little sequence of gentle interaction being fully in service to its story and visual gags rather than presenting any sort of difficulty or mechanical complexity. Think of it more as an interactive cartoon than a game, if you must.Seriously though - play it. One of the best of 2024, easily.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, although it's mostly about punching things and I honestly don't know how people outside of the UK would respond to this one. The humour is surreal and very, very northern. I finished at about 3 1/2 hours with the majority of achievements unlocked.I would highly recommend savouring it rather than rushing through it in one sitting.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Utterly brilliant surrealist journey into a completely normal Yorkshire town in the 1980s. I adored its art, its amazing characters and the stories they tell. The gameplay its self is very simple. You move, jump and hit things. that's it. Yet through these simple interactions a complex, surreal, disturbing and completely gripping story emerges that had me  so absorbed that I played it through in one sitting without even intending to! Maybe it helps that I have lived in Yorkshire most of my life so the abundant little nods and jokes about life "up North" had me grinning and giggling to myself throughout. Your mileage may vary depending on your familiarity with the culture...That said the absurd surreal nature of many of the jokes would probably equally appeal to the "lol random" crowd so this is still well worth a look for lovers of the bizarre even of you know almost nothing about Northern England. I will be 100%ing this game at some point now I have completed the main story just to see the weird and hilarious stuff that I missed.  I feel like some real love and passion went into making this game and it really shows! Reccomended!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: OMG this was so much fun i am not sure if i missed anything but will know more after a second playthrough.I will also be making sure my young nephews get to play this as they are a little obsessed with a bit of british slag (literally the youngest calls us all young bobbies and he's only 6) and the fun obserdity of the game is sure to tickle their funny bones.NOW i must say this really gives me a monty python feel in the joke/storyline aspect which i love, its a bit random and a lot silly. def worth having in my game library!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Watch the trailer. If you like what you see, then commit to the purchase.You have two main inputs - movement and interact. With that in mind, enjoy the ride. The comedy is non-stop, the animation is gorgeous, the voice acting is top-notch and did I mention the comedy? You will be giggling all the way through, interjected at points by outright raucous laughter.Expect 2-3 hours and minimal replayability. But that one run? Worth.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: A must-play of its genre. Its a bit like you're watching Slapjack or the Regular Show if an episode was feature film length, raunchier, extremely English, and you can slap the dickens out of absolutely everyone and everything. My first playthrough of Thank Goodness You're Here took ~3 hours, but in every scene little things change and characters have new dialogue so its very easy to miss things making a second playthrough worthwhile. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: I've been expecting this game for a while. The art style, humor and music in the trailer seemed to be right up my alley and I was not wrong.Its a cheeky game with filled to the brim with visual gags and jokes.  The game flows nicely, except during a couple of sections in the middle in which it "drags" a bit but it honestly has a killer beginning, an amazing ending and most of the middle is also top-notch.So what are you waiting for! Go on, lad!Thank goodness, you're here!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant game, as soon as I started to play I never stopped until I was finished, everything here is beautifully done, the visuals, music, sound effects, gameplay, the writhing, everything is impeccable, truly a labor of love and dedication, the team deserves all the glory and standing applause for this beautiful gem of a game but what got me to love this game to my dying breath is the humor which is so zany, absurd, dark and twisted and still lighthearted at its core amazingly done, the other aspect is the gameplay which is simple and fluid anyone can play and enjoy this game which such well though design bravo to that.One of the best games of the year for me, and I hope you guys have plans to make more gems like this please, I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This game is very accurate simulator of everyday's life in Britain.It also keeps crashing on my pc and despite what Steam says about my playtime I've only played for almost 50 minutes and the rest of the playtime was me opening and closing the game in an attempt to play this game.I hope it gets fixed soon but despite this issues the game is a solid 8/10 for me.Now excuse me but I need to drink a cuppa of tea and attempt to play this game
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: An enjoyable game with a wonderful vibe. I didn't laugh at all like many of the reviewers were but I was grinning quite a bit. A 2 hour playthrough with 12 missing achievements so I didn't do everything it seems. But honestly 2 hours seems perfect for me I felt it was getting a bit long in the tooth by the end but then it ended so perfect length lol. If you like fun experience games I'd say its well worth a buy. If money to length matters to you what are you even doing here.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: There's nowt wrong with this'un, you'd be a daft ape'eth not to try it! The visual gags, animation, and voice cast were all top notch. Wish there was more like this, it reminded me of TV shows like the fast-show and league of gentlemen. It might only be 3 hours long, but it's got more value and passion packed in than a tin of Peans or any of the corporate-games we're having to suffer through these days.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: The game took just over two hours to complete, but even if it had been under I don't think I'd complain, it was a lot of laughs and fun to play with a lot of crazy and sometimes dark humour.I would recommend it and say that its worth noting there is a lot of rather British humour that might not appeal to all but for me it was on point.I wont spoil it but the ending felt so Monty Python and made me laugh, a wonderful way to end this wonderful little adventure.But could I add you should have hadIt's all over so off you pop,Recommend to friends on steam shop.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid game with good humor.  The game play feels very similar to that of a point and click adventure game, just without an inventory mechanic and in its place a slap mechanic. Slap things to make people talk, slap things to have funny things happen, and occasionally jump repetitively when the time calls for it. It's all very simple, which while nice and straightforward, also means there's a lack of depth to a lot of the game.     The game is extremely linear, and because of how little there is to do for the story, most of the time you spend playing the game will be on seeing the fun ways to interact with the world rather than furthering the story itself. In addition, the game has a lot of abstract moments, ones that are just unexplained and really out there. Some of which are the disturbing kind of weird, not the funny or charming kind.      If you want a silly game that has good humor but not a lot of depth to it, this is the game for you. It's a fairly middle of the road quality game with more good parts than bad. For how cheap this game is, it's well worth the investment I'd say.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Is this Britain simulator? Constant laughs from beginning to end. A fantastic little game that doesn't overstay its welcome, says what it wants to say, respects the player, and doesn't waste your time. Loved every moment of it. The found footage footage and dialect language option pile on the charm, and turn this into what feels like a very personal work of art.Thanks to Coal Supper for making this absolute gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutely delightful little game that I think will stick with me for a long time. The humor is on point and the presentation in general is top notch.The only potential negatives I can point to are the fact that it's short and that the gameplay is pretty basic, however I'd argue that these aspects actually support what the game is trying to accomplish.The price is also a bit higher than one might expect for a game of this length, but the quality here is so incredibly high that I feel that offsets it.Thank you for making such a wonderful experience, Coal Supper. Can't wait to see what you make next!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Whether you find this funny will of course depend on your sense of humour, but regardless the animation and bits are amazing. I found it quite funny with a few laugh out loud and brilliant moments. Playtime was around 3 hours (I went offline midgame which screwed up the registered game time). Unhinged and entertaining, and at this price it's definitely worth a punt. Only downsides are lack of interactivity and the looping nature of the game can mean you are sometimes wandering not quite sure where to go, but usually this means you run into more gags and the areas aren't big so it's not too bad. Hope the devs carry on in this vein!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Really loved this one, completed in one sitting which took about 3 hours. Not sure if there is much scope for replays but the humour as someone from Northern Englad was right up my street.Definitely worth a punt, you will be able to tell if it's your vibe within the 2 hour refund window.Give it a go, support small indies such as these!Art style impeccable, fab voice acting including the man the legend that is Matt Berry. I played it along side my non gamer partner who enjoyed it as much as me.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this literally the minute I have finished my first playthrough and my god, I am struggling for words, in the best of ways. (Will keep this as spoiler free as I can though)If you enjoy fun story guided , partially open world with bits of platforming games, this is the one for you!I knew I would love this thing (just from the style alone! It is extremely charming and pulled me in from the first trailer) but I didn't realise just how much I'll enjoy the chaos of it all!There's also replayability, plenty of hidden bits and bobs all over the place, with hidden achievements that are a lil trickier than just 'wander about and find out' which I very much enjoy (cause believe me, I have combed through every inch of every one of those maps and I'm still missing a fair few!) and I even found a few references to  which tickled me greatly! Anyway, I'm rambling on now.All in all, a wonderful experience full of unexpected twists and a very adorable protagonist!I hope  finds this useful, I know I will definitely be recommending  to anyone who is willing to listen!
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Having lived in the north of England for a many years of my life, this game's comedy really resonated with me. Not a minute went by without me laughing - the sort of comedy in this game is right up my street, and was made even funnier by that beautiful Yorkshire accent. This game will have you exploring a small town in the heart of Yorkshire, which is filled with plenty of insane characters. You'll be helping out the townsfolk with their many problems, whether that be mowing the grass, fetching tools or helping out a really stretchy man with his shopping. It's not a difficult game at all, and it'll only take you a few hours to complete, but if you're in the mood for a game that doesn't take itself seriously and you need a break from the long and serious games, then I really recommend this! It was such a pleasure to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Mark my words, this'll win a Bafta Games award. A rich, coherent vision executed to the highest order. Jam packed with jokes, visual gags and everything that makes a fun game fun, I had an absolute ball playing this tonight and no doubt I will again and again in the future.Edit: I played it again and it was just as fun! So so so so good
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Great little indie title with some extremely accurate humour true to northern sensibilities. Very comfy vibes, with puzzles that don't require too much thought but still offer satisfying and sometimes unexpected punchlines upon their conclusion. with bright animation reminiscent of old British comics like The Dandy and Beano, Whizzer & Chips etc. Visually easy on the eyes. Only criticism would be mic quality and some of the voice acting was a bit spotty but I can forgive that for a game that cost me less than £15 bob. Also love Matt Berry but he can't do a convincing northern accent to save his life. Could have got David Firth (a yorkshire native) instead. If there's ever a sequel I'd love to audition.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the most British game I've ever played. If you're not British like me, I would recommend playing with subtitles, because I don't think you're going to understand a lot of what's said due to regional accents and slang. I'm also not 100% sure you'll get some of the very British references peppered throughout the backgrounds, but if you are you'll find yourself, like me noticing stuff all the time 🤣I've only played about 40 minutes so far because I don't want to race through it too quickly, but if you enjoyed the demo, definitely buy the full game.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

_childDocuments_.review:
After arriving early for a big meeting with the mayor of a bizarre Northern English town, a traveling salesman takes the time to explore and meet the locals, who are all very eager to give him a series of increasingly odd jobs...

Thank Goodness You're Here! is a comedy slapformer, which unfolds over time as the players' exploration and antics leave their mark on the strange town of Barnsworth. With each completed odd job, new areas of the town open up, stranger and stranger tasks become available, and the clock ticks towards our salesman's big meeting. The town's colorful inhabitants are brought to life with vibrant hand-drawn animation, fully voiced dialogue, and wall-to-wall double entendres.
_childDocuments_.name: Thank Goodness You're Here!

name: Castlevania Dominus Collection
detailed_description: In addition to the three action adventure games from the Castlevania series, Haunted Castle Revisited, a redesigned version of the very first Castlevania arcade game, makes its debut! And you can also play it in its original format! Experience the world of Castlevania like never before, with never-before-seen art and handy new features such as rewind, quick saves and much more! - Titles Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow The adventures of Soma continue! Discover a completely new way to create countless weapons by combining souls, in stunning 2D graphics. One year after the events of Castlevania: Aria of Sorrow, a boy named Soma Cruz is once again put at the center of a plot to resurrect Dracula led by a mysterious cult.. Will he finally be able to face his own destiny and put an end to all this? Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin Not one but two heroes join their forces to fight the evil this time! Switch between Jonathan and Charlotte with a single button press and make the best use of their unique abilities. Dracula's Castle has suddenly resurfaced, but something doesn't add up. Jonathan Morris and Charlotte Aulin make their way in to investigate, they soon discover that the mind behind all this is not who they thought... Castlevania Order of Ecclesia The enigmatic Shanoa is the only human capable of using the glyphs, symbols full of magic. Gather glyphs by exploring the Castle and its surroundings and absorb the power of the mighty foes you fight! The three most powerful glyphs, thought to be able to even defeat Dracula himself, have been stolen. Can Shanoa bring them back to the Order, and finally destroy the Dark Lord? Haunted Castle Haunted Castle Revisited, an redesigned version of the very first Castlevania arcade game, makes its debut! And you can also play it in its original format!

_childDocuments_.review: NOTE: This (first impression) review is about the quality of the emulation/package of this collection - not the Castlevania games themselves. Feel free to correct me on details I might've missed about the games themselves - then I will correct them in this review.---Castlevania Dominus Collection is the latest collection from KONAMI. Developed once more by M2 ((recently) known as a Japanese emulation powerhouse, for their previous works such as the "Anniversary" and Castlevania Collections for KONAMI and the "mini" emulation consoles for both SEGA (SEGA Mega Drive Mini and Mega Drive 2 Mini) and Konami (PC Engine (CoreGrafx)/TurboGrafx-16 Mini)). HOWEVER (contrary to earlier collections), this collection seems to be partial ports of the original DS games to PC (and the other console platforms it has been released on).This collection contains the three Nintendo DS games of the Castlevania franchise (Dawn of Sorrow, Portrait of Ruin and Order of Ecclesia). These were not re-released on any platform, Two other games are included - the arcade game Haunted Castle (already been re-released under KONAMI's Arcade Classics Anniversary Collection also available on Steam), alongside a new "revisited" version of the game (it being a new pixel art based remake).Now since this has been released on Steam (PC) and other home consoles, it is probably the last Castlevania related re-release out that Konami will work on in the nearby future as most notable games have been re-released through M2's emulation suites (excluding the MSX title Vampire Killer).Knowing M2 for their quality emulation, the emulation of the DS games is definitely nice. The audio seems to be clear (most likely using audio files over the DS' original sound capabilities, as done with their previous GBA-rooted collection for Castlevania). Compared to the previous GBA emulated release (Castlevania Advance Collection), there is no toggle between "normal" and "high quality" sound. Their result of using audio files over the handheld's own sound results into letting the player choose between Japanese and English voices, along with setting the volume for Background Music (BGM), Sound Effects (SE) and the Voices.For the DS games, there is a "third screen" added for visualising maps during gameplay. This was not present in the original (or VC re-release0 before.  You can switch between the visible screens (on the side) with the Select/View button of your controller. You can choose several different arrangements between the three screens - including only showing two like the original DS games. You can also show a background colour in the menu (out of black, white and several coloured gradients. You can check the settings by holding the A button on your controller to temporarily hide the menu screen. For Haunted Castle (both the arcade as the revisited version), you can choose for pixel filtering ("No filter", "Smoothing", "Scanlines" and "Scanlines & Smoothing").The Controller/Keyboard settings are per game, binded by "action" basis, although the keyboard settings can not be changed in-game, requiring a third party tool. Only Xbox controller button prompts are shown in this Steam version - no keyboard button prompts will be shown despite using a keyboard to control the game. The touch screen controls of the DS games are handled (by default) with your right controller stick. Clicking the touch screen controlling stick changes between three speed sensitivities. You can also use a mouse to control the touch screen.At last, every game allows using Save States (through the Load and Save menus), and the DS games include a full compendium to help you read up on moves, equipment, items and enemies.Other settings for the entire collection include the ROM/Game version (American/Japanese/European, also Korean for Order of Ecclesia), swapping the OK/Cancel actions from A/B to the "Western" and "Japanese/Nintendo" orientation, using either the left stick for touch screen controls or regular controlling the character (similar to the D-Pad), swapping the screen refresh timing by V-Sync or an in-game/emulator timer.While this is a very well presented collection with FMVs in the menu, full artwork galleries for the DS games and a music player for all the games (loose .m4a files are also easily present for off-game listening): the lack of UI refinement for PC is still an annoying trait most M2 games share. You can not easily enter full screen mode through any in-game binding - only with using the (left) Alt and Enter button to switch between four screen modes (windowed, full screen, a second full screen option and possibly borderless). And the fact the button prompts do not swap between Xbox controller and keyboard is also a nuisance for the PC port.Otherwise - this seems like another solid collection for those craving to (re)play the Castlevania classics along with its newest title being a remake of the arcade original.This game does work on Linux as well through Valve's Proton (tested on an Arch Linux PC - should yield the same result on the Steam Deck systems), although the full screen modes do show a white border. I'd personally recommend this emulation compilation as another one to add to your Steam library!

_childDocuments_.review: So, as someone who plays a Lot of these games, Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin is my favorite metroidvania of all time. And it's not close.It features one of the most unique and fun character controllers in the genre - two character controllers!The game is fun, filled with beautiful pixel art and incredible music, a lot of my favorite boss fights in the whole genre, and some of the best environment and level designs in genre. Portrait also features a Ton of alternate playable characters. One of whom in particular is, I won't spoil it. But you know those old rumors that went "if you beat 20 enemies in Cruel Smash you get Sonic in Melee"? It's like that but like actually real. The character you unlock is incredible and unique, and I'll leave it at that.There's two other 9/10 games here, too. Dawn and Ecclesia are honestly just as good and well-rounded games. There's just. So much good to say about every game in this package. I would strongly encourage all fans of metroidvania games to sink a month into this trilogy. Any one of these games by themselves is worth the cost to entry.Other notes uhh. They made Dawn's annoying touch screen gimmick into a QTE with buttons, a Huge improvement. I'm glad they didn't just axe them completely. But they also included a pointer to do touch screen stuff if you want optimal DPS on certain souls, or to play as Sisters/Albus I imagine.UPDATE: 1000% map completion on Portrait, with most of my playtime spent on Steam Deck. The game crashed once when giving me the achievement for beating the Stella & Loretta fight, but I was able to complete it second try no issue. All in all, the game feels, looks, and sounds better than it ever did. I carry around a DSi with this game in it in my purse so I would for sure know. The only downside is they scuffed the translation a good bit. Improvements like spelling Richter's name correctly come at the expense of errant typos in the game's script. Ah well. Small downside for an otherwise perfect collection, albeit one I hope they address.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated on October 16th, 2024 to include that windowed/fullscreen state is now saved.Steam Deck:While this game is not officially listed as compatible, it runs absolutely fine and you can draw the magic seals and break the ice blocks with the touchscreen.Good points:* It's a solid collection of the Nintendo DS Castlevania titles, with more than one way of handling the touchscreen elements of the games. This was the big thing I was actually most worried about-- how would the Magic Seals be handled? Well, you can use your mouse (or touchscreen on a handheld device such as a Steam Deck) or use QTE button binds. This was well thought-out.* 3D effects had their resolution increased, though the textures are still the very low-res NDS ones.* The updated version of Haunted Castle fixes a lot of the issues of the original game while keeping the basic jank intact-- the game wouldn't really be Haunted Castle without most of that jank to be completely honest.* Configurable screen layouts. The default takes full advantage of the full size of a 16:9 monitor by putting *both* of the alternate displays onscreen along with the action, something you can't do with just an emulator. Now you can see the map AND enemy details at the same time, for three display action!* They finally fixed the package to save fullscreen status, so once you get things set the way you want, you're good to go.* If you like using classic game-breaking glitches, many of those have been re-implemented in the October 2024 patch to allow speedrunners to do things exactly as they remember.Bad points:* Keybinds can't be changed. This game really wants you to use a gamepad. With the number of buttons in active play, a gamepad makes sense, but this really needs to at least let people rebind buttons on keyboard. This makes it very clear that Japanese developers like M2 struggle with the mindset differences in PC development VS console.* The GBA Aria of Sorrow bonus (for having the cart in the other slot) is not included here. They could have easily detected the save data from Castlevania Advance Collection and used that to let you get the bonus Rare Ring you'd start with.* Haunted Castle is included in only two forms-- the remake and one original Japanese arcade version. It doesn't include the Legendary Kusoge "Version M" version of Haunted Castle, which is the way TRUE masochists would play it. Additionally, the remake version is.. perhaps a bit *too* easy. Most dedicated CV players should be able to 1LC (one-life clear) it within a day at most.* Some high-framerate monitor users may run into problems with the game running at abnormally slow speeds. I run my display in G-Sync mode at 144Hz with Timing mode (NOT VSync mode!) turned on in-game, and I haven't had any tearing or slowdown at all. I suspect that the VSync timing mode tries to run the game at whatever the monitor's refresh is, and this creates problems. YMMV here, depending on your PC specifications. Definitely don't expect this to support ultra-widescreen or anything like that.Ugly:* Dawn of Sorrow still has the serious problems with the luck stat.* Things that crashed the original cartridge will definitely still crash here, and a few of those crashes are relatively easy to trigger.I get that these are accurate, but maybe we could get a bit more out of a re-release..Overall:It's not perfect, but it's quite solid. With a bit more refinement, it could be just about perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: Possibly the greatest collection of RPGS all put into one beautiful bundle, and I been happily playing through all of them with zero complaints.PROS:-All three games function beautifully, no bugs or any sort of problems with the game play. -The art for its time is incredibly well done given these games were around the mid 2000's era of DS games.-You don't have to use the frustrating cursor anymore for a lot of the games, and its mostly automatically made to where you can input buttons to go past a door or seal a boss.-The story for the games are very straight to the point and don't mess around, for the most part they just IMMEDIATELY throw you straight into the game with some bits and piece of dialogue, but me personally I enjoy that because I rather just get into the game quickly instead of sitting through boring text boxes like what most games try to do. -Every game has its massive worth to it and alot of hours you can willingly dump to enjoy gaining powers from monsters, exploring all corners of the map to your liking, or grinding out monsters so you can steamroll or hack and slash your way to the next area. -The music is clean and just as good as what it originally sounded on the DS, if not better. -You get basically three full RPGS that will take you a long time to invest into for a good price of 25$, if you absolutely love RPGS with exploration in maps as well as plowing through rooms you are going to LOVE these classics.CONS:-No symphony of the night.Please give these games a try if you are a huge metroidvania fan such as myself, THESE are the grandfathers that pioneered all those 2D side scrolling rougelike/exploration games you see today, and without castlevania you wouldnt even be seeing nearly as good of inspirations. Give it a try! And by you supporting it we may potentially get more collections or (Hard coping mechanism) A new castlevania game since we haven't had a new title for over a decade. 10/10 Collection.

_childDocuments_.review: Nothing like enjoying some classics am I right or am I right? lol the Dominus collection is what you'd expect, the whole DS collection with some extra functions and menu customisation, you also get two bonus classic games in there which is real nice, the games run smooth and any issues you'd expect from the touch screen aspect of the games was handled nicely enough that I have no complaints at all, never played them before? Then here's your chance to enjoy them and with a save anywhere and rewind function at that dood!Okay a more meaty review, for newbies it's a 2D sidescrolling game that most would call a metroidvania due to how it plays like metroid in terms of map traversal and items and buffs you can find, each game you can find a variety of weapons, skills and spells to use, very different from your usual classic catslevania's where all you have is your whip and sub weapons, ya level up, get better equipment and the chances of getting items and skills/spells off of enemies is purely chance that can be upped by spells and equipment dood.What improvements have they made? I mean the games didn't need much changing but as for what they did do, they for starters in dawn of sorrow the symbol drawing is now replaced with button presses, the only issue of which is that you need a hecking good memory to remember what to press, or beat the boss a second time where the devs decided to make the prompts flash, which I feel should have been the norm or at least an option to have automatically, that or you can use the handy dandy reverse time function! allowing you to erase that unsightly mistake that totally wasn't your fault I swear dood! X3They also have menu options, you can switch between both the map and enemy/player information being on the right, making it just the map or other info on the right for a larger size and I believe I saw a just the game screen option too for max screen fun times, what's more you can save anywhere you want now too with what I'll basically just call a save state menu dood.The next two games barely really used the touch screen bar for one mode for portrait of ruin but you can use the right analogue stick or I assume your mouse if you use keyboard to use as your stylus as you would have on the DS with three varying speeds based on clicking in either one of the sticks dood.And that's it really, played through all three games, no issues at all and they are just as fun as I remembered! Hopefully the review helps you decide on a purchase or not and if ya do I hope you enjoy the games a whole bunch! Thanks for reading dood. ^-^

_childDocuments_.review: The Castlevania Dominus Collection is exactly what I was hoping the previous Advance Collection was and more. All of the games in the DS Trilogy are nothing short of excellent and the new inclusions are a great addition to what I consider to be the best Castlevania collection on offer so far. As always, I will provide brief individual reviews of each game, but the TLDR is that they're all good anyway.As a sequel to one of my favorite games of all time, Castlevania: Dawn of Sorrow is a great followup that in some ways surpasses, but also fails at exceeding its predecessor. The biggest point of contention was the infamous magic seal mechanic where you had to draw symbols on the DS touch screen in order to kill a boss for good, otherwise they regain some of their health and you have to try again. The Dominus Collection changes this so you have to input buttons for each point of the seal, which while I'd prefer magic seals to be removed in their entirety, is a genuine improvement. I was also never a fan of the weapon synthesis system as most souls are hard to come by, but after several playthroughs I've learned to get by with what I find. DoS knocks it out of the park with its graphic and music, with the soundtrack being one of my favorites from the franchise. While not my favorite entry, I have a lot of respect for what DoS accomplished and how its mechanics carried over to later games. 8.5/10.If Symphony of the Night and Aria of Sorrow didn't exist, Castlevania: Portrait of Ruin would be my favorite game in the franchise. It's a game I always enjoy replaying because of how fluid the combat is as well as the unique premise. I've always loved Jonathan and Charlotte as the two leads and how you can swap between them in combat as well as use them for assists. I never bother with the quests unless I'm going for 100%, but the rewards are definitely worthwhile with new weapons and martial arts. The design of the castle has seen a downgrade after DoS, but the Mario 64-esque paintings lead to some of the most varied locations in the series, from the pyramids of Egypt to a nightmare clown world. The presentation is about on par with DoS so nothing's really changed there. PoR also has the best final boss in the franchise with the Dracula/Death teamup which is a great way to end an amazing game.  If I'm in the mood to play a DS Castlevania game, chances are I'm picking PoR without a second thought. 9.5/10, only negative is the Stella Loretta fight for the best ending.Castlevania: Order of Ecclesia was a game that eluded me for the longest time until earlier this year. Having only 2 playthroughs and an Albus mode run under my belt, I wish I played this game sooner. The segmented world and stamina mechanic are interesting additions to the Metroidvania formula that I'm surprised almost no other game in the genre expanded upon these ideas. While difficult, OoE never borders on being unfair and always encourages you to experiment with different glyphs to gain the upper hand. I think the maps themselves are fairly lacking especially in Dracula's castle since most rooms in an area are repeated more times than I can count, but like PoR, the combat helps subdue the otherwise bare layout. The presentation once again is top notch, but this should come as no surprise by this point. Overall I enjoyed my time with OoE even if it did hand me my ass on a silver platter every now and then. 9/10, only sour points were the crab, sand fish, and Eligor boss fights.As per tradition, the collection contains one classicvania as a bonus, this time being Haunted Castle originally released for the arcades. However, M2 Studios went the extra mile and gave us a remake on top of the original game. I spent more time on the remake as it is the newest Castlevania game we've gotten in a long time, and it did not disappoint. It doesn't do anything new with the formula, but it is a fun, if short adventure lasting about half an hour. The graphics and music as expected have been given a great makeover, with the soundtrack having the best official version of Bloody Tears I've heard. The original game is only here for novelty's sake and worth a look if you're curious, but don't subject yourself to it longer than you should. The remake gets an 8/10, and the original gets a 3/10. This really makes me wish they gave us a Dracula X remake for the Advance Collection, but as is I'm incredibly grateful for this remake. Aside from some retransaltion issues in some of the games's text, the Dominus Collection is the perfect way to experience the amazing DS trilogy and well worth its full asking price. Aside from the original Haunted Castle which is already irrelevant by its included remake, there is not a single game here I'd consider bad. If you've never played a Castlevania game or are just looking for a good time, you won't find many better options.

_childDocuments_.review: I've noticed very minor stability problems with this release, otherwise, it's the perfect release of these games, exactly as they played on DS, but with both info screens at once.These versions also have new speedrunning tech because things that crashed the DS version don't here, because the emulator appears to be more stable than real DS hardware.The brand new Classicvania is a huge plus. I personally liked the Advance collection for it's polish, and this is about as polished. Just, this game crashes if fullscreening before getting past the title screen, which can only be done via Alt+Enter, and I've had a very small number of in-game crashes throughout my playthrough, 3 or so.As for the games themselves, they're my personal favorites of IGA's Castlevania games, especially Portrait of Ruin. I've played them all many times, and replay them every few years, similar to how I also habitually replay Kingdom Hearts 2 Final Mix and the Battle Network games, where they're just timeless games I keep coming back to. Not to say I don't revisit the GBA games and Bloodstained every few years too, but the DS games and SotN are my most frequent IGAVanias, and metroidvanias as a whole, that I revisit.EDIT: Apparently this game is a hybrid of ROMs and a true port, which explains how some details actually work. The ROM is used for assets, but the game code itself appears to be ported. Some dataminers have been looking into this, someone tipped me off on my profile, credit to Afevis Solmunko, I did at least look it up before writing this.

_childDocuments_.review: A very good collection of games, the highest standard actually. Besides perfectly emulated all 3 DS games, the collection allows for save states, rewind, in-game compendiums of information, all tucked into a pleasing UI. _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: I am going to be honest and say that I am not the biggest fan of the direction that post-SOTN castlevania games in general took with focus being shifted to search action (metroidvania) games but I love most of the major classic castlevania games right from Castlevania 1 to adventure rebirth with my favourite being Castlevania X68k in sharp X68000 (and not the chronicles demake to be precise). Although this collection features 5 games in total (DoS, PoR, OoE, Haunted castle and its remake), I bought it because I was interested in haunted castle revisited and maybe to replay hard mode of Ecclesia if I get the time since it is the closest the DSvanias get to classic castlevanias. Do I still find this collection worth the asking price? Hell yea, let me explain why.this is hands down THE highest effort Konami has placed in porting its games and blows their previous collections out of the water in terms of sheer features and improvements such as a variety of screen layouts, a great UI with save states and rewinding features, proper HD intro videos, several fold faster loading times, along with access to soundtracks and never before seen artwork which most devs would have gated behind a digital deluxe edition. M2 is the developer who Konami commissioned to get this done and it is safe to say that M2's god tier track record stands unblemished with this amazing collection. Even if I personally don't enjoy most of the games in this collection, this was worth it in principle alone as a lifetime castlevania fan, hoping that we could someday perhaps see SoTN, Rondo of blood and Harmony of Despair ported to PC, if not a new castlevania game, with just as much as effort, care and love. the upcoming portion of the review focuses solely on haunted castle revisited which is included in this collection: Haunted castle revisited is a proper and great remake of Haunted castle which was infamous for being ruthless especially the US arcade version. It is a highly significant inclusion for the fans of the franchise as it is the first new classic castlevania game in about 15 YEARS. I believe that HC revisited is made in the same engine as adventure rebirth (which was also made by M2 and I would be referring to the game as A:R from now) but it is much better than A:R in my opinion. A:R had more emphasis on traps and platforming while not focusing enough on combat and bosses but HC revisited just has the perfect balance between the two and is by far the better of two. the new track remixes are great especially Lullaby sent to the devil, the boss battles are in every way an improvement, the boss roster is pretty good too compared to A:R. the branching paths of A:R are done away with but that it is to be expected since the scope of Haunted castle is much smaller. As I have already said, HC revisited is a PROPER remake which means that they remade a mediocre game into an actually good game unlike the remake trend which is ubiquitous in the current gaming industry where games which are already good are being remade for no other reason but to cash in on nostalgia.Overall, I am glad to support Konami after all these years if they are making a clear effort like this to deliver products with that good ol' Konami seal of quality which was the norm back in the 90's and early 2000's. I am cautiously optimistic after this collection but let's see if this trend continues.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Dominus Collection is a compilation containing three Metroidvania-style games in the Castlevania series from Nintendo DS, along with the arcade action-platformer Haunted Castle and a brand new remake of that game, Haunted Castle Revisited. The original Haunted Castle is clunky and dated, but everything else here ranges from good to outstanding. This collection does a decent job with the dual-screen and touchscreen elements of the original games, and adds a bunch of features and bonus content, overall making for a great package that’s a must-have for any fans of Metroidvania titles and the Castlevania games specifically.PROS:✓ Haunted Castle remake alongside the well-transferred original just adds to the quality here✓ Compelling extra features and settings✓ Wonderful collection of bonus illustrations, music, and manuals✓ Three exceptional NDS games beautifully presented✓ Loads of content to get through✓ Glorious exploration and level layouts✓ Implementation of UI layout works well✓ Another great ports from M2✓ The soundtrack which was already great, now sounds even better as that grainy, noisy sound typical of games on the DS was removedCONS:- Solution to touch screen sections feels clunky, yet serviceable - The original Haunted Castle is still as unfair and insane as ever- Luck stat in Dawn of Sorrow is still busted- Order of Ecclesia has very boring level design- No single screen option in display modes- No display of the entire map in the Dawn of Sorrow menu as in other titles
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Castlevania is really a remarkable series in that there just aren't that many games that aren't someone's favorite. It's kind of disgusting how much amazing art, music, and game design this series lays claim to. I was there for the first game as a rental on my old NES and my first purchased title was Castlevania 3. Most of us hated Castlevania 2 back then, it's really MUCH better with a full internet guide at your side. Super Castlevania was a blast, but my college days were dominated by the classic Symphony of the Night, which I played so often that the game is etched on my soul. I thought that it couldn't get better, but I have to admit that there was just something about the generation of games that this collection represents that is special. Maybe it was because they were giving us cool twists on the lore with our boy Soma stepping in as a MC or the amazing duo of Jonathan and Charlotte being so anime that we couldn't help but root for them. Finally we got the gorgeous Order of Ecclesia which basically leads us right up to modern day Castlevania (which is called Bloodstained now, btw).This is a must own collection if you love Metroidvanias and really almost anyone can enjoy these games. Sure, you can be a nerd and get 100% and do all the extra modes, but the game are very forgiving to even novice players and you can play them while watching Youtube or Netflix without much issue (although you should do yourself a favor and listen to each tune at least once).

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I am very happy to have this collection on steam.Regarding the emulation, it was pretty good. I just wish they included better achievements, like collecting all souls, all glyphs, etc.Now when it comes to the games, well, I have played all of them on the DS ages ago. Those are some of my favorite games, especially Dawn of Sorrow, which is my favorite Castlevania game. My impressions after beating all of them:Dawn of Sorrow: It's really amazing. I love the soul system. It has one of my thematically favorite areas in any Castlevania game , but also one of the worst (. The combat is fun, the story is decent (I mean, Castlevania games are not really known for complex stories, but this one has a couple of twists), grinding souls is fun, experimenting with souls is fun (especially if you get ). It took me around 9 hours to collect all souls and then beat the game (but the game is super short if you just go for the ending ).Portrait of the Ruin: It is my least favorite between the three. It has a nice concept of two protagonists, but I really dislike how they split the game in stages. That alone is not terribly bad, but I think the stages lack creativity. Since they are portraits, they could have used that as a way to create very exotic places, that wouldn't realistically be in another Castlevania game, and also, as a way to create unnatural words. Well, they actually did those, but only one of each. The first example was the  stage, and the second example is  . The other  stages don't fall too far from what you would expect from any other Castlevania games. And to make it worse, in the end, . Again, that is a missed opportunity, as we could have had stages in the moon, in a dream world, in the Jurassic times, whatever they wanted. If there was one game where they could have been creative, was this one. I think that was a missed opportunity. Another problem I have with this game is how easy it is to exploit damage without even trying. For example, in Dawn of Sorrow, you have an early game exploit , but you must be lucky to find it, or you must know about it beforehand. In this game, your first spell is already super powerful and can carry you literally to the end of the game. One of the first special attacks you get  is ridiculously OP, and destroy a bunch of bosses, mostly all of the bosses where you can get . I have no problem with damage exploits, I just wish they were a bit hidden. The story of this one is the worst of the 3... it's actually kind bad lol, especially when we find out that . It took me around 4 hours to beat, but I didn't do much side content.Order of Ecclesia: This game gave me nightmares when I was a kid. It was sooooo hard. I remember having lots of problem trying to beat , and I still had problems with that now. This game also uses a stage selection format, and even though some stages are very similar between them, I think it was done so much better than Portrait of Ruin. They made sense in the context of the game at the same time that they were diverse and interesting. Also, I remember how my mind was blown when I  and thought the game was basically over, but no, now ! When I was a kid I thought it was a genius idea. I am not a kid anymore and I still think it's a genius idea. The combat in the game is super fun and somehow different from the other games. I think it's very fluid and I like it a lot. When it comes to the story, it's definitely the best one of them, and it took me around 8 hours to beat, although I did grind a bit for a few specific glyphs.Now I hope Konami finally releases Symphony of the Night :)

_childDocuments_.review: While not as perfect collection, 2 of the 3 DS titles are among some of the best 2D Castlevania games in existence. Talking about Order of Ecclesia and Portrait of Ruin. Dawn of Souls is still a good play though all things considered. There's also Haunted Castle which was previously released in the Konami Arcade Classics Anniversary Collection, which was an odd one considering the other games in that collection were all shoot 'em ups. Haunted Castle definitely feels more at home here. and what's more they even did a full blow remake of the title with some QOL improvements like better difficulty balancing for starters. Haunted Castle and it's remake are the only 2 classicvania titles in the bunch, with the other 3 games being full blown metroidvania titles which are styled after Symphony of the Night. this means they have a less linear approach to progression with the environments offering many branching paths. As well as offering RPG progression, inventory systems and several types of powerups that are necessary for navigation through the big maps. Each game also offers it's own unique style of gameplay, like the glyph system for Order of Ecclasia, or the dual character control of Portrait of Ruin for example. Dawn of Sorrow also makes more use of the "touch screen" controls than the other 2, which can be done with the right analog stick if playing with a controller. If you own a steam deck or any other type of touch screen device you can also just use the screen to do this.Speaking of screens, these games were originally on the Nintendo DS, and much like ports such as Etrian Odyssey for example, or some of the games from the Mega Man Zero/ZX collection  you will play these games with multiple windows. In this case you have a main gameplay window and 2 smaller windows which show the map and also a status screen. You can also orient these windows in one of several ways to fit whatever style you want. And despite having a smaller main window, it still looks perfectly fine on the Steam Deck. This being a collection you will also be treated to some extras such as a gallery that features tons of artwork and manuals in different languages for the various games, plus soundtracks to listen to for everything included. There's also English and Japanese versions for the 3 main DS titles, plus some other languages where applicable. On top of that you have a handy rewind feature for those times you might make a mistake and the ability to save at any time you want without the need to find save rooms. Konami shadow dropping this was a pleasant surprise. I'm sure a lot of Castlevania fans were dying for ports of these games, and I am on of them. Here's to hoping Konami follows up with the rest of the 2D titles. I'm looking at you Symphony of the Night and Rondo of Blood.

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished as a kid the original games gathered in the Dominus Collection, which are some of the very best Castlevania games, I decided to buy them again to not only support more Castlevania games being released on Steam but also due to the extreme quality of the whole port, the quality of life changes made, the individual art galleries and the higher resolution opening cinematics. Congratulations to M2.Considering its price, I would highly recommend not missing out on these games (especially Order of Ecclesia) and prompting Konami to release on Steam the following Castlevania games with, at least, the exact same quality of this port:-Harmony Of Despair (Very fun 4 players co-op Castlevania with a lot of characters)-Rondo Of Blood (Classicvania featuring Richter; not the Dracula X version, please)-Symphony Of The Night (Metroidvania with Alucard as protag)Thanks for taking the time to read my review! _childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: If you haven't played the games collected here, then do yourself a favor and experience some of the highest tiers the genre has ever offered. Every game in the collection is a wonderful masterpiece and now they're in a format that is better than ever. High res renders of polygons and the animated cutscenes, controls that are customizable, all regional versions of each game and an arcade (along with a remake of it from the legendary 2D game dev M2 to boot!). Konami does a lot wrong, but let it be known, this is a very strong step in the right direction. Emulating literally isn't as high quality as this collection for a few reasons even like the high res bits I mentioned, plus having BOTH pause screens on screen plus the game itself at all times! That along with the removal of some (honestly bad) touch screen elements that were in the originals makes for a collection that actually gives people who care about these games a reason to BUY this and not just pirate it. I don't say this very often, but you did good, Konami. I'm damn happy.

_childDocuments_.review: These are some of my favorite Castlevania games of all time and the fact that they surprise released all three of them should be applauded. There are some issues with slowdown if you're not running the right monitor or don't have reliable VRR, but after getting a new monitor it's not longer an issue for me. However, if you don't have VRR or a 60+hz monitor, you may encounter issues with extreme slowdown. Besides that very big issue (may have been patched out since I original wrote my review, I don't know), these are still fantastic games and an incredible value since these on Nintendo DS would cost hundreds of dollars if you were to find them now. Play these if you haven't and enjoy hours of weapon and soul harvesting.

_childDocuments_.review: is not only a collection of three great CV games, it's also the definitive way to play them.I played through most of  with a keyboard and mouse, which had a serviceable (if a little clumsy) control scheme. You can use the mouse to perform all the functions formerly reserved for the Nintendo DS stylus; on a Steam Deck, you can use the touchscreen to draw runes and chip ice blocks, with the benefit of having a much larger screen. This is definitely my preferred way to play.The extra screen space on your 16:9 monitor is taken up by the "second screen", displaying your stats and the bestiary entry for the monsters you're fighting. I much prefer this over pillarboxed borders, I almost wish I could play Symphony of the Night like this!The games themselves are excellent. After beating Dawn of Sorrow, I immediately replayed it in Julius mode. They scratch an itch that few modern metroidvanias can, which is why so many fans begged Konami for this collection. It was worth the wait, I can't recommend this one enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: Really good re-release of classic Castlevania titles that until now have been locked on the Nintendo DS family of handhelds. I played tested this in three ways - on my Steamdeck, on my desktop with both an Xbox controller, a generic controller (specifically a PlayStation Classic controller), and on my Windows laptop, playing on a keyboard. All 3 games worked and controlled well on all the devices and controllers I tried. It retains the same quality and additional QoL features as the previous compilations - e.g. the Rewind and Save features, choice between Japanese (and Korean where available), US, European versions of the games, artwork, music player, now coupled with a serviceable implementation of touchscreen controls - basically you can use the analogue sticks or mouse if you are playing on a PC with a controller or keyboard, and buttons for stuff like the charting seals in Dawn of Sorrow, where touchscreen controls were most extensively used, and it mostly works. It is also (almost) perfect on a Steamdeck, as you can actually use the touchscreen as you would on real hardware. Also, please, KONAMI/Level 5, if you are reading the reviews, add the option to have the main screen aligned to the right, which would make it easier to use the touchscreen on the Steam Deck while still controlling the movement, like on a real DS.  You have several options of how you want to divide the screens (these being ports of DS titles, you do have additional information being displayed on what on a real DS would have been the bottom screen), with several layouts to choose from. I wish there were some more visual options, and there's some weird flicker of certain background elements that can be mildly distracting. I am not sure if it was present on the original hardware, with its small screen, but it's not a big issue. I would, however, like to see some options with regards to screen filters to make it look a bit less sharp, like on a real DS LCD.I haven't yet had time to put extensive time in any of the games, but I have tested all of them, and all of them work very nicely indeed. If you enjoy Metroidvania titles but haven't played these because you don't own a DS or don't want to set up an emulator, get it. If you are a Castlevania fan missed these titles and want to experience them again on a large screen, get it. If you, like, have played these games ad nauseam back in the day and want to experience them again without (mostly) touchscreen controls, get it. Unlike with the GBA and older titles that have been re-released before, the only other way to properly enjoy these games is  either with original hardware or through the use of fan-made conversions and emulators. This is much simpler, cleaner, more content-complete, and, in my opinion, enjoyable way to play these games.
_childDocuments_.name: Castlevania Dominus Collection

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great collection of some of the best DS games.  Portrait of Ruin is one of Koji Igarashi's best works if you can get past the uncharacteristically generic anime illustrations.  Order of Ecclesia has some of the best story and best boss fights in the series.  Dawn of Sorrow was cursed with launch-window tech-demo gimmicks at the time, but this version patches over them.  I emulated all 3 games earlier this year, and the versions included in this collection seem to run smoother.  Also, this version displays both supplemental screens at once, so you don't have to flip between the map and the enemy status screen.  Haunted Castle Revisited is included as a bonus game.  The original Haunted Castle is a janky and unbalanced mess- either memorize the exact location of spawns you can't react to, or spam credits to cheat out a victory.  The Revisited version improves the controls, adds some more meat to the boss fights, and overall makes the game conducive to an actual casual playthrough.  It only takes about 30 minutes, but it's a fun bonus. Oh.  The original Haunted Castle is also included if you want to see just why this game was too ass to release anywhere else.  There's a reason it was never up there with the other Classicvanias.  My main gripe is that there are romhacks that categorically improve the DS trilogy that could've EASILY been made official.  I would've liked an option to swap out the generic anime portraits with Ayami Kojima's art.  YOU HAVE IT RIGHT THERE IN THE GALLERY.   I also would've liked to see the drop rates buffed in Dawn and Ecclesia.  Finally, you should be able to break ice blocks by attacking instead of the touch screen with the Balore soul.EDIT:  PSA, One of the trophies is bugged.  The trophy for defeating Death in Portrait of Ruin doesn't trigger if you skip the cutscene after defeating him.  The trophy doesn't pop when you beat him, it pops when you see the aftermath.

Any Castlevania fan owes it to themselves to play these games.  This port was done right with extra QOL features and Steam achievements.

_childDocuments_.review: no filters or blur effects are included in this game so we are stretching the small 256x192 nintendo ds resolution onto screens several times bigger in resolution thus everything is looking overpixelated and blown up out of proportion. use reshade with crtfrutbun with curvature toggled off, scanlines toggled off, and blur strength somewhere in the ballpark of .50-.70. i am running .55. use frutbun and lcd grid combined and adjust the screen height in lcd grid to 720 and the height to 480 and increase those numbers if game text is not readable. you will have to figure out how to add lcd-grid.fx to your shaders pack. its easy just install the game and then reshade. add the lcd-grid.fx to the shaders folder and it will show up on start of game in the list when you press the home key. doing this gets the resolution closer to how i remember it on my og ds phat from back in the day. for reference, my monitor is a 1440p gigabyte 165hz gaming monitor. good luck to those trying to make the game look decent. it is possible.edit: oh yeah, the frutbun and other crt shaders can be found when choosing the retroarch shader pack during initial install of reshade. sorry, forgot to mention that.
