detailed_description: Digital Deluxe Edition About the Game DELUXE EDITION INCLUDES: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name Legendary Fighter Pack Floating in the bay, away from the prying eyes of the public, is a mysterious container ship known as the Castle. At its center lies the Coliseum, and three legendary yakuza have entered the battle arena as playable characters. Enter the Coliseum and play as or alongside: Goro Majima – The Mad Dog of Shimano Taiga Saejima – The Slayer of Eighteen Daigo Dojima – 6th Chairman of the Tojo Clan Claim victory with these allies in the ultimate showdown! ERASE YOUR PAST TO PROTECT YOUR FUTURE Once a legendary yakuza, Kazuma Kiryu faked his own death and abandoned his name for the sake of protecting his family. Now, he is thrust into conflict by a mysterious figure attempting to drive him out of hiding. Under the codename “Joryu,” Kiryu embarks on a gripping action narrative with bone-shattering combat in vibrant locations filled with exciting characters and activities. ULTIMATE COMBAT WITH TWO HIGH-IMPACT FIGHTING STYLES Dynamically switch between the Yakuza and Agent fighting styles in visceral melee combat. With the Yakuza style, strike fear into enemies by unleashing wildly aggressive moves powered by Kiryu’s unparalleled strength and flair. Or up the ante with the Agent style by delivering blows with absolute speed and precision, while using an array of high-tech gadgets like electrified bind wires to stun enemies then send them flying. Strategically adapt to the situation and leverage both styles to dominate and destroy hordes of enemies. ENDLESS ENTERTAINMENT Whether you're brawling in the secret Battle arena, singing a new karaoke song, enjoying a drink at the live-action cabaret club, or racing in the pocket circuit, the world offers a variety of immersive experiences. An intriguing informant named Akame also provides thrilling sub-missions, drawing you into an epic showdown that unfolds the more you explore and enjoy Sotenbori and Yokohama. LIKE A DRAGON: INFINITE WEALTH SPECIAL TRIAL VERSION ALSO INCLUDED! After completing Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name game, a Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth Special Trial Version will be unlocked for you to enjoy! This game may be updated over time and have paid for and free additional content released for it. Please be aware that this may increase the minimum requirements for running the game above the specification stated here English voice will be implemented in a post-launch patch distribution

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay is good, seems to be an alternate take on the Dragon Engine compared to Lost Judgement if I remember correctly. Lost Judgement had faster style switching and more ways to juggle enemies around while Gaiden has slower style switching but there are more ways to quickly K/O enemies, such as holding normal to use Kiryu's old Beast style attacks or the gadgets. _childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is by far the shortest game in the Like a Dragon series so far, and it only took me just under 14 hours to beat it while going for quite a bit of the side content along the way. However, make no mistake, this is probably one of the best games in the series to date, with solid combat, story, and setting.The combat is by far the most fluid and fun in the series to date, beating out Lost Judgment as it takes all the strengths from that game and combines it with new and interesting mechanics to make it more interesting. Kiryu has 2 styles, Agent and Yakuza. Yakuza is very similar to Kiryu's Dragon of Dojima style from 1-6, with a few extra moves added in, but the Agent style is completely different, with 4 different gadgets to use during combat, and a moveset that is more suited to dealing with large groups of enemies.The story, without spoiling too much, perfectly bridges the gap between the end of Yakuza 6 and the end of Yakuza: Like a Dragon, showcasing Kiryu's perspective during that time. It also gives you extra info about what some characters (I won't say who) from a previous game are up to in the present. The game itself is set in Sotenbori (with a brief section in Isezaki Ijincho towards the beginning of the game) now expanded to include the park which was noticeably absent in previous iterations of Sotenbori in the Dragon Engine. It may seem like a small change but it really makes Sotenbori feel a lot bigger and more lively with a wider variety of places to visit.Finally, there's the part I was most excited for before this game released, which is the trial of Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth included after beating the main story. I haven't played much of it so far but it's an amazing reward which offers a sneak peek into what the next game will be like.Overall, if you enjoyed Yakuza 6 or Yakuza: Like a Dragon, I'd definitely recommend purchasing this game, as there is so much that's offered in addition to a preview of the next game in the series before it's released.

_childDocuments_.review: Another AWESOME Yakuza game. While the RPG formula and slower pace of the now mainstay series grew on me to the point I prefer it, it was nice to get this on the side. An old-school, simpler game, with an interesting story, where you again run around and beat a lot of people up. Sure, the game is much shorter and smaller in scope, there's no XP, no working vending machines, no elaborate sub-stories or mini-games (though the "homeless HQ" half of the story attempts to make up for it), but the game plays great, looks great, and the story is captivating and characters interesting. In some ways, it feels like an elaborate Yakuza 6 DLC in a super-modern engine with all the bells and whistles, with simplified mechanics, but a cool and unique alternate fighting style. It also answers a lot of interesting and previously mysterious questions. Overall, I'm having as much fun playing this as I did playing Yakuza 6. It's not quite Y0 or LAD, but it's still an amazing game I wouldn't hesitate to recommend to anyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name

_childDocuments_.review: It's streamlined Yakuza which isn't a bad thing since not every game has to be 100 hours long. A lot shorter than the full blown Yakuza games but a good storyline that fills in some blanks with one of the best protags in gaming history, Kazuma Kiryu. The game does have a stripped down open world with some of the usual sidequests/games you find in Yakuza games (no baseball though, surprisingly).

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having a rather short main story, about 10 hours long, this game packs everything a Yakuza fan could ask for: good story, amazing gameplay, sick boss fights, and of course it ain't a Yakuza game without the outrageously hilarious and random substories, and hundred thousand mini games.The game takes place in Sotenbori and on a ship called The Castle, a lavish entertainment center, explaining what Kiryu was doing after  in Y6 and how  The game contains some heavy spoilers from previous titles, hence if you are new to Yakuza series, perhaps you shouldn't start with this game.As everyone know, the biggest introduction to the game was Kiryu's new fighting style and the new gadgets. I'm glad RGG brought back style switching mechanism. Besides the Judgment games, Y0 and Kiwami had the best fighting simply because they had the style switching mechanism. This game offers not only a new move set and animations, you get to use high-tech gadgets that are best suited for dealing with multiple enemies -needn't to mention they are also super fun. Who would've thought tossing people around with a literal Spiderman webshooter and blowing them up with explosive cigarettes would be this much fun? It's a shame that we will not have them in IW or future games.Things that are different from the previous titles: If i remember correctly, this is the first game that require money to level up. You need money as well as Akame points to upgrade your abilities. But needn't worry because the Coliseum arena fights as well as the thugs in the streets give fair amount of money for you to spend on bentos and boozes. All the substories are available through Akame instead of randomly running into fake Kiryu or Majima dressed as a cop in the streets. And it only has 26 substories total which is super low compared to the previous titles e.g. Y0 had 100.You can customize Kiryu's outfit FINALLY. There are plenty of outfits as well as make ups for both outside activity and coliseum fights for Kiryu to wear.Simply a masterpiece. Can't wait for Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth.

_childDocuments_.review: A very enjoyable title from the RGG/Yakuza series, it of course revolves around Kiryu living a 2nd life as per agreement at the end of Yakuza 6, this is a nice tie in with the next Ichiban game as it happens during the first one, which leads to them both in the next title.This game is what you expect from a Yakuza game, however be warned this is shorter than the other titles, some things are missing, however the Racing game is back. Which will take a bit of time to farm the extras for your track car to be up to snuff for the top tier races.The graphics are up to date, the engine is performs extremely well, some nice reflection effects show in game. This will add to your enjoyment of the title. I won't go into the story much as people want to enjoy that without spoilers.The install size is large, I wish they would have offered the Infinite Wealth demo as a DLC to cut the majority of the download, but at least you can test out the next Ichiban game before buying.Overall 8.5/10 - again I just wish there was more to do in the game, more side quests or mini-games would have been good, the full motion video hostess club probably added more giggage to the install size too, and to be honest it was a bit weird to have that after years of rendered girls, but still enjoyable.I would wait until the price comes down, because that is where the 1.5 score lost comes from, the price for the content you got is a bit steep.

_childDocuments_.review: I ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ LOVE THIS GAME TW///SPOILERS(?)about it hooks me, really hooks me. The way the story flows is just so good, there are no crazy plot twists like in other Yakuza games that are too much. There are plot twists in this game, but compared to the other Yakuza games, it feels so different—it just feels right. It makes sense, and I love it so much.Now, I want to talk about the combat that I yearn for. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, man! After playing Yakuza: Like a Dragon, I reinstalled Yakuza 0 just to fight, just to feel that combat. That's how much I miss it. To be honest, when I bought this game, I expected it to be turn-based like Yakuza: Like a Dragon, but to my surprise, it's not. And my heart is filled with joy. Let me tell you how nice the combat feels in this game—it's amazing. It's not clunky like in some Yakuza games; it is smooth. I love it!Most importantly, Kiryu's character development. Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ dude. This game puts me at the edge of my seat sometimes with the cutscenes because of Kiryu. I like the idea of Kiryu changing his name to Joryu and that he doesn't know who Kiryu is, and he's like a secret agent and stuff. But in some scenes, Kiryu plays his new character too well, and it makes me want to scream so much. There are some scenes that would make more sense if there's Kiryu and not this Joryu guy. And I see the development with Kiryu slowly realizing that if you're once Yakuza, you're always Yakuza, and that ♥♥♥♥ is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome. So awesome that I cried so much watching the ending.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is the perfect, most service to die-hard fans RGG studios have made to date! I don't write reviews on Steam that often, but this game I simply had to write a review for no questions about it. As someone who's played all the Yakuza titles, starting with Yakuza 7 Like a dragon, then 0-6, and with the Judgment games, I absolutely felt so emmersed and invested into the game at the very start to the very last moments. When I've seen the trailers for LAD Gaiden and seeing it's gameplay, features, new additions along with us figuring out where Kiryu went after the ending of 6, it was one of those games that I simply HAD to pre order and play on day one! And I'm so happy I did. (WARNING: SLIGHT SPOILERS TO PREVIOUS GAMES BUT KEPT TO A MINIMUM, NO REAL SPOILERS TO THE STORY)For those wondering, LAD Gaiden takes place after the story of Yakuza 6, and during the events of Yakuza 7 Like a Dragon, where we figure out and follow the story as to where Kiryu went and disappeared to after the events of 6, and how he ended up in 7 Like a Dragon. 3 Years after the Y6 you understand quick and clear why Kiryu did what he had to do to keep his loved ones safe and erase his name. His challenges and trials during the game to keeping his situation a secret as he's supposed to be a dead man. Only for him to realize Yakuza guys can't take a hint or keep a secret.The story as always is heaven sent, with clear and very concise understand everything without having to go back. It sucks you in just like every single game they've made for Yakuza. The boss battles and long battles are always a joy to get into, and you feel like a kid in a candy shop just from doing the wacky side quests. And upgrading Kiryu with his Agent and his Legendary Yakuza style was a pure joy grinding for and then taking it into battle with some hooligans on the streets. There is only 5 chapters but of course there is no sense of this game feeling short at all. There is plenty to do, as long as you are not in a point of a story where you can't go out and explore. They will make that clear, but you can really take your time with the game without feeling like you have to prioritize anything. Here's just a taste of what you can do.*Pocket Circuit Racing (Yes it's back for our 50 year old Kiryu XD)*Fight in The Castle Coliseum (Yes it returns and it's so easy to make money for upgrades)*Karaoke (Real fan service here with references to the past Yakuza titles)*Akame Requests (which is reskinned wacky side quests but the wackiness and humor is still here. With a TON of references and special guest appearances from past games and even from Judgment.)*Buy Clothes for Kiryu (Coliseum, Free Roam and Story)*Go to the Casinos*And of course give knuckle sandwiches to street punksI also wanted to speak a bit on the final chapter without spoiling anything. It was the perfect tie in and ultimate way to finish off the game with preparing for the Omi Alliance and Tojo Clan disbandment. Main reason why I love this so much is because I got to see Ichiban and his friends there, and (in a way) seeing them fighting side by side protecting Watase and Daigo. I was totally fanboying from start to finish, from the moment the camera pans into the room before his speech just seeking and looking for Ichiban like it's Where's Waldo, to seeing Kiryu come in with that punch and remove his glasses to Ichiban, Maejima and Saejima. Seeing this through Kiryu's perspective and seeing the dragon himself meet his successor and equal, along with that heart filling smirk Kiryu gives to Ichiban when he saw him reveal his dragonfish back tattoo really helped make this game for me. And to end it all off with a epic long battle with the Yakuza legends, and then to finish off, a boss battle to end the game that will have you remember the events and villain of Yakuza 5. Just a big chef kiss.And of course, Kiryu's breakdown and him crying at the closing moments of the game was enough to bring me to tears just like everyone else. We all want Kiryu to be happy and he deserves it and the world 10x over for his heart of gold and influence on others. I'm hoping there will be some closure and happy ending to his story, but I'm already looking forward to Infinite Wealth so much.In conclusion, RGG has made yet another 10/10 classic for the Yakuza franchise. THIS, is what gaming is about, and what AAA gaming should be. No bugs, god sent story, ultimate fan service, never ending action, fun and remarkable gameplay, and no micro transactions or nickle and diming fan-bases. From the bottom of my heart, thank you RGG. You guys deserve the whole world and more for making incredible games. I pre ordered this game from you guys, took a day off work just to play it, ordered pizza and I didn't regret it not one bit. I'm already putting down my pre-order for Like a Dragon Infinite Wealth and it's going to be probably the best birthday gift (or in my case belated Birthday gift since my bday is on the 22nd of January) I will ever receive. I'm looking forward to seeing Ichiban and Kiryu side by side together against the evils they will face.Thank you for all the memories and heart gripping stories RGG! Never change!

_childDocuments_.review: So, getting this out of the way at the top, this game is probably not worth a 50 dollar asking price. Taking the game out of context, there is a lot of game here, but it has little to offer people who aren't already significantly invested in the series, and people who are already significantly invested in the series will find this a very paltry offering compared to RGG studios' normal offerings. Yakuza 0 costs 20 dollars right now and offers easily three times as much content. So, if you're not someone who already desperately wants to know what Kiryu was up to between the events of Yakuza 6 and Yakuza: Like a Dragon, or someone who just wants more Kiryu wherever you can get it, this is not a good investment.For invested fans of the series (which, despite some attempts to make the game accessible and interesting to anyone) Gaiden does offer a great and emotionally gratifying experience. The game is certainly short for a Yakuza/LaD title, as it was originally envisioned as a standalone DLC, and there's only a few notable additions to the formula, but what is there is solid, and the story is on point. The port is also well done, and performs great on my aging hardware while looking beautiful.In short, it's a game that will only appeal to fans of the franchise and might feel a little lacking to its target audience, but it delivers where it counts enough to be well worth fans picking up.

_childDocuments_.review: Relatively short for a Yakuza game (hence the Gaiden in the title); probably 1/3 the length of Yakuza 8 (also known as Yakuza: Like a Dragon). However, it's almost all killer, no filler. The ending sequence had me in tears. 10/10I liked the return to the traditional Yakuza combat; I didn't mind 8's turn-based combat as much as some die-hard fans but it was definitely a slog at times. It definitely fits the more standard Yakuza theme of "Kiryu keeps punching things until the world is as it should be" that this game has.My only complaint is that there is a specific fight that overlaps in this and 8 () that I would have love to have played from Kiryu's perspective, but that was just shown in flashback form at the end. I was really looking forward to it, and was bummed it wasn't there. Not a huge deal though, as the rest of the game is fantastic.One thing that I liked / disliked was the Akame requests system. I do like that it was really easy to find and complete all the substories without wandering around looking for the triggers or relying on a guide, but it also felt less "Yakuza-y", in that there wasn't an equivalent of, for example, randomly getting roped into a Michael Jackson music video. It certainly streamlined things though.All in all, it's a great game, and whets the appetite for Infinite Wealth without burning you out on the formula.

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to review this game without spoiling plot points in Yakuza 6 and Yakuza Like a Dragon so I'll just point out pros and cons so you can decide if you want to get this chapter of the saga or would rather watch it on a video.[PROS]- STORY: The story picks up where Yakuza 6 ended. I feel like many people might have had issues with the way the story ended, so this one tries to expand on what happened after the events of 6. And the story happens at the same time Yakuza Like a Dragon's plot happened, so if you played that one before you'll be able to piece together pieces and understand better the reason behind some of the plot points in that one too. And the quality is pretty good, without spoiling anything the ending had me fighting the tears off.- COMBAT: I've heard multiple opinions on the combat of this game, but as someone that has yet to play Judgement the combat in this game feels polished. Again, I jumped from the combat of 6 into this one and it feels so much more polished. Game has two styles: Agent - A style that is characterized for being ultra fast but low damage and Yakuza - Basically the style of 6 where you hit like a truck but attacks are way slower, leaving you open to getting hurt. So, if you liked the combat in 6, it's here. And if you wanted new combat you also get that and can easily switch mid-combat with the push of a button.- SIDE CONTENT: Lots of minigames to play. It doesn't really introduce a whole lot of new stuff, rather it brings those minigames that were more popular and polishes them, giving us sort of a "Best of" selection of things to do. Things like Pocket Racing, karaoke, coliseum battles, they all make a very strong comeback.[CONS]- STORY: This game is the shortest in the entire saga. And it's not an exageration, it's VERY short. I don't know how regional pricing might work for other countries, but right now this is the most expensive Yakuza game in all of Steam, so having a game that you can complete in around 35 hours (I took my sweet time to play it, tried all minigames, completed most of the side content, walked around the map instead of running and still finished it in 32 hours) for that price is one thing you might wanna keep in mind. The quality is there, RGG put out a fantastic product, but it's short.- COMBAT: While the combat is polished, the fact that the game is so short gives us a smaller list of heat actions and all of the abilities are gained with money rather than experience or training. Depending on how much you play the side content you might be super weak the entire game or super strong, there's no really in-between. And the game ends before you can get properly comfortable with your fighting style.- SIDE CONTENT: Again, the fact that the game is so short makes this part a gray area, while there are plenty of side activities and these are well done you don't really experience a whole lot before the game ends. The number of side stories in this game is surprisingly small, and now instead of getting them by walking around and helping the residents of the city, you are given side stories from a side-quest hub in your hideout which I don't know ... for me it sort of robs the charm these games have. You're not a good samaritan helping people anymore, you're an agent hired to do odd jobs. And I know it's only for this game but I can't not mention the tonal shift the game takes. Yakuza games are always a serious story with a side of silly. This game is very serious from beginning to end, couple of side stories are funny but overall the game mantains a very serious tone which might charm some and polarize others.[ACHIEVEMENTS]This must be the easiest game in the series to 100%. I've seen people do it in around 45 hours. The Completion List means nothing, you don't have to finish it on a high difficulty, and I'm pretty sure you can complete all the achievements in your first playthrough if you have the patience for it. Personally, it disappoints me a little, but I also understand how it can be due to the length of the game.[SUMMARY]Overall a very strong addition to the series. One that in a way was needed to tie up all of Kiryu's journey on a nice bow and send him for what might be his final adventure in Infinite Wealth. I'm very satisfied with the product I got, but if you think the price might be too much and want to wait for a discount that is a very valid option.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly floored by how much I enjoyed this game. It's a short one, well for a game in this series, only having a small handful of chapters and a fair bit of side content. The combat in this game is fun. The Agent Style adds quicker moves together with gadgets that are fun to use in certain fights when you've figured out how to control your opponents with them. The Yakuza style is probably the most fun Kiryu has been to play in a non RPG game in a good while. Overall the usage of these two styles together can make fights with enemies and bosses alike interesting if you use them in fun ways. A fair bit of the side content is related to The Coliseum which gives you your standard 1 V 1 fights of past games, vs groups of enemies and the new mode where you have a team you assembled face off against an enemy team. This mode is fun when figuring out how to best support your team to make sure they don't get eliminated whilst fighting everyone although leveling up said team mates does feel a bit tedious and time consuming unless you have a lot of money on hand already. That being said, when your team is the appropriate level it's a fun side mode to figure out how to handle battles. You can also play as the fighters you recruit although they have a limited moveset so Kiryu is usually who I stuck with.The story and music is some of the best the series has had. Almost all of these tracks are amazing and the composers of them went above and beyond! The story is genuinely something I did not expect to hook me as it is a side story that seems like lead up to Infinite Wealth but oh how I was wrong. This story goes from a small steady thing to one of the most engaging bits of story this series has ever had. I am honestly amazed with how they hooked me so good towards the end. This is a must play experience for fans of Kiryu's story. Beyond that this game has side activities you would expect from the series. Golf, mahjong, gambling, cabaret clubs, side stories, pocket circuit, locker keys, Master System games, arcade games, claw games, pool, shogi and darts. This is a game that is worth it for long time series fans and if you are new to the series start with Yakuza 0 or the first game on PS2, otherwise this game will probably not do as much for you.

_childDocuments_.review: 9,5/10 Wonderful game!I had so many questions when I played Yakuza: Like a Dragon. Like "What was Kiryu doing before chapter 12?", "Where was he?", "Is he okay?", etc.Most of my questions are solved with this game. It's a wonderful spin-off game that takes place after Yakuza 6 and during Yakuza 7. It also offers a preview of Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth (e.g. why the story takes place in Hawaii).The story is just as emotional as the last Yakuza games. The graphics look almost realistic. And I love the gameplay. Finally we get the good ol' beat 'em up game that almost feels like a Dynasty Warriors game. XDThe only thing I don't like about this game is that the game is too short compared to older Yakuza games. Only 5 chapters. You can play through the game in 10-12 hours. Therefore, I would advise you not to buy the game for the full price. It's only worth it if the game costs less than 20 euros. Unless you really want to experience the story of Kiryu and not watch it on YouTube. Then you can get it. Overall:To sum up, I can tell you that the game is very good. However, it feels like a DLC for Yakuza: Like a Dragon. You can also play the demo version of Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, which is also interesting. If you don't want to have the demo version on your PC because it takes up too much disk space (25 GB, iirc), you should delete the Runtime2 folder in the game's installation folder. I look forward to playing more of your older games. ^^

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe Gaiden is that it's a greatest-hits compilation celebrating Kiryu Kazuma, the Dragon of Dojima.While it's a rather short game, only comprising 5 chapters – it's a fun little jaunt that put you back into his shoes and reminds you just how great of a character Kiryu is. I personally think that this game respects Kiryu more than Y6, and truly has a sense of finality – which is funny given how Kiryu is present in the upcoming LAD: Infinite Wealth. Great callbacks, with Takaya Kuroda's incredible voice acting really showcasing just how much Kiryu has changed over the past 7 games.Combat-wise, it's not as great as Lost Judgment. I'd put it slightly above the first Judgment, but it's still fun to beat up random dudes. This game shines in it's side-content, where I've spent majority of my playtime doing. That's not something I usually do in a Yakuza title, as I greatly enjoy the story content more, but Gaiden incentivizes you greatly for checking off that list, and I couldn't help but continuously support the Akame Network.I'd rate it a solid 8/10. My only downside would be the humungous file size. I hope RGG puts out a patch to reduce the storage taken up by the Cabaret Club FMVs, and also consider making the LAD8 demo a separate download / DLC install. 98GB is too much space for a 15-30 hour bite-sized Like a Dragon game. _childDocuments_.review: I would like to begin by summarizing my history of the Yakuza franchise. Being a Yakuza fan, I enjoyed Yakuza 0 and thought Yakuza: Like A Dragon was a masterpiece. But I wasn't particularly fond of Yakuza 1-6. Among my reasons are dull gameplay, repetitive game and level design in every game, similar stories with ridiculous plot twists, boring main characters (excluding Akiyama), same map in each game etc. As you might have guessed, I've had issues with the repetitive nature of this series. I considered the Yakuza series the Call of Duty of the East, even though Yakuza is much better in almost every aspect. But Yakuza: Like a Dragon changed it all for me. Thankfully, the combat system had changed completely. It was extremely well made and we got a main character with actual feelings and one who displayed them. Ichiban is such a likable character and I enjoyed seeing him as the protagonist dearly. I completed Yakuza LaD 100% for the first time in a Yakuza game. That's how much I love the game.After all this positive work from Ryu Ga Gotoku Studios, I had high hopes about this game, so I pre-ordered it. I feel sorry to report that this is a game with the same formula as Yakuza 1-6 and I didn't enjoy most of it. A generic plot with characters that I am never going to remember after beating the game, predictable plot twists, and an undercooked villain. I mostly have no issues with the feel of the combat (except Yakuza 3) but this one feels kinda off. I cannot put my finger on it. One of the selling points of the game, the new "agent combat style" looks fun, but sadly is very weak compared to the "yakuza style", so I barely played the new style. They couldn't adjust the balance between them.Let me move on to the positives of Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name. The most important topic of the game: Yes, the cabaret club is very fun just like the previous ones. This one's slightly better because they made it live-action this time. Secondly, I can see that most of RGG's effort has gone into creating the castle. Yeah, the castle looks amazing and has cool stuff in it to spend time with. The graphics are getting better with every game. The interiors look extremely good, but the outdoor graphics need a little bit more work. I won't go into spoilers, but I just cannot skip that finale scene when Kiryu was holding a tablet. Phenomenal scene. It made me tear up! I hope it results in something beautiful for Kiryu in the next game. That sums up the positives of this game.Unfortunately, the best point of the game is the playable Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth Trial after you beat the main game. During that hour, I had an absolute blast and it's barely visible that LaD 8 is their focus and this is only a cash grab. Dear SEGA, I know the main reason you made this game was to please Kiryu and the Brawler fans out there, other than making an extra 50 bucks per purchase, of course. But please just let Kiryu and this dated combat system alone. Because it surely doesn't work anymore for me. People will get used to turn-based combat. Look at Baldur's Gate 3 for an example. Just keep doing amazing RPGs after Like a Dragon 8 as well. I am immensely excited about that game!Follow My

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is a decent addition to the series and offers an enjoyable even if a little short roller coaster ride of a story along with yet another iteration of the brawler style combat. As a long time fan of the series I had my fun with the game but at same time I couldn't help but to feel like I was playing through a glorified expansion sold at a premium and one where it might be a little difficult to justify the price tag unless you plan to do most of the side content as the main story is really short.Combat system is a fun iteration of the older brawler combat which is a welcome improvement after the somewhat lackluster combat of Kiwami 2 and Yakuza 6, although it isn't without its flaws and the more you level up the more those blemishes start to show especially in terms of balancing. In addition to the familiar fighting style of Kiryu game introduces a new agent style which focuses bit more on finesse, stylish counters and utilizes some rather hilarious spy gadgets that you unlock as you progress through the story.As expected of a Yakuza title there is a plethora of minigames and a chunk of side content, minigames could be described as a sort of "best of" collection of various things you've seen along the years with some new things sprinkled in here and there, side content on the other hand felt like bit of a letdown. Substories for the most part are rather generic and a far cry from some of the more whacky and memorable ones the series is known for, combine that with some bland "fetch quests" that the game introduces - I think the best way to describe them would be disappointing.That being said I had my fun with the game and enjoyed the roughly 26 hours it took me to beat it on professional difficulty while doing all of the substories, almost all of the fetch quests and a good chunk of the minigames. If you're a huge fan of the series I think this is an easy recommendation even if it might be worth playing the game on game pass or waiting for discounts instead of purchasing it at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: For a smaller-scale game, this is an extremely comprehensive Yakuza package; it easily triumphs many of the mainline games in all around quality. These games are so great, and I hope RGG continues to work their magic until the day I die.I had soured on Like a Dragon Gaiden a lot since its initial release. The way its narrative is treated in Infinite Wealth did not mix well with the fact I found myself decently disillusioned with the two action-based Yakuza-adjacent games I've played most recently. Upon a spontaneous second playthrough, I have learnt that my hindsight had failed me. This game is great, nay more than great!The combat in this game is so much fun. Both styles are infinitely expressive and are smooth as I am after my bi-weekly full body wax. Most older Yakuza games have combat that would not feel out of place in the worst sort of licensed game, but, subtly, they've sharpened their craft quite a bit over the years. The music goes crazy style, with subtle melodic call-backs to some of the series' greatest tunes. I'm no (D)Anthony Fantano, but to me this soundtrack is scientifically divine. The narrative also fervently owns. It may have several lulls, but I believe it to be a well written and exciting drama. In particular, the final scene in this game is a masterclass in the type of soapbox storytelling Yakuza games aspire to. It made me cry a lot more this playthrough than I did the first time around. I did not expect that.These games have slowly found their own little pocket within my heart, and I now think it's fair to say this series means a lot to me. I love Kazuma Kiryu. I love the Yakuza games. Often I throw about the word love carelessly when writing about videogames, but I use it here in the most emotional and the most affectionate way. They will remain a part of me forever, and will always push me forwards. For that, I am appreciative. And when searching for a word to describe this appreciation, I find that love is the only one that fits. This game is good. You should play it. Thanks for reading.There is a hefty chunk of other stuff in this game which I did not talk about, as I skipped through it! There is a free trial for this game on Steam right now. You can play the game for a whopping 4 hours! I can now confirm that if you put the game on easy mode and skip through all the cutscenes (apart from the ones you really like) you can beat this entire game within this time constraint. You can even play the Infinite Wealth demo for a bit! Pardon my French, but that is pretty swell!!

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is an amazing, short but well-polished title, considering it took only six months of game development.Similar to other fans of the series, it was a joy to return back to an action brawler genre game with Kiryu ("Joryu") at the helm as the main protagonist.  The new agent style, probably inspired from James Bond, was quite unique and interesting to play as, especially when clearing large mobs.  Though for most of the game's key bosses, the tried and tested yakuza style with heavy hitting moves still held strong, especially with pretty cool juggling physics thrown into the mix too.Another key feature was the upgraded coliseum which many agree must be the best iteration in the series thus far.  It didn't felt like a chore as each mode has its own unique challenges, which kept things interesting.  I thoroughly enjoyed the chance to recruit other fighters and form my own team to fight in the large scale battles.  Definitely a thumbs up to also be able to include and even control the legendary yakuza fighters - daigo, majima and saejima, in these arena battles.Substories were interestingly woven with the unique Akame network storyline which felt fresh in the very familiar backdrop of Sotenbori.  Completionist achievements were very manageable and it was a really nice touch to also be able to re-experience Sega Racing Classic / Daytona USA 2 - many fond childhood memories of this at arcades!The main storyline was well-paced, given it's meant to be a short title.  It helped to fill the many supposed plot gaps between Yakuza 6 and Yakuza 7, whilst also featuring a new niche location being the Castle.  I was blown away by all the fancy neon bright lights of the area, which truly brought out that premier nightlife feeling in the map.Overall, RGG studio never ceases to amaze fans with their work, be it large scale numbered titles or even the smaller titles such as Like a Dragon Gaiden.  I'm personally looking forward to sink a sizable amount of time into their next title - Infinite Wealth.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I want to say that I don't recommend this game to someone that hasn't played all the previous games or atleast 6 and 7. Even though the game tries explain some things that occurred so far I still recommend to go play those games because the plot can get a little complex in these game and you might get confused, also you will miss all the fan service stuff. Alright now that we got that out of the way time to talk about the game. Kiryu returns as the protagonist in this one and at first I was a little skeptical about this after the great send off that Yakuza 6 gave him. To my surprise however after completing the game I would say that this was a much needed storybit that had to be added not only to tie any lose ends to the Yakuza 7 story but to Kiryu's character and relationships also. I won't get into spoiler territory but trust me this game is really emotional (it made me cry like 2 times). The new characters are also quite good, the antagonists really stole the show for me and like every yakuza game there's a twist you might not see coming. Now for the gameplay part of the review I think we all agree that this is the best Dragon Engine Kiryu. His Yakuza style contains his classic moves from the other games with some new ones added and overall better balanced. Now his new style is called Agent and I FREAKING LOVE IT! They gave him so many gadgets that if he had a cape and a mask he could be batman and I know that doesn't sound like the aproach rgg usually takes with styles but trust it is really fun. I mean how can a game where a japanese middle-aged man uses his wire from his watch and freaking cigarette bombs not be fun. Honestly my only complains about the game are that you acquire heat much slower than the other games and that there's a bit of padding in the story to make the game longer that I think could be removed (it's some substories that you must do in order to progress the story). Overall this game offers so many different and fun expierences in the different minigames, combat scenarios and story missions that I recommend it to every yakuza fan out there

_childDocuments_.review: Bringing back a character whose story had been concluded close to 8 years ago is no easy task.To say that I was skeptical about this game's story and the impact it would have on the legacy of one of my favorite characters would sure be an understatement. RGG somehow managed to beautifully tie everything together and also deliver an even better send off to the legend of Kazuma Kiryu than his initial "final Game" Yakuza 6.Everything that was missing from Yakuza 6, due to its rocky development is here.- better combat- better minigames/side activities- better bosses- more light on the old cast of charactersSome of us were definitely expecting this game to be a cashgrab, a cheap asset flip, just to cash in on people's love for the character. They definitely cut some corners in the very short 6 months of development, but the end product is one I'm more than satisfied with.I only have a few small gripes with this game:- The Coliseum (while cool on paper) is very underwhelming,movesets of pre-existing characters were butchered and really don't offer any kind of depth.The huge team battles are also just a cluster ♥♥♥♥.- The Dragon/Yakuza Style is extremely broken and just kills bosses with like 2 combos.- Small pacing issues in an already short story: you could erase Akame from the plot and it probably wouldn't change a thing. I found her inclusion to be quite useless. She is just a tool for you to start grinding.- The flow of combat feels a bit off in big groups at times.But other than that, Gaiden offers basically anything a Yakuza fan could ask for.Lastly I would like to say:Nishitani III has become one of my favorite bosses in the series, this guy is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is a side story of what Joryu was up to after Yakuza 6 and during 7. It's a relatively shorter game at just around 20 hours for the campaign. But don't let that fool you into thinking it'll be lower quality because it definitely isn't. The story is one of the best in the entire series and has some very emotional moments. The gameplay is a refinement of Kiwami 2's with a hint of Judgment. The new agent style is very fun as well. Kiryu + grappling hook is a very fun combo as it turns out. Of course the usual Yakuza insanity also returns in full swing. Pocket circuit is back baybeee and it is glorious!Oh and it comes with a demo for LaD 8, and it's great! It's a massive improvement over 7 and I can't wait to get my hands on it.The one big downside is that it doesn't have new game+ so consider that if that's a big deal for you. Otherwise this is a solid entry in the Like a Dragon/Yakuza series.

_childDocuments_.review: A quite short entry with probably the most managable 100% achievements in history of Yakuza saga (mostly because it doesn't require you to play mahjong for completion, don't worry though, mahjong is still included in the game).To indirectly quote one of the comical substories - they really went balls out with this one. We get the marvelous, over-the-top combat with wacky special agent/007 style gadgets, which in my humble opinion culminated in the most memorable  fight in the series.The main story consists of five chapters, which together with requests (substories), colliseum and minigame completion required for 100% achievements take about 35 hours, possibly much shorter if you decide not to take your sweet time with it. After completing the final we get to play premium adventure mode which allows to experience all side content. There is no NG+ implemented (yet).Once we finish the story we get the possibility to play the demo of Infinite Wealth. The transition from finale to story demo is quite smooth, but once the first combat starts one might realize how bittersweet this demo inclusion is. After hours of having a great time and silly fun with Gaiden's actual combat system we get... the JRPG turn-based combat. Of course it had some major revisions since release of the 7th installment, including combo attacks with party members, possibility to move around during combat (crazy, I know), and area of effect display for AoE skills and attacks. Those changes allow a much more tactical approach, but still walking away from the great active combat style to turn-based one is the saddest part of the series current direction.So grab Like a Dragon Gaiden and enjoy the action combat, we Yakuza fans all know and love, in its possibly greatest display, as it may very well be the last time we get to see it.I intentionally avoided mentioning the story not to spoil anything, so let me just say that it is very good. Especially the finale. The finale is perfect.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is just as fantastic as the ones before it, it doesn't use the turn based mode like the previous like a dragon game instead sticking to Yakuza's iconic gameplay. The story is shorter than the previous games as well as less substories (150 down to 35), other than that everything about the game is great. The new fighting style Agent gives you more AOE type attacks so its easier and a lot more fun to take down large groups of enemies. All the new gadgets are fun except for the drones, don't waste your time upgrading the drones it's not worth it. The Story is great it fills in the blanks from Yakuza 6 to Like a Dragon on what Kiryu was up to and boy do I feel bad for Kiryu, talk about a rough situation with limited options. The Story sets up infinite Wealth pretty well and fills in a lot of the blanks Like a Dragon had.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Story, 8/10 Gameplay - Overall 9/10.Outstanding game - As someone who's played the entire series, this is a love letter to fans, and those who've followed Kiryu's story from his life as a young punk to his life as a surrogate father to his kids. I am sobbing at the ending, and dear god I am not ready for Infinite Wealth.You really should wait and play the other games to understand Kiryu's story before this - it makes a lot of the callbacks and some of the fights themselves have just that much more oomph to them. The combat sadly is not as smooth as Lost Judgment, despite Kiryu's style switching and Yakuza style being as brutal and weighty as ever. Thankfully, juggling is back and Kiryu can do it, which is honestly pretty awesome. The story though, wow. Remarkable, and while it may have some filler, it was engaging to me from start to finish. The last act was a highlight, and it def shows the writers and whole team are much better at crafting a proper ending to their stories. I don't think I've cried that hard over a game in years.Will always be a fan of RGG Studios, and hope to see more and more from them as the years go on. Just make the Yakuza style hit slightly faster FFS.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is what I would call, Yakuza lite. It has all of the things that you would expect from a Yakuza game, but in very small quantities, such that I believe it would be a great introduction to anyone new to the series, it has minigames, substories, an epic boss song and an epic boss battle, it has easier to obtain achievement lists and a simplified ability tree.It has everything you know, just a lot less of that everything. So to keep this punctual and help you make your mind up, here's some points about the game!- Numerous minigames make their way back into the Yakuza series, Shogi, Mahjong, Koi Koi, Oicho Kabu, Golfing, Sega Arcade and more- The Completion list is shorter than usual and not tied to achievements, making a 100% significantly faster than before- The normal Yakuza series averages 12-13 Chapters of story, sometimes even more. This game only has 5 chapters of Story- The events of this game happen at the same time as Like A Dragon's story about Ichiban Kasuga, if you do care about the overarching plot, it's still worth playing that title first- Classic Yakuza combat with an albeit simplified 2-style system.- Only a couple of boss-fight cutscenes in this one sadly.- Despite being connected to Ichiban Kasuga's story, this is the classic Action RPG style, not the JRPG Style they used for that game.- Great music- Only some comedy- Substories rework here falls very flat for me, lost a lot of the charm and personality.I'm a die-hard fan, and I do not regret this purchase, however this is definitely a Yakuza game where I think "wait for a sale" is a justified stance to take. It has all the things I love about this series, just not enough of it. It left me wanting more by the end instead of feeling exhausted like I'd been taken on an intense, emotional journey.First Yakuza game in the series to not make me cry.Good game though.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden is a nice surprise as it is another game using the , and we know that RGG Studio wanted to move on to using Unreal Engine, as we saw with Like a Dragon: Ishin!, this year.But I am happy to see good old Dragon Engine coming back, and it does seem we’ll be seeing it in January 2024 when Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth comes out, as well, as the Demos included in Gaiden also run on Dragon Engine.From a  standpoint, the fact that we’re dealing with Dragon Engine means that this game runs pretty similarly to how both Judgment games run, and with my  I can run this game at Max Settings, 1620p DLDSR resolution, downsampled to my native 1080, with DLSS set to Quality, and the game can run quite above 60 FPS, sometimes close to 100, depending on the moment, so I choose to cap to 60 in this case, to save some power.Alternatively, another option is to run 4K DSR and use Balanced DLSS, still holds 60 FPS most of the time, except a few places like some areas within the Castle, which are quite crowded.Performance DLSS would likely fix that, though. wise, this game has pretty responsive , and Kiryu feels pretty awesome to play, especially with all the new fun stuff from the Agent Style, but his Dragon Style is still pretty good for 1v1s and some enemies with tons of HP.There are some very interesting combo and juggle set ups when mixing up both fighting styles, and it really feels great when you manage to pull off a big combo. in this game is pretty decent, with some fun callbacks to older games and moments in the franchise, and its characters, and this time most of the sub-stories are gathered from the same NPC, Akame, which I found it was a nice addition to the cast, and hopefully we see more of her in future games.The Arena is also fun, I love doing arena matches in all the games in this series, and I had fun with this one for sure.On the hardest difficulty available from a new save, I found the game quite balanced and fair, but against strong enemies, I needed careful tactics to not get destroyed, and that pretty much is quite similar to how it works in previous games.Once you get to a point when your skills are quite maxed or almost there, Kiryu feels like the usual beast he normally is by the end of every game, and it is so much fun.The  is pretty nice, some classics from the franchise and some really great tracks, the final boss track is especially great.Overall, a nice “smaller” game which I spend like 40+ hours with, so not that small, but I reckon others are way longer.Nice to see Pocket Circuit back too…that ate quite a bit of my time, for sure, but I love it.The ending is absolutely incredible too, exceptional performance from Takaya Kuroda in that scene, I have no words, it really elevates this great game into one of my favourite in the whole series. A fun game to tie us in from the end of Yakuza 6 to the next game in the series, coming early 2024, definitely worth playing to experience all the bits in the story from Kiryu’s perspective, those who we didn’t get to see in Like a Dragon (the 7th main game).

_childDocuments_.review: Set between 7 and 8, a conclusion to a certain bodyguard's story. The main story is very short relative to past games, so it is very obvious it is being padded out with Akame side content to slow down the progress. During the early parts it does not affect the pacing that much, but during late game the point requirements forces the player to do all the substories and minigames for points, on top of grinding for stupid amount of money in the Castle, to upgrade abilities.The battle system is  like Judgement(two styles), one for solo and another for group. Classic battle style is good from the get go but Agent requires a lot of investment in abilities to become usable and eventually very fun. Suzuki Taichi's basic moves are greatly simplified in this entry so being able to call 20 drones to do the fighting instead is great to have. On the topic of fights, from a pure game play pov there are no memorable fights nor bosses in the mainline quest, maybe in a longer game there will be more time for character developments to hype things up, but boss fights are shockingly plain. Past entries you have some random guy that bust out the door with machine guns, and chainsaws, and some other . In this entry the most interesting boss is a dude wielding a tanto that gets knocked out before he can even show anything.....Perhaps the most praiseworthy aspect of Y7.5 is the graphics. On a mid range set up I can max out every graphic setting and still run the game stable at 60fps. The lighting, assets, special effects and detailed character models looks amazing in most environment. Compared to Y7, it felt like there is a greater emphasis on uping the saturation and contrasts to make cut-scenes more dramatic, sometimes it gets too dark to see any details on default gamma settings.Overall: Amazing teaser for Y8, play it.

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game. This game is the pure Like a Dragon/Yakuza experience without all the failing of the other games. The combat is very good, importing many of the improvements made in the Judgment series and altering it to fit Kiryu's gameplay. Juggling and mortal reversals make a return, while Extreme Heat has become very akin to EX Boost. The only thing I would complain about in combat is there is a fairly low amount of heat actions, but the ones they brought into this game are excellent. The progression is pretty good, returning to using money and the new Akame Points to buy upgrades. Bringing money back into skills make it really fun and interesting to actually earn money, due to its direct impact on gameplay now.The story is amazing. It ties into Yakuza: Like a Dragon but from the perspective of Kiryu, giving us a fresh look at the events of that game, while also tying up Kiryu's story, since Yakuza 6's bittersweet ending left something to be desired. All of the new characters in this game are to become instant favorites, they did an amazing job with the cast of this game.Visually this game is beautiful. The game is visually darker than other Dragon Engine titles, but they also use more highlights and brighter colors to offset the darker shading present, giving us one of the most striking titles yet. All the UI and menus look sleek as well. Everything is expertly shaded, animated, modeled, and rendered to the point where they would splice in real-life footage cause they were so confident. The quality of the visuals is so good that there are no more pre-rendered cutscenes, the in-game just looks that good now. The game length is about 1/3 of a full Yakuza title. Not the worst thing though, since it bypasses the long, confusing stories of the previous game with a short one that does everything that it needs to. Plus, if you need more game to play, there is still tons of side content to dig your teeth into. All of the side content in this game got an expansion (except for golf, sorry DJ Khaled). The Colosseum is tons of fun, with a huge amount of fights to do. Pocket circuit is back, with more races than ever to do. The Akame Network side content is filled with either well-written personal stories, or silly one-offs to fight homeless guys or convenience store clerks to recruit to your army. The cabaret minigame is all live-action 4K footage, which takes 23.4 gigabytes of space on your computer sadly. OST is full of bangers, its on Spotify if you want to listen after you play this game. Game reuses some songs from Yakuza 0 and Judgment/Lost Judgment for substory music, which is kinda funny. All the karaoke tracks in this game are good, some being brand new and some being remastered ones from previous games. Overall, an amazing game. Taking the best from the previous games while improving on the shortcomings of previous Kiryu games makes this a must-play for Yakuza/Like a Dragon fans. Can not recommend this game enough. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start by saying as a fan of the franchise the ending to this game is so cathartic and unbelievably emotional. Its a roller coaster ride. Its a kick in the chest. It genuinely feels like a reward for playing the last 7 games and It makes me all the more excited for infinite wealth. I can not wait. How in the world did RGG studios make such an incredible game in only 6 months? Hell, they gave us more game in 6 months than most devs give us with years of development. What once was meant to be a DLC side story, came out as its own feature game at a reduced price, that barely feels reduced in any way. There is so much on the plate with this game. Returning to sotenbori was a treat, Pocket circuit us back with a vengeance and the Colosseum mini game is better than it has been in like ever. I thought i was going to hate the agent fighting style, but my god its actually fun. Dont let the over the topness of it all steer you away. Game play is king and agent style is super fun. The story is amazing as i expected, it was great to see the events of 7 from kiryus perspective, but as i stated before the ending of this game takes the cake and is probably the best in the franchise. I would not recommend this one to first timers though. This game is the culmination of YEARS of games and the impact of the story will be greatly lessened by not having played all of that first. go play 0 or kiwami first.The performance is out of this world. The game Looks and runs incredibly. How does it look better and run better than all the games before it? So many games get released broken these days and get fixed as they go, but i didnt have a single crash or bug in my almost 50 hour playthrough. SEGA remains my goat, and they do no wrong in my eyes. I have one complaint. I wish the mid fight cut scenes had more QTEs like they use to. There are like 4 in the game and i think the QTEs made the scenes feel 1000% better and more involved.  Please SEGA. More of this. More Gaidens between major releases. You have a wealth of amazing characters to make a wealth of new stories. You know a Majima game would sell like crazy. love u

_childDocuments_.review: Folks: it's over. There will never be game in the series to top Yakuza Kiwami 2. This game is maybe 10 % as good as that one. It has less reason to keep existing than Yakuza 3 AKA Blockuza. Sure it has tons of references to the previous games, though all of it feels hollow and the new stuff seems silly (Akame network, live video hostess segments, etc.)I used a taxi for the first time and the game crashed to desktop. That is the level of cobbled-together quality this game represents.50 to 75 % of the gameplay is loading screens. This is not like Kiwami 2 where you could seemlessly enter everywhere and have reasonable loading screens. Even when entering small interior sections, the game loads minutes on end for a relatively minimal environment. It is like Yakuza 0 in that it trashes all data and even minor changes in the location make it re-load the whole thing, costing minutes every couple of minutes. This game is really short and you can beat it in 90 minutes if you have good computer with an SSD drive. If you don't, it is likely to take 8 hours because of the loading times. Even the cutscenes have sizable loading times that can last for minutes on end.Gameplay-wise, this feels worse than Yakuza 6 and that game was partially incomplete. This game has a stupider plot than Yakuza 3. The conclusion is that he beats some new Omi guys you will never have time or the preceding story build-up to care about and you are likely to forget the whole game.The fighting system is still the same irritating one where you either slide wildly around or feel like your feet turn into immovable concrete every time you do a move as if you were proposing for marriage. Reacting is super clunky and often delayed. There is also the arbitrary input buffering that can confuse you about how many of the inputted moves are still waiting to be executed before the character can accept new ones. You feel more trapped than in control.The plot is a weird back-and-forth thing much like the gameplay. A lot of the main quest is about thinly-veiled minigame tutorials late into the game. There is a golf center tie in after the halfway point of the game. It is also so badly paced Chapter 2 is longer than the rest of the game.Bottom-line, if you cannot segment your game to keep the loading times reasonable, do not make a 98-gigabyte game. This game is both technically and content-wise undesirable.

_childDocuments_.review: I haven’t played many of the yakuza games. I have all of the main ones (aside from 6, judgement and ishin), but I have never played them. I was a couple chapters into zero, but I stopped and got burnt out. This game is a master piece. The ending genuinely brought tears to my eyes and don’t know much about the prior story.In this yakuza game, there is only two styles. If my knowledge from playing zero is consistent, there’s usually more. However this isn’t to say they aren’t varied. The agent style and all of its gadgets are absolutely amazing and allow for some great combinations. The yakuza style is also great and has that impact. Due to having only two styles, it’s extremely easy to swap to a different style. This allows for an amazing chain of heavy yakuza attacks and utilising the agents gadgets. This honestly makes this one of the most creative combat I have seen in gaming. This really links back to a core ideal that is shown throughout the game that combat its self is art. The fact that the combat parallels so well with the story itself is amazing.The story of Like a dragon gaiden: the man who erased his name is not your typical mob story. It’s intricate, it shows the dynamics of honour and what it truly means for someone to go underground and lose everything that had meaning to them. It also shows that there are two ways to go about it. You can rise up and keep on going or you can just give up. I don’t want to go into too many details to avoid spoilers, but the ending was perfect  is just so endearing to see that such a stoic figure can such deep and intricate emotion.The minigames, as with any yakuza game, are heavily prevalent. Every game is fun. I will admit, I didn’t try nearly enough, but the karaoke was amazing and the pool was fun. Not to mention the cabaret clubs were… fun to say the least ;) . All of these things packed into the small map is amazing and really makes it feel so good. Speaking of the small area, I actually got to memorise the place and I didn’t have to use the map at all at one point. I knew where ashibata park was and I knew where shokofuchu street was.Like a dragon: gaiden is truly amazing. I am ashamed it didn’t win any awards this year, but that doesn’t change the testament that this is an amazing game. I am happy I played through it the way I have been doing prior games at just one game at a time. I truly must recommend this to anyone who wants to get into the yakuza/like a dragon series.

_childDocuments_.review: Deliciously tightly packaged Yakuza!I'm gonna be honest and say that at first I didn't expect much from this game. It seemed like recycled content with some Kiryu story that could have been part of the other games. But as more info got out and I learned more my interest got picked. Now I regard this among my favorites.I think right now my ranking goes something like this: Y0, Y7, YK2, Gaiden, YK1, Y5, Y6, Y3, Y4.In the end I feel that although shorter, this is a complete Yakuza package. Everything we've come to love and expect is here. Twisting heavy drama story, whacky side quests, great minigames, memorable characters, awkward content to explain to your loved ones, Japanese weirdness and so on. The difference is that the game does all this without any bloat.I really liked how they portrayed Kiryu in this one and made him a bit more human. I also really enjoyed some of the new characters and how they got developed throughout the game. And I loved Akame! More Akame in the next games or we riot!I think RGG packaged the story they had with just the right amount of side stuff and fluff to leave you wanting just a bit more in the end. Which sucks! I was intending to wait a little to get Infinite Wealth cheaper but who am I kidding?

_childDocuments_.review: 9.5/10An absolutely beautiful love letter to Kiryu and the "Yakuza" saga of Like a Dragon. While it seems Infinite Wealth will be our farewell to Kiryu, Gaiden feels like a heartfelt farewell to the games that introduced us to him.The gameplay was a lot of fun. I'll admit, I definitely favored one style over the other, but even primarily using one style throughout most of the game, I still had a blast playing. As per usual, this game is chock full of minigames and side stories to invest your time in to, and they are absolutely worth it! Also in usual RGG fashion, the soundtrack was phenomenal. While being a game focused on Kiryu, it featured a cast of primarily new characters, and I loved them. Akame was an instant favorite for me. Shishido and Hanawa were strong favorites as well. But the story is where this game absolutely shines. It maintained continuity from the stories that came before, while also building up immense anticipation for the next game to come. The ending in particular was phenomenal.This game was absolutely meant for the Yakuza fans who have been along for Kiryu's entire journey. If you're new to the series, this absolutely should not be your starting point. But it is a fantastic destination to look forward to.

_childDocuments_.review: RGG Studio has truly outdone themselves with the Dragon engine. Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name truly highlights why the Dragon Engine is so good. The graphics in this game are top notch and this game is really well optimized in terms of PC performance requirements. I love that RGG Studio incorporated juggling into this title's gameplay like they did with Lost Judgment. It's really fun especially when switching between Agent Style and Yakuza style constantly. Continuing RGG Studio's long track record of great and memorable video game music, the soundtracks in this game are all very catchy and enhance the experience greatly. I also enjoyed the variety of the minigames in this title. While not my favorite set of minigames out of all RGG Studio games, I still had a blast playing through all of them, with the Coliseum being my personal favorite as it allows you to play as any character available in the Coliseum which is a first for the series!The new cast of characters introduced in this title were all a delight to watch from start to finish. Despite the shorter runtime in comparison to other RGG Studio games, this title's story is just as focused and even more engaging than some of RGG Studio's other titles. In fact, this title made me really empathized with Kiryu even further and I really love this game's conclusion. I would recommend to play this game after Yakuza 6 and then Yakuza: Like a Dragon to truly enjoy this game's story to the fullest.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed the story in roughly 20 hours, absolute must play for any Yakuza fan, the gameplay is the best it's ever been for Kiryu, Agent style is pretty neat and innovative, but Yakuza style was a huge standout for me due to the new rework of extreme heat, it's an absolute blast, and the regular moveset feels like the best of both worlds from the early dragon engine games Y6/YK2, and the earlier games which I found great. Loved the story, it really broke my expectations of what I thought it would be, a very classic and satisfying yakuza story with great characters and hype moments, the ending in particular gave me Yakuza 5 vibes, except even better.The minigames are a good collection of everything from the series, but I actually found the new substories to be extremely engaging, even moreso than the old games, they felt very focused and well curated, albeit at a numerical cost, but that's fine though, since I think it could be easy to get burnt out on them due to how it ties into progression (also a good thing)So for 50 dollars in 2023 you're already getting a really decent bang for buck in regards to the actual quality of the game even if it's not that crazy long, I felt it was similar length to Anno Mutationem (25 bucks), it's awfully nice having a fun, polished, gorgeous, optimized game on launch in this day and age, so I still recommend it regardless, this game is about quality over quantity.

_childDocuments_.review: You must have played the previous games for this game to hit you the right way. I've played through all the Yakuzas so far. I'm pretty picky about games I write reviews for. They have to strike my fancy in a very specific way. I reviewed Yakuza Kiwami, Kiwami 4 and Like a Dragon negatively for the way the story played out. In my opinion, Yakuza games often suffer from "we need to finish this" syndrome, where the story accelerates at an unsustainable pace and you have some weird mechanic that trumps all the effort you put. I don't have infinite time, so I try to maximise my efficiency. That usually means grinding out the money-making minigames as fast as possible, which is a chore. The Man Who Erased His Name is perfect. The soundtrack is the best out of all the games. The graphics are the best out of all the games. The game is optimised so much that I've run the entire thing on 144 fps, 2k ultra, while streaming. The story is absolutely amazing, so much so that I even shed a tear (or two) at the end of the game, although I won't spoil you the reason. There is no grinding that is no rewarding. They took all the complaints from the last few games and simply avoided adding the problematic components of the previous games. Beautiful game, whole way through.The two people who watched this game with me agree, this was the best game out of all the games, from every aspect.

_childDocuments_.review: Am on the final chapter of this game, and I have some thoughts about the experience so far. Visually, it's a 10/10 - especially the stunning "casino nightlife design" of the Castle. But story-wise, i'd probably give it a 3.5/5  because it's pretty short, and I wish Akame was a more fleshed-out character. If you attempt the final fight without too many ability upgrades, then it's near-impossible to beat it unless you're good at timing your doges and blocks. It's not enough to rely on health and heat replenishments. And honestly, it actually takes more time to upgrade your abilities than to play through the story mode. For experienced Yakuza players, it's an enjoyable challenge. But for most new fans or inexperienced players like me (e.g. I only finished playing Yakuza 0 and Yakuza 7 - Like a Dragon), this game will require a bit of patience in grinding for cash from the Castle fights and skill points from the Akame Network. The challenges still don't ruin the overall experience; I had a blast. Highly worth recommending this game, and can't wait for new adventures in the Yakuza series.

_childDocuments_.review: While I enjoyed my time with this game, I feel that with a $50 price tag, 5-chapter story, and being mainly locked to Sotenbori there is not much to justify the price. For newcomers to the Yakuza series or those who haven't played Yakuza: Like A Dragon, this game may is not the best.I specifically have issue with the story and pacing. I was hoping the story would be a little longer especially where there were time jumps or just small slideshows explaining how the story went. While I understand the game's relatively short development cycle (6 months according to a dev), it's easy to see in the lack of fleshed-out gameplay elements. Going into the game I was really hoping to  Even an appearance by  would have been satisfying.I would recommend the game only if you've played Yakuza: Like a Dragon AND have played most of the other Kiryu games. It effectively explains Kazuma Kiryu's whereabouts and his appearance in Yakuza: Like a Dragon. The ending is particularly well done, then transitions into the upcoming Like A Dragon: Infinite Wealth game and bundled demo for it.I do like what's been done with the Castle and think the system could integrate a lot more battles and opponents to make it interesting. To get some of the achievements and skills in the game, you effectively need to grind battles over and over again which loses it's charm pretty quick.Overall, I think this game exists to ease you into the Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth game coming out next year. It does an OK job at explaining the side of Kazuma Kiryu during the events of Yakuza: Like a Dragon but most of the payoff comes from the ending. However, I would hesitate to recommend this game to casual fans of the series or newcomers. I do not think $50 is a good price for the game ESPECIALLY since you can get Yakuza 0, Yakuza Kiwami, and Yakuza Kiwami 2 for $18 in a bundle right now.

_childDocuments_.review: Released on November 08, 2023, Like a Dragon Gaiden successfully continues the Yakuza saga with a captivating plot that serves as an epilogue to Yakuza 6. The narrative seamlessly connects with new protagonists, Ichiban Kasuga and Takayuki Yagami, while maintaining a strong link to the beloved Kazuma Kiryu.Strengths:    • Accessible for Newcomers and Appealing to Veterans: The game strikes a balance, making it accessible for newcomers with thorough explanations and Portuguese subtitles, while also catering to series veterans who can relish the return of Kiryu. The central characters are charismatic, revealing a more sentimental side of Kazuma Kiryu, providing a well-rounded experience for players of varying familiarity with the franchise.    • Engaging Setting and Activities: Set in the Sotembori district, the game offers a visually stunning and lively environment with diverse activities such as karaoke, game rooms, and casinos. The Coliseum, now known as the Castle, provides exciting challenges, adding depth to the gaming experience. The district's visuals, especially in the Coliseum, shine with impressive graphics, even on older generation consoles.    • Innovative Combat System: Like a Dragon Gaiden introduces a fresh combat system for Kazuma Kiryu, departing from the traditional stances and incorporating modern gadgets inspired by Eastern culture. The game maintains an engaging combat experience with improved gameplay, making combos more accessible and adding new strategic elements, such as using gadgets for unique effects.Bugs/Weaknesses:    • Short Duration: Unlike previous titles in the Yakuza series, Like a Dragon Gaiden has a considerably shorter completion time, with the main journey lasting around 15 to 20 hours. While this may cater to players with limited time, it may disappoint fans accustomed to the longer gameplay experiences offered by previous Yakuza titles.    • Potential for Expansion: The game's brevity, coupled with its narrative starting immediately after Yakuza 6, may make it feel more like a DLC than a standalone installment. While it serves as a joyous reunion with Kiryu for longtime players, it also raises questions about the potential for a deeper, more expansive experience.    • Distinctive but Separate: Despite its connection to Yakuza 6, Like a Dragon Gaiden's journey with Joryu feels somewhat detached from the core Yakuza narrative. This separation, while providing a fresh perspective, might leave players feeling that the iconic character of Kiryu deserves a more integral role rather than a side story.In summary, Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name excels in storytelling, accessibility, setting, and combat innovation, but its brevity and potential for expansion may leave players with mixed feelings, particularly those expecting a more extended and integral installment in the Yakuza series.

_childDocuments_.review: A bit pricey overall, but a must-play for anyone who played through Kiryu's saga and 7 and is looking forward to 8 (Infinite Wealth). Spices up the combat with unique gimmicks, adds the best Coliseum the franchise has seen so far, really nice outfit customization (mods are gonna make it wild 100%) and a nice variant of Part-Time Hero for things to do in Sotenbori. Having finished the story, it is definitely more entertaining than a lot of story beats of other games in the franchise, that's for sure, and there's nice references to previous games scattered across the main story and substories. It ties into the events of 7 really nicely and the finale is amazing. for best experience you'd have ideally played all of the previous games, but in general here are the recommendations:- 6 and 7 are absolute must-plays: Gaiden goes into the story beats of 7 a lot and connects the timeline between 6 and 7 and doesn't hold back on going into all details of what happens in 7. It doesn't go into much detail of events of 6, however, other than the one reason why Kiryu is The Man Who Erased His Name- 3 and 5 are next on the list of must-plays: to fully grasp the emotional side of Kiryu's experience throughout his journey in Gaiden and to basically feel the feels for the man. I felt many feels, ok, and I didn't enjoy 3 at all but ngl what they did here kinda made my suffering of playing 3 on Hard worth it- Kiwami 1 and 2 aren't a must-play, but it's good to have played them both to understand a few references and callbacks here and there- 0 and 4 are kind of not really relevant at all, surprisingly, other than for Pocket Circuit I guess
