_childDocuments_.review: For $50 this game is a scam, straight up. This feels more in line with $20 DLC than a nearly full priced release. The only new things in this game are the story(which didn't grab me at all and just felt random even for this series), the secret agent fighting style, and a singular new area that turns out to be a tiny location thats only home to some old gambling minigames and the arena. 99% of the game actually takes place in Sotenbori and it's exactly the same as it was in Kiwami 2. Some old minigames we haven't seen in a while, like Pocket Circuit, are back and while it is nice to have them back they are exactly the same as before. The arcade game selection is pretty choice though, Daytona 2 rules and Fighting Vipers 2 is cool as well. Paired with Sonic the Fighters, Motor Raid and VF2(wish it was swapped for VF3)all returning, its a solid line up. Unfortunately the biggest dropped ball here is substories. There are hardly any. Instead they decided to put about a hundred random fetch quests of zero substance all over the map. Give a guy a random food item, pick up kids lost ball thats mere inches away, etc. Many of these do not even reward you in any way either other than filling up a sidequest experience bar that you can get a poultry amount of money from once you fill it and level up. There is a very small number of "real" substories but even those do not satisfy. You have to activate them all manually at your base first, where you're then given a run down of whats going on without actually interacting with any of the characters they pertain to, then you just go to where they are on the map, get a little more dialogue and context (if you're lucky), fight and its done. None of them are particularly memorable or funny, but are inoffensive and would all be considered "low-tier" in a real Yakuza game that usually has 70+ substories where its more acceptable that not every single one was a knock out. These few substories are quite literally all this game has outside of the insanely short main story so the poor execution and quality of them are immensely disappointing. If they just ditched all of the nonsense and just made 50 or so classic substories, it could have saved this game and helped make it feel more worth the asking price.Really the only positives I have are the new secret agent fighting style and the combat in general. The whip is a lot of fun to use and the explosive cigarettes are absolutely chaotic in small spaces. I know not everyones not a fan of the Dragon Engine combat but I have a lot of fun with it and its no different here. The final boss was great too, awesome choreography and a comical amount of healthbars.Somewhat unrelated to the game but I'd figure I would mention, the performance on PC is yet again worse than previous games. I really don't understand why but these games have very steadily been running worse and worse with each release despite running on the exact same engine and taking place in the exact same cities and reusing all of the same assets. I have a 3090ti and an i9-12900Ks. Kiwami 2(which is just about the exact same game as this) and 6 both ran at 4K native and a mostly steady 120FPS maximum settings on my machine. Judgment ran a smidge worse hitting about 80-90FPS and Lost Judgment ran considerably worse barely able to even hit 60FPS most of the time. Unfortunately this game runs like Lost Judgment does just scraping by at 60FPS. DLSS does help tremendously but Ive never been able to fully ignore the smudging and occasional artifacts it introduces, and I shouldn't need it anyway, these games are all literally identical in engines and assets, there is genuinely no reason they should be running worse than they did before.Overall I wouldn't spend more than $20 on this game, and even then it still wouldn't be all that great anyway. The fact that you can buy just about the entire back catalog of this franchise 0-6 for about the same price(often even less when theyre on sale) as this nothingburger of a game is pretty embarrassing. Each of those is easily 100+ hours if you go for completion and are simply better quality games. Sega really needs to do better because I haven't enjoyed an entry in this franchise since the first Judgment game in 2019.

_childDocuments_.review: After Yakuza 6, I was very skeptical of the idea of Kiryu returning in any role as a protagonist or major character in future games. However, the game does a wonderful job connecting Yakuza 6 and Yakuza: Like a Dragon together, while also setting up Infinite Wealth in a way that makes me extremely excited to see what happens next. For a shorter title compared to RGG's other works, the game is still full of content that can very well take over 30 hours to complete. Side content like the Coliseum are obvious stand-outs, and there's a decent selection of substories to go through as well. Combat still feels fun to mess around with, and the soundtrack features a very different feel that other entries haven't had (in a good way). For me though, the story, while relatively short, was the obvious star of the game, featuring a great cast of characters and a deeply emotional ending that broke me more than any other Yakuza game. In all, Gaiden is another excellent entry in the franchise, and one that makes me very excited to see what's in store next for Yakuza fans. While I wouldn't recommend this title for newcomers, the payoff after playing all previous mainline titles is fantastic, and very much worth waiting for.

_childDocuments_.review: Loved the game, bought it on sales. Would 100% wait for the sale. In terms of a reboot, it's clever, fun and feels more like a teaser rather than a full fledged Yakuza game. I would say that the MSQ is probably 7-8h. The rest is substories, grinding the "Castle" which has a Coliseum, which in itself is not new aspect but like each Yakuza game, there's some level of mini game that makes you stupid rich. It's the prettied Coliseum of most Yakuza game in my opinion. You can use the taxi to get on it, which I felt was breaking my immersion that it's a boat in international waters. The critique I've read so far is that you can play with other character in the Coliseum but their moves/fluidity is far from being fleshed out and is by far a let down.As for the story, I feel it's pretty good, this feels like a kind of "Multverse" where Kiryu looks not older than 35 yo but this appears to be set in the future when the kids from the orphanage are in their early 20's. The vilains are mid, the overall dept of the Yakuza line of story is not good. Well to be fair, it's still pretty fresh, I like that Kiryu works as Joryu a covert agent which works for some covert government agency also collaborating with the CIA... Kind of sexy spy who get in to leave the life of crime, protect is children while pretending to be dead. (an absolute easy card pulled each time in Yakuza).So overall the structure of the game is good. The fluidity of the fighting system - the way it's been kind of dumb down is still very fun. The gadgets are super fun and OP AF. The levelling can be pretty much fully done by chapter 4. Which is 2/3 into the game. Doing all the substories unlock some nice stuff including the 2nd point system needed to level up. So they are kind of extremely important. Like every Yakuza game, we are in extremely familiar territory. The mini-game are stale and basically feels like a copy-paste of all the universe and feels lazy.  It's a plus and a con. The pocket circuit comes back and it's a blast! The datacom/SEGA console old games are ok but when I play Yakuza I'll admit, I'm not interested in that. The Karaoke is also not scalable (no difficulty level adjustment); I suck at it! Still enjoyable. The Cabaret is ok. It's a film cutscene of JAV actress, which is OK I guess. Like in every Yakuza game, you have a side partner which here it's Akame who was a ok new addition but didn't felt like a mark in the Franchise. Meaning, I wouldn't care if she's not in the next game. She share a drink with you, she talks about why she's doing what she does. There's an attempt to build a rapport, but only feels like a tick in a box to achieve a level of narration, rather than an ally that's actually OP (like all past close allies usually are in Yakuza game) that you find either funny, interesting or add tons of fun to the game. By the time you're ready to do the final chapter and you've completed S rank all of the coliseum, gotten all the sexy expensive gear, you've filled up in potions and food. You've had some fun challenges in the Coliseum, you're thinking, Let's freaking go!! Last Boss, Last chapter, action pact +100 low level yakuza, with 30 mini boss and 5-6 big boss fight... Right? Nope! It's OK but it's just not good enough, In fact after you're done with it and you're like... Oh... Ok. There's No New Game + , much MUCH shorter than other games. The added features are mid and overall the polishing of the scenes and the custscene as still very good.  It's a solid 6, low 7/10 - Still pretty ok

_childDocuments_.review: A great story with a lot of fan service and a brilliant combat system.I played Judgment and Yakuza 0 before this game and can definitely say that the combat feels much nicer and crispier. The only annoying thing is the ragdoll stun attacks that just force you to wait a few seconds to recover. The problem is so much worse with pistol enemies who just stun spam you. Also surprisingly there is no quick select of items like there was in Judgments. That just makes it more annoying to heal as you need to go through the menus every time.In terms of story, it is engaging right from the start and I am glad that you do not need to play all the yakuza games to understand what is going. The only game I would say you need to play before this one is Yakuza Like a Dragon as the story would make a lot more sense if you do. One minor complaint I have about the game is that there are a few times where the story is locked behind progression in the open world. The grind is not too bad and it honestly never affected me as I was already doing the side objectives anyway but I still find this game design annoying.The fact that this game is shorter than others in the series actually plays in its favour as it picks up much faster and the story is just overall lean. That is especially praiseworthy as these yakuza games tend to be a bit bloaty and consistently run about 8 hours too long. Here the story is to the point.Overall a great game and a nice change of pace to have a brawler as a bridge between two huge 60+ hour turn based rpgs.

_childDocuments_.review: 150 words or less review:Gameplay:An action-RPG at its heart, Like a Dragon Gaiden combines its seasoned-past with their newer IP, Judgment, to craft an engaging and combo-orientented brawler. While there could be room for a little more refining in a specific fight style, gameplay never felt boring and there is always something new to do. Even if the player doesn't love the fighting mechanics, rhythm-based karaoke, pocket circuit racer, shogi, darts, pool, and much more offers a variety that makes this game addicting to play from start to finish.Graphics:With AAA games making it harder to stand out from the crowd, LaD still manages to capture the world and its characters with very little infidelity. Facial expressions, pores on a face, and detailed landscapes makes this game still beyond worthy to look at. The only aspect stopping it right now from being more "modernized" is raytracingMusic:Not "gotta-download-this-album" worthy, but still music that purposefully matches the tone of the moment,Story:Long-time fans will love the story of Kiryu's tale into obscurity. The questions of legacy and if a legacy is worth it if the person cannot witness it all unfolds and proves to be the Dragon of Dojima's strongest chracter study yetScore: 8/10 (One of RGG studio's best action-rpgs yet, with a story that will satisfy longtime fans and motivate them to see what comes next)

_childDocuments_.review: While I disagree with SEGA that this is a good point for those who haven't played any Like a Dragon games before, for those who have kept up with the series, it is an excellent albeit short entry in the overall story that helps wrap up a lot of hanging plots in the series. This game leans pretty heavily into plot points from Yakuza 3-6 and a little of Like a Dragon 7 so it would behoove anybody thinking of playing this game to play those at the very least. As far as the gameplay goes, the combat is back to the older beat-em-up style offering many of the previous moves from Yakuza 6 with an all new Agent style that starts off feeling a bit underwhelming but evolves into a fantastic means of crowd control by the end.  Many of the series' staple minigames are back which serve as less of a healthy distraction in this game and more of the bulk of the overall gameplay. Ultimately, I believe that this game may be a bit rough for those who are not familiar with the series already and may be a bit short for those who aren't super into the franchise or aren't one of those who force themselves to complete the game 100% but outside of that, it still holds up modestly well to the other entries that precede it.

_childDocuments_.review: Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name is a spin off game which details the story of Kiryu Kazuma more or less during the events of Yakuza 7: Like a Dragon. First and foremost, I remember I was pretty annoyed when this game was announced as I remember (perhaps incorrectly) reading somewhere that the writers were done with Kiryu's story and that Kasuga Ichiban would be the new protagonist going forward and that turn based combat would be how the games would proceed. As someone who fell completely in love with Y7 I remember getting frustrated at the idea of going back to beat 'em up. But quite frankly I was just wrong in my entirety. LAD:G plays like all the Yakuza games before Y7, it is a beat em up but the story itself is significantly shorter than what we're used to from a Yakuza game, if you're like me and like to do a lot of side content (not to 100% completion, just messing about a bit) and doing the main story, you're probably talking about 25-30 hours for a standard playthrough, still a lot, but less than what we're used to. Much like every Yakuza game, the story is compelling and it's very easy to get invested in.Gameplay is similar to Yakuza Kiwami 2, feels great, punches and kicks are heavy, overall very satisfying. Although I'd say one of the best improvements is the seamless blend of running around then transitioning into combat. No more little "Crack knuckles" mini cinematic, no more money counting up at the end, it's literally just run around > Guy wants to fight > You fight him > Money added. There is no downtown between any of the random encounters in the game, which is a huge improvement as I'm sure a lot of us have been frustrated at times having to do random encounters in previous games one after another; this feature really saves a lot of time.Has everything that hallmarks at Yakuza game, daft little mini games, a bunch of substories, bigger sidewquests that hold their own weight alongside the main story, it's all here.Overall I can definitely say that my initial opinion on this game being released was wrong and I should have had more faith in the Development Studio and the Writers, I guess I just wanted more Ichiban that I forgot about just how good it was to be Kiryu again. If you're looking for a short quick beat 'em up, or something just to tide over that Yakuza desire until Infinite Wealth comes out, this is the game to play. 8/10.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great Yakuza game.  This game has everything you expect from a Yakuza game.  Great story, interesting characters, fun side missions that are more than simple fetch quests.  Combat is great.  I love the inclusion of all the gadgets for your second style of combat.  You really feel like an agent using wires to tie up your opponents and exploding cigarettes to defeat your foes.Story is a great tie in between Yakuza 6 and shows some of the events in Yakuza Like A Dragon from a different perspective.  It does a great job getting you ready for infinite wealth.  The game is fairly short for a Yakuza game, which I actually liked.  It was not too short but does not wear out its welcome.  The story does have one or two confusing aspects, like why Kiryu insists on keeping up the charade he is dead, when literally no one in the Yakuza universe believes it.  The only issue I would say is I see some people saying this is the perfect game to get started with the Yakuza series.  I would disagree and say this is one of the worst games to start with.  True, most of the characters are unique to this story, but the game will spoil aspects of Yakuza 6 and pretty much summarizes Like A Dragon, spoiling the game but lacking the emotional depth the game has.  If this is your first time playing Yakuza and the Like A Dragon cast is going to be used more and more going forward, it would be a horrible introduction to them.  Works great as a refresher, but not a starting point.

_childDocuments_.review: If you generally tend to enjoy the Yakuza franchise (or Like a Dragon at this point) you will most likely enjoy this one too. It's your very usual post-engine change Yakuza game with one classic and one very fun new fighting style for Kiryu but a noticeably shorter main story. However, there's still a ton of side content most of which is pretty fun, the coliseum is also very short but sweet with a new and very chaotic but fun team building/fighting mode, the regular humor and fun beat em up gameplay is mostly the same. The main story is full of over the top moments and twists as usual. Unfortunately there's only one city that you get to explore properly.The overall length of the game is around 40 hours which is pretty decent considering the game is not full price and was supposed to be an expansion. I personally enjoyed this one more than Yakuza 6 honestly but I still think that the main story could have been a little longer so I do consider that as the main drawback of this game. Anyways, Like a Dragon Gaiden is fun and is worth buying if you are a Yakuza fan so I recommend it mostly to this franchise's community. If you didn't like Yakuza I do not believe this will change your mind either.P.S The ending is a serious tearjerker so props to the Japanese voice actor of Kiryu - Takaya Kuroda.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game on Normal, took about 21 hours for the main story, most of the side quests / coliseum. I suppose on it's own, it'd still be entertaining, but a lot of the heaviest-hitting moments will be lessened.Gameplay-wise, the two fighting styles both feel great to use, and the new gadgets only add to the wackiness that Dragon Engine-era combat feels, which I love personally. A short(er than most in the franchise) game, I highly recommend it to fans who've completed at least one of the games in the Yakuza/LAD series.Also, the demo of LAD8: Infinite Wealth you open up after the ending is fun to screw around with.

_childDocuments_.review: From once being an uninterested fella to taking the Yakuza world matters to his personal interest, the man who erased his name evolved a lot after being reborn giving up his prior lifestyles and all things once he achieved. Say it world design, combat systems, interactions and all the side hustles. The Akame network is troublesome, forcing you to run errands and fulfilling the needs of all types of people. You can take hours to grind or follow the main quests.The grand Colosseum is majestic and attracts lot of fighters. It also allows you to recruit new fighters on your side. However the brawling challenges are ridiculous throwing some unrealistic opponents and thus may force you to hit at max stats to beat'em all. Lots of cash burning follows this process. It has a rank system from Silver all the way to the Platinum to access all the arenas.Joryu the main character is mainly depicted as a saint once again involving into clan matters while being backed up by his own Dojima. name: Haunted House
detailed_description: NO ENGLISH SUBTITLE !!!!!! The whole play is full of foreshadowing. This is more than just a single 'ghost story' experience. By unlocking different endings, it can subvert your established imagination and give you up to two completely different thoughts. 'Haunted House: Locksmith on the First Floor' is a unique work. Players will play Li Cheng in the public housing estate 'Cheong Wing Building'. This young security guard will be in this mysterious building. Experience an unforgettable and exciting adventure. Background The background of the story is set in a residential building that is about to be demolished and rebuilt. Since there are still a few residents who have not moved out, the main task of the protagonist is to collect the 'relocation consent' from the remaining residents. However, in the process, he discovers There is something strange everywhere in the building, and every resident seems to have various weird behaviors. At the same time, various terrifying ghosts are rumored to live in the building, making Li Cheng's exploration process full of fear and challenges. Unit The first unit of the game will focus on a locksmith who lives on the first floor. Players will need to do their best to get the locksmith to move out of the building and solve the mysteries. Every choice in the game will affect the development of the story, leading to a variety of different endings, allowing players to enjoy a richer gaming experience. It all depends on the player whether the residents live or die, and whether the protagonist Li Cheng can see through the truth and overcome the difficulties. Game features -Probably the only long story game with Hong Kong as the background on this store. -The entire plot is dubbed in Cantonese, giving you the most authentic style. -3D modeling and production of public housing buildings for a more outstanding visual experience. -The game has a complete story line and multiple endings. Some truths may need to be played several times to unlock. ​

In Haunted House, players take control of Lyn Graves, the precocious niece of legendary treasure hunter Zachary Graves. Lyn visits her uncle's mansion with her closest compatriots, only to find the house overrun with ghouls and monsters who quickly grab and spirit away her friends. In order to free her uncle and her friends, and capture all the supernatural foes, Lyn must find the shattered pieces of a magical urn and put them back together to contain the troublesome poltergeists.

Through procedurally generated room layouts, shifting walls, unpredictable enemy placements, and unique ghostly encounters, Lyn must creep, sneak, and dash her way through hordes of ghouls and eerie ectoplasms in order to locate her friends and uncle.

Also well designed because not only do you have to beware of the boss itself, but you also have to beware of your surroundings otherwise you might die. The Story is good and the game has two endings. The dialogues are fun. They don't change anything in the game, but they try to make you more interested in the story, and, as I said, they're fun. The game has good humor and it uses it on those dialogues very well. And the soundtrack, it needs to be released ASAP. It goes very well with the combat and the soundtrack is very, very good. I've also noticed a few bugs like if you spam multiple buttons on your controller, the character stands still and doesn't respond to anything, no feedback for 2-3 seconds. _childDocuments_.review: Jokes aside, this game is an indie hidden gem!I do believe this game took inspiration from some other great games, like ’s visceral and quick-paced combat, and ’s plethora of dialogue options and ambience. But that doesn’t make Anomaly Agent any less original, in fact, it feels very distinct and definitely has its own identity!In this game, you play as Agent 70, you work for , a special facility dedicated to containing anomalies that could threaten to uneven the balance and the stability of reality of the very world you live in. Also, your chief is very mean :( .The combat and platforming experience feels very satisfying and responsive, and it only gets better as your character progresses, in fact, your character can even  anomaly powers from the bosses you defeat! Opening up a wide variety of new combos, yes, this game also has combos! ! And you can get  crazy with it!Things might be a little tough at the start, even in normal mode, but as long as you put effort into it, you’ll get better. Being at a sliver of health will put you at the edge of your seat, and leaving a tough battle as the last man standing just feels  satisfactory.Pro Tip: You can hold crouch and then input a walking direction, you slowly walk like a badass.The level design is great, and I seldom find myself confused about what to do, the design also incentivises level exploration, leaving you to find things that might help ease your journey, not only at the beginning, but also towards the middle of the game and the end of it.The storytelling and worldbuilding are equally surreal and fun, and I love it! The witty references embedded in the experience and dialogue as well as the beautifully designed levels make it all the more memorable of a game. It is very evident the developers put a  of love into this game, both dialogue & asset-wise and just in general. And the soundtrack? Oh, what a soundtrack! They are pretty energetic and some even catchy, they'll definitely put you in the mood for the game for sure! They fit each level & occasion very well, in my opinion. Currently, there are no parkour/platforming upgrades that can be obtained, but this does not devalue or take away from the parkour/platforming experience, and to be fair, it doesn’t need any, as it already feels very good as-is.Took me about 6:30 hours to complete the game, you might be able to complete it in less than that, but I’d recommend not to rush this experience and take your time exploring this game and what it has to offer.Overall, I think this is a great game, the characters are funny and some even charismatic!. The progression system is intuitive, you have quite a bit of agency when it comes to selecting upgrades, and the subsequent story and dialogue can be influenced by your choices. Overall a very captivating game! I don't regret a single cent spent in this game.(Personally, I bought this game while on sale, but the original price seems rather affordable compared to other indie games, which seem to be quite money-hungry nowadays)Well, watcha waitin’ for? Go get this game!And if you can’t right now… Wrestler will be waiting for you!Thank you if you’ve read it this far.This is my mini love letter to this game and its devs, and if the devs ever get to read this, I just want to say thanks for making such a fun game! Much love.

_childDocuments_.review: I have been enjoying Enis Kirazoğlu's content for over 6 years now. Enis is the head of Pew Pew Games, the developer of this game. At the same time, he's a highly famous YouTuber. I have always liked his personality, that was the main reason I have been watching ever since. Let alone his character, he is a gamer who has experienced 100s of games and critiqued them many times. So since he announced that he was developing his first game alongside a team, I kept looking forward to it to this day. So did Enis, Furkan Kirazoğlu and their team work wonders? Is Anomaly Agent a great game? The answer is unfortunately no. But it's certainly an impressive debut indie game. It has nice visuals with cool pixel art. I liked that there were way more bosses and mini-bosses than I expected from a game this sized. The animations look good and the controls feel okay. I especially like the parry mechanic, a fun addition to the game. It has some ideas on the level design, but they feel basic. There are cool easter eggs. They tried to diversify the levels in terms of background design making most levels look distinct from each other. But there is no wow factor to the art, like in games like Owl Boy, Blasphemous, or Dead Cells. Speaking of pixel art games, Anomaly Agent is heavily inspired by Katana Zero, which is not a bad thing. Every single game takes inspiration from others. The game's design, the level design, the storytelling, the visuals, the dialogue boxes, the dialogue themselves, and even the text fonts are very reminiscent of Katana Zero. But their gameplay and storytelling differ from each other. Differently from Katana Zero, Anomaly Agent is an action-adventure brawler. It's a game where you mainly use melee combat to defeat enemies and you rarely use the guns because of the ammo restrictions. Ironically, almost %90 of the skill tree consists of gun upgrades, so purchasing upgrades is kinda useless. Thus I have never felt the "I am getting stronger" at any point of the game. I think the main issue of Anomaly Agent is something else though. It is its tempo and pacing. You are frequently interrupted by the dialogue and the cutscenes. And the dialogues are not few. I know the developers wanted the player to interact with the story but seriously, I think this decision has done more harm to the experience than good. The game never lets the player smoothly enjoy the gameplay. This shocked me cause I have heard many times Enis complaining about indie games telling needlessly much "story". The dialogue is not bad, they tried their best to deliver a fun narrative. But the writing and the storytelling are not that good. Celeste is a good example of what I am trying to explain here. Amazing gameplay combined with minimal storytelling yet had memorable characters and an impactful story. Another issue of Anomaly Agent is enemy placement in its level design. The enemies are often placed very tightly or misplaced, causing a chaos-like gameplay sequence, where the player has to spam roll to dodge countless attacks coming at them. These encounters usually result in unfair damage to the player's health bar and, more importantly, the flow of the gameplay. This reminds me of The Callisto Protocol or Lords of the Fallen (2023). Another game that Enis specifically criticized for this very reason, strangely. Special abilities are another problem. Because you are immobilized when using them, you take damage. There had to be a short invincibility window to prevent cheap deaths. I liked some tracks in the soundtrack like the main theme, but nothing much else. The music could have been better. Regardless of my criticisms, I think Anomaly Agent is a quality game, especially for the first game of an indie studio! I shared my criticisms because I saw no one mention these problems when I checked. Also, this is how I review games. "Brutally honest". I recommend Anomaly Agent, give it a chance on a sale, at least. Anomaly Agent is definitely a way up in the Turkish game development sector.Follow My

_childDocuments_.review: I just wish there was no difficulty option. I started on and played a big portion of this game on "hard" difficulty. It adds a challenge, that is for sure but it is for the cost of fun. Let me explain:Certain actions let you stagger enemies thus opening up windows for options like squeezing in a combo you see fit or deflecting a bullet coming from the other side, this all happens in the heat of the action and it is fun to perform combos of your choice and see them success or fail. The core gameplay loop is centered around creating these windows according to the given enemy types and the environment. But when you play on hard difficulty, after you die in an action sequence, assessment of the situation comes down to "precise inputs" every time. Only one set of inputs would bring you the victory. The reason for that is, that the "staggering" concept in which the combat system of this game is a main element, is almost completely thrown out the window by the hard difficulty setting reducing its duration significantly. There is just not enough room for the frames of some follow-ups when your target was stunned for a quarter of a second instead of two seconds (compared to normal difficulty). This "challenge by artificial difficulty" makes a very fun part of the game just disappear, unfortunately.Other than this one complaint, I enjoyed this game. I believe having some humble expectations was effective in that. But even though I booted up the game without grand expectations, it managed to keep me engaged through various aspects of it that all have been done meticulously and passionately, resulting in me beating this game in one sitting! Well done. Well played. ^u^

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Anomaly Agent put me through a rollercoaster of emotions and I’m still not quite sure whether or not I actually enjoyed playing it. When I first saw screenshots and trailers for the game, I was pretty much immediately hooked. It looked like a somewhat slower paced take on the side-scrolling beat’em up action of Katana Zero with a similar neon-infused visual style and some dope electronic music. Playing for a few minutes was enough to tell that this was indeed the vibe that Anomaly Agent was going for. However, there are some fundamental differences, that set this game apart from games like Katana Zero. Step by step, you unlock a wide range of abilities to deal with your enemies. It starts fairly traditional with beating up bad guys with your fists while dodging or parrying attacks. Soon enough, your arsenal of attacks is enriched by all kinds of gadgets that you can use in battle. Initially, I thought this was pretty cool. Even though I love Katana Zero, I have to admit that it is fairly limited in terms of gameplay variety. You have your sword to attack and deflect. You can turn back time and use items that lie around in the environment. That’s it. In this game however, you have a million ways to deal with any given situation. Unfortunately, this led to me being overwhelmed by the sheer number of abilities. To make this clear, let me give you an overview of all the ways in which you can approach a battle situation. You can attack normally, use a combo-attack which comes in the form of a staff-, sword-, or hammer-attack, jump-attack, throw a boomerang, throw and electrified boomerang, throw a boomerang to trigger environmental traps, use one of 3 finisher moves, or shoot a weapon that you picked up from an enemy all while dodging or parrying your way through the level. This was all a bit too much for my old brain :D To be fair, I have to admit that most situations can be resolved in any way you wish. The game doesn’t force you to use a specific combo or weapon but lets you fight the way you want using the moves you feel comfortable with. Still, there were situations in the game where I felt like I just couldn’t act fast enough or didn’t use the moves that would be perfect for the situation. I played this game on the Steam Deck and my hands were cramping up after each session (about 1-1.5h each) since I had to fumble around with the controls so much. This is all amplified in the boss battles. Again, at first they were quite promising and I would still say that most bosses were fun and played around with a cool gimmick or mechanic. However, towards the end of the game, the final battles were a bit tedious at best and a horrible and frustrating slog at worst. This brings us to another point of criticism which is the pacing of Anomaly Agent. Even though the game is quite short (about 5h), it didn’t really offer anything new or exciting after the 3-hour mark and definitely felt like it overstayed its welcome a bit. There’s this feeling that sometimes, during a platformer section or a fight, there’s just one or two screens too many. I wish the game had cut some of these sections and switched to new parts of the levels sooner. Would I still recommend this game? I would say that if you like fast-paced action platformers with beat’em up elements and a retro neon-vibe with pumping electronic music in the background, you should give this game a try. The story and overall writing weren’t doing anything special for me which also goes for the more humoristic storytelling. But the gameplay was good enough to entertain me all the way till the end. It’s not nearly as good as Katana Zero or Hotline Miami but it’s still an impressive debut title from a small indie studio which absolutely deserves some recognition.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game in hard and hard+ mode (mostly offline) and I want to share my thoughts.First of all, as you can see from the photos, the game looks very similar to Katana Zero. That's why I started wondering if I was going to play a katana zero clone, however, since combat is 1000 miles away than katana zero the game feels different and refreshing. Even though choices you make don't affect the story, the jokes are entertaining and I liked the overall story. The music was composed specifically for the game, and although it's not perfect, it's beautiful. There are small puzzles and parkour sections in the game, but they are basic and doesn’t improve overall game experience. The locations and enemies seem nice at first, but it gets a little repetitive towards the end. The strongest aspect of the game is the fluidity and pleasure of combat. In order to pass the levels, especially in hard mode, you need to follow the movements of your enemies and parry and dodge them at the right time. When you add the fun of hitting enemies, combat becomes a real deal. Considering that it is cheap and indie, I recommend you to try it if you like this type of games. It’s the first game of this studio so I’d say let the developers cook the second game.Score : 8/10Pros: Combat, Fun story, Price.Cons: Repetitive areas and enemies, Start of the game feels so basic.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly I didn't expect to like this game as much as I did as l'd purchased it just to support the developers. I'm only 1/3 of the way through the game. Despite my short playtime and low familiarity with the genre l have some things to say about it.On the gameplay front the game does a phenomenal job. It is a solid action game to the core and that shows in the combat system. A couple creative decisions made during the development play to the games strengths (like the enemy merging gimmick and the dodge not breaking combos) and add a layer of tension and complexity to the combat. You have to move fast, dodge bullets, block at the right time all with very precise timing (the PC's responsive controls allow for that preciseness)as your character can only take a couple hits without biting the dust, and in the middle of all that you have to strategize in which order you're going to take out the enemies lest 2 identical ones merge and become a single stronger foe making it all the more difficult for you to stay alive. It is exhilarating. At least that’s what it’s been until now (at 2hrs) and I’m looking forward to what's to come.As for the story, it is pretty good. There are some unexpected funny bits of it that catch you off guard and so far it’s intriguing enough to keep me playing. Apart from the amazing soundtrack and very cool character arts you see when you’re first introduced to new enemies I think this is all the praise I can give to the game for now. Of course I didn’t like every aspect of it and the game has its fair share of problems, some of which being;- The progression system of boss encounters. Bosses have multiple phases but there is a checkpoint placed after each one. Imo a souls-like approach would’ve worked better here. Of course it would up the difficulty a bit but I truly believe the game would’ve benefited from having uninterrupted full length boss battles.- Despite most of the enemy attacks being well telegraphed there are some that feel unfair, when engaging in close combat with gunner enemies for example some of their attacks feel off. Idk how to put it into words exactly but it’s there.-The UI being an eyesore -The dialogue could have had sound effects. I know there were budget constraints but you could’ve at least added some reaction sounds. It would add to the immersion (groans,humphs,grunts etc.)   But these aren’t at all dealbreakers and can be overlooked, especially this being the developers’ first game. Speaking of, good job to the folks at Phew Phew Games for putting out such a well made game with a team of only 3 people.Well that’s all for today. If I have anything else to add I’ll update this post.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the first game by Turkish YouTuber Enis Kirazoglu and Phew Phew Games. Due to Türkiye's currency being highly devalued, the Turkish gaming industry is quite weak. Despite this, Anomaly Agent has been added to quality Turkish-made titles such as Demonologist and Contain.The gameplay is quite enjoyable, of course, playing with a controller is a must to maximize the enjoyment of the game. I've only had half an hour of experience with the game, but even that half an hour of experience showed me that this game really has potential. I will also update my review after I finish the game.The illustrations are nice, and the dialogs that you will laugh often are well placed in the game. The accessibility settings allow you to turn off and on a sign indicating enemy attacks, screen flash and screen shake.I play games like this on easy mode, because it's more important for me to be immersed in the story. As someone who is not used to using a controller, I found some parts quite difficult, even on easy mode.Since the price of the game is at a very affordable level, I can characterize it as a game that everyone can experience. Give the game a chance and discover how much fun you can have.

_childDocuments_.review: Barely saved by its low price, Anomaly Agent is a basic action platformer game with above average game feel and not much else. Levels are pretty uninteresting, enemies only come in two types and boss fights are irritating. Tried to make it to the end but the Alpha Defender boss fight with the endless floating platforms got so boring that I couldn't stand it any longer.Encounter design is altogether a problem - it never really feels like there is a design vision behind the decisions made. Feels like devs were having a lot of fun with wonky mechanics, fun narrative quips and level elements that make the player feel stupid for trying something different. But there wasn't much fun to be had on the player side beyond the basic, visceral fun of the combat.If you have time to spend on a game that is certainly not groundbreaking, get this game. Otherwise keep your money for better indie games. Anomaly Agent is a barely fine attempt for a debut and I am hopeful that the team can do better things in the future - but not necessarily today.

_childDocuments_.review: The game I expected to finish in one sitting. Yes, actually it was like that, but I played for 7 hours.A production that is really ideal in terms of playing time and has done a good job for its price.First of all, I would like to state that it could have been a crappy game because it would already be played and sold thanks to the recognition of Mr Enis Kirazoğlu, but the team really tried and tried to do the best and it makes you feel it.I started to note the bugs I saw when I first entered the game, such as blocking and not hitting while hitting, and not being able to escape while avoiding at the most critical moments, especially when double hitting. There were patch that the team immediately updated and renewed and solved these problems, I did not come across a fatal error.The team really laboured and although they could have made some parts simple, I liked that they tried to make those parts as beautiful as they wanted. It is clear that they are trying not to make a game but to make a good job.Apart from that, the level of humour was just right for me, for example, the fact that there is a feature such as being rude for money is very cheesy and funny. For example, throwing kartvisit in the first episodes are very well thought out and nice details. Apart from that, I laughed a lot at the jokes made by the characters, I liked making fun of the little brat and other absurd characters. In the loop where we were in disguise, while asking questions to robots while trolling the robotic robotic game, it was very funny that it suddenly said CATCH. For example, when the hooded man turns into an aggressive state, the jokes such as the hooded man coming out as WITHOUT A HOOD are very good.I was happy that the characters I found ridiculous in the game made sense at the end, except that the story and concept was good, but when you come to the end of the game, you establish a little connection with the characters because you are trying to understand something until the end of the game. 1 hour before the end of the game, I thought something like I couldn't connect with the characters, so a little more actually the story could have been intense when I was in the game.Anomaly Agent has never repeated itself, I congratulate the game designer here because just when I thought it was boring and repetitive, I came up with a brand new gameplay. And the game is very comprehensive in this regard in order to avoid repetition. Special abilities really increase the pleasure of the game. It is nice that the side characters find meaning and develop with the story. The disguise scenes were very good, giving a sense of secrecy is exactly what I expect from an agent game, if they had more of this in the game, something good could have come out. Maybe it came to their minds later and they added such a thing.There are loops that we solve the game not only by fighting but also by dialogues, those places were very nice and it would have been nice if they fed this feature to the game.Bosses did not repeat themselves, only the first boss reminded me of the web-based games I used to play, the explosion effect was funny.Features such as environmental death added a nice taste to the game, apart from that, the merging of enemy characters and the ability to stop it also added a very nice colour.Apart from that, there is another detail that caught my eye, you could have made this portal design more beautiful, I couldn't help saying that the design felt very lousy, so don't misunderstand me, if it was something that came out once, I would say okay, but the general game could have been made more beautiful on flying from portals .(.....If I come to the art design part of the game, it was really beautiful that I didn't expect, I said that some really nice designs were made in some scenes, I really liked the design part, in general, nothing caught my eye.The music of the game was really good, especially in some scenes, I really liked the music that came out when they wanted to give chills.Finally, if I were to liken the game to a game, I felt the Katana Zero inspiration, some sequences reminded me, whether it was the dialogues and the character's progress by discovering himself, and as my own interpretation, the game got faster and faster in fighting, it was slow at first, but as I opened the powers, it got faster, but knowing that it was difficult, it would be very nice if it was faster, I would feel the action more clearly.Yes, it was a very professional work, I congratulate the whole team and I want the team to continue in this business because I liked, understood and liked the vision. I would like to thank Enis Kirazoğlu and his team, whose game taste and humour I like very much, for their efforts and contributions to the country in this sector, hoping to see more such beautiful productions......I have to say I laughed so hard at the pets of the Pew Pew Games's in the credits :D damn.

_childDocuments_.review: A little too much button mashing for me. I didn't feel like the combat was very deep. Mostly mash X, occasionally toss in some gun shots at the end of your mash X combos. Or use whatever long cooldown skills you've unlocked to do some area damage. Parrying was easily spammable and dodging was hit or miss. Sometime's I get hit mid-dodge. Sometimes I'd roll right through the attack. Fighting groups was kind of a visual mess. The pixel art was decent but the animations were kind of choppy and hard to read. There's the ! above their head when they're about to attack but I found it was almost too much notice. I kept parrying too early. If I didn't see it pop up, then I had no idea how long before dude was actually going to attack. Once their attack starts, you're getting hit because there's like 1 animation frame between idle and attacking frames. Oh and the story was a bit too goofy. Pure sarcasm from nearly every line. I enjoy puns and jokes but every line was just empty sarcasm and I didn't really capture that the story was going anywhere serious. I know it's based on the 80's action genre but still, it felt like an over-exaggerated generic 80's movie where the entire plot is cheesy one-liners.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game was fun and dynamic with its first 2 hours (that time is really generous), the story was not really that captivating with some weird character choices, and story line beats. The game should've ended with it's first 2 hours probably, the game's  feels like was made with the sole purpose of making the game longer, the bosses were mostly uninspired and overall enemy diversity was not enough for a game that I spent around 4 hours. Other than that the "comedy" of the dialogues and game was poorly implemented, but that is a personal opinion. The art style while it was captivating at times, there was a lot of rookie mistake, for example: and feels like the main character's main style compared to all the other characters in the game was weird. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this indie gem of a game! It's a delightful 2D side-view action RPG that punches way above its weight. The music is simply enchanting, setting the perfect mood for every adventure. The script is witty and entertaining, keeping me engaged and eager to uncover every bit of the story. And the game mechanics are surprisingly smooth and enjoyable, making every battle and exploration a blast. For a low-budget indie game, it has exceeded all my expectations and delivers everything it set out to do with flying colors! I appreciate the effort put into this project, and it's clear the developers poured their hearts into it. I'm eagerly looking forward to their future game projects, as they've shown great potential with this one!

_childDocuments_.review: The story is short, but well written and funny. I enjoyed the characters and the narrative choices involved. Having the option to be nice or mean to people and it affecting your ability progression is an interesting way of encouraging the player to think about what they are saying. Combat is interesting. Enemies don't suffer hit stun, so you're forced to learn dodge/parry timings while mixing in basic attacks and special abilities. The cool part about this though is that your reward meter will go up for finishing the chain as defending yourself does not interrupt the progression of your combo chain (that is, your basic attack is 3 animations: A, B, and C. You will not restart at attack A for dodging. Instead you'll go to the next in the sequence and get a reward for finishing the whole set.) This as a whole made me want to keep practicing as the game gives you new weapons and abilities at a good pace while it introduces its mechanics so there's always a cool reward ahead and something new to learn.The platforming is creative. Don't have much to say about that, as I'm not a fan of platforming, but it didn't detract from the experience to much.All in all? Great game. Buy it full price.

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent is a fun little action platformer with a great sense of style.  It doesn't take itself too seriously, and has solid pixel work combined with a great vibe.  The action is pretty intense and if you just try and mash you will get smoked.  That being said it is not one of those action games that asks you to be perfect, you can slop through it a little bit and still be okay.  The plot involves crazy time travel shenanigans, and the main character give no f**ks, it all works together pretty well and makes for a good old four hour romp, priced just right at $12.  I enjoyed myself.  7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Since it was made by a turkish developer that i follow for years and years, the main reason i bought this game is not because i wanted to support him, i am actually very into this genre and i thought it would at least feed my desire to play these kind of games for a little bit since i know it wouldn't be fair to judge it at the same level as games made by huge companies. The funny thing is i didn't even buy it before finishing it, i used it via family sharing from my friends account and bought the game to be able to write this review and support the creator, yet still i was quite disappointed, there are positive things i want to say about this game but more are negative, the gameplay is sometimes confusing like walls coming at you, developer decided it would be a brilliant idea to sometimes show how long the wall is going to open, and sometimes not, other than that on city levels it is way too confusing to see which buildings are supposed to be floor and which aren't, it is quite frustrating that i've died not more than 20 times and all of them were because either i got confused by what floor is and what isn't or i was killed by a wall i didn't know how long was gonna be when it opens. Gameplay wise the combos are not good and the game difficulty is reaaaally easy, if you have played and finished more than 5 games like this you will have no issue with the most difficult difficulty, like i have. But all these could be forgiven by the fact tht story is way too short, just as i started to enjoy the story, it ended. I was able to finish it on one go, which can be understandable but it isn't because IT IS NOT INTERESTING neither does it have any Replayability except for multiple endings and New Game + which does not really matter to me since i want to stay out of this games way as far as possible. Now for the positive things, it is good considering it was made by a very small team on their off-days or when they had time to put work on it. Yeah, thats all the positive things i can say about this game, gameplay is meeeeh when there are way too many alternatives if you haven't finished them all like i have that do the combos and attacks or platforms even way better. Story is honestly really really not interesting at all even though they try to make a little plot twist in the end, all i thought was "oh well this was called for and not interesting or anything that makes the story rich at all". And don't even get me started on the German localisation, i am really hoping the the "jokes" are not this unfunny in original version, if it is that way i take it back and make it another minus for the whole game, the german localisation is terrible as usual in other cases though, i am really uncertain if people who translates games to german nowadays are german even, i couldn't stand the german version so much i changed to turkish after 45 minutes of playing.Now the result is, do i recommend you to buy this game? Depends; If you are reaaaaaallly hungry and have no other alternative left, it is going to make you play and finish it one go and you will not enjoy it, but it will make you stay away from this kind of game in the end, so money well spent since you already don't have anything to play in this genre. If you are one of those people who wants to buy and play the game just because of the team behind it, sure, go ahead and be a fanboy, it is not a bad thing they are  a relatively small team and i believe even though they ♥♥♥♥♥♥ up in my opinion, with what they had this is a good work and i want to see them do better (please) and improved games which are not considered dull when you look at the other types of games of the same kind.

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent - 7/10As the first beat-em-up I've ever played I did not know what to expect, but this game proves to be a stellar entry to the genreFun and likeable characters, a phenomonal soundtrack, and incredibly stylishThe story is unique, you essentially play as an scp foundation agent dealing with an anomaly. Walk cycles are the most obvious examples but some area's are a little drab, especially most of the boss arenas, but it doesn't get in the way of the fun of turning clones into mist.Enemies are reused frequently, there's only about 4 types really, which can make the gameplay feel a little stale at times, but the intractable environmental hazards make up for it.It does do an excellent job at making you feel like a badass though. Dive into the depths of a rich world, confront conflicts to the beat of synthwave music, shape the story with your choices, and overcome obstacles with acrobatic movements. In this adventure where time is warped, use specialized equipment to halt anomalies! Anomaly Agent immerses players in a deep world with its cyberpunk aesthetics and atmosphere. Cityscapes, neon lights, and technological details enrich the game's ambiance. Accompanying synthwave music enhances the cyberpunk atmosphere, intensifying action moments and completing the overall gaming experience. Anomaly Agent offers players various acrobatic movements to overcome obstacles. Quick reflexes and agility allow players to handle challenging situations. Players engage in battles in a world where time is warped. This mechanic provides strategic advantages within the game and introduces new dimensions to puzzles that need solving. Anomaly Agent provides players with various specialized equipment to effectively combat anomaly events. The game's cyberpunk aesthetic and synthwave music offer players an attractive and immersive atmosphere. Acrobatic movements contribute to a dynamic and enjoyable gaming experience.Anomaly Agent stands out as a captivating cyberpunk-themed action-platformer with its atmospheric design, synthwave music, and acrobatic gameplay. Features such as the depth of the story and specialized equipment contribute to providing players with an impressive and engaging experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Good soundtracks and style, but severe issues in combat, level design and accessibility, which make the game chaotic, frustrating and repetitive. It is especially repetetitive in its macro-patterns.In more details:• Combat- Anomaly Agent immediately introduces far too many different buttons and combos which are needed to fight, which feel overwhelming especially in the first half of the game.- The majority of the game is composed by groups of enemies in small environments, which the combat system cannot handle too well. It makes certain key mechanics pointless and it requires to keep dodgind and dodging (as the enemies are not synchronized between themselves) without giving a chance to build momentum.- Hitboxes are not always very clear.• Level Design- Although the game starts by looking good, it soon starts to repeat the same style of environments and platofrming sections.- Platforming is relatively strict and it easy to fall, especially considering that you have to fight on many small platforms, and falling off of a platform is considered instant death which will load the latest checkpoint.- To players who are not well-versed in platform games, most levels of Anomaly Agent will feel frustrating in an unrewarding way, while for navigated platformer gamers they will just feel like a boring chore.• Accessibility- With so many buttons needed and so many unsynchronized enemies in small rooms, the game is basically unplayable for anyone who doesn't have fast enough reaction times and reflexes. Difficulty options are there, but even playing at Easy, the game is not "Easy" at all.- No form of accessibility for checkpoints, platforming sections or combat.

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent is one of those games which are easy to learn but hard to master.I know that many will at first be unsettled by the mobs resilience towards their attacks in terms of not getting stunned easily (the player not being able to interrupt their attacks by attacking first), but that is one of the very things that make this game a unique piece among the multitude likes of it. After the first 45-60 minutes, the player gets a hang of the "feel" of the combat, and then things begin to flow. Each hit returns a satisfactory feedback, and the combat toolset is complex enough to make sure that each encounter is tinged with a sense of variety and freshness. If you would like to spend a couple of fun hours playing a 2D action/platform game with tasty dialogues, Anomaly Agent is your game.Pros:+ Satisfactory combat+ Fresh level designs+ Fun little dialogues+ Some really fun boss fightsCons:- The visuals strained my eyes for some reason (this might have something to do with me)- Levels at times feel as if they are dragging for too long; I would rather have shorter levels, each ending with a boss fight- Encounters with mobs sometimes get too chaotic (but that could be in the nature of the genre)TL;DRFor couple of fun hours, I would definitely recommend this game.Such a promising debut for the future of Phew Phew!

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent: A Critical Review"Anomaly Agent" is an action platformer developed by Phew Phew, blending retro aesthetics with modern gameplay mechanics. The game stands out with its pixel graphics and fast-paced action. However, like any game, "Anomaly Agent" has its strengths and weaknesses.Visual and Art DesignThe visual design of "Anomaly Agent" takes players on a nostalgic journey with pixel graphics inspired by old games. While some players may appreciate this style, those looking for the graphical richness offered by modern games might find it lacking. The game world and character designs are detailed and meticulously crafted, but some players may find the graphics repetitive and lacking in variety.GameplayIn terms of gameplay, "Anomaly Agent" offers a challenging adventure filled with platforming elements and enemies. However, the game's difficulty level can sometimes be inconsistent. Some sections may be overly challenging, while others can be unexpectedly easy. This inconsistency might cause players to become disengaged. Additionally, the control mechanics can sometimes feel clunky, which can be frustrating, especially during precise platforming sections.StoryThe game's story revolves around an agent's survival and mission completion in a world filled with enemies. However, in terms of storytelling and character development, "Anomaly Agent" can sometimes feel superficial. The depth of the story and the background of the characters could have been elaborated further.Sound and Music DesignOne of the strongest aspects of the game is undoubtedly its sound and music design. "Anomaly Agent" boasts an atmospheric and captivating soundtrack. The music in each level successfully draws the player into the game and perfectly complements the action. Similarly, the sound effects support the retro vibe of the game and positively enhance the overall experience.Conclusion"Anomaly Agent" can be an appealing option for players who enjoy retro games and challenging platformers. However, it has some shortcomings in terms of gameplay and story. If the criticisms regarding graphics and control mechanics are addressed, the game experience could be much more satisfying. The sound and music design, on the other hand, are the game's brightest points and truly deserve praise in this area.

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed Anomaly Agent quite a bit. The combat was snappy and fairly intuitive, though I found myself constantly forgetting to parry, which is a pretty integral mechanic if you don't want to repeat sequences over and over. The biggest highlight of the game is its soundtrack -- it may not necessarily be anything brand new, but it's catchy and extremely fitting for the setting and helps to give the game its smooth rhythm. The story has its moments, though I'd say it really relies on the quirkiness of its setting, characters and the fluidity of a time travel-based narrative to fill some gaps in the plot. While I thought the dialogue was endearing overall, the humor is very hit or miss. Thankfully the tone is fairly consistent and the branching options in each conversation kept things interesting.My only real complaint about the game is its art direction, which is EXTREMELY inconsistent. The pixel work varies from being good to fantastic, though at points the simplicity of it can come off as a bit lazy (looking at you, title screen). Environments are visually interesting but very, very repetitive, and the character animations, while low on frames and simplistic, still manage to pack a decent punch, with certain moves having much more impact than others (the giant fist comes to mind). Sadly, the worst part of the overall presentation has to be the character portraits that pop up periodically throughout the story. They're drawn in an amateurish western comic book style and most of them are straight up ugly. This is my personal opinion of course, but the illustrations are bad enough that I think they bring down the entire game, especially with how ridiculously often they get re-used. It might not bother other players, and it certainly wasn't enough to put me off the game as a whole, but they really stand out in the worst way and could stand to be replaced entirely. I'm sure much higher quality concept art could be commissioned for not much money. There appears to be replay value based on the different story paths you encounter throughout the game, as well as a new game plus that I unlocked after beating the game the first time, but the ending I did get was ultimately uneventful and underwhelming. However, Anomaly Agent's gameplay is good and meaty enough that I'll probably give it a few more shots to see where else the story might go. Hopefully it doesn't disappoint.All in all, the game is worth your time and money, despite my few squabbles with its art direction. I'm interested to see what else the developer puts out, and will keep my eye on them going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: I first played this in a Steam Next Fest a while ago and am glad to finally play the full release. The story is fun and quirky, but I think they could have spent more time developing the characters and premise more if they had wanted to. However, I know the game is more action-focused and the fast pace of the plot helps keep things moving along. The gameplay is really solid; it's simple but still satisfying. There are enough combos and special moves to keep things interesting as you defeat the game's various enemies. Some encounters can be rather challenging, though, as you're often faced with clusters of enemies attacking from both sides with both melee and ranged attacks. Overall, though, it's not overly difficult and is still quite fun. I genuinely appreciate how enemies reliably warn you with a "" to notify you when to parry, as well as the fairly generous dodge roll ability. It's rather reminiscent of Dead Cells in that way and I wish more action games were like that. The campaign is relatively short and can be easily beaten within 4-5 hours depending on your skill. Even so, I still think this is a good game for anyone interested in 2D beat-'em-ups.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit: I did get a chance to jump into the Rogue Agent roguelite mode, and I'm enjoying it so much that I'm changing this review from negative to positive. The assets from the main game are implemented somewhat how you'd expect - backgrounds and enemies are randomly pulled from various areas, and upgrades are randomly pulled from the campaign's permanent skill tree - but, without the frustrations of the main campaign's shortcomings, Anomaly Agent's extremely fun core combat can shine through. You can also acquire the main game's combo chains (which were always a strong point) as permanent upgrades that last more than one run to help you get a bit farther each attempt.For a free update, Rogue Agent is executed about as good as it could be, and it very well may double the hours you can reasonably expect to spend with the entire game - that's remarkable. And, frankly, I'm having more fun with Rogue Agent than the main campaign - it shows off the high points of the game (combat, art, and music) without a lot of interfering design noise.So, overall, whether your drawn to the campaign, Rogue Agent, or both, I do think there's enough good stuff here to recommend the game writ-large. I'll leave my original review, which has my thoughts about the campaign, below, for posterity. -----------------------Anomaly Agent makes a very strong first impression thanks to its unique and charming style. A sense of earnestness permeates the entire game - while "weird" media can sometimes come off as contrived, Anomaly Agent has a weirdness about it that feels totally genuine. While playing, you get the sense that every quirk is simply an idea the developers had, liked, and put in the game. Unfortunately, Anomaly Agent wore thin on me pretty quickly. A big culprit is the use of environmental hazards: one-hit instakill mechanics absolutely litter the game, which get very annoying very quickly. The core combat systems are really fun, but the game has a habit of stacking 5-8+ enemies on top of each other at once, which sort of neuters the player's ability to meaningfully craft combos and parries. Platforming sections blur together, as a lack of movement upgrades constrains and homogenizes the design of every platforming section. The dance bar sections in particular were excruciatingly tedious to go through.The pacing of the game is all over the place, too: the downside of cramming a bunch of ideas into a game is that its playspace starts to lack identity. Is it a beat-em-up? Is it a platformer? Is it a stealth game? Is it story-driven? The answer to  all of those questions, to some degree, is yes, but the implementation of each feels random and arbitrary. Rather than taking inspiration from each genre and blending them into something new, Anomaly Agent sort of just pieces random, mechanically-unrelated segments to each other. The execution lacks the elegance of a truly well-designed game.I can tell I'm toward the end of the story, but I just feel sort of... done with the game. I enjoyed the first hour or so, but every successive hour felt worse and worse to the point that I am simply not having fun with the campaign anymore. The new roguelike mode is actually what grabbed my attention, so I may still check that out. But slogging through the story has left a bad taste in my mouth, and I just don't feel like playing anymore. Anomaly Agent has its charms, but it's a bit too messy for me to really enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not know about you but if I got to work and gravity was reversed, I am heading home. Luckily, I have an office job and do not work for a super secret agency that deals with world-ending catastrophes. Speaking of disasters, does said agency even have an agent that could handle gravity on the fritz with a little dash of broken time travel?Developed by Phew Phew Games, Anomaly Agent is a cyberpunk action platformer where you punch, kick, and just cause chaos amidst a retro backdrop and killer soundtrack. Become Agent 70 of the TDY where your boss hates you and your co-workers are not too fond of you. Perhaps it is that warm and fuzzy personality. Somehow, Agent is being promoted today BUT must finish out all current missions including figuring out why gravity has gone on the fritz.I cannot speak to the actual training of TDY agents but Agent 70 can fight. He’s extremely agile and can punch, kick, and dodge without breaking so much as a sweat. Belonging to a super secret agency has its perks too as Agent 70 has a few gadgets at his disposal. First up is the business card. Huh? This is no ordinary business card though. When thrown, it can stun enemies. As you progress through the game, the business card can be upgraded and even electrocute unsuspecting foes or be used to cut wires or reach hard-to-reach buttons/levers/etc. Your briefcase may or may not contain documents (I am leaning towards not) but what it does do is block melee attacks and deflect bullets. Who needs guns when you can just pilfer them off the bodies of enemies? Agent 70 is proficient in all types of firearms and when all else fails, you can just throw the gun at your target. The combat described may seem like it would lend itself to a standard beat ‘em up but it is quite deep while remaining easy to navigate. If you try to just punch and kick your way through everything, you probably will die (even on the lowest difficulty setting). Anomaly Agent’s combat just feels super fluid and smooth and as such, utilizing all the tools at your disposal felt natural. Both melee attacks and weapon attacks make use of combos that can be performed. The longer you can maintain a combo (aka staying aggressive), the more damage you will dish out plus it will earn you more and more coins used for upgrades. The aforementioned blocking and deflecting are also incredibly simple to pull off as the game has a warning system for incoming attacks. I am horrible at using parries in any game (Lies of P made me get better though) but this is more just a responsive button press when the on-screen prompt occurs. Blocking and deflecting can be upgraded later in the game to cause damage and stun making use of it even more worthwhile. You can also just use Agent 70’s roll dodge to avoid everything but you miss out on the satisfaction of stunning an enemy and going all Babe Ruth on him as you send him hurtling to his demise.In addition to the masterful combat the game offers, the platforming was quite enjoyable. Agent 70 is quite agile which can be seen in the responsive controls. There are plenty of lasers to dodge and moving platforms to navigate (perfect places to send enemies over the edge). I will not go into full detail but there are a few “chase” scenes that have you ducking and jumping down a corridor and it was an absolute blast each time it happened. For those who feel their skills in this type of gameplay are lacking, the checkpoint system is very forgiving. Most restarts will only take you back mere seconds before your death. How do you feel about shaping your narrative? During the story, Agent 70 often must ask/answer questions or participate in conversation with various characters. You can either give a normal response (read: boring) or be a sarcastic wiseass. Now, before you think, I’m just going to be a smartass all the time, there is a point to this. Your response will trigger a reaction from the character you are speaking to. Answering in a manner that is agreeable with this awards you with a positive emotion. Being a jerk earns you negative emotions. These emotions can then be spent on either health upgrades (positive emotions) or more coins (negative emotions) used for upgrades. While it may seem fun to talk back to your boss, sometimes it is worth it to go along with the other person. There does not seem to have a lasting effect on the general plot but it was a fun way to introduce choice into the game.Health upgrades are not just limited to emotions. They can also be found hidden in chests throughout the levels. Every four you collect will increase your total health. It is worth keeping in mind when “gathering” emotions as it costs 5 positive emotions for each upgrade. On the other hand, it only takes 3 negative emotions to exchange for 300 coins. Coins are dropped by enemies and also by items destroyed and found in most chests. Coins are then used to upgrade Agent 70’s ability such as decreasing the recharge time of the business card or increasing the damage of ranged weapons. To access additional tiers of upgrades, one must purchase a set amount from the previous tier. If you are looking for a fun platforming, action-packed brawler with a clever dialogue system and witty humor, look no further than Anomaly Agent. Phew Phew Games has nailed it on all fronts here between the super-responsive controls, fun factor, and retro but futuristic cyberpunk aesthetic. While the campaign is relatively short (approximately 5 hours), there is a new game plus (that costs 0 dollars) allowing you to bring all your upgrades to a new playthrough, and the upcoming Rogue Agent mode (roguelite anyone???). This is worth every penny and one of the first cannot miss titles of 2024. It is available now on PC and Switch.Full review available at

_childDocuments_.review: Well I certainly wasn't expecting this game. I also wasn't expecting to have little to say about it. Tonally something we don't get a lot of. Combat's alright, although the sheer volume of enemies and attacks means I'm often panicking and not using the best moves I could be for the job. But that's a skill issue. Maybe. It's a good game. Functional and stylish. I'm just shocked it's at 97% positive reviews and at nearly 5,000 at those. It doesn't feel  good. Then again, neither is it bad enough to justify a negative review. So yeah, get it.My biggest disappointment is that the business card you get is replaced by a generic boomerang, which is a bit disappointing. It's a shame it doesn't lean into the more agent side of things with your abilities and equipment. The business card and case are neat but then you have some amorphous anomaly bat that, despite being an anomaly, is... just a bat, or a staff, or a hammer, or a sword, and that's not an anomaly; that's just your standard RPG inventory.Also, more seriously, the game's emphasis on two dialogue choices hinders the ability of your Anomaly Agent to exhibit their own personality. For how much the Steam page emphasises "shaping the story", the game only has two endings and bugger all really changes.
