_childDocuments_.review: This game's really fun. I wish there was more depth in its combat system with more combos and weapons, as well as more complex bosses, but what's here is very solid and fun to play with. If anything, it makes me excited for what this studio will make next. This is an extremely solid gameplay foundation that I hope they build upon further in a future game, be it sequel or not. The weakest aspect is, by far, the platforming. It's not bad, but it's very simplistic, a bit clunky, and it ultimately feels pointless. The story, art, and music are all good, but safe. They're not groundbreaking and that's alright. If you like Katana Zero and Sanabi, this is a more light-hearted take on the style.
_childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: Enjoyable game with solid platforming and action mechanics. Introduction of new action mechanics and game elements is good paced and keep the players getting bored. Combat mechanics are also exciting causing rapid pulse. Graphics and musics are complimentary with cyberpunk theme. The game may be challenging sometimes, especially for people who play fast paced action games rarely4.5/5 for an indie game
_childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: This was the best 5.7 hours of my life. My favorite thing about this game was the music.  The game is very fast-paced and the controls feel good. When I lost or made a mistake I knew that it was my mistake and not the game's. Anyway, I want to thank Enis Kirazoglu and everyone in Phew Phew games for this game. When I was 20 I felt like games were getting boring and I was very scared of that feeling. But this game rekindled a fire in my heart for games. Definitely, this is a game worth playing 900 hours. _childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot compare it with similar games as I am unfamiliar with this genre, but I completed the game in one go with an Xbox controller, and I'm writing this review immediately afterward. _childDocuments_.review: A fun story, nice art style and music, combined with a fun gameplay. _childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. Gameplay is actually S tier. And story telling with humor is great. First game fir a indie developer, this is such a gem. I am sure people in genarel love this game and I hope team make some money to develop other games. I really wanna see what their next advanture will be. Good f.job guys and girls and others <3
_childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: I have this as one of the better games I've played in the past few months. The music is up there as some of the best, and the storyline for most plays it's role to introduce you to some really interesting characters and level sequences. Gotta keep kicking that lil imposter! The fighting mechanics are quite good, and towards the end I got the hang of the special abilities although at times it was punishing trying to use them when you're surrounded by many enemies. The boss fights are fun, and for most of the part it's a challenging game without ever being so difficult that you wanted to quit. I loved the little links in the game, such as When the Wrestler calls you a random name but it all comes back later. The upgrade system was pretty average though. Chat to me about indies on twitter if you like!
_childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished the game. It was really fun to play the game, and if you have a day off from work, you can just play it in one go. The length of the game was really great; I am happy that they didn't try to make the game longer by making it very repetitive. I played half of the game with a keyboard and mouse, and I played the second half with the controller. I could say that, for me, the controller experience was much more fun. The soundtrack and the art style of the game were really good; I really enjoyed looking at the small details. The only downside is the story could have a bit more depth into it but considering this game to be the studio's first game, it is really understandable. I wish to see the new mode soon and the upcoming games from this studio.

_childDocuments_.review: A really enjoyable experience that has exceeded my expectations from the team, in terms of both the ideas and their delivery. _childDocuments_.review: Rahat kafayla hikayeyi oturup dinleyeceğiniz zaman yolculuğunu tema alan indie yapım bir oyun. 4 saat süren oynanışında, mekanikleri sürekli yenileyerek oyuncunun eğlence anlayışı yüksek tutulmaya çalışılmış. Ancak yer yer, 'döngü' konusunun işleyişi ile alakalı uzun bir anlatım olunca, oyuncunun tam keyif alacağı noktada oynanışın kesilmesi biraz tat kaçırdı açıkçası. Oynanış eğlenceli, oyun içi atmosfer gerçekten güzel düşünülmüş ve tasarlanmış. Oynanış adına belirteceğim 2 kusur, kendi hissiyatımca, zıplama teknikleri 2 çeşitte de akıcı hissettirmedi oynarken. Gerçekçi karakter tasarımı yönünden ilerlemek düşünülmüş zannımca o yüzden de stüdyo tercihi diyerek çok üstelemiyorum. Hikayeyi beklenmedik şekilde ilerletmek için kafa patlatılmış, yer yer bazı konuşmalar güldürdü, bazıları da karakterleri yaşayan bir birey olarak hissettirdi. Emeği geçen herkesi özverisinden ve ince düşüncelerinden dolayı kutlarım. Araştırmalarıma göre ilk oyununu çıkartan bir stüdyonun yapımıyla karşı karşıyayız. İlk oyun bence 7.2 seviyesinde denebilir. Prince of Persia Lost Crown ile yakın tarihlerde çıkması biraz talihsiz olabilir. Umarım hak ettiği değeri görür.I bumped into the game's videos through XBOX and Nintendo's game premiere videos and in a price like this I thought giving a try would not hurt. It took me 4 hours to finish it and I can say it is a solid game with simple but entertaining mechanics. Not a fan of either types of jumping but in a game with this type of budget I think it is acceptable. The story telling and narrative are creative to some extent.  Level design is quite similar to katana zero but it is not fast paced. Moreover to that, it is much more forgiving when it comes to dying so if you are looking for a challenge throughout the game I'd advise hard option for the optimum experience. It is the first release of the studio so my hopes are up for the future. In my perspective, gamers who have a thing for this genre should give it a try. 7.2/10
_childDocuments_.name: Anomaly Agent

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun game, but it feels really slow in the beginning before you start getting some of your "heavy attacks", once you get through that it starts to really pick up the pace and they become an essential component in the late game.There's an element of getting so good you feel like a god, weaving in and out of a group of enemies, parrying and dodging nearly perfectly, but some of the enemies really put the brakes in the action with incredibly short cooldowns between unparriable ranged attacks that slow down the pace to a crawl. My playthrough was entirely on Hard so it may be more tolerable in lower difficulties.Dying isn't a big deal since you can restart so fast, but some of the screens stubbornly make you sit through the opening dialogue/cutscene while others do not, it's a bit inconsistent and it hurts the game slightly, if you were to keep dying in a forced cutscene arena you'll probably get frustrated really quickly.The bosses were all quite tough except for the two last ones, one was mostly a waiting game, the other was easy, or maybe I had just improved by the end.The music is incredible, kept me going the whole way through.The story was alright, There's two endings, but you only choose from one or the other at the very end, your choices during the game don't matter, which I was fine with, I was playing the game because it was a demanding action experience.Incredible action game that ended up being longer than I expected, incredibly demanding on your focus and inputs on Hard which is exactly what I was looking for.

Bu türü seven biriyseniz düşünmeden alın, oyunu bir kez bitirdim şimdi new game+ ile tekrardan bitireceğim. Ardından da zor mod ile tekrardan new game+ oynamayı planlamaktayım. Gerçekten zevkli bir oyun.It's really proud that such a game came out of our land. However, the review I wrote here is an objective review, completely free of my personal feelings. We should call the good is good and the bad is bad; so that much better things can come out in the future.If you are someone who loves this genre, buy it without thinking, I finished the game once, now I will finish it again with new game+. _childDocuments_.review: I knew the game from what I saw from a few streamers. From the streams I watched, I thought the game controls were a bit clunky. It has truly turned out to be a very, very nice game. The controls are very good, the in-game character development mechanics etc. are very enjoyable. My only criticism would be that the combo bar is in a far corner and I can't follow it during the action. Long story short, even if my motivation for purchasing the game wasn't to support Enis, if I had played the demo of this game, I would definitely have bought itKudos to the developers for their hard work.End game edit: The game's story paints a captivating picture of time paradoxes. You need to make game challenging to extend duration of gameplay)- You can cheese game with Parry but it is ok.- You can't knockback enemies (at least at 1 hour of the game)Grade: 8.5 "Buy this game without hesitation. _childDocuments_.review: I beat the game in one sitting and started NG+ right away. The most obvious issue about the demo was the difficulty, I'm glad they changed it. Now enemies are pushing you to dodge and deflect more, and dodging doesn't interrupt your combos which makes the action nonstop and more fun. Bosses are not that memorable but I enjoyed most of them, especially Alpha Defender and the the last boss were pretty decent. The most disappointing part of the game is platforming, I expected more in terms of both challenge and platforming mechanics. Anyway, I spent a fantastic 6 hours in Anomaly Agent and I can't wait for the next game of Phew Phew Games, because this one proves their potential.

_childDocuments_.review: Anomaly Agent. Bringing retro synthwave tunes and presenting an absolutely smooth gameplay with a pretty interesting story, has stood out in so many aspects in my honest opinion. Putting the popularity of the developers among the Turkish fan base aside, this game includes a lot of quality aspects within the experience it provides. I'll specialize my focus on these various aspects of the game in this review without further due. First of all, there is an astonishing combination between the theme, story and even the soundtracks. These retro synthwave soundtracks fit wonderfully with the theme of cyberpunk which has also been depicted impressively through the pixel design of the game. With these, the story also is very interesting. I've been getting some vibes similar to Hotline Miami's while playing it, though I believe that in Anomaly Agent, you tend to get more "tangible" objectives throughout the progression of the story. Retro soundtracks, an interesting story with a fascinating theme, smooth gameplay and wonderful pixel graphics... There is truly a beautiful combination.As for the mechanics, they are pretty simple as it's satisfying to see your character moving like Jagger. Combos and characteristics improve as the story progresses. With this, unlike the other 2d platformers which often include rogue-like, Anomaly Agent is a pretty quick game where auto-save system is present. It takes 'seconds' to pick up from where you left off in case you die. In conclusion, it's easy to learn, and not really hard to master :)Some additions that I'd personally like to make, includes my thanks and appeciation to the developers. Thank you Enis Kirazoğlu. I wish you and your crew the best in this new sector that you have got yourselves into, as you have done it in style. This here, is a work of art, and I wholeheartedly believe that Anomaly Agent will get popular among the Steam fan base in almost no time. Thank you.Edit: I believe that the last section of the game was made unnecessarily difficult. This is why I won't finish the game as I don't want to spend hours to just get past that single boss fight. I hope that the developers will make a better gameplay review of the whole game before releasing it.

_childDocuments_.review: Cherryson goes Phew Phew!Anyways, I completed the game and here is my serious comment on it:I enjoyed the game in general but the most outstanding part of it for me was its humour. I don't mean it has a crazy sense of humour by that but I find it as the most important aspect of this game. Its humour isn't only in its story but also sprinkled in gameplay too. It has a solid story for a short game which I wouldn't necessarily ask for more. The music and the graphics are pleasant.Isn't there any flaw? Yes there are some. At some chapters when you enter a room your double jump won't work and only solution is to restart the game. Luckily I had to do it only twice. Also after I defeat the first boss I wasn't able to move or do anything as I pressed the interraction button. I had to fight the boss again because of it. Again it happened only once and never occured again.Some may complain that enemies are repetitive and boring but I won't. Progression makes it playable. Only time I got bored while playing this game was final boss. It was easy yet unnecessarily long. I would prefer a harder boss fight instead of doing 3 or 4 moves again and again until he dies. Since I mentioned it I want to add that enemies are not intimidating at all. I played it on normal difficulty and I know I shouldn't be complaining about this without playing hard mode yet at least the bosses could be more intimidating in a way. It would be nice to say "damn I'm ♥♥♥♥♥♥ now" as I see an enemy or boss but it wasn't the case even with the final boss.Last thing could be done better was the distrubition of puzzles/platforms in chapters. They appear often after chapter 2 whilst there isn't as much at first chapters.To sum up; despite the fact that there are things could have done better, Anomaly Agent is a fun game to play and I'd recommend it without a second thought. I believe that Phew Phew games will consider these comments and learn from this experience to come up with a better sequel. Cheers!

name: Balatro
detailed_description: Balatro is a poker-inspired roguelike deck builder all about creating powerful synergies and winning big. Combine valid poker hands with unique Joker cards in order to create varied synergies and builds. Earn enough chips to beat devious blinds, all while uncovering hidden bonus hands and decks as you progress. You’re going to need every edge you can get in order to reach the boss blind, beat the final ante and secure victory. The definitive poker roguelike experience. Endless possibilities - every pick-up, discard and joker can dramatically alter the course of your run. In-depth campaign mode complete with 8 difficulties, as well as challenge and seeded runs. Deftly deploy an array of potent tools: different Decks, Jokers, Tarot cards, Planet cards, Spectral cards, and Vouchers. Use these versatile instruments to ignite a combo frenzy and turbocharge your poker hands, crafting electrifying, adrenaline-fueled synergies. 150 Jokers, each with their own unique abilities 15 Decks with distinct modifiers to choose from for each run 5 potential variants of each Joker which add further abilities 22 Tarot cards variants that can enhance your regular playing cards 11 Planet cards that help level up your possible poker hands 32 Voucher cards to help provide permanent buffs for your current run Immerse yourself in Balatro’s distinctive psychedelic world. Let the synthwave soundtrack wash over you - wind down, escape the daily grind and prepare to enter the ultimate roguelike flow state. Improve your collection and discover new cards and secrets with every single run. Make use of the in-depth stats screen to study your best hands, most used Jokers, and more! Immerse yourself in the CRT fuzz and enjoy detailed, hand-crafted pixel art.

_childDocuments_.review: There was a time when I would walk. Sometimes in the morning, if the sun's flourishes were enough to lure me from my hole, sometimes in the evening in a bid to catch its face once more before it left for the day.There was a time when I would meet friends in coffee shops or pubs for either a cold pint or warm brew. We'd update each other on the highlights of our dispassionately normal lives. I would tell them the true story of how I was kept waiting on a train for three hours due to a small landslip. They would tell me about the rash they had on their arm, that turned out to be a ketchup stain that just required a bit of persistent scrubbing.There was a time when I'd wash things. My car, my dishes, myself.There was a time when I'd chop garlic, boil water, season ingredients, eventually collecting them together on a plate to create a meal.There was a time when at least once a day, I'd lay my head on my pillow in bed, as I thought over every human interaction I'd had that day. I'd question if when I said to Daisy in work "your hair looks nice,"did she think I was suggesting that it usually didn't? or when trying to say "hi" to the random gentleman at the coffee machine, and accidentally spurting "hey!" did he thinking I was condemning his choice of a Mocha? All these thoughts eventually leading to some time asleep.There was a time when I would do my job.There was a time when I would make sure my nails were cut, and teeth were clean. When I scratched an itch and the skin of the scratching finger made zero connection with the itchy flesh, that's when I knew it was normally time to act. When I would breath in and out and every swallow tasted like five day old warm tea mixed with bile, toothpaste would be introduced.There was a time when after placing my mug, throwing the tea bag in (from a much less impressive distance than I'd like), and fetching the milk from the fridge ready to pour in, I would pretend to fight off a platoon of cloned soldiers from a parallel universe with nothing but a single knife and two small imaginary pistols. Then I played Balatro. Now I play Balatro.There is only Balatro.The thought of a power cut throws me into a dissociated state.Because then I would not be able to play Balatro.I tried to stop once. Futile.When I mute the game, I still hear every sound because it has become a part of me now.I briefly fell asleep for 20 minutes. I had dreams of playing Balatro.

_childDocuments_.review: ̣Balatro is a deckbuilding rogue like based on poker where your goal is to play various hand types, spending most of the early game trying to build your deck while also setting up your economy, and focusing on trying to score as high as you can late game.On the earlier stakes, Balatro does a good job at balancing luck and difficulty, and on every single deck you can easily score a win or even go endless if you are playing the white stake.However as the stakes increase, especially around the point you get to purple stake - there is an increase in luck required rather than pure skill - nonetheless, we would say that this game is excellent even on the highest stake, the Golden Stake at providing an interesting challenge and truly testing your ability to make your deck work, and build up a strong economy as a backbone.If you are a fan of roguelikes balanced around skill and luck, deckbuilding games, or poker in general, Balatro is definitely the game for you.

_childDocuments_.review: It got me a good 7 hours of interest. It is poker, without the poker faces. So luck is something that matters a lot in this game. But it is not everything: for starters, there is a small RPG aspect: you have up to 5 jokers in that that can consider your "level ups" / equipment. You have also initially 2 consumables slots that can contain "magical" cards that can change the existing cards, to change suit, or give cards special powers. Jokers may give special powers to cards, powers to other jokers, and some jokers can be "groomed" from humble starts to very strong ones. Also, planet cards can increase the value of hands: for example, you can make a two pair become the most powerful hand in the universe, depending on how you administer these. Again, it is a matter of luck.The goal of the game is to beat a score using a limited number of hands. In the beginning, each poker hand type (pair, two pair, 4 of a kind, etc) has a chip value + a multiplier: chip X multiplier = hand score.At the end of each round you gain money that you can use to buy new jokers and booster packs. Each level consist of a small blind, a big blind and a "boss" blind, that contains special limiting rules: you can only play one hand to beat the score, you lose two random cards, diamonds doesn't score, etc.For people who are completionists, there are 150 jokers and a lot of special cards. As you progress your game you can have special "decks" that gives startup advantages/ changes.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is so excellent that it feels like it was discovered, not created. It effortlessly evokes the brainy strategies of the best roguelike deckbuilders while also tying itself back to a poker theming that all those games were mechanically riffing from anyway.An approachable UI welcomes players who don’t know their flushes from their straights, but there’s still plenty of challenge to be found in the management of your deck and economy—all wrapped up in an intuitive package that would make your grandpa take pause and watch over your shoulder.The result is a simple yet compelling deckbuilder that’s as infinite and as classic as a deck of 52.Balatro is a roguelike solitaire version of poker. Each run starts by dealing you eight cards and asking you to produce the best five-card-hand you can. Repeat over the course of a few rounds.Rather than having a table of opponents,  you’re attempting to hit a score threshold. Each hand has its own score and its own multiplier. The short term strategy is born from Balatro’s drawing and discard rules; you get a few free per card mulligans each turn, and in a deckbuilder-like fashion you refuel your hand after each play.Within your first minute you’re being asked to answer strategic questions about your risk tolerance: do you discard a guaranteed hand in pursuit of a better one? Or do you play it safe and work with what you got?The fact that each card replaces itself on play makes them act as a secondary discard, too. Have a hand that’s just short of a flush? Why not open round one with playing a modest pair from different suits and chucking in three other random cards alongside them: even if they’re not contributing towards that pair and its point value, they are freeing up those hand slots and give you greater flush opportunities the following turn. It’s not guaranteed to work but that’s the beauty of it: you’re always looking for little ways to stack the deck in your favor.That's just one example among dozens where Balatro is constantly giving you decisions in small but provocative ways.That philosophy becomes multiplied after your first few hands when Balatro exposes you to some of its run-wide systems. You get a shop with “booster packs”, which sounds corny for a deck-of-52 game like this until it gets coupled with the game's concept of “jokers”.These would be your “relics” or “artifacts” in a title with a more “video-gamey” theme, they’re passive bonuses that will stay with you for an entire run and you can hold up to five of them under normal conditions.One run I got a joker that multiplied my score if I only played three card hands instead of five. Now all of the sudden I’m pivoting to a style that boosts three of a kinds and pairs, and flushes are near useless because they force me above that three-card limit by their very nature.That changed how I looked at those “booster packs”: now suit was less relevant with flushes off the table, allowing me to target specific numbers and faces to maximize my three-card-hand potential.Almost every joker can warp a game in this way, so you get this long term strategy of crafting good jokers for your deck and crafting good decks for your jokers. It’s so deep and so fun, once you start to see all the pieces come together it’s easy to imagine all the ways you can arrange them to make for truly unique runs every single attempt.It’s a time black hole, the hours just melt in front of you.Part of that is probably because of how well produced it is, too. Not only does it have a simple, replayable little gameplay style but it also has a presentation that makes infinite play so appealing. Mechanically the ‘blinds’ are kind of like enemies, but they don’t really feel that way. You don’t get any smashing or crashing animations into them when you successfully score points, just little bleeps and the sound of stacking chips.It gives Balatro a very non-confrontational vibe, where the focus is always just you and your cards. Each turned in hand gives you a brief animation of your cards cashing in their point values but also a little visual indicator that shows your jokers boosting their power. It makes it obvious who your load bearing jokers are and the fact that the score acquisition is so multiplication heavy gives you this big explosion of points once every card has done its little dance that makes the result so satisfying.Beyond just being a game with immediately interesting rules and endless strategy, Balatro is also just a damn good roguelike in the conventional sense, too. The meta progression is a steady increase in options and scope. You’ll get more potential jokers, more consumable power ups, and more card types.There are multiple ‘boss encounters’ that you’ll want to start building around, too. They apply modifiers that can be a counter to your exact strategy. One of my first almost successful runs leaned on beefing up easy hands like pairs and giving myself additional hands per round: going for consistent additive plays instead of singularly big ones. Imagine my frustration upon meeting the Needle, an encounter that allowed only a single hand to be played.Obviously, I lost; but the lesson might not be what you think it was. The standard approach would be to have a more flexible deck next time, but there’s nothing wrong with single-mindedness in Balatro as long as you bring insurance: either jokers or consumables that let you re-roll or nullify a boss encounters’ modifiers.There’s also thought that needs to be given to the relative strength of your deck. Maybe that consistent ‘two of a kind’ will get you through the early game, but it may not yield the points you need as the run gets tough (and it literally ups the ante). A strategic pivot into strengthening higher point value hands is always on your mind, and you need to be aware of how much hand manipulation you currently have and if you’re ready for that pivot.Balatro isn’t just a loving ode to standard playing card decks but also a subtle homage to cards and collectables more generally. It creates intrigue in opening up a ‘booster pack’ of regular cards by sprinkling in lots of modifiers. There are ‘lucky’ cards that have a chance of giving a small bonus in addition to their regular effects, steel cards are incentivized to be held and give multipliers to played hands they aren’t in, and golden cards help boost your economy.Holographics, foils, and more are attributes you can find on jokers in addition to their regular behaviors, which give you this exciting boost and maybe a reason to alter strategies into a joker that may otherwise be suboptimal for your deck.Balatro does so much with so little. With a deck of playing cards and some powerups, it’s created a timeless card system with high stakes but low pressure. This game of probability manipulation and strategy is one of the best deckbuilders of all time, and its intuitive ‘playing-card’ presentation might also make it one of the best versions of Solitaire ever made, too.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really great game with a lot of depth to it.+There's a lot to do in the game+There's many difficulties to pick from and they're all fun+Each deck and challenge plays differently+The game really makes you think about your moves+There's a lot of combinations you can use in terms of cards and joker synergy+visual and sound effects in the game are really satisfying+Runs perfectly on steamdeck with no issues= Some of the achievements require way too much playtime in my opinion= there's barely any text, no story/lore/explanations just a few words when you win or lose-some of the jokers are really imbalanced.  It feels like I end up using the same handful of them to win, so the game turns into rng of just finding those good jokers.-A majority of the jokers in the game are really weak and not worth picking up sometimes.-The game's music is nice, but it's only like one track and it gets really annoying to listen to it for hours on end repeated.  Overall rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is really difficult. Expect to not get a single win for at least the first 10 hours. There's a lot of luck involved and even though there probably doesn't exist a seed that is "unbeatable" - it certainly can feel this way if you don't know what to expect and start building a certain way that might fail you later because of an unfortunate boss blind or absence of fitting jokers. That said, it's pretty straightforward. You don't need to be familiar with card games to play it and you can kill time with it while watching something or waiting for something with nothing better to do. 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: Picture the difference between meth and sugar. Balatro is the same, but for crack cocaine.[+] Immense variety of builds resulting from complex emergent behavior.[+] Fun modifiers in the form of alternate decks.[+] Item unlocking system that feels constant keeps the game fresh.[-] No perma-progression. (I understand that it would make Ascensions trivial, but it would be nice for endless mode only)[~] I personally love  the art style, though I do realize that *some* may be negatively affected by nausea and the like.[-] A bit of item bloat is present. Sometimes you simply don't roll any good passive upgrades (Jokers) to get a build running.[+] Lovely QOL and UI decisions make the game feel smooth to play. (Speed slider is great, but would like to see 6x as well)[-] Black deck is hell on earth.[-] Many of the blinds (Read: bosses) are a far too punishing.

After that it's so RNG dependent that I find myself wanting to wipe my save and start over.

_childDocuments_.review: So I'm not a doctor or anything. But I have been suffering from very intense treatment-resistant depression made worse by adult-onset ADHD. Long story short, I've been in and out of hospitals for the last couple of months, trying desperately to find any form of treatment that would lessen my despair... or at *least* find a hobby that might be able to capture my incredibly evasive attention span for longer than five minutes.Again, I'm not a doctor. But this game has been a godsend for me. I'll admit: before I bought Balatro, I secretly hoped I would love it as sincerely as the other reviews suggested, as card games tend to hold my attention better and for longer than other forms of tactical or strategy games. But it wasn't until I discovered the option to crank up the speed of the UI in-game that Balatro became that shining gem of a game that I'd been searching for.Again again, still not a doctor. But *dang* did this game help me through the last few weeks. It absolutely rocks. And even though I feel like I am absolutely terrible at it (as my memory forbids me to remember that the Boss Blind requires me to play five cards AND NO FEWER... AGAIN), it's got that rogue-like flavor that makes every run a different kind of fun. I seriously take my Adderall, boot up Balatro, and allow hours of time to pass having fun instead of *probably* sulking in the dark corners of my bedroom.In other words: this game deserves its "Overwhelmingly Positive" score. It just works. :D

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is an amazing roguelike that solves a lot of issues with the genre that many other games struggle with. These issues are:-      This refers to the problem in many rougelikes where you get an item and it says something like "Improves attack damage when an enemy is frozen" or in some cases just says some flavor text like "toxic". This tells the player nothing about what the item or whatever does and it makes it very difficult to get into, many times requiring wikis open or other such things. In many cases, even when the stats and effects are clear, it can be very difficult to figure out how good it is before you pick it up, and sometimes even after you pick it up. This makes it take quite a while to really get into a rougelike because there is so much knowledge you have to learn to know what items are good and which suck.     Balatro solves this by having each card description being relatively simple and very clear. It helps that the base of the game is simple too. The scoring system is also pretty simple to understand, to the point where you can calculate things on your own if you so choose (which I have done on a few occasions - its fun). When you play a hand, you clearly see how each joker effects your score and how they effect each other. This helps you get into the game quickly by very clearly showing you what each and every item does-      This is something thats hard to do, so I understand it, but many rougelikes suffer from it. What I mean by "poor balance" more specifically here is a decent amount of items that are either insanely run-winningly good and/or items that sound neat but end up being complete and udder trash. This creates runs where you get wins that you didn't really work for along with runs where you try to commit to a certain strategy or build that ends up sucking because the balance is off. This ties into the point above but it gets worse when something is really bad but it isn't obvious how bad it is.      Balatro isn't perfect about balance, but it feels a lot better than other rougelikes I've played. I've not encountered a joker that has been so good it won my run on its own, and I also haven't encountered any jokers that are uselessly bad, and even if they are, the game makes it pretty clear that its gonna suck. Even so, they usually work in some build somewhere, or have a niche during a certain point in a run which makes them useful. -      This one is a real big problem with rougelikes. Many rougelikes out there are very very unclear about what builds you can go for and if they are even worth your time at all. The items may give some impressions here and there, but many times it will be difficult to tell if its worth it to commit to. There is also the case in some games where certain mechanics or calculations that are INCREDIBLY obtuse and unclear to the player are INSANELY important to the game and creating good builds. It also hurts when games try to make a bunch of items for certain types of builds, but those builds are god awful because they don't work within the game very well.     Again, Balatro solves this with incredibly clear synergy and calculation. As I said above, you can calculate what is going to happen yourself so when you are thinking if a certain card is worth it or not, you can do the math to figure it out. Not many other games have that ability. The way the game is played, again, is also very simple which makes builds pretty easy to figure out. I've found a lot of success and fun in this game by buying a decent joker early on and trying to commit hard to building around it, and it works!-      This could be considered a good thing I guess, but I tend to have issue with it. What I mean is when a rougelike throws a boss at you that you've never seen before and you die very quickly. Then, in order to fight it again you have to play a whole new run, get to that point, die, and then try again. It makes it really hard to learn patterns and learn how to fight the bosses, especially when they are late game or don't always appear.     Balatro solves this by not really having much player skill involved. Most of Balatro is figuring out which build would be the best, making tricky decisions, and hedging your bets. The "skill" in balatro is knowing when to discard and what to discard to achieve which hand. Everything else is trying to figure out which item or card or whatever will help your build the most. It's also a chill game without any urgency which means you can take your time and think a lot if you so please. To be fair to other rougelikes, many games solve some of these problems on their own, and I'm sure there are games other than Balatro that don't have any of these issues. My main point, really, is that Balatro gets you to the "end game" of a rougelike much quicker than others do. By "end game" I mean when you get a lot of knowledge and experience in a game and know what you want to do and what decisions to make and what is good. Essentially Balatro is good and a ton of fun if you love to strategize and think about numbers. I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Be as cautious before buying this game as you would be in a sketchy part of the town before getting actual drugs. I saw the reviews saying this game is addictive like crack. _childDocuments_.review: Being older than god, I remember card games on your 386's with EGA graphics and this game has some serious vibes from the past I love, the pixel graphics, the music could be pure midi on your sound blaster pro, or Roland MT-32, it's great. The concept is amazingly well done, you can play in the think tank, or just freestyle it, the number of synergies and anti-synergies are amazing, And losing feels great, you just go, d'oh I turned all my cards into face cards and the last boss dealt all face cards face down, oops, and play again. _childDocuments_.review: I had tried this game during early access and jumped in upon release. At the time of writing this I am nearly at 100 hours of play and can tell any Deck Builder fan that this is the game to get, My previous go to Deck Builder was Slay the Spire. Both games are incredible but I can see Balatro getting poker players into the Deck Building genre, we could say a gateway game to the roguelike genre for poker players. I like how the game unlocks cards that allow you to gradually understand their utility in the builds you have already developed. You can save the game mid-game and continue playing that game on another device like the Steamdeck. It plays perfectly on the Steamdeck.The only downside I can think of at this time is the repetitive music. It would be nice to have a track per deck or unlockable music. Also, I sometimes find the animations to be a bit long. It would be nice to have a non-animation mode where you get cards, effects, multipliers appear more quickly. All in all, this game is a must buy, you won't be disappointed. I can rarely say this about a game. I am confident you will enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: It's poker, but the only way to survive is to amass a series of expensive cheats. "Buy this thing and your flush will score more, every single time!" Sometimes the best way to play is balanced, playing the best hand you can muster between X number of discards and re-draws and Y number of total allowed hands you have to play. Other times, the best strategy is to always fight for the same hand over and over. The diversity of ways you can play make this a relatively consistent challenge, and the luck of what the game offers you for those cheats determines your fate for the rest of This Run.It is fun, light, and a whole run can be completed in an hour. Or, you can play a blind, take a break, and come back later. So if combining hand types, altering the types and number of cards in your deck, and trying to build silly exploitative combinations between the 5 jokers you can have in play sounds like fun to you, then this will be a big win.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Really cool game. One of the best card roguelike games I've played and it was a bless to find this game when I was finally ready to let slay the spire go.I was reluctant about givint this game a go because I'm not the biggest poker enjoyer out there, but I quickly understood that other than the card combinations, poker is just a theme to the game.The game is really fun, there a lot of synergies and I love how you can choose different decks that basically change the rules of scoring or the base card structure you start the game with. This alone will make a lot of different playstyles viable, so the game keep being fresh for longer.The only real downside IMO are the high stake runs. The stakes are basically difficulties to the run (if you've played slay the spire, think about ascensions). You first start at white stake that is the base difficulty. After beating it, you unlock a new optional stake that has some modifier that can increase the difficulty. This by itself is fine, because the game start to demand from you better decision making and game plan. The highest difficulty is the gold stake, which in my opinion is really unbalanced and not fun to play at all. At this point, it is really hard to get a run going and most of the time you will need to reset a lot to be able to have a real chance of winning.The problem with the stakes in comparison with the ascensions from slay the spire, is that in slay the spire you have a lot more agency around what you should look for and what risks you take. You know the act boss early into each act, so you have plenty of chances to get what you need. At gold stake, it's common to get runs that even if you get the same seed and try it again, you wouldn't be able to get past a certain ante.Luckly, the stakes are optional and individual to each deck you unlock, so there are plenty  progression to make even if you're not a fan of it.

_childDocuments_.review: This game has perfected the arcade-rougelite. The fast paced gameplay, perfected systems, chaotic balancing, and visual effects make it a great game to pop in every now in then. I find myself racking up hours not in the evenings staring into the screen, but in passing periods, school lunch, waiting for water to reheat, or if I have a few minutes for any reason. I’ve never seen a rougelike before that does that, and Balatro does it just as well as something like Tetris, Puyo-Puyo, Super Pinball, or Dr. Mario. Great game, would recommend to any fan of strategy games or Rougelikes.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a roguelike deckbuilder stripped down to the essentials: no story, no endgame, just pure addictive gameplay with infinite replay potential. There’s no storyline to follow—progression is entirely up to you, allowing players to set and achieve their own goals in this endlessly replayable experience.Gameplay and MechanicsIn Balatro, every "run" is an exercise in balancing luck with skillful deckbuilding. The game’s strategies involve creating synergies between various “jokers” in your deck, and how you use them can make or break a run. The beauty here lies in the flexibility—whether you go for a simple approach or dive into complex strategies, Balatro adapts to your playstyle. While being simple makes you rely on luck and may have a more gambling feel to it, you can choose to fine-tune your builds to try to beat the odds.Aesthetic and StyleBalatro employs a retro, pixel-art style that keeps it exceptionally lightweight, requiring minimal resources and ensuring accessibility on even low-end systems. Despite its simplicity, the game remains visually appealing, with a clean design that complements its straightforward, strategic gameplay.Final ThoughtsWithout a story or endpoint, Balatro focuses on what roguelike deckbuilders do best: offering endlessly variable runs and a mix of luck and strategy that keeps you coming back. For fans of deckbuilders who want the freedom to create and master their own goals, Balatro is an absolute gem.

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game premise on my third attempt in just under three hours of gameplay, so it isn't very hard or maybe I got very lucky. With that said I usually drop games after less than 20 min because I find them boring, this game was not and the replay value is there.It reminds me of Slay the spire and FTL with its gameplay loop and the cards visuals remind me of when I used to play Magic the gathering with foiled cards and other extras, which I liked. I bought Balatro full price and would've done it again. With that said I do recommend this game.

_childDocuments_.review: TIP IN BOLD FOR THOSE WHO NEED IT SPEEDING UP GAME PLAY IS IN OPTIONS FOR THOSE WHO WANT IT.My grandmother would sit in the office playing solitaire for a few hours while drinking a cup of coffee and listening to some tunes, I thought it looked boring and still today solitaire wouldn't be for me. However I'm 30 now and shes passed, but I feel like she could have had a blast playing this or watching me play it. I spent 22 hours and still have a little left to complete. _childDocuments_.review: The game is great overall, but I'm very frustrated by the RNG that makes high-difficulty game plays miserable. Here're some suggestions to the developers that could make the game more enjoyable:Boss blinds can sometimes be lethal by completely disabling a specific play style, and it's very frustrating if at late game the player encounters the exact debuff that simply destroys the deck. It's particularly depressing since there's usually nothing the player can do to react. I'd recommend adding a forecast of future boss blinds so the player may have sufficient time to react (instead of helplessly praying the worst blind won't appear). Of course, there are other ways to achieve this, such as:- Rebalance boss blinds that target specific play styles. (For example, instead of disabling all hearts, the blind can disable every second red card in a hand.)- Provide a reroll option (that doesn't require the voucher) that costs all money.- Instead of the current boss blind, the player can choose 2 out of 3 random blinds. In Balatro, players rely heavily on item combos to scale, but obtaining them is extremely RNG-dependent. Based on my experiments, the possibility of having a specific Joker accessible is less than 1% per restock, while uncommon and rare Jokers significantly fewer. This gets even more frustrating in high-difficulty modes that demands players obtain a functioning combo quickly, and leave them no choice but to restart if they can't find their items. I suggest that Balatro adjust the probability of Jokers according to the current items and deck, so that players are more likely to receive Jokers that function together. Of course, there are other ways to achieve this, such as:- An interface to disable a proportion of Jokers from appearing before each run.- Larger shop or cheaper restock.- Categorical shop that allows player to choose which type of items to purchase (tarot, planet, joker, etc.), which can be restocked separately.- Decrease possibility of lower-ranked Jokers as the game progresses.- An option in shop to prevent the item from reappearing later in the run. - Legacy system that smartly reduces probability of Jokers that player doesn't buy across multiple runs.

_childDocuments_.review: “I’ve grown tired of the rogue-like genre”, is what I thought, until I played Balatro. Balatro takes the addictive nature of poker and gambling, makes it risk free, and then adds in hundreds of variables that make each playthrough unique. One playthrough you might build towards making every card in your deck a suit of hearts, and then run into a boss that completely nullifies heart cards, ending your run. Another run you might have a combo built around flushes, and then end up getting an unlucky hand that doesn’t have a flush, ending your run. Essentially, Balatro plays into the same logic of poker, but allows you to enhance cards, and multiply bonuses of cards, through each of its different systems. Like other rogue-like games, you unlock cards as you go, further increasing playtime as you find new ways to play/strategise. The main factor that draws me into the rogue-like genre, is how randomness meets synergy; how multiple items can synergize together, seemingly from complete random chance and luck. Binding of Isaac was the first game I noticed that took this to an absurd level, with 1000s of item combinations, making every run feel unique. However most rogue-like games only do this partially, and never enough to make each run feel truly unique, mostly with small bonuses to stats (boring). Balatro has 150 joker cards, multiple booster packs that each have several random card/hand modifiers, and 32 vouchers. While this isn’t as much as what a game like Binding of Isaac offers, for a simple poker game, it offers a lot of re-playability, randomness, combinations, and synergies, leading to a lot of different builds, decks, and scenarios. In short, Balatro is a game that makes you say “just one more”. It’s simple, but deceivingly complex, just like chess or Tetris – just as addictive as well. A basic understanding of poker is all you need. Game is cheap, buy it on sale or full price, either way you’ll get your moneys worth.

_childDocuments_.review: The good- Awesome pixel visuals. Each card and Joker looks unique like having a personality. Customized decks from famous games are gorgeous. Menus and various effects give it a retro feeling.- Great concept. It starts with basic poker rules, but you don't play against other players, instead you're after specific scores in each stage. Then it introduces Jokers and some other cards (arcane, celestial, spectral) and chips that completely transform the game. For each different setup and combination the games looks like having new rules and whole new strategies appear out of nowhere. Its amazing how some Jokers initially look useless and weak until you combine them with the right cards. Then new opportunities and tactics appear and they can become powerful. The game requires mathematical thinking as you need to calculate possibilities and potential score. Luck also is a major factor, so there will be moments that you'll need to take some crazy risks.- There are various decks, each with different rules, many difficulty levels and extra challenges that can provide a lot of hours of gaming. The way that all these have been built by the developers is very clever and manages to reveal the abilities of some Jockers and value of other initially underappreciated cards. After you complete them you'll have understood all the potential of the game and new strong tactics will be taken into account.- Effective and responsive controls. The game feels light and quick. Each action happens instantly while transition screens are fast without tiring the player.- Fantastic animations. They're not sophisticated at all, but the way the cards score,  the Jockers activate, the way the chips and multipliers are added, the numbers are rising and the flames are rising during big scores, all these are making it so satisfying to watch.- Simple, yet cool sound design. The sounds are inspired from old 8bit games but manage to create a pleasant audio environment especially when you manage to hit consecutive and big scores.- There's essentially only one music track, but it's more than enough. After hundred of hours you'll never get bored of it and it will stick in your mind.- Overall design is very good with vivid colors that help the gameplay and the player to acknowledge what's in front of him really quick. After several hours, when you have learned Jocker's abilities you'll need to read only a few things here and there. Because everything is color coded you'll understand what's going on in a screen with a single glance.The bad- The game is great, but advertising it as a rogue like is inappropriate. Yeah, you unlock new cards and decks and you play it again with altered rules and new skills, but essentially there is no continuity. Acquiring a new powerful weapon or a tool in a shooter alters your tactics for the upcoming levels, but this doesn't make it rogue like. Unfortunately, there is no plot or characters that react on your actions in previous runs. There are no events that connect runs somehow. It doesn't feel like an evolving organism and each run is completely separate with just some new tools.- There are some balance issues. One or two hands, like straight, are much strong than others as they scale too quickly and aren't too hard to draw them. This forces players to choose them as their main hands for most of their runs, so the game can get repetitive. Some two Jockers combinations are so clearly overpowered that if you find them at early antes you're sure that you have won this run and there are not erven boss blinds that can stop them. At harder difficulty levels it feels like your run depends entirely on luck and cards that you'll find on the first two or three antes. There's nothing more that you can do, no specific strategy to follow, just hope for something good early.- Most challenges are very clever, but there are various questionable decisions, like they needed more thinking. For example all these tarot cards that affect Jokers in Jockerless are just thrash. A lot of tags at the first antes of each run are completely useless, mainly because of not having money yet, and just force the player to restart annoyingly again and again until something reasonable comes out.- For all these unique, fantastically designed Jocker cards it's really unfortunate that there is no story at all. I'm sure most of them could have amazing personalities. I would be happy  even if they could at least interact each other somehow, react on your plays or when you combine them.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a lot of fun, though it's somewhat random and thus you can feel frustrated waiting for your first win. As with all games like this (where more items are unlocked as you play) it might actually be easier to win early in the game since the number of potential items is lower thus increasing the chances that you'll get a good combination of jokers and other things.So you might ask yourself, what is this game about?  Well, it's a card game where you play poker hands to earn points in the form of "chips" to achieve a set round goal (called a "blind") in a set number of hands with a set number of discards.  Each Ante has 3 rounds (Blinds): Small, Big, and Boss. You play poker hands from a deck, discarding cards. The Boss is mandatory, and each has unique challenges (e.g. "Verdant Leaf" prevents scoring until a joker is removed, "The Eye" prevents hand reuse). Defeat each Blind, earn rewards and shop access for Jokers, Arcanas, Planets, Vouchers to buy cards that boost score, discard, or restock, or affect gameplay. For example, the first round goal is 300 chips and you start with around 3-5 "hands" to attempt to reach that goal.  You'll also start with 3-5 discards per round with each discard being up to 5 cards at a time.  Your hand size will be around 7 cards to start out with but the actual number depends on the starting conditions given by the type of deck you play.  There's 5 colored decks: red, blue, green, yellow and black.  Some decks give extra discards, some give extra hands, some give extra money. Each deck presents its own challenge.  Once you beat the game with a given deck, you can change the chip color which further changes the game difficulty.Anyway, as I said, this is kind of random, so you may find yourself losing a lot even if you play the game perfectly.  OR You might find yourself winning even though you play really sloppily (If the random seed is just so stacked in your favor)  You don't find out the seed until after the game is over though, but if you've ever thought maybe you could have won if you did something differently, then this is a great option.  The only caveat here is that you don't unlock anything from playing a seeded game, and so it would  purely be for the fun of playing.There's lots of room for strategy, but since you can buy usually 2 jokers at most per round, you may find that it's difficult to form a good strategy with what you have.  One of my favorite combos is to have the four finger joker (allows you to make straights and flushes with only 4 cards) combined with the Square joker (starts with +16 chips per hand played but increases +4 chips for every time you play only four cards) and the Seance Joker (straights or flushes creates a random spectral card).   You can see how each card works together, but the odds of these jokers all being available together is slim. Cards can be modified to have extra effects like +multiplier (+4 per card played), Wild (used as any suit), Bonus (adds +30 chips to the current card value), glass (x2 multiplier but 25% chance of being destroyed once played), Steel (1.5X multiplier added as long as you hold it in your hand and it's not played), and there's more.  You can also have card editions (foil/polychrome/holographic etc), and seals applied to the card (small colored circles that give an extra effect to that card under certain conditions). You can also add cards to your deck to have more than 52 cards, or you can destroy cards to have fewer than 52. The card modifications aren't permanent so you don't have to worry about messing up the deck, but you CAN mess the deck up for your current run.  For example, it's possible to change cards so that you have extra cards of a certain suit by changing them from another (e.g. from Hearts to clubs), which can make the odds of making a flush go up for Clubs but down for hearts.   There's also a spectral card that will change a large number of cards to be all the same rank (e.g. a whole hand full of 8's) making it possible to get a 5 of a kind.You don't have to have any special knowledge of how to play poker to enjoy the game as the game will tell you what the hands are as you select it and you'll learn the difference between a flush, a straight, and a straight flush as the game goes on. In conclusion, if you like games that are both random AND give options for strategy, and you like unlocking new stuff, this game will give you all of that.  If you prefer games that rely more on strategy and skill, this will be a bit frustrating for you, but honestly, how many card games are there that rely solely on skill? I think it's a fun game though, and worth the purchase.

Theoretically the interface and play experience could be slightly polished, but the biggest downside is that the hardest difficulty feels too reliant on good RNG at the start to get runs going at all, leading to a lot of early resetting. Thankfully this can be mitigated by just playing on lower difficulty. But while we're on the subject of lower difficulties, my other difficulty-related gripe is that Eternal Jokers are locked behind a relative high difficulty level - they are a considerable enough gameplay changer (most importantly, a Joker being eternal isn't always going to be negative, it can very much be positive as well!) that I would personally like to either see them on base difficulty already or alternatively have them added into the mix on the second difficulty already so you could play base difficulty + eternals, without having to deal with any of the other difficulty modifiers.Also, while I already praised the audiovisual presentation at the start, I have to give an extra shoutout to the music - it's amazing how you just don't get tired of it despite the game's soundtrack consisting of basically just a single song with some slight variations. One does not simply achieve something like that unless the single song is really, really, REALLY good. Mad props to the composer.

_childDocuments_.review: It's fun in concept but fizzles out fast due to being very poorly balanced, too grindy (to unlock everything), and way too RNG heavy. Balatro is the kind of game where you either hit it high and land on the moon, or die in the first ante (on higher stakes). The deck balance is also all over the place, some are basically unplayable (e.g. black deck), others are way too powerful (e.g. plasma deck).It was fun when it was novel, but at some point you find yourself just spending half an hour rerolling for the perfect start because some of the challenges and decks are literally unbeatable without getting insanely lucky in the early game. It is a far cry from the likes of the well-balanced roguelikes it draws inspiration from.Apart from fixing the massive issues with card, boss and deck balance, an easy improvement to the status quo would be to e.g. guarantee a powerful joker after beating a boss, the way most other roguelikes do this. Rather than just leaving it up to chance.There are another couple of design choices I dislike, e.g. stakes being tied to the deck choice - which makes it so you basically "lock yourself in" to a certain deck and have to grind out the lower difficulties again if you want to ever play a different one. This really hurts the replayability of the game. Adding to this overall monotony is the fact that most strong decks rely on the same few jokers and tarot cards, and the strongest strategies consistently spend a lot of time just idly abusing some value-generating joker, only to lose all this progress to some unlucky boss.Balatro is the kind of game where it's more fun to watch somebody else's high roll video on youtube than to play for hours trying to get that high roll yourself. Or just save your time by unlocking all of the collection at the start with a cheat code, so you can actually play what you want to play instead of being forced to suffer through a monotonous grind to unlock it in the first place.

_childDocuments_.review: A fun roguelike deckbuilder in the genre of , but with a focus on making and scoring poker hands.Unfortunately, while Slay the Spire has thousands of hours of skill cap, Balatro so far feels like tens of hours.  There is far less depth and balance in Balatro which spoils an otherwise intriguing idea and  clever implementation."Runs" are broken up into 8 "Antes".  Each ante consists of three "rounds" or "blinds".  The first and second blinds ("small" and "big") can be played or skipped for a reward.  If played, you make poker hands and score points attempting to reach the target number of points.  If you fail, the run is over, but if you succeed, you get money and a visit to the shop where you can buy things that to help you in future rounds.  If you skip the blind, you get a randomized bonus item.  The final blind is against a boss with an extra effect to make the game harder (e.g. "debuff" certain cards, meaning they don't score their individual points -- but the hands they make still do).In my experience, skipping blinds ends up being a bad idea almost always.  This is because the reward you get is often equivalent to one item purchased from the shop, but if you win a blind, you win enough money to buy at least one item from the shop, and playing a round can often activate lots of additional bonuses, like discarding cards to receive consumables (tarot cards or planet cards).  In addition, skipping the blind skips the shop, meaning you lose out on any other sources of improvements for your deck.With StS, every aspect of the game has depth to it.  Pathing through the map is an important skill, but no such element exists in Balatro.  Enemy combats are far more involved in StS than simple rounds in Balatro, all of which are the same except with the boss blinds.  In StS, you start with around 12 cards, which makes customizing your deck to remove starting cruft far more feasible than in Balatro where you start with a full 52 card poker deck.The Jokers don't feel all that balanced, either.  Some are effectively completely worthless, and you keep getting bad common jokers even late into the run, which makes it pretty hard to improve sometimes.  Meanwhile, other jokers can be pretty broken, like the "red card" joker that gives +3 mult for skipping a booster pack (meaning it can gain +6 mult every round -- but again not if you skip the blind and receive the bonus).Some suggestions to increase the skill cap:1. At the start of every run, the game should remove 10-20 cards from a standard deck at random.  Then the player should be allowed to choose and remove 5-10 cards.  This means you'll be able to make decisions about whether you're aiming for straights, flushes, or pairs/etc, and makes newly added cards more valuable.2. Every blind should have different buffs/debuffs that are potentially potent but not as bad as the bosses.  These should happen semi-predictably based on the ante/blind.3. Skipping blinds should provide better rewards, or at least allow you to revisit the shop with renewed stocks.As a nit-pick, I found the system of enhancements/editions/seals a bit counter-intuitive.  It's not at all obvious that enhancing a gold card to be wild would remove the gold enhancement, but it's valid to have a foil+gold card.  And the game doesn't warn you when it would remove an enhancement.Overall, it's a fun game that I don't regret buying, but I will say I was hoping for much more.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro will ruin your life. It could steal your partner, kick your dog down the stairs, cause you to lose what friends and family you have left, get you fired from your job; and you'd still come back for another hand because that's how good it is. Balatro starts with the fairly simple premise of building poker hands to score points to beat challenges, and then tears away all the rules that make up poker, and replaces them with a really creative engine building system. Layer that with a really wide variety of challenge modes, deck types, and jokers; and you've got a game that will yield a never ending fount of gameplay. For me, Balatro manages to hit that sweet spot of 'unsolvable' (and thus, constantly compelling and experimental), and yet still entirely making you feel like all of your failures are on you. You can certainly lean your deck one way or the other with different ideas, but I always feel like a bust is because of something I didn't catch a few games earlier (which makes decisions feel like they have weight). The one critique I would have (and honestly, I could see why this isn't an option); is to include a way of tabulating what a hand will contribute if played before you playing it. Balatro does an initial calculation of the strength of the hand (telling you chips X hand multiplier), but it leaves you to figure out what the actual end score will be. As someone who's frankly garbage at  math (and too lazy to break out a calculator to figure out  how much each card will add and how my jokers will contribute), it'd be nice if the game would just give me a running tally of 'With this combination you've selected, it'll be worth X points' and then let me make a judgement from there. But that's a nitpick, and I understand the appeal. There's almost a slot machine aspect to 'I need at least 7,000 points on this, and I see from the multiplier and my various jokers that this should get me... pretty close? Here goes nothing' to playing hands based on what you recall. The information is there if you want to dive (including which cards you have remaining in the deck to set up your next hand), but the appeal of just playing whatever you think is the best thing in this moment is there for you. All in all, Balatro is somehow a game that doesn't take up a lot of time to enjoy, but will leave you in a stupor at 3am when you're trying out 'just one more hand'. Great game, and a strong recommendation for anyone who really enjoys engine builders.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a straight-forward, incredibly designed and radically fun game that uses the gameplay of poker as a foundation, and builds upon it massively with no-nonsense roguelite mechanics. It's relaxing and distinctive atmosphere provided by its graphics, sound design and music help it to stand out as one of the most unique games of the decade. Balatro's gameplay loop is simple: play high-scoring hands to earn chips and defeat blinds. What makes every run unique is the player's choice of Jokers - unique items that change the rules of the game you play. Jokers can range from straightforward e.g. Jokers rewarding you extra chips if you play flush hands, to incredibly complex e.g. Jokers that multiply your score for every time you a play a hand that isn't your most-played hand. This is the magic in Balatro. Its core gameplay is so intuitively simple yet so rewarding to master that it'll have you hooked with play-sessions lasting for hours at a time. As you experiment with Jokers and different playstyles, the game will reward you with more Jokers to garnish your future runs with. The majority of Jokers you discover will be unlocked naturally simply by you playing the game and pushing its mechanics to their limits. At 88 hours in, I have unlocked 149 out of the 150 Jokers available at the point of writing this review, and I have never had to Google how to unlock Jokers or look at the 'Collections' tab available in the game to figure out how to unlock that last one. The wonder of discovering the game is just as rewarding as the fruits of that labour - playing runs at the highest difficulty (or 'Stake' as its affectionately referred to as in Balatro) is some of the plainest fun you can have in a game where the only thing you need to do is press the left-mouse button.It's a labour of love, and I'm wholeheartedly glad that Balatro is getting its flowers because we need more innovative games like this that push the envelope on what a simple yet fun game can be. I simply can't wait for the first major content update coming to Balatro in 2025.

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is the "Idle clicker" of roguelites. The card interactions are certainly interesting, and it can be addictive to watch your Jokers stack multipliers as you submit a hand. But there is little to no interaction during a round. Just like some Titan Clicker game where you have to keep a certain DPS for 30-60 seconds while never getting hit back, Balatro gives you a static goal and a set number of turns to reach it with no opposition. For all of the comparisons to poker, there is no betting or bluffing, no other player to face down, and in most cases you aren't even required to play 5-card hands. None of these elements make this a bad game, but I do believe that the community discussion around this game has been highly misleading.

_childDocuments_.review: Updated review:It's a fun game, creative and clever in many ways.It just suffers from the same problems as every other roguelike: - runs are too long - good synergies are rare - success is largely chance based - restarting gets progressively more tiresomeI think the core problem with the roguelike genre is that chance is applied to builds, not just to the challenges. This is effectively a trick to get around the difficulty of balancing a large set of varied abilities. Restarting runs would actually be fun if it was about trying out a new idea (instead of hoping for a good dice roll), but that would require player builds to be carefully balanced against challenges, which is impossible without making the set of build options much narrower and less interesting.In competitive games, other players solve the balance problem. My hope is that AI will soon offer an analogous way to solve this problem for the roguelike genre, by adding an opponent that learns and adapts to force you to keep evolving your strategy. Maybe something like MuZero will evolve into a general purpose AI model that can be used to solve this problem for any game.Original saltier review:I'd been playing for an hour.I was on the final boss.I was thiiis close to the goal amount.I had one hand left...I hit Play instead of Discard.Not sure I can stomach playing again after that. I mean... I know I'm an idiot, but it needs to be IMPOSSIBLE to confuse these two buttons. Yet on Steam deck they are each used for multiple purposes and I've made this mistake multiple times.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't quite know why this is being labelled a "roguelike" at all. It's not an RPG, it's not a dungeon-crawler, it's video POKER... on steroids and shrooms.If you enjoy card games (especially casino-style games), deck-builders, and retro style arcade aesthetic, this is for you. Play poker hands to reach a specified score goal each round, which earns money to spend in between rounds on cards that enhance your scoring in various ways, or that add/remove cards from your deck. It's not complicated, but working out strategies to maximise your scores, utilising the cards you've added to your deck is where it gets interesting.Well worth the full price, IMO, although I bought it on sale.

_childDocuments_.review: Deckbuilder at its finest, up there with Slay the Spire. Your engine is poker hands, mixed with roguelite elements to make every run feel different. You have meta progression through deck and joker card (your relics essentially) unlocks to add to the lifespan of the game. The deeper you get, the more variety and challenge each run offers as your pool gets wider. For some, the challenge ends after winning a few runs with a few or all of the decks available to you. For others, you have the option to take it much further and challenge yourself to win runs with outrageous and synergistic combinations and chase huge scores. This game is highly recommended for all levels of players.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been looking for a game exactly like this one for a LONG time. Deckbuilding roguelike with charming graphics, plenty of unlockables, lots of different viable playstyles so no run feels the same, challenges and secrets and increasing complexity....I've tried tons of games looking for this, and really only Inscryption or Crop Rotation ever came close to what I was really craving....but this game? This game hit the nail on the head. This game might singlehandedly bring my GPA down from a perfect 4 because I've been playing it instead of studying, and to be honest I can't even be mad about it.The music is fun, but not too obtrusive (does it's job perfectly). The animations and sound design is top-notch. The UI feels streamlined, intuitive and uncluttered. The colours are well coordinated, and the different foils and holographics appropriately cool to look at and mouse over - i adore that they move with your mouse so you can admire the pretty reflections! The card descriptions are concise and easy to understand, the font choice is top-notch, the fire on your score as it gets bigger and the booster pack opening animation is fantastic tactile feedback. SO well designed.10/10. Would absolutely recommend for people who like seeing the Big Number Go Up but also want really fun, clever and unexpected synergies. I can't wait to start tackling the harder difficulties and the challenges.My only non-positive feedback is very nit-picky, subjective, and has nothing to do with the gameplay itself: I would really enjoy if the collection was displayed a little differently. It would benefit, in my opinion, from having it's own proper background and a UI thats a little less minimalistic rather than floating in the void in a box over the main menu. Navigating through it through those identical featureless red buttons is kind of underwhelming for something thats meant to be a record of your progress and accomplishments. (Ditto for stats, which I wish were a little more comprehensive - the graphs are great! But why cut off anything past the top ten or so? I wanna see them ALL.) Again, though, this is super nitpicky. This game is AWESOME.

_childDocuments_.review: Update at 90h played: I think this is the best roguelite ever. No hyperbole. It's at least a refreshingly fun play if you're exhausted with bullet heavens. There is no requirement for any hand-eye coordination or reaction speed as long as you have functioning hands, which is perfect for when my body doesn't feel like gaming but my brain does. I am reminded of how my mother would play Solitaire during her downtime... and I am totally going to be playing this if and when I hit old age.Poker on the outside, solitaire on the inside. One of those games that makes you go "why didn't I think of this?" You could argue that there's too much RNG but... it's a poker game, and you still have to not know what you're doing to not have a decent run, which is nice. Don't take it too seriously - leave that for the real poker table.Personally I don't find it as addictive as others seem to, merely satisfying. Great for a couple of rounds here and there. Balatro seems designed for the Deck from the ground up, 100%, which fits nicely with that pick-up-and-play nature. It's a straight-up better experience on that platform than either a desktop or laptop, especially with the touchscreen. (Edit: I got an OLED now and the touchscreen on that is way better, to the point where I mostly now play this game with touch controls.)As for the difficulty, it starts off relatively easy, at least for me, and ramps up the difficulty as you unlock more decks and stakes. With the basic default decks, I've noticed that the game will rig it in your favour slightly for the first couple of blinds when on easier stakes. Later decks and stakes ask quite a lot from your potential mathematical prowess - you better know how to card-count and multiply on the fly. I suppose you could use a calculator if you're so inclined... but I personally find that ruins the satisfaction a bit.However, one issue that I've run into at 117h played is that Balatro's later, more difficult decks are way too situational and box you into making specific hands, often only one or two types. This can make the RNG nature of the game a bit too much of a factor, but I guess that's why they're "special" decks. With some of those, whether you lose or have a chance at victory is determined by the first two hands you play along with the store behaving itself in giving you the right jokers and planet cards.This game could also really benefit from an optimisation patch, since it uses way too much electricity for what it is. Judging from battery use, Balatro seems to be not very optimised under the hood. 30 minutes of Brotato, which is a game with a hell of a lot more CPU stuff going on, will sip my LCD Deck battery down to 90% or so, often higher. Balatro? 60%, especially if you get a ton of combos going. I recommend capping the framerate to 30fps or even 20fps, since it doesn't really need more than that, and doing so reduced battery consumption for 30 minutes of play to about the same as Brotato. Given that this is a simple enough game that a version of it could feasibly to made that works on 30 year old computers or even older, I think this speaks to a larger issue of game developers and game engines simply not caring about optimisation.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally secured my pre-nerf gold stake win (of course I need to add the nerd flex) and I feel compelled to sing Balatro its praises.
