_childDocuments_.review: If you have been to Dear Gamers before, you know I am particularly fond of roguelites. If you are new, welcome to Dear Gamers and my borderline-dangerous addiction to roguelites. Last year, I thought I saw it all with a sports roguelite (Tape to Tape - a fantastic hockey game). Someone, somewhere assumed that was a challenge and I present (drumroll please): a card game roguelite (technically, Solitaire is a roguelite, more accurately a roguelike but Solitaire is boring and….anyway).Developed by LocalThunk, Balatro is a poker roguelite. THE poker roguelite. Play some poker, try to beat the blinds, rinse, and repeat until you lose. The DNA of a deckbuilder is buried in here but it remains a game of poker throughout. What if I told you that you could turn two pair into such an amazing hand that it would make 4 Aces look like a high card? You might think you know how to play poker but throw all that out the window when you play THIS game of poker.Everything will start somewhat normal. All rounds have a small blind, a big blind, and a boss blind that require you to reach a certain score. You are dealt 8 cards and can play up to 4 hands to reach the score. Hands can be 1 card or up to 5 cards. You also can discard up to 5 cards at a time 4 times per blind. Any legit poker hand counts here but the better the hand, the more you score. Scoring here may seem daunting at first but in no time at all, you will make Alan proud.Scores are calculated as Chips times Multipliers. Every hand has a base score value. For example, a high card is worth 5 x 1 and a full house is worth 40 x 4. The Chips side is increased by card value which is as simple as 1, 2, 3, 4, etc. with face cards equaling 10 and Aces worth 11. The game does all the math for you but I will admit that I broke out a calculator a few times when I was down to my last hand just so I could see my chances of winning with a straight versus a flush. What is great here is that basic poker logic gets thrown out the window. The more you play the more you realize that things like a full house is not necessarily better than two pair and a single 8 could net you five times the points as four 10s. Winning each blind rewards you with some cash to use in the shop that is only accessible between each blind. You earn a set value just from the blind itself and an extra $1 for each remaining hand you have left. Once you start accruing money, you can earn $1 interest for every $5 you have saved. There are additional ways to earn cash but these are standard. The aforementioned shop is how you make this regular game of poker into something of legend. Shops provide you with the following: 2 cards (these can be any type), 2 card packs (you get to pick a card from a number of cards), and a voucher. Vouchers generally cost a lot and are not as flashy as other cards but generally have long-term value. If you do buy it, another will not appear until you clear the current boss blind. Some of their perks include providing an extra item choice in the shop or permanently increasing the number of cards in your hand. Buying any voucher will unlock it for future runs although some vouchers only appear after some in-game milestones are reached (these can viewed from the collections screen in the main menu).What exactly is in the shop that makes your cards better? First up are Jokers. Jokers may not be used in normal poker but in Balatro, they are super important and almost crucial to your access. They serve as temporary (they only last the current game) buffs to the hands you will play. For example, a Joker may add a +4 multiplier to all played hands and another Joker may allow you to go up to $20 in debt in the shop. Shopping spree!Many Jokers have insane synergy with other Jokers. A favorite of mine was getting the Joker that granted +30 chips every time you play a face card. While this may seem tame because you have to hope for favorite deals, there is a Joker that treats all cards played as if they are face cards. Any card played in a hand, regardless of regular value, would also give me +30 chips. Throw in the Joker that scores all cards played and you could play a single Ace with a 2, 5, 9, and Jack, and the game will score the hand as a high card but also give you points for each card. That’s an additional 150 chips played (before adding in card value) on a simple High Card hand. Jokers can even affect how hands work like allowing for a 1-card gap in a straight or only requiring 4 cards for a flush. Jokers can be sold to fit new/better ones and once a Joker is discovered, they can appear in all future rotations.The other cards appearing in the shop are called consumables as they change your existing cards versus being cards used in your hands. Tarot cards can alter your standard cards into enhanced cards. There are  8 types of enhancements to encounter. Two such enhanced cards are wild cards (the card can become any suit) and stone cards (the card value is completely removed but the card is worth +50 chips). Tarot cards can also change a card’s suit, increase their rank (J to Q, 2 to 3, etc.), or give money. Planet cards improve the value of your hands meaning they increase the base score of a chosen hand. This also has a chance to synergize well with Jokers cards specifically ones that affect a certain type of hand. Last but not least are Spectral cards. The player has less control of what the Spectral cards do as the buff can be somewhat random such as granting 4 cards an enhancement while destroying a random card or changing all cards in your hand to a random suit. Consumables can be found in the shop, usually purchased from a pack that allows you a choice of the given consumable or from a tag. Like Jokers, all of these only affect the current game and do not carry over but once discovered on one run can appear in future runs.Most people hear poker and think of a group setting or something played online for money. LocalThunk has managed to take that and flip it on its head. What we have here is a genuinely fun, single-player experience. The gambit of runs can easily go from outrageously fun and adrenaline-pumping to incredibly frustrating in a matter of seconds. The “one more run” feeling seen in many roguelites can be seen here in spades (PUN INTENDED). Hands in Balatro last mere minutes and whether you have a successful run that goes many rounds or an early elimination, you will want to try again almost immediately. On top of all that, you can dive into the seed system as the game allows players to share their favorite runs (be sure to check out both the Steam forums and the game’s own Discord). Card games on PC have come a long way from being pre-packaged with the Windows Entertainment Pack to provide literally hours of fun. Become your very own card shark in this delightful twist on an old game.Full review with screenshots and video can be found at

_childDocuments_.review: Actually really good. The poker hands could be a stand-in for literally anything else but I think the devs were tryin to capture the sort of "cool vibes" of playing poker which is appreciated, but it's still worth acknowledging it's not poker it's just poker hands.Having unlocked most of the jokers the game is admittedly beginning to get a little stale. I've seen critics going crazy about this game acting like it's the next slay the spire in terms of cardbuilder roguelites but I disagree.Critics tend to just link any new concept to old concepts that they like and I think the constant comparisons to better performing games in the genre actually hinder rather than help the game's perception mainly because this game's strength is the fact that it takes you by surprise with it's depth.When you're expecting wow best roguelite ever made wow amazing so cool you're just setting yourself up for disappointment. It's better to go in with middling expectations and find that enjoyment in my opinion anyway.I'd definitely recommend it it's a fun game lots of interesting stuff to do and discover and I think there's a lot more of the aforementioned depth to it that I haven't quite breached, however it's nowhere near as genre-defining as critics are making it out to be, mainly because there's just not enough run variety.I'd love to see either jokers or a new card type that grant you access to "illegal" poker hands outside of the secret five of a kind and royal flush etc. the joker that allows you to more flexibly build straights (Shortcut?) is a favourite due to the fact you're looking for more than just your standard poker hands and actually have to think a bit more about things.Visual style is gorgeous; CRT crunchiness is always welcomed and every little animation from discarding to card selection to opening tags is so so satisfying.From some reading I understand that the tags upon skipping a blind were supposed to be a 1 in 4 chance like the wheel of fortune card and my God am I glad I didn't play when that was a thing lmao, although skipping blinds if you get the right tags does feel massively strong since first blind (at least from where I'm sitting) dies to 2 maybe 3 at most 5 card unbuffed hands.In conclusion, there's a lot of fun to be had, a few issues here and there but nothing that stops the game from being an extremely fun and accessible visual and auditory treat that definitely does tussle with the titans of roguelite games. However it's getting just a teeny tiny bit overhyped.Despite that, if it hadn't been for every YouTuber in my sub box creaming jorts it probably would've passed under my radar so I'm pretty grateful for the big hype around it.

_childDocuments_.review: If you can imagine what a shady, back-alley, underground poker lounge run by the dark wizards from a gritty rogue-like/rogue-light game looks like, you'd be close.  Just add some kick-ass pixel animations, trip'n backgrounds, and those satisfying casino noises; then flavor-blast that bastard child of a game with enough crack to OD a walrus and BOOM.  You get Balatro.  Once you try it for the first time, you'll be hooked.  But don't worry, this game is hard AF, so you'll be busy trying to unlock new decks, or beat the next difficulty level for ages.  You could spend $15 on crack, or you could spend $15 on Balatro; either way you'll be addicted, but Balatro doesn't ask for your money every time you want a taste.  What Balatro does do is make all other variant of poker feel as boring as watching beige paint dry.  <3 this game and look forward to the updates!

_childDocuments_.review: The game by it self is great, especially for the price, and even though I have over 65 hours already in it, the last month or two I've barely played it for a couple of reasons:My number one complaint:- If you don't get the right jokers you just die way too easily. Due to the limited options of only being presented 2 jokers during every blind you defeat you there will be runs where you aren't presented with a (strong) mult joker or chip joker. Which is the main mechanic to get large numbers and actually win the game. The reroll mechanic is supposed to help with this but the cost is so high that you only get to do it once or twice in the beginning stages of your run.Secondly, due to the way how interest works in this game it actually promotes you to hang on to your $'s, so it feels double as bad to re-roll and get bad jokers again.- The recent introduced perishable mechanic: Maybe some people like this, I personally don't, mainly cause it ties with my first complaint, on top of being presented bad jokers now the good ones also have a chance to disappear after a couple blinds.Most of this feedback comes from orange stakes (highest difficulty), so I understand there have to be certain mechanics introduced into the game so there's a higher chance at dying, but I wish there was a wider gap between dying from pure bad RNG or actual decision making, the survival rate from trying to make good plays just doesn't feel high enough.

_childDocuments_.review: At its core, Balatro is a testament to the creativity and depth possible in video games. The game challenges you to create powerful synergies by combining valid poker hands with unique Joker cards. This innovative approach not only tests your strategic thinking but also your ability to adapt and overcome the various challenges presented in each run.The journey through Balatro's meticulously crafted levels is a rollercoaster of highs and lows, much like a good poker game. Earning chips to beat the blinds while uncovering hidden bonus hands and decks adds layers of strategy and surprise. The game's roguelike elements ensure that no two playthroughs are the same, providing endless hours of entertainment.What sets Balatro apart is not just its gameplay but also its presentation. The game's aesthetics are both charming and immersive, drawing you into a world where each hand can lead to victory or defeat. The soundtrack complements the experience, enhancing the game's mood and tension.In conclusion, Balatro is a must-play for fans of deck builders, poker enthusiasts, and anyone looking for a game that blends strategy, skill, and a touch of luck. Its unique premise, engaging gameplay, and replayability make it a standout title in the crowded field of indie games. Whether you're a seasoned card shark or new to the genre, Balatro promises a rewarding and enjoyable experience that's well worth the ante.Highly recommended for those looking for a game that challenges the mind and rewards strategic play.Cons:- Only has around 10 hours of content, we need more stuff! and a reason to keep playing beyond finding all the jokers etc- Does not have multiplayer

_childDocuments_.review: As an up-front note, I had to jump through some pretty annoying hoops to get this game to be playable on my laptop, which I found to be a headache and for many games would have just meant refunding it.But for this one? _childDocuments_.review: Great little Roguelike card game.  Close enough cousin to Slay the Spire to mention them in the same breath. Definitely worth doing some research on the game before playing as some interactions are non-obvious, and getting high scoring decks rely on some particular approaches. The biggest weakness in the game is the very large number of Jokers (which are the prime contributors to the scoring system) which makes targetting particular styles, or play very hard and, dare I say, very Rogue-like. Second to this is there's no very easy way to thin decks which is what a closer relative to StS would have.  It's a lot of fun, it's a quick and easy game to play, and to learn about.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so addictive, I haven't been this hooked into a rogue like for ages. Probably since the Slay the Spire! It's so easy to jump into 'one more' game, and the power creep as you work out the perfect joker engine is so satisfying!You sometimes get to a point where it feels less like you're playing a card game, and just maintaining a well oiled machine you've constructed, maximising chips and mults for each hand.I love the art style, that sort of grain pixel art, and each joker is uniquely designed, visually and mechanically. The progression is what you'd want, new deck types and more card unlocks, but no permanent player upgrades. Probably my only big gripe with this game is the Boss Blind's bonus rule. I don't mind - even enjoy - most of them; a certain suit being debuffed, or some cards being drawn facedown is fun to work around. However some are just serious run killers and it doesn't feel particularly fun or satisfying.Specifically I'm talking about the blind which cranks up the cost very significantly, and the blind which only gives you one hand to play. While it's satisfying if you do overcome it. Unless you've already cracked quite a broken engine, these will often kill runs. I personally think that instead of it being a voucher you can buy, you should always be allowed to pay to reroll the Boss blind. Very often $10 is a lot of the player's money so no one is rerolling on a whim. The extra big blind should also be scaled down just a little bit.I say all this, but it's still a really fun game and you can burn through a run quite quickly so perhaps it doesn't matter that much. Just wanted to offer my thoughts!

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT EDIT: Many hours later. 29/31 of the achievements are vanilla attainable in a reasonable amount of time. I believe I got everything but Completionist+ and Completionist++ in ~300 hours. It is abundantly clear the last two achievements are not vanilla friendly unless you're planning on spending a couple thousand runs and a couple thousand hours on it. Highly recommend installing a few QOL gameplay mods to make the runs less RNG focused and more skill expressive and strategy expressive. Then I believe the last two achievements are reasonably possible.EDIT: First balance patch just dropped, I've been playing the balance patch on the beta branch for weeks. I really love this game and with the new changes can confidently recommend this game to everyone. The launch edition felt largely unbalanced and unpolished, the new balance patch has since remedied most of my concerns there.Loved the demo. Enjoying the full game, but the full game is a lot less balanced (read too difficult). They need to nerf some of the blinds, the Arm needs to be deleted from the game, worst blind design IMO. I had a lot more fun playing the demo, I find myself a lot more frustrated with the full game. Jokers need rebalancing, some rare jokers are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, if you're unlucky you'll see only ♥♥♥♥♥♥ common jokers into the late game and just die. Sometimes it feels like the game picks a blind to counter your current build. So many jokers are useless and not worth the cost they come with or their downfalls. Buff positive effects, nerf some of the blinds, re-classify or buff uncommon and rare jokers. Most grow effects grow far too slowly to be useful/worth the investment.Really fun, but needs a lot of love before it's back to the quality of the demo, lots of the new content in the full game feels un-playtested. I love roguelikes based on skill, and churning thru run after run due to luck and or poor play testing on release is annoying. Will update if the game gets the balancing attention it needs. Dark Souls is fun cuz it's hard but skill can get you through most of the difficulty, Balatro feels entirely too RNG-based right now. The demo felt MUCH better and I had much more consistent results.

_childDocuments_.review: I have no clue how this game managed to be as disgustingly addictive as it is, but here we are.While we've seen a LOT of deckbuilding roguelikes in recency (quite frankly, too many), Balatro is not only one of the most literal versions of that genre name, but probably the last one you'll ever need to play.Turning the unchanging constant of table card games that is poker into this weird twisted roguelike is something that sounds pretty simple on paper, but LocalThunk turned it into an extremely nuanced game. This game has a solid core gameplay loop, good visual feedback, a very distinct personality, and is very easy to pick up and play, even if you have no idea what poker is or how it works.I've put so much time into the demos in anticipation for its official release, and here we are.If you're thinking about getting this game, absolutely get it. _childDocuments_.review: I managed to resist the call of Balatro for the longest time because of its poker theming, as I've never gotten into poker and in fact actively dislike it as a game. But then I decided to give Balatro a go finally, on a whim. Despite its dislikeable theme. The price was inviting enough and there was nothing interesting on my wishlist. Why not? I can refund it  within the 2 hour grace period anyway if it's not my thing. It then managed to sneak 11+ hours of playtime from me in one day. That's quite unusual these days. When I went to sleep, all I could think of was all the hands I could be playing, all the combos I could build. The different Jokers in a line smirking at me. Goading me to go on. Just one more round.While the game superficially has a poker card game theme, the actual gameplay has very little to do with it. Sure, the different hands are there and so on, but that's just a safety rail for the player to hold on to. The real Balatro is in the interplay between all the different card types you can have. This Joker affects that suit, this other one gives you multipliers on certain numbers played. The deck building aspect of Balatro is incredibly impressive. It's easy to grasp, but very hard to master. It straddles the perfect balance between being challenging and random, but not frustrating enough to make you go for the Quit Game option after you fail a run. Instead, you'll find yourself starting another one immediately. Maybe this time around the Jokers will grace you with all the right combinations.In short, Balatro is an excellent deck builder with a hypnotising gameplay loop that is sure to captivate your for hours on end. It is easy to pick up but very, very hard to put  down. I am scared of the day this will officially be ported to mobile. And not just for the monetisation opportunities this presents, but for the reason that it will then always be available for me to play. It will be freed from its virtual pen inside my PC. There's always time for just one more round. Right?

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a truly innovative twist on the classic game of poker, seamlessly blending familiar elements with an array of exciting new features. The introduction of 150 unique types of jokers adds a rich layer of strategy and unpredictability, transforming each game into a dynamic and engaging experience. These jokers can do everything from increasing your score and negating losses to granting powerful bonuses to your hands and nullifying negative effects, keeping every round fresh and full of surprises.In addition to the fascinating joker mechanics, the inclusion of tarot cards and bonus card attributes elevates the gameplay even further. These elements introduce additional layers of strategy, allowing players to activate cards twice and unlock special effects that can turn the tide of the game in an instant. Balatro's blend of traditional poker mechanics with these creative twists makes it a must-play for both seasoned card players and newcomers alike. The game’s depth and variety ensure that no two games are ever the same, providing endless hours of entertainment and strategic challenge. Whether you're a fan of poker or just looking for a unique card game experience, Balatro is sure to captivate and delight. - ChatGPT

_childDocuments_.review: I havent been this drawn into a rogue-like for a good while. First thing is the art style, I am completely in love with it. I'm not articulate enough to explain exactly what its like, but the best I have is like its playing a modern/ CRT asthetic. I could totally belive this was a game rebooted from 20 years ago. All the Jokers are just so unique and despite there being so many crazy abilities, you really could ID a Joker (your primary method of creating a 'build' for your run) visually only with enough time. The game play is of course, also excellent. Starting out, it felt like my runs were dying so early and the game is too hard, but with just maybe 2 hours of putting it together you'll start to cook. Poker really is just pattern recognition, and this game makes it fun without any monetary risk. Having a deck with 16 Kings and no 7's is just one example of deck building. Maybe you want NO face cards, maybe you ONLY want face cards, maybe you want all Clubs, maybe no Hearts. Balatro will let you do all that and reward you for it, of course, if you have the wit and luck to get it. This game also lets you get stupid. Its another one that wants you to break it. It wants you to be able to play your 3 of diamonds 4 times and score more than had you played a pair of aces. The game also really feels feature complete from the get go. There are a bunch of unique decks to try, endless mode, challenge decks, harder antes (a regular run with more restrictions). A bunch of Jokers and unique modifiers. All for $15 and you dont need a keyboard to play it. If you like rougelites at all, its easily worth the blind (hehe)Side note this would go hard as a mobile game

_childDocuments_.review: After spending another 35 hours in this game, I'm ready to give a proper review.Let's start off with the main question I've seen..and the main question I had when delving into this game initially: I don't know how to play poker / I'm not good at poker... why would I play this?I'll be real, my only experience prior to Balatro with Poker was playing Poker Night at the Inventory (when I was a young teen) and playing the Mario Poker DS minigame.This game is NOT a poker game as much as it is a roguelike deckbuilder akin to Slay the Spire or Monster Train. Yes, the core mechanics to score are poker related -- but the game allows you to see what you need to score these at any point. It also lets you know if a hand would score.The main scoring will be making choices that impact your run, then rolling with what you're given to proceed to Ante 8 and beat the run. I FULLY recommend this game, it is genuinely close to perfection. My only complaints would maybe be balance at the higher stakes. Overall, this game is a unique experience that will shape future roguelikes to come. The music is fantastic, the presentation is great, and the gameplay is snappy and addictive. Runs can be played at your own leisure, so go as quick or as slow as you'd like.If you like this genre of roguelike at all, do yourself a favor. This game is worthy of being up there with Slay The Spire. If you are reading this and are already addicted and want more of a fix, go check out Luck be a Landlord too :)

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option; it's a seriously fun idea, but the way it is implemented is frustrating. Some jokers, hand types, and boss blinds (especially the bosses) are completely overtuned and overpowered/underpowered. A good run can disappear in an instant when you simply get poor luck trying to fish for the one hand you need to win. _childDocuments_.review: Balatro delivers an addictive rush of pure gaming bliss straight to your brain's happiest receptorsThis game blends the thrill of roguelike deckbuilding with the tense decisions of poker into one irresistibly compelling package. You'll be so focused on assembling ludicrously overpowered combos and watching the numbers get stupidly big that hours will vanish before you know it. Just be ready to snap out of your trance at some point, check the clock, and wonder where the last 6 hours went!

_childDocuments_.review: Balatro is a very exciting, albeit mildly flawed game that I am absolutely *obsessed* with. It's like poker, but you don't really need to know anything about poker, just about the complexities of how to put all these jokers to good use. Nearly 20 hours in and I still feel like I suck, but I'm steadily learning and improving!That being said, I do think the game could use a little more replayability, mainly through content updates that add new jokers and new things to play with. It'd be cool if we could get special joker packs that put only certain joker types into the mix, to add some new types of synergies!I could see the game feeling a little stale after a while, but I've already gotten more than my moneys worth anyways, so who cares? Buy this game.

name: Dystopika
detailed_description: Dystopika is a small city-builder inspired by cyberpunk and the wanderlust of cities that never sleep. Place buildings, giant billboards, and towering holograms, working in harmony with procedural generation for landscape, traffic, and lights to create your own future metropolis rich with vibes and ambience. Escape to your own little dystopian dreams (or nightmares). No goals, no objectives, no wins or losses. Just relax and embrace creative cyberpunk zen. If you love to turn on the cheat codes and just build, this one's for you. Welcome to the Darker Side Of Cozy. Dystopika is an evolving passion project by a solo-developer. Join the Discord community to share your creations, give feedback, and help shape its future.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fascinating little game-toy-thing. You can really get some exciting vistas from it if you put in the effort to carefully place things, and there is absolutely a sense of relaxed aesthetical focusing.That said, here are some things that I'd like to see in the program (consider these as constructive feedback).- Proper height differences in the map, possibly an ability to terraform height levels. This would give variability to the environment and make certain city layouts even more striking. (Like imagine one of those pyramids on a tall hill surrounded by the city.)- Water, or rather, some ocean or river that would give some striking low angle shots of a built up shoreline.- Better control over district types, and preferrably more districts, while the building-based influence system is workable and provides a sense of soft transition, it lacks control, some kind of a map painting system with borders that can be toggled visually on and off depending on if you want it or not- Roads, huge winding highways cutting through a city are a classic staple of especially Japanese style cyberpunk aesthetics. Being able to place those would be fantastic. And in the air, more control over hovercar movement and organization into lanes would make the environment look more "realistic", or rather, "believable". Perhaps via designated "rails" or rather, bezier curve defined routes? Roads and hovercar paths combined with proper terrain (water and heightmap instead of just impassable hills at the edges) would naturally help segment the city in districts in a more believable fashion and also to give some natural transition space between districts.- And of course the thing that no developer wants to hear: more assets. More basic buildings, more billboards, some special ploppable buildings perhaps.All of those things said however, this is a very fun game-toy and I highly enjoyed the time I spent with it. Thank you dev for making this.

_childDocuments_.review: I love it already, it's basically a Blade Runner version of Townscaper.Style and overall vibe/design is straight on point. It's already really well made with a lot of attention to detail, ticks all the boxes of your favourite cyber city and works like a charm. And the music brings it all together.Nonetheless, here is a list of improvements I'd love to see in the future:-please don't force us to unlock everything again, I for example wanted more traffic in my second city and now have to figure out which building unlocks it- more control over colours, for example the red/blue glowing buildings, let us give them our own colour, would diversify the buildings a lot!- more buildings on the different categories, but yeah, that's a no brainer for sure- different maps with other sceneries-the option to turn off lens dirt completely-different fonts for the signs, would diversify the signs a lot and fit the universe even better- let us change the size of the assets in general, not just the height of the buildings, but the overall size of the buildings (with scaling windows perhaps, so they stay the same size and fit the rest) and expecially the size of the decorations. I love the antennas, but some are a little too big and it would diversify the possibilites of adding detail without everything looking the same-ultimately, a simple hover car to fly through the city would be the pinnacle- a little more control over the screenshots, for example to export them as .png or to control the .jpg quality- and of course, mod support! this will make the game immortal for all eternityI do understand some of these will be very difficult to develop and I don't expect you to, some of these are somewhat utopian for a niche title, but I will play and recommend this game nonetheless, have two cool new screenshots already, I am very happy!(yeah, I just discovered the roadmap and now I'm even happier, I'm so looking forward to these updates)

_childDocuments_.review: DystopikaCity building simulator + Cyberpunk. This is Dystopika. The game is a relaxed, chilling city-building simulator in a futuristic cyberpunk world. You have the opportunity to build various high-rise buildings and decorate them with holograms and billboards, for example. You can even upload your own pictures and design your own world. There are many setting options, such as the color of the sun, time oft he day, fog, rain, and many color filters that make the city look different every time. A camera mode is also included to record short videos. There is also first-class, chilled music, so that building becomes a meditative experience, as there is (fortunately in my opinion) no management. This game is just right for players who love cyberpunk + city building, without any kind of management. 10 / 10

_childDocuments_.review: This game has an incredible amount of untapped potential. As much as I appreciate its focus on relaxation, it makes me really want a full-fledged cyberpunk city builder with deeper mechanics challenges, objectives, and resource management. The immersive atmosphere of the cyberpunk genre would blend perfectly with the complexity of managing a sprawling futuristic city, balancing growth, technology, and societal needs.While I'm aware that the current direction of this game is to provide a more laid-back relaxing experience, it's hard not to imagine what it could become with a broader scope. The foundation is already here, and it shows promise for something much more ambitious. I absolutely love what the game offers, and I hope we might see a true cyberpunk city builder in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a game. Atmospheric and moody; visually... neat. But you don't really do anything. Even the building doesn't require much input. You plop a building down and drag it to whatever height you wish, then the surrounding areas automatically populate with smaller buildings. Plop another one down and maybe a billboard appears. Maybe it unlocks a new building style. There are no goals, resources, population, traffic bottlenecks, or any other kind of management. It's a concept. Nothing more. It could be the bones of a pretty interesting game, and I love the aesthetic, but it's definitely not a game yet. With all that said, why am I recommending it? Was that a mistake? No, I meant to do it. The price is on the cheap end, and they're pretty up-front about the fact that it's not much of a game. I took a chance on it, and it just turns out I do need slightly more structure. I didn't think I needed all that much, really. I'll spend hundreds of hours in Space Engineers designing a ship on an empty, dead world, but the ship at least has specs. I have to design around limitations to make something space-worthy... or atmo-worthy. Or both. In Oxygen Not Included, Terraria, Factorio, Rimworld, et al, I rarely complete the "objective" of the game because I'm just enjoying building things, so I thought this might by right up my alley, but I guess I'm not as creative as I'd like to think I am. I need goals and limitations. I need a reason to place the 10th, 100th, and 1000th building. But if you just want to spend a few bucks to scratch that bladerunner/cyberpunk itch without any expectations, then this might be your thing. It just wasn't mine.It's also possible that some things could have changed since I played it. I didn't get around to writing this immediately. It's been a few months.

_childDocuments_.review: Read the store description. There's no management, there's no resources, there's only placing down buildings. That's it. That's all its advertised as, and that's what it says as soon as you open the game. Its never been touted as anything but. You place buildings, buildings interact with eachother sometimes and spawn smaller ones surrounding it, and you build a city. That's all it is.Its a wonderful, beautiful, dystopian building placer, and it lets you clip them and kitbash new kinds. Its wonderful and for not even $10, I've gotten a good amount of time logged, just building a city. I love it.

_childDocuments_.review: Although few people probably want to actually live in a Blade Runner-esque megalopolis, you have to admit they have an extremely cool aesthetic going on. The soaring buildings, the neon glow, the 80-storey tall holographic billboards - they have style to burn. Building a city like that would cost trillions of dollars, real estate's expensive, and let's be honest, who has that kind of time? Well, don't let the visual artists from Johnny Mnemonic have all the fun. Dystopika lets you build the futuristic hellhole of your dreams.Calling Dystopika a game is a bit of a stretch. It's more of a minimalist art project, but without the pretentiousness and pointlessness of the average "art project." There isn't really a game here - there are no resources to collect, no budget to manage, no endlessly irritating little electronic citizens to placate as you run for re-election. There's no zoning to worry about - you want a skyscraper right here? You got it, just plop it down. Oh, you wanted a  skyscraper? Why didn't you say? Take the short one and stretch it until you're happy. Nice building but it's pointed the wrong way? Turn it. No civil engineer ever had it this good. There are a variety of "district types" (read: building aesthetics) you can use, and each one has a few variants. How tall you stretch a building changes how it will look beyond simply height, and if you place buildings close together synergistic elements like skybridges can appear. As you populate your city with buildings, more and more skycars will begin to flit about, their lights dancing in the foggy, drizzling night. (It's always foggy and drizzling in dystopias, but your godlike municipal powers let you turn that off too, if you like.)What would a futuristic dystopia be without ubiquitous, intrusive visual marketing and neon signs? Well, we have a lot of that too, right at your fingertips. Place neon graphic screens the size of the Chrysler building as you see fit. Free-floating holograms? Check. Bright neon signs in pseudo-Japanese characters? Check. Ominous vapor-spewing smokestacks? Well...Okay, so there is a small element of gameplay here. Not everything is available to you at the start. If you want that vapor-spewing stack, you're going to have to unlock it. How? Easy: build stuff! As you build more things and vary what you build, you'll unlock  things. New signs, smokestacks, comm towers, skycar highways - all kinds of stuff awaits. There's even customization. Want that 200 storey holo-billboard to be your friend's face or your Twitch channel logo? Import the graphic and it's done. Bonus: there's a wonderfully atmospheric soundtrack with suitably dystopian-yet-wondrous music. This is something you can pick up and with a few minutes of messing about be creating an awesome looking city. It's that good.Okay, so this title isn't perfect. Very few are. Fortunately, the gripes are pretty low level.First of all, there's nothing driving you here. No scores, no quests, no lore - just your desire to flex your inner Blade Runner architect. So, if you don't have a self-motivating mindset to just create things, you might tire of this one pretty quickly. This isn't a criticism, it's merely a statement of fact.The other thing - also not a big deal but disappointing - is that while there are signs you can place with customizable text, you can't resize them and they don't scale. So if you enter more than about three or four characters, your ubiquitous-marketing-neon eyesore will only be readable with a microscope. That's not the future dystopia way. Worse, they look like they're resizable, but that's just the UI aesthetic; they're fixed. (Or if they're not, I've yet to find out how to change the size.)Finally, there are no tooltips or other guidance. It's strictly trial and error. Granted, with this title that's not a big deal, but it could be a little frustrating for some users. Don't let that put you off, though; there are only a few tools - you'll figure them out quickly.If a chill artistic builder to relax with sounds like something you'd like to do, by all means get this. It's relaxing, it's fun, and it's satisfying to watch your city come to life. With the tools available to you, you can craft your own little future dystopian world ready for you to headcanon a story together for it. It's that good.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Blade Runner when it  was released back in the 80's, I went to see it  with some of my university friends and was enthralled by it.   When  games that remind me of that movie are released I usually buy them as   it brings back fond memories of my university days and the  great friends I made.   I  rarely  buy games on release  these days unless they have a discount; however,  when i saw Dystopika yesterday, I had to have it.   The Steam sale was still on, but I purchased this in preference to a few other games I'd had my eyes on for some time that cost basically the same as  this game  but  they had  decent discounts. That  says a lot for this game.Just watching the  couple of videos  and scrolling through the images on the Steam page, as well as watching  a few  You Tube videos  saw me immediately  going to the games  Steam page and buying it; the first  game I've bought in the Summer 24 Steam sale  together with Green Hell and the only two I've purchased  in this sale.  Well,  diving in and literally spamming my mouse button, moving  the mouse  XY and Z planes  with no particular plan in mind  saw a city  appearing before my eyes, with various unlocks appearing when creating various buildings .  30 minutes later I  had created  a what I would consider a  beautiful  Blade Runner-esque like city;  and, after exploring a few of the  buttons on the left of the screen, I was able to add advertising  screens, floating bill boards and  logos on many of the buildings, as well as the ability to change the  time of day and other environmental effects. The game was made with Unity,  and I must say, it was  very well made.  Okay I've only played the game for about 45 minutes and  have thoroughly enjoyed playing  it.  That said I would expect extended play may become a little tedious after several hours of game play unless the developer has more extend plans for  the development of the game.   There is apparently a development  road map, but I've not checked it out yet as I wanted to post a reasonably positive  initial review of the game as soon as I'd finished playing it for the first time.   I reckon  the occasional  play  would be a great  way to unwind and see something gorgeous appear before your eyes after half an hour or so's game  play.For the future  I'd love to see  the ability to  walk, drive or fly  around the city in third or first person;  IMO that would   make this game amazing.  Whether that is possible using the Unity engine I really do not know?Anyway,  big thumbs up from me;  for the measly full price of  £5.89,  Dystopika is well worth buying at full price; more so if you love Blade Runner, if only to support the dedicated  sole developer of this game.Thank you for creating Dystopia, I'm very impressed and pleased to have    bought it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is actually really fun and I found it quite enjoyable for these reasons.- A cyberpunk city builder- the dark synthwave/ synthwave soundtrack that fits seamlessly- Meming on billboards is a big plus- making the buildings big or small and watching them bridge together- no resource farming, just click and build to your hearts content- after a while the city really does feel lived in especially with hundreds of billboardsI've played about 3 hours to get all achievements, so it's not a long or difficult game to 100%, but that said those 3 hours have been fun and enjoyable to bring a cyberpunk city to life.I will definitely be adding more hours in the future and can't wait to see what will be added in future updates.

_childDocuments_.review: really fun to just build, highly recommend it for anyone looking just for a relaxing game to build, although there are some issues i have that i hope the developer can perhaps patch out.- the option to have the same building i just placed down, since repetitive placement feels a bit annoying- workshop support would also be really nice to further the diversity of the buildable structures- while i could just say "more buildings" i want more small buildings, just things which i can use to fill that blank space and give my cities a more impressive sense of scale- on the similar note, more district categories for more diverse areas so that different stories could be shown, perhaps some sort of neo-gothic architecture sort of like in the first blade runner, or any number of new districts would be a delight to explore- better road management, since roads currently are really hard to make into well crafted straight lines, or perfect circles, and can be hard to work with since their chaoticness can destroy the futuristic look, yet when theyre used well they work super well to ground your city and to sort of seperate the city in a way which makes it more aesthetically appealing.- in the photo mode, having the option to have more than 2 keyframes would also be pretty useful, along with some way to recording what you have made in the game natively.all that aside, this game is 100% worth the 7 dollars, i highly recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Desktop Simulator 2024.What we have here is a city builder but without the fluff of resource and population management. Indeed, there are no resource mechanics at all. This is a pure plug-n-play atmospheric adventure as you build the Cyberpunk city of your dreams (or nightmares). There's only a handful of things to "unlock", and it's usually just a matter of scaling some buildings to their maximum heights but there's also a handful of new decor items you get just by placing the right kinds of buildings around various places.The dev put out a video stating that he played City Sim games with cheats on so he could make a city befitting his own vision. I felt that to a severe degree, it's the exact thing I did on the first successful Cities: Skylines game, I barely played a vanilla run of that at all and vastly preferred to just upload a bunch of prefabs from the workshop and just shape a cool circular city to my own proper vision. And I believe workshop support is on the to-do list here.This game has a fun feature in that you can upload a variety of images from your computer to serve as advertisements and postings in the game, with a holographic filter. I had great fun shuffling through my 2077 screenshot folder to discover that it's like, 90% glamour shots of my character, making my mercenary look like a model or movie star in this game. I should probably find a bunch of screenshots of cars or something.Any nitpicks I have might be fixed over time. For example; You can rotate, rise, and move your buildings around but I find controlling that is incredibly fickle. I find myself accidentally placing another building, or just trying to move my cursor around to find the right "spot" where the game registers that I want to rotate or move it properly. I'd prefer to be able to rotate my buildings before placing them at all to avoid this frustation, and a user on the Discord said that it was another thing on the "to do" list.On a similar vein, I wish we had more control over which of the sets of buildings I can place. This game is in serious need of hotkeys so I could quickly tap 1 through 9 to cycle through a specific "look" of buildings. As it stands the only thing we can really do is spam our right click in hopes it eventually gets to a type of building I want. It's possible to do but taxing and time-wasting.Ultimately the nitpicks here seem to amount to "control". I need more control over what I'm about to place and how I'm going to do it. Again, at least one of these complaints is already on deck to be fixed.As of typing this review I have recorded and edited an hour-long build, followed by a sequel video of a few minutes with the in-game's drone-shot capabilities. The cuts lead to some hiccups with the in-game's soundtrack (of which there are only two tracks, I'm sure he'll add to that as well).It's still an absolute vibe of a game and highly recommend if you just want a pure asset-plop sandbox.

_childDocuments_.review: It looks very impressive and has a lot of potential, but for a game with an accent on creativity it's lacking way too much freedom. When placing buildings the game would automatically generate tiny filler-type buildings to create density, but there's no control over it. I wanted to take advantage of clipping buildings through each other to create my own type of megastructure, but the more buildings I place - the more filler generates around them, creating a mess I have no control over. We need a tool to brush away these filler building, similar to the existing lighting tool. It would also help with creating a wasteland type of area, where I'd prefer to have a select few buildings with no density.I felt like Alpha and Omega were antipods of each other and wanted to create districts based on that, but there's not enough gritty structures to match the Alpha megastructure aesthetic. Storepage screenshots make it feel like you have control over the city's color scheme, but you can't theme the city around a certain color for there's no setting to control lighting aside from the lighting brush, that just lights up buildings in preset random colors.The worst sin of the game by far is the roads management. You can't seemlessly connect roads. Forget about tidy intersections and branching routes, you either can make singular point A to point B strips or loops. You can make roads any length, but they always only have 4 nodes, so the longer the road - the harder it is to adjust. Also these nodes are tiny and impossible to see when zoomed out, not to mention that they're also hard to pin point with the mouse.I would personally like to see more militaristic props and buildings. Omega's design enspires to create some sort of space related military base.I love the concept and I love how it looks, but it feels like it's a beta of the game with some of these seemingly obvious fundamental features that a city builder needs missing. Every time I get a cool design idea for the city I get shut down by the game's limitations. It's worth buying, but also heavily lacking. I hope I could finish my city in the future with more features added. 6/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a sandbox city builder in a dystopian cyberpunk setting. It takes a very different approach compared to other games of its type and is more of an 'experience' than a game in a way.In Dystopika, there are no goals or barriers. No ressources to manage, no money to run out of, no buildings to burn down. All you do is place buildings, rotate and scale them. Then, you can add decorations. These are quite varied and range from typical neon-lit billboards all the way to the floating cyberpunk aerial ad things to custom images you can import from your device. This in and of it self is really cool and allows for the players to create some truly creative cities. And that is about all you do.After spending some time on your very own version of Night City it is time to capture it in all of its glory, and if you so wish turn Night City into Day City. Thanks to lots of sliders and camera options you can tune everything from the weather, time of day or fog to your liking and create a perfect screenshot of your creation.In the beginning i said that Dystopika is more of an experience. And that is made clear by the ambience it creates. Thanks to the fantastic soundtrack that really manages to hit the ambient cyberpunk vibe you feel a lot more immersed in the world and the city you are shaping. In combination with the clear image of the city itself, it helps create that very distinct and special cyberpunk feel.This game is still a WIP. And as such, there are always incoming updates adding new features. Highway streets and rails were added in the last one and thanks to community contests with set themes the game is kept alive. However it is still quite easy to get bored with this game. After building my very first city, i was done with the game and pretty much forget about it again until recently, since there is not really that much variety in what you can build. I think this game would greatly benefit from even more options, like landscaping tools, more streets as such and even more buildings and decorations.But overall, Dystopika is a pretty cool game and a fresh take on city builders. However don't expect it to keep you busy for a long time. If you're creative and looking for a quick relaxing trip into a cyberpunk world, then you'll be right at home.Check out my curator page;

You plop down structures and watch as a dystopian future city grows and evolves with every new thing you add to it, megastructures seamlessly connecting and interacting with one another, while smaller buildings start rising up around them while oppressive neon signs start popping up and filling your jungle of concrete and steel with corporate color. _childDocuments_.review: Shockingly relaxing city sandbox game, given that your "goal" is to build a dystopian cyberpunk metropolis. "Goal" is in quotes because there isn't really a goal for you to hit - from the moment you start your new city, there's nothing stopping you from doing whatever you want. Buildings and structures are placed as opposed to grown (no zoning), and flying traffic starts populating the skies as you continue placing more and more buildings. You can drag buildings to be taller, changing their design the taller they become. Signs - static and customized (you can upload your own images for most signs) - can be placed against your buildings. Skyways can be built atop your skyscrapers.There are unlockables which will provide a sense of progression, but you can likely unlock everything within the first hour or two of gameplay (as of 6/26/2024).Dystopika has a LOT of potential. Here's hoping the developer adds more buildings, structures, and maybe some sort of first-person observation mode? The one con I can give right now is that there really isn't much building variety at the time of this review - and for a sandbox city-builder, variety is king.Definitely the sort of gaming experience which encourages short game sessions. That said, each session - at least for me - proves to be really peaceful as I explore and craft the cyberpunk megacity of my dreams. And I have every intention to continue promoting this unique city-building experience!

_childDocuments_.review: So I want to be 100% transparent with this review. I only have 46 minutes logged in game. But believe me when I say that that's more than enough to experience what Dystopika has to offer.      Don't get me wrong. It functions well, no loss in frame rates surprisingly. The content that is here is ROCK SOLID.  It's a great foundation to build off of, and on the right track.     But the issue is the lack of control that I have as a player.  It allows me to erect a city from nothing in a quick easily accessible format that everyone will understand no problem. But if you're trying to build something EXTREMELY specific, it's hard to grasp anything that isn't random.  Let me clarify. If you already have a detailed map of what you're attempting to recreate in this game, you  might as well just scrap that design, because it'll be far more effort for you to replicate a detailed blueprint than it will be to just make something simple and quickly.  I am in the camp of people who purchased this game in order to build something very specific. I have a bird's eye view map, and that's all it is.  2 dimensions. I had hoped with this game, I could fully realize that city in a 3D environment. At this rate, I'd be far better off going to VR and working with a program known as Tiltbrush/Openbrush.   But this is not a knock against the singular dev behind this game. This is GREAT and very impressive work. It's just that this game has a long way to go. As a city builder, it really needs a good measure of ultimate control. And outside of building itself, it lacks an identity. And that's something that I strongly feel that it needs.  As it stands, you're not gonna see a bunch of players dedicate several hours to this, and that's a shame, because as I said previously, the mechanics work surprisingly very well.I understand that the developer doesn't want this to be another city building sim. But it needs to fulfill a greater purpose than just a "chill" city builder. Perhaps they could include features that allow this game to passively run in the background of your PC, and give you an animated desktop?  Perhaps you could zoom in to the micro scale and see the life that inhabits your streets like an artificial ant farm? The type of things that gets procedural generation.  I'm just trying to insert ambition here where there is none. This idea can and SHOULD be expanded upon.  Let's give it a few more years in the oven, and see where it goes? That's my current stance. I think most people are gonna arrive at the same conclusion as me.  The asking price was great! No complaints there. I honestly can't complain about anything that is here. I can only complain about things that aren't here. And that's a great creative place to be! Hope it all works out for the developer and the fans!

_childDocuments_.review: As a kid, I would always draw a futuristic skyline on paper with my imagination. I used all of my imagination based from what I've seen in the movies and also utilized my own skills. Recently, I've seen an ad somewhere on YT regarding on building a dystopian cyberpunk city without objectives, and stress free. That's exactly what I've been looking for! Without any hesitation, I purchased this game with excitement. I am well aware that its not for everyone especially for someone who wants a fast pace game play. In my own opinion, I would not even consider this a game, but its more on a PIECE of ART. This is such a unique piece where someone can build their own and express their own skills and the ability to plan, design and construct. It has a various building types, multiple options to select and create your own, and you can even upload your own photos and literally paste it on any building you desire. Not to mention where you can select your favorable weather and time of the day. All of these for a price of Ramen. It is truly a darker side of cozy where you can immerse yourself and explore from the very bottom of the gritty, dark world, to build from one establishment, into your own empire! My only wish for this into a foreseeable future is to have more additional content such as building designs, floating restaurants or similar, an expansion of a building area, more customization designs, and music options. I'd personally pay more for additional content. I'm very impressed, and I highly recommend this to anyone who are into cyberpunk city and those who loves to express their own designs without limitations.

_childDocuments_.review: In a genre so dark and filled with the despair associated with late-stage capitalist sprawl (and cybernetics, of course), Dystopika is the light at the end of the tunnel that is commonly found in Cyberpunk titles. Relaxing, calm, everything you would not expect to find in a city builder within the very genre that spawned the TTRPG of the same name, Cyberpunk 2077, Blade Runner, etc. Gameplay is fluid, as if you're dynamically painting on a 3D canvas that only allows the palette of towering mega-complexes and neon lights to take form. I should also note that the artistic style of Dystopika does well to not overdo the nuances of the genre - the balance between east-Asian commercialism and western Brutalist architecture is perfect. It does not come off as "cartoony" or satirical, yet does not take itself too seriously. This is a passion project from someone who is enamored with the Cyberpunk aesthetic, and it shows. With that being said, I would like to see a little more variety in the buildings you can place and maybe more weather options.This is a passion project of a solo dev that only costs $7.00 USD (the total cost of an expansion/DLC in Cities: Skylines) and given the masterclass representation this game gives to the Cyberpunk genre, I have to recommend this game. Whether you enjoy chill city builders, creative sandboxes, or have a taste for Cyberpunk cues: this is a great game to relax and let your creative juices flow.

_childDocuments_.review: Surprisingly addicting for a game with no set goals or objectives, Dystopika is a self-described "darkly cozy" city builder where you can create the cyberpunk skyline of your dreams. Or, if you're me, a solarpunk city on a rainy evening.Created by a single developer and inspired by nights walking the streets of sleepless cities in Japan, Indonesia and the like, Dystopika allows you to place a number of buildings anywhere in a large square area, adjust their height and facing, and then decorate them with neon signs, configurable text and image displays, the latter of which let you import your own images to project. Smaller structures and flying car traffic will appear organically around the ones you place through procedural generation, and you will unlock new decorations, including rotating holograms, simply by playing around with the tools. There is also a lighting brush that will cause smaller lights and neon signs to appear where you click.Currently available structures are grouped into categories or "districts", with special ones set aside for two available Megastructures- The brick-shaped Alpha Corp and ziggurat-esque Omega corp buildings, strongly remencisent of the Genom building from Bubblegum Crisis or the Metacorp building from Beyond Sunset. Other structures include "Central BD", whose buildings most closely resemble typical high-rise office buildings of the genre, with more sparing use of neon, "New Eden", which have more fanciful, sloping architecture and prominently lit surfaces for more of a Hong Kong or Shanghai look, and "Lowtown," which have a grittier, blockier appearance, looking more like the stacks of habitation blocks from The Ascent, with red lighting, loose cabling, and interconnecting bridges, more closely resembling the buildings of Judge Dredd or Cyperpunk 2077. One hexagonal Lowtown building strongly resembles the police headquarters of Blade Runner, and by extension, Nagatomi Plaza of SNATCHER.You can also set the weather effects, time of day and soundtrack, though at present there are only two playlists consisting of low-key synth music to vibe to. There is also a photo mode that has tools to further fine-tune the visuals of the scene.A roadmap is already in place, promising new buildings and features down the road.There's not a whole lot else to say, merely that the vibes, as they say, are immaculate. Dystopkia has come the closest to letting me recreate the city that my OCs live in of any program I've used. I've heard that screenshots from the game will be able to be used in other projects under a Creative Commons license- great if you're an artist like me who loves drawing characters but hates drawing backgrounds. And, to quote the developer, it costs less then a bowl of ramen.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'll open with a heads-up. This isn't exactly a city builder. You won't be laying roads or water pipes. You won't be building schools or airports. You won't be managing, well.. anything. It's really more of a city painter than anything. And for the price tag, that's just fine.Crank up the rain and chill to the cozy dark-synth tunes while you plop down buildings, move and rotate them or even raise them up to the skies. As you go, you'll unlock little doodads to attach to your buildings or the surrounding landscape to provide a little more personalization to your dystopian concrete jungle.What more can you ask for the cost of a cheap lunch? Check it out!

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING: If you go looking for mods, like billboard mods, on the discord server for this game, be careful of AI artists posting on the modding channel. Usually, they mention what they share is AI, but not always.Onto the review.If you liked Islanders, you'll love this!Simplistic, satisfying, cheap in price while high in quality and customization.The options in photo mode are especially impressive, including a video clip mode!And with more planned, it's only gonna get better.Here's my feedback on what's still needed.- A way to swap back to a structure you passed by, so you don't have to cycle through the whole thing to find it again.- More structures per district to really flesh out the look of the districts.- Toggle to keep the structure you placed so you can place multiple of the same thing more easily.- Way to view the city from the ground as a citizen, if possible. Get an immersive up-close feel of the city as you walk around it.- Way to reposition lights and holograms, similar to structures.

_childDocuments_.review: Not quite as expansive and expressive as Townscaper. It teeters uncomfortably between the idea of "wave your mouse and magic happens" and "you have to micromanage everything".  For instance, you have to place and resize every mega-building. Every. One. Each one you place will be the smallest version, so you've got to do a second motion to size it up. On the other hand, all the little buildings pop up automatically. Similarly, you can attach decorations to large buildings, but you just kind of paint them on to the lower levels.So, I want control but also less control. I wish there was a mode that just made a random city like POOF and then did a flythrough of it. I'm not sure the developer understands that the joy I get from their work is not in the building so much as the flying.I still recommend it, of course, but there's a healthy bit of hope that it continues growing and changing.

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a cyberpunk city builder that offers an incredibly relaxing and creative escape from the hustle and bustle of everyday life. From the moment you dive in, you'll be captivated by its stunning futuristic aesthetic, inspired by neon-lit Asian cities at night. Imagine walking through rain-soaked streets, with towering skyscrapers and huge, glowing advertisements straight out of Blade Runner or Ghost in the Shell. It's not just a game; it's a canvas where you can build and decorate your own cyberpunk cityscape, adding corporate logos, commercials, and a myriad of decorations to bring your vision to life.What really sets Dystopika apart is its focus on creativity over traditional gameplay mechanics. There are no end goals or stressful city management tasks, just pure, unadulterated building fun. You can let your imagination run wild, creating everything from small neon-lit alleys to sprawling, futuristic metropolises. Sure, there might be fewer building options compared to something like Cities: Skylines, but the charm and beauty of Dystopika more than make up for it. Plus, the ability to import your own images and add flying traffic or holographic light shows makes every city unique.Highly recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: A therapeutic game with no real objective, no stress of city management but you can make some of the prettiest (or grim) cities in the genre. Would also be nice to have customizeable media on the flying vehicles and holograms. Custom MP3 implementation would be great as well, just give me all the personalized media possible. On top of that, a pathing system for the camera flythrough mechanic, instead of the camera choosing its own path (it looks good as is but I want a flyby tuned just how I want it).Will be buying this for friends before the Steam sale ends. Ridiculously good little city building tool.

_childDocuments_.review: The game's motto "the dark side of cozy" is a phrase that resonates with me on a personal level. As a long-time fan of the Blade Runner series and other cyberpunk media, I have found most of this genre’s atmosphere, soundtracks, and visuals to be so relaxing and tranquil. However, this has caused some existential struggle within me, because despite loving the odd "coziness" these worlds emanate, they are inherently dystopian futures, the worst possible outcome for humanity. Yet, somehow, falling to sleep to the ambience of the neon-soaked streets is the only thing that will allow me to sleep these days. Dystopika is the embodiment of everything I have written above. It is relaxing, cozy, dark, and ambient. The anxiety and pressures of life seem to melt away even for just a few minutes. Constructing the darkest, most miserable, dystopian city my mind can conjure, with every meticulous detail correctly positioned and placed, is enough to pull me out of a bad mindset and feel some sense of odd *validation*. It is as if the game is saying, in all its umbral windy whispers "Yes, that feeling is misery. Weighty. Chronic. Misery. Let it wash away in the rain and run down the gutters. This is *home*.” I am still not sure why I find cyberpunk cities so appealing. Maybe it is the neon lights, the sound of the rain, or the urban ambience, but to finally have a game that is just purely the cozy side of cyberpunk, with no goals, no management, it feels validating. It is the perfect way to unwind after a long day, or when getting ready for bed. My only complaint is I cannot walk the streets in the first-person perspective and experience my cities at the most gritty and personal level possible. However, with the roadmap outlining a plethora of future content and the promise of mod support, I am dying to see what else this game has to offer. Thank you, developer Matt, for creating this game!

_childDocuments_.review: This game found me in a very dark time. _childDocuments_.review: First off, yes, I only marked this review as negative for the attention, BUT BEFORE YOU SEND ME THE CLOWN STEAM AWARD: Know that I'd far rather mark this as informative if I had the option, as that's what I want this review to be. (also if you want to, send me the award anyway I'll enjoy the free steam points). If after these things said you still come into the review with anger at me, fine.Now, why did I refund? _childDocuments_.review: Dystopika - Chill Cyberpunk City CrafterTLDR: Good, relaxing but very simple city-builder game. Watch a review (maybe mine?  ) before you buy so you know what you are getting.Full Review:Dystopika is a cyberpunk city builder developed over one year by a single Dev, Matt Marshall. This is reflected in the Price, complexity and development schedule of the game, but is not in any way a criticism.This is one of those games where you need to be fully aware of what you are getting before you get it, and whilst the game info is very clear about what it is, I see some other reviews stating they were disappointed or got bored quickly. This is not like a traditional city builder where you manage finances,services,population, traffic and much of the other minutiae you would expect in a more realistic city builder.Dystopika is a game rooted in aesthetics and relaxation. Think of it like a zen sand garden, but instead of moving sand you are placing buildings in a Blade Runner-esque dystopian world. This is the main game play element here, pick, place, rotate and scale buildings in your cyber punk city until it looks and feels as you want it to. There is a light painting tool which allows you to selectively light your city and a great camera mode to photograph the end result. There are also some small decorative pieces that you can unlock and place on buildings for some customisation also.But the main game play is Pick, Place, Rotate and Scale, that is it. Now depending on who you are and where your expectations are set this may be a problem for you. That is why I recommend doing some research first and watching some game play, as to leave a bad review for the game on that basis when it is so transparent about what it is would be disingenuous.The game looks beautiful and was inspired by the Dev's travels around Asia and films like Blade Runner and Ghost In The Shell. For me I got really powerful Blade Runner vibes, giant holograms, advertisement airships that fly around the city, hover vehicles and the architecture of the buildings themselves all screamed Blade Runner to me. If you remember the opening scene to Blade Runner where the camera pans over the City you will know exactly what I mean.Speaking of camera work, once you city is complete and looks as you want it to there is a great camera mode where you can fiddle with loads of different environmental and camera effects to take some beautiful shots of your city. Rain, fog, time of day, light colour and direction, exposure, lens flare and a host of other options make the photo mode a joy to play with and capture what you have created.In Summary:If you want a beautiful game with very little learning curve that you can pick up and put down almost instantly and put as much or as little thought into as you want then this is great. Its the kind of game you play to decompress after a hectic day and just make something beautiful quickly and easily.If you are looking for cities skylines or games of that ilk then this is not the game for you, do not expect hours of game play  per session or massive amounts of unlocks and customisations (although more are coming). This game does exactly what it says on the tin, and does it very well. Just make sure you read the tin!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: First, as the game will tell you in the intro, this game has no goal, no challenge and no win or lose state.  If you do not like that then this game is not for you.This games designed to unwind to...its a catagory of game known as a chill game...designed to, as the name says, chill out to.You'll be given a nice big square of land and you literally create a cyberpunk city, with, as of writing, 5 styles/districts to choose from, ranging from super scifi with the new eden set to blade runner or megacity one with the central BD and lowtown sets...it also includes two 'megacorp' buildings.  As you play you will unlock new decorations, ranging from giant holograms to things as simple as radio towers and landing pads for the many tiny little flying cars.You can also place billboards and signs on said buildings, with the option to fully customize them...image billboards can be switched as simply as hitting I while a billboards selected and clicking an image of your choice, with the game smoothly handling autosize and cropping for you.  You can also select time of day and weather, as well as alter the bloom and glow on billboards and signs and ingame lighting to your satisfactionOnce your masterpiece is complete, you can take screenshots with a selection of filters at your disposal which will be saved to both your steam folder and a screenshot folder that can be accessed instantly via a button on the main menu...and thats itThats dystopika, a work of love by a guy called Matt.  He already has a development roadmap up that promises more features too, ranging from new decorations, bug fixes, language settings, usability features, increased camera controls, city presets...new megastructures and districts...the list goes onMy only warning is that due to the huge detail this game has, it will make even a high level graphics card run hot but that is one tiny ♥♥♥♥♥♥ in a otherwise perfect game.  If you wanna put your feet up and create the next night city, blade runner or megacity one, then this game is for you.

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika Review: A Neon-Soaked Sandbox of ChillIf you've ever dreamed of escaping to a world where neon lights never flicker out, traffic flows like glowing rivers, and towering holograms loom over streets drenched in perpetual rain, Dystopika might just be your digital sanctuary.This isn’t your typical city-builder. Forget about managing budgets, appeasing virtual citizens, or fending off disasters. Instead, Dystopika hands you a blank cyberpunk canvas and says, “Go wild.” It’s the perfect playground for the creative spirits who just want to build—no strings attached, no stress, just vibes.From the moment you dive in, you’re greeted by an infinite grid that’s yours to shape. Skyscrapers rise at your whim, massive billboards beam ads for products you’ll never buy, and holograms shimmer with that retro-futuristic charm. Procedurally generated landscapes, ambient traffic, and dynamic lights keep the city alive, even as you tweak and perfect every corner. It’s like being the architect of your very own sci-fi daydream—or dystopian nightmare.The lack of objectives might not be for everyone, but that’s kind of the point. Dystopika isn’t about “winning.” It’s about zoning out to a lo-fi synth soundtrack, watching your city’s glow grow richer, and losing yourself in a neon utopia of your own making.Final Take: If you're into city-builders but hate the stress of deadlines, or you’ve ever wanted to live in a Blade Runner postcard, Dystopika is a must-try. It's like a warm cup of cyber-coffee: comforting, creative, and just a little dark. Welcome to the darker side of cozy—we think you’ll want to stay a while.Rating: 🌃🌌🌟 (3/3 neon lights)

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a standout title in the city-building genre, known for its **relaxed pace** that distinguishes it from more traditional management games. Set in a captivating cyberpunk world, it invites players to create without the stress of strict objectives or resource limitations. The game offers a **chill experience**, allowing you to build your city at your own speed. Starting with a blank canvas, players can gradually expand their metropolis with stunning skyscrapers and vibrant neon lights. The leisurely pace encourages appreciation of the game's beautiful visuals and atmospheric soundscapes. Dystopika's simple mechanics make it accessible for newcomers, ensuring that anyone can enjoy the creative process without feeling overwhelmed. This game prioritises **aesthetic choices** and personal creativity, making it ideal for those looking to unwind. It transforms gaming into a meditative experience, perfect for casual sessions focused on relaxation. Overall, Dystopika provides an enjoyable escape into a beautifully crafted cyberpunk universe, where creativity flourishes without pressure.
