_childDocuments_.review: A nice cozy game with relaxing music. I'm a big fan of cyberpunk and miniature diorama's so this is a natural fit for me.As it is the game is fun for about an hour or two, at which point you have seen most things it has to offer. Whether that's worth the cost is up to you. It is for me. There's definitely room to expand upon the game:-  More (distinct) buildings and sectors, more industrial looking buildings are a good start. -  Better controls over road building, especally for making roads and combining them. - More control over the automatically generated buildings, they function well as filler but can become a nuisance if you want more finegrained control- More weather/light options, and a randomizer button you can easily press without going into the menu to change the look- Modding or workshop support, even in the form of simple themed packs of images that can be used in game would be great. - In general with some of the above changes one could easily give more of a futuristic scifi-vibe to the game. Some of the themes of the weekly challenges suggest we're not playing on earth per se, so the dev could easily push into that direction with more outlandish weathers and buildings. The more buildings you place, the more the world fills out. Then you can move things around to make them look more natural. Once you've finished, zoom out and appreciate your work. Snap a pic of it. Then start again, or add/subtract more to your current city.Dystopika is a work of art, you just gotta find it!CONS: All that being said, it's lacking a bit on the finer details. I feel like there's a limited selection of props/buildings to choose from, and when you get to the nitty gritty, it can be tough to make a consistently unique city.PROS from the CONS: From far away, the skylines look *chef's kiss*

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I played Cyberpunk or saw the Bladerunner movies I've been wanting a game like this so badly... This game is so good, its definitely one of those games to play when you've got nothing to play, you can just chill and listen to some music and hours will pass before you realize. One thing I wished this game had is a bigger map... I like building many things but run out of space quickly and all i can do is to start a new city, the game REALLY needs bigger maps.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I just completed building my first cityscape (2 hours gameplay). At first, I just fiddled with the controls and buildings, but slowly as I began getting a feel for the (very intuitive) controls, districts and city flow began surfacing and taking shape organically. The music and atmosphere of the game are amazing. If you enjoy city builders, sandbox modes, cyberpunk/distopian settings - this game is absolutely for you! Lose yourself in the ambiance of a city you bring to life - or as many cities as you like! I'm sure next time I boot this game up, I'll go down a far different design path, allowing my brain to explore even further into what this beautiful game has to offer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The game is quite nice, very reminiscent of older city builders - without worry of running out of resources or bringing down some bar mechanic that would be detrimental to your playthrough. Just plain ol' building while beautiful and calm music plays. Wonderful for late nights without any stressful rushing or worrying about having things set as perfect, you just enjoy and build. A wonderful escape. Definitely worth the money, and time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I picked this up pretty much to take a peek and support a project that looks like it was worth supporting. Bought it, messed with it for a few minutes and that was it.Today I just spent nearly 2 hours with my five year old and we are both having a blast!Well worth the price, and I am looking forward to seeing where this goes in the long term.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is one of those games that just feels cool right from the start. its not just a game you are entering a mood, cool art that pulls you in and the music? super chill—it’s perfect for just zoning out and getting lost in the dark dystopian futuristic vibe. its fun how you get to add buildings and watch them connect, adding lights and decors and slowly turning into a city. and its satisfying to see your dystopian world come together and becoming alive. If you’re looking for something to relax with that still keeps your interest, Dystopika is a solid pick. plus you get super cool screenshots 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Fun and simple. Very aesthetically pleasing and relaxing. Not much more to it than that. Wish there was some more substance to the game, I don't think it is something that will keep me coming back, but I was happy exploring it. Certainly not for those who are looking for a fully fleshed out city builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I have played little, but I have nothing bad to say. The game is at an early stage and still very entertaining. Mostly I have faith in it for the future. It would be awesome to add more customization for the neon and advertising signs, as well as more variety of buildings (which you can actually make interesting combinations anyway) and add workshop. The community would undoubtedly make this game a sandbox masterpiece. Imagine being able to model buildings for the workshop, incredible.  In short, the game is what many people, including me, have been waiting for a long time. An entertaining and relaxing sandbox. It has a lot of potential, I support it a lot. I hope this game makes history in the genre, and more in the Cyberpunk aesthetics loving community, we deserve to be pampered once and for all. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool and I hope it is popular enough that the dev gets the space and funds to update it and make a sequel. Relaxing cozy late night vibes. Lot of customisable images and writing to give your city its own story. I've made post-apocalyptic cities, dystopias and android-supremacist cities. Dev very engaged on Discord and making lots of updates based on user requests too and community upload reusable images and such. If you like the game definitely check that out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Happy I gave it a chance, think this is a game that I've had the most fun with while "playing" the least, and often find myself just watching and listening rather than creating. I can't think of any issues I had with the content it has so far, just wish there was more of it, along with better/more advanced camera controls as I'd love to have some looping sweeps of the city for a background/ambient screen, and given the current roadmap I'm excited to see what is added.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game. It's the perfect game to just relax your mind and chill to. Very dark vibes as you build a dystopian city. There are no goals or achievements or anything, just building and editing this super realistic/steampunk sort of chill metropolis. I truly hope that they continue to add more building, props, and lighting effects, as that would be the only area for critique. But, the fact that it's so cheap, you definitely get much more than your money's worth, which feels odd in this day and age to say about any company. They could double the price and I would still recommend the purchase, especially if they continue to add those few things.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Nice chill cyberpunk city builder sandbox. Has you play around a bit to unlock a few styles of building and decor/billboard, but no major roadblocks to getting in and playing around, or just letting it sit as some atmospheric ASMR.Looking forward to seeing the future updates planned to expand it further, but already recommend it as well worth the low asking price already.Update: Continued to see great updates, plus community challenges on the Discord.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: What a lovely game to get lost in. Just build and expand at any rate you like, there's no goal just drop buildings and signage as you please.Some notes: I'd like to move the camera around by moving the mouse to edge of the screen like most builder games. I would also like to be able to plant many of the same building without having to rotate through all the buildings.Lovely game and worth the money.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A chill cyberpunk game where you make a city, that's it; the whole game is chill and take screenshots. The game doesn't try to be anything else, it is upfront with what it is. No management like City Skylines.One guy's passion project that is reasonably priced and is being updated still not sure what more you could ask for.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw the movie Bladerunner the images that stuck were the spinner (flying car) travelling over the dystopian, cyberpunk city of the future.  It was amazing and influential in my world view.  This game captures that those feelings.  Actually I don't think this is not so much a game as it is a medium for creating art.    A visual, dynamic, dark, urban, and dystopian art. Well worth it.Edit.The updates to the game have been really neat to see.  They really add to the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you need some inspiration for a short story, ttrpg campaign or terrain for 40k, then this game is what you're looking for. Just build a couple districts, make a screenshot and keep it as a reference. Much faster than building things in a 3D software or drawing a whole city. Music is pretty good too.There are some features that I'd like to see being added. For example making long bridges and more transport systems, but overall I'm pretty pleased with the work put into this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is what you need if you want to relax and go to another realm of creation.  Similar but still has differences to Townscaper.  Different vibe and theme for sure, and some extra mechanics.  I don't know where to start, because I'm still getting into it and I love it.  The random unlocks from combining buildings is pretty cool too because they are added to your list of options to decorate your buildings and make them different from your last city.  The music fits very well with the game and has a vibe that puts you into the game.  I was watching the developer live video, was recorded when I had watched it.  he mentions finding some more music for the game and I think something that might fit the theme would be some synth-wave.  i could go on but don't want to type a wall.  And you can run it in the background and have some chill music while you work or read.  Try it out its cheaper than a drive through coffee!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Really a great game, especially for the price. It's fun to mess around with and I've made a few wallpaper worthy cities. The building system is intuitive, the graphics and lighting make it look really nice, and the building styles are cool and give you a lot to work with to create your "vibe" of futuristic city. From tall, fancy looking neon cities to low down, gritty looking slums, you can really create the kind of city you're going for. The camera system is nice as well, and gives you a lot of filters and options to get some really nice screenshots. Overall, a very nice game, would recommend. (Also, huge props to the dev for being so active with community challenges and updates!)
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A relaxing game that allows me to unwind and design a city with a dark synthwave/ synthwave soundtrack that fits wonderfully. No resource farming, complications of any sort. just build and sort and enjoy. I for one, cannot wait for the future updates and designs that I will be able to add to my cyberpunk city.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Good game, immediately addicted, however needs some more buildings but the game has only been out for a few weeks so its not very surprising. Customization through billboards is amazing.EDIT: I also bought summerhouse awhile ago and its also pretty decent. It's also 20% off so I recommend buying it now!!!!!1!!11!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn't expecting much but this game absolutely shattered my expectations. It is surprisingly fun and captures the cyberpunk / blade runner atmosphere excellently, it lacks right now a few features that would make it more than exceptional but the dev is still working on it, and willing to hear what people are requesting. Honestly for the price it's pretty dope.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful little thing to mess around in.  I believe the developer plans on adding more, doing more, but they are solo, so this is expected to take some time.  As much as I'd love some massive, super-mega city that I can then go into a flying car and zip around in, I don't think that's on the table for this game...Still, something to mess around in and have a little fun with, as well as a Cyberpunk/Shadowrun-esque feel to it all?  Lovely.  Play it, chill.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Pure cyberpunk vibes shot directly into your eyeballs! Paint yourself an end-stage-capitalism monument of glass, steel, and broken dreams, complete with pictures of your cat ten stories high.. if that's your thing. Already a cozy urban masterpiece, Dystopika is still in active development, so expect even more edgy goodness.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill. Love not having to worry about strat or econ, just place and enjoy. Some controls that I feel should be there aren't but its not game breaking, just had to stop over thinking the controls. Love the camera tool and the video camera tracking.Looking forward for further additions. Well done!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I remember when I was a kid and would see the commercials for various city building games, the fast building speeding up the game to make it look thrilling, only to then get the same game and realize that you have to wait for that experience by spending hours micro managing your city.Not this game. this game lets you build no set backs, no economy to micro manage just the thrill of watching your city grow and take shape just like those commercials all with the click of your mouse or space bar, a truly amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just absolutely chuffed to have found this. No stress, lots of fun little surprises, just enough dynamics to reward your curiosity, and an absolutely *gorgeous* aesthetic. It's clear that this is a labour of love, with so many details crafted with care and unabashed nerdiness. Worth every lithium yen, don't even wait for this to be on sale. If you enjoyed games like Townscaper, you'll probably like this more. Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible. It is simple and peaceful. There is no stress, just "vibes." If you have ever watched Blade Runner and been in amazement at the cool city lights at night in the rain, this is the game for you. You build those cities without any stress to you. There is no resource management, petty game play mechanics made to artificially make the game harder, or anything else meant to make this game a challenge. It is about you chilling out and making cool looking near future-cyberpunk/blade runner like cities and thats it. While some may see its lack of any kind of in depth mechanics as a bad thing, if you are looking for something cool to look at and tinker with, this is the game for you without a doubt.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Very relaxing, chill, and intriguing game that lets you control the design of a future city. Not having to worry about resources, population, happiness or any other metrics as you mindlessly build has been a nice change of pace. I absolutely enjoyed being able to use your own pictures as ads and to design the city- it really makes it yours. Grab a drink, kick back, and just lose yourself in the atmosphere.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very relaxed no frills builder. I'm hoping they come out with some updates soon  because you run out of things fast and you start to tinker with meshing buildings, but even that runs this course. There simply isnt a ton of variation. I know that doesn't sound good and I still think you should totally buy this game, its priced right and the updates WILL come. This game has good bones and I enjoy it. People are already coming out with some cool screenshots and billboard concepts. So in the next few years I imagine this will be even better, especially if the modding community gets their hands on this stuff and adds blade runner and cyberpunk 2077 stuff. The game will get wild!!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Technically, Dystopika is a sandbox game, in that you just enjoy relaxing and building a cyberpunk cityscape without any objectives or challenges. I feel like this sells the reality short - it's absolutely beautiful, and takes the cyberpunk/Blade Runner aesthetic to a relentless level, letting you place buildings of different designs and themes, various decorations from streams of flying cars to advertisement blimps to customisable holograms, and you can adjust the weather and time of day for whatever aesthetic you prefer. I've been finding it incredibly relaxing and fun to just casually build a beautiful and rich-feeling metropolis while chatting with friends late into the night, and the photo mode is fantastic for making some great wallpapers. It's a lot of fun, very relaxing, and a lot of thought and effort has gone into the design and atmosphere of the game. Fantastic piece of work, and I look forward to keeping it as one of my go-to 'chill games' for a very long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I am a fan of Indie Games and this game really grabbed me. Make my own Blade runner style of city in sandbox mode? For sure! It is the right price for the right amount of polish and features. Despite there being no objectives/mission, the dev embedded in the game hidden features that are rewarded as you explore. This is a great mechanic employed by AAA studios, kudos! A must buy.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Great Game for Artists, Special thanks to Matt Marshall and Voids Within for their incredible game and art. Their dedication to exploring new perspectives and creating rich, atmospheric environments has added a unique visual dimension to my music productions in my channel Adil Mhouar. I highly recommend checking out Dystopika for an immersive, contemplative experience that blends creativity and wonder in the world of cyberpunk.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: it's a nice cozy game that allows to make a cyber punk how YOU envision it. i love that it allows to light all the neon lights as much as i want, or turn them off as much as i want. the different building designs are so nice, and fun as well as all the holographic designs that you can put in. music is really fun in a lofi way. just nice background music. The only thing i wish for is an expansion on the different corpo building that are in there, but i havent played the update that was released earlier this moth so maybe that was included but other than that.... a really good game to loose yourself in for a few hours or more
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Exactly the dystopian cyberpunk Townscaper game you've been looking for, only better. Visuals, atmosphere and music are simple but amazing, the camera feels incredible and intuitive, the ability to place things with perfect geometric precision endlessly feeds my OCD, and watching the flow of air car traffic that I just created floods my brain with endorphins. Dystopika is Blade Runner city-building heroin. Please Matt, continue working on this masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It's a toy. It's a fun toy, but don't buy it assuming there's gonna be much game in there. You unlock new stuff by placing stuff. You find yourself withing you had more buildings and distract types very quickly, but I imagine those will come if the dev keeps on it. The grid feature can be very handy, but if you rely on it too much I promise your city will wind up looking pretty uniform by the end. I use this to create a sort of visual rep of the hub city for a tabletop game I'm running. It's very fun to tinker with when you know what you're getting into with it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A very simple but chill city builder/screenshot generator, with a building system and selection of buildings/decorations that make it basically impossible to create something that doesn't look cool alongside the atmospheric affects. Also has great music.The game literally came out today so saying it lacks content feels unfair however you will exhaust all the buildings and unlock everything VERY quickly, I would expect/hope that Voids Within will be adding some more structures/environments in the future to add more variety however I would still recommend this game if you are looking for something chill to mess about with for a couple hours.8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Good simple game that eliminates the stress from a city builder, honestly at 7$ and only playing it because I saw Vinny Vinesauce play it I expected this to become instant abandonware. That being said there have already been big updates like video billboards and additional props and improvements to the camera mode.  I have enjoyed my time and pop in every week or so to play around and build a few more things which has been very enjoyable!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Loving the dark side of cozy with this beautiful game, very meditative and relaxing. I can't wait to spend more time with this and really looking forward to the upcoming additions mentioned in the roadmap! Hopefully more people discover this hidden gem, it feels lovingly made and scratches the cyberpunk itch.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty much what it says on the box. Build the dystopian Cyberpunk/Blade Runner-adjacent city of your dreams (or nightmares). No population or resource managment to stress over, no budget, no annoying city advisors. Just build stuff to your heart's content.It's a little bereft of QOL tweaks and features for my liking in some aspects, but what _is_ there does a fantastic job. Hats off to the devs. I hope they keep supporting the game and can't wait to see what they come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Been trying to find a game PRECISELY like this for AGES. Love games where I can just build with no limits. I always find myself playing games just to build things and nothing more so this really scratches this itch! The game feels super polished and nice too! I'd say if you're like me and need games like this where you can build with no objectives or obstacles in your way this is totally for you but if you're not so much of a sandbox builder type of gamer this might not be your cup of tea but I still think it's worth a shot since its such a nice Zen experience. If you like townscaper or flotsam this is almost exactly like that but the blade runner version!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful.  Ever wanted to create your own dystopian future city where it's raining all the time and dark save for the bright lights of the manufactured variety?  This is the game to do it.  No stress of managing anything, (The mega corps already do that I guess?) and no objectives.  You simply create.  It's so simple and relaxing.If you want a chill game to wind down with, this is a great choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The moment you boot up the game, the developer emphasizes that Dystopika is a passion project. It's 100% true. Although here and there are some things I'd like to be expanded or improved in the future, keeping in mind I have an indie game before me, I really enjoy building my own cyberpunk megalopolis. Dystopika's relaxing, cozy and inspiring game worth its price. I'm also very thankful for the presence of photomode with many functions to try out.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely recommend this game, It is one of my new favorites, I love the features and the unlock system, I love the camera systems, and I adore the aesthetic, very simple, not stressful at all, and its an AMAZINNG game!i'd actually say if your looking for a nice, cared for city builder, Its this over many steam games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Being a sci-fi and cyberpunk nerd, a synthwave/dark ambient BSO lover, and an architect, I can recommend this game on each of those fields.This is a relaxing game, extremely loyal to the main visual references in the cyberpunk world. I would define this game as, rather than you drawing a city, you crafting your own images. You will enjoy this game even more if you "get in character", crafting your own stories as you position everything around, giving a meaning to the landscapes you will be creating.Can not recommend enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Did you enjoy Townscaper? Did you wish it came in cyberpunk?Great news, ye person of somewhat specific tastes, because that game exists and it's Dystopika!The cities feel a little more alive than in Townscaper, with tiny vehicles visible going about, and the vibes are chill, if a little less warm and fuzzy feeling, what with the dark synths and neon landscape. If a bird's eye view of your own version of Mega City One, The Sprawl or Night City sounds like it would be your jam, then you should pick this up. Then, pour yourself your favorite relaxing beverage of choice, crank up the synth and build your cares away.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The deeper we dive into this game and test it's limits the more we realize just what a gem Matt gave us. While the Dev has a Roadmap to continue adding things to the already fully launched game (this is NOT in Early access), it's already such a treat to see what we can build with the tools given. I often find myself spending hours finding images and video to test out on the Billboards just to see how cool I can build my City. I love this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is already a pretty solid product so far. There are just enough tools, tricks, and surprises packed in the game to give you quite a bit of variety in your builds. The photo mode is surprisingly robust, and supports taking video of your city as well as still shots, which was a pleasant surprise. The developer has been active and communicative in updating this title thus far, and has a clearly-defined set of goals for the game's lifespan, too. The music playlists are also a nice touch, at least for my personal taste -- reminiscent of HKE's work in some respects. For those who already enjoy games like this, and for the price it's currently listed at, I consider it a worthwhile purchase. I'm looking forward to watching this one develop more depth over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is for those who enjoy a cyberpunk setting, and have always wanted to build a city and just relax. it is addicting and time can easily run away. the music pulls you in and you find yourself wrapped in your own world. There is no quests or goal, just build and watch your city grow. i needed a game like this in my life. a game with no goal, a cozy  game that is a tad dark, and DYSTOPIKA is that game. i can play it hours, and come back in three months and still be pulled in to enjoy the simplicity and cyberpunk vibes.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is the game I never knew I always wanted! Wow, what a great experience. I have just started building my first city and I'm digging the vibe. I love that the developer says more content is coming. The Bladerunner/Cyberpunk aesthetic is very good and the price point? No brainer. I'm loving the dark side of cozy! Thanks Matt!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you're like me, and you just like building things that look nice without much care for strategy or management elements, this game is for you. Perfect for relaxing and letting your creativity run wild. It's a little light on the amount of content, but since the developer says this is just the beginning, i have high hopes for what's to come. This game is a top notch foundation for something truly incredible to be built upon, and i can't wait to see what's in store for the future. (By the way, a bunch of Alpha Corp buildings placed in a line with traffic props placed on top is a great way to make a highway)In conclusion. vry gud gam 10/10.If Matt's reading this, here's some ideas/suggestions I thought of while playing.1: More buildings. The relatively small selection was a bit disappointing.2: A way to select and build specific buildings3: A way to select objects in a certain area and move/rotate everything within4: More traffic related things. I really liked using the prop that creates traffic, and I think expanding on that aspect of the game could really pay off. The ability to create highways with twists and turns for flying cars would be awesome. The ability to create roads that generate regular non-flying cars would also be pretty cool.5: More options for time of day, or a way to change the color of the lighting. It's great you can do this in photo mode, but having that option during regular gameplay would be nice.I hope i didn't make any typos because i am too tired to proofread this review. Anywho, that's all the ideas i had, or at least the ones i can remember. Keep up the great work!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you are the person who would rather look at a skyline, then figure out how to better perfect traffic flow this game is sooo for you.  The pure joy in this game is to be able to just zone out and make your own world.  I like to name all the buildings and come up with my own backstory in my head.  I can also see this being useful to someone wanting to make a set for their own story or use it as background footage for a video.  It's great to kill an hour or two to unwind, while keeping the mood dark and mysterious. I can't wait for all the post launch content. A GOTY indi game contender.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is such a cute little city builder, in its current state it feels more early access more than finished. it preforms well on my system, Graphically and power (amd ryzen 7 5700, 3060) it does need more content, i doubt there is a team working on this game so updates are sure to be slow. im hoping for more buildings, as in lower density placing, also a more low income areas. that way there can be a dystopian themes. it would be cool to see more corps, like addons to alpha and omega. overall the game is fun, enjoyable for a sandbox game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a trip, like literally, as fan of cyberpunk and huge cities, I gotta say this game offers a solid foundation, the assets variaty is great and atmosphere fit almost perfectly.My only point criticism, is that I would like to build taller building, like ridiculously tall xD but yea that just personal preference xD
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a nice "toy", where you create a cyberpunk cityscape. That's pretty much it. Everything you need to know is in the product description.It has cozy atmosphere with rain, smog and slow music. No matter the time of day you set, the game will always have this dark lighting that fits the theme. There's a good variety of posters to put on buildings, but you can also upload your own images. I would like to be able to scale text boxes, so i could write long Star Wars intro walls of text, but otherwise it is fine.Like the description says, there're no goals or management. There's a little bit of progression, you unlock new decorations by meeting hidden requirements and that's it. You're your own director.For me the game ran just fine, there weren't any slow-downs or obvious bugs besides some long unlocks.I would like to see more building variations and districts, as well as more interactions, but you can kind of combine existing ones to make new stuff.Now, the reason i decided to write this review is just looking at negative ones and going, like, "Huh?". A bunch of people complain about not having more mechanics and management and stuff, and that's what the game is advertised as. A few go really hard on this too, like, really mad. And none of them have the comments on.It reminded me so much of Townscaper situation when people expected more from the game than it was promising. Like, just read the product description, guys!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It's a beautiful gameIf you are looking for a city management game, with economy, resources, and the like, then this game is  not for you. I love it precisely because I can just sit back, place buildings, billboards and take pictures of my blade runner city. Already recommended to friends. Hope the developer continues to add little decorations and buildings with updates, but it's pretty awesome as is.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Use it to make images for writing stories. Use it as backdrops in art. Play it for TTRPGs and use it for set dressing.Make a cool background for your desktopIt's a fun tool to do what you want with, a niche with a lot of room to grow and a lot of power behind it.Things I want to see in it.Ruined buildings and debris. Space ships/ship yards. Water/River tool. Dome structure. Better stuff to make walls with. Fortresses.They added monorail, best game eveeerrrr!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Wow ,  I liked the Demo, so  I purchased the "game" when it came out and i like it  more.  The demo didn't have an option for adding a new images as a billboard like the full does and just recently it got update to add full video billboards. Its an interesting way for the developer to allow user created assets .  I make live wallpaper for myself with it from screen captures.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is deceptively simple. At first, it looks daunting as hell...how do you even build a city? *Especially* without clear goals or mechanics? That's what I thought at first. Eventually you start messing with the tools, and then it rapidly becomes clear just how easy and intuitive it actually is. Matt describes this as a "passion" project, and I still think that's understating how incredible this is.Tightly packed hellscapes of neon and towers, sprawled cyber-suburbia on the outskirts of a downtown dominated by a gigantic black pyramid that plays adverts on every surface, it's genuinely amazing what flows out of the tools. Things like road/airway traffic, roads, "detail" buildings that fill out the spaces between objects, sometimes as a scattering of buildings ad mini-malls, other times you might just link a bunch of towers together as they auto-build skybridges between one another, forming one massive superstructure surrounded by any number of things. It feels amazing.That's the core of it, by the way: feeling. That won't make much sense unless you're both into cyberpunk settings, and love cities themed to it but don't like having to play a complex sim game to make it happen. If you are, this will call to you like a siren at sea. If not, might still enjoy it anyway! If you've looked at those screenshots and thought "yea, that looks pretty awesome", then you will love this. Give it a chance, certainly glad I did!EDIT: forgot to mention, but someone earlier did already: this game's camera controls, especially in photo mode, are phenomenal. Kinda mad that no one else has done this yet. XD
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a fun and surprisingly for me a relaxing game. At first I went wild and created something akin to a eperopolis (a continent wide city). After getting the hang of it I started to create something with a bit of artistic approach. I know nothing of city planning and that was the fun part of it. If you have no expectations of the game, but your imagination you'll have a great time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A good fun city painter, a good way to unwind and make your cyberpunk city of your dreams. Also there is image and video importing for the holographic billboards so you can add some unique aspects to your city, want to have Google on your building why not, maybe your cat go ahead. Also with the ability to write captions onto a bilboard and import pictures and video you can create your own lore into your little city,.I think this will be one of those games I will sink some time into, walk away for a few months and with new features over time I will put some more time into it again. For its cheap price it is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It is more like therapy than playing a game. I feel like I got out of a meditative session every time I play it. Sure after a while the choice of buildings and holos become repetitive, but the ambiance and visuals really make up for it. If you want a calming game where you can imagine yourself just chilling in a cyberpunk setting, this game is for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've never written a review before, but this game just had to make me do one. This is an absolutely beautiful game. This is exactly what I've been needing to wind down and let my creative juices run free while aimlessly making a cool looking city.I do hope that the developer continues to add new buildings and features to the game to keep it replayable. I have no doubt that they will, as it seems they are pretty active within the community. I can't wait to see what else they have in store.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, yes. This is actually something incredible and worth your money if you are into casual city builders. I've waited for something like this for a long time, a game that lets you build and decorate with custom images pulled from your hard drive. Now with the v1.0.2 update you can also use videos and it's incredible.Such a simple premise, such excellent execution.Matt is single-handedly putting mega corps to shame with a one man release using realistic expectations and good community support and updates.10/10 would buy again.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Want to build a cyberpunk sim city without all those pesky game play aspects? Me too! that's why I got Dystopika. You start with a giant square city, and you add buildings, signs, billboards, lights, and all kinds of other stuff you'd find in a cyberpunk city, but you don't have to work for it. Just navigate the menu, and plop. Solo dev, but he's very active on discord, and has big plans for the game. What's here is not a whole lot, but it all runs very smoothly. I can't wait to see what else is coming!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to add my voice to the chorus of: "Get this game!" This is a unique experience somewhere between a work of art, a creative meditation, and a city builder videogame. I honestly thought that I would try it for about ten minutes and return it, largely because I wanted to see the hype for myself. Instead I've come back to it for little twenty minute sessions of designing some new cityscape to an absolutely amazing soundtrack. Definitely listen to with some headphones on! Oh, and again: get this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It is what is says on the box.A little sandbox to make a dark future city. Much like the ones seen in Blade Runner and Co.Easy controls help it a great deal. Buildings can be plopped down all willy-nilly, or on a nice grid.The option to import images and videos onto the large neon signs adds endless possibilities to make the city just like one wants to.Well worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun little creative game. A very unique take on the City Builder genre. No stressful management or annoying goals you have to strive for. Just pure unadulterated creativity. Once you have played it for a few hours you have experienced everything, but it's definitely worth the price. Hoping the roadmap of future content will be big enough to bring me back to this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The game is exactly as advertised: a dystopian city building game without any mechanics beyond placing down your buildings and decorations. Not a game that you'd play for any extended period of time. However, I find it great to unwind in after spending the whole day working for our corporate overlords. IMHO certainly worth the price. If you get bored of the game within the 2 hour window, you can easily refund it so don't hesitate to give it a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: A very cozy city builder that allows (and rewards) creativity. While I don't think this game needs any management, I still feel hungry for something extra. A catastrophe to wipe the city when I'm ready to reset. A robot plague that I can watch tear apart the city in real time. I don't want scenarios or a campaign or anything. In fact, I love the sandbox mode. However, part of me wishes I could activate or enable a parameter or two to keep things interesting because I have a feeling this game will get a bit stale once its novelty wears off. Until then, I'm finding myself enjoying spending 20 - 30 minutes messing around on this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so cool, I lake how you cant quite see the bottom level of the city that you're building so it make it a little more mysterious. However there isn't much variety with any of the districts but I understand that this is a very new game and there will probably will be more updates in the future. I also hope to see some sort of monorail building system implemented at some point.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful little toy. I hope this gets updated with more things to look at and interact with, and hopefully even some sort of optional light progression system or infrastructure, or just moving things that interact with each other and patrol/roam areas. But until then, it's nice to look at and a good way to wind down. I'm really happy that things like this still get made, just for the sake of appreciating beauty.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: "A city-building sandbox for futuristic cities."Yep, that's what it is. A fairly simple one without a lot of depth yet, but you can probably tell from watching some gameplay if it's gonna scratch an itch for you. Priced fairly for what it promises and delivers I feel. Hopefully the lone dev stays motivated for a good while to add content and keep improving the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It's incredibly meditative and creatively satisfying. The music and the whole look and feel of the game perfectly captures that futuristic megacity vibe, and it is surprising just how many little rewarding details there are to discover. The only missing feature that I wish was present would be a day/night cycle.. You can adjust the time of day and sun position in the photo mode, but it would be that much more immersive with the light shifting as you build. I'm really surprised how much I love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The best way to describe this game is that it's a fidget spinner in software form. The diversity in the game comes from the fluff (holograms, building accessories, etc...) and not the buildings, of which there are few. Most of your time will be spent getting that perfect screenshot which makes this more like tiltbrush or some other artistic program and not really a "game" per se.But, for 6 dollars, it's worth it even if to just space out for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying my time with this application. It's calm and entertaining. It reminds of me of when my brother and I were much younger trying to build Mega-City One from Judge Dredd in Sim City. I can certainly recommend this if you want a relaxing zen garden of building and painting a cyberpunk city. If you're expecting city management and budget concerns, this is not that game. My wish list to further expand this application, I would love to see the following:
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is awesome, I love it, and I look forward to the future of this game.  First off, I absolutely love the concept of being able to build the city and not have to worry about managing it.  The idea is great and the execution was great as well.The developer nailed the vibe he was going for, the music, the lighting, the aesthetic of the buildings and the decorations along with the flying cars.  Amazing, actually, pretty much perfect if you ask me.  It 100% feels like Blade runner or Ghost in the machine or any other dystopian future megacity... Except you get to build it!I like the buildings and the sub-categories.  I wish there were more options of buildings, but i saw in the roadmap that this was coming further along.  The random option, in my opinion was a bit confusing at first.  I was just plopping random buildings and guessing what would pop up.  BUT this game is really simple and I figured the building selection in the first 2 minutes.  The base system of choosing your building and growing it by dragging up is simple and fun, and the fact that the surrounding cityscape changes to match is also great and gives a tiny bit of unpredictability which I find great The cherry on top is the ability to add your own text and upload your own images as holographic advertisements.  I absolutely adore this feature, and when I heard about it in the trailer it is what originally sold me on this game. You can make your city 10X more dystopian or make it funnier or completely satirical with your own signs, posters, slogans, etc.One example, I built a city and added Mr. House from Fallout as the "Big Brother" of the city (I Suggest you try it if you like Fallout, it is pretty funny and cool) .  Don't like your EX? Put her ugly mug on your tallest skyscraper and label her a traitor.  (If my ex reads this, I did not do this, I don't care enough about you to do it, this is just an example of what you can do in this game, I am also not calling you ugly) is there a company you love? Advertise it to the millions living in your mega city.  Want to be Patriotic? Get pictures of your favorite flag and paint the walls with the future of flag technology... DIGITAL FLAGS!! never worry about winds EVER AGAIN!Lots of fun and lots of options to customize your city as you want it.  This was a fantastic addition to the game that really really makes it unique.Now some things I hope to see in the future or things I hope to have changed1. The cursor always seems to have something on it (a decoration, a building, the magnifying glass (I think that is what it is) and there is never the ability to just scroll around without worrying about clicking on something and plopping something down. If there could just be a "free cursor" for when you just want to look around the city, that would be great... maybe in a future update.2. I wish you could add some form of transport options.  (My profile picture is an airplane so as you can imagine I love aviation and transportation in general) so if some form of metro system, monorail, maglev, or even a *Sigh* Hyperloop and if possible an airport or spaceport (The last one is asking for a lot I know) that would be FANTASTIC and I believe will make the game so much better3.  It doesn't seem like you can name your cities. Which, one, kind of sucks just like that, two makes it harder to find saved game profiles.  Maybe when you start a new city we can have the option to name it.  I think it would also add the opportunity to add a bunch of cool decorations with the city name in it.So yeah, great game! I'd give it an 85/100 (the cursor thing is why it's not a 90)  but with the updates coming I have a feeling this is going to get even better.As for the price , I would have paid more for this game quite honestly, it is a steal at $6.99.  I won't say how much I would have paid because I do want people to be able to get the game for cheap, but yeah, it is 100% worth the price. Best of luck for the future development of this game and happy citybuilding!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely love and enjoy this game. This game has so much potential to be the little cyberpunk world that has countless ideas for good relaxing game play with just the city building aspect. If mod ability does become available, people looking for the cyberpunk city aesthetic that they are able to build themselves and take nearly infinite personally stylized creations like buildings and decorations would really make this game explode. The ability to add your own art to make the perfect adds for the city is already in the game is pretty cool to me personally. Great potential, I bee leaf in u guys <3
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: As other reviews have stated, this is much more of a toy or a tool than a game. With that said I found Dystopika to be a fun little experience that's worth the price tag. I should state, of course, that you get what you pay for and—while I do not wish to suggest that there isn't enough content—I did find myself wishing there were just a few more options or designs, but I say as much in the game's favour; what's there is good and I'm hungry for just a little more and would be happy to pay for it.So, yes, I heartily recommend Dystopika based on what it offers and the cost associated with it, yet I must admit that I also recommend this game because the More-Toy-Than-Game experience that Dystopika brings is something I would love to see more of in future, and I hope this game finds enough success to inspire similar game-toy-tool experiences.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Not really a game, just a cityscape painter and a very limited one at that.  Don't expect Tiny Glade style piece by piece building, you can't stack or heavily customise buildings and the number of building models is very limited.  But for $7 its a fun little toy that will keep you entertained for a few hours.  If there were more buildings, a more modular Tiny Glade style building system where you could stack more generic skyscraper modules together, and generally just more content this could be a really interesting game.  Maybe one day?
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: To be perfectly honest, I was expecting something totally different. But, this is truely my fault, as I didn't read anything other than a small article about this game in a german games magazine. The looks had me speechless immediately. I love this visuals.This game is perfect for a gloomy evening just you, a faceless town and the amazing music!I absolutely love this game and for the prize it's perfectly reasonable to buy it and play it occationally.To the dev, thank you for persuing your dream, for making this game and for trusting in the community that it will be met with excitement.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a work in progress, so don't expect City Skylines from it. It isn't even Townscaper. It has great potential so be patient for the roadmap to be developed more fully. It's entertaining right now but still limited. I can't see getting more than 2-3 hours from it at present.Basically you place dark buildings in a night (or dark) setting, add some decorations as they get unlocked, add some advertising and logos, and tinker with the limited options for ambient lighting and weather. The result is a sort-of Blade Runner city that you can rotate and zoom to a limited degree. Then take screenshots.Some things I would recommend be added:1. A real daylight mode so users can place new buildings more accurately in brighter light. Maybe add a grid to help exact placement.2. A tweaked growth mode for tall buildings that doesn't create vertical streaks of lighting in some.3. Helicopter pads on top of buildings not just on the sides.4. A street-level zoom mode (maybe a walkable mode?) and generally a greater zoom ability.5. More control over building lighting (like the ability to light an entire floor on all sides, or to change a floor's colour)6. An option or decoration for rooftop gardens/restaurants/bars/pools7. Tooltips for the menu options. Their use is currently a bit opaque.8. A sandbox mode where everything is unlocked9. Move and resize options for placed ads, decorations, and buildings (if these already exists I couldn't out how to do it).10. More atmosphere filters with different effects or a fully customizable interface for filters11. Snapshots available from the top of specified buildings or at street level12. Rain slick effects, not just rain itself.13. More building types. Maybe a workshop feature so users can contribute their own designs. Towers like those in Seattle and Toronto would be nice.14. User-placeable walkways between buildings.15. Different colours for building materials (maybe shades of grey instead of all-black).16. A method where users could share a code to recreate the cities in their own computers (like Townscaper has)17. An overhead view looking straight down on the city.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I love this. I absolutely cannot ignore recommending this. I only hope and pray that it gets more attention and detail added to the game.Because right now, while parts of me would give it a thumbs down with what little it has to offer I am still going to thumbs it up because I just love this.Let us add roads, see people, etc.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Delightful mood builder rather than a city builder. That's my main takeaway from spending over 6 hours on it and still feeling up for more. Big thanks to the Dev for making this game <3If there are few things I'd love to see in future updates, these are the ones I think would be very nice:* Streets. Understandably this game is trying to emulate the mood of a sprawling metropolis where urban development outpaced any concerns for logical traversal, and I like that quite a lot to be fair. But without any kind of streets, it's a bit hard to give your city any kind of appealing structure. My current workaround is to plop down Alpha Buildings and then put the little Hover Car Arcs on top to emulate highways. Totally see why streets and roads might not be a core focus for the developer, I'd still love to see them in the game.* Color wheels. Or at least a way to alter the colors on the big skyscrapers. It feels a bit underwhelming to only get red and cyan for the buildings currently in the game. Maybe let us have a sharp lapis lazuli blue or a mellow orange just to spice things up?* Factory District buildings. This is just me being entitled here but with the Smokestack decorations I would really love to see some big ugly factory buildings that break away from the skyskraper aesthetics. You could put them on the outskirts of your city with some short LowTown buildings and all of a sudden you've got an oppressive slum/factory area.Thanks again!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you love Cyberpunk at all, then you owe it to yourself to pickup this "digital toy" because it's AWESOME and the price is right for all that you get and what you get is Townscaper if it had been designed by Ridley Scott and Syd Mead. I LOVE Cyberpunk and this is so much fun to play around with and chill. Fiddling with the buildings, adding in my own text and images for building signs, adding traffic, smoke stacks, all sorts of  built-in doo-dads to complete your Blade Runner-esque metropolis. Oh yeah, and of course, rain and fog to top it all off. The camera controls are buttery smooth and the screenshot mode is great and even has a camera motion widget to move the camera from one position to another over 5 to 30 seconds to create a cool vibe - it would be nice if you could record that as a video natively but maybe that will happen later. I can't wait to see what features get added down the road.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure I'd consider this a city-building game at all.  Instead I think of it more as a diorama builder.  I don't think that's a bad thing at all.  It's a chill experience.Lots of buildings to choose from,  tons of achievements, an unlock system that works quite well through encouraging you to try out new buildings.  Also you can add your own photos which I think is fantastic.  Too bad there wasn't an option to add in your own custom videos.  That would have made the experience relatively perfect, I think.  Personally I'd of added in the cinematic masterpiece Troll 2 to watch, but that's just me.  Maybe one day we'll get webm, mp4, or similar support.You can add text, and customize it.  There's this really cool level of obvious love and passion that went into making this game, and it is easily one of the most compelling reasons to play Indie titles.  This sort of passion is often lost on the "AAA" industry.Anyway, onto more stuff.  Graphics are good, it definitely captures the cyberpunk feeling.  There are a few weather options, but they're pretty much: Rain, more rain, Pea Soup.  I guess I'm not sure what else I'd add.  Snow?  Snow would've been cool.  You can increase/decrease the amount of rain, speed, mess with lighting, and a whole slew of other customization options.  There's also a camera mode that needs to be about 5x longer to make me truly happy.  I want a long video with more control over the pathing so I can set up a cool clip that really shows off my city.More music tracks would've been nice.  I feel like there were more than 2 in the demo, and hey maybe there are more than 2 in the game.  But so far, 2 are all I've heard.Overall if you're looking for a game you can play with the chillest of mindsets, this is a game for you.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice little piece of software to sit down and play with. I can see myself using this to make some city maps for tabletop cyberpunk RPGs. For the price, it's hard to go wrong, just don't go in expecting a city manager. There are still some issues around optimization that need to be resolved, but I enjoy what's there.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to build a pretty little thing and chill out, it really isn't hard to miss with this game. Easy to build whatever you want, but you can get complex with how you position and decorate. I like to build for screenshots, and this game is real good for it. Looking forward to possible workshop support! Def recommend, 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: it's a good-looking game, but it does not have any substance, wish there were goals and some management to keep me in the game. I can see the appeal of this type of sandbox city builder but after 18 mins of playtime, I did everything in the game. It is as advertised but I hope the Dev/s has plans to make a more city skylines-type builder version on top of this sandbox builder.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: What is there to dislike about this game? Yes, there are many improvements that could and should be made. And they will come, in time. What we have for the time being though, is a great little time killer. Create a dystopian blade runner type city. How you go about it, is completely up to you. Your imagination is your only barrier. This is a terrific little game which will only continue to get better. The potential is enormous.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Incredibly beautiful, casual, gloomy, atmospheric game where you literally just place, rotate and scale buildings and decorations while getting lost in the music and general ambiance.It's very simple and that's perfect if you just need something to unwind.Oh, and the photo mode is incredible, if you're looking to create your next wallpaper!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This IS NOT a city management game. This IS a city builder game/tool. This is a game/tool that gives you all the things you need to build your own Cyberpunk City. No money, no research, no traffic management and no real goals. You just build.Regardless of your reasons for wanting to do that, this game does it very, very well.A nice relaxing game and toolset to just create a Cyberpunk landscape on. I will be using it for Artwork and Cyberpunk: Red (TTRPG) City scapes and skyline images etc. The developer very clearly understands the cyberpunk aesthetic and has nailed the assets and vibes in the game.Worth the price of a medium coffee that its being sold for.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Cyberpunk 2077 meets TownscaperMakes you want to monologue while staring out at the vast horizon.In all seriousness, this is a fantastic city builder with a ton of potential and I look forward for updates to customize my cities even further!Make no mistake, this is not in any way a game and more a tool for relaxing or expressing artistic expression in a city building sort've way. So before you spend your hard earned cash, keep that in mind.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: So, I've been a fan of city and theme park builders/tycoons etc etc for a very, *very* long time. By far my favorite genre of games I can always go back to when I don't know what I want to do or play, or if I need to let the creative juices flow. This game is such a simple yet absolutely enthralling extension of that genre, just a blank, cyberpunk themed canvas for you to let your imagination run wild. As a kid, I would always play stuff like RollerCoaster Tycoon 3 for hours on end with infinite money, just to see what I could build. As a teen, I'd do the same things with Planet Coaster, or Cities Skylines. This game captures that same feeling, beat for freaking beat - building gorgeous vistas and skylines to take screenies of, and just bask in "The dark side of cozy" as you put it, lol. Absolutely loving my time with this one, hats off to you Matt!!!Thank you for making this game, I'm excited to see what comes next <3
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a lovely piece of work. In mere minutes you can create a 'Blade Runner' megacity, full of eye-searing neon,  Above and around your buildings a horde of air buggies zip in and out of view, dodging the floating ad blimps. It needs little imagination to picture the teeming streets at ground level, constantly dripped on by high humidity, and populated by shadowy figures darting from ramen and sushi bars to opium dens and other dubious pleasure houses.The city creation process was, I found, almost meditative in its execution. Try it - you'll love it!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I fondly remember playing games like this as a kid. I love the cyberpunk/hyper industrialized aesthetic and this game NAILS IT. It also has interesting elements where it's building atmospheric buildings/particles/vehicles around what you build. It's very cool and it's sort of emergent in terms of look and feel. Thanks Matt!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: After playing intense, time-consuming games, this one really allows me to relax. I spend half an hour building my city, then two hours taking screenshots and recording videos.In the end, I still managed to make a small area very Cyberpunk-like.The city center is made into an authoritarian government zone that restricts people's access, plastered with government slogans: "One Earth, One Gov, One Man". This central area prohibits civilian activity, and not a single civilian sign can be seen. However, behind the government district lies the conglomerate of financial groups, with skyscrapers reaching into the clouds, filled with massive advertisements. Each tall building has advanced aerial vehicles.In contrast, the buildings in the outskirts are extremely low, but this is where the people actually live. You can see signs everywhere, and although there are no aerial vehicles, ordinary citizens reside here peacefully. They just have to coexist with the large power plant clusters that supply energy but also cause air pollution.The most amazing thing is that this game can actually create all these effects.I named my city "Eco City".
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I HAD A TINGLE WHEN I FOUND THIS. if u r looking for a game that is a city builder with no management or anything to worry about then this is your game, if u are look for the complete opposite, leave and dont buy the game. but if u are like me then this is your game. I love it and i cant wait to see it grow. all i can ask for is the ability to make buildings wider.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: is a very zen sandbox in a theme that I don't see too often (in this genre I mean). There is a minor puzzle element just in the unlocking of decorations, and you can get some achievements this way. That said, I wouldn't call this a puzzle game. This is still very much a sandbox. It is a tool through which you can create your own interesting cyberscapes using a variety of assets with well crafted procedural elements. I can see this program being great for making wallpapers, moving or otherwise--especially with the camera tool.If you like the idea of just taking a breather and spending some time just exploring your creative side, then  It won't cost you too much, especially on sale and/or as part of a bundle; plus, you'll be helping out a clearly talented, artistic indie dev in the process. I look forward to seeing what they do next, which includes the future updates for this game as there is still content planned for down the line.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent city-creation sandbox. It's a bit limited in its early state, but there's a lot of potential (especially with the workshop). It's gorgeous (despite graphical limitations), easy to learn and pick up, and very intuitive. I'm currently using it to design a cyberpunk city for some tabletop RPGing. This is an easy recommend at full price.Mods will soon become available and the dev seems to be interested in supporting them. This just makes me recommend the game more.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: i have hijacked my hubbo's acct to play this. i am the person who only plays SIms to build stuff and could care less about the actual game. i'm here for the mental check-out. this is magnificent, from the music to the low-pressure zen of it all. adhd dopamine + approved! I can't wait to see what other developments happen with this game. imma need more buildings. cheers! keep up the good work!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The Dark Future has never been this chill.I was concerned a city builder with no real objective would get old fast, but it hasn't thus far. The game does not hold your hand but it is very easy to discover for yourself secrets about the buildings, how to make them interact with each other. Additionally being able to stick neon all over your city and just watch the aircars fly by is quite relaxing. For less than $10 this is a bargain as a relaxing take on city building in a theme that usually doesn't have this kind of relaxation.

_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've had this game in mind for a while in terms of game dev, I just never had the time.This game scratches an itch I've had for all that time, while not quite the exact same, it scratches that itch of cyberpunk-city builder.The aesthetic and vibe are on point, the soundtrack is fantastic and it's brimming with its own idea of what it set out to be.I hope this gets updates in the future of some kind to allow for customization/addition of several other aesthetics in the cyberpunk genre that allows one to cultivate it in different directions (occult: Shadowrun, nostalgic: Hypnospace Outlaw)Thank you Matt.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Like the lone developer of this title I'm also the kind of person who likes playing city builders mainly so I can see what cool looking city I can create (though I tend not to play on "god mode").At first I was hesitant to buy it because of the few negative reviews Id read stating that theres nothing here, or at least not enough to be worth calling a "game"...but I think its great!The whole experience has a great atmosphere and it's a joy to see how the city grows as you place buildings. Sure there could be more content (buildings, props, even the ability to grow beyond the starting square), but I think it's a great start.And, having just watched Blade Runner its clear to see where a lot of the inspiration came from...but it works!

_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Highly Recommend Dystopika.It's such a chill and cozy game.It is a super simple city builder with no management so you can be as creative as you want.Yes there isn't much to it in terms of variety but they're in the road map which I look forward too. _childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Does exactly what it says, if you want to chill out and create a Bladerunner'esq near future Cityscape, with an element of random chance and lighting effects thrown in, whilst listening to a atmospheric soundscape or the sound of the rain.... here you go.Dystopika does all this quickly, without needing to learn the in's and out's of an Art Package. Just the use of your mouse, shift, alt and ctrl combos is all that is required and where ever else that takes you in your minds eye.Has a nice feature where you can set a start / stop point, to fly through your scene hovercar style in a brief clip, or add filters and effects to take screenshots of your creations.£5.30 well spent, as can see myself chilling out and seeing where these scenes can take me.

_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika gets its name from the classic 1980s science fiction film, "" and its sequel "" I don't really remember what the movies were about, but I loved the atmosphere and special effects, and that's what this game offers.Read the description, then read it two more times before you buy. This isn't a traditional city builder, and the developer is 100% upfront about that. It's more of an art tool or meditation program. There's no deeper meaning inherent in the mechanics, apart from what you assign yourself. In theory, your city could very well be a wonderful place to live, there's just nothing to quantify it as such. These are pure cyberpunk aesthetics with no further depth to speak of.In keeping with that spirit, I'm going to keep my criticism relevant:Game needs more art tools. More decorations, more building styles, better camera control, ability to record video, and the ability to zoom in to street level. It needs better ways to explore and experience this city you've built, and less emphasis on "unlocking" new decorations through arbitrary tasks.If your game has no intrinsic goals, then the player will create an extrinsic goal for himself. Give us the tools to realize those goals.The developer has been active in the steam discussions, talking about what is and isn't planned, or viable. Roadmap looks promising, too, so keep an eye on that.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I came across this game randomly and after seeing the price and the note from the dev I couldn't resist. I have always loved city builders and cyber punk aesthetics. This game is exactly what it says it is. Not as much  a game as a way to kick back, relax and let your mind chill out. The ui is simple, atmosphere is gorgeous and it's a really nice way to kill some time. While it is a bit bare-boned, I highly recommend it. Assuming this sounds like something you would be into. The dev says more is to come, and who doesn't love supporting a passion project from time to time.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you're looking for in-depth city management, this is not the citybuilder for you.If you're looking for total commitment to a vibe with excellent execution, this is the citybuilder for you.At the moment it's maybe a liiiiittle shallow even with that in mind, but it's under active development and I'm really looking forward to seeing how it expands. The polish is already there, now they just need to stack it high with content - and with mod tools planned for the future, that's sure to happen.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: You get what it says on the tin. A city-building sandbox for futuristic cities. No goals, no management, just creativity and dark cosy vibes. Those vibes are quite immersive IMHO. Simple game that you can take as seriously as you want! Few minutes in and I already have a few cool screensavers.Nice game for a cheap price.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Works as advertised! A neat cyberpunk city builder in a mindset of the megacorps, no care for the population and no care for the budget! I like the buildings and styles, especially the Blade Runner-esque pyramids. I also enjoy how ads work, I love them! I love that I can import pictures from my PC, and that was the main feature that drew me to this game, that and the idea of building my own cyberpunk city. The idea of putting my own ads on these massive cyberpunk towers and structures appealed to me so much so, that I can't really explain it. I spent two hours, more than playing this game, in searching and downloading interesting-looking ads on Google. It's sad to say that I won't be playing this game for half the time I spent looking for the ads. I'll be honest, I got bored of it extremely quickly. As already said, there is no progression, no people to manage or fire departments to build, and so I build, and build until I got bored. The type of game, or rather, this genre doesn't appeal to me that much. It's not the game itself, it's a neat little game, but not for me, I got bored of it quickly, and that's that. I'll be giving it a thumbs up out of respect for the game, developer and genre, but as you can see from this review, the game itself isn't from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game, especially because it delivers on what it promises: a relaxing sandbox city builder where yo uplace building belonging to a specific buildset and the city procedurally generates around it. You can then add holograms and other decorations and then take pictures. That's it. It's a great way to kill time, or spend an hour being creative. Definitely worth the $8 CDN spent on it and would absolutely recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Really enjoyed it even in the demo stage.
