There's so much potential for additions & improvements that other people have already mentioned that will hopefully happen in the future (more building types etc) but still enjoying it for now in it's first stages.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a nice toy for what it is but it does lack a few things which would add to the experience significantly. Basically a DIY wallpaper "game"10 bit support/HDR  - this game has horrible color banding - and for a game which is all about a dark environment and looks...that's something once you see you can't unsee. The game fails to detect the correct display resolution unless in exclusive full screen, which makes just having it on as a "wallpaper" of sorts basically impossible while you're doing something else - Not to mention the lack of an option to select which display the game shows up on...another thing keeping it from good wallpaper use. There is a weird...digital "filter" on the ui in the city view that is on all the time, you don't notice it when looking down at a dark city, but point the camera towards the sky and it's always there..and when you notice it, now you notice it while looking at a dark cityscape as well.None of these are really killers aside from the fullscreen issue really, and hopefully they'll get fixed in time. I'm moderately satisfied with what I have, and don't feel the need to refund - but there really could be some..improvements in certain departments.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've been wanting this game since I saw Ghost in the Shell as a kid, and especially the city map display which gave me cyberpunk SimCity vibes before I even knew what cyberpunk was. I just never wanted it enough to actually sit down and figure out how to do it myself. So, thank you for bringing this to life, this game is fantastic! I adored the demo and I am loving the changes that I am finding in the release version. This has been one of the easiest purchases on Steam for me, not because of the low price point, but because it ticks all the boxes. 'Progression' being linked to a hidden element is a fantastic choice and completely removes any pressure or expectation while turning that proogrssion into a little gift of sorts that rewards tinkering. And the soundscape is simply phenomenal. It gives me chills when using my headphones, and it's so easy to lose myself in it.My only two wants for this game would be a neutral lighting mode that can be toggled on/off  that clears up all the fog and shadows for more precise detail work, Edit: The latest update added roads in two different sizes with traffic density that is controlled with a slider, a very nifty addition that really helps bring a city to life! The roads can be elevated with adjustable heights. As a bonus, elevated rail was added as well!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a game developed by Voids Within and published by Voids Within and UNIKAT LabelThe game offers some nice graphics and a really beautiful aesthetic, although some ugly glitches here and there, it is pleasant all the sameThe game does suffer with some repetitiveness at certain areas of the game but a fun game nonethelessDystopika overall, however, is a fun yet challenging game to play, yet sometimes repetitive and it does get boring and tedious if being played for a long time, but is a very good calm sandbox cyberpunk city builder game to play in short bursts!

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is exactly the game it claims to be. It's more of an art tool than a video game and that's all it really needs to be. Just relax and place buildings and tweak your ideal futuristic cyberpunk city without having to worry about money or food or any gameplay mechanics from other citybuilder games that would distract players from the creative process. There is also a nice set of photo tools because what's the point of building a beautiful futuristic city if you can't share it. I'm currently writing a video review to put on my channel on YouTube The Many Talented Mr Jefferson but the developer Matt mentioned that it would be nice to have 500 positive reviews before the Steam Summer Sale so I took a little time to recommend the game on this platform because it really does deserve the attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy citybuilders in creative mode but hate managing economies/resources, this is the game for you! You can build endless neon-soaked cyberpunk cities with a variety of different "district" themes that all mix and match and interact with one another through some procedural magic similar to Townscaper. This game is incredibly relaxing and you can easily throw a few hours into it without even noticing. Looking forward to future additions and mods!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Super chill and relaxing game. Really enjoying the soundtrack options. Even if you just blindly click around on random you can end up with some nice looking designs. _childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Right, first thing is first, my playtime is short but the game is so simple there isn't too much to learn.I recommend it for those who like to chill, Like the Cyberpunk genre and like City builders.There isn't too much to this game which isn't bad. _childDocuments_.review: This is a truly unique one. _childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly an amazing tool for anyone that is planning to or actively building a Cyber Punk TTRPG world and wants to make stunning city scapes. _childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: When I bought this game I already had a pretty good ideia what it was about, and it was exactly what I wanted, but even then I was still expecting myself to get bored after a couple of hours in, which I think is natural. But it turns out I was wrong, after 9 hours straight I haven't gotten bored in the slightest, and I only stopped playing because I had to sleep.Like the developer, I always played SimCity and Cities Skylines on cheats/sandbox mode (and before that, I would draw cities on paper as a child), so this game is pretty much perfect for me. However its important to keep in mind that people looking for urban planning, traffic simulation and just management in general might be disappointed, as this game isn't about that. You just place buildings and decorate them, although its amazing how much freedom it gives you and how easy it is to build cities that look straight out of Blade Runner, which seems to be its main inspiration.Overall this game is gold, and the developer has put real love into it. Can't wait to see how it will look in a year after the planned updates and mod support.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a casual city builder, this is the game for you. You just build the city; there are no objectives, no money, and no people to take care of. It's pretty relaxing, and you can make your city any way you want. Either all the buildings are small, or you can raise them and have a city full of skyscrapers. I've only had it for a couple of hours, but I believe it was worth the small amount of money I paid for it. However, if you want to be able to micromanage your city like City Skylines or Simcity, then this is not the game for you. If you want to spend hours just building your city while unlocking some items to add more stuff, then this is the game for you. However, the one pet peeve I do have about this game is that there is no control settings page or tutorials. You have literally jumped into a building, and you have to figure it out or read the discussions for help.

_childDocuments_.review: Well... _childDocuments_.review: saw a friend playing this game, decided to look into it as the name alone sounded cool, then after looking at the trailer and screenshots, i just fell in love with this game.it feels so relaxing just to place buildings around the place and watch your city come to life as it grows, as well as the style! this is the kind of style for the environment that i love.i do feel more building variety could help out the game, but that is already in the road map, so looks like that is already on the Devs mind.all in all this game is very relaxing, lovely to play when you dont really know what to do and honestly could be a fun way to get some nice Desktop backgrounds.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is amazing, the quality of everything is great, i do hope for more updates with building types and more decorations, and or tools! Me and my friend love this game, i do have a suggestion for being able to have the images change to different ones on a time scale so for example a new image every 30-60 seconds at random intervals.

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper: Blade Runner edition! Just picked this up and put about an hour in. It's basically a tool that lets you "paint" cyberpunk cityscapes onto a landscape "canvas". Pretty fun and chill, good soundtrack and if you're missing cyberpunk vibes it'll scratch the itch in a new way.I only wish there was a little more depth to it, akin to an arvadey cities skylines, or cities skylines lite: cyberpunk edition lol. It's not a very "gamified" experience. I'm very excited to see how this game grows, and popping in now and again to paint up a quick city here and there.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing video games for a long time and what surprised me the most was the lack of needing mechanics and overall goal. This is less of a game and more a creative piece of software that allows you to play around with variety of buildings and decorations to create a futuristic cyberpunk city. Its peaceful and scratches my commercial photographic itch without the need to learn complex build orders or learn specific game knowledge to compete against others or Ai. A true sandbox for people who just want to create and take screen shots.It won't be for everyone as it has very little content, however this is a solo dev project with incredible attention to detail and theme, it does exactly what it set out to do and it does that very well. I look forward to seeing more from this developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Τhis is a game I've followed closely from the earlier stages of its development and it's been the first game in years to actually deliver on the expectations it set for me. It is exactly what it advertises: A cozy dystopian city builder sandbox. Anyone with a small interest in cyberpunk, or city builders (let alone in both) should give it a try. I'm confident you won't be disappointed. The price is ridiculously low for its quality and Matt, the developer, deserves every single penny of it. Sadly you don't get games that deliver on their promises that often anymore,. This is a solo dev game that didn't try to overachieve. The developer knew exactly what he was capable of creating and he did that: He delivered a masterpiece! As if that wasn't enough, the roadmap promises further refinement and replayability. Just imagine the diversity of cities once mods come in! Not to mention a feature I've been begging for from the beginning: road networks.  This game is a 10/10 on my book.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Great game to relax with. There's no goals or limits, just building. The more you build, the more random stuff you unlock too. I love how you can upload your own photos into the game haha. It reminds me of Tiny Glade, but with a cyberpunk aesthetic instead. It also works pretty well on the Steam Deck. Bigger cities won't be a smooth 60FPS experience, but you don't really need it in this kind of game anyway.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a fantastic sandbox game that delivers exactly what it claims to : A futuristic city sandbox for you to create your own cyberpunk cities. It's easy to lose yourself in the arranging of cities and their props and the beautiful screenshots you can take of them.Easy recommend, especially with the roadmap showing it will only get better from here!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is aesthetic, it's 'your' pace, it's interesting and at the same time so absolutely refreshing. I've been looking for a game in which I can create a city and not be constricted by such a silly concept as pfft money, or citizen satisfaction or ... Heavens forbid! Advisors!  Just chill, take in the music, make a city as 'you' envisioned it in games such as Cyberpunk or Glitchpunk or whatever so happens to be your fancy of futuristic settings. This - game - is - worth - it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: ok, i love the cyber punk aesthetic and it drew me in. at first i wasnt so keen on it as it seems so streamlined as a city builder. howver, the more i played with and messed around with it the more it grew on me and you start getting anal with details and it just looks so beautiful. no constraints really so no; city budget, political, social nor economic ramifications. i look forward to see where this goes, especially with the price being so low give it the old college try.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Townscaper but with its cute aesthetic replaced by a neon soaked cyberpunk night. There's no goals or simulation here, it's a city builder in the same vein as Townscaper or Tiny Glade, but on a much larger scale. Love being able to import custom artwork for billboards. For $6 you really can't go wrong if you enjoy the cyberpunk genre. Also soundtrack is crazy good.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: So far a really good game and delivers on what it promised to be. I highly recommend for those who want a relaxing way to be creative, but enjoy the dystopian cyberscape environment to use as a canvas. I hope to see more building types, an increased music library, and more detail in the inhabitants going about life in the scrawling metropolis you can build. But other than those minor requests, I personally am excited to see what more Matt adds to the game overtime. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Delivers on its promise as a nice little cyberpunk sandbox with no management or goals other than unlocking more neat features to place in your city.  The price point of less than $7 is great, considering there is enough here to keep you entertained for several hours at a time if you are like me and get in a zone while meticulously building your city.  The dark, futuristic cityscapes will lull you into a zen state as you contemplate the nature and potential of your existence.  I'd say it's the perfect game to play on a quiet night if you just want to relax before drifting off to dream of electric sheep.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is everything I've ever wanted in a city builder! Incredibly simple and peaceful experience. I've never been one for the city sims that force you to manage streets and resources, but have always wanted to create a Blade Runner type city just to relax and watch. Buy this before the dev realizes what a mistake it was to price this under $15.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Dystopika is a whole lot of fun for anyone who's ever enjoyed the mood and setting of dark future/dystopian literature or media.  I enjoyed the ease of use of the building system.  I'm not an experienced city builder, but Dystopika's system makes errors easy to fix, and even makes errors look good enough that you might decide to leave them in place.  The building variety is impressive and fun to work with.  Overall, you're getting a lot of fun for a few dollars.  It's well worth the purchase if you like city builders.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I was recommended the trailer for Dystopika by YouTube and after watching it, the culmination of "chill cyberpunk-atmosphere building game" was something that intrigued me. So, why not? I decided to take the plunge, buy it, and dang-skippy, it satisfies that itch I didn't know needed scratching. If you just wanna vibe with a lo-fi ish cyberpunk aesthetic reminiscent of Blade Runner, this is your jam!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a fan of Cyberpunk and/or the Bladerunner films and you want to relax and build your own Night City or your own dystopian Los Angeles, this is the game for you. No management, no resource farming, just city building. Hop in, drop some buildings and watch your city come alive before your eyes.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: I got into contact with Dystopika a little earlier, in January when it was still just a demo with a few basic features and simple buildings.I Instantly got hooked by the ambiance as I've been a big fan of Blade Runner-esque movies and games for as long as I can think back.The gameplay is simplistic and straight to the point; you build a futuristic city the way you want it and dress it with fancy looking lights, billboards and other little props to shape up your imagination of such a dark dystopic future city.The developer poured his heartblood and personal experiences in big (Asian) cities as well as fandom for cyberpunk-esque movies, games and architectural art style into this and in my opinion that's visible in every little notch.Even just letting the game run in the background can be very soothing and adds a vibe to whatever you do.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very nice game to chill and build within. It's one of the easier to get into city builders. It's very replayable. I like the soundtrack as well. Definitely captures the cyberpunk vibes. The game is also great for screenshots. No reason not to check it out at this price point. Gameplay Impressions:
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: It does exactly what it says on the box; A delightfully dark, stylized, neon-drenched sandbox.The controls feel intuitive and quick to pick up. The generation and shifting of other smaller building as you place districts invites creativity; encouraging you to tinker with and develop the neighborhoods that rise to meet each skyscraper, and adorn them with all sorts of bright neon lights and decorations.The soundtrack is incredibly relaxing. An entrancing blend of ambient drones to help you focus in as you shape the minute details of your perfect city. I can see myself simply having the game open while doing other work to have a nice visual and gentle music.The game plays and feels great as is. I'm excited to see the improvements future QoL and content updates may bring.We've burned plenty of cities. Now c'mon, Samurai.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: At launch? Complete game, relaxing vibes, sweet city builder without the pressure of economy nor management. Just endless dystopian vibes. It's a huge sandbox, and I love it. I can't wait to see what else we're gonna get in the future updates. As the default set of buildings and models is not as large as I'd like (for now).However, clever placement of several buildings in the same spotwill fix that, as the models have been textured to fit together and make seamless transitions between buildings. I highly recommendtrying that out, especially with the "four towers" from the Lowtownset being put into other skyscrapers to make unique tall buildings with "legs" to populate your residential areas.I wish there was an OST to buy to further support the game! Thanks Matt!
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: i don't know what exactly i was expecting+ very chill+ you can do whatever you want+ no pressure+ you find new stuff as you explore what you can do and how+ literally costs less than a bowl of ramen as said on TV+ photo mode offers relatively deep functions - you can get neat screenshots out of it- not much to complain aboutas a hopeful wish; i'd love cd red project to let this guy have his team and make a city builder spinoff for the cyberpunk franchise - with story objectives or goals and the like, this was a neat expedition to build a city of my own with no limits

_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is simple and to the point. It does exactly what it says it will with very little fluff - build a city in a stereotypical cyberpunk setting. You can change the time of day, change the weather, and add as many neon billboards as your heart desires. There's even a photo mode, which is perfect - with manual camera adjustments and built-in cyberpunk-y filters. And a nice soundtrack for your building background. I'm a HUGE fan of the cyberpunk genre, and this game is a superb addition to my collection.Only 40 minutes in, 10/10 game. Does what it promises for a very reasonable price. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a Bladerunner/CyberPunk fan's wet dream.Absolutely in love with the futuristic dystopian vibes this game has. Paired with a chill, no-stress style game play... this game is perfect for anyone, like me, who want to play more city building games but are easily overwhelmed by complex and cumbersome game mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: This game is precisely what it promised to be, live out your creativity or just place stuff down and see what happens, eitherway you'd probably be surprised, the achievements adding a few smaller cosmetics is also a very nice touch and for that price you can't really do anything wrong.Not sure I ever tried to perfect a game as quickly as this just to see what cosmetics I'd get.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The game promised "Simple" in all of its promotional material, and when you first jump in, it seems almost TOO simple, but once you play around with the controls and learn a little about how things work, it becomes obvious that the game delivers exactly what it promised. The ambiance is fantastic, the fog and rain transport you to that neon-soaked noir near-future that hearkens back to properties like "Blade Runner" and "Judge Dredd". It's fun to unlock the tidbits that pop up as you build, and they truly add to the overall feel of the whole thing. The sole developer has promised to continue adding features and elements to the game post-launch, and we're already off to a great start. The potential for true, immersive depth has a strong foundation to build from, and I can't wait to see where it goes. The only minor detraction from the overall experience might be that the game does not hold your hand at all. You pretty much have to learn about features and mechanics as you go. This may appeal to some folks, but it might mean you will scrap your first creation once you know what you're doing and can really open up creatively when starting from scratch. Overall very fun, and well worth the money if you are a fan of cyberpunk, and/or city building. I often found myself wondering what sort of stories could be found in the dark shadows of my city as I built...
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: Well I saw and heard about this game on random just by browsing new upcoming indie titles.Honestly and this game does as it says,It is an enjoyable calming sandbox games it gives me the same feeling as if I was playing Universe Sandbox but with the addition from city building titles that we all enjoy and play. Its really relaxing of a game and enjoyable to play since it has no rules or goal except just mess around and unlock new items! Its really just an amazing calming title.Although for the developer!!I would like to see hopefully upcoming maybe a little bit more usable buildings, lights, and things to solidify the experience and add more of the cyberpunk immersion feeling. I would also love to see a tutorial either a separate mode or optional when starting out this is helpful to explain maybe what you can do goals and etc cause it does just throw you into the experience and it isn't hard to understand the mechanics of the game and what to do but it is also nice knowing there is a tutorial or some form of explanation in case we want to reference or go back to something.Amazing title and price keep it classy and I cant wait to see where it goes from here.
_childDocuments_.name: Dystopika

_childDocuments_.review: The game that I have been waiting for has finally arrived. Have you ever wanted to create your own slice of Los Angeles from Blade Runner? Or maybe wanted to explore your own creative persona and build a cyberpunk city with no punishing requirements of resources or citizen demands. Dystopika blends zen chill city building vibes with an absolutely amazing cyberpunk aesthetic. Get lost in the large looming buildings, neon lights, flying cars that zoom by and brilliantly appropriate soundtrack. This is only the beginning of what's in store of this experience. Future updates will add more content and features. If you've ever wanted to play a cyberpunk city builder, Dystopika is the only game you'll need.

_childDocuments_.review:
Dystopika is a small city-builder inspired by cyberpunk and the wanderlust of cities that never sleep.

Place buildings, giant billboards, and towering holograms, working in harmony with procedural generation for landscape, traffic, and lights to create your own future metropolis rich with vibes and ambience. Escape to your own little dystopian dreams (or nightmares).

No goals, no objectives, no wins or losses. Just relax and embrace creative cyberpunk zen. If you love to turn on the cheat codes and just build, this one's for you.

name: Star Trucker
detailed_description: Wishlist another new title from Raw Fury! About the Game Hop into the driver's seat of your rocket-powered big rig as you haul cargo, scavenge for salvage and interact with an eclectic cast of star-hopping truckers in this Americana-infused journey on the ultimate open road - space! Cruise the hyper highways, taking on a variety of jobs such as fuel hungry long hauls and hazardous drop-offs to earn cash and unlock new content. And don't forget to monitor the CB radio for chatter from fellow truckers; it's a fantastic way to uncover side gigs and stay updated on galactic gossip. Keeping your rig runnin’ isn’t always easy. You’ll need to keep your core systems online, gravity compensator spinnin’ and hull patched to prevent your cab from leaking lung juice. Be sure to make pre-trip shop stops for replacement parts, and consider upgrading your truck at a local garage. These improvements are vital for safely navigating volatile sectors and ensuring timely deliveries. Use the galactic map to plan your journey and warp jumps, while keeping an eye on your fuel reserves and power levels. Once your route is set, kick back, crank up the cab hi-fi and cruise to a selection of original songs covering starburst blues, galactic rock and asteroid infused americana. The open road is waiting! Star Trucker is the passion project of a small team: Monster and Monster. A two-person indie studio with a love for all things sci-fi and sim. With the help of some talented friends they’ve developed an out of this world experience filled with emergent challenges and complex systems to master. So buckle up and join them for the long haul!

short_description: Haul cargo, trade salvage and keep your space suit close as you search for fame and fortune among the stars in a game that puts an interstellar twist on the truck sim genre.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll be honest, I only bought the game because of the screenshots. I thought the idea of ​​trucks in space was totally silly and as an old Elite Dangerous trader I had to see it. And to get straight to the point, I like the game but there are two things I would like to mention.Firstly, you don't fly through a huge galaxy, you just make small jumps from sector to sector. Each of these sectors is unique and brings its own challenges to get your cargo safely to its destination. So far there is enough variety and you can find your way around the sectors more quickly.The second point has to do with the balance of the game. I can only recommend not playing on the standard difficulty, systems are constantly breaking and are extremely expensive to replace. If you want less hassle, you should start a custom game and reduce the energy consumption and the use of wear parts by a level, I had so much more fun with it.Oh and the soundtrack on the radio is absolutely great, it's a real shame that there are only so few songs.So I have to move on, the truck is calling"Keep on keepin' on"
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: You're in space. In a vacuum. You need a space suit to go outside on EVA and still be able to breathe. But your truck has a horn and you can honk at other trunks in space. Take a moment to think about that.While this funny little break of realism may be merely amusing, unfortunately the game comes with a lot of more unrealistic game mechanics that only exist to annoy you. Like that all your truck's systems are being powered by individual sets of batteries instead of pulling power from its propulsion system (apparently the technology of generators and cables has been lost to the fog of history). Or how in a space ship with an artificial gravity generator that sometimes fails, there is no provision on this ship to strap anything down. Or how the designers of your ship made sure that your internal lighting and magnetic coupling system have both a set of redundant batteries for backup - but apparently such trivial secondary systems like gravity and life support only have a single one. Practice holding your breath while floating when you have to change their batteries - which you have to do a lot. The same batteries that can power a magnetic coupling able to pull 40-60 tons behind you outlast the batteries that simply power the lights in and on your truck.The visual presentation of this game is really top notch - but whoever was in charge of the game's mechanics needs to revisit Game Design 101.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Might rigs in space. Played the demo to death, more than once. So far loving the full game.It's graphically pleasing whilst not being overly taxing. Throw in the the music and Yee Haw were hauling.Can be a little slow to start with, and you have to watch where you're driving to avoid random damage occurring. Remember, brake pedals don't work in zero gravity. There's this thing called inertia that you'll need to deal with.If you avoid the "rush" jobs and plan out a trading route, it's a nice way to chill out.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Resource micromanagement simulator. Not a bad game, just different and often frustrating. "Recommended" difficulty may not be the best for beginners. As of the date of this review, no key rebinding available. Some bugs, including soft locking progress if side missions are not done in a certain order. Do not expect this to be ATS/ETS. Think giant, poorly maneuverable brick in space surrounded by debris that can potentially kill you with hull breaches.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I REALLY wish i could recommend that game. I love the idea and aesthetic. I have I've played for around 7 hours on game pass and the gameplay aspect of driving through space is awesome. I wanted to actually buy the game on steam, but i kept getting more frustrated, postponed it and now decided against it. The thing that holds back the game immensely is the tediousness of maintenance. I started the game on recommended mid difficulty and after 2 hours and learning that batteries are disposable and you cant charge them, i started to look through in game options to lower difficulty. And well... you cant. You can only start the game over. In the skill tree I went to the left and maxed just-in-time jobs, where you have short window to deliver the goods after few hours. Well guess what, i was lucky with first few ones, and just driving there normally allowed me to be on time. But a third one, i was in the system 30 min early. I went to the bed in the truck and was astonished to find that there is no sleeping to forward time in this game. At this point you have to wait 30 minutes IRL with game on and unpaused to finish this job. Freaking unbelievable. I kept playing, getting more and more frustrated. I thought maybe as you progress story there will be QoL upgrades that make it all less tedious. But no. There is no progression like that. It's too frustrating to continue at this point, I'm dropping the game.And if any dev reads this and wants some feedback, here it is:The initial tediousness of maintenance is ok, for beginner greenhorn trucker. IMO game needs a separate skill tree for QoL (and 1+1=2 skill points on lvlup). In there should be upgrades for onboard workshop and charger for batteries, maybe where the second bed is now. As game progresses and you lvlup, this skill tree would allow you to clean filters and repair UCCs to give them a second life, charger would allow you to charge 1 battery at a time, later upgrade to more, for increased fuel cost. Less important, but also cool options for that skill tree: remote job board connection, delivery drones for the shop, auto-docking.That's how I would see proper progression in this game. But for me to return to this game, the bare minimum, is to allow to change difficulty options mid game and sleeping in bed to pass time. Please devs, I dont see it mentioned on the roadmap at all, and its like a day of coding, if your code is not spaghetti.'This game is a rough diamond, still feels like early access. Hopefully the devs can get more people on board as they said in the post, and they'll help them realize what the priorities should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Game Review: Space Trucking Sim (2024)Rating: 5 out of 5 Lot LizardsAfter just 30 minutes of playing this ambitious space trucking sim, I’m hooked. The game throws you right into the world of space trucking with fuel management, repairs, various jobs, and hazards that keep you on your toes. The trucker music sets the perfect vibe as you cruise through the stars in some seriously cool-looking rigs.While the core gameplay is engaging, I’m hoping the developers plan to expand on truck customizations, refits, and add more trucks to choose from. The idea of multiplayer features or even creating a character to hang out at community hubs (space Truckstops) with other players—alien or human—would be a dream come true.It’s an ambitious project, but with more content and community interaction, this game could become a favorite for space trucking fans. For now, it’s a solid 5 out of 5 lot lizards!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: the care,fun, and affection the devs must have had for this game is palpable. The style is great, the maps are unique. Driving, maintaining, repairing, customizing my big rig is really interactive and addicting. Why is it so fun to check the map for gas prices and where to unload my used batteries? Why do I love spending time sorting all my salvage? The learning curve isn't as scary as some other simulation games. Just keep an eye on when things will break down! and if you're really nervous, there's different levels of difficulty so you can ease yourself into it. I'd highly recommend this game to anyone who has an interest in trucking and space world building!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Difficulty levels are extremely unbalanced. In easy mode power consumption is somewhere around 20% per hour, on medium its around 90. I recommend for those who want to keep truckin without a stress just start custom game with everything default except power consumption set to low.  Other than that game is really fun. Wish we could buy different rigs tho

The physics are also a bit off, and the stability assist doesn't seem to work that well. After getting that under control. It is a blast I would say it is a RPG/SIM space truck driving game. I am enjoying it very much. I would love to see DLCs and multiplayer/CO-OP.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Been following this game for some time and wondered what it could actually become upon release. So far, I'm not disappointed. It's in a lot of ways like American Truck Sim which I love. I find myself being immersed with the side story missions which come across the CB radio. The voice acting is decent and there's a nice array of characters. The way you can organized what's being stored on your truck/ship is pretty cool too. Currently there's the silly way of keeping the lid of your cargo open to keep them in place on the shelves. I hope this is addressed and maybe they ad fasteners or something to counter this. My only issue with the game is the lack of survival I guess. Now, there's nothing in the description of the game that says it's a survival game, but since there's food and drinks that you can transport and even find as salvage floating out in space, I'd love to see them add some type of vital system where you had to eat and drink. It would be awesome to pull up to a Space McDonald's and order a space burger and a cosmic drink. Now, the music is amazing in this game. Sometimes you get the random ambient music while you're doing repairs to your truck while floating outside your truck and there's an actual radio that you can turn on and off. To sum everything up, I highly recommend this game if you're looking for a chill game to sink some hours into.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Step 1 accept long haul job for $5000Step 2 accumulate a $5000 in debt for batteries, air filters, and gasStep 2B truck runs into you at a warp gate. Too many holes to fix in one go, Die Step 3 get revived -$5000 dollars for recovery fee -$1000 dollars for breach of contractStep 4 Debts up to $11000 Repeat steps 1-3 Truck gets repossessed, realise the american dream
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So, day one analysis.First off, its a really fun and quirky game idea.Secondly, the game literally just came out and will obviously undo further updates and QoL changes.As I said, this game literally just came out and already its a lot of fun. The controlls take some getting used to, and as of rn you cant change them either, but that doesnt change the fact that the gameplay is one-of-a-kind. Its a game you can always pick up and just keep doing what you were doing last time. It can be easy but at the same time its own, strangly difficult challange. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Don't be fooled, this is survival horror hell at it's worst not some cosy truck sim. If you have debt in real life, prepare to escape into a world where you have even worse debt. I've asphyxiated in my cockpit twice because I couldn't afford air filters and was charged a small fortune for the ambulance call-out. I was sometimes afraid to leave the station because my truck couldn't hold a vacuum and I didn't want to die in space, but then realised air isn't free on stations either. I grinded a few hours to try and pull myself out of debt all the while being heckled over the radio by the local truckers and their quirky side missions which playfully waste your time while you accrue more debt. I ended up getting my truck re-possessed only 57 space bucks away from clearing my overdraft and had to start a new game. 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far I'm enjoying the game, it's rough and can be improved in some areas but overall I feel it was worth the purchase. I think I can fade away and spend a couple hours a day chilling and playing the game. When I bought it, I didn't realize it had just released a few days earlier, but I see the developers have already made notes about the patches going forward, so I feel good about the future of the game. I'm glad to see they're going to be making some changes to the availability and pricing of air filters and power cells, It's been a challenge to manage it on the recommended difficulty level for starting out. I would love to see air filters, power cells, and cards available at fuel stations. When we get fuel, we should be able to buy the necessities. To balance it out, they could have a premium price, and shopping around can get you a better price... maybe even a points card to get you a discount.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It has always been my dream, since the 1996 release of the hit movie Space Truckers, to be a space trucker. Since this game was announced in the steam store I have had it in my wishlist. This game is the PERFECT product for me. It has all the little nuances of operating a space craft but on a really accessible level. It also pulls all the perfect elements of trucking and americana to make a truly awesome experience. The music is fantastic, all the sounds are amazing, just sitting down in the pilots chair has so many neat noises and animations. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm still early in the game, so I feel like I'll have more to say as time goes on.  My early impression is that I'm loving the game but the learning curve is brutal.  This is not a relaxing sit in your truck and haul goods through the stars kind of game.  Maybe once I've had time to get the hang of it, but wow it's unforgiving.  There's a bunch of highly necessary equipment that your truck needs to stay running.  Power cells, air filters and circuit breakers.  They all deplete over time and don't recharge.  Compared to the rewards for completing jobs, they're quite expensive, and some of them don't last very long.  You can sell all of them, but they don't hold their value.  And they're all active right from the start of the game.The game directs you to a manual in the glove compartment immediately upon starting.  I've read the whole thing, and I recommend everybody does the same.  However, there are a number of things that I think should be clarified.  Easy changes, because it's just text.  Well, I suppose they then need to translate it to 50 different languages.First, make a list of all the critical systems and how to keep them running.  Explicitly state that they are all consumable, nothing recharges it needs to be replaced when it depletes.  Second, explain exactly where all of them are.  I went for quite a while with cargo bouncing around the inside of my cab before I finally found where the gravity control system power equipment is.  I also didn't realise there was a second set of air filters until I passed out (again).  Now, I have to say that I have been enjoying figuring all this out.  It wasn't unfun.  But it does get frustrating to have my bank hit negative again after finishing a lengthy story job because the air filter that I needed to change was more than the job payout.  Here's my suggestion.  Difficulty levels.  I think this would be easy to implement.   - Casual relaxed mode: depletion rates have a 0 multiplier (0.25 for fuel), so power cells and air filters will never run out, they're just a trade commodity.   - Easy mode: depletion rates have a 0.5 multiplier, so they take twice as long to exhaust. - Medium mode: depletion rates have a 0.75 multiplier - Realistic "trying to make it as a freelance trucker in a nasty economy" mode: depletion rates have a 1.0 multiplier.   - Mean "we want you to fail and be miserable" mode: depletion rates have a 2.0 multiplierSo, other than the very unforgiving learning curve, this game is great.  I've been having a blast.  Learning to control the truck took a bit of time, but once I started to get the hang of it I've been running successful deliveries and having a great time.  The vistas are absolutely gorgeous.  I've discovered that I enjoy country when it's being sung about space trucks.  It has a trading system that is familiar to anybody who has played a space trading game before.  Commodity type X is worth more in this system than that system.  Buy some low and sell them high.  These commodities are illegal in these systems, be careful if you have some in your cab.  I haven't gotten into the customisation part of the game yet because I can barely afford to keep my truck out of impound, but the default look is great, so I can only imagine the possibilities.

_childDocuments_.review: Nice chill space truckin'The game seems to use newtonian style physics for movement, so if you move in one direction, you need to apply thrust in another direction to turn. Will you stay on the marked highway, or risk a shortcut through that debris field to save time? Loads of potential for fast and risky trucking if you want to.As others also say, the ability to remap the controls would be nice and i don't kno why it wasn't included at launch.Overall an enjoyable game.

_childDocuments_.review: super fun game, arguably one of the best this year, the soundtrack is a MUST HAVE too. great style too, very unique and defining.if you like driving sims, open world games, or space games, but want something that's not racing and instead doing hauling and story missions, pick this up. totally worth it, especially on sale. it's kinda simple on the surface, but still really fun and really enjoyable and a great game to chill on if you're comfortable with space navigation, but it gets more complex due to the hazard system and the maintaining of certain systems on your rig. if you want a challenge, turn off the driving assist to up the difficulty and make it a true sim experience. turns things up a notch. that said, here's some key points that make this a great game:1: full 6dof, turns difficulty up a ton2: customizable difficulty with 5 options making it very fun for anyone3: solid gameplay loop with some great story rolled in4: chill and relaxing and once you get established it gets really really fun to play for hours on end5: AWESOME SOUNDTRACKgame also runs fine on Linux Mint 22, i recommend fullscreen windowed (full screen exclusive has an alt+tab allergy) and using Proton 9 as with Proton Experimental you get less frames. that said the game could definitely use some optimization to boost framerates in the first placemy only criticisms are as follows:1: it's not entirely optimized and suffers from pretty low frames, lower than i'd expect.2: the driving manual needs improvement because some of the ways the game seems to calculate things like careful driving are a bit wonky and not entirely clearly stated, only offhandedly mentioned in the mock contracts you accept in the job boards in game, and could use some clearing up in the driving manual in game as it's not explained what constitutes "good driving".

_childDocuments_.review: On my first job I ran into 8 pebbles and all 8 times I had to stop what I was doing, get out of the truck, and hold click on where the pebble hit.  I was looking for a euro truck in space where you actually get to drive your truck but no you just teleport places and then scoot along to the gold diamond while repairing 30 hull breaches. I just am unsure if the game directors were shooting their self in the foot for the fun or if someone in charge really thought people looking for a trucking game would want to, rather than drive the truck, repair the truck. Or make sure the truck is powered, or make sure the truck is this or that. I say the same thing every time a game fails to keep an audience. If you are going to make a game, every single aspect of it needs to do one of a few things. 1. Be fun (why *IN THE RECOMMENDED DIFFICULTY* am i stopping everything im doing because you wanted a gas leak mechanic)2. Reward the player (this is a must) (this game immediately filled my time playing it with remedial tasks that never felt rewarding.)3. Sense of direction (I cannot tell you how many games get this so game killingly wrong however this game did a great job at that)TL;DR This game shot itself in the foot. _childDocuments_.review: Mutha Truckin great so far!PS. If you are playing this on keyboard and mouse and find it hard, here's a hot fix. This definitely needs some economy balancing...air filters (which you need to stay alive) cost more than most of the job payouts!I'm currently 20k in debt with 2 days left to pay it all back which I've got no chance of doing on the poxy payouts.Also annoyingly, if there's 2 single delivery jobs in the same system going to same place or somewhere else on the way you cant pick both trailers up. So if you sign up for both, you have to do one at a time.The only multi-trailer jobs are those that already specify that it has 2 trailers.Like to see the engine sound more beafier too, the current whine can get on your nerves and doesn't exactly sound like a powerful rig.Still great though, well done to the 2 devs!

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I don't think this game is necessarily bad. It's more of a case of "not my cup of tea" with a pinch of "my expectations were wrong". But Steam ask me "Do you recommend this game?" and the most honest answer I can give is "no".So what happened?In Star Trucker, the player takes on the role of... Well, a star trucker. You drive a space truck that looks a lot like your regular trucks from Earth and deliver cargo across the galaxy. Cool concept, right? As a fan of the Truck Simulator and MudRunner series, I was really looking forward to the release. I love the meditative gameplay that usually comes with these types of games, and the sci-fi space setting definitely seemed like a welcome addition.But here's the thing: this is not your average meditative truck driving game where you can peacefully drive many miles down the road. The “roads” here are quite short actually, and large cosmic distances are covered in seconds with the help of gates that are located in each system. So you don't travel for long. Instead, most of the time you're dealing with the complexities of moving and docking in 3D space, as well as maintaining your truck. And although the gameplay is competent, it is not particularly exciting and sometimes even annoying.There is a story/campaign of sorts with characters and radio conversations, which is a welcome addition - games of this type don't usually bother with that. But it wasn't interesting or exciting enough to make me stay in the game longer.So while the Star Trucker concept is fun and the game overall is well made, I unfortunately didn't find it interesting enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's as if an Elite: Dangerous space trucking meme took on a life of its own. It's not the greatest at anything but everything is done well which makes it hours of enjoyable space trucking fun. It is a higher quality than its price suggests and feels like a great value in a game. If you like space games, trucking games, or just hauling cargo and trading this game is for you. It even has a story straight out of a 70's trucker flick if one's interested and does a great job being immersive and environmental.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is super fun. Great graphics, music, and sound. The space trucks are simulated using full inertia so you can prepare for stopping or a turn when parking or manoeuvring. Inside the truck you have racks for storage, compartments for batteries and PCB boards, and you can buy storage containers to put all your spare parts in. The simulation of truck systems is simple and fun but you do have to watch your battery levels and change them out for new ones before they expire. There are plenty of cockpit controls to play around with in the truck. You have CCTV from different vantage points to make reversing easier. If you do run out of oxygen you can quickly put on your space suit until you get to a shop to buy more parts and you can perform EVA's to repair leaks on the external parts of the space truck.There is a story and at various points you can speak to other truckers on the CB radio but the progression seems to be locked to how many miles you have travelled. Overall the game is awesome and if you want a chilled out ATS experience but in space I can definitely recommend Star Trucker!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Ngl, this is probably just a personal issue, but I do get a bit of 'space sickness' from playing this. It keeps my playtime in check, but whenever I do play, I have an amazing time. It's one of the best space experiences I've had in gaming so far. The truck feels weighty and, in a way, 'authentic' for what the game is aiming to be, I guess.I’m not the biggest fan of the exclusive Space Truck designs—it’s probably more iconic this way, but at least the designs look good and suit the style.This game has so much potential for future development, and I hope the devs expand on it even more.Easy recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game!  I tried on recommended level and died twice fairly quickly.  Third time I did a custom game where I could change the settings.  Gave myself $25000, purchases were cheap, batteries and filters lasted longer, and damage was less severe.  No difficulties after that so I could learn the game.  Up to level 7 and I'm enjoying it.  Have put in 5k hours on ATS and ETS2, and Star Trucker isn't the same.  You are flying a space truck (freighter).  The is a spaceship flying game, not a truck driving game.  It reminds me of X4.  It's cool!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Has the game improved since alpha demo builds? Sure.Is there significantly more content now that the game is released? No.And that's the problem.It technically functions the same as Euro Truck Simulator but the detailed lively map is what makes a delivery sim great, and its non existent here.Sectors in the galaxy map which you warp through are small, undetailed and dead. There's not really much to do or see in them. And designated roads are utterly useless as you can just beeline to warp gates in and out of sectors. Few NPCs running around and they all drive the same trucks. No space police or authorities, no major consequences for actions. No new space trucks to buy. Few things to customize on your trucks. No homebase to buy and park your trucks in. Nothing to see, nothing to do, nothing to really work towards.Its an okay game but not worth base price. Expected way way more after the demo. This is basically an enhanced demo build.I'm quite disappointed in this game, waited a while for this.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: To start with I really like this game. Its a breath of fresh air in the sim games I've been playing. The game looks stunning, the music is fun, great variety in different star systems and challenges. If you have played ETS2 you will feel right at home. However this is not a cozy sim where you can turn your brain off. Its the opposite. This game is hard, very hard. This game will test your strategy, time management and resource management. I can only speak for myself but at the beginning I have gotten close to death several times, constantly running in debt from having to buy very expensive air filters and batteries to stay alive at the end of a haul Id be lucky to profit 500 bucks. I am playing on default difficulty. The more I played however I started to understand the games kinks, I read through the manual in the glove box and that really helped when I was in trouble. This game is not for everyone. I think this game desperately needs adjusting to at least the economy and prices. I understand how the game works now but I can barely keep up with maintenance. Also the game for me does not run well in some sectors with low frames and there is barely any graphics and key bind options. I've seen more options on some console games. This is not acceptable on PC in 2024 I'm afraid.  I'm keen to see where this game goes. I recommend this when its on sale.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'll start with "Hey I know I don't got much play time"I like the game, the visuals and all that jazz my issue for me at-least was the beginning tutorial was barely helpful, the hud objectives are small, and hard to read at points. And is there a way to actually find what routes you need to be taking? I took a contract and I flew across the entire map trying to find the right highway to take to get to my location with little to no help with navigation. The controls are messy and yet loose, I crashed into two small dinky things trying to maneuver cause I couldnt see them till the last moment and its kinda hard to advoid. I personally would like to see a way to actually visually understand where I should be heading; or hell even just a GPS.Now argueably this was my first truck sim, Im a sci-fi space enjoyer so maybe im not the target audience

It's also something the devs have said they are working on. As someone who loves these kind of games, it gets a definitely thumbs up from me. Very well done, especially from a really small developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I'll sorta recommend it.  As a huge American Truck Sim fan I was stoked about trying something different.  But I dunno it's just not my thing.  The game design and idea behind it is cool and creative.  I just found the controls too difficult, even with a controller.  Not only do you have to deal with sideways trailer angle, you have to deal with vertical angle as well, and I just found it frustrating to the point of just saying the hell with it.  I guess if you have extra time to spend getting the hang of it, it would be fine.  Just not my thing I guess.  So my review is more of a personal preference, so not gonna give a negative review.  If I could I'd give it a mixed.  Cool concept, needs better options for controls, like a simplified mode or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: As a big ETS2 and space-games fan, I had big hopes for this, but ended being a disappointment. The game has some good points, like:- the atmosphere- visuals- decent music- truck upgrades (that I found by luck when I ran out of oxygen)But that comes with a lot of cons:- Your truck running out of resources very quickly (basically the power cells that power up systems like oxygen, gravity, temperature) make the game feel more like a survival than a chill hauling simulator, and I was playing on 'recommended' settings, so I guess this is intended. You also can't disable this in the 'custom' game mode, just lower the rate they are consumed.- not being able to recharge power cells is very bad, making the point above even worse- you need to dock to do everything, even to get a job - we have warp gates but dont have wireless?- controls are... incomplete. you can roll on forward axis, move forward and back, and also roll on lateral axis, but you can't strafe left or right, or up and down, making dock and aligning on warp gates very hard and annoying- the guy from the 'campaign' talks to you and you need to answer by going in the internal camera, getting the radio talker, holding right click and then choosing an option as an answer. But the distance between things on each system is very small, so if you are at medium-high speed and want to answer, then you need to full stop so you dont crash- also on distance, we dont have that 'road feeling' that we have on ETS2, like taking a super far job and taking literally 2 RL hours to deliver. Every job is just a 5 minutes in each system until you reach each warp gate, then you make 2 or 3 jumps like this and it's over.- in each system you dont know where anything is (like a shop to buy a very expensive power cell), so you need to guess and try to get close to something and hopefully is what you're looking forAnyway, these design choices make the game what it is, maybe you'll like it, but I didn't because I was expecting a more relaxing experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: After playing (and getting bored) of American Truck Simulator, this game is a great refresher to the trucking genre.  Not only is it beautiful, it is innovative.  I can walk around the inside of my truck, I can turn off the lights in different parts of my truck, hell I can go outside into space and fix my truck.  There is a lot to work towards in the game right now but I do wish for more new content in the future.  Maybe a way to personalize your truck's interior, more types of playable cabs, or someway to make a convoy with your friends.  I can't wait to see what the future holds for this hidden gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Nice space truckin' game! The atsmophere in this game... And driving feel of your Space Rig are both very well done. Space can be silent, in a good way, but luckily you have your trusted radio in the upper left. In this game you'll manage a lot of systems but as for me in Driver mode it's not too hard to handle and you can see when things go south and need replacement.One thing though ; even in Driver mode it's kinda hard to make some cash, because most of the time you spend all made money on maintaining your rig. Now, after 25+ hours i feel jobs get better and more specialized and therefore more profitable. But don't assume the first hours aren't enjoyable, it is a great -somehow- realistic feeling 'driving' through space and hauling cargo and you're always making progress one way or another. Highly recommend!!Cheers to the dev's :P
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome! The game is exactly You get what you expect. It's full,it's ready to play, it's new and fresh. Live in your truck, spend vacations under your truck and sometimes travel from repar station to spare parts shop :)Parts from floating space trash are better than the ones from my truck manufacturer... is it Ford Motor?
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing Game.It can be cozy or really challanging, depending on the difficutly you choose.So I think everyone that likes trucking and survival games will enjoy this game.I personally like the easier difficulty more, because you can RP as an actual Star-Trucker without being afraid of dying by a dumb mistake (which will happen a lot; dont get greedy or speedy)The story is also really nice and well delivered via the Radio, which has really really good voice acting. Its nothing special but it helps to deliver the feeling of beeing a trucker in space really good.The space walks are also suprisingly well done: gameplay wise and also physically.For this price I dont see any reason to not give it a shot at least :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: How is this "mostly positive"? Why are a lot of the negative reviews talking about the economy being impossible? Literally just do jobs, you come out net positive if you're not a total crashout, at least when playing on the recommended difficulty. I'd say most of these guys just tried the basic contracts before levelling out other types, but I see most of them have the same hours or more as me. Or maybe the devs patched the economy post-release, not sure.Regardless: Really enjoying the game, the space spin on the typical ATS/ETS gameplay is great and well done. Being able to walk around the truck and EVA outside, tactile everything, the maintenance... all of it is right up my alley.Big bonus for having an actual story, and all the characters being likable. I watched the movie Convoy recently, definitely get the same vibes from this with the frequent CB radio usage etc. The radio is brilliant, all the space-related songs and in-universe ads are a nice touchI've gone up to the first set of upgrades. The shock absorbers are meh, just another part to replace. However I really like the shutters and solar flare systems, having to shut the windows and drive using the cameras mixes things up and is enjoyable
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly a good experience, feel like its only going to get better.A few highlights are: being able to choose the experience you want, be it hard and fast, red lining your engines the whole way, or nice and slow, getting your cargo there in one piece, often with a nice bonus that comes with it.The maintenance side of the game is pretty well thought out and its rewarding to learn and understand and i found it fairly engaging, trying to squeeze that last bit of power to get to the next stop or pulling something from one less important system to keep things together.customization is very nice, a small drawback is not being able to change the color scheme on company liveries you can make your Rig look how you want it too, and the incremental upgrades are nice too. though I wish they didn't need to be serviced so often, Especially the structural components, but it is rewarding to have something that can hit an asteroid 10 times my rigs size at 200 mph and only be Inconvenienced by it... still need to get it fixed, just, Later instead of Now.Characters are better then expected, find them to be rather interesting and somewhat relatable which is Not what i expected to find, voice acting is also rather charming. a Surprising but Very welcome plus.Overall i'd give this game a 10/10. there is always room for improvement but for what it is now I like it.Keep up the good work M&M team!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Let me state first: I do love this game. Coming as someone who still holds Elite: Dangerous as their favorite game of all time (and Star Citizen trying for number 2 and failing because  doesn't know how to prioritize and set deadlines for meaningful features)... with some time put into American Truck Simulator,  the  of the game is solid.I like the atmosphere, the general design of the world they've built here, and yes, the fact that someone seems to have actually done their research when it comes to the CB conversations (though, completely inconsequential, every time I look at that CB I wonder why a non-SSB capable CB has a clarifier knob, which is only needed on sideband... and sideband is more of a DXer thing not a driver thing). The  is sound. The implementation could use some work. I'm not saying don't buy this game... but do know what you're getting into, especially... (checks notes) exactly 1 week after release at the time of writing this.Everything is just  Note for what I'm about to say next: I've been playing on the balanced difficulty setting thus far, except where noted.Like, we have all the good trappings of a nice leisure game, a nice "dad" game here. (Especially since, to be frank, there's really not that much involved gameplay otherwise. You drive things. End of story. That's not necessarily a negative, that's just what it is.) But "leisure" doesn't generally insinuate having to get up every 5-15 minutes to swap power cells, to reload an autosave because some NPC driver hit you while you were going in a perfectly straight line, to have to weigh every single purchase you make (of things you need) because every dollar that ends up in your bank account goes right back into parts that'll fail before the day is over, or fuel that takes like 1/4 of the tank per job.My advice: Wait for a round of patches. or three. I can't  recommend it in it's  state, but the devs seem passionate enough that I'm hoping I'll have to edit my review in the future once some tweaks have been made. If you do want to play right now, don't pick a difficulty. Pick custom, set the settings up the way you'd like. That'll be a more enjoyable experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: overall I like the game and have played it pretty much everyday since bought it.  the variety of area's are nice and its a relaxing game most of the time. The bad is that there is definitely a balancing issue. The only thing that really affects the payout for a shipment is the number of jumps you need to make. so the only license that really matter are the long haul ones. even then it can be inconsistent. you could find a job to jump two systems and a job to jump five systems be the same payout or the two system job will payout more than the five jump job.The batteries have three tiers of capacity. buying the high tier battery is a waste of money as it is usually more that triple the price of the low tier one, but it only has double the capacity.you have two air filters you have to keep serviced. they last a hour at most and cost a jobs worth of money. you would think in space the filters and batteries would be  in supply at every store but are not. overall its a good game it just aggravating at times.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I'll throw down a review since this is such a unique title and deserves recognition for that. The theme is top notch, 80's trucker mixed with space is a match made in heaven.This game is a combination between a space flight sim and a trucking simulator. One of the game design issues you run into with that is you have to pick and choose per feature which type of sim you'll be more like. And this game and I have a serious disconnect on that, everything I think should operate more space simulator like, operates more like a trucking sim, and vice versa. It's not a knock on the game at all, just a mental disconnect that I personally have to work through while playing.For the mechanic aspect, I find everything that happens in the cab of the truck to be mildly irritating in some way or another, whether that's items taking damage from being looked at wrong, or the gravity generator battery not being a redundant set of two, so your things go flying every time you change it, UNLESS you're parked at a store. Personally if I were going to space, I'd strap everything down, yet there is not a strap to be seen.All the complaints aside, the game is fun, an arcade-y trucking sim in a nice setting, with easy trailer management and fantastic voice actors. Don't mess with the law, they may not arrest you, but those fines will put you in student loan levels of debt.Like many of the other reviews mention, this is NOT an easy game. If you want a cozy drive'em'up then make sure to tweak the difficulty. Recommended will hurt early game, financially and emotionally.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I rarely write reviews.  Usually it's because the game so bad I need to. NOT IN THIS CASE.This a SUPERB game. What a two dev team has accomplished in a EZ is fantastic!  And before you nit-pik saying it lacks this and that, take time to read the Dev updates.  They are working on a lot!  The skill set needed to accomplish something like this is incredible 2.5 people on a team. (I don't know how they got that number lol).  Consider the physics of space.  It take a lot of work to get it right as you've probably noticed in lots of games.  Now add the complexity of physics within physics.  You have a truck in space.  And you have different gravity in the truck that can turn to zero G.   Very complex. I not run into any bugs myself, but I am aware some people experience some issues.  The dev's are paying attention to reports and fixing as fast as they can.  Personally if I had the funds I'd invest a few grand into this team.  That's all for now.   Take it Easel!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It is with a heavy heart that I give this a thumbs down. It's a super charming game with all the tell-tale signs of a really passionate team... but no battery charger?!?! That's outrageous. I didn't even make it 2 hours into the game and I had replaced 5 batteries! At a cost of $500/$1500 a pop, and they aren't unlimited, so you have to check out each trader you pass, which increases the amount of time between your loads and opportunities to make money. God forbid you run into something and get fined/docked pay for reckless driving/ damage your hull.I like the maintenance side of the game, it's very cool and seems so deep and interesting, but there should be goal to reach for. I should be able to go through the tough times to unlock a battery charger and increase my QOL and my overall income stream by cutting out those costs. I AM FLYING A ROCKET FFS, I CAN SPARE SOME ENERGY TO CHARGE A POWERCELL.Apparently it gets worse with air filters too costing some crazy price like $3000?Disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Game is pretty fun they made improvements since the two demos they released. Controls are okay on controller I understand that we are in space but it does sometimes feel that turning left or right feels a bit loose. Would like to see more sectors added in post launch content and more banter from our cast of truckers characters it nice that they have them introduce you into the different systems of the game but it would awesome to hear them communicate with each other more often other then asking us could they do us a favor and deliver a load someone where.
