_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game, and it's not perfect, but i hope the devs are willing to keep adding onto this very solid foundation.I think the biggest hurdle for players to clear is the fairly slow start.  You'll be spending several hours just trucking goods from one system to next closest one, earning peanuts compared  to your regular upkeep expenses, and kinda forces you into deep debt.   The game really doesn't come into it's own until you unlock at least three  of the sectors, thus making actual 'long-haul' jobs viable, and those feel a lot more like traditional truck sims.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I like a lot of games, but this is one that's going to be for the ages. It gives me great vibes, there's clearly a good foundation for amazing things. The atmosphere is gorgeous, the story is engaging, the sounds are *just right*, the controls really feel like you're driving a heavy vehicle. I love the interior of the cab, it makes it feel like you're actually living in there (well, it's a bit barren but that's just details that we might see changed in the future).If I were to change one single thing in the entire game, and I know it's going to be a little controversial, it's the damned battery management system. I know sometimes these mechanics can be fun, but no, I do not enjoy having to buy limited-supply batteries and stow them and swap them in the middle of a run just because game developers have no clue about how power management in actual systems work. It's gamified for the sake of being gamified, with absolutely no logic behind it. These cells are like if I had to swap AA batteries in my radio to make it work, and put some D batteries in a glove box compartment to get A/C in my car. More AA batteries in the break system too, obviously. Oh and imagine if rechargeable batteries weren't invented either, because of course, "recharging" isn't a concept that exists in this awesome space trucking future? This is almost a deal breaker for me, and I'm tempted to just skip the tutorial, and start a new game with low power/consumable drain. In fact I wish there was an option for *no* drain. I have a big generator in the rig - it's called a motor which I recharge using *fuel*. Using more power reduces fuel efficiency, it's that simple.*NEVERTHELESS* I still recommend this game to anyone that enjoys space games, travel games, truck sims and even just good old space exploration games. Just because I'm triggered by dumb battery systems doesn't mean you won't enjoy that challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far a pretty fun game. Relaxing, except at 150 mph drifting sideways to avoid another truck while doing a barrel roll to miss some debris. Gasping for O2 because you were too busy with a cold one in your hand and hammering down to get a load to its destination on time. I must have all your batteries! I have not ran into major issues so far besides self inflicted. Only thing I have to say is silly AI drivers, watch out they will straight run you over.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I love cargo hauling games. Unfortunately Star Trucker needs a bit more spit and polish. Some of the side jobs bug out and can't be completed, and just in time jobs are just not workable right now as the game progresses in real time. Show up half an hour early for a job? Read a book and let the job idle, or hop back and forth between gates and waste money, but a simple time skip would resolve this easily. I'm going to wait for this to get a few patches and see how it looks then.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I brought this game as a joke, as I wanted to drive faster in euro truck sim and a friend suggested this as a joke and wow im in love.Good PointsThe visuals are amazing, warp gates send you to unique, interesting and different environments. The music is perfect! GameplayYou can trade items, run illegal items for trading or transport illegal cargo, you can transport legal cargo (obviously), keep your rig maintained from 02 leaks and component break down, choose between taking the longer safer road ways or risk getting hit by debris fields flying straight to the drop off points. A good balance of risk and reward.Bad PointsI will admit, when I started playing I choose 'Recommend' and the game felt more like a Hardcore survival game rather then a truck sim game, but I restarted and started a custom game with the rewards for jobs turned to High and components drain to low and its a lot more chill now. but the difference from low to medium is pretty insane, especially when the game felt to be very hands off with showing you all the parts of your truck that could go wrong and even when you are recovered they don't fix your rig which confused me at first as it felt like the rig was perfect again, turns out it gives you about 5 to 10 minutes to go to a shop and replace the broken parts, problem is the game doesn't tell you this. so there is a lot of trial and error. So I did have to abandon my first save due to being in so much debt and never being able to work it off, due to the rewards for jobs being so low, also If you fail a job, you have to pay DOUBLE the amount you would have been paid to completing the job which is insane. Also if you did the medical cost £4000 so if you die during a £4000 mission, then you will have to pay £4000 for medical and another £8000 for the contract fail, also if you bust up your rig then you can add another £3000 on top of that (£15000 total). And to try and come back from that while also trying to keep all the components up and running is impossible.Takes till your second play/ or restart to start having fun.RecommendationsIf I could change anything about this game, is to give the player more hand holding at the start of the game, yeah I know there is a manual but when the rig is beeping at you and your screen is going black, the last thing on your mind is to sit in the drivers seat and pull out the manual, I do love the idea of a manual I just never used it.Also the difference between medium component drain to low is insane, When I was first play it felt like every 5mins I had dead Batts or air filters needing changing, In my new run on low setting I have only changed 1 batt in 2 hours of game play which doesnt seem right at all.Maybe make the contract fail fee less, as its crushing enough that you dont get paid.I cant wait for more customisation for the rigs, like bobble heads and hula girls!Long story short, Great game especially now I have found out it was made by 2.5 people. But Medium difficulty is too annoying and hard. While easy is just too easy.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: 4 hrs in, love it so far!!I've been waiting for this game for months and started playing immediately after launch. I loved the concept of truck sim in space from the start, and it's really well executed! The atmosphere and style is beautiful and I'm really enjoying the radio music and chatter with the characters!So far my only issue with the game is the controls, I play on pc and don't mind the default key binds that much (unlike many of the other reviews), but I still wish there were alternatives to control schemes or some kind of drive assist that makes controlling the truck easier. I understand that controlling the truck physics is half of the game, but sometimes it gets a bit frustrating.

Also, we would like the game to be keyboard compatible, as it is sold on Steam, and most PC players use this platform.Cordially, a player who appreciates your game.

_childDocuments_.review: Well life is complete:  I started way back with 18 wheels of steel, then across america, then to my ultamate favorite American Truck Simulator and to complete the life of a PC trucker we all have come full circle with this GEM OF A GAME space the final frontier, I hope the developers keep adding to this like for example: Maybe having an apartment to rest after a long week of driving which you could furnish, maybe the possibility of landing on the big blue planet, converting rockets to wheels just for extra fun! _childDocuments_.review: For a two-person dev team, this is very impressive! Great visuals and atmosphere. The latter might not be for everyone that is expecting elite dangerous levels of solitude while space hauling.Personally I think all there is left to do for the devs is a bit of balancing for the truck maintenance aspect of the game. Add customizable keybinds, and for those eager to fly around with a HOTAS - the support for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker delivers what I wanted in each truck games and space games :- The ability to walk in the truck/space ship and get out of it, in FPS view.- Many systems to manage and which can break.- Neat fuel and energy management.- Fully interactive cockpit and multiple cameras with monitors, allowing to play only in FPS view.I also love the fact that you really place the items in the storage boxes (it's not a window in the UI like most of the games).The docking procedure is also pretty fun in FPS view.My only grip for now is that the game is very hard to play if we remove the hud markers, as there is no detailled map.I would love to see, in a DLC, a more deep trailer management, with the need to manually organise and strap up containers/box on open trailers and with some risks to lose our cargo (could we have a space forklift ? :) )
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I was really struggling if I should leave a positive or a negative review. I went with a positive one because I like the vibe of the game and the concept is really great. I hope the devs will take the negative reviews as feedback and make the game better.Pros:- The atmosphere is lovely. Really feeling the vibe of being a spacehauler- Songs on the radio really fit the trucking genre. Shame it's only 5 (if I am correct)- The interactions through the radio are fun and the missions are fun- Truck design is awesome (only seen the basic truck so if excited what's to come)Cons:- There is just too much micromanagement... I mean I know it's part of the game but even on recommended it becomes more of a chore than being a fun mechanic in this game. Power cells and UCCs run out very fast, making you buy new ones at stations that sometimes only sell 1 while you need 2 (but mostly more) Feels like your doing jobs to keep ur truck running. Which is kinda lame. The fact that this already happens at job 2-3 when you start the game and there's no explanation in a tutorial way is kinda odd.- There's small space debris everywhere. Dodging it can be hard since sometimes it's so small you won't see it and there is no clear path towards your objective so you will find yourself around debris all the time. I've had to fix my truck numerous of times and when the battery or UCC of your suit ran out, you are just done and have to wait until you either find a shop or repair station or just pass out and pay a fee to the repair shop.- It's very hard to tell what is where. The map tells you if there's a certain kind of store/repair/job place but when you are at the spot it's hard to figure out which of the station have those. You have to get close to see what's there which is kind of lame if you have a map. Would be a great help to also have a map of the certain places instead of the big map.- The game is VERY hard to get used to with keyboard and there is no way of remapping keys. I've played Elite Dangerous and that game works very well with mouse and keyboard. Don't know how this feels so clunky and unresponsive.As I said; pretty big cons that will impact gameplay and fun in a negative way but a great concept. Hope the devs will take the feedback and make some changes!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Very weak game so far.1. Controls to drive your truck are pretty annoying2. There is no sector map3. Having to dock the truck to pick up a job or shop is a contrived game mechanic, and it feels stupid. 4. I can understand having to dock to pickup inventory, or a drone can fly it to you. However the real issue is wasting time docking with a shop and it doesn't have a single power cell. This is just idiotic game design.5. There are no radio controls that I can find other than off/on. So 1 station and no volume controls.6. There are insane amounts of space debris everywhere, like right next space stations and roads. This is another contrived game mechanic. I understand the need for some risk/reward mechanics in the game but this is outlandishly stupid, everyone in the sector\town would be dead with that much debris floating around.7. The space highways within a sector are basically pointless, too narrow, since there is no sector map you can't really tell where they go or make use of them. From a design perspective they don't even make any sense. There is no divider for the "lanes".8. From what I can tell so far there are only space trucks flying around. There are no passenger vehicles, apparently only truckers exist in this universe.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty good idea of if you took trucking and mashed it into a space sim. I can't think of a better execution of the idea and I've tried. I've played the regular Trucking simulation games and the biggest part of those in the journey and how to get from A to B, Well in space there's not a whole lot to look at like you would on a highway, but you do see neat areas which function a lot like cities. The A to B is still there with on/off ramps replaced with warp gates, it's all much easier than a typical trucking game, at least I thought that until the next area. Things do get significantly complicated.Truck maintenance is much more important and kind of a chore sometimes. In a regular truck game you can do several jobs without needed tire and engine maintenance, In this game you'll need to be changing batteries for several systems as well as checking on the control circuits for those systems pretty much after every job. Not everything fails at once but one or two need to be replaced. There is an upgrade system which I hope devs expand upon, but all it does now is simple stuff like accel/decel, top speed, shocks, etc.It would be really good to slowly upgrade my truck out of these smaller headaches or trade up for higher end model trucks over time.

_childDocuments_.review: In the current state of mid-september 2024, don't bother.The game is an harrowing experience of terrible user interface and tedious grind. ECONOMY- Income is ridiculously low. Grind.- Upkeep is ridiculously high. Grind more.- Wear & tear consumables cost twice the amount you earn from your average haul. Grind hard.- Upgrades make little difference and cost more with each tier. Opposite that, income hardly ever grows. Grind harder.- The fines work well, compared to the rest. Not a single time will they not trigger when they should. They will even trigger when they should not, because they're fun like that. - If you dare stop grinding you die, btw. And get fined into oblivion.The economy is such a mess, that I have to convert the fines and the grind into hours of gameplay, for clarity.GAMEPLAY- If you hit debris *BONK* you get fined 15 minutes per hit. If you don't hit debris, you swerved to much and damaged your trailers, and get fined about the same.- Driving slow won't make all debris spawn far enough ahead for you to avoid it. Driving slow won't minimize damage; that's a 15-minute fine per hit no matter what. Using headlights won't make it easier to spot.- Plenty of systems to toggle on and off constantly. You can't bind them to any button or key. Use your analog stick to look away  *BONK* from the debris and press action. Whoops, you just hit something while trying to push a button, get fined, 15 minutes.- You'll prefer using your analog stick because keyboard controls are a mess. So forget using you mouse, or get fined constantly. *BONK* See? Told ya.- There are 'just in time' hauls, that require you to deliver within a 1 hour window. You will typically get to the destination system 30minutes to 1 hour before the window opens. So you have to wait it out. IN REAL TIME. You can't fast forward time. Warping out and back into the system will advance ingame time two to three hours, so you will miss the window and get fined 2 HOURS of gameplay. I'm not kidding, the game is litteraly designed to make you wait ONE ENTIRE HOUR of your actual real life time just for an empty loading bay to light up. I mean we could go out into the real world, but we're gamers FFS! We're not supposed to do that and you're not my mom, videogame!- There is cruise control. You need to look away to *BONK* toggle it and to set it *BONK* to the desired *BONK* speed. You should not use cruise control.- You can deactivate stabilizers to save fuel. Cool to travel in a straight line. But if you travel in a straight *BONK* line you *BONK* hit debris and get fined. You should not deactivate stabilizers. Burn all the fuel. Only costs 30 minutes of grind to fill up every 2 hours of grind. Bargain.SALVAGING- You can salvage stuff in the debris fields. Salvage pretty much never spawns outside of scripted missions, and will despawn if you spot it too late.- When you've wasted 3 hours of past grind in wear and tear into looking for salvage that never happens, you'll forget about salvaging.- There supposedly is a salvage scanner that could help. 20 hours of harrowing grind aren't yet enough storyline to get it, though. Grind more.TRADING- You can trade items which you keep in your cabin, for a profit across systems.- If you drop them a couple inches when you put them down they take damage.- You have to find a high surface to put them down, because if you look down at your feet to try and put them on the floor... Well you're still 5 inches high, silly! (Spoiler: crouching would be convienient so it does not exist in that game)- If you hit debris, they fall and take damage.- If your gravity generator fails (with no prior warning, by the way), they float around and take damage.- Thankfully, SOME of them fit in containers that will protect them from hits. Of course some items don't fit into containers and WILL take damage at every opportunity.- The slightest bit of damage will make the item lose enough sell value to forget about any potential profit from the sale.DOCKING- The handling of the rig makes docking a pain initially, but rest assured that once you get the hang of it will still be a bore. No fun allowed here, remember.- You have to dock to your trailers (makes sense), but also to the store or to the job board.- You have to unhook your trailer to go to the job board or store.- The job board and the store are usually in the same place, but you can't get jobs at the store or buy and sell items at the job board. You have to undock from one, then fly 100 feet, do the same haphazrd backing-up dance and dock to the other. I mean they could have made it simpler, but the devs opted to make it more complicated for themselves just to get that little bit of extra pain in there. Such dedication to mediocre gameplay is commendable, I guess.- There is no auto-docking available as an upgrade or gameplay option. It would be a quality of life improvement and that is a sin.BUGS- Now let's be honest here, there aren't that many bugs, the game is indeed terrible, but rest assured it's mostly by design.- NONETHELESS, for however little bugs the devs chose to let slide, they did ensure they were game-breaking, and that, my friends, is what you call dedication.- The game autosaves into a single slot after warps, which are where most of the bugs happen. If you encounter a bug, tough luck, the game just autosaved and you can't reload to fix the issue. No, you can't disable autosave, it would be player-friendly and we don't want that.- You can manual save into 3 dedicated slots, to anticipate for bugs. But don't fret, manual saves come with their own array of game breaking bugs, so you won't be safe from pain there either.Overall, this looked like a chill game, the kind most people would find boring, but in which you would go about progressively earning credit to upgrade your rig and get new features, but the devs managed to instill suffering in every nook and cranny of it.Even the saves won't save you!You have upgrades, you have things to unlock, you have progression. But you cannot be chill about it, every second that flies by means your overpriced consumables get wear and tear, and if you don't complete that job quick, you WILL lose money trying to replace them.And they even added a system that FORCES you to wait for DOZENS OF REAL TIME MINUTES for the gameplay loop to close, all the while watching quietly as your rig wears itself into ruin doing NOTHING.And the icing on the cake is, the actual core of the game seems interesting, the gameplay mechanics would be nice if implemented correctly: the rig maintenance, the salvaging, the trading, the various job types, the story all show good potential...The good game is RIGHT THERE, but the devs mischievously put it just out of reach.I've spent 20 hours trying to get to the point where it gets better, and now I regret I did not get out to take a few walks in the park instead. What the hell is happening to me?This is a masterpiece in cruelty. Honestly, no sane human being can put out that mess and think it is acceptable, this has to be on purpose.

_childDocuments_.review: RECOMMENDED BUT WITH ISSUES!(Reviewed on Launch Day, 2 hours in on Default difficulty)Short & Sweet:Game is good. Not a deep story, but a nice "zen out & play" with some managing of things. However, some things need tuning, some things need fixing & I HIGHLY recommend you pick a custom difficulty & go through things. Read below for more details...I've been waiting on this game for months & am VERY happy that it's come out. Never cared for those American or Euro Truck Simulators, but trucking in space? That caught my interest. So far, I'm loving most of it. However, there are some glaring issues that make it hard for me not to down-vote it. First, I should state that MOST OF THIS INFO IS BASED ON MY FIRST OPINION PLAYING THE RECOMMENDED "DEFAULT" DIFFICULTY SETTING! I have not yet tried the other settings as I believe most players will jump on & just hit "default" difficulty so they can get in & play.Pros:1: No glitching, stuttering, obvious frame drops, screen tearing, etc. Feels well formatted & the game engine tuned in.2: Settings are pretty fleshed out. They even mark the Horizontal & Vertical sensitivity settings as such instead of just using X & Y (I always forget which is which). Same for graphics & other game options. More than I might have thought I'd get for a game this price.3: Controller or Keyboard & Mouse capability.4: The in game "user manual" is simple, easy to read & also easy to find what you're looking for.5: Sound depth. Loud sounds are loud (your truck horn) while the settings let you dial volumes in quite well. I didn't feel like "oh, why isn't there a volume to change this".6: Dashboard from your temperature gauge to the rear camera is clear & easy to see. No text too small & no button or icon still hidden after spending only a minute or two looking around.7: "Story" is simple & follows along well with this slice of space trucker life. Don't expect high octane thrills or a deep story, but there's plenty here to just zen-out on & enjoy.Cons: 1: No keybindings controls. No layout map to show a visual of said controls & no way to change any of them. I don't mind the default control scheme, but I know there are people extremely frustrated with the lack of this.2: Fuel efficiency is pretty bad. By the time you're done with 2 or 3 hauls, you need to fuel up again & it doesn't feel like you've gone very far.3: Power cell efficiency is just horrible. Much like fuel, you burn power cells quite fast & need to replace them all the time. Problem is, a single normal grade power cell costs about as much as completely refilling your trucks fuel tank. And your truck needs multiple of them. Never mind the UCC & the air filters you also need.4: Debris fields everywhere. The game warns you about this, sure, but almost all of the first star systems you can go to have large debris fields. By that I mean you still have debris next to stations, jump gates... pretty much anywhere that isn't directly within the "space lanes"). And I mean DIRECTLY next to. The moment you exit the lane, even if a station or gate is right in front of you, guess what? Debris.5: There's no notification when you've blown out a UCC despite the accompanying power cell still showing charge. Or at least if there was, I couldn't find it. Had no clue my gravity had gone out until stuff flew into my windshield from behind me. Checked the power cell charge on my dash? Still good. Got up & checked the UCC? Supposedly, a piece of debris I had hit approaching a gate (see Con #4) fried the thing upon impact as nothing else had happened to cause it.6: Frozen engines. The game manual will tell you that if the engines are off for too long, they can freeze up. Flip on the choke for the relative engine & you'll burn more fuel, but get it back up to temp faster. Here's the thing. I had issues with this in the demo & wanted to test it. So, I spent an hour (real time) driving with frozen engines & no choke. Yet it was only when it turned on the chokes that the engines finally started heating up. That is way too long in my opinion. It felt more like a frozen engine is hard locked not to heat up unless the chokes are on.7: Cab weight limits are too low. You grab just one or two things more than the game automatically starts you out with & suddenly you're overweight & have to give up stuff upon getting your truck weighed. I didn't think this would be a problem, but apparently its very easy to hit that weight limit. This is troubling because of all the power cells, UCCs, Air Filters & a spare gas tank or two you'd want. Even just carrying around a few UCCs & Power Cells will have you hitting the limit unless you don't mind buying & selling at almost every star system you go through.8: Store & job board. These need to be merged into a set of tabs on a single screen or something similar. There is no reason to have the store & job board at separate docking bays when they are right next to each other in whatever station you visit. Nothing but a waste of fuel & power to undock & then have to redock at the next bay over.Bonus tip! Wanna save a little power? Turn off any lights you don't need (rear cab & mezzanine for starters) when in the middle of a haul. Just remember to turn them back on before getting out of your seat.Concerning the controls. I see some people complaining that the controls are difficult & not just because they can't remap the key-binds. I think it also has to do with how "heavy" the truck feels. Nothing really touches on this in game, but you are in SPACE & driving around a multi-ton vehicle, in SPACE. It is going to feel heavy & it is going to drift. Objects in motion stay in motion & all that. If you speed one direction & turn your truck another, depending on your speed, angle of the turn & any trailers you're hauling, YOU WILL DRIFT a bit before you start going entirely in the new direction you're facing. It's not horrible, but it's something to keep in mind if you want to avoid crashing into things.So, as I've described here, there are some problems despite the rest of the game holding great potential for its type. Once again, all of this is based on playing their "recommended" default difficulty setting, something you can't change at all beyond the initial new game screen. It just feels like a bit too much is piled against you early on. You don't even have the time to get up & look around your truck & get situated because by the time you sit back down, you've been burning fuel & power cell charge & now you're running out. Replacing these things cost money that you're not given very much of & while I haven't yet gotten to the "upgrade your truck" portion of the game to see if any of this can be improved, I wanted to share how much it felt like all this was leaning on you early in. I've up-voted here, yes, but I'd still feel better if the developers could go through & tune at least some of these problems.If you read all this, thanks!

_childDocuments_.review: Gameplay Review: The 'loop' is taking various hauling contracts dictated by your skill tree choices to earn money. Money is spent on part supplies or consumer goods you store in the cabin to make use of the buy low/sell high state of various locations. Example; antidepressants bought low at a store can be placed in your cabin to be sold for a higher price elsewhere and this is separate from your hauling contracts.  During or between hauling power, fuses, and air filters will degrade requiring manual replacement.Personal Thoughts:A lot of fun! The system management has just the right amount of manual and sci-fi technowizardry cheese and there can be some rather hilarious circumstances like realizing too late that your gravity is about to lose power then spending a frantic few moments trying to turn it back on only to then discover that objects in your cabin have durability they lose when they come crashing into each other or the floor when the gravity is restored, lol. To help this you can buy boxes to store a good amount of stuff and protect them.I would almost say it is a cozy game if it wasn't for the sudden difficulty spike for the unprepared and the lazy players who 'brick' their game state by only trying to replace things last minute and find themselves in a location with none of the parts they need. With generous manual save slots and an auto-save every time you jump the only one to blame is really themselves.Note: 43% of people have the achievement for traveling 100 miles in the game. Keep that in mind when you look at the negative reviews. The gameplay video in Steam really does a decent job showcasing things and if you really still aren't sure just watch some gameplay on YouTube. It is a really straight forward like it or hate it decision.

_childDocuments_.review: So far, this game has been extremely fun and interesting. There are some quirks here and there with how things work. _childDocuments_.review: Overall a very fun game. I actually like how you must maintain your truck with replacement parts, but I do fine certain parts annoying. The game play loop and feel of the game is good. The controls are fine and manageable. If you like trucking games, you will enjoy this as long as youre not expecting nothing but driving like ATS/ETS. I have more pros than cons with Star Trucker and I highly recommend it. I just have some suggestions for QOL. - Not having any way to recharge batteries is quite a pain. I feel like I run through them constantly and early game its impossible to afford the better capacity ones. I would very much appreciate having atleast one shop in each sector to swap/recharge batteries if not a truck addition. -There's no map for specific areas. You have the overall map with icons showing you what type of shops are located there, but not their actual location. Spending fuel flying around huge systems with debris everywhere looking for a shop is just frustrating. We should atleast have hud icons for each specific shop. There is several on the HUD already, but it can cover up what you're actually looking for. Maybe even a icon highlighter?-Air filters are insanely expensive early game and you have 4 of them. Even buying them when the price is good is still going to bankrupt you if they all go out at the same time. They do have a decent durability which is good, but I just wish you had two filter slots instead of four.-I can buy large containers of food for a few hundred, but drinks only come in small jugs and 6 packs? Yeah they're cheap, but making 3 or 4 dollars off of them a piece is nothing and I dont have enough space for crates to shove 100 of them into to make anything worth while. Kegs/packs of drinks would be a nice change-Currently the meta to hauling things in secure crates is sticking them on shelves and opening them so they cant fall off (Assuming you have your gravity turned off or the power is just dead). It would be nice to have a strap/rope/gate to hold containers in place.Edit: I just unlocked the Solar area and I have to say, I really dislike it. The idea is really cool, but being forced to shutter my windshield and using a camera that barely even functions during flares is just painful. I just can't see anything and I'm forced to just stop what I'm doing right then and there. Being forced to use the camera is fine, but please make it less glitchy. I get it, its a solar flare. For the sake of gameplay, please :'(

_childDocuments_.review: Okay - normally I wouldn't leave a review this early... but this is so freaking cool lol. Picture American Truck Simulator meets Pacific Drive; that's the feelings. Even if you're a strict simmer this *will* tickle your fancy. Every button can be pressed. Climate controls, cruise control, individual thrusters, individual lights, etc. You can get up and move around your cabin arranging hand cargo and tools, there's a bed, there's *tons* of compartments that house things from air filters to power cells. It's just really, really cool. Then there's the failures, which I've only had a couple so far but that's why I say Pacific Drive, random stuff and inventory management and all that. The one thing I'll come out and say... how is it that there's no control options? I mean... I get it - part of the challenge is frantically looking around your cabin to hit the emergency brakes and stuff. But really wish I had some options at least. Lastly, the game runs great - and actually looks really decent. It's so light to run though, lol. Like I have everything cranked, even 200% scaling and it still won't get me more than 85fps because it's simply not enough work for my 7900xtx. That's not a flex, I'm just saying give me 400% so I can saturate my GPU and get more FPS then I do at 200% resolution.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended difficulty should be easy or costum rather then normal. Normal is still incredibly punishing and hard for "normal"There are no key rebinds, even for a indie thats kinda lame since this is a industry norm on PCThe game uses 30-50% of my GPU and 20% of my CPU. Optimization is lackluster and its leaving huge amounts of performance on the table. I can run most indie games, especially Unity ones at 200-240fps, not below 60fps at times because it doesnt even use my computerThere have also been twice now, where I have jumped into a new star system from a gate and ended up losing all of my monetary savings. One time another truck spawned inside my cargo before I left the area. The other time I spawned inside of a asteroid that was blocking the exit gate. Would be nice if trucks didnt spawn inside me, and if spacerocks didnt float on top of exit gates. This have set me back from slowly progressing, to panicking and constantly going into debt on repairs/maintenance and right now I cant even afford to repair my hull. I`m in a debt spiral due to bugs costing me metric tons of cash in dammages. Not coolIn its current state I can not recommend this game to anyone, even ones interested in a elite dangerous/eurotruck simulator crossover. The game need to fix bugs and glitches, as well as reconsider what "difficulty" is for "normal" players. Constantly stressing and rushing about replacing air filters and batteries due to how insanely quickly they drain and how incredibly little starter missions pay out makes the beginning of the game a rush to level up to unlock higher paying jobs to fight the decay where the game is the hardest at the start and becomes easier over timePoorly balanced, frustratingly buggy, lack of industry standard optionsI like this game, and I will give it some more time to grow on me because I really enjoy it. But this is a mess. Feels more like a early access game then some early access games

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful mixture of part No Mans Sky and Euro Truck Simulator 2, both of my favorite games. So far, i am enjoying this game and would recommend this to the people who are space game lovers, though I have my fair share of Feedbacks. What I love about this game:1. Good implementation of space environment with truck hauling simulation.2. Graphics are awesome, as expected and better for an indie game.3. Good country music and radio implementation that they have integrated along with ambient music.4. simplistic controls and not steep learning curve as of now.5. Space game (which is always a plus).What can be improved:1. Multiple save slots instead of 3 save slots present at the moment (which is very stressful if i want to fall back to a particular checkpoint while cargo job.)2. Though the variety of cargo jobs are good, they can add a little more categories to the cargo job types and also add variety in the same category of cargo jobs (example - all oversized cargo jobs needn't need to be same point A - point B, just a little variety)3. More list of music as the existing one gets repetitive pretty.4. Game is not optimized at all. More optimization is needed. For GTX 1060, it shouldn't be running in 30-45 fps at medium settings.5. More bigger map area along with more things to do in the selected sector (individual sectors feel small and a tiny bit empty IMO).6. More quests and a longer storyline if possible.7. If any little bit of community interaction is possible like in No Mans Sky.will edit the review as and when the game expands in future.

_childDocuments_.review: Very satisfying trucking simulator set in space. I enjoyed the story, and the gameplay can be tweaked depending on how hard you want the game to be. I like the cartoon art style, those are always cool to see. The space backgrounds are beautiful and breathtaking, I really like them.This is one of those games that I can relax to. The only things I think are missing is multiplayer and maybe VR (I heard VR is one of the things the two-man team is looking into, so that's cool), but I am satisfied and appreciate what Star Trucker already has to offer.I think this game should win the Game of the Year award and Best Art Style awards because of how well its unique take on truck simulators and cartoon-ish art style work.This game is more of a trucking simulator than a space simulator, so keep that in mind when buying it. But if that's something you think you'll enjoy, then go for it!

_childDocuments_.review: === EDIT ===Several patches in a the devs still haven't added custom keybind support, leaving the game literally unplayable for many people, especially left handed. The devs only hours after release promised that adding custom keybind support was their #1 priority... Clearly not, almost two months in.===========Fun time spender with some issues that gives it a thumbs down for me. First of all, I love space games, I'm a long time Star Citizen player, so this tickles what it does very well, which of course is cargo running. What really annoys me is the controls. This game needs options to reconfigure keybindings ASAP, as in, it should be in the next patch. The current keybindings are horrible and there is no strafe option, in space with thrusters. Also no mouse steering option with a button for free look.Next thing I noticed actually just made me Alt-F4. You can get fined for crashing into other vehicles, this is fine. I got fined over $1000 because some vehicles follow a very strict path and will not move away from it. I was barely moving forward and due to the lack of strafing I couldn’t get out of the way of a small yellow service vehicle. It crashed into me, not the other way around, and because of its strict pathing it got stuck in me, because it got stuck in me the game would consider this as an ongoing violation and fine me with $100 every 10 seconds. I had to start spinning to get the vehicle back on its pathing and stop driving into me.At least add keybinding options and strafing into the game and this will be a thumbs up.

_childDocuments_.review: There is the potential for a great game here. It has beautiful visuals, a great atmosphere and an engaging gameplay loop, but in it's current state I can't recommend this game for anyone but the most dedicated of resource management aficionados.The numerous flaws and possible fixes have been explored in detail in other reviews, but I will mention my two major gripes.1: Poorly balanced resource usage. The "recommended" setting is far too punishing, especially when it comes to power usage. Add that to the baffling scarcity and expense of power cells and other necessities it becomes an annoyance very quickly. There is a custom game option that can alleviate the issue to some extent, but in my view it needs a complete overhaul.2: Diverging control schemes and a lack of custom key bindings. The latter the devs have pledged to fix, but why the space suit has an unintuitive control scheme (at least when using a controller) that wildly differs from the truck to begin with is a bit of a strange one.Bonus: Only 3 save files? Why? For now the lack of polish on these fronts will make me put the game on a shelf for the time being, and come back to it at a later date when hopefully these and other issues have been smoothed out by the devs.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I love the concept of the game, but it was incredibly frustrating to run into resource depletion at a rate that maintained a level of stress that drained the fun for me. I like the idea of keeping my truck maintained, and I don't mind having to check my energy levels, etc. However, the cost of a single filter required 2-3 loads. While you are trying to finish these jobs I ended up suffocating halfway through one. It is not enjoyable nor have I found a way to get the funds ahead of time. I've uninstalled the game, as every time I got the urge to play I found myself in a loop of death just trying to get enough funds to buy a single resource, I applied for a refund but was unsuccessful. If you are the fence, just stay away for now. Read up on others experiences of resource management, and if you feel up for the challenge go ahead, I think there is a lot to enjoy. I was simply left with a sense of regret for my purchase.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I've refunded after realizing it was included with GamePass. I have about 2 hours in it. It's very obvious the game was developed with controller players in mind because it's FAR better. Controls are smooth and intuitive, where as keyboard controls were made by people who have never played a PC game.Star Trucker has the potential to be a REALLY great game, hitting the niche of people that have always wanted to be a space trucker. That being said, there are some glaring issues I've noticed 20 minutes in.Likes:1. Unique art design.2. Fun truck physics.3. Pretty seamless intro/tutorial.4. Inventory management is fun. Organizing your gear into the back of your rig, having it get thrown around in a crash or float around if your gravity generator dies.Dislikes:1. No keybind editing?! Who makes Shift to brake and Space to accelerate? (developers are working on this now).2. No proper IR tracking support.3. No HOTAS support?!4. FOV slider does not go high enough. (There IS a FOV slider but it simply doesn't allow us to go wide enough).5. "Tech tree"/Certifications seems pretty basic. Other than getting better jobs, the ability to pull more trailers at once, nothing too exciting in the tree.6. Lack of animations that affect immersion. Example, when repairing your hull, your character should pull out some kind of blow torch.Another thing that blows my mind. You can't recharge your power cells?! We live in a universe where we can warp through space but we can't recharge batteries? Give us more to spend money on. Truck upgrades, new trucks, more cosmetics, etc rather than implementing a pointless annoying game mechanic to slow the gameplay loop.Just another example where they need to be taking inspiration from ETS/ATS. We need a career mode where we are trying to start, run and expand a trucking company. Gives us something to spend money on and significantly lengthens the gameplay loop.Long term this game would do extremely well if they implemented multiplayer similar to TruckersMP for ATS and ETS , private servers and the ability to talk to other driver's via the CB radio and full modding support. The biggest issue is that there are only 2 developers working on this game. This can be a thing fantastic due to attention of detail and love for the game but also be it's downfall if they burnout or do not have the technical skills to handle big implementations such as multiplayer.Will update as I continue playing.

_childDocuments_.review: Is it an out-of-the-box superhit? Not quite.Does it still need some work? E.g. in regards to keybindings and maybe a bit of difficulty adjustment? YesHowever, starting a custom game and pushing the energy usage to a lower level made the game really enjoyable. Check after a trip whether your batteries are fine, replace them, sell them, buy them, trade goods, salvage... it's fun.My wishlist for changes:- Keybindings (e.g. to change the speed on cruise control)- A scanner (if it doesn't already exist) to mark debris in front of the vehicle- More music variety or ability to add a stream/custom music- AI that avoids running into you just a bit moreStar Trucker is a good game at this time, but I think it could be a fantastic game. Give it time!

_childDocuments_.review: I want to love it, so badly I want to love it.Rebinding keys is an insane thing to leave out of a game, I'm sure there's some technical reason it had to dodo, but the fact that I can't tell you why specifically makes it harder for me to understand - keybinding is standard. Not just from a quality of life standpoint, but general accessibility as a whole. The game-play loop is exactly what you expect, but some of the limitations (might be progression based so if this prickles your hair do some research) like only being able to haul one job at a time and not being able to "wait" or "sleep" to pass time makes some of the "arrive between" jobs downright BORING. The aesthetic of the truck is cool, but not worth the sacrifice of practicality. If there were any alternative system for avoiding debris (currently your choices are "squint" and "pray"), it would be closer to understandable. Having the choice of any other shape of vehicle would go such a long way, but this game is devoid of customization beyond colors and patterns. You get to choose how you level, as well as how you upgrade your truck, but to my knowledge none of that will keep rocks out of your radiator.Finally; once you're in debt, ya better break out the baby oil and start haulin' loads, cause delivering cargo ain't gonna get you back in the black ANY time soon.

_childDocuments_.review: I've only been following this game for a couple of days, so I went into this game blind and without any hype built up.I really like the setting and the visual style. The atmosphere is also great and the vistas so far are also nice.I don't understand why other reviews get so upset about keybinds, as to me that is not an issue at all. The game is playable with controller just fine, and I suppose it was made with a controller in mind.The quest board and the various services do feel like ETS2, but of course it is impossible to create the feeling of traveling just like in ETS2 since one game takes place on earth and the other in space. So I don't understand those comparisons.. I so far quite like the game in and of itself.However, there are five key points I would like to see changed/that bother me:1. Unclear "road" beginnings/coursesWhen selecting a destination, you will get a marker for the jump gate needed to get to the next system en route. However, driving there directly ruins the immersion and is discouraged by debris fields. Sadly, though, it is not very clear where the road you are meant to take towards the jump gate is located or how you would get there from your current location.On the other side, occasionally when you leave a jump gate it is not clearly communicated which road you are meant to take to your destination point. So I ended up just driving straight there, which was not very fun imo as it is akin to just driving through fields on earth.2. Unrechargeable Fuel CellsIdk if it is simply not documented in the user guide book, but it seems like fuel cells are non rechargeable, which makes little sense to me. Batteries have been recharageable irl for decades and yet I am meant to sell empty fuel cells and buy new ones at great expense? Maybe I missed something, but it seems like the fuel cells are non rechargeable. Even if they are, it should be communicated more clearly where I can recharge.3. No vertical/lateral thrustEssentially, you are flying a space truck that can yaw left and right, thrust forward and backward and can tilt up and down. You can also roll, but that is not helping the thrust. Since you are very limited with your movements and docking is a very precise endeavour, it is frustrating to reverse your truck into the docking port. It would have been ten times more enjoyable if there was a way to thrust up and down and left and right directly instead of awkwardly pointing your truck upwards and then thrusting, then pointing it downwards again. There is a reason games like Elite Dangerous allow for thrust in all six directions as manoveuring around in space becomes super frustrating without it, even more so when you need to move precisely such as when coupling to trailers or when docking. It even makes following the roads unenjoyable, since you will often drift from left to right and up and down.Maybe you can upgrade your truck with additional thrusters? Idk. Let me know in the comments :-)4. Not being able to set waypoints within a system from the mapI would really have liked to be able to set a waypoint from the map to a specific shop in a system. As far as I can tell, that is not possible and you are left guessing where to go. Exploring a system does seem enticing in general, but due to the sluggish behaviour of a truck it is not really. I don't think I would like to drive a real life semi around for joy rides as an analogy.5. Small systemsI do have to agree with at least one review that mentioned that the systems feel rather small. So do the distances you travel. My fully fueled starter truck has a range of 93km? What? It makes sense in that you really only "travel" from jump gate to jump gate and those distances are rather small, but this game would have greatly benefitted from a "Wild West" feeling, where there are great distances between stations and jumpgates. Sure it can be tedious to some, but you are making a game for the crowd that enjoys ATS, ETS2 and space trucking in Elite Dangerous! Honestly when I saw that a mission was gonna take 2.5h I thought to myself: Alright! And in real time it took maybe 15 mins. I am the kind of person who will drive 1k kilometer routes in ETS2 because the sense of travel feels great!In this game you are like a delivery person within an industrial complex, you take stuff from a shelf in warehouse A, then take a car (travel gate) to warehouse B and then put it on a shelf there. The sense of distance is miniscule, which in my opinion really is what the whole point of this game should have been.Conclusion:All in all the setting is really enjoyable and I have only gotten started so far. There are very few good looking 3D space games out there and so this becomes a good game to me by merit of that and the premise of space trucking alone. It's like a fetish to me. Therefore I would recommend this game for now, however I am still on the fence. While writing this review the weight of the points I made really hit me. Again, a mixed review score would be great, but alas, I will for now give a thumbs up since I think I am going to play some more later today.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first: This is *not* a trucking sim, it is a survivalist game wearing the skinsuit of one. You're not so much truckin' the spacelanes, you are forever scrambling to keep health bars up.This is for you if you ever thought: 'These Valheims and Ark Survivals are pretty good, I guess. But how much better could they be if there would be more bars ticking down? I mean, a lot more. And if some are obfusticated, that would just be the cherry on top.'Never fear, Star Trucker is here and has all your needs covered. And it even has health bars within health bars. We're entering inception levels of territory here.Here's a breakdown of the health bars when starting out (There'll be even more later in the game to look forward to):2 Core Systems Batteries, one bar each.2 Mag Batteries, one bar each.1 Bar of Oxygen to maintain, for which you have to keep 1 Battery for on board gravity. 1 Control Unit for onboard gravity.1 Bar for your space suit, with the subcategories of:1 Fuel gauge.1 Truck Hull integrity bar.You are looking at 9-18 health bars. If that isn't some kind of record in the genre, it should be. How do these all fit on the UI? They don't, you spend a lot of time panning the camera over the dashboard to check on them. A hassle? Maybe, but this way you get to keep up with the various system alerts which are also not visible otherwise if you would only look out the windows to, you know, drive your truck, dodging traffic and space junk.On a side note, the status of the various control units isn't even shown there, you have to leave the driver's seat to go over to the relevant panel to check their status.While the individual bars take a while to whittle down, the sheer number ensures that you'll be replacing and buying parts constantly. - Don't play a drinking game where you have a shot every time a part needs to be replaced, you'll get alcohol poisoning within the hour.Another thing is, you should really, really like the docking maneuver ingame. You'll be docking to hitch your trailer, to check the the shops (1 docking maneuver for each), and the job board (another docking maneuver - yes the shops and the board are in different places). If you are of the mindset of 'Yep, this will never get old.', that'll help.We could go into the nitty gritty of the lack of key bindings, how picking an upgrade on the skilltree can screw you, the inability to change game options midgame, why there isn't one battery for all systems, etc.But really what it all boils down to is the question wherever being bullied to juggle all these bars and timers is the kind of gameplay loop you are looking for. Because that's what it is at the end of the day.This is not the zen-like relaxing experience of ETS/ATS, this is wheelspinning(tm) the game. If you are fine with that, have a go. For everyone else: Avoid.(edited for text formatting, spelling)

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE: Known bug exists where you cannot progress the story line. Im fully upgraded and leveled up and cant finish the game. Cool. Was this even play tested? TLDR; Set the custom difficulty and enjoy some space truckin'. Its great.Worth the price but a couple considerations;The recommended difficulty setting is not a chill 'ATS/ETS vibe' it is a hardcore survival mode with permadeath enabled. Unless you fly perfectly with no damage and no fines, failures compound until you will be broke with no life support and permanently softlocked. You need to be completing paid cargo jobs just to keep your head above water on truck maintinence which leaves no room for the storyline missions as they dont pay or give you XP. If you're a veteran ETS/ATS player looking for a similar experience, set all the custom difficulty settings to as 'easy' as possible. It seems excessive but provides a more consistent experience. There is definitely room for multiple playthroughs and scaling the difficulty to your taste. The gameplay itself is great. Maneuvering/docking is rewarding when you get a hang of it and I agree with the decision to omit translation thrusters as it makes your truck maneuver more like..well, a truck. Its like ATS/ETS with a Z-Axis. Storyline/Progression/Upgrades are pretty stock but familiar and thats not a bad thing. The transition from driving to EVA and back is very smooth, and jumping around systems while completing jobs feels very organic. No perceptible loading screens.

_childDocuments_.review: this game really rocks. it's so much more intense and involved than i figured it would be. i can see myself spending tons of time in star truckera few notes, including two major gameplay issues that i hope can be patched and/or fixed:1. the biggest problem imo: the lack of vertical/lateral thrust. it would make things so much less of a pain if you could just scooch up or down if you need to, especially for docking but also for avoiding debris. the controller configuration could let you do it either with the d-pad, or the d-pad with a "shift" button (say, hold down LB and use dpad to thrust). the only two things the dpad currently does, zooming and external camera, could easily be moved to the left and right stick buttons or the shoulder buttons. (side note, i would also love to have the cruise control mapped to a shoulder button or Y/Triangle, like the cruise control buttons on the steering wheel of your car you already have your hands on)2. power cells deplete WAY too fast. it is such a hassle to constantly be swapping out and selling old cells, and constantly losing a lot of money buying new cells. if the game let you try the different difficulty modes on the same save i'd be happy to do that, but it doesn't, and at this point i don't want to start a whole new game just for the chance that power drain would be a bit lessened. if there is a way to either recharge power cells (yes please) or make your electricity use more efficient with upgrades, i have not yet found it. 2A: the game is set in (at least close to) real-time except for when you use jump gates, so they really wanted us to literally have to change the power cells more than one time every single day?2B: now that i'm thinking about it, it doesn't make sense that the gasoline doesn't recharge the power cells like it would keep a car battery charged. i understand it's a game mechanic, but are big rig truckers having to pull out batteries for individual components for their rig and replacing them on the regular? like more than once a day?3. the solar flare mechanic absolutely rules. i figured the separate temp/fan a/c controls were just a cute little thing, but no, they are very very important! i cant wait to see electrical storms and whatever "anomalies" are!4. I can't place items down on the floor without damaging them. People are saying to just use the crates, but that takes longer to do than just putting an old power cell on the floor while i'm changing it. Give me a crouch button, or make the fall damage on items trigger a little bit further away!i'm nitpicking because i really REALLY like this game and am going to spend tons of time in it. it's so kinetic and detailed, and the lever you have to push to jump to new systems feels very great every time. the ability the game has to simulate this seamless world where you can get out of your ship with no loading screens (even when jumping between systems) to pick stuff up and repair your ship must be a technical marvel considering how many space games can't figure that part out. starfield, eat your heart out - star trucker did it right!!!edit: the radio station! the effort that went into making this radio station including advertisements and station ID clips and (what i'm assuming are) original songs!!! incredible!!! my friend and i created an 8 hour long "space trucker" playlist for when we would haul stuff in elite dangerous, and it's a fantastic fit here too.

_childDocuments_.review: I had so much fun playing this game! Although I imagine some people might find the general concept of space trucks to be unimaginative or tacky, I think it's actually an interesting concept to build a game around. The world is very beautiful and colorful. Makes you fell like you really are in space, and has a very calming effect on me personally. The steering and moving capabilities of the truck makes me feel like I'm truly flying a heavy beast of a truck!The fact that the game allows you to customize the difficulty level is a huge plus, and I favour this over pre-configured difficulty levels. I would love to see additional customization options in the future for that.The controls in the truck's cockpit are easy to understand, and I especially love that the devs didn't add hundreds of buttons/dials which would personally overwhelm me. Although I would again love to see a few more buttons added in the future for different functionalities. In addition to that, it would be nice to control systems like gravity, climate regulator, etc directly from the cockpit, as opposed to having to leave your seat all the time, walk over to the back of the truck to toggle these systems on or off.I would like to see more customization options for the truck. For example headlights, roof, shapes of thrusters and colors, exterior logos, the ability to change how the engine sounds, and of course interior designs.Overall this game got me pretty hooked and I would definitely recommend!

_childDocuments_.review: The feeling of managing and keeping your flakey rust-bucket of a ship flying is fantastic, if that's your kinda thing. Razor-thin margins and a gravity generator that drinks energy like soup keeps your wallet twitching and your buttocks clenched. Where one solid collision is enough to spiral you into the abyss, and a ship handles like a drunk Italian bistro, this is certainly not a game for everyone.But I bloody love it. Some early tips I wish I'd known at the start - - Explore your ship before you even start the engine, and when you can - read the manual in the glove compartment. Make a note of where everything is, what it does, and what parts it uses so that when things (inevitably) go wrong, you at least know where to look.- Highways seem optional, but they mark safe paths with no debris/junk floating around. Use them whenever possible (unless you feel reckless, or are in a really big hurry - trust me though, debris fields are deadly). If there's no highways, watch/follow the other rigs - they tend to follow fairly safe paths. - Batteries are expensive, but pay attention to the capacity - 100 cap batteries aren't too bad (around 400-500 credits). The more expensive ones are bigger, 150 and 200. Also, ALWAYS turn off your cab interior lights when driving - this saves so much energy! The gravity generator is the biggest drain, so give it the big batteries if possible to save frequent stops.- The storage boxes you have in your sleeping area are ESSENTIAL. Open them, and store your batteries, UCCs (little computer things used alongside batteries in your systems) and filters in there, as they will keep them from being damaged from accidents. The boxes hold several items each, so fill them up to keep your expensive spares safe.Fly safe! :D

_childDocuments_.review: I’m absolutely in love with this game. It’s so fun, unique in a way that it combines two of my favorite settings: trucking and space! Everybody has played ATS and ETS2, so just imagine those games but in space with the ability to leave your truck to make repairs. Pretty simple in concept and nearly a perfect execution of itStrafe controls for the truck would be nice, it would certainly make backing up to connect to a trailer or dock much easier, but are they necessary? No, not really. Not having the ability to strafe vertically or horizontally does not make the game unplayable by any stretch, it does make it a bit harder compared to a regular truck sim. Also would be nice if they included an internet radio and/or letting you add your own music to the game. But other than those two points this game gets a solid 8/10 from me. I can’t recommend it enough if you want to be a space truckerSteam Deck: the game runs okay on with 15W TDP. If you play on any setting above Low then expect frequent dips below 30 fps, that’s also with me running the game at 1152x720 and using FSR to upscale.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. The radio and the CB create a great atmosphere. I love maintaining the truck by changing batteries and patching hull breaches after I've crashed. Intra-system navigation can be confusing because jump gates get pinned, not the highway to get to it, but travelling is fun. There is traffic, but unlike terrestrial truck sims, getting stuck in it is a choice. You're in the endless void of space, after all. Flight is semi-realistic with some kind of flight assist on top of a newtonian model. That means you have to slow down for turns or over-turn your rig to drift it around corners. Be warned, though, drifting a tandem may get spicy.Make sure you're always carrying spare batteries and filters. Needing one of these and not having it could get you stranded or dead, and not every system has everything you need for sale. Important systems like the drive core and mag-lock use two batteries for redundancy. You can hotswap new batteries in as an old one expires. Unimportant systems like the suit charger, the gravity, and the very OXYGEN you breathe have no redundancy. You'll want to keep an eye on these and swap them while you're docked. You can change them as you like, but reorganizing your spares after replacing the grav-batt gets old. Worse, letting it die in transit will have your spares shifting around the cabin in accordance with your driving. Big stop? All your stuff now lives on the windshield.This is a great game to sit back and veg out with while singing along to the radio. "Cross my heart and hope to die. Oh forgive me, know I tried..."
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: chill game with some story on the side, so yes, its a nice game. I just finished the story and it took me 45 hours in total (I had already spent quite a bit on the story quest) and for €25 it's perfectly fine. However, the developers should urgently do something about the end of the story. The menu and conversations say something big is coming, but unfortunately not much happens. That was very disappointing. The only thing that really annoyed me was: you press the spacebar to accelerate, but if you look at the map, you can also press the spacebar to set a waypoint, which means that if you close the menu and then want to accelerate straight away, you set a waypoint that you don't want to set. This has happened to me dozens of times, which means you follow the waypoint and then think you're there.... but what happens is you follow the waypoint you didn't want to set and then realize “ohh I'm suddenly 3 systems further away than before” This annoyed me sooo much until I figured out how this happens. Please fix thanks7/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is set in 3-D space, but only has 2-D controls. There are no translation controls at all so "driving" and docking in this came is impossible. The camera views are super clunky and it's pointless to use the exterior cameras because you will be constantly hitting space debris or other vehicles you didn't see. Also, if you want to sit in the cab and use the monitors, they are this ugly green color for the camera views. I get it for the status screens, but why would you want to make a beautiful game look so ugly. Also what are the point of the "roads" if the other trucks don't use them or if you are mandated to go off-road at times. Lastly the normal mode is more hardcore survival. You will be constantly replacing batteries, filters, and UCCs. The jobs don't even come close to making up for it and you will constantly feel like you are in the hole. Why in the world do the I need to get gas and also get batteries for systems I feel like should be charged by the engine when I'm driving. Lastly for the love of god, please change the gravity mechanic. Even if I am completely stopped to change the battery before it goes dead, all my stuff goes floating off anyways. I never encountered any bugs, but this game feels like an early access title that slapped a 1.0 release on it to make money. It's missing too many features like keybinds, Give this game a wait. There is soooo much potential, but the game in it's current state falls flat.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a review from about 10 hours in  - I absolutely love it and I'm addicted.The star systems look incredible and once you get used to the controls it drives so so smoothly. Hauling is fun, the characters are fantastic. I love that they even made ads for Gold Rock Radio, and even made up artists! The world building is great.However. One thing I've personally been bashing my head against is the lack of - and overpricing of essential items you need to survive. UCC's and the air filters are the biggest offenders of these. Air filters will cost you like 2,5k while jobs barely give you that amount to begin with (they start off at 1-2k per trip). Not to mention that shops will carry 1 or 2 of these items, so finding batteries/air filters/UCC's and keeping up with them is... stress inducing sometimes. On top of that the game later introduces shock absorbers. Those barely last, are really expensive, and there are so few of them around you're best off just flying around the thunderstorms if you can.It's REALLY easy to get into debt, and then stay there. It's also REALLY easy to ding up your truck, and after a small grace period of it being free, fixing it costs a set price of  dollars. Doesn't matter how small the damage is. In my humble opinion there should definitely be a change to that. Maybe degrees? Calculations? 3k is really way too steep.Some minor things(for me):Game is ridiculously fun and the worldbuilding is incredible, despite items necessary for survival being overpriced and super scarce - this all in . For now I recommend using custom difficulty to suit the game to your liking!

_childDocuments_.review: Great game but also some missed opportunities but considering the small sized dev team, these are probably not "missed opportunities" but rather conscious decisions against features they probably would have liked to implement. I am excited to see where they take the game but for now it feels only 90% finished. There are some tiresome mechanics in the game related to fixing up your truck but I also chose the "recommended" setting in the beginning and I do believe you can change the balance between constantly having to fix up your truck and taking long trips so maybe that fixes that issue.Maybe I was just being inefficient with my hauls but making money also seemed pretty rough for the first playthrough, I found myself constantly going into debt because I needed more power cells and power cells are freaking expensive for something that seems to be a basic need in this game.The skill tree not having any cool features to look forward to when leveling up also feels a bit underwhelming. 95% of the skill tree only unlocks new hauling jobs, which is not something that belongs into a skill tree and should just unlock automatically in the background while progressing the story(imo). Another annoyance (to me), is not being able to pick up multiple things when picking up salvage. Having to go in and out of your truck for each salvage piece becomes really tiresome(something that could be fixed with a perk in the skill tree. Maybe one perk could be an item magnet or a backpack, that allows picking up multiple items when collecting salvage).All in all the progression in the game needs more exciting stuff to look forward to or maybe there already is but you just can't see it at the start.Unfortunately Steam only allows for either thumbs up or down as a rating(instead of a more nuanced star system) but giving this game a thumbs down would be a disservice to the devs, so I'll give it a thumbs up for now.Hopefully some good stuff to come but the game is already in a decently enjoyable state.Personally, I might hold off on playing for now, see where the development goes and pick it back up in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Real truck driver approved :) I played a bit before my shift and im having fun with it so far. To address previous reviews regarding the keybind issue: According to the discord they plan on implementing it later on. The controls as-is are not unplayable, and work just fine on an xbox controller.I love the artwork, the setting, the music, and the semi-realism of the controls. The game is a perfect balance of realistic enough to be sim-like and arcadey enough to be casually enjoyed. Im an OTR driver and ATS was too much like my job for me to play it casually without taking it seriously lol. I played the demo for this game a while back and it was a bit rocky, but the game seems to be running smoothly now with no issues. Thank you M&M for providing a worthwhile experience. Please continue to support the game long term. :)EDIT: After playing for a few hours, I’m genuinely not understanding the issue everybody is having with managing the systems. I haven’t run out of anything yet in standard mode and swap a couple of batteries out every few trips. Some tips:-Swap gravity and oxygen batteries when docked. The dock keeps these systems stable for you while you swap out.-Hold onto batteries over 10% to use in your suit slot. The suit slot uses very little charge.-Cut your breakers when changing UCCs-Only fuel as much as you need to and keep your jug full.-Don’t drive recklessly. You lose a lot of money by doing so. Only do it to avoid late deliveries if needed.-UPGRADES PEOPLE. Upgrade your truck ya’ll. You’ll be going through maintenance a lot slower.Otherwise here’s a few things I think should be addressed gameplay wise: -The job board/store only being accessible by the airlock is a bit annoying and it took me a minute to figure out how to get back to the menu after closing it. Id implement a button or screen on the dash or even just a keybind to reopen the menu.-The lack of strafing is definitely a bit of a gripe. If the devs decide to implement it I strongly recommend the way ED does it. Provide it as a toggle switch on the right stick on controller. -I may be missing a container somewhere but an upgrade for shelf tie-downs would be nice. Ive started just leaving everything on the floor lol.

_childDocuments_.review: It's out?! Oh come on!So I did a quick hour or so in this game and I will just start off by saying that I love it. That's the TLDR.If you do want to read my one hour play review, here goes.I love Euro Truck Simulator but the thing that breaks it for me is the fact that we're driving through Europe. In short we're driving through familiar territory but the game can't be too detailed so I couldn't, for example, drive my truck through my street. This game takes away that one small problem, by giving me a gorgeous galaxy to gape at, and gives me a dozen new problems to think about. For example, why am I freezing to death?!The idea that this cab is a spaceship is very well executed and I simply adore the problems which you can run into. Your power isn't one big battery supplying everything, there are small batteries for all manner of systems. So what do I run out of first? Artificial gravity. While I was flying at speed. With my shelves full. I had to spend a good fifteen minutes cleaning up everything that had been flung through my cab, meaning I missed the delivery deadline.See that doesn't happen on Earth and a normal wheeled truck!There are 4 standard difficulties and a fifth which gives you the option to fine tune anything you want. It's a nice addition to those who want to go off into the distance or want a lawless, or fineless, galaxy. The soundtrack I had thought would grate on me, not my usual style, but it's actually really nice to listen to and fits with the aesthetic. First thing I do is turn on the radio every time. I am looking forward to more commercials too; they are nicely weird which is perfect for the 'space is huge so there's probably somewhere we can make something sketchy' mindset of businesses. There is an RP element for me personally, just the under the breath grumblings when I'm carrying stuff, that make it more fun for me. Yes, I'm weird, don't judge me.The downsides? And please keep in mind this is after 1 hour of play so who knows if this comes up later.However, like I said, I enjoy adding an RP element to these kinds of games but the game itself doesn't lend itself well to that. The cab has a bed, you can't sleep in it. There are food, drink and even cleaning consumables but they don't appear to have a 'use' function. If this is something which happens later in the game, or an option I have to turn on, I'll amend that here. If it's not in the game, I sorely hope they do add it in. I'd also like to see a custom music option. Again, I love the soundtrack, wouldn't have bought the DLC if I didn't, but I enjoy putting on an audiobook and playing these kinds of 'work' games and it'd be nice to have that be a function in game rather than what I open on a second screen.Seriously, to anyone out there, buy the game now or later; it's a good price for a good game with its own weird aesthetic and we need more of them. _childDocuments_.review: The premise is a novel one, and it is a space-sim. However, not much has changed from the demo version, and there are a handful of kinks that still need improving. Some QoL features that are still missing, and some mechanics that still need some more thought are still there. The simulation, however, is quite good. The lumbering hulk you pilot is quite nice, and all the features (from cab light, to CB radio) gives it a cozy feeling.Anyway, still needs some ironing out. I would've released this as an Early Access title to get some players' feedback before going gold. Might change the review after the devs take a look at the feedback and change some stuff.EDIT.: Let me expand my review. I would say Elite Dangerous' long trips feel more like "ETS/ATS in space" than Star Trucker*. In Star Trucker you don't get to travel using cruise control for long streches of vistas like ETS/ATS. It's a , instead. It seems the focus of the game is to micromanage your trucks' systems while delivering stuff.Some of the management features seem like they were made intentionally harsh otherwise the game would feel too "slow". Batteries drain fast, they can't be recharged, and the systems' highways are more of a suggestion rather than a layout one would expect from humans in the 31st century.* - I was gonna say Freelancer, but I don't know how many people know of that game, and FL has fighting/piracy included, so that is a bit too different for a good comparison.
