_childDocuments_.review: So I played for about 7 hours. So far I see that on the recommended difficulty there are some problems that need to be addressed by the devs before I give this a thumbs up. And just on a side note, I was really hyped up for this game. But as it stands, it is more a battery-swapping sim than hauling. Store and mission board in separate locations, come on really? And super low payouts, I mean how am I supposed to fix, refuel, buy batteries and filters and whatnot for my rig when I make 2k on a haul? Either you drive super safe or you run out of money, following this logic taking the left skill tree is impossible since doing anything risky ends up at the body shop with you taking a loan to fix the truck. And somehow there are 15 tracks on the radio but I feel like I listen to the same 4 for hours, I mean it's a game about hauling stuff in a truck and not getting out of it, this should have been a major priority, so the feel is right. I swear to the gods if the devs take the same route with this as the guys from Voidtrain. I'm hoping for a patch and some more content that makes this more of a real game, now I just feel like playing a demo.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm confused as to why this isn't labelled as Early Access.Bugs I have encountered so far:- NPC Drivers will ram into you standing still even on the side of the road- NPC Drivers don't merge properly, you essentially have to hit the emergency brake and dodge.- Switching between younger save slots removes the ability to save altogether unless you are on your Autosave slot- Death by low Oxygen - Debt Spiral caused by overpriced Air Filters (3-4K) in a game where your agreed overdraft is 2.5K.Meaning you have to constantly maintain the Truck while also repaying your debt with lower triple digit amounts and if you die you have to pay another 2K with a possible Breach of Contract fine (3-4K).- Warping in a younger save slot sometimes malfunctions and you get stuck permanently in one area, unable to use any Warp Gates- I. e. once you get stuck in debt on your Autosave slot, the best thing you can do is delete the save entirely and start a new one.

_childDocuments_.review: First, I'd recco creating a "Custom" game and setting all consumable stuff to the minimum. Makes things a lot easier until they adjust things later. This game chills me out. Get a trailer, jump to another system, navigate some hazards and get to the drop-off for some sweet credits.Things I've noticed - just running two air filters seems to work fine under the "Custom" setting I mentioned. When one dips under a threshold and your air production can't keep up, just swap out the lesser one. The "Climate Control" panel is what controls the battery/control unit for Oxy.Try to swap out batteries around the same time if you can. Makes balancing it all a bit easier. Having your gravity compensator go isn't game-ending, just have an eye on the drain and get to it before it falls under 20% or so.You can go into debt to get things, which helps a bit. I recco using the "Upgrade" shops (piston icons) to boost your hull plating first and foremost. This prevents small dings from debri costing you a lot later to fix, which adds to the debtload. Second thing I'd upgrade is electric shielding, popping modules adds up.Some things that I love - the environments, the music, the customizable paint, the fact you feel really grounded in this world being able to be inside the truck walking around and doing EVAs to fix things outside and scavenge. If this integrated some mechanics like Hardspace Shipbreaker for stripping derelict ships, I'd be in heaven.Stuff that will no doubt be balanced out/fixed a bit later but I wanted to mention:The warning bar of "Debris Detected" or whatever obfuscates the screens, which normally isn't a big deal but if you are in one of those Solar Flare regions, you have the shutters down and using the monitor to navigate, and that warning makes it nearly impossible to see anything.There is a friggin ROCK in the right hand 'lane' of Crossvale as you approach the Purity gate that I've hit more than once. I don't know why, but I get there and forget about it, and BLAM it is on my front grill knocking hull integrity to near zero. Even the NPC trucks hit it, lol. Just wanted to warn people.Not a great fan of the void regions, with the crystals. I can navigate them, but pinging stuff all the time just becomes a bit of a hassle. I'd rather do a mission to Hell's Pocket where I can barely see than do the void stuff. Sorry, it looks great, but not so fun to me.Debri - sometimes, the field of debri that generates when you go 'off track' really can be supremely annoying. Not just a obstacle to thread the needle, but a shifting matrix of nearly impassable things that you will have to plow through just to get somewhere. I hope this gets balanced a bit.Otherwise, I really like the handling mechanics and how it flies. I also have the final mission thing being "stuck" but I think that is a common problem the devs know about and will likely fix.In short, great game, good aesthetics and makes me really want to play as you can see from my cumulative time. Got all the certifications and would like to totally complete the achievements, which isn't something I can say often.Good work, look forward to the fixes and potential additions.

_childDocuments_.review: It's a fun simulator game and puts a new spin on the concept of a driving/trucking/delivery simulator.It's a novel concept that works well that honestly had me hooked while I had the time to play it. I like the management aspect of the truck itself, especially managing power distribution, air filters, as well as navigating repairs to the hull when damage occurs. _childDocuments_.review: Space Trucking... wow!First: The game is DIFFICULT! If you put it on Normal or above you will have to balance being broke and having some money constantly, you are not going to just jump hoops and get rich instantly. This is not ETS in this way.Second: It is FUN! the game has very good controls both on controller and Keyboard. Sadly no HOTAS support from what I know, did not bother trying.LINUX: Works, beautifully under Proton Experimental and even on the Steam Deck, tho there the framerates are dancing around 30. So you might not enjoy it as much.Honestly I got bit by this loop, I was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ through the first like half an hour then my mind clicked into the 'grind' and I managed to keep my truck alive and floating, albeit looking like a rust bucket, but MY rust bucket. The game is insane fun, has moments of chill when you are flying down the highway, or just line up for a jump gate. And has those nail biting moments when you are 2 miles on fuel and have to float to the nearest station to refuel, or run out of batteries and scramble to stack up on more before you lose power in your cab.The learning curve is Steeeeep but damn it feels rewarding as I slowly start to grasp the game.I'd say jump in, try not to look up too many things on guides, and let the game immerse you into an experience of fighting for survival, or take it easy, kick the settings down through custom settings, and play as you'd like. Loving it, HUGE UP! looking for further updates, and perhaps more truck types down the line :3

_childDocuments_.review: I’m absolutely loving this game so far! Personally, I prefer a more relaxed experience with high profits and low consumption, which allows me to focus more on driving and less on the details. The game's initial customization page let me set my play-style up perfectly, making a lot of people's negative reviews (re how often they need to tend to the truck's systems, batteries, etc.) seem minor and not worth taking seriously. I almost didn’t purchase the game because of these reviews, but I’m so glad I trusted my instincts!Here’s my breakdown:Pros:- Immersive experience- Stunning graphics- Fantastic truck sounds, ambiance, and music- Enjoyable trucking gameplay- Controls are simple, but offer complexity when reversing trailers- Mostly bug-free—nothing game-breaking- You can save at any point, no need to wait for a checkpoint- Great to be able to leave the driver’s seat and move around, a rare feature in similar games- Mesmerizing jump-gate animations- Simple map interface with all necessary information- HUD markers are useful- Love the truck dashboard with various controls like power levels, reverse camera, radio, lights, etc.—it boosts the immersion!- The game is highly customizable to suit most players' styles, allowing for both relaxed and challenging experiences.Cons:- Minor bugs, such as when I entered a jump gate and got hit by an asteroid mid-jump, causing $3,000 in damage. Thankfully, I had saved not long before.If the devs create DLCs which add more mechanics and more zones, I will be first to buy them.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, advertises itself as a truck sim but is so far from it to be laughable. The setting would be interesting, if there was much to it. Most of what you're doing is flying through empty space in a see of debris that will destroy you while going from jump gate to jump gate. Very little interesting in the way of driving.This game is too incredibly punishing to be fun. The truck needs a ton of consumables to keep running. It's too expensive to rely on completing jobs to keep on top of repairs, fuel, and all the other in-cabin consumables. The best part is, you're not even guaranteed any ability to get what you need. Need 4 batteries? Too bad, the shop is selling 1. Need an air filter? Those are so rare that most shops seem to have none.So... making money. Leveling up makes jobs more valuable and unlocks new cargo types. Fine. It's not enough in the early game economy. It feels like merchanting is the intended way of making money in the game, which is extra punishing early when you can't buy a lot of goods.Docking is annoying. Want shop? Dock. Want to view the jobs? Undock, then dock 50 yards to the left on the same building. It's tedious.For extra fun, oxygen is not connected when you're docked, even though power is. So every second you spend docked is constantly chipping away at your O2 system. You cannot ever take a break in this game, it's relentless.Trying to find things in a system is annoying. You might know there is a job board in a system, but you won't know which white diamond it's at.Shock storms... what a miserable mechanic. They spawn on top of places you need to be, like stations with job boards. It will disable the cameras making docking extremely difficult. And if you do dock by some miracle, you're still affected by the storm. So you'll pop all of your shock absorbers trying to find a job.There is WAY too much debris everywhere in space, and even hitting the tiniest fragment can be quite damaging. If you're driving fast, the pop-in will make it impossible to dodge. And map markers can hide the debris so you can't even see it. The more trailers you have, the more zoomed out your camera is. But you simply cannot see enough from inside the cabin to be able to dodge anything either.The only interesting thing is that the game has some kind of story, but the actual gameplay is too frustrating for me to want to continue.tl;dr this is some kind of survival game masquerading as a truck sim, and the gameplay is tedious.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I did run into a bug finally. I ran out of oxygen while hauling this sign for some moron across multiple zones. On step 7... i died.. when i came to there was no marker or way to lcoate the sign. They recovered me and my truck, but didnt think to also recover the thing i was hauling. = This is game breaking. A lot of the convoy people tie together, some dont unlock until youve done X with person 1 and X with person 2. Now that I cant continue I had to start over....This is a quick 10 hour review - Its emergent gameplay. At first it seems simple and 'fun'... but its challenging to the point of being grueling for some. If you look at the forums youll see people complain about how hard it is... instead of just lowering the difficulty. You need to be an organized player with sharp situational awareness. You need to be able to intuit how the systems work and how to maximize your resources. This is not an easy game, even on standard difficulty. That challenge is what makes it fun. I have unlocked 10 skills now and completed 5 long distance runs. I have done wide loads, multi-trailer, heavy and valuable loads.s Each has its thing you need to manage. There are ways to upgrade your truck to be better at things but I havent spent any money there yet as even as skilled as I believe that I am at this game, accidents do happen and it will cost you. I have died twice, both from lack of oxygen. Dying is EXPENSIVE, much more than just paying that 3000$ for an air-filter in the first place.My best payout so far was around 7000$. I assume it gets better with the different types of runs and longer distances.I have only unlocked one additional area so far and there are 4 more to unlock. Based on that, i assume that I could pull 20-25 hours of out of this game which meets my standard for a recommendation of $1 for each hour played. i have experienced zero bugs and zero crashes.

_childDocuments_.review: I've not played the game as heavily as some yet, however I figured I'd throw my thoughts on the pile of hopefully helpful feedback. I really like the style and vibe of the game. There's a lot of comments talking about the lack of content which sure yeah could be an argument, but that presumably and hopefully will be added to in the future. For the gameplay side of things there's the common thread of power and part management. I have read through a few of the reviews including the dev comments. and to me It's a bit rough around the edges, but I had a few ideas that might be a way to address the issue. I get the devs might be wanting to go for a more "realistic" environment or management style game instead of a relaxed trucking simulator which I don't mind in the slightest and would enjoy if there wasn't a severe lack of a grace period. What I mean by that is when something goes wrong you never feel like you can actually stop and resolve the issue or take a moment to plan out your next steps. My solutions for the lack of grace would be a rest stop/service station. These would be located at some of the major 'hubs' where you could pull over to something like a diner and you'd be supplied power so you can repair and swap cells without too much stress or /having/ to connect to a station where you can't EVA. Having them be at main hubs means if you are in the Junkfields for example you'll still have to make it to Emerald junction if you want to conduct maintenance in relative safety. If not you'll still have to do things roadside. They also give you a good place to stop out the way of other truckers and debris. This idea could also be incorporated into the fuel stations so they pull double duty and provide a dedicated place to pull over and maintain your truck.POWER Then onto power cells and the strange absence of ways to recharge them. Seen a lot of comments about how the highways are basically pointless, so let's give them a function and a mechanic which is how I thought they would have functioned before actually playing. Make the trucks either not use power when you are within the designated path of the highway (In between the pylons) or have them provide a small passive charge enough to cover a moderate power draw. This would actually give you some benefit of staying on the highway. Since currently they are a complete waste of time and fuel to follow and them not having debris really isn't that massive of an upside. An extension of this idea would be having the ability to install some solar panel type devices onto your truck. The truck has some massive blank spaces that would be perfect for a panel or two. These would be an upgrade that you can initially pay to install then an additional cost to upgrade to become more effective. The panels could maybe cover the passive draw of an unloaded cab without its grav generator and lights on at the start and slowly be able to cover more systems. Or for the unfortunate trucker the ability to sit with the panels facing the sun for a much needed charge.Now some suggestions for the power cells themselves. There's two ways to go with them: The first way is to have the basic power cells be your dirt cheap non-rechargeable ones that you can /always/ access at any shop with a certain reliability. Your then more expensive cells the ones with 150 capacity and up being able to recharge. And as you get more expensive cells they gradually become more efficient or charge faster, with the down side then being slower charging or being less efficient with maybe at the end of the chain a cell that is the definitive best in both departments as maybe a reward or for a higher cost. Second way is having all the power cells function to the same extent where they all have a degree of rechargeability and the more expensive is just better overall. To make this not so trivial let's say you have 4 total types of cells. The first tier starts out fully charged and over time starts to break down eventually only being able to charge back to 25% of the full capacity, this then follows on with the next tier of cells only being able to charge to 50% and so on. Leaving the final cell obviously still being able to hold a full charge.PARTS Onto parts. Obviously the pricing on certain parts is crazy. Primarily the air filters cost from what I've seen 2700 -3000 in some shops which early on might completely screw you over if you had to swap out the starter one already and haven't made enough to cover for a new one. First thing most would suggest is to just lower the price, but I think this is boring. My suggestion for this would be a way for us to clean out the air filters to squeeze a little more life out of them, maybe in the form of shaking them out in space or some kind of compressed air hose on the rig that would use a bit of oxygen like the air break in exchange for a few more minutes of breathable air. To add some fuel to another suggestion I saw was the UCC fuse's not having a way to monitor them from the seat other than waiting for something to stop working or having to manually check which just feels a bit glossed over. Adding another screen to the cycle for the fuses would be really cool to aid in the micromanagement. Another thing that I've noticed that has been a bit frustrating is the lack of a way to drop items safely. You are perfectly positioned to damage every single thing that you try to put down by your feet, So everything including the rather large gas tanks somehow gets damaged. You can avoid this by placing it on a raised surface or just not using the grav, but it just feels like an oversight and doesn't add any substance.QOL and MISCBeing able to access job boards and stores without docking would reduce the headache massively, maybe you still need to dock there at least once to get the information permanently in the case of job boards, and for stores you obviously would need to dock to actually purchase and receive your items. At least then you won't waste several minutes moving across the system to dock to then only leave empty handed because the store has none of what you need. Alongside the above having a basic local map of the systems or at least a way to mark potential POI's like a store or job board in a system would help with the navigation side of things.Proximity warning: This could definitely be improved and why not do that in the form of another upgrade in the form of either a radar that can tell you what direction the debris is in or some flashing lights that can give you a general direction to make it easier when navigating, because honestly even when zooming in the combination of restricted cab view and mark 1 eyeball doesn't work for everyone. Hard Case: Another idea I really like, but could be improved one of two ways: the first adding a lip onto the shelf so they can't just float out. Or second having a option to 'attach' them to the shelf. Sure you can open them to get the same effect, but I think these would be a better intended way of keeping things organized.Side jobs: by default these should payout way more. I realized on my first save that these bankrupted me. And sure yes there are ways of preventing that, but it's not something a first time player will inherently know and may turn them away. Difficulty isn't a bad thing its just when it happens in the first handful of hours when the game seems geared towards figuring things out yourself is just a bit meh. If I didn't have a friend give me some pointers I probably would've struggled avoiding debt in my second playthrough.Time: I like the short hauls but coming to this after other games where you really have to drive or fly in Star Citizen and Euro Truck it would be nice to have some more intense distances although I haven't gotten super far yet in the overall progression so I'll leave this as a soft opinion for now.Conclusion in comment.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty easy to sum up Star Trucker: it's a trucking simulator in space. You take jobs to pick up cargo from point A and drop it off at point B. You maintain and upgrade your space truck. You buy fuel. Rinse, repeat.The thing that sets Star Trucker apart is the most obvious: the setting. Moving your typical trucking simulator into space changes some of the fundamentals. You're not bound to roads and you don't need to worry about traffic too much. Instead you have to avoid debris and asteroids; shield yourself from solar flares; shield your truck from electrical storms. If you don't properly maintain your truck, the gravity shuts off or you run out of oxygen. The stakes are higher.You can also carry smaller cargo, organized on shelves at the back of your cab (which you have to reorganize if you're in a collision and it all comes flying off the shelf). This lets you make a little cash outside of cargo hauling. You'll occasionally come across beacons that mark cargo spills where you can perform EVAs to collect some of these smaller goods.There's a skill tree that lets you unlock specific types of jobs (fragile goods, oversize loads, long hauls, short times, etc.), and other truckers you perform tasks for to unlock new areas of the map and upgrades, both of which do a good job of slowly increasing the complexity of the game.Overall, it's a great game that's easy to recommend. It improves on the trucking simulator genre and there are things here that I think other spaceflight games could learn from as well.

_childDocuments_.review: YES! AFTER 12 HOURS I CAN ABSOLUTELY SAY I LOVE THIS GAME! But it took a lot of trial and error.***Long story short: I set the contract payouts to [HIGH] and it alleviated most of my complaints for this game***Long story long: I had a hell of a time with this thing. I love flying haulers and space mining. This game is exactly what I was looking for in terms of concept, features, etc. But on the default settings, it's surprisingly punishing and the story missions actually make it HARDER (because they usually consume a lot of resources but don't necessarily pay you anything). It all comes down to economics: your truck/ship/thing (I will call it a "rig") runs on a combination of fuel, batteries, fuses and air filters. Your rig consumes all of these things and when any one of them runs out, you die. On the recommended settings, these items burn out comically fast. You will find yourself scrambling all over your rig swapping out consumables almost as much as you actually drive the damn thing. And it's fun! Until the money runs out. Then you die. And die and die. You can even fall into debt, which is as much fun as it sounds.When I hit that wall, I swallowed my pride and said "OK, well I guess I'm just not up to scratch yet. I will turn down the difficulty." But I couldn't. You literally have to start a new game to change difficulty settings. SO I STARTED ALL OVER, I lost over 5 hours of game play. There are custom settings that let you tweak the different features of the game and the solution seemed simple enough: tweak the rate at which consumables wear out. So that's what I did AND IT BROKE THE GAME.I like all the maintenance. I like taking the time to go over all the systems and equipment to ensure they'll get me through the next contract. I can't say this for certain, but I'm pretty sure that lowering the difficulty regarding consumables like batteries/fuses/filters just disables the need to replace them entirely. I played for hours and none of them seemed to wear down at all. The game went from sadistically difficult to boringly simple. So I had to start over again.I didn't want a survival/horror experience, nor did I want to do away with all the (fun!) maintenance features, what could I do? Finally, I took the easy way out and just multiplied the payouts for completing contracts because just like in real life, money solves everything! Now I can fret over my dwindling stock of fuses and merrily swap out dead batteries without feeling like I'm trapped in the same debt-slavery I have to live through in real life! The game is a great mix of slow burns through gorgeous space vistas and panic-stricken moments of oxygen deprivation.If any devs are reading this: please consider joystick/HOTAS support and let us re-map control inputs. And for heaven's sake include the cruise control in the tutorial mission, I was tapping space bar for hours before I discovered I didn't have to.

There are however, a few things that could use some changes/tweaking, at least in my opinion.1. The difficulty- The difficulty is fine, don't get me wrong. Another solution would be, to allow a grace period when you switch the grav battery. Give me some time to switch it before everything starts flying around.3. Controls- Keybinding is already being addressed by the devs, which is awesome. But I believe being able to strafe would be very beneficial to the overall experience.- Flying backwards is a bit of a pain in the ass. Don't know what to do, just figured I mention it.4. Store Items- The only reason I could find why those exist is to sell them? Radio- Adding more radio stations would most likely require too much work. BUT enabling the user to add some internet radios to their game, shouldn't. _childDocuments_.review: In today's gaming landscape where so many games release into early access purgatory or release fully but with countless patches in the following weeks, I was absolutely not expecting Star Trucker to release in a very finished manner. Sure, there have been balance tweaks and work with control remapping and HOTAS support post-launch, but on launch, the game had very few noticeable bugs and felt like a finished product. Gameplay wise, it is very reminiscent of SCS Software's truck simulator duo but with story missions and a focus on micromanagement of inventory, your truck's subsystems, and time itself. To be honest, I wish it was more of a space driving simulator, instead of relying so much on the jump gates, but I am still more than content with its gameplay loop. It's obvious the devs care deeply about this game and want to make it as best they can, in a way that reminds me of Ghost Ship Games and their wonderful game, Deep Rock Galactic.As a bonus, the game feels like a playable version of the  episode from Cowboy Bebop.

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game. It successfully takes what's compelling about trucking sims, marries it to what's compelling about space sims, and wraps it all in a pretty accessible package. There's a fair amount it doesn't tell you (check the manual in the glove box), but compared to something like Elite Dangerous or Euro Truck Simulator, it feels very streamlined.It's also no slouch in the difficulty department! Don't go in expecting chill vibes; there are some of those, but you're in space, and space is dangerous. You'll be managing batteries, fuses, and air filters to ensure you don't run out of oxygen or freeze to death. You'll navigate some truly gnarly debris fields. You'll fly through electrical storms and have to lower your shutters and navigate by camera when there's a solar flare.But, man, is this game satisfying and engrossing. It sits within the center of a venn diagram of my interests.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly what I wanted based on the demo earlier this year.This game can be a little unforgiving at times, but that's the case with any good "simulation" game. The sound and visual design for this game are spectacular. The sound-track is one of the best, most perfectly themed original sound-tracks I have heard in a long time.Here are the things this game simulates:- Newtonian space physics, with the ability to turn off "Drive Assist" and coast. You have to manage the weight of the truck, as well as the weight of attached cargo trailers, and you will crash into stuff which leads us to...- Repairs. A rig in space, it's rather fragile. Collisions, even small ones with small debris leads to hull breaches, much like issues with space debris that real astronauts have to deal with. So put on your Hardspace: Ship-breaker (Available on Steam) hat and get to repairs. Even if you drive, er fly perfectly, you still have to deal with...- A number of subsystems simulated in a medium complexity vehicle. You have to maintain your subsystems, such as artificial gravity, magnetic couplers, and oxygen/air filtration systems by frequently changing batteries, control circuits, and filters. The manual is included in your glove box, but no one reads it. So put on your Tin Can (Available on Steam) hat and get ready to replace some stuff. But running a well maintained rig runs into...- The typical struggles that real truckers deal with including inspections, permit limitations, speed limits and fines for unlawful driving, and other traffic making everything more complex. Plus, backing up a trailer on a road, in two dimensions is already tough enough, now you have to reverse while wrangling a mass dangling off your rear magnetic couplers in three dimensions.- There are a ton of subtle simulation touches that really help bring the universe consistency together such as 1. The illuminated circle of all docking ports aligns perfectly with the circle rendered on the reverse docking camera when the truck is aligned and ready to grapple.2. The lights next to the jump gate all indicate important information, whether you are close enough, aligned correctly, and at a stop.3. You have control all the exterior and interior lights and other functions within the cab.4. There's cruise control!Here are the things this "simulation" game-ifys - very much like American Truck Simulator or Euro Truck Simulator 2 (Both available on Steam):- You can pick your difficulty using a pre-canned setting, I chose "standard," or customizing various parts of game-play to suit your style.- Earning money for deliveries. At first, money is tight, and you have to make some tough choices. Do you use that old 12% battery in the space-suit recharge unit to give you just enough juice to patch that hull leak, or keep that 12% handy in case your artificial gravity dies? But soon enough, with a little patience, you'll have a full crate full of spare batteries ready to go.- Upgrades are available to improve handling, efficiency, etc. I haven't gotten into these just yet, but I can see that I'm now making more money than I'm spending, and the first wave of upgrades are affordable in the early game.- Lots of places to discover, permits to unlock, and new delivery types in the skill tree, very similar to American / Euro Truck Sims.- Travel times are helped a lot with the jump gates. Games like ATS and ETS2 handle travel time by compressing the world. Star Trucker divides the world into sectors that are all unique with jump gates in between them.Here are the things that could be improved:- HOTAS support not yet in the game, but the devs are working on it.- No VR - this game would be spectacular in VR.- Some performance issues on some current / powerful gaming builds, they are aware as far as I can tell and are working on it.- The cruise control doesn't automatically disengage when you tap on the brakes, like in a real truck. (It should, take this as my request for this minor feature!)Here is my Final Verdict: I played the crap out of the demo when it was out; the full release has not disappointed at all. This is going to be my binge-play game for a while. At the end of the day this is a futuristic "sim" is really fun with plenty of complexity and subtlety to explore in this "simulation."

_childDocuments_.review: I'm having a lot of fun with this game so far. I'm not usually one for trucker sims but add a sci-fi twist and I'm sold.Maintaining the systems of the truck might be a bit tedious for some (though I know there are settings to alter the amount of tedium), but to me swapping out batteries and circuit boards, keeping your storage organized and restocked, all feels tactile and satisfying. Not to mention being able to EVA to patch your hull and scavenge parts from floating debris .On the default difficulty, the payout from the jobs vs the amount it costs to maintain the ship feels just about right to keep you invested. If your driving is reckless and you're getting into a collision every job, you're not going to be able to cover your expenses. The better you drive, the more you profit. This overlaps well with the design of the play space. The shortest route is almost never the safest, with asteroids and debris clouding the way. You have to decide which route to take given your finances, skill, the type of job and your patience.Different types of jobs add a bit of variance to the driving. Fragile loads need to be handled with the utmost care, heavy loads are less maneuverable and slow to accelerate, perishable loads slowly degrade over time and require a speedy delivery, multi-trailer loads are harder to navigate through small spaces, etc. Some hauls are sensitive to certain atmospheric conditions and you have to plan your route out accordingly to avoid any systems that would be harmful to the cargo.There is also the optional side mechanic of trading. You can pick up various goods from the stations around the galaxy to keep in your cab. Prices fluctuate at different stations letting you turn a profit if you make a habit of checking the local economy. The amount of goods you can carry in your cab is weight limited (unless you can avoid the occasional weight check), with a weight limit that increases with the skill tree progression in the game.I think the skill tree is probably the least interesting mechanic in the game. As you level up you can unlock different types of hauls (like the aforementioned fragile loads, heavy, etc). You can invest further into a particular type to increase your payout. There are other options in the skill tree to improve EVAs, and increase cargo weight, but I wish there were more interesting options (though admittedly I'm not even sure what those would be)There are some upgrade options for your truck; improved thrust, stronger hull etc, and plenty of customization options as well, though they cost a pretty penny.I've not run into any bugs or visual glitches, it's well polished.Overall it's a pretty solid game. Definitely give it a try if you're a sci-fi geek and just want to play something to relax and take your mind off things!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is an inspired fusion of sci-fi and industrial sim. It's a trucking story with all the trappings of American Truckin' you would recognise from Smokey and the Bear. It's a futuristic glimpse into a vast galaxy of busy Kessler-syndromed planets and cold galactic outposts.I love how unapologetically the game drops highways, CB radio chatter, bootleg beer, and upward-pointing exhaust pipes into the same space as jump-gates, gravity-compensators, solar flares, and dark matter. Somehow the resulting universe is seamless and rewards my suspension of disbelief.Mechanically, I've seen other people complaining that the trucks don't have more ability to strafe like a real spacecraft might. That's true... but like. it's a truck. It's not a spaceship optimised for hauling cargo. It's a Big Rig Truck, but in space. That's the devs' vision, and a good metaphor for how they've combined other aspects of the two genres: the space mechanics and appearance are right there, not ignored, but always in service to the long-haul trucker aesthetic and theme. Like the music on the radio: classic rock and blues with subtle mentions of space scattered through.Finally, I also want to specifically praise the other folks we meet in-game. Though it's rare to see even their vehicles up close, the voices we hear over the radio still convey engaging characters. They make the galaxy feel populated with their gossip and insights, and importantly they punctuate the procedural cargo-hauling jobs with more unique side-quests. These requests usually also come down to moving something from A to B (our main skill, after all) but each one is memorable, and develops our connection to the character or the world as a whole.

You have to figure out how to keep your trucking going with managing power, choosing what system you can do without as needed, fuel, O2, Temperature. Sounds daunting? Nope. Just a little curve tossed in. It adds some management that is important. But it gives you a chance to choose how you / if you want to alter things. Customize settings.Sadly, there is not a lot to change on trucks yet. You can upgrade systems and your skills...I hope they give more to customize and more variety in trucks you can run.Overall? I like this game as a neat little truck / space / kill time game.Expect some butthurt at first on figuring out batteries. Once you do, you got it. Keep on (space) truckin'.

_childDocuments_.review: Startrucker is one of the coolest and most interesting games I’ve ever played! It took me exactly 24 hours and 2 minutes to complete, and every moment was absolutely worth it.One drawback, though, is that sometimes the gameplay can get repetitive and feel a bit less engaging. There are moments when you're sent back and forth between locations—fly to one place, leave, return, and then leave again—and it feels unnecessary. Despite this, the game is still fantastic, and I’d definitely recommend Startrucker to anyone looking for a fun and immersive adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a solid space trucking game with survival aspects that does everything correctly but doesn't give You a massive wow that's amazing effect however it does deliver a good blend of trucking and survival. That's something new and unique on the current market if You're into trucking games.The game is fun to play, depending on the difficulty settings You can just chill and cruise through space with your cargo or constantly check all your systems, batteries and fix stuff as it goes wrong. Everyone will find the balance they enjoy in this game. There's a simple and easy to learn system for storage and replacing all the components as we haul cargo in space.Graphics look good, there's a variety of sectors offering different environments, some are friendly and some are dangerous. It's not always smooth sailing through space.There's only one truck in the game but there's enough customisation for it to keep the experience fun and rewarding especially when it comes to paint jobs. To get them You have to complete achievements that unlock them. My only complaint is that there isn't that much driving in the game. You can drive withing the sector, go fuel up, check out what's in the store or go pick up a job but You can't drive between sectors. You go to warp gates and they teleport You between sectors. You will do a few miles, then teleport and repeat. It makes sense considering we are in space travelling between different planets.Overall for the price it's a solid space trucking survival game that's worth the money. Grab it and enjoy your space trucking adventure. Space cowboy over and out.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to like this game I really really did, but it's just got too many issues for me to recommend it. There's many other reviews that have said what I'm about to say better than I can but I'll just be brief. 1. Everything breaks too fast. You need batteries for everything and those will last maybe a jump or two. Shops not only have very very few in stock but they're also way too expensive, costing upwards of 600 bucks per battery. For context an average job will give you about 2k. so with 8 batteries you need and each costing nearly 600 you're constantly scrambling for money. Additionally batteries cannot be recharged in any way which is mind boggling to me. 2. Everything is too expensive. Mentioned above is the price of batteries but most egregious is air filters. You can have up to 4 of them but you only need one. Having more means they all supposedly break slower. The in game tutorial (which is horrible but we'll get to that) implies that they are actually not needed but helpful, that the more of them you have and in good condition means the less your oxygen generator uses up power. This isn't the case however and running out of them all together means that despite having a literal oxygen generator, somehow you begin to rapidly lose oxygen and then die. I don't know how having no filters suddenly makes oxygen just leak out of the ship in every direction but it will soft lock your  game, but again more on that later. 3. The tutorials are lacking to say the least. Some are ok but the majority tell you very very little info. Such as the "core system" which requires 2 batteries. It does not explain why it needs two or what happens if one runs out or you just don't put another one in at all. Turns out, you don't need two, you can get by with one. Would have been nice to know. As mentioned before with the air filters, I had no idea that having none of them would make the air in my cabin suddenly dissipate out of nowhere. Air filters clean the air, not produce it, so it was really confusing when I was getting notifications about a massive air leak but with no hull breaches. A tutorial would have been pretty helpful there in explaining that. Because that soft locked me. Speaking of which. 4. It's way too easy to soft lock yourself. Any time you'd "die" you're sent to a garage with a hefty bill you now need to pay off. Problem. I can't afford air filters with are around 4k a pop and I'm already spending most of my very little income on batteries already. So if I couldn't afford filters when I was in the green, how am I supposed to now that you've dropped me several thousand dollars into debt? Which I need to pay off first before anything else? Thus you die again, and again and again, going further in debt and fail spiraling. 5. The AI is just some of the stupidest things around. I've been hit more than a few times by drones and trucks coming out of nowhere and colliding with me. The game wants you to be on the "roads" but there's hardly ever any at all. AI trucks can stop and turn on a dime when you can't so you'll be following them when they suddenly stop moving and then you feel like a train conductor hitting the breaks despite knowing you can't possibly stop in time.6. Hey game, why do I have to go out of my way to find the shop in each sector? Sometimes it's highlighted no matter where I am, sometimes the body shop is highlighted, but not the store that might have the air filters I need to not die. The game tells you that some places prefer to not get bogged down with people and so don't have their pings set to be visible from so far away. Not sure why companies are literally going out of their way to hide from customers but ok. Maybe I thought, that would only apply to some seedier places that take back alley goods or something, but no. Even the most basic stores will be completely undetectable until you're right up on them. 7. The "recommended difficulty" is not the hardest one, in fact there are 2 above it, but this is grueling. I wanted a fun relaxing experience, I wanted to do some maintenance on my truck but not have to replace every single component every 30 minutes. This has completely ruined the game for me and with no way to actually change the difficulty on a save, I'd have to create an entirely new save, start from the very beginning, only to hope that it's not so punishing. If you can even call it punishing, because punishing implies that I did something wrong, but when the game gives me two star ports in a row with no filters and only 2 batteries, then how the hell am I supposed to do anything at all? This game doesn't feel like a fun sim. I don't even know how to describe it, because I genuinely feel like the main gameplay loop is replacing batteries and finding filters, over actually driving the damn truck. Hopefully they can update the game with a very very much needed balance pass but until then I'm not touching this thing again.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm really enjoying this game so far. The salvage and maintenance portions do a nice job of breaking up the traveling in a way that something like ETS2 or hauling in Elite do not.That said there's definitely some improvements to be made. Keybinding and being able to change difficulty mid-save are obvious ones. There's some little things as well like how I feel the exterior and interior lights drain a bit too much of your power. You can of course just keep them off, but that's not really an interesting choice since there's not much of a gameplay benefit from having them on in the first place. I'd also like more customization of which waypoints are showing. I'm one that prefers learning my way around instead of just following markers, but turning waypoints off also disables the markers for shops and job pickup locations. The problem there is that there's really no visual difference between the two. My ideal would be to have a separate setting each for gates, stations, cargo dropoff/pickup, and docking locations.The recommended difficulty has been keeping me on my toes so far in a way that I'm enjoying. I can see how it might be a little much for someone who just wants to chill out though. I think part of the confusion is that the difficulty settings aren't really an easy, normal, and hard like most are used to. They're more of a setting of choosing how often you'll do maintenance. You'll either do maintenance rarely with more expensive parts, frequently with cheaper parts, or a balance of the two. To make the game actually easier you have to use the custom difficulty.All that said, there's quite a bit more that I love about the game than not, and there's plenty more potential to the game with a few additions. It's an easy recommend from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I'm disappointed. I thought people's complaints were exagerrated, but no, not really. I wish I didn't try to like it for more than 2 hours, as now I can't refund.So, what I don't like:1. The game claims to be "realistic" and a "simulator". This is a bit ridiculous. I get that it's set in space and therefore cannot be a real simulator, but come on. Neither the infrastructure (of which there is plenty) nor the truck itself is really well prepared for "driving" in space. Like, the windows are similar to real truck, so you can't see below and above you, except when using external camera. Flight assists are irritating instead of being helpful. The space infrastructure is ridiculous and not at all prepared to handle 3 dimensional traffic. "Highways" have traffic in both directions in the same space with "right" side going forward, which is just ridiculous in space, nothing prevents it from being separated. The highways often end suddenly in front of a construction or an asteroid/trash field. They are disconnected with each other. The flight itself is simulated terribly, it does not feel like moving in space at all, there's a huge drag of air, the truck slows down very quickly when not accelelerating etc. etc.2. The size of the world. While there seems to be a decent amount of "systems" between which you can jump, each system is very small. "Highways" have nominally just a few kilometers each, which in space feels more like maybe 1 km of what normal road feels. They are never straight too. I would have expected 10-20 times longer highways, mostly straight, and way higher max speed, requiring you to turn around around the middle and start breaking (btw it's ridiculous, but you break way faster than you accelerate in this space game...). There is no in-system map at all and you can't know what points of interest are hidden where and how to get there (it's only manageable because of the small sizes, but irritating still).3. The big focus on things outside of "driving". Replacing a battery is interesting and fun experience the first few times. Later it just feels like a chore. You spend way more time doing other things than driving (also because the distances are so small).4. AI drivers are really bad. I think big part of this is that the game designers do not really have any proper idea of driving rules in space that make sense, and the infratsructure is also not adapted to it. So, for example, everyone tries to keep the same "height". It doesn't make much sense in 3D space. But also AI is bad in other ways, for example once while I was going left from a "road" to park, an AI truck going the same direction as me, but to the left of me, stopped, making it look like it was letting me go, even though I stopped earlier to let it through. But nope, it stopped, waited until I was perpendicular in front of it, then it hard rammed me, straight into my "fragile" cargo.5. Overall the gameworld seems artifical and devoid of life. There seems to be a lot of scripted conversations and some storyline, but outside of that you don't really get to contact anyone. You can't talk to other drivers on the road, you don't talk to anyone about job offers or shops, they are just menus.

_childDocuments_.review: As of the time of this review it has been only 48 hours since launch, so any issues or complaints with the game brought forth in this review may be subject to change as the issues may or may not be fixed within the week as the devs continue to work on the game and provide updates and patches/fixes.Steam only has thumbs up and thumbs down but not in between and honestly i'd give it an in between right now, but for the review I will give it a thumbs up because I have high hopes for this game as it was still somewhat fun from what I played. It's a fun game with a lot of potential, and if it's really made by just 2 devs it's amazing. However, that being said I don't think I'll be playing it any further until they update a few things.1) There are no keybinds. Keybinding is pretty important and a standard of most games these days. Not having the key binds makes it difficult for some left handed players and honestly having the keybinds would also be essential for joystick/hotas setups. 2) It needs Joystick/HOTAS support. In their FAQ they addressed the lack of stick/hotas support and said it's a top priority so they've already made it pretty clear that right out the gate it doesn't have stick/hotas support.3) The directions are limited. You can pitch and yaw, and roll but that's it. It moves like an airplane but it's still missing those other two directions of movement (Y and Z) where you can just strafe left/right, or ascend/descend straight vertically. It being a space game, i feel, needs this and is an essential  in pretty much every space game as well. Without these, docking your truck is a pain in the ass if you find you're either above or below the point. Auto-docking isn't a feature in the game yet, but for people who want less challenge it would probably be nice to have though not essential.4) Game play right now seems a bit.. unbalanced? I don't want to say punishing because sometimes it's good to have a game with some difficulty or a great challenge but this is different. The whole vehicle relies on batteries which you have to constantly replace with new fresh ones. The batteries themselves are expensive and that can rack up rather quickly in cost and make it difficult to make money in the game without going negative if you're not careful. Perhaps having your batteries recharge via docking with a station or something would help? It's one of the largest game play grievances on the forums at the moment. While this is also a trucking game and about hauling goods through space it is not a long haul space game. Unlike American Truck Simulator or Elite Dangerous where you take these long routes to deliver your goods, the hauls in ST are manged via a warp gate which only lasts a few seconds. The game is more about maneuvering through tight small spaces and avoiding hazards and parking/docking.So, is it fun? It can be and has potential. If you're looking for a game like it that also has::KeybindsStick/HOTASLong HaulsY and Z movementAuto-Docking/Auto-ParkingCo-Op..then just get Elite Dangerous.

_childDocuments_.review: I was split on this, but since this is not marked as an early access game, I would not recommend purchasing it right now. This was released in a state which feels pretty beta, maybe 2/3 of the way through that phase of the development cycle. The gameplay loop can be fun, but there are various asinine choices made by the devs which take away from the fun. It is also really risky to release a truck sim game that doesn't have a similar level of customization as other truck sim games. Really, the difficulty options need to be adjustable on the fly with a lot more granularity. The instantly-assigned tickets are not fun, the $2000 weigh station fine isn't fun for something so irrelevant in space, dealing with the AI's inability to queue at single gates is frustrating. All stuff that could have been caught and revised if this was early access, with a lot more community feedback. The farther I go in the game, the less 'alive' the world feels, and that combined with the unfun gameplay elements which you cannot tweak or turn off have me stopping before I finish the story (about 85% done). Maybe I will revisit it in a while, see if there's been progress in making the game more customizable and user-friendly.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is so close to being really awesome but there's several QoL features that are missing that just makes it fall short.1. The consumables system is uninteresting and punishing.  Also it's immersion breaking.  Essentially only three consumables, universal circuits, batteries, and air filters.  And all they do is run out and have to be replaced.  At high difficulty/consumption rate if you don't pick up batteries every job, you will run out and die.   Batteries are horridly expensive, UCC's just break for no reason, and air filters are I guess air filters.  Apparently sometime between now and when humanity started building big-rigs in space, we forgot how to make alternators, so even if you have fuel you can run out of electrical power which is solely supplied by batteries.  Humanity also forgot how to make rechargeable batteries, so you're stuck stocking up on duracell alkalines the size of your face.The minigame associated with consumable maintenance is more of a nuisance than engaging, so there's that too.  It's not like you need to learn a checklist and do things right.  No, it's just pull out old battery, shove in new battery.  Wham-bam done.At least you can create custom difficulty settings and basically disable that crap.Related: most of the systems that draw power don't seem to have any gameplay relevance.  Haven't figured out what benefits the running lights give, etc.  You don't get fined for running dark, and boy are your headlights power hungry.  You can turn off gravity when you're strapped in, but apparently the trucking industry in our glorious space future has forgotten how to secure and strap down cargo so any small cargo items in your cab will then just randomly float around.2. The truck is missing two movement axes (sway and heave) which seems like a really big design oversight for a spacefaring civilization, and also just serves to make docking procedures unnecessarily fiddly for you as a gameplayer.3. Jesus there is space junk EVERYWHERE.  Yes yes.  I know to stick to the spacelanes.  But dear god, why is there space junk at the exit to the spacelane going into the jump gate?  And related, you can turn off drive assist to save fuel, but there's really no point in doing that since all the space lanes are curved or you're flying through the great space garbage patch anyway.  I'm not opposed to having a mechanic that encourages the use of spacelanes, but there's no minimum velocity at which space junk won't ruin your day, there's no tactical way to decide if you're going to take on space junk as a hazard (i.e., declining a job that goes into a hazardous area), there's no real way to mitigate space junk other than pray and dodge, and it doesn't feel like there's any rhyme or reason to its existence other than an artificial "stay in your spacelane" mechanic.  It's not like "warning, entering asteroid mining remnants debris field", just more like, "yeah, the largest commercial transport hub in existence can't be bothered to sweep".4. You can't mix and match jobs.  Sure, you can take on three jobs, but you can only ever work on one at a time.  I guess this means you can save yourself a docking at the jobs board if you can line up and chain jobs, but if you want to get your multi-trailer certification and maybe tow two trailers headed in the same direction simultaneously?  Sorry, can't do that.  Your multi-trailer certification is really only so that you can pull a single trailer with a weird slinky-kinky in the middle.5. Speaking of docking ... what the hell happened to remote data connections in the future?  Why do I have to physically dock my truck every time I need a new job?  In order to get a new job, I have to physically dock with the station ... and if I want to visit the general goods store ... well I have to undock and then redock at the same station but at a different docking port.  Because apparently stations aren't internally connected.But the actual cargo?  It's all good.  Nobody needs to actually load or unload the cargo containers, just leave it in the space shed outside just kind of floating free.Honestly, I *really* want to love this game.  I really do, I was looking forward to it since I saw the initial reveal trailer.  But the implementation just falls short on so many metrics.

Hopefully they'll make a scavenger DLC titled something like "Clean Spaceroads Initiative" or something so you can clean the impressive amounts of debris from the zones. I do wish there were more upgrades for the trucks or different trucks you could buy that'd offer different advantages or disadvantages.Either way give this game a try if it looks like it might be your thing.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The extreme battery situation.The key mapping I could get used to, as many other reviews have stated, but the reality is that you will spend 60% of your time aggressively seeking out batteries. You do this by stopping at every single shop you come across, and you will definitely not be able to afford batteries in the level of astronomical frequency you will require them.And that's the game on "standard".I was hoping some nice chill gameplay of a truck in space, instead I got an intergalactic battery market simulator where I play a person who can't afford to exist.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Game is a pretty cozy truck sim and the environment is great. Change the soundtrack to a cowboy bebop playlist and the aesthetic is on point. Well worth the price.Some annoyances I hope are changed in the future:You have to back in a lot, which is quite satisfying once you get skilled at whipping up to stores and cargo and hitching up easily.  But this gets annoyingly repetitive, an example of how repetitive it is to have to constantly hitch in is: Need some supplies, hitch in to store. Now I need a new job, hitch into job board. Now I need to pick up the cargo, hitch to cargo. Repeat. It makes the game a bit too tedious and i hope they make the job boards places you don't have to hitch. I imagine like a truck rest stop in space would be way better.Also there's no citizenry anywhere in the galaxy. Meaning you're only in the galaxy with other truckers, which is quite boring since I'd love to see other space crafts. Space debris is too common for how clunky the controls are sometimes. Hope the game keeps getting patched into the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game was made for me.I am a space trucker heading through a lightning storm so I can sell sensitive electronics for a huge markup. I keep my visit short so I don't chew through all of my shock pods. I jump into a sector where the star throws out flares so big and intense, I have to shutter my windows and navigate solely through cams next to my dash. I get rammed in the ass because the police want to scan my truck literally seconds after coming through a gate.This game is without a doubt on the same level as Snowrunner. This is the space truckin' I've always wanted from Elite Dangerous. It has all the cool space views I desired from No Man's Sky.Some glitches are present. Try to peel off to the side when at a security checkpoint, you might get rammed in the rear. If you have to use your shutters, pray that the sector has little debris, or your video cam screens will be blocked by a big warning sign telling you that there is debris, which last several seconds and will pop up again in a few more seconds. A space station in the middle of a lightning storm will for some reason not protect you from taking electrical damage, forcing you to either be quick or willing to spend 2.000 Woolongs every trip there.But I love it.This is my game. It was made for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: For a game where hardly anything is present on screen (cartoony space graphics) it could run better, or provide more graphics customisation settings to better compromise on whatever is hogging the GPU. Same goes for keyboard binding customisation, mouse input lag, FOV adjustment option, etc.. The lack of all this makes up for a certain jankiness which gets in the way of me relaxing.The idea is good, but I'd say it needs to simmer for a little bit and wait for a couple of updates.My point of comparison is Hardspace: Shipbreakers - which achieves a very similar vibe, in a very similar environment, but somehow does it a lot smoother.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: It's a nice sim environment, but expect repetitive tasks.  Overall I enjoy it to chill: plan my route, grab what's on sale, grab a load, "drive", drop the load, sell what's in demand, repeat.The "Fast" jobs are by far the most annoying.  If you arrive too early  because there is no "skip time" mechanics you literally have to wait 10... 20 minutes of real life in your truck for the loading bay to be announced.The other job types so far are alright.  If you see people complaining about money, is they didn't understand you have to play the market or salvage.  If you aren't salvaging and aren't playing the markets, there's no way you'll make any money in this game.You need a side job son.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Be me, blue collar space trucker minding my own business.Get asked to haul an over sized, extra wide, volatile reactor that's set to blow at any minute.Do I risk taking it through electrical storms?If I go around I'll risk solar flares.This thing could go off for any reason killing me and whatever is in the system I'm trucking through.Suddenly get an alert on the admin channel."Your truck has been flagged for a mandatory weight check."What the actual %$&#?10/10, totally recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This ticks all the Space Trucking boxes for me, also some areas look pretty amazing on higher end GPU's.That said, there is one Caveat, but from the Patchnotes the Dev's seem aware of some problems: - This Game is rough on you, like unintentionally IRL realistic rough where some Issues like Breakdowns, Accidents, or a missed Deadline can wipe you out financially.Think of it like driving your own Rig in Places like Alaska or Siberia, only in Space, and you get an Idea how this can go. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Bought game and been hooked on it since, there's a steep learning curve to get over which may require you to start over once or twice but once you know the mechanics of the game it's very satisfying to play and very worth the price, also well made even on release of course there's a few bugs to work and some tweaks to the gameplay but overall a very solid release and title :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a great time if you're looking for a chill hauling experience with the same vibes as hard space: ship breaker. If you're okay with a little bit of jank this is a great 40hrs of casual gaming
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Alright.  So I got a little over 2 hrs into Star Trucker.  Its great as a Trucker Sim.  Its no ATS of course, but I feel like a space trucker.*There is definitely inertia and it feels pretty good once you get used to it.  It feels like youre piloting a big ass truck, and when youre outside the scale is pretty damn good.  Really gives you a perspective to make driving a tad easier.*The flying is nice with their inertia system, and from what ive read (i havent gotten any truck upgrades yet) the upgrades help ALOT.*Lots a varying missions, like shipments of things from one system to another but the item is restricted in some areas, so you have to plan your route to not go through systems where its not restricted.*There is trading with an economy.  Grab items from one system in the red and sell in the green.  Im not sure yet how much of an effect you have on that.*Witty banter over the CB isnt bad, and VA'd.  They say some corny space trucker jokes, and they're nice, but I'm not dying laughing.*Side missions dealing with the other truckers aren't bad, I haven't done very many, so the opinion may change.*Skill points are used to unlock what type of cargo/how many you can pull.*You can move around the cabin, get out and repair which is fun, but on just regular settings, but if you stray off the "highway" debris can come literally out of nowhere, and youll spend more time than you want repairing damage, which causes you to need filters/power cores more, and that gets EXPENSIVE.*You can upgrade the truck to make it faster, brake better, etc.  You can unlock paintjobs for your truck and you can change certain colors within those paintjobs which is pretty awesome because you do spend time outside of the truck picking up salvage.*Using the space suit isnt bad at all, I would like it a teensy bit more sensitive, but its not bad the way it is.*The customization options for gameplay mechanics is pretty deep and a welcome thing.  You can change all kinds of things, but (i think i dont remember) it causes you to get a little less xp for things if you make it easier.*There is no strafe or just up down thrusters for your truck which makes backing up to hook onto cargo/shops/job postings at stations can be a little frustrating if you dont pull up to it just right (there is a gameplay option to make this distance more forgiving).*There isnt an FOV option or a spring to default look button, so if you dont line up your sight in the 1pp camera, it looks real weird and hard to tell if you're drifing in an odd direction.*I do wish there were more safe spaceway instead of just the major highways, and also better signage floating when you come out of a jump where they are and where they go.*Really hoping for VR support.  This seems like a no brainer, but I understand how difficult that could be.*Mod support would be AMAZING.Its a chill arcadey Space Truck sim, and i'd say its worth the $22 I paid for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So far so truckin'!I loved it since the demo at the "Next Fest!", though i haven't played that much back then to not spoil myself from the moment the game releases.I've played almost 2 hours now, looked around some, tested a few things.From what i can see it's solid but has potential and a few things that need improvements.The first and biggest improvement (thing that should be added) is a proper keybinding option. I know, many things are meant to be clicked right in the cockpit, but to be honest, when i am trucking about, i want to see my truck from the outside and be able to just hit a key and jump through a gate for example.Right now i kinda have to break my "enjoyment of watching my trucks outside", jump into the cockpit via camera and pull the lever and jump back out.Also, not sure it's even possible with the trucks layout/model, strafeing left/right/up/down would be amazing, and "realistically" speaking, should be a thing in space.I was a bit lost about energy cells, sure i should/could have checked the manual resting in the glove compartment, but well a simple hint right in the tutorial at first would have saved me from a death in space..of suffocation.But i am still loving the game and look forward to updates and improvements from the devs! <3
