_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: (Too Soon Won't Read: I love this game so far. Well worth the purchase!!)2hr First Impression:Wow! As much as I loved Snowrunner, I hated how it's driving mechanics worked. I have been looking hard for a game with the same laid-back feel to it, but still requiring skill and thought to it. This is EXACTLY what I wanted! When I saw it a couple days ago I was HYPED!!There is clearly a lot of love put into making this game. Well worth the money spent. If only more games did that these days huh?9hr Edit:My view on it still holds. Nothing to add. Been playing Mechanic difficulty. Powercell replacements and UCC failures are quite frequent, but purchase of lvl 1 and 2 powercells and ample stocks of them and UCC means quick fixes make it manageable. Still satisfying to think ahead for this.Overview:The drive-flying mechanics are very cool. A fair blend of truck style and spaceship style flight. I thought these things (US truckin, space, country) would make for a silly but unique game. This is much more than that. Skill Expression:So far, with normal cargos and first few systems, it is pretty laid back. But I went in prepared to NOT underestimate the potential for a mistake. There are quite a bit of opportunities for risk + skill = benefit/reward.Pre-drifting/aiming into turns at high speed, heading directly to your location = debris navigation. Preemptive purchase and management of powercell/filter/communication-card and a close eye on power levels means satisfying swap jobs and not an annoying extra task.This game does not hold your hand like many others will do. It puts all the info right up in front of you in a quick simple and clean way for you to brush off or read up on.Graphics:This game looks good and performs well on low and high settings.It has a style that kinda reminds me of old space sims. Kind of makes me think of X2 era of style, but totally Monster and Monster's own modern take on the genre. It's fantastic.I really look forward to playing through it much longer. I'll update my review later on.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: this game is hard to get used to in the beginning. So much debris in space and hard to control the truck, but when you get used to it, then this game is so much fun. Love the missions.Best to start the game in custom settings and make it easy when it comes to power, then you can go harder when you get used to the game
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Part trucking simulator, part power and time management simulator, Star Trucker is a genuinely fun and exciting foray into the world of interstellar cargo hauling. You get your own big rig, and you have to keep it stocked and maintained as you transport various cargoes around a network of star systems and quick stops.I enjoy flying the space roads, taking shortcuts through debris laden asteroid fields, and getting out of my truck to patch a hull breach every so often. The real gem about this game is the soundtrack. You'll feel like you belong among the stars while you listen to the custom songs written for this game, just well done all around.While there are still some bugs to work out, the game has only been out for a day, the potential of what this will become is just exciting, and I can't wait to see what the developers do next.See you in the space lanes, good buddy.10-10.System Details:Fedora 4064 GB DDR4 RAM2 TB SSDAMD Radeon RX 7600 8 GBSo yes, this game runs very well using Steam's Proton on Linux.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Positive recommendation on the condition that you're in the niche audience that would enjoy this game. As I am in that group I've been really enjoying my time with the game, and the soundtrack has joined the Pacific Drive radio tracks on my commuting playlist.It's not a six degrees of freedom space game like Elite, it's more of a cross between a truck and flight sim where you have all three degrees of rotation but only forward and reverse thrust. The game is based around the concept of a space semi truck, not a space ship and personally I think the way it controls helps sell that. Elite is still around, it feels weird to buy a game that's trying to do something different and complaining that it's not the same as every other space game.Otherwise, devs have confirmed they're planning to adjust the maintenance costs and availability of parts and I would recommend playing with reduced maintenance when you start the game until that point but having done so I have been highly enjoying it.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand why they have missions which makes u deliver cargo after a certain time in the game. Sure u can go different ways to waste time and actually get at the delivery spot after that specific time, but there are beds in the truck which u can't use to skip time?Once u have a cargo mission that only needs u to jump once it's pretty dumb. This would mean u have to jump to the location, jump back and finally jump again to arrive 'after a certain time' Because if u don't, u end up sitting in your cabin doing nothing for an hour, yes a real hour.This makes no sense at all, you have express jump 'highways' which are extremely expensive, this shaves of 20/50% off of your paycheck (depending how many jumps u take to waste time). Either make the pay checks more or make the jumps cheaper. Why does it have to cost money in the first place when it's part of the core game?The way you interact with 'spots' to buy/sell items or get jobs are extremely annoying, the back up parking to lock yourself in and interact with the shop and/or mission board is becoming boring after a while. At least have the jobs on the dashboard screens in your truck.Also, weighing and cargo controls are way too often.Would I still recommend this game? I really want to, but it feel like I need to give the game on more go.I actually rage quit after I decided to wait in the cabin for a timed mission and ended up dying because I shut down some systems to preserve power. Because battery's/filters and electronic parts are EXTREMELY expensive compared to job paychecks.And when u die you have bills to pay which made me end up 4000 in debt, keep in mind one mission pays around 1000. and takes aprox 10/15m to complete.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Having finished all the side jobs now, I think I can give my review of this game.Yes I did come from playing the Euro Truck and American Truck sims, but I saw videos of this game pop up, so I decided to get it myself, and I can say I wasn't disappointed.First off, I think the game looks absolutely stunning. Seeing the aesthetic of the different areas you can drive/fly to are simply awe-inspiring. I'd say they knocked it out of the park. And there's a definite appeal with some of the onomatopaeic sound-effect for the controls in the cab which just sound extra satisfying, whenever you hook your truck to a trailer, or when you slam the jump lever. And the added instance of having to look to flick the right switches adds a more joyful involvement with your truck, a miniscule that some hotkeys can't seem to scratch.Controls are fairly easy to adapt to, even after numerous instances of having sticky key warnings. Though as of writing, the devs have released an update for keybinding which is a plus. I'm aware of complaints of HOTAS controls not being available, but I believe it is on their list of priorities, so I'd give them time and patience so they can iron out all the kinks for it.Yes, the AI can be awkward, especially when there's impatient AI trucks honking at you for merely passing by. And often seeing some new trucks arrive, only to drive straight into security checkpoint barriers, which is nothing if not hilarious.I am aware of issues regarding missions not unlocking in the game, which I didn't have a problem with whilst I played. Hopefully the devs can work out the fix for it!As well as the tricky piloting/driving in some sectors, I do enjoy the involvement with looking after your truck.; replacing worn components and even doing spacewalks to carry out repairs. Again, another element which hotkeys can't match sometimes.If you've enjoyed mellow games like the trucking sims, then I'd say give this a go. Though the game is only a couple of months old at time of writing, I'm looking forward to see what the devs are cooking up for the game! Well worth a pick up!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I think this game has a great foundation and I've semi-enjoyed playing.... a few glaring issues that I'm faithful the devs can fix. I was playing this on Mechanic mode, in case this matters.Firstly, hull damage. Love-tapping a pebble at about any speed results in at least 50% hull damage and a near-guaranteed breach. This becomes frustratingly repetitive when you go through more challenging systems. The hull really needs to be able to take a beating. It should be doing 20% MAX for such a small object, and that's only if you hit it at about 150. I can understand if you hit a building or massive boulder going a significant speed that it would wreck you, but for right now the damage system is dramatic.Batteries and UCCs. It would be great to have a method for charging batteries while on the ship. I had high hopes that the shock cells (?) would provide a function such as this, but it does not. The batteries have two separate values, health and charge, which implies that you may be able to charge them. I really hope this comes later. Changing difficulties and settings in-game is a MUST for a game like this. There's a lot of balancing playstyle and features to tailor the experience and I really don't want to start a new game every time I want to do this. Lastly, and the most frustrating of all, is the AI traffic patterns. Trucks stopping and U-turning out of nowhere, ramming into you if you dare to slow down or stop to repair a hull breach or change a battery for the umpteenth time in an hour, and you always pick up the bill for it. A few hundred here and there adds up, especially when it's not your fault at all. There needs to be either work with the AI traffic patterns or a system that better detects player fault and maybe even the AI paying you insurance if they hit you. With all of that being said, the concept, art style, and immersion of the radio ads and music are truly brilliant, and I look forward to changing my review to a positive one when improvements are made. Please don't take my comment as negative or bashing, but rather constructive feedback. Thank you devs :)

_childDocuments_.review: Very cool take on trucking. I played the demo when it first came out and it had a few issues but those are all cleared up now. The controls feel solid, very accurate when you go to hit a switch or lever. It actually feels like your the pilot of a space truck, you have total control and even some outside cameras at your fingertips. I really like the fact that you have to exit the rig to fix leaks and use fuel cans and much more. I do own flight controls for my other games and hopefully those may be integrated into the game in the future but as of right now, im happy with how well the controls already are. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Really nice atmosphere, and great decision to include "space legs" gameplay. Standing up, walking around, and interacting with the truck's cabin is such a great feeling, especially seeing as it's tied into the maintenance and upkeep of the vehicle, and not just walking around for the sake of it.The omission of keybindings is odd, but I find the default layout decent (if a little unorthodox). Granted, the gameplay could massively benefit from HOTAS support. Maybe one day devs? Please?So far so great. Looking forward to see what the devs implement based on the feedback :)
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Hello there, dear devs, one of the star truckers on the phone here! Got some thing to say after 5 hours of playtime, though most of them are complains, there will be a talk about upsides, I promise.And let's start with them right away. First, theme - it is handled really well. The levels do be looking marvelous, as well as the textures with the low-poly style. I really enjoy the wiew outside the window during the rides on the road, sometimes maybe a bit too much to hear a loud horn somewhere up front.Second would be optimization - great job on that, my Asus Vivobook Pro 15 runs the game on highest settings with no problems, though I have not encountered midgame levels yet, and might feel some freezes here and there in the future, but overall it's really good. And thanks for not taking much space with the game files too, love ya indie developers for that.Third, comes the music - the radio addition to a car (spaseship?) game is always the right choise, and the tracks are nice too. Not all that relaxing, we don't want to sleep on the road, so the punchy beats of rock-n-roll hit you in times of need on a trip with a nice slam.Fourth is localization. Thanks a lot for adding russian and other languages into the game. I am not considering myself to be bad with english, but it's definitely nice to see your native words being used for terms you're truying to understand and learn. Big shoutout for that.This is all great features, even if they aren't special. Doing things right is much more than truying to stand out. But now I will have put my complains on the table. I will not be bragging, as the game does interest me a lot and I will stay with the community it forms for the brighter tomorrow, and I hope my vision of this product will be taken into account of further development to improve the game and make it more accessible and enjoyable.First will be the difficulty, out of which my choise was normal. I am not against the game being challenging, but here I feel like some aspects just outrigt crawl behind and strangle you out from nowhere when you least expect it (sometimes literally, talking about em filters here). My first game started with me delivering the tutorial cargo to the delivery point, when I accidentally lost control for a moment and apparently hit the trunk too much. After detaching the container, I was greeted with a summing up screen, on which my salary of 500 or so bucks was owertrown with a penalty of 573. At least I didn't had to cover the expences this once, but later I also got hit by a meteior on a great speed, and from that point on, my run was basically doomed. With not enough cash, broken truck, broken cargo and energy running low, no guide book was able to save my ass - I made about 2 more trips, broke my spase truck completely and started a fresh game. Of course, this all can be called a skill issue, and I will try to give it doublethough myself after playing on easy and custom difficulties, but in my eyes this is not how a game about delivering cargo should feel on normal difficulty. I read a rewiev form a fella who played hardcore and reached lvl8, and he mentioned filters and energy being huge problems, as saving money for them on that stage seemed impossible, so he ended up softlocking himself on a same state with not enough supplies to continue playing. Please, think about the game from the perspective of all the newcomers and try to do something about balancing the skill floor for an average novadays gamer. Oldies still got hardcore and custom to play around, so this should be fair enough.Second complain (much less detailed, I promice) is thecontrols - I do understand that this is also a skill issue type of a problem, but the feel of what we got now is just too cluncy to be enjoyable even during learning process. Movement in 3D enviroment in all the directions is a rare example in videogames of first-preson experiences, and there's a reason for that. There is a 3rd person to assist this problem, but I am personally assured that I must be able to handle all the thing from inside the cab if I want to.Third, (here comes my personal neatpick) it seems that the world is quite empty. Yes, this is space, but inhabitet space. It would be nice to see (em, maybe there is some of thoose things on mid and late game levels, sorry if I go ahead of myself, sorry if so) some parking lots outside, more sighns, neon add banners and more transport types. Maybe space stations containing towns, which you're able to see underneath the fibre glass. More background action, like occasional starfalls, nebulas and black holes, or some big ships jumping in and out the hyperspace. This is all for the future, of course, as the game is raw enough now to think more of the next occrance.Fourth: bugs. Not a lot of them I encountered, but the ones which were here are good enough to be concerning. Like that one time I went out for the lost cargo, only to find out half of it got stuck in the texture walls and cannot be retrieved. Or that time when I put the container on the untaken bedshelf, then opened it, and then it refused to close because the to got stuck in the ceeling. I am hoping that this will be the priority of your work for now, even if I wish for thing uptop to be worked on as well.Fifth, and final for now, another neatpick: radio adds. They feel too real. I hate them IRL, and I sertanly do not enjoy them more in my videogames. Please, make an option to disable them.And, this is all for now. Gotta go sleep, so will end it quick: I like the game, and the overall score for me is positive, but there is a lot to be done, and I'm counting on you guys. Best of luck, and see you around, space truckers!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: When I first saw this game, I was looking for a game to play that I could enjoy and relax while still experiencing the fun of space. Star Trucker is a unique blend of sci-fi and simulation. It takes the familiar concept of long-haul trucking and transplants it into a vast, awe-inspiring cosmic setting. The result is a relaxing and challenging game, with a strong focus on realism and immersion.What Works:Stunning Visuals: The game's visuals are a standout feature, with breathtaking vistas of nebulas, distant planets, and futuristic cityscapes.Realistic Physics: The handling of your massive truck feels weighty and responsive, adding to the sense of realism.Immersive Atmosphere: The game's soundtrack and sound design create a captivating atmosphere that draws you into the world.Challenging Gameplay: Delivering cargo across the galaxy isn't easy. You'll need to manage your fuel, oxygen, and cargo carefully, while navigating treacherous space lanes.What Doesn't Work:Steep Learning Curve: The game's complexity can be daunting for newcomers, with a steep learning curve.Limited Replayability: Once you've completed the main story, there's not much incentive to return, aside from exploring the open world.Overall:Star Trucker is a bold and ambitious game that offers a unique experience. While it may not be for everyone, those who appreciate simulation games and sci-fi will likely find a lot to love. If you're looking for a relaxing and challenging game with stunning visuals, Star Trucker is worth checking out.Rating: 4/5 stars

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutly love the game, it fun and its about the 2 things i love the most in a game, space and trucksI do wish there would be food and drinks and some sort of irl survival to it, like u have to eat and drink and sleep sometime, hopefully that will come in the future, but other than that 10/10 game love it big praise to the devs for this amazing game

_childDocuments_.review: I so want to like this game, the graphics are great and the flight is a lot of fun.  However, and its a big one, trying to dock with a station or cargo is a horrible experience.  I have had the benefit (or misfortune) of getting to hitch a rig a couple of times in my life.  even the basic truck with only a simple rearview mirror was more forgiving than this system was to line up.  A system that doesnt provide alignement until you are right on top of the item and a 'generous' alignment setting that still requires almost perfect alignment to have any hope of a connection against a cargo that flys off if you so much as touch it, makes this game too much effort for any kind of enjoyment.  Add to that the cost of goods and the small amount of time your consumables last and you have a game that looks fun but is difficult to enjoy.  I do hope that the docking system becomes simpler or they add an automated option for those of us that want to just enjoy the game, as well as make it so that the player can at least break even on a trip, i would be willing to try this again.  But for now, its only for those who have a really good 2d spatial sense or can spend hours lining up a cargo.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good game. Especially if you like American Truck Simulator. Yes, this is a space hauler game. But, they really gave the truck spaceships a real big-rig truck feel. It seems best played with a controller. By the time you finish a few hauls you will get the hang of flying/driving these trucks/spaceships. They did a great job on the physics. The game has a great soundtrack. My favorite song being the main menu song. An interesting aspect of the game is that you have to keep your truck in working order. You have to keep power cells, control circuits, and air filters replaced on a regular basis. Otherwise you leave yourself stranded in space or pass out due to lack of oxygen. So you have to manage the money you earn between maintenance and ship upgrades. I would recommend this game for those that like the hauler genre of game.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Truck Simulator in Space, manage your rig's vitals, look for salvage, avoid asteroids, safely deliver cargo, and explore the cosmos. Live the dream of living like Ellen Ripley before she got attacked by a xenomorph. Did notice there is no current method to map controls so keep that in mind before checking out. Hoping they add HOTAs support in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: the first 5 or so hours you trick yourself into thinking its a skill issue "that is why i keep crashing". then all the shops run out of batteries and you realise the one spare air filter you had is used up and they costs more than an hour of trying to get the lest useful controls to work for you. plenty of revues are like "give it some time its just a skill issue" this isn't a fromsoft game, i wanted to truck around space looking at cool stuff listening to a book or podcast, i cant do that cos the controls require that much concentration because one little mistake and your suddenly in 6k of debt on a load that has a max profit of 2k. and half the time that mistake is all the local shops are out of batteries and your O2 generator is spluttering cos the last place you were also had no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ battery's.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: So it is a good game, and it is fun. and it just came out so some things are to be expected.but the batteries... the dozens and dozens of batteries, and trying to find an air filter when you need one. or a gas station oddly enough. suddenly there were none. but more importantly during the pyrite job while I was stopped and waiting out a solar storm I got a colision warning and a hull breach and when I could finally get out to sort it, the truck started moving and I had to fight it to get back in, then I realized that it was the solar storms pushing me around, not sure if that is meant to be a thing... but it shouldn't be.other than that I'm running the game in 4k on high with 60fps and I've been hit by a couple invisable objects and another truck drove into me in medusa somewhere while I was dropping off a container and I got the fine?? I'm just chalking it up to the game is early.it is a lot of fun and a very beautiful game, fortunately I know what tnt stands for so I got galaxy wide bragging rights :P
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The developers have broken the mold when it comes to a space trucking game.The graphics during a space jump is just amazing.The different sectors designs are unique and troublesome in their own rights.The beauty that each sector has as their "background" is well designed and created.The livery, hood ornaments, exhaust pipes, grills and sensors are very well designed and crafted.The story line has been very well thought of and the process of getting the necessary upgrades so you can enter the other regions.All in all I would give this game a 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun, but the difficulty on the "Normal" mode is far too hard, 9 hours in and I'm 2.5k in the red haha some is my fault but it's more battery, computer, and filter manager than a trucking simulator, also the needed parts are so expensive that it would take multiple loads in the start of the game to get 1 air filter, I stopped playing for now.  Going to try the suggested Custom mode since stopped playing my original save on "normal".
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Needed another 6 months to a year.Pretty fun idea but driving for 2 minutes before having to go into a loading screen (hidden as a warp cutscene) to drive for another 2 mins before dropping off cargo.The recommended game mode needs balancing as everything runs out of power too fast.Small 'nodes' to drive around in (think single city in ets/ATS).No keybind customisation.Overall I'll probably still play when I want to relax but in hindsight it feels more like an early access demo
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: As a huge fan of sci fi and American Truck Sim, I expected this to be a perfect game for me and I'll be honest, I wasn't 100% sure what I expected. The atmosphere is spot on, just enough tongue and cheek for American trucking nostalgia, but the "roads" are less of a network connecting everything and more of just random strings that don't feel like they connect anything. The controls are also overwhelmingly picky, with the slightest touch of a joystick or button and your truck either doesn't move or starts flying off making it near impossible to stay on said "roads". The maintenance minigame is a great concept and cool at first, but I can easily see where it'll get tedious as it just seems to be "replace power core/O2 filter" or "go out of truck and place patch". If the controls were more manageable I'd say recommend, otherwise I say hold off.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Visuals and Audio are really nice .Feeling of space trucking is there .This is really good game in ganre that  is not easy to pull off.Be warned tho  this game (at least the beginning ) is hard .If you don't have any expirience flying in other space sims start with lower difficulty settings , save often , and prepare for a lot of swearing. Unfortunatly i think that the difficulty curve  is quite steep, and the game does little to help with it.  That for me is the biggest problem for now for me in this game .
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Id like to start by saying that this is a very good chill game. Ive enjoyed the feeling of both the simplicity of moving from one place to another, combined with multiple things I need to keep track of to make the game engaging. However, a few things would hopefully change in the future to make this a great game. Mainly the damage to items in the truck. There's no way that an object getting dropped from the shop into the truck, or placing it on the ground normally causes it damage at all. Just a bit harsh. All other damage to myself and to my truck however is my fault for going 200km/h into avoidable space junk.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty fun, lots of people complain about inventory management, saying batteries and air filters run out too quick, but I completely disagree, that is the most engaging part of this game- having to keep an eye on those things while getting shipments from one sector to the next keeps me conscious, otherwise I'd crash into an asteroid or something.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Needs work.  Slow and not super balanced, even during the early game, which is more tutorialized.  There's a lot of subsystems that are all fun to manage, but the overall experience doesn't seem to gel out of the various cool ideas.  Not recommended right now, but will give it another shot.Edit: The standard mode needs balance tweaks, but the custom mode lets you get something that works a lot better.  Lowering battery drain and bumping payouts goes a long way to deal with the battery + air filter balance issues.  It's too bad you can't modify the settings after starting the game, because it really feels like you have to tweak it to get the experience you want.There's QoL issues as well, minor gripes but a lot of little friction points.  You can't turn lights on while not in the chair, or check the map in the job listing screen.  You have to dump items out of boxes before you can sell them, and go to the airlock in order to reopen the store / job interface.  Salvage would be more fun without constant airlock travels (even using a box, because lots of things don't fit in the boxes).It's still really slow, but that's probably what you want for this style of game.  I'd enjoy some upgrades for auto driving on the highways and auto docking / alignment, which would make this a bit more like elite.  No joystick controls if that's a critical decision maker, but mouse and keyboard controls worked fine for me.With the initial difficulty options set up correctly, I think this is a recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: the first problem when you play the game arrises with the powercells, without these your truck isnt working, however, the drain is MASSIVE and no way to recharge this except form buying it. second of all, to get a good fundamental grasp you are over 2h of gameplay so its already outside the steam refund policy, third, there is no way to contact the devs trough social media except an e mail, which makes asking question and getting answers a pain to deal with
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic. love the cab, everything is functional / great diagetic design/ layout. Its easy to interact with while giving you lots of information and also feeling like you have power/control. (CIG/star citizen could really learn from this!) the atmosphere is great. Only thing i don't like at the moment is the scenery is a bit too dark and the batteries are a bit too short lived in the standard mode. but these could be easily patched later. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, I'm going to be real, the game is good for a short bit of fun but whoever came up with the 'just in time' deliveries is actually insane. The idea that if you arrive too early for your delivery you can't do anything for 20-30 minutes is genuinely poor game design, there is a bed in the truck that could have been used to allow the player to speed time up or at least as a truck stop that can be used to let the player pass time without expending fuel or core energy. It's such a bad game mechanic that has actually killed my motivation to play any further.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Its definitely a lot harder than it looks. Piloting a giant rig in the vacuum of space is a whole different beast and can feel like your driving on ice if you're trying to turn while going too fast due to having nothing to stop your inertia other than your dampeners. It's a really fun and unique experience though especially with the cassette futurism art style and the literal space trucks that can look like space trains half the time when you watch the ai drivers slink around the void of space, the space highway signs are a nice touch too and helps form this games identity into something I wanna see explored more. onto my gripes however mostly with the way the ai trucks. I've found myself having to reload a save a couple of times now due to the ai crippling my truck and my cargo after flying into me which usually happens to me after arriving at purity. The game just came out so I know there is 100% a few things that'll be tweaked later down the line and I'm hoping the issue of getting rear ended is going to be one of those fixes. But hey it could be a feature for all I know, bad drivers do exist. Also I've found that the game penalizes me for careless driving even though I am doing everything I can do drive save so I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong. On a lot of the pseudo highways passing trucks tend to blare their horns at me and I'm not sure why and it makes me feel like I'm driving carelessly as every time this has happened I've gotten penalized for careless to which makes me frustrated and leaves me wondering what I'm doing wrong. These two things could be completely underrated and for all I know honking could be trucker language for hello but I digress. Overall the game has been a blast so far but also fairly challenging mostly due to my own mishaps but other than that I absolutely adore the unique cassette futurism aesthetic this game has and it inspires me to get creative and make worlds with something as silly as space trucks because they look cool and its fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Godawful controls and you can`t rebind them, maneuvering is literally pain. Tutorial is garbage "just read a handbook" while everything breaks down around you with no idea where to go or where to get replacement parts.Gone refund this. After thousands of hours of ETS2 and ATS this looks like a insult.

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty fun but it's also pretty stressful at least for me.It's always a struggle to keep your energy cells for all systems running and when you have this under control  you have to change fuses. But besides that it is fun to "drive" a truck through space.In addition to accepting delivery orders, you can also buy goods from stores cheap in one sector and sell them more expensive in another this gives a bit variety.Something what bothers me is that the ego perspective is almost useless. You can't really see things around you or more like its hard to estimate the distances which is a bummer because driving with 3rd person cam takes away the immersion.I am excited to see what comes next. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that just needs some more time and love from the players, especially those who have given up wayyyy too early on it. Yes there are issues, but not game breaking/ruining ones, and here's to hoping development is smooth sailing from here. Also, imo, this game deserves so many more players :(To preface: yes, I played the demo and loved it so maybe I'm a bit biased here, but I'll do my best to stay neutral. Also, I don't have many hours yet of course but have played a good bit since launch 3 days ago.I'm not gonna lie, I was worried; demos are great but you're never quite sure how the actual game will turn out.  I'm happy to say that this game did not disappoint for me. Between the different game modes and straightforward gameplay I'm still enjoying the crap out of this game! I love the maintenance mechanic so you're not locked in to only driving and it's great that I can see all the statuses for my truck from the drivers seat. I love the compactness and quick turn around for the game early on, it made it so easy to get the hang of things and I can easily see haul times getting longer, if you want, as you unlock zones. I also love that fact that I can hop on and off this game whenever I want. It's such a chill and simple game that doesn't stress me out so I can play it for 15 minutes or 2 hours. Finally, big vehicle go brrrrr so my brain is happy lol :)I've seen a lot of people complaining in these discussions, and yes there are bugs. I mean what new game doesn't have them? This doesn't bother me though, because there's not an insane amount of them and none are too game breaking. For example, one of the worst I've seen/read about right now is that you can't take free cases from salvages due to them and their contents disappearing later. No this isn't great but I can live without it for now because it doesn't ruin the core gameplay at all. I'll be honest, these are gonna be cheesy, but I love the idea of the CB radio and talking to the convoy members, however I don't like the lack of direction. The options making it a "choose your own story" are really cool but I wish I had context for each, like just a bit of small text or something from the AI explaining the situations better. Another complaint of mine is the lack of ability to see market prices or job boards outside the specific sites, like I'm sorry but we got galactic highways and expressways that we basically teleport to but no way to communicate outside the sites?Lastly, is my issue with the lack of tutorial/explanation of game systems. Yeah there's a manual in the glove box below the dash, but I didn't know it was there for the first 2 hrs so I had to figure out repairs and such on my own for things not in the tutorial. (Also, UCC statuses don't show % in the dash :()What I really don't understand is why people are complaining about power drain and money management for the recommended game setting, I've read so many people saying things wear out too quick and loads don't pay enough. Well I'm sorry but in my experience this just isn't true. Proper management of resources just takes some planning, and no much at that! Through (mostly) careful driving I've consistently kept my rig running while getting my cash up to 5000+ multiple times now. I've been able to afford extra cases, parts, body work, upgrades, etc. and this is even while I've fully wrecked my hull about 3-5 times already!I love the game and it reminds me of playing things like farming simulator where you can change settings to make it smooth sailing or high maintenance or somewhere in between. Any way you play it though it's a game which I find very nice to, no pun intended, space out and chill in. Also, as someone who likes space games I like the idea of taking more mundane earth'based activities into space, because why not?! Yes the game has issues and it certainty isn't perfect or 100% complete, but it's good for what it is and it's not grossly overpriced or anything either. Another thing, people need to give this game some more time, not everyone is gonna like it but it's great for what it is!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This game looks so good it's accidentally tricking normies into buying a trucking sim game - one literally marked 'Automobile Sim' with user tags - and then they leave negative reviews whinging about how 'tedious' the game about... hang on let me check my notes... driving a truck can be. It really does seem like there's a disconnect as people who are hearing about the game purely through hype/content creators are simply hopping on the bandwagon and then realizing they aren't the right kind of neurodivergent to genuinely enjoy a game about balancing survival mechanics and doing a good job delivering a trailer of cargo from one place to the other.Sorry, neurotypicals, for once us autistics get a pretty game. It'll be fine. Gentle jabs aside: I have been following development of this by following Monster and Monster on TikTok for what feels like over a year at this point. I was well aware of what state the game was in at launch. I had a bit more caution going in. I've also seen the 'discussion' about balance. Frankly, I don't see the issue. I picked Recommended knowing it's a trucking sim, and guess what, it does a pretty good job of simulating the premise of being a trucker. Truckers are constantly balancing buying consumables and doing a job where if you even slightly mess up, you incur thousands of dollars in fines. It has problems. I've jumped into a system where, just as the game gives back control of the truck, it glitches location so the truck clips the ring and completely destroys the trailer. Manually save at the beginning of each job/mission you take, save every now and then if you do multiple jumps, and genuinely have a think about what kind of experience you want before initially picking your difficulty. You'll be fine.The in-game music is amazing. I love their commitment to having an entire bespoke soundtrack of in-universe songs. The voice acting feels on par with the characterization you experience in A Day of Maintenance or Hardspace: Shipbreaker. Well worth the money IF this is the kind of game you'd like. There's very little to the game the trailers does not explicitly communicate. There is no clever twist that, actually, it's a trucking game with combat. It's just a trucking game with the flavor of an extra axis of control over the truck.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The idea is cool the game plays well i highly recommend it it does need some balancing the rewards are not enough to cover the costs of transporting but they can be adjusted i only refunded my copy because i couldnt see myself personally playing it for long periods of time i already drive a lot for a living i needed more excitment
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I give this game a thumbs up for one simple reason.1. It does what it set out to do.Now if you're not into the trucker simulator games then you can go ahead and skip on this one. It's not anything different from those except it takes place in space which actually makes it a lot harder than those other ones and more complicated.If that sound appealing to you then this won't be a rippoff, you'll enjoy the game. It's not broken, it's not asking for too much money, the graphical quality and the sound quality are great as is the stability (at least for me) and the overall idea.In fact there's a lot of good things in this game which makes that 25 dollar pricetag seem even more appealing.But there's some negatives too. It's a lot harder to deliver or recieve cargo in space and it's a lot harder to maneuver in space making the gameplay downright frustrating. Your truck is made out of tissue paper, otherwise how does it break so often and so easily. And the AI of the other vehicles is ridiculously dumb. They ran into me several times despite the fact I did nothing wrong.Also the controls are super awkward and hard to manage or learn. If you didn't like those other trucker simulator games you won't like this one. but if you did like those games then you'll like this one. If its your first time playing one of these....good luck.But I give it a thumbs up because as far as I can see nothing is broken, the price isn't ridiculous, the idea is cool and the gameplay is (more or less) legit. But if you'd like a more in-depth look at the game feel free to check out the review on my YouTube Channel (link below).Otherwise, thanks so much for reading and I hope I managed to help some of you out there spend your money wisely.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: The game is good if you are willing to learn how to fly this thing correctly. It's not an Easy fly around game like No Mans Sky or even X4. If you can live with that the Game is fun.Docking backwards and dock on Cargo backwards can really be frustrating if you are not into that. But I have played harder games. It's just not super easy at first. I like the maintenance you need to do in and out of the Truck.Only thing i don't like is the not so good performance no matter what setting I use in some sectors the frames go down to 50 FPS in others its around 70 to 80, would like it to be everywhere at least 70 or better 100+....I hope some performance tweaks from the developers are planned!
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: First off i would like to explain that i began the game in custom difficulty, so i didn't have the same experience as the other reviewers. Even so, the control are a bit of a pain, i hope they fix this in the future by allowing us to remap them. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very good game nicely polished ! Indie gem for people who like space simulators. The truck movements are slow, take some getting used to but once you're accustomed with it its very pleasant. The visuals and graphics are very original and very pleasant. It's a shame there's only one vehicle tho, I'd loved to pilot other space trucks.TLDR: if Elite Dangerous and Truck Simulator had a child.

_childDocuments_.review: I like it. _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: To keep it short, if the aesthetic and the general idea of the game interest you I say it's worth giving a shot. _childDocuments_.review: A dark and brutal future, where there is no safe harbor.  Even while docked, your batteries and air filters run down.  The bed in your sleeper cab is unusable for a good reason, for falling asleep in this world is a death sentence.  The last thing you hear, before asphyxiating in your sleep? An echoing call, repeated a hundred times: "Things ok L.J. ? Looks like you've unhitched from the trailer."
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was an in-between thumbs up/down vote, cause this game is neither good or bad. It just feels that it missed the most important thing that makes logistics fun in the eyes of a trucker. Hear me out:The game itself looks good, the concept is brilliant, the ability to go first person and into EVA mode right in space is great as well... so why the negative?The heart of all haulers is the journey, its the things you see along the way, the different highways, the changing weather, the traffic and ultimately, the satisfaction that you've done a longhaul and have made it there after a long drive which felt eventful, challenging yet rewarding. This game has a bit of everything, but its missed the long haul part. These journeys between stars are simply taking the gates... then Yay you've arrived at the next system within a few seconds. Now go park your load and be done with the mission.... WHAT?? thats it? what about the traffic? What about asking for docking permission? What about being assigned a parking/landing bay?? what about having the ability to swap out your truck to a different model? none of these are in the game as far as i can tell.For a true space trucking game, one must take a look at a few other games which gives a sense of belonging and immersion. How about adding the following:1. Piracy - This is sooooooooo needed in a space logistics game where the player is only tasked with delivery. Give the players the option to choose different routes, do they want to take high security (Where police roams) space or risk it by delivering faster going through dodgy space where the player has a chance of being targeted by pirates. Delivering early earns them more money and reputation. Allow the player to upgrade the trucks with light defense systems like auto turrets or armor plates... later through research, the ability to turn their truck into a blockade runner meaning their warp drives can't get jammed by pirates.2. Freedom to chose - You give them a mission to pickup and deliver cargo from system A to system B... its up to the player to legitimately deliver these cargo and earn rep, or risk it and sell it to the market earning them more money but losing heaps of rep with the faction giving them the job. Make it that they can be bountied by the police.3. Less than legal contracts - Make some contracts high reward, but high risk, asking the player to deliver cargo from System A that resides in high security space to a destination system B that resides in lawless space. Some of these contracts are setup to scam the player of its money, but if the player can deliver the cargo there, then Big big big rewards.This would've given this logistics game a sense of space trucking with its own uniqueness spill that to be honest, is already in a lot off other space games that isn't centred around logistics. Even the earliest iteration of Elite Dangerous's courier missions seems more interesting and somewhat rewarding than this. Not saying its a bad game cause the concept here is there, it just needs a good core and reason for players to continue delivering, tempt them to do the wrong thing and reward them for resisting, attract them to take dangerous contracts and spice things up with pirates or illegal goods which can get scanned by police... forcing them to take less than safe routes... you know the spill.GL with the development guys, if any of these features are added in the future, then ... I'll be back.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserves more credit than what some of these reviews are saying...Battery draw: Yes this can be annoying but there's no penalty from going to an easier difficulty or creating a custom difficulty and setting the battery draw and consumable consumption rates to low. This drastically reduces the amount of times you need to do maintenance and allows you to focus more on space trucking.Key re-bind and HOTAS support:I too use a HOTAS for most sim games but the game doesn't support it... YET!!! The devs are aware we all want this and at a minimum we want keybindings, both of these features are going to be implemented soon as it is at the top of the dev teams list to fix these issues. The keyboard controls are fine too, clearly we all like custom controls but i have no issues with what they are now which are:Space bar - AccellerateShift - Decellerate/ReverseWASD - Pitch/YawQE - RollBugs and support:The game has a few very small issues that can pop-up from time to time but my personal experience with support has been amazing. They replied within 12 hours of submitting a bug report and assured me the dev teams are aware of the issue i submitted and even provided work around for the issues to reduce any impact they have on the game.Its a freshly launched low price game which offers tonnes off game play so yea it is going to have issues, hell even AAA titles have more issues than this and this team is far from as large and are charging like 1/5th of the price tag.Conclusion:Give the game a chance and don't review bomb it if one little thing irks you, the devs need to know the issues so they can fix them so i urge anyone to report their bugs on the RAW Fury support page. Ill leave the link in the comments below if needed.So far ive had a blast playing this and im going to continue to so hopefully more people will give the game a go!!

_childDocuments_.review: This is NOT a space truck driving simulator.  It is a space truck maintenance simulator.  As others have stated the economy is brutal.  Not made any easier by the DUI (Difficult User Interface).  ETS2 and ATS are not in danger from this title.  The real charm of this game is in the story.  But the maintenance costs make the process of making money and upgrading your truck a brutal challenge that, IMHO, ruins the drive a truck vibe.  Your futuristic truck could desperately use a satnav system.  Finding your way safely through a system is at best a challenge in and of itself.  God forbid you drift off the well beaten path, you'll damage your truck and the cargo costing you money you can ill afford.  Money both in terms of bonus pay outs, penalties and repair costs.Maintenance is what really kills you.  Apparently I can fill my truck with fuel, but a generator is technology outside the reach of the future.  Because you are in constant need of buying and replacing batteries.  IF you can find them at a reasonable price a 100 charge battery is $500, 150 charge battery is $1000.  Yeah, 50% more go juice for 100% more price.  Don't let the battery drain completely either, lose core power and you are now on a ballistic path to a crash and costly repairs.   This is all assuming you can actually find some batteries.  I just replaced 4 of my critical battery systems,  pulled into a shop and there wasn't a battery to be found.  Air Filters?  You need those too.  4 of them.  At $2500 each.  I got a few thousand stashed in the bank, thinking maybe I could stop and invest in a truck upgrade, but then I had to replace 2 air filters and some batteries, plus some UCC modules and I was down to $300.  So you better hope you can actually find what you need WHEN you need it at the best prices otherwise those prices can soar even higher.  Did I mention your truck breaks and the components wear out at an alarming rate.  Batteries for the gravity system go so fast you end up having to buy extra batteries just keep your stuff from flying all over the cabin.   And then the UCC fails and your stuff goes flying anyway.   And something is CONSTANTLY failing.  Would be fun to just be able to drive the truck, but honestly you spend all your time in the stores, or making repairs.  The couple of miles you drive on a delivery is an all too welcome break that doesn't happen enough.  You drive a couple miles to a gate, jump to a system, drive a couple miles to a gate, jump to a new system, drive a couple miles, drop cargo and done.  And in that time you consume hundreds of dollars worth of fuel, because $1000 of fuel is only good for about 50 miles.  I REALLY wanted to like this game, but I'm not masochistic enough to truly enjoy it.  And mind you, I have managed to mostly avoid the worst aspects of the punishing penalties for failure.  I had an NPC truck make a U-turn right in front of me once, with no chance to avoid the crash it cost me my entire delivery payout, an entire battery for my suit to make repairs and then costs of repairs.  In that instance I just killed my game and started over.  I can't imagine ever getting out of debt.  Save often and scum is probably your best option.  I really shouldn't HAVE to save scum to overcome a poorly balanced experience that fails to reward success.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best games I've played this year, very immersive with a lot of content, slow but very fun progression, it's not for casuals (even though there's a casual mode) if you want to play as intended, there are some challenges you don't just sit on your ass for 5 hours like ETS, you're a space trucker not a truck.Warning: if you're not too smart you won't be able to handle the battery management, I'm not gonna tell you what IQ you need but it's NOT like ETS, you upgrade your truck and these upgrades actually help with the management (part of the progression) so yes it gets easier later on so my advice is to play on recommended and not change anything.If you put the consumption to low in settings you won't have to change anything for hours, it's way too low imo, it gets boring real quick, but slow-witted players might enjoy this.Controls are also very intuitive, keybinding isn't necessary unless you have physical issues maybe, don't be discourage by these reviews.Same for truck behavior I can back up in the mag lock in a few seconds now, clearly these people are bad drivers in real life, the truck reacts to your action through the camera which is obviously reversed, it's good for your brain.Can't wait to see what the devs bring later on, the potential for this game is huge, as long as they don't dumb down this game for casuals coming from ETS/ATS.

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, and considering the size of the development team they've worked miracles to put together such a polished product.Star Trucker had a bit of a rough start with fast depleting power cells and truck systems that were a little too sensitive, but since the most recent patch this has been addressed with larger capacity cells and a few behind the scenes tweaks.They story line part of the game is fairly rudimentary in terms of missions, but is well written and has some fantastic voice acting and characters. It's a little short, but hopefully in time they'll expand this as well as the skill sets that you can work through.Levelling is reasonably paced, and there's a decent amount of specialisations to unlock. My main criticisms of the game would be:- Not being able to run multiple trailers from different jobs together, so you can haul more than one job at a time and drop off trailers along the way, or pick more up.- Multiple trailer physics - as someone who's driven an articulated truck, the behaviour of trailers needs to be toned down a little so they're less prone to flailing behind your rig. They're a little oversensitive.- Longevity - I'd love to see more story based content over time, as well as map expansions with more systems to explore, and even more types of cargo to haul.Outside that, the game is a fantastic piece of work, with stunning visuals, varied environments and really great mechanics.

_childDocuments_.review: What a fun game! It has the feel of "Tin Can" resource management, "ATS" early trucking gameplay when you are just squeaking by to make it down the road, and a whole lot of just chill and play a game vibes.In my most humble opinion for this review, you'll be best served by this game IF you play the game by its rules for a while BEFORE you go off to explore and make your own. The game itself is not terribly hard (on the "recommended" start settings), but it rewards patience. If you treat the game with respect and let the content come to you, you'll likely find a smooth and enjoyable ride out here in the stars.On the flip side, this game will punish the player if you rush to get to new content/zones or equipment unlocked. You don't need those things until you unlock them. And you are not forced to unlock them until you have the funding to back it up,However, one of the "problems" with the game, that many players run into, is that the new zones are locked behind story missions, and these missions can be BRUTAL. This is not a terrible mechanic in and of itself, but the game gives the player cues that say, "go do this thing," very early on in the game to get them progressing in short order. However, the cues don't slow down one the initial "tutorial phase" has run its course and the player is left with missions in their log. While this helps the player know they CAN continue on, it also draws the player towards content that they are not ready to handle (I'm speaking here from a purely in-game resource/economic point of view--player skill is usually not the problem once they learn the controls).And that's why, I believe, that this game has a "Mostly positive" rating. It is missing some design elements that would help the player know WHEN they are more likely to be ready to move on, in favor of saying, "if you move on now, you get more things!" This leaves the player fearing that they are missing out but when they try to get to the content they fail or suffer in game consequences that feel unfair and are left feeling helpless or unprepared quite early on--which makes the game feel "bad" to play.(We're not white-knighting here. There are things that need to be fixed and balanced, but this game is better than the reviews might lead you to believe.) Mostly, you'll see a lot of people complaining about money problems and the resource costs.There certainly needs to be balancing for delivery payouts (to align them with salvage work AND to have short runs balanced against long runs which do not pay out as well as they should) but this can all be mitigated if you take the game slow, drive carefully, and manage your resources. We all want to drive the long-haul long trailer rides...but we've got to earn it to get there.In short, if you want a positive vibe with this game early on, it would be my humble recommendation to play the game as a short-haul "one day's run" trucker for a good long while. Just go out there taking small jobs before moving on in the game. Spend some time getting into the world, building up your experience and your bank account via many more short deliveries over a longer period of time--treat it more as a role-play experience than a driving/action game.Doing this, you'll never need to buy a full tank of gas, thereby saving tons of money, and you'll make small amounts of money more frequently while using relatively small amounts of resources. This will create a "snowball effect" and you'll be happier as you see successes piling up instead of hitting a brick wall. It will also mitigate the costs of making mistakes like slamming into debris (or a highway sign--ask me how I know :D )Yes, of course you'll be itching to go out into the world--but if you take it slow you'll be ready when you finally do get out there.That's more than enough jawing. The game is fantastic! Buy it, learn it, and get on truckin'!

_childDocuments_.review: I feel like this game is going to have the same discourse around it that Elite Dangerous has. A euro truck simulator experience set in space albeit more akin to Pacific Drive than Euro Truck. Much like other games where you haul cargo, this one comes with the added caveat of having to more intimately maintain your S(pace)truck. Having diegetic systems is always a plus in my books, being able to manually press all the buttons and know that they all have a function is a great and satisfying feeling. The less UI on my screen the better. You'll be driving and zooming all over the place but try to stick to the space highway lest you feel your Struck needs extra debris decorations embedded on the hull.Similarly when playing other hauling games you'll definitely be wanting to put on your favourite podcast while you fly from point A to B. You can have some really long flights in this.Only criticism I have is that there's only one station for the radio which if you're not a fan of country music then you'll probably be playing with it turned off for the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: It didn't take long for this game to fall short for me. It feels "confused" as to what it wants to be and has a bunch of gameplay and design issues that ultimately made me decide to refund. I enjoy truck driving sims (for some reason I don't even understand) and space adventure games, so I figured this would be a home run but I was disappointed. Everything is a manual lever to do anything which for a simulation game, I would expect. However, the game is also in a fantasy futuristic world and setting and it seems completely unbelievable to me that in the far flung future of space trucking, there would not be more automation. We are already, right now in 2024, looking at how to automate the trucking industry in many ways. I'm not talking about self-driving either, I'm just saying, why do I need to pull a lever to engage a mag lock to dock? Shouldn't the docking station be doing that? Why do I need to pull a lever to go through a warp speed tunnel or whatever it's called? Can't I just drive into it when it's ready and active? If you have any vision impairment at all, you might as well skip this game. I am far-sighted and have a pretty low prescription for near "things" but I'll be damned if I could ever find the road/highway with any true accuracy. Sometimes there's gigantic arrows pointing you in. Other times I had no clue if I was on the highway or not. If you go off the highway you get hit by debris. If they are going to penalize players for going off course, they should at least make it so the highway course is WAY more obvious to see and be on. Also, z-axis control should be somehow locked in or have less impact in small movements if you are on the highway. Being able to move up and down inside the highway lanes is totally pointless unless you are trying to enter or exit from those angles. That aspect needs a lot of help, again, not looking for self-driving here but just a little more indication where the hell I even am.To support that above issue with the highways, let me also say the camera sucks. If you're hoping switching to external cam will help you when you get flipped around, it doesn't. It feels like when N64 was new and game designers / devs were still trying to figure out how to make 3D camera controls work well. So in addition to having no idea where I'm driving to, the camera is of no help at all and as difficult to control as the truck, which leads to my next issue.The truck drives like brick ♥♥♥♥-house. I get that they are giving you a feeling of inertia and weight and you have to plan your turns and such but it's really over exaggerated. Again, thinking of the far flung future, and simulation... there is no way in my mind that for futuristic sim realism, a vehicle like this would not be better outfitted with better/stronger means to control acceleration, deceleration, and maneuverability. Maybe you can upgrade your truck later with this stuff but it was not playable for me, out of the box. I only played like 45 minutes so maybe this is an unfair judgement but overall it lacked the "feel" of a roadtrip like you might get from ATS or ETS. You jump through warp tunnels to locations. Sometimes you need to do several jumps to get to your ultimate destination. There's not really a time that I could see where you're just cruising space and going past planets, nebulas, oort clouds, and whatever. I just expected this game to feel more like that rather than a jump from hub to hub. I never even got to a salvage mission so maybe it's there that this happens but I also don't love the idea of doing salvage missions. That sounded just, not fun at all to me. Really all of the above just immediately sapped the "fun" out of it which was the reason I chose for my refund.

_childDocuments_.review: I really want to like this game, but i can't recommend it in the state its in.most of my gripes Im sure will get fixed soon, but they are as follows1 the most annoying on to start with is "Just in Time" missions. you are provided with a time window to make the delivery, i and apparently meany people assumed the time displayed is the time you are expected to make the delivery by, but no it's the time you have to arrive at the sector and then make the delivery,  any way small difference shouldn't matter if you arrive early you can just wait right? ... right?yeah no, in my case i had to wait for just over 30 minutes in real time to continue with my mission.you would assume the bed in your cabin would bring up a waiting screen but that not implemented.2 This game is very hard to make a profit, I've been playing for around 10 hours now and I'm in 10,000 bucks worth of dept, this is mostly because the air purifiers are 2000 each and have to be replaced often, i'm not sure if they are bugged or if the user manual needs more information but the health of the filters decrease faster then the filter bar.3 bad cockpit visibility. i don't think this will get fixed, but you bump into thing quite often because you just don't see what your about to hit due to the bonnet being so high.  there where time i leave a shop and then directly crash into another vehicle because it was obscured by the bonnet. the only way to avoid this is to play in 3rd person, but i would rather not have to. 4 hidden mechanics. with the game balanced the way it is you have to learn hidden mechanics in order to turn a profit, like this means you will fail your first play through,  I call this stuff hidden because its not explained in the user manual in the glove box or anywhere else in the game.I think this game could be great but it's not their yet

_childDocuments_.review: Brilliant setup, good balancing and a novel take on the hauling business simulator. Making free-roam more than just driving your vehicle around. Challenging regions with unique issues to navigate, a simulator trucking tree that you'd expect from such games, and to top it off a little narrative driven plot to open up new regions and not make you feel you're the only one roaming about in space.Get out of your seat, get out of your cabin (don't forget to put on a space suit) and get right back in your seat to get the heck out of dodge! Comprehensive systems, realistic integrated systems that require components to help stay alive and on the floor in a space vehicle.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is lacking. There's no charter model. You talk to these npcs but you never meet or see anyone. There is a part in the game where you go to a "party" the screen fades to black and you just get to hear party noises, they tell you how crazy it is. They don't show you. That in my opinion is a glaring flaw. This game also feels like a battery hunting sim, it does not allow you to recharge batteries. _childDocuments_.review: It's not a bad game, but I think it has a bit of an identity crisis.It's not as realistic as any Truck Simulator game with controls, repairs etc... but it's also not full on arcade with a high level of customization, different Space Trucks, upgrades, etc.. so it would turn into more of Trade / Management game.It can be kind of fun, but I returned it for now and will keep it on my wishlist.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since Cowboy Bebop's "Heavy Metal Queen" the idea of a space trucker fascinated me. I loved that episode - the whole series of course - but that one really was a great one for me. Just a bunch of space truckers with their little baubles and customized interiors. The space gates that brought them from one place to another. A seemingly innocuous group of people that have a big impact on the space around them: making sure things get from A to B. Would it be automated in the future? Maybe. But the idea and atmosphere that the episode brought out, and that this games brings out, is that you are a necessity in the grande scheme of interstellar life and I kind of feel like it when I play this game.The visuals are great and you can see wear & tear on your truck. You can upgrade it and gain levels to get better access and improve your space truck. I hope to see different types of trucks. Ideally not behind a paywall but it seems many a game tries to become a live service and make the half-life of their games go ad nausea. I don't know if this dev will go that way, but I like this game.The only thing I do not like are the controls. Not customizable and a bit clunky. It did not like my PS5 controller I had connected via a cable, and kept on losing connection. If the controls could be customized, that would make it better, instead of just being able to choose inverted or not when steering. All in all I recommend this game and I believe I will definitely hit a 1h = 1€ ratio at least, and probably many more as I turn on "Life in Baghdad" and venture into the vastness of the space lanes.See you, Space Cowboys.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: As-is, I'm going to have to non-rec this game.It has a lot of potential.  However, at the moment the game is basically a battery installation sim.   You buy batteries, you install them.  You take a load somewhere, and you have to buy and install more batteries.   I like the mechanic, but it's far too needy of your attention, and it's constantly interrupting the core gameplay loop.  What's worse is that the lower level batteries, the ones with less power, are more economically viable.  You can purchase two 100 power batteries (200 battery power) for about $1,000 or you can purchase a high-end battery with 200 battery power for $2500.  That doesn't make any sense, and makes it cheaper to have to manage your batteries more often.I like the game, but it needs work.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: From my perspective, it seems like they hastily slapped a truck into space without giving much thought to the mechanics. As someone who loves and is passionate about outer space, I find this game’s design choices quite offensive.The concept of this game—a truck simulator set in space—is intriguing. However, the actual game design and gameplay leave much to be desired.Docking System: In reality, the International Space Station (ISS) has five docking ports, and the docking process follows the International Docking System Standard (IDSS), guided by radar, visual aids, and computer systems. Unfortunately, the game's docking system is a complete mess. Players are forced to manually dock their "truck" to the station using an overly complex and clunky method that feels like it belongs in the Middle Ages. It's disappointing that the game designers didn't take the time to study how real space stations operate.Gameplay Guidance: Early in the game, the gravity system's battery is deliberately designed to run out of power. However, the game does a poor job of indicating where this system is located. I wasted a lot of time trying to figure out if the battery could even be recharged. The in-game manual needs to be much clearer about these mechanics.Battery and Oxygen Usage: While managing contracts and the gravity system while docked at the station, I noticed my battery continued to drain even though I was already docked. This is an incredibly frustrating design flaw. To make matters worse, I died due to a lack of oxygen because I couldn't repair my ship while docked. This is simply poor game design.Field of View in the Truck: The truck's field of view is terrible. I tried to stay inside the truck to operate it, but it was nearly impossible due to too many objects obstructing my view. The interior UI of the truck desperately needs a redesign.Overall, this game has a great concept but is terribly executed. I do not recommend buying this game. Two hours is not enough time to fully grasp how flawed the gameplay is. Worse yet, it feels like a scam, as you can’t even get a refund after 2 hours play.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good but really hard at first. The trucks are difficult to operate and get around. I have only played the standard game mode but the truck batteries and all the maintenance is too much and everything depletes too quickly to even enjoy the trucking part. Also, the other trucks in the game don't seem to care about you. I brought a delivery across the galaxy just to get rammed by a truck coming out of the warp gate and the came charged me a $200 fine (kinda dumb). Other than that this is a good game and I want to see more update and features. Buy it but also understand that the movement is difficult to get the hang of and you have to pay for the mistakes of the other drivers when they crash into you for no reason.

_childDocuments_.review: It is what it says on the tin. It's pretty lush, handles nicely and has a nice amount of fodder there from the top. I appreciate both kinds of games and I'm enjoying this for what it is, tho I'll be honest, I wouldn't mind riding out the gateway jumps for a bit longer, even if it was 5/10 minutes, with the odd course correction  or something, maybe as an optional to save being taxed or as an iron man style thing?On think that does annoy me tho is that sometimes the AI will just plough into you while doing repairs.... even when you think you're parked out of the way...

_childDocuments_.review: 6 hours in and I'm having so much fun playing!  I know a lot of people gripe about the keyboard key binds, but it's not like you need to learn a ridiculous number of functions. The controls are more simplified (especially on controller) than your typical truck sim. I use a controller to play this game. I would call this a trucking "lite sim" with a a Sci-Fi twist. It's fun to listen to the NPC banter that occurs over the CB radio at certain times. The DMCA free radio station is pretty cool too. Totally gives Smokey & the Bandit vibes, only without crazy police chases lol!Hauling multiple loads is not available until you unlock a skill tree, and even then, it's limited to hauling multiple trailers that are part of the same job. You can't link up individual trailers from different jobs. Hopefully that changes down the road.Honestly though, it's a great game that is both chill but also requires precision at times.

_childDocuments_.review: Far more in depth survival/simulation than expected in a good way! Game looks wonderful with decent voice acting and missions to continue along the progress in the system. Recommended mode feels fairly hard at first when you are learning the ropes but once you get the systems down at driving, planning routes for jobs and vehicle maintenance then it all comes together. The game challenges you to properly plan your actions and do your best to be prepared for unexpected situations. Super fun game!

_childDocuments_.review: Before you play it:Try to read more comments since clearly the correct expectations for the game have to be set before playing.What to expect? I fell in love with this game and i'm pretty sure it's because i've set my expecations on the right path.- It's not ETS2 with long distances - distances are usually pretty short and try not expect ETS2 mechanics from this game.- the game puts emphasis on managing resources and taking care of your truck- It's a space - i repeat a SPACE, no up and down - space- People complain that the game is too difficult and i'll be honest - i'm playing on the hardcore and i have no reason to complain. Beside me crashing 200m/h into a rock (i was peting my dog), i had no problems in hardcore to sustain my ship/truckPROS:- OMG you actually can walk around the truck, you gotta press buttons to turn this and that light on and off. You press actual buttons in game instead of keyboard buttons. For sure that's more difficult and might even be an artificial difficulty but it's hella engaging and i wouldn't change a thing about it. I love pressing looking around the cabin for a button to press. Love it- another OMG is that you can go out of the truck and move around it, you can be an astronaut in space, collect resources outside in space and get them into your truck. Love that.- The game clearly shows that the DEVS had idea for this game, they knew what they wanted to do, they didn't just copy and paste cheap version of ETS into space - they knew what they wanted to do and they did it hecking well. IMO most of negative ratings are from people that expected ETS in space and you just shouldn't compare those 2 games.- Price fluctuations are great, especially that it's important to manage resources. You can be a truck driver and a merchant in one :DCONS:- I love the game but my labyrinth makes me vomit while playing too much of it. Thats why i probably won't play it any longer than i did. Very unlucky :(- Most people complain about the game being too difficult, i don't find it difficult at all even on hardcore, but i guess you should take that into account- If you think about it a little, the truck with no vision on the bottom makes no sense. There were too many times i've been thinking why ♥♥♥♥♥ is 70% of the vision obstructed by the engine... If one wanted to create a space truck, one would do whole front a window... but i guess you just have to deal with the game design.. but yeah thats the flaw - it looks cool but its impractical
