_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, I'm going to have to leave a negative review. I was looking forward to this game and generally like to go into games blind. However, I didn't really get the opportunity to play the game because the controls are significantly different from what I'm used to. I don't play a lot of space games, but in both Star Citizen and previously Star Wars Galaxies, I was able to fly the ship comfortably. Without the ability to change my keybindings (at least, not that I could see), the default setup—where W and S control pitch and the spacebar is for thrusting (with shift for stopping/reversing)—just isn't playable for me. After too many years of instinctively using W for moving forward and the mouse for changing direction, I just couldn't play the game.Additionally, I couldn't find a way to thrust up (like using the spacebar in Star Citizen) or thrust down (ctrl in Star Citizen). I won't be requesting a refund, though, as they are a small dev team, and I'm happy to contribute to their funding.I will definitely revisit my review and replay the game once I'm able to better control my ship with customizable keybindings or different layout options.

_childDocuments_.review: This game really shines in the first 10 hours of the campaign. It hooked me with how immersive it felt navigating a big vehicle through these cool environments. I was especially having fun with going in and out of debt, and carefully choosing tasks to keep my head above water while simultaneously moving the campaign forward. It reminded me of a similar enjoyment I had from GTA Chinatown Wars many years ago which has you travelling the map, buying goods low, and selling high. The voice acting over radio comms was very good, and the one radio channel and tastefully rarely played ambient music were phenomenal. I swear that lonesome guitar would only ever kick in out of nowhere right when I started craving it and humming it in my head. Nicely done on the sound design. I am shocked how this game got such good quality music that fits so perfectly with the unique world.On to my criticisms, of which I have many. But when I like a game a lot, my game design brain kicks into overdrive on all these things that would have made the experience even better. The game is held back in these many ways.Game design considerations (some mild spoilers below):-There comes a point after 10 hours of playing carefully when you suddenly find yourself filthy rich, and you buy out every single upgrade to your truck in 2 or 3 trips to the workshop. It was honestly more fun when I was under pressure of repeatedly going in the red and possibly getting my vehicle repossessed. Even though this will practically never happen, because a 4 day deadline to get back into the green is an insanely generous amount of time. After suddenly becoming rich, the game design felt like it was falling apart - devolving into mindless repetitive tasks just to be able to see the next story beat. There was no more planning or reacting to any danger in the entire game any more, and that's where the game falls short.-EVA (space walk) was very underutilized. There were many story beats that almost seemed to call for cool EVA moments. For example, finding a stranded trucker and offering to do some repairs on their truck. Sabotaging private network relays floating in space. Potentially going inside Moon Baby's Father's abandoned home to search for clues to the story. Going inside a space penitentiary to deliver spice to a chef. But these moments would just resolve with some dialogue or a screen fade to black and sound effects. Fairly late in the game, you will unlock ping scanners to identify scrap to recover via EVA. But this is so late in the campaign, that you are already at the point of completely filling up your airlock from floor to ceiling with goods from stores. So the airlock is unusable at that time in the campaign. It's just not worth the time and effort to clear out the airlock for one sector of scrap recovery only for it to be completely full of junk again after you visit a shop again. My favorite part in the whole game is one where they did the EVA justice. You have to go on a spacewalk to clean up your mess after a rough night of partying in Spark City. The dialogue is also so cute here. And then your ship is an absolute mess after all that time absorbing lightning while partying. It was a tense introduction to the electrical sectors, and even more exhilarating having gone in for the first time with only 3 spark plugs for protection. But the short-lived moment fades away, and you'll upgrade the ship to withstand most lightning impacts anyway.-The skill tree is full of lazy features that don't really change the game. Upgrading cab weight limit is the only feature that I was excited to get. Every other "skill" is pretty much just gaining access to delivering other types of cargo each for the same increased XP, and increased pay. It makes no meaningful difference to the gameplay in my mind when I picked heavy loads, multi-trailer loads, perishable loads, fragile loads, etc... Deliver quickly, and safely no matter what. Some of those types maneuver a little more clumsily or have to avoid certain sectors with extreme temperatures, but that hardly matters at all. Even the multi-load trailers are effectively like one single trailer.-What would have been far more interesting and engaging would be if the player could unlock the skills to carry 2 and then 3 trailers. With complete control over docking and undocking each segment, this would open up the game design tremendously for planning and managing several contracts with different destinations at once.-Also on the topic of skills or upgrades, it would be so much more interesting to have options to completely alter the gameplay in and around your rig. For example, it would have been awesome to unlock some webbing that would keep storage crates snug against the back of the cab even in zero g. I found online that the way to do this is to jam them into the shelving units by opening the lids of the crates once inside. That is such a weird solution, and I can't even tell if it is intended by the developers. Yet it is very important to learn this trick.-I beat the game with less than half of the skill tree unlocked (rank 17), which goes to show something is really out of whack with how stingy this game is with XP.Final criticisms are generally about the UX which needs some improvements:-It could be so much fun to tear through asteroid fields at breakneck speed, but the asteroids spawn so close in front of you at these speeds it is usually not safely possible. I was incessantly switching in and out of first person to tap the ping scanner and narrowly pick out newly spawned dark asteroids against the dark skybox. I found myself repeatedly frustrated when a collision would come as a result of the short spawn radius for this type of game which is all about efficiency. Ironically, Junk Field sector is one of the easiest obstacle courses to navigate because most of the hazards are spawned into the entire level. So why wasn't this possible in all the sectors?-Even with all the UI icons on the screen, the game fails to show the necessary info especially when you are focused on speed and efficiency. Toll booth markers don't spell out the connecting sector name unless it is at the edge of your screen. Space stations don't reveal the exact shop and job board bays until you are already so close that your approach trajectory is completely wrong. The bays don't even have any visual indicator of what service they offer except for in the frustratingly close-proximity UI icons.-There is a 'Z' key to zoom into the reverse hitch camera, and it really needs to have a toggleable setting or it needs to be rebound to the right mouse click. Both of which are not possible. The zoom feature is completely useless because you can't hold 'Z' while using 'WASD' and 'shift' to line up your trajectory.-Pretty much every contract I completed would ding me with a $5-$20 "careless driving" fee. Even when I hit absolutely nothing. It was just kind of funny. It's such a small amount of money, that I didn't care to figure out why it was applied. Maybe it's because I was cutting off other truckers at the warp gates. But the contract completion notes should have more detail notes than these vague fines when you hover the mouse over them. One time I was even fined almost $800 for "public endangerment".-Dropping an item from literally ankle-height damages it. So weird, but I eventually found my work arounds of using the railing corner as a table.-Your seated character strangely lags behind the ship's extreme acceleration and decelaration. This means your mouse cursor will be thrown off from the hitch lever, ping scanner lever, and warp drive lever. This really needs to be fixed, because it is mentally draining to hyperfocus on every moment the game is perturbing my mouse cursor for 50 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I am changing my review from no to yes I do recommend. I am still jaded that a fine could be so high that it makes the run unrecoverable but I have learned a lot since my initial review. I have found the drop down on the map that shows what items are considered contraband and that has helped me not repeat that mistake. I have also played long enough on my new run that I have unlocked the hidden compartment to put illegal items in. Key to early game play is to avoid restricted items unless you know exactly where you are taking them and the route is clear. My new run is on Driver difficulty which is a joke. Yeah everything is easier to manage since things last much longer but the loads are also greatly reduced in value which makes you have to do twice as many runs to earn the same amount of money. {Note to developer} It's sandbox mode cant you let the player become over powered? Pretty sure that is the point of sandbox mode. Driver mode is boring. It takes an eternity to earn any real money with loads. I earn more money with trading. Repeating my sentiments from the previous paragraph, its sandbox mode, let the player have the freedom that they should have in said difficulty. The real issue I am having with giving a yes to recommended is now that I have learned how to play the game in driver mode, I want increase the difficulty but do not want to play the hours of early game play a third time just to get to that difficulty. I believe having a better "tutorial" on contraband would prevent other players from having to play thirty hours to simply avoid a game ending fine that is frustrating and does not contribute to the game in a positive way. Rant over. Game is fun but I think it will be a while before I start over AGAIN just to increase the difficulty. (Old Review below)Let me start with I want to and do love most aspects of this game. I am saying no to recommending this game for a couple game breaking problems. The problems that I encountered were on the recommended "normal" difficulty. I did not do these things on mechanic or hardcore which would make them more reasonable. There should not be a single mechanic that can ruin you on a "standard" difficulty. 1. Security checkpoints are fine, BUT they need to show you what items are considered contraband. Unless I am missing where is shows you then you only learn what is contraband, and where, is by trial and error. I had a few crates of alcohol on my truck and went through several security checkpoints without issue but then I went to purity and it was contraband there. The fine was over 20k and it was unrecoverable ending my run that I had already spent hours working on building. I enjoy a challenge but when one single thing can end everything. That is a poor design. 2. If you accept a cargo shipment that is picked up outside of the zone you are currently in, it frequently ends stating that you did not pick up the freight in time and fines you multiple times more money than the shipment was worth. This can probably be avoided by understanding jump times and when the quest ends but it is still something that should not be possible IMO. If there is no possible way to get to a load in time, it should not be an option.3. Fines are outrageous, at least early on, This may not be a problem later in the game but one fine can easily end your run. As stated previously, I enjoy a challenge, but when one mistake can make a run unrecoverable after doing everything by the book for hours, there is something inherently broken within the game. I have no issue with the above stated issues on higher difficulties. After having time to learn some of the things listed above on normal difficulty without breaking the game,  i would enjoy facing these challenges when I choose are higher difficulty. Having a single game mechanic end your run is the definition of hardcore and should not exist in the normal difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: Game got dinged on reviews a bit when it first hit the store due to some major bugs and an economy that was skewed a little unfair, but devs have been resolving all that, so don't mind the complaints about the economy from the day one reviews.So basically this game combines the trucking sim vibes from popular games like Eurotruck with the space trading vibes of games like X2, X3, X4, Evochron Legacy, and maybe a little bit No Man's Sky if we're exclusively talking about trading between stations. The game also includes vehicle maintenance vs the environment gameplay and is very "run based", so in that way it does have some elements that feel comparable to games like Pacific Drive.Eurotruck + space sim + Pacific Drive = Star TruckerOne mistake you don't want to make when considering this game is assuming it's a casual or cozy type experience. The simulation aspects in this game are kinda complex and diagetic and there are a lot of different plates you need to keep spinning when managing your funds, almost entirely related to maintenance and upkeep of your craft.Your ship requires fuel for thrusters, power cores for various ship systems, and a few ship systems also require circuit boards. Fuel is burned as you burn your thrusters. Power Cells lose their charge as your ship systems are in use. Circuit boards slowly degrade over time and need to be replaced. Some examples of these ship systems include artificial gravity (needs power cell and circuitry), oxygen (needs power cell), internal cabin climate control (requires circuitry), air filtration (requires air filters), mag locks (needed to hitch cargo and to dock at stations), space suit (requires power and oxygen recharge after use).The thing is, if you are using all of your systems at all times, you are wasting money, because you might be burning fuel when you don't need to, or wasting power when you don't need to, which means you are wasting money when you don't need to, because you have to pay to replace fuel, power cells, circuitry, and air filters. So in order to save money, you can use the newtonian physics in space to drift long distances (especially with heavy cargo giving you more momentum) and conserve fuel. You can turn off all the lights inside the ship when you don't need them. You can also disable the artificial gravity inside your ship when you don't need it (but be careful that you might damage loose cargo if you don't take precautions). When you are swapping out the circuitry in your systems, you have to remember to cut power at the breakers first or you will blow the breakers on the entire ship, which you then have to act fast to restore.There are a lot of tiny things to manage, and tiny corners you can cut to save money, and getting used to all of this takes a bit of time and patience as you are learning.Once you've got a handle on things, there are different ways to make money.  different kinds of cargo from A to B is the primary way to make money in early game. As you build up more of an income, there is also a secondary form of trading. Every time you stop at a store to purchase supplies (power cores, filters, etc), you can also purchase miscellaneous others goods that are just for ], such as pharmaceuticals, chemicals, foods, etc. You can even trade the supply items themselves (power cores, spare fuel, etc) if you want. There is a fluctuating economy on these, so you can buy low and sell high. Rather than there being a hard limit on capacity for these items, you instead have to watch the weight of your truck, since you are only permitted by SPACE LAW to have a certain weight. You can be randomly called to weigh in at a weigh station at any time, and if you are over weight, you will be fined. So whether you take the fine or dump the cargo, it hurts either way, so mind your weight.There is also  of course, which is the primary use of your space walk equipment. Salvage is eventually one of the best money makers and it can even get you some free maintenance (salvaged power cells or fuel etc). But if you dilly dally too long on some salvage you happened across, you might also get penalized on a late delivery if you are in the middle of a haul.The game does also have , if you want to be a contraband-hauling criminal trying to pass under the radar of the law, but you will not be getting into any dogfights in this game. You just haul the cargo and try not to go broke, get fined, freeze to death, burn to death, crash into an asteroid, etc. The game also has story jobs that you must perform at your leisure, and completing these story jobs unlocks new sectors of the galaxy for you to explore. These new sectors are more challenging and have their own simulation challenges. For example, one of the first sectors you unlock takes you extremely close to a star that is prone to random flares every several minutes. The external environment here is hundreds of degrees normally, but thousands of degrees during flares. During a flare, you need to pull a lever that lowers your ship's protective shielding, which prevents it from being obliterated by the flare , but the shielding also covers all windows, so you're forced to steer your ship via an external camera feed on your dash. The extreme temperatures also mean you need to crank climate control far into the AC / cooling range and probably increase air blowers, which means you are burning more power on climate control in this region. You CAN bake yourself alive inside your ship if you don't do this.Finally, I appreciate that this game is very diagetic as a sim.  A lot of space sim games just put literally every game function on 100 different keyboard hot keys. But in star trucker, you instead have a functional dash covered in monitors and buttons. All these buttons and monitors are functional and convey actual information. So instead of doing everything with hot keys, you use the mouse to literally push the button, flip the switch, pull the handle, twist the knob of whatever control it is on your dash. This gives the game a more tactile and immersive feeling and makes you feel much more that you are in the captain's chair. (Some things are, of course, done with keys, such as steering and breaking, etc).Devs have noted that HOTAS controls are coming in the future, if that's your bag.It's really a pretty interesting game that has the slow grind of driving for money as found in games like Eurotruck, but it's a more challenging vehicle to drive and there are many more numbers to watch, so if you sorta like things like Eurotruck but find them just a little too sleepy and wish there was a little more tension and management involved, then Star Trucker might work for you!It's one of those games where you need to be willing to suck a little and put up with a little frustration at the start while you get comfortable with the systems and learn about what problems your ship might have and what the solutions are, not to mention getting a feel for the economy and how to make good decisions in that economy. But once you get there, I think it's one of the more interesting sims in the job sim / space sim category and the only game that blends the genres in this specific way.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having thrusters in the appropriate positions, your truck can only go forward, backward, or rotate in place. Lining up your maglock to pick up a trailer, visit a shop, or pick up a mission is needlessly difficult and takes way too much time because of that, all the while your fuel and batteries are draining at breakneck speed. Without access to thruster control there's also no way to manually stabilize yourself, so you're forced to use the auto stabilization which you cannot toggle without having the camera inside the cab and looking down past the dashboard to press the button.Aside from the infuriating controls (and no way to remap them), there is space junk littered everywhere that isn't a "road", including directly in the path of you getting from the road to many destinations, like a dropoff, and the space junk is nearly impossible to see from any of the available camera angles.It's not fun to struggle against poor game mechanics that are intentionally designed that way to artificially increase the difficulty.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Where we are going we  need roads, actually.Right so, first off the bat: Star Trucker is a simulator game. Far from a  simulator, mind you, but it is a videogame that puts a strong emphasis in recreating a complicated machine, with multiple co-dependent systems dedicated to keeping you both alive and moving, and turns out, in the future your survival is a bit more hands-on than it is now.The first few hours of your playthrough will be both wonderful and terrifying. The game does provide a tutorial mission, and a reasonable manual, and your truck has so much stuff on it, with clicky buttons and levers to control from the lights on your cab to your AC, your thrusters, breakers for each individual system, flight assist, most of them with actual applications that you are encouraged to micromanage to get the most out of each one, and the larger part of them can, at any point, start screaming at you which will launch you in a mad dash to find what's wrong and how you can fix it while barreling down a space highway at 120mph, trying to complete the job that will pay for your next air filter.And I mean, this will really depend on how much you enjoy in-depth system simulation and more importantly, how relevant this simulation is to your minute-to-minute, but I was immediately hooked. I had seen nothing about this game until I picked it up, and exploring the sheer depth of all the fiddly bits in my truck was really cool, and resulted in moments I do look fondly on, like when I realized I was almost out of oxygen and had to figure out, on my feet, a way to replace my busted filters and race to a replacements shop, o2 level steadily decreasing, vision getting blurry, when I was like "wait! spacesuit!", managing to run the last few kilometers wearing it, finally reaching the shop and resolving the crisis. It's stressful at first, and I can understand how you can easily die during these first hours, and I can see players being frustrated at it. But if you are in the same spectrum that I am, man, it's really nice to come out on top at the end of it.As you finally start getting settled into the complexities of your truck while panickedly running non-stop jobs to just be able to stay on top of spares, you'll inevitably question yourself if you can even keep up with this, if you'll be able to reach the next filter change, if you'll find enough batteries before these go, running through systems, checking new shops, making a sense of what's where, and eventually, through much work and grinding, you'll finally reach the "mostly space truckin" part of the game.Your space truck flies... well, like a truck. You don't get lateral translation, however, you do have lateral thrusters that will keep you moving forward. It's more kind of like a boat, where it's more about momentum than direction, but once you get used to it, it's really great. Learning how to coast, what turns you can take at what speed, how to account for your haul, dealing with traffic, using the external cameras in your MFDs to get a sense of your surroundings... There's an external camera (with no hud), but you don't really need to switch to it. You can upgrade several aspects of your truck, and soon you will be piloting your cab as an extension of yourself, flipping around to dock into hauls and drifting a 3 trailer into a turn while well over the speed limit. Which, oh yeah, space roads.So you'd think you can just go from A to B in a straight line, since, well, this is space, right? Well, most of this space is filled with debris, and trust me that a single debris strike can become VERY problematic for your truck, so you'll want to follow space roads. This is something you'll quickly need to get used to, and at first it won't be easy because you don't get sector maps. You will need to figure out and get used to the layout of every system, and how to get from A to B with the least amount of pain. Every sector is unique and has it's own personality, from the tight and industrial Edgeburgh to the Outrun-esque Dependency Loop, the windy and dangerous Haze Way, some of them almost feel like racing game stages, and they are really fun to go through haul after haul after haul.To go along with this space truckin, you will sometimes get a little bluegrassy kinda music from time to time, and you can also turn on the radio in your cab, which will play a selection of rock/bluesy songs, all purpose made for this game, and all absolutely bangers.The main point of the game is to do hauls so you can stay on top of your maintenance which, after the first hours, is something you will have to deal on the regular but in a way, WAY more routine manner. Swap a few of batteries every couple of jobs, keep a few spares of everything, angle your hauls towards systems with cheaper spares, or several shops. You can salvage space debris and sell it too, which is very lucrative, but to me space truckin was my main gig and if you like your truckin, you're gonna get a hell of a lot of it, and it's  space truckin.Once you are in a good enough spot, you can start doing the story missions that, while have very paltry rewards, will open new sectors to play with, alongside a new truck subsystem to deal with them. They don't add a whole lot of complexity, but their gimmicks are alright. The story missions feel very disjointed, and their existance seems more out of obligation to somehow pace your progress through the game than anything else. They're not terrible, but nothing special either. The "story" ends abruptly at an arbitrary point, with no rewards, so it feels like there might be more to come in future updates, but as it is now, there's more than enough content to get 40+ out of it. Much more depending on how much you want to truck for the hell of it.Anyway, this is a really great game for what it is. The developers have said that they will rebalance how the maintenance side of things works so I would expect it to become somewhat easier to deal with, but right now I think it is alright, and besides, one can freely customize the difficulty of their games with 0 negative repercussions, if you find it too hard, or if you just want to space truck. But even so, having beaten the game in "recommended" (with "poor" engine efficiency) without having died a single time, I think the difficulty is pretty okay if a bit wonky.Absolutely recommended. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: If your favorite episode of Cowboy Bebop is "Heavy Metal Queen" this is the game for you! The "space trucker" vibe is perfect, and the customization and progression is rewarding.  The artwork is also beautiful, and the ability to walk around and personally maintain your rig is great.  You're not just a "model ship", you're the pilot.   I will say, at least in early game the payouts seem pretty low.  one load pays like 1,500, about enough to buy ONE air filter (your truck needs four to be fully efficient, and they degrade over time)  and a tank of fuel is like 1,000 as well.  maybe payouts get better over time, but early game is pretty unforgiving and grindy.   You really have to be mindful of the cost of maintenance.  You can set the difficulty lower to counteract that, but that's not how you become a super trucker, is it?  Keep the pedal on the floor, driver.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is brilliantly thought through in my opinion. At first glance it may look like "ETS just in Space', but there's more to that! _childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent blend of calm driving and survival. I see lots of people stating that the survival aspect and economy is too hard. I have played one save on the suggested difficulty for 12 hours and I've found it to be fine. It honestly seems to be in a perfect place right now. I always have full containers of spare batteries, chips and air filters. If I focus on hauling jobs I can slowly upgrade my rig while keeping my reserve parts high. The occasional accident, botched job, or god forbid, 10 000$ smuggling fee (I unknowingly brought explosive into Atlas Prime once) gives you a challenge, as you start delving into your supplies and becoming more desperate. Even so, if you focus on doing jobs you can overcome these challenges and that feels good. I've never been stuck somewhere, died or needed a haul. You just have to play smart.There are lots of beautiful areas to explore and the atmosphere is very relaxing and serene. The story line unfolds as you like and I enjoy that there isn't much financial incentive for most story missions because it forces you to just do you job, haul space cargo. Some aspects of the game are simplistic but at the same time everything works really well. I've come across almost no bugs and mostly everything is well thought out.Small gripes:-Please let me put the below rig camera on my left screen or put the battery charge one there. Those are my two most important screens and it sucks they have to share the right side while the left side doesn't show me much that's important.-Dear god, take the giant square debris proximity box off my screen cameras. I know debris is close, why do you think I'm using my cameras!? I already have a proximity light on my dash and the square warning text box covers exactly where I need to be able to see to avoid said debris! Super frustrating, especially in the solar areas.-I'd LOVE to be able to customise, or at least change, the colours of my interior.-Radio music, while fitting the theme of the game, is waaaay to high energy for the atmosphere of the game. The radio needs some nice low fi-tunes. They can still have a country twist, the music you get when entering zones is done really well in this fashion.Those are minor gripes though, overall a fantastic game. Props to the devs for knowing their scope and executing it perfectly!

_childDocuments_.review: Most of the negative reviews are because the game doesn't have the ability to rebind keys (which I do admit is very strange) and the fact that there are no vertical or strafe thrusters. And to the latter argument, how exactly are those gonna work when you have 1 or multiple trailers? If you want vertical controls, Elite is right there. This ain't elite. My personal biggest gripes are the lack of in system maps, and the fact that there are like 5 songs on the soundtrack, and listening to Space John Mayer for the 5th time gets a bit annoying lol. I do like the soundtrack overall though. Just very minimal unfortunately.In terms of gameplay, its EXACTLY what I was hoping it would be. Great podcast/ second screen game! Chill delivery routes through space, with fun little distractions in maintaining your ship. I tried leaving the designated roads a couple times and got my truck WRECKED so, yeah I see why those are there lol. But if you need to make a delivery quicker, I like that you can take the risk!Its too early to say whether or not the gameplay loop gets stale, but I mainly wanted to post this to combat a lot of what I see as bad faith reviews for what I think is a perfectly excellent game for the price!

_childDocuments_.review: The game is really fun so far! I see all the reviews about controls and what not, I played on keyboard and mouse. I didn’t mind, they seem okay to me. I have been enjoying it though. I think my main concern is just that, there isn’t a whole lot to do. Even a simple system where you have to sleep would be cool. I want to utilize the whole truck and have it be more realistic. Some probably won’t agree with that point, or even the next one of having the need to eat, and there being fast food places. Where you go through the drive through and what not. Again, this shouldn’t be the devs top priority, or maybe it shouldn’t be in the game at all, but there’s just so much potential. It really just feels like you deliver cargo and that’s it. Which is fine, it’s a very fun gameplay loop, but at the same time, it feels like it’s just missing something, and can feel a bit dull at times. I’m also just concerned that I’ll play this for a while, get bored, and move on. Overall I do recommend the game. It’s super fun and it’s a cool concept. I’ve enjoyed it a ton so far. So we’ll see what happens with time, if I get bored or if I play this for hundreds of hours.

_childDocuments_.review: The experience I wanted being a trader in Elite: Dangerous, but augmented by a very well-built world, and a superb art style, audio and soundtrack. _childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker Review: A Shiny Shell with No EngineAt first glance, Star Trucker dazzles with its sleek visuals and futuristic aesthetic, but once you're behind the controls, the experience quickly stalls. The gameplay loop is as simple as it gets: pick up a load, point at the gate, hit cruise, jump, and repeat. Unfortunately, the lack of depth in both the mechanics and the characters leaves much to be desired. The one-dimensional characters fail to engage, and the gameplay, though initially promising, rapidly devolves into a monotonous grind.While it might look cool, there's little substance beneath the surface. The game offers no real challenge, other than the increasing cost of maintenance, which feels more like a chore than a progression system. If you're hoping for a deep, engaging trucking-in-space experience, Star Trucker may be a road you’ll want to skip.

_childDocuments_.review: While the game's movement is difficult to grasp right away and the battery/UCC drain is overwhelming at first with some time you start to learn what needs to be done.  Here are some things i learned while playing and experimenting.-System batteries don't have to be 100% all the time as some are only drain power when in use(Mag system and Suit Charger). -Turn off the system breaker before removing the old UCC to avoid a short. -While docked you can swap the Grav and O2 power cells without issue as the station provides those systems. -Keep partial cores for use in emergency or for the suit charger as that system doesn't use much power, it's perfect for low % batteries. -Another key thing is that each system shows the price of certain goods. Try to buy ship components where the market is down so it's cheaper. You can also use this information to buy and sell goods across systems.-If you leave a Job board or Store menu, you can re-access it from the airlock door. This may be said in a tutorial but i had my door open and didn't realize until an hour in you could do that.-Buy containers to store Truck components or Trade Goods. Keeps them from bouncing around and keeps them safe from damage in the event of a Grav failure or collision.-Your truck keeps its forward momentum. So if you are going 120 mph and then turn to the left you will still be going 120 mph the way you were facing. You have to then thrust to add momentum in the new desired direction.-Air brake literally uses air, don't choke yourself out.-SAVE OFTEN! You will mess up Battery management, you will drop a UCC from too high up and bust it, you will hit Astroids/debris, you will hit trucks/drone/stations by accident. This game is unforgiving even on the normal difficulty, save often and reload if you've made a mistake. -Follow the side quests to unlock new ship upgrades and new regions.Hopefully these tips can help get you in a better place to experience the game and have fun.While i agree no keybindings menu is not right, they are working on it. That being said the keyboard controls grew on me and don't seem too strange to me right now. All in all if you like space, trucking, fun characters and a kick ass radio this game is for you. It's extremely fun as well as challenging, I can't wait to see what the developers add in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: The right game for you if you enjoy:- learning the docking procedure in Elite Dangerous (you can feel like a noob yet again)- the clumsiness of trucks (without ability to strafe), extended to the third dimension- parking in reverse, using a monitor (again, in 3 dimensions)- drifting- going for a spacewalk fixing your vehicle after hull breaches- walking around inside your vehicle and regulalry fix systems (especially if you liked Tin Can)The game has quite a learning curve at the start, but it shouldn't take much longer than 1-2 hours to get familiar with the controls. At the start if you're not comfortable drifting and maneouvering I would recommend to stay on the "roads" so you don't have to constantly dodge debris, and also to step down from the gas every once in a while. Turns out a space truck with 50 tons of cargo takes a while to adjust direction, let alone come to a standstill.I think the game does everything it set out to do, in a fabulous way. It's challenging but forgiving, slow enough to let you relax but never boring (e.g. there's no such thing as accelerating and decelerating towards a planet for 15 straight minutes like in ED).I give it a solid 9/10.Some things that can be improved:-  (nevermind, that just got fixed)- uninspiring skill tree: It mostly lets you accept more difficult contracts and increases rewards. I'd love to see more RPG style stuff in there- only one radio station

_childDocuments_.review: I highly recommend the game, but be mindful that you've got to like the following two things:> Inventory and resource management (you will have to switch out depleted cells and broken modules very often, as well as organizing your cargo load if you're like me doing a lot of scavenging and buy-and-sell)> Flight simulator (it's not easy navigating the sectors, the rig you're flying ain't no space fighter and you'll have to learn how to maneuver the highways filled with traffic and the huge fields of debris and asteroids in between)If you're on board with those, then this will be an excellent single player experience that I'm sure has quite the replayability potential.Some mechanics and bugs need ironing, but overall it plays smooth as butter. The controls are very responsive, and all the various game mechanics play into each other pretty well, although some should be expanded on. I, for example, find that shop prices swing a bit too wildly, since every time you make a jump you suffer from massive time dilation. I would love for there to be a way to predict these prices, so that buying and selling items could be more viable - not that it's useless at the moment, far from it! I managed a single run worth 26k dollars, 10 times more than the average hauling job. My point is, you'll find it quite annoying when a sector's shops that were paying extra for electronics end up being a dud by the time you've reached your destination. It's basically all luck, which I understand, but I would love for a more predictable system, even if only slightly, presented in game.The progression is good, with upgrades to your rig that make it safer, faster, more nimble and all kinds of other stuff which are all fairly priced (every level is a simple 250 dollars price increase). These upgrades also have a noticeable impact straight away, despite there being several levels for each system. You can't get it all on day one, but it is also very possible to grind your way up to the top if that's your style. Meanwhile, the xp levels seem to be a bit slow, but most of the unlockable skills serve to gain access to new types of jobs, so it's kinda fineAs well as that, story progression features engaging characters, nothing too crazy but definitely enhances discovery of new sectors to travel to, as well as being an overall fairly good "long term" tutorial for each new game mechanic (such as types of jobs, dangers you might encounter etc), and the whole thing is well disguised as these characters "showing you the ropes". Very fitting.Overall, a damn good game, definitely worth the price tag even if not on sale. Perhaps give it some time for the developers to iron it out if you're not entirely convinced yet, but as it stands it's a solid addition to my favorite games.

_childDocuments_.review: In general the game is not bad, it's well done and once you get used to the mechanics it is cool but it still needs improvement. It has no compatibility with HOTAS controller and there is no way to customize key bindings so you are literally forced to use that brainless keymap in which you use space to accelerate, shift to break, W/S for vertical alignment and based on every other game where you drive something, that is straight non-sense since is not customizable. Another big problem is the "momentum" of the truck, it doesn't work to keep the truck moving at a specific speed so you need to be using cruise control or struggle to keep a constant speed since the last thing you will see in your screen is the speedometer, but every time you are going to do a turn it will eventually throw your cargo to the direction you were going, I’m not a physicist so I don’t know if that’s realistic or not (and tbh, I don’t care, that’s not my job to know) but it’s annoying as hell even in not so high speeds. If it’s a feature, okay, but this lack of consistency makes it annoying even more while driving in the specified space-roads.I have played space-based games for quite some time and not having control of movement in up/down or left/right directions without needing to maneuver the truck going back and forth to reach a gate right below you is weird, if it's a base definition for the game since it's build around those american rigs that has no maneuverability it's fine, but why does we need to reverse dock everything f time we want to do anything? Stores, job listing, customization... everything has its own docking port that requires reverse docking and it's really annoying when you are buying something and want to get a gig and you need to waste time maneuvering just to get to another docking station 10 meters away from where you are already attached to.Speaking of annoying, I don't know if it's a bug or a feature but man those batteries and air filters got me nervous. The batteries once you start the game are crazy expensive and 1 gig allow you to purchase 1 battery, but there are 7 batteries that run out pretty quick if you use the cheap ones (that already cost much) but once you get more done the batteries seem to get cheaper and you can also afford more so it's not a big problem anymore. But the air filters are a different story, at first they are so expensive you can afford it if you keep your batteries replaced properly and after you get able to buy it, they can't be found anywhere in the first 6 systems. Literally every store has no air filter to be bought and you get forced to be rescued, lose a lot of money and once you get rescued and sent back to Atlas Prime the store magically has air filters again. If that's a way of showing how the recovery system works, well it sucks. Btw, air filters were still crazy expensive so I had to get a loan to buy 2 of them, another crazy thing because this was supposed to be a chill game not a "Fight for your life your unemployed slut" game.Another thing that bugs me off is that reverse and brake use the same key. When you are going forward and want to fully break you just need to hold SHIFT and it will eventually completely stop and that's it, but if you are in reverse and you hold SPACE you won't just stop, you are going to start moving forward and that is definitely not a good thing when you are always running out of batteries and air supply and even to sneeze you need to reverse dock somewhere.The game performs well though and has a great future, just needs to be tweaked more.Extra: That first cargo that needs careful handling with those ♥♥♥♥♥♥ controls in a brand new game you don’t know anything about is nerve wrecking, if I was not into this kind of game I would have refunded immediately because that was really stressful for a supposedly chill game.

_childDocuments_.review: Great game that really nails the aesthetic it's going for. Music especially is really on point. Only other little tip that wasn't so obvious to me: even if your rig doesn't have a hull breach, you'll still need to take it in to get properly repaired, otherwise any little bump will cause holes that need repairing.If the aesthetic looks like something you'd like, you'll almost certainly like the game. _childDocuments_.review: Tentative yes.I'm ten hours in, and for the most part it's a very fun game. Didn't even notice that time fly.We'll start with the bad, though: For a full release game, I've already encountered a bug where a bunch of items disappeared, and a bug that required me to reload a number of times and ate up something like 45 minutes. Pretty heinous.Other than that, judging whether an air filter needs to be changed or not is either A: something I haven't fully figured out yet, or B: poorly designed. With most components, they hit zero quality (HP for chips, charge for batteries) and you swap them out. These have two bars, and apparently when one reaches 10% they're useless? I don't know, but I've found myself suddenly suffocating more than once.The shock pads don't register as popped or not when sold.There's no readout on the terminals for chips. Maybe this is an intentional design, but it's mildly irritating. If it's an intended mechanic, I get it, but meh.The maybe bad: It's a relatively small universe, I'm only ten hours in and I suspect the endgame will be zero. Hope I'm proven wrong. (Similar games get away with this by having a stupid-large map making the same missions/jobs feel new).The good: The controls are weirdly satisfying. There's enough mass-based drift and sluggishness that it's a challenge, but the controls are responsive enough that you can, "get good," and whipping a space truck through systems.I played a lot of American Truck Sim, and backing the trailers into a drop zone in this game is so so so much less awful than in ATS. Very manageable with one, but I fear for the day I have to back two or more into a drop zone. I'll probably edit this in a rage if I do (but thankfully most drop zones can just be nosed-into).The trade system isn't a note-taking endeavor. They did a pretty great job on indicating how much of a profit or loss you're making/taking. Also when things are marked up, the average price is right there. Fantastic.Finding salvage pods is a pretty great mechanic. Using cargo boxes to reduce the amount of trips is a good use of other game mechanics. Well done with that.The setting and missions aren't mind-blowing, but they're pretty good. The game's pretty, the missions are detached (why should I give a crap about any of these people?) but entertaining enough. The dialogue is well voiced and often chuckle-funny.Customization (compared to games like ATS, sorry I keep doing this but it's a frame of reference) is mediocre, but not bad. Basically just change paint jobs. Kind of regretting the DLC with that in mind.The balance (in the recommended mode) of income vs. ship component/fuel degradation is actually rather well done. I play pretty safe and I'm generally well stocked, yet always have an eye on energy levels. Learning to check chips, I suck at that. The air filters are a mystery and I just hang onto a few extra and wait until I start suffocating before rushing for the space suit and swapping one out.Trade of standard/contraband is pretty well done. Supplements income well enough to be worth it, and sometimes you get lucky and make a good bit of coin. Or paper. Or whatever space money is made of.Docking is notably well-done. The controls are intuitive, the docking camera is fantastic, and once you get the hang of it it's pretty quick.Draw distance on small debris is also well done. It's small, and depending on star location/shadows it can be just tricky enough to spot to be fun, yet not punishing enough to make me fearful of going, "off-road."That's all I've got for now. I'll probably forget I wrote this and never come back, but if I do I'll edit over time.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: BEFORE YOU BUY -  9/10This game is like Star Citizen ( flight system without the combat ) + American truck simulator hauling. Imagine having to maneyver the NOSTROMOS in Space, like a gigantic submarine that float in the water. It's exactly that but in space instead.It's NOT HARD if you practice your maneuvering. At start, you will have to adapt because like any other game, you need to learn from scratch to progress. You can't be a PRO right away at everything.  So everyone who complains it's hard... maybe they didn't practice enough. I practice for few hours and made a lot of mistake, now I'm making TONS of money and seem to be able to maneuver my space truck comfortably.SURVIVAL: As for the Survival aspect, this game is very "challenging" as to ALWAYS keep an eyes on what's missing ( I mean "always" literally ). So if you like challenges, you will like this game. It will take trials and errors to adjust. But once you get the hang of it, you're good to haul like a BOSS.SETTINGS TWEAKING: You can also adjust the SETTINGS ( if you want easy mode... hum. Which is fine I guess ). But the point of getting better into any type of game, is to learn by doing mistakes and repeat, adjust, adapt, get better. I didn't tweak any settings. I just kept practicing. You don't get better by playing everything at "easy mode". I mean.. not for me.GRAPHIC is SICK. Wow.... if you have a good graphic card, you'll love the graphics garanteed. 10/10MUSIC : Only one channel I think but I rarely use it. Many complains about this.. this is not American truck simulator so you cannot wish everything to be to the same. Alternatively, you can simply open a YouTube video with a mix of song you like... or even better, use your own music in the background if you have a library ( Ex: Itune? )  So music is not an issue for me tbh since you'll be more busy not crashing into anything the entire time then to listen to Bon Jovi telling you "Life is Alright no matter what"... SFX: The sound effects are very "realistic" which add to the immersiveness of the game 10/10STORY: Oh boy, never thought I would enjoy the story in this... whoever wrote the story = 10/10  Very fun and engaging. Mission are also versatile. It's not the same thing over and over again. You do "crazy stuff" that makes you go.. WHAT DA F***... if you see what I mean.SPACE WALKING: Yes, you can go outside your space truck to float in space and fix your truck. Nice little touch.  Be careful of solar flare or you'll become a Supreme BBQ Roasted Chicken for sell in Space...ouch.DIFFICULTY: If you've never played space game like Star citizen or Elite Dangerous, you'll have a "very hard" time maneuvering the space truck. So my suggestion is for you to be patient and just keep practicing. It's "muscle memories" after that. There's no shortcut to get better. Just keep practicing. For veterans who plays Space Game a lot, this will be a walk in the park after trials and errors.KEYBINDS: Ah, yea, no Keybinds.... No Strafe Down or Up... does that bother me? Hmmm... not really. I mean, it could be great to have a strafe down or up option... but it doesn't kill my immersion of the game nor my competence in maneuvering my truck in space.SHOULD YOU BUY IT?:  If you like "real immersive" hauling in space with all it's velocity, damage from hitting something ( even a tiny rock ) which will have an impact on your truck... if you like crazy graphic design and a story that makes you laugh and enjoy the game as you go, then yes!If you hate space game and frustrating survival mechanic... don't buy this, you'll most probably complain it's too hard.. when it's not. It depends on how fast you can adapt. Everyone is different, it's a not a good or bad thing. It simply depends what type of player you are.See ya in space Commanders o7PS: If you see a solar flare, bring a BBQ Rib with you just in case. Thanks

_childDocuments_.review: American rigs floating thru space, how goofy yet the devs have actually nailed the concept and made it very believable. So many new games that are coming out now are missing the immersion or "vibe." Star Trucker does it very well.I started with the recommended setting but in no-time I was over 20k in debt. The survival elements of looking after your rig is very cool but while learning the jobs doesnt get you ahead but more into debt learning the ropes of the game.When you are here for the relaxing gameplay of cruising through space go to custom and lower the consumption to low. You still have to replace the batteries once in a while which is a fun game element but it doesn't get to frustrated.I really hope there are more Trucks/Space ships coming Perhaps some cabovers or actually more realistic space ships to haul cargo. With more of a interior to explore. Eventually hauling cargo can get repatative really quick so I hope this gameplay becomes a bit more engaging and satisfying as well.Also, would be cool to see some basic survival elements for the driver as well, Water, food, sleep. Be able able get off your truck and walk around the space stations to buy supplies or shop. Pick up new missions or task with bit of a engaging story behind it. So far I like it and I hope the devs are really going to develop and expand this game further.

_childDocuments_.review: If you were like me and played Elite Dangerous avoiding combat as much as possible just being a freighter pilot you'd probably love this game.I'll break it down as easy as possible.This is not a simulator.  Your rig does not maneuver like a space craft on a x-y-z axis.  It also does not handle like a semi from American Truck Simulator.  It takes a minute to really learn.  Sci-Fi over Sim.  Add a load and it handles completely different.Then there's the survival element which is no joke.  On the recommended level you will probably bankrupt quickly once, maybe twice.  There are batteries, circuit breakers, air filters and more to maintain during your travels.  Debris, space rocks and other traffic can hit and breach your hull forcing you to dawn your spacesuit and do some emergency repair.Skill tree unlocks different types of cargo, trip length, upgrades and new areas.  Different NPC's offer side jobs which unlock special upgrades.Visuals are very pleasing, great sound, and a fantastic Americana soundtrack.Easy thumbs up from me.
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the "I would rate it neutral if it was an option" cases.Generally it is a fun game, which I would recommend AFTER a few more updates/fixes.Currently the balancing of costs and income is a bit off and you basically have to play the game a few hours to figure out what you are struggling with and then restart the game with custom difficulty to make up for the balancing.For example:Do you like to micro manage each docking process or would you prefer to turn down how much aligned you need to be to successfully dock?Do you like to take breaks on your route to make sure your trucks systems won't give out in the middle of the road oder would you prefer to just drive?How much of an impact should an impact with space trash have? (On default it can force you to save scum quite easily if you are strapped for cash.)The other thing that annoys me is that you can take damage while being docked.You are in the way of an delivery drone? Too bad, now your hull has a hole.You docked in the middle of an electric storm? Better be fast while shopping or looking for a new haul before your systems get fried.Like I said the game is fun, but all these minor annoyances and bugs make the game frustrating in the long run.

_childDocuments_.review: **What I Think: This game has a lot of promise, and I love the actual gameplay of driving the truck through each sector. However, the constant need to purchase supplies, fuel, manage hull integrity, it gets a lot after the first few hours in a save file. In my opinion, the maintenance aspect of this game somewhat ruins the chill "truck driver" atmosphere, since I found myself sweating about whether I should fill my truck's gas tank, if I need to buy batteries (since there are 8 items that need batteries, with no way to recharge them), or if I could buy an upgrade for my truck for the shop. Oh, and forget about ever repairing your hull integrity, there is no way to scrape together $3,000 without being at risk of going bankrupt trying to buy the life support supplies. I really love this game, and I always feel bad about cranking down the difficulty since I should be able to enjoy a game on the recommended settings, but I find it hard to enjoy the gameplay when I am in a constant race against time to out-earn my truck's resource usage**Improvements: I feel this game is missing a few elements to make it really great. -To start, there is no place to rest and decompress. When docked to a station, your truck is still draining batteries, O2, and air filters. I wish, when you are docked to an outpost, you could get free O2 and batteries, or at least being able to exit your truck so you can do repairs while you are safe from debris. -Secondly, I have never been able to afford repairing my hull's integrity, the price tag is just too much. This means the slightest tap of an asteroid creates multiple holes, and repairing the holes takes time, which in turn burns more batteries and O2, etc. -Lastly, and this is the biggest one, there needs to be some way to recharge batteries. Maybe you drop the empty cells off at a station and return in a day, maybe the truck has a slow charger that can harness the engines to recharge empty cells slowly. No matter the method, there is such a drain of resources and no way to renew them, I feel like the least they can do is allow us to replenish at least one of the resources, and I feel that the batteries would make the most sense.TLDR: The gameplay of this game is really promising, and with a few quality-of-life improvements and a few gameplay tweaks, this game can easily be as popular as the big-name driving simulators. At the moment though, it is just a bit too grindy and stressful to fit the "chill trucking game" genre, but I have faith it will get there
_childDocuments_.name: Star Trucker

_childDocuments_.review: Fairly good, I've seen a lot of complaints from others that do not make sense. For one, there is a difficulty setting you can select that reduces the resource management/maintenance aspect of the game so you focus more on the driving/haulingTwo, personal goods trading can be done at shopsThree, longer drives are available later in the game, the early contracts only ask you to go a system or 2 over, but later on you need to go across basically the whole map.However, there are a few valid complaints,One, no key rebinding, I'm not a developer so I don't know how hard or easy this would be to implementTwo, no hotas/hosas support, although the devs have acknowledged that they are working on it.Three, not really a major problem but for whatever reason they made the spacebar accelerate and shift brake, and I find that choice odd.As for performance, it runs very well on my system of 12600k and 3070ti.For whatever reason, fullscreen exclusive mode has performance issues that bring framerate down to around 80 while not using the full power of your computer.But setting it to fullscreen windowed mode removes that problem entirely and I was getting a solid 144fps most of the time.Overall, it's probably one of the most unique games set in space I have played in a while because it isn't trying to be like all the others and is very stylized.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite having had a rough start at launch, this game is everything i was hoping it to be.Driving around the galaxy, hopping from one sector to the other, listening to the ingame music - everything is just perfect. The voice acting is phenomenal, the visuals are stunning and the physics are well simulated - it really does feel like flying a brick that weighs 500 tons! Luckily, i also feel like you can get used to almost all annoyances once you figure out what type of game you want to play (get on a custom game ASAP!), so at the moment i don't really mind the "recommended" mode being a pain to play. I'm sure that this game will only improve, the devs seem to be listening to a lot of our concerns, we can only hope that they'll get to work soon!

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is a sci-fi twist to a handful of our favourite "Dad" games.  To me, it's lodged somewhere between a trucking sim, a "simulator" game, and the " Space Truckin' " style game play from Elite/Star Citizen.  Uh...Okay, look--I really haven't put enough time into this game to give it a proper review.  But after playing it for seven-ish hours, I can at least tell you this: The game-play has its... "quirks."  Like, the story (and some of the voice acting) is mid, the hazards thrown at you can be a bit of a learning curve, etc.  This isn't the type of game where you can just plug in a wheel/joystick, set the controls and be on your way.  It's a GAME with rules 'n junk.  It's NOT a full blown sim.  In other words, please don't come into this looking for the games mentioned above because you WON'T find that here!So if you end up buying it, only to find that you don't like it--you'll find out within the game's refund window.  This sort of game isn't for everyone...but if your shopping addiction kicked in, you slogged through at a higher difficulty and were too slow to realize the game isn't for you... whatever, dude.  It'll just be another game that'll sit unused in your Steam library.edit: I initially wrote this review because I thought some of the negative press being given to this game (during it's release) was a bit... harsh.  I ended up rewriting this + removing the unmarked sarcasm (guess I forgot an /s or whatever.)  Maybe that'll stop the ATS fanboys from wojak'ing it in my IMs. 😂

_childDocuments_.review: This game is exactly the kind of relaxing sim I've been looking for. For years I've played Elite Dangerous and Euro Truck Simulator trying to fulfill the trucker fantasy but the former had way too much sitting around with jobs being very samey, while the former was too realistic for my liking with jobs taking very long and the driving not being very fun in my opinion. Star Trucker does its own thing and does it well. Aside from actually star trucking there are scripted missions that let you interact with a cast of truckers you become friends with along the way as well as the option to engage in trade on the side, allowing for more ways to play. Long hauls don't feel like boring highway drives or automated hyper jumps and take a reasonable amount of real world time. The way each star system is designed, and that fact you're in space, gives the player a choice to stay on the marked path or trying to take shortcuts between star gates, which trades the risk of running into debris and damaging your rig. Taking care of your rig breaks up the game play by adding a tactile cargo management system with consequences for not keeping up with part replacement. (This system was controversial at launch but has since been balanced nicely and game mode options let you tune your experience.) Finally I'd like to praise the art style and unique design of the game. Making your spaceship in the shape of a modern American tractor trailer is so fun and lets the game lean in to this not-too-serious tone.TLDR: 10/10 not-too-serious space trucking sim that lets you have fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Note, this is a MIXED review, but STEAM is forcing my to choose between yes/no on recommend: I choose yes because I think this game is very well built and will entertain you for long enough to justify its price (got it for under $20 on release day).PROS: great graphics, sound and space mechanics.CONS: forced storyline to get key upgrades and unlock the map. Infuriating design decisions: no straffing, cargo straps, not even magnetic boots, no HOTAS support on a spaceship?, 1st person game with no eye tracking (TrackIr) support, wtf?.PROTIP for game devs: if you are going to force a storyline on us, make sure it's really good (like best seller novel, or Oscar/Emmy nomination good). The biggest problem with this game is the TERRIBLE storyline you are FORCED to follow to obtain key upgrades and unlock new sectors.PROTIP 2: storylines are NEVER good enough, once play through them (or watch a youtuber do them), they lose all the value you spent in writing, coding and voice actors.PROTIP 3: some gamers like storylines, it's ok to put them in your game, but always provide a SANDBOX MODE for those among us who don't care for them.As of today 9/22/24, most of the current issues in this game revolve around bugs in the implementation of the storyline which prevents you from finish it if you happen to complete some quests in the wrong order, however, this only blocks you from finishing the story, not unlocking all but the last sector and getting 2 key upgrades.

_childDocuments_.review: After the recent (sept. 24) update, game balance has been adjusted and bugs fixed. The annoyance factor of the recommended difficulty was lowered. Better batteries have more charge per $. Airfilters and batteries are more common in shops. Payouts have been fixed, so players have more income from transport jobs. Fully recommend the game now, however be prepared to scrap your save if your chosen difficulty is to annoying.Old:Cant recommend this game atm. In many ways, this game should have been an early access release. Game balance seems of (airfilters, batteries), basic systems are bugged (trailers from the same consist damaging themselves for no reason, skill bonuses not being applied during payout), etc. All fine in early access, but not for a finished game.Furthermore, while this looks like a chill ETS/ATS like trucking game in space, it is more of a survival game. And if you find that the "recommended" difficulty is to annoying for you, you cant lower it without starting a new game, wasting 5 or more hours of gameplay.The game has great potential, both as a chill and hardcore game, once the bugs are fixed, systems are better balanced and explained, and the difficulty can be adjusted mid save.

_childDocuments_.review: Star Trucker is an endlessly frustrating game to play, at least in its current form. Which is a real disappointment because on paper I should love this game, but there were some glaring issues with the game that just kind of ruined it for me.You have four different resources you need to constantly juggle to keep your truck running. Fuel, Power Cells, Air Filters, and Universal Circuits. These deplete  quickly compared to the amount of time you actually spend driving, so you are constantly replacing them. That would normally be fine, but there's no guarantee that you'll find any of these essential items at a given shop, even in the bustling hub systems. And even if you do find some, there's usually only one or two of each available. They're also really expensive compared to your income, at least in the early game.This is what killed my first run of the game. I started losing oxygen rapidly because one of my two air filters dropped below 50% durability (which itself is kind of ridiculous), so I had to go speeding between every shop in the first hub system because  of them had replacement filters. And when I did finally find one (and only one), I suffocated while I was in the process of buying it. IN THE MIDDLE OF ONE OF THE MAIN HUBS, where you'd think supplies would be plentiful.The NPCs you'll encounter on your travels have the self-preservation instincts of a toddler playing in the cabinets under the kitchen sink. I've seen better driving in Grand Theft Auto, where the NPCs are actively trying to crash into you. I was straight-up kamikaze'd twice, and narrowly avoided a few others. In each instance, I was driving in a straight line, at a more or less constant speed. And the great thing is, when you're involved in a collision, it's always your fault, and you always receive the full penalty for it!This is what killed my second (and ultimately final) run. I was doing one of the tutorial missions after unlocking fragile loads, and while I was dodging some debris coming out of a warp gate, another truck exited the gate at about 200 miles an hour, dove directly for my cab, and brought my hull integrity all the way down from full to 0% in a single hit. I made no money from that mission because of "Careless Driving", and the repair bills put me so far in debt that there was no point continuing.Apart from those two major issues, there are some rough edges to the game. Some things are not communicated to the player effectively, like Universal Circuits failing, or the fact that you can't haul multiple trailers from different jobs at once, despite the fact that you can accept multiple missions at the same time,  can haul up to three trailers from a single mission. It sort of makes sense in hindsight, but I just wish I hadn't had to learn that the hard way, because there are  penalties for cancelling a mission after you've accepted it, which can easily put you in debt.You have to dock at different nodes at each station for different purposes, like buying supplies and accepting missions. The captain's chair also blocks some of the controls you might need access to when walking around, like the cab lights, which I would usually turn off to try and save a bit of power. All of this got pretty annoying after a while.Also, navigating around some of the hubs can be a bit confusing. There is a galactic map that shows all the systems for route planning, but there aren't any maps for the systems themselves. The only way to navigate those is to study the "roads" in each one visually and try to pick out the one that leads where you need to go, which isn't always obvious and costs you precious fuel and time if you get it wrong.Fundamentally speaking, this game is pretty good, and the issues I do have are all eminently fixable. But right now, it's just too frustrating to play, so it's a no from me until this stuff gets addressed.

_childDocuments_.review: Yet again I wish steam had a neutral option instead of yes or no...The game is, overall, decent. I wouldn't say it's Euro Truck in space, because it isn't. And for the price, it's a good deal, especially if you like space and simulator games.And yet, I'll be lying if I said you won't be disappointed. I feel like the game struggles to find it's place, it's like the devs kinda threw in what they wanted to see in the game (which isn't a bad thing) but never went all the way into one direction.Like... the game got some simulation elements that are fairly interesting, manual repairs, batteries, fuel management... It's great, I love it, and I crave for more, and yet there is nothing more to it. That's it, that's the end of the simulation part. A few steps from perfection, and yet we fall short.Same goes for more arcade elements, or the story/narrative, and why can you only carry 3 trailers ? And then you end up exploring every corner of the galaxy and there is nothing more, well maybe I can get some change with a new truck ? But there is only one available.It's trying to be everywhere, and is decent everywhere to be honest, but not a single element reach even close to perfection. And if I agree that focusing on one aspect might end up making the game too niche, I still think being just "average" everywhere makes it just as hard for it to find its audience.The only real downside of the game is the handling of the ship, especially at higher speed, even with a maxed-out ship (as a matter of fact not a single upgrade improve handling). I've spent my time on highways taking those curves like I'm drifting in space, when I don't straight up crash into the side poles. Side thrusters would help too, the community has been asking for it ever since demo, hopefully the game gets that updated.So in conclusion, do I recommend the game ? Well, yes, even more knowing it's made by only 2 devs that worked hard on it, and for such a small team it's pretty impressive.Are you gonna have fun playing the game ? Yes, probably, at least in the couple first hours. And then you'll realise there isn't much more to it (yet ?), so you'll go back to either your simulation games or your space games, which ever took you here in the first place, maybe both. And then, if the devs cherish this game like their baby, and give it updates for years to come, then maybe one day you'll come back to it, and enjoy this game as what it should have been, a true space simulation of cargo-hauling, with attaching characters and a lovely galaxy to explore.

_childDocuments_.review: "Space trucking sim" = no keybinds menu.Need I say more?*DISCLAIMER*I am clearly reviewing the games marketing here, not the game itself.  Keep that in mind before you leave an angry comment.  I am sure the game is great, but the advertising is not.*sigh* Why do I have to do this?  I have been waiting months for this, I have never sat here refreshing a page waiting for a game to launch before this, and yet I also haven't been this disappointed in years.  What were you thinking to release a "space trucking sim" without even a keybinds menu?  A complete disconnect from the audience this game will attract if you ask me.I get it, this is clearly a very story driven game, however I don't see that mentioned once anywhere in the description or about page...  This game portrays itself as everything it's not, only at the bottom in the section about the devs does it say what it really is, "an experience".  I could tell from the demo this game wasn't as advertised, I also forgave the demo for not having a keybinds menu, considering it was a demo and all... In hindsight, I should have seen this coming.I feel bad leaving a negative review after only 5 minutes of gameplay and right after launch, but I played the demo for several hours, completing it many times.  The game started off exactly where the demo did (and actually bugged for me the first run because someone hit me and got me a traffic offense before I even left the truck, when I got out my truck was flying off and I had to restart).  To be blunt here, I feel lied to.  I'm all for a story driven experience like this, but sell it as that, not some space trucking sim that it's not even trying to be.I bought this game for what it said was, and refunded it for what it actually is.  In no way do I support any game without a keybinds menu, but a "sim" game?  Come on... this is a joke, right?

_childDocuments_.review: This game is geniunely awesome. I've been looking forward to it all year and it's not dissapointing. It's very much a game of process. It's a little bit like Sea of Thieves in that the way you get from place-to-place is central to the design of the gameplay loop; it's moreso about the journey than the destination. As far as maintenance goes, it's just complicated enough to keep you engaged without becoming so obscure that you don't know what's going on or why you're dying (which was a pretty common experience in the demo).As far as presentation is concerned, the devs knocked it outta the damn park. The vibes are frankly immaculate. The in-universe music is excellent, and fairly well-mixed. The environmental design feels simultaneously believable and stylish. The various spaceports all have their own unique feel, which is something I was really worried about coming into this game. The characters are charming, and interacting with them is a genuine motivator to progress in the story. That being said, there are glaring oversights I'm noticing about the game, and since I know the devs are actively looking for feedback right now, I think I'll share what I've noticed so far: -No keybind configuration-NPCs don't respond well to player behavior. I once had another truck slam into me for no good reason, dropping my hull integrity to near-zero from full and damaging a lot of valuable commodities. -No lateral-vertical thrusters (though I suspect this is a deliberate choice by devs to preserve the "big rig feel" of these starships)-No ability to control lights without being seated at the front of the cabin. Surely it'd be nice, at least for immersion's sake, to be able to control the lights from the living space in the lower-back of the vesselRegardless, this game is scratching my brain in a way that's doing something for me, and frankly a game this ambitious coming out in such a stable, functional, and polished state feels like a miracle in 2024. All things considered, I'm more than happy to recommend this game, even at full price.

_childDocuments_.review: This game Is a very interesting take on the classic trucking simulator game.-- I really like hooking up to other trailers -- Replacing parts on your truck is pretty easy to understand and manage-- Making deliveries can feel very satisfying -- I really like how each environment feels different with the station layouts combined with the sun and planet position and also elemental effects like lightning storms or heat waves.-- When you are docked to a store your batteries and fuel do not get used so it allows you to plan your route and think about what you are doing.This game can feel like american truck simulator mixed with space engineers/pacific drive and I love it.There is some flaws as of right now that I am not happy with but for the most part some of them maybe just might be my lack of skill.-- I wish the truck cab would give you warnings when in third-person view.-- When using the docking camera with debris nearby the docking camera will be covered with a warning about nearby debris which makes it harder to line up your truck.-- Whenever you are docked with a job board or a store your can access the store by closing the airlock and pressing the hologram that appears which is nice but it was not explained in the tutorial very well and as such i thought I had to re-dock at any store any time i forgot to sell or buy something..-- I got fined for littering at a truck weight inspection and do not know why.I still have much to explore and am looking forward to all of it
