_childDocuments_.review: My initial encounter with Ultros was during a Steam Next event, where I played the demo. The unique plant mechanics, alongside the compelling art and sound design, caught my attention, though I didn't progress to the first boss fight due to the somewhat cumbersome movement and combat. I was uncertain how the upgrades would enhance the gameplay. Fast forward to its official release, I spontaneously decided to dive back in, dedicating 2.5 hours in my first session and momentarily setting aside Persona 3. This time, the gameplay mechanics felt intuitive and satisfying, particularly on the Steam Deck.The game's visual and artistic direction is distinct, intricately linked to the gameplay mechanics. The concept of planting as a core mechanic significantly influences the game's world, with each plant offering unique abilities that can alter the environment. The world of Ultros is both vibrant and grim, each area exuding its own peculiar organic essence. As the game progresses, the encroaching organic elements enrich the sense of advancement, both through gameplay mechanics and the evolution of the game's world. The visuals sometimes conjure the essence of a disorienting psychedelic experience, emphasizing the game's theme of an unnatural ecosystem.What sets Ultros apart is its level design, showcasing a profound understanding of guiding players through environmental cues and storytelling. The game masterfully directs the player without feeling restrictive, maintaining a sense of freedom and exploration throughout. Although there are moments when the game enforces a more linear path, these are balanced by the overarching sense of openness, allowing players to explore and progress at their own pace.I've even tested the game's boundaries by trying to bypass picking up certain items or attempting to sequence break, yet the game has stopped me from doing anything major while still rewarding such exploratory efforts in unexpected ways. This level of design foresight and the encouragement of player experimentation are among the many reasons Ultros is so good. Here are some of the cons: Some aspects of the movement, especially flying, could benefit from more refined controls. Additionally, the combat system lacks complexity, and I've yet to face a boss battle that presents a significant challenge. The availability of unlimited healing somewhat diminishes the difficulty, even though the mechanic where food can be knocked from your grasp during healing adds an interesting dynamic. The cortex system also appears overly forgiving in subsequent playthroughs, allowing for effortless accumulation of resources and complete skill tree respecification without much effort.Similarly, using an incorrect plant necessitates waiting for a specific upgrade to rectify the mistake, forcing backtracking and potentially another waiting period for plant growth to achieve 100% game completion. Moreover, while there are methods to enhance the potency of plant fruits, the abundance of resources makes this feature feel underutilized. Currently, with access to the fertilizer, it remains to be seen if a second cortex tree or additional benefits for maximizing resources will alter this dynamic. For the moment, engaging with this system seems optional, primarily for those aiming for full game completion.Overall, Ultros is a great little game, and its some fairly cool moments that will satisfy most metroidvania fan, but its not nearly as ruthless as many of its contemporaries.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: very innovative metroidvania. the whole traversal function in this game is very innovative. knowing what to put where is essential, knowing what everything does... this game and the functions in it are not yet cataloged so figuring it out is pivotal at this point and makes it super fun figuring it out. good luck! i love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Great aesthetic, obviously. There are moments when combat can shine, with  good amount of abilities to do combos with. The environment feels consistent but every area is distinct enough and feels different. I'm not sure if the game gains anything by forcing the loop mechanic, a standard metroidvania with slower skill unlocks could've worked better, but I understand that there are lore reasons for this. On top of that it supports the way plant system works, which is kinda sick, but also confusing, making chasing the final unlocks a little bit too tricky for me to even try it. Some music is lovely, some just tolerable, but the overall experience was cool. And I have no clue what was even happening. I recommend playing this while sober.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros teaches me that each of us is alone, individual in our ability to create a better world around us.Ultros teaches me that it is only when we engage with the Whole -- the society that we exist in, the world we exist in, the galaxy and cosmere that we belong to, all that we are and someday will return to -- only then do we, as Individuals become whole, and maybe only then can We, collectively and meaningfully, build a better world around us.Ultros is a good game. It is not especially difficult and Hollow Knight players might find it wonting, but that does not mean that it is lacking for interesting mechanics. The art and soul poured into this game by its creators has left me feeling inspired.Please buy this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a beautiful game. It's a metroidvania, not a roguelike. Your upgrades reset when you complete a "cycle" but you'll eventually get ways to lock those in. The game itself is not really difficult. It's hardest at the start and then it quickly becomes a rather peaceful game. The game will not hold your hand and it will let you get yourself stuck. Be prepared to reload a save if you like trying to do janky things. That said, I think this game will have some very cool speed runs.As enjoyable as the game is, I don't recommend going for 100%. Definitely DO NOT try to connect all of the statues. I spent a large chunk of my playtime trying to connect a couple of statues that absolutely were not worth it.The "true" ending is quite nice and very satisfying to achieve. It is a fair bit of work to pull off largely because the whole growing plants mechanic is a bit tedious and not very intuitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Before I get any negative comments, the audio and video aspects are top notch in this game. But the gameplay is dull and boring for me. I don't like how the progression works and it feels more like a semi metroidvania than what you would expect when a game has the tag metroidvania. Is it unique? Sure but that doesn't mean good.Try it at your own risk.I can't recommend the way this game plays.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Lots of visual influence from Metroid, but with THE MOST unique mechanics for world exploration/methods for unlocking secrets that I've seen in a game.  Although the combat has lots of cool combo potential, i feel the actual fights so far have been lacking in pacing and challenge. The imagery and themes presented in the story are what really have kept me engaged, and keep me intrigued to see where it leads.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Not sure why all of my hours aren't tracked on Steam, but whatever.  This is probably one of the most visually unique looking games released in years.  The combat is quick and fun, and the alien ship you're stuck on looks amazing with lots of really cool things to find.  Of course, finding your way around the game itself is pretty taxing at times and it almost feels like an absurd amount of time is spent backtracking or going back and forth.  In any case, game's pretty great for anyone looking for an interesting metroidvania.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Being used to the more traditional style of Metroidvania's, Ultros was not what I was expecting at first. But after playing for a while I realised that the game brings a refreshing and fun take on the metroidvania genre. The loop mechanic challenges you to start thinking in a different way then you would for most games of this type. Ended up really enjoying Ultros and would definitely recommend every metroidvania fan to give it chance!
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: It's difficult to describe, really, but it's probably the most "oh, the game's just like that now, huh?" sort of exploration/platformer/adventure/metroidvania(?) in the last couple years, where you find an upgrade or thing that suddenly changes how you look at the situation almost entirelyAlso it's very pretty and the soundtrack is good
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I will tentatively recommend this game. Beautiful game, some interesting mechanics, but for one reason or another it just didn't hook me. Still though, I can't really point to a specific part of the game that led me to this. I might give it another try later, I might not, but I'd still love to see more games with a unique aesthetic like this become popular.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The Cosmic Gardening Simulator You Never Knew You Needed🌱 Plot: Imagine crash-landing on a giant cosmic uterus (yes, you read that right) and being stuck in a time loop. Your mission? Gardening. In space. With monsters. Welcome to Ultros, where your green thumb might just save the universe.🎨 Graphics: Think of a neon fever dream where someone spilled all the highlighters on a black canvas. It’s like Bob Ross decided to paint while chugging energy drinks. The colors are so vibrant, you might need sunglasses to play.🕹️ Gameplay: It’s a Metroidvania, but with a twist. Instead of just fighting monsters, you’re also tending to your garden. Because why not? One moment you’re battling a tentacled horror, the next you’re planting space tulips. It’s like if Alien and Stardew Valley had a very psychedelic baby.👾 Monsters: The creatures in Ultros look like they escaped from a 70s sci-fi movie. Giant eyeball fruits? Check. Glowing mushrooms that might be sentient? Double check. It’s like someone let a botanist design the alien fauna after a particularly wild party.🧠 Story: The plot is as trippy as the visuals. You’re in a cosmic womb, trying to break free from a time loop by talking to aliens and fighting anything that moves. It’s like Groundhog Day, but with more tentacles and less Bill Murray.🌌 Overall: Ultros is a wild ride through a neon-colored, monster-infested garden in space. It’s weird, it’s wonderful, and it’s definitely worth playing if you enjoy your games with a side of “What did I just experience?” Just remember to water your plants and watch out for the tentacles.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Not recommended to anyone and not worth a full price, unless you have a ton of free time for exploring and mastering this metroidvania with a sprinkle of roguelike on top (what adds at least an hour or two of unnecessary backtracking "because designer thought it'd be a good idea"), where new skills/mechanics are barely explained at best (most of the time aren't explained at all), scripts are working as they want to (not as you'd expect them to and not as it'd be handy), the picture is constantly burning your eyes with acidic colors (they've even added a "blur/desaturate background" option because were understanding that the gameplay look's like a mess) and all of that is seasoned with the barely understandable philosophical story and item descriptions. The only thing I can praise here is a built-in god-mode, which makes the struggle a bit less painful, but surely doesn't solve main issues. I'd refund it without hesitation if I still could.In a few words: it doesn't look like designers don't know what to do, it looks more like they HUGELY overdid in attempt to give birth to something unique.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect performance on the Deck.So. I got lost. A lot. And I thought it was a me thing, because I'm an idiot. But when i searched the forums, it seems it happened to most people. If you're a Geoguessr pro, you might not have this issue, but be aware it's pretty common with this game.Then, there's the loop system. Each time you achieve a primary goal, the ship will reset and you'll have to find a weapon again, level up again, and find your way. Again. There are some stuff you can find to freeze some skills and you can plant a seed, which will grow thanks to a loop or compost. But it was more a chore than a fun thing for me.The visuals are stunning, the music is fine, the gameplay is mostly dash and slash, which is okay, but the loop and progression systems really bothered me. Why would I want to redo an entire area? You put the fast travel so far into the game... Wish I could say I enjoyed it, but I'm just glad I won't have to play it anymore.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: We got Blasphemous, we got The Last Faith, and we got... whatever this is. There you go. I understand writers want to feel important, but come on. Taking a mix of side scrolling analog slashing and mixing with bizarre, psychedelic artistry -- doesn't make it a good game. I had hopes. It was an interesting mix of side scrolling with repeat levels like Hades, but the amount of nonsense written to create lore, objects, purpose of objects, and overall cohesive storytelling fell short. I'm going here, I should not need x, y and z to get there three play troughs later. And don't tell me that's, "brilliant storytelling," or, "innovative design". Wonderfully looking game, great ambiance and sound. Poor game play, weak battle system, level design is basically recycled compost to save money. "Plant this here, at hour 2," then, "At hour 6, it's still not big enough"! Wait more hours, or cycles, or whatever. It just got boring. I'm sorry, you just didn't keep my attention for the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The game is beautiful and interesting. Easy to beat with the violent path. But It too much bother to do the other. Connecting the network is too much work, it is unintuitive and the plants system, that is part of doing it, is obscure and convolute. When you succeed in connetcting a path it is disconforting to see that it is a dead path or you can't find the next connection point. At a certain point my patience run out and I have to quit. _childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a masterfully crafted Metroidvania. The universe is unique and full of details, you're lost most of the time trying to understand the world you evolve in.The story is intriguing specially because of the implications of our actions told through loops.The music and general art direction is sublime, trippy and really makes you want to progress.However, that's where I have some issues the game, the progression. Unlike other titles you can't get lost and try to find what is now accessible thanks to your new skills, revisiting old areas. You also likely won't need anything from the skill tree to progress, aside maybe the wall jump but it isn't that great or the plant upgrades if you're connecting the network.The only way forward is by hunting down the 8 shamans and unlocking new abilities with your companion.However, discover a zone, get back to 0 rinse and repeat isn't that stimulating and feels limited as you'll only be able to discover a zone at a time in a set order driven by the story.Pick it up if you love Metroidvanias with intriguing universes and incredible art and sound direction.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Any game with this many proper nouns in  conversation needs an in-game encyclopedia. I've played and enjoyed media with incredibly-dense worldbuilding and lore (e.g. Axiom Verge 2 or The Fountain), but this one just feels like it's too happy to sniff its own butt.But any game can still manage to be fun if the gameplay is fun, right? Too bad Ultros feels like a bog-standard "we really like Hollow Knight" metroidvania, but with even more punishment. Combat is your usual dodge-rolling, counter-striking, combo-grinding souls-lite. It has an interesting tie into progression with the monsters dropping food (better quality based on how you take them down) that both refills health and advances you on the skill tree, but that's all I saw of interest in the hour I played.The worst part of gameplay is that the game is supposedly loop-centric (like many roguelikes), but dying dumps you back to your last save, with all progress lost. I thought we got rid of that particular stupidity a decade ago. Are they going to bring back lives systems and quarter-munching next?So the lore is obtuse and the gameplay is alternately unimaginative and overly punishing. What about the front-of-the-box selling point, the art? It's ugly. The artist clearly doesn't understand  we have restrained palettes per sprite, or simplified backgrounds, or any of the other dozen techniques that make game worlds comprehensible during play. If you want crazy-weird art with restrained color schemes, try Hollow Knight. If you want basic art with vibrant colors but proper palettes, try my favorite metroidvania Dust: An Elysian Tale. More colors does not equate to better art.It's fugly, it's boring, it's frustrating, 2/7. There might be a good game in here somewhere, but I don't have the patience or endurance to find it.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Review! or at least some bulletin points.    • Gameplay - was nice and responsive. I was never hung up on something do to lack of control or spacey feeling controls. Also the "hunting" aspect of not repeating yourself in combos to yield better results was cool addition that ended up playing into the whole aspect of the game. everything by the end melds really well together.    • Lore - I personally would have like a little more abrupt in your face story telling (that's just me though). I did like the lore and the story that unfolded through the characters and the environmental storytelling that was there. By the end it stuck with me. I highly recommend after beating it going for the "true" ending and beating the pacifist run.    • Visuals - Easily the thing that stood out the most. the game is gorgeous and the Art style is what drew me to the game to began with. The psychedelic colors, characters and environments really made this game pop. Definitely sticks with ya after completing it.     • Mechanics - Some mechanics took a bit to understand this is where I wish some of it was more in your face with tutorials as too how somethings interacted. Like the plants interactions with the environment, or being able to upgrade your equipment. In the end I loved how they worked  and mesh together and experimenting was really fun. How the spun classics like the double jump into a new take with unlocking your skill tree through cycles it was great and I enjoyed the slow burn of it. Also adding some things I'd never seen  before made for a really cool experience. I didn't run into any bugs during my time with the game.Might be a slow burn for some but if your on the look out for a great Metroidvania you'll remember after the credits roll, then this one is for you.Also 10/10 didn't have to take drugs to enjoy the psychedelics.

_childDocuments_.review: Refunded after the first reset where all my powerups were suddenly gone. It might make sense from a lore stand point, and the story might make more sense down the road. _childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: If you're expecting something akin to Hollow Knight with a psychedelic art style, and an equally interesting narrative, this is not it in the slightest. It's a roguelite (thus it loops, and you lose abilities on the reset) that is so high on its own sense of mystique that it offers little motivation to bother finishing. Both the information relayed to the player and that which is kept secret aren't all that compelling when examined outside of the eccentric dialogue. The art, while great to look at, is in effect jingling keys in your face and does not make up for the amount of meandering you'll be subjected to. If you're looking for a roguelite more than you are a metroidvania, there might be something here for you, but know that the price is steep for what you're getting.Edit: For clarification, the issue for me is not only that it has roguelite elements nor that it can be argued to be one. My last purchase was Oblivion Override, and I enjoyed it very much. The issue is that the demo provided ends just before the looping begins, and if there was ever a roguelite tag before release I didn't see it. So not only was I not interested in playing that genre in this setting, I wasn't expecting it at all. "Who cares?" You might ask, "You like other roguelites/likes so why is there an issue now?" Well, apart from the aforementioned, this one tries to be both a roguelite and a metroidvania, and as a result is great at neither. You don't need a dozen hours in game to figure that one out.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I want to play this game.I am a big fan of metroidvania's - even some admittedly bland ones. This games artstyle appeals to me and I would love to check it out, but for whatever reason my controllers do not work with this game. I'm a long time Linux user, I know that these things are not designed for my operating system and exceptions must be made, but I don't have this issue on ANY other game in my library that can be played with a controller, only Ultros.I tried playing with the keyboard, but it was apparent immediately that this game should not be played this way,Again, I would LOVE to play this game, but at present I cannot - I'm going to try and get a refund and purchase later on when this issue hopefully will no longer exist.

_childDocuments_.review: I do have high hope for this game because of the unprecedented art style and concept. When I started to play, I just wanna say the ACT system is a piece of st. It's okay if the dev team wanna make something new and not cliche, but is that a really bad idea to accept the general ACT system of other ACT games? I mean the jumping and climbing system is harsh, there is little room for mistake on certain climbing. And why bother introducing a arial stepback instead of general jump+dash combo? I dont see any sense when I activate the skill on the skill tree, cz I didn't see any use of that on map exploring or boss combat. Speaking of boss combat, the ulmost reason that I quit this game after one hour is the combat of the first boss, it took me 5 times to know how to deal true damage on the specific spot. And after that, even if I know, I still cant do any damage.  The mechanism of the boss is that it will create a step, and you can jump on the step and jump in the air to hit his head and cause damage. The question is once the boss create the step, it almost destroy it immediately or just throwing utility to deter your jump, leaving almost zero chance to get a hit. I'm not opening this game until the dev team gets an overhaul on the ACT system, and modify the logic of the first boss. The experience of my first half hour is good, but not on the second half.

_childDocuments_.review: I hate time loop games.Utterly ruins what would had been a perfectly great game for myself.---Editting after letting the sheer disappointment leave.I wouldnt had bought it at all if it was mentioned in the marketing that it was a Rouge-Lite.The game is perfectly well crafted, Great visuals and fun core combat loop.But i strongly dont enjoy Rouge-Lite elements in my games, Lord forbid in the game that is all about progression.Id rather not be dealing with this horrid game mechanic in my Metriodviana's.Oh and if a negative review means so much to the fans of this game, Get a life. _childDocuments_.review: I was really excited about this game prior to it's release. The artwork in it is beautiful, and I tend to be drawn to anything time travel related. Ultros does have some genuinely cool ideas, and some groundbreaking mechanics. I love the gardening and time loop mechanics and the way they work along with each other to open up secret areas as you progress through the game. Unfortunately these are the game's only redeeming qualities. The story is nonsensical and convoluted, and full of pretentious sounding Sci-fi gibberish words. The enemy design consists of maybe 10-12 enemies throughout the entire game (excluding bosses) and those enemies have predictable, repetitive attacks. The combat system encourages you to mix it up with your attacks, but then provides you with a repertoire of repetitive and/or unusable attacks, and the level design is some of the worst I have ever seen. The game only has one questline, and even that is impossible to keep track of. map markers will not show up when you need them, and will refuse to clear after you have completed objectives. Paths that you need to take will be randomly obscured by black mist that you cannot pass. Doors that are supposed to open will randomly open and close without being triggered, and the game will frequently allow you to enter areas that you lack the abilities to escape from. When you do happen to wander into areas that you shouldn't be able to access yet, the game punishes you by locking up your maps and menus and forcing you to exit the game and restart the time loop you are on. I put a LOT of time into this game and finally gave up on it after spending several hours trying to enter the final map area with no luck.Garbage. Don't waste your money.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: i'm on the fence with this one.it's a fine game. an alright metroidvania. if you play too many vanias, this is still a good buy, I recommend it.if you play just a few games here and there, I'm not sure this is the one I'd go with.still a thumbs up. it's fun, absolutely beautiful. the mechanics are alright.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a vibrant, psychedelic, visual feast, and for me was the main initial draw of the game. Not taking into account the dazzling colours, what it does when it comes to gameplay, it does well. It is more of a puzzle game, than action, and they are what truly shine in the game. The combat that is featured is smooth, and not just a button mash fest. It encourages you to use different combos and attacks to benefit yourself with in-game loot. And that is if you choose to use the combat, as the game can be played largely passively if you so choose. The gardening and seed aspect is also well designed, making it fun to figure out what goes where and does what, allowing you to progress more and discover more interesting  areas. The loop cycles of the game, which I have seen others criticise, was personally enjoyable, and given the game is not too long, approx 15hrs, it doesn't become repetitive. The story it self is intriguing. It doesn't tell you too much, and leaves you to figure it out over the course, as it takes you in deeper.The few NPCs that feature are beautifully designed with interesting backstories and lore. Overall this was a truly fun and enjoyable experience, and personally my game of the year so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: "A Trippy Castlevania"!! says me.At the time of this review I'm a little over 12 hours in and there has been some interesting shifts in gameplay (you'll see), interesting characters without having to read volumes of text, some cool bosses, a plethora of truly incredible 'blacklight poster' art, chill background music, unusual 'skills' that aren't annoying combos of the controller buttons, and a very expansive map still left to cover. There's the usual backtracking of any metroidvania, but this was actually more FUN and relaxing than anticipated. It's challenging enough to satisfy any serious metroidvania fan, but manageable for someone looking to just PLAY a cool game with a thoughtful backstory. You aren't just running around the map lost. It's a submersive world. This game stands on it's own and isn't a 'copycat' game like many that are out there now. Overall, I think this was extremely well done!! It's worth the money, especially at it's current sale price. Buy it. You won't be disappointed!! Have fun!! <3
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Right off the bat, I can see why some people don't like this game. It's strange. Especially if you're expecting just a run of the mill metroidvania. But what this game offers in tone, story, and feeling is probably unlike anything else you're playing right now. It has a way of making you think about what you're doing that is unusual for this genre. I can't say how far through the game I am, only that I'm hooked and I think I have only begun to peel back the mysteries. If you're a fan of stuff like Environment Station Alpha, or Void Stranger, you'll fall right into it. The combat is pretty interesting too. It has a kind of parry/dodge mechanic and you're rewarded for perfection. I like it, it makes combat tense and I'm big fan of games like Sifu and Sekiro. The visuals are awesome. Cons: Bosses are pretty easy so far, and a bit repetitive, with no idea how much longer to beat the boss (no health bar, damage, nothing). It can make you feel "ok, how much more of this is there?" with no indication that you should be doing something "more perfect." A mario64 style "three stomps" would have worked well, and maybe you need to do more if you're not perfect. Maybe that is how it works? I don't know.Soundtrack is bus, so grab that even if you don't play the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning. If you are the type of player that likes min-maxing, you're not gonna like this game. There's a lot of points of no return where the game deletes your inventory, and it isn't always clear when these points of no return happen. This isn't really a problem, since the game is pretty easy doesn't demand perfection at all.If you're wondering if this game is for you, just look at the pictures and videos on the store and ask yourself "would I enjoy just walking around in this game and looking at the world?". If you do, you can expect a visceral and responsive combat system, as well as intrigueing lore to keep you occupied.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: If you've ever enjoyed breaking a Metroid-Vania, or experimenting being a central mechanic in a game, or speed run routing or doing challenge runs of a game, I'd recommend Ultros.There is so much fun experimentation in this game. The marvelous gardening mechanics can open up insane pathways if you're creative enough. You can couple some plants with some cheeky high skill movement options to really get all over the map all out of order.That's so cool that I went back to play the game three times using different plants and routes, and I honestly still want more.The visuals are inspired, the VFX blew my socks off, and though there's not enough of it, the music is awesome. Ultros is for sure one of my favorite games.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Great Metroidvania with gorgeous art and amazing soundtrack, definitely underrated . A few tips to enjoy this game more in my opinion : - In post processing graphics options, turn off chromatic aberration, blur, scan lines and color grading. The game is psychedelic looking enough, no need to add these filters, they only muddy and distort the beautiful art.- Don't expect a major focus on combat. The rewards for diversifying your attacks are a nice touch and definitely worth going for, however a decent sizable part of the game is the puzzle of gardening and interacting with the fauna in a non-violent way, so be aware of that. I feel it stands out from most metroidvanias in that regard. The game's difficulty is not punishing at all.- This is not a roguelite or roguelike. There is a loop mechanic tied to the narrative, you will lose unlocked upgrades the first few times you loop, but there are no randomized environments, randomized loot or restart from beginning on death. - You will very quickly find items that let your unlocked skills persist from loop to loop, so don't freak out after losing your abilities, you will get them right back quickly enough. If you miss your double jump that much at the start of a loop, just go get it in your first 2 minutes before exploring again.- I recommend letting yourself be guided by the natural progression of the story and only start gardening more extensively when you have all tools available to you. Plant what you find as you go by giving it a tiny amount of thinking in the moment, but don't go overboard with trying to develop a network of plants until you have all tools.I think by having the right expectations, you can have a great experience with this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is one of the best games of 2024, and stands among the most creative Metroidvanias ever made. The art style is dazzling, the music is symphonic and mesmerising, and the gameplay design audacious in its scope and invention. It's hard to go into quite why it's so good without touching on spoilers, but let's just say, there's more to it than first meets the eye.  Overall, it's a sensory treat, and an unforgettable game with a unique resonance, and a beautiful message at its core.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most creative and beautiful metroidvanias out there (perhaps better to call this a gardenvania?). It's a bit rough around the edges: combat is trivial and not really that interesting and movement/traversal could sometimes be a bit frustratingly opaque. But it more than makes up for that by allowing you to shape the map you explore by cultivating plants and, of course, the absolutely stellar art and music.

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible atmosphere, music, sound design, and obviously the visual art style is very intricate and unique.  It's fun to run around having sort of no idea what's going on, but somehow always making it to the right location and finding the right upgrades.  Feels like a result of excellent level design.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is very much like an incredible psychedelic experience, but not in the way one may initially think. Clearly, the visuals immediately jumped out at me, and the style captured my attention. But it is in the experience of playing the game itself where we can see the developers crafted us a truly immersive experience that rewards our patience. I urge you not to rush to a guide to figure it all out, because so much of the beauty of the game comes from the process of slow discovery.In a psychedelic experience, I was always captivated by what happens when I allow the journey itself to guide me. Initially, nothing makes sense, and it can be overwhelming. But when one surrenders and lets go, that's where the true rewards lie. There's a kind of multidimensional communication of information unlike anything one's encountered before. As one immerses themselves, it all begins to coalesce and make perfect sense in its own unique way. This is the essence of the reward.This has been my experience with this game, and this game has rewarded me greatly. Be patient, enjoy the ride, and you too shall be rewarded.

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderfully creative metroidvania. The game felt like there was more of a puzzle emphasis instead of combat. The rouge-like elements I actually thought brought a lot of value to the game - and I generally don't like that genre. The map was fun to explore. Movement was fluid. Really enjoyed the last 1/4 of the game. Definitely recommend the game for any metroidvania fans.

_childDocuments_.review: An extremely beautiful game with a soundtrack that takes several hours to get old. It does get frustrating at some points, when you're trying to treat it sort of like an immersive sim, because you can feel the hand of the creator in numerous ways and it's rarely in your favor. This message was brought to you by the inability to graft augeas leaves onto anything else. I've been a fan of El Huervo's music for quite a while now, and I was expecting to see some overlap between this and the rest of what I know him for, but there's almost nothing. I can only think of two references he's made to song titles. Very strange.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is beautiful. This is obvious from the game's cover art, let alone the in-game graphics. There is no art style quite like what Niklas Åkerblad does. It is psychedelic biology - combining an acid trip with nature and biology. To be quite honest, the imagery alone in this game is worth the price and time of a playthrough.Ultros is a difficult game in some aspects but not in others. It has generally easy combat that rewards you for perfecting your skills. There is a pretty large upgrade system with things to work towards. But the game itself is a bit obtuse. It tells you nearly nothing and you're left to figure stuff out on your own. To the game's benefit, it is well designed in that there is a certain flow to the game.Ultros is a metroidvania but equally as much a rogue-lite. You will do some backtracking but it's largely just to go back and get a specific upgrade you need for completing the new loop. The way Ultros' progression is designed is that each section of the world map is essentially its own loop. Once you complete the loop, you'll naturally head towards a different, unexplored corner of the map. I think it's important for people to understand the game's design to prevent the frustration that may come with the game's abstractness and lack of direct information.The story in Ultros is good and plays very well into the theme and graphics of the game, but it's also not too in-depth. There's no voice acting and cutscenes are short and relatively basic from an animation perspective. Again, the graphics are the foundation of the game's design.What I love about Ultros aside from looking at it is how rewarding it is for someone who wants to dig deep into the complexities of the game. It is very rewarding for someone who wants to take notes on the different types of plants, wants to connect all of the map together, and wants to complete the game through its pacifist ending. I'm not the type of person to commit that much into a game but I love dipping my toes in and seeing how layered a game is. Ultros for many people might seem a bit too simplistic but for those that want to dig deep, there's a lot of complexity, strategy, and puzzle solving to it.Ultros will be remembered for its imagery. It's such a visually stunning and evocative game that it's hard not to be disappointed that the mechanics of the game don't match the impossibly high levels of its graphics. While not bad, it's really just a bit too easy. It's not a fast-paced combat system which I think makes the argument for it to be more difficult, as you can strategize mid-combat and reset pretty easily without fear of death. I think anyone with a little patience, a sense of exploration, and the willingness to just live in the world they're playing will have a great time in Ultros. It's not designed to be like Dead Cells with fast-paced, snappy combat. It's an experience - one certainly worth diving into.

_childDocuments_.review: THIS GAME FREAKIN RULES. Solid 9/10 easily. "DMT fever dream Metroidvania" was the most accurate description I saw before purchasing this game which caused me, along with the visuals, to instantly purchase it. It's absolutely gorgeous, and pretty easy to learn. There is a lot of poetic and flowery lore, but its all vague AF and not built upon, so as long as you can accept "game pretty, game fun, game very unique" and not care about not understanding a gyaat dayum thing that is going on literally ever... you've got a great game ;)Pros:- Unique skill tree system I've never seen anything similar to before- Insanely creative art, lore, creatures and characters, world, etc- Familiar and unfamiliar new powers and world-traversal skills/systems- A very cool progression through the story that feels like Majora's Mask meets Metroid Prime meets Dead Cells with a dash of whatever games care about how "cool/special" the way you fight is and reward you for it- It was VERY affordable for the amazing and super novel content you get - WOWCons- Combat isn't explained until you've already cleared the first area- While the vagueness of literally everything is also the games charm, it does kind of make it hard to emotionally invest in anything going on and feel driven to continue - I feel more driven by curiosity of seeing more pretty art and new areas than the "story/plot"- You have to play through the whole game almost to so that you can (assumedly) go back on the second save file and do everything more intelligently and plan things out to get what I call/assume is Ultros' version of "the true ending" by using items in "the right spots" at the "right times." It's reminding me of the dream bosses in Hollow Knight that are totally skippable, but if you know what to do and when, and what secret areas to go explore, there is a whole other half of the game to be unlocked and seen. That's the best non-spoilers way I can think to explain it with my understanding so far.- There are certain skill tree skills that just sound absolutely useless and they don't really add anything super useful or necessary to the gameplay.- (trying to prevent spoilers here) After each boss, if you don't use the "skill saver" things you can pick up, you lose them. this wasn't explained and I forgot twice now and am short 2 skills in my tree because of it. Don't be like me, just choose a skill and lock it down the second you get this item.[[ Edit disclaimer ]] — I'm about 50% of the way into the game and realizing that you start to understand more the deeper you get. This game feels like Memento or Inception or Shutter Island type movies, but a game. You understand more the further you get, and I assume you than can go back to the beginning on a new file and do it better with your end game understanding.

_childDocuments_.review: Taking apart plants and putting them together like Lego was not on my bingo card. 10/10 would disassemble plants again.This game is incredible. The plants thing is a core and more fun mechanic than I would have imagined. So there are spots you can plant seeds. You can also dig those seeds up and plant the seed again or a different seed. You can take the parts of those plants and splice them with other plants in structurally impossible ways. Some parts you can stand on. Some connect the station's wifi. They also can be used to break certain barriers, block line of sight, and provide nutritious fruit.The rebuilding thing is important to reach certain areas. The networking is important to access certain areas. AND then, you can feed the stations inhabitants who will create new places you can plant seeds. AND then you can pick up and move the monsters so they create MORE places you can plant seeds.EDIT: At 100% I'm sad it's over. This could be my game of the year. I recommend getting to the bad ending quickly to get the Returner. This lets you reset and keep your gear. Keeping your eyes open gets you the memory locks you need to save your entire skill tree (there are about double memory locks than you need in the entire game).It doesn't get tedious because there is so much you can do. I was initially annoyed that the game forced you to loop and start over (kinda) a few times. However, that helped parcel out the mechanics and keep the HUGE map from being too overwhelming.Not to mention the combat mechanics that reward you for killing enemies with all unique moves.I am still not done and I've been ready to write this review for hours.

_childDocuments_.review: A delicious masterpiece but it's not for everyone. It's difficult to describe what make it a truly unique and fun experience so I'll just say that it's something that Shigeru Miyamoto would have designed given his passion for gardening and exploration. The demo and trailers does a poor job of selling the game, this you just have to commit to and be receptive to its weirdness and vision.

_childDocuments_.review: It's so beautiful, but equally dull and tedious in every other aspect of the game. Map progress is often confusing (which, I admit, suits well "psychedelic" aesthetics of the game, but I doubt it was intentional, just a bad design), the movement is clunky, the combat is boring, the levels are nice to look at, but there's virtually nothing in them game-wise, the skills available with food updates are almost all useless, the tree mechanic is nice, but with the inventory wipe on every time loop you rarely have the necessary seed on each planting place. And I finally gave up on the game at the ball-juggling sequence in the Infinity Lake which is utterly frustrating, clumsy and just doesn't work with the game controls.
_childDocuments_.name: Ultros

_childDocuments_.review: I played a bit past mid-game and quit there. The game felt like a very frustrating experience, where you don't have good direction and end up spending a lot of time wandering around similar looking corridors amongs confusing graphics.  All the time while playing I always seemed to have a feeling of not knowing where to go, what to do, or if I'm even doing this thing properly. The graphical style doesn't help. In a metroidvania it's good to have openness, but Ultros goes somewhat overboard with it, leaving the player quite frustrated. Last straw was the ball juggling mini game, but I felt a lot of fatigue a lot before it. Sometimes your multi-tool can break down a fuzzy wall, sometimes it can't. You can never know if you have the right seed for a certain spot. Things like this are frustrating. I'm guessing there are a lot of people who tried / saw the demo and then made the purchase based on that. For me, in hindsight, it didn't feel a good representation of the final game. This game has a lot of neat ideas but combines them in a way that feels like a real frustrating mess to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Ultros is not a bad game, it’s just a bad metroidvania. Yes, you explore a large map, fight enemies, and gather upgrades, but the game at its core is about coexisting in a space, whereas the genre is more about dominating everything in your path. It’s taking tried and true territory and trying something new with it. I dig some of the stuff it’s doing, I just wish it was wrapped up in an experience that felt more constant.Full Review:

_childDocuments_.review: This is an amazing game that continues to stun me with its beautiful environment and unique mechanics.  (Soundtrack is pretty good too ) I have not finished this game yet and will update the review when I do.However, I would like to clarify somethings. This game is a gardening puzzle game. Not an action game, and certainly not a rougelite. People leave bad reviews complaining about the "Rougelite mechanics" and they do exist, and I do admit it is a little annoying to get your upgrades back, but within 2 resets you will basically be able to lock all of your important abilities in place. _childDocuments_.review: Ultros is a refreshingly unique take on the metroidvania genre. Right away it immerses in an enigmatic narrative, as your almost insect-like heroine wakes up aboard a mysterious space station nestled in the far reaches of the galaxy. Soon you'll discover that in the very center of this facility there lies an enigmatic, hostile alien demon Ultros that trapped everyone on board in a never-ending time loop.First thing that is immediately visible is the extremely unique art style, which is truly a feast for the senses. The vivid tapestry of colors and the bizarre yet captivating designs of its inhabitants evoke a sense of awe as you explore this weird alien world, filled with strange multicolored plants, exotic fungi and bizarre creatures that feel like they've been pulled straight out of some kind of LSD-induced fever dream. Despite that, Ultros is a remarkably easy game to read, and there are few accessibility options if you want to blur the background or change the font, for example.I didn't find the game overly difficult, which I don't necessarily think is a bad thing. It definitely doesn't focus on combat or tricky platforming; rather, it focuses on exploration, inviting on a journey of discovery through its labyrinthine corridors and ethereal vistas. Each step forward unveils new pathways, abilities, and secrets, fostering a gratifying cycle of progression. Sooner or later, you will bump into perhaps its most interesting mechanic: the cultivation of various plants. You can find different seeds that, when nurtured, can grow into otherwordly species which basically open new pathways or methods to travel around.Combat is not just about defeating enemies; it's about experimenting with different strategies. Simply relying on basic attacks may yield meager rewards in the form of low-nutrition food. However, diversifying your combat repertoire with a variety of attacks unlocks tastier morsels. Consuming these grants access to unlockable upgrades, which get wiped on every time-loop, but later on you can preserve some of them with items you can find.Ultros is not very long to complete, but if you want to truly 100% the game, then there is a lot to do here. I very much recommend this metroidvania for its unique experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Great idea, great soundtrack, but on the long run not very convincing mechanics. The game does not guide you through the world and the story well. Not knowing what is going on and having to figure the story out is of course the main part. But the game leaves you quite alone, the logic of the loops remains quite opaque and vague, and this is not related to the story but quite rudimentary level design. It tries to be mystic and artistically pleasing, but the mechanics (loop, fighting) are not completely thought through and the games comes only to the point of being a glimpse of what that game could become if worked upon. Should be an early access title with much more player feedback.

name: Dying Light
detailed_description: DYING LIGHT: THE BEAST Kyle Crane returns! The Hero of Harran may have been missing for over a decade, but he's back in Dying Light: The Beast! A thrilling standalone zombie adventure, The Beast carries on Crane's story! For more information, check out the dedicated product page and wishlist the game today to keep updated! EDITIONS COMPARISON About the Game From the creators of hit titles Dead Island and Call of Juarez. Winner of over 50 industry awards and nominations. The game whose uncompromising approach to gameplay set new standards for first-person zombie games. Thanks to its legacy and seven-year post-launch support, today it goes down in history as one of gaming's greatest zombie titles. Survive in a city beset by a zombie virus! Discover the hard choice you will have to make on your secret mission. Will loyalty to your superiors prove stronger than the will to save the survivors? The choice is yours… VAST OPEN WORLD Roam the city with unprecedented freedom and bask in its unique atmosphere. Use parkour to scale every building and reach remote areas. CREATIVE COMBAT Engage in gory combat and discover limitless options to confront your enemies. Use the environment paired with various weapon types and abilities to gain an advantage. DAY AND NIGHT CYCLE Experience the dramatic shift in the world, as you change from a hunter to hunted at sundown. Face the coming threat or run away without wasting your time to look behind. 4-PLAYER CO-OP Join forces with other players and raise your chances of survival in an exciting co-op mode. Tackle the story campaign together and see how far you'll go as a team.

_childDocuments_.review: 24 hours in and I am only at 22% completion. LOVE THIS GAME. Unless something major brings it down, I am giving this a SOLID 9/10.Very entertaining FPS open world zombie survival game. Would recommend to any fans of FPS.  Especially if you, like me, enjoyed the Dead Island games, this is a major upgrade without loosing the fun of those games. And yes, you can still stand on truck and clunk down 20+ biters with no danger to yourself. just don't get caught in the open.If you're worried about the parkour elements, they are not as necessary as they are in the Assasins Creed series. They just make it easier to move around the city.  Ane a beautiful city it is. Very well designed, multi levels, with tons of depth and clutter.  Good story, voice acting and the game looks great on modern hardware.  The map is one of the best I have ever played. It really feels like a city. So much depth and levels.I would recommend getting it now, especially since its on sale. Don't bother with the season pass imho, the dlc looks very thin.Spoiler Review:well, one more piece of good news, there are more than one map, including one whole new city one and a bunch of mini areas, not including buildings. Now, the bad. Crappy ending that makes no damn sense (well, maybe sorta in a video game). They done ruined it, by taking away any sense of immersion with a cartoony villain. Who gets multiple chances to kill you and in true retro-Bond fashion, taunts and plays with instead of just shooting you. Why oh why do developers keep doing this?? All his parts after the initial meeting are so lame. Makes the damn "challenges" in a zombie apocalypse seem logical. At least these can be mercifully skipped. So, an updated score is 8.5/10. Still a good game, but not in the ranks of the great games. Buy it on sale or when/if you hardware can take it, you can probably afford anyways.

_childDocuments_.review: I had fun with this game, and i'd encourage other people to play it. But i find the other reviews too much generous. The game is full of negative aspect and bad design choice.The parkour is fun as hell, WHEN IT WORKS. And that's it, that's the cool part of the game: using parkour to run away from zombies. Combat is absurd, you have to hit a zombie 30 time to kill it, and too often you cannot avoid the fight, even with endgame weapons you'll end up hitting them repetedly. That's a shame because when you manage to kill them in 2-3 hit and dismember them it's vary satisfing (for some reason damage is inconsistent)Killing humans is the same, but they deflect 90% of your attack, so you'll end up fighting them forever or simply using a molotov since they attack in group of 3 very often and you dont want to spend 40minutes killing them. Sad because the combat is actually good and the feedback is nice. Designing it around a more realistic damage would have make the game thousend time more fun.  Wasted potential. There are a tons of way to make the game harder and escape-centered without making the enemies so resistent.IDK why but they made the game so that you'll need to carry like 10 melee weapons because they broke very quickly. Why not simply give you 2-3 slot and much more resistent weapons? Not wasted poetential but certainly dumb design.During the night the game gives its best(vary spooky). The problem is that there is only one mission were you are forced to play at night, why?? Other than running around for fun and exp there are no  reasons to play during the night. Wasted potential.The parkour in the game is used to move around, but this element is central in the campaign only during scripted platforming sequences which are horrible compared the freerunning experience. Except for the challanges scattered around the map, which are really fun. For some reason the developer didnt think that would have been great to make some main missions where you have to chase someone freely using your parkour skills. But no, generic fetch missions are better, i guess. Wasted potential.The story had potentential but guess what? it was wasted. Ending up with a generic villain that is evil because is evil. And the sad moments that arent sad bacause i saw those people 2 time wtf why should i feel touched? But voice acting for the protagonist was good.They also made a DLC where they added a car and deisgned a map where the parkour is not possible(it's a bunch of hills and fields)... in a game where parkour is the main thing. DUDE WHO TF IS MAKING THE CHOICES IN THIS STUDIO.I also experienced a constant and very high frame drop(had to always tweak the video options to fix this each time i played), i'm well above the recommended  spec.6 out of 10, could've been a 8-9. Wasted potential

_childDocuments_.review: The last freaking mission is single player only! WHAAAT?Story in this game is like a nasty wet fart. As the main voice actor of this game is Roger Craig Smith, I would often imagine crazy scenarios involving Resident Evil character Chris Redfield. After a while I would imagine myself playing Resident Evil 5 instead.Enemies are too spongy and the melee-combat is a drag compared to Dead Island. Upgrades are boring and mostly useless. After opening the skill that allows you to jump over zombies, you are basically invincible against the basic dudes.The basic zombies are no fun to fight. Even after you have leveled up the base-dudes remain spongy and will stun-slap you around like the little b*tch you are. The special infected are even more boring than their counterparts in Dead Island. Dude, Left 4 Dead came out more than a decade ago. What you get in Dying light is stripped down versions of those enemies. Lame boomer, lame hunter and lame big dude. The melee in this game feels a lot like unmodded Oblivion. The enemies are always leveling up faster than the player. Even at max level you feel weak. Unlike Dead Island, you rarely get to feel decently powerful. Most of the weapons are useless because of the stamina drain. The sledgehammer slam and spinning feels useless. It's slow, does not stun enemies with consistency and leaves you open for massive counter damage barrage. The weapon modding is more restrictive and tamed-down than in DI. You will have to buy the dlc to get more variety. I felt that DI had the weapon modding more integrated with the whole. The skill system overall is disappointing. After you unlock all of the mobility options there is really nothing fun or game-changing to discover. The endgame consist off grinding multiple levels without any unlocks to unlock. Agility system encourages you to just run over the enemies and the ineffectiveness of melee steers you towards avoidance of all non-story encounters. The grappling-hook was almost fun, but makes you avoid enemies even more. And some of the skill-unlocks killed me more than any of the enemies. The wall-jump is a beginner’s trap for sure. It does nothing useful, besides killing you randomly. It is that Oblivion feel again that the levelling feels detrimental.We played Dead Island and this back to back. Most of the eurojankiness of Dead Island feels ironed out. More we played on, the more I was playing just because I loved DI. Last third of this game is like a plane crash. Feels like the developer runs out of money before your eyes, as you play the game. The cheapness was more pungent here than in DI. Strange sidestepping overall.To not be able to play that last mission with my friend, just because some lame quick-time bs, makes me even more angry. We had co-op -quick-times in Resident Evil 5 all those years ago, why not here? Overall its somewhat fun with friends, but the game will fight you back at some points. If you really liked Dead Island, you will maybe like this game too. On sale ;D.Here hoping that devs will bring back the fun of Dead Island for their next game.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: This reviewer has 500+ hours on an alternative accountDying Light is the third edition to Techlands Zombie Killing games, and manages to incorporate some familiar, and improved features from Dead Island 1 and Riptide, with a few weak points here and there.You have your weapon crafting and repairing system, similar to how Dead Island Riptide handled it, but this time, you're able to have increased stats from weapon mods which effect how much damage your weapon does, or even the speed and critical rate, which is nice to have once you learn how it works.Weapon Quantity has been increased too, with more unique variants of weapons, and base weapons when compared to Dead Island or even Riptide, with the rest being DLC weapons that have their models and textures locked away until you purchase the dlc, which isn't bad, but the Bozak Horde DLC is a bit questionable, but we'll get to that later.The graphics and animation are a major step up from Dead Island 1 & Riptide, with more fluid animations, more animations in general, and proper god rays and beautiful textures that are nice to look at.Low-Tier gaming rigs should avoid playing the game on ultra, anything with, let's say a 550ti can run the game on high settings or more.The weakest point of the game, cardboard box tier character interest, and an annoying QTA sequence that'll happen to you makes it a bit frustrating to get through, there's some interesting characters here and there, just not enough of them.One of the earliest DLC's done with Dying Light, you're able to be invaded by Night Hunters controlled by other players, or do it yourself!You can turn this off or have certain conditions before it happens, It's pretty fun and hilarious to surprise friends with.Mostly used for its weapons, The Bozak Horde offers a short story alone or with your friends, with the story being mostly forgettable, and the final boss being poorly implemented.The Following offers and entirely new world, rivaling that of the main game itself, with places to explore, side quests to do, and an all new  to ride in, so you can mow zombies over and get to places faster.Sadly, It's exclusive to the DLC Worldspace, but the main game is cramped enough and meant for parkour so it's reasonable.Dying Light is a pretty decent zombie killing game, one of the underrated games that came out in 2015, It's fun alone, and even more enjoyable with friends.

_childDocuments_.review: + Gameplay/ControlsThe Gameplay of dying light is very good. You have various ways to distract zombies and kill them. The World is also filled with traps which can be used given the player unlocks skills to use them. After unlocking the third and last tier of abilities the game really is fun to play. With help of the grappling hook your way of traveling through the world and avoid obstacles completely changes. While climbing up something can be fun getting down is a complete different story. I died many deaths just to get down a tower. At times this can be even a frustrating experience. Thats why I am thankful for the existence of objects like  zip lines and trash heaps which can be found at most places.~ Inventory, Items, Crafting and UpgradingAt the beginning the player can only carry four weapons.  Of course it is possible to increase the amount of items the character can carry with the skill system. Weapons can be repaired 3-5 time depending on their rarity until they are completely useless. While limiting the amount of possible repairs is realistic it defeats the purpose of an upgrading and crafting system. Why create new items when they degrade that fast by using them? The only weapons which don’t degrade are guns.  I personally did not upgrade or create many items as the degradation through use takes all the fun out of the upgrading and crafting system. - Main CampaignThe main campaign is probably the worst campaign I ever played in my life. Many missions just allow for certain ways to play it. While the game is open world the story missions don’t allow for different approaches. Items like the grappling hook are essentially useless for most missions. There even is a mission where you are forced to use quicktime events although no other mission before even indicated that quicktime events were even part of the game. During the campaign some important character die. However the game utterly fails to create an emotional bond so you would care for the characters. All in all the story combined with the level design of the missions is a complete disaster. ~ Skill systemThe skill system has three main trees: survival, combat and agility/acrobatics. The agility tree improves by climbing obstacles. The better you are the easier and faster you can jump and climb obstacles. The combat tree improves by fighting and killing enemies. The combat tree mainly focuses on melee combat and improves strength and attacks on enemies. Lastly there is the survival tree. It improves by doing quests and reacting to random events which occur in the world. Improving these abilities increases their levels which in turn gives points with which it is possible to unlock improvements for the character. Some Unlocks allow for increased inventory space other unlock a grappling hook or even a shield. Unfortunately the system is misused as an “unlock” system rather than being skilltree which reflects the growth of the character. Best example would be the inventory system. So what do I mean by that? There is an unlock for the ability to carry more weapons. However combat unlocks which improve strength of attacks which logically could increase carry weight don’t affect the number of carryable weapons. Unfortunately this is a problem with most games which try to combine Action with RPG mechanics.+ EnemiesThe enemies are diverse enough for a zombie game. Many enemies have their weak spots. While most of the time you will encounter the “walker” zombie which is slow there are areas where you can encounter stronger zombies, venom spitting zombies or “runners”. Also fighting humans forces you to a different strategy. As every human is a master of self defense in melee combat you are bound to use guns. That way you are forced to decide whether you use guns and attract zombies with the gun fire or just avoid them. - Dying light vs. Dead IslandThe game was developed by the studio which created Dead Island so is it better? Dying light is in terms of gameplay is a step forward as opposed to Dead Island. In Dead Island I had many encounters which to me were just unfair. The problem was it’s combat system. In comparison to that I never had that feeling in Dying light. If I died in the open world (not the story missions) I died because I made a mistake which I easily could avoid. In dying light it is also more important to be aware of the surroundings. Your approach is much more tactical. After all you can lure your enemies in deadly traps, use firecrackers to distract them or kick them of roofs. Unfortunately this is the only instance where Dying light shines. I rather prefer the tropical atmosphere of Dead Island. Although Dead Island has not the best story - it is a zombie game for crying out loud - I felt more connected to the characters in Dead Island than in Dying Light. Dying Light strifes to be more realistic in its approach. It does not have levelling enemies and hitting enemies where it hurts is more rewarding. The Skill system has no super powers and you have access to all the abilities with your character, there are no more classes. Still as the story missions are extremely lacking. You end up with a game where just the controls and non levelling enemies are better than Dead Island.- ConclusionDying light has really good controls running and jumping from roof to roof can be fun. Unfortunately this is the only good part of the game. Story, characters, item system and many more just aren’t good enough at all. Back when Dead Island first came out it got a very harsh critique. However at least that game allowed me to keep my weapons and had characters I felt some emotional connection. Not to mention of the campaign. It seems as if the developer behind dying light were only interested in creating an open world and good controls to move around in it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a mixed bag. It is pretty casual zombie slaughtering fun and the parkour stuff is fun. There are some very frustrating drawbacks though. The game teaches you how to climb, but not how to climb down safety so you will die quite a few times learning how those mechanics work. There are also some decorative things in the game that you think you can grab but nope, it only appears to be a hand hold, loading please wait. Part way through the game you get this bad ass grappling hook that makes you like spider-man but then because you end up using it all the time you stop getting better or even get worse at climbing. Then the game just takes it away from you when you need it most. There is no story reason why you can’t use it, you are just suddenly ‘exhausted’. I understand that its to make that part of the game less trivial but there should be a logical reason given. The final mission is lame as hell. By this point I was a little tired of the game, but I wanted to complete it and suddenly it gets more difficult than it has been by a large margin. For the almost the entire game you can take things pretty much at your own pace. I like playing it slow and methodical but that isn’t an option anymore after 90 hours. It’s hard enough sometimes to know where to go next but it’s that much harder when you have to figure it out in ½ second intervals. In the final encounter of the game it introduces a new game mechanic without warning. In the middle of what seems like a cinematic scene suddenly letters start popping up on the screen for you to press in time to dodge an attack. I’ve never liked this mechanic in games but its extra frustrating for it to come out of no where after playing the game for 90+ hours.

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game, even better if you have friends to play with. Gameplay is solid and fun. It feels great to parkour through the city, especially in a game where running and moving quick is most times better than fighting the zombies, who can overrun you pretty fast and are really though in the beginning of the game. Weapons feel fun to use, and the durability of weapons forces you to change weapons often and have an inventory of extras, but with the ability of repairing them a limited amount of times and the many weapons that you find scavenging, this system didnt get annoying once. It has great voice acting, especially your player, and every loading screen in between side quests and main missions has a voice acted narration from the protagonist. Game area doesnt seem too big, but when your only mode of moving around is running, it seems huge, plus you get a whole new second map in the base game that changes gameplay a bit with many more buildings and close quarters situations. Guns will take a long time to find but are pretty powerful once you get them. They can be a little too powerful sometimes, but with the need to headshot zombies to kill in one shot and the lack of easy to find ammo, they seem more balanced. Plus enemies wielding guns will also be really powerful. Nearing the end game, zombies will not be too much of a worry and you'll choose to fight more often than running, but nights will always be brutal and can go from 0 to 100 reaaaal quick.Overall, I really recommend this game if you're looking for a zombie-survival game or a fun 2-4 player coop. If you're like me you'll find yourself playing this game with your friends for hours without realizing that you've been playing for that long.

_childDocuments_.review: Despite only having 13 hours in the game on Steam, I formerly played this game on Epic Games and have about 60 hours there. With that experience, I can confidently make this claim:Dying Light has, and I do not say this lightly, the best skill tree or upgrade system in any video game I've ever played. Every single thing on it isn't just some throwaway situational thing that you'll use once, or just some simple stat upgrade, but a unique mechanic that perfectly fits in the game. Once you unlock it, it almost feels like you can't play without it, yet it's not something that they simply withheld from the beginning, but something new that they add. And the fact that you unlock them in an order makes it so that you learn each and every skill as you progress through the game. They could have given you all the abilities in the beginning of the game, and leave you faced with dozens of mechanics and abilities that you somehow need to learn how to smoothly integrate into a completely unfamiliar environment and playstyle, but the progression allows you to develop your skills in the basic mechanics, then slowly increase the complexity of your gameplay as you naturally become better at playing the game as a whole. The fact that there's three skill trees makes it so that you can spend your skill points to enhance your individual playstyle and add to what it is you do as a unique player, but the game doesn't make you choose between the three permanently, allowing you to unlock from any tree at any time at any level.

The combat on the other hand was nothing to boast about. It basically feels just as static as skyrim. Most enemies will probably not even stagger if you hit them with a hammer, and unless you upgrade your melee weapons a lot, then you might as well use your hands. I went through the game just avoiding fights at first, then when I learned how overpowered kicking was I spammed that until I got guns later on in which it was a balance of both. This mostly worked except for one boss in the late game, which made everything a living hell.---{Audio}---The audio of the game is stellar and helps a lot with the atmosphere and intensity when needed. Being hunted at night or just in general being in scary situations, is made so much more nerve-cracking with the music that runs in the background.---{Audience}---There's blood, swearing and lots of not pog stuff, so older teens/adults is the audience it's made for---{PC Requirements}---I was able to run the game with max graphics and 60fps with my pc which has:AMD Ryzen 5 1400 ProcessorNvidia GeForce GTX 1070 Graphics Card8GB RAMAnything signifcantly worse than that would result in you maybe being forced to play on lower graphics if you want to keep your framerate over 60---{Difficulity}---The difficulty really depends on how you approach the game. For me spamming E to kick the living ♥♥♥♥ out of everything in my way when needed as well as guns to counter the bad guys with guns was how I got through most of the game. and there was only one point of the game where that would result in punishment. Enemies rarely ever stagger from melee weapons so if you wanna use those then a hit and run tactic is you best shot at making it anywhere. Kicking will send most common enemies flying to the moon and guns... they shoot and things go boom. Bigger enemies and most bosses don't stagger at all, which sometimes is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ but whatever. Overall the fighting in this game, especially bosses just sucks and I had little fun with them.---{Grind}---If you grind stuff, abilities and upgrading weapons then you can maybe be able to go through the game without spamming kick and gunshooting, but there's only really one point where I feel that will be greatly rewarded, which is a late game boss that no one likes and that has more ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ in it than a bull that hasn't pooped in a week although it's fat and has been running 24/7. If you've been grinding then that fight pretty much becomes free but if not you're going to suffer from the amount of "wtf" emotions it'll give you. Grinding is for the most part completely unncessary unless you want to indulge more with the game's atmosphere.---{Story}---The story is pretty solid, nothing ground breaking but does the job well. One thing that puts me a little off is the voice acting, which just doesn't sound as lived in as it maybe should've.. idk maybe it's just me but it just sounded a little odd and not fitting at times. It does pull you in well though and is a story to pursue throughout the game.---{Game Time}---All main missions took me around 9 hours to complete, and if you include the side quests then it would probably take around double that time. DLCs on top of that might double that again. Overall you should get a good amount of hours into the game.---{Price}---In my opinion the price is too high, and therefore I reccomend that you instead buy it when it's all on sale.---{Bugs}---I did not really encounter many bugs, some things would happen that annoyed me a lot but other than that I don't think I came across anything mayor.OVERALL I think it's a solid game that will provide a fun experience. Everything except for a certain point in the endgame was awesome to go through, with the mentioned part spiking in difficulty if you don't play the game in a certain way and is overall just super annoying. I would reccomend it neverthelss though since I think it'll give a fun experience!7/10
