_childDocuments_.review: Just look at the reviews. This game is amazing, apparently. Why? I really don't know.This game is mediocre, it's not bad. Take Far Cry, switch out the militants and animals for zombies, switch out the stealth and heavy gunplay for parkour and make-shift, post-apocalyptic DIY weaponry. There you are, if that sounds like it'd be your thing, go for it, this game is pretty cheap on sale and you'll probably love it. My main problem here is that anything this game does, there are other games that I've played that has those same elements, but does them better. This game just does a lot, competently. Like open world sandbox-y games? Well the market is flooded with them. Like first person survival games? Far Cry is cheaper and does it better (The whole time playing this I was having flashbacks to how much I'd rather be playing Far Cry 3). Like zombie games? The market is flooded with those too, but I prefer ones with more of a horror element (Resident Evil Remake, RE4, RE7, Dead Rising, Left4Dead). Like parkour and mobility? Honestly, I DO NOT THINK parkour works in the first-person (like, at all), so I think you'd be better off with an Assassins Creed game, and if you like power trips with your mobility, Prototype or Saints Row 4 may be up your alley.I just found this game frustrating. You're supposed to be this secret agent badass, then in a comical fashion immediately upon starting the game, you get overwhelmed by a streetpunk, drop your gun, and get the one dude trying to help you killed. You then get given a toothpick and some rubber bands, and have to travel the city unable to do jack against anyone. It takes a WHILE before you get anything good, and every death just feels super cheap and unwarranted. Now, you MIGHT find it fun if you have a friend willing to play along through the game with you, doing a stride-for-stride coop campaign. If you play with randos online, they'll just give you  game-breaking sh*t immediately that you haven't earned, which kills the point of playing the game. I might as well be playing GTA with cheats on at that point.Also, the controls are super wonky on a keyboard. I typically play any first person game with a mouse and keyboard because it controls way better, but the keybindings for this one make navigating menus make NO SENSE. You flip through menu tabs with F7 for God's sake. I NEVER see that. I guess this one's made mainly for consoles, and they didn't care about converting over alternate control schemes? Your guess is as good as mine. I REALLY tried to like this one, I promise. I put in 7 and a half hours cause I thought "maybe my initial impression is wrong, I'll play again another day afresh, and then I'll see the charm and appeal." But nope! Oh well. Once again, if you REALLY like zombies and parkour, you'd probably like this one. Doubly so if you've never experienced a Far Cry game before.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is an exhilarating and immersive experience that masterfully blends open-world exploration, parkour mechanics, and intense zombie survival. Developed by Techland, this game sets a high standard for the survival horror genre, offering players an adrenaline-pumping adventure in the fictional city of Harran.Immersive Parkour System: The game's parkour mechanics are incredibly fluid and intuitive, allowing players to navigate the urban landscape easily. Whether you're scaling buildings, vaulting over obstacles, or making daring rooftop jumps, the movement feels natural and exhilarating.Dynamic Day-Night Cycle: The day-night cycle significantly impacts gameplay, adding a layer of strategy and tension. During the day, zombies are relatively manageable, but when night falls, the fearsome Volatiles emerge, turning the game into a heart-pounding race for survival.Engaging Combat: Combat in Dying Light is visceral and satisfying. The variety of weapons, from makeshift melee tools to firearms, combined with the ability to craft and upgrade gear, keeps the combat fresh and exciting. The melee combat, in particular, feels weighty and impactful.Rich Open World: Harran is beautifully detailed and offers a diverse environment filled with secrets to uncover, side quests to complete, and challenges to overcome. The world feels alive, with dynamic events and NPCs that react to your presence and actions.Co-op Multiplayer: The game shines even brighter when played in co-op mode. Teaming up with friends to tackle missions, scavenge for supplies, and survive the night together adds fun and camaraderie to enhance the overall experience.Repetitive Quests: While the main story is compelling, some side quests can feel repetitive over time. The objectives often involve fetching items or clearing out areas, which might become monotonous for some players.Difficulty Spike: The difficulty can spike abruptly, especially during night missions or encounters with special infected. This can be frustrating for new players who might need more preparation for the sudden increase in challenge.Voice Acting and Story: While the story engages, some voice acting and dialogue can be hit-or-miss. Certain characters may appear clichéd or less developed, which might detract from the overall narrative immersion.Dying Light is a standout title that delivers an exhilarating, immersive zombie survival experience. Its innovative parkour system, dynamic day-night cycle, and the rich open world make it a must-play for fans of the genre. Despite minor flaws, the game's strengths far outweigh its weaknesses, offering countless hours of thrilling gameplay. Whether you're playing solo or with friends, Dying Light is a game that should be noticed.
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: The opening scene pretty much sets the mood for the game: you're a badass special forces dude responsible for air dropping into a zombie quarantine zone, infiltrating the leading gangs, and locating information vital to saving millions of lives.  So... you botch the landing, get caught by some gangsters who somehow know exacly where you're going to land, then let them beat the ♥♥♥♥ out of you with pipes/wrenches instead of shooting them with your gun.  Lucky for those guys, their pipe wrenches are much more durable than anything you'll find in this game.  10 lbs steel pipe wrenches stop working as clubs after ~12 hits.  Any fancier weapon you build out of a solid looking piece of metal is even more fragile.  And despite your badass commandoness, you have the biceps of an 8 year old because it takes like 4 head hits to kill a zombie.Speaking of durability issues, walls are invincible.  There are cans of propane all over the place that will wreck you or a group of zombies pretty easily, but they won't put a scratch in a wood fence.  So don't think about doing anything clever like killing rival gangsters by knocking a hole in their compound to let the zombies in.Lastly, I hope you have 8 fingres per hand because you're gunna need them when it's time to move + run + jump + kick + slide, all of which are different buttons.  And you can't map the same button to multiple functions, because programming is hard, or something.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll simply start by saying that Dying Light is -- hands down -- the best open world game I've played in my entire gaming career. In fact, it's fast becoming one of my favorite all-time games (and I've been gaming since the '80s).As opposed to others in its genre (Assassin's Creed, Sleeping Dogs, Red Dead Redemption, Skyrim, ...), this game does not propel you from one mission to the other, having you grab for fast travel at every opportunity. No, you'll be crawling through the streets or jumping across roofs to try to get to your next mission alive! The in-between is just as much fun -- if not more so -- than the actual missions.Which is not to say that the story is bad, far from it. You'll find yourself engrossed in the unraveling story line, meeting interesting and colorful (and every now and then comical) characters, with voice acting well done ... finally!Add on top of that a seamless parcour gameplay, four completely different parallel RPG-style skill trees, a crafting system that finds the perfect balance between having to search for new material and using awesome weaponry -- until they are broken and you either repair it or build something new --, fantastic mo-capped animations for monsters, a tense and exciting day-night cycle, and to top it all off -- the lush cherry on the delicious whipped cream -- an unbelievably stunning graphics engine.Oh, and the zombies are sufficiently creepy and so very believable! This game has my heart pumping with fear, excitement, and relief dashing for the nearest safe zone while a viral or hunter is chasing me down. Something that hasn't happened ever since I played Thief in '98.Another thing I need to mention: every other game I've played like this is only really exciting for the first couple of hours. After that, I rely on save games to get away with recklessness and, given enough tries, complete whatever task I'm undertaking. Not so with Dying Light. Death is not permanent and you'll respawn in the nearest safe zone, but you will lose plenty of survival skill points, making you fall behind on that skill tree. That's incentive enough to be careful and make for a continuously tense and exciting game.Just one piece of advice, though: turn of the minimap and take your time to try to learn the layout of the city by heart. There are plenty of landmarks that help you find your way. This greatly improves on the immersion and gameplay.
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: If you've played Dead Island 2, come back after checking out some Youtube clips etc. The game is a lot of fun if you're a fan of Mirrors Edge and fancy a bit more combat mixed in. The storyline so far in my limited exposure to it is average, however the gameplay more than makes up for that as does the city you've got to explore. I've wasted a lot of time simply messing about with zombies, rather than following the plot and to be perfectly honest this for me is essentially a relax and bash game and it's perfect for that.I'd recommend it, but do your research first - this isn't going to everyones cup of tea especially if you're a bit of a hardcore zombie game fan.Personally I think it'd be improved by removing the Safe houses, or limiting their size so those with a court yard and building are smaller, perhaps just the building itself. Volatites should be allowed to chase you right up to the door, I understand the UV lights, but since they're on the perimeter why not simply had them charge past if they're already after you - Right now it feels a little too much like a carebear zone.Lasting the "Sixth sense" should be removed, simply makes finding loot and avoiding non-standard zombies that little too easy.Personally I'd say it's 6/10 solo and 8/10 coop, multiplayer is fantastic fun.

_childDocuments_.review: I genuinely loved original Dying Light; both on console and PC. The combat and parkour felt satisfying and there were loads of things to do, as well as, goof around with. I actually had fun goofing around with these brain-dead, zombies and their evolved brethren. I'll always comeback to this game if I just want to mess around or genuinely replay the story.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is good, but apart from the main storyline, it seriously lacks enjoyable side missions. It's main storyline is also devoid of any depth or character development. It's far too short in my opinion. I was playing it for 9 hours and following the storyline half-arsed because me and my friend got distracted by loot or fighting zombies. Anyways, after 9 hours had passed, I was pleased to see we had completed 9% of the game. However, after a few hours had passed, storymode completion shot up to 53%! We didn't concentrate on the story more intensely in those hours though, so really I was expecting it to go up to 18% or something. We were just playing it as normal so it's very bizarre it did that. So, I feel like the developers deliberately did that to dupe people into thinking the storyline was going to get more immerseive when it finished a mere 2 hours later.The last mission is really, really long, and it's really enjoyable. Lots of parkouring, zombie killing (though I just avoided them to get to the more interesting parts) and scares. But for some stupid reason, you can't co-op the last mission! What were the developers thinking?It also seems like 50% of the game is set inside the sewers (which I just hate because there's nothing much to do in them). While not doing the main storyline mission or the side missions you can parkour around the place (there are various challenges set up but I've played none of them so don't know what they're like). I've been co-oping it with a friend and it's been great. But, I must say, I've been quite disappointed when there weren't sniper rifles in the game as the game seems perfect for them. You have bows (exploding, electric, incendiary and regular arrows - although I think you can only get these if you purchase the DLC), along with one type of rifle, shotgun and pistol. For me, the assortment of guns in the game is very limiting (I wish there was a whole load more). There's loads of melee weapons (which can get boring after a while), I just wish there were more guns and even an RPG in the game (there's molotovs though). I bought the DLC as well, so in total you have quite a large area to cover (there are 3 maps in total).All in all, it's a really good game at a very okay-ish price (bought it for $15 through a steam sale plus the $9 for the DLC). Would I ever pay $60 for this type of game? Hell no. Would I pay less than half as much? Yeah, sure. Only buy this game if it's on sale, otherwise you might find you've been ripped off a little. Would I also ever play this in single player? Nope. I wouldn't recommend it. I would only ever do it in co-op (where you can have up to 5 players in one map).

_childDocuments_.review: UPDATE JULY 2016 - the following (SPOILERS):After playing a few hours one day I found myself loading Far Cry 4, which I have already finished, just roaming the land or playing outpost master, because it is still more fun than DL-The Following.Why? Because The Following is as tedious as the original. The car breaks even faster than the weapons, every third box, locker or car needs to be lockpicked, the map is too dark (why?) and you have to learn the roads by heart for driving (no indicator like in Far Cry). All this, plus the annoying day/night cycle make the game just no fun to play. So today I checked out he ending(s) on Youtube, and they are both unhappy endings. I am not playing an incredibly tedious game with beautiful graphics and great parcours running (I give 'em that) for hours only to see an ending that sucks - ♥♥♥♥ You Techland - I am done with the Dying Light series.Dying Light review:Single player is incredibly booooring! Takes a long time to get good weapons, weapons break easily (metal parts are made of paper in this crapfest of a game). The day-night cycle is just tedious: if you don't have good weapons you have to wait out the night by going to a safehouse and sleep instead of continuing with the mission. Open world may be good (the graphics are, I give them that) but in this case it's just all the same - at least it feels that way. And you can't drive any vehicles (at least in the first few hours I have played) ...sucks.If you want to buy, wait until there is a sale, where it's at least 75% off. More than 5 bucks I would not pay....

_childDocuments_.review: A game what Dead Island was meant to be. The story is not that long and kind of reminds me of Dead Island series, but it's definitely better and different. This is an action survival game presented in first-person perspective and is set in a vast and dangerous open world. During the day and night, you run around an urban environment among the dead, scavenging for supplies and crafting weapons to help you defeat the hordes and fight even more terrified monsters during the night.Dying Light has a great story, amazing music/atmosphere, graphics, fighting mechanics, executions, weapon handling, night life () and awesome monster designs. In the recent patches the game got a huge story/world expansion as well as Steam Workshop, which adds even more content to already huge game. This game is well worth it's price and I can definitely recommend the expansion pass.

_childDocuments_.review: As I have poured 40+ hours into this already I will give my review.Dying Light is Mirrors Edge and Dead Island smacked together with a sandbox. Really, its a bit of fun. And you have to make the fun by taking chances. You can stay ontop of buildings, run like a madman, smash zombies in, or just fool around.One them this game does so well is kept me engaged. I found myself wanting to do side missions to get more stuff...and the fact random suvivors suddenly call out to be helped, or airdrops fall in make you INSTANTLY lose track of what you are doing and mad rush for the drop to get all of the supplies before the enemy can. I found myself more than once hearing the background noise of a plane, perking up, only to not see the plane and be disappointed.This game does have some setbacks. The multiplayer is a bit shimmy shammy. Everyone has the same skin/look.  Every once in awhile you will experience a glitch or two, like one time I got stuck mid air above a safe zone... but that only happened once.Overall, the game gets a solid 8/10. If it had better skins for multiplayer and if the storyline was a bit more...written, It could easily be higher. But the fact the game has so much going forward, it is definately a game worth buying, playing, and messing around with.
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: It's a typical Technland product, that's for sure, but it was also to be expected that there will be issues (performance optimizations).So far however that is my only negative aspect. I already liked the Dead Islands and Dying light improves every aspect (controlls, story, characters, gameplay, overall size). It's by far not perfect, but in my opinion the best zombie game right now. Not too arcady and not too much realism simulator either.Also, the combination of Dead Island and Mirrors Edge feels like a natural fusion and pretty much all I wished for. It always hurts in fps games, that even small obstacles stop you movement and the constant feeling "in real live getting up there wouldn't be an issue at all. (There are still places and borders you can't go around, but those are at a minimum and don't affect the gamplay too much)There are a lot of people that have an issue with decaying weapons, but honestly, there are more than enough lying around, and you can repair your weapons and with skills you can delay the decay.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are looking to experience a zombie apocalypse, then this game is the best for it. Very eye appealing graphics, realistic animations for everything, loads of ways to cut a zombie(vertical, horizontal, just head, arms or legs) and a lot of skills for doing so. Also, I recommend buying Dying Light The Following if you enjoyed Dying Light, because it offers a vast open world, new blueprints, weapons, a new type of zombie, and also the buggy for traveling long distances. This game can be played for an extremely long time if you want to get the Legend rank 250(about 200-400 hours of hard grinding I guess). This game is a must-have for your steam library.

_childDocuments_.review: minor spoilersThe quick version:Buy for the stunning, engrossing man vs city vs zombie action, awesome stuff.Don't buy for a good story or satisfying ending. When I play again I'm going to see if the storyline can be changed significantly through my actions.As it stands on a single play through...One of the worst story-lines ever with some of worst characterisation ever. Completed with probably the worst final boss fight ever.The protagonist is an absolute moron who from the first 5 minutes shows that the entire plot-line is built around cutscenes of a gullible, naive idiot with no obvious skills. This despite being portrayed in previous cutscenes as an experienced soldier. Nothing you do seems to  change the never ending sequence of screw-ups our main man keeps making. After a while you notice that the game is still trying to catch you out but you just find yourself quietly giving in, already knowing the outcome in advance. This is because the plot-line reuses the same tired shocks over and over and over. In other areas the plot is just plain wrong and contradicts itself.One really noticeable point of consternation is the startlingly obvious missed opportunities to end the entire game (yeah I know we don't want that). I found myself thinking - "just shoot, now, do it , gimme back control, shoot him, SHOOT HIM, ah here we go again......". You cannot immerse yourself in a game that you fundamentally think should have ended already. It just needed a single shot that couldn't be taken because you had no control of your character. Also whilst you had no control major parts of the story-line were advanced in ways that most experienced gamers will find infuriating.Special mention here must go to the final boss fight - it's unbelievably bad and features all of the above mentioned issues. To put it bluntly the entire boss fight was summed up with about 6 presses of the keyboard, intentionally. My weapons were yet again taken from me, my choice removed and all fun erased. That fun was replaced by yet another WTF cut scene of terrible quality. It's hard for me to put into words how bad this is. This is a game, let me play it, if I have made some bad decisions give me the chance to get out of them.  If you want to make b-movies go make b-movies.The writing is lazy and annoying but the badness doesn't stop there. The character has forced upon him regular limitations, for often obvious reasons because the devs couldn't write the story to match the scenery. For example:"you cannot use 'spoiler' because you are exhausted" - after seeing this you'll get to sprint a life or death race through the sewers. Or fight a dozen zombies at once. Clearly not exhausted?or the often repeated scenarios where: if you shoot this guy now you'll win!- at this point you'll suddenly have no control of your character, or you have had your weapons/gear taken from you during a moment of having no control of your character.if you use an open radio system, (that you set up pretty much for your enemy), to communicate sensitive information then your enemies will find you and the peeps you just revealed, and they will kill everyone you love.-throughout the game you'll use the open radio system to communicate all plans, locations etc etc. and the ones you love...... how many times will our protagonist go to the rescue of someone they truly, madly, deeply care about? This depth of feeling feels very strange having only arrived a couple of days ago! In this oft repeated scenario he always finds himself disarmed and thrust into a life or death arena designed to limit player skills with the devs choice of weapons only to...... ultimately lose ? over and over? after a short while care for any character in the game and the excitement is gone - replaced with "I know whats coming, lets get it over with". Really poor.The voice acting is good, but the script is incredibly poor, the sound editing though is worse if that could be possible. On more than one occasion you'll have two important dialogues going off at the same time, through no fault of your own. And damn, if one more character says to me about how good the radios are now!!As a story driven game this is a mediocre experience overall  - however, forget the b-movie plot and acting and enjoy the physics - then Dying Light becomes a whole different ball game.Racing across the city (at night ?) collecting items, killing zombies and rescuing people is quite simply awesome. When played as a zombie killing simulator or perhaps a 'runaway from zombies' simulator then this game truly comes alive (pun intended). With a gentle learning curve in the parkour/combat skill sets you'll be racing across the cityscape in no time whilst performing death defying leaps and zombie kill stunts to die for. Its for this and this alone it gets a thumbs up.A final thing - yeah I know it's a game, but given the whole time sensitive mission to prevent the you know what from arriving, I dunno maybe a single satellite photo of the city would have said everything. Maybe I'm thinking too hard. OK how about a single photo from any aircraft ? No? Does it interfere with the plot too much. I don't think it would be hard to see survivors in the city from outside. And the whole story is based around this premise.another final thing - the scenarios with the big smiley fire face and its outcome Versus the super tall antenna and its outcomemake your mind up devs.Get it for the action. Not the writing.
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game that does not respect the player. It's a single-player skinner box designed to waste your time, but tricks you into thinking that you're having fun. First thing you see when launching the game is the option to buy Dying Light 2. Not off to a great start.Stupidest thing I've ever seen in this game: crafting takes time. Which would make sense if it also took in-game time, so you couldn't craft in the middle of a fight. But no: gameplay is paused. So there's this stupid progress bar that only exists to annoy you.You have no agency. The entire game is a series of repetitive fetch quests or "go to three locations and do a thing, then go to a final location and do a thing." At one point the villain is monologuing about his "pit" that he has people fight in. I thought, "wow, I bet there will be a mission where I'm captured during a cutscene, stripped of my weapons and equipment, and forced to fight a bunch of zombies in a gladatorial arena." ...aaaand that's exactly what happened a couple of hours later. It's a shame, because this could have been a great game. The core mechanics feel good, and the art direction is pretty nice, but in the end it's just another Ubisoft-like open world game. Vast but shallow.Oh and one more thing: remember the boomers from Left for Dead? They're in this game, and guess what they're called?They're called. "Bombers." That's the most blatant rip-off I've ever seen in a game. So lazy...
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: If i could make this a mixed feelings review i would, but there are too many negatives for me to give Dying Light a thumbs up. Also, some light spoilers, you're warned.I'll not cover the movement/parkour mechanics which are one of the strong point, even if somewhat a bit glichy at time. The graphisms and sound design are also great. Also good point for the voice acting which was really niceThen there's the rest._No manual saves and a strange autosave one. I wasted between 5 to 10 hours because of that._Survivor xp loss on death,  even after finishing the dlc, i was still not maximum rank survivor because i died so much  to complete ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. _Exploration : one of the ok point of the game thanks to the open world maps,thare are a lot of buildings and  places to explore and things to find.  Unfortunately, after a while , there are too many back and forth and it takes too long since there is no fast travel between safe points. It is even worse in The Following because of how the map is made, even with the buggy, there is so much clutter on the roads that it makes it difficult to enjoy it.Also far too often, just wandering around is ruined by randoms spawns of virals, or at times an overabundance of volatiles that made it impossible to do anything. But even more, i feel that exploration is mostly lacking purpose past a certains point. Money has no use, craft ressources are common,   and there isn't much else to find aside from collectibles which are useless by themselves. _Combat, skill and weapon system. It is too inconsistent. you start the game as a god of kick, you can shoot any zombie into spikes 20 meters away and almost never use any weapons except against humans.     Then as your survivor rank goes up, so does the zombies that scales with you. And the kick no longer works againt anything. Even the dropkick ability, that is dangerous to use in a lot of situation, become really quite underwhelming and often get really dodged or just "doesn't work".  So yes, unfortunately, the early fun of kicking basic zombies à la Bulletstorm is really short lived.-Then there are agility and combat skills, and some of them are actually detrimental to the gameplay, so detrimental that thankfully i knew about them beforehand and did not unlock them since skills can't be "turned off".  -Weapons :  durability is bad in its current form, and melee seriously doesn't do enough damage. Firearms on the other hand are really strong, and ammunition isn't rare. -Ennemies : quickly it gets into the melee/bullet sponge territory which is unfortunate. Also, virals,  these guys ruined the game for me far too often because they would randomly spawn at times, directly come to attack me and they are hands down the most annoying ennemy to fight in the game. Even volatiles are better than them. All special types of zombies, while not original, are fine on the other hand.    Then there are humans, and if at the beginning i tried to play the game with its melee mechanics, i quickly switched to just shooting them in the head with the AR because meleeing them was just so bad.-buggy : The DLC adds a larger and more "open" map , with less buildings, and a vehicle to help explore it.The buggy handling felt great, even if it was a pain to use it more often than not because of the the amount of clutter there is everywhere on the map. The associated mechanics are also nice, though, i felt that durability for parts was also too low since at times i had to repair twice to go from one side of the map to the other.  The buggy skill tree is also solid, but i barely made it to the second tier when i finished the dlc.     Overall, the addition of a vehicle is nice, but i feel it could have been better handled. _Story/Pacing :-For the base game :This is the worst part. It is just bad, really bad. Like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ bad. And it culminates in you parkouring to reach the top of a building to fight a boss which consist of doing 7 QTE while listening to his 15 minutes monologue while your super american character still try to reason with him on how to be a decent human being.At least the pacing is ok, and some of the side content is good enough or even fun where the rest is really just fetch quests.-For the following DLC :  here it is the opposite; from the beginning to the end, the main story is intriguing and interesting.   Unfortunately, the pacing is bad on this dlc, mostly because there is no fast travel, and also because of some fillers between major events.  The side quest are on the level of the base game,  To conclude, what made me get Dying Light was actually the prospect of playing Dying Light 2 after seeing its gameplay footage. i though i would have enjoyed this game more , but halfway through the base game, i already had too much frustration too many times which made want to finish it quickly.  I sincerely hope that 2 will improve on the points i listed, especially the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Dying Light

_childDocuments_.review: The overall game is good. In my opinion, there are times where the running/climbing mechanics don't do what you're asking of them - to the point of annoyance. Honestly, This game feels like Assassin's Creed with Zombies, but is basically Dead Island 2. If you're into that sort of game, then this game is right up your alley. Running, Climbing, Grapple-Hooking around, Simple-to-Complex fighting styles (Depending on perks you unlock, etc.). The game runs the gambit on these types of mechanics. Nothing new, but what's there is for the most part - done pretty well. It's worth picking up on sale for sure. 7.5/10 - Climbing mechanics aggrevated me pretty bad at times. Other than that, was a good game.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is something of a spiritual successor to Dead Island, made by the same company and containing many of the same mechanics. You run around killing zombies, attach various junk to weapons to make them cause more and different kinds of damage, and you progress in the plot by running chores for various survivors in the city.However, this time around they've completely removed the enemy level system, making it possible to become an absolute zombie-slaying god among men once you got yourself levelled up and crafted some high-end weapons. You'll face more difficult enemies down the line for sure, and as is true to form you can get overwhelmed when too many swarm you at once, but you always have the option to level up and get more powerful stuff and come back to absolutely stomp the enemies later.They also added two new key features: Day/night cycle, and parkour. Both of which help immensly to spice up the regular zombie slaying.During the day you'll mostly only face regular zombies and the occasional special variant. You can safely run around the rooftops and outmanouver them, take them head-on with whatever blunt or sharp instrument of your choice, set up traps and blow up several at once, or just ignore them and use them as jumping blocks to reach that annoying ledge you couldnt otherwise (this move is hilarious. get it early :)During the night, however, the tone changes. The normal zombies get a little feistier, but more importantly the streets will be stalked by deadly hunter zombies called volatiles.These beasts constantly scan for anything you-shaped or you-sounding, and once they see you you better run for your life. They are NOT to be trifled with until very late in the game, and even then they're pretty dangerous. They also investigate any sound their fellow undead make, so if you take a swing at something, You better leave before they come looking.The Parkour elements provide you with the means to escape the Volatiles, as well as a fun & fast way to get around the city. You can jump and climp almost anything, giving you near total freedom of movement. Later in the game you even get a grappling hook to quickly scale even the tallest building, though it has a cooldown so you can't rely on it to save you every time when you're being persued.The story is ok. It's nothing too fancy, but it's interesting enough to keep you playing. It's definitely not the main draw of the game, but at the very least it doesn't detract from the experience.My main gripe with it comes at the end when you are suddenly forced into a QTE event which instakills you if you fail a single press. The rest of the game has only mild QTE influences, like hammering the use key to open a door, and this particular sequence come at you without warning. You'll likely die in it many times before you learn the right keypresses. The game did not need this part.All in all, the game was great fun throughout and I highly recommend it to anyone who liked the Dead Island series. Dying Light improves upon the formula in many ways, and (aside from that one-off QTE event) it all adds up to a satisfying game all the way to the end. Pros:+ Zombie killing in creative ways+ Fun parkour in an open-world city (a bit like Assassins Creed, but faster paced)+ Levelling system with abilities that heavily impacts gameplay+ You can dropkick people (great fun!)+ Crafting system from Dead Island (mostly unchanged. If it ain't broke, don't fix it?)Cons:- Not as optimized as it could be. The game has been patched to fix several issues, but you'll probably want to set draw distance to the minimum. It only reduces far away terrain detail, as far as I've seen, so you'll likely not even notice any difference.- If you want to go singleplayer-only, the game will constantly nag you about wanting to go online with no way to turn those messages off. A nitpick to be sure, but it annoyed me quite a bit.- That instakill QTE event near the end. Seriously, wtf?

_childDocuments_.review: I've been pretty burned out with gaming for awhile except for retro style games or stuff from the modding community and recently even that had my gaming well of desire to play completely run dry.Enter Dying Light:I'm just getting started with this game, will update my review later. I honestly thought for years and years Dying Light was a Left 4 Dead type game that neglected a high quality single player campaign. I feel Left 4 Dead really let me down so much that I kept overlooking this game due to the type of vibe it gave off. It's a 2015 game, that right there is a fair indication that it's not like the modern dumpster fires one comes across these days. A game I overlooked so many times it's not even funny, glad I'm trying it out now. Excellent meld of mechanics. The biggest thing that won me over to at least try it out is that its well regarded for it's single player campaign, it wasn't just designed for coop with single player as an afterthought. Tons of people highly rate single player for this. I usually don't sink this much time into a game starting day one. This like most games is a very common rinse and repeat type affair but with a lot of good elements. I passed over this title so many times in the store it's uncountable. I thought well zombies! Yeah not that many great zombie games out there, they are few and far between. Very cliche premise but that didn't stop me from getting into it. Lots of exploration and crafting, I feel like I've barely scratched the surface. For me a few words sum it up so far, engaging and enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine if Mirror's Edge had a great melee system and a metric ton of open world sandbox fun activities. Plus actually fun co-op and competetive multiplayer! Good! _childDocuments_.review: Whether their Romero “shamblers” or Dawn of the Dead (2004) “sprinters”, there’s just something cool about zombies which elevates them above all other B-Movie monsters. They’re human, they used to be us and that thought is as scary as hell.An Outbreak starts with just one infected but their numbers continue to grow as ours diminish, if we get bitten, we’ll turn ourselves.It’s such a perfect apocalyptic scenario and one which is happily experiencing a renaissance at the moment.From reality TV shows to block buster movies, Video games to survival manuals, zombie pop culture is everywhere these days and I love it.I’ve seen all the movies, I’ve watched all the TV shows, I’ve played most of the games, I’m a consumer of all things zombie (although, should the opportunity arise, don’t actually consume a zombie, it’ll only end badly for you.)I’ve also put a lot of thought into what actions I would take should I open my curtains one morning to find the zombie apocalypse taking place on my front lawn.Amongst all my plans of stockpiling Pot Noodles and keeping a bucket in the attic to poo in, I’ve never considered that being skilled in the art of parkour might be a useful survival trait; at least I hadn’t considered it until very recently when I stumbled upon my latest piece of zombie content to consume.You remember the first Dead Island game? It was pretty good right? Well the fine folks at Techland have released another tasty undead treat into the world, a stealthy, action, parkour, survival zombie treat in the form of Dying Light.In Dying Light the undead plague has emerged, but the powers that be have responded quickly and contained it to a small area, the fictional city of Harran.Quarantined off from the rest of the world and relying on vital air drops courtesy of the Global Relief Effort, the situation inside the city continues to deteriorate, and if HBO’s The Walking Dead has taught us anything, it’s that you don’t just need to worry about the undead, other groups of survivors can be for more deadly.This rings true in Dying Light as a gang mentality has gripped the crumbling city of Harran where two prominent groups are vying for supplies whilst struggling to survive the undead, but all is not lost...Whilst there isn’t a cure, there is a medicine (Antizen) that the infected can take which delays the turning, as long as they keep taking Antizen they’ll be ok, however the only source of this medication comes from the supply planes flying relief missions over the city.The game opens with your character preparing to parachute into Harran whilst receiving instructions from his employer over a radio; it seems that there is a survivor in the city that holds some very sensitive information, information which cannot be made public and it’s your job to retrieve it.You’ll then find yourself falling through the sky towards the infested city, but things don’t start off well at all!A hard landing and an encounter with the locals (both the alive and dead varieties) later and you’ll be bitten, infected and dragged to the first safe zone of the game. This is where you man hunt truly begins.From this point you’ll be meeting new characters and trying to earn their trust by running missions for them, and I literally mean running, the big thing that sets Dying Light apart from the Dead Island titles is the “Free Running” game mechanic.You’ll be tearing across roof tops, leaping alleyways and scaling the sides of buildings.The safest way to stay alive in Harran is to stay off the ground; a casual walk down the street will see you surrounded and overwhelmed by zombies quicker than you can say “Assassins Creed of the Dead”.In the increasingly crowded zombie gaming genre this parkour style of play is hugely refreshing and better still it is exceptionally well implemented.With a gamepad in hand, you’ll find the controls are really dialled in, look where you want to go, hit the jump button and there’s a good chance you’ll make it, it’s not only intuitive, it makes you feel like a free running bad ass!The missions themselves are the usual mix of “go there”, “kill that” and “fetch this” quests that we know and love, completion of which will give you the experience you’ll need to level up your various abilities enabling you to hit a little harder and jump a little further, you might even learn some new skills along the way.Dying Light also boasts a pretty deep crafting system. You’ll be rummaging through bins and patting down corpses like a perverted Womble looking for the things that every day folk leave behind.There are plenty of crafting recipes to learn, from Med Kits to Molotov’s there’s a plethora of useful items and weapons just waiting for your crafty hands to bring them into existence.I can’t overstate how useful a well placed Molotov is when you’re in a tight spot.All zombies are not born equal in Dying Light, the recently infected will move a hell of lot quicker than the common stale variety of zombie you’ll see shambling around.You’ll discover zombies that spit, zombies that explode, radioactive zombies in hazmat suits, and plenty of others, Hazmat is a dangerous place to explore at any time of day.But at night, that’s when things really become scary. The whole atmosphere of the game changes when night falls, it’s much tenser and you really want to stay out of site, stealthily moving from one secluded spot to another. You really don’t want to attract any attention at night.There are super fast zombies lurking in the darkness and you’re going to have trouble outrunning them. The pitch dark makes your parkour aerobatics much more difficult to pull off as you rush through the streets, the feeble pool of light from your torch dancing along the landscape in front of you.Being outside at night is a serious business, but you do have the option to sleep through the night in a safe zone if it all becomes a little too much, although some missions will require you to go out at night, there’s no avoiding it completelyIn addition to the daytime being slightly less stressful, being out in the sunlight gives you a chance to drink in the scenery, the city of Harran can be a visually stunning place to explore.From the sun bleached rooftops to the ominous darkness of the underpasses, everything about Harran exudes atmosphere, the whole city feels alive, which is no easy feat for a city full of the dead!If the Dead Island games were the warm up act then Dying Light is the main event.With  glossy visuals, satisfying combat mechanics and an outstanding parkour system, Dying Light is a fantastic game and the city of Harran is a beautifully realised setting begging to be explored. You should take the time to visit, just don't go for the night life, it's dead.For the full review and others please take the time to visit

_childDocuments_.review: Dying light is one of the best zombie games, this game is special, letting you go almost anywhere you can see combined with the exceptional parkour for which it is known, not to mention the very fluid and detailed combat system, at least against the infected.The atmosphere of the game is unique and desolate which really blows your mind to an apocalypse that immerses you even more in the game.The graphics and artistic style of the game combine very well with the apocalyptic theme of the game and it is a very good one for its time and holds up well even today.The music in the game is perfect and describes the game perfectly and what happens from the moment the music starts.The story of the game is quite mediocre in the main game but much better in the fallowing dlc.The attention to detail in Dying light is very good, for example, your weapons degrade over time and every time you repair them, they have a new look.Dying light is a very pleasant game to play and that's how it should be, a gamegameplay and clean graphics must always come first, at least in my opinion.

_childDocuments_.review: First off, My RIG:ECS A960m-m3 MotherboardAMD Fx-6350 3.9ghz/4.2ghz with CoolerMaster Hyper 212+evoAsus Strix GTX 970 4gb oc16 GB Geil Dragon 1333 Ram1TB HDD (game on this one) 256GB SSD (os on this one) - irrelevant -First Impressions: The game is fun! As you may have heard, it is a mash up of a 'good' dead island, mirrors edge, a bit of assassins creed (securing safe zones - like in creed claiming borgia towers), fallout (looting and lock picking) and the movie I am Legend ( night time play ).  Parkouring around the map is fun because it feels natural at times.  Sometimes you will struggle to climb a ledge and sometimes you will flow across rooftops as if you were Aladdin!  Almost everything seems scalable/climbable!  The first part of the game actually reminds me of Metro where characters are talking amongst each other and you can just listen in.  You get a slight sense of character understanding, but am sure that you do more so along the campaign.  At times your main character sounds like Nathan Drake from Uncharted and at times he sounds like Rick from PawnStars.Graphics:  This game demands graphics AND cpu performance!  Off the bat, I notice as you may have read elsewhere, the god awful fiiiillllmmmm graaaiiinnnn effect (film grain, noise).  You can disable this, which I highly recommend. Just google it. I have done this and set my graphics to high and get between 35 and 50 fps in the outside world and a solid 60 inside buildings.  Here is the kicker - I have the draw distance set to zero. I've noticed only a few trees have popped in and out from zero setting to full setting. I advise setting to zero because you really only need to see in your viscidity anyway, which is a good (simulated) 300 feet, don't get me wrong, you can still see across the map, and i bet you won't notice much change between the settings.  You may read in threads to set sun shadowing to 0, but when i did that, it looked really bad, certain inside areas and face shading got muddy and dark, but frame did jump like 15-20.  I'd leave this on for the sake of playing a pretty game.  The one thing I really enjoy about games like this is the level of detail in the environment. Random real pictures of things like people and animals and little note, the knobs on a radio,  the crusting on a picture frame.  This kind of stuff makes the world feel more real and less game like. Besides that, lighting and shadowing are great, some textures look real, some look fake, i'd say its pretty, but not really ground breaking.  This is one of those games that looks good, and gets better along the way, because your mind is creating what the world is to you ... Story:  You get dropped in this town called Harran, which has been affected by the infection, and you are part of what is called the GRE ... some government cleanup crew maybe... isn't that always the case. Anyway, along the way you seem to question your morals on who you really want to help, the GRE or the citizens trying to survive. Only a few hours in, so not really deep into the story, but seems interesting enough to keep playing.  Oh and your name is Crane.Gameplay: Ragdoll Ragdoll Ragdoll! Gotta love rag doll effects!  Killing zombie and then kicking it around...that can be a game in itself! oh wait, look at that, it is now! :)  Besides that, melee is near identical to dead island, you may get frustrated trying to bash a zombies head in about 10 times before it dies, but its surprisingly satisfying. Searching for items is kind of silly, you just feel the air when prompted to search.  Also opening doors, you have the hand of god which magically opens and closes doors! Silly, but meh, negligible. When running and parkouring, you have to look at the ledge or area you are jumping to, this makes for more realism and excitement, especially at night when "they" come out to get you.  As far as quest, this is like dead island too, but seems less annoying, sometimes things are hard, but everything seems manageable.  Some areas you will think with you head more than your brawn. The lock picking seems straight out of fallout, which is cool, cuz that was fun. Crafting is simple and easy, just find blueprints, find the items and craft. There is also a simple skill tree which you can level up with skill points and branch out the skill tree. There is also a level up bar for running and melee at the top of your hud in game. Stamina comes in to effect when running and melee, but its actually not annoying, its done very well. I have not played multiplayer, but would imagine it is awesome... i mean come on.. you can be a zombie!Overall:Pros++Pretty Graphics+Fun Gameplay+Easy crafting/skill tree level up+Parkour is fun and real-ish+Level of detail is nice+Not annoying like Dead Island gameplay+Ragdoll and melee is satisfying+Movement is fluidCons--Weapons kind of degrade quickly ... but you're not always bashing things, you are running too.-Apparently use of on core on whole game seems to create performance issues, but plays good still depending on rig.-film grain ( you can fix )-lip movement when characters speak ( not synced correctly - negligible to gameplay )Last Words:Get rid of film grain in game files, set your draw distance to zero, but them graphics up and enjoy the island of Harran!Oh and when nightfall hits ... Run to the Hills!!! (Iron Maiden reference) ... or just run like hell to a safe zone, because it is scary and you may pee your jammies...

_childDocuments_.review: Not fun. Boring story, bad character design, but worst of all is the gameplay. Zombies seem to all have 15ft reach when grabbing you, and they can take one hit to kill or fifteen. I'm sure there's a reason for this, but it's not explained in the game, and when I'm smacking a regular zombie ten times in the head with a purple level weapon (which I assume is good, honestly I'm not even sure) and it still isn't going down, I start to lose interest. The parkour system which was touted as revolutionary just. Doesn't. Work. "Look at the ledge you want to go to and press jump," the tutorial tells me. And yet, when looking , the character launches into the air and slams chest first into it before plummeting to the ground. This happens about 60% of the time. Sometimes you'll be able to climb, sometimes not. And I'm talking about the same ledge, from the same angle, at the same distance, at the same speed (or even standing still). If you're curious and it's heavily discounted then go for it. Absolutely not worth full price though.

_childDocuments_.review: I've changed my review to thumbs up, however, everything I originally said still stands (see below). Definitely play co-op with a friend. I would avoid this one, it feels incredibly incomplete. A great idea, but the driving is terrible, the cave sections are annoying and the map feels under-utilized.~original review~....My main complaint is that there don't seem to be all that many consequences for using loud weapons and dying. Sure, you'll lose some xp on death, but it still doesn't feel like all that big of a deal. And when you use a gun, sure, you get some of the fast moving zombies coming at you, but they aren't hard to deal with. The world design and music are really cool and the parkour mostly makes sense but the story lacks tension and most of the NPCs are obnoxious. It's definitely more fun co-op than single player, that's for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light - Survival Struggle in Harran[Introduction]Dying Light is a survival horror game developed by Techland and released in 2015. Set in a city overrun by zombies, the game offers players the opportunity to explore an open world, engage in a struggle for survival, and battle dangerous creatures. Dying Light stands out with its dynamic day-night cycle, parkour-style movements, and thrilling atmosphere.[Story]The story of Dying Light unfolds in the city of Harran. Players control a character named Kyle Crane as he fights against a zombie outbreak. Crane works with a group fighting against the zombie outbreak while uncovering the city's mysteries and dangers. The game's story provides a journey filled with suspenseful moments, drawing players into a dark and dangerous world.[Gameplay]Dying Light is a first-person perspective open-world survival game. Players explore the city, complete missions, and combat zombies using parkour-style movements. During the day, players scavenge for resources, complete missions, and explore the city, while at night, they encounter a dangerous and deadly environment filled with aggressive zombies. The game offers players freedom of choice and provides a variety of weapons and skills to shape their playstyle.[Graphics and Sounds]Dying Light features impressive and detailed graphics. The city of Harran is vividly depicted with its ruined buildings, narrow streets, and atmospheric lighting. Zombie designs are also frightening and realistic. The sound design enhances the game's atmosphere, with zombie screams and environmental sounds increasing players' tension.[Conclusion]Dying Light has received generally positive reviews from both critics and players. It stands out with its dynamic gameplay, dark atmosphere, and impressive graphics. However, some players have criticized the game's weak story. Nevertheless, Dying Light has been beloved by a wide fan base and has been successfully received.Rating: 7/10

_childDocuments_.review: Watch as action man climbs towering skyscrapers without breaking a sweat then fail to bruise a frail zombified woman with a metal axe. Then watch that metal axe break and become useless after swinging it a few times. Then repair it with some trash. I feel like this game has a personality crisis. Is it a stealthy, parkour-your-way-around-enemies and use strategy to achieve the objective type game? If so, why does one of the earliest missions have you turn on a communications tower in the middle of a horde of enemies while simultaneously introducing a new enemy type you've never seen before right in front of your face after you interact with a door? Is it an action-packed-kill-all-the-zombies type game? If so, why do I get combat fatigue and go through breaking one or two melee weapons to kill a single basic enemy? I found pistol rounds, so I assume that guns are a part of this experience. I wonder if they break too... Frankly I don't care to find out.

I hadn't paid attention to the time at all. I can turn on my flashlight, but that would just attract attention. I leave it off. Rooftops are out of the question, as I can't see, I don't want to risk a fatal 40 foot drop. THEY are coming.  RUN!Straight out haul across blocks, at street level in pure darkness, through hordes of the undead, being pursued by nightmares. I manage not to get eviscerated. realise I'm more than halfway to the haven. Can't breathe. Two blocks to go. See the glow of life saving UV lights. Begin weeping with relief, but don't stop running until I hit The Ledge.The Ledge is the greatest thing ever invented.Darkness is terrifying.11/10

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light presents an open-world zombie survival experience with light RPG elements. Assume the role of Kyle Crane, a generic shaved head, gravel voiced, special military operative air-dropped into the zombie-infested city of Harran, tasked with reclaiming stolen viral sequence technology that has ravaged the city.Narratively, the game falters. Scenes unfold in a manner reminiscent of COD, with characters shouting their intentions while your protagonist remains muted or providing only meaningless contributions to the conversation. Tonally, the story's mix of dark main plotlines and whimsical side content creates a jarring experience. The main villain's cartoonish motives and underdeveloped allies fail to evoke any real feeling towards the events of the story, leaving the narrative feeling disjointed. On the gameplay front, Dying Light is quite good. Explore a vast playground teeming with diverse zombie types, navigate dynamic day-night cycles which change your approach to the world, and utilize verticality to your advantage with extensive parkour and  climbing mechanics. Combat emphasizes strategic movement and risk management, though significant repetition sets in with time. Quest design suffers from monotony, primarily revolving around mundane tasks. The abundance of uninteresting side missions contributes to a sense of bloat, reminiscent of Ubisoft titles. Dying Light features a perk-based progression system akin to Skyrim's XP progression, rewarding strength and agility actions with skill upgrades. Weapon crafting adds depth, allowing players to modify and upgrade weapons with unique attributes. However, the durability mechanic introduces an element of risk to encounters (love it or hate it, I'm personally not a fan but I recognize that it adds strategy and risk/reward to the combat). Multiplayer enhances the experience, offering drop-in co-op functionality. Despite its flaws, playing with a partner can amplify both the positive and negative aspects of the gameplay.Dying Light provides a somewhat enjoyable experience when played casually with friends. However, those seeking a compelling single-player narrative or immersive zombie survival or RPG may find better options elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: From the very moment I stepped into the chaotic world of Harran, I knew I was in for an unforgettable experience. "Dying Light" is not just a game; it's a testament to what survival horror can achieve when meticulously crafted by developers who truly understand and love the genre.The first thing that strikes you about "Dying Light" is its breathtakingly immersive environment. Harran is brought to life with stunning visuals and intricate details. Every alley, rooftop, and desolate street tells a story of its own, drawing you deeper into its post-apocalyptic embrace. The day-night cycle is a stroke of genius, transforming the cityscape from a sunlit playground to a terrifying nightmare with the setting sun.The parkour system is an absolute game-changer. Never before has traversal in a game felt so fluid and exhilarating. Running, jumping, and climbing across the rooftops of Harran is an adrenaline rush like no other. The freedom of movement empowers you to explore every nook and cranny, finding hidden treasures and escape routes that are crucial for survival.Combat in "Dying Light" is visceral and satisfying. The melee system is robust, offering a variety of weapons that can be customized to suit your playstyle. The thrill of bashing through hordes of zombies, each encounter fraught with danger, keeps you on the edge of your seat. And when night falls, the Volatiles emerge, transforming every skirmish into a desperate fight for survival. The tension is palpable, and the fear is real.The narrative of "Dying Light" is compelling, with well-developed characters and a plot that keeps you invested from start to finish. The voice acting and motion capture are top-notch, adding emotional depth to the storyline. Kyle Crane's journey is one of redemption and determination, making you root for him every step of the way.

_childDocuments_.review: This was on my wishlist for a long time and I finally decided to pick it up over the summer sale. I wanted to like this game, but I just can't. Things about this game that suck:1. story2. characters3. enemies4. combat5. combat6. combat7. the combatThings about this game that are ok:1. free running2. game performance (my PC is relatively high end but nothing special anymore)Things about this game that are good:1. Literally nothingI don't have any issues with crashes, optimization, or anything like that; the game runs fine. It's just not fun. The story is stupid, the characters are stupid and annoying, and every mission is just a glorified fetch quest. All you'll meet is a series of NPCs who want you to do everything for them, a villain you've seen a thousand times before, and a hero who's just an idiot. Honestly, I can get past all that. I don't expect complete originality in every game I play. This game tried to be original with the parkour and free running, but the novelty there wears out in a hurry. The biggest issue I have with this game is the combat. It is truly terrible. For the most part you'll fight either basic slow shambling zombie enemies, or human enemies. Occasionally there are faster zombies who can also run and climb, spitter zombies, zombies that explode when you get near, or larger thug type zombies. None of these enemies are even the least bit fun to fight.Even the basic zombie enemies have ridiculous amounts of health. I get why this is, you need to fight to increase your combat level, but even 10 levels in (of about 25 or so) I still have to hit a regular zombie about 10 times in the head with a hammer to come close to killing it. Hit a zombie in the side of the skull with a big wrench? It will keep stumbling toward you and either stagger your or grab onto you. It takes nearly endless beatings to kill even a single enemy often times. You'll wear out all your combat stamina multiple times fighting a single enemy. And now that you're done with the fight, guess what? Your weapon is broken. You can apply this same formula to every other zombie you fight. The zombies are easy to run away from, but if you play the game like a free runner, you won't increase your combat level and won't be able to fight when you need to. Combat with human enemies is hands down the WORST PART OF THIS GAME. Combat with other humans seems to be based almost entirely on luck and not at all on skill. Probably around half the time I swing my weapon at a human enemy, they will simply block it. There's nothing you can do to stop them from blocking. This wouldn't bother me all that much, except there is NO WAY FOR YOU TO BLOCK THEIR ATTACKS LIKE THEY BLOCK YOURS. You can eventually craft shields  but they are 2 handed pieces of equipment that do not help at all. You can dodge by jumping backwards about 8 feet, but then you're too far to attack again and make any use of your dodge. The other half of the time when they don't block your attacks, they will simply dodge them. And when I say they dodge your attacks, I do not mean they move out of the way; they simply perform a dodge animation while remaining in place and your attack does nothing. Even if you swing where they are, if they perform a short animation, then your attack was worthless. Combining these two things, it's often almost impossible to actually land consisten hits on human enemies. All you can do is swing your weapon and hope the game lets you hit them while wasting all your stamina. But say that you do manage to nail a bandit 3 times in the cranium with a reinforced crowbar. They don't care at all. They don't stagger or stun at all. Even if you manange to land good hits on them, they will still strike back with a quick kick or uppercut with their weapon with no delay. OK, so let's try to step back and use throwing weapons. You can craft items like throwing stars to deal ranged damage. It's a cool idea. So you chuck a throwing star at a bandit. Guess what? He parried it. He parried your throwing star using a lead pipe like he's Geralt from the Witcher. If he didn't parry it, he simply dodged it. If you think there's a way for you to parry an enemy's thrown weapons, then you obviously didn't read the rest of this review. Finally, guns. This game has guns in it, but not like you'd actually notice. They are nearly impossible to find, and even if you do find a gun, you won't find any bullets for it. But even if you've got a gun and ammo, it's still not worth using. Loud noises attract the fast zombies, so every shot just means you're going to have deal with 5 more zombies than you started with. I would not recommend this game to anyone.tl;dr this game is trash and no one should play it

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a FANTASTIC PARKOUR game! But a really AWFUL ZOMBIE SURVIVAL game. Pros:Dying Light has wonderful and engaging combat, every hit feels weighty and forceful. The dodging is slick and smooth. Speaking of slick and smooth the parkour! It's great, sure there are moments when you're convinced you should've grabbed that ledge but you couldn't. Besides that the parkour feels fantastic, speedy, swift, especially with the combat roll skill, it feels incredibly cinematic. It's got pretty lighting effects too!The game also makes guns and ammo quite rare for the start of the game which feels really cool!Cons:While I do reccomend this game and got my moneys worth (bought for £9.99 in the summer sale) I sure couldn't reccomend it full price, at all.  The game seems to have been a parkour game first and the zombies and survial taccked on as an afterthought.The game creates artificial difficulty by handicapping the player with a very limited stamina bar, so instead of making the zombies more challenging and difficult, therefore making them scarier, the game just grossly limits your stamina. Especially when you can run for miles before needing to catch your breath, and the character you play is supposed to be this SPEC OPS, secret agent guy, it doesn't make sense that you'd have such little stamina for combat. If we were a civilian or random Joe off the street I could believe it, but when knowing who the character is and what he does it feels strange. (Hard Mode gives you even less stamina!)The items and crafting seems too abundant for a game about surviving. I never find myself short on supplies as I can get by and manage just fine with what is given.  Plus with how often items break, I find it's not until I get a Orange Tier item that I bother upgrading it anyway. Even then I could go swimming in how many materials I find.Night time is scary, quite dark and lots of scary moments, the zombies become quicker and there's mutant varieties too.But it barely lasts 10 minutes before it's day again it's far too short! (Hard mode does lengthen it though)The story is laughable! There's really good plot points, and even some actual touching and meaningful moments too! But the story as a whole feels, much like the zombies tacked on! -SPOILERS- You get bitten at the start of the game and need the antivirus to keep the infection away. There's an airdrop mechanic in game where you have to race and aquire the airdrop before it's stolen by the badguys or other survivors. BUT instead of the game have you manage your infection by trying to aquire the antivirus and by which present you with moral choices such as; Do I take the antivirus for myself or give some to others who need it, no you can just ignore it because it's only a plot point and doesn't affect the game at all. All in all, I'd reccomend the game at the price I bought it at £9.99. Because the parkour is good and the combat too!  But anything more than that? No way! Again, Fantastic Parkour game, Awful Zombie Survival game.

_childDocuments_.review: After 30 hs. of playing I can say with confidence that this game is a disaster. - You only get ONE "tutorial" for the ONE thing that doesn't need it ("parkour", yeah, between inverted commas).- DMC has parkour, PoP has parkour, Tomb Raider has parkour. Mirror's edge has parkour. Dying Light has "parkour".- Zombies are stupidly hard to kill for the sake of annoyance and nothing else.- Additionally, zombies are INFINITE. I have spent several times half an hour  or more killing zombies from the roof of busses/houses by spam hitting them with a stick in order clear an area because I wanted to open some van's trunk. AMAZING ABILITY BASED GAMEPLAY (sarcasm in case you didn't perceive it). And yes, it was not necessary to open said van's trunk, but one of the main points of an open world game is exploring, right?- You may be asking "why didn't you face them head on?" because I would have gotten killed, and that is just at the beginning of the game.- No learning curve except for the aforementioned "tutorial" for "parkour"- Some stupid decisions like giving players a challenge that requires killing zombies pushing them against spikes and placing almost no spikes in the area (O.M.G. how did this pass the beta!?!?!?!?!?!)- Picky physics when doing "parkour".- Non-responding controls- BTW, I have completed almost no quests that involve night time. That's right, zombies were infinite and hard to kill DURING DAYLIGHT, I am already fighting depression thinking what nighttime game play will throw at me (probably more zombies, probably harder to kill, certainly to serve as an obstacle to pull some lever or reaching some place). EDIT: now that I have, night time gameplay is based on avoiding conflinc.- ZERO opportunities for ability expression. Equip your stick of choice and spam the melee button, if you get caught by a zombie press F or E to free yourself then rinse and repeat. If you get tired, you can always use flammable fluid and use molotovs.I plan to finish the story of the game and then uninstall it. I only wish I could free the space it takes on Steam's cloud, what a waste of storage.EDIT: Finished the game, I can finally free the disk space it was wasting but not before I expand on my review.There is one thing I didn't mention earlier. I started the game in hard difficulty, but soon lowered to normal which translated to less clicks with your stick of choice and A BIT less annoyance from the zombies."Parkour" was hold DOWN the SHIFT key while you are moving around and hit the spacebar at the right time. At some points you could add to this "and hope Crane grabs some ledge so you don't die, lose "exp points" and try again until you get it right" because, AGAIN, no opportunity for skill expression whatsoever in any aspect of the game.- The final boss fight was more laughable than Zelda BOTW (yes, it was that bad). Additionally, "beating the boss" involved distracting you from the final exchange with the boss (so you had to chose between the interesting dialogue or "beating the boss")Final conclusion: Get this game for free ONLY and if your goal is to wear down your left mouse button for no reason. I don't see any point on playing this game. AVOID 100%P.S.: I am shocked that this game came from the same country as The Witcher series. Polish video game developers will be forever stained by the existence of this game.

_childDocuments_.review: Arguably the best mash-up of parkour, trickery, mouse and cat games, zombies, loot grabbing and brutal onslaught. Some of them essential if you run in the night, to gain huge advantages, some gameplay-breaking (looking at you, grappling hook, except for the DLC "The Following", where you are often screwed without it during the night, especially at the very start of it).Apart from that, a lot of houses can be entered and looted. No, they do not all look unique, if you have ever been to an apartment complex in low-tier countries, then you should know they all look pretty much the same. Even the interior, yes. Sometimes, humans paint them in weird colors. I can not ask the Developers to do the same, to be honest. Lucky they share my beliefs.No, you can not run around naked. But you can blow naked mutants, called Volatiles, up. So I guess it's a good trade.Also no, you are not a killing machine by default. Leveling up will make you one, with the right blueprints and merchandise (available in your undying friend's apartment) to support the inner maniac inside of you.Lastly, no. In Dying Light, you do not get good stuff for free. Only during events, and, more importantly, the night.Good NightEqualsGood LuckPeriod.

_childDocuments_.review: It's like Dead Island but better in every way and not filled with bad Australian accents(Actual boring serious information)The game does a fantastic job of taking various elements from other games and implementing them all into it's own.There's an invasion mechanic that's pretty similar to the PVP invasions in Dark Souls games where you can invade or get invaded by player controled hunter zombies, there's a crafting mechanic where you find blue prints to construct silly powerfull weapons(like a flaming crowbar) ala Dead Rising 2, there's outpoust (aka safe areas) which you gotta clear out and then turn on a power switch so you can use them to store you equipment and sleep through the night(Far Cry 3), it has a fantastic parkour system that's very fluid,responsive and makes even doing simple things such as running a frekin fun experience (Mirror's Edge/TItanfall parkour),there's qurantine zones(Dungeons) which you can run over and over to get better loot(any MMORPG) and the game also supports 4 player co-op which makes an allready fun game even more fun and ridiculous.The only two major flaws the game has is the 1 dimensional villain that's desperately trying to be like Vaas but fails completely at it and the game uses an insane amount of video memory if you set Texture Quality to high, so much so than you need 4GB of VRAM to be able to play the game with High Textures otherwise get ready for lots and lots of stuttering and micro-stuttering. Thankfully the medium textures still look fairly good in my opinion so it's not an extremly big deal but to people who consider a slightly muddy texture to be the anti-christ of PC gaming then this optimization issue will annoy you a lot if you have a card with less then 4GB of VRAM.All in all, it's just fantastic; Solo or with some buddies, you'll most likely have a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a really well made and very fun game; but it seems to be personally offended by that so it goes out of its way to be as frustrating as possible.This game wastes so much effort being simply infuriating.Parkouring over zombies? Tons of fun. The strange weapon crafting is fun too, attaching a blow torch to your axe so you can have a fire axe. Neat. I really enjoy the early-game story where your secret mission demands screwing so many people over. The grappling hook is amazing.But there's so much to piss you off. Like the enemy getting to a supply drop first and automatically stealing half of it, no killing them to get it back, it just teleports to villain HQ. The night zombies will absolutely kick your ass, which isn't too bad; it's the fact if you parkour to a spot they can't reach they'll spam deadly, hitscan vomit at you. So now your greatest strength turns into a fatal weakness.Hope you enjoy some great story missions that have you running from gunmen, where success is basically random. Did you pick the correct path? Too bad, they decided to be accurate this try. Pick the wrong path? Get gunned down.Those fun weapons? You can't use them for any single boss fight. Every single boss has an excuse to take your toys away from you. Have a crappy tier machete!Any time a gun goes off or something explodes the sprinting zombies come straight for you. For YOU. Enemies spraying bullets or tossing grenades? Have some adds focused on you. Grappling and parkouring three blocks away? They home in exactly on you.So, you'd like a silencer for your gun? Understandably, can't just have one, it's some late-game upgrade. I get that you shouldn't be able to just outright ignore a given game mechanic easily through most of the game, even a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ one. So try a bow instead! It's really fun to use and effective, aside from its eight-foot range. Archery can't hit straight across the street without you having to adjust for arrow drop, which takes a lot to get used to. But then you do get some fun arrows to craft, at least one of which explodes and attracts sprinters to you.I don't remember everything that pissed me off at this point. I finished the game, I spent 66 hours on the various side quests and exploration and whatever. I didn't hate the game; not for a lack of trying on its part. I own the DLC as well and the thought of playing it after finishing the game was too much, uninstalled to maybe pick up again much later.Get it cheap. There's so much to enjoy and it's a good quality time; time designed to piss you off for no reason, time and time again.
