_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game, it's everything Dead Island should've been.The combat is so fluid and visceral once you get good at it. Starting off I'd say weapons are far too weak, but once you reach the second map, I'd recommend turning the difficulty to at least "Hard", otherwise the game gets too easy (and you'll get way more XP on Hard Mode). You have and gain so many options for movement, combat, evasion, stealth, etc.. The Melee weapons stay relevant long after you've gotten the best guns in the game, but the guns are fantastic as well. You really have to use all of your resources, and no weapon type, move, or skill is much better than anything else. You'll start off running away and being quiet, and will end the game slide-kicking  and other special infected.The zombies are varied enough, meeting all the archetypes we're used to (think Left 4 Dead) while throwing in some surprises. Zombies don't just pop in and spawn, either, and while they'll continually flood areas, they come in from sewers, buildings, under cars, doors, etc.The game supports full co-op and asymetrical invasion-style multiplayer. The co-op is really one of the best features of the game, and basically the whole game can be played in drop-in co-op. I recommend leaving invasions ON since the community is much smaller than it was before, and it's a hell of a lot of fun playing against the infected players with friends. Be sure to hop into co-op when you're high level and help the new players out.The story is actually pretty great even if it really doesn't need to be in these kinds of games. Kyle Crane starts off as a fairly generic protagonist, but really comes into his own and becomes so relatable by the end of the main game. In The Following (the only "expansion"-type DLC), he's even better and the writing is improved by tons.The music is perfect, about all I can say. In The Following, it's even better. Keep it on and listen.Only get The Following DLC, it's honestly better than the base game (and the buggy is amazing). The rest of the non-free DLC are pretty "meh" even if they've made a lot of improvements to them as of late. Looking forward to the sequel!My only complaints are the DLCs outside of The Following being artificially difficult (seriously, The Prison (which was free) has the most tanky boss fights I've ever seen in my life) and not fitting the theme of the game. I didn't encounter many bugs, but the few I did involved the Tic-Tac ability to scale walls just randomly activating, sending me off ledges. Death isn't a big deal in the game and these moments are rare, so no biggy, I just hope they get the movement perfected in the sequel.

_childDocuments_.review: This game turned out to be a pleasant surprise, as I was getting a severely bad taste in my mouth due to the absence of early review copies being sent out and the general preorder brigading that has been going on lately. I bought a copy for myself and a friend mostly on a whim, and so far I've been having a blast. Point-by-point review to follow:Pros:+Graphics are extremely well done and the game runs quite well on my 970 (see one exception below)+Combat system is quite nuanced, even if it seems simple at first glance. It is very much a risk-reward system, with stamina  levels being quite well-balanced and even nail-biting at times.+Story so far has been enjoyable, although I've been getting pulled away by the innumerable side quests that become available with each progression of the plot.+Crafting system gives you a sense of accomplishment when you manage to get the parts for that badass weapon you've been eyeing, while the limited repairs force you to continue scavenging for backup weapons at all times.+Loading sequences are quite short, even though I have this loaded on a conventional 7200RPM HDD.+Skill trees are infuriatingly well-balanced, insofar as I have had trouble deciding what skill to get pretty much every level, with the ever-elusive grappling hook taunting me from afar.+Parkour allows for speedy travel while still maintaining an air of danger. Narrow ledges do not clip you to them, so if you accidentally walk off, you're toast, and the addition of destructible roofs and awnings that draw volatiles (freerunning zombies and the ilk, all of which are pretty much terrifying) forces you to stay on your toes at all times.Cons:-Online multiplayer, while fun, gets a bit...weird at times. Zombies will phase through walls when you're not looking at them, overrunning a previously secure area with zombies that have no right being there. Can probably be hotfixed with relative ease, so I'll see what happens with this in the coming weeks.-Perhaps it's due to the fact that I have this game loaded on an HDD instead of my SSD (no more space, unfortunately), but the first 2 seconds or so of cutscenes usually freeze up for me, making a rather jarring transition between game and cutscene.Overall, a great game, even though it was riddled with speculation about review embargos and such. Worth the buy at full price, especially if you're a sandbox fan like I am.

_childDocuments_.review: My friend and I were looking for a zombie thriller to play as a co-op. This game doesn't disappoint. It's definitely worth the money. The player progression is fun, and there are a few cool ways to build up your arsenal. So let me outline a few pros first: unleashing melee on zombies is a blast, whether you blow 'em up, chop body parts off, or annhilate them with an assault rifle. The parkour element is pretty cool, and allows some creative freedom to get from point A to point B. The campaign story isn't amazing, but does a well enough job to keep a post-apocalyptic world in focus. The weapons are pretty cool to play around with. You can add fire, electricity, or explosives to certain weapons. It's pretty awesome. Dead Rising is the only other zombie game that I've played that can rival such capabilities.The cons: Things did feel like they started off a little slow at first. My friend could only keep asking, "where are the guns?!" It took awhile, but we finally got to them. Ammo will mostly require trips to the trade/sale posts which are scattered throughout the map. It's not difficult to find, but a bit of an annoyance to re-stock. Perhaps, we just run through our ammo fast because we like blowing away zombies...go figure. At times the quests feel a little bit annoying. They feel like a chore-list, rather than a fun mission. You can skip or change quests, so there is at least an alternative option. All and all, if you're into zombies or first-person shooters, this game does not disappoint. My friend and I always have a hard time finding fun co-op games, but this is one we keep coming back to. Give it a chance, I think you'll have some fun!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredible game.I always seem to love the free roam games like Skyrim, Zelda, and Super Mario 64. This game is no exception. The level of freedom in this game is beyond that of any of those games. You see a place where you want to go? You can go there, unless it's out of the playable area. The massive variety of weapons and tools that can be used in the game are wonderful. If I had anything to recommend to the devs, it would be to add more tools that affect the player.The story is pretty cool, too. It might seem a bit overwhelming if you're not paying attention your first playthrough, but it's easily understandable if you get into it. Crane as a character is pretty realistic as he changes his mind throughout the story based on what he knows.The graphics are beautiful. Positively breathtaking in some areas. There are details in places you wouldn't expect them. NPCs have animations for everything they say, as well as a variety of idling animations. Lots of interesting and entertaining visual effects for different events. It even includes a trippy psychadelic scene for people who are into that kind of thing. Framerate is consistent if you have a good computer.Multiplayer is great. Love playing online with other people and seeing the unique weapons they found and what they do with them. Racing challenges are the best. I love competing with other players to see who can get to the next point the fastest.The DLC is nothing short of incredible. The amount of time it took to make something like this implies that these guys are obsessive. Some parts of the story really tie together certain unexplained parts of the original game. The buggy is so much fun. Love running zombies over, and of course racing friends. The plot is so crazy, especially at the end. ***small spoilers*** There should be a sequel to both endings of the game. ***end spoilers***The developer secret weapons are one of my favorite parts of the game. These guys made a serious game, but have all kinds of silly secrets that are totally unrealistic. It's a game, why not include some random button that teleports you to different parts of the map, or a chicken on a stick that does more damage than most swords?Seriously. If you play first person games, I can't recommend this game enough. It's worked its way up to the top of my list of favorite first person games. I kid you not.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Dead Island and Dead Island Riptide, and since Dying Light was made by the same people, I expected to love it as well.I did not. Honestly, it wasn't worth the $12 I paid for it. Sure, it was released in 2015, but you'd think with all the attention the ads bring to how much the developers have kept working on the game and updating/improving it, that at least some of the wonky features would have been fixed.The parkour is atrociously bouncy, such that I can hardly ever run the path I mean to and just end up getting bounced around/off things. I dreaded climbing antenna towers because I was afraid the bouncy parkour would just bounce me off the tower to my death.The human combat is a nightmare. The enemies are superhuman fighters while the player is essentially a toddler with a lead pipe. They block everything you can throw at them, and parry literally every attack. Dodging is pretty useless, they still hit you most of the time. They have so much health that even if you spam attack them with your best weapon, they still kill you before you whittle them down.I played a couple hours so I never got to experience a lot of the special zombies, but the few that I encountered were frustrating to the point of me just running any time I saw them. Sure, I get it's a parkour/running game but a game where you have to avoid most of the enemies isn't much fun. The zombies will also snap to the player even if you're mid swing/jump/dropkick. I feel like a machete pointing directly would trump their grapple but - hey my machete is gone!The fact that I felt compelled to write a review for a game that is 7 years old should be enough information on its own. I bought this game to make sure I'd like the style before I bought Dying Light 2. Needless to say, I will not be buying Dying Light 2 for fear of paying $60 for a prettier looking pile of junk.Really wish they'd just made another Dead Island. Honestly, the mechanics were all the same, they just added a really ♥♥♥♥♥♥ implementation of parkour and made combat way less interesting/more frustrating.

_childDocuments_.review: Originally I was lookin for a slowpace zombie open world/looting voyage with very wide distances to travel like Day-Z or similar games but I just dived straight into Dying light without lookin much into it since web searches says it is one of the top zombie games ever. I had an idea the gameplay was quite mobile yet I still got kinda surprised on how fast the pace really is and it can be quite intimidating at the start but I didn't get dissapointed for even one bit! The handling of the weapons is very satisfying whether it be melee, throwing weapons or guns. It's kinda like Dead Island but better in every aspect. The story provides a creepy good atmosphere of survival, I felt no rush in focusing on the main quests for story progress even if playing on solo since the game is kinda addicting once you get used to moving quick on routes especially when paired up with plenty of subquests, awesome visuals, great gameplay with a wide array of skills/weapons and superb map design. Also kudos to the devs for including so many details, like how goons with melee weapons responds when you suddenly pull out a gun- they are not braindead that will just come rushing everytime and will sometimes get their hands up or just run for the hills. Freshly turned aggressive zombies will sometimes cover up when u hurt them and show some last remnants of human traits like talking and begging before eventually succumbing to full blown biter. And so much more! The kind of subtle details that makes sense and within it makes you appreciate a game more than the typical. If you can get the Definitive Edition(good price on sale) then definitely go for it! it Includes all DLC's which means more more badass weapons and I think it includes an expansion but I haven't got to it yet. P.S Just when you thought being fast is enough.. wait till night comes

_childDocuments_.review: Take the best elements from Dead Island and throw in some semi open world Assassins Creed style cross city missions and you will get an idea of what this game is like.It is fun to play and the added element of nightfall with more dangers yet bigger XP rewards is certainly a good touch to bring to the game. The parkour element of running and scrambling over walls and rooftops is different - and essential if you want to avoid the hordes of zombies below.I think the downside is that you can get bored possibly from the repetetive nature of running and jumping around buildings and ledges. Clearly the game is massive in size and has a lot of gameplay time to clock with main storyline and side missions etc - so this is somehting i found and therefore have to play it in smaller lots than say Skyrim or any other leng ended open world game.Overall i have enjoyed what i have played so far and will continue to play this game in and around other titles that i own.I would recomment that if you are a fan of co-op gaming then this is a good shout for you as having someone watch your back is very helpful, and the game is more fun when playing with a partner through the main story.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros-Good story-Lots of environment to cover-Fun gameplay, movement, and fightingCons-You are a solider that has to hit the lowest level zombie 5 times to kill it-You are a solider that can't swing a weapon more than 3 times without needing to recover/rest-You are a solider that can't run for more than a 100 yards without almost passing out and needing to recover/rest-Everything has an incredibly low durability, and you can only repair a limited number of timesI understand there is an emphasis on survival in this game, but the mechanics they put in place to accomplish that are lame.  If they had made resources more scarce it would have provided a similar survival scenario, but you'd at least feel badass.  Or maybe gate off some of the abilities so that you need to actually learn new skills to get to other locations, etc...I'm an out of shape desk jockey and I can swing a sword more times than this guy.  He can scale the outside of a 4 story building without breaking a sweat and he can't swing a sword 3 times.There area  few other things, like how some zombies are just apparently immune to fire.  Or that an exploding shuriken to the head won't kill...The good news is, there are enough mods still that you can somewhat "fix" flaws in the game and make yourself a little more badass.  I played with enhanced weapons, so i can kill a "normal" zomie in one swing, and it's still a challenge; cause of the hoards of zombies that never stop coming, and the elite ones that are super fast, or spit, or are massive in size, etc etc.

_childDocuments_.review: The positive aspects of this game are discussed at length in several other reviews, so I'm not going to focus on that. What I am going to focus on is the fact that this game deleted my player data out of nowhere. I had been playing multiplayer with my brother over the course of several months - we played a bit here and there. First we had frequent multiplayer disconnection issues. We almost quit playing then, but finally solved that problem with an uninstall/reinstall. Fine - that I can forgive because it was resolved, but then about a month later with only one more quest in the main quest line to go, all my data just disappeared when I joined his game. We had changed no settings, touched no save files, etc. My inventory was gone, my character looked like a character that wasn't mine (but wasn't the default either), my skills were reset, etc. I lost everything. I have no idea how something like this happens, and I looked all over forums and discussion threads to try and find a solution, but only found fixes that didn't apply or more often than not I found threads that essentially concluded there's nothing to be done to reverse it. It's not only a letdown to not be able to finish what I was well on my way to completing, but it's just incredibly frustrating for this level of brokeness to be present in a game that has been out for so long. I don't know how many people have had an experience like mine, but just be warned that there is some kind of massive player/account save issue that can allow this to happen.

_childDocuments_.review: Edited as of august 24thI got this game imagining it would be closer to Dead Island and DI Riptide, but not quite. And, while I recommend this game with the caveats below, it's not like previous Techland titles, this one takes a bit more of time to be more enjoyable, somewhat like some RPGs, specially since better weapons are locked by "survivor level".Combat:Combat feels off at the beginning, but gets better as you get blade weapons and more skills. Game is always spawning new zombies from blind spots, where previously it had none. Also, for a chunk of the beginning of the game you get no cutting weapons, just blunt. And even when you do, the sound they do when slicing is... weird, it shouldn't sound like that, it really feels forced and artificial.Plus, I really disliked that weapons have limited repairs, some not even being able to be repaired. Now besides crafting a weapon from an existing one, you can add permanent upgrades (from loot and random map quests, like assisting survivors) to it, which is a nice touch.Progression:The game is initially divided into three main skill trees: survival, combat and agility.Survival:Get the air drops (orange crates, blue on the map). ALL of them. Your survivor level equals your weapons levels, be it in drops or stores. Dying takes those points away. Missions, be they main, side or radiant quests rewards with those survivor points and some neat rewards.Combat:Points for hitting, decapitating and cutting limbs, or killing enemies in any other way (traps, fall damage, etc). You don't lose exp in this treeAgility:Do fast-paced parkour like a good monke. You only lose exp in this tree if you eat too much doritos and skip leg day.Story/protagonist:I still can't say much about the overall plot, but sometimes the best is in the side quests, both in dialogue and plot, and in rewards. Sadly, only one playable character, nothing to customize on him (aside outfits but it's first person), and his personality is mostly bland and unremarkable. A mute character would be better, sometimes.Parkour:OK, the game has a good parkour, works like early assassins' creed series games, yet faster. However, it pretty much forces you to escape from combat due to enemies spawning where there was nothing nearby each five seconds sometimes, at least in the beginning. Sure, it's an overrun city, but how annoying! It gets better, tho.Overall, it's a good game, with the early game being the more frustrating, until I got somewhat good blade weapons. Also it's a loot fest, but not loot crates, just game drops. If you want a more traditional open world zombie game, go for games like Dead Island and Dead Island Riptide, there is still some people that play it.As for DLCs, they can be good for the weapons, if you get the complete package + game in a good discount.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most obvious things about this game is the story is just plain bad. The villain feels totally unoriginal and the protagonist is just  bland with really weak motivation for his actions. There honestly is not a single interesting character in this game. With that out of the way, this game plays simply amazingly and is easily my favourite zombie game. Put the difficulty up to the max and the dead will take a realistic beating before going down, forcing you to use the environment and the abilities you unlock to better deal with them. Nothing beats avoiding and running away from them however and in a game with such a fantastic parkour system this is what you want. It blows Assassins Creed out the water despite being first person and at night when you have the real scary stuff chasing after you it makes for incredibly intense chases. Get some friends to play this with though, it makes the experience so much better and the story isn't worth focusing on anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok, a friend of mine offered this game to me some months ago.Today another friend finally persuaded me to give it a try.After almost 4 hours of playing, I definitively can't recommand the game to anyone.Here are a few of the reasons :1) The game has too many "cheap" bad mechanic that are mixed with bugs that render the whole experience a pain more than any 'fun'. One exemple is the 'breakable' roofs. Having the same exact looking roofes reacting differently is not helping the player plans a travel. Thing get worse when the roof that 'break' under your feets don't let you 'fall' to the floor under, but teleport you 'over the street' (some 20m away) and drop you among a horde of zombies. And when that happen in the Tutorial, then something feel 'wrong'. Another is the spawn of zombies that appear in your back when you cleaned the whole place in a closed area. 2) Change in Mechanic for no reasons : You can jump and climb a lot of places, but suddenly in some 'quest area' you reach a point where you are unable to climb the exact same looking 'structures' just because "Boss Fight". Never a good thing to design some area that look like they are 'normal' but the normal game mechanic don't work there.3) Bug in quests : In 3 hours we did hit 3 bugs in quests, the 2 first made the quests impossible to validate, so we 'swallowed' it and cancelled the quests. The 3rd was a bit more problematic, as it was the Radio Boys. After the fight with the boss we found all the needed pieces to get to the 'top', only to find out the passage is bugged. No way to climb. And the only way to escape the whole building is to use the Grappling hook. As a lvl 2 Survivor player that's not an option, so the only way to 'escape' the bugged quest was to leave the online game or die...4) Bug with the zombies 'reactions' to distraction : Being forced in an area with 41 zombies, and supposed to use "distraction", I found out that the zombies who are "just too far from my position" don't react to distractions, so even if I throw firecrackers, the zombie near them don't react to the sound. The worse is that once the firecrackers finish to distract, the zombies do walk back to their starting position, defeating the whole  effort.5) Wanting to play with friend, mean you are forced to do the Tutorial and reach the first 'sleeping', never fun when you are forced into some 30+ minutes tutorial just to be "authorized" to play with friends online (they went as far as disabling the invite friend to game from Steam until the tutorial is 'finished'.)6) Last but not least, after the Radio Boys bug, my friend managed to get out of the building, but died outside from a fall. I just left the game, and tried to join back. The result was not exactly what we expected. As I ended up 'starting' in the Countryside area instead of joining his game (as if starting a new game myself), and he ended up losing his character progression fully, having his main character being fully reseted. That kinda made it for us. So all in all, after close to 4 hours of trial, the whole experience was not something of a 'fun time', but more of a sum of frustration. As much as I can enjoy a good parkour game, or a good 'survival' game, or even a 'messy hard to survive horde of zombies', the whole time passed in game did only leave a sour taste in my mouth and got me coming here to post this review.Edit :I know I only played 4 hours. But when hitting major game breaking bug while doingthe tutorial, and encountering bugs that were refered to the devs since January2015 and that are as severe as Reseting your whole Characters progressionto lvl 1 without any reason, and other such 'not fun situation', then the gamedeserve a Thumb Down.And yes, I tend to come and warn customers when a game is not worthto be bought. That's my right as a customer

_childDocuments_.review: While I would recommend this game, it is for a few points that I do enjoy, though there are many issues that I find very immersion breaking. I like the ability to climb objects and to play smooth online co-op. This game hits those notes perfectly. The story is absolute garbage in the main game and the DLC The Following. Reason why the story is garbage without spoilers. The person you play as condemns everyone to death by one of their actions, then blames someone else for it, never revealing that they (the player) are the evil one.The player acts like they care about the people they are helping but at no time shows any guilt in killing countless innocent people. This logic is mirrored in the DLC.Virals are supposed to be recently turned zombies that still have a slice of humanity left in them. This would be a great concept, if they didn't all fight you using master level capoeira, Wire jumping like in the Matrix, had the ability to scale 30 story buildings and were not everywhere in The Following DLC.The majority of the population in Turkey are white people and all have multiple pictures of the developers wedding in their offices, homes, garages, etc. These photos are so over used that you will be speaking with a character and there will be three of these pictures behind the person speaking. Other then landscape and buildings I wouldn't know it was supposed to be in Turkey.Having to play co-op with clones of yourself makes no sense and would be nice if there was a female option because playing as Bill from left for dead makes just as much sense.Frog zombies that shoot flying snot was pretty dumb.Confronting your nemesis to sheath your weapon or to completely lose all your weapons for no discussed in game reason was pretty gamey too.However, jump kicking a zombie off a roof does release stress.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to start this review with one statement: DO NOT BUY THIS GAME UNLESS IT'S ON SALETL;DR: Dying Light is a fun game with tons of potential, made un-fun by too many stupid design choices and it being so obviously optimised for console play that it's frankly quite insulting to even offer it on PC. If you can get it from a Steam Sale or Humble Bundle, definitely do it, but this is not worth £40.Pros: - Parkour. Seriously, this is great and the main reason I'd recommend this game. - You can dropkick zombies. Seriously, this is the greatest thing to ever happen to the zombie game genre.Cons:- Combat is stodgy, drawn out, lacks any elegance, and weapons are frankly useless. It takes half a dozen smacks directly to the head with a claw hammer to finish even the most basic infected. Humans can take upwards of 30 strikes, and are also cabable of reading your attacks and blocking them with some insultingly bad animations to justify their invulnerability. Swing a hammer at a dude's legs? Oh look he swayed his head, attack invalid. *facepalm*- Level design. Oh boy is this my biggest gripe after combat. If you're going to have a parkour game, EITHER you need to go Mirror's Edge and railroad the level, or you need to go Assassin's Creed and spend a lot of time making sure all buildings have logical routes up and down. Dying Light decided to go with secret option three of "let's just slap everything together in a hastily assembled shoddy mess and watch players slide back down walls that look identical to the ones they were climbing earlier". Seriously, nothing is more frustrating than seeing that they've only bothered to make half the ledges climbable and you now have to walk 100 meters round a building to find the route they wanted you to take, rather than the actually sensible one you found.- Durability is a joke, and not a funny one: if they're aiming for "hard hitting realism" then how about this? Drop-forged steel hammers don't break into a million pieces after two swings at a skull. The skull breaks. So good luck having to break flow every 10 minutes to pointless trash a piece of gear to get the weirdly specific components you need to repair the weapon you're using. And thank goodness that while you're doing all this you have to use a controller-friendly menu that refuses to give you even basic information and is about as mouse-friendly as a cattery- The story so far (no spoilers but some critque) seems railroady, cliched, and dull. Pretty much everyone is a boring horror movie trope with appalling-decision-itis, you have no choice as to what you might want to do in cutscenes (even if that is 100% against how you've been acting the entire rest of the game), and frankly I don't care about anyone in the damn city. It's a real gripe for me when games say "free and open world" then force you to follow their stupid, predictable path in cutscenes. - Night-time is scripted for certain missions, and scripted BADLY. Walk out to do a mission at dawn? OH NO, that short walk you've done a dozen times actually took 18 hours! - Enemies aren't scary. The only difference between day and night is not "heart-pounding action" it's "how many bloody times am I going to have to repair this pipe before his head finally explodes?" - Graphics are decidedly average. I'm running on highest settings across the board and I keep thinking I've fallen into an old Far Cry game. The "survivor sense" that lets you see enemies skeletons is a shoddy knock-off of Sniper Elite, and fails to show bones breaking thus rending it utterly pointless. - AI so far is deeply underwhelming - stand on a roof with survivor sense on at night and you can literally watch it rain zombies onto the cold unforgiving concrete below as they're too stupid to navigate the terrible building design.- Multiplayer is great with friends, but an absolute joke if you leave it on public play. Anti-cheating is OFF by default, and "Public Game" is the default online setting, and since there's no kind of level cap between people joining your world you're basically in for a crap shoot. I got lucky and got someone nice and friendly willing to go at my pace, but as he was a million times more powerful than me he could have just run off and complete the entire story, and I wouldn't even have been able to keep up with his running speed.- Side quests are all the same thing: "X wants some Y, got to Z and find some Y for X". There are occasional gems but be prepared in the most part for flow-breaking slogging with crumby rewards.- Levelling up isn't really a chance to feel powerful, as much as a chance to remove one of the many stupid limitations placed on your character.A good level system should make each upgrade feel like a serious bonus to your character. Dying Light has one or two like this (See: Dropkicking zombies, above) but the majority are just things which should have been built into the game. Your character constantly feels like he's got those abilities and has just decided not to use them, it's like playing the first 10-15 hours with a person who has deliberately handcuffed themself to a fridge and won't explain why.And finally, the "skill trees" aren't trees at all, they're lumps. You need very nearly everything in each lump so basically enjoy grinding the wretchedly bad combat to earn enough XP to make the combat less awful. The only choice you have is do you want to throw your weapon and walk over tediously to pick it up, or break it against the adamantium bones of the zombie wolverine horde? I'm going to give this game more of a chance since so many people seem to have different feelings, but after 6 hours of solid game-play I feel less rather than more hooked. Maybe I'll edit my review somewhere down the line if the story manages to pull some kind of miraculous heel-turn and when I've earned enough lump-points to put down the Plotonium weights I'm forced to carry, but I sincerely doubt it...

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to start out by saying; wow.I first bought this on Xbox One when it originally came out and it was the first game I bought on Steam when I built my new PC and honestly each time playing it through it only gets more fun.Recommend?: YesPlay with friends?: If you don't you're missing out on a lot. Do it.Before I review I want to point out that Techland is still ACTIVE in not just supporting the game, but dropping FREE DLC's as well. They're small, but add to the fun of the game, and at the time of this review are working on DL: Bad Blood... CAN'T WAIT...REVIEW:How can you not enjoy walking around in a zombie filled location holding a katana that both electocutes and sets zombies on fire while at the same time slicing their heads off with a clean swing. Overkill? Maybe, but that's not the point. Those night-time pursuits? I'll let you figure that out for yourself... ;)For what the game is the story is good and I enjoy the voice-acting. The story gets exponentially more fun when played with at least one other as you jump around the map completing missions.Side missions? They're pretty unfullfilling, and there's a lot of them; however, occasionally you'll come across a weapon blueprint as a weapon reward and you can't help but feel like a kid in a candy store.Long story short: if you're looking for a game that you can enjoy single-player but quickly jump into a multiplayer game with friends to conquer missions and have a great zombie-filled experience. This is 110% the game for you. My friends and I have spent many hours on this game both on Steam and on Xbox playing this and haven't regretted a single minute. I can truly say it's one of the best gaming experiences I've had in my gaming lifetime. Props to Techland for making me cry for joy, and simultaneously crapping myself while running at nighttime on the hardest difficulty.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Despite the current issues with performance/optimization and the occasional crash, this game does something that most games fail at: making the core gameplay elements the best part of the game. I find the parkour and the dismemebering amazingly fun. I just did a mission where an npc caused tons of zombies to come running towards us and so I just jumped on a roof and kept kicking the oncoming zombies off of the roof, which was just one option that I had to choose. I also really appreciated the way the devs made it feel like a real zombie experience because you are actually scared of the zombies; you can't run in with you machete and expect to make through the other side in the main game (unless it is the super OP lighting one that you get from a side quest). _childDocuments_.review: All in all a entertaining and somewhat suprising game.The gameplay starts off slow, where zombies, the walking kind, are your biggest threat. This goes on until you find an amazing blueprint, one of many, that allow you to destroy them all in one shot. And this may sound unbalanced to you, but when the push comes to shove and there are upwards of 30 zombies hording you and you need to get out, slashing your way throught them is a hell of a time. And then the other types of zombies come into play, wherein you stop destroying them with your almighty Angel sword, and you turn to the flowing parkour mechanics this game supports.More on parkour you say? Well, all together, you start off quite slow, and this is kind of to be expected, as you are an unexperienced runner and all. However, this slowness kind of does last a litle longer than nessecary, and it probably takes an unnessecarily long amount of time to get the grappling hook. But when you finally do, the becomes a breeze. You are the fastest thing out there, or so you think. And in that moment of brief glee for your new found grappling hook freedom, you decide to go out at night, because 'dem Volatiles aint got nothing on you!In that reckless moment, you hear it. The blood curdling scream of the night hunter. You have been invaded. All of a sudden, your told of your new threat, a speedy, cunning hunter, with so many tricks in his arsenal, and, in the same strokes, none of your tried and true zombie killing method work. No longer does your enemy mindlessly hobble towards you, oh no, this guy is like f**king spiderman on steroids. He is everywhere. And you wont be able to keep up. Through time and a whole lot of bloodshed, you will learn good old spidermans weakness's, and develop your own strategy to destroying him, but it takes a decent amount of time for that to happen. In summary.Campaign 8/10 Some unexpected twists, some expected ones. By the end you will wonder how your character hasn't had a mental breakdown yet, as there is some heavy stuff in there.Co-op 9.5/10 There is always something to do, wether it be slashing down the hordes, saving survivors or competing in the constantly popping up impromtu competitions, this never leaves you wishing it was a solo game.Multiplayer 7.5/10 Very steep learning curve. Your first invasion will nearly always end in your defeat without the assistance of another experienced player, and the same goes for the zombie. To be honest, it would not be harmful if they had an hour counter beside each player in the Zombie joining lobby, or some system alike that, as the skill levels are  incredibly noticable.In summary, fun alone, better with friends and intense as hell when invasion time comes.

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a gamer. I have never been a gamer. My experience with games was limited to booting up HOMM3 about once a year. But then I saw a trailer for Dying Light: The Following on a website dedicated to horror - the one with practical zombie make-up. I was intrigued - so I went looking for more information, and found the gameplay demo. For the first time, I found myself wanting to play something other than a casual game. I will omit the long journey from wanting it to actually playing it and the relationships that were forged on the basis of this game - let's just say it was a chaotic mess; what's important is that I now own DL on PC and PS4, and have completed the game at least twice on each platform.So what is the Dying Light neophyte experience?First and foremost - it's a ton of fun. The open world has plenty to do and plenty to loot. There is something ridiculously satisfying about coming to a city square full of zombies, clearing them all out and collecting the loot. The parkour system, as a reviewer pointed out, adds another dimension to the available direction of movement, making traversing the map an adventure rather than a chore. Combined with the DLCs (The Following, Bozak Horde), DL offers a wide variety of activities and environments to suit every taste and mood without becoming overwhelming (looking at you, Far Cry 4).Second - it was easy for a noob like me to grasp the gameplay mechanics. So if you have a partner who doesn't play but needs a way to let off steam - try introducing them to DL. Kicking a screaming viral's head in or watching them fly into the air on a car bomb explosion can be quite therapeutic.Third - the community. I have seen experienced players joining the games of those with lower ranks (myself included) and helping them out: watching their backs so they don't get killed, pointing them to humanitarian drops for them to get the XP, showing them easter egg locations. (I've also encountered a-holes - but let's not talk about them).The script and voice acting are a mixed bag. The main plot is cheesy and full of holes, the main villain might as well be a cartoon character with how hyperbolic his evil is. But where DL really shines is in world-building: tiny tidbits of information about the lives of the people of Harran are often genuinely heartbreaking, from a voice message left by a mother to tell her daughter who her real father is, to the diary of a mentally disabled man who can't grasp what is going on and is interpreting the zombie epidemic in his own way.There is co-op play and PVP, but I'm not a fan of it and prefer to play alone most of the time, so I can't really comment on it much. Like I mentioned earlier, you will encounter some incredible players who will take low-ranks under their 250-level wings - and you will encounter a-holes who treat the game as if they're training for the Olympics and see it as a personal insult if you're not on their level. Pay them no heed and play the way you want to.Do I recommend Dying Light? 100% yes.

The loot makes you much more powerful and means that you feel like you can explore further and further for better loot. _childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game. I do. But it's just so... boring and generic. There's nothing that really sets it apart. There's nothing new or interesting here. There's nothing about it that makes you go 'I should play this over all the other ones.' As a single player experience, it's just very uninteresting. Melee weapons are worthless compared to archery, elemental abilities are barely useful, and customization yields no real benefit. If the fluff is all less useful than an arrow to the face, why use it? If you can set basic zombies on fire, and all it does is allow them to get back up while looking a little burned... then why use it? That's what I keep asking while playing. Instead of being interested in anything, I'm constantly barraged with crafting materials for things that are all less useful than a basic bow and arrow. Furthermore, there's nothing interesting about the setting; having your zombie game in a foreign slum isn't unique or novel. It's just an easy way to explain why everything is already run down. It's the default. There's nothing that stands out about it. Hell, even the main villain is a rip off of a Far Cry villain. In short, you got a game that wishes it was Dead Island, with a story that wishes it was Far Cry, with zombies that wish they were in Left 4 Dead.Is it technically sound? Yeah, but that's the bare minimum. There's nothing about the game that makes it a 'must play' title.

That and there are a lot spoiler zombies that will have you worried (Volatile) when the sun goes down.Had a very “Fun” moment where 2 people had joined my game just as it was getting Dark, we were pretty much playing Sandbox. Running around and bullying the “biters” laughing and comparing different ways of killing them and the few “virals” that interrupted us. (Coop makes it a lot easier as you can gang up on more powerful zombies and watch each other’s backs)This changed big-time however as the sun went down, we went from hunting to being hunted real fast. Trying to keep it together as a group when a hoard of virals are hot on your heals is both terrifying and hilarious at the same time, we ended up chased into an apartment complex which turned out to be a dead end. But thanks to great teamwork we actually held out till morning by holding a small apartment with one entrance, one person would heal and repair his weapons while lending an occasional kick while the two others held the Volatiles at bay with UV lights and everything from leg furniture to screwdrivers and wrenches.Most heart racing experience I have had in gaming for a very long-time, our elation at surviving however went south when we realised the battered and retreating Volatiles had been replaced by a hoard of zombies “biters” that swarmed the building we were in. Seeing your team being dragged down one at the time by a wall of dead flesh, before being pulled out of your corner and devoured was surprisingly enjoyable.Only real thing I can put my finger on is optimization, the game doesn’t seem to be 100% optimized and if you have AMD graphic card you might encounter some FPS drops that shouldn’t happen. Hopefully this will be addressed in patches.If not a 10/10 then defiantly a 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Regarding the new PVP changes:- PVP is fun but a lot harder for humans to do now. Due to gear changes, it is a lot easier to play against Night Hunters solo due to gear cooldowns. I advise playing solo in PVP now or playing with someone you trust very much. Death From Above attacks no longer are the go to as they modified the range for activation to the point where you will land face to face with the hunter more often than not.- Cheaters are everywhere but not many people turn on VAC because it's disabled by default and people don't realise this. Your options are to either leave it switched off but risk coming into contact with cheaters, or leave it on and have far less games to connect to. There are work arounds for this, but not the kind people can really be bothered to do themselves.Regarding the rest of the game:- It's a great game with fun mechanics, you'll struggle to play any games similar to it again like Dead Island due to wanting to run up walls and jumping over rooftops.- The story is... ok. In my opinion the story is just a means of driving the interesting mechanics of the game. It's not bad  and is worth going through all the way.To conclude, I suggest you buy this game on sale like I did. The season pass is really only useful for The Following so if it works out cheaper I'd buy that stand alone. You don't really need any of the cosmetics or weapon packs, the other items are good enough on their own.

_childDocuments_.review: If you are unsure whether to get DL or not, be unsure no more: get it! _childDocuments_.review: Dying Light opens incredibly strong, having a great parkour system to make running around and exploring the world fun. Zombies start off as an interesting threat, with the threat of nighttime hordes and chases entertainingly tense at first, though in part due to combat being clunky.Combat smooths out later on, but essentially turns into QTEs where you're regularly animation locked into instant kill animations while completely vulnerable to damage. In addition the camera is fairly constantly jerked around in combat outside of player input, which can be headache or motion sickness inducing.Finally, unfortunately by the latter half of the game, the bugs become fairly constant. Audio desyncs, subtitle desyncs, and a janky save/load system that can soft lock progression ended up making the story barely comprehensible in my playthrough after a certain point.

_childDocuments_.review: This game saved my life.I am 37.My ex-wife and I have a daughter together, and adopted our son together. They are now both 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I found myself lost and miserable. I was self destructive. I got so mad one day from everything spiraling out of my control that I punched some concrete in a moment of overwhelming emotion. That caused me to break my 5th metacarpal in my right hand... my working hand... my games hand.. the hand that I held and carried my children to bed with.. The hand I desperately needed to make sure I could continue to provide.After learning of the severity of my self-inflicted damage, I was borderline suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man with no history of depression or anxiety. I have never had fits of rage, or been one to break down and cry, but I was in a low spot that just really buried me from being able to see the light on the other side.Having nothing better to do, I searched for a game I could play, ONE HANDED while I recovered. I somehow stumbled upon this game and read some of the reviews. I decided that it had to be worth a shot... I must admit, I didn't beat the game, or play nearly as long as some of you. In fact, I may have only played this game a day or two.. With that being said, after doing so, I had a new found joy and hope for life. I was able to put behind me the pain and suffering that had been cast over me. I was able to experience other peoples joy and happiness. I was able to see the fruits of my "labor". I relaxed for 5 minutes to this music long enough to realize that I was going to be okay.After coming to that realization, I turned the game off, and I went back to work. It hurt my hand like hell but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so damn sorry for myself, and I became the father I needed to be in that moment, not the weak boy I was behaving as.Today, I am close friend with my kids mother. We don't fight, or argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents, and friends.I now have 3 kids. My third child is, wait for it, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The woman I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my own separation, and we just stumbled in to each others life unexpectedly. We have been in a relationship for a year now, and are very happy together.Moral of the story, you never know what life holds in store for you, and if I would have given up when all the odds were stacked against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you

Its easily worth the full price and It looks and plays and amazing in 2023! 10/10EDIT: I just completed "The Following" It was a good DLC and was very much a standalone game in of its self. _childDocuments_.review: Where dead island failed, dying light succeeded. it's a fantastic game with an interesting story line, if you do not own it just yet, i'd highly recommend trying it. day time is easy, you'll spend it doing quests, traveling and looting while night time is challenging, you'll have to sneak about and use your wits. run from volatiles and infected as once they spot you they will hunt you down. the first few levels is challanging, only because of the low damage your weapons deal, you can cheese it by finding spike traps and kicking zombies into them, around level 5 your damage output should be high enough to 2 shot most standard zombies on normal.one thing that i find nice about this game is the option to run your game in vac secure mode or not. that way if you dont want to waste your time looting just cheat engine and dupe items. i find the human enemies to be far more challanging than any of the zombies (except the volatiles) luckily once you get a gun you can shoot them in the face! :Dthe free running is well done, once you get the grappling hook, it's a breeze.the first area is designed for freerunning with rooftop pathways, blue tarps and piles of garbage to guide your way. the second area is more for the grappling hook with plenty of tall buildings to run and jump around to avoid the annoying groans of the undead below you. then the DLC is open farm land, plenty of beautiful sites but the question of why the ♥♥♥♥ are there so many zombies in such an unpopulated area (seriously, it's mostly farm land and the zombie count doesn't match up.) it being mostly wide open lands makes it easier for driving around, need to level up your driving? no worries just drive through a horde. this review is not accurate as i haven't played past the slums in a very long time, i am mostly going off memory. eitherway it is a great game and if you were a fan of dead island, i highly recommend giving this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Story line is boring, voice acting is bad, mission development is lazy, development as a whole is pretty lazy with this game (aside from visual), there is no REAL incentive to go outside at night aside from being forced to by missions, free-running will kill you a LOT with no fault on your part, and the writing for all the missions (including side missions) seems to have been written by someone trying to portray everyone in a apocolyptic situation as either a whiny ♥♥♥♥♥ or ruthless dictator.To sum up this game, all you need to do is play through the finale. No real spoilers here, just going to list off non-story related things (even though the end of the story is pretty unimpressive as well): you are forced to run back across the maps to get to the finale (because there is no fast-travel and going anywhere takes forever, ESPECIALLY this ridiculous run that they only make more difficult), once you get there you basically get entered into a giant platforming mini-game without the use of your grappling hook that you leveled for and have equipped, get introduced to a zombie that sprints at you and kills you on impact (which is the only one in the game and is positioned right around a corner that you have to die to discover and potentially die more to get past), more platforming that you just trial-and-error through by dying over and over, then once you get to the actual finale it's a quicktime-event cut scene (THE ONLY ONE IN THE GAME) with about 7 buttons that you just have to die over and over to memorize unless you have the reaction time of a 17 year old on crack. The end. No final battle or anything, just a huge, annoying, unecessary, anticlimactic, jump/die fest.The only redeeming qaulity is running around in co-op and being absolute idiots with other people online. I would actually be 100000% down if that was all this game was, but with the weapon damage and the tiny trickle of money you get in the game, that's not really possible.The versus mode is entertaining for the first couple rounds, but once the survivors realize to just stick together and have UV lights out constantly, it's almost impossible to beat them. Not really scary from the survivors point of view, mostly because it's pretty easy to win. I didn't even really get any enjoyment out of the wins because they felt like I was handed them on a golden platter.In the end, Dying Light is not that great. I would actually put it on par with Dead Island (the team's last zombie game), ignoring all the hiccups and technical issues Dead Island ran into at launch. Add fast travel, an adventure mode that encourages running around and being stupid with friends (and no, the challenges aren't enough; potentially a survivor vs survivor mode?), tweak the free-running to make it more reliable, and give me a real reason to go out and die over and over in the night, then we'll talk about whether or not this game is worth getting. Deal?

_childDocuments_.review: I do recommend the game because it was a good starting point for DL2 to improve on, but coming back to this game after a few years, I'm really annoyed with multiple aspects of the game. Mainly, the stamina system is ridiculous. If you attack before your combat stamina COMPLETELY refills, it's drained entirely again and you don't even get a normal attack out of it. When sprinting, there is no indication when Crane is becoming tired and can't sprint. You can climb indefinitely, sure but running? No you don't have the cardio for that apparently. The combat system also annoys me. The most basic zombie can somehow catch themselves on fire, take NO damage from the environmental fire, and then when you hit them with a weapon they'll fall forward and turn that into an attack which will both hurt you regardless of when you try to dodge and then hit you with fire damage. I have over 100 hours of this game played on PS4, 30 hours on Steam, and over 100 hours in DL2 and when I started this new playthrough (for like the 5th or 6th full playthrough) I was fighting a basic biter that was on fire and it took me down from full HP to 20HP and went through AN ENTIRE WEAPON AND NUMEROUS KICKS before it finally died. This is only like 30-45 minutes into the game. This game is only worth playing for the story (that really isn't even connected to the sequel aside from a brief mention of Harran and a Spike cameo in the beginning of the game) and the Following. And maybe gunplay since they decided to completely remove it from DL2 for some reason. Not worth $30 anymore but at least they managed to integrate the game into the new Pilgrim Outpost hub since the companion app was completely broken, but even then you could play missions on your phone and play almost an entirely separate game that allowed you to send your character items to use in the main game. What happened to this franchise?

Characters have nice voice-overs which make them more believable. As for romance, there's some slight sexual tension but not anywhere near Mass Effect.Be a Zombie was pretty boring.. I thought it would be more subtle than "oh you're being invaded.. go kill nests and try not to get eaten by a tentacle-hentai super-zombie"Overall, the parkour zombie killing is a somewhat fresh view in this genre. The guns are "guns".. they make noise and they are powerful. Co-op is a bit glitchy but alot of fun.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is a summary of my opinions on Dying Light - To this day I'm still impressed by the graphical quality of this game.  It was released nearly two years ago and I'm still often surprised by how detailed the environments and the textures are.  Granted, I don't really have the time to stand around and stare at the floor textures as I'm usually fighting or looting.10/10 - This is another high point for me. I take huge stock in the sound in games, whether it be soundtrack quality or actual in game sound.  The in game sound itself is nigh perfect, with an excellent mixture of visceral detail and gory effects.  A good example of this is when the goon does his spin attack, you can hear the little pieces of gravel rolling around on the ground beneath him after he stops swinging.  Along the same lines, the voice acting is actually pretty good as well.  It's kind of "campy" sometimes, but it's not overpowering and doesn't distract from the feeling of the game itself.  The soundtrack is also excellent, and I have found myself listening to it by itself from time to time.  It adds a significant amount in the way in tension and ambiance, and I can appreciate the use of a kind of pseudo-techno vibe that it carries.  My only minor complaint is that I wish there was a little bit more variation in the sound effects, as you start to notice repetition after about 10 hours of play.10/10 - As far as open worlds go, I really enjoyed immersing myself in Haran.  As is typical of a game of this sort, there are a lot of locked doors and inaccessible areas, but I feel as though there is not much to be done here.  Still, there are a great many interiors that you can explore and loot, so I would say that this is just a very minor downside.  I thoroughly enjoy the accessibility of the exterior, as there aren't a whole lot of invisible walls impeding your movement.  I only came across an unnecessary invisible wall maybe twice in my entire experience.10/10 - Generally, the animations of yourself from a first person perspective, the zombies/humans, and the big baddies are pretty good. Sometimes the virals can slide around a little bit, and this hurts the game slightly. Also, while the facial textures look amazing, the facial animations just aren't quite up to snuff.9/10 - The story of Dying Light is pretty good.  It's pretty much what you might expect in terms of a two groups of people trying to survive a zombie apocalypse, but that's not a bad thing.  Even though it's open world, you're pretty much pigeon holed into a specific story line, so there's not a lot of choice you can make.  For example, (minor spoilers) early in the game the voice of the GRE tells you to burn the antizen to force an interaction between your group and Rais' group.  This all happens in a cutscene so you can't stop it from happening.  Granted, if you had decided not to burn the antizen it would have changed the entire story arc.  I'm not too upset about this though, as I feel like it was executed correctly, and often times giving the player the illusion of choice when the ending is already set in stone can be worse than just forcing them into a decision.  I think I completed the story mode on hard in around 25 hours or so.8.5/10 - Character development in this game is pretty shallow. Didn't really become attached to any of the characters, and I was alone so much that I couldn't really remember who anyone was.  The only character I really know anything about is Rais. Maybe this was by design?6/10 - The items in this game range from good to useless. An example of a good item is the molotov, as it is excellent at clearing out moderately sized groups of zombies allowing you to save your precious weapon durability.  I would consider the shield to be useless, but I can imagine if you're playing this game with 3 other people having a dedicated shield bearer would be very useful.  I only played with one other person and the loss of damage output was not even remotely made up by the reduced damage taken.  Also, I kind of hate the fact that you get the grappling hook so early in the game.  For a game that revolves around the parkour aspect, they don't waste any time giving you a tool to just ignore it completely.  My friend and I decided that we would only use the grapple whenver we had to as to keep the game from getting too simple.7.5/10 - The main story quests in this game are actually really fun and enthralling.  Sometimes they can be very challenging as well, which in a coop game is pretty hard to balance.  I feel like they did a great job with this aspect.  That being said, the side quests... ugh.  When you start it's not too bad, as they are pretty standard types of open world RPG quests (i.e. go here, do a thing, come back and tell me and I'll give you a reward).  Pretty quickly, however, it gets ridiculous.  Sometimes they don't even make any sense.  For example, you'll walk up to a guy after he calls to you and will say something like "My son is sick and needs his medication.  Can you get it for me?"  "Sure" you reply, but then randomly he says "ehhh I don't know if I trust you enough... go to the other side of town and pick up my backpack that I dropped as well as 30 metal pieces and 12 pieces of gauze, and when you do that then you can get the medicine."  So many times I just wanted to say "lol no", but the completionist inside of me made me do it.7/10 - The AI in this game is just okay.  Sometimes a viral will get stuck trying to climb up something and just stand there and growl, or the goon will get stuck attacking a wall.  Also, sometimes when you go to pick up an airdrop and Rais' men beat you there, if you toss a molotov on them they will literally sit there and burn instead of coming after you.  Kind of goofy to watch.5/10 - I'd say the game is pretty good. I certainly had fun playing it.  Replay value is kind of lacking.  I kind of wish they made it so it was a lot harder to unlock the skills so you actually had to kind of specialize.  That way you could replay the game as an entirely different "class" and thus be challenged in a different way.  I guess they did this because they wanted solo play to be viable, which I can understand.  I'm writing this during the fall sale of 2016, and the game is 50% off (or $29.99).  I HIGHLY recommend this game at this price, ESPECIALLY if you have a friend to play it with.

_childDocuments_.review: 7/10, good game (+1 with EE: The Following)--- edited review ---(quick review update for game version 1.11.1, Linux tested, played multiplayer The Following addon)Good news. Game finally seems to be fixed and actually is playable on 680 GTX. I assume game is not up to par with Windows version but framerates are way better than on 1.5.0.Mouse re-binding WORKS. Even SIDE BUTTONS. Hear that, 4A Games (Metro: LL)?You still have interface designed for gamepads, but doing more complex actions like selecting arrow types for the bow etc. seems to work well.Fixed: + framerates + keybindingWorth of trying, especially if you grab the enchanced edition from the Steam sales. EE includes addon campaign The Following and several minor DLC's.--- old review below ---(review for game version 1.4.0, Windows playthrough, Linux tested)edit: Plus: + generic gameplay: movement and combat is fun + woo-effect: nice looking, lots of graphical detail + gore effects: good gore effects which are not ultra-overdone Minus: - lame boss fights, QTE WTF? - exploring is not rewarding (unless for Steam achievement) - game console syndrome (awkward UI, feels like non-PC game)     - grappling hook Dying Light is Dead Island re-animated... er... zombified? Worst parts of DI have been rotten out, so you now have actually playable game.Gameplay is heavily parkour-styled, so your character, Kyle Crane, will climb and jump around the city of Harran in search of cure research for the zombie virus. Harran is made up from two large areas Slums and Old Town, which are enough distinct to spark your EXPLORE!-fire again when you change the map. The game world is quite amazing and graphics developers have been doing marvelous job to add lots of details all around. Exploring the world will give you XP, but when you hit the level cap the rewards from exploring won't account much unless you play for Steam achievements. On the other hand, as there aren't any practical reason to explore more, two large map areas will suffice.Movement is fluid and usually you get intended action (grab a ledge, jump off from the wall) so you actually feel like you're doing parkour moves. If surface looks like it could be grapped or climbed, that's usually the case. Movement skill level also adds to the feeling that Kyle Crane physically learns more as he goes on. Having seen some games which kind of sucked (Mirror World *cough* *cough*) and some games where all surfaces are fair game (Ninja Gaiden), doing parkour in DL is simply fun. Of course some movement restrictions are in place as game world is finite, there are surfaces you can't grab and gameplay area is confined by magical invisible walls. Later on you get grappling hook, while it speeds up gameplay considerably, you lose most of the illusion of being parkour runner.Combat system is fairly simple. Neverthless it's entertaining enough for few hours just to bash, slash, maul and maim zombies with whatever weapon you get on your hands. Zombies react to physics, so they can tackled, toppled over fences or forced to climb on high places to even reach you (and then they get kick in the face). You're able to target generic body area so usually button mashing is a great combat tactic. There is unfortunate auto-targetting when doing some combat moves but I guess it's price to pay for playing console game. Story is kind of mixed bag, as side quests have more story than the main quest. Most of NPCs have at least somewhat interesting dialogue and voice acting & animations are ok, some overacting, but also some really excellent performances. Most of the default story line aspects living in the city full of undead are handled in way or another through side quests or collectibles. Unfortunately main quest includes some really dumb forced story events, bad boss seems to have constant grip from Crane's balls whatever Kyle tries to do. Kyle Crane voice acting shows him as quite strong-willed character, he's not on par with JC Denton but delivers his punch lines with real punch well enough (except every time when Kyle meets evil boss he puts whimp clothes on so he can receive good spanking). I have kind of insight after my playthrough that Techland can't make a game without horrible main story twists. Dead Island was such a dog puke, DL is bit better though as side quests will give some credibility for the story writer.Of course the zombie game aren't zombie game at all if there aren't any gibs! In DL zombie gibs are also finite, for example you can't cut only fingers off, then palm off, wrist off and so on, you only chop off whole hand from elbow. Gore effects are fairly well done and stay within reasonable limits so you can enjoy the effects and do not get WTFs every time. Gore with taste, I say! Also splatter effects on walls seems to correspond with weapon you're using.User Interface is designed for consoles, game has "hold this key and move mouse"-style weapon/item menu. This might work if you have gamepad or such, but I played this with keyboard and mouse. You can rebind the keys, but you need to limit yourself to only some items or juggle through awkward inventory if you want to use more items (especially elixirs). Also keybinding on Linux version is horrible and mouse recognizes only 3 buttons.Also final battle with the boss is just one facepalm moment you can't forget. So, you're ready with best weapons with best upgrades, holding boss' own gun to give it back one bullet at time and lots of invulnerability elixirs to gulp. You climb on the final ledge ready to pump this guy full of lead and then chop him to tiny grilled evil zombi-snack bits with your Fiery Sword of Death. Well, that's how it should go? Instead you're treated with Quick-Time Event (QTE) where one-handed man beats your zombi-killing hero to ground only using one hand and whole battle...  no, not battle... watching interactive movie... consist of pressing seven buttons in certain order. WTF? In fact, here's pro-tip for you: in this game you can discard your weapons before playing any main quests against boss as you can't never use them.Conclusion: despite some shortcomings this is quite fun game. Main story sucks but as one NPC said to Crane, blockbuster movies are all about happy endings and badly told stories. Here's story for 70€ (incl. Season Pass). As long you remember to turn your brain off for the main story quest, you should have fun. On the bright side, gameplay is fun and entertaining for one playthrough. Multiplayer might add some more hours, but I'll suggest you first try the game on single player or with newbie friends as best parts of the game experience is at the beginning of the game. I would say with more experienced story designer,  and adapting interface more for keyboard/mouse this could have been excellent gem.

_childDocuments_.review: NOMINATE THIS GAME FOR LABOUR OF LOVE 2019I'm not usually a fan of zombie games, but the skills that this game gives you to traverse the enviroment are an absolute blast to use and were even better than I'd hoped for when I bought it. Combat is simple, but responsive and satisfying enough to stay fun (outside of unclear shockwave hitboxes and rubble sometimes knocking you in the direction it was thrown in), with enough enemies to keep thing fairly interesting. I do wish human AI was more complex, though.The game isn't particularly tough on normal and it's even easier in co-op, but higher difficulties do more than just make enemies stronger so there's room for more challenge for those who want it. Co-op, on that note, is actually a LOT of fun, although the assymetrical multiplayer mode is somewhat confusing and seems unbalanced at first. Whether or not it's good is basically at the mercy of what area you're in.Story isn't anything special but it's surprisingly decent for what it is. Feels like a dumb B-movie.Game doesn't have a ton of replayability if you don't enjoy the mechanics and/or multiplayer, but the devs are releasing tons of free content, so props for that. There's plenty of room for self-imposed challenge.If there were a few more enemies, better human AI, and the missions/their areas were more open-ended, this'd be perfect in my eye. It's still great as it stands though.

_childDocuments_.review: WARNING FOR AMD USERS:  This game is not optimized well for AMD, I've heard its gotten better since release, and I am technically running a CPU lower than the minimum (im on FX6300 OCed to 4.5GHz 6-cores/threads)  and it still looks great.  I have textures and shadows on medium, turned off some of the extra effects such as motion blur, and just reduced the LoD to around 20% and its golden.  1080p, full 60fps without fail.  Just be wary if you have AMD cpu, it MAY not run well if you aren't on a pretty nice overclock.I don't have a ton of hours in this, but I can already tell you its a really good game.  Perfect? Most games aren't.  There are a few flaws, a big one being the lack of AMD support and very minimal graphical and game options (texture options are medium or high only) .  But despite these things, you have a really solid game here.It plays a bit like a first person Assassin's Creed.  Climb buildings to avoid detection on the ground, but instead of stealth, its really just to not get eaten by zombies.  There are collectables hidden in the lovely verticality of the world, competitions for co op games, challenges that are both co op and solo, and the story is at least motivating enough to keep you wanting to uncover some stones, something I can't say for all games I play.  The mechanics are nice, the combat and free running are quite fluid.  It will never get old sprinting up to a lone zombie only to drop kick him, sending him backwards.  There are rpg elements to your character, similar to the way a WB game like batman might allow you to increase your health, damage, or even add moves to your arsenal.  In Dying Light you get more combat abilities as well as parkour abilities.If you like the feeling of being chased, exploring, climbing, or just kinda enjoy the whole atmosphere of a zombie infested world with humanity clinging on, this is one you don't want to miss.P.S.  Someone mentioed something about getting motion sickness while playing.  While I have never experienced any motion sickness playing any game, I do feel like if you have a tendency towards that sort of thing, this MAY NOT be the game for you.  Parts definitly start to make me feel a little strangely, but I noticed the effect is lessened at higher resolutions (and possibly with a higher FoV for which there is no in game option.)

_childDocuments_.review: So Zombies huh.. there surely are a lack of Zombie games at the moment methinks... However.. This would be a fantastic action game without the obligatory `biters` so it is in fact all the better for their inclusion. The freerunning element works really well and with a bit of practice you will be drop kicking an enemy into spikes, sliding and then breaking another ones legs, through a gap in the fence and setting off a trap with the minimum of fuss. The controls are rock solid and the way the Combat and Parkour blends together is totally seamless.Being chased by a pack of Zeds through the city at night and making it to a safe zone is totally pulse pounding and hugely satisfying.The mixture of crafting, scavenging and combat is nicely balanced and the ability to customise that Superior Cricket Bat (no really) is a nice addition. Weapons schematics can be found for all sorts of effects including Bleeding damage, Electric attacks and Fire attacks. You can also mod them further with increased damage,better handling and all sorts of goodies. There ARE guns available but making alot of noise will attract the recently infected (AKA Virals) who are fast, vicious, intelligent and can pretty much climb up to any vantage point you care to retreat to. Basically if you want to make something go `BOOM` make sure you are tooled up and ready for a fight. There are so many ways of killing your foes I am beginning to lose count but if you love Throwing Stars, Molotovs,Grenades, Bombs,Pistols,Shotguns,Assault rifles,Exploding Barrels,Car Bombs... well you get the idea. ( Not to mention the Burning,Freezing,Exploding and Toxic effects you can add to thrown ordanace.. >:P  ) In short this is a fantastic game and I cant recommend it enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light started off as a game with potential.  An opening that peaks your interest and leaves you excited for more.  Within a few minutes I realized that there are some mechanical flaws within the game, nothing that can't be over looked, at first.  This game features a Breath of the Wild like weapons system where your weapons break constantly and require replacing.  Enemies require ridiculous amounts of damage to defeat prior to unlocking conditional executions, which don't unlock until an annoyingly late stage of the game. The free-running system the game has is a fun idea, but poorly executed.  Controls are likely to leave you dead before you knew what happened.   Progression within the "skill" trees is incredibly grindy and by the end the perks you want are out of reach in favor of forced unlocks for perks you'll never use.  The crafting system also features a short progress bar during which you create the items you are crafting, which servers no purpose other than wasting the players time since the rest of the game is paused while in the menu.  The animation for picking up items in the game also serves to be annoying and waste the players time. All these mechanical problems add up to an awful experience that I couldn't wait to be done with.  The "final boss" dialogue speaks to the character being weakened by anger and I couldn't help but wonder if this was speaking directly to me, the mechanical flaws of the game sure had me frustrated and angry by the end.  Worst of all was the climactic "boss battle" ended in the absolute worst implementation of quick time events that I have ever seen.  Dying Light is a bad game that tried so hard to be good.  I'm embarrassed to say that this game didn't end up in my "did not finish" list.

_childDocuments_.review: ⭐ Dying Light is a standout title in the survival horror genre, transporting players to the zombie-infested city of Harran. It's more than just another zombie shooter; it's an open-world adventure packed with challenges and surprises.⭐ Key Strengths:- Vast and Immersive Open World: Harran is meticulously crafted, featuring towering skyscrapers, sprawling slums, and diverse locales. Players have the freedom to explore, scavenge for supplies, and undertake side quests.- Diverse Gameplay: Dying Light offers a blend of gameplay mechanics, from intense melee combat and ranged shooting to parkour and crafting. This variety allows players to tailor their playstyle.Dynamic Day-Night Cycle: The game features a compelling day-night cycle. Zombies are slower and less aggressive during the day, but as night falls, they become more agile and dangerous, introducing new, formidable variants.- Engrossing Storyline: Dying Light offers a deep and engaging narrative with complex characters and dramatic situations. Beyond the action, the game delves into character psychology and societal themes.- Thriving Community and Co-op: The game boasts a large and active community, and its co-op mode allows players to team up, explore the world together, battle zombies, and complete missions.⭐Areas for Improvement:- Difficulty: The game can be quite challenging, especially in later stages. Players may need patience and practice to overcome obstacles.- Optimization: On some systems, performance issues like stuttering or frame rate drops may occur.⭐ Conclusion:- Dying Light is a must-play for fans of survival horror. With stunning visuals, diverse gameplay, and a compelling narrative, it offers countless hours of thrilling entertainment. Whether you're a seasoned survivor or new to the genre, Dying Light is sure to keep you hooked.
