_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light could so nearly have been a great game, but it suffers from an addiction to lazy design. The core gameplay encourages you to learn how to respond to your environment in new ways, using combat and parkour skills in combination with carefully selected and crafted equipment. Key missions repeatedly strip away your equipment, or nerf your character in a way that is not justified by the plot or gameworld. You then have to grind your way slowly and painfully through these sections, gritting your teeth and setting your sights on getting back to the enjoyable parts of the game. What finally killed it for me was a sequence in the final mission that I had to repeat 40+ times, which begins with you having to kill a child zombie. Each time. 40 times over. It was harrowing and there is NO excuse for depicting this in a game.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: I have played this game on PS4 for 20+ hours prior to this review. Dying Light is a breath of fresh air, in this landfill of games that copy one another. If you enjoyed the likes of Dead Island, or similar games, you will be right at home with this game, but be wary, there are major differences between the two. The parkour mechanics are very reminiscent of EA's 2008 cult classic, Mirror's Edge. The combat system can be clunky at times, and it is easy to get flustered especially in the early hours of the game; Upgrading weapons is highly recomended if you plan to survive in the late game. Now to talk about what makes this game special. The day and night cycle. During the day, the zombies are your adverage infected that you have seen before, plus a few special infected types.Night time is when things get interesting. A new, fast, and very powerful infected type come out during the dark. Best bet is to always have flares and firecrackers.In conclusion, this game does have a few bugs, but they aren't substantial enough to cause a drop in score. Final verdict: 9/10.   It has been a while since a game has exceeded my expectations on launch day.

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed the Dead Island games so I figured Dying Light would be a sure fit but I was so far from being right. The combat isn’t bad but it feels like it is more tedious than Dead Island and it also feels like it is abnormally hard. In Dead Island I died plenty of times but I always felt like I had a chance at success but in Dying Light if I am facing more than 2-3 enemies then I just run as I usually end up dying. The tougher enemies are just a chore as well. I pretty much had to engage at a distance with every range weapon I could muster and about 5-7 minutes later I may have won. Once again I just decided to run when I could. Getting access to guns made things easier but I saved those for human enemies. Blade weapons felt far more useless than in Dead Island as they were far less likely to sever limbs. The kick function seems to be weaker than in Dead Island as well with much less of a chance to knock enemies onto the ground. They are now able to be kicked onto spikes though and kicking them into objects made of wood will damage the object and be fun to watch. The parkour aspect of the game is interesting and opens a lot of new options but I felt like the game was clumsy more often than not. It felt like more luck then skill when I would be climbing up a tower and would connect with the pipe I was trying to jump to and grab onto. The lock pick mechanic was well done, it felt very similar to Oblivion but that is a compliment. Graphically the game was a mixed bag. The clothes; faces; water; sun; fire; and rain were all top notch. The hair; beards; clouds; and zombie gore were all sub par. The story seemed interesting enough but my dislike for the game play kept me from seeing it through. One annoying event was every time the game would load the main character would scream “holy sh*t !”. This would happen even if I would load into a safe zone. It was funny the first few times but after 18 hours of several loads it lost it’s charm fast. The game would also bring up a menu to buy DLC every time I would get to the main menu which was tacky and during game play it kept spamming me with messages to join community events which broke any immersion the game had at that point.  The night parts to the game made it almost into a stealth game at that point and I dislike stealth. The volatiles aren’t fun to fight, especially with hordes of normal zombies around. More and more missions were taking place at night which was sapping what little enjoyment I was getting. The humour in the game was good in characters such as Tolga and Fatin and the side quests were mostly enjoyable. There were a good variety of weapons and the crafting process was simple and effective. I thought there was a good use of environmental weapons such as fuel that you could spark with firecrackers. 	I played Dying Light on Linux. It has had a myriad of issues since day one of the Linux version being released. Mainly the game hasn’t always launched properly when using Mesa drivers. Over the years I have tried the game on several distros and hardware configs but always with issues including this most recent play through. Every time what I have had to do to solve the launch issues has been different. I have had to do everything from set launch options to use a different version of OpenGL; replacing newer libraries with older versions to this most recent time of having to set the game to use the native Steam run time but there has always been something. The game crashed on me twice during to game play. There are several small glitches such as watches going through arms; being able to climb THROUGH a balcony; hands going THROUGH  shelf when grabbing items; as well as taking damage from enemies hitting me through a wall. Load times took 30 seconds every time I initially loaded the game which is pretty long even for AAA games given my hardware. There is no manual save options, just auto save after certain events. My Logitech F310 game pad worked without issue except for the game not allowing me to customize controls for it. I ended up using my keyboard/mouse for that reason among the more precise movement. There are 7 graphics options to go with Vsync; and toggles for ambient occlusion and AA. There is an FOV slider as well but it doesn’t give any numbers so you have to fiddle with it to get the FOV you want. Alt-Tab worked just fine. You can’t change the difficulty option once you’ve started the game. You can skip most cut scenes but not pause them. The game ran pretty smoothly this time, my frame rate was usually 90-100 with a few drops and peaks. The game was not playable with a 60+ FPS on my lower hardware such as the RX 580; or RX 480 even though the recommended GPU on Linux is an R9 290.Input Used: Keyboard/MouseDisk Space Used: 32.82GBVRAM Usage: 2149-3027 MBCPU Usage: 23-59 %RAM Usage: 5.4-6.7 GBGraphics Options Used: Everything on High. AO; AA and Chromatic Aberration on. Motion blur and film grain off.Frame Rate: 72-144 FPS	I really wanted to like Dying Light but ran out of reasons to pretend I was still having fun. One could argue my issues with the game play are subjective but from a technical standpoint the game is a mess and has been for a while. I have sunk a total of 19 hours into the game and feel that is enough time to know I won’t enjoy it any further. The game retails for $49.99 CAD and while there is a lot of content for that price the quality of that content leaves too much to be desired.My Score: 6/10My System:AMD Ryzen 5 2600X | 16GB DDR4-3000 CL15 | MSI RX 5700 XT Gaming X 8GB | Mesa 20.1.3 | Samsung 970 Evo Plus 500GB | Manjaro 20.0.3 | Mate 1.24 | Kernel 5.7.9-1-MANJARO

_childDocuments_.review: Having survived a nuke by hiding in a refrigerator, John parachutes back to earth only to find those dang zombies up to no good again! Johns voice may sound a bit different, ( a kiwi hit his throat while flying through the air) but he still knows how to kick some ass. In Dead Island, you played a pansy who tripped on shoelaces and could barely step over a brick; but not John! Now Sinamoi can show you his running and climbing skills as well as tackling anything that gets in his way.Even his mighty skills are put to the test however; common zombies tend to group up more (instead of 5 or so, you can get groups of 10 or even 20.) and the specials can present more of a threat. John also has the choice of going out at night to get bonus expierence and loot.You can customize your Sinamoi adventures in a more varied way than in Dead Island. There are three different skill trees that level independantly; this gives the player more Sinamoi action and less time theory crafting!For those who liked Dead Island but thought it was a bit too buggy and not enough Sinamoi, then I would definitely suggest this game (though maybe at a sale.) For those that didn't like it, then there isn't enough change to have you bother with it.

Many complain that the story is full of cliches, but what game has no cliches? There is also a very deep customization system that has something for everyone. You have:-Outfits-An impressive range of customizable weapons-Vehicle customization-Player development-Deep crafting systemAfter the release of The Following DLC, the experience was made so much better as a plethora of, well... everything was added. The Following was a crowd pleaser of a DLC that brought cars, more enemies, guns, swords, clubs, knives, outfits, quests and an insanely large map.This is without a doubt the best game I have ever played and is certainly worth a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Coming close to the release of Dying Light 2, I decided to replay the whole game, with all DLCs, aiming for 100%.I had to stop at %90. Dying Light is an amazingly fun, arcade-y open world for the most part, however, the game design surrounding the core gameplay is majorly flawed. Most games that lack level creativity, enemy balancing, and robust mechanics will increase the amount of enemies that you come across or make them super spongy to compensate for the lack of an interesting encounter.Dying Light is replete with this issue, especially in the later half. "Special" enemies like the L4D tank-rip-off are nigh unkillable with melee weapons, and are super easily dispatched through ranged weapons. You would think that this is intended by the devs, however, most encounters will also crowd you with runners, since you can just sit outside the aggro range and keep pumping shot after shot into the tank's head, only for it do nothing.Zombies are not balanced, and this is the worst part of the whole game. Basic zombies will sometimes get one-shot by your ♥♥♥♥♥♥, non-modified weapons, but sometimes they will endure 15-20 hits against your kitted-out sword with flame AND electricity modifiers IF you don't run out of stamina before. Basic zombies will also shrug off your attacks, actually coming closer to grabbing distance while you are trying to hammer them down."Runners", or special parkour zombies are the worst thing to be included in this game in this state. They are supposed to have recently turned, thus keeping their motor control intact. They can run, climb (to absurd extents), and relentlessly chase you down throughout idiotically long distances. Their dodge abilities, and the humans' for that matter, are straight-up unfair; they will dodge 6-7 consecutive attacks to flurry you with 3 jabs, and if there are more than 1? They both will flurry you, stacking damage so quickly that you can neither fight, escape, or heal.Overall, the enemies of this game are highly unbalanced. All tiers of enemies have stupidly high amounts of health, any non-basic enemy can dodge you to hell and back, your weapons generally feel void of girth and weight, and the only compensating factors are skills like the stealth takedown or the head stomp. These are also useless in group settings, which the game frequently forces you into without alternatives for different builds.By the way, the set pieces of this game are infuriating. You hoard your weapons throughout the game, keeping the best and most rare ones for difficult encounters? Well nearly all bosses will deprive you of your inventory in some ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ manner, giving you a basic weapon. This is artificial difficulty, aimed to compensate for the shortcomings of level and enemy design. There is actually no point to me looting or building weapons, if I can only use them throughout free roam and not in missions. Imagine an MMO doing the same thing.To sum up, Dying Light is a good game in free roam. When you are out with friends, drop-kicking zombies off the roof or running away from the knock-off predators at night are some of the most fun I had. However, the story-plot design and enemy balancing made me hate parts of the story, pushing me to just get the game over with. Bugs are existent but not game-breaking in my case.

_childDocuments_.review: Heads up, game fans! It's time to review the new zombie apocalypse game that so many people are playing and talking about: Dying Light. I've had a taste, and I want more, but will you? Read along and hopefully find out. I'm not going to tell you everything, and I'm trying to avoid any serious spoilers, but I will give you just a taste so that you can judge for yourself. Please keep in mind that this review is current as of the date of publication, but I have no idea what features may change, improve or get nerfed after this point. I am not including in this review aspects of the DLC, but I may review that later. Or not.If I had to give just a brief idea of what this game is like, take a little bit of Fallout 3, just the tiniest taste of Crysis, a dash of Skyrim, a sprinkling of Far Cry 2, a little more FC2, toss in some inspiration from L4D2, and then top it all off with some Mirror's Edge, and you might get an idea of what this game is like. Maybe. Also throw in some optional asymmetrical fps with some rather unfortunate choices on the part of the developer to get even closer to the full experience. You start off parachuting into a situation in a quarantined city somewhere seemingly in the Middle East. You have to find that one guy that your organization needs you to find; you know the one. You get infected, and you need medicine. That's how you're compromised, and that's how you begin working your way into the local sitch. You make yourself at home and begin doing odd jobs to improve your standing, gather intel, and make reports back to the peeps in charge in the rear. You can probably guess where this is going, so that's all I'm going to say about the back story. If you don't get medicine regularly, you get sicker and could possibly turn. So far it hasn't affected my gameplay as much as the same mechanic that was used in Far Cry 2, but I haven't gone very far in the main story line either. In the relatively brief time I've played this game, I've only had convulsions the one time. You spend all your time climbing, running, jumping, ducking, dodging, and generally trying to outmaneuver, overpower, or out-think your opponents. You constantly have to think about where you're going next and how. The game has freedom, but with it also comes a terrible price. Sometimes you choose wrong, and it hurts so bad when you do. Conversely, when you choose well, and it works, it feels really good, too.You get three skill trees, each with a different focus--one for gear, one for agility, and one for power. The things you do build your skills in the respective area, and if you want to get better at something, try doing it repeatedly or things closely related to it. Craft items and you'll be able to craft more items. Take on zombies one on one in melee, and you'll get better at it. Try extreme stunts, and you'll become a world-class parkour... -er (actually, the proper term is "traceur" if you didn't know... I didn't). Your opponents are a blend of frightening zeds with some specials mixed in who will not always stand out at a distance the way they will in L4D2. Once you know what you're looking for they will be all too apparent in most cases, but there is a slight learning curve involved. Yes, the big guy with the insane hammer is easily spotted in any crowd, but the little screechy ones not so much. There is a level of unpredictability to every encounter. One guy goes down with a single blow, another saps your weapon of its remaining strength. Be wary of that. Weapons can only be repaired a few times. Also, if you upgrade a basic weapon, apparently you cannot then use it as part of crafting an advanced weapon. And when you can no longer repair a weapon, don't forget to dismantle it for the spare bits.You can find a lot of loot everywhere you turn, but most of it (especially the better stuff) is behind locks that you can pick. If you've played Skyrim, you shouldn't have any issues doing this. I've heard Thief players should also know what's what. If you've played neither of those, watch a video before playing your first time to get a sense of how it's done. If somebody says you need tons of picks everytime you go looting, don't listen to them. You only need tons of picks to practice with until you're good. Skyrim players who've already cut their teeth on these locks should have no issue even with the toughest locks in this game.During the day it's a parkour rpg with FPS elements, but at night, if you're out, it's totally stealth. At least until you know what you're doing. Bold precision pays off in this game. The developers have relied on player fear to a good extent, but how can you know the limits until you have tested them. Climb to the top of that communications tower. You never know what you might find. Plan your exit strategy and then hit that guy with the tank on his back. After he explodes, if you survive the swarm that will descend upon you, you will come out the other side stronger for it. Stronger or more agile, or both. Make your painful mistakes early on, because if you wait until later, you will feel the pain as you lose tons more points as a higher level character dies for the mistake of not being bold early on. Clear all your safe zones straight out from the prologue before you complete any quests. I did it my first day after the prologue, with the exception of the last one which was too well defended.  I think the daylight cycle might be tied to story progression and perhaps even side quests. Also, another pro-tip, if you're stuck, consider leaving the game and coming back because there are still glitches and bugs to be worked out. Can't reach a certain post from the roof of that one building? Maybe you're not supposed to. Trust me and see.If you want to know what awaits you in the dark, play the Be a Zombie mode. You get to play as the Hunter, which feels like a cross between a vampire or werewolf and Venom. You get to play as one, that is, if you can find a match where people don't automatically leave as soon as you join. In my experience almost every one of the matches where I was actually able to stay and play, the human players knew what to do. If you decide to play this mode, expect some frustrations as a result, from the learning curve or from the game mechanics or from the matchmaking system. Being the Hunter is fun, but frustrating--until you get better at it. And you will get better if you stick with it. I feel the system is kind of limiting and almost misleading, because you aren't playing as any of the other zombies, only the Hunter.One of the poor choices I feel the developer has made is seen in the multiplayer part of the game. You have extremely limited options in controlling online game play, and the game doesn't distinguish between sides. Say you go into Be a Zombie mode and open your game to public games online, when you go back into your solo campaign, it's not solo anymore. You have to go back into online settings and set it to solo once more. I wonder if this isn't part of the reason behind the large number of players who quit when a Hunter joins their game. Also, apparently, though I have yet to play with friends on co-op, I can tell you the voice communications in multiplayer are set to be strictly always on or always off. No push-to-talk. Perhaps they will fix this in the next patch. We can hope. Until then, better consider your third party options for game chat. Headphones, people. Wear. Your. Headphones. And play in a quiet area or turn off your mic please, for the love of all that is good and true.There are ugly sores on the backside of this game. The repetition of certain dialogue branches when you walk past certain NPC's is irritating. The feeling that I've played this game before, especially when it feels a lot like those other games I listed at the beginning of this review, is a little disappointing. But where the game shines, it shines. I'm out of characters... See ya next t

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR -• Story: 4/10• Characters: 4/10• Gameplay: 10/10• Quality (glitches and bugs): 8/10• Graphics: 8/10• Sound: 9/10• Music: 7/10• Repetitiveness: 5/10• Replay Value: 5/10• Personal Enjoyment 10/10                                                               Total: 70/100A game that is a real mixture of flaws and strong points. It is a revolutionary "milestone" in the zombie genre and at the same time "just another zombie game".So, let's start with the story. When you put everything together after finishing the main game, it reveals itself as a cliché and forgettable story and you get a déjà vu perhaps from seeing many of the moments, done way too often in other games and movies. One thing it does right though is making you interested in what is about to happen next. If you relax and are not critical about everything as me, you'll have a good time with the story and will enjoy it, it is entertaining but nothing special when you look back at it after finishing the game.Most (not all) characters are very forgettable and you'll often find yourself feeling like you're talking to the same NPC from who knows when before. I don't know how many voice actors they used, but 1/4th of the male NPCs and 1/2 of the female ones sound almost identical. Although I personally grew to like a few of the characters that are mainly connected to the main story, but they still could use a bit more of a buildup and character development. Some die, some get to live and you never hear anything from them again, knowing almost nothing about them from the start to begin with. And now you wonder, what made the game the masterpiece of its genre that it is? The answer is the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ brilliant gameplay and the (imo) perfectly executed horror atmosphere.The parkour is hands down the best one in the first person category (Yes, I prefer it over Mirror's Edge by miles and have backup arguments behind that statement). It's seamless, rather fast but you still remember that you're a human and not some steroid overdosed anime character. It is satisfying and thrilling when combined with the zombie apocalypse theme, the chases and of course the iconic nights that Dying Light is mostly famed for. The first night in this game is an experience comparable to a first kiss, it's something you don't simply forget about and will carry on with you in the distant future as a strong memory, except the night is terrifying and you realize how f-cking much 300 meters are in this game when it is dark and you've forgotten how to turn on your flashlight. The atmosphere of the game nails it down as well. The realistic and creepy sounds, the not so special but really well fitting music, the overall theme of the world and let’s not forget the graphics, which are really good too and hold up really well to the today's AAA standards. It is not so colorful overall, as big chunk of the game takes place in the slums, but it has its colorful parts and of course the gory and creepy places like the tunnels, sewers and some of the bigger buildings. Aside of the horror, there's also coziness found in the safe zones, there’s almost always someone to talk to, you feel the warmth of the place and feel like home, you simply feel a relief. As I said it nails everything in this department of the game perfectly from my perspective. Important mention is also the co-op. Joining a friend is really easy, it's literally clicking a button. There's no catch to it, you simply can play the entire story with a friend, you watch the cut scenes together and hear the dialogue from the same perspective. The only reason I actually give points to replay value is because of the co-op, I can honestly play through it like 5 more times with (a) friend/s without getting bored even a little, there are many additions to playing online, like challenges, competitions and overall really fun goofing. Though, it might break some of the horror atmosphere as you'll get more comfortable when playing and talking with a friend.Another really good aspect of the game is the leveling system. It is divided to 3 categories (a 4th skill tree for car upgrades is added in the DLC The Following), Power, Agility and Survivor. Power is mostly for combat, agility obviously for agility (parkour moves and speed) and survivor for crafting and overall utility. You gain XP for each by doing different tasks, so if you prefer less fighting and more running, you'll get more agility points. Survivor XP is acquired from finishing quests and some challenges. It is overall an easy to use system that does its job well, there are almost no boring skills, some are less useful than others but still fun to play around with.The combat doesn't have much depth to it but it can be greatly satisfying at times, for example when slicing off a zombie's head or its whole body in half. Human enemies can be tough damage sponges at higher difficulties. The game starts off rather hard as of killing goes, but later on you become op when you acquire some of the guns (which might break immersion for some, but hey, higher difficulties are always an option), but they can attract zombies when shot. Bows on the other hand are balanced, they don’t deal a lot of damage unless you hit your enemy in the head and are hard to shoot accurately on mid and long distances. Overall in the end it’s a solid game based on gameplay but falls off with its story based on if you’re looking at it critically and noticing the lack of character development and the bunch of awkwardly acted moments, though the story is still interesting and draws you into wanting to know what happens next. For the sake of delivering the critical truth in this review I rate the game 70/100, but based on my own experience with the game, I can say it is one of my favorite games of all time, one of the best games in the zombie genre and the best one in the open world department. I strongly recommend it even on full price, though the game often goes on sale so you can look out for that too. (PS, buy the Enhanced Edition, you wont regret it)Good night, and good luck.

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR: enhanced Mirror's Edge+enhanced Dead Island=Dying Light=Awesome.A fresh take on an old concept is always nice. With a genre that is crowded with mediocre attempts at making money, Dying Light comes in and kicks (or should I say, jump kicks) every other zombie game's ass so hard that is almost unfair.  From the same developers as the good (not great) Dead Island games comes yet another zombie game that focuses on the same idea: loot and melee your way to victory. But this time with a little added feature: parkour! Techland took the amazing gameplay from Mirror's Edge and turned it into a freerunning dream come true, enphasis on "free". You can parkour in pretty much everything in this game, there are no limitations (like there were in Mirror's Edge). Freerunning around town is so fun that you'll forget where you're going or what you're supossed to do to complete the quest, which, by the way, is cliched to the max, but the gameplay is so smooth and rewarding that not even a pretty lame storyline can mess with it.  Think of Dying Light as an enhanced Dead Island meets Mirror's Edge meets Assassin's Creed (the parkour part, not the boring stuff). Plus, you get to kill all kinds of zombies and undead in various creative ways. What's not to love?  Beware though, when the lights go out and the night hits, the real challenge begins. The aptly named "nightmares" come out to play and you are their favorite toy!  All in all, this game is extremely fun to play. The pacing and the abilities that you unlock by progressing are impeccably timed, and the DLC that have been released just add to the enjoyment of an already amazing core game. The Bozak Horde tests your skills in a brutal fight against tough enemies and the clock, but offers a reward that makes it worth the effort. The Parkour Fever challenges offer a really nice challenge for those who want to perfect their freerunning abilities to the max. The Be the Zombie mode adds a nice challenge as a competitive multiplayer mode and a chance for the player to be the nightmare! And the Following expansion pack offers some really nice new alternatives and a story that, while is better than the core game's story, still falls short.  On the negative side are the weak storyline (side quests are better than main quests) and the fact that there is little to do after you've beaten the game, outside of trying the higher difficulty levels (which are pretty hardcore for an average player), or playing in Be the Zombie.  I absolutely recommend this game. It made it to my top 10 list incredibly fast and I've no doubt that the same will happen to anyone who likes parkour and killing zombies.

_childDocuments_.review: Bittersweet isn't enough to justify how much I HATE the way the story was written.Man, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Rias, I should've cut his head off clean not The Story and I HATE IT, it leaves Frustration, and that amount can vary depending on the Player, but for me personally, A LOT of Frustration, I can't explain why I hate the way the Story is written without mentioning Spoilers..  UGH 4/10 Story.The Game is okay as a whole (♥♥♥♥ the story), it's about ~19 Hours of Gameplay, if you make your Game's Lobby Public or Friends-only, you can have other Players joining your Game to help you out or enable Raids to allow Night Hunters to show up and make your Night more fun, in all honesty, I REALLY like and enjoy Games that allow other Players to Raid your Game and mess around with how you're supposed to Play, they've nailed this Raid system, the way they've designed Night Hunter VS Runner is super fun to Play. Play your cards right and you'll kick the Night Hunter's ass, fail.. and you'll get pounced and the next thing you know is that you exploded. Counter it with UV Flashlights, destroy it's nests, avoid it's spits, and above all, do not get Pounced. You've got 10 Lives, infinite Combat Stamina, 5 Nests to destroy, and last but not least: One Night Hunter that can instantly kill you if you're not aware of it at all times.The Start of the Game could've been handled way better, it was a mess, things went too rapidly for my liking and I was left with a lot of confusion more than anything it was awful.The Gameplay mechanics are unique and quite interesting to me, being able to freely parkour, climb buildings, slide, dodge, vault over enemies and obstacles like a monkey basically, is just a whole new feeling to me and I like it, movement is awesome and well designed in this Game, it took me a while to understand how the mechanics work, but when I got the grip of it, I never let go of the feeling of wanting to go up and over every car, lamp post, train car, rooftop, a Zombie's head, everything, it was just infinite dopamine anywhere I looked. You also have a Skill tree system, blueprints, Inventory and information about Quests that you can do, a mini map and a Map in general, so it's well organized.It's also worth mentioning that there's a Day/Night cycle, so you can watch the sunset and you can watch the sunrise, but beware of when the sun does set, that's when you'd better get to a safe spot or don't, as XP is DOUBLED during the Night, and Skill Points that are gained during the Night are also doubled, so sometimes it's better off not sleeping to do something that you'd otherwise not want to do, for a good reason like getting more XP or doubling the Skill points that you could get, but beware that there's lots of dangerous creatures that roam the streets during the Night, and they do not like UV Light.Speaking of Zombies, there's a lot of them, and they come in various shapes and sizes, and so do your Weapons!There are several types of Zombies that you can encounter, but again, cannot mention any because of Spoilers so just know that you'll meet more than your average walky flesh eaty Zombie.As for the Weapons.. (my favorite part about this Game besides parkour), there's so many, Gas Pipes, Nailed Planks, Hammers, Sledgehammers, Hatchets, Sickles, Axes, Knives, Machetes, Batons, Katanas, Ninja Stars, throwing Knives, throwing Axes, Crossbows, Rifles, Pistols, Shotguns, Grenades, Electric Grenades, Molotvs, Shields, etc.. the list just goes on and on, you have everything you need to bash a Zombie's head in or hack and slash some Bandit's Head off.The Difficulty and oh my gawd how did play testers find the difficulties fine??? I played on NORMAL and I SUFFERED, the Enemies are Health Sponges and certain Enemies were WAY too tanky than they needed to be. I do not recommend you Play it on anything past Normal, it's way too hard, trust me.The Level Design though.. that surprised me, the moment you fire up the Game it tells you that none of the places nor Characters were real and if anything was, it was a pure coincidence, meaning they didn't want to include any real areas nor people. Huh. Well, I'm sure they've had their reasons, the Level Design was pretty solid and believable, despite none of it being a real place. And the Graphics were good, it came out in 2015, technology back then was alright so the Graphics are good and the Sun is nice, it brightens up my world for me to parkour around in nicely, seeing sunrises and sunsets are cool to just sit and look at, they get the job done.Despite settings being on 100%, the Main Menu track wasn't loud, neither was the Music in-game, except for those high moments where the Player's getting chased and all that, even then the Volume's just right, and the Sounds of crushing a Zombie's skull or slicing the head off are just so satisfying to hear, and the slow motion that happens when the Player's doing it makes it perfect, although, like I said, Enemies are such Health Sponges.. There was also the problem of Mouse Sensitivity that took me about 3 minutes to find the right amount because it's a slider without a Number.. UI disappoints me sometimes in Games..The Soundtrack is quite good, in most cases it fits Dying Light very well, I like the chase Music, Main Menu track's okay, Parkour Music tracks are decent.The Achievements are many, there's +70 Achievements to unlock, some are story Achievements that just kinda unlock, some you gotta actually do certain things to unlock them so yeah, there's plenty of Achievements to Achieve.7.5/10, Good Night, Good Luck.

_childDocuments_.review: I initially played Dying Light upon release on PS4. A bit later, after The Following came out and was received so well, I decided to pick up the enhanced edition on PC to play with a separate co-op partner. Although we've yet to complete the main game this go around, I can tell you that it is absolutely as good as I remember it being.First off, the traversal. Dying Light, to me, feels just as good or better than Mirror's Edge, which is often seen as sort of the gold standard for first-person platforming. You'll spend a lot of time in Dying Light planning routes from rooftop to rooftop to avoid the mass of zombies below. Due to the absence of fast-travel, you end up learning the city and the quickest routes from point A to point B. You will "know" Harran better than comparable cities in open world games.The game also has a comprehensive and compelling crafting system. You're constantly looting the city, now mostly abandoned by governmental authorities, putting together tougher melee weapons, medkits, and even explosives.I also appreciate the way that the game does skill trees. You level up survivor skills through quests, agility skills through traversal, and power skills through combat (a la Elder Scrolls). Many skills in Dying Light completely change aspects of the game, rather than providing passive buffs (though there is some of this as well). Camouflage and Vault change how you move through the city, and Grappling Hook revolutionizes it. Stomp and DIY grenades change the way you approach combat and your relative effectiveness.The wrapping of the game is done well also - the soundtrack is fantastic (especially the menu music), and the story balances the mundane with the heart-wrenching in a way that Rockstar still hasn't figured out how to do. The voice acting is great, especially Crane's handler in the GRE. Although it's unfortunate that my mind has these associations, the setting of the game (in what seems like the Middle East) adds to the feeling of danger. During my lifetime, war has been a constant in the Middle East and I often hear of atrocities at the hands of religious extremists and the like.The game also nails the co-op. It's seamless, drop-in/drop-out, and makes a lot of smart decisions. If a quest requires you to collect items, five herbs for instance, the game will accept two from one player and three from the other. Additionally, if one character reaches a quest location before another, the game will prompt the other player to hold down a button and fast travel to their partner. In this way, the game keeps moving at a brisk clip.The only issue I had with the game is actually with the main protagonist, Kyle Crane. He has a very dismissive way of speaking to most of the characters that he interacts with, and I very much disagreed with a decision that he makes during a cutscene towards the beginning of the game .I'm always looking forward to my next play-session with Dying Light, and there's absolutely a reason that it was one of my top three 2015 games.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a big step-up from Dead Island. The side quests aren't all generic fetch quests and the main story is actually engaging. The combat system has been reworked and the game has you feeling helpless at the start which is a very good thing. I was positively surprised by how open the map is. The only invisible walls are the boundaries of the map and story-related locations. The parkour system is also fun and pretty intuitive to use. The use of skilltrees prevents the game from going stale and adds some really big changes/additions to how you play the game.If you liked Dead Island and/or Mirror's Edge, get it.The main story quest will net you around 10h of gameplay. I have done all of the sidequests and I'm currently sitting at around 35h. The game is fun enough that I might replay it in co-op though.There have been some CPU and RAM management issues but they have all been fixed with the 1.40 Patch resulting in a dramatic increase in framerate. Props to Techland.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my UPDATED review on Dying Light as of 2021 with over 236 hours of game time.We will be talking about why and what you should buy, first of all, I will say that this game is great and is worth getting either way. But consider reading my review before you buy.Dying Light is from the creators of one of the most popular xbox 360 zombie games ever, "Dead Island". It has plenty of weapons, consumables, throwables, missions, quests, secrets, etc. Moving onto the pros and cons.Pros:Lots of storyLots of things to doLots of weaponsLots of side quests and daily missionsDying Light Companion App for RewardsHas multiple fun DLC's.Cons:No Anti-CheatMany hackersA decent amount of glitches-------------------------------------DLC 1: Cuisine Cargo is a DLC which includes "Quarantine Zones" these are areas that have exclusive loot and more!DLC 2: Bozak Horde is a great DLC where you can run through and do time based trials and kill zombies for rewards to use in the real game!DLC 3: The Following is a story expansion onto the main game and is a must-have and it has vehicles!DLC 4: Hellraid is the newest major DLC in the Dying light game, it is based on a cancelled game that was being made before dying light. It is about a medieval castle full of elemental skeletons and zombies, with over 10 new weapons and plenty of missions!Free DLC: Be The Zombie is about you, being the zombie, invading other players at night. It is very fun you get to unlock skills and you can do a bunch of cool things, only down side is there is a lot of hackers, and I mean A LOT.Summary: This will wrap up my review for the game "Dying Light" by Techland. My review is a 89/100. I highly recommend buying this game. Whether it is off-sale or on-sale.Thank you for reading my review and I hope you found it helpful!

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't get how this game is so highly rated (read: overrated) by so many people. I guess everyone is totally okay with gameplay where you either have to constantly run or constantly shoot because the zombies JUST. DON'T. STOP. COMING.No matter where you go, they always spawn just out of your sight to hunt you down relentlessly. I guess they all have some really high-tech radar and x-ray vision too, because funnily enough, they know where you're at no matter how far away you are and no matter how well you're hidden. The only place you're safe are the Safe Zones.Why are are the Safe Zones safe? I don't know because structurally speaking, they look just like everywhere else on that map except there's  more fencing. There's still places where the zombies SHOULD be able to get in, but the devs decided that there should just be magic forcefields that make the zombies finally decide to leave you the hell alone when you get into these Safe Zones.You know something's wrong with the game when even though they tell you not to make too much noise, shooting your guns at all the zombies coming after you seems to be the only way to get any of these stupid objectives done. Especially since melee weapons are much less effective and break too often. Luckily, guns don't ever break for some reason, and they regain all your ammo when you die, even more reasons to stick to your guns. Still, even after you manage to kill every zombie coming at you for a while, you can only catch literally a few seconds' break.But that's better than the other option: running away and hoping they'll lose you. Spoilers, they don't. You could be hidden in a damn bank vault and they'd still know you're there! What's more, you have to worry about your running stamina, which isn't shown on a meter like the combat stamina is. In a game with magic safe zones and zombies that harass you to no end, is unlimited sprint too much to ask? Oh hey, you can throw fireworks bundles to distract them though! Or at least, it distracts MOST of them. Not enough for you to stand still and arm one of those traps you were asked to arm, though.I didn't even play long enough to find out what nights are like, and there's no way in hell I'm sticking around for those if DAYTIME is this bad. How in the hell so many people find this game playable, let alone enjoyable, I don't know. I guess you just have to keep dying until you catch a lucky break for every single objective of every single mission. It's a wonder so many people found this enjoyable.Maybe I'd like it if the parkour wasn't so clunky too. If it was more like Mirror's Edge parkour, where it's actually fun and flows reasonably well. Instead, you'll find yourself experiencing stupid moments like having to slowly pull yourself up a ledge that's only 4 feet off the ground while you're getting spanked in the ass by those damn zombies!I won't be buying Dying Light 2 unless things change, that's for damn sure. Like the name says, there's too much dying involved. So I refunded this one. What a waste of almost 2 hours.

_childDocuments_.review: If you enjoy running errands from point A to point B a zillion times, then this game is for you. The parkour takes a little getting used to, but after a while, it seems to be just a fancy gimmick to add to the chore of getting from one point to another as you do ENDLESS fetch quests. This game is a mish mash of Far Cry 3, Dead Island, Mirror's Edge, Last of Us, and maybe some Assassin's Creed. Basically, it's a game filled with recycled ideas. I thought the Dead Space Trilogy was bad when it came to a protagonist that always said: "Sure! I'll do it! No, don't help me, I'll do it ALL BY MYSELF!" This game is labeled as "open world" yet it is so linear when it comes to its quests that anyone you encounter in this game has a predictable request for you. You almost feel like saying: "Lemme take a wild guess. You want me to get something amidst this whole city filled with dangerous zombies. And on top of all that, practically armed with a melee weapon that will last me 7 to 8 hits before it falls apart, and on top of all that, i have to survive. Great. I'll get right to it!" The game is fun and after a while, it gets rather redundant after the 6th and 7th hour. It's too bad there's no dialogue option in this game which allows you to say: "Why don't you go get that thing you need yourself!?" - A decent game overall, but wow, fetch quest, rinse, repeat, fetch quest, rinse, repeat, ad infinitum.

_childDocuments_.review: This game taught me many things about real life:Episode 1: I was locked out of my house last week, and I realized I had a paper clip and pocket knife in my car. I figured, "this will be a cinch" I started to pick my lock: click, click. Sh%#. Paper clip broke. Yep, lock is ruined. *Hops wall, grabs key from under mat, and enters through back door* Wife: "Why the hell did you come in from the back?" Me: "I locked myself out" Wife: "Why didn't you just knock?" Me: "I've been trying to learn parkour." *parkour into back room* Pursuit evaded.Episode 2: I have to take the trash out, but it's getting dark outside. Wife: "the trash is still overflowing" Me: "True, but its almost dark. I don't think I can risk it." Wife: "Risk what?" Me: *looks at couch; chooses to wait until morning* I wake up. Wife: "now that it's light out, how about that trash?" Me: "HELL YEAH. DOING IT!" *Grabs machete out of closet; ties up trash bag* Wife: "what the hell is with the sword?" Me: *parkour into front yard* Trash delivered. I feel stronger. Episode 3: It's night time. Wierd noise on roof. Feeling unusually brave, I grab my new teddy bear (aka my machete) from under my pillow. Using my parkour skills I climb up my aluminum rain gutter. Rain gutter buckles under my weight and I crash to the ground. Startled, the cat on my roof scampers away. Mission accomplished. Episode 4: My wife and I make dinner. I am cutting vegetables with a Hardened Beef Cleaver. I go to the bedroom and grab my Machete. I lay the Machete and Beef Cleaver on the counter. Me: "Which of these is better?" Wife: "For what? Why have you been acting so wierd lately?" Me: "Agreed." *Chops carrots with machete* 11/10 Would take this course again in the Spring.The Following taught me even more about real life: Episode 5: Been training for awhile now with Teddy. Let’s just say we eat a lot of squirrel for dinner. Came across a Javelina unexpectedly while trying to fix our stupid water pump (living in SW USA) and realized my skills weren’t exactly “legendary.” Teddy failed. I failed. I ran. Wife understood, but I could see the disappointment in her eyes. So, naturally, I think, “F-THIS” *Jumps through kitchen window; hoofs it to the tool shed* *Sets Teddy on the workbench, grabs tazer, duct tapes tazer to Teddy, wraps metal wiring from tazer around blade, activate tazer, Teddy lights up like a F’in Christmas tree*YEAH! *Heads back to water pump* Javelina is there, staring me in the GD face like a drunken frat kid. “OH, I’LL COME AT YOU BRO” *Charges Javelina, Teddy sparks like a damn firework*Wake up 3 days later in the hospital with a giant gash in my side. I see the blurry outline of my wife, “Did I get him?” Wife: “No, he got away; the cops took your weapon.” I pass out again. Episode 6: After some time at the hospital, I come home, wrap some alcoholic gauze around my arm like thirty times, and I’m back to full strength.  Wife: “Did you hurt your arm too?” *Looks at gauzed up hand* Me: “I need more firepower.” *Looks at wife* Me: “Honey, do you trust me?” Wife: “No! I absolutely do not trust your judgment right now. You just nearly died!” Me: “Exactly! We need wheels.” *Grabs car keys, limps out the door* Me: “I’m gonna need more gauze.” Episode 7:  I return home with PigF$&%er, my sweet new buggy. I honk the horn in the driveway. I stand brandishing my recovered Teddy in all his glory and as my wife opens the door, I activate taze mode. Teddy lights up like a damn sword with a tazer attached to it. Wife: *closes door* I realize she’ll only love me again if I kill this swine. *Buggy screeches out into the night* Experience Doubled.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished this game in 61 hours. I completed pretty much all side quests and challenges. I found 41 zombie trophies and a few flags without using the internet to cheat. There really isn't any game out here like this one, that's for sure! This game is a lot of fun between how you get around by jumping from building to building and slashing away at enemies with numerous types of weapons. The way the zombies explode and ooze blood is great. I love the gore. It's just one big world for you to explore with plenty of stuff to do along the way. There are some open world zombies games out there, but this one is for sure unique in It's own way. It does have It's set backs though. After plugging in about 15-20 hours It was starting to get pretty repetitive. You run around exploring the same areas with chests that re-lock themselves and containers that re-fill to give you the same stuff. You kill enemies with the same ole moves. It got a little boring for me, but not enough for a bad review. The story wasn't too bad either, and some people didn't like the ending, but I really didn't mind It; every game you have to fight a big boss at the end, so It's nice to have something different.Pros:- Intense cinematics - Good graphics - Parkour- Save anywhere/anytime- Nice cut scene monologues - Music- Skill treeCons:- Zombies clip through walls- Reappearing items/chests- Zombies find you even when you're quite - Combat can be very buggy- Money and tons of items are useless- Loading saves brings you to different locations

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action-horror games around, everyone likes it for a reason.The star of the show is time as a mechanic, and how the game uses time (or, rather, the lack of it) to make everything feel tense or threatening.  There is a literal ticking clock in the corner of your screen, counting down to either the arrival of safety that you just have to hold out and stay safe for (dawn) or to the point where all of the monsters are coming out to play and your current task needs to be thrown aside in favor of bolting home like a scared, very acrobatic rabbit (dusk).  Combat is tense not because it's hard (though sometimes it can be) but because every moment you're stuck in combat is a moment your weapon is ticking down towards zero durability and the sounds you're making are pulling in more (potentially _infinitely_ more) enemies.  Stealth is tense because it's slow and you only have so much time, forcing you to take chances.  Movement abilities often balance risk against time saved.  Even something as simple as opening a box is rendered more dramatic because you know how much time it takes to open a box, and during that animation time the enemies who could notice you don't stop patrolling and won't hesitate to jump you just because you're looting.This is a game where a skill tree has a "fast hands" skill that makes you pick things up marginally faster, and you WILL spend a precious, limited skill point on it instead of considering it a vague quality of life convenience because anything saving time is an actual tactical concern.Honorable mention to the traversal/parkour system itself, not because there's anything in there that any other parkour game doesn't have, but only because this is the only game I've ever played where the parkour actually does exactly what the controller inputs tell it to do consistently.  If you die to a parkour misfire in this game, it's because you made a bad call and the game dutifully executed your dumb idea: not one single time did I ever have a piece of terrain that looked like a ledge not actually be grabbable, or the game arbitrarily decide to chain a move a second after I input the command for some indecipherable reason, or to perform an action properly but in a different direction or on a different terrain element than what I was pointing at, or to just outright do the wrong move because of some contextual whatever or redundant controls.  This is one of the things I feel like I shouldn't NEED to praise a platforming game for, but even the game's own sequel didn't pull off this fairly basic requirement, so...Also the day/night cycle is kind of fun, it's obviously a cheap way to provide a lower-difficulty setting for the quests without losing the feeling of tension, but it's effective enough that even knowing what they were doing... well, I still felt tension in the later parts of the day and would race the clock.  Night itself is unforgiving enough that I found myself actually memorizing routes along the roof-tops and where enemies tended to spawn, since being spotted by a volatile without already having an escape route in your head was inevitable death even in the late-game when I had the maximum power level and skills going on.My one negative is that the sequences involving human enemies with no zombies were incredibly boring, because the dynamic is basically just that of a generic shooter with none of the interesting "half enemy, half hostile environmental condition" thing involved in dealing with the zeds going on.  Just cutting every single one of those levels entirely and accepting that the game would be shorter as a result would have been better-- they're not bad but dedicated shooter games do it better.Really well-designed game, highly recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Dying Light is a great game. It's one of the best open world zombie games that's built on this fantastic parkour system and a big variety of weapons to slaughter the undead. It's fun, intense, and even a bit scary at times (especially if you're a new player).There's many positives to this game. The two vast open areas of the Slums and Old Town are detailed and has a lot of exploration in them. It's fun to run around these areas with the fantastic parkour system. The parkour in this game is easy to pick up, and it makes this game unique compared to other open world zombie games. There's 4 player co-op so you can bring a bunch of your buddies along with you. There's plenty of main missions and side missions, and some agility and power challanges to participate in, and they're all playable in co-op! There's many weapons to choose from with many blueprints and upgrades to make them more badass. There's a leveling system where you gain XP for doing just about anything, so you always have a sense of progression, and your character always feels like he's getting stronger. Speaking of your character, there's a decent amount of outfits to decorate him with. There's a dynamic day and night cycle, and nighttime makes this game much more intense compared to day. Sometimes, I prefer to play at nighttime. The graphics are great, supporting NVIDIA HBAO+ and Depth of Field, and it looks great. I can pull off a consistant 60 FPS on my 960 4GB on High settings but with no View Distance. Lastly, there's official mod support. Yes, OFFICIAL. There's a Steam workshop to download a bunch of custom maps from, and you can go on the  to find a decent amount of mods to install, although it's a bit weird how you install mods. It took me awhile to figure it out. You can even run mods on co-op if your buddies have the same exact mods you have, and mods don't disable achievements (like some other AAA games).The characters are pretty weak. Rais feels like a bad knockoff of 's Vaas, and everyone else is pretty lame. You never care that much about your teammates. Me and my pal would skip all the cutscenes pretty quickly because they can sometimes be pretty boring. The story on paper isn't actually that bad, but it's executed poorly through the weak characters. I have one minor negative with the parkour system, and its how you can't wall run. I think the parkour would've been pretty fluid if you could wall run. Nighttime is WAY too short. I think I heard it's like 7 minutes long compared to around 60 minutes in the daytime. It's ridiculous, as the nighttime is awesome! I run a  that tweaks a bunch of things, including making nighttime the same amount of time as daytime, so it's not that big of a deal for me, although it was on Xbox One.Dying Light is one of my favorite games of all time, next to Skyrim. It stands strong along with other great AAA titles because of its gameplay and parkour, and it's a worthy title to have in your library.Should you buy it? I'll eventually write a review on the Following DLC. I'll link that here when I do!

_childDocuments_.review: Dying light is the most fun i've had with a classic "zombie game"!It takes some features from dead island, for those who played it, but it's a lot better.It's best features are the parkour system, the day night cycle and of course the zombies!At the start of the game you feel really powerless even to the weakest zombie (biters), weapons don't do much and they break a lot requiring metal parts to repair them; running from zombies or volatiles in the night is almost pointless because they are faster and have more stamina than you.All of this changes while progressing the game, unlocking more abilities and crafting more powerful weapons, even guns come into play, all of this will make you a perfect zombie slayer machine!The story is not very interesting, it follows most of the cliches that zombies stories have, but it's not very important because there is the expansion pack "The Following" that will really deliver!The Following adds a new map with new gameplay mechanics and it's a direct continuation of the story.The biggest thing is the implementation of a drivable buggy, this changes the focus from the parkour in the city to driving the buggy through farms in the countryside.The sidequests are interesting and well made, every different from the other, some involving characters from the main campaign.The story is where the expansion really shines, it is at first misterious and then, when you think you know everything, it gets you whit an incredible ending! ---------------------------------------- ----------------------------------------

_childDocuments_.review: Imagine Dead Island that's actually a well-made video game without most of the annoying/stupid stuff. Featuring a great parkour system and a meaningful day/night cycle. And Arabs (or whatever imaginary people they are)... for some reason.Looks very polished and is a technically impressive good looker overall with the aesthetic that sets just the right mood (acceptable texture artworks; great lightning effects and shadows: the nights are dark and full of terrors; one of the best drawing distances ever coupled with the possibility of cranking level of detail to insane levels even on the furthest objects, which require very powerful machine). The game feels well-paced in terms of story and activities and balanced in every gameplay aspect. Skill progression is mostly enjoyable and worthwhile along with the functional crafting system.It is true, however, that the game is an ultimate hodgepodge of gameplay mechanics burrowed from dozens of predecessors with not that many new ideas, but the end result is worth it.Also the game fully supports Dualshock 4 (Playstation 4 controller) with the correct button prompts without any additional software requirements (no need to emulate Xbox controller, for instance).

_childDocuments_.review: I'm so conflicted on whether or not I want to recommend this game. On one hand, it has great visuals, awesome parkouring, and believable (albeit short-lived) atmosphere; but on the other hand, it has quite a lot of flaws. I'll focus on said flaws for my review.Chunks of poor level designDying Light is a game that emphasizes running and pathfinding during certain sequences, scripted or otherwise. Often times I find myself perfectly able to navigate the landscape... but some instances, like the mission where you arm C4 inside a half-built skyscraper, have downright confusing level design. I've died plenty of times and lost uncountable numbers of survivor points due to simply getting lost. And not only that, but randomly placed explosives that enemies (somehow) set off has killed me more than what's acceptable. Having a "wtf killed me?" moment is not enjoyable. There are also several instances where an exploding undead appears out of nowhere (scripted or otherwise) and insta-kills you because you did what the game taught you to do: attack the zombie. Gimmicks like this don't help the game.Goons are unfair and poorly designedThe idea to kill Goons (the undead with rebars) is to use ranged options. But if that doesn't work, then what? Guns attract more undead, so you can't use that. You'll simply have to get in close to finish them off. But there's a big problem; a Goon's range is far longer than your dodge skill. This makes for an intensely frustrating encounter where using the dodge function is effectively useless. You just have to take the hit (since you can't dodge far enough), get knocked flat, wait to get up, rinse and repeat. You also have to use power attacks, or you'll be repeating this process for a long, long time. Overall the game limiting you to one effective method of killing Goons is a discredit.Demolishers are unfair and poorly designedMuch like Goons, Demolishers have a ridiculously unfair attack range, though they don't have the AoE ground pound like Goons do, so using dodge is somewhat viable. Instead, they can swing and charge on a dime, and each attack will knock you flat and take a lot of HP. You'll also be forced to use guns - or power attacks only - to finish them off. Their ranged attack is also ridiculously hard to dodge up close (since it locks on to you), so you'll be S.O.L. when trying to melee.Main villain sucksRais is uninspired and spews the same tired tropes of bad guys in modern media. The whole "I am chaos" spiel has gotten pretty old by now. Nothing new or surprising about him, and killing him at the end of the game wasn't impressive at all.Cliche, predictable plotYou figure with zombie genres being so interesting and mainstream that people would come up with something fresh. The only twist that surprised me was Jade dying. The rest was mostly ho-hum. Not much to write home about.Mini map sucksGoes hand in hand with the bad level design. I've found several points in the game where HUD markers don't correctly account for what floor they're on, or even show the proper way to an objective. The mini map also doesn't help me when I'm desperately trying to figure out a way into a particular house because all the windows and doors are locked up, which usually means I have to figure out some obscure, gimmicky parkour-based way to get inside (this has happened far too much).Moves like Grapple suckI never got the hang of grapple, because a lot of key combos the game requires don't translate well on a keyboard. There are also skills I never bothered using, like the ones for 2-handed weapons, since they don't seem all that feasible in a fast-paced game like Dying Light (2-handers are simply just too slow and cumbersome).Zombie drops don't scale and are essentially useless mid-to-late-gameIt doesn't seem that the items zombies give are useful at all after a certain point. The amount of money or items you get from them simply don't scale with the player. After a while its just not feasible to loot corpses anymore."Swarm" events happen randomly for no reasonSpecifically when you cause an explosion or fire a gun too much - you'll hear infected screams in the distance, and a few runners will spawn and attack you. In Old Town, these events would happen again and again and again, even when I wasn't doing anything. I've also seen swarm events happen after simply getting an elemental effect on a regular undead, who will scream and writhe and then cause a swarm. Makes little sense to me, and adds a ton of frustration to the game since I was already being quiet.Artificial difficultySlowly but surely, Dying Light lumps more and more zombies onto the player, especially in Old Town. This combined with the bad Demolisher and Goon designs, infected and humans that can magically dodge your swings, and the random swarms makes for gameplay that's far more artificially difficult than it should be.No fast travelThe parkour is fun and the levels aren't so big that its entirely a chore to navigate, but fast traveling from safe house to safe house would have been a good addition, especially since some safe houses are extremely inconvenient to get back to (i.e. the bridge safe house, the tower safe house in Old Town, etc).Ruins its own immersionDying Light started out with a fantastic atmosphere. The sound design, before getting used to all the ques, was fantastic. It eventually wore off due to a combination of factors like limited sound effects for zombies (especially the Toad, which makes the same damn sound every time), a few whacky, immersion-breaking characters, and overuse of gore and dead body piles. I mean seriously... there are points in the game with Dante's Inferno levels of gore in the form of mountains of corpses, and it made me think several times "how did these bodies even get here? Are there even that many people in Harran?". The devs abused this aspect of horror and it broke the immersion for me.Uninspired special infected designsRunners. Undead that explodes. Undead that charges and throws rocks. Undead that spits acid. Undead that screams. I basically just described the special infected cast of Left 4 Dead 2. None of the undead besides the Volatiles were unique or interesting. The only special infected that have alternate appearances are Volatiles, runners, and Goons. The rest have the exact same appearance throughout the entire game. Additionally, the Volatiles are barely the stars of the show, despite being the most interesting and intimidating. They only appear twice in scripted main quest events (to my knowledge) and in the unscripted main map at night.Terrible final boss "fight"I've almost come to expect triple-A FPS titles to have poor, uninspired final bosses. Dying Light, unfortunately, was not an exception. Leading up to the final encounter was a frantic chase, where you run from undead and then eventually Volatiles; but at the top of the tower, all that waited was a quicktime button pressing event, which was not satisfying in the slightest. Was very disappointed with how dull it was.Overall I'm on the fence (pun not intended) about Dying Light. Its definitely not worth a full $60 purchase, so I'm glad I got it on sale. My review is neutral overall, but just for the frustrations the game put me through, I have to set it as not recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Decided to change my review to a more serious one, because why not.Pros:-The resilience of the zombies: I distinctly remember setting a zombie on fire with a fire weapon. It was still walking around so I decided to cut it's head off. (It was technically dead by this point) It was still walking around after that so I decided to cut it in half. The torso was still on fire and walking around so I decided to cut the legs off. It wiggled around for a few more seconds and then finally died. So much for putting things out of their misery.-The side quests: They can be very fun to play, but they actually have some good  twists in their own story, and they sometimes foreshadow what is going to happen next in the main story quests-The atmosphere: Harran feels very much like a dead city. Flaming cars, occasional screams, hordes of zombies everywhere, and even dead silence-Mods: One of the few AAA games I can think of that actively encourages modding of the game. There's already a lot of custom maps for the game in the Steam Workshop, including a couple that parallel Techland's work in terms of quality, and there's the possibility for other kinds of mods further down the line (ex. new weapons, blueprints)-Night time: Techland isn't pissing around when they say "Good night, good luck". The game changes from a zombie slasher to full-on horror once the lights go out. Predators called Volatiles come out only at night, they are nearly impossible to kill, are very fast, and can often kill you with a single hit.-Hard mode: Some people complain that the game becomes too easy towards the ending half, this fixes that. "Survivor sense" is limited to seeing Volatiles through walls at night, normal zombies become much more damaging (killing in just 2-3 hits), medikits do not regen your health instantly, and certain items become harder to find. This mode addresses most of the issues I list in the "contriversial" section-Game looks pretty good graphically: Very good textures, amazing foliage, and nicely detailed weapons. Apparently the lighting is based on physics, I don't know what that means but it looks beautiful-Pack mentality of the zombies: If you kill one zombie, there will probably be two or three more that come around a corner and try to eat you-Uniquely balanced firearms: Sure, you can use a pistol to kill that zombie, but there will be a group of Virals (fast zombies) that will come for you almost immediately-Surprisingly tactical melee combat especially when facing other survivors: The enemy survivors are very, very smart. They can block your hits, dodge them, kick you, dodge your kicks, throw knives at you, and knock the knives you throw at them out of the air (but you can do all of that, too). This requires you to time your attacks well since they can beat you to death very easily if you only try to attack-The physics in the game are amazing: For some reason Techland decided to add actual weight and momentum to your player. This means you can jump from the roof of a van, land on a zombie, and you will crush it under your own weight, leaving it's head vulnerable so you can beat it in with a gas pipe. Also, you can dropkick a zombie into a car, and if it hits headfirst, it will die.-The map design: Techland has designed certain subtle paths for parkour you can take, which flow very naturallyControversial (aka some people hate it, some like it):-The way the weapons hit enemies: It seems like Techland decided to treat the weapon in your hand as an actual physical object with weight and force. This means that all weapons in the game feel REALLY, REALLY GOOD. A blunt weapon will likely stop in it's place when it hits an enemy, which feels realistic and pretty brutal when you're trying to bash a zombie's head in when it's laying on the ground. If the game triggers slow motion, you can sweep the camera around, and hit other zombies in that sweep without touching the mouse button. However, this has a bad side effect - if you have a weak weapon like a pipe and there's an enemy standing to the right of an enemy you want to hit, the weapon will likely bounce off of the enemy on the right and will not touch the enemy you want to hit, which can be very frustrating.-The parkour system: People have praised the parkour system as the best of the new generation so far. However, I feel like there are some problems with it very similar to the problems that most parkour systems have, like things you should be able to grab onto, but can't. Trying to grab onto something below you is a HUGE pain in the ass, usually it ends up with you flying off, then mashing the spacebar trying to grab on again. Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't. Usually you don't end up where you wanted to go. However, in just about every other movement, it feels pretty natural and flows nicely.-The damage the weapons do towards the end of the game: You start the game off with a pipe for a weapon. It does 24 damage. You will likely end the game with a katana/machete/longsword/shotgun. These things do upwards of 1000 damage. The enemies' health do not scale to the weapons you have, so, you can just slice through hundreds of infected with no problem, and can even kill Volatiles with just a few hits. However, this doesn't compromise the way the weapons feel. Somehow, the weapons still stay incredibly satisfying throughout the entire game.-The plot: The antagonist is pretty cliche, he's someone from the Middle East who is terrorizing the people of Harran during the infection. The guy you play is pretty cliche as well, he's an American who just happens to be really good at parkour as well as killing zombies, even though he's never done either of those things before. However, outside the rivalry, the plot does take some interesting twists and turns, questioning the morality of the "greater good" and whether or not Rais (the antagonist) is really your enemy.Cons:-The motion blur is overused: It looks like Techland decided to put motion blur on literally everything. This makes it very hard to appreciate the graphical beauty of the game with it on.-Some enemies are almost impossible to kill without taking damage: There's a strong enemy with a giant piece of rebar in the game. His main attack is hitting the rebar on the ground, which creates a shockwave that takes away most of your health. 30% of the way through the game, the size of that shockwave doubles. Before, you could easily dodge out of the way, now, it is close to impossible.-The controls for throwing/grappling an enemy are very awkward: Alt & W/A/S/D at the same time. I'll let you try that one.

_childDocuments_.review: "Dying Light" is a captivating and immersive gaming experience that excels in various aspects, making it a standout title in the survival horror genre. With its realistic and expansive game world, the developers have created a dynamic and multifaceted environment that adds a layer of authenticity to the overall gaming experience.One of the game's standout features is its intricate and compelling storyline, which manages to evoke a range of emotions. The narrative is rich with twists and turns, keeping players engaged and invested in the characters and their fates. The emotional depth adds a meaningful dimension to the gameplay, making "Dying Light" more than just a typical zombie survival game.Moreover, the game boasts a high replay value, ensuring that players will find themselves coming back for more. The diverse gameplay elements, coupled with the open-world exploration, contribute to an experience that remains fresh and exciting with each playthrough. The combination of challenging missions, dynamic day-night cycles, and the constant threat of zombies creates an adrenaline-pumping adventure that players can enjoy time and again.The cooperative multiplayer aspect enhances the enjoyment factor, especially when playing with close friends. The game's design encourages teamwork and strategic planning, elevating the overall fun factor. The thrill of surviving together in a perilous world amplifies the sense of camaraderie and accomplishment.Despite its many strengths, "Dying Light" is not without areas for improvement. The game could benefit from additional updates, particularly in terms of expanding the map. Players eagerly anticipate new locations and areas to explore, hoping for more variety in the landscape and fresh challenges. Additional maps and regions would undoubtedly enhance the longevity of the game and provide players with new and exciting experiences.In conclusion, "Dying Light" is a stellar gaming experience that successfully combines a realistic game world, an engaging storyline, and high replay value. Its cooperative multiplayer feature further enhances the overall enjoyment, making it an excellent choice for those seeking a thrilling and immersive survival horror adventure. While the game is already outstanding, the potential for future updates to expand the map and introduce new areas would undoubtedly elevate it to even greater heights.

_childDocuments_.review: Oh My GodI can't believe I didnt get this game for four years. I thought meh its probably another zombie game, and the gameplays on YouTube weren't that convincing. But I saw it was on sale and decided to get it and Oh My God :O Gameplays on Youtube dont even begin to show how amazing this game feels. It really makes you feel like you are partcoring over zombies, drop kicking them, or jumping 40 feet to the ground. And when you get chased by zombies it gives you an accurate viseral gut feeling, the same as if you are getting chased by zombies in real life. This is the game that you would get if you mixed in Assassins creed (but in first person) + Left For Dead (but the realistic version) + For added measure you give it community made maps + online campaign/co-op (you can make it private/friends only) + You can craft a buttload of items. Oh and did I mention that you can bash the ever living crap out of zombies with meele weapons.Controls:The controls are super twitchy and responsive, so you definitly dont feel like you are waiting for animations to finish in order to execute another action. Which is extremely frustraiting if you have ever experienced it. Luckily this game achieves the complete opposite of that.Graphics:The graphics are really nice and it really gets you immersed into the game, sometimes I forget about everything and I feel like I am Crane (player's character). Especially when you are jumping roof to roof and then drop kicking a zombie down on the street.Performance:The performance is really good. With a a GTX 1080, Ryzen 5 2600 @ 3.7Ghz, 16gb ddr4 3000Mhz Im getting 150-230fps with high settings and every other graphics setting turned on. Btw the cut scenes are a little janky but surpissingly that makes it actually quite funny and enjoyable. Unlike the super realistic games that feel too serious and boring sometimes.In Short, this game is a cluster F***k of awesomeness, and might be the best use of your money on a game.   (TIP): You can farm a load of money in game by picking up the rifles of the enemies during the prison mission. Pick them up and then run back to the player stash and stuff that bag with 20 rifles (each can be sold for $892). Then die and start again, you get to keep all the rifles even if you were carrying it.
