_childDocuments_.review: Like all of Kyle Thompson's games, Crypt Custodian is excellent. I like how each game explores a new mechanic. The top down view is a nice departure from the majority of the genre while still allowing for interesting movement mechanics and gameplay. There are a ton of different biomes to explore. Each has its own enemies, which follow a few architypes but expand on them (so for instance, you'll find a basic archer in the first biome, an archer who shoots a boomerang later one, an archer who fires multiple shots, etc.). There are also curses to find which give you specific situations to endure until you've killed enough enemies,  in exchange for a power up. Speaking of which, there are a huge number of upgrades to found (similar to charms in other games), but you also find and can buy slots for those upgrades. There's no limit to how many slots you can have so you can really build out your character in any way you want. I really enjoyed using upgrades that my own blue projectiles to the mess of bullets being fired in some areas and boss fights. As well, there are special attacks to be found (you can activate one of them at a time, and they charge up pretty fast), and jukebox discs which allow you to play songs in the inn.The world is quite expansive, and traversing it is pretty good. You can fast travel to any previously visited save point straight off the bat. You can add a number of your own markers, as well as buy markers for missed secrets or the next area to head to; otherwise the game doesn't handhold you and you can pretty quickly decide to go in whatever direction you'd like. The map itself is good but not ideal with a controller - there are two zoom levels but scrolling the zoomed out one doesn't scroll the zoomed in one which makes the map a bit hard to navigate, especially if there's a specific warp point you want to go to across the map. You also can only fast travel using the zoomed in version, as far as I was able to determine. I'd also say that some of the power ups you get do not have nearly enough places to use them (or require you to find a room to use them far away from your goal), but they're also used in surprising ways.Took me about 15 hours to get to 100% completion in game. There's also a boss rush mode that I played around a bit in but isn't really my cup of tea (in order to get S+ you need to kill bosses quickly and without taking any damage).It is amazing to me that at the time of writing this, 25% of players have gotten the 100% completion achievement. This really goes to show how amazing this game is. It's a very comfortable experience and you can tell that QoL was really considered. If you like metroidvanias, and especially if you like Kyle's other games, you're definitely going to love this one. Can't wait for the next one!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: After trying the demo for Crypt Custodian at the beginning of the year, it was very much one of my most looked forward to games.The premise is both melancholic, and adorable, there's so much personality in the world and characters, sound track is a banger, and the gameplay, while simplistic, is very fluid and engaging.Highly recommend to all, while it only took me 20 hours to 100% the game, it was a fantastic time and im ready to start a new save.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It’s wild that such a well rounded game was developed by a single person. Kyle Thompson has knocked this cozy Metroidvania out of the park and if you played and enjoyed Islets then this should be an easy purchase. I’m thankful for the ease with which I could see unexplored paths simply by zooming out the map to the grid view. While not overly challenging from a combat or platforming perspective I still died plenty of times and appreciated that I never had to retread too much of the map for my next attempt.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games that, in my opinion, have a cozy feeling, no matter where you go. The graphics are pretty, the music is relaxing, and the story is simple, yet cute.Gameplay-wise, I liked all the mechanics implemented, tailored to simplicity yet still fun. As a metroidvania fan, this game did not disappoint. Highly recomended to those who like cute looking games and metoidvanias alike!!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Very nice game overall that I would definitely recommend. To me it’s not as much metroidvania as it is Tunic/Zelda. Levels blend together in my head just a little, and I think part of the reason for that is the overhead view, but also because the music isn’t super memorable to me. The tracks are fine but forgettable. I would have loved to have seen Eric Thompson really get creative and make some deep, unique tracks and just go crazy with this ost. My favorite Eric Thompson track is still “Grass Valley” from Islets. Eric if you ever read this, sorry to critique your work as a layman but next time, strive to give each song character and make it give off a “feel” for the level it’s on. Draw inspiration from some of the best game soundtracks ever. Don’t phone it in.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It brought me a lot of joy and it put a big smile on my face for most of my playthrough. In some ways similar to authors' previous work - Islets - and in some aspects it's quite different. Differences feel like a breath of fresh air and I could see the progress the authors made between their games. Still, I love that the characteristic sense of humour is still going strong in this one. Definitely worth buying and checking out.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Cute and creative game. Various fun challenges while weaving your way around the map. Cool boss battles, music, and some chuckles.  Nothing is very difficult in the main game, but that's okay and feels like it was designed that way.Two minor things I think could use some slight improvement are the broom throw aiming being a bit tighter and a couple of the time trials felt a tad janky/annoying.If you like the genre and there is a slight sale, I'd recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game really is a joy to play. There’s so many thoughtful quality of life mechanics that make traversing the world less of a chore. The abilities are unique and lead to some interesting puzzles and level design. The story is charming and the character’s personalities and backstories are told well. Definitely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic metroidvania. Huge map, some novel power-ups, few skill needed puzzles; simply had loads of of fun and wanted to clear the map. Bosses? Not easy at all. Story? WHY DO I WANT TO CRY BASED ON 3 PHOTOS OF AN ANIMAL CHARACTER?! Cute, cute, cute. And challenging in just the right amount. It was a delight to be a player, was sad to end it. Chapeu bas.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is incredible right off the bat my favorite thing about it is the sound design it invokes joyful exploration and that feeling of getting lost in the woods. This game reminds of a few of my other favorite indie games them being NiTW for the sound design truly incredible work, Hollow Knight for the smooth gameplay and exploration even to a lesser extent Metroid this being of that genre. I love the art style of this game it is fun to see the different enviroments and enemies. The combat is fluid and fun with a fairly short learning curve I will say. I highly reccomend this game to anyone looking for a relaxing and comforting adventure.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Really chill but full of action metroidvania.The musics, art style and gamefeel make the experience as an all really enjoyable and makes me want to test my performance on the speedrun aspect of it.I'm not a story guy but the characters and their simple quite deep stories makes it smooth and easy to understand.Overall this a great game for the chill players, the players in search of challenges and for the speedrunners.Great job guys :)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is classic comfort gaming to me. The mechanics and combat are engaging without being too complex. The characters and world building are likewise just present enough to add some surprising pathos to some later moments without ever hurting the pacing. An excellent game for a palate cleanse and just good clean metroidvania-ing. Equally loved Islets and really happy to see the creator(s) still going and achieving these gems.Editing this to add that having the circle around the player and so many of the enemies and attacks also clearly marked on the horizontal plane really helped with the combat for me, and made the game significantly more enjoyable for me than other games with similar perspectives.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A good game of reasonable length and great bosses. Overall the balance is very well done and manageable even for first timers of the genre, its a chill metroidvania. Low stakes and easy to medium difficulty makes it an easygoing and enjoyable experience. The exploration did start to get repetitive towards the end for me though, it might just be a tad too large for how easy and samey it gets.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypto Custodian is a fantastic blend of Zelda-like and Metroidvania gameplay, all presented in a captivating top-down style. It’s one of those games that you can easily pick up and lose yourself in for hours. The combat is dynamic and exciting, while the platforming elements are incredibly engaging, making every moment feel rewarding.As a game developer myself, I find Crypto Custodian to be a great example of what indie games can achieve. It’s inspiring to see a game like this come to life, reminding me—and hopefully others—that the key to success is persistence. Don’t stop at just one game; keep making more and better games. With each release, you’ll improve, just like Crypto Custodian has done in its own right. Keep creating, and the results will speak for themselves!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I have been on a metroidvania games tour since I bought my handheld PC, I love those types of games, now I am not your young player but I fancy a little challenge, what I noticed is that some of them became a bit too challenging for me and wanted something fun and gives you a nice balanced sense of achievement and boy did this game deliver.The wonderful dynamics and that satisfying jump and smash feeling breaking all those elements just make you enjoy every part of this game. The Art is just wonderful, for me those photo snippets stories are so clever and fun/sad depending on which side you view it.This is definitely a game worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I was first introduced to Kyle Thompson's games with Islets, two years ago, and immediately I fell in love with his charming style, innovative ideas, and thrilling gameplay. Well, I'm pleased to say Kyle has absolutely outdone himself with Crypt Custodian.Crypt Custodian presents you with a vast labyrinth to explore, full of monsters, puzzles, and secrets - your typical metroidvania fare. But your environment is 3D, with an angled forward-facing camera in place of your standard 2D display. This alone is an intriguing departure from the norm. It also presents a strong, emotional story told in bits and pieces of a number of different ghosts in the afterlife. It was hard not to cry at the ending cutscene tbhAs for the actual gameplay, the platforming is sharp, and the rooms do a great job of keeping the pressure on without overwhelming you. Jumps are quite generous, helping hone you into the edge of a platform if you're close enough. I found this highly useful when some movements of mine weren't perfectly cardinal (I used analog stick) without being overbearing or too much (you absolutely can still fall like an idiot :) but when  you do, it's 100% your fault imo).The combat was rich and highly entertaining, with some great upgrade ideas that strike a balance between rewarding your progress with improvements but keeping your character from ever becoming OP. Unless there's some OP postgame stuff I haven't gotten to yet (I'm writing this after any%ing the game rn, but I still have some stuff to do for hundo). Some combat moves even upgrade to help you with the platforming later, like Speaking of combat, boss fights in particular were superb all around. One of my (extremely few) criticisms of Islets was that I found that, even on hard mode, the bosses were all pretty easy (except for one mid-game boss, which made me feel like the difficulty curve could have been massaged there). In this game, the bosses are all satisfyingly tough on hard mode, without being a completely evil rng-fest. Kyle had a lot of different ideas for them as well, which I really appreciated. My favorite was probably That said, I will say, I found that for a few of the bosses, a pretty easy strategy to deal with bullet-hell style attacks was to  it's not a bad thing at all, but for the number of bosses I was able to do it to, it made me feel like a bit more tweaking to these kinds of attacks could be useful. It's a super minor nitpick, however. On the other end of the range, I did find the  After 4 or 5 deaths, I managed to beat it by developing a strategy that seemed a bit like a cheese -  But these are very minor nitpicks.The only other nitpicks I think I have are that, for one, I personally didn't find the challenges all that intriguing; there were only a few distinct types of "curses," repeated a number of times throughout the land, and these represent most of the remainder of what I have to do in the game (as far as I currently know) simply because I'm not that interested in them. And I guess the other one is that I felt like the  But that's really all I would say on the side of nitpicks.I very much look forward to 100%ing this game eventually, but with my current schedule and the other games I want to play, it may be a hot minute. In the meantime, however, I can absolutely recommend this to any metroidvania fans out there. It took me a little under 10 in-game hours to any%, and I spent a lot of that time exploring outside of what I needed to for just any%, _and_ I was on hard mode, so hypothetically it could take you faster if you wanted to rush it a little. And on the other hand, if you want to fully complete it, from what I've heard, I definitely have a few more hours to go. In other words, this is definitely worth it imo if you're looking for an excellent metroidvania but don't have a whole lot to spend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: it's just great, feels great to play and is imaginative and addicting. i prefer more mystery and a darker setting in these kinds of games, which i wish the dev would try his hand at sometime. gameplay wise this is pretty much perfect, so much fun to play. story is cute but not my cup of tea. as i said, wish the dev would work with someone who's good at developing darker stories and settings, that partnership would be great.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ 5/5I previously played "Islets," so I knew what to expect from the start. Everything just fits perfectly here. The art style, the gameplay, the music, and the story all come together seamlessly. The story and dialogue don’t take themselves too seriously and have many humorous moments. The combat system is simple yet incredibly fluid. The boss fights aren’t too difficult, and the skill system allows for different strategies to be used to defeat them. The isometric map style might deter some players, but it works surprisingly well, making navigation smooth and intuitive. The only downside I noticed were some small technical obstacles, like the zoom ratio in the map display, which could be more precise, and the maximum resolution being capped at 1440p. Other than that, I highly recommend it to everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: That was nice. Not spectacular or outstanding, but I had a good time. I saw it described as a cozy metroidvania and that fits, especially the atmosphere. In the middle I had my favourite metroidvania experience, that of "there are so many places to explore and so many places I could go!" I switched to easy mode pretty soon and that suited me well.It took me a little under 11 hours to get to the credits at 72% completion.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DRGood MetroidvaniaThe good: - You can sequence break if you know how to use the game mechanics; - The game gives you just enough ability points for you to feel strong but if you want more you can grind and buy as many ability points as you want; - If you are having a bad time finding the secrets you can use the currency of the game to buy markers stuff you missed; - The curses are the harder stuff on the game and they are optional, most of the time they will give you ability points and if you want to you can straight up buy those; - Distinct art style; - Good enough enemy diversity, not only in designs but in moveset as well; - Each area not only have a specific theme but they also have unique mechanics and enemies; - It is strange that I need to mention this, but the day and age requires it, the game is very stable, the only bug I've experienced is the animation of "falling" playing when I barely made across the precipice, so yeah, pretty solid.The "meh": - Although the weapon is part of the character background story and it is solid I missed more weapon options; - The story is kinda shallow, but to their credit you don't usually play metroidvanias for the story.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I have so much fun with this game. It is so polished, looks amazing, the combat feels awesome and the sound design is spot on. I was skeptical first because I was not sure if a combat with a broom will work out but it is so well pulled off. Also, you can change the difficulty in the game at any time. The enemy design is also fantastic. Each enemy has a different attack pattern and the enemies show in different ways how they will attack so you can dodge and avoid. Can only recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing game. Cute and funny characters, lots to do, love the art style and the music. Satisfying combat. Really appreciated the option to add more time for timed challenges (as I can't handle time pressure) and also to add some extra lives if you want/need (as I am just not very skilled :))  Tried the demo after really enjoying Islets (by the same developer) and loved it so paid pretty much full price soon after release - absolutely worth it IMO. It was so good I was kind of sad to complete it!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Good solid game.  Controls smoothly and although the combat isn't revolutionary the movement and actions you have make every encounter relatively fun.  Bosses can pose a real threat though nothing in the game is super punishing.  The story and characters are good, and if you like animals or have pets it might resonate a little more.  The music and sound design is also quite good.  A charming little gem of a game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Ultimatley, Crypt Custodian is a fun and simple metroidvania.The characters are super cute, the world is mostly enjoyable to explore, and the visuals are cartoony and sweet. The combat can get a little repetitive, especially once you find a "build" that suits you. The bosses are unique and well-designed - some even offer a challenge.I liked it, but it won't go in my "hall of fame" so-to-speak. However, considering this is all done by a single person, I have to admit it's really impressive.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is adorable and fun. I liked it for every moment of the 11 hours I played before stopping at credits and 77% completion (as is my normal pattern).It's a little bit like if deaths door was easier and had a more adorable cat protagonist, with a little bit of the sensibility of Chicory in it's storytelling. And some Cat Quest in there in terms of combat feeling. But it's definitely a traditional metroidvania in structure, movement abilities gating locations and a really fun map to connect and unlock and all of that stuff.A great 8/10 game that feels like somebody is just having a great time making games that feel great to play and have cute art without trying to blow the walls offI think this is my favorite genre of game, the "cute and fun and nobody would write a novel about it they'd just play it while smiling but sometimes it's still a little hard" genre. More games like this one!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty great 10+ hours long relaxoidvania. World exploration is getting better and better as you progress in game. Combat, movement, art, sound - I simply can't name a single aspect of the game that would stand out as silky smooth, as each single detail in this game is polished to perfection. The game is very forgiving, meaning you won't be losing progress upon dying. (Nice detail - there are "challenge rooms" in this game and failing them won't even require you to re-enter the room for it to reset). Yet despise relaxed pace some aspects can be really challenging and definitely won't bore you by difficulty being too low. Definitely worth the price and your attention.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I am not one for sweeping generalizations, but if you don’t play this game you are a fool.It’s relaxing, cozy, perfectly balanced for players of average skill, and has a wonderful soundtrack.Controls are superb - tight and responsive, you know exactly where you will land and always have full control on all of your actions.Combat is satisfying - perhaps just a tad too heavy on the bullet dodging mechanic, but always fair and fun.Bosses are a lot of fun, and this is coming from someone who despises boss fights - you always get a checkpoint right before the arena, and the patterns are easy to memorize.Level design is a bit peculiar - there is no verticality! You move up and down, in addition to left and right, but you never have to climb up or down. It’s not inherently a good or a bad thing- just an interesting design choice.Really, can’t recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly the most fun I've had playing a game in a long time. Much appreciation to the developer!Perfect balance of chill / interesting game play, I played on hard difficulty which I felt was just right as the bosses weren't a pushover and required some thought but weren't frustratingly difficult.Took me about 9 hours to finish the game with *most* collectables. Probably around 10 or 11 hours to 100%, haven't had a chance to try out the boss rush mode though.Extremely cute/10. Totally worth the full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: The Thompson brothers have made another brilliant metroidvania, just as good if not better than Islets. This is such a joy to play and explore the beautifully rich world full of superbly crafted characters and environments, with great dialog, amazing music and some interesting quests. Combat is well balanced and I love that the bosses have health bars, so you get a good idea if you're ready for them or might need to swap out your items or upgrade. 10/10 from me!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great game. It ticks almost all of my boxes. I just love little guys who swing their meele weapon and get to explore a beautiful vast interconnected world. I also like how it's pretty chill on the normal difficulty, so I can play after work. But the bossfights were still fun and somewhat challenging. My only unfullfilled desire is that I preferr my metroidvanias more non-linear as it adds replayability for me, and this one was pretty linear up until the last areas. Maybe, that's why the shuffle mode was a bit underwhelming - you can't randomise the abilities or you won't be able to progress, and even upgrade points and cats aren't randomized. And I don't think that randomizing just upgrades and special attacks matters enough to create a different experience.And a separate appreciation message for the developer rather than his game. For a single dev, this is an insanely good work and I love how Kyle is engaged with the community, responding to posts and bug reports on Reddit and just being an active member of the community. I'll definitely look forward to his next works!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is probably my favourite indie game, challenged only by Hollow Knight, and one of my favourite games full stop. The art is gorgeous, the music is charming, the world feels like it goes on forever, the combat is simple yet unbelievably satisfying, the enemy and boss design works flawlessly, with an emphasis on a bullet hell style of combat, the list goes on and on. This is a criminally underrated title, and I would love to see it gain more appreciation in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Story / Writing / MusicI'm going to lump these aspects of the game together, as they are all very well done as standalone design components. Combined, they are even stronger. I enjoyed that the characters and writing were comical and lighthearted against a backdrop that, for any pet owner, goes a little deeper if you want it to. The soundtrack was an easy 11/10.Art DesignAgain here, beautiful game. By the time I'd seen every biome, some of the environmental designs did start to blend together a little bit.Combat / PuzzlesI have over 200 games in my STEAM wishlist. I don't have the attention span for every game I play to be a Souls-like endeavor (which has been a trend for some recent Metroidvania games). With that in mind, I liked that this game had what I would call 'mild difficulty' in terms of its overall challenge. I died a few times to a few different bosses before I learned their move sets, but never to the point of extreme frustration. The puzzles and locked areas all worked fairly well with the exception of curses, which I'll touch on below.Technically speaking, I did find combat was somewhat simplistic. Some cool moves related to movement (like leaving a trail of spikes when boomerang dashing) didn't really seem to incorporate fluidly into the combat system (at least for me) due to the time necessary to charge up the boomerang attack. Most fights boiled down to how fast I could smash X on my controller while dashing out of the way of projectiles. Ultimately, for this game, I did think that felt fine. Still, it left some of the abilities feeling a bit unnecessary.I didn't play boss rush mode. That's not really my thing, so I can't review that at all.Nit-Picks / RecommendationsCurses should disable fast-travel and result in a slight bump in enemy density. It was a little too easy to simply fast-travel back to the easiest area of the map to knock out curse-kills without there being much risk. However, it was also sometimes difficult to find nearby enemies, quickly, to knock out the curse.It wasn't clear what button I was supposed to press to exit certain in-game menus. For example, when purchasing map markers, I'm still not sure what button backs me out of that dialog (without my character performing a jump or a special attack).The game needs a 'Story-Mode' difficulty setting and/or clearer parameters around 'Easy' mode. I bumped the game down to Easy for my seven-year-old and honestly, we couldn't really tell that big of a difference from Normal mode. Getting hit still deducts a single armor node (and there were still projectiles flying in all directions).I'd highly recommend this game to pretty much anyone. At worst, it might come across as slightly too easy and/or repetitive for gamers with highly upgraded gaming chairs.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: What a delightful game! Crypt Custodian is an adorable evolution of Kyle Thompson's previous projects (Sheepo and Islets). Like those games, it has a cute art style, typical Metroidvania elements (unlocking new areas by finding abilities, etc.), and a wholesome story (your "sword" is actually a broom, and your goal is to befriend the various quirky characters you meet). But Crypt Custodian has a different perspective, literally, in that it shifts from the typical side-on view of most Metroidvanias to the more top-down RPG-style view from games like the Legend of Zelda or TUNIC.I completed the game 100% in about 11 hours (although I did look online for a hint to a specific late-game puzzle), which is about the same amount of time I spent on Islets but Crypt Custodian feels like the bigger game. I'm perfectly happy with my 11-hour experience, but there's unlockable post-game content for people who want more, including a boss rush mode and a remixed story mode.I've thoroughly enjoyed the game, just as I enjoyed Kyle's previous projects.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this game. A classic metroidvania, doesn't really have unique features or anything, but excels in the core fundamentals of the genre. Gameplay and combat is not hard, but feels smooth overall. The heartwarming story is pieced together nicely. It's not a long game, I 100% my first playthrough in about 12hrs. Still, this is definitely a game that I would recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Perfect on the Deck.I think I like this one more than Islets. It still has the charming graphic style, but this time it's a little bit more difficult. This comes down to low HP and some nice bosses. Still not sold on the music. You may be lost here and there, but you can buy markers in a shop to show you where to go next. A lot of options with the upgrade system, not that much in terms of gameplay, but it's a short ride anyway. Looking forward to the next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute mix of a top down metroidvania with some Zelda influences. Very pretty to look at and all the music are bangers/cozy. Easy to understand combat that is not too difficult, and challenging but fair parkour. It does nothing really new but everything it does is solid. Large expansive map and some post game. Loved all the characters. They were used sparingly and i would have personally liked there was more progression in the interactions, they have a set dialogue for each area they are in and no matter what point you are in the story they same the same things. Encountered no bugs or crashes which is fantastic for such a small team. Please give this a go if you like this style of game, this one is definitely one of the easier ones, but i also played on normal, so Hard mode might be difficult? Dunno i'm not a hardcore gamer, i'm a newbie trying things out. Also works perfectly fine on steam deck. My entire playthrough was played on mine.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED THIS GAME!!!!!! It was a total blast! Normal felt actually normal, good for a semi-casual semi-serious gamer, very balanced. The boss fights were all unique and super satisfying to fight and defeat, and fighting all of the enemies along the way never got old. It was great to explore new areas, always felt nice! I totally recommend this one! 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really excellent little game. From the art direction to the gameplay, everything is cohesively and intuitively designed. It offers exciting moments and a few tricky challenges, as well as an atmosphere that's charming and cute but also offers moments of wistful melancholy, helped by the great artstyle and soundtrack. I'm a fan of the Metroidvania genre, and though in this perspective it also becomes something of a bullet hell game at times, I enjoyed pretty much everything it had to offer. I continuously wanted to keep exploring the areas and pushing through to the next one. I have nothing but praise for all the QOL and anti-frustration features, including ways to not accidentally fall of ledges and to round up any random missed items in the endgame. My only complaint is that remapping a few buttons led to mostly wrong prompts, and that I can't experience more of the creator's vision.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so... First time I make a review of a game but I had to do one for this game.It's a simple metroidvania. Simple in a good way. There a tones of little ideas from upgrades to vania power, through special attacks.The gameplay might not feel new for everyone, but it's really well made and executed!The controls are really simple and straight forward, that makes it easy to handle and master.Difficulty might a tiny bit simple but I think I played in "Normal" difficulty if I remember correctly, and I'm kinda experienced of this kind of games (80+ hours on Hades, finished Hollow Knight true ending and working on The Rogue Prince of Persia gives some training ahahah)The art direction is really cute. Simple again, but works great.Enemies are recognizable, bosses are funny, friends are lovely <3The music works great too! So chill and viby.That makes me connect with the narrative, because the music and how the story is told are kinda chill. All friendly characters (despite Kendra...) they all just seem lovable at worse ahahah.But the story itself sad as hell. I lost my cat 2 years ago, just before he turned 2 y.o.I consider him as my own son and it was really devastating to me.So seeing Pluto's story really resonated with me.You can only be empathic for him and all his friends.Kyle, Eric, a big thank you for this game.That's been a while since a game had such a grip on me, emotionaly.I loved it, it's a gem in all the MV games we can see around there, always so dark... you're showing to everyone that you can make a game with simple mechanics (again that's not an insult, even the contrary, god it's difficult to keep it simple) well realized and in a feel good yet dramatic setting, which are two style that quite opposites themselves most of the time.Thanks again, I can't wait to see your next game (in 2 years? ^^) and before that I'll take a look at the previous ones.Take care and please continue to make games!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A clever sense of charm, wit and whimsey elevate this metroidvania above most others in the genre.The combat and exploration isn't out of this world difficult, leaving breathing room for players to just enjoy the adorable characters and vibrant varied areas the world has to offer. Absolute blast from start to finish.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a cute game where you play as a cat in the afterlife. You meet fun and adorable characters which you can befriend. If you like games where you need to explore a map, this game is for you. The map is quite big, and it is nice that each area has its own theme and enemies. The game is extremely chill (sometimes the bosses are stressful but in the way that they should be), has nice music, and many upgrades for you to collect and choose from!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: wonderfully simple yet somewhat challenging game. very relaxing even when faced with failure. Ever since i found this dev's second game (islets) i started searching for more similar games and then i heard about this game releasing i knew i had to try it it. 10\10 did not disappoint. (will definitely try the first game one day)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem.It's cozy, and I found it to be on the easy side, but that doesn't matter because the fights, the exploration, the puzzles, the collecting, and even the story were incredibly engaging and fun. I'm not huge into metroidvanias, but this was right up my alley. I love that there's so many options to make things easier or more challenging (the optional ability to buy a hint for where to go feels ingenious), and the inclusion of a randomizer mode and boss rush is great. I can't wait to watch the speedrunning scene.A really cute, really fun, refreshing spin on the genre. Well worth my money and my time. Looking forward to checking out Kyle Thompson's other games now, too.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: You should play this game. Crypt Custodian is the third game from Kyle Thompson, and his best work yet, surpassing the already-fantastic Islets which is well loved in the Metroidvania community.With gorgeous design, great combat and platforming, charming and distinct zones, a plethora of enemies, abilities and upgrades, Crypt Custodian is an absolute delight to play from start to 100%. Kyle's sense of charm, humour and wit is found frequently throughout the game, interspersing challenging combat encounters and bosses with bursts of joy when interacting with the characters that inhabit the world. The music is produced by Kyle's brother and perfectly meshes with the game's style, the boss theme in particular really gets you in the right mood for a great fight.If you're comfortable with this kind of game, definitely play it on Hard, it's never excessively challenging so the difficulty bump shouldn't bring you any grief but will let you see the game in its best form.I rarely if ever give games 10/10, but I can think of nothing I'd improve, Kyle's truly made a masterpiece and one he should be incredibly proud of.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I went into Crypt Custodian slightly skeptical of the top-down Metroidvania concept, but it more than delivered. Being able to jump over enemy attacks made the fights more dynamic and rewarding, being able to warp between save points from the get-go is amazing QoL, and it was so very refreshing for the traversal powers to break the mold instead of being the standard set of "double jump, super-dash, and ground-pound."10/10, screw Kendra all my homies hate Kendra
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Another absolute treat from Kyle Thompson.  I've been looking forward to Crypt Custodian since it was announced, and it delivered what I had hoped for and more.  A fun metroidvania romp around an interesting, expansive map; fun, fluid and quick movement mechanics; interesting and motivating collectibles and power-ups.  Combined with a charming art design (familiar if you've played Islets.. and you should!) and an excellent audio track - it's beautiful.  Playing Crypt Custodian, you can immediately tell the developer also enjoys this style of game.  He's put in so many thoughtful and quality of life details like fast travel, clever and satisfying puzzles, and interesting enemies that all teach you something important.  While there are plenty of unique elements to Crypt Custodian, I also appreciated the nods to and influence from other recent giants of the genre, in particular Hollow Knight and the Ori series.  The "Grubfather" nod was especially fun.  :)If you enjoy metroidvanias, you owe it to yourself to play Crypt Custodian.  Worth it at full price!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I put this one up there with the Momodora games, Hyper Light Drifter, Dustforce, and Child of LIght. 10/10 indie game considering it was just one guy that did pretty much the whole thing except the music.My nitpick is that the floating platforms tiled backgrounds gets a smidge samey after a while. I love pretty much everything else about it. Story, music, gameplay, animation, style are all excellent. Especially love the little in-game hint system that makes me feel like I don't have to go looking stuff up online if I get stuck. 👍
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely love this game! I think the special abilities and puzzle portions are really unique and creative. The characters are so cute and the gameplay on normal is challenging yet still has a cozy feel to it. I struggle to play games unless I really enjoy them, and this game did it for me. I'm 15 hours in now and I can't stop playing! 10/10 recommend
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I love every single character in the game, maybe Crouton slightly more <3.The OST is amazing, every single track fits perfectly in the environment of each area. Combat feels nice, I love the variety of enemies + Bosses.Great artstyle, I can't stress enough how much I love it.Great job to Kyle for amazing game with such a cute artstyle and to Eric for amazing soundtrack throughout the entirety of the game
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waking up early to play this game before work for the past week since getting back into the world of Crypt Custodian has been all I can think about!  I would say I am still pretty new to gaming and I have tried to play other popular metroidvania games, but the gameplay in Crypt Custodian feels simple and supportive, but also very detailed and challenging.  Thank You so much for this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Still not done but 17 hours in and around 8 bosses defeated (and i believe there is between 10 and 12, excluding mini bosses and challenges). It is a great metroidvania which is not too challenging but has a nice cat themed aesthetic. I think my worst performance was 10 tries on a boss, but it is usually around 5 until you learn the move set you need to avoid damage.Some very good QoL design in the game including 'edge stickiness' when you dash and a map which zooms out to a simple block version with gaps in the block lines for unexplored sectors.I got lost a couple of times as the map is HUGE and one gate I needed to remember to use an ability which I had not needed a lot up until this point. There is an in game shop to buy a hint (which is a nice touch as it encourages you to keep trying to save that money).The dev of this game really understand good game design, and I look forward to their next game.Overall I am really enjoying it as a relaxing steam deck game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: pretty good its not hollow knight but its the best metraiodvainia ive played in while. most indie games have very obvious game design issues, but the worse one ive found in this game is that the player death animation has a needs a skip button, while being pretty unremarkable but apart from that everything else is good, solid game deserves overwelmingly positive
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A well polished metroidvania with smooth gameplay, fun (and fair) bosses, a good story, and soothing music throughout. More or less finished it in a weekend, and will likely be looking at the developer's older games next given how much I enjoyed this. I would put this on or very very close to the same level as both Ori games, so if you like those, definitely give this one a spin.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is the new game from Kyle Thompson, an Indie dev that's become a staple for me. Similar to Sheepo and Islets (If you've not played these, check them out) Crypt Custodian is a Metroidvania with a charming style and a lighthearted adventure (Albeit being about death). You take on the role of Pluto the cat, tasked with cleaning up the afterlife. Along the way meeting a variety of characters throughout an expansive world. Unlike the devs prior games, this one is 3D and plays more akin to games like Death's Door and Bastion, albeit with a bit more metroidvania elements. You'll be jumping, dodging and swinging around as you progress through the game collecting abilities and making friends along the way. Like Islets, there's a great feel to the overall gameplay, especially as you get more abilities. There could be some minor improvements here and there such as the charge speed of a specific ability but overall it's very polished. The world is intricately designed with varying areas and unique mechanics, enemies and such for each. The game is quite open in terms of pathing as you will typically find areas branching off in different directions. This can lead to shortcuts, upgrade points, skills or collectables. There's a tonne to find and the map is huge with a lot of secrets hidden around too. In terms of visuals and sound design the game is yet again a step above the devs prior work. The soundtrack is decent as are the sfx but the main improvement lay in the visual design of the game. Sheepo to Islets was quite the jump and now Crypt Cartographer which looks fantastic. The devs games always have this great charm to them and this one is no different. The writing also remains on par for the prior games with some great moments of humour and engaging characters. All in all it's another great title from the dev and one well worth checking out if you enjoy action adventure games or metroidvanias (And if you enjoyed this, check out their other games too)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever 100% games. I play them to credits, try and complete as much as I can along the way to credits, and then move on. That wasn't enough for this game, however. I felt compelled to go back and find every memory, skill, disc, everything available until I hit 100% completion. I enjoyed every minute over my 16 hour playtime. Kyle Thompson has become a can't-miss developer and he'll get my money with every title he puts out! Play this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It's a game where you play as a cute cat beating up garbage and garbage monsters while making friends along the way. Nothing bad to say. Fun gameplay, good music, didn't run into any bugs, playing through on normal wasn't too tough or easy. Definitely worth picking up if it looks like something you'd be interested in.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Kyle does it again by releasing another banger of a game!  Played Islets and have had Crypt Custodian on my list ever since.   Played the demo and was a little worried I wouldn't enjoy the top-down style of game, but boy was I wrong. Could hardly put this game down exploring the expansive map!  10/10 recommend you pickup and play through.  Some fun upgrades and a couple of the sections had awesome music.  Thanks for the game Kyle and I certainly look forward to whatever you'll be working on next.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the standout features of "Crypt Custodian" is its richly crafted narrative. The story unfolds gradually, with compelling lore and mysterious characters that draw you deeper into the game’s world. The attention to detail in the storyline makes every discovery feel significant, adding layers of depth to your quest.Additionally, the game’s sound design deserves special mention. The eerie soundscapes and haunting melodies perfectly complement the visual experience, enhancing the overall atmosphere and making the crypts come alive (in more ways than one!).In summary, "Crypt Custodian" is a gem in the world of dungeon exploration games. Its combination of stunning visuals, engaging gameplay, and captivating story makes it a must-play for anyone seeking an adventure that is both thrilling and thought-provoking. Prepare to lose yourself in the depths of the crypt and enjoy every moment of it!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Overall good simple metroidvania 7/10 + art style is cool, looks good+ map is fairly interesting with distinct zones+ no major bugs (only some janky ball physics)+ most bosses are interesting with cool mechanics and phases+ crow metal- music is pretty boring, also some is reused from islets game- last boss and after the boss content is meh (maybe I am spoiled by Tunic)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: a rather quick game, but it's super sweet and fun all the way through, and doesn't stretch out its welcome. you might not know where to go next at times, but i think that's okay, you'll find the way eventually, i got 80% completion in hard difficulty without little to no time spent searching for goodies.my only criticism is performance/optimization, i repeatedly got super slow frames for extended periods (especially in certain environments), without my 4070M ever feeling the need to throw the fans on super sonic. don't know if the problem was integrated graphics being used (i hope that was not the case) anyway, that was definitely annoying.definitely worth the modest price for what it is. a warm thank you to the devs for a great time is in order.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This top-down Hollow Knight had some immense charm with its bittersweet story, satisfying combat, and snappy movement options. With a power behind every new area, you are always incentivised to explore and expand your map.This was an unexpectedly fun title to play and would highly recommend to any platform enjoyer.Also Pluto's massive eyeballs as a kitten? 9.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is terrific. It's not super long (you could probably rush through in less than 10 hours, or take more like 15 to get 100% in game, not including the boss rush achievements). But I definitely feel like I got my money's worth.It's full of great animation, clever writing, and some actual tender dialogue. But the dialogue is sparing, so don't expect a JRPG where you'll be paging through hours of conversations. But through the photos and their captions, I found I actually connected with the characters and sometimes got the feels.I found the platforming to not be too difficult, and the puzzle elements were interesting but infrequent. Overall, I found the combat to be more challenging than these types of games typically are. While not approaching soulslike levels of difficulties, you really do need to do more than just button mash. Even "low level" enemies can kill you if you just try to blindly rush in and kill them (at least until near endgame levels of upgrades). Likewise, the bosses definitely require you to pay attention to their attacks and time your counterattacks.All in all, this is another great game by Kyle Thompson. I very much enjoyed Islets, but this is a step up. I'll certainly be on the lookout for his next game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Very cute little Metroidvania. Not as big as the likes of Hollow Knight, but the map still keeps on expanding hours after you expected it to stop. Beautiful art and banger music combined with maybe  movement and combat system I've ever played. Super snappy and smooth, makes for some very fun boss fights. Luckily this game also has a very engaging boss-rush mode, even if it's not built into the universe like the Pantheons are in HK.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Stellar. Features fluid and fun gameplay, a well designed and interconnected map, a wide variety of upgrades, great progression, stylish graphics, charming characters, a variety of well designed bosses, and a good difficulty curve.As a bonus, some minor sequence breaks and glitches are possible - but only the kind that benefit you and make you feel cool. No jank I encountered ever prevented the game from progressing, the level of polish and robustness in the overall design seems almost off the charts.For downsides, um...A little light on story I suppose, and maybe the music could have been a bit punchier?? It tended a little more ambient and some bolder choices may have been able to further differentiate the areas.Overall 10/10, probably the best game I've played in 2024 so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This is an absolutly wonderful game. It is fun to play and the story makes me kind of cry (in kind of a good way, very good story telling without much tamtam). Do not recommend if you've recently lost your cat (especially if it was black), as it will leave you on the floor as a miserable mess.Love this game
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game! I'm a huge fan of Islets and Sheepo, and couldn't wait for this to come out - so many interesting tweaks and new details that make the gameplay more enjoyable, all while keeping the Islets/Sheepo vibe intact! And as always, the music is amazing! (...thank you for keeping the jump sound the same - I'm also pretty sure there's statues that pay homage to the previous games, tee hee)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I enjoyed this demo and am happy to have purchased the game.  I head a reviewer comment this game wants you to complete it and I 100% agree.  I was able to 100% the game (100% the game/map, not Steam achievements) on my first playthrough on easy mode.  I was able to enjoy the story without feeling so overwhelmed it stopped being fun.With the exception of a few timing/jumping puzzles I never really struggled with the game.  I also wasn't constantly running to YT to figure out what to do.Overall I really enjoyed it and yes, I played on easy but there are harder modes for those who want more of a challenge and even has a 'speed runner' mode that I believe skips cutscenes for you?This was well worth the price and I had a lot of fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great story, music, puzzles, and boss fights. I especially appreciate the boss rush mode to go and relive those cool fights. Nothing not to love here if you enjoy metroidvanias. My only nitpick would be the final bit of story involving a puzzle with some cat statues. It doesn't feel very in line with how the game has handled puzzles up to this point and the presentation doesn't, in my opinion, provide enough of a hint as to what the player must do to solve it. If this were purely completionist content I probably wouldn't care, but since it is the final piece of the story I don't think it should be something quite as complex to solve. TL;DRHighly recommend!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A really good metroidvanian game that tugged my heart strings. I greatly enjoyed playing this game, the puzzling. I also always love when games allow you to change between easy/normal/hard at any time throughout the game because I suck at the speed challenges and I was able to switch to easy just for those, good looking out for accessibility!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great visuals, catchy music, a very sweet story and... surprisingly difficult! I'm not ashamed to admit that I suck at this genre of game. But man, sometimes the barrage of enemies and then having to find my way back to where I was got annoying. I wouldn't consider that a bad thing though. Sometimes you have to get frustrated to get that sweet release of serotonin. I think if this catches your eye then you should play it! Even with the back tracking, this game is pretty forgiving.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: New metroidvania from Kyle Thompson (Sheepo, Islets). As always, it has cute artstyle and characters, very satisfying movement, and a diverse world. While it's longer that the previous games, it still doesn't overstay its welcome, and remains engaging all the way to 100% completion. Highly recommended!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: i'm not too far into this game and honestly haven't found anything to complain about yet, but i have many thoughts and feelings so far. the short version: 10/10, it would thrill me to no end to see this game get more attention because it was clearly made with a lot of love and care and it deserves all the success it gets. the long version:
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: fun cute solid top down metroidvania. Recommend. You play as a ghost cat and make ghost animal friends and help them with their personal problems. The trash mobs are literal trash and you beat them up with a broom. Beautiful interesting environments with new exploration mechanics in each area. Good QoL map features for tracking items and routes to return to later. Post game rewards with options for ferreting out uncollected items on the expansive map. I played on Normal and finished in ~10 hours. If you're experienced in this genre go for Hard. Lots of fun upgrades to discover and experiment with. The NPCs have fun personalities.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game after Islets and Sheepo, now with a new perspective! Lovely level design that loops around itself, Combat that is fun/snappy and fun characters along your adventure! If there are any negatives here then it's the power ups, often they feel more like keys than switching your perspective how to navigate the world. Also really fun bosses, but they are quite a lot more difficult than the rest of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this developer's previous title and was excited to try this game out, too. Similarly to Islets, this game is fairly straightforward, but it still manages to accomplish what it sets out to do. It's a Zelda-like with an emphasis on melee combat and simple puzzles; it's not that hard, but not boring, either. Overall, I think if you like hack 'n slash games and want a casual title in the genre, you should try both this and the developer's last game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Highly recommend this game. If you have played the developers' previous games you can see a real progression of skill and ambition as each title has built on the previous in every way. Lots of special attacks, power ups for customizing play style and responsive gameplay. The art style is very cute with a large cast of critter npc's to befriend. There is even a randomizer and boss rush mode to unlock if that is your cup of tea.If you have a pet that you love dearly, or are a lover of animals in general, be ready to play this game with a box of tissues cause you will be bawling by the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: this is simply a good game. amazing dialogue, good mechanics. the art style is impeccable. thank you kyle thompson i hope you continue to make more games like this. I loved islets and I loved crypt custodian even more. i may have shed a tear at the end too...but i have a real soft spot for kitty cats
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a very charming take on the Metroidvania genre. Everything just works fine: the game world is vast and fun to explore, the platforming sections are tricky but never frustrating, the challenge level is reasonable (I played and completed the game on hard) and the art style is very colourful and pleasant to the eye.I'm definitely looking forward to the Thompsons' next projects. In the meantime, I guess I need to play Islets...
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a amazing! The beautiful art and smooth, responsive gameplay make exploration and combat a joy. While it's on the easier side, it remains enjoyable all the way to the end. The well-paced progression unlocks fresh areas and secrets, and  atmosphere are captivating. It also runs great on Steam Deck, even though it's not marked as verified. A must-play for fans of the genre!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A sweet metroidvania, feels great to play. The 2.5d perspective sets it apart from other metroidvanias I've played in the past, and added a nice dose of platforming challenge along with the combat. Other mechanics are standard; finding new abilities, buffs, and mementos, trying out different combinations, and amassing new platforming abilities as you go. I really enjoyed exploring the map, and being able to warp between checkpoints made it so doubling back never really felt like a chore. I also super appreciate when a game has mechanics to nudge you toward items you missed. the characters and setting are all very cute, the game has a cozy feel. But Kendra is NOT my friend
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Game has very similar art style to Islets, and equally, if not more, charming friends to meet along the way. Soundtrack is pretty nice and mostly chill.You can choose difficulty from the start (which basically just changes attack patterns) and change later if you want, as well as additional options for extra attack damage and extra health if the default settings are too difficult.  I just go normal but the option is nice.Game is not too difficult in normal difficulty. I could beat most bosses in 3-5 tries, which I think is appropriate for a mid-difficulty setting. I was able to 100% a normal difficulty file in 10ish hours casually for my first run, so the game is a little on the shorter side if that's what you prefer.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Not finished yet but I'm loving the combat and exploration in this game. The music is lovely and I look forward to meeting all the characters. The game is not super stressful even on Hard - it's still challenging enough but there's no stakes to dying which personally is a great quality-of-life improve for me. In general the game has a ton of really nice features that make playing and traversing throughout the world such a pleasant experience! Highly recommend for all metroidvania enthusiasts!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Fun little metroidvania. It has a nice exploration feel for it, not too difficult to find everything. Playing on hard, most of the boss fights felt reasonably difficult for me (typically had to fight once to get a feel for tempo). Towards the end, the last couple bosses I fought felt more like a button mash "kill before I die" thing though, where Grief in particular felt like I couldn't dodge attacks. Overall though, I think it was a fun game, worth the price.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I haven't seen such an enjoyable metroidvania in a long time. I like the atmosphere. The plot is simple, but pleasurable. Some moments invoke the feeling of touching melancholy and sweet sadness.The gameplay is just as nearly flawless. Backtracking is quite convenient and not time consuming. Map is convenient to use, and you can buy items that will mark missed things on the map.I sincerely recommend the game to all fans of the genre... And cats ^_^
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: It has been lovely watching each Kyle Thompson game become more ambitious than the last.  The controls feel smooth and intuitive.  Bosses are fun and well designed.  There are different difficulty options that you can change at any time and you can adjust the difficulty even more based on what abilities you equip.  It was a joy to play and I'd recommend it to anyone that likes Metroidvania games with a more relaxed vibe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I'm an old gamer and a fan of this author after the last Islets project, because I don't like over-complicated metroidvania for pain and suffering (which is a lot nowadays), and prefer nice entertaining gameplay and a spirit of fun adventure.Both Islets and Crypt Custodian do a wonderful job with that. It's a very cute and enjoyable world with cool and fun characters. These are worlds that are nice to just be in. P.S. I'll add a small request from myself: if possible, leave the option of very low difficulty, because it distinguishes your projects from others - just explore and enjoy. Islets I passed with my girlfriend (not a gamer), also I gave it to my son and he passed it. Unfortunately, Crypt Custodian already they both found it too difficult even on low difficulty. I realize that your main audience is probably more oriented to more complex gameplay, but I think there is a niche for less experienced players who like your universe.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely fun and enjoyable metroidvania. Not excruciatingly difficult or too hand-holdly, but actually a nice middle ground with adorable characters and such a nice hand-crafted vibe to the whole experience. The mechanics introduced throughout the game are fun, the backtracking is lessened by the teleport system on the map, and the whole upgrade system isn't too grindy either. Overall, it's just a really fun and laid back take on the genre and it's definitely worth picking up if you want to not tear your hair out with boss timings and hours of backtracking.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Cozy and cute metrodvania with some light bullet hell mechanics. The game feels great to play, very responsive controls, cute visuals with distinct themes for each area, funny dialogue, and some great music! Took me about 10 hours to complete 100%. I started the game at Normal which felt quite easy for the genre, so don't be afraid to turn up the difficulty if you're cool.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Great metroidvania, very cool map, nice exploration, interesting movement, good bossfights and very touching story. Difficulty is a quite a bit on the easy side, but also very even, no spikes or slumps in it, so it feels pretty good. My only complaint would be having ability to teleport to any checkpoint at any time, which makes all the cool map connections and shortcuts a bit useless. But that also makes clearing the map after main story a lot less tedious. Maybe there's a great solution somwhere in between having teleport at all times and not at all. After Islets and Crypt Custodian Kyle Thompson is definitely becoming one of the noticably important indie devs on my list because of unique art style and storytelling and great understanding of how to make an enjoyable metroidvania. Definitely looking forward to the next game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked the story and enjoyed the game play. I did appreciate that they built in the ability to dynamically adjust the difficulty in various ways under the accessability menu. I also liked that they did make an in-game method for locating hidden items that's easily used towards the end of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game. I 100% completed the story mode in about 10 hours, and I had so much fun I did it in 3 sittings. The map shows you which areas you haven't ventured into yet, and that just kept me wanting to explore every inch of the world, even when I should have probably stopped to go to bed. The music is wonderful and peaceful when you aren't fighting the big spooky bosses, and the art style is lovely. It was a great package all together. I didn't get all the achievements because the last 3 require you to play boss rush mode, and I do not care about speed running.  Also runs perfectly on steam deckSolid 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game that provides an engaging challenge on its hard mode. This kind of quasi isometric view brings such a fresh view to metroidvanias. The game is very charming, the movement and combat is tight, and the game respects the player's time on a higher level than a lot of metroidvanias. I really do think there's something for everyone interested in metroidvanias here.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Really fun game - great music. It had me often thinking of watching Adventure Time.Definitely not overly challenging. I started on hard and completed the play through at 100% in little over 13 hours.The only achievements I didn't try for were the boss rush mode stuff.Highly recommend the game for - story,  music, mechanics, and approach play.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet metroidvania. The art style is quite pleasant, and there is a decent variety of locations with their own themes and gimmicks. However, pretty much all the space in the game is platforms floating in the air, so that hurts the diversity of levels somewhat. The combat and platforming, while simplistic and not too challenging, are fast and fluid, and control very nicely, I particularly liked that you could do a lot with jumps rather than only relying on dodges. The writing is a bit of a letdown. Your animal friends are sure cutesy, but not much developed as characters. And the way the game is structured, the plot doesn't move for 90% of playtime, barring a short introduction and ending. The music is alright, I was neither impressed nor put off. While this may not be a glowing review, I enjoyed my time with Crypt Custodian, and wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Mastapiece.Kyle Thompson's games are the among the very few that I ever 100%, because it never feels like a chore, and is just delightful the whole way through. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I loooove this game. It is super cute because cat. I am still technically still playing it (trying to 100% it) but the story and game play is really neat. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Islets and this game has improved on it in basically every way.There's a lot of good stuff going on here. Atmosphere is on point. The ambient soundtracks are lovely, with a lot of emotion behind them and each one matching its environment perfectly. On the visual side, we have the same cozy art style from Islets. It looks great and has a nice level of background detail + special effects (like raindrops on the water).Gameplay is excellent. I love love loooove the way the QoL features are integrated right into the game. The way that the enemy moves are telegraphed is a masterclass in game design, and it works great given the relatively fast pace of combat as the game goes on. Combat is a good level of difficulty and it's interesting how the lack of heals plays into this. It's not particularly deep, but it feels balanced and interesting. The movement mechanics and platforming challenges are fun although fairly basic (as of 50% completion).Area variety is fairly good; it gets much better as the game goes on (the first 2-3 areas are a bit monotonous IMO). The neon area is my favorite so far due to the creative way it leverages the dash mechanic. The demon park area was also a cool concept that I hadn't seen in the genre before. I'm not sure exactly how non-linear this game is, but it definitely opens up after the ~20% mark giving you a few different areas to choose from. I'm at about 50% right now and still have at least 3 different areas that are open to me which I haven't explored.The story also feels nicely balanced - it's easily digestible and filled with a small cast of likeable and quirky characters. The overarching goal of the game is pretty clear and it's also a fun one. I like the way that you learn more about characters by collecting their pictures, and it all ties into the setting in a kind of melancholy way given how sweet most of them are.All in all, greatly enjoying this game. Would recommend to any fans of Islets or MVs with a 50/50 combat/exploration focus.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Extremely charming and interesting metroidvania with a super cute art style and a lovable cast of characters. Combat does exactly what it needs to and the accompanying boss fights and platforming challenges are just challenging enough without ever feeling unfair or frustrating. I did run into one minor bug where I managed to dash jump into a wall and get stuck (which I was easily able to get out of by teleporting to a nearby save point (and in fact I'm only mentioning this here because the dev requested people post any issues they run into here, so hey here ya go)), but other than that it's been an excellent way to spend my long weekend.(Also as a heads up, don't let the listed playtime fool you, I'm almost 12 hours in just from running around and soaking in the sights and wanting to get all the unlocks that I can, my play time just looks weird in Steam because I was bouncing back and forth from PC to Steam Deck. This likely doesn't matter but wanted to mention just in case. Game good though. Buy game. Play game.)
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian
