_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Defy the god of the dead as you hack and slash- Ah, sorry.Crypt Custodian is another quality basically-Metroidvania from Kyle Thompson of Islets fame. Condemned to the worse side of the afterlife with a dubious justification, Pluto the cat sets out to make friends and clean up garbage, by way of exploring strange locations and battling even stranger creatures. Crypt Custodian uses an overhead view rather than the side-scrolling world of traditional Metroidvanias, but the feel is quite similar. Most of the runtime is devoted to exploring the world freely, gaining traversal abilities, equippable passive effects, and special moves, with the ultimate goal of befriending all the spectral inhabitants and pulling off a scheme together. Combat retains some elements from Islets, like non-recovering HP and the general shmup feel of enemy attack patterns. The writing as well has the same relaxed, deadpan humor to it. I don't think I should over-describe the game, though. I recommend trying it for oneself.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Crypt Custodian is a fun and charming metroidvania. I like the theme and setting and the characters you meet are all whimsical in their own way. If you've played the developer's prior game - Islets - you'll find a fair amount of similarities but it's also apparent that he has grown in skill and knowledge since that game. There are some really interesting abilities here and they interact with zones in different ways. My favorite is a dash that will phase enemies and objects in one area into or out of existence. Game seems to be about 8 hours long, probably a bit less if you wait for guides to be available as there were some points where I wasn't quite sure where to go next. I'd recommend playing the demo if you're interested, as that's a great sneak preview of the first half hour or so.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Writing this review after the first boss, so I’ll come back and edit it if things change, but I have such a good impression of this game already that I want to leave a review. This game is, so far, a relatively chill (but still somewhat challenging, on hard mode) top-down metroidvania with great movement, interesting mechanics, excellent art and animations, engaging dialogue, and surprisingly cute themes for a game called “Crypt Custodian.” It *just* came out and it already feels like it’s got a lot of polish.The most interesting part of the mechanics is the upgrade system, which lets you customize your mechanics directly, and gives you optional challenges (which you can complete for “Upgrade Points”, which let you equip upgrades; it’s a badge system). There doesn’t look to be *too* many, but there’s a good variety, and it seems like it’ll flesh out nicely as I progress through the game. The boss design is also interesting, with more stages than I expected, and some surprising attacks during some of them. I’m on vacation the next week and I’m gonna spend a lot of it playing this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: After playing Sekiro, I needed an easy game and this was a perfect palate cleanser, so I give it a thumbs up. The boss encounters can be a bit challenging, but if you learn the patterns and play patiently, they're not too hard. Normal enemies can be a bit spammy in some areas, but ignoring them and running through is always an option, except for certain group encounters. The game has a lot of accessibility features. Although I haven't tried them, they seem to allow any player, regardless of ability, to see the full game.The Metroidvania aspect of the game falls a little flat. The game, and the map in particular, does a good job of letting you know where you can and can't go. The marker system is almost over-engineered for the few places you might want to mark for later. The upside is that you never have to walk around aimlessly trying to figure out where to go next. The downside is that the game doesn't test your ability to navigate the world. I didn't mind, I'm not nostalgic for the old days of drawing my own map, but if you're looking for the kind of game where you'll get lost if you're not careful, this might seem very hand-holding.The story is straight out of a children's book. That's what it's meant to be, and it's tonally consistent. The characters are all friendly, hostility is always a misunderstanding and bad characters are misguided, not evil. It's very relaxed and light-hearted, and doesn't let the concept of death and the afterlife weigh it down, while still acknowledging the sadness of loss.Crypt Custodian is a fairly short game, in my 13.6 hours of play I got all the collectibles. This was a big plus for me, as I wanted a shorter and simpler experience. It told its story, showed me what it had and didn't overstay its welcome or insist upon itself. I would recommend this game to all but the hardcore Metroidvania players or people who hate Metroidvanias.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: The game is a little short even if the world seems big, less than 20 hours to complete. Game is a little to easy even on hard, a few bosses give a little bit of a challenge but the hardest section for me was a random "beat wave of enemies without taking a hit" section. A lot of deaths don't require you to back track very far which is nice but I think is one thing that makes the game shorter than it otherwise would be. Had a lot of fun but I'm glad I got it on sale and would recommend picking up anytime the game is on sale for under 10 or 15 dollars.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I played Sheepo and Islet upon release, and now am having a blast diving into Crypt Custodian. The change from a side view platformer to an isometric hack n slash is one that might make the first two games more appealing than this one, but I highly recommend giving it a try anyway if you liked the first two games Kyle Thompson made even if you're not a hack n slash person. This game is the best of Islet and then some. Thompson is one of those developers who keeps to a simple idea, but builds on it creatively and iteratively. I only just beat the first boss and I already love this game. Just like the other two he's made, i'm sure i'll 100% this one too. Thank you, Thompson, for your dedication to making these awesome games that I have loved and continue to love playing!!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I can recommend this game to anyone who likes good games. Long and interesting story, interesting puzzles (not easy but not hard), good bosses and a lot of them and they are different. Great artwork and level design. A bit sad story on photo cards, but it's life.So, I really enjoy playing it and want to find all collectibles. And you can buy upgrade that will show if room have any collectibles! That's great idea, I don't need to spent hours for searching them everywhere.Controls and enemy fighting feels fair and polished. You both feel relaxed on levels and some enemies and a bit tense on bosses.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Dev's recognizable style shines through again in a wonderful metroidvania that doesn't take itself serious but provides tons of entertainment. The controls and the gameplay is smooth, the difficulty just right and can be easily tweaked up or down (as you wish). It was a joy to explore pretty big map. There puzzles do not overstay their welcome and are a nice break from combat. Art style is gorgeous and the music is adorable and lackadaisical as it fits a game like this. I loved exploring every minute. I really liked that most mechanics are gradually introduced to you through puzzles, rather then being explained to you. I expected to find way to heal first few hours of the game, but quickly realized it is in vain. What you got is what you get between save point. It emphasizes evasion, learning patterns. Once you embrace it, it's even better. There were moments where I briefly felt things were repetitive, but it seemed like the dev could read my mind and usually the next screen would change things up. Didn't encounter any bugs, it's really well made and ton of fun. I liked the humor (as I did in the previous games by the same dev) but it may not be for everyone. There were a few boss intro scenes that I wish could be skipped, but they were only 4-5s so it's alright. The combat system could be more complex and/or provide for more variety. Certain abilities feel more useful for traversal than combat (feel clunky otherwise).I couldn't get enough and just kept coming back to it. Finished it except for the last achievement in roughly 11h. You can expect somewhere between 10-15h of content. Amazing metroidvania. Wish it was longer.9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Everything I hoped for when I played through the demo! So many small, quality of life decisions that just make this such a fun casual game to play! My only gripe is a bit of repetition in enemy attack patterns, and a lack of difficulty for me personally, even on the "hard" difficulty (although props for making it actually have new content instead of just being more health more damage!Overall, would highly recommend for anyone who enjoyed games like death's door and wants a relaxed, fun experience to journey though.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece.Most importantly: movement and combat feels on point. Plus the map is huge and the graphic style is just gorgeous.It has a great mix of combat and exploring so it doesn't feel repetitive.Backtracking is actually made very easy; it's great it doesn't feel like a chore.Well done, Kyle!Thank you very much for such an amazing game.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I was anxiously waiting for this game! I played the demo and instantly fell in love! While waiting for the release, I completed the previous game (on Xbox) from the same author - Islets, which I highly recommend to everyone. Everything in it is brilliantly done, particularly the characters, they are superb, I haven't laughed so hard playing a game in quite some time!And now Crypt Custodian has been released, and I couldn't be happier. This game is incredibly awesome, a huge leap forward for the developers. It excels in every aspect - the combat, world exploration, art, music. It's all simply out of this world! And the signature humor is there too! If you're a fan of Metroidvania, don't miss out on this game, or else we risk losing such unique, stunning projects like this one. A huge thank you to the developers, I'm in love with your game!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I've played for about 3 hours now, but from what I've seen so far I have no doubt that I'd recommend this game. The art style and the music are really charming. The controls are snappy, and it feels great to move and fight with our kitty character. The map is pretty vast and there are different "biomes" with consequent variety of enemies. It's really a joy to explore. I wasn't too convinced that I would like playing with that camera angle, which is a bit uncommon for the genre, but after the first 15-30 minutes it grew on me. I can't say much about the story yet, but the premise and character I've seen so far seem interesting! Overall it's a pretty solid metroidvania at a more than fair price. Go get it!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely great top down metroidvania.  The map for this game is massive, and plentiful fast travel combined with a great map makes backtracking painless and fun. _childDocuments_.review: Absolutely worth the price, especially if its on sale. artsyle and gameplay are amazing, the backstories of some characters are surprisingly morbid (in a good way), and the boss fights (on hard difficulty) are challenging yet not aggravatingIf you like this game, I'd highly suggest their other games.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: 1000000/10. This game is hands down one of the best games I’ve ever played. Story, gameplay, combat, originality…and cute animals! I cried. I laughed. I cried some more. The animals all have amazing little backstories and personalities that make you connect with them. My personal favorite outside of Pluto is Grizz. The fluidity of the movement and different mechanics make the game feel smooth. There’s a lot of different upgrades and skills to get. There’s collectibles. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: very cute metroidvania with a wholesome story, I own a cat and was on the verge of crying with the ending. Love the movement mechanics and the responsiveness, and how fluid the game feels. Exploration feels great, the map is huge and there are many hidden secrets and puzzles scattered around it.Boss battles are nice too, bullet-hell themed but does not get overwhelming or frustrating - comparable to Islets boss battles in the sky, or Minishoot boss battles.Also includes some veeeery nice quality of life features that make this game 0% frustration and 100% enjoyment, I wish more games followed that path sometimes.You can totally finish it in one sitting, took me about 12h to beat 100%. But it also features some mechanics that add replayability which is much appreciated - like shuffling upgrades (first time I see such a thing in a metroidvania unmodded game) and boss rush.If you've played Islets, you'll recognize the boss battle music, btw another great game from the same dev
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: I'll start by saying this is the height of indie games; a game made by a single person with minimum assistance. It's good and deserves your support.Just as fun as their other game! I imagine it'll be pretty short, but these are solid metroidvanias with fun mechanics and a cute coherent world. It's pretty unusual for me to have nothing to complain about with a game, but these have just been solid. Are they my favorite metroidvania ever? No, but do they do what they do solidly and feel great to play? Definitely. if you haven't played their other game Islet it's also quite a fun game with great feeling controls and movement.Just an incredible treat coming from a true indie developer.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Metroidvanias i've played in a while. It has a cute, yet sad story, a simple but beautful art style, and really great music. But it's the gameplay and exploration that really shine. The world is very non linear, but never confusing to navigate, and there is almost always something worthwhile to find when you go off the beaten path. Haven't finished it yet, but six hours in and i can tell it'll be one of my games of the year.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the previous game from these brothers, Islets, and thoroughly enjoying it, I eagerly awaited this game as soon as I heard of its announcement and put it at the top of my wishlist. And yeah, I can confidently say it exceeded expectations. I haven't had this much fun with an adventure/exploration game in ages.Combat: Amazingly smooth and very fun. Almost like a hack and slash. You have a special attack that needs to charge up by killing enemies, as well as a charm system reminiscent of Hollow Knight. The enemies all look great and behave very differently, and from what I have seen so far, the bosses are wonderfully designed.Exploration: Tonnes of collectibles like skill points, spirits, CDs and "charms" encourage you to explore. The map gives you 50 markers you can use to make note of places you can't reach or items you can't grab, so there's no worrying about forgetting things. Also, did I mention this map is VAST? I'm less than halfway through the game (48%) and I have already seen so much. Wetlands, gardens, a spectral void of spirits, abandoned amusement parks, technological towers... each area is entirely unique and so wonderfully distinct from each other. And I mustn't forget that you'll be making friends throughout the game, all very humorous. Oh yeah. And there's easy fast travel. No trudging across vast areas after dying in this game!Music: Eric Thompson delivers yet another banging soundtrack for this game. There are almost melancholy tracks like Lunar Lullaby and Something Strange, upbeat silly ones like Bar Song and The Palace, and chaotic ones like for boss themes and combat challenges. And tying back into exploration, you can actually find CDs around the game that play these tracks back at the "hub". Awesome!Length: I'm almost halfway through the game and have over 8 hours of playtime. Yeah, it's a great length.And of course, the game is pretty damn funny too.So in conclusion, if you loved Islets, play this game. If you love metroidvanias or really any adventure game, play this game. If you want a chill yet still challenging experience, play this game. Seriously, if you don't you'll really be missing out!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review a whopping  of all players have the "100% Complete" achievement. A real testament to how great of an experience this is.  Once you pick this game up its hard to put it down. The gameplay loop is exciting and rewarding especially if you love a classic metroidvania style with clever puzzles scattered along the way.  The combat and platforming are crisp and feel great.  If you liked Death's Door (most similar) or Tunic (CC has much simpler puzzles) you will love this game! 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: A fairly short and sweet metroidvania experience. It's nice to see a game that despite being created by a small team has all its core elements feel polished: battle mechanics, arcade challenges, platforming. Everything has a feeling of having been done well enough to have a good ol' chill and fun playthrough.The lore is lighthearted, with characters having a mostly cutesy childrens' book vibe that doesn't distract too much from having fun exploring the world.To name a few weak points: at times the game might feel like it's not sure of its own identity - moderately challenging bosses with strong bullet hell focus and notch-based (think Hollow Knight) abilities / passive bonuses, but the "update points" are fairly ubiquitous or can even be bought for a low set price, so there's no resource scarcity that would require mixing and matching different abilities and especially late-game can feel a bit pointless. That said, I was still captivated to keep going and the game is short enough for the above to never get tiring.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Not gonna lie to you, this game is great~ Two best things about this game is its art-style and music. The music is absolutely amazing, keeping it both cozy and challanging atmosphere of game, as well as fiting atmosphere of envirement of game. The art style of game is absolutely super duper cute. It not just looks amazing and cute, but also feels nice to play with. All the characters, the story writing and cutscenes, the battle animations and envirement of levels. Every piece of art looks amazing. Other than that, i can say, that playing this game makes me very cozy and comfortable. Game can be challanging sometimes, but nothing too serious and nothing you cant beat. All the enemies you can learn their attacks quickly and addapt to them. Most of bosses can look hard at first, but actually can beat most of them in under 5 tries. The platforming and puzzles part of game is fairy simple and easy to learn. And exploring world is actually feels fun. Going where you want, exploring on your own peace. Nothing force you to 100% game, and nothing force you to go one direction only.Overall, for a game, that was made by two people only - its definitely a great game. And definitely worth its price. Loving it~

_childDocuments_.review: Kept me hooked the entire length of the game. Pros:- Has some of the most customization for accessibility that I've ever seen in a game in quite a while, just need to look in the menu's for it.- Cute characters and good writing, no one overstays their welcome- Generally good music overallNeutral:- There were a few spots that I got stuck and unsure of where to go next as the paid hints are pricey, so just make sure to use the map markers when you find things you obviously can't get past at that time to save yourself grief later.- I think I sequence broke the game several times by using the jump+air dash+slam to cross gaps I wasn't supposed to have? Hard to say as you get a move later that would've made some of them a lot easier for sure.Con's:- Is a rather petty one, but the player/boss dying sound, or picking up a major power-up is really grating and doesn't feel like it fits the mood of what's happening on screen

_childDocuments_.review: Charming is the perfect word to describe this game. Every character is so engaging, one of the few games in which I never got bored talking to npcs. All of the systems, mechanics, and controls flow very nicely, I never felt like I was fighting the game. Backtracking is woven into the exploration quite well, along with other additions to keep it from ever being a hassle. Solid amount of biome, enemy, and boss variety which means the game keeps feeling fresh. There's a good amount of post-game content with hard mode and other surprises. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Played the demo and fell in love with this game! Have been following the release ever since! This game is somehow EXCEEDING my expectations! Combat is fun and can be challenging, especially with the bullet h377 aspects. The art style is charming and the music is great. However, where this game just oozes fun, is from the movement mechanics. The game has an amazing early game progression rate (1 new mechanic every 45 minutes until you start encountering newer areas. This game is by the same developer as Islets, and you can tell. if you played Islets, you would know the end game movement mechanics are some of the most fluid and fun movesets to move within a game!I HIGHLY recommend this game! _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent metroidvania, and quite a nice continuation to the evolution shown by Kyle Thompson from a somewhat irregular Sheepo to a very enjoyable Islets, and now this gem!The controls feels really great, almost flawless. Traversing the map is very enjoyable and the game integrates puzzles, bullet hell and platforming in really nice ways. The characters are very charismatic and the variety of enemies (so far, still early in the game) surprisingly wide.If you look for a game with an accessible difficulty level, polished controls, heartwarming visuals and a story that really wants you to keep exploring, definitely give this one a go.P.S. _childDocuments_.review: Not often do I come across a game with an art style so appealing that I become skeptical if the gameplay will hold up. Within minutes though, I absolutely fell in love with Crypt Custodian. Its gentle atmosphere becomes readily apparent from its calming title screen, that balances the morose curiosity of death with the onset of a spiritual journey, and even more so in its first tutorial level that has such a beautiful flooded ruins aesthetic that I wish I could steal it and make my entire Animal Crossing village mirror its splendor.The game never takes itself too seriously, but it doesn't undermine itself either and shrug off its premise like a lot of cozy/charming games do where they have to turn everything into a terse joke and refuse to put any heart into its premise. The nature of the many micro-stories you discover, via the friends you make in each zone, are uniquely grim as you find 3 photos that tell a quick tale of who these ghosts were in life, and what led to their ends, landing them in the afterlife just like you. But that sadness is offset by how warm and pleasant the spirits you interact with are, many of which are downright lovable within only a few dialogue boxes.Most of the game's content is focused on combat, which keeps things simple and satisfying. Zelda meets Hollow Knight feel like the main inspirations as you have hefty sword attacks (or I guess Broom attacks, in this case) with a particularly good feeling plunging jump attack and a very fluid dash attack. The Hollow Knight angle comes in the form of the dozens of equippable charms to modify your abilities and a magic meter that builds up from mopping up foes that lets you unleash a powerful Special Attack which they nailed the amount of time it'll be unavailable to help give combat that perfect flow of building up for your big moment as you dart through enemies surrounding you.Something unique is there's almost no limit to how many charms you can eventually equip as they're only gated by ability points which most games would cap you out on, but in this game's case, if you're willing to put in the elbow grease of finding its many, maaany upgrades that dot every crevice of the map behind optional puzzles, platforming challenges, hidden areas, and combat paths, you can become God. It's a fun and rewarding powertrip knowing that exploration will always contribute to your power level and you don't have to make hard decisions on which charms to use and basically never use that one that's "okay, but definitely not better than this one" the freedom's in your paws.But that freedom does lend itself to something I'm slightly mixed on. The game's challenge starts pretty decent, but it quickly disappears as you gain an ability which makes your dodge roll have virtually no cooldown. Between your jumps and fast dodge rolls, it's almost impossible to realistically take damage as long as you're flailing around and most enemies attack in very similar predictable patterns, so you quickly understand how to fight pretty much every enemy in the game, even ones you've never seen, since they get rather same-y and you're way too well equipped to deal with them. By the end game, I could pretty much destroy any enemy before they had a chance to blink and this made the game start to feel a bit mindless. I was still having fun, but I wasn't very engaged. This got so bad that I one shot the final boss with health to spare and had a "that was it?" feeling moment. An even Harder mode would be very welcome that increases enemy HP and perhaps restricts your resources a bit.Though I was able to find that desired challenge in the form of the surprisingly brutal Boss Rush achievements which task you with S+ ranking every boss, meaning you basically have to be flawless. Beating the bosses into paste with as many charms as I want was one thing, but no hitting them with only a few carefully selected powerups was the daunting sendoff challenge my 100% completion of the game hungered for. I was *very* satisfied suddenly having to take these bosses waaaay more seriously.Bottom line, this game is great. Its lite-ambient soundtrack always feels fitting for its ghostly tone with melodies that feel sentimental and just a bit sad, like everything is a reminder of a life passed but one to be celebrated in memories. The gameplay is well fitting to its action adventure genre, satisfying every curiosity you have behind each corner with some sort of reward or puzzle to solve. The visuals are obviously drop-dead gorgeous. And the game gives you the freedom to play it pretty much however you want.
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a fantastic third entry for Kyle. The environment and soundtrack are cozy and the characters are adorable. The combat is going to be more simple than some other games in the MV genre, but it's not too simple that it's boring. The "charm" system gives all the reasonable upgrade buffs that people like to typically see along with a few combo synergies for a couple different types of playstyles. The boss fights aren't too difficult and enemy/boss attacks are well telegraphed for quick-to-react players to quickly feel rewarded for learning the patterns. If more hardcore players want more of a challenge the boss rush mode requires you to no-hit the bosses for an S+ rating.The game respects your time and the only things I wish to have gotten more of would be another enemy type or two per biome and for the base biome models to differ a little bit more. What I mean by this is instead of the areas being more or less platforms that you fall off of, maybe in the earlier zones the boundary limits are defined by thick vegetation.One of my favorite games of the year so far. I'd suck Kyle's weiner just to get a taste of the artistic recipe.

_childDocuments_.review: I played 2.5 hours of the demo, literally scouring the map & when I reached the end, I checked the steam page on the daily to see if a release date had been announced. I LOVE crypt custodian. Pluto is charming, the setting is great, and the platforming is really fun. It reminds me of Garden Story, which I also love very much. I'm haven't caught up to where I got to in the demo yet, but I took a quick peek at the achievements & there is SO SO SO much depth to this game that I haven't even scratched the surface of!
_childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: crypt custodian was one of the games i was most looking forward to in 2024 and it hasn't disappointed! i loved kyle thompson's previous game islets, and crypt custodian is just as good if not better! the humour is charming, the art and music are gorgeous and atmospheric, and the controls/gameplay just feel really good to play. the combat is fair and challenging -- not to mention there are difficulty settings for those of us (like me) who don't have great reflexes but still want an enjoyable experience. i'm really excited to explore every nook and cranny of this game :]EDIT: after 9 more hours i can confidently say that this game is absolutely fantastic, exceeded my expectations and i can't believe how much map there is. oh my god. it's awesome!!!!!

_childDocuments_.review: You know you have a gem at your hands when you drop the demo before completing it, because you don't want to spoil it and wait it for the full game. Another excellent game from Mr. Thompson. It was my most anticipated game this summer. I cannot wait to grab my steam deck every night to play some more and get to know its sweet and funny characters. It plays like a great metroidvania with awesome bosses and areas with great puzzles. _childDocuments_.review: Great art style/work, solid controls, wonderful music, and an interesting story. As the game progresses you have some degree of freedom as to where you'd like to explore next, limited only by the unique abilities you may require to access certain other areas. Some bosses can be challenging; but, the death penalty is negligible. There are a variety of enemies and mechanics. _childDocuments_.name: Crypt Custodian

_childDocuments_.review: Love this game!  The charm, the fighting mechanics are varied and more interesting than I expected.  Love the small battle challenges.  The npcs are interesting. _childDocuments_.review: This is the third game from this band of brother developers, and it is quite apparent that they have been improving their craft with each release. Their games provide plentiful nourishment for longtime metroidvania lovers, while also serving as digestible morsels for anyone looking to get their first taste of the genre. Just like its predecessor Islets, Crypt Custodian may not be a genre-defining behemoth like Hollow Knight or Ori, but it serves as a testament to how much individual developers can accomplish with today's tools and a loyal fanbase.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is great so far. The vibes and presentation are fantastic. It feels great to move around. _childDocuments_.review: Kyle Thompson has become one of the most reliable indie devs out there.  You know what you're going to get. _childDocuments_.review:
Crypt Custodian is a charming metroidvania/zelda-like about cleaning up the afterlife.

You play as Pluto - a mischievous cat who has just died, and landed in the afterlife's palace. After a brief and disastrous meeting with the Afterlife Guardian - Kendra - you are banished from the palace and sentenced to clean... FOREVER!!

Explore the vast grounds that surround the palace, battle beasts with your trusty broom, and gain new abilities to expand your map. Solve puzzles, discover secrets, and... organize an ambush to break back into the palace!

name: SteamWorld Heist II
detailed_description: All is not well on the waves— a water crisis is brewing! Mysteriously, this precious resource has become deadly, corroding metal limbs and mechanical hearts. As legendary Captain Leeway, it’s up to you and your ragtag crew of steambots to uncover the source of this threat and save botkind before it’s too late! TURN-BASED STRATEGY AT ITS BEST Dive into an upgraded tactical experience that builds on the beloved gameplay of SteamWorld Heist. Every move matters as you plan your turns, position your crew, and carefully aim each shot. Ricochet bullets off walls and use your surroundings to outsmart enemies, but remember—victory hinges on a well-thought-out strategy, not just a quick trigger finger. NEW WATERS, NEW ADVENTURES Set sail across the vast ocean in your trusty submarine. Face real-time naval combat challenges and steer your crew through tactical ship-to-ship battles while discovering hidden treasures in every wave. Your decisions as captain shape your journey through the Great Sea. CUSTOMISE YOUR CREW, YOUR WAY With over 150 weapons, utility items, and ship upgrades, the possibilities for crew customisation are endless. Equip your steambots for every strategy—whether you prefer a sharpshooting sniper or a hammer-wielding bruiser. Unlock new crewmates, jobs, abilities, and gear to perfect your team for each mission. DIVE INTO A HANDCRAFTED WORLD Immerse yourself in a beautifully crafted world filled with unique environments, eccentric characters, and a captivating story. And yes, Steam Powered Giraffe is back with an all-new soundtrack that will stick with you long after you’ve docked your ship. Plus, with over 30 hours of gameplay, your adventure will be as vast as the ocean itself! FEATURES: Precision turn-based combat with satisfying ricochet mechanics Discover a vast world filled with real-time naval battles and hidden treasures Customise your crew with 150+ weapons, items, and upgrades Explore the rich new job system to create a crew that fits your playstyle A stunning new adventure set in the SteamWorld universe, with over 30 hours of gameplay Music by the fan-favourite Steam Powered Giraffe! The fate of botkind rests in your hands—are you ready to lead your crew through treacherous waters?

_childDocuments_.review: I played every single SteamWorld game (even the forgotten one for DSi/3DS, SteamWorld Tower Defense) and I have to admit: While the original SteamWorld Dig was my all-time favourite for a long time, SteamWorld Heist II (SWH2) is the game that finally took its place.The graphics are beautiful. With the addition of dynamic lighting, it really adds more depth to the even more improved 2D style. The map is a very nice upgrade to the first Heist, as it really feels like you are on the shard / overworld and not just on a map. The steering is a bit wonky, but adds to the challenge. I also like the fact that there are lots of secrets to uncover.The new job system is easy to learn, but also easy to miss. One mission brings it up, and it's really worth taking time to get into it, as it really adds much depth - and extremely fun and almost OP techniques - to your trick shots. One time I was able to shoot 42 times with ONE character during ONE TURN because I used the right combination of skills from different jobs on that character. Gives you some real #BigSteveEnergy!Without using the new job-system, some levels might be very hard even on lower difficulties. It takes some time to level jobs, and you will have to replay some levels you already completed for sure, but it's very much worth the time!I beat the game (story wise) at a playtime of 28 hours and I still have to complete all levels on full stars as well as collecting all the hats and level-up all teammates to the max. It has lots of replay value for sure! I was shocked when I thought the game was almost over, and I was actually only halfway in.At first, I was very skeptical about the new cast of playable characters, as Heist players like me are very used to Piper and her Crew. But I got to love them really quickly and following their individual background stories as well as the games' story, I really felt like they grew together like a family. Especially after the one VERY spoilery event that made things kinda emotionally on Captain Leeway's side. #CharacterDevelopmentDoneRightThe story is brilliant. It's nothing that deep and nothing extraordinarily new, sure. But it fits really well into the SteamWorld lore and adds a lot of new context to what happened in space after the Earth exploded at the end of SteamWorld Dig 2 / SteamWorld Build. It also captures the SteamWorld humour very well.SWH2 has cool references (that I won't spoil) to the first Heist, as well as some other titles. One was a very QUESTy surprise at the very end of the game, so keep playing!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: I really loved the first game, and I the sequel is excellent as well!  I beat the game in 42 hours (higher than what Steam reports as I played a good bit offline on my Steam Deck), which included getting full stars on all missions, unlocking all upgrades, and unlocking all crew.+ Great combat, which is like a combination of turn-based tactics and the Worms games :)+ Beautiful visuals+ Fun story+ Very satisfying to have a turn where multiple abilities work together to let you get a lot of kills/deal a lot of damage+ Hats! 🎩+ Moving around the overworld in the submarine and having some real-time combat was fun and a change of pace between missions* Job system -- I'm a little mixed here. You level up a character's "job" based on their currently equipped weapon type (e.g. sniper). All abilities are active for their current job, and you can enable abilities from their other jobs they have leveled up using a limited amount of "cogs". What seemed to make sense to me was get each character's main job up to level 5, but also cycle through the other jobs to get characters to level 2-3 for most other jobs (otherwise you are missing out on other abilities/synergies and sitting on unused "cogs"). So it's good that it forces a little experimentation and lets you unlock abilities, but through the mid to late game I felt like I was constantly swapping weapons around to try to get characters leveled up, so they were rarely being used for their "best" job.  There were some really neat combinations I found, but most I didn't discover until the game was about over.- No way to inspect your characters, enemies, etc. which is unfortunate. This is pretty much expected in most tactics/strategy games (for example, to see what status effects a character has and what they mean, the movement range of enemies, etc). - UI for some of the floor hazards could use some work. For example, if a player ends a turn on some tiles they will get a negative status effect. Most of the time you get warned with a big ⚠️ symbol on your move cursor, but if that tile also has an item or interactive element, it will just display the ⚙️symbol indicating interaction. IMO, it should display both symbols to avoid a user moving to a tile not realizing they would take the negative status effect.- Alarms/countdown timers -- It seems that just about every mission is forcing you to be aggressive because of "alarms" that will increasingly spawn more enemies or achieve the objective in X turns. . While I don't mind this concept entirely, I found its frequency annoying (way more than the first game from what I can recall)- I was surprised to never unlock any kind of fast travel ability. While I overall liked the overworld and submarine combat, I would have found it useful a few times in the 2nd half of the game to be able to warp between bars or something.Overall a great game! 4/5
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful game, it took me 30 hours which is plenty of content for the price.If you are familiar with steamworld heist 1 here are the improvements:-overworld map with ship combat. You can get new abilities to reach new areas-pretty complex job system. This feature gives you much more control over your units' progression then in the first. You can make some really op combos-meta upgrades. You can upgrade your ship, crewmate abilities, and job skills.-ability to load during battle, taking you back one or two turns. This is a great addition!Aside from this there is also a lot of great music in the inns. Overall I think this game is better played after the first one, so you have a good understanding of the base mechanics. But that aside, its a much more tactically deep game and it has a much better atmosphere imo (the world map does a lot here)I noticed one negative during my playthrough, which is that hats are very awkward to use. I equip a hat that looks cool, and if it is knocked off during a mission i have to equip it again. This is mildly annoying, hopefully the devs fix it. But overall wonderful game, give it a try!
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Not long into it, but can already tell it's everything great about SteamWorld Heist 1 and more.  The SteamWorld franchise titles are instant purchases for me and this is no exception.  Was counting down the minutes to release and am eager to dive back into this beloved world!  Heist 1 was my favorite in the franchise so I'm beyond eager to see where this new adventure takes us.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 2 accomplishes something quite rare in the modern gaming age, being an innovative yet true to their roots sequel. I've enjoyed everything about the game, what set Steamworld Heist 1 apart from similar-ish games of it's ilk was the unique world and characters, all this has been expanded upon in this sequel, to the point where I felt a lot more emotionally attached to the Leeway Crew than to the one captained by Faraday. This is a good thing and does not leave the original in a worse light by any stretch of the imagination. The music production has been amped up significantly, and really immersed me into the unique world of..Steam...world. I was slightly worried about the game prior to it's launch because I felt Steamworld Build did not quite grasp it's universe's feel, those worries have been dashed quite expertly. For those who can't afford too many games: The price-quality ratio is perfectly fine, the game is not that long, but the devs clearly respect it if you look at the pricetag. If you want a unique experience in skillbased turn-based battles, as well as a charming story, buy the first one, and if you're hooked? The second one is right here as well.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Great piece, both as a standalone, and as a second installment in a series. Comprehensive story, neat visuals, handy controls.Provides tension and challenge at all stages of the game, while being approachable and open for experiments: free restarts, mid-combat checkpoints, multiple build options, etc.The star feature of the series is its aiming mechanic. It brings a tangible, interactive way of both judging and controlling your chances. Most tactical games incite massive outrage with misses on 95% shots, but this one doesn't: if you miss, it's entirely on you. Fair. Good sport.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Lengthy (and mostly personal) review: Long story short, a wonderful game ESPECIALLY in comparison to the firstThis game. It's just really hard to explain what this game did to me.I bought the first game just as a bi-product of being an avid Steam Powered Giraffe fan and also the crazy sale that was going on. I wasn't sure how much I was going to like that game as turn based games in general rarely intrigued me. So when I played the game, I was pleasantly surprised with how involved I was in the gameplay. I ended up having a lot of fun and became quite the fan of Piper Faraday, but it didn't leave me feeling any particular way. Not like this game did. Despite all the new features this game offered in its trailers, I wasn't sure it would be too different from the first game. I thought that all that was offered in those trailers was all that was going to be new but man was I wrong. This game was a serious step up from the original and I LIKED the original. There's a lot to admire. The artwork, the voice work, the slice of life features (no more limited inventory!) but man, the gameplay and the story, the CHARACTERS left me feeling strongly about this game. I can already taste the nostalgia. Obviously I loved the music. Even beyond what Steam Powered Giraffe did, the environmental music was SUPER effective.I had a lot more fun playing this game with the many new gimmicks and features constantly being offered both within the missions and outside the missions. Absolutely LOVE the resting mechanic. A big gripe of mine with turn based games is that if there are a lot of characters, you'll probably feel more inclined to stick with just a few. I even had this problem with the first game but not in this game. As you progress, using other characters becomes much more necessary and the game makes doing so an easy decision. Also the checkpoint feature. I didn't realize it was there at first but boy do I abuse that thing now. Might be cheap, but does feel very strategic on my end.The story felt much more cohesive in this one than in the last one. The motives of each character were very clear and it's real nice to see plot points beyond just "We need to defeat these guys because they're bad". I was motivated by the story. That's what kept me engaged. What REALLY surprised me though were the characters. I was not expecting to find myself gaining a sense of attachment to each and every one of these characters. I'm not sure if it was pacing or if the characters were just that interesting if not a little cliche, but either way, it all made the characters really enjoyable for me. All this makes me really interested in all of the other Steamworld games. It made me even more interested in the FUTURE Steamworld games.This has got to be one of the first games I've ever played where I told myself "I need to play it again" even though I was only half way through the game. Of course, there are little things that bother me, like how the RNG can really mess with the difficulty on some levels, but it's all really easy to look past compared to what the rest of the game has to offer. And these are just the more comprehensible things I like about this game. There are many other things that I LOVED that I just cannot describe. I kept getting feelings that resonate with me deeply. It just makes me really happy. Everyone should absolutely try this game. I love this game, and I'd love to see where it could end up and what it could mean in future Steamworld games.Also, notice the hours? I am very bad at this game. I'm also very stubborn, and refuse to change the difficulty, but I still ended getting each and every star in Experienced mode :]

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly good continuation of an already incredibly good 2D turn-based tactics game Steam World Heist. Lovely presentation and music, really addictive "just one more mission" gameplay, highly customizable difficulty (you can even run missions with incomplete crew), a story that does its job (there also are a few cool references to other games in the SteamWorld series) and fun exploration.The exploration part is a new addition and I think it fits well. You need to pay attention to it though and make timely upgrades to you submarine, otherwise it is easy to miss the Unsinkable achievement like I did as there is no reloading if you've died on the world map.I've played the entire game on Steam Deck and it was a really smooth experience. If you play on PC, make sure to use a controller, as the submarine is probably clunky to control with a keyboard.I've payed the day 1 price for it and it was well worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: If this is your first time in SteamWorld, welcome! If not, welcome back for another great adventure! Put on your best pirate hat and strap in for the best SteamWorld game so far. Get ready to shoot, bomb or brawl your way through enemy ships using turn based action combat, and battle it out with cannons and torpedoes in naval battles with realtime shooter combat. Can you find out what’s turning water bad and save the world once more?This game is set in the SteamWorld Universe, an alternate history starting on Earth with the development of steam-powered artificial intelligence bots back in the 19th century. This alternate history is explored through the various SteamWorld games, through the evolution of steambots from simple defense towers to mining bots and to fully functional intelligent beings, the war with electronic vectron bots, the destruction of Earth, the rise of dieselbots and the fight against their Royal Space Force, after which this game starts.Some time after the defeat of the Red Queen at the end of SteamWorld Heist, on one of the bigger shards left after the destruction of Earth, water is turning bad, slowly rusting all the steambots. Clean fresh water is a rare currency. The corrupt Navy is profiting off of this scarcity, tyrannically ruling over the common folk with an iron fist (literally!). And in the frigid waters of the north, the crazed cult of Rattlers are purposefully sacrificing bots and water to their new god, forcing everyone to replace their metal parts with bones, since “bone does not rust”.You play as Captain Quincy Leeway, son of the legendary “Krakenbane”, destroyer of the Kraken. Finally able to track down and take back his submarine from the Navy, it’s time to start earning a reputation worthy of the Leeway name. Employ a shipful of ragtag crewmates and send them on missions to win better equipment, currency, and most importantly, experience!As you move from region to region, you’ll gain reputation and start being respected by the free bots, and not just as the son of a legend. Soon you get a message from a scientist tracking down the source of the water problem. A few encounters with the Rattlers reveal that they already know the source, and it’s their new god. The defeat of the Rattlers’ leader points you in the right direction: a strange frozen ship far to the north. And this is where I’ll leave it, too many spoilers after this.There are three different parts to this game: the overworld, the friendly places, and the enemy places.The overworld is mainly for selecting the next location to visit, either a bar to rest in, a shop to buy things, or a quest location to fight in. But this is also where you fight naval battles against enemy ships, either on the surface or underwater. Defeated ships may leave behind a salvageable shipwreck, which usually gives you water (the main currency in this world), but sometimes you may find more valuable currencies or rare items. Each day fresh flotsams may be sprinkled throughout to boost your gallon count, if you have the patience to scour the oceans looking for them. You can mount weapons on your submarine, either forward facing torpedoes, side mounted cannons, or weak 360 top turrets. Each weapon takes time to reload, so in a battle you’ll have to learn to circle the enemy ship, staying clear of its weapons while trying to alternate between your front torpedoes and both side cannons. The good thing is that your submarine is usually much stronger than one enemy ship, and if your integrity goes too far down, you just have to find a calm spot to rest a bit and wait for it to go back up a bit. How much it goes up by itself depends on the difficulty, between half in the easy Story mode, and barely enough to withstand a handful of bullets at the highest difficulty. And one more thing about the overworld, keep an eye out for secrets.The friendly locations, the interior of your sub included, involve moving freely with the captain, talking to people, hiring new crewmembers, buying merchandise on display, and again, looking for secrets. In your submarine you can talk to your crew to discover more of the story, or you can spend Fragments (the rarest currency), to upgrade your submarine or your crew.Combat is turn based. Each faction takes its turn, and every bot has two action points, which can be used either for walking or for using one of the abilities. The main ability is, of course, firing your gun, but there are many other abilities or items to use. Firing the main gun automatically ends a bot’s turn, spending both action points if you didn’t already use the first one. Other items and abilities can either cost one action point, or be free, so in one turn you could fire 3 sidearms and the main gun, or even more when combined with other abilities. There’s a lot of strategy involved in combat. The type of bot matters. Brawlers use melee weapons and are strong and healthy, boomers fire rockets with a lot of area damage, engineers fire multiple times and weaken enemies, snipers are precise but need to manually reload, reapers fire machine guns and can fire many times, and flankers cover a lot of terrain. Terrain matters, since you can duck behind obstacles, shoot from above, or line up and shoot through multiple enemies using piercing weapons. Speed is important too, many missions have a turn limit after which the epic loot is destroyed, or have tiered alarms with more, and more powerful enemies joining after some turns. In the easiest difficulty, Story Mode, you can easily run through missions without much thought, even with half the allowed bots, but the higher the difficulty, the more you have to think and plan every move, every bot you bring in a mission, every ability you use, every enemy you destroy. Missions are of good length, usually around 10-20 turns, more on higher difficulty. If you’re looking for a challenging turn based combat game, this is an excellent option.Excellent turn based combat requiring strategic thinking. Good story. Good graphics. Good music from a real band. Plenty of difficulty options, including a fully customizable experience in which you choose how easy/hard each aspect of the game is. And you can change the difficulty at any time, if at one point the game gets too hard, you don’t have to start a new save with a lower difficulty from the beginning, or if you feel like it’s too easy, just amp up the challenge a bit, with instant effect. Excellent worldbuilding and story continuity from previous games, expect lots of references and a few cameos from familiar heroes. Great challenging achievements requiring multiple playthroughs with different styles: speed, safety, completionist, tricks…No pause/menu access during the enemy turns, and these may take a lot of time, with only a “skip this animation” option with limited benefits. The story structure is becoming a cliché for all SteamWorld games, with all the plot twists predictable. Only three save slots available.The combat is identical. Retreating from a battle is free. The quest selection is a playable map. Crewmembers don’t have a fixed specialty, they can have any role if they carry the right weapon. Multiple currencies, not just water. In missions you are allowed to rewind two turns.A great quality game, fun and challenging. 20-30 hours for one playthrough, but you’ll probably have to play it a few times to beat the hardest difficulty.

_childDocuments_.review: I was hyped as hell for this after loving the first installment - it comes as a shock that I'd feel the need to give a thumbs down for this after 9 hours of playing.More isn't necessarily better, something that too many studios fail to appropriately grasp: - The overworld is tedious, as it's essentially here to inflate gameplay time through not-so-good real time combat. The whole point of the game is the turn-based tactics, adding anything else that isn't 10/10 in between makes the whole experience more annoying. It makes going back to earlier levels a chore, too. - I don't remember the first installment having so much constant reinforcement right from the get go. Suddenly, it's not about strategizing against a specific enemy setup, but rather managing to survive long enough against an unending onslaught of enemies. What that does, is make you feel that the issue isn't so much the strategy you used, but rather the fact you haven't farmed enough to get better gear for your characters and level them up. It leads to a vicious circle as the difficulty makes you flee the level before you can grab all the loot (and sometimes even the epic one), which means less stuff to improve your characters, which means the next level is gonna feel even tougher, and so on and so forth. Of course, the solution for me would be to lower the difficulty. But once you do that, you absolutely stomp the enemies and there's no challenge/thinking needed anymore. Some of the enemies' powers (damage, stuff they spawn) are literally halved between the third highest difficulty and the second highest.This leads an absolutely gorgeous game full of personality and promise to be a tiring experience that felt like a chore right as I was entering the second zone. This isn't a bad game per se of course, but the result in terms of fun vs. what it could be unfortunately warrants this negative review.

_childDocuments_.review: Steamworld Heist 2 is everything I wanted it to be as the excellent Steamworld Heist 1's sequel: If you haven't played the original Steamworld Heist, don't worry - there is no requirement to play it before playing this one. The sequel's story makes some light references to the original game, but nothing crucial. Either way, you're in for a very polished turn-based tactics experience! Oh, and if you're a veteran of this genre, do yourself a favor and start on Elite right away - the game's difficulty slider is tuned to be on the easier side this time, unlike in the first game.

_childDocuments_.review: In short: A simple gameplay loop executed really, really well.Everything in this game is simple, but smart and well polished. The missions feel satisfying to play, the mechanics are tight, and the art direction is gorgeous. Lining up the perfect shot to ricochet across the map and execute half an enemy crew feels fantastic, and so do many of the other plays you can make in this game. The gear/abilities you can give your crew feel meaningful, and there are some super interesting combinations you can make work if you experiment. It's worth the price, especially if you like strategy games already.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Heist 1, this met my expectations and slightly overshot them. The boat combat is more fluid than expected. Controls are slightly changed and they have a new action system for combat. That's interesting so far.They introduced resting after missions and a daily bounty system in addition to the sea map, so I am worried they'll pad playtime via grind. Steampowered Giraffe is obviously the best thing about it still.The gunshots are.. sharper.. than the original, imo. Might just be me, but I got a headache after 2 hours. Then I played some more on Deck speakers and it was much more bearable.I'll update with more thoughts as I progess. Initial impression: Worthy sequel.Update:On Experienced difficulty, the alarms start out so early on missions past the parlay, it encourages me too much to rush through the missions; So I tuned down the mission urgency.Update 2:Yeah the game can definetely feel a bit stretched at parts in the arctic and.. later on.I am enjoying the story quite a bit. It has some nice callbacks to the older games, but should stand ok on its own legs, too.

_childDocuments_.review: A very solid sequel to the original, which expands on everything but doesn't take any massive risks with the formula. If you didn't like the first, there is nothing for you here.Game runs around 25ish hours and I think that runtime is really about right, as the animations and time it takes to progress turns with so many lategame enemies and effects makes the game start to overstay it's welcome.Achievement hunters should expect to have to slog through many more hours, if not the whole game again, to mop up a handful of lengthy achievements (not hard, just long)
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, I really want to give this game a good review. It gets a lot right for a tactics type game, but it falls into the worst and most major sin: Reinforcements.I get it. You want your game to be challenging, and giving players too much time means they can crawl their way through. But why, why in god's name would you think the solution is to spam adds at random throughout the stage? The entire game is about positioning and reinforcements literally flip over the chess board. You can do everything right, but too bad, the game spawned a shotgun guy behind you and now you're dead. It also bloats the turn-end as you monotonously watch the AI cycle through orders for dozens of enemies, half of which you don't care about.It doesn't even solve the main issue, because I'm just going to reload and account for this lazy garbage. It changes nothing at all about the problem.There was every opportunity to do better here, with the way the game works making beefier enemies with more skills would have worked. Even a rising water level, you set it up perfectly with the polluted water story! But no. Random adds. Disappointing.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: Obscenely good game. My brain is absolutely rotted from dopamine addiction and I typically cannot play a strategy-like game for more than 10 minutes before having to switch to Overkill so I dont go into dopamine withdrawal. SW Heist II takes everything that I liked about the first and doubles it. It takes everything I didnt like and halves it. One of the most enjoyable tactics games I have every played. I can see how some nerds might not like the "balance" since theres so much more variety in potential crewmates. But since I play games for fun instead of min/maxxing like its a second job, I actually enjoy that variety. Easy 9.5/10 and possibly my 2024 GOTY
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: It's another great addition to the steamworld franchise, great music, fun strategy combat, cool theme all nailed yet again. The new leveling system is really awesome, tons of variability if you choose to level up multiple "jobs" on one character. The bounty system is fun, helps you feel a little bit better about the tedious resting system. The snipers are a huge upgrade from the previous game, lots more ways to reload without wasting a turn. The SMGs feel way better compared to the first game. Tons of gameplay upgrades all around. The naval combat is braindead, basically an auto battler. That's both a positive and a negative for me.As with all steamworld games they can't help but put in an annoying mechanic or two, in this one it's for sure resting. In between just about every mission (maybe 2 missions if you have enough crew) you have to sail back to your nearest tavern to rest. It's pointless and doesn't really do anything but increase the amount of time you'll spend in the game sailing back and forth. The positives outweigh the negatives in a huge way, definitely worth picking up if you enjoyed the first steamworld heist.
_childDocuments_.name: SteamWorld Heist II

_childDocuments_.review: *SteamWorld Heist 2* is an absolute gem and a brilliant continuation of the tactical, turn-based shooter series! It takes everything that made the original great and elevates it to new heights. The combination of strategy, action, and charm is perfectly balanced. The precision aiming mechanic, where you manually aim each shot, adds a level of tension and satisfaction that keeps every mission fresh and exciting.The new environments are gorgeous, with even more variety in level design and enemy types. The tactical depth has been expanded, allowing for even more creative and strategic approaches to each mission. Characters are vibrant and full of personality, with humor and style that fans of the series will love.Whether you're a fan of the first game or new to the *SteamWorld* universe, *Heist 2* is a must-play. It’s a rewarding blend of strategy, skill, and fun that feels endlessly replayable. A truly unique and unforgettable experience!
