_childDocuments_.review: I've been hyped for this game since the announcement day. But it needs to stay a little bit in the oven. MADiSON VR will constanly remind you that this game wasn't designed for VR and that it is a port with lot of mechanics that works on PC but doesn't work in VR. Let's start with positives: + Holy f##k this game is scary. This really is the scariest VR game I've ever played or seen. + The game looks fenomenal in terms of graphics and it feels real. I don't have the strongest PC (GTX 1080 ti, i7 8700) so I played the game on Low settings first but because the FPS weren't the best I tried to turn the settings even lower. That switched the settings into Ultra and I decided to atleast look how the game looks in VR on that settings. And it was day and night change. What I don't understand tho is that on Ultra settings the game runs better for me than on Low settings. But maybe that's because I changed the resolution. It seems like that only changes the resolution of the window on PC but not in VR. I am not 100% sure about that tho. But if you can play this game on Ultra settings, do it. + The polaroid feature works great in VR + you can equip a few skins from the menu on it (unlike in PC version where the skins are locked behind DLC). It would be nice if we could hold the polaroid with both hands but that's just a tiny detail that has no impact on the gameplay.+ I like how you can see your entire arms and not just floating hands like in most VR games. It's way more immersiveNow the negatives:- The VR control is clunky and unreliable. It happened to me many times that I want to grab something but I either couldn't or it didn't happen on first try. Example: In the room where you get the polaroid, there is a drawer with a key. I tried to open it but the character either drop the handle or didn't grab it at all. And when I finally managed to grab it, I couldn't open it. So I assumed that the drawer is locked (this was after the section where you take the picture of the painting that you put on the wall). So I spent 25 MINUTES walking back and forth trying to figure out what am I supposed to. Than I gave up and looked on YT and to my surprise, the key I needed for opening the door was in that drawer I couldn't open -_-. So I tried to open it again and after 8th attempt it finally worked. - You can't use both hands at the same time. For example is you hold the polaroid in your dominant hand and with your other hand you want to open the door, you can't. You have to hide the polaroid into backpack and than open the door with your dominant hand. And this applies for more interactions. This needs to be fixed asap - Scrolling through items in inventory is extremely slow - If you pick any item (besides polaroid) your movement is blocked. You have to hide the item in your backpack or drop it in order to be able to move againThis game has huge potentional but the controls is sinking it to the bottom. For now I will leave a negaive review but I really hope that the devs will fix the VR controls soon so I can change the negative review into a possitive one.
_childDocuments_.name: MADiSON VR

_childDocuments_.review: You can view my full review after completion here: This game is currently on a Mixed Review status on Steam (5/5/2024), however, the devs have released an update today which I believe fixes all the issues mentioned on the Steam forums. After this update, this game is a must buy for any VR horror fan. It is simply put, the best VR horror game that I have ever played (and I have played almost all of them). See my video for more details, both good and bad, which explains my review score below.---- Original Initial Impressions below: So I will be doing a full review, but it will take me some time. Early impressions though are great. This game is terrifying. It looks great & runs good. The sound mix is top notch. I really haven't noticed any major issues. My biggest gripe so far is just the force grab mechanic, it's kind of weird. You have to stand back a certain distance, then do a whip like motion. I'm not sure why they did it this way, but it just leads to some frustration. The game may be too dark in certain areas, but the lighting overall is very good to keep you frightened. The VR interactions are nice for a VR port, but obviously not as good as a built for VR game. A lot of them are point and click or highlight and grab. The walk speed is kind of slow (even the run speed is slow), but it makes sense in a horror game. However, the game's atmosphere is top notch. I don't know that we've ever had a game with visuals as good as this, that is actually horrifying. You'll hear noises in the distance that just shake your composure. Then something spooky will happen. These aren't cheap jump scares, but directed scares that will rattle your soul.I haven't played too much, but I had to take a break because it's kind of late here. I have loved every minute so far though. So far this is one of the best VR horror games that I have ever played. It may be be the best. It's definitely one of the best looking VR horror games. It may be a contender for VR GOTY. We shall see though. It's still early on for me (18% complete).Game is running on the Unity Engine. On my RTX 3080, I was getting a steady 90 fps on medium graphical settings. I did not experience any bugs or issues. You do have full locomotion, along with smooth or snap turning. You can play seated or standing. You have both force grab and button crouch.
_childDocuments_.name: MADiSON VR

_childDocuments_.review: As a (heavy) VR gamer you need to be aware: This is a port from a flat game to VR and a very small team. Given that, you sometimes need to let go of what you expect to do. You rather need to click on some things instead of trying to grab them. If you have that in mind and get used to it, playing gets a bit more easier the more you go.Game went well, I only had one major bug that was solved by a restart and after I wrote the devs about it, it was fixed in the game so it should not occur again.From a scary factor it is the most scary game I played so far in VR. The puzzles are sometimes a bit hard, but not unsolvable. You can get easily annoyed though if you are out of ideas - or just want to get out of a certain situation but that puzzle still stands in your way to escape...Save points are fair, not as cruel as I have expected from earlier reviews/reports. Not sure it was adjusted, but as a fan of "closer" save points in order to not do things over and over again I am satisfied with them and did not get frustrated as a lot of progress was saved sometimes even without seeing a save symbol.Story wise also interesting and all in all cleverly made.
_childDocuments_.name: MADiSON VR

_childDocuments_.review: Bloodious Games has finally given me something in this VR version of Madison that I've been craving in my 7+ years in VR; a game that is almost irresponsibly frightening. A game that probably ought to carry a health warning due to the sheer relentlessness of its frights. Bloodious proves here that they simply do not give a ♥♥♥♥ how badly Madison VR scares you, they will not hold back, and they do not. For a horror fan (particularly VR horror!) I cannot convey how refreshing this approach is. I came into Madison VR thankfully blind and finished the game in under 6 deliciously terrifying hours (or so the achievement I triggered told me) and I thoroughly dreaded each of them. I'll share my thoughts on The Good, The Bad, and The Ugly with this one.THE GOOD:⦁ As stated above, the game is relentless with its scares and does not hold back. The pacing of the scares is just right, but expect to be kept in a state of constant dread and "on edge" for the game's entire runtime (for me, under six hours).⦁ Audio design is top notch; a constant swell of atmospheric sound creates a palpable tension every moment you spend in that house, even the quiet moments where seemingly nothing is going on. Jumpscares and other spooky moments are expertly punctuated with Hollywood-quality orchestral string swells that sent my stomach into my throat even when I expected them!⦁ Graphically this is a beautiful game (if you can consider rotting wood and blood-stains "beautiful"). DLSS and other graphics options kept the movement fluid and running smooth. I experienced this visual feast on a Bigscreen Beyond, and the deep dark blacks were inky and gorgeous on the micro-OLED display. Play this one on an OLED HMD like the BSB, PSVR2, Vive, etc. if you're able!⦁ Puzzles felt like they had the right level of challenge; I was rarely left stumped for long, and when I did figure out the solution the puzzles felt satisfying. I'm sad to admit I did look up a few minor hints online to point me in the right direction in a couple of cases where I felt what I was supposed to do; honestly if this game felt "safer" to play I'm sure I would've puzzled these sections out on my own, but the atmosphere is so unsettling in this one it can be difficult to think straight and you really don't want to be spending longer in some of those situations than you have to.⦁ The story is actually engrossing. As with most horror, you've generally seen all of this game's themes before, but rarely are they presented in such a compelling manner. I genuinely wanted to follow the story to its conclusion to find out what happens, even though that meant forging ahead into the terror.THE BAD:⦁  The game originated as a flat game and is being ported into VR, and unfortunately you're reminded of this fact when you invariably can't interact with every object that you want to, or when inventory interactions rarely amount to more than "pull this thing from your inventory and place it on this silhouette in the game world while standing in a stationary spot." The worst offenders were ladders and stairways that I wanted to physically climb but were relegated to a trigger pull and a scene fade out.⦁ Somewhat related to above, scene transitions were of the "fade to black" sort which I found terribly immersion breaking. Fortunately there's not much of this, and it never interrupts action, but it's a shame to squander opportunities like having someone lower themselves trepidatiously down a ladder into a well by dissolving the tension with a fade-out.⦁ Speaking of dissolving tension, a couple of Madison's most famous frightening moments I found spoiled by an over-reliance on some "video-gamey" mechanic like pointing an object at jussssst the right spot to trigger an event. I'd have really appreciated some grace in this part. I started one of these sections utterly terrified, but my terror quickly devolved into frustration as I tried desperately to end the "pixel hunt" and move on--come on guys, we get the mechanic here, let's just get to the scary stuff!⦁ Another way the game got in its own way was its tendency to pop Steam achievement notifications in the middle of moments that otherwise would have been HORRIFYING. +Pro-Tip+: silence your Steam achievement notifications before diving into this one! Learn from my mistakes, don't rob yourself of scares! And Bloodious, if you guys are listening, can't you have these achievements trigger a bit later (i.e. on a respawn or something?) so we aren't taken out of intense moments?⦁	The save system is really poor by modern standards; the game arbitrarily saves with an easily missable visual indicator only when you trigger certain events, or solve puzzles--it doesn't even save when you pick up all items. This means that when life invariably gets in the way and you have to quit your game session, you'll almost certainly be doing some backtracking when you load the game back up.The Ugly:⦁ I don't understand the choice to make some... let's call them "character models" blink in and out of existence; they look great, they're well animated, why display them like computer glitches? That took me out of the experience somewhat.⦁ Some of the game's more frightening ideas tend to get overused. The first time I flick the lighter back on JUST in time to see the evil presence recess menacingly into the darkness, I shriek. By the 7th time the game requires me to do this, it's just gotten old. ⦁ Having rewatched on YouTube, there are elements I missed in the game's climatic finale because I physically turned the wrong way. I recognize this is tough to get right in VR, where we can look in directions that weren't intended during a "cut scene," but I feel it wasn't handled particularly gracefully here.While I share a healthy amount of constructive (I hope!) criticism in this review, I want to make it clear that I enjoyed Madison VR IMMENSELY. Not only was it exactly the sort of unrelentingly terrifying horror experience that I was looking for in VR, it's a game of exceptional quality. I cannot WAIT to see what Bloodious does next. If you've got the stones to play this one, it's a horror adventure journey worth taking.

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually made me feel unease and scared me a few times which is very hard to pull of as I got so used to VR horrorgames that just rely on jumpscares of the cheap kind. Madison has jumpscares too, some are predictable and some are don't (so it's done right). But it also has a really really good atmosphere and set pieces.I can say this is finally a game that made me not want to do what I had to do to advance in the game because I didn't know what will happen next.Highly recommend this game.For the complains of the slow waling speed. _childDocuments_.review: *Updated since patch 1.01*Played on Quest 3 via Steam Link.A lot of things have bit fixed, but my frustration with the VR controls continue.The "grab over your shoulder" mechanic to grab the camera still doesn't work properly. The only way I can guarantee I grab the camera is if I tilt my head to my right shoulder while grabbing for it. Is this because I'm tall? No idea.I also found out why opening some drawers/cupboards can be so frustrating. The game doesn't seem to like when you grab things that are lower down. It helps if your arm is a little more straight-on with the handle you're grabbing. So, instead of naturally opening drawers from a standing position, I have to lean/kneel down so I'm closer to being level with them before I can open them.There are also so many times where something I'm supposed to interact with (puzzle, key item, etc) is way too dark to notice. There was clock I was supposed to interact with that, from far away looked like just a dark outline of a clock. I basically had to put my face right up against it before I realized it was a key item.I'm happy the devs seem to be addressing these issues, but there are still a few too many frustrating things holding it back from being an otherwise solid recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: Totally awesome game - haven't been this much immersed for long. But maybe you need to enjoy horror movies like Saw, The Exorcist, The Conjuring, and Evil Dead. Comparing to Alyx is a big thing and overused - but Alyx also is a horror game (Jeff, jumping spiders, headcrab zombies etc.), and in Madison the story works 10 times as adrenaline-pumping as Alyx, lol. Many may stay away from this game due to the horror - and it's there, but this is also an exciting adventure game where you pick up items and use them. Like Alyx, the game can be set to auto-adjust the res (super-sampling) to maintain 1:1 fps:hz-ratio, which works fine - for this to work, set DLSS to Auto. I did try using 80 Hz, Ultra graphics, DLSS Auto, Index res 300% with an RTX 3090, and performace was 80 fps. Graphics settings: This is one of the best-looking VR games for long, textures, lighting, dynamic shadows all look great. This shot shows the high-res hand textures:Here's an example of the real-time lighting:If you beat Jeff, you can do Madison VR too. This game is a VR diamond in the rough, it's not to be missed, The game uses OpenXR, so you'll get optimal performance using Meta, Index, etc.First I got annoyed with the lcd blacks using the Index, and I switched to oled (Rift CV1). Oled is better, and this game looks incredible with the Rift CV1 - but I found that I really had no issues using lcd, my issue was not related to lcd. For now this game could be game of the year 2024, but I need to play it more. Sure, it's a VR port of a 2D game - but that's probably why it looks so amazing. Btw, often you do stand still when picking up an object (and cannot move in the game), but there are also items you can hold in your hand while moving. There are several objects you can pick up and interact with, and the game feels like a great VR game and not some lackluster 2D port. For now my rating is 9.5/10.

_childDocuments_.review: As I started to write this review, at some point the Steam restarted and I need to start again. Lesson of Patience.So, where shall I begin?I will give my honest feedback and recommendations, just don't kill yourself.As this game is made into VR from a desktop version, despite various minor bugs and glitches, such as not able to pick up an item from under the floor boards or needing to play the record longer than normal to produce that what you are looking for. So, the mechanics at times are not perfect, however overall the developer did a good job on making this game VR. Despite some moments of frustration, I was able to complete the story, so it works on PCVR.As for the actual game and whether it actually is a horror game, well, it depends how you play it.If you play this game in the desktop version, and having experience of VR horror, it will lack the feeling of being there, so I recommend you get yourself a VR equipment and do this more properly.If you are reading this, then I suppose you already own one or are pondering to get one.So, once you have your VR rig, you kinda ready to experience this game properly, but you will be missing something, at least I would.In my humble opinion VR horror begins to be a horror when experienced on psychedelics.It might get frustrating at times, because solving puzzles can get a bit difficult and takes more time to solve than average, so in a sense tames the horror, meaning that even under the influence of lets say the incredible psychiatric medicine called lysergic acid diethylamide, when you spend over an hour walking around the house trying to solve a puzzle, you kinda get used to the freeky feeling of the house, and what was meant to be horror becomes daily bread.Eventually you are able to solve the puzzle and you begin to dread the unknown horror ahead.I mean, this game is f**ked up, not only because it is worthy to enter the VR Hall of Horrors, but also because my name is Luca.I don't play games much, but as for VR, it is either flight simulation or VR horror.I tried quiet a few VR horror games and only 3 are in the VR Hell of Horrors, in the following order in my personal experience perspective:1) Exorcist Legion VR2) Madison VR3) Rise of Insanity VR (Madison took the 2nd place)I played Don't Knock Twice and the Demo was very scary, but the actual game made me feel compassion for whatever victim in the game, and that just killed the horror.Actually, a really good short horror game that never developed further would be probably even scarier than Madison if made VR, that one is a Japanese made called Lurk in the Dark: Prologue. That was one of the best horror desktop experiences I played and if the game ever was completed and then made into VR, the way that game was going it would be pretty f**ked up.So, anyway, from these 3 VR horror games, Madison is the longest one and if you ever played Exorcist Legion VR, you can tell that they have something in common, that makes them both superior over many other VR horror games.Exorcist Legion VR, though shorter than Madison, is superior in my experience.If you do it properly, maybe you will come to understand.Still, for Madison to reach that 2nd place, and for years that place was taken by Rise of Insanity in VR, this means it was not an easy VR horror to experience and Rise of Insanity wasn't either, but Madison had to go in the foot steps of the Legion, hence it is superior.The Truth is that if the developer of Exorcist Legion VR continued on the path of VR horror and made something as long as Madison, but to the level of the Legion, then that would be another level to VR horror in my honest humble opinion.To conclude, if you own a VR headset, then get yourself Madison VR and do this properly, however if you have not the experience of doing this properly, I recommend not doing this on psychedelics if you have no experience, It can traumatise you and mess with your mind. _childDocuments_.review: This might be the first VR horror game that I legit just cannot finish and I mean that in the form of the highest praise possible.    Flashing that polaroid camera down a pitch black hallway to try and light it up for a split second to capture a look of the thing chasing me is nearly just too much to comfortably process.  Well done devs, I'm honestly really impressed at the amount of dread and terror you've managed to stuff into my eyeballs here.  The graphics are unexpectedly beautiful and the game seems to already run fairly well as of v1.01 on a 3080.  There's some goofy control issues that I hope will get sorted out and the inventory is a little too unresponsive for its own good but the mood of this game is unmatched from anything I've played in VR in a long time.   This is a genuinely terrifying game and if you're a horror junkie, I'm not sure anything else hits quite as hard as this one.

_childDocuments_.review: This game gets a positive from me because while it isn't perfect, its atmosphere and horror completely compensate for any issues and thus makes the game entirely worth getting. This will most definitely augment your experience if compared to the desktop game.Now, the issues: There are quite a few. First the remote interaction/grab mechanic has a very narrow, awkwardly angled aim range. I instantly struggled with it and at the very beginning reverted to physical interactions. The game has stutters and they're not consistent. For the majority of the time framerate is smooth but there are moments where things are loading in or the camera is being used that cause sudden dips. I did play on default graphics settings on an RTX 4080 which shouldn't be a problem. Finally I had a softlock at the very beginning of the game, at a point where I'm just fresh in and have no idea what's going on... turns out when I got the photos out of the container, somehow the game attached the photos to my dominant hand, conflicting with the container. I will link my video at the bottom of this post as it contains a clip of this incident.Interestingly, though, by the time I was at the bottom of the well where the game ramped things up progressively, I had forgotten about most of these issues as the atmosphere took over and overshadowed most of the negatives I ran into. This is definitely made with heart, has a nice and sneaky way of getting your nerves going and if you're ready to put up with a few imperfections you'll definitely get some thrills out of this one!Here's my first impressions video, recorded shortly before Halloween 2024

_childDocuments_.review: I know that the Devs (two man team) worked very hard on this game, but I do not recommend it and find this game to be very boring and NOT SCARY at all.  AND I disagree 100 per cent that it is the scariest game in VR to date. It is classified as a psychological horror but is far from it.     I initially did a positive review after playing for about an hour but deleted my positive review as the more I played the more bugs and unnatural click vice using button controls I experienced...constant reverting to menu, blue screen, horrible auto save system, awkward controls, etc.  And the more I played the more bored I became.  I am using a top of the line PC with VIVE pro and NVIDIA 3080 TI with 32 GB RAM. The graphics are good but that is all I found to be worthwhile as the game and the story are extremely boring and not scary as I mentioned earlier.    Walking in this game is very slow;  taking pictures is overdone and overkill; the inventory limit is not necessary and awkward;  and game play is often unclear as what to do.This game tries to be super creepy but I thought it failed in this area.  The puzzles are relatively easy, but some can be challenging as you will get pieces of a puzzle way before you can actually use them.   There are some aspects of the story which do not make sense, and I ran into a few graphical glitches.Overall MADiSON VR is labelled a psychological horror game without any psychological horror.     And the ending is a BIG disappointment!I rate this game overall 6/10....it is OKAY but it is not as good as many of the reviews make it out to be.

_childDocuments_.review: Highly advise against purchasing this game. I had been excited for this for months, hadn't played the original, and am beyond disappointed. I had 1 crash at the beginning, which was fine but whatever. the main issues is the game itself, there is never a clear mission path, the inventory management system is janky, the photo shaking gets tedious especially because you end up taking pictures of everything, since you don't know what to take pictures of. Then you also need to go BACK to these images, which are all saved, making it a pain to look through all of them. the interact buttons are unclear, and unpolished. I expected way more considering the price tag. I lost patience after I had gotten far throughout the house (side note the walking speed in this game is insanely slow) only to realize i had to (slowly) walk back to a really early part of the level, as it had let me progress with missing something important. The game looks and runs fine, however I don't know how it runs on lower end systems, as it for some reason recommends a 3080ti . As i said, it runs fine, but a game like half life alyx looks 8x better, while not recommending such high end hardware. The puzzles really should be a lot more straightforward, maybe on the flatscreen version they are fine, but on VR it is ridiculously tedious, with a whole lot of walking back and forth waiting for stuff to happen. Also the handling of things like opening doors, and drawers is buggy.I hope this game improves, because i have heard amazing things about the original game, but in its current state it sadly just adds onto the library of unfinished, unoptimized unintuitive, VR clutter on steam.

_childDocuments_.review: First off...WOW! For any horror fans that also happen to have VR, this is a must play! I had heard great things about it, but held off bc i'm cheap...finally got it when it hit 20$ and i am so glad i did!!! I love all things horror, and i'm mad at myself for holding out so long now that i've experienced it . What is here is fantastic, a great balance of unique puzzles, environment, jump scare, tension, confusion and gore to create a game that not only frightens you regularly, does so that even at the end of my 11hr playthrough i never felt burnt out or like any one scare tactic was driven into the ground. This is crucial for good horror imo, and Madison does it like no other! The puzzles can baffle you a bit, but once you start to put pieces together it all starts to click. Only once at the start did i have to look it up, but after that i felt i had a good idea for how the game worked and was able to go the rest of the way with no help. Of course as a pc gamer i have to mention the technical side of things...i am running a 1080ti and 6700k , with a Quest 3 via AirLink. I had to create a mix of medium and high settings to lock in a smooth 90hz , i believe my older card isn't helped much by the DLSS. With that said, even with all at medium this game looks FANTASTIC! The lighting, effects, the textures all look amazing in the headset! I had the occasional stutter or frame delay in an intense scene, but with an aging gpu, that is becoming expected. It was never enough to cause me nausea or make me want to cut my sessions short. Today alone i played for 6hrs. That is a testament to the performance and gameplay, as someone with adhd getting me to do any one thing more than 30 minutes is a struggle...so yea, go buy the game! I feel pretty confident you will at the very least be able to tell within the 2hr return window if the game is for you or not! Also try and play when people in your house arent trying to sleep, bc you WILL yell out often!

_childDocuments_.review: This is an AMAZING VR port, I would say one, if not the scariest VR titles to date. Negatives :-Very very small nitpicks. Some of the VR objects controls are a little janky, but I had much worse experience with other games-The inventory system needs some work, can't hold two items at once and you have to put away the item before you can use it, but you can store items in a safe which comes pretty handy.-I'm not gonna lie the game is pretty demanding, I have a 2060 and I could play it with an SSD with minor stutters, the minimal recommendation is a 2070 Super for this game but completely undestandable, I need a better build, I'm working on it.That's all about it.Positives :-AMAZING graphics, I've never seen this realistic light and shadow in a VR game before, (maybe Half life Alyx) the objects and the enviroment is beautifully detailed as well.-Good story, voice acting is allright, the main character is a bit of a whimp, but you can turn off his voice (which is pretty funny)-Mechanics and the puzzles were amazing, really clever, They never felt too long or boring or if they are, they have jumpscares to keep you on your toes, clues were plenty, I was stuck at one or two sections, but It took me very little time to find out what to do. -Pants ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ scary horror game. Atmosphere, Jumpscares, Darkness. I'ts all here. It got me several times and I'm used to horror titles.This is 9 out of 10 for me. name: Neva
detailed_description: Neva is an emotionally-charged action adventure from the visionary team behind the critically acclaimed GRIS. Neva chronicles the story of Alba, a young woman bound to a curious wolf cub following a traumatic encounter with dark forces. Together they embark on a perilous journey through a once-beautiful world as it slowly decays around them. Over time, their relationship will evolve as they learn to work together, helping one another to brave increasingly dangerous situations. The wolf will grow from a rebellious cub to an imposing adult seeking to forge her own identity, testing Alba’s love and their commitment to one another. As the cursed world threatens to overwhelm them, Alba and her courageous companion will do whatever it takes to survive and make a new home, together.

short_description: Experience the moving tale of a young woman and her lifelong bond with a magnificent wolf as they embark on a thrilling adventure through a rapidly dying world.

_childDocuments_.review: The best stories teach us simple lessons. They remind us, that whatever state the industry, the country, or the world might be in, if we allow ourselves to let go and to listen -  we can find something beautiful.That's what Neva is. A harmonious blend of sound, color, and emotion wrapped in a simple but mechanically tight package that undermines the current noise of battlepasses, angry articles, and million dollar missteps. It reminds us that gaming, at its best, is a story-telling art-form.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Fair warning: this is NOT going to be the same experience as Gris. Neva employs a different (but still gorgeous!) art style, presents more of a challenge with the puzzles and combat (nothing too difficult, but not breezy either), has a less abstract story than Gris (though there is definitely some room for interpretation here and there), and is emotionally heavy from start to finish compared to Gris saving the most emotional gut punch for the end. Neva follows the titular magical antlered wolf (why don't they exist IRL and why can't I have one???) and her guardian Alba, who must fight to survive a rapidly decaying world brought on by a mysterious, malevolent force. As the seasons pass, the bond between wolf and woman grows stronger, granting you new ways to solve clever puzzles and fight grotesque enemies. Throughout the game, I kept thinking to myself "the devs are huge fans of Princess Mononoke" because there were a LOT of moments that reminded me of that movie. Since Princess Mononoke is one of the greatest anime movies of all time, it added immensely to my enjoyment. This game really does feel like the closest we'll get to a game actually made by Hayao Miyazaki rather than just something that takes inspiration for the art style and vibes. In other words, we get a breathtakingly beautiful and emotional game that emphasises the power and importance of nature, the bond between people and spirits, and the devastation caused by environmental destruction, topped off with an amazing score by the always great Berlinist. I'm so glad Nomada Studio is still making games and I hope they make many more for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: I jumped into Neva right away because I loved Gris.  It was a once-in-a-lifetime game for me... a beautiful story, stunning graphics, fantastic scenes, and lovely music. It is a hard act to follow.After an opening scene that pulls the heart strings, Neva is a journey by a girl and her wolf-like companion. You traverse a landscape that is beautiful and treacherous. The game has gorgeous graphics and music but I have not found the early sections to be as compelling as Gris. Combat has been added which is not my favorite feature. Luckily, the developers have provided a 'story mode' option that eliminates death-by-enemies and the need to manage your health. Six-plus hours into the game, I am enjoying the adventure and looking forward to the story developing. Then, I hit the end of the "Fall Part 1" section that requires a long sequence of precision platforming up a disintegrating tree. This is a timed exercise and it is a very tall tree with no intermediate save points. Miss a jump or run out of time and you start over. If this were for an achievement, I'd just move on and give up on 100%. But, I have to get past this tree in order to continue the game. At this point, the tree is winning and I've seen the death scene ad nauseam. I keep coming back to try again and, when I make the jumps, I run out of time near the top and experience (yet) another death.  The fun factor is wearing off and I am beginning to dread my next tree encounter. If this is a harbinger of the skill level required to complete Neva, I am in trouble.I have not given up yet but would describe Neva as a 'Precision Platformer.' I had some tough jumps to make in Gris for achievements, but never got stuck like this. I should have believed the reviews that stated Neva was much more difficult than Gris.I can't slam the game. It is beautifully crafted for the player with the proper skill set (which apparently is not me).  If you are uncomfortable with speedily performing precise aerial maneuvers with a controller, then Neva may not be for you.Meanwhile, that darn tree is still mocking my feeble attempts to conquer it...

_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: From the onset, Neva is a tearjerker. Its opening moments introduce the protagonist, Alba, a warrior traveling alongside a mighty white wolf and her pup, Neva. Traveling through the forest’s splendor, their peace is broken as a bird falls from the sky, tainted by a black inklike corruption. Quickly, the corruption spreads, taking corporeal shape and overpowering Alba and her wolf. In the end, the wolf is slain, leaving Alba comfort and care for Neva. Together, they’re what remains of the family. The game itself is both highly accessible and deeply affecting, there wasn’t a single moment during my playthrough where I was more than a beat away from sobbing; the game’s six to seven-hour runtime is an emotionally exhausting journey seen mostly through watery eyes. But the story is a hopeful one, although heavy on melancholy. As Neva comes into her own, she begins to accomplish more and more, making Alba feel less useful or needed. Neva’s going to grow up one way or another, maybe even becoming a parent of her own, will the time come to let her go ? While the gameplay is not particularly complex and overly challenging, it is pretty fun for what it is, its balance of exploration and simple combat makes it perfect for fans of narrative-driven games over long, grind-heavy experiences. Overall, the gameplay is solid, if shallow. Combat is methodical, centering on properly timed dodges and the right balance of siccing Neva on foes while attacking with Alba. Missteps can be costly, but there’s little penalty to dying as combat sequences will simply start over. Big enemies and bosses aside, there’s only a handful of monster types and the game has a slow build toward any kind of real difficulty. Its gameplay is tight, but simple. Its puzzles are inventive but not overly complex.Neva is a game of profound beauty. Its minimalist art design is portrait-like, with soft lines and vibrant color imbuing its increasingly fantastical world with a cozy hue. Whereas GRIS resembled an illustrated sketch jumped off the page, Neva feels like a dreamlike take on an oil painting. This work of art is a clear inspiration — it all feels very familiar to Ghibli's Princess Mononoke, both in terms of story and sublime visuals. The game’s soundtrack is heavy on somber piano melodies but ratchets up into stranger, more haunting places as the story goes deeper into dreamlike territory. There’re also multiple instances where the game, which despite never feeling truly small, goes very big with soaring operatic tones for huge chase scenes and boss battles. These moments are infrequent, but well-earned, narratively and emotionally.Straightforward hacking & slashing feels nice and responsive and I was surprised by how challenging it could be at times. Platforming, specifically puzzle platforming is a slightly more significant part of the Neva formula. Each level introduces compelling twists to the game's central mechanics, which keeps jumping from box to box interesting despite rudimentary locomotion abilities. Solving each platforming puzzle won't require too much effort, but this might warrant a slightly greater demerit than the simplicity of the combat. There were times when it felt like Neva was holding back, not stretching each level's new mechanics beyond their logical conclusion. The most interesting level-based platformers tend to go this extra mile, so it's a bit disappointing that Neva spends so little time with such promising ideas.All told, Neva is one of the games that enchants you with its stunning visuals and touching story, rarely do games move me to tears but this tale of a woman rearing her cub in a world plagued by demons had a deep emotional effect. A very special platformer that everyone should get to experience in my opinion, especially if you enjoyed playing GRIS. 10/10 recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Completed with all collectibles (not all achievements) in 4 hours so slightly longer than Gris. It's another amazing game. I think this is what made Gris so emotional. Neva probably doesn't have the same emotional impact throughout most of the game (there are definitely parts later on in Neva that are on par with the best parts of Gris) as Gris did because you're "distracted" by the combat. Not a bad thing, just a change of theme. Anyone saying it's not as emotional as Gris, probably hasn't played through the whole game.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a decent game. You should buy it. It is a gorgeous looking game, with okay combat, okay platforming, okay puzzles, good but not memorable music and an okay story (though it makes a logical error in its narration; more further below). It is a bit on the short side, though.Why, then, do I give a negative review? Because I think that there are big flaws that need to be addressed that nobody seems to talk or think about. I also do not want my critiques to be buried beneath the mountain of positive reviews.First point of critique, the game took a lot, maybe even too much, inspiration from Princess Mononoke and Spirited Away. Especially in the first half. You play as a girl with a big white wolf. You fight a possessed boar, multiple times even. The black goo spirits are basically an evil version of No face from Spirited Away. The black goo spirits rattle their heads like the Kodama in Mononoke do and even produce a similar rattling sound when doing so. The antlers on the wolf are reminiscent of the antlers of the deer God in Mononoke, though there are visual differences. When is an artist inspired by, paying tribute or making a reference to something and when does he or she blatantly copy? It is a tough question. In any case, it gets way too close for comfort here, in my opinion, for very front and center elements, such as main character designs and critical plot points. Second point of critique, the opening of the game is very problematic in terms of narrative clarity. It basically ruins the game in terms of narrative logic. It leads people astray that actually pay attention to such things, including me. A lot of people are unaware, though, it seems, given that only a few mention it online. Let me say this: If you are one of many (have a look on reddit) that thought the plot had a loop in it (I did too, at first), well then, you thought wrong. Spoilers up ahead. The third point of critique is about that which a story rests on: themes. The developers have the disadvantage that they are making this game after their own hit game, GRIS. Why is this a disadvantage? Because a lot of people, myself included, were wondering if and how the developers were going to surpass their previous game. GRIS, unfortunately, is better in every regard. Not only does it have more diversity in puzzles and environments, more memorable music (I love Gris Part I and II from the official soundtrack and I still listen to these songs from time to time), but most importantly, GRIS had a far stronger UNDERLYING THEME. Apart from a stronger theme, it also integrates the theme far better into other aspects of the game (audio, visuals) than Neva does. In GRIS, you go through the five stages of grief. Each level there has a distinct color pallet and reflects the stage of grief the main character is in. The music in a level reflects the stage of grief and therefore the theme. I dare to say that GRIS is a prime example of how one should integrate theme into your visual and audio aspects of your game. What is the theme of Neva? Life versus death. As plain and blunt as it gets. The chapters are seperated by the four seasons. For example, you have a winter level and some puzzles involve ice. *snore* Okay, using ice as mirrors for platforming is a neat idea, but I am not blown away here. The question is, is it a problem to have a simple theme for your game? No. Does every indie game need to be about depression (insert meme here)? Again, no. But I wish the developers had given Neva another layer, like they did so expertly with their previous game. I have no idea why they chose to not do so in Neva. As for the critiques other people give: Is the combat shallow? A bit, yeah, but the game is not trying to be Devil May Cry here. It is an atmospheric, story driven puzzle game with combat elements and I doubt the developers were going for an in depth system. Game mechanics feeling incomplete. Yep, I agree. You could have done much more with every ability. More puzzles per game mechanic, expansion on each mechanic as you go. For example, using the wolf as a projectile. Maybe expand into a grappling hook, different types of shots, et cetera. In summary, inspiration is good, directly copying is not. Remove the opening cinematic or change it completely. Have a stronger theme. For example, make the story about renewal and borrow from the Abduction of Persephone (the rebirth of seasons). Expand upon the game mechanics. Thanks for coming to my TED talk. Nomada, hire me.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a beautiful game where the devs have let the aesthetics overtake gameplay and accessibility.Make no mistake, the game is gorgeous, but this comes at the expense of gameplay. Pop-up text is sometimes lost as white text on white skies, because the designers felt it would be too "ugly" to outline the text. The devs so want to show off their art that sometimes the main character and enemies can blend into the background, or be obscured by foreground. Character animations are very pretty, but as a result the controls can feel floaty and unresponsive because some (but not all) animations are uninterruptible.On a technical level, it's disappointing that there is no ultrawide support for such a pretty game. There's also no borderless windowed mode, so you can't easily mouse over to a second monitor. The keyboard support is also extremely lacking, I played it mainly on an xbox elite 2 controller, but better keyboard controls would have made it playable on my laptop (come on, guys, this is 2024. Games like Deadcells, Katana Zero, Gunpoint, Hollow Knight have shown time again that it is possible to have good keyboard controls in platformers).Neva is one of the most beautiful games ever made. And the gameplay is not as bad as my criticisms may make it sound, because it is still perfectly playable except for a few places where aesthetics get in the way of the gameplay. It does get a bit repetitive, and some sections can be a bit frustrating when you can't see clearly or when you're wishing the controls were tighter. Thematically, it is a bit more one note compared to how well the devs managed to integrate themes and nuance into the structural narrative of GRIS. I hate to leave a negative review for such a beautiful game with obviously a lot of love put into it, but it needs some kinks ironed out and some QoL improvements.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Nomada Studio is in the business of making you feel things. Gris hit me like a sledgehammer and I still consider it one of my favorite games even though it only directly impacted my life for a few hours. Neva wasn’t quite as hard of a hit, maybe just a standard 3 lb. drilling hammer, but enough to make a crater that more than justifies a recommendation.Abbreviated Review: Much like its predecessor, Neva is a beautiful game. The premise puts you in a variety of outdoor environments during four distinct seasons and each one is expressed in exquisite color-appropriate detail that made me want to stop and stare at the background rather than finish the game. The effort taken to create areas that are visually appealing, but also functional, is clear to see throughout the game. The dense forests of Summer lead into the vibrant autumnal leaves of fall, and there are actually plenty of surreal moments depicted within these seasonal transitions that provide their own spectacular designs for you to enjoy.This is all coordinated with a surprisingly expansive soundtrack that feels like it has a new audio treat for every single scene that takes place. For a game that once again can easily be completed in four or five hours, there are 36 tracks that, put together, run for nearly two and a half hours. With this combination, from an audio and visual perspective, Neva is among the most appealing games I’ve played this year. Yet, that wouldn’t be enough to earn a recommendation on its own and of course, it’s not the only reason I am giving it one.There is technically a narrative in Neva in that a single word is spoken in the entire game: “Neva.” You can say it whenever you want with a dedicated button to call your antler-topped wolf creature to you – though it is almost always following you close by. Much like Gris, the story is the foundation of the experience and the true reason to play the game. However, in a change of pace, your effort to care for and raise your orphaned wolf creature is a much more grounded and stated premise than the somewhat abstract initial experience of the previous title.Without getting into any spoilers, the story and progress within the seasons convey every plot point through the world, creatures, sounds, and music exclusively. There’s no text or voiceover, just your understanding of the events that are happening in front of you. This is a great way to experience a story, and it lets you interpret things as you encounter them, however, it also leaves a little ambiguity and had me confused for a second at the end simply because I wasn’t paying attention. However, despite its sullen introduction and journey through an increasingly hostile world, the story was still the most compelling aspect of Neva. The subtle interactions with the world and Neva (the wolf) add just enough nuance to the story to make it captivating and hard to put down.The one aspect of Neva that doesn’t soar to the same heights as the story, music, and visuals – and the biggest departure from Gris – is the combat. It’s not a bad experience, even when it can be a little clunky with hit recognition and determining if you have dodged an attack. Yet, it didn’t feel that exciting to me or have much depth at all. Your character’s move set is practically set from the beginning, the only thing that expands is what you can do with Neva as it grows. You’re relegated to light short-reach swings of your sword – which you use against everything from the simplest enemies to the final boss. Despite your repeated encounters with combat and being the driving force for your progression through the game, it doesn’t bring down the overall experience. It feels like something you have to do to get to the more interesting parts with mild puzzles and platforming and, of course, exploring the beautiful world you get to do that within. It’s hard to describe exactly what makes Neva so enjoyable without spoiling it, especially because it’s so short, but I can say that it is well worth it to check out. Whether you want to spend $20 for something that’s only four or five hours is up to you – but at the very least, keep it on your radar and get it when you can.

_childDocuments_.review: Currently typing this up wondering if it'll even be seen or read. Why? Cuz I'm sure there'll be a LOT of positive reviews for this game out there.But regardless, I'm still gonna shove my two cents in. Why? idk..Anyway this game is pretty good. But I wanted to give this one a try and I'm glad I did.It's got some amazing visuals, great sound design, simple and yet fun/engaging gameplay components, an intriguing mystery and fluid motion and stability. _childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved Neva. The game took me a little over 3.5 hours to beat, and I really enjoyed it. The game starts with a bit of walking to admire the beautiful scenery then starts throwing in puzzles and combat. The puzzles weren't hard, but you felt that satisfaction when you solved them. The combat was a great addition too with some moves to keep it interesting. if you enjoyed GRIS or Ori, definitely give this one a shot because you won't be disappointed. One frustrating bit were the areas that had an intense bright (white/yellowish) glow and this was hard on the eyes especially since I was playing at night in a lit room (I turned my brightness to the lowest setting which didn't help that much). I hope they can tone down some of the area's glow because not only is it hard on the eyes, but also it distracts you from the beauty of the scenes. Thanks for an awesome adventure and great job on another banger Nomada!

_childDocuments_.review: extremely pretty game and loved the doggies.  fights were quite fun apart from one frustrating boar. platforming at one point was actual d*cks tho. which seemed an unnecessary/unbalanced inclusion given the rest of the game was pretty chill.   oh, and yes, ending gives feels.  overall, a recommend but got to admit i had high expectations and they were not quite realised.

_childDocuments_.review: When I played this game it felt like...50% button mashy combat against nondescript blob enemies25% walking for really long stretches across a horizontal plane without anything happening (seemingly just to show off the background scenery)25% puzzles and platforming challenges (the good parts of the game)As to why uninspired combat mechanics became the central focus of this game is beyond my comprehension. As to the overwhelmingly positive reception...also confusing.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After playing GRIS, I knew Neva would be another gem. You can tell a lot of love went into this game. It's absolutely beautiful. You journey through a world with your beloved companion and as time passes, subtle things change, keeping the gameplay fresh and interesting. Genuinely, what a great story. Even as the END CREDITS rolled, it added a little more insight into bond you share with your companion (I can say I have NEVER enjoyed end credits that much before).If you adore friendships with sweet mythical creatures, love dreamy visuals and a moving story to go with it, I highly recommend Neva. I added this game to my wish list a year ago when it was first teased, and the end result did not disappoint.Ok I'm going to go cry now =,)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The star of Neva is of course the visuals - every frame of this game is a work of art, just like Gris was.The story and settings reminded me of Princess Mononoke. It has some environmentalism themes to it, and you get to ride on a cute wolf. The combat and platforming are simple but solid, and there are a few segments that give a little bit of a challenge.It's the perfect example of how a studio's second game should be - they take everything that make their first game good, and add and expend on it.Gorgeous, fun, emotional at times. Great game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Where's the rest of the game?Don't get me wrong: I loved playing this game, it was a delight, I was having fun the whole time.It's got a nice story element, wonderful art and music, and also some fun and rewarding game-play mechanics.It's got good bones . . . but it seems glaringly incomplete.The entire game is spent introducing new game-play mechanics. But it's only ever giving you one new mechanic at a time, so I was thinking "Oh yeah, cool. Good design. They don't want to overload me with all the new mechanics at the same time until I've got them all figured out." And then the game just ends.Boom, it's over.They gave us all the pieces, but they aren't putting them together. Hope you enjoyed the components of a game though.The credit scroll ended and I was dumbfounded when it didn't go to a "Year 2: Start" screen. Or at least have a new game + or some additional game-mode or other replay value.  It might just be a personal standards thing: but, under 6 hours does not qualify as a finished $20 game in my mind. The realization of "Wait, that was the whole game"  legitimately undercut the emotional ending of the game.TLDR: This game felt like the tutorial for a better game that does not exist.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's a really good game that's, unfortunately, overhyped.If you are expecting a tearjerker, narrative with deep philosophical meaning, a 10/10, game of the year candidate, and a perfect masterpiece - too bad, your expectations are too high.It is a puzzle-platformer with fantastic visuals and audio design, interesting platforming sections, great pacing, and a bittersweet story. You might be put off by it's combat sections, but there is an adventure mode to exclude it. Boss fights are really cool though and are worth experiencing.While the game might seem simplistic for those looking for Gris-level gameplay, the good news is that it does improve at the halfway mark.Should you play it - yes, it is a good game that's worth your time and money.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It is a beautiful and emotional puzzle platformer. Bonus points for the fact that you can cuddle with the wolf. No missable achievements and completion takes around 4 to 5 hours.  5 hours 2/10 on the easiest difficulty 1 Yes, I used  No No, there is chapter selection and it saves automatically when you pick up a collectible No No No No No No, you can play on the easier difficulty and still unlock all the achievements NoNeva starts with a heartbreaking scene. However, you will not yet feel the full impact as you haven't formed a connection yet with the main character and the wolf companion. This will change later on as you can cuddle with the wolf and see it grow up throughout the game. Seeing the pup change from a scary small creature to a majestic huge wolf is beautiful. In Neva, you play as a young woman who fights and traverses through a dying world. You climb through beautiful scenes, solve light platformer puzzles, and fight the corruption. you play through the different scenes which change the look of the world so much, but if you think away the corruption that is going on, the world is always beautiful. I find it very impressive how a game without text is able to tell such a deep story. It requires you to focus, to not miss a story point. Neva taught me that I prefer a game with text, as the ending got me a bit confused, but gladly there was a topic on the Steam forum to help me understand it just a bit more. However, I still had an amazing time playing through Neva and following the story. The movement set feels very responsive and well done, and the abilities you get later felt thought out well and just as responsive as the ones you start with. I highly appreciate all the attention to detail that got poured into Neva. Not only in the artwork, but also in gameplay mechanics. For example how the game saves when you pick up a collectible, and how it has multiple spawn points to return to in a chapter. This means that Neva not only has no missable achievements, but it also isn't torture to go back to an earlier part of the game to collect the thing you missed. You don't even have to finish a part if you find the collectible you missed because of the saving that instantly happens. Unlocking all the achievements in Neva takes around 4 to 5 hours. I give Neva 4 out of 5 stars. The artwork is breathtaking and I just want to cuddle the whole day with the wolf.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is ♥♥♥♥♥♥ bvllsh1t, can't reccomend it enough if you have stuffy nose.Apart from jokes, this amazing game makes use of a simple gameplay, graphics and story, yet it delivers extremely well. First: it's got very simple gameplay yet it still manages to be extremely original and entertaining (best absolute part in my opinion is winter part 1), bolstering satisfying combat, amazing bosses (definitely NOT the big boar tho, hitbox at release is too big, please do change that, don't be scared tho, you can always turn off and back on combat mode so you can't die and you can still beat the boss), very fun enviromental puzzles and puzzle bosses. The bosses are definitely not hard, they flow beautifully and a big emphasis is put on aesthetics, which brings me to the second point: it makes use of simple graphics, yet I've never seen better art direction in any other indie game, NOT EVEN JOURNEY, and Journey has been up until now my favorite game of all time. Btw, if you know Journey and you enjoyed it, you're gonna have a blast with this one, both aesthetics (even tho this one's way more colorful) and story are definitely inspired by that masterpiece and they managed to recreate that sense of beauty that I always longed for since playing that game for the first time. DO NOT get me started on the music, just... amazing. Anywas, third: the story. I am a SLUT for soft worldbuilding and dialogueless enviromental storytellying and this sh1t DELIVERS on that. Extremely simple story: world is really pretty, peaceful, nature is at it's prime and blablabla, SUDDENLY bad thing happens, world starts decaying, bad guys pop up everywhere and now you gotta fight them. The way this simple story is so elegantely told through visual art heightens that apparent banality into an extremely powerful emotional experience. Final thing: game progression. There's no level up system, just 3 phases: summer, autumn and winter. Throughout each one of these seasons the relationship between your human carachter and Neva the deer-wolf changes, and so does the way you interact with each other to face the world becoming ever more hostile: from you having to protect Neva, to mutually cooperating, to her helping you, it's a beautiful progression that just feels right. This game is unique in its genre and has definitely surpassed its already perfect spiritual master Journey. (a lil advice: don't bother exploring too much, the game is very linear and you won't miss virtually anything by just following the flow of it, I feel like the devs really meant for you to run through it as smoothly as you can, taking in the scenery combined with the amazing and everfitting music).TEN OUT OF TEN!!!

_childDocuments_.review: I had to make an appointment at the vet to put my dog, Rocket, down.  Everyone is telling me it's time, past time even.  He's a husky/beagle mix and he's 15 years old.  He's a great companion.  We got him from a rescue as a puppy, he was a stray.  He got me through hard times by demanding walks everyday just to get me out of the house, it helped immensely.  He had a couple strokes we think and he's probably got dementia.  He needs help getting up sometimes.  Needs to be carried inside from going to the bathroom because he can't get up the two steps in the house.  Sometimes he pees inside.  He'll growl a bit at me when I try to help him stand up or when he gets himself in a corner, or under a chair and can't back himself up.  My family says he's suffering but I don't know if I see it.  Maybe WE are suffering is what I tell them.  Anyways the appointment is made and now this game is out that I've been waiting for since it's reveal, and even though he's not allowed on the couch... _childDocuments_.review: This is a tricky one for me. I loved Gris, so I was very excited for this game. And this game has a lot of good stuff to it, the visuals are astounding and the music is excellent. But would I go to someone and tell them they should buy this game? No probably not. Why? Because it felt kinda half-baked. To put it in direct comparison with Gris: Gris put full focus on the platforming while Neva has both platforming and combat. Problem is, both feel undercooked. Not necessarily bad, but basic, like they were not fully developed. The combat is very basic buttonmashing and dodging. The puzzleplatforming has a lot more potential, but while there are certainly some interesting ideas, it feels that by the time they finished teaching you how to do something it is already over.I wouldn't say a bad time, but I also didn't rly have an exciting time with the game and knowing everything about it that I know now I would probably not buy it again.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva does not hold up to Gris.Visually the colors are beautiful but they are more generic colors related to nature's seasons. In Gris, the progressive addition of colors felt more powerful.Musically, the pieces are ok but not memorable and the music is not integrated very well into the action. In Gris the music was animating the environment (wind level) or rythming the boss encounters, here it is mostly background music oscillating between traversal and combat. Gameplay wise this is still smooth but the combat is not very interesting. The pacific approach of Gris was more interesting IMO.Finally, the story did not connect with me. It felt like a generic game about nature being corrupted, with very strong inspiration from Princess Mononoke but without the human aspect. The main emotional arc is about your relationship with Neva, but if you are not a dog person like me this feels weak compared to the more dramatic human thematic of Gris.All in all the game is not bad, but I finished it in 3 hours without the emotional impact of its predecessor.

_childDocuments_.review: WELL I HATE TO SAY THIS... BUT I WAS DISSAPOINTED..As a passionate admirer of Gris, I approached Neva with high expectations, eager to see how Nomada would expand on their unique blend of narrative, art, and music. From the moment the trailer dropped, I was captivated, pondering the depth of its story and the beauty of its visual design.In my review of Gris, I even crafted a poem, highlighting how Nomada’s artistry seamlessly intertwined with its compelling narrative. They truly set a high bar wit NEVA, creating an experience where art and music coalesced into something extraordinary. The combat in NEVA was engaging without overshadowing the emotional journey—an experience I wholeheartedly recommended to others.However, I must express my disappointment with Neva. Don’t misunderstand me; the game is undeniably beautiful and offers an impressive experience. Yet, for someone who loved Gris and hoped for something even more groundbreaking, I found it lacking.While Neva shines visually, it doesn’t quite achieve the same level of narrative integration as its predecessor. In Gris, the mechanics and storytelling were inextricably linked, creating a profound emotional impact. Neva, on the other hand, feels like it leans heavily on its stunning visuals to evoke feelings, which, while captivating, is something many games do today. In a landscape filled with artful titles on platforms like Steam, Neva risks blending into the crowd.The musical score, crafted by Brinilist, also left me wanting. In Gris, the music was layered and impactful, enhancing key moments of the story. In Neva, however, I struggled to find those moments where the music truly resonated. The variations felt minimal, and I often missed the emotional peaks that were so prevalent in Nomada’s earlier work.While I won’t critique the combat, as it met my expectations and functioned well, I found the level design to be one of the game’s strengths. The designers did an excellent job of teaching players the environmental mechanics and then challenging them with advanced puzzles, which was rewarding.In an era dominated by narrative-heavy games like God of War, Plague Tale, and Gris, Neva attempts to explore the theme of parenthood but falls short of leaving a lasting impact. It often resorts to conventional storytelling methods that feel superficial, relying on its stunning scenery to evoke emotion rather than a robust narrative.Ultimately, I believe Neva would have benefitted from existing in a world without Gris. It feels more like a DLC than a standalone experience, lacking the depth and innovation that made its predecessor so memorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I thoroughly enjoyed watching my SO play this game, and I also played it a bit. I do intend to finish it; however, I felt the need to post a review much sooner whilst the feelings linger. Let me tell you about it :>Neva is a platformer game whose narrative is driven with finely woven puzzle elements within a shattering realm. Story is that of a journey, subtly centered around breaking the 4th wall to evoke emotions in the player, portraying a need for a salient bond to the spirit of nature. It does it in such a subtle yet profoundly evocative manner, that you can’t simply put the controller down. You are drawn to it, as if it was a sweet and playful spring fragrance. You yearn to play a bit more, to sense yourself getting enriched by its lush visuals.However, the visual narrative has a peculiar spin, unlike most platformers. It revolves around evoking the sensation of motherhood, in this case - towards a wolf. And it does it so beautifully, too, that I couldn’t help but feel sad whenever I saw the wolf hurt. It would squeal, in pain. It’s heartbreaking, so you are instantly focused on helping the wolf, and this gives you determination to progress further through realms of serene nature, all whilst getting glimpses of longing beauty in the distance. And, even some spicy themes of loss that are to follow.You assume the role of this one girl called Alba, a brave adventurer and a protector, who is trying to navigate deeply shattered, yet magical world.Alba is accompanied by an orphaned wolf cub, and their bond becomes the heart of the game’s narrative, reflecting the essence of maternal love. As the game progresses, Alba nurtures and protects the wolf, finding herself shielded by it in return.Mechanics wise - the game transits through puzzles in a seamless visual way. However, right from the start you are given the ability of Double Jump mechanic. and the Sliding/Rolling prowess. It feels free and liberating for a platformer, as movement done right can make all the difference for an Indie game. A much-needed sense of freedom and agility is pivotal, and I will always advocate this as the crucial element for a platformer, as it just feels like properly engineered coherence.Nostalgia-wise, Neva returned me to the days of Sega Genesis. That’s no small feat, as I am ruthlessly critical. We have a strong emphasis on nature and environment, whilst the protagonist uses the spirits of the forest to both navigate the world, remove obstacles, and protect the homeland from harm. You can play as the Racoon in Pocahontas to solve puzzles and remove the obstacles. In Neva, this is done interactively by signaling the spirit of the Wolf. Not to mention that both Pocahontas and Neva were drawn/painted by hand. Both games share the message that goes in the blend of Coexistence, Restoration, Harmony, Nature, and Love. Neva encourages exploration without handholding. It is relying on subtle visual cues and an intuitive camera that nudges players toward the correct path.The theme of protecting the nature was immediately obvious, and it just clicked right off the bat.A simple visual que was enough, and driving the narrative forward with this method is quite potent.The sound is spot on. The music begins with serene piano melodies during exploration and intensifies into epic, choral orchestrations during battles, reminiscent of Nier: Automata. This shift adds a very latent emotional depth, turning every encounter into a testament to Alba’s bond with the wolf. Sound design is masterfully crafted, too. Listening through Sennheiser HD 800s paired with a Topping DX9, I found the audio design to be spot-on. I could pinpoint bird chirping, and I found the soundstage felt fully immersive. You’d find me always advocating that the video game’s audio is as essential as its visual and narrative elements. It adds to the immersion by enveloping the player in an intricate world of memories.So the game simply managed to capture the core elements of gaming by creating a platformer that is visually enchanting, emotionally rich, and musically immersive.Neva is filled with evocative storytelling, aquarelle visuals, and rich sound design. Everything lends together well, delivering a fantastic experience.The game felt like living inside a beautiful, resonant dream, and I would gladly recommend it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game arrived at a crucial time in my life, just like GRIS did back in the day. Nomada's first game helped me through my Mum's journey with cancer and the inevitable loss of her in 2021, and I just lost my Dad to the same illness two weeks ago. I finished the game tonight - and I can say with my whole heart it was magic. Despite the tragedy, there's resilience, hope and most of all... love. The gameplay is beautiful, the animation and art direction breathtakingly gorgeous, and so is the music and story. All I can say and recommend before playing, is simple: make yourself a nice cup of tea or your favourite drink, lower the lights around you and immerse yourself into this world of Neva and Alba. And have some tissues nearby - learn from my mistake!

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece!Roller coaster of feels from start to finish!GRIS was about colors and Neva is all about seasons.This game focused more on combat as other reviews has pointed out.You will start fighting alone at first and as the story progress, time changes, and Neva grows, she will join the fight too, from doing background timed attacks, to direct aimed attacks and then combination attacks with MC at final stage.Puzzles are still around but not as much as GRIS since here is as said more combat focused.Overall another great ride from start to finish, will try to 100% the achievements sometime soon.OVERWHELMINGLY RECOMMENDED especially for those that already enjoyed GRIS!

_childDocuments_.review: AVOID | LACKING | MAYBE | WORTHWHILE |  | UNMISSABLENeva is an side-scrolling action game with a huge focus on art direction/atmosphere. It also has some light platforming, puzzle, and combat elements in it. It is the latest game from the studio that developed Gris, which is probably immediately obvious to anyone who has played it (in the best way possible).If you enjoy beautiful environments, a compelling and wordless narrative, a game that includes multiple elements such as platforming, puzzles, and combat that aren't difficult, and incredible music, then Neva is sure to please. If you require a comparison to Gris, it is shorter (this took me ~5.5 hours whereas Gris took me ~8), easier, and less compelling, IMO, mostly from a narrative point of view. However, it is still an excellent game that stands on its own two feet. The inclusion of combat is a nice change and it is implemented well. The music is striking and lends to the overall atmosphere. My only real complaint about it is that a large part of the art design relied on a sort of haziness when I vastly prefer bright and crisp colors.All in all, if you enjoy Gris, I suspect you'll enjoy this game. If you haven't played Gris, but you're looking for a highly enjoyable experience in terms of overall gameplay, then this is a solid title to pick up. I probably only wouldn't recommend it to people who need really high action games to have fun.

It's not often I find real beauty in a video game but here it is.  Truly magnificent.

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece of art by Nomada. Everything is litteraly wallpaper material. The sound design and soundtracks are as good as what you can expect from Berlinist if you've loved playing Gris. I just love this. I loved the experience when playing Gris, I loved how it felt confronting Mourning. I loved how it felt to feel lighter after Gris. This is exactly the same here. The gameplay in "normal mode" is slightly more difficult than what you had in Gris, there are some parts where you have to die and retry, but it's never frustrating. Every little difficulty you overcome is rewarded by another beautiful painting and scenery. The game is neither too long, nor too short. The collectibles though, are making it a bit too difficult sometimes, but it's meant to be more challenging. I just wished my progression wouldn't be erased just after i started a new game with automatic same. I would have appreciated a feature that let's you pick the chapters to collect every single collectible to get the secret ending.I knew almost for certain how it would end, because you know frome the very begining that everything is related to seasons, and how it's cycle-related. I've been torn between 'please dont make this end' the more you get through this seasons cycle  but also I couldn't resist the urge to go on. This experience is very similar the the cycle of seasons in real life, you can't really fight it, and you know what's coming next. You appreciate every single piece of what the present has to offer you. I just saw the secret ending cutscene, and my mind is even more satisfied, and wondering exactly what that means at the same time. This game really echoed in me for two reasons : - When you are confronted with the loss of a beloved animal you know how it feels. - this reminded me a lot of the philosophy of Nighteyes the wolf in Robbin Hobb's books. Brilliant. Powerful, Cathartic. Thanks Nomada, Thanks Berlinist for making these 5 hours such a beautiful experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I received this as a gift. Kudos to Conrad and Nomada!Neva is a beautifully crafted artistic game, a perfect balance between challenge and immersion. _childDocuments_.review: The game is very pretty and doesnt feel bad to control but honestly thats all it has going for it and im honestly kimda disappointed considering how excited I was for it after gris but this kind of just feels like that game's shadow or something.where gris explores interesting themes through well thought out mechanics, this game has uninteresting combat.where gris has cool puzzles or platforming challenges, this game has combat.
