_childDocuments_.review: I'm glad to see such warm reception to such a delightfull game, almost everyone seems to love it except for those who are dead set on comparing it to gris. Ofcourse my brain did the same thing when playing this but Neva certainly is its own thing and should be evaluated as such. The game was an incredible journey from start to finish, with nearly every facet of it being perfect. First of all and most obvious are the impeccable visuals, each area wether vibrant or decayed is a feast for the eyes. With great composition and brilliant use of colour it is hard to resist taking screenshots every other step while playing this. I'm gonna check if Displate has any Neva posters after this, as the art direction most certainly deserve to be framed.Musically i was very happy to see Berlinist take up the mantle of composers for the game again, as Gris is still one of my favorite game OST's ever. There's a lot less vocals this time around which is a bit of a shame but didn't make the music any less impactfull. The melodies are beautiful and sombre when they need to or upbeat and relaxing when gameplay demands it so.  At times there was even some Ori vibes in the soundtrack which is my definitive favorite OST ever, so take that as you will. Ofcourse it is once again a must to pick up a copy of the soundtrack with your game (and slap in the art book for good measure). The OST is as much part of this game as the visuals so they compliment each other wonderfully whilst telling a beautiful story.Said story is once more told in a very heartfelt way, and while i personally didn't shed any tears as only a very select few games managed to do this, i can see many people who would. And that's a great thing, art is emotion and Nomada studios has mastered this craft. I really enjoyed the pacing, payoff and overal telling of the story. Said story has some conflict to it in the form of combat, and while this game won't make my top combat in games list it was still perfectly fitting to the game. Not hard, not super easy but very enjoyable nonetheless both regular combat and bosses. The former won't kill you often but the later can the first time you tangle with them. Luckily death isn't punishing as you're treated to a beautiful animation and a near instant respawn.Loading times in general were super short even on a HDD so i can imagine them being near instant on an SSD. The whole game is top notch on a technical level in fact. Not a single frame drop, bug or crash in my 4 hours with the game. This length is an issue for some at this price point but i know games like this are such memorable experiences that they're easily worth the price of admission. I don't think there's any excuse to not get this game as it's not hard (& can be made even easier for those who wish so), it's not long so it won't burn you out and it can probably run on very dated devices judging by the minimum specs. Just get this game, play it in one sitting and then spend the next few days thinking about it <3

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, this game connected with me on a different level. As someone who loves animals, the bond between the protagonist and Neva is extremely relatable. My cat Nala is everything to me, he is sleeping next to me as I type this. We take care of each other in difficult times and he is the most important thing in my life.Just like in Gris the visuals and sound design is out of this world. But next to the fun puzzles the studio introduces a fun and sometimes quite challenging combat system. Sometimes even interweaving them with their clever puzzle mechanics.The last hour of the game brought it through breathtaking heights with incredible vistas. I am sure I will be revisiting this game in years to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: As a big fan of Gris, I was very disappointed by this game. And don't get me wrong, it is pretty. But that's kinda the thing, it's nothing more. Just, pretty. I didn't like Gris because it was pretty, I like it because there was a boldness and a simplicity to it that made it very evocative emotionally, that it could get me to cry just through an intense combination of sounds and visuals. I would describe the appeal of Gris as raw abstract emotion. In Neva, the visuals are more detailed and busy, which means individual elements don't have as much impact. And this somewhat more realistic approach makes it more bland, more mundane. I'm seeing a forest. I am not seeing deeply stylised and abstracted shapes and textures that create a world and a story of their own. I think a similar thing can be said of the addition of voice acting. It grounds the game in a way that limits its evocative power. Music also makes itself more discrete, more held back. But music is what gives the game its emotional coloration, and tells you how intensely you should feel it. And the very powerful moments like in Gris when a new colour appears, where the music soars and visual effects invade the screen and beautiful animations transform the character and the landscapes. Those moments that were fascinating to me, leaving me shaken and wondering why I was so emotional. They are nowhere to be seen in this game.So all these aspects slide in the background, become flatter and more secondary to the experience. And, this isn't necessarily bad, it could allow a game to put the emphasis on something else. But what else is there? Gameplay? Gris didn't shine for its gameplay, even got criticised for it a little. And my assumption is that Nomada Studio attempted to fix that by putting more of it in Neva. But at no point did they take the time to consider the impact it would have on the experience as a whole, or if it was good.Unfortunately, this half-assed at gameplay makes the game tedious, repetitive and frustrating, in my opinion. And takes away from everything that makes Nomada's work interesting. The experience I had was that of a game made by people who put an emphasis on gameplay in it because they thought they should, but they never took the time to actually play with it. They were ticking boxes rather than taking the game where it wanted to go. In my opinion, the studio's response should have been the opposite. Saying "no, gameplay is not what are works are about, you got it wrong", and put even less of it. It's okay for games to not have gameplay, if it's not what they're about. But even if they chose to put an emphasis on gameplay, they could have done it well. We know it's possible because Gris with good gameplay exists: it's called Worldless. It results in a very different experience of course, but one that is just as memorable. The one thing that could have made this game interesting despite its many flaws is the wolf. The interactions and attachment to another agent in the game. Something reminscent of Ico or The Last Guardians. I think that would have been a cool thing to explore in a game like that. Exceeept... That's not what the game does. The dog is just there so you can say you can pet the dog. It's just there. It follows you, sometimes it doesn't, sometimes you have to press a button to call it, sometimes you have to go back and hug it. It is just a chore and there is no real connection happening here. But the best example of this missed opportunity is the combat I think. After the first chapter, the dog can fight alongside you. But it's not really fighting with you. You do your things, it does its things, and that's it. There is no collaboration. No mechanic is making you feel a closeness with this creature. It is just there. Anyway, I got a refund after the 2nd chapter. Maybe the game gets wonderful after that, I wouldn't know. And at this point I don't really want to. To me it feels like the devs did not understand what made Gris so special and powerful. And I am sad.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful piece of art, perfectly fitting for a one-weekend experience. Simple story and combat, gorgeous colors and heart fulfilling motives, heavily inspired by the "circle of life" theme in Miyazaki's works (especially Princess Mononoke).Is it better than Gris? No.Worth playing? Absolutely.PS.People who keep leaving comments like "game is boring", just keep playing COD or Fortnite, stay where you belong.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Atmosphere and music are killer but the gameplay is super thin, I also really like the visuals at parts but so much of the screen usually ends up being covered by fog or blown out gradients its hard to appreciate. If the gameplay formula was less repetitive I would have beat it but I could only make it to the end of chapter 2 before the apathy from boredom was too much to bear.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Gris was a masterpiece and Neva is another, as good or better. Both games follow a similar format - a platformer with the most stripped-down possible user interface, telling a moving story with almost zero text or dialogue. Not a long game - I apparently finished it in seven hours - but stunningly beautiful and with solid gameplay. It didn't seem that short due to all the different environments, a few interesting play dynamics, and a couple of punishing boss fights. Bravo Nomada. Most of the platforming is pretty easy so you can admire the beautiful art direction while you jump around, unlike some other games (I'm looking at you, Cuphead) where you have no time whatsoever to admire the art unless you want to die (again). Anyway, solid recommend, 10/10, paid full price on release, no regrets.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game. It pulled me in from the get go and took me on a breath-taking adventure. The music and the art alone was enough to tell the story without any dialogue or story text to distract me from the environment.  I'm a sucker for games with animal companions so this hit the mark.I only wish it had been longer.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's so good !I knew it would be good when I saw the first trailer, and I'm delighted to say it's fantastic so far.It's so gorgeous and the music is incredible, gameplay is very competent if not a bit floaty in combat (still works really well).Story seems quite standard (fighting the plague that destroys nature) but it's well done and the monsters design is very good.It seems fairly short but I don't mind if it's continue to be this good.Edit : Finished it in 3.6 hrs, incredible from beginning to end, utterly beautiful and gameplay kept evolving during the game so it was fresh all the way. _childDocuments_.review: Most beautiful game that I have ever played for sure!! The colours, the music, wow! Gris is a favourite game of mine, and this one was no disappointment either! The game play is tougher than their previous game Gris, a lot of new mechanics, but it makes for a fun and sometimes tricky play through. I sometimes had to put the game down and come back because I couldn't get through a part right away, but the feeling of finally getting through it was always amazing!Also, expect to get punched right in the heart more times than once!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I should start by acknowledging my biases. Gris is one of my absolute alltime favourite games. I played at the absolute perfect time in my life to let it impact me, and still do regularly. So when Nomada announced this game, my expectations were already incredibly high and my hype was unmatched. I played this game in a single four hour sitting today, and I absolutely adored it. I cried several times, including on the title screen and pause screen somehow? This is of course where my nostalgia comes in, because feeling nostalgic for Gris was the biggest reason for that I think. That being said, this game improves on Gris in a number of ways. The addition of combat makes it feel less like a walking sim, which I never minded, but I know some did. This also means we get Berlinist combat music, which is just as incredible as the rest of this beautiful masterpiece of a soundtrack, which is to be expected from Berlinist of course.All this is to say, if you enjoyed Gris, you will enjoy Neva. I highly recommend this for sure.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a cute little game that falls more on the artistic side but its gameplay doesn't lack depth, it's fun, a little maybe too short but it has nice things to offer - some interesting use of game mechanics, beautiful music on its background; you can finish it in a few hours and it is a really beautiful journey. It adds combat in it; it's weird if you think about it, an art game with a poetic tale using aggressive slashing? How does that work? But it works pretty nicely to the point it even becomes iconic.Its different than Gris and way more aggressive, while the other game uses grief in a poetical sense almost as a self-induced hikikomori dream, in NEVA you're thrashing your way in a quest that feels like a challenging rush, with some kind of urgency. And it remined me of Ghibli's Princess Mononoke because of the white wolves and also of the "eco-goth" vibes which really bring the artistry on front on this game through environments and color and it's definitely a step forward from its predecessor game in terms of arts quality: the world of "Neva" feels alive and has tridimensionality in is two-dimensional world even tough its art style is portrayed by an overlay of 2D art assets. Knowing this sometimes "broke" the wall between me and the piece of fiction looking at the technicality behind it all but I still found myself truly immersed at least at the chapters towards the game. And I found myself smiling at the screen several times. There are different style in both games but even then Neva reminded me of some scene in Gris even though those memories were drifting years apart in my mind, separated by countless other games; and it felt nostalgic somehow playing this.I did love the themes of nature in combination with its life cycle, and it does feel like something original in combination with something we already know. It is a beautiful, interesting often heart-breaking tale carefully crafted in an art game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After the game Gris, which I LOVED, I have to say that I loved Neva even more. Visually stunning accompanied with very beautiful and emotional music, the gameplay feels smooth, and Neva just sucks you in into it's beautiful world. Can't recommend this game enough to casual players, who just want to lay back and go on a little journey!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful both in visuals and narrative, and each chapter tugs at your heart in different ways. I only wish it was a longer, because when the gameplay really clicks and goes into flow, it is a magnificent experience. The music really elevates this game, making those triumphant moments soar and those sad moments devastate. A masterpiece on many levels. Don't forget to pet your magic deer puppy. She needs the pets.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; It's okay, Gris was better. Some things worked out, while some didn't. If you liked Gris, you will enjoy Neva. Looking forward to the next Nomada Studio game.After Gris, my expectations were high. What I can say that Neva definitely delivered was beautiful art and music. The gameplay didn't change that much since Gris and it's okay. The story was touching, but I'm not sure if I understood it completely. Puzzles were sometimes very interesting (especially in the Winter part) but often the case, they were just plain and simple (Summer, first parts of Autumn). These arguments are enough for me to recommend this to people who liked Gris. It's good enough to be enjoyable. BUT, the shortcomings are numerous.First of all: although the art was beautiful, it wasn't used to it full potential, especially in the Autumn Chapter. It was mostly overly dark and boring. I understand that it was a compromise between beautiful art in the beginning of the game and dark side of the story, so the art had to be adjusted accordingly when the story advanced. The fights were frustrating. The final boss was much easier to beat than normal fights with group of enemies (especially with the flying enemies). The idea that the HP of the enemies is not visible is absurd to me. I felt like I was hitting a wall sometimes. Especially when the fight was dragged out, it felt just boring and discouraging when I died for the 5th time and I still don't know how much hp the enemies had left. The fight mechanics were just too simple in my opinion. I hope that it was experimenting on the side of Nomada Studio and in the future they get rid of it, or they develop something better.Next, I don't understand why there was introduced the mechanic of riding on Neva, if it was not possible to use it in 90% of the chapter. It made no sense to me. If it was introduced, then the puzzle should have been adjusted to utilize this skill in any way. Lastly - minimalistic style of the characters. When we compare the faces of gris and the main character here, there is an absurd difference in the beauty. It was a big bummer. I loved how in Gris there were closeups on the main character and we could admire her beauty. In Neva it is completely opposite - the face is compromised of 5 strokes with minimal details. The same with Neva (dog). I didn't like the minimalistic art in these cases.I wrote up that much critique is because I had high expectations of this game after completing Gris. In most of the aspects Neva delivered, but the truth is there were numerous places, where the game could be better. Nevertheless, I am looking forward to the next Nomada Studio game
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I can't give this game a thumbs down as there's too much beauty in it and I want to support the great dev team, but I really REALLY HATED THE COMBAT. Even on the easier setting, it took me out of the experience every time. I wish I could've just turned it off. If they make another in this series (and I really hope they do!) I hope they go back to the non-combat format (or at least have an option to turn it off completely).I also would love more puzzles and for them to maybe be slightly more challenging, but that's not as important. The most important aspect of these games for me is having beautiful worlds to explore, and they did amazingly on that front! I would say the worlds in Neva are even more beautiful and epic than those of Gris. They made me feel things! I just wish I could've explored them without having to pause and mash buttons every few minutes!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who picked up GRIS for nearly nothing, and dropped it for not catching my attention fast enough, I nearly did not begin my journey with Nomada Studio. One night, I decided to give GRIS a go, and finished it in one sitting. One of the most beautiful, artful games I have ever played and likely ever will play. Pensive, gorgeous and with an incredible soundtrack, I loved every minute of the short but sweet platformer.NEVA took what worked with GRIS, and elevated it beyond what I thought possible. I bought it day 1, because I knew that I would be in for something special no matter how long the game was. The artstyle was changed, but made more beautiful, there was actual combat in between and against the beautiful vistas, the platforming was just as interesting, although having lost the steampunk aesthetic, could not be as visually stunning. And finally, I was accompanied by a beautiful and powerful animal that grew alongside me and eventually could help me with platforming and combat, tying all the aspects of the gameplay together. Short and sweet, just like its predecessor, Nomada have made a wonderful game that is well worth the relatively cheap asking price and perfect to curl up on the couch and bask in the environment and soundscape. 7.5/10 - short, sweet, beautiful and well worth the price

_childDocuments_.review: I am so conflicted, to be honest the only reason i choose to recommend it is because of the art & sound design.[Do not take note of playtime - i've left the game idle far too many times - it totals around 4 hours]So let's talk about the good:- Art is amazing and that's not a surprise, but Gris had somehow much more impactful design. This one is a bit flat. - Music is great as well.- The platforming is actually really fun for the most part and I personally think the game didn't need combat.The bad:- The combat is really annoying - yes, when you learn the move sets of the enemies everything is easier but the hitboxes are imo terrible - you never know when you're touching an enemy if you're gonna take damage or not. That oftentimes feels really bad, especially when you have combat with multiple enemies/moving platforms which is often the case. I quit the game many times out of rage from fights such as these.I think Nomada should stick to platforming as they are pretty good at it and skip combat. There are some amazing sequences in a few mirrored areas that prove that this is where Nomada shines (besides art & music).Story wise I feel conflicted as well - I did not experience as much emotions as with Gris, but even previous title aside, I didn't get a satisfying enough resolution or justification on why things were happening.Overall I think Neva is still worth experiencing but for me it's a step down from their previous title. Still, I'll happily try any other game they make, should they choose to continue making games.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game and have taken a few days to process.  This game is gorgeous.  The music and the graphics, just like Gris, are elevated from anything I've seen.  That being said, I bought Gris because it was recommended to me by someone who struggles with mental health issues, as do I.  Gris may have saved my life.  I wanted that feeling from Neva, but it never came.  With Gris, I could apply my own struggles with mental health with what she was going through in the game.  The developers may not have intended that, but to me, gaming is reflective of life.  I had difficulty going into my own struggles with Neva.  Maybe it's because I'm in a better place, maybe the struggles and battles in Neva were meant for someone with their own way to look at it as healing.  Gris was life, Neva was a fun game to play.  The puzzles aren't as difficult as Gris, but that may be because I knew what to look for because of Gris.  The bit with the mirrors was epic....great job on that!  Super fun to try to figure it out, and once I figured out WHAT I needed to do I was still VERY challenged by trying to actually do it.  I LOVE everything you do, Nomada.  I'll always see your name and buy that game, forever and ever.  Devolver...you are so diverse and when I see you've made a game, I'm there for it too.  Thank you for sharing your gifts with me.  If you're reading this because you're wondering if you should buy this game....buy both Gris and Neva.  I promise you won't regret it.  I've played Gris 4 times and will definitely play Neva at least two more times.  I went straight back to play Gris again when I finished Neva.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful and sad. "I've only had this puppy for 5 minutes, but if anything happened to her I would kill everyone in this room and then myself." You can pet Neva, find food for her, soothe her when she's upset, ride on her back, and even help her climb up when her jump falls a little short of clearing a gap. _childDocuments_.review: Neva is a beautiful, short, 2D puzzle adventure, much like Nomada studio's debut game, Gris. The art style, while different from the distinctive staining water colors of Gris, are breathtaking nevertheless.The sedate beauty of the scenes, along with the magical background score sometimes lulls you into a numb navigation of the game world, but then there are moments where it jolts you and demands attention. Unlike the solitary experience of Gris, Neva introduces the titular companion creature which makes the game experience fresh, dynamic and serves as the hook that makes you invested in the events of the game all the more. By choosing a more well trodden nature/corruption theme, I feel Nomada may have played it safe. The more abstract and personal journey of Gris felt a lot more bold and rewarding. Even the game play elements, especially in some sections made me feel I was playing Gris all over again, which is not necessarily a bad thing! Those subjective observations aside, Neva is a great followup by Nomada and I look forward to more of their remarkable artistic expression along with their brilliant musical collaboration with Berlinist.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Much like Nomada's previous game, GRIS, this is a beautiful piece of art that, in my personal opinion, everybody should experience at least once (unless you can't stomach harm to animals - in which case, stay far away). Featuring striking environmental design, emotional musical accompaniment, pulse-pounding combat encounters, and a gut-wrenching visual narrative, Neva will leave you absolutely breathless. The option of either Adventure Mode (where combat has risk of death and enemies have additional health) or Story Mode (squishier enemy encounters with no deaths) allows the game to remain just as accessible as GRIS for players looking only to enjoy the overall gameplay and story, while offering a new, more difficult experience in Adventure Mode for those seeking challenge.Character movement is fluid and mostly intuitive, at first building off of basic, familiar mechanics from GRIS, then progressively adding fresh ideas to the mix of abilities which differentiate Neva from its predecessor. Combat is mostly simple, but enemy encounters and boss fights are varied enough along the way that it never feels tiresome or repetitive. My only nitpick with the controls comes from a few sections late in the game where the platforming difficulty curve felt like it peaked a little too high for a casual experience in Story Mode.Chapter selection is unlocked after finishing the game on either mode and you can go back to find all of the hidden secrets in each chapter without having to fully replay. This makes getting all achievements a bit easier for those who seek completion.The story and overall presentation borrow familiar aesthetics from GRIS, Journey, and the Studio Ghibli film Princess Mononoke (which is no surprise, as GRIS featured a nod to the same movie), while taking some uniquely dark twists along the way to set Neva apart. As mentioned at the beginning of the review, this is not a game for anybody who has difficulty seeing animals die or be in perilous situations, as the core gameplay and story often lean heavily on the struggles to be overcome by your furry companion. If you have the stomach for it though, Neva offers an intensely emotional journey which will not be soon forgotten. Much of the success of that narrative comes from the impeccable level design, built specifically for environmental storytelling, and another brilliant soundtrack from Berlinist that can tear at the heartstrings all on its own.Pros:+ Satisfying gameplay mechanics and progression+ Memorable and emotional story+ Beautiful art design and visuals+ Outstanding soundtrackCons:- Significant content warning for animal death, harm, and distress- Some platforming sections which could prove frustrating to casual playersScore:9/10 - Highly recommended
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Flawless soundtrack, art, and animation on par with Gris, their prior game. 3-4 hours of walking through wallpapers you could only expect from Nomada. It introduces combat though gameplay is still very simple. I was impatient in numerous walking sections, which there are many of, but was never bored. I did not relate with the characters or story much. There are higher stakes and animal themes which I know some get more emotional over than others. Not a flash in the pan like Gris, but I am eager for more of this quality over length to see what games are capable of.

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an incredibly beautiful and emotional experience. Neva's simplicity is part of its charm, allowing the stunning art and heartfelt storytelling to shine. The emphasis on storytelling is what truly sets this game apart. The only thing I would have appreciated even more would have been a slightly longer game.I highly recommend Neva to anyone looking for a game that offers both aesthetic beauty and emotional depth.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game. Nomada Studio has done it again. While I quite liked their previous game, Gris, this felt like a step up from that. Neva is one of the best-looking 2D platformers I've ever played, accompanied with sweet music and more involved gameplay than Gris, I loved it. Some of the combat is way too simple, but at other times, it can be quite challenging. It's a nice mix. The main thing that makes Neva great is its story, though. It's simple, but very effective and emotional, and it draws several allegories to humans' effect on nature. Easy recommendation.

_childDocuments_.review: At about five hours it is a bit short, but it's also one of the few such games I actually feel like I may want to replay, so there's that. It does manage to avoid being repetitive, as it introduces new enemies (and new abilities as Neva grows up) as well as new environments.Art style is similar to GRIS but it doesn't seem to be a sequel as such. It's a lot less abstract and it's a lot clearer what the heck is happening. Music is also pretty great.There is combat that can be fairly challenging if you're playing it on Adventure mode, but also fun once you get the hang of it. There is also Story difficulty that does not track health/hitpoints, making it a lot less frustrating if you don't really care about combat as such.Platforming for the main path isn't particularly challenging. Reaching some of the collectibles can be a bit difficult. But the difficult ones are generally puzzles that require some thought and attention, rather than hardcore platforming skills.In some contexts the Y button does more than just interact with Neva. It's easy to miss some of the achievements on the first run if you're not looking out for that. But you can also go back to specific parts of specific chapters so you don't have to replay the entire game if you just want to 100% the achievements.Expect cuteness. Bring tissues.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A total evolution on what made Gris an excellent game. Amazing visuals, audio, music and storytelling. The combat is a great addition to the gameplay loop and the puzzles are both more challenging and interesting, yet it never feels unfair or impossible to beat. The story is wonderfully told and hits right in the heart. Everything is told visually and lets the player come to their own conclusions and interpretations, even though there is a very solid and clear message told by the symbolism and subtext of the game. Amazing work!This one is my Game of the YearEnhorabuena al equipo de Nomada <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Having been mesmerised by Gris—with its beautiful watercolour aesthetics and poignant story of grief—I had high expectations going into Neva, and I’m thrilled to say that it didn’t disappoint! The developers of Gris have once again captured magic, but in a refreshingly different way.Right from the start, I was enchanted by the shift in the art style. While Gris flowed with smooth watercolours, Neva opts for something more textured—repeating small blotches, almost like a brush's distinct impression scattered across a canvas. It’s an interesting evolution, still breathtaking but in a more tactile, raw manner. The difference feels deliberate, bringing both depth and a refreshing change, while remaining visually accessible for any viewer to easily perceive and appreciate.The music, another stronghold of Gris, makes a powerful return but with a new flair. Given the addition of combat in Neva, the score rises to the occasion. It swells during intense moments, giving the fights a heroic and inspiring edge, yet it never overshadows the beautiful art. Instead, it perfectly complements it, enhancing the emotional depth and atmosphere while allowing the visuals to shine. The combat itself is simple, which I appreciated, as it allowed the core elements—art and music—to remain in focus, reinforcing the game's identity as a work of art in motion.If I had one wish, it would be for a photography mode! There are so many stunning frames throughout the game, and I found myself yearning for a way to capture them. Whether it's a shot with Alba or Neva (or both or neither), having that extra layer of interaction would have been delightful!I have to say—calling for Neva never got old! I found myself petting and interacting with Neva often :')  (It added a personal touch to the game.) To summarise, Neva beautifully blends evolving art, enchanting music, and engaging combat to create a journey that feels both familiar and fresh. It's a game that, much like Gris, leaves the player with something to think about—though perhaps not to the same degree of impact. However, sometimes parental love doesn’t need to be as profound and complex as grief to resonate deeply.

_childDocuments_.review: Save the doggo, save the world.From the same developer that created GRIS, Neva brings a lot of what made GRIS great, and adds a combat system to the mix.  The combat is overall fairly solid, but I will say that players who are a bit more on the casual side may have more trouble with this game compared to GRIS.  There is a Story/Casual mode available to make it easier, but I don't have experience in what is actually easier.  I believe it said there are no deaths in that mode at least, which should help some casual players out a lot.Neva is quite appealing visually, and there are definitely a few in game scenes that are great to look at, as well as cutscenes that are enjoyable to watch.  Some puzzles can be a bit tricky, but overall I didn't have too much trouble with them.  The combat is solid, but like I said earlier, could be a bit difficult for some casual gamers.  The sounds in the game are nice, and both main characters are well done.  Definitely a fun experience, and I'll soon be getting the last few achievements I missed to fully complete the game.Both Neva and Gris are definitely worth playing, just know that Neva has more actual combat.  My personal take is that GRIS is a bit better overall, and I think I really enjoyed the color coded areas of GRIS a bit more too.  I did find the combat decent overall, but not enough to where it overtakes the other parts of the game that GRIS did a little better.  I believe they are similar game length as well, and visually you can see a lot of similarities between the two when it comes to the structures and just overall feel.I definitely recommend Neva, and also GRIS, if you haven't played that game either.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Neva felt like playing Princess Mononoke The Game. The animations were beautiful and music was emotive.But despite the short length and generally enjoying my time with it, I definitely felt like I had to push through to finish the game.Without spoiling anything, the abstract nature of the story didn't grab me and I didn't quite understand the point of it. It was trying to say... something? I understood the metaphors but didn't find it compelling. There were large swaths of the game where I was simply just holding down the directional button/stick to go in one direction - it's almost like I was being forced to "see how beautiful everything is!" The platforming and combat was pretty basic and didn't really evolve, and the puzzles were alright.I have mixed feelings about my experience with Neva, but still positive. I do recommend it because I think it's important to support studios that clearly pour a lot of love and passion into their games.

_childDocuments_.review: I liked this game, but would struggle to recommend it given it's short length and overall lack of depth. This isn't a walking simulator by any means, but aside from stylistically exceptional visuals, all other aspects of the gameplay are weak to mid at best. There are some interesting mechanics, but the game is just too short to ever really fully explore or appreciate them. Even the stunning artwork seems to stumble in places with some assets that (in my opinion at least), seem jarring and out of place. I see little replay value in the game either as other than "find the secret flowers", there isn't anything to do. [1]Sound and music is on point for the themes and the characters, Neva especially, are adorable (disclosure, I love dogs so this was an easy sell). Clearly much of this being inspired by Princess Mononoke.Would I pay £16.99 for the game? No, there are far more engaging and long lasting indie titles available on Steam that offer much better value. Would I pay maybe £8.99 for the game. Yes I probably would, just to experience the visuals. At full price however, I'd say give it a miss.I will now however, go and give my 11yo Samoyed a long hug as the themes of loss in this game has reminded me how precious she is and how little time we may have left![1] I'd love btw, for someone to correct me if I'm wrong on this, but I didn't see anything other than linear progression in the story.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall I would recommend this game, but for those wondering how it compares to Gris, personally I would say that Gris was the superior game. Gris and Neva share some obvious design elements, and both games are pretty and feature some fun and interesting platforming, but I think Gris was stronger narratively, as well as more interesting musically and artistically. One big and obvious difference between the games is that Neva features combat, and this, as well as more precise and difficult platforming, makes the game feel more punishing, while I found Gris to be a more relaxing experience. All of this brought me back to Gris several times, whereas I don't think I will be replaying Neva. Of course, your experience may very well differ if the themes of Neva resonate with you more strongly, or if combat and more challenging platforming are right up your alley. If you found Gris challenging enough, or are looking for a more laid-back experience, you might want to try the game on story mode, or otherwise give it a miss entirely.

_childDocuments_.review: I do not recommend this game, but it is only after passing the first few levels that the disappointing features become apparent. This is a game in which a protagonist and her pet wolf maneuver through obstacles.  Similar themes are found in the Japanese movie, Princess Mononoke. The graphics are beautiful. I have not encountered any puzzles, despite the Puzzles tag. It's mostly action-adventure/physics/hand-eye coordination. Unfortunately, the keyboard controls (as shown in the game settings) do not advance the character to the degree necessary to succeed, especially in the harder version. Had to switch to the easier version. This offers fewer features to replace the glowing fountains of life, so there's a lot of wasted space. Additionally, the character mysteriously cannot leap to reach a glowing hibiscus/lily flower - but she can leap exactly the same distance to traverse the level. The control triggers and responses seem arbitrary. The fight scenes do not produce better results from planning attacks vs simply button-mashing and there's no real satisfaction. I could not get a refund because level one is very easy and it was only after awhile that I noticed the problems in this game. So, I'm playing it through, but I would not purchase it again.

_childDocuments_.review: As a successor to GRIS, Neva has a lot to live up to. I believe that Nomada Studio delivers. I appreciate that some reviews don't feel that Neva has the depth GRIS does, and I'm not one to compare two mediums, but I have to state my disagreement outright. There's a difference in approach with each game. For one, grief is a universally-felt emotion. It's inescapable. Anyone who played GRIS will find an easy self-insert with the player character. However, many of us can only imagine what it's like to claw and scream and beg your way forward in a world that isn't built for you anymore.-No spoilers, but some social commentary that might spoil the theme for the smartypantses in the room-That's where Neva absolutely shocked me. I was elated to see a black woman as our protagonist, especially in an adventure series. It wasn't until the end of the game that I realized how absolutely necessary it was that the protagonist be a black woman. Nomada Studio has a clear point they want to make. Sure, we can relate what happens in the game to climate change and greed and colonialism, but it's much closer to home than any of those themes.I adore this game. GRIS struck me in the gut. But Neva gently took my hand and flipped me upside-down.Aside from the theme, the combat does feel unpolished. I don't care too much because I'm not invested in this as a combat game, but if you care, that's between you and your god. Additionally, Neva's progression feels well-engineered, but I wish some of the elements (eg, achievements and collectibles) helped with the world-building.In short, Neva is gorgeous. If you want depth, it's staring you in the face. You may have to go outside of yourself for this one. It's a doozy.11/10 I would kill God and punch the sun for the goodest doggo.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifully crafted game, very reminiscent of Hayao Miyazaki's work in game form. I haven't played a game like this in a while but I saw the trailer a few months ago at some game awards show and added it to my wish list. I'm on the Winter chapter now and it hasn't disappointed. Great art and a protagonist that just happens to be black, something that has no bearing on her character at all...as it should be. _childDocuments_.review: **Before reading this review, please keep in mind that this is MY opinion and shouldn't affect how other people view this game**The moment I heard about this game, I knew I needed to get it. As somebody who truly loved Gris, I was excited about it, which was only heightened when the game was finally released. I decided to play it right away and man, I loved it. The story is so beautiful and the visuals and the music definitely pair well with the emotions that the game was trying to convey. It definitely made me tear up a little as well, but that comes as no surprise. Won't go into details for the story as to avoid anybody to get spoiled.Overall, the experience was pretty phenomenal. _childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a neutral option because I don't think Neva is bad, but it could've been a lot better. It didn't do well enough to earn a thumbs up from me, but it doesn't warrant a thumbs down either. I eventually settled on a thumbs down by the logic that it's currently 'very positive' on the steam store, and I think it should be a bit lower than that.The main problem I had is that it was too similar to Gris visually - a woman with hair that doesn't go past her shoulders and flowy clothes walks left-to-right a lot through a watercolour-y land with strong colours and symmetrical architecture with a lot of arches and towers. She collects white dots to activate big floating squares, and is attacked by a black, amorphous monster that changes shape fluidly and screeches. Personally, I just found it really hard to get immersed because I was so often being reminded of Gris and couldn't stop comparing them while I was trying to enjoy the game.Later areas innovated more (I loveddd ), but I wish the game pushed itself to be more different in aesthetics and music. Especially since the visuals are simplified down (understandably, considering the more detailed world of Neva), it sometimes feels like a cheap copy of Gris' design. That's not to say it's bad, it's just too similar to something better.Speaking of different, Nomada studios did an excellent job of adding combat - movement is fluid and easy to control, and the attacks feel intuitive and seamless. Getting Neva to . I have no complaints about that aspect of the game, but the non-combat parts can drag a bit. It gets more fun when movement goes in other directions , but Neva has quite a few sections that are simply walking/dashing along long stretches of perfectly horizontal terrain. While Gris was slow and meditative, Neva verges on slow and repetitive. TL;DR: Good game, but probably a lot better if you haven't played Gris first.Also I am a bit biased tbf because I'm neutral about dogs. It would've needed to do more to get me emotionally invested in Neva - at the end

_childDocuments_.review: It is a good game, but it does not impress me much like KRIS did.There's not much to say about the visuals. But I get the idea that this game is pretty combat focused so it's not that much of a big deal but still I'm a little bit disappointed. As to combat, it is engaging and requires some focus. However, without any skills supporting (except for Neva's help) the combat sometimes feels repetitive. It it decent but it's not outstanding. Boss fights are decent too yet they're too basic to be something unique. Also the game features couple of Ori's style ''escape run'' but they are honestly pretty mediocre.The game is pretty short, I finished it in 4 hours. There are only 4 chapters. And even as short as that the whole chapter 1 is like a ''tutorial chapter'' and the chapter 4 is like an ''ending chapter'' so there's only 2 chapters that actually matter.Neva is cute and I can pet her. _childDocuments_.review: If it would be possible to give a neutral review I would. The new protagonist is essentially a reskinned Gris, now a Black female samurai. She looks, runs, and jumps almost identically. It's the same game with a new coat of paint. They haven't even tried to create something new.Gris sold well, received critical acclaim, and won awards. Yet, the developers inexplicably decided to address criticisms by adding combat, weapons, and death. These additions might be beneficial in other circumstances, but they already had a masterpiece with global recognition. They've tried to fix what wasn't broken.Gris took place within the subconscious of a young woman grieving the loss of her mother, which explained why she was the only human present. Neva, however, is set in the physical world. WHY is the protagonist alone? Where is everyone?Why am I forced to babysit this creature the entire game? I feel nothing towards it. With the statue mother in Gris, the player's connection developed gradually. Through imagery, we understood her importance, her suffering, and the reciprocal nature of our relationship. The theme was developed, allowing us to empathize—that's how it works. Here, it's just, "Here's your furry Pokémon, now babysit it." I don't want to! Seriously... I don't want to do this. I don't want to babysit a kid. I don't care about him; let him go grow a tree out of his head in the forest. I'm a Black feminist samurai on my way to African Japan; leave me alone!The monster, the black one with the white mask, is ripped straight from "Spirited Away." If you haven't seen it, watch it.The forest being infected with black ink blots is stolen from "Princess Mononoke." Again, just straight-up plagiarism.Regarding the visuals: The technical level is similar to Gris, but that game's surreal world masked its limitations.  The game is way too short, it will take you about 4-5 hours to complete it, hence I cannot recommend it at full price. It costs 76 rmb (10.70 USD)  in China region. I would say something in 45-50 rmb (6-7 USD) price range would be fair. Hence, wait for discount if you want to get it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Not a bad game on its own, but compared to Gris does feel inferior in pretty much every way. I might change this to a positive review once I've read other people's theories regarding the story and ending. Right now, the story as I interpret it, falls flat. It just feels like a generic nature good vs outside forces (dark) = bad. I couldn't really detect anything deeper in it. The music in this game is also quite forgettable (compared to Gris), which I believe to be because Gris intertwined gameplay and music, making the music feel part of the world. Here's it's mostly just background noise. I also think Gris did a better job in the art department. Blending abstract and organic looked wonderful in that game. And it worked because Gris was all about emotion, which is both raw (organic) and human (abstract). In Neva organic and ''human'' / abstract are clearly seperated, making it all feel a bit cold. As if anything other than naturalistic is not good, to be avoided. Again, this view of mine might change once I've read more theories regarding the story and ending. I understand that Gris set the bar pretty high, so this might just come across as rambling, but these are just my two cents.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: GRIS is my most favourite game ever. No other game has left a mark on me like GRIS. It's a masterpiece. I was expecting either an equal or elevated experience in Neva and I have never been more disappointed in a sequel in any form of media. Okay, maybe Boruto is a worse sequel but I digress.For me, Neva is a wholesale downgrade from GRIS. The platforming, puzzling and narrative lack any depth. The whole game has nothing to say. Its generic and unoriginal, it feels uninspired. While the combat can be fun and there were some highs, the combat really feels like a distraction from the lackluster story and platforming. I can't imagine what people who played the narrative focused version went through; without the combat there is barely a game. Again, only in comparison to GRIS. The mirror level was the only spark of GRIS-esque brilliance, but was so short lived, and still falls short without a story to ground it.And on the note of the story, the ending would be clever if what came before was interesting in any way. The whole time I wondered why Neva never showed any pain, regret, anger or frustration for losing her mother. It makes more sense why it was such a empty revenge story, because it never was one in the first place. Regardless, the only progression in Neva is her size and abilites. Then there's the main character , she doesn't really go through any narrative journey. She's there, she calls for Neva, she fights and then rinse repeat. There is no real masterful subtlety in this game, there's no real reason to connect with the characters and there's no reason to replay this game, especially after that ending.Sigh, if this was a first game from a studio I would say the game is fine, nothing to write home about but fine. Very pretty but fine. I did have fun, sweaty moments with the combat and some puzzles but the journey to those moments was so empty. Unbelievably empty or to be fair unbelievably empty in comparison to GRIS. GRIS was brilliant from head to toe and it arguably has one of the most memorable indie soundtracks out there. Neva's soundtrack, like it's story, like it's platforming will be memorable only in that it is a reminder of my disappointment. This whole game is memorable in a way it neva intended to be, and that's why I have to dub it the Joker 2 of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: This takes its place among my top three games of all time. I have cried again and again playing this game, and I can honestly say that it is a piece of art which has truly changed my outlook on family and motherhood. I do not say this lightly, of course. I would like to keep this review more about Neva, but I will say that I do love Neva far more than GRIS. While GRIS is beautiful, and its exploration of grief is enrapturing, it pales in comparison to the sheer weight of emotional impact (at least for me). I see myself playing this game every so often just to get a good cry in. I counted how many times: 12, four of which were ugly cries. Keep in mind Neva is not a long game either - I cried approximately once every 15 minutes. I encourage anyone who loves GRIS to play this game, and for those who haven't played either, I'd say to give it a shot anyway. Any acclaim I can give this game would simply not be adequate.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is an absolute masterpiece! From the very first moments, I was captivated by its breathtaking art style and deeply emotional narrative. The game masterfully weaves a story of loss, growth, and love, all while immersing you in a beautifully crafted world that feels alive and vibrant.The gameplay is smooth and engaging, perfectly complementing the storytelling. I loved how the puzzles and challenges were not only fun but also tied seamlessly into the emotional beats of the game. Every moment felt purposeful, and the connection between the protagonist and their companion was genuinely moving.Neva isn’t just a game—it’s an experience. It left me reflecting on its themes long after the credits rolled. If you’re looking for a game that combines stunning visuals, heartfelt storytelling, and meaningful gameplay, Neva is a must-play! Highly recommend it to anyone who enjoys indie gems that truly stand out.

_childDocuments_.review: I will proudly say this is the most beautiful game I have ever played. The cinematics are breathtaking, and I particularly enjoy the shift of camera focus throughout it. The soundtrack in this game is so moving. It tells the story for you, and the score perfectly captures the emotion of what's at hand. From the story, to the environment, to the SOUNDTRACK, it's absolutely amazing and this will be a game I will encourage everyone to play. _childDocuments_.review: I streamed this game for Extra Life just a couple days after it was released. It immediately drew me in with its gorgeous art style and music, punched me in the feels, and then pulled me along to find out what happened next! The environment is full of things to discover, intuiting how to navigate the terrain and puzzles with minimal UI to distract you, and leaving you wondering when the next conflict will jump at you. I also recommend acquiring the extra items like the art book if the visuals are what appeal to you most--there are full pages of nothing but plant designs! Half of my Steam Awards nominations are unapologetically for Neva.

_childDocuments_.review: I knew the games of this studio thanks to Gris, at the time, made me enjoy it beyond what I would expect from a platformer. Of course, as soon as I heard about the upcoming release of Neva, contrary to what I usually do, I pre-sold the game. I was not disappointed, the game is that reset of calm that we all need, it has the necessary action, without reaching the level of frenzy. The art is a visual ride from start to finish. And also the game has a message without falling into the fanaticism of the wrongly called `woke` movement.It is impossible to play it and not feel in the world of Ghibli with Princess Mononoke. Buy the game, whether it is on discount or not, it is worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a true testament to how video games can transcend entertainment to become pure art. Visually, Neva is a living painting. It’s impossible not to stop and admire the sheer beauty of its hand-drawn animations and vast color palette, which rival even the most celebrated animated works. The environments feel alive and layered, drawing comparisons to the works of Miyazaki. The soundtrack by Berlinist wraps it all together, evoking melancholy and hope in equal measure, a perfect complement to the game’s stunning visuals.

_childDocuments_.review: A Masterpiece of Emotion and AtmospherePlaying Neva felt like rediscovering the magic I experienced when I first played Hollow Knight. This game is a heartfelt journey, beautifully crafted in every aspect.First, let’s talk about the art style. It’s simply breathtaking. Every frame feels like a painting, blending delicate details with vibrant colors. The world feels alive, with stunningly designed environments that seamlessly shift between awe-inspiring beauty and haunting desolation.The music deserves special praise as well. It's not just a soundtrack; it’s an emotional compass, guiding you through the highs and lows of the story. The way it adapts to your actions and the unfolding narrative creates a deeply immersive experience.The controls are incredibly responsive, making every movement feel intuitive and precise. Whether you're navigating intricate landscapes or engaging in combat, the gameplay flows effortlessly. Speaking of combat, while it isn’t overly challenging, it’s undeniably fun. The straightforward mechanics make battles enjoyable and accessible, adding to the game’s overall charm without detracting from its emotional depth.But what truly sets Neva apart is how it makes you feel. It captures that rare magic of a game that’s not just a series of levels but an emotional experience. It’s a game that will linger in your mind long after the credits roll, much like Hollow Knight did for me.TLDR: If you’re looking for a game that blends stunning visuals, evocative music, tight gameplay, and engaging combat into an unforgettable experience, Neva is a must-play.

_childDocuments_.review: I've adopted Neva since the day the first trailer came out, which I cried every time I watched it. Now that I've gotten to play it, it's so worth the wait and this will have a big place in my heart. I love wolves, I love nature spirits - I love fighting against corruption upon mother nature (love their concept). This game is so breathtaking, the story is beautifully told, and it's heartbreaking at times. I hope to see more, if not more of Neva somehow but different story, same universe - maybe.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is definitely a step in the right direction for Nomada Studio.While Gris was an impressive audiovisual experience, its gameplay mechanics were quite barebones. Neva takes the core mechanics of Gris and improves on them by adding combat and interactions with the animal companion. This results in a more challenging gameplay experience, which experienced players should find more appealing. On the other hand, there is also a story mode suited for more casual gamers that just want to enjoy the beauty of the game without the extra challenge.Speaking of beauty, the art style of Neva is as breathtaking as that of Gris. The ambiance of the game is a lot darker compared to Gris, but there are also some impressively colorful scenes projecting hope and the feeling of renewal. One obvious influence when it comes to the art style is Studio Ghibli. One can see Hayao Miyazaki's influence when it comes to both the enemies and the animals.A review of a Nomada Studio game wouldn't be complete without mentioning the music of Berlinist and the way it blends with the art style to guide the flow of the story. Every note enhances the experience, be it a calm moment enjoying the ambience or the heat of battle.I must admit I was worried whether Nomada Studio would be capable of repeating the success of Gris. But the creators of Gris proved they can not only replicate the brilliance of their previous game but even improve on it.

_childDocuments_.review: In Neva, you embody a child of nature who must confront a dark, sinister force corrupting her homeland. The storytelling is entirely wordless, relying on stunning visuals and your actions to convey the narrative. The game is visually mesmerizing, with vibrant color palettes that shift dramatically as your journey spans all four seasons. The soundtrack at times reminded me of a mellower Godspeed You! Black Emperor record, which feels thematically perfect. While it doesn’t quite reach the dramatic crescendo peaks of Godspeed, it excels at building tension effectively and conveys that light melancholic mood pretty good.While GRIS was primarily defined by its hand-painted visuals, Neva shifts the focus toward a more gamified experience. It combines its artistic charm with light combat and puzzle mechanics that, though not overly demanding, fit seamlessly into the game’s overall flow.Your companion is a white wolf-like creature that undergoes significant growth throughout your journey. In the first chapter, she hesitantly jumps over large gaps and often needs reassurance and support from the protagonist. By the next chapter, she has grown considerably and displays much more confidence. By the end of the game, the dynamic shifts, with the protagonist relying on her more than she relies on you. This clever narrative device fosters a deep bond and evokes a strong sense of empathy for your companion.I was deeply invested throughout the entire game, and there are some truly gut-wrenching moments. One that stood out was witnessing a happy family of boars you meet early on get hunted down by dark, mask-like creatures, transforming them into wild beasts, and the game is full of similiar moments.The destruction of nature by greedy corporate interests is a daily reality. While Neva doesn’t offer a solution to this crisis, it presents a cautiously optimistic perspective, culminating in a deeply moving conclusion. The ending left me with goosebumps and teary eyes, a testament to its emotional resonance and a strong contender for this year’s Games for Impact category.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a really awesome game which manages to draw one magic moment after the other. The art is superb. The music emphasizes the many different situations perfectly, and the gameplay is more challenging than the studio's predecessor "Gris".It's a pretty shot game with about five hours from start to finish. But it's pacing for those five hours is damn great. The game gives you time to breathe and process the colorful scenery as well as events that just unfolded.I'll highly recommend this game to everyone who likes 2D art and is down for ambiguous story telling as there is no written an spoken words (with a very few exceptions). So imagery has to do the talking and boy does it talk!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: 5/5  Graphics:Visually stunning, Neva draws inspiration from Princess Mononoke while maintaining a unique, emotion-driven style. The *Winter* section is especially breathtaking, with seasonal colour palettes that perfectly complement the story’s tone.Mechanics:The gameplay is simple yet engaging, with creative use of Neva as a battle mechanic that evolves throughout the story. Each season brings unique puzzles and level designs, keeping the experience fresh and exciting.  Story: A moving tale open to interpretation, Neva explores the bond between Alba and Neva. It beautifully depicts their evolving relationship, highlighting themes of growth, independence, and the passage of time.  Sound: Berlinist’s score is hauntingly atmospheric, amplifying the story’s emotions without words. The ambient sound effects are subtle yet immersive, enhancing the overall experience.  Replayability:At 6.5 hours for 100% completion (for me at least), Neva is short but memorable. Achievements, chapter selection, and speed-running potential make it easy to revisit your favourite moments.  Final Thoughts:Neva is a masterpiece that combines stunning visuals, innovative gameplay, and heartfelt storytelling. Nomada Studios delivers another unforgettable experience, cementing their reputation as visionary developers.

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful. Gris was an amazing game by all rights but do not make the mistake of assuming this is Gris 2.0. It is a new game, an entirely different theme. The emotions this game makes you feel are different. This game's combat could be challenging at times but I had lots of fun with it. The gameplay is entertaining and the difficulty of the puzzles is not discouraging if you are looking to play this casually. There is an option to lower the difficulty if you are only interested in the story as well.Now to rate some aspects of the game.+ Music is wonderful. It makes me happy Berlinist worked on music again because I absolutely loved the Gris OST and I feel the same regarding Neva. There were times where I leaned back and closed my eyes just to take it in. The pause menu music is also amazing+ It goes without saying but the ART in this game is spectacular. The level design couples perfectly with the art style that was employed for this game. It is odd enough to make you question it, beautiful enough to make you stop and absorb it.+ The gameplay and combat is refreshing. In an era of gaming where all forms of movement tricks and techniques have to be employed to feel as if you did well, this game keeps it simple but allows you to be as nifty as you'd like. The movement system is fluid and responsive making your character move exactly the way you want.+ The story is wonderful. Contrary to those who disliked the ending, I believe that this game created a great story. It is hard to describe any of the elements in it without spoiling it, but I will say that (possible spoiler) - I do not feel as though this is a game that could be experienced more than once. While that does compliment the game it is one of those games that you feel sad for finishing.- The story is on the shorter side, it took me approximately 4 hours to finishI would rate this game a solid 8.5/10

My only big complaint is the ending. 🟩 Positives•	Beautiful art•	Highly emotional story •	Really shows a deep bond growth with Neva🟥 Negatives•	Combat can be annoying at times•	The ending may be hit or miss for you, it was a miss for meGameplay: 9/10Audio: 1010Story: 7/10 (ending for me really took it down)Graphics: 10/10Bugs: None encounteredDifficulty: Moderate Length: 7 hours with going back for achievements Overall: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: This game is something else. The short: take Gris, with all the amazing that is, add a sword, a dog like companion, with a painting like quality, and you have Neva. And you should play this game.The long: I loved Gris, and when this game out it was a no brainer purchase. I was so worried that it might be a massive let down, and thankfully I was completely wrong. I think that this might just have become one of my all time favourite games. Every single moment I was in awe. The visuals are outstanding, I can't stress how much it feels like you are playing a painting. The colours, the design, amazing. The soundtrack is phenomenal again, Berlinist have knocked it out the park. Married with the visuals, the game is a visceral feast. The combat is really well done, and there are lots of lovely touches when it comes to health regeneration, placement of check points, clever introduction and re-use of enemies, solid sword mechanics, and the way your character abilities evolve as you play are extremely satisfying. You feel like the game wants to play and not punish. There is exactly enough system there to play and nothing more. I really appreciate that.Performance wise it worked amazingly from the Steam Deck OLED to 4K on a 4080.I have no complaints, it is pretty much perfect. Having finished a first playthrough in about 6 hours of play, I will go back and play it again, making sure to take a million and one screenshots of all the differing areas in the games. I will be continuing to listen to the fantastic soundtrack. Well done Nomada Studio, thank you for making this.

_childDocuments_.review: WOW. Only been playing for about 3 hours and this game is incredibly gorgous. Not only is every scene breathtaking but also the story/gameplay is just so clever and well thought through. _childDocuments_.review: Neva is good, fun game for such small and independent team. I don't want to give negative review because Gris has a very special place in our life me and my wife. I enjoyed Neva but the story lacks details. We do things we don't know why we do. It feels like it's just a good guys vs bad guys story. There was no connection to the protagonist as well, no character development. I was expecting references to Gris or even connecting both stories at some place but no. Visually I wouldn't say better or worse, Neva is just different and I liked summer and spring the most. But I gotta say that Gris had much more detailed animations/environment/characters. Neva is like a lite version of Gris. Funny that this might feel a bit unfair for Nomada team to have such a greate first game as Gris. Now everyone is comparing both game including me. Neva is a good game in terms of art and game mechanics. It's just good but nearly no story and story is the most important thing in those independent games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me cry. Multiple times. It is beautiful in every respect, from the story, to the art style and animations, to the immaculate soundtrack. It is poignant, touching, and conveys a beautiful story about growth and connection with barely a word. The style is puzzle/platformer with combat against various enemies. Gameplay mechanics are simple, but requires a level of finesse (no button mashing here!) but it does make for a very satisfying success when you take out the opponents. If you love a touching, compelling story with an incredible game score, and beautiful art, I highly recommend this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, beautiful game. If you enjoyed GRIS, you'll be similarly drawn to the art style, but be warned that Neva's gameplay is very different. Like GRIS, Neva is on the shorter side and is worth getting on sale. Fans of combat-oriented platformer games might have an easier time with Neva's mechanics because they require reaction time, combos, and aerial movement. It's less challenging than your Ori and the Blind Forest or Hollow Knight, but expect to die several times during boss fights. There are a few times when bosses had ambiguous hitboxes and it took me a while to figure out how to dodge certain attacks. I attribute this combat awkwardness to the lack of outlines on drawings because Nomada Studios primarily uses lighting and shading to contrast the foreground from the background. Another minor complaint is changing the brightness settings to see better. 8/10 solid game; pick it up if you like Nomada's work or wait for a sale if you're just browsing
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even know what to say. This is now one of my favorite indie games I've ever played. It takes everything that made GRIS so great, and it improves upon it. Better gameplay, more interesting mechanics, excellent sound design, and of course art and music that more than live up to the standard GRIS set.What a delightful game. Truly. This is what indie gaming is all about. It doesn't matter what genre, what a game truly needs is genuine heart. And man does this game have that. You can just feel the thought and care of the developers and artists. You can see it in the numerous immaculately drawn scenic vistas. It's like playing a video game in the most beautiful watercolor painting you've ever seen. And to go with the artistry, the soundtrack is deeply moving and rich. It swells and recedes and swells once more, emphasizing each scene and story beat.The story is emotional and moving. Similar to GRIS, it is told with almost no words. Not that words are necessary when the art speaks for itself. Something about this story made me remember things in my life I'd forgotten for so long. Happy memories. Long lost friends. Things I dearly miss.This game has impacted me so deeply. Thank you, Nomada, for this incredible, beautiful experience.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: The team at Nomada Studio has done it again. This game is very much in the vein of their previous game, GRIS: a work of art, a moving painting, each and every single moment of this game is absolutely beautiful, both in term of art, music and story. In only a few hours this make you feel a ton of emotions. It honestly made me tear up.Gameplay wise, it's a bit more refined than GRIS, a bit more challenging too, though I played in "Adventure mode", one of the two level of difficulty, regardless it never felt unfair, just challenging enough to elevate the art of the game. All in all this was a beautiful experience, one that, albeit short, will left an impact on me. Can't wait to see what's next for the team.

_childDocuments_.review: For a little bit of context, I'm going to briefly mention Gris, and my relationship with it. I played it years and years ago in a single play session and immediately fell in love. It was the defining game for comparison every time I played a new one, a step above everything else. Eventually, a few select games began hitting similar levels of connection for me, and Gris became the framework for my favourite games list, which is pretty gosh darn exclusive still. Neva is the 7th game to make it on this list. So let me talk about it a bit.I followed every scrap of news about Neva from the beginning, and was just immediately enraptured. How couldn't I be? It was another story by the studio who made the pinnacle of gaming for me. When the trailers started hitting, they alone made me cry my heart out. Neva had essentially reserved its spot on the list, and it wasn't even out yet.And now here I am, finally able to play all the way through Neva, and what do you know, I'm just as enraptured as I was with Gris. Neva is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ gorgeous. The art is of course immaculate, the story is heartbreaking and heartwarming, the movement and combat feel fantastic, and the music, oh goodness the music is everything I wanted it to be and more.Play Neva. Play Gris. You'll be doing your heart a favour.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: 'Neva' is a beautiful arranged platformer/metroidvania which sellingpoints are:1. The graphics, which are absolutley stunnig. The watercolour-artstyle fits the narrative perfectly and the colours and there saturation are beau-ti-ful.2. The music, which is as calming as it gets. No whatter in which part of the game you are, the music carries you and adds to the experience.Combine these two with a purely non-verbal driving story and I promise, you'll get immersed and absorbed very quickly.Whilst being a game which focus is the story it tells, action plays a minor roll, but isn't absent. Equipped with only a sword you do have to take down smaller and bigger enemies. No skilltree, combos whatsoever. And they did the right choice, since it's just not that important feature.On the pro-side:- Amazing graphics, with a stunning world-design- Beautiful musical arragments- A very heartfelt story
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game. Genuinely beautiful to look at, wonderful on the ears, and the ending hit me like a TRUCK. I can't really put it into words how much I loved this and loved playing it. Highly recommend it to genuinely anyone. The gameplay can be challenging in some aspects but I always understood that it was fair, and that I could get back and try again. It's very forgiving--almost understanding when you make a mistake. Just... Just a wonderful wonderful game... it had me in tears struggling not to cry in front of my friends watching over a stream. It broke me in the best way possible and I would do it all over again (and hurt all over) if I could be given the choice.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Simply a beautiful adventure.I'll start with a comparison to these devs other game, Gris. I believe, that while they share the same beauty, art-style, devs and composer, that they are very very different games. Gris's themes connect on a much deeper and more personable level; and in that sense, may hit harder for many people (myself included). Neva is not this, instead presenting its own very different but no less wonderful story. Simply put, I don't recommend expecting an experience similar to Gris when you play Neva, it will only leave you disappointed. Neva's gameplay consists simply of platforming, some basic combat and cute wolf/deer interactions. I found combat to be just challenging enough to prove a constant struggle, but never completely overwhelming. The final fight was especially cracked. Similarly the platforming found a nice balance of slowly building upon your skills, while never becoming super hard. Paired with the phenomenal music, the game has an extraordinary sense of flow to it, and while it's not perfect, I think it's about as close as you can get. My only real complaint is that collectible backtracking can be quite a pain sometimes. That said, with a cracked story and stunning visuals, I found this game to be most enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game. You will get absolutely drawn into it.The art style is gorgeous, but the music is stunning.Some scenes can be quite difficult to play. There was one point where I had to try over and over again for half an hour until I got the timing of the button presses right. But that is rare. Overall it is not that hard.
