_childDocuments_.review: First and foremost, this game is completely standalone from GRIS, so you don't have to worry if you don't know or haven't played it.Neva is the second game from Nomda Studio and it is openly inspired in some aspects from Princess Mononoke.If you have played GRIS, you can expect similarities in the art-style and the gorgeous shots characteristic of the previous game, but the story and themes are much different.The combat is fairly simple and easy to grasp. It offers some challenges but ultimately nothing too difficult.You can also choose the "Story" difficulty, which removes the death mechanic and helps you focus on the story.Worth noting that the majority of the game involves platforming, with some combat inbetween.When comparing it to the first game (yes, i know, everyone makes the comparison, though stick with me), i'm sorry to say, but this one doesn't really hold up to the masterpiece that was GRIS.However, don't let that discourage you from playing it.Neva is still a great game in of itself. All throughout the adventure it offers a fantastic athmosphere that keeps you engaged and eager to see what comes next.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: "Perfect" is an impossible standard to achieve. That being said, this game is within hand's reach of being so.The environment of this game, as expected, is exquisite. There were multiple times where I had to set my controller down and take it all in. You travel to many places, all with such different aesthetics but they all work so wonderfully and it never feels like a departure from the main game's energy.The combat in this game makes you feel powerful. Your character's mechanics are simple but are so nice to control. Every combat encounter you win feels like a serious victory you worked hard for.The puzzles in this game make you feel smart. They're the perfect middle point of not being too difficult while being difficult enough it gives you the satisfying "A-ha!" moment when it finally clicks.The gameplay, overall, is immaculate. It surprised me so many times how smoothly the game transitions from peace to action- and it never felt too jarring.Neva is a story told almost entirely without words. As such, there are no words I can possibly think of to describe this game in the way it deserves and in its full glory. Only 20$ for this masterpiece.  Please, please play this game.Thank you, Nomada Studio, Devolver Digital, and everyone who worked on Neva.(P.S: You can pet the dog!!!)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I did enjoy most parts of the game and would overall recommend it if you enjoy great visuals. But it never reached the level of Gris for me. Still some of the visuals especially during the later stages of the autumn and winter levels were great and left me in awe. There were also some new platformer mechanics. Which I found refreshing to see and play. Sadly some of the combats and jumping sections were quite frustrating for me. I'm glad the game includes a story mode otherwise the amount of deaths and frustration resulting from that would have killed the game's mood too often for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva...neva give you up. A name just reminds me of "never give up". The same studio that produced the splendid "Gris" now making the world stunned again with their new game "Neva". It's more than just a game, but more like an art work. The atmosphere and the graphics are as wonderful as ever. Gris focused on the five stages of grief  “denial, anger, bargaining, depression, acceptance”. Gris is about finding yourself and finding inner peace. And thinking of the five stages thing, if Gris is talking about death, then Neva, on the other hand, is talking about life or living. It’s the life cycle in the nature, the time, the great cycle we all living in. Starting from the summer, I’ve come a long way. Alongside Neva, we defended this land and protected the forest. The story ends in season of Spring, a beautiful season. And Spring means hope, means life. But we all know that’s not the real end. Nature has it’s own way of keeping a balance and the life cycle is real. The old Neva is gone, but there’s a new Neva being born. From generation to generation, I can see the story will never end. And the protecting nature thing makes me think of ABZU, also a very beautiful game about life and nature. It’s just that Neva is set in forest and land while ABZU is about water and sea life. I really really like Neva, the ending actually makes me cry. It touched my heart and all the time I spent on this game is worthwhile.  I would definitely recommend this game to my friends. And as a matter of fact, I did : ) The story is nice, the gameplay is fun, the graphic is so beautiful, the music is wonderful. I love it and spend some quality time with it. I hope you do too. Enjoy :D
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is genuinely a work of art. It makes you feel for them, it makes you miss Neva, it makes you cry for her, it makes you happy to see her. The game art is phenomenal and breath taking. It made me giddy and it made me cry, that makes for an invalubable piece of art. The gameplay is fluid, it teaches you step by step and changes the game in new ways constantly so youre always playing some new kind of way and that only makes combat more interesting too because you start to be able to do all kinds of new things as you and Neva grow older and learn how to help one another. Its this perfect companion story that is heart warming and beautiful and I honestly can't praise this game enough. This might have just taken place as my favorite game just because of how beautiful and well thought out it was, challenging but once you understood the mechanic it was just a matter of platforming the right way. The combat was amazing, the platforming kept changing and was always fresh, and each scene and season felt different and new but familiar which made the atmosphere rich and set a tone that kept me immersed and hanging onto ever moment. And the cycular nature of the plot so it is replayable, its genius. I played through the whole game at once, I was so enthralled in this beautiful story. I don't know if you will ever read this, but genuinely thank you for creating this work of art. Your game will stay with me all my life as one of the most fun and beautiful stories I've ever experienced.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Genuinely the most gorgeous art, animation, and soundtrack. For that alone, this is worth it. It tells a simple story about the cycle of life, if anything I wish there were more story. Huge congrats to Nomada for well-deserved success.My one note is that this game is not very readable The platforms/where to go next are not obvious at times. I appreciate that the platforms are supposed to blend in the background so every frame looks like a screenshot, but it was at a sacrifice to my understanding of the gameplay.Overall though, I really enjoyed this game as I did Gris and will play whatever Nomada releases next.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It could use some refining with how combat is tackled. More than once I've ended up having to redo sections simply because a chunk of some situations would catch me off guard with little time to react. Now yes, I didn't play it on the dedicated 'story mode' difficulty, so there was bound to be some challenge anyways.But other than that, this game hits like a truck in a lot of things. Artistic design, attitude, and the message. I almost hate it for how beautiful it all is, and it makes me sad that games like this can only really be experienced once. But that's okay. It's well worth the full price, and with game industry standards as they are, I fully recommend handing that $20 over, to encourage the continued efforts on passionately made games over the typical churned out garbage. (Though if you really  to get it on sale for any number of personal reasons, that's understandable too.)9.99/10

_childDocuments_.review: You can view entire review (& more!) here: Neva is a visually stunning and emotionally powerful game that tells the story of Alba and her wolf companion, Neva, as they journey through a forest decimated by a mysterious force of decay. After witnessing the destruction of their home, Alba and Neva set out to find the source of the devastation, facing dangers together and forming a bond that grows over time. Alba’s skills—sword fighting, double-jumping, and dodging—are enough to get her through encounters with the decay’s monstrous minions, while Neva starts as a smaller, vulnerable partner and grows stronger and more capable as the game progresses.The game uses seasonal changes to mark progress, bringing fresh obstacles and enemies as you move through the decaying world. Each area offers unique puzzles and hidden collectibles, adding extra layers of engagement without overwhelming you with mechanics or complexity. Combat is intentionally simple, focusing on attack, dodge, jump, and heal, with a smooth learning curve that keeps the action accessible without sacrificing the challenge of well-timed dodges and strategic attacks on larger enemies.Although Neva has a short runtime, it creates a lasting impact through its captivating visuals, emotional storytelling, and unique wordless narrative style. The game may not have extensive replayability due to its memorable storyline and limited upgrades, but it’s a well-crafted experience that leaves a lasting impression. It’s a quick, heartfelt journey that will resonate long after the final scene.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, the artwork and the music in Neva are so beautiful. There’s replay value in the game just from wanting to experience those two things again. If you’re someone who likes side-scrolling obstacle course games like the vintage Marios, you’d enjoy this. This is a prettier version of those games, except here you have some genuinely emotional moments.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Neva felt like stepping into a world where every element — from the gameplay to the music and visuals — is woven together to tell a profound story of life, death, and rebirth. This game is a masterclass in storytelling, embracing a purely visual narrative with no descriptions or dialogue. Instead, it relies on stunning artwork and an intuitive progression that guides the player naturally through the character's journey.One of the standout aspects is its gameplay balance; it strikes a perfect line between accessibility and challenge. It's never too easy nor too difficult, allowing players to stay focused on the emotions of the story without frustration. The soundtrack is another highlight, accompanying each moment with incredible timing, enhancing the mood and moving seamlessly with the narrative.Although we never learn the main character’s name, I felt a profound connection to her — and the beauty is that we don’t need to know it. Her story feels universal, capturing emotions and experiences that transcend individual identities. We are draw into her moments of joy and sorrow, to the point that I found myself smiling and crying right along with her and Neva.This game succeeds in creating an emotional experience through a minimalist approach, making it an outstanding and moving journey that I’d recommend to anyone looking for a heartfelt, art-driven game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Gris was a work of art.This, is a masterpiece.Everything is beau-ti-ful, the visuals are magnificent, combat and platforming feeling is perfect, heartbreaking story as usual.Yes, video games are fabulous way to artistically tell a story.And Neva must be one on the greatest.10/10 you can pet the dog (and so much more)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: WOW! WOW! WOW! This game is everything I could want; it's moving poetry at its best - with the stunning watercolour art, the imagery, the metaphors, the music...plus I get to have a wolf pup companion (who I feel I've spent the most time interacting with so far). I enjoyed Gris so much that I've played through twice - I loved the emotions of the story, and how it spoke volumes using no words at all. The same can be said for Neva, but it has exceeded all my expectations...this is love at first sight!!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautifully crafted heartfelt game. The art-style is soothing, and the colors simply pop between the layered rendering bringing this little story-driven plat former to life. I find myself immersed in its world and sound design and in love with the environment art. The story is simple, but shines through as you navigate this game's gorgeous world. It reminds a lot of Okami with the wolf and bringing life to desolation. A must play.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another beautiful game by Nomada studio but not without some flaws. A couple segments have a jarring shift in color that physically hurt my eyes when they happened. But the biggest issue is the combat leaves a lot to be desired as hitboxes for enemies can be very deceiving. Much like Nomada's previous game Gris, Neva is also very short; taking me less than 3 and a half hours to finish and with me  only missing one hidden collectible puzzle along the way.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautifully designed and heartbreakingly honest.  It really captures the pride and love you feel when you own a pet. I recently lost my dog who looks so much like Neva, playing this game made me reminisce the journey I have had with her. Everything from the backgrounds to the story is a delight to play. Is a definite recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely loved this game and its art style. It is as gorgeous as Gris was and I would highly recommend both games. I especially love the mechanics and I totally did not take like a million screenshots because of how beautiful the scenery is ;-; nuh-uh. While it was only 7 hours of playtime, which includes the time I took after completing the story to get all achievements, I think it was worth every minute.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The game is visually stunning, just like GRIS. Colours, sounds, music, everything pulls you in. The detail of art, like in the flowers and tree leafs, and the beautiful expressive colours, is just out of this world. The one thing I think could improve the game, is to remove the hard platforming elements from story mode. I found my focus was pulled away from the story immersion when having to deal with the jumps and timings of attack, which in some areas were too hard. If the developers found a way to solve this, then story mode would be just perfect for it's purpose. Either way, this is another amazing game. Thank you!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Gris, you'll like this. It's not that difficult and not that long, but a relaxing play which takes you through beautiful scenery worthy of desktop backgrounds. I think I took more screenshots in 5 hours as many much longer games. the gameplay is a bit slow, but if I let myself be absorbed into the world I found a calmness most games don't provide. The game won't be for everyone due to the slow pace, but it's worth a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is an absolute audiovisual masterpiece. Every frame of it should hang in a gallery and the music and sound design is excellent. The stunning environments make you just want to stand there and stare at them. The gameplay itself i can only describe as pleasant. It is very nice. It feels good, the game is not difficult in the sense videogames usually can be, but you do have to retry fights a couple times. However the fights and puzzles aren't so hard they would be pace breaking. The puzzles are satisfying and cleverly made. The game is advertised exactly as what you are getting. You are getting a short, calm and pleasant walk through a beautiful tragically decaying world, you are getting smoothly flowing and well paced puzzles, enemies and bosses that feel really good to beat and a story that makes you wonder what the true theme is and what the characters representA couple things to note before playing the game. Some are critiques, others are things that might be good to know- The game is very linear in progression. There is no exploration outside the way you are supposed to go outside of collectables. I found the linear progression very pleasant but i think it is worth noting-  The game is very short. It took me 4 hours on my first playtrough but i am playing it again just to look at the art.- The game's default resolution is 1920x1080, if your monitor has a higher resolution then you need to change it from the settings. i was absolutely devastated when i found this out only halfway through the game. - Most of the platforming challenges are very well done but there are a few parts where the hitboxes of ledges are too precise and will cause you to fall. I found it a little annoying in places, but mostly it is not too horrible.If you want an audiovisual masterpiece that is overall a very lovely playing experience, Neva is absolutely worth every penny but it might not appeal to an audience looking for a challenging or fast paced action-platformer.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: For the better, Neva has a lot of the same DNA as GRIS. Wonderful music, a beautiful art style, careful use of colour, a few mind-bending platforming puzzles, and heavy reliance on visual storytelling. One thing that will stick with me is the feeling of repeatedly passing through the same spaces and watching them degrade, the world around you slowly being consumed.Overall I think I prefer GRIS because emotionally it hits you like a sledgehammer, but both are great games and great experiences that are well worth your time.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

My controllers also work on other games on mac but Gris and Neva are the exceptions. Sad because the game is way better with a controller.The game is still a jewel !

But, as the weeks go by, I'm confident it will get patched out.  It did not hinder my experience and enjoyment ultimately.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Ever since I've played Gris, I've been such a fan for Nomada Studio. I've been waiting for Neva since they announced it last year and am so delighted with it! There were familiar gameplay mechanics and some new ones too that is totally manageable for a casual gamer. Neva's storyline looks like it was heavily inspired by Mononoke Hime by Studio Ghibli. The strong, combative spirit of it's protagonist truly reminded me of Mononok as with her relationship to Neva, a guardian of the forest. The art is breathtaking in Neva I couldn't stop taking screenshots and the music by Berlinist is spot on again in Neva. Thank you so much to the wonderful team at Nomada for this gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautifully done - the team that developed Gris did not disappoint. Everything from the art style to the music conveys the mood perfectly. Overall, the game felt more linear than Gris, yet there is still room to interpret the events as you see them.One interesting departure from Gris is an adventure mode. This is on by default and gives you lives to make the fights more challenging. If that's not your cup of tea or you want to focus on the story without fear of death, narrative mode can be selected instead.It's a really wonderful game with simple puzzles and fights for the story, and challenging puzzles tossed in for the completionist who wants to go item collecting. Easily worth the price and worth playing through.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: All jokes aside, one of the most beautiful games I've ever played but also quite the tough platformer (I'm not good at platforming). I wouldn't say this takes away from the experience and the game is worth it for the music alone. Once again, a short experience compared to other games I've played teaches a valuable lesson.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is one of my favourite games for this year.It is an audio-visual delight that everyone should experience. It feels like interacting with a painting. I started playing it on the Steam Deck (where it played perfectly) but I simply had to switch to my TV because I wanted to experience its art on a bigger screen.And it's not just the art really that steals the show. The controls are crisp, the combat is surprisingly solid and each level has a new mechanic or situation that you have to adapt to. Gris was criticized for being a bit lacking on the gameplay front but I feel this is really not the case with Neva.There aren't many games that I want to replay just because I want to experience it again - but Neva made it to this list, and that is a high praise coming from me. It very easily earns my wholehearted recommendation.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: What an absolute joy this game has been, soulful!Breathtaking visuals, stunning music, touching story line, fun combat, thought provoking concepts. Neva was so (in my opinion) accurately depicted as a canine companion, everything from her personality to animations and barks/noises, which made everything more palpable and impactful for me. Barks and sass! 💛Highly recommend this game, a must have unique experience, especially if you enjoyed Gris. 💛✨Abracitos✨
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva deserves your money. The game is so very lovingly crafted from every little painterly detail to bold full-screen hand-drawn animation. All seamlessly blending together. The camera is smooth and never gets in the way. Gameplay feels responsive and quite easy to get a handle on. Combat often feels a little drawn-out and sometimes a little unfair due to bad visibility (small) or the cheap "just add more enemies to make things harder"-trick, but overall it never really gets in the way of pretty it all is. There's some light puzzles scattered throughout and some neat mechanics that felt fresh, I won't spoil them.Music is okay overall, but gets annoying during exciting moments, both emotional and physical ones, it tries just too hard to force an emotion on me and leaves no room for interpretation while the graphics do. It's just too loud. The quieter ambient music in the game much nicer.The story isn't too deep, but touching nevertheless. That said, I probably won't play this again as it's a bit depressing throughout. One big gaping hole is the main character, on the surface, she's basically just an empty avatar who can say "Neva", don't expect the game to elaborate on who she is. Maybe Neva 2?I'd welcome that. I really enjoy shorter games with a strong, coherent but still surprising style.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: First I have to say I really loved Gris, made by the same developer, so probably a little biased and I was really hyped to play this game. And oh my does it deliver!This is such a beautiful and well produced game in every way. I really love the level design, the fantastic art direction and general game-play topped up with a great soundtrack and sound design. I think this is one of those few games that really proofs the fact that computer games can be art. I really can't wait for what this studio does next!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly Gris was great, but this...is even GREATER! Music, graphics, art style, everything was simply awesome. My expectations were pretty high from Gris, and when i saw that the same developer was publishing another game i couldn't resist, i just had to buy it, in fact i bought it almost the very same day it launched, and i do not regret my choice at all, great work.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I want to start this with saying im a huge fan of Gris, I still think about it from the day I played it !!! When I heard the announcement of Neva I was so hyped up and all I thought of was how could they make a better game than Gris which to me was PEAK. I played Neva and oh my god... what an experience, I was so immersed and invested throughout the whole playthrough !!! now all i could think of is HOW ARE THESE DEVS THAT GOOD WITH THEIR CRAFT???? Neva was an emotional journey for me :( a beautiful journey, I loved the art, music, voice acting, literally EVERYTHING !!! I dare say this game was once in a life time experience for me. I will never forget how Neva have saved me when I was dealing with many hard obstacles in life. Thank you so much Nomada Studio. I will never forget <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterpiece that draws you into its world where every frame is carefully crafted, with vivid colours and subtle details that blend to create an atmosphere both haunting and enchanting. The visuals are breathtakingly beautiful, yet carry an underlying tension that keeps you feeling both in awe and on edge.The bond between the protagonist and Neva is the heart of the game and feels deeply authentic. Neva is more than a pet; she’s a guide, a friend, and at times, a guardian, giving weight to each shared moment. Their silent communication and shared trust create emotional stakes that make every step feel personal and every challenge feel urgent.The game excels at pulling you in with its rich, immersive environment and then grounding you emotionally through this heartfelt bond. It’s rare to find a game where the story, art, and companionship feel so perfectly intertwined. Neva is a must-play for those who want an experience that’s as visually stunning as it is emotionally resonant.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva fails to deliver on the same level as Gris did in my opinion. The game feels rushed and a little sloppy. Some of the hit boxes are weird and the timing for some things is odd. The puzzles are simple and too easy. Each area of the game also feels just the same with not much uniqueness to it. In complete honesty I just don't think anything could ever come to the same level as Gris did..Its a very good game though and extremely artistic, I definitely enjoyed the experience and art more than the game-play.[SPOILERS BELOW]...The opening sequence is extremely emotional and very charged a great way to start the game. The final scene being the opening scene is just a huge letdown. It fails to deliver any kind of actual closure because its no different. It doesn't show any actual change within the game happening. You just end where you started and it feels incredibly cheap compared to Gris. The game confuses you into thinking your playing the present when your playing the past and you have already seen the end. But it doesn't actually explain that well and with the seasons themes you could be lulled into thinking its just the same thing happening over and over again in a loop. All in all though a very nice visually pleasing experience that felt a little bit like it took too much from dark souls. Definitely hope in the future they can top Gris because Neva is good, but its nowhere near having an impact like Gris had.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Its a very good game, but it didnt reach the level of gris in terms of emotional value. Mechanically its pretty simple overall, and it feels good to play, but it stays simple all the way through, which is NOT a bad thing, except for the fact that the game is kinda overpriced for its content, I'd recommend waiting for sales or find good offers in key shops
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I don't think I've ever taken as many screenshots in a game like I have with Nomada's games.  I loved this game!  Gris is one of my all-time favorites, so this was an instant buy for me.  Great story, art, and music.  The option to play with combat was nice.  We just need trading cards and point shop items!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Magnificent game. The combat is simple but engaging, as are the puzzles and exploration. The visuals and music are absolutely *stunning*. Much like Gris, the story is told with no dialogue, but is very approachable and 'universal' - it definitely got me :,)Especially good if you're a bit burned out on huge games or punishing difficulty, and need a little break in between longer titles. A perfect little morsel you can finish in a weekend.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A gorgeous platformer game.  The audiovisual presentation is one of the selling points of the game. Graphics looks like animated watercolor painting, with pastel colors and no hard lines. This is coupled with fluid animations. Music is excellent and fits the mood. There is a noticeable inspiration from multiple Ghibli movies.  Gameplay is a mix of platforming, combat and some basic logical puzzles.  It is well polished and it evolves between chapters. The length (cca 4 hours) is just correct so it keeps being engaging and focused experience.  The story is told only visually. It is inspired by mythology and cycles of nature, similar to Ori series.  Possibly the strongest experience this year, even with competition from Kunitsu-gami.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: An excellent second game from the company, gorgeously done. The ONLY thing I did not like was the Winter section with the floating blobs. It really feels like they only made it doable for controller playing gamers and left us keyboarders in the dust. That part was so hard I had to step away multiple times from the game out of pure frustration. I understand that there's a mechanic and timing to learn with the jumps, but a game shouldn't make you cry in frustration from a jump sequence.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game so much, Not gonna lie, it took me sometime to get into the game, but evetually i really enjoyed it, the story here was very good and the final boss was really feeling goo d and challenging to fight against. But let me just say... the achievement "Memories" made tear a little. In a way i really wanted the game to be like Gris, but i love the fact it was diffrent, i mean that's what makes this game in some ways better than Gris. The game feels alive and it fels really good to play and fight. And the soundtrack while not as rememrable as Gris maybe i just need to give a second chance and listen to it on Spotify or something. Alli in all, this game deserves a 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I want to like this game, the visuals are absolutely stunning, the gameplay is actually really fun when its not getting in its own way, and some of the puzzles are extremely visually interesting. The issue I have is with how punishing the platforming is. Once I've figured out what the puzzle wants me to do, I then have to sit and repeat the sequence over and over until I find the exact right frame to make my jump/dodge/sword swipe. The puzzles feel less rewarding and more tedious because this game wants you to do tight fast platforming with very floaty and deliberate movement controls. I find myself getting annoyed a lot because I can see the solution to the puzzle, but I still have to do it over and over because I haven't found the specific pixel where I need to make the jump in order to progress. It's a testament to how good the visuals and overall premise are that I keep playing even though the platforming is driving me batty. Recommend playing through on story mode initially, until you get the hang of the mismatched platforming controls, otherwise you're going to see the death screen constantly.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Short and sweet. A bit pricey for length of game. Can be a bit challenging at times, but overall not very difficult. Has some puzzles, but they are pretty trivial, although some are unique/innovative. Wish there were more abilities and RPG elements. But game is more like interactive novel than anything (i.e., you can turn death off without any consequences if you really like). Don't understand the incessant need for games to have so many useless cutscenes, especially since the story/lore is nicely told/implied/suggested through the background artwork/elements. I mean the game doesn't have very many, but "time to keyboard" is still unnecessarily long at the start.Game is beautiful and overall pretty enjoyable. Elements of Princess Mononoke and Spirited Away. Can be 100% completed in a day or two. Achievements are all trivial to get (although if you missed some it requires some tedious replaying/backtracking). Game is linear. Definitely still recommended despite minor annoyances. Also, doggo/wolf. Definitely made for dog/samoyed lovers!I wish you could crouch so you could teabag enemies, but you can kind of mimic that by tapping forward in quick succession.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The folks at Nomada have been absolutely cooking with this game! Like Gris before it, Neva feels great to play, with some of the most beautiful visuals and music in any game I've ever seen. Building on what they did with Gris, they've pushed a lot of the mechanics further, adding challenges to the puzzle platforming and fluid, intuitive-feeling combat that is never frustrating or repetitive. The threats in this game feel very present, with horror elements throughout that are often quite intense. There's never any doubt in my mind that we will win, but the theme of loss throughout is genuinely upsetting which creates stakes for the story. I was so excited for Neva ever since it was announced, and honestly have been looking forward to seeing what the folks at Nomada would do since the first time I finished playing Gris, and they did not disappoint.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Really moving game.As someone who has not yet played Gris, to me this felt like a blend of Hollow Knight, Journey, and Princess Mononoke.The game itself is very linear, but it makes up for this in its fluid gameplay and beautiful visuals.I really loved the artwork. The backgrounds and foregrounds were so well done and created all kinds of different atmospheres perfectly.It was a short game, I got through it in about 6 hours and I just need to go back and round up a few collectibles. I would have loved more play time and exploration, but as it is Neva is a wonderful gem.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so beautiful! The art style is gorgeous, the gameplay is fun. The combat is exciting and challenging (but also forgiving), and there are wonderful puzzles. It's a short game, I finished in about 4 hours, and I was brought so deeply into the world. What a masterpiece! This truly was a piece of art. I cannot recommend this enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Much like GRIS, it's utterly captivating and beautiful. Animation work, cinematography and sound design are all 10/10. The minimalist approach in some areas creates a sense of space and calm that invites contemplation, which is a nice way to break up the more action driven sequences, this makes the pacing feel great. The subtle changes in how close the camera chooses to be works wonders for evoking feeling, when it closes in you can see the intimacy between the two characters, when it drops back you can appreciate the scale and spectacle of the levels but also be overcome with a sense of loneliness, both are used to brilliant effect. The theme of reflections and symmetry are clever symbolism for the maternal undertones of the narrative. You see yourself reflected quite literally in mirrored surfaces, but more importantly you see yourself and your actions mirrored in your companion. Which really drives home the maternal aspects of you helping an orphaned pup into adulthood, especially when you see that pup all grown up and a sequence where you helped them over a jump is replayed with them and their pup, which was a heartwarming moment of realisation for me, you helped them learn how to be a mother by being a mother. Truly beautiful. Sadly I just didn't appreciate the combat, it felt a bit unresponsive, with enemies that take far too many hits to take out. This made the boss fights feel like bad copies of Hollow Knight which is silly because you have to do VERY well to compete with something like that. I think it would have been better to focus more on puzzle and mechanic driven boss fights, as I feel like this is where the studios strengths are. But I respect the studio for branching out into game play they don't usually do and think overall it could have been a lot worse.However, I was very impressed with the concept that hitting enemies without taking damage refills your health, as this streamlines the process of healing. You simply just need to play well and you will always be refilling health. This lends itself to a game feel where you are always able to rally yourself back into a fight, you aren't limited to a certain amount of heals. This allows those moment where its almost all over but you manage to fight your way back to win, which is VERY exciting, great mechanic.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an absolute delight to play, and I enjoyed every minute of it. The art and soundtrack are both superb. I felt right at home with the 2D platforming, which is fun but not too challenging until later parts of the game where I felt like my Ori and Celeste skills were coming in handy.The combat was a bit more difficult than I was expecting for a game like this, especially coming from Gris, but after a few attempts at some of the boss fights, I came out on top. There is an option to reduce or eliminate the combat/death if you want to focus more on the story, which by the way is very well done. I was captivated right away from the very beginning, and felt super connected to Neva, my furry companion. The two of you grow and gain abilities as you progress though the game, and each new ability was easily to learn and fun to play with.The game is a masterpiece all the way 'til the end. I don't think I've ever cried at the end of a game, ever, except for this one. It's that good. It will hold a very special place in my heart, and I can't wait to see what the developers come up with next.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Breathtaking - Neva is a gorgeous game in every respect - visuals, music, storytelling, gameplay, ect. The intersection of all these components is seamless. Games are capable of so much as an artistic medium, and Neva displays this flawlessly. The runtime of the game is about 3-4 hours for a single play-through. I always appreciate when a game respects my time since I can only really allocate 30 mins-1 hour a day to gaming anymore. For me, I don't measure the value of a game by how many hours I can pour into it (I find that game-length can often be artificially inflated by menial tasks that serve very little purpose), but by the size of the impact it has on me. Needless to say, Neva impacted me greatly and is an experience I will look back on and cherish for a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Well, anyone could say this is an "artsy-fartsy" game, sure, but you can always tell when something is done right and there is in fact real talent behind it, and this one, just like Gris, is an amazing game, it is kind of "short" you could say as well, but it simply does not overstay its welcome, the addition of the new combat mechanics are great, nothing too complex in that sense but it does not need more than it has to offer.Nice little platforming and puzzles (and is just great that even if the game is not too difficult, it does not tell you how to proceed 3 seconds after you engage with something you need to solve, at least not in the Adventure Mode, it has a Story Mode and things might be different there and it would be fine there, should that be the case)Oh and and look, a woman as the protagonist in a 2024 game that you do not immediately hate because it feels like a feminist lecture or propaganda for no reason what-so-ever, she even has a dark skin tone, and you can enjoy the game just fine and appreciate it for what it is and as it was imagined, no forced or out of place diversity, inclusion or whatever, imagine that!Pretty good game in general, all things considered with amazing art direction. It is worth getting, no doubt about it. Support these games! 10/10 indie game IMO.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Already loved the first one, this one is just as good. I played the normal version, not the story mode. I was surprised about the fighting aspect but really enjoyed it. I am not the best gamer, and for me it was the right mix between easy and some challenges. The landscapes, the art, amazing, sometimes I didnt want to continue to play and just look. The music is awesome and emphazises the emotiones and experience in an awesome way. I can only recommend this game !
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Outstanding art direction and sound design, simple but great voice acting, and breathtaking atmosphere. Advance with a great progression of mechanics in a mesmerizing world that is being corrupted.I encountered unnerving bugs and issues with the checkpoint system only when trying to get all achievements for the game. But when played focusing on the story during the first playthrough, the game went smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Never thought a game more beautiful than Gris could be made and leave it to NOMADA to surpass themselves with Neva, the visuals are twice as beautiful, the puzzles are just as fun, plus the addition of combat makes it more engaging on another level. The story won't be as resonant to most people like Gris largely due to it being a completely different subject matter, where as Gris dealt with Grief which is a universal experience, Neva deals more with parenthood which is a position not everyone has been in but it's still resonant nonetheless. watching Neva grow throughout the chapters was quite beautiful. I personally enjoyed this one more than Gris, although i do like Gris's soundtrack a bit more.The final boss is hella awesome btw, wish we could've got more rounds with her.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's so peak, like ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥. There's a part about halfway through that I was taking screenshots through about once every few minutes. I think this is the only game to make me actually cry. The artists and Berlinist are names that could be put on anything and I'd check it out. I think Gris had better music, I think Neva has better gameplay (though I like platforming, and it can be tricky at points here, it's harder than Gris for sure), and both games have mind-bogglingly eyegasmic visuals, I wish I could see myself or others' first looks at some of the stuff in these games, I was awestruck.Play this if you have 20$ and a few hours to spare, and get Gris while you're at it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Finished now, like, literally now. I'm shattered, I cried like 4 times in 4 hours.  It's perfect in everything it does, you can see Roset's touch. I thought he got lucky with *Gris*, but he has proven himself again to be a fantastic artist. And all of those beautiful colors are a perfect fit for Berlinist's music - "Altrove" and "A place for us" are defo my outstanding tracks. Simple, linear, quality over quantity, very inspired level design as always, and the combat held up well without ever getting boring. The enemies fit perfectly and blend seamlessly with those mechanics and they managed to deliver a simple but yet enjoyable final boss fight.   I won't even start talking about the story—I'm particularly affected when it comes to dogs. 11/10 - they did it again.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely beautiful experience, and a big step up for Nomada. Gameplay: 4/5 - Smooth, simple, serving the story. I love how much was grounded in the connection to the wolf; it felt different than the usual "to-the-right-em-ups."Style: 5/5 - A masterclass in art, animation, music. Truly gorgeous *chef kiss*.Theme: 5/5 - Almost made me cry in the final scene <3. A more nuanced story than I was expecting, and powerfully told without words.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Nomada Studios has created another beautiful emotional journey.  A gorgeous tale in terms of emotional depth, musical score, and art style with a greater focus on gameplay over Gris.  Not an incredibly challenging game, but I don't think it should be.  I found the fights and platforming challenging enough to keep me feeling engaged with the game play.  Gris told an emotional tale of grief, and themes of this really struck an emotional chord for me.  I know the developers were going for themes of motherhood and that shines through, but for me, the emotional relationship with Neva, so subtle and well thought out, just made me miss my own dog who died last year.  The bond with Neva just kept reminding me of my own bond with my passing dog, and that ability to bring up memories and draw out our emotions is what makes this game a great demonstration of video games as an art form.In my opinion, this game is a must play for everyone.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is a great game in all aspects. A small Gem, once again thanks to the artists at Nomada.The visuals, the sound, the game-feel, each is beatiful, and all work very well together to provoke strong (and quite diverse) emotions, what else could we ask for?For fans of Gris, i'll warn you : this is a bit harder. Nothing insurmountable, but the plateforming and combat are a bit more dynamic. It flows just right, but might get quick for some.Everything is also more "down to earth", in a way. The decor is more natural, the themes and symbols too... And the themes are seen through an arguably less abstract lense even though the presentation is very much symbolic.I'd still note Nomada has lost some of its power on one respect. Gris made me cry with no word. Neva needed... two.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I played Gris on my switch a few years back so wanted to try out this game also as I really enjoyed it back then. The visuals of course did not disappoint coming from this game company, breathtaking as always! The story was truly heart felt and the ending made me cry. The game play can be quite challenging for people looking for a chill/story game, as fighting is a mechanic in some areas as well as puzzle solving to progress, but for me it was all so worth it! When you are stuck it didn't take me too long to continue. They do give you options for a simpler game experience or a more challenging one if you wish to test yourself! The love I have for this pup is real, you'll want to protect her with every ounce of your being and in return she'll protect you. And yes, you can pet her so that instantly gives this game more points!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is the example of how refined level design, a simple but meaningful story, and stylistic visual research can teach one lesson or two to the entire AAA title industry.I had been waiting for Neva so much since the announcement, and the gaming experience was beyond my expectations.Gris was a surprise for me, an inner cathartic journey that I took together with the protagonist. Neva blends the Studio Ghibli style, embellished with the same symbolism, sending me strong Princess Mononoke vibes. A story about parenthood, the cycle of life, the protection of offspring, their growth. Neva envelops you in this cloud, drawing you into surreal and magnificent settings performed by the Nomada studio, plus excellent musical accompaniment by Berlinist.Neva is pure art in motion, a perfect choir of one of the most talented artists out there. Thank you Nomada and Berlinist.Astrid
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is a level-up from Gris. Don't get me wrong I loved Gris but it didn't have the combat system, which makes all the difference to me. The art is fantastic in chapter 2 the use of the fog is just breathtaking the fact that you cant see most of the surroundings gives it just the right vibe and kept me engaged in the game
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: One of the most beautiful games I ever played. Finished it already twice, in both modes. Though I don't find combat mode to be very challanging,  it is very nice to not have to worry about avoiding taking damage. As it goes to combat mode itself - to me it was only a bit challanging on a level I needed to try a few times on certain moments, but it wasn't a struggle. Puzzles were fun to solve.Playing Neva is like being inside a paiting- every scene is a masterpiece. Very illustrative, detailed and made with passion and love.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: While I would say I marginally prefer the art style of GRIS, it is a very thin margin. NEVA more than exceeds GRIS in all other ways though. It has a story that is very clearly follow up to the end, and the surprisingly competent combat system allows for some incredible set-pieces and vignettes throughout the game. It's challenging at times, though never to a degree where someone who played GRIS wouldn't be able to play this, especially with their designated "Narrative" difficulty option.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous game with a a magical atmosphere. The visuals are quite an experience.The makers seem to like Ghibli studio movies a lot, the character design and story have a number of similarities.The addition of combat and platforming that can result in deaths sets this game apart from the studio's previous game GRIS. I personally preferred the approach of GRIS. Fortunately, you can turn off combat deaths in this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is a great successor to follow in the footsteps of GRIS. Where GRIS focused on each step of overcoming grief, Neva is a well told, heartfelt story of the greatness found in life after loss. The world puzzles are fair, (not super easy but a few make you sit back and think for a minuet) and the details in the world are beautiful. The wolf (Neva), herself is a wonderfully played out character that feels like a real companion anyone could fall in love with down to the simple yet full-filling animations. Combat is fluid, satisfying and not overly frequent like some side scrolling games tend to do. The music is also immersive, moving and captivating. If you're debating on playing this game I can't recommend it enough even though I knew from the start this game would have me crying (tears in the first 5 minuets). High praises to this Development Team.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is an incredibly good looking game, following the beautiful story of Alba and Neva you will come across incredible landscapes accompanied with an perfectly emotional score to elevate them even further. What has been achieved here is a true visual storytelling masterpiece crafting it's narrative and world brilliantly without dialogue. Though the combat and platforming are a little uninventive and simplistic the overall experience more than makes up for it.A wonderful game would highly recommend it!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for this game for so long after playing GRIS. What I loved about GRIS was the gorgeous art but most of all I loved how fluid the movement controls felt. With the addition of combat and an added dash, I am happy that Neva retained what I liked from GRIS and expanded on it to make it feel unique and fun. I love that I can pet the puppy and the animations are so gorgeous. The soundtrack is once again a banger. It is a refreshing game and I am happy to say that it lived up to my expectations. Pet the dog!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Just as with Gris, I'm totally blown away by the artwork and the ability to tell a story with virtually no voice lines. Steady progression of abilities felt really good and jump puzzles ranged from easy to fairly difficult but not to the point of frustration. Just as with Gris I wish I could play it all over again for the first time again. Well done on this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: About a year ago I cleared GRIS from my backlog and enjoyed it for what it was. When Neva was announced, I was exited to hear it was from same developers from GRIS.Regarding the game itself, like the game before, it has amazing visual effects, music, and wonderful storytelling without any need for dialogue. It doesn't take very long to become attached to the wolf and the game does a good job making tense moments because of it. The game is rather short but it takes a lot of effort to make the wonderful art style it has so that alone it worth it. Game takes supposedly 4 hours but I was constantly dodge rolling and dashing. somehow that is faster than running lol. Definitely worth playing!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This is the greatest example of the phrase "show, don't tell."  I don't need anyone to tell me what is happening or how to play the game or what I should be doing.   The game shows you what to do in the most natural way.;  perfectly balanced.  not too difficult, but not too easy (adventure mode).  Play style is very organic.  now add to all of that the beautiful artwork ;-; just an amazing game.  have tissues with you.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Seeing a lot of comparison so I'll throw in mine. Since this is a game for people who enjoy atmospheric artsy fartsy stuff, It's kind of like what INSIDE is to LIMBO? To me that's kind of what Neva is to GRIS.Of course it won't have the same *wow* effect, it can't. We already kind of know what this studio excells at. In that sense, GRIS has already "spoiled" the fact that Nómada Studio really has a god-like understanding of progressive storytelling through color and composition. It's their thing, they absolutely deliver. Neva doesn't feel quite as "drawn on paper", it has a slightly more digital aesthetic, but the play with color gradients, contrast and saturation, is  phenomenal. Some of the scenes where the camera pans out are truly breathtaking. The melancholy is definitely there. Combat and puzzles are very frustration-free and casual (there's also a "can't die" play mode"). I super appreciate the fact that the bond with your animal companion feels really organic, in the sense that the game isn't cluttered with drawn-out cutscenes. There's a really good balance with how much of your relationship is pretty much built into the gameplay. Beautiful piece of art. ❤️
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I bought this the day it came out! I was watching this closely after playing and loving Gris! I finally got to sit down and play through this entire game! Once again you made something that shocked us with beautiful scenes and the music was so well matched to the emotions. This story was phenomenal and the whole playing with the trailer/opening was truly genius! Your team did such a great job! I got the album, just such amazing work! Thank you! Also, bring tissues along for this journey, you're going to need them!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva was such a delight to play! I thought that it would be an atmospheric, easygoing game but it turned out to be so much more! The art is gorgeous (creatures and animals seem to be inspired by studio Gibli) and even though the characters do not speak, the story is told very clearly. It's a platform game with puzzles and hack&slash combat. The combat can be challenging at times, which I really liked! I recommend playing the game! Just don't expect it to be like Gris :)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story. Different thematics from Gris. (I personally think they are a little bit similar in a certain way tho)The combat system is very simple (still good) but we don't need sophisticated combat in these type of games.Puzzles like in Gris.The art is flabbergasting to say the least.for me it's a 9.5/10 game.The game offers you a gamemode without combat for those who want to enjoy only the story.The mix between art, music and story makes the game very immersive, really positive experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Difficult to review.Art and atmosphere are really great, but combat and platforming seemed quite rudimentary and repetitive. Many parts of the game were not clear in terms of meaning and function for the game's progression. The progression by Neva getting "new abilities" is rather minimal and did not drive the gameplay forward. Of course, the game is intended to be different to Gris, and that is absolutely ok, but nevertheless, the game seems to me like a step back from the quality of Gris. Sadly, in the end I was glad when I saw the end credits.The game left the impression of a rather minimalistic, unfinished, cheaper and shallow version of Ori (especially regarding the story).
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a breathtaking work of art, with mechanics that are nothing short of fantastic. Each moment felt perfectly balanced, embodying what makes a game truly engaging. I’ve been eagerly awaiting its release ever since I first heard about it. While Gris was incredible, this game takes it to another level. I’m immensely proud of the developers and everyone involved—this has quickly become one of my all-time favorites. I feel so lucky to have had the chance to experience it.A huge thank you for creating Neva!P.S. I can't wait to see more like this in the future! :)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's simply beautiful. The feeling, the gameplay, the environments, everything is beautifuly done and executed. The mecanics are great, so satisfying, the fighting is really good. It's not Gris 2, it was never meant to be it. I loved every single second, and I plan on playing more to get the 100%I highly recommend it, sincerely, this resonated in me, as a Princess Mononoke fan. Beautiful story, and cinematics are really good too. Have a good time playing !
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A better GAME than Gris while being a less memorable EXPERIENCEVisuals and Soundtrack (by Berlinist again) are stunning and fit the mood perfectly with some oustanding tracks throughout-Gameplay is solid, if a bit basic and monotonous but definitely way more engaging than Gris'.Puzzles/challenges are alright. Enemies are okay with some really frustrating design decisions. Bossfights are a mixed bag.The story is fairly solid, if a bit too on the nose and predictable but it's still told beautifully.Game takes roughly 4-5 hours to beat and 6-7 to 100% complete (using a guide for missed achievements etc)Definitely more of a game than Gris and thus more engaging on a momentary level but the story doesn't resonate as deeply as Gris' and the art design feels a fair bit less inspired.and evocative.Price might be a bit spiicey for the amount of content you get but the craftmanship is worth it and the game should be considered a must buy on sale. Can't wait to see Nomada's next project!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This was hands down one of the most beautiful games I have ever played. I have started to realize how much I love platformers cause of this game. It is a beautiful and awe inspiring game. A gorgeous soundtrack and a very clean and well trimmed interface and play style. It is not often that I find a new game where it makes me want to get home from work so I can get back to playing. On top of that, it is especially not often I find a game that invokes so much emotion. There were many times my jaw dropped and eyes opened, and the ending... lets just say I haven't cried about a game's end in a LONG time.I absolutely loved the puzzles and battles, and they invoked the perfect amount of difficulty and struggle. Some of the battles can definitely prove to be a challenge but some are easy to sight read, and they are some great battles for sure!I cannot stress enough that if this game got extended or got an expansion I would buy it in a heart beat. Would highly recommend for sure! (It isn't crazy long, but depending on how difficult some puzzles and fights are might make it longer than average. It also depends on how long you take in the beautiful look of the game, and explore for secret collectibles! Either way, I would never take back hearing about and playing this game!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I cannot begin to describe how beautiful and heart-wrenching this game is. The art style is amazingly detailed and colored. I think I spent half of my time in game looking at the scenery. The game does an amazing job being subtle in its themes and slowly you grow so attached to Neva. This is one of those games where you leave a different person than you started the game. I cannot recommend this game enough.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is one of if not the most beautiful game I have ever seen. Amazing combat; not too difficult, not too easy, and always enjoyable- the story breaks you and puts you back together again, and is one of the best I've seen. And the art- oh, the art. The game uses a lineless animation style and it's animation, cutscene to gameplay, is incredible. The landscapes and character animations are smooth and gorgeous. This game is definetly one of my favorites, I wish I had the time to write about all of the amazing things about it. Neva is a downright beautiful game in every way. I wish everyone had the chance to experience Neva. I'd reccomend getting the soundtrack, too, the music hits immeasurably.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game made me ugly cry in a hotel in front of my entire family. It's almost as if I bought a ticket to an interactive movie. The relatively easy difficulty makes this beautiful experience readily accessible even as a first game. Even after experiencing Hollow Knight  and the like, this game had me hooked, never bored for the entire run time with the stunning art/animation and music. Would recommend to anyone 10/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Worth playing. It's purely personal taste, but will say that I found the ending unsatisfactory; it mirrored the beginning in a way that was an interesting artistic choice but left much of the character arcs' progression unsatisfied from my perspective. The art and music are beautiful, though, and the combat is fun, though a little "floaty" if you're used to 2d combat games like Hollow Knight or Ori 2. Just keep in mind that you might not like how it ends.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another gem from Nomada. Beautiful environments, animation, characters, music etc. The game introduces new mechanics slowly but steadily. Combat is simple yet satisfying with great animation. There is strategy required later on as the enemies shake up their attacks and the environments/mechanics become more complex. Simple button mashing won't cut it.But it's the growing bond between Alba and Neva where the game truly shines. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I have just finished Neva, after about 4 hours of gameplay. I haven't completed it, but daaaamn. This hit again. With the only dialogue being calling for Neva (and by all that is holy, the amount of emotions put into it depending on the storybeat was absolutely stunning), once again the world really is another one where each image, each location, each twitch of the surroundings or the characters tells a whole story in and of itself. I was taken by the colours, the design, the way it all unfolded, and I was almost screaming at the ending, while it was unfolding. No spoilers. And the sound design, the music as well, really, another masterpiece, and I am glad that I played it.While it is more challenging in gameplay than Gris (I gotta draw the parallel, as I have recently replayed it due to Neva's release), I believe this difference was handled quite well too!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Everything is gorgeous - the visuals, the music, the gameplay, everything! I loved the studio's first game, GRIS, so I knew that I would love Neva. I love that the speaking lines are very minimal, and they let the music and visuals tell you the story. It's relatively short, it took me about 4 hours to get through and that's because I took my time going into extra spots and taking in the scenery. Give Neva a try, you won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 game, I think this is something every artist should play. The visuals, design, animation and music are flawlessly breathtaking. Its not a hard game but I think theres just enough critical thinking and strategy involves that is still satisfying making it past an obsticle. I've finished this game twice and about to finish t=my third run through and I've only had the game for a few days
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Chills, just chills- that's all I can really say. It's been a long time since I've been this genuinely blown away by a game at every turn and new corner. I never thought I would play a game more visually stunning than Gris but within mere moments of the first chapter it was clear that Neva would blow Gris out of the water. With a similar style to Gris but with a world that felt more full than it sometimes I would find myself stopping for a moment just to wait and watch. I cannot recommend a game enough, it was a lovely experience and worth every last penny. I could rave about it for a while more, with the sound design, beautiful music, characters, and everything else but I'm afraid this review would get ridiculously long. So take my word for it along with everyone else's- if you're on the search for your next game, pick up Neva
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Thank you for this game ... I hugged my dog for 45min after finishing it !Everyone is already commenting on the amazing art and music, but what struck me the most is how the game design is polished. The encounters with enemies (and the enemy design!!), the platforming, the walking/running around, everything is calibrated so you never get tired or bored. I can't wait to see what this studio does next !
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: For me, onee of the most standout aspects of NEVA its captivating atmosphere, brought to life by the incredible music from Berlinist. The score knows exactly how to manipulate the mood—calm and soothing when the world is at peace, but shifting to anxious rhythms whenever tension rises... This subtle use of music amplifies the emotional depth of each scene, or playthrough, making every moment feel significant.The game's lore and style are also a refreshing change from the GRIS. It's clear that the developers put a lot of thought into crafting a world that feels unique, pulling players in with a rich setting and intriguing story with a Canine companion.Of course, I can't talk about NEVA without mentioning the wolf companion, Neva herself. For me, she’s an absolute highlight! Not only is she adorable, but the game uses her brilliantly to pull at your heartstrings. For example, I was genuinely scared when Neva whimpered after a fall, and the close call during the rescue attempt had me on edge... On the other side...Watching her grow and fight alongside me made for some of the game's most triumphant moments.In terms of gameplay/storywise, the emotional manipulation is spot-on. You feel every moment, whether it’s fear, joy, or relief. Neva’s progression especially tugged at my heart, from her vulnerability early on to the sheer excitement when she became strong enough to help fight off enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The tutorial is great but it got to a point of confusion and a bunch of questions in my head. Most of the time, I am like. What the heck is going on. Even to the very end I was so confused. Who's that, who's this, why's that happening. It would be nice for hidden lore like a book or maybe a scribble somewhere but not a single one. Besides that, I guess it's an okay game if you love being led by the game
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: good game. not quite the absolute masterpiece the first one was, but a really solid addition.sometimes you can't tell what you can pass through or what's ground and what isn't, sometimes you get hit by really cheap shots like blocks falling from the sky, and sometimes you try to attack an enemy and they're actually invulnerable until they finish their animation and the little guy pops out,but on the plus side, the combat feels really solid, the enemy death animations are amazing, the movement is buttery smooth and intuitive, and the final boss fight is straight fire.Overall, I enjoyed it and I'm looking forward to the next one.Also, rolling was faster than just holding a direction, so I spammed roll the entire game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Even better graphics, story, and overall feeling than Gris.  Highly recommended.  Slight nitpicks - the combat system is a little unforgiving and frustrating at times, but when I did get stuck, it was only for a few minutes.  Plus, if you really got stuck, there is a game mode that supposedly skips the combat altogether (at least that what the description sounded like - I haven't tried it.)  And the achievements are a little annoying and random, but I feel that way about achievements in most games.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This was the most beautiful game I have EVER played and it also made me literally sob for 10 minutes straight after finishing it. I teared up several times throughout playing, sometimes just because of how beautiful it was, but the ending really ripped me apart. BEAUTIFUL game. I cannot express how much I loved it even though I was devastated (bitter-sweet) by the end. I will never stop thinking about it and never stop telling people they should play it. Stunning art, beautiful story, very fun combat, emotionally damaging but also made my heart feel so full?? I'm in awe. Just play it, please. ｡ﾟ(ﾟ´Д｀ﾟ)ﾟ｡
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: When I first heard about Neva I truly hoped it will be half as good as Gris, which is one of my absolute favorite games ever. After finishing it, I cried a lot. Neva is a beautiful masterpiece, I loved my pure hearted wolf, . If you have heart, you should play this game. If you don't, you should play even more.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After I had first played Gris, I never expected to see a beautiful game like that again. I was wrong. Nomada Studio delivered and it was worth the wait. Gris will always have a special place in my heart but Neva did not disappoint, and just like Gris has managed to become one of my favourite games of all time. The art and visuals, music, story..it was all magnificent. This game brought me to tears over and over, and I wouldn't have it any other way. Neva is a masterpiece in every way, it's not particularly long but a game doesn't always have to be very long, the time this game gives you is more than enough. The pacing is outstanding, the combat isnt overly complicated and even then you can always turn on story mode if you want to focus only on the story, which is something I did. Berlinist delivered once again with such beautiful music that puts one at ease. I cannot recommend this game enough. Nomada studio you will forever be my favourite game studio, from now until forever.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Note: Since I played GRIS first, I cannot not compare GRIS and Neva.Neva feels like the older sibling of GRIS. Beware: it is really much darker than GRIS regarding themes and presentation.Difficulty: I switched rather fast to story mode (not dying in combat) since the adventure mode was just too hard for me (only 3 lives etc). I play Nomada Games for the atmosphere, not for the frustration. So I am super grateful that they included these too modes.I liked Neva very much, though GRIS stays my favourite game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game brought me such comfort. The colours, the music, Neva, it is all so wonderful. If you enjoyed games like Gris, The Last Guardian, or studio ghibli movies you should definitely play this game. There is combat but there is a story mode so you don't need to feel stressed about it if you prefer that. Also, I would say it is definitely worth it to spend time collecting all the flowers. :)
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: As they said, "A true work of art". Ads:Every interaction with Neva is so sweet, the theme and hand drawn art is just super cool, and mobs bring many flashbacks to the Faceless Spirit.Cons:I wish some cut-scenes and chasing/escaping gameplay to be made shorten and more compact so they're more emotional.Overall:9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I really love this game and I am happy Nomada Studios did pull another masterpiece with this. It's such a simple concept about the four seasons, the cycle of life but made into a painterly, cosy and emotional game.I really like every detail in this game and the inspirations it took from. The combat is quiet challenging when you are used of the cosyness and no-fail-state of GRIS. Gladly though there is a story mode for accessability, which is always appreciated.I really enjoyed the gameplay with your puppy Neva, with additional abilities you get over the seasons. The watercolor artstyle, the flash-like animation style and the story-telling without dialoque is a trademark of this studio and I am sure they can come up with additional cosy games like this but with different twists.✨✨ Keep on creating these beautiful games that make you cry and smile. ✨✨
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After GRIS, expectations were high, but Neva more than met them. While -just like in GRIS- much of the game could be described as a "walking simulator", it does matter what kind of "walking" it is. And oh my, it is BEAUTIFUL yet again... It is Journey. It is pure, condensed Art. The combat is fairly simplistic, but it flows flawlessly, the platforming challenges are fairly good. While it is not the deepest game there is out there gameplay-wise, in fact, it is quite "casual" friendly, Neva, just like GRIS, is a masterpiece everyone should experience at least once in their lifetime.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a masterpiece, from the level design to the backgrounds you run across as you traverse the different seasons. The combat is simple yet incredibly fun especially as you progress further into the game. If you are on the fence about trying this game out let this be the push you need to experience a story that will leave you staring at the screen long after the credits have finished rolling.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Gris, which is one of the rare games I played several times. Neva is another beautiful experience, with an impressive artistic design. Game is simple, but you gain some abilities the more you progress, and combats can be tight (but I found difficulty to be well-balanced). The game is short though: about 6 hours to finish it while taking my time, maybe two extra more if you really want to collect all the flowers and 100% it.I found the story moving, even if it felt uselessly sad to me. I understand the main theme the creators wanted to express, but I think there was room for more positivity or hope. Maybe I just needed some uplifting vibes at the time I played it, I don't know. The price tag feels slightly overpriced to me, as again, the game is quite short. 15 euros would have felt more appropriate. But this game is so beautiful that you'll probably feel like you are buying a work of art, more than just a video game. I still recommend playing this game, as it is really unique. I'll definitely keep following this studio, who have an amazing talent for connecting players to a variety of powerful emotions. Good job!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another masterpiece of ART and GAME. Everything about it was so beautiful and immersive. Every person that was involved and support in creating this game: bravo, chef's kiss, I love you, and thank you. The entire time I was playing this game has made it to my core memory and will cherish this experience. From the bottom of my heart, I thank you for creating such a wonderful, thrilling, meaningful, and sensational game. Truly.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful game that is beautiful and emotionally powerful.  Berlinist produced another great soundtrack that complimented the game nicely.  However, I thought Gris was more impactful as a whole and Berlinist's soundtrack in that game did more than just compliment the game, it elevated it to a different level.  Nomada Studios is fantastic!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A very beautiful game. The gameplay is fun and provides a challenge without becoming frustrating. There is also a story mode if you don't want to have to worry about the difficulty. The artwork is incredible and definitely the star of the show for me, over story or gameplay, and the music and other audio is well done.It is a little short, but to my mind that had the advantage of the game never overstaying it's welcome. I never got sick of it or wished it was over faster.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The art of Conrad Roset as well as the wonderful programming team Nomada Studios is an must buy.I have played the game to 100% now in under 5 hours. Tho am not disappointed at all.The story was very beautiful. Combined with the right colors for the right scenes and emotions it really hits hard. The same feeling I had when I was playing Gris too.Thank you for this wonderful game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I finished the game after playing around nine hours of playing and can confidently say this is one of the most beautiful games i've played. I bought it for the art and it followed through. the story is deeply touching and had me crying at the end. i'm for sure going to do another play through to 100 percent it. i bought this game on a whim and i'm very glad i did.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Again, Nomada Studio creates a little gem. Following Gris, they maintain the high quality on graphical art and music, while adding a new beautiful story and new mechanics to make the game a bit more challenging and long. Easily one game that will share my 'play again every year' list with Portal, Portal 2, Inside and other short but impactfuly and beautiful games.As a catalan myself, I can't help but feel connected and love the names they chose.
