Neva in catalan means 'It is snowing'.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: holy moly this game is a work of art. visually and auditorily immaculate, emotionally compelling, fluid platforming, varied mechanics that build on each other steadily and interestingly, satisfying boss fights, press P to pet the dog (which is actually meaningful/functional in-game), what more could you ask for. Worth the couple hours and tear(s) shed!!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Short review: 😭Longer review: If you loved Gris you are going to love this as well. It has all the elements that Gris had: Beautiful graphics that look like a painting, amazing music, touching story that might make you cry. The gameplay is also pretty simple similarly to Gris. So it is mainly 2D platforming but unlike Gris this one has combat as well which is not overly complicated but responsive and enjoyable. The game constantly brings in new and interesting gameplay elements. So it never gets boring. Just as Gris, this is also on the shorter side. It was about 6 hours for me to complete it and then a little longer to collect the remaining achievements. So if length is something that's important to you then take this into consideration.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A short but beautiful game. Decently challenging, but not frustrating.  The story is minimalist but touching. Very Princess Mononoke vibes.Almost every frame is a painting, and there are some amazing shots. As well as some shots out of a horror film.While the game is short, about 4 or 5 hours. It's definitely fun and a great experience.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: GRIS is my favorite game of all time, so seeing Nomada release a new game had me extremely excited. Neva is similar to GRIS in alot of ways but also very different as well. The story revolves around you and your wolf companion (Neva) traversing what seems to be a crumbling world corrupted by black goop (sounds kinda familiar). The art and music just like GRIS are fantastic and vibrant and every just looks and sounds amazing. I could stare and the backgrounds or listen to the soundtrack for hours! The story is also a real tear jerker (no spoilers) though I still prefer GRIS's ending. ALSO, I love they have an adventure and story mode. Basically, you cant really die to combat in story mode, and thats about it. Unfortunately, there are a few things I either found frustrating or flat out hated. Im sorry, but the combat is terrible. It's extremely basic, clunky, and gets really stale really quickly. Even when they try to introduce new enemies they usually boil down to more health or kinda harder to hit. I really wish story mode just let you one shot everything cause by the 10th time i was rolling my eyes that i had to fight another boring group of basic enemies. I hope going forward they either dont have combat in their next game or figure out a way to spice it up or something cause man, its just awful. The two other points are somewhat combat related but 1. hitboxes were sometimes extremely janky and the platforming just felt a bit worse than GRIS. IDK what it was but sometimes id just clip through a platofrm i was very obviously supposed to land on and was clearly flat in the center of it, or sometimes id just not perform the action i imputed. Ill chalk that last one up to maybe either a bug or my controller, but still, it frustrated me alot. FInally, PLEASE changes the way you aim Neva. Once you get the ability to launch them at enemies, they use it in platforming as well. But it just auto locks onto whatever thing youre closest too. You dont actually aim it. At one point i got stuck on a really basic puzzle cause no matter what Neva would always lock onto a platform i didnt want to destroy and instantly break it. I would literally tilt the joystick in the opposite direction but nope. Please actually allow me to aim Neva when it comes to platforming or add an option to turn off auto lock.Even with all the jank, I still really loved this game. Another great tear jerker from Nomada and I really hope they continue to make more games, but hopefully next one they expand on things abit more, maybe try another style other than a 2d platformer cause as said, not everything really worked. I still personally think GRIS is better, but its 100% down to preference here, cause i could easily see how others would like this more depending on what kind of stories and gameplay you prefer. Please support Studio Nomada, they make wonderful art and I hope they continue to do so.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The game is gorgeous, but you have eyes and can see that for yourself. Combat is solid, pretty basic, but it's satisfying and better than I'd have expected from an artsy game like this.It's pretty short and unfortunately leaves the beautiful forest pretty quickly, veering into more surreal landscapes. It's still gorgeous, but I would've preferred more time with the natural world.I'd recommend it, with the caution that it's very short for the price. My 6 hours includes going back to get all the achievements and collectables. Expect 2-3 hours on your first playthrough. I think it was worth it, but that call will vary wildly based on your gaming budget.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is beautiful. Plain and simple. The visuals, the music, the gameplay, it all just is so seamless and flows with a level that is just unmatched. You will smile, laugh, cry, and just thoroughly feel fulfilled by the end of the story. I rarely have games like this where I have to thoroughly recommend with zero complaints, and also feel totally comfortable in feeling like its a 10/10 game. Don't care if its like a 3 hr game, its 3 hrs that will make you feel something, and as gamers thats all we look for in life.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: After GRIS, Neva is another stunning visual experience. You've got to command Nomada Studio for their beautiful sceneries and masterful use of color. The music by Berlinist is wonderfully composed and it does really work in synergy with what's in front of your eyes.I found Neva to be slightly harder than GRIS, not for the combat which is simple and immediate, but when it came to certain jump sessions, as you have to execute your movements to a millimetric precision. As for the story, I liked it fine, though I have to admit that I liked GRIS better. However, I'll for certain replay Neva, to look for details I might have missed.All in all, Neva is a wonderful game and does shine along with its predecessor in Nomada Studio video game production history.10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Easily one of the most beautiful games I've played this year. Neva is the second game from Nomada Studio, the creators of GRIS. While I'm a bit bummed that it doesn’t have the same watercolor aesthetic as GRIS, but it’s equally breathtaking on its own right. I couldn't help but take screenshots every few minutes. Complementing the gorgeous art is the enchanting soundtrack, which is soothing during moments of tranquil and ramps up during the more intense moments.The moment to moment gameplay is more varied this time, featuring light platforming, combat, and puzzles. The combat is simple, where your character has access to one basic attack string which you will be using throughout most encounters. However, the progression comes through your wolf companion, Neva, who gains new abilities as she grows. These abilities aid in combat, platforming, and puzzle-solving. This is no precision platformer with complex combat and puzzles but it is engaging enough to keep you interested. Although at times I feel there are too many combat encounters. The boss encounters were pretty good though.The real heart of the game is the journey of Alba and Neva. The theme of parenthood is wonderfully expressed through their interactions with each other, their bond, growth, and the struggles as they make their way through a dying yet incredibly beautiful world. Their fight against the spreading corruption, in the hope of a better future, is emotional, with both a heartbreaking opening and a moving conclusion.Overall, Neva is a wonderful experience, and I hope Nomada Studio continues to create such impactful games in the years to come.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game was an emotional rollercoaster! The gameplay was amazing, the art and overall visual are such eyecandy, especially the cutscenes, the soundtrack was so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ phenomenal, and even though the story isn't told through word and can be a little confusing, it's still an emotional story about a woman and her lovely wolf companion!I would highly recommend to anyone, it such a great time!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva  is a visually stunning and emotionally gripping adventure that combines the best elements of side-scrolling platformers with a rich narrative. Developed by Nomada Studio, creators of the acclaimed "Gris," Neva follows a young woman and her mystical, antlered wolf companion as they navigate a rapidly decaying world.The artwork is breathtaking, with hand-drawn landscapes that seem like they're pulled straight from a moving painting. The atmospheric soundtrack perfectly complements the emotional weight of the story, which will tug at your heartstrings from start to finish. The relationship between the protagonist and her wolf companion is the core of the narrative, and it’s impossible not to feel attached to them as they face increasing challenges together.Gameplay-wise, Neva offers smooth mechanics with a balance of puzzles, action, and platforming. While not overwhelmingly difficult, the game presents enough challenge to keep players engaged. The combat system is fluid, and the exploration is rewarding, offering unique mechanics introduced at a steady pace throughout the game. The emotional highs and lows are expertly crafted, leaving a lasting impact on players long after the credits roll.For fans of "Gris" or anyone who appreciates beautifully crafted indie games, "Neva" is a must-play. It's not just a game but an emotional journey that beautifully blends art, music, and story. Nomada Studio has once again delivered a masterpiece.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's a masterpiece. Short but sweet. Fantastic visuals, phenomenal soundtrack and a great story. The gameplay, puzzles and platforming were just challenging enough to keep you engaged throughout the whole playthrough. There is a bit of replay value to find all of the hidden flowers throughout the game as well. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Fantasic. A very strong Princess Monoke vibe. If you grew up reading books about wolves (Julie of the Wolves). Or had a wolf obsession as a kid, imagined living with wolves, running with wolves, playing with wolf pups. This game fulfills that. Its like my childhood dreams laid out before me in a compelling story and intense platformer. Wielding a katana and fighting alongside with a wolf to defeat evil. The music and art work is just amazing, soothing and intense. If you have played Gris, you'll love this game. Neva has more concrete themes and a story line that takes place over time through the seasons with a clear understanding of who the villain is. Gris is a dream of overcoming grief, rebuilding your world after the devastation of losing a loved one and re-establishing identity. Neva is the story of a girl and her wolf, set out to defeat evil and save the forest. But there are also wonderful themes of motherhood, adoption and self sacrifice to protect those you love. Another huge plus to this game is that you can interact with the wolves with hugs, pets and affection. The game is full of art, music and emotion. The story line had me in tears and I was devastated that the game ended so soon. I wish it could have gone on and on and on. But I still get to go back and find all the achievements and bonus puzzles I missed the first time. I love this game and you will too.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Nomada Studio has knocked it out of the park once again! This game is a masterclass in atmosphere, action, and storytelling. The gameplay delivers an intense and satisfying experience, where you step into the shoes of a badass, female John Wick meets Constantine, battling demons in the underworld with your loyal dog companion by your side. Each combat sequence is a mix of adrenaline-pumping action and strategic precision. The visuals and music amplify the mood, pulling you deeper into the dark, captivating world. An absolute must-play for Gris fans! Goosebumps all the way!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: From the same developers, I had played Gris and knew I'd be in for some tears and heavy feelings...But I was not expecting just how hard this game would hit me.The visuals have improved massively from GRIS, while still maintaining the watercolour charms of the original one, enhanced by striking and visually interesting usage of gameplay mechanics and music.This is a game not to miss out on, if you are a fan of art, puppers and in search for an emotional outlet :')Thank you Nomada Studio for bringing this beautiful experience to us and demonstrating again that videogames are a form of art.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is just art and its so amazing. I didn´t encounter any buggs or glitches it worked perfectly fine for me. It totaly hooked me with the artstyle and music. I was positive suprised how good the combat works with this artful game and it never destroyed the awesome atmosphere of the game. All in all its a very good story and even without any text I could understand whats going on. Please keep up this awesome work :). I can only recommend everyone to play it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Beauty is in the eye of the beholder. This is art more than gameplay.If you're willing to pay the price for an artistic kind of experience, it's really worth it. Aside from one instance of a glitching wolf, I didn't get any noticeable issues.The game being a platformer is on the decent level, actually. It has some moderately difficult and pretty creative moments but nothing too grand in that aspect. The highlight is clearly on the art and sound direction for this game, both of which were integrated well into the level of gameplay it has, with the Winter level platforms being very competitive. Very nice presentation of the worldbuilding, all in all. It's Color Pallette (the game), and it definitely deserves praise for that.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I definitely recommend this game, especially for fans of their previous game, Gris. It's gorgeous right from the start, as you'd expect.  The platforming sequences are done quite well, but not so challenging that you'd need to be an expert in Celeste to get through them.  The combat is simple, but thankfully requires looking for openings and patterns instead of button-mashing.  There are a few small knocks on the game.  It's short (though I knew that going in) with the only replay value is in getting collectibles.  The ending was good but not entirely satisfying.  Finally, it didn't have that immense emotional punch that I got from Gris.Still I was far more pleased than not for this game.  I absolutely hope there's a third game from them coming in a few years' time.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game like GRIS but not quite as good. Combat is pretty basic, music is wonderful, visuals are great but you tend to get zoomed out really far way too often. As good as the artwork is it can be a bit annoying to see where and what the enemy is at times. Might be a bit too expensive at its full price considering its about 3-4 hrs.Works perfectly on Steam Deck.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Around 7/10Art - 10The art is really good, combing hand-drawing with some 2D shaders and the animation is smooth and gorgeous. It's better than girs from my perspective.Music - 8Good but not impressiveGame Flow - 6Like a hero journeyGameplay -4So many repeated enemies and the battle system is so boring. The first two chapters are disasters to me.Level Design - 4I don't know why they made some really boring long walk. And most levels are not that interesting at all. The third chapter is well-designed. Another thing is like why they don't utilize the main mechanic of the chapter in their boss fighting.Overall, it's a gorgeous, beautiful artwork with some mediocre gameplay and a normal game flow. But I still really admire people who made this and who is trying to make games like this.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: First off, I think the art in this game is very pretty and I love the whole concept. The black creatures with the white masks are interesting and remind me of No Face from Spirited Away.On the downside, I found the battling to be kind of a slog. I don't mind a challenge but some of it felt like just trying to dodge hit without a lot of thought to it. It felt a bit frustrating. I'm stubborn so I wanted to beat it in normal, but if you're just here for the environment or don't like repeatative battles, probably doing story based mode is better.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A compact, beautiful game. There's less puzzling here than Gris but this game adds combat. The combat comes in short chunks and failure will only send you back a short time. Like Gris, this game is really about the setting. The camera is not shy about pulling way back and letting you take in the view. The game is very good at throwing you into new situations to mix things up, so you're not getting the same handful of actions over and over again for the short runtime. If you liked Gris, I recommend this one as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is an absolutely amazing game that offers a perfect blend of simplicity and challenge. While the gameplay isn't too difficult, the mechanics are perfectly balanced, making every action feel smooth and well-thought-out. What truly stands out is the captivating storyline—it's incredibly engaging and filled with so much emotion, it drew me in from the very beginning. Every moment of the narrative feels impactful, and the emotional depth adds an extra layer of immersion. I genuinely love this game and highly recommend it to anyone looking for a memorable experience. Without a doubt, it's a 10/10 for me!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Not even three minutes into this game and it already had me tearing up. Nomada Studio have absolutely come out swinging with Neva! After an hour and completing the first part of the game it definitely feels like they took all the feedback, both good and bad, from Gris and brought it to this game. The artwork is just as good, if not better, than in Gris. Berlinist is absolutely outdoing themselves with the soundtrack and the introduction of an actual combat system adds a much needed kick to really make this feel like a game rather than an interactive story. I can not express how ready I am for this game to hurt me (in a good way).Also: you can pet Neva!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Amazingly beautiful game, the most beautiful game I’ve played. The landscapes, the colors, the atmospheric music. I've waited long for this game and it certainly lives up to expectations.The gameplay is a nice smooth puzzle platformer with challenging combat. If you’re like me and motor skills are not your strong point, or if you just want to chill, then you can play in story mode to take the combat down a few notches. You can then still experience the puzzles, story and platforming.Bonus points:1. Cute dog2. You can pet the dogIf you enjoyed Gris, you’ll most likely enjoy Neva too. Play it on the biggest screen you have.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I am not sure I can put everything into words here, but I will try to! I have only completed it once so far though I am very much looking forward to playing it through again sometime soon! While simple at first, the fighting and platform mechanics are progressively built upon in intuitive ways as you progress through the game. The traversal feels great and fits the style excellently! The developers of this game were incredibly good doing so much with less! While most of combat is focused on jumping, dodging, attacking with sword/range attacking. It is enhanced so much by the use of the environment and its beautifully creative design! I found myself lost in this game for the 4 hours it took to finish my play through and I was brought to tears towards the end of the game! If you are a Fan of games like GRIS which this developer made previously or titles like Journey, I would highly recommend this to you! If you are not, I would still recommend it to everyone else to at least try it. As it feels to me like a gem I will remember for years to come!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely breathtaking game. I loved GRIS and Neva is an exceptional follow up to a previously stunning game. The visuals and music are absolutely gorgeous, every scene is a painting rich in color. The story is heartwarming and pulls at the heartstrings all the same. The puzzles and combat are fun and clever without being too punishing. Absolutely 10/10 just like GRIS. Thank you for making such a beautiful game. Highly recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This will be remembered as one of the most memorable games of all time for me. Firstly, the introduction of the combat was welcomed. It adds just the right amount of tension and complexity to the game without straying away from the flow, purpose, and emotion of the core game. Any more complex and it wouldn't fit the philosophy they were going for. The puzzles were quite simple, but the collectibles required a bit of thought and were fun to figure out along the way. The art... oh man the art. The colors, environments, music, and sound design danced with each other so perfectly that it felt like I was living a dream and not playing a video game. The use of imagery is simply astounding. This is one of the first examples I'll use to explain to people why video games have the most potential out of any form of media when it comes to expressing art. Phenomenal work Berlinist on the music!The story is something that I am still trying to unravel, but I know plenty of people will find value in the poignant message. The dynamic between your character and Neva was sincerely touching. It's fun how throughout the whole game, she is the one to evolve, not the player's character.Thank you Nomada! I shall have my eyes on whatever comes next!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: For all those who have played Gris, there's definitely a lot of recognizable architecture/subtle references in this one. The art has definitely improved (and I thought the art in Gris was already beautiful). I like how this game keeps going from "aw this is so serene and beautiful" to "oh my god what is that no STOP THAT IS TERRIFYING".This game also feels much more uplifting and hopeful than Gris, at least to me. Gris was more bittersweet and heartwrenching, at least to me. Some might disagree with me and that's okay!When it comes to the combat, it's very creative and cool, but also a tad repetitive? This is likely because I am not always into that sort of stuff. I tried playing on adventure mode but then quickly discovered that I have a massive skill issue so I went into story mode. It kind of felt like fighting mobs while in creative, which was a little boring. I wish there was some sort of in-between the two.I loved the platforming, my absolute favourite part was the ones with the "mirror" in winter. I wish it was longer! It was so good!But all in all, a good game. Good job Nomada! Looking forward to whatever you all make next <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Masterpiece. Neva isn't only a feast for the eyes, but a genuinely clever game and a moving experience, especially since I'm sensitive to its themes. While the gameplay is fairly simple, the pacing and mechanics that keep getting added through the game always make it engaging. If only it lasted a bit longer!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Stunning game from a visual and sound design standpoint. Absolutely gorgeous. Very quick to play and great storytelling without dialogue. The ending made me cry and I do think elements of the ending took away from the story a little bit, but hey it evoked strong emotion which meant I was invested. And had some super creative mechanics and level design throughout.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Video games are art, and this is proof. Once again Nomada Studio delivers a beautiful, vibrant, and compelling game with a story that is sure to stir quite a few emotions. Similar in art style to Gris, their previous game, the visuals in this game are striking and memorable. The audio as well is very well crafted and seamlessly blended into the experience. Unlike Gris, this game features more proper combat. I played on Adventure mode and died many times. That being said, I don't think this game is very difficult but for anyone that may not be a fan of combat there is a Story mode that I would assume dials it back a bit. As far as negatives go, I can imagine some people not liking the fact that it is so short. It took me about 4 hours to beat (not doing every optional collectible but most of the ones I found) but I don't feel like that's a bad thing. The length of the game is perfect, I think it tells its story and then stops. There is no need for extra stuff (more combat encounters, etc) at least in my opinion because I don't think it would add to what the game is trying to do and say. Honestly, I could have actually seen the game being a bit shorter if they cut out some of the time when your just holding down a direction on the controller and just running across a flat plane. I'd say those sections would be a negative were it not for the beautiful art on display during them. Total pass in my book for the showcasing of what the art team could do. I don't feel like I can oversell how great everything looks.My recommendation is you play this as soon as possible, it isn't very long and will leave you with a more memorable experience than a lot of other games would. I found it fun and interesting to play, and the story says so much by only uttering a single word.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Visually, it's absolutely stunning—it's hard to find a frame that isn't beautiful. The gameplay is good, and so is the music, but nothing compares to the highlight: its art direction.I can't help but compare it to Gris, which this game visually surpasses, though it doesn't match in emotional impact (partly because the music wasn’t integral to the story, so the soundtrack took a backseat, being "only" nice but not "meaningful").Still, I wholeheartedly recommend it. Unique games like this deserve support.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: OK, I really LOVE this game! But guys... Why are u doing that to me? After ending scene i was literally speechless, devastated and crying like a baby. 38-years old baby. Anyway, thank you for amazing experience! GRIS and NEVA forever in my heart! Love You!(sorry for my english, it's not my native)Neva is a goodest girl ever!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: If you liked Gris why haven't you bought it already and still reading this...!For everyone else, easily a 10/10 if you like calm and emotional storytelling with wonderful music.I highly recommend playing it with an HDR capable device and a good audio setup (good speaker or headphones). It adds a lot to the game.I recommend playing it in one go which is like 3-4h, splitting it pulls you out of the atmosphere. If you have to I recommend doing so when the seasons change.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is an absolutely fantastic experience. My heart runneth over with love and sadness and happiness and hope and so many emotions mixed into one. The amount of detail and symbolism that went into every moment of this is pretty astounding. As a mother, this game tapped into the heart of what it feels like to care for a young child and watch them grow into their own person, knowing that there is so much darkness in the world. But you have one another, care for one another, love one another, and will always be there to protect one another.I hear so many people say there aren't enough mother protagonists in games. Well Nomada Studio has created yet another to join the growing list of games that highlight the strength of a mother's love: Venba, Endling: Extinction is Forever, and now Neva. A big thanks to the team for this journey that will live in my heart always.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Nomada Stuidio is now 2 for 2, with Neva being not only a worthy successor to Gris, but a triumph in and of itself.It shows they took everything they knew or learned from Gris and built upon it, creating an experience that feels familiar yet new and refreshing all at once. The visuals and music are as jaw-droppingly gorgeous and evocative as they were in Gris, with dominating color pallets giving identity and segmentation to each chapter and area. The platforming is satisfying and challenging in sections without feeling unfair. Finally the combat, for a developer that hasn't had a game featuring combat before, is immensely satisfying. Simple enough that anyone can do it and with just enough challenge to make enemy confrontations feel satisfying and rewarding.The story, heavily centering around parenthood and the importance of properly raising a fully functioning child that can grow to become independent and autonomous on their own, stirs the emotions and tugs at the heartstrings. If I were made of lesser stuff, I know I would have shed tears near the end.I believe with this game, Nomada has solidified its place in the indie game sphere as a true force to be reckoned with, and I eagerly anticipate anything else they will ever release.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: If you're on the fence about this game: Buy it. Buy it now. Do as little research into it as you can and go in blind. What a fantastic game. When I heard that the developers of Gris, my favorite game of all time, had a new release I bought it immediately. I was nervous to play it because you can only play it for the first time once, and I wanted to love it. It did not disappoint in the slightest. The visuals are breathtaking, as is custom for Nomada at this point. I stopped constantly while traversing the landscapes to simply admire the fantastic art that the game takes place in. Berlinist nailed the soundtrack again, I'm so glad they were brought back to do the score. I didn't look very hard at the store page before buying and playing it, so I went in without knowing that there would be combat. It was responsive and fairly forgiving, providing a respawn point nearby for any challenging moments. It added to the story and gave a sense of challenge that got me invested in the plot and characters. Spoilers below: 10/10. Will return to 100% it once the feeling of the initial playthrough wears off.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: What a beautiful game. I can't emphasize how much care went into every moment of this masterpiece. Every part of each season decorated so eloquently with perfect color palettes. Your character and Neva's relationship is one of pure joy and love for nature and for connectivity to all living things. The theme of darkness being present all the time and light finding a way to coexist with it speaks to an experience that everyone who plays this game has had before. This might've been the most enjoyable time for $20 I have had in a long time.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A game of unparalleled beauty.Neva was my most anticipated game of this year and it managed to surpass every one of my expectations. Everything from the challenging but never frustrating puzzles, the combat, the platforming, the music, and of course, the art, all left me captivated and in awe from the first to final minute. Even the credits were stunningly done. It is the best game I have played in many, many years, and I have added it to my short but treasured list of masterpieces.I cannot get over how unspeakably gorgeous this game is. It lives in my heart now and I don't think it'll ever be moving out.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I think Neva is a very solid game. The combat is smooth and simple, and offers challenge without becoming obnoxiously hard. The story is pretty straightforward and not particularly entrancing. I felt frustrated at the ending, and although the music from Berlinist is still very good it doesn't quite hit the notes of GRIS.I think GRIS just set the bar really high for me, but I won't say I regret playing this game or didn't like it. This is still a very pretty and enjoyable experience. Highlight for me were the puzzles in Winter 1.8.5/10
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Somehow Nomada managed to increase on the beauty of Gris, all while adding significant depth to the gameplay.Basing my expectations on Gris I wasn't expecting nearly as much of a challenge but it worked out perfectly. The challenge was there to force you to actually take the time to learn that part of the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Incredible experience. This game is truly something special, and I was left wanting more (in a good way) Every season is beautiful and the visual storytelling here is exceptional to the point where I hardly noticed the lack of dialogue. The game is short, so if $20 is a big ask for 5ish hours then hold off..but absolutely come back to this one
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is another masterpiece from Nomada, I must say... They were able to create a completely new game with an emotional and super incredible history and soundtrack, these two mixed together with the game design/scenario (one of the most beautiful game scenario that I ever had the pleasure to see) they created that big massive bomb of *emotions*. This game reminds me of my dog... She passed away a year ago and I'm still not over it, and this game took the role of a door that opened my eyes and made me reminds all good moments that I had at her side when she was alive, overpassing the sadness and melancholy, that resides in my heart. Amazing game, congratulations Nomada
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This was a truly beautiful game! It was sad, but it was so beautiful that instead of sadness I just felt warmth.There were people in the negative comments saying the story was lacking, but as a father, this one hit every bit as deep as Gris. I agree that this one was particularly shorter, but I'm saying that before I try to 100% it, there might be some more lore around the corner. Even if not, this was an amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the perfect successor to Gris. Fun fluid platforming with an incredibly soundtrack and beautiful environments to explore. I love the combat, I was originally worried that it would feel sluggish and lackluster, but every single swing of your sword feels like you're hitting the screen with a hammer. The combat is so crunchy and it feels so smooth. The game is soothing and yet incredibly tense. There a heart pumping platforming "boss" sections like in Ori, as well as incredibly fun actual boss fights. Dying is super quick and has a terrifying death animation, but you don't hate yourself for dying because you can get right back in again. It has another mode for those that want to focus more on the platforming and storytelling rather than the combat, but I urge you to play on the intended difficulty and change it if you don't like it. I've been waiting for this game to come out for a long time, and it's even better than what I thought it was going to be.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It is worth playing for visual art and music alone. Very atmospheric and emotional. The gameplay is also engaging, at times developers even show a few clever tricks.That being said, I actually prefer Gris. The previous game had symbolism in it which elevated both the art and overall mood. Here I feel like this is just a simple (but nice!) story, there is nothing more to it, you get what you see. The ending is also needlessly confusing. Everything else is completely straightforward, but for this one scene it is quite easy to get it wrong. When watching I got it wrong, near the end of the scene I got it half right, and only after a while I got it completely right. Alas, most of the emotional impact was lost in the process.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: it's not like i needed any kind of confirmation that nomada studio was amazing because of how beautiful and dear to my heart gris had been to me but god they've done it again......... i have loved every aspect of neva and nomada studio has once again struck the strings of my heart throughout the entire game. the elements of the story were absolutely gut-wrenching and the story telling was once again masterful... the gameplay was incredibly fun and diverse and i didn't expect anything less than gorgeous from the studio when it comes to the artistic direction and music.please play both gris and neva.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Games are art and this game is the proof. Mozart sould be jealous on its soundtrack, Picasso and Michelangelo on its artstyle. Hideo Kojima for its gameplay and Miazaki for its final boss fight.I don´t know if this game is the best of this year, but for me right now after first playthrough it is one of my favorite games ever and I hope you will like it as well. This game is not easy but it is not hard aswell. Everyone can play it and see what is art. I will come back Neva and we will howl on the moon together someday again and we will complete all achievements.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: As being huge fan of GRIS, I really was looking forward for NEVA. Was it good? YES! The artwork was stunning and I really loved the way they added combat to this. I'm totally going to play it again and again! Still... I'm a big cry baby when it comes to games and stories. GRIS touched my heart and I don't know did my expectations kinda ruined this. But I couldn't really feel that emotional roller coaster while playing this at all.Really pretty game with the music making the atmosphere even better! Go and play it you will love it.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Phenomenal game! As in Gris, the audio and visual components convey a full range of emotions. I was taken from melancholy curiosity in chapter one to thrilled horror as the world warped around me. The entire game sings with feeling and I, personally, am going to demolish a tub of ice cream to cope with the ending
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: i knew this was gonna be good going in and i have to say that indeed my hunch was correct, it is a masterful blend of storytelling, video games and art. the game is a little short at around 4-5 hours playthrough, although i think i missed some paths that were optional although idk how many i missed. there was an earlyish boar enemy whose hitbox was a little stupidly behind him so rolling through him felt bad but otherwise it was a wonderful experience that i loved and will undoubtedly talk about and revisit in the future. dev is doing amazing, i would have liked to see some progression but really hte game length isnt suited to that and it would be bordering it onto other genres so that just me. still 9.7/10 for me
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Short answer: they did it again.Long answer: while the quality is over the top there are some few less impressive moments. You may disagree, anyway this is just my opinion. The plot in general feels somewhat generic. No spoilers here - the basics is shown in the trailer: some "dark forces" are conquering the forest and you with your magic dog must defeat them. No personal drama (beside the death of big dog in the very beginning), no complex world building, the mood of a mystery is also not very deep unlike in "Inside".The combat is beat-em-up with low number of enemies and no special combos. While it provides more gameplay in comparison with Gris, it definitely a thing to improve.Boss fights feels hard (or maybe just my personal skill issue), jumping is also sometimes hard forcing you to make very precise jumps, while occasional puzzles are simple.PS: final verdict - 11/10, everyone must play (:
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I don't know what to say about this game, I just absolutely need to recommend it. I love how it feels just as artistic as Gris while introducing combat and even slight horror(?) elements.Oh, and the soundtrack is phenomenal. If this soundtrack doesn't get a Materia Collective Piano Collections book, I don't know if I'll be able to die happy ;) The Gris Piano Collections was stellar, and this soundtrack deserves the same treatment
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: absolutely stunning. the visuals are BEAUTIFUL, as well as the music carrying a lot of emotional punches. i do have to admit that i played through in the story mode to avoid dying 300 times over lmao, but that's more a result of my lack of gaming prowess than the game itself. with that setting turned on the combat is pretty simple & easy, but the game's atmosphere is so well crafted that the fights still felt tense, and the visuals were still thrilling. i appreciate the simplicity here and that the narrative can be interpreted in various ways, but still feels powerful. definitely a game I'll be replaying again and again in the future <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Felt like playing a Studio Ghibli movie. There's some very strong Mononoke vibes and environmental subtext. Which is Amazing! If Hayao Miyazaki made video games, this is what it would look like! Another GORGEOUS game from Nomada Studios, Conrad Roset, and The Berlinist. With full use of color pallet they have absolutely exploded the screen with something so lush and vibrant you could almost mistake it for 8K Monitor test video or some Imax reel. It's dripping in saturation. It looks like a living oil painting.The game is not as emotionally devastating as GRIS which is fine and maybe subjective. It's still emotional, especially if you are an animal lover. But where GRIS firmly plants you in midst of despair and grief and left me curled up in a fetal position, this is much more of an adventure of life through the cycle of the seasons. Where grief is just a passing stage and you get to pet the doggo the ENTIRE GAME WHENEVER YOU WANT! The gameplay is challenging if you want it and if you'd rather not there is a story mode. I didn't find the combat overly difficult except for not knowing what I needed to do on several occasions which lead to some frustration. The on screen button prompts are VERY faint and blend in entirely if you don't know to look for them. I got Stuck on a section intended to teach you a new ability because I literally couldn't SEE the button prompt. I had to look up a walk through to realize there was a button prompt on screen. It's funny, the game has that thing where you tune the brightness so you can barely see the picture, but while normally this is used to keep the game dark enough but still visible, in NEVA it's the opposite. You MAY need to turn down your monitor brightness if you are sensitive! If you got one of those high nit oleds, good lord you are in for it!GRIS was a masterpiece and it's hard to follow that up, and while I doubt anything will ever hold up to what GRIS managed to do, I think Nomada knocked it out of the park with this. If you like art and platform games, if this game interested you at all, then get it! You won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Solid 8/10, I think GRIS had a deeper meaning to it with the colors and stuff but the art and depth of gameplay help it set Neva apart as a standalone game. Combat is serviceable and feels pretty good, especially in the latter half of the game specifically the final boss, story again is good but not great, though I may come around to it in the future with hindsight
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: It's hard to find the words to describe a game this incredible. The music, art, colors, sound, gameplay, I could go on for hours about how every detail somehow blew my already high expectations (based on my love for their game GRIS) completely out of the water. I took off work the day this came out and played it right through because I knew I would not be able to stop. Both beginning and end were heartbreakingly beautiful, this game was an experience I wont soon forget or leave. You will not regret playing one bit.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Buy Neva if you like any of these things:- astonishing visual design- buttery smooth gameplay- satisfying cloak animations- misty vistas- really big trees- whip thin swords- Princess Mononoke- unique, masterful color usage- quick, clever platforming- spectacle boss fights- low run time, high impact gamingMy two points of criticism:- I wish my character walked 10% faster- I wish Still a 5/5 experience for me.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Once again an absolute masterpiece from Nomada Studio.Stunning visuals from Conrad Roset and the creative team perfectly paired with an emotionally charged musical score from Berlinist. Neva is definitely a project made with love.The story was unforgettable. Without spoiling anything PLEASE. PLEASE get to the end before you judge it!There is a bit more gameplay and challenge to Neva than Gris - Metroidvania style but definitely on the easier side of things. The platforming was fun and each area felt fantastical and unique.It's about 4 hours long which is what I look for in a game since its hard to find time committing to extremely long epics. I can enjoy the entirety of Neva in one sitting.I may have already bought this game, but I love it so much that I am going to continue buying it for other platforms as well.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a beautiful masterpiece and left me in tears by the end of it, despite there being so few words. The colors and the art is like nothing I have seen in a game before, and it is excellent at invoking deep feelings. Everything in here is made with passion and intention, and even the dark forces you fight against are some of my favorite depictions of evil I have ever seen. It is a short game, it took me about three hours to get through, but I don't think this is a bad thing. The creators obviously had a specific image in mind and they kept things clean and simple, which allowed it to feel very complete overall. I have no other thoughts, I think it is wonderful and I will be suggesting it to my friends.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not go out of my way to play single player games, let alone own them, but this is one for the books.  The story brings you through an emotional journey, where you grow trying to put together the story of what is happening.  My gosh does it delivered.  I cried several times playing this game, and it is beautiful.  The combat is simple but you also have to be a little mindful.  The visuals are unique, giving the vibe of watercolor and vibrancy.  This is a great game, 10/10, and I hope to see other beautiful games like this one in the future
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game play, beautiful music, and difficult gameplay mechanics bring their own image that is very different from the previous Gris games. We are accompanied by a little wolf named Neva who will grow over time with each season, which is amazing in my opinion.However, the difficulty of the game is very hard on par with platform games like Hollow Knight that I played, mostly dying at the beginning of the game but I slowly learned not to always fail from previous mistakes. I highly recommend it for players who want to try a new challenge!
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Just stunning, visually, musically, and emotionally.  The level of care and detail that went into this to make all of the aspects of the game complement each other so well is immediately apparent.  Beyond the amazing artwork and music, I was particularly impressed by the detail of Alba and Neva's interactions throughout the game.If I had one critique it would be that the platforming and combat controls did not feel quite as precise as I would have liked them to be (I used an Xbox Controller on a PC that easily ran 4K resolution at 144 FPS), but this was a fairly minor distraction.The game has a short run time (I finished in 4.2 hours collecting most things but not obsessing over them).Overall, this is one of the best games that I have played in recent years.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I had been looking forward to this game for a long time, and had to play it right away.The music is absolutely stunning, the art style and light design is breathtaking. It was slightly more unsettling than I was expecting, but that just added to it in my opinion and made it even better. I cried as well, which wasn't unexpected either.BUTKIND-OF-SPOILERS ABOUT THE ENDINGI won't say anything too specific, so don't continue reading if you don't want sort-of-spoilers:The ending ended up making me so annoyed. It left me massively disappointed, and it kind of tainted the rest of the experience for me. I won't get into any more specifics, but I never expected to have such mixed feelings after finishing the game.I still recommend it of course, because everything else was great. But overall I'd say GRIS is a more solid game from start to finish (imo).
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A worthy successor to Nomada's first masterpiece, Gris, in every way. You can feel the studio's DNA in each facet of this experience, and the addition of a surprisingly enjoyable combat system elevates Alba and Neva's adventure beyond that first installment. This will probably be my GOTY 2024, and joins the ranks of a few select games that have left me sobbing like a baby when the credits rolled. 10/10, would recommend to anyone, at any time, for any price.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished my first playthrough. This has been the best 4 hours I've ever played I would gladly do it again. The visuals are stunning, music is on point, and the fighting/puzzles are balanced just right. Got punched left and right ever since the trailer I've been with the feels, can't believe I never really stopped crying the whole way through.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: [/i] Neva [/i] is a visual and emotional triumph. From its stunning hand-drawn art to the delicate portrayal of Alba and her wolf companion's evolving bond, every moment feels meaningful. The way the game intertwines its themes of growth, loss, and survival with beautifully crafted puzzles and combat is masterful. The emotional weight is undeniable, making this journey one that lingers long after completion. With minimal UI and a haunting soundtrack, [/i] Neva [/i] is a perfect blend of art and emotion, proving once again that Nomada Studio knows how to craft experiences that move the soul.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I loved Gris, but more for the music and artstyle, the gameplay itself was a bit less interesting and didn't give you a lot of agency. Neva, however, fixed that completely.Still gorgeous music and visuals, with an engaging story that you felt the weight of the whole time, but also the gameplay is great! Because I felt like I was in control in combat and that I could lose I felt desperate and satisfied with what I accomplished.The gameplay grows as the game goes on and it further pushes the relationship between you and your buddy.The different levels have such unique gimmicks and tones as well.Truly lovely, maybe even my game of the year.I'm going to go cry now <3
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: A bit underwhelming compare to Gris, I strongly suggest story mode for difficulty to not break your immersion from a bit clunky combat system. Stunning as expected, it is a short title, if you preferred waiting for a sale you may but I opted to pay full price for what I think are rare gems that need our full support.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: The art style is obviously beautiful and haunting, music beautiful, gameplay is fun and challenging at times; the world is simply a pleasure to be in, even though it's a fairly linear game. For me, the story wasn't able to hit the emotional heights that Gris was, and I found I was able to predict some of the beats and the ending, once it became clear what they were going for (possibly because I've played Gris a few times). But I don't really see these as drawbacks or negative aspects, as the game as a whole is good, and it is it's own story, it's own game. I also liked some of the innovations in the platforming a lot, really cool stuff. And vibey as heck! Would definitely recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: I usually do not write reviews.However, I hear some people say the game is too short, or that it is not "action" enough, or it does not have enough tough platforming challenges.Not every game needs to fit into the same mold. Neva is a beautiful work of art and an emotional journey, like other games before it (Gris from the same developers, Journey, to name just two examples.) If you like games where an emotional core, beautiful music and stunning visuals come together, you will like this one.Some experiences are just meant to be played and enjoyed. I enjoyed this, I did not mind the price at all and have bought the artbook and soundtrack DLC to further support the creation of emotional pieces like this one.Oh and I also took 414 screenshots while just running around the beautiful areas. I am sorted on wallpapers for the foreseeable future.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful story that i liked. Some combat puzzles were a bit frustrating but the game is worth it in my opinion.Those who compare it to Gris.. Can you really? Why? Is this game not gonna be its own thing? Why compare them. Different games. Gameplay will be different and i did like it. The puzzles were fun and the cute interactions with the wolf itself is adorable.
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Neva presents a visually striking experience; however, it ultimately falls short of the emotional depth established by Gris. While the game features elements of combat and platforming, there are moments that lack engaging content, which can make the experience feel like just a "walking simulator".Although the art direction is undoubtedly the standout aspect offering a mix of breathtaking landscapes and some way less successful surreal elements, this visual appeal may not be enough to sustain  interest. Even the charming presence of the wolf cub fails to fully captivate. On a positive note, the game is short !
_childDocuments_.name: Neva

_childDocuments_.review: Another good game by people who actually take the time to make a polished product. Beautiful art and music, and a simple but still fun combat system. Enjoyable platforming mechanics that work well in and out of combat.A very emotionally heavy game, but I didn't find it to be as moving as their previous game (Gris). Not to say that it doesn't do a very good job at what it sets out to do, but that I personally was less interested in the subject matter.Overall, go play this game. 9/10. _childDocuments_.review: Neva has the emotional and artistic weight of GRIS but with the addition of extremely satisfying combat and an animal companion that propel the story forward. This game is a masterclass of "show, don't tell," with essentially no dialogue and very minimal tutorial text (basically just telling you what a button does when you can use it for the first time). There is a sentimental and thought-provoking conclusion after about 4-5 hours of gameplay. Encourage your friends to buy this game (or buy it for them) and have a nice heartfelt talk about the meaning of life when you're done.I found the difficulty level of "adventure" mode to be in just the right sweet spot: not ridiculously challenging but not a pushover either; you aren't set back too hard for "failing" a particular fight or environmental hazard, but you do need to restart that screen until you get it right. There is also a "story" mode that allows you to play the game without deaths and with "slightly easier challenges." I haven't tried it, but I'm glad the option exists for people who want to use it.

_childDocuments_.review: Neva is undeniably gorgeous, dripping with iconic Nomada style. The game opens strong and does a fantastic job of getting you invested in the relationship between Neva and Alba. The soundtrack is of the quality you'd expect from Berlinist, but generally more subtle and less moving than Gris', with a few notable exceptions.The gameplay is similar to Gris in many regards, with the addition of some extremely basic hack-n-slash combat which feels like a response to critics of Gris' gameplay. It's... Fine. The swordplay is serviceable, but not especially weighty or satisfying. The special attack does deepen the combat ever so slightly, but ultimately the combat detracts from the Nomada experience more than it enhances. Rather than being fully engrossed in the audiovisual experience, you need to stay vigilant for ambushes and combat encounters which can break your momentum and break your immersion through video-gamey frustration. A "story mode" option exists, which makes you unkillable and slightly eases combat encounters. If I ever revisit Neva, that's likely what I'll be using. The watercolor aesthetic of Neva is at times quite similar to Gris, but also much darker and even a bit grotesque, in a Studio Ghibli sort of way. I appreciated that, while the game clearly shared a lot of Gris DNA, Nomada gave Neva its own distinctive flair. Gris was a phenomenal debut outing, and left Nomada with a very tough act to follow. They didn't quite capture that lightning a second time, but there's no shame in that. I respect their ambitions, even if I don't always like the changes, and the end result is a fantastic game that's well worth the price of admission.

_childDocuments_.review: If you´re searching for a beautiful game full of art, meaning, and emotion, then you found it. It's a solid 9.5/10 for me solely because I wish it would´ve been longer. Such a nice balance between challenging and improving your character's skills with Neva to the mechanical changes in the fights which always made it exciting again and not at all repetitive. As for the 19,99€ the game costs ... I would've even paid double for it. I do understand that it might be not it for some people considering the fact that the base game isn´t longer than 5-6 hours but there is so much work and love behind this game that I didn´t even bat an eye when I bought it. I can 100% say that it's been absolutely worth every cent. Ever since Gris came out in 2018 my view on video games has been permanently altered. The pure emotions and art mixed up in a game were simply breathtaking. So when Neva was announced back in 2023 I was so excited to see what Nomada Studios has come up with. My only expectations of this game were beautiful art and that it would leave me in shambles. Neva did exactly that. _childDocuments_.review: Global grade (final impression, not section average) : ★★★★★★★★★☆Neva succeeds at everything Gris was already succeeding. There is a clear change of tone, mainly in the story and the conveyed message, but other than that it shares the same traits: beautiful, an interstellar sound design, a simple and efficient gameplay. The game is pretty short, count 3-4h for main story. I didn’t do the 100%, but I assume it should require around 5-6h to achieve. I recommend the game without hesitation.At first I thought the gameplay would be the weak point of the game because the beginning of the game is… kinda dull, you don’t have much to do. But as the menace ramp up, so does the complexity of the game, both in difficulty and richness of the gameplay. You have a pretty simple move set, but the game does shine in how you progress in the environment. It does not revolutionize anything but work darn well to deliver a smooth experience, with a well balanced difficulty (the game is easy by my standards), with some slightly harder moments and a death with virtually no progression penality. For casual gamers, Neva constitutes a perfect blend. For more seasoned players, it will be a story game but interesting to play nevertheless. Also, a quite nice perk: you can pet the doggo, at will. Pet the doggo. Pet it more.The strongest point of Neva, the game is just, well, subjectively I suppose, B-E-A-U-T-I-F-U-L. The animation is quite good overall, but the real deal is the environment composition of Neva. Every landscape is gorgeous, multi-layered, and often evolves with your progression. And the best about it is that the environment has such consistency you can sometimes hardly delimit what constitutes pure decoration and elements you can interact with, without really confusing the player more than a couple seconds. The game features several moments of pure “Oh wow” sceneries. And a fair part of what does not constitute “Oh wow” sceneries, constitutes instead some “Oh ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥” epic moments, adding to the immersion of the intense parts of the game.Neva is some 2D gourmet stuff. Assuming you like its artistic style, as usual with those kind of games with a strong visual identity.See what I said on graphics? Well transpose that to sound design. Enough said.Neva has no character development as there is no dialog.Let’s be honest, Neva story is similar to Ori and Gris: post-it sized and made primarily for feelings, not for lore. It constitutes the still reasonably okay weak point of Neva because with the addition of minimalism comes, unlike Gris, a pretty dull and Manichean message with the subtlety of a bull in a china shop. But while it is not exactly the memorable part of the game, it does the job, especially at filling you with emotions.Bugs: None encountered on Day 1 on my side (the game did required for me to enable steam input), it should be noted however that some players seems to be experiencing difficulties with controller support at the first release version. But I trust the devs to address that. In case of doubt consult the discussions.

_childDocuments_.review:
Neva is an emotionally-charged action adventure from the visionary team behind the critically acclaimed GRIS.

Neva chronicles the story of Alba, a young woman bound to a curious wolf cub following a traumatic encounter with dark forces. Together they embark on a perilous journey through a once-beautiful world as it slowly decays around them.

Over time, their relationship will evolve as they learn to work together, helping one another to brave increasingly dangerous situations. The wolf will grow from a rebellious cub to an imposing adult seeking to forge his own identity, testing Alba's love and their commitment to one another.

As the cursed world threatens to overwhelm them, Alba and her courageous companion will do whatever it takes to survive and make a new home, together.

_childDocuments_.review: I started playing this game during my 5 weeks of holiday. I enjoyed it a lot until my holiday was over and I had to actually combine it with my life. The moment my holidays were over, I decided to quit. I was in a top 10 guild and was in the top 10 kill ranking on my server. Here are my reasons why I quit:- The story is boring and forgettable. I spam clicked through it all, that's how bad it is.- The targeting system is horrible.- The game is p2w in the sense that it will accelerate your progress greatly, making you reach important breakpoints faster. This means that if you want to be competitive in PvP, it is mandatory to spend money. It's still very much enjoyable as an F2P player and you can do very well. But as a F2P, you don't pay with your money but with your time, life and sanity. If you are unemployed and don't mind playing this game every hour and day of your life, yes you can be competitive as F2P.- There are only a limited number of viable weapon combinations (classes).- Once you are invested in your build, you are completely locked in. Tired of your class and want to play something different? It will cost you a lot of time and/or money.- The whole weapon/class system is extremely unbalanced. Rangers/archers are supposed to counter mages but the mage gear has ranged evasion and endurance on it. Also, for what it's worth I played greatsword/dagger with magic and ranged evasion and if there is no melee tank (my counter) around, I could 1v5 if I played it correctly and kill everyone with little to no counterplay. Conversely, if there is one melee tank around, I can not play the game at all. Also, if someone stacks melee evasion against me, I can't do anything to them. The rock-paper-sciccors is good in theory, but not implemented well. It's very black and white, all or nothing. This is bad design.- The stat distribution on items and synergy between weapons is unbalanced and is in favour of some classes. For my class, greatsword/dagger, I am forced to build 2 armor pieces (field general, in order to get Heavy Attack without which I can't function) that give melee and ranged defences while the rest of my armor and passive skills give ranged/magic defenses. This means my end game BiS gear set is less optimized than for example crossbow/dagger that simply just synergizes to the maximum.- The offensive/defensive stats and how they interact with each other is not very intuitive. You need to watch a lot of external guides to understand how stats work and interact.- There are too many types of cc stats and too little ways to stack defences against them to have any impact at all. For example, collision, weaken, sleep, stun, petrify, bind, etc.. You can essentially only pick one, and are exposed to all the others.- The game revolves around large scale guild vs guild battles. Small scale PvP is there in the form of Arena. But you need a specific build for that. And as I mentioned above, I was already locked into another build, so I just had to accept that I can not be competitive in Arena, or sink in another few hundred hours. No thank you.- Some weapons are just outright broken/overtuned (shield and sword and greatsword in small scale, longbow with flash wave in large scale).- The entire game was practically shoved through an AI generator and is badly translated. It's as if they took parts of their code and ran it through a translator with ctrl + c and ctrl + v. Tooltips don't make sense when you read them or just flat out contain wrong information.- There are a LOT of bugs that interfere with the core gameplay. Movement is horrible, there is rubber banding, you can get stuck somewhere and not get out, you can randomly teleport in a fight, you can use a dash skill without dashing, the grappling is unresponsive and just bad, and much more. Also, if your inventory was full and you opened loot pouches, the loot would disappear.. etc.- Every update fixes some things, but adds more bugs than it fixes.- The guild alliance system encourages all the hardcore players to join each other in the top guilds. These guilds then form an alliance and completely dominate the server, making competitive PvP impossible for the rest of the player base.- Random words are censored in chat for no reason all the time.- The loot and upgrading system are extremely RNG based and feel unrewarding once you reach a certain stage. Drops are worthless and drop chances are extremely low. On top of that, you can not trade items in any meaningful way, making the economy stale.- It depends on the guild but usually, the loot from world bosses and raids will go to the guild and it's up to the guild to distribute it. This sucks because you will almost never get any loot. The other way around, where everyone acquires their own item also sucks, because a random person who barely plays the game could get a big drop and it could go to waste.- The daily and weekly tasks are a repetitive chore and unrewarding. The loot is garbage, bugged and the activities are boring. You could say this is part of an MMO and that is true. You can also not log in for a few days and let your points stack for the week, but this just delays all the work you have to do. If you are casual. this doesn't really matter but if you want to be competitive, you HAVE to log in and play at least 2-3 hours EVERY SINGLE DAY, including weekends. And this is for the daily farming alone.- The only meaningful PvP you can do is with a guild. You are a slave to the guild, a little cog in the machine. Does that sound fun? So if you want to be a competitive PvPer, you have to join a top guild. On top of all the daily/weekly farming activities, you have to be present for rift and boonstone fights, night pvp at saurodoma island, weekly world boss fights and siege war soon. Sure you don't HAVE to, but if you don't, the hardcore no lifers will and you will be locked out of PvP. This means you have to completely no life the game in order to be anywhere relevant at all. The root cause of this is that (daily) events are time gated.- There is very little skill expression in large scale PvP. it's just one big blob 'fighting' another big blob. If you are melee dps, it's basically go in to fight, die within 5 seconds and hopefully take someone with you, respawn and do it again. Meanwhile, if you play longbow, you just use flash wave that is litterally a screen wide AoE without maximum player hit cap, use your refresh skill and do it again, wiping an entire group of people at once. Yes, melee dps sucks in large scale and is good in small scale. But again, this is bad design. I didn't know this when I chose my build in the beginning and now I'm stuck with it. As I mentioned, rerolling is almost impossible, so I just quit instead.- I forgot to add, the worst of all. The 'PvP' in this game revolves around 'who has more numbers'. If you like to go solo like me, it is horrible. It all boils down to more players killing less players with 0 skill involved. Expect to get jumped 10v1 over and over and over. So it turns into an endless grind of massing players, ending up in the tasteless zerg 'fights'.There are some good things about the game, namely being the nice graphics. The environment and world is very immersive and amazing. The visual and sound effects are nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally, a new MMO! Although the age of MMOs seems to have passed, this one really reminds me of the games we used to play. Being NCSoft there are elements of Aion and Lineage, but there are also elements borrowed from newer single player RPGs and even WoW (such as the great vault).Customisation: Very detailed character creation. A lot of variety with armour/weapons unlike some games where a crowd of players all looks the same whilst levelling. We all know the true endgame will be the fashion parade, and I'm sure NCSoft will not disappoint with the cash shop cosmetics. They have a great track record making players look fabulous.Combat: Action-based and satisfying, but still has remnants of tab-targeting. Not as smooth as games like Black Desert due to sticky targeting, especially for casters.Life skills: A little bit thin on the ground (with only fishing, cooking and expeditions) for now.Story: A bit janky at times which I guess is fairly typical for a Korean MMO translated for the west, but it has some strong moments (love the vampire hunter quest and the giant sand-worm quests).World: I think they have really done well with the world. The instant teleport with no loading screens. Seamless transitions into instanced areas for certain quests and building interiors. The world really feels huge and alive, and the ambient sounds and music definitely contribute to the top notch immersion.Overall a solid start, and I really look forward to seeing what the future brings. It's free - why not give it a go?

_childDocuments_.review: DO NOT LOOK AT NEGATIVE REVIEWS. A lot of these reviews are coming from people who cant run it for some reason or from people in the EU angry they bought early access. I found fishing the most fun so far as a life skill. YOU CAN SEE THE FISH COME TO YOUR LINE. The progression system is quite nice with all your old gear feeding into the next tier of gear up so on and so forth and it is quite constant like im upgrading constantly at least during leveling. I would say the game does not start until end game but I currently have taken my time and am only at level 30 and have had a very enjoyable time. Skills are nice and generally depending on what weapons you use depends your playstyle and role. I play a paladin like character who is tanky and also heals. There are a lot of builds out there but I have found myself actually kind of going with the flow and doing my own thing. Its interesting and new and the devs are fully behind the game. Even though there have been disconnects sometimes I have played quite constant they even sent out a big chunk of currency for players as a thank you and a sorry. The damage output combined with a high heavy attack chance is ridiculous. Just look at the numbers—players are leaving the game. Check the arena rankings; SNS/GS and GS/Dag combinations are everywhere, and they’re ruining game balance.People claim it’s a "rock-paper-scissors" system, but I’m sick and tired of getting one-shotted by these toxic setups. Does the dev team even play SNS/GS or GS/Dag? Do they want everyone to only play these combinations because it’s a PvP-focused game? If players keep getting frustrated, like I am, they’ll leave. There is no way to run as a crafter type because the required items are just not in the game. Blue Ink, I am looking at you. These special coins are limited daily so you can only really run those a couple times per day. And they are fast, like :15 - :20 minute experiences if you want to clear them. If you speed run some of them can be done in five minutes.Loot in this game is completely non existent. Playing this amount of time and I have gotten like seven open world drops. There is just a bunch of running and collecting quests from one side of a zone to the other side of the zone. And multiple clicks at the same object. Like click the stuffed animal. _childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty gives a good first impression, pleasantly surprising with its beautiful visuals powered by Unreal Engine. However, this is only on the surface. Beneath that, the game is completely generic and won’t impress you with many new mechanics. There is no class system; instead, the game features a weapon system that is largely borrowed from Guild Wars. Additionally, the game includes "live events," which are also inspired by Guild Wars. The game’s UI is heavily influenced by Korean games, especially Black Desert Online. The game is completely free, so there’s no harm in giving it a try—unless you consider wasted time as a cost. Personally, as someone who considers themselves a hardcore MMO/ARPG player, I don’t recommend the game.- Great visuals- No loading screens- Good optimization- Limited skill variety- Underdeveloped professions- Very average story- Dungeons? _childDocuments_.review: It's fine. Leveling up until 50 is interesting and addictive, but on max level you hit kind of a wall in Throne And Liberty. The game looks very good for an MMO, though the skill effects are very bad in comparison. The game has some interesting aspects to it, like being able to send your small Amitoi stuffed dolls on expeditions for materials, binding found equipment in Litographs to sell to other players on the auction house for Lucent, the real money currency (or selling the equipment's traits so others can upgrade and customize their equipment) or participating in dynamic events. I do think that the game is a bit too guild centered, as many activities become only possible or drastically easier with guilds, which also means that, depending on the server you play on, there may be some guilds just dominating many activities, some of which are PVP focused, which makes progression a lot harder and less fun. My personal biggest gripe though, and why I will stop playing for now after being at 50 for a few days, is that the endgame loop is somewhat repetitive and way too time gated - you do dungeons hoping an item you need or you can sell drops, or do contracts hoping for good materials or blessing pouches that can potentially have some good equipment in them. You can fish and cook, and level those up, which can be fun, but ultimately fishing is also very repetitive and fish are really only used for food, though sometimes you can find small sacks with loot from fishing. The game is heavily centered around weeklies and dailies, so you have to play a certain amount of time a day if you want to keep up, and if that wasn't enough, dynamic events and world bosses are also on a timer, so you have to play at certain amount of times per day and hope the event you want shows up (and is not a conflict event because that means people will just PVP each other instead of doing the boss). If you have only very little time to play, it's not like you will be prevented from doing things, but you will progress very slowly. But, of course, since the auction house only works with real money currency, you can just swipe your card to become equipped with the best equipment for your class. It's pay 2 win, but at least you can make that money easily in game as well if you farm dungeons and contracts a lot, and sell good things in the auction house. The game also gives you constant small dopamine hits, rewards for doing certain quest chapters, rewards for finding codex entries, rewards for getting rewards - it's blatant dopamine overload to keep you playing, as is standard in Korean MMOs. Overall, I think Throne And Liberty is a very inoffensive, but also typically korean MMO with all the bells and whistles you'd expect. It's not going to revolutionize the MMO genre, it's chock full of weird barriers, time gates and design choices, but it's also oddly addictive at times and can be fun if you have enough time to play and don't mind a repetitive endgame loop. It's free, so no harm in trying it out and I would give it an overall recommendation - I had my fun, will keep an eye on it for future changes but will be moving on for now.
