_childDocuments_.review: I'd love to say Yes, I am so very, very close to recomending this and game has many really cool features. I don't regret playing, but more and more I am loosing interest to continue.My pros:- world is beautiful. One of the best looking MMOs on the market.- excellent character customisation.- excellent zones, they are varied, well designed, lot of attention to detail.- dungeons, events and world bosses are all excellent- I love the game UI, very clean, nicely animated and does good job at displaying and conveying information.- Most of game quests are fully voice acted.- Voiced narration of the main story, gives context for what is going on, even when skipping dialogue/cut-scenes.Now cons:- Very often voiced dialogue does not match the subtitles- Weird, non-idiomatic use of language/grammar at times, feels like translated by AI and no one bothered to check.- Poor audio mixing at times, background noises too loud, voiced dialogue too quiet, etc, voiced dialogue gets cut mid-sentence, etc.- Combat is very clunky. For example lot of animation locks, annoying stamina system that so often leaves you vulnerable because you can't use Q-block, or even move, yes, learn to play, but even so, annoying.- Flying is clunky, lots and lots of desyncs, inaccurate landings. "Flying" is really a misnomer, more downward gliding really, with very limited to gaining altitude.- Grappling mechanics are atrocious and frustrating to deal with. Often desyncs, sends you flying missing the landing spot, camera jumping widely all-over-the-place, or simply unable to grapple despite having clear line of sight. - Gearing is boring, complex, grindy, lots of currencies and several systems.- For PvE, end game is very limited. Just events, dungeons and contracts. All three are fun for a while, but quickly overstay their welcome.- Subjective, but feels players becoming more and more toxic with each passing day. Demanding higher gearing score, requiring to already know all tactics in dungeons, etc.- TOO MANY SYSTEMS. It is giving me a headache how many systems, upgrade paths etc. this game has.- Amitoi are annoying and game would be better off without 'em.- While morphing is kind of cool at times and something different from other games, I did grow tired of it and prefer traditional mounts instead.- Confusing ability descriptions.These are just my thoughts after about 70 hours, but do give it a go and you might enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: The graphics are nice and the character customization offer several options. What stands out most is the facial features of characters and NPCs. NCSoft once created an absolutely legendary MMORPG called Lineage 2, a game that still has a strong following, especially in private servers of previous chronicles (expansions).THRONE AND LIBERTY feels like a corporate project that needed to be finished on a deadline. It lacks completely any resemblance to a good MMORPG like World of Warcraft or Lineage 2, where characters progress gradually and learn skills and gather equipment by gaining experience and victories against strong opponents. The goal of this game is unknown to me as the progression is boring and predictable. One character can have all classes and unlock most of the abilities early on. The abilities are nothing special and are super spammable with very low impact. If you want to run around and spend your time just for fun in a visually and graphically intense game then this is alright. The UI is nice and supports joystick too. Luckily I did not pay for an early access, because this game is unfortunately not playable for me and it does a great disservice to NCSOFT's player and MMORPG players. Regrettably.

_childDocuments_.review: It starts out fun but drops off a cliff once the game stops feeding you with stuff through the main story and side quests. After that the only way to progress is to farm dailies and abyssal dungeons in order to get the materials needed to craft the books you need to continue upgrading your skills. If you do the math, the amounts you need is staggering.The world bosses are a joke. Only the top damage dealers get anything worthwhile out of it. Good luck doing them with a lot of people at a time.Coop dungeons have ... mechanics. I refuse to call them hard. The difficulty only stems from them being unintuitive, untelegraphed and partially hidden. The matchmaking is broken most of the time and building a party with the partyboard is like pulling teeth. That dialogue cannot even remember what you put there in the first place. So if you just want to edit the group's description you have to fill out everything again. Oh and you better watch a video guide of any dungeon you want to do because most people you meet in those dungeons are touchy minmaxing sweatlords who will either flame you or leave outright if you don't run along the pixel perfect optimized route. Dear god, don't even dare to aggro one additional mob that is normally skipped.All of the content I've mentioned before is gated. The dailies (resistance contracts) require so called contract rights of which a certain amount replenishes daily. The abyssal dungeons require a different type of contract rights which replenish daily to a certain degree. You can do the coop dungeons as often as you want but you can only roll on loot from the final chest by using another currency which (you are probably guessing it) replenishes daily for a certain amount.The game features so called 'dynamic events' but these aren't dynamic at all. There is an actual timetable on the map when each of them will take place. All of those events are the same. Kill any mob in the area, collect things, turn in things and get ... nothing of note.The game tries to push you into a guild real hard and has an obsession with PvP. World bosses or events can have PvP active. Abyssal dungeons become PvP zones at night. Guilds can even force a PvP zone during the day by using a guild skill that causes an eclipse. If you are not riding the bleeding edge, you will get steamrolled by those who do. Must be a Korean thing.Final verdict: Spend your time playing better games.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, my experience with this game was marred by significant technical issues. Frequent frame drops during battles disrupted the flow of gameplay, creating an uneven experience. Additionally, the camera controls were unresponsive at times, resetting position with each click. This unpredictability made combat feel unreliable, as attacks often failed to register due to problems with the UI processing button inputs.The game's art style, particularly in its animations, bears a striking resemblance to certain adult-oriented fantasy videos found online. This similarity detracts from the game's overall potential and makes it difficult to distinguish from other China-based MMOs. The market is saturated with titles that share a homogeneous art style, making it challenging for any one game to stand out.The prevalence of these issues suggests a lack of polish and insufficient development time. It's disheartening to see games released in such a state, as it reflects negatively on the entire industry. Developers deserve fair compensation for their hard work, and adequate development time is necessary to create games that meet player expectations. The video game industry would benefit from a greater focus on quality, ensuring that players have engaging, immersive experiences. As it stands, this title feels rushed and in need of further refinement.

Delays and teleports happen. - Mistranslations (lamenting underground is cave of desperation? what? cooldown reduction in some cases means duration?)- Fishing is very questionable, the difficulty of fishing is still same no matter the level and it is very boring mechanic, fishes can break line often because they don't follow, even low level ones. Perma stuns, perma cc of one kind allowed, evasion not working on critical hits because yes, multiple really sketchy mechanics that make it impossible to enjoy the game. Reference to Greatsword users that can stun you for 10s+ and kill you in that duration while you just watch and even having purification stone, you can't do anything than just wait and die.- Graphic optimization is terrible. Game drops FPS even on best machines with latest graphics cards. Large scale events invite hundreds if not thausands of people but the game servers are not able to handle it either. Constant lags. Teleports. De-sync issues. FPS drops. Terrible performance given to players. This should not be released at all until such big flaw was fixed. - Dominion events are interesting, altho they keep being messed up. People wear red colors and are in blue team or wear green and are in red team, which is very confusing. Should have been tested before release. - Large scale PvP in this game is very sketchy due to huge AoE abilities like flashwave and lack of multiple optimisations for combat. Game system is very weirdly made. Healing is not very hard in large scale combat due to no ability to even click HP bars of people. Problems with targetting in PvP are real. On top of that there are issues with perma-cc that were just granted to classes.- The game design of multiple mechanics is terrible, Evasion is only for hit chance because guess what? Critical attack is not evadable, there is no hit chance roll first, so you can drop making hit chance and just go full crit and you will destroy all enemies as long as they don't have too much endurance. Amazing. Overall score: 4/10PvE in the game isn't this good. It's a bit below average. PvP due to optimization and mechanic... _childDocuments_.review: After dedicating nearly 200 hours to Throne and Liberty, I had a mixed experience with this MMO. Initially, the game hooked me with a unique narrative style and a well-paced story that made me curious to see what lay ahead. The narrator in particular added a special touch, making it feel like you were truly part of the story. The quests were well-designed too—they weren’t too grindy, and the “no-return” quest system was a fresh take, helping create a sense of forward movement without constantly backtracking.The combat, while a bit off at first, improved with time and familiarity, but it still felt like something was missing. Once the main story ended, though, the game struggled to hold my interest. It was easy to hit the max level quickly, and after that, the only activities left were grinding bosses, dungeons, and PvP events. This would have been fine, except the long wait times for bosses and events dragged down the experience.While PvP can be fun, it felt like fighting clones. There was very little room for creativity because everyone wore the same gear and used the same weapons. Customization options were practically nonexistent unless you wanted to spend extra on skins. For players like me who prefer to express individuality in a game, this lack of customization was disappointing.In the end, Throne and Liberty feels like a game with great potential that’s held back by monetization strategies and limited content. If you love PvP and don’t mind the uniform look, it might work for you. But for those who enjoy a more unique, customizable experience, this game falls short. I won’t be returning to it, and I wouldn’t recommend it to players looking for freedom and variety in an MMO.
_childDocuments_.name: THRONE AND LIBERTY

_childDocuments_.review: Throne and Liberty is an ambitious MMORPG that has recently caught the attention of gamers worldwide. Having had the opportunity to explore its mechanics, I found it to be a game with solid potential, though it ultimately falls short when compared to giants like Guild Wars and World of Warcraft.Game MechanicsThe game mechanics in Throne and Liberty are generally enjoyable, with a fluid combat system that encourages strategic thinking and cooperation among players. The graphics are stunning, with beautifully crafted environments and character designs that immerse you in the world. The movement and agility of characters make exploration feel dynamic, and the quest system is engaging, offering a mix of solo and cooperative gameplay options.Build Switch SystemHowever, the build switch system left much to be desired. It felt clunky and unintuitive at times, making it difficult to switch between playstyles effectively. This hindered my ability to adapt to different encounters or roles during gameplay, which can be frustrating, especially in a game that heavily emphasizes character customization and specialization. A more streamlined and user-friendly approach to switching builds would significantly enhance the overall experience.Pay-to-Win ElementsAnother concerning aspect of Throne and Liberty is the presence of pay-to-win mechanics. While the game offers a variety of cosmetic and quality-of-life purchases, there are elements that allow players to gain significant advantages through monetary investment. This can create an uneven playing field, especially in competitive scenarios where those willing to spend more can progress faster or acquire stronger equipment. For players who prefer a fair competition, this aspect can be quite disheartening.Comparison to Other MMORPGsWhen I compare Throne and Liberty to other MMORPGs like Guild Wars and World of Warcraft, it feels somewhat average. While Guild Wars offers intricate world-building and deep lore, and World of Warcraft is renowned for its rich content and community-driven experiences, Throne and Liberty doesn’t quite match the depth and polish of these established titles. The game has its strengths, but it lacks the compelling narrative and expansive world that have defined its competitors.Final ThoughtsOverall, Throne and Liberty is a nice addition to the MMORPG genre, especially for players looking for a new experience. However, it has room for improvement, particularly with its build switch system and in-depth content. The pay-to-win elements may deter some players from fully immersing themselves in the game. While I enjoyed my time in the game, it remains a step behind the benchmarks set by Guild Wars and World of Warcraft. For those looking for a fresh MMORPG, it’s worth a try, but seasoned players might find it lacking in certain areas.

_childDocuments_.review: I came into this game knowing virtually nothing about it.  Seeing 'Amazon' attached made me instantly expect a New World type of game.  Though I could see the aesthetic was completely different.  In short, I enjoyed it to a degree for a while, but it never really hit for me, and the more I played the more the shortcomings became apparent.  At this point I've made it to level 31 and am teetering on the edge of moving on.To start, it's a very pretty game.  I love the character models and environment, especially on high settings.  Though it's not easy to run; my $230 graphics card I bought last year (that's expensive for me) is dying on anything above medium settings, and I'm still seeing 5 fps in towns with a lot of players.They deserve special recognition for the ability to upload your photo and have AI create your character based on it.  It worked surprisingly well.  Also awesome is the voiceover summaries at the end of each set of MSQ quests; great voice actor and nice feature.I like the combat so far.  Blocking is well telegraphed, though I've missed blocks that I shouldn't have (well beyond just latency). Healing is supportive, unlike most games; if players stand in stuff or don't heal themselves the healer can't save them.  I like that.  And the environment is designed in such a way that I don't feel overwhelmed and lost, even when up in melee.  And thankfully, no ridiculously giant bosses yet; not sure if there are later.The P2W situation isn't great, but could be worse.  The Battle Pass is bad, but I see a lot of purchasable items that are purely aesthetic.  That's the way it should be.  That there is anything at all that can affect gameplay for real money is over the line for me, but it honestly wasn't as bad as I was expecting.The fishing minigame was fun for the first 2 minutes.  It becomes quickly frustrating due to a combination of no-win situations (the fish will get away no matter what you do), no instruction on how to do it, no clear value to progression or explaination as to what helps you, and, well, it's a twitch mechanic which I'm just not really a fan of.The controls are clunky and don't work quite right.  Autorun doesn't turn off when you manually run (yes, I've run over several cliffs now).  Action controls only leave room for about 6 skill keybinds, but you need lots more.  Classic controls aren't bad, but I would have prefered action.  Many menu items say I have something to do when I don't (especially battle pass and codex).  There's just a lot of refinement needed here.Then there's the bugs.  I sent all my family members friend invites last night.  I logged in today and they were all gone.  My game has crashed to desktop 3 times in the last 24 hours.  And my only death yesterday was when I tried to jump over some mobs to get in a better position and ended up stuck in a wall unable to move or attack.Gathering and crafting is pretty much nonexistent.  No progression.  Most nodes look the same.  There's only a few mats and they just come in different rarities.  A real disappointment after New World, which most of my friends who played said they played mostly for the gathering and crafting.So far, I haven't really seen any "dynamic events".  I've taken part in wolf hunting, starlight stones, and the brown mica event; mostly just "who can kill the most".  There's *nothing* like Guild Wars 2's dynamic events where a story plays out and the zone changes based on player interactions and success/failure, and nothing yet with cooperation.  So there's nothing evolutionary here; if anything we're moving in reverse.And let's talk about cooperation.  The questing is beyond easy, so you will never save or need saved.  Mobs are tagged, so you're discouraged from working with others.    Oh, and did I mention you cannot trade with other players...at all!  There's an auction house but it's locked until 40 so I'm not sure what that's like, but I can't pool resources with my friends so whatever.They do try to encourage silo cooperation in other ways (guilds, manually formed groups, etc).  But so far I don't actually know a single guild member.  There's just a lot of individuals working on individual stuff that happens to contribute to a community goal.  Very much like every mobile game out there.And they've taken a *lot* of cues from mobile games.  You see a bunch of little things here and there that have obviously been influenced by them.  From individual contributions to group goals within which there is little to no individual recognition, to the Battle Pass reward track.  Or how about the 'do things outside the game for massive rewards' thing; like the Discord quest that awards as many ornate coins as finding *50 books* in-game; it trivializes actually playing.There are followers and missions in this game, but it is simplified beyond belief.  You can have one mission at a time, there are no follower stats or levels, and the success depends on just choosing the follower of the right faction for an area.  STO got this right with their duty officers over a decade ago (hundreds of followers, 20+ missions at a time, etc).  Not sure why no other game can figure it out.  The way T&L does it, it would be better not existing as it's just a chore right now.  So again, not only not improved from older games, but notably worse.PvP does not need to mean that players act like jerks towards one another, but like many others, T&L has mechanics designed to create that environment.  Gathering nodes can only be gathered by one player, mob tapping has made a return from 2008 making mob stealing a thing, and dynamic events seem setup to reward steeling mobs and resources from other players.In short, too many oversimplified systems, too little reward for (or even ability to) cooperation, too much reward for jerkiness, and a generally rough UI and interface.

_childDocuments_.review: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐⭐☆ (4/5)After 625 hours in Throne and Liberty, I can say this game delivers a grand, open-world MMORPG experience that feels both captivating and challenging. With massive battles, intricate skill systems, and constant updates, it’s got a lot to offer—if you’re willing to invest some time. Here’s what makes Throne and Liberty stand out:The gameplay revolves around large-scale PvP battles and world events that bring players together in intense clashes. Combat is strategic, demanding careful timing and positioning, especially in group PvP scenarios. Skill-based mechanics keep things challenging, so you’re always engaged, especially in high-stakes raids and dungeons.Highlights:Epic PvP Events: Massive faction battles make the world feel alive.Skill-Intensive Combat: Strategy and timing are key for success.The progression system is one of the game’s strongest points. With numerous classes and skill trees, you can build your character in ways that suit your playstyle. Skills are customizable, allowing you to create unique combinations that are rewarding in both PvP and PvE. It’s a grind to level up and earn new abilities, but each skill unlock brings a satisfying sense of power and growth.Highlights:Flexible Builds: Mix and match skills for unique playstyles.Rewarding Grind: Progression keeps you invested and engaged.The game’s open world is breathtaking. From dense forests to desolate mountains, the visuals are detailed and atmospheric, adding a lot of depth to exploration. Weather and time-of-day systems add immersion, and large world bosses or dynamic events draw players together in awe-inspiring encounters.Highlights:Beautiful Environments: Rich landscapes keep exploration exciting.Dynamic World Events: Large-scale encounters make the world feel alive.The events in Throne and Liberty add a lot of excitement, especially the seasonal ones. Right now, the Halloween event brings a spooky, festive vibe with exclusive quests, special rewards, and eerie world changes. Events are frequent, so there’s always something unique to dive into, adding a nice change of pace to the grind.Highlights:Frequent Events: Keeps gameplay fresh and exciting.Seasonal Themes: Unique, time-limited challenges and rewards.Whether you’re teaming up for raids or battling rival factions, the community aspect is a big draw. Players are competitive but often helpful, making it easier to find allies and get advice. Guild alliances and rivalries add a layer of strategy and immersion that enhances the overall experience.Highlights:Active Player Base: Plenty of teammates for PvE and PvP.Strong Guild Alliances: Adds depth to PvP and world control.Throne and Liberty has its rough edges, but it offers a truly immersive MMORPG experience with grand battles, rewarding progression, and a community-driven world. For fans of strategic combat and large-scale PvP, it’s definitely worth the time. The frequent events and seasonal updates keep things exciting, making it a game that keeps pulling you back in.

_childDocuments_.review: edit: Just leaving an update here. If you consider playing this game, doit with the mindset of reaching lvl 50 and quitting. Unless you are in the top 1-5 PvP guild on your server, it is not worth it. Big guilds are creating alliances (or are outright making multiple guilds on their own) to keep anyone else from having fun. Contested dungeons are gatekept by them and even peaceful zones aren't safe because the top PK players can turn any day into night and PK you. On top of that dungeons have the most toxic people running them and the systems do not protect you from being kicked when the boss is at 1% life. This is Revelation Online all over again. _childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - It's worth playing through until you get bored or hit the pay/guildwall. It's free, and you'll get some good hours from it without needing to pay anything. Don't expect to enjoy the endgame (or a lot of features in general) unless you're in a big guild.-----I'll preface this bit with "I'm still only halfway-ish through the story".- Beautiful game. Environment is incredible. It sounds weird, but its one of the few games that got rain to feel right.- It's got all your favourite Korean MMO features.- If you played Lineage II,  this feels like a spiritual sequel.- The 'class' weapon system is a neat take and I enjoy it.- Combat is simple, if you like that.- It has a very Guild Wars-y list of things to do when you enter a new area. Finishing these lists is very pleasing to my monkey brain.- The voice acting is dreadful in places.- The setting is not very well established and you're thrust into the story without much explanation. You can come to terms with it later on, but for me this was something I disliked.- Not incredibly optimised, but easily rectified by lowering settings.- It's got all your hated Korean MMO features.- Movement is clunky, but that's related to the above point. The addition of "Action Mode" somewhat helps.- The game expects you to be in a big Guild. It's designed around that. It's less accomodating to a small group of friends who just want to play together.- The servers don't handle you getting stuck in scenery very well, leading to lag.- You will have to pay for anything "nice". This includes glamour (transmog), removing limits on things etc. You got this game for free though, so what did you expect...

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I want to say the game isn't bad, but its not great eitherMy biggest problems with game are:Once you high level 50 you will notice that all forms of content you do is almost identical with minor differencesAlmost all of the even remotely endgame mobs are incredibly tanky with genuinely 0 differences between them other than stat changes and reskins this also applies to dungeons.All of the grinding zones have no mechanics.There are no elite monsters just zone minibossesMonsters in zones are just scattered around randomly, with no pattern or reason (eg no packs of mobs no roaming guards ect)No reason why we cant have mobs grouped up in packs or large gatherings E.G no reason why some zones cant have squishy trash mobs and like 1-2 elites per pack with some cool mechanics, no reason why some zones cant have intractable mechanics like in other mmos. Like why cant a zone have rotations ect from other mmos, seems like such a simple and easy QoL change that i think would be heavily welcomedAll classes abilities "look impactful" but barely, they could of made abilities look and feel significantly more impactful with this graphics engine. Even criticals and heavy hits dont feel impactful at allMost bosses and dungeons feel lame, almost all the bosses feel lame and repetitive while feeling boring and non intensive. Most of the "dungeons" feel so repetitive and boring my raid group can run them in 5-10 minutes 0 communications (we could easily fight the bosses blindfolded)Healing is almost entirely reliant on a healer, there is atmost like 3-4 heals outside of healers and they would take over 4-5 minutes to fully heal youRegen is genuinely non existant, even with the regen buff in towns it can take me over a minute to get to full hpMost "classes" are just as tanky. It feels like their is no genuine tank role, and even when built full tank in pve you cannot do anything you could do as a tank in any other mmo. This is caused by tank stats having almost 0 trade off damage wise and vise versaAlmost all traits are BiS across 90% of archetypes besides daggers (only weapon type that consistantly build evasion) All weapons build the exact same traits 99% of the time no matter if your tank or full damageThe loot in dungeons is spread out so atrociously that most classes have 0 gear drops from 5 out of the 6 dungeons (good luck finding a healer for the tank dungeons, or a tank for the dps dungeons)Build variety feels almost nonexistant their is very very obvious BiS gear for your archetype, Most armours are either high dmg high deffence or utterly and undeniably useless EG shock commander set is your 100% pick no matter what weapons you use if you wish to be tanky Field general set for melee dmg, and the crit dmg bonus set if your ranged dps (idk name) and maybe the offhand chance set (also forgot name) if your crossbow dagger (only for crossbow dagger)You are entirely reliant on world boss drops or market place for any form of decent end game gear. And world boss drops are outstandingly terribleOver all I feel like the games abilities are actually lame and no where near as impactful as they could feel. Almost every zone (including dungeons) shouldnt have hyper tanky high damage mobs. Gear should be more diverse and their should be more of it. Weapons should be more diverse and offer different stats. Traits need to ENTIRELY overhauled or removed and added to gear (i shouldnt have full dmg armour set on and build complete evasion as traits and never die)

_childDocuments_.review: I had high hopes for Throne and Liberty, especially given its atmospheric world, beautiful graphics, and immersive sound design. From a visual and auditory perspective, the game absolutely nails it. Exploring the open world felt captivating, and the sound effects enhanced the overall experience. Unfortunately, the game’s combat system was a major deal-breaker for me.While the combat tries to present itself as action-based, it's actually rooted in a clunky tab-targeting system, which felt unpolished and frustrating. Combat mechanics that should have been intuitive were either poorly explained or skipped entirely in the tutorial. In an MMORPG, combat is a core component, and for me, it has to click 100%. Sadly, Throne and Liberty didn't deliver on this front, and that ultimately led to my decision to quit.If you're drawn to an MMO for its visuals and atmosphere, Throne and Liberty might capture your interest, but if smooth, responsive combat is a must for you—like it is for me—this game may leave you disappointed.

The p2w is pretty bad, shoving a battlepass and leveling pass down players throats which is nearly required to be competitive in end game pvp. I also dislike the auction house system which allows players to buy items using a currency that is a MTX, but also allows players to sell earnable in-game rewards for the same currency. I feel like being able to swipe your card and have an advantage takes the rewarding feeling of getting better gear away from everyone. It creates an environment where players who buy their gear are only satisfied by winning in pvp, and players who grind it out feel like they wasted hours of grinding a boss that they could've just skipped if they had a few extra bucks to spend just to be competitive.Another Odd system they have in place limits the amount of dungeons you can do per-day. I don't find myself being affected by it all that much as someone who doesn't run dungeons a lot, however a LARGE part of getting better gear is through dungeon rewards. Having a limit on how much content a player is allowed to experience in a day is insulting. servers shutting down for 7+ hours unannounced multiple times a week is insulting. telling me to pay my way through pvp is insulting. giving me a half baked combat system is insulting. this game is waste of time. _childDocuments_.review: To give the game some merit, the game has some fantastic visuals and the World is fairly unique. The story was also half decent. To this day, the friends list still does not work, the auction house is very temperamental. Secondly, I have never encountered such a convoluted loot management system in an MMORPG before. No matter how hard you try to make loot options fair for anyone, there will always be upset and drama around it. Thirdly, a guild roster limit of 70 is ridiculously small. I understand, it's a new game and this should settle down over time, but constantly having to worry about inactivity (due to how the guild ranking system works, another jank system) you are constantly battling kicking inactive players and invite newer, active members. As you could imagine, this causes further upset when people's friends etc get kicked for inactivity. Overall, the game is merely "OK" but is let down by some backwards systems that have been implemented poorly, or designed to promote pay2win and a greedy attitude amongst the playerbase. If all you care about is fancy visuals and a decent story for a f2p MMO then fair enough. However, don't let the p2w and greedy community consume you, in fact, do yourself a favour and turn all social chat channels off, sadly the game is not designed for decent, good-hearted people.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all I am a PVE player. I have other games which I enjoy PVP and I play Throne and Liberty purely PVE.Pay to Win (P2W) is a subjective term as there is no universally accepted definition.My definition of P2W has always been "The game offers players the ability to gain things which give an advantage only obtainable by spending real money" This means if these things can be obtained without spending real money it is not P2W.By this definition, Throne and Liberty is Pay to Advance or Pay for Convenience. You can achieve everything for free that a player can achieve for cash - if you're upset that it can take significantly longer, then that is on you.Personally I'm not in a rush to get BiS and partake in PvP so maybe I just don't understand the expectation and demands of F2P players wanting to PvP.But all the youtubers and streamers are calling it P2W! Since when were these guys the creators or definitions? Also lets not forget they're clickbaiters and masters of creating titles and videos to draw views and likes in - they will say what needs to be said to achieve the highest views and likes for their content. Because lets be honest my review will not be appreciated.Edit: I forgot to add that whilst I don't believe the game is P2W, it is unfortunately built around it's business model, which will ultimately damage the game. Things such as daily cap for dungeons - the things they do to encourage spending money, I feel is bad game culture.

_childDocuments_.review: Positives:Combat is smooth, visuals are amazing, servers paired with the visuals are very well optimized, the landscape and scenery are some of the best I've seen in games. The fast travel is also one of the most technologically advanced things I have seen in gaming, with 0 load times when you're fast travelling between locations. Negatives:Gearing is from an upgrade-based system. I've only put in 30hrs, but I've gotten 3 total main-hand weapon which is a similar story for the rest of my gear. It's not my preference, it might be for others, but for me it eliminates a major part of grinding I like in MMOs. The grappling system is *TERRIBLE*, half the time my character will leap to the side of the ledge instead of grabbing, or ill go inside the floor, or I'll not grapple at all even when I have stamina and I'm less than 10m away. Questing goes along the lines of - talk to this guy, talk to another guy, go and maybe kill a few things for the guy, talk to the guy again, talk to another guy, guy helps kill boss, maybe a puzzle that a baby could solve. When you reach level 50, you do get a wide variety of dungeons, but the main loot and everything you work towards at the end is going to be locked after doing a few runs in the dungeon, where usually all the purple drops are. And finally, the game feels like it's leaning to be P2W. Given these MMOs history, I wouldn't be surprised if it becomes P2W slop in a few months time. The auction house is even non-existent for F2P players unless they get a super rare drop that would give them a little money.There's probably more that I could list that I forgot to mention, but even in this state the game feels rather stale. I wish there were more open-world things to do, better quests, and more engagement between players besides the PVP (which I don't do).

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played over a dozen mmos, in it's current state, I would not consider Throne and Liberty to be P2W, at least not in the traditional sense, It leans more towards "pay to progress faster" and, quite frankly, it seems like barely an advantage when you factor in how the AH functions.  Uses the paid currency, Lucent, for AH transactions, at a very surface level it would appear to be P2W. However, this model is very similar to Warframe's, where you go to different areas farm an item and then put it up for trade with real money currency. F2P players have been able to make 100s of dollars worth of lucent from boss or dungeon epic drops. More than enough to fund both the battle pass and the leveling pass which I believe are 500 lucent ($10 USD.) Unlike warframe, you cannot buy fully crafted weapons or equipment directly from the in-game store with cash or real money currency, this forces any lucent that would be used for "P2W" to be redistributed throughout the player economy giving more opportunity for more F2P players to reap the rewards. These level 50 dungeons are something else, it is refreshing to see an mmo with dungeons that rely so heavily on cooperation to surpass boss mechanics regularly. Honestly, I find nothing more tedious than a dungeon needing to be classified as Mythic+5 in order to be considered difficult. At a baseline these things be difficult. The crap just looks good, I was concerned because usually these F2P games will have some god awful looking armor in the base game to encourage you to spend your hard earned cash for pretty cosmetics, while this game does have cosmetics, I enjoy the way most of the end gear looks way more than anything in the shop...well except for the leather cowboy outfit which I couldn't help but make look like the American flag, wasted $20 for a meme. Incredibly fast so you can get right into end game by mostly just speeding through the MSQ with EXP foods. There are quite a few events and they're posted on a calendar in your map, so you can plan your activities in advance. These events can be conflict or peaceful while also being cooperative or competitive. There are also open world dungeons that you can farm materials for, falling under these peace or conflict windows as well. The option to participate in conflict activities definitely spices things up sometimes. It essentially feels like Archeage + ESO systems in terms of being able to create your own class, mix and match the skills/passives of your weapons. It is honestly great.  I usually hate parrying in any game I play but it actually feels good to me here, you are sort of forced into it, but being able to mitigate stuns or damage as a dps or healer just feels rewarding. It is pretty much non-existent and it is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ perfect. I find myself constantly laughing at the insane conversations that manifest within the world chat. That being said, don't try to spam your way through the censors, that seems to result in a pretty good chance at a ban LOL. Oh my god, it is such a cool idea in theory but the execution feels so poor, at least on my end. Even worse when the grappling mechanic is essential in some dungeons and quests, it is one of the most frustrating things I've ever experienced.The parry mechanic is nice but when you're up against a large group of enemies and they all require parrying at different times, you miss one because of the minor cd of your parry and boom, you're stunlocked until further notice. I definitely think there should be some minor CC immunity after getting hit with CC. This is also an issue in PVP, it would be nice to have something in arena like an on demand CC cleaner, similar to a Smite purification bead. Now maybe there is some mild CC immunity after hard CC but I just haven't noticed it myself. In dungeons, or large groups, I can't see what the heck I'm targeting half the time and I prefer using tab-targeting instead of clicking so this causes an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: Best MMO RPG I have played in a while.The in-game systems have a good amount of depth and are not shallow.Amazing skill customization system that lets you make different variations of the same skill, offering a lot of different ways to build your abilities based on content and situation.The game has a good endgame loop; you'll never log in and not know what to do.Crazy good optimization allows hundreds of players to be in the same spot fighting with little issue, though it still requires fairly recent hardware, so be careful.Combat is basically the same old tab targeting we all know. Whether you like it or not will depend on you. As a tab targeting system, the combat is 9/10. It has a few small quirks, but overall it’s very well made and is one of the best tab-targeting systems currently available in MMORPGs.Best-feeling massive PVP fights since the Lineage 2 days. The game has a big focus on PVP and Guilds/Alliances. If you don't like group play, you can still get a good amount of solo/party content, but it won’t feel like a complete experience.The biggest negatives are the mid-story and fast leveling (for me).Regarding pay to win: This game is most definitely pay to win. But in my eyes, it’s one of the best P2W systems I have seen in an MMO so far. People tend to ignore the fact that all MMORPGs since the start were P2W. You were always able to buy in-game currency from the black market for real money and literally pay to progress. Sure, it was against the terms of service, and people usually didn’t see it advertised publicly, but it was always there, and some shady guy was getting the money.In contrast, Throne and Liberty has the whole game designed around P2W, with an in-game shop and premium currency that you can buy for real money. At first, it looks bad, but when you look closely, you will see many in-game blocks specifically designed to prevent P2W players from progressing too fast. Instead, it gives players with less time to play the game a chance to compensate with their money, but just in regulated amounts. Nothing is simply "pay and forget about it" – you still need to grind and actually play the game.Also, the best premium currency idea is the auction house based solely on premium currency. Every purchase of Lucent (so-called "whales" or anyone else) is not only for them. This person goes to the auction house and buys items for themselves. What items? Items other players grinded for, which free-to-play players are selling. So the Lucent this person buys for real money is distributed to the whole community sooner or later, in a slightly reduced amount. This player who is buying cannot get anything that hasn’t already been dropped by someone in the game. They gain no huge advantage over others, as most players use the best gear they need themselves first and only sell extra drops or items they don’t need.Sure, this system is not perfect, but as a whole, combined with in-game limitations, such as server milestones for new dungeons and events, it makes the balance of power fairly equal.To simplify, it works like this:You play for free, you spend more time playing.You play and spend small amounts of money (equal to subscriptions other MMOs have), and you grind a little less.If you spend big amounts, you can play less, but if you still want to play a lot, you’ll simply hit walls of progression constantly, making it boring for you, as all you did was get to the progression block slightly earlier than free-to-play players.My recommendation is to play for free and take your time to get to know the game. Reach level 50 to experience the peak of combat performance. After a week or two, you will need to decide if you want to play more seriously. While not mandatory, it will be more convenient to spend small amounts of money each month (equal to comparable subscriptions in other MMORPGs). If you don’t feel serious about the game, just don’t spend anything and play for free. You won’t be missing out on much fun, as most content will eventually be accessible when your gear is better. Always try to join a guild and make some friends – it will make the content more enjoyable.

_childDocuments_.review: I've put over 60 hours into this game across 2 betas, and I can't recommend this game enough! Sure, p2w exists, but just barely in my opinion. You can get everything to max without having to spend any money, and you can purchase the battle pass by just selling gear and unnecessary mats on the AH. Compared to many other f2p mmos I've played over the years, this is the MOST fair! I'm very excited to experience the entire endgame, but this is one of those games that I really wanna take my time with.Story is interesting so far, lots of the dialogue doesn't match the text shown on screen, and bits of the VA is rough, but I'm enjoying it so far!Combat, as is the case in most (not all) mmos, is very slow in the beginning. As the game progresses and you get to around lvl 30, the combat starts to pick up.World is beautiful! I've never been one to really take in the scenery, but this game constantly has me stopping to take screenshots and just admire the world around meEvents are probably my most favorite content in this game so far. From world bosses and open world events, to giant space whales, I've never been more satisfied with the early hours of an mmo in my life. Sure, FFXIV has Fates, but those are mostly pointless and don't offer anything, and it's pretty much dead content. But this game has lots of goodies hidden behind the events, which makes them worth doing when you have a few minutes to spare!Haven't really done any dungeons yet, as the only ppl recruiting for dungeons in the betas I participated in only wanted ppl who "knew the mechanics." like, really? the game hadn't even come out yet! How am I supposed to know how the dungeon works? Watch a youtube vid? Umm no! I'm not playing an mmo to have a wiki/video pulled up on my 2nd monitor just to figure out how the game works! I wanna figure things out on my own, with the help of other players who are either new to the game, or willing to teach new players!In the end, this game is the only mmo I've been excited about in a LONG time! I'm planning on sticking with this game for the duration of its life, however long that may be! Obviously it's better than Blue Protocol, since that game is shutting down, so I'm hoping the global audience is enough to keep the game alive! If you read all of this, you're an absolute champ! I appreciate you sticking with me through my thoughts and feelings about this game, and I hope that this is enough to move you to try the game out for yourself, rather than listen to some stranger on the internet who doesn't know how to be happy! In the words of John Henson, host of the American Wipeout show, "Good night, and big balls!"

_childDocuments_.review: As a 20 year WoW player, this game is a lovely break, I've played GW, GW2, ESO, TERA, RIFT, etc and while they each are unique in their own right, none of them really caught and kept my attention compared to WoW or any game similar. That's where TL comes in. It's got such a simple gameplay loop, simple rotation, yet you can be killed easily by the mobs if you pull one too many and don't time your dodges, parries, and CC's properly. I do M+, raiding, and PvP in WoW so I'm used to juggling 10-25 spells at a time as a full toolkit. In TL I only have 10 plus a handful of nonclass specific spells.I like the weapons based class system. The armor and weaponry themselves are extremely limited and that is pretty disappointing, however that doesn't necessarily detract from the overall appeal of the game. I am an avid transmogrifier in WoW, constantly making and changing outfits as I get new cool pieces. You can't do that in TL unfortunately, but again it doesn't break the experience of the game.Honestly I REALLY love the cinematic experience of gameplay with TL. The player in cut scenes are so expressive, the NPC's are well crafted, and it just feels nice. The lip syncing is...not great, but everything else is wonderful. The spell animations are apt, the UI is easily readable. I'm not a fan of constantly having the notification flagged in inventory ANYTIME I get literally anything and I have to hover over to get it to disappear, I'd prefer a toggle, but not a game breaking thing. Just annoying.The world bosses are mean. The dungeon end bosses are mean if you don't know the 2-3 mechanics and if the group doesn't communicate. I've only ran into 1 group so far who were antisocial, all the others were very chatty and helpful with explaining mechanics and callouts.I am really enjoying the pace of the game and the difference between it and my longtime favorite. I definitely can recommend this to anyone who loves mmo's and just wants a simpler experience.

_childDocuments_.review: First off I want to start with one fact, this game is not as P2W as many claim it to be, especially because often times there are simply NO items to buy on the AH, most guilds prefer to auction them internally in the guild. By the time people start whacking them on the public AH, it won't matter if you get it, people who are much better players than you already have the better items anyway.Yes you can buy items to get your traits faster, but let's be honest, if you suck you will suck even with traits. Great players know how to earn their lucent and don't mind swiping a bit for some faster trait progression. But WoW is similar, or even worse, you can pay to get raid/PVP carried with gold which you get via token, soo.... it's worse :DAnother thing is that even if you have T2 weapons and BiS items with traits etc. it still does not make you a god, not even close. The classes and specializations work in a Rock Paper Scissors way, so there's always a build that will wreck you, especially if they are a better player mechanically and know their rotation better. Battle pass and Leveling pass items you get from it are laughable to be honest, it doesn't really boost you by much...Some classes are definitely better than others (GS/dagger, probably the overall winner for most people) and there are some dubious choices which are simply not good enough. Hopefully in the future the dev team will introduce more benefits for various choices which will make them more viable.Leveling and story is pretty decent, the early progression feels nice. Leveling also gives you enough materials to upgrade most of your gear to at least L9 blue, same with skills, they are easy to get to at least blue, and most crucial ones to at least L1 of purple.The graphics are very nice, maybe not the best ever, but very good in my opinion. Same goes for sound.The content is quite nice and while there is a lot of content for large scale PVP, there is also content for loners, where you can always just go and do some dungeons via dungeon finder, or just go kill some stragglers in a PVP event (usually not the boss fights, but the collect X events). Overall material farming feels nice, but I would like a bit more variety on what you can do to get materials. Guild chest IMO needs a boost :)The problem for many people is the combat, and while it's much better than what it was when beta came out, it's still not perfect. But I have faith the combat will only get better with new additions and polish. I have experienced some issues with a couple of skills where sometimes they keep channeling but nothing happens (no stun, sleep, silence etc.) and sometimes it works like a charm, maybe just a lag issue. Also I really like the block feature which is not just a block (Q) but there are different versions which give you some bonuses after you block.Once the game launches as F2P, it's definitely worth checking it out. Hopefully Amazon can fix the servers, improve the netcode as it's painful to play from Australia on US... so every little bit of optimization helps. Or maybe just open OCE servers? :P

_childDocuments_.review: Bear with me, this will likely be a very long write up, but if you're looking for an unbiased, no bullcrap review, you've found it.I'll start with the positive. Combat is pretty cool and engaging, but nothing unique and special. It's just alright. There are both pros and cons, and I'll touch up on this below.That's it for the positives. Let's start with the extensive list of negatives. Combat itself is alright, but it is flawed because of controls and its functions, as well as external factors that will be mentioned below. While it does somewhat feels smooth and fluid, it falls flat and reminds you of how bad it really is. It is clunky and options that should've been on by default must be manually activated, which still don't really fix the fundamental "clunkiness". The movement of the game is slightly awkward to the point that combat is heavily affected by it, not allowing you to perform as perfectly as you can during fights like many other MMOs. The movement animations themselves aren't the problem, but rather the mechanics involved behind the movement. The world is so clunky as a whole, that simply jumping over a rock will cause you to magically teleport all over the place. This is even more evident when using the terribly designed morph/glide travel options, when attempting to glide to a puzzle and your character somehow gets stuck teleporting in air upon reaching the rock. It's clear the character has a sort of ifCollision>isStuck>UnstuckTeleport type of function, even though you're not actually ever stuck. It is a fundamental function that should be completely overhauled or scrapped. There's nothing positive to say about this. This is the equivalent of a Ground/Flying Mount, except there's nothing there but constant annoyance over the "clunkiness" of forms. In a world as large as this, it is extremely slow and extremely aggravating when trying to navigate the terrain. Another way to navigate the terrain are via grappling hooks, which are mixed with the movement/collision system and just as flawed. In return, you get a ridiculously annoying blend of features that you must contend with, if you want to play the game as a whole. You might then ask a simple question: "How can we make it faster?". It is Free-To-Play, so there's really one way to make money, at least for these modern gaming developers. Much like Lost Ark, and others, you are able to buy real money currency, which then translates into buying upgrades and items themselves. If you take Lost Ark, as an example, even though it is P2W, it doesn't really matter as much because the game is focused entirely on PvE, and one shot mechanics render gear useless, so to speak.Unfortunately, this is not the case here. This game has a heavy focus on Guild PvP content, which means if you swipe your card, you can get the best gear available and upgrade everything to max in minutes. But wait, there's more! How can we make travel mode faster? You guessed it right. To get more speed, you simply need more "forms", and there are premium and FOMO forms for sale that if you miss, you likely may not be able to max out the speed. In turn, that means not only does the enemy player that swiped has an advantage over you gear-wise, but also passive speed. There's really no point in doing PvP when it's like this, which brings us to the next point. If you're looking for an MMO with both PvE and PvP, this is not the game for you. While the game does have PvE content, aside from the obvious leveling experience, the endgame is extremely empty in every way. You are currency-locked to get rewards from dungeons to only a certain amount per day, and since this is a korean MMO, you have to grind a  amount of materials to craft your upgrades.This is essentially your daily PvE routine. Complete your daily contracts, do your 3 daily dungeons, and that's it. You could do world bosses and events, but these are locked behind schedules and don't actually help you as much in farming. Let's take it a step further. Let's say you don't PvP ever, and you got everything you need from the dungeons, and you're fully upgraded.Now what? Nothing. You're done, there's nothing else to do. There's a "Tower" PvE challenge content like Lost Ark, but once you get the rewards, there's no reason to do it again. Every weapon type has a mastery system with perks. It takes a colossal amount of time to level, and I truly mean a colossal amount of time. This essentially means that if you choose a set of weapons, then later on decide that you want to change, you're now way behind, because you have to start from the beginning. It also means you're going to have to grind a hell of a lot to catch up, or open your wallet. This applies to equippable items, and travel forms. This is yet another "large" game released with barely anything content-wise, which includes items. Each weapon has a skill tree, but there's barely any weapon types. There's also not a lot of travel form "morphs", especially depending which form. For an MMO, this simply doesn't make any sense. If MMO means regular, engaging content, then no content essentially means dead game. I don't understand how these developers continue to make the same mistake, unless they don't really care about any of this, aside from the potential profit on an empty game disguised as large simply due to the scale. The game itself is not difficult, and once you figure out how to bypass the overall "clunkiness", you're able to have some sort of fun, until you do content with other people. Much like Lost Ark, there is a skill ceiling in dungeons, and if you're not on top of it, you will cause the group to wipe, potentially causing players to rage quit. Unfortunately, as simple as some mechanics are, such as just press Q to defend when boss counter icon pops up, perfect or not, some people are unable to do this. Essentially, this means that you are forced to join a guild, and play with people that you may or may not particularly enjoy. That's not to say you can't achieve your goals solo, but it will take way longer due to randoms not doing mechanics.The problem with difficulties such as these in an MMORPG, is that you completely alienate a majority of your players. What happens if there's no content for your non-sweaty players? They'll simply leave, and spend their money and time elsewhere, case in point, Lost Ark.The reason World of Warcraft, as an example, is still one of the best MMOs out there that cannot seem to be "dethroned" is simply because there's no real difficulty for you get started, and you're not completely penalized by screwing up once, not counting the higher endgame difficulties that only a small percentage even bother with. This creates an environment where any players can play and progress without anything limiting or restricting them, like Lost Ark and this game.I do not recommend this game, whether you're solo, in a guild, or with friends. It is not made with longevity in mind, and will very likely have the same fate as New World. It's only a matter of time.It is a very flawed MMORPG, lacking the most basic MMO features, such as ability to transmog your gear. It doesn't matter if it comes later, it's the fact it wasn't included in the first place. This doesn't look good for developers, as it shows they're unable to do the proper research into what works, what doesn't, what should be included, what shouldn't, in order to create a gaming environment that keeps the only currency they need in order to survive. PEOPLE.One could hope that future developers would understand the simple fact that PvP only games die by the thousands, for one tiny reason. If you don't have people, you don't have a game.

_childDocuments_.review: This game does not respect your time in the slightest, so at least you should respect your time and your wallet. Do not be fooled by the PVE content it offers, this is first and foremost a guild-focused PvP game.After the atrocious first 30mins of intro to the game, the biggest highlight of this game, aside from the beautiful world - was leveling. Fun and interesting quests, and every quest felt new and different. Side quests are either the most fun you will have in the game, or the most annoying, abysmal crap you will have to do. Flying around the map on a whale is the coolest thing you will experience in this game.And.. That's about it. You enjoy the beautiful world and exploring while leveling, and then you hit max level and.. the honemyoon ends:- abysmal night and day mechanic forced into content (do this part of quest at night, when day turns into night or night into day, open world dungeone become pvp zones at night) - 0 respect towards people making time in their real life to play your game only to have to schedule in game time to play as well - certain pve content only available when it rains in game (it doesnt rain that often) - forced world PvP events (sure, you can ignore them, but the issue here is that these zones sometimes are a part of MQS and your 25lvl character is going to have to wait 30minutes to turn in a quest to continue leveling because lvl50s are just obliterating everything in sight. Seriously, who thought of this?- 1 large guild split into mutliple smaller guilds allied together control the entire server, and this is true for every server. Good luck competing for world content if you're not in one. Especially once the seiges are released.- Auction house currency is real money currency ( althought you can earn it ingame by just selling this should never ever be a thing! )- you have a sad low chance at crafting and looting an item that is tradeable. Between 10 and 20% chance- gearing system is probably the worst I have ever seen- PvE content is lacking, unpolished and uninspired. It was added last-minute, so some things can be forgiven, but the amount of lazy insant-wipe mechanic in dungeons is just sad. The dungeons currently give mostly role specific loot which makes for some interesting que times. World bosses are okay design wise but the droprate and amount of drops is abysmal.- System upon a system upon a system, many different currencies. Nothing new for a Korean game, but it is so obvious on every inch of the game that it wants you to spend. This game WANTS to be pay to win game and it's not afraid to show you this whatever menu you open.- Bots are running wild left and right, highly populated servers are literally unplayable because you cannot kill a single mob to participate in event or contracts.- For a game that allows change of classes on the go, the mastery XP for weapons takes half an eternity, so don't expect to flex classes anytime in the near future.- If you have limited time to play, and want to play as f2p, you will fall behind fast, and fall far. Everything in this game is on a schedule!- numerous other issues such as gliding, bugged quests etc.Tldr: this should have been a mobile game.

Since these stars were part of a paid pass, this approach feels like a scam. I haven’t seen another game handle paid content like this.Overall, the game feels repetitive and uninspired, filled with daily tasks that lack freedom or variety. Players are expected to complete the same few actions daily without much thought or strategy—just join a random group and mindlessly smash monsters. There's no depth or need for actual knowledge in these tasks.

Everyone better pay money for it.Want the cool looking ground travel look?  Gotta pay.As gamers, this is our fault.  It's my fault.  I bought early access.  Sure, I got a few things out of it, but not enough to justify the cost.  But I was so starved for a new MMO, I was weak.  They knew that.  They prey on that.Everything in the game is designed to take your money, either through subtle means or just flat out directly.  It's not a game meant to have fun, it's meant to force you to pay to have fun.  To place first.  To have the cool new look.It's not the first game to do it and it won't be the last.  I hope it will be the last for me.As gamers, we need to do better.Still am, probably through the day this review is posted, but I doubt much longer.I have been a gamer for over 30 years.  I tend to play mostly PC games.  I also bounce around between games A LOT.  I may purchase a $60 game and play it for 2 hours or spend $10 on a game and spend 50 hours on it.  Even if I played a game a short time, it does not mean it is bad.  It just means another game caught my attention.  I also complain about flaws in games a lot, even about the littlest of things. _childDocuments_.review: Not bad but ultimately forgettable.From the time I started the game until my character was at the level cap was just under 39 hours.  Most of the world map is still unrevealed.  The questing was okay but obviously waaaaaaay tooo XP-rich, IMO.  It should take weeks or months to get to a level cap; it should not be something that can be achieved via a binge weekend.  The game has a decent look and combat is relatively well done.  Now that I'm at level cap I have no interest in the game.  The game wants me to continue to do quests and open up the world map, etc. but there's just no incentive other than completeness.On the technical side, despite the game having an overall good look, it runs like garbage on my RTX 3060 Ti.  Constant blurs, skipped frames, etc.  The game does not run cleanly for me ever.The gear progression & acquisition is beyond maddeningly unnecessarily complicated.  As is the ability/spell progression.   And crafting in general.Throne & Liberty (horrible, stupid name for this game, by the way) was a fun diversion for a couple of hours a day for a couple of weeks, but the lack of anything different from any other MMORPG and the rush-to-the-end-game focus just leave me unenthused.  I don't regret the time I spent playing but I won't remember it much in a couple of weeks, either.

_childDocuments_.review: The story is very fun, the dungeons are great, and the combat style is neat. However, what really detracts from the game is the semi-forced PvP. You can say there are scheduled peace activities, but let’s be honest: the top guild on each server can dominate everything and earn double the rewards, further outpacing the entire server. These same guilds often form alliances with other strong guilds, and all the spenders come together to control every conflict event. If you’re not in one of these top guilds, forget about joining—if your gear score isn’t around 3k, you won’t be accepted. Overall, the PvE content is great; I would gladly pay a subscription for the game if it focused solely on PvE with optional PvP.The Good:Public dungeons are fun, and there are always groups available for them. However, the need for tokens to access the drops diminishes the experience. With a limited number of contract tokens each day, much of the appeal is lost.Co-op dungeons are enjoyable as well; the boss designs are great, and the mechanics aren’t very difficult. However, the experience suffers again due to the token limit—you can only complete three per day at most.The Bad:The drop rate in co-op dungeons is not friendly unless you have the luck perk or choose to spend money. I’m not opposed to low RNG, but without a pity system, it feels pointless to play this game beyond finishing the story content.Overall, for the first 30 hours, you will have fun, be confused about what to do, and be amazed at the size of the world and the variety of monsters. However, the game quickly changes at level 50; it starts to feel like a job. Each day, you have to spend all your resistance contracts, use all your abyss tokens, run your three dungeons, check the schedule for peace events, find one you want to do, complete it, and log off until the next day or the next event starts. And don’t forget: if it’s a PvP event, you might be executed before you can even see the boss or complete a task.As a final straw, if you join a guild, any drops you get go to the guild for distribution unless you claim them first. If you receive something you could sell for a lot of lucent on the auction house, it could be quickly taken, and there’s nothing you can do about it because the game is designed that way. There have already been several instances of this happening, and it is not a punishable offense.As I write this, part of me wants to recommend the game based on the PvE, but due to the constraints that the in-game systems impose, I doubt it’s worth the 30-50 hours. However, it is a free game, so at least you only lose time playing it and not money. Why listen to someone review a game when you can try it out and find out for yourself?

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, Throne and Liberty suffers from an all too common blueprint found in many other Korean MMORPGs adapted to the West (Archeage, Black Desert Online, Lost Ark). The game lures you in with stunning visuals, an appealing epic castle siege, and cool particle effects. But under that new coat of paint are the toxic mechanics coupled with a toxic community:Classic mode controls are the most clunky, janky feeling in a 2024 MMORPG. Playing on Action combat mode will just make you an easy target for the people playing on Tab-Targetting.The PvP Meta Builds have been solved from the Korean Version, Melees are unkillable tanks that can pull you in from 30yard range into a infinite CC stun chain. Range are glass cannons that can do do AoE filling up 1/4 of your screen. If anyone is playing a pure healer build, you're going to have the worst experience imaginable. You either become the DPS Support the game wants you to play as or play as a build that ruins the fun for other players.The weapon swap mechanic is shallow and doesn't flow smoothly, the taxes are high, and returns are diminishing, making progression unbearably slow. Crafting is terribly boring and tedious, one of the main value points for many players. You will be trying to farm for days on end just to get the ingredients you need for a CHANCE at a single upgrade. When you add in the fact that pretty much all these crafting materials can be bought in a cash shop, it starts to seem almost designed this way purposely to encourage spending, instead of playing and enjoying crafting.The PvP Guild vs Guild Castle Sieges that's advertised are no better. It's just whichever side has the biggest AMAX Credit Card. A re-occurring theme in a lot of PvP oriented Korean MMORPG-Losing a Castle Siege is a real detriment to the guild. To give you an idea how much money is at stake: The winning alliance on Asota server earned roughly $30k USD worth of premium currency by winning the castle siege. An estimated 1500-2000 players showed up to the siege.The End-Game oriented guild I was apart of is basically forcing people to max out their gear with the best stats via the premium currency Auction House by next week's castle siege. If we didn't pass the gear expectations set by the guild officers, we would ultimately be kicked due to "leeching" off the earnings of more hard-working guild members.Bringing to my last point about the PvP, with so much resources on the line. Korean PvP oriented games are prone to large scale alliances. "If you can't beat them, join them" is the motto for Korean PvP Zerg vs Zerg MMORPGs (Black Desert Online, Archeage). Resulting in multiple guild alliances spanning across one server. Draining the competitive PvP scene to nothing but the largest and most P2W guilds left standing. The server will merge due to low player count, and it will just be P2W guilds vs each other. The Bot problem is up front and center. It's tough, knowing that botting is more of a feature than a nuisance. With the farming process requiring a NEET lifestyle, players will feel the need to run 3rd party bot software to remain competitive. The same end-result in BDO.This is a yet another brazen cash grab from Jeff Bezos' Amazon Game Studio. Mechanically shallow, monetarily aggressive and extremely tough to recommend.But it's always fun to experience an MMO at launchWhomp Whomp

_childDocuments_.review: Part of me wants to give the game a thumbs up for the graphics and the fact that it's free to play which means you can get some decent mileage out of it without ever paying, but the other part of me that wanted to give the game a thumbs down for everything else ultimately won out in the end.Amazing visuals, and the gameplay initially feels really good, but after a few dozen hours, you start to realize how repetitive the gameplay loop is. The game pretends to be much deeper than it really is, but it's actually extremely barebones and skimpy across the board. The game world is smaller than you initially think, gear/weapon variety is terrible (a major issue for a guy like me who likes cosmetic customization), dungeons are all very samey and there's only a few of them, and gameplay pretty much boils down to "do cookie cutter quests in <insert zone here> and hope that PvP isn't currently enabled in the region and hindering your ability to do anything".The PvP in this game is trash tier. When PvP is on, it's ON. There's no toggle on/off, there's no dedicated area for it, nothing. Random locations just become open world PvP when world events start (every 2-3 hours). People of all levels do these events, including people at max level who go back and do the events in the low level areas. This leads to people just trying to level and ignore the events getting one-shotted REPEATEDLY by max level players who are just there to grief. I've experienced it firsthand, and it's just awful game design. Forced PvP is fine when the players in the area are all on an equal footing (same gear score, level range, whatever). It's NOT fair when it's a geared level 50 hardcore PvPer ganking a level 10 guy repeatedly who is just trying to experience the game in the actual area the game tells him to play in. This. Is. Not. Good. Game. Design. Hardcore PvP nuts who love ganking/griefing may be salivating, but it's not healthy design. There's a reason why most western MMOs abandoned this style of play YEARS ago (it's bad), but Asian developers still haven't taken the hint yet.There's also a battlepass. Like, a straight up regular battlepass in an MMO. This immediately injects a little bit of P2W in the game, even if it's not substantial. After examining what paid players get, I've determined that they get some degree of an advantage over players who don't pay. Again, something that should not be a thing in this type of game. A cash shop with various in-game items that can be purchased, fine, but battlepasses shouldn't be in games like this, and when they are, they should offer cosmetic/QoL rewards only.The UI is also pretty bad. Too many pop-ups saying other players in the game world acquired items, too much annoying chatter boxes from your amitoi (a cute minion that follows you around). On top of this, UI customization is below average, there's no easy way to see all in-game currencies at once with the press of a button, the quest tracker is garbage (I've had quests direct me to areas where the quest objectives were not even at), and more. This game takes the award for second worst UI I've ever had to deal with in an MMO. Fortunately for Throne and Liberty, Black Desert's UI was just far too god awful to ever be challenged by any other game ever, so this game can happily know that it will never be the worst in this area.The game has a lot of issues that slowly creep more and more towards the forefront as you spend a few dozen hours with it. Throne and Liberty looks VERY pretty thanks to being backed by Amazon's bottomless bank accounts, but the actual game itself is still extremely shallow after you come to grips with things and see the game for what it is after passing the 30-35 or so level range.WHAT'S DONE RIGHT:- Animal forms, while nothing revolutionary, shake up gameplay just enough to be a positive.- Fishing is actually pretty fun and better than what most MMOs manage.- Graphics are well above average for an MMO. Reminds me of how good Black Desert looked on launch, which is a very good thing. Even still, the fact that the only time I mentioned the graphics in my main review was at the start in just a few words does highlight how the graphics cannot save this game and can only do so much of the heavy lifting.- It's free to play. While the game makes up for this in other areas in some pretty gross ways, being able to still play the game for a bit without spending any money on it is a plus. Just don't expect that to last if you plan to make this your main MMO that you spend hundreds of hours in.- Lots of repeatable quests for people who like to chase dailies.- Skill customization is actually pretty okay and you can augment some skills in interesting ways.- Sound direction isn't too bad. The music is serviceable and does what it needs to without being memorable while the sound effects are definitely pretty good. Voice acting can be hit or miss.WHAT'S DONE WRONG:- Dungeons are overall pretty bland and samey when it comes to location and mob variety. Final bosses of each dungeon are pretty unique and interesting, but aren't enough to save the dungeons from being pretty ho-hum overall.- Equipment variety is really poor. There's only a small handful of pieces that you can buy. The rest all need to be crafted, and chasing the requirements for them can be a hassle (especially for superior quality pieces). Because of this, you'll only upgrading to new armor/weapons maybe 5-6 times before max level. MAYBE.- Gameplay loop does not change significantly in the grand scheme of things after you pick your favourite weapons to play with.- Grappling hooks. Why are they even in this game? They feel like just a gimmick tacked on to make "exploration" feel more rewarding. It didn't work.- P2W mechanics via the battlepass and the previously unmentioned auction house, which uses a currency that can only be obtained if you purchase it with real money. Free to play users will NOT be able to use the auction house in any meaningful way whatsoever. - Pretty clunky UI that is barely customizable, has poorly designed elements, and really finnicky tab-targeting.- PvP is implemented in a horrible way. I've already explained why, so I won't beat that dead horse again.- World is deceptively small, and there's virtually nothing to do in it outside of do repeatable quests and PvP. The developers try to mask this and make the world feel grand and alive, but it falls pretty short of the mark once you invest some time in the game and see enough of it.I'm not extremely picky when it comes to MMOs, but I'd probably rather play almost any other MMO in my library over this, and I've already started doing so as I fall back on a WoW private server which I enjoy playing on more than I do this game. Even with my complaints and the thumbs down (I hate the thumbs up/down system, Steam should give us a five star system instead), this isn't really a bad game. It's just not a great game. Proceed with caution.
