_childDocuments_.review: Jan 3, 2024 - This is my new review. I will admit that this game has come a bit of a long way, but there are some issues still and YES the game is installed on my SSD. My gaming PC is brand new that I have built myself  (I'm an athletic nerd, dont judge me lol) with all of the hardware from late 2023. Issue One - There are a bunch of graphical bug in the game where they are either "manageable" or not at all to the point where I had to reduce my graphics quality to medium. I dont mind doing that, but there are still a series of lags, glitches, and freeze time that make the game unplayable.Issue Two - Multiplayer has been a bit below par due to not just the graphical issues, but also due to matchmaking. There would be instances where I would be in a race/lobby where everything is fine, no one is trying to be a butthead or anything like that, but then in the next session there would be a group of people who would blatantly cheat and not get caught. ITS NOT A SKILL ISSUE for me before you think that, but it not only effects my experience but everyone else's too. Personally, I don't care until some random person would be in the session and he or she is losing so badly that they end the session for everyone while running a bunch of game logic scripts to the server or using macros that go from slowing everything down to having the server timeout and not reachable.Play at your own risk or let this cookEdit - After the recent updates (and YES, the game is installed on a SSD since the beginning) the game has improved a bit with some lesser to moderate bugs still in it.Score: 6.5/10 (For now)

_childDocuments_.review: I have always been a fan of Forza Horizon games but I have never tried out any Forza Motorsport games, so when I saw that Forza Motorsport was coming out in a few days, I bought it immediately. I was expecting a photorealistic and fun racing game that could rival Gran Turismo 7, but what I got was a slight disappointment. Sometimes it looked like a 2017-2018 game with the lighting looking horrible and textures being extremely blurry/pixelated, but most of the time it looked pretty good. Despite the meh graphics, I only got 40-50fps at high graphics + my pc was as loud as a jet engine most of the time. I have a high end pc with and RTX 3070 Ti and a Ryzen 7 5700G, yet the performance was so bad I had to take breaks because of my eyes hurting after playing for 1-2 hours. But if you have a Nasa computer you'll be (probably) fine. Moving on to the gameplay, the career mode is a bit too boring for a racing game. You do 3 laps practise and then do the race. That's it. And from doing that over and over again and leveling up your car you can upgrade it. Instead of you choosing out which parts you want to switch/upgrade, you can just click one button and the game does it for you. The best thing about this game is the controls for the gamepad, they feel extremely nice.In it's current state I just really can't seem to enjoy it, and therefore I can't either recommend it to someone else.Edit: I tried playing this game with a steering wheel, and had the worst experience in my life. Just do not play this racing game with a steering wheel.Another edit: I got myself a pc not too long ago, and right now, the performance is decent. With max settings (no RT) I am able to get around 120 fps. Got a RTX 4070 and an i7-13700 inside this thing with 32 gigs of RAM. Still wouldve expected a bit more fps for the "nice" graphics...

_childDocuments_.review: Steam keeps asking if I want to revise my review, so I will.  After several updates and 20 more hours of play time the game is just as frustrating as ever.  The car handling is wonky and not very realistic, and the AI is just dumb.  That sums it up.  If you want more detail my original review below still stands.If you're on Steam/PC, I would avoid this iteration of the Forza franchise.  I'm a big fan of Forza and it can be a fun game, but it's more frustrating than fun, especially if you are a career/single player.  I've not played multiplayer so I can't comment on that, but this game is actually getting worse, not better.When this game launched, it was fairly lacking on cars and tracks.  There was enough to enjoy but it felt extremely incomplete.  As they have updated the game they have added some tracks and cars, but it still feels incomplete and we're not well over 6 months past launch.  One good example of the incompleteness of cars is the fact that the only WEC Hypercar in the game is the Cadillac, and to "balance" the game with what they have Forza has mixed in LMP1 and LMP2 cars with varied ratings and stats.  The Cadillac, in my experience, is about worthless in this game and gets passed pretty easily by LMP2 cars.  There are other examples but that is one.Another thing that burns me up about this game is they STILL have not fixed the livery and vinyls issues for Steam players.  I've read that you can access previous title designs if you launch through the MS Store but that sort of defeats the purpose of playing on Steam.  For some people this won't really be an issue but I have THOUSANDS of hours in FM5, FM6, and FM7 making very specific vinyls to use in liveries that I can't access in this game, which takes a lot of the fun out of it for me.Additionally, the campaign is very weird.  There are a few different race series that you can do but they don't really give you the full gambit of car divisions/classes.  Once you finish them all you can replay them or just wait around for the next update when more will be introduced.  But once the new races are introduced they are often locked so you can't even race them till Forza allows you to.  Also, old races will be removed so you can't do them any longer.  It's just a really weird thing to do with a career/single player mode in any game.  It would be fine if there was a single player section where interesting races were put up for a limited time, but there really needs to be a more traditional, longer career mode like in FM7.  The final issue with the career mode is that most of the time you will not earn enough money in one series to buy a car for the next one, so you'll have to replay races to earn money.The other MAJOR issue that I think people will want to be aware of is that this game is becoming more and more unstable and inconsistent as they update it.  According to the change longs and update press releases they are working on reducing load times and crashes, but at least for me, they're getting worse.  This was very playable for me on day 1, in terms of performance.  After recent updates I almost always have to verify the game files regularly to fix crashes.  That could be a Steam problem not a Forza problem, but I'm going to blame Forza by default because it's always after an update and the only other game I've played through Steam that does that is COD.  Also, the load times for tracks have increased about 20X or more.  Nearly every track has to load, just to the "start practice" menu, and that can take several minutes.  Then loading the actual race can also take a long time.  It's just becoming more work than it is worth.The AI is terrible.  TERRIBLE.To sum this up, I mostly enjoy the game.  It looks and sounds decent and I believe that in some ways the physics are slightly improved over FM7, though it could just be my uninformed opinion.  And the multiplayer may be great.  But with the bad AI, the wonky career, the lack of historic design access for Steam users, the crashes, and the long load times this is a pass.  I've been a pretty loyal Forza Motorsport customer since the first edition on OG XBox, but I'll be passing on future titles unless they can prove they know how to complete games.

_childDocuments_.review: Cars are sometimes invisible and not affected by physics, so you will get rammed off the road by an unmovable car. This is often the cause for the chaos in races, especially at the first turn.Sometimes the fuel calculator decides to not work and you run out of fuel half way through an online race.Races are unbalanced due to poor matching making and there are usually a limited number of people with fully upgraded cars.You will get rammed off the track by others players, and if they go off the track first, you will get a penalty for it. The penalty system seems to only be aware of what happened after the incident, and not what happened before.You can't tune your car during Rivals but you can during other races, even though it says that tuning will invalidate your lap at the start of Rivals.You have to level up cars before you can even tell if they are competitive or if they can reach the PI that you want, since you can't see upgrades until you level up. Want to drive the Mazda 787B? It can't even get close to max PI in any class and it's completely useless.The leveling system is pointless time sink that adds nothing to the game. This is why people are running up their power bills driving cars by themselves overnight to level them.The AI drivers will often ram you off the road and ignore you are there. They will randomly brake on straights and through flat out turns.There is nothing you can do with drag tires or drift suspension.This game is an unfinished buggy mess and I don't recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: I hardly ever leave Steam reviews, but I think that it’s warranted on this one.This game is the definition of “I’m not angry, I’m just disappointed.”While I do believe they got the driving physics much better this time around, and the online does seem better as well, that’s right where my praise will end. I seriously cannot believe it took 6 years for this half-baked mess. I can barely run it at my native resolution (5120x1440) and get 60fps maxed out with a 13900k and a 6950xt. Excuse me for my ignorance as I am not a game developer and have a lot of respect for these folks, but I can’t imagine a track racer like Motorsport 8 should take up more system resources than Horizon 5, especially when it looks barely half as good. Seriously, I wouldn’t have a lot to complain about performance wise if it looked beautiful like other new titles releasing such as Baldur’s Gate 3, but this doesn’t even come close, and at times I’m not even sure if I’d call it good looking.I’m not a huge fan of the constant crashing either. It has gotten bad enough that it’s a 50/50 shot if I’ll get through a race or not, with all the practice laps and everything in between. I genuinely would like to keep playing because the game does feel good to play, but at this point I guess I’ll just have to wait till they do some patches. Afterall, why should a product work as intended at launch? Go live service!As far as the upgrade system goes, I like what they were trying to do, but this sucks. My best suggestion would be to bring down the car level cap from 50 to something like 20 or 30 and make sure that progress is transferred to any car of the same model. If you don’t wanna do that then just go back to using credits or something, it’s not rocket science. Just fix it.Reader, do yourself a favor and save the hundred dollars you’d spend on the premium edition and go pick up a copy of Forza Motorsport 4 and a used Xbox 360. Not only will it probably be the same price, but you’ll have a better career mode, more tracks, more cars, better music, those great voice-overs from the old top gear crew, and no constant crashing. On top of that, you can invite your car buddies over to set lap times and play split screen, it makes for a great time.Thanks for teaching me a lesson Forza, I’m finally done pre-ordering games.This review was built from the ground up. The game wasn’t.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 2.6 hours in and I just can't do this again. Turn10 took all our complaints and grievances from Forza7 and Horizon# and doubled down on them. The agonizing tutorial I can only described as 'Mansplaining'. You are forced to use the car that they give you (or one of three choices). I finally completed the "Builders cup" with a bloated yellow mustang that i didn't want, only to find three more "cups" with the same limits on creativity and choice. It seems the entirety of career mode is like this. The big sin persists as your forced to race a specific type of car/class. Complete one championship to unlock the next. Want to race a vintage Ferrari,?an old Miata? that's immediately locked. No, i don't want to race a "hot hatch". No, i don't want to race in some gangling Audi. I want to choose, I want to putz around in that Miata or a MGA to start. All the championships need to be unlocked from the start. Now that actual "Building"? That seems largely unchanged. Unless we count the multiple forms of currency that parts are locked behind. First your car has to be a certain level before your allowed to even peruse specific parts. Then you are allotted a certain amount of CP (yes CP) that can't be exceeded. Each part subtracts from your total CP. You gain more CP by leveling up your car?i think? Its honestly a thoughtful way to add RPG elements to game that is about the furthest thing from an RPG. So no more buying that 240sx and immediately ricing it out to go drifting, you gotta level it up first. Instead of qualifying we get "practice laps" which are skippable. Any would-be qualifying is rendered useless because your allowed to pick your own start position in the next race. I just cant Turn10, I cant sit through this like i did with you before. Everything that was painful in the Horizon series is here too, and its atrocious. Its over, were through. Some good things-                    - You can finally (Finally!) turn down the windshield/dash reflection (quality)                    - Sound design is better than ever                     - The rebuilt physics feel great, i would have loved to explore them further (in a car of my choosing).

_childDocuments_.review: Edit Review, November 21st of 2024: After a year I have come back to review Forza Motorsport. What I have found is a more polished game that allows you to feel the real weight of the car you are slinging around the track. I must give credit were it is due to all the developers whether they are permanent or temps that have poured their souls into this game. Your efforts have been noticed and I'm pleased with the corrections to color (EI: black is no longer just a dark grey and wheels stay the same color they were painted.), the constant crashing and boot-looping has been fixed for the most part, and the penalty system, while I don't care for it, is much better at recognizing context for the penalty or warning. Before I end this, I do want to touch base on what is essentially the core of Forza Motorsport as we see it today. Does it have the freedom the previous titles have given players and hooked me into the series all those years ago. Now I can say yes. They have brought back the fun and enjoyment of being able to race with my friends in any car we want and a great list of tracks that were originally missing on release. So in good faith I can recommend Forza Motorsport in the hopes that they continue on this course of improvement. I hope that this backlash they received is a wake up call to upper management to not fumble the game on release and that they allow the developers to continue their fine work to create an even better Forza Motorsport in the future.Original Release Review: All I can say is, I'm disappointed. I have been a fan of Forza Motorsport since FM3 came out and I played the demo in a Game Stop at my local mall. The passion that was put into the previous games are what made me a car enthusiast today, but that is gone. What was once a celebration of motorsport is nothing more than corporate pandering and a false sense of accomplishment to drag play time further than it ever should have been. All to make the stockholders think this was a success and what the business model should be for the future. If this is what they have in-store, if they even make another game, then count me out.

name: Bloomtown: A Different Story
detailed_description: Bloomtown: A Different Story is a narrative JRPG mixing turn-based combat, monster taming and social RPG set in a seemingly pleasant 1960s Americana world. Play as Emily and her younger brother Chester sent on their summer holiday to their grandpa’s cozy and quiet town. May be too quiet… Children starting to disappear, nightmares getting more real… Something’s not right, especially for a 12-year-old girl with an adventurous mind! It is up to you to solve this mystery and free Bloomtown and its inhabitants from a glooming fate! Bloomtown is a quiet and cozy American town with its cinema, grocery shops, library, parks… But this is only a façade! A demon world is growing on the underside, children are disappearing, and it is up to you to save the town! Embark on mysterious adventure to save the townspeople from their own demons: Fear and vices have taken monstrous life form in the Underside. Follow Emily and her group of friends, figure out the mysteries of the mystical disappearances and save Bloomtown’s inhabitants souls! In the turn-based tactical battles against giant demons and dungeon bosses from the Underside, Emily is not alone! Use each character abilities and strengths to come out victorious. Summon your own inner demons as well as the captured ones to set up devastating combos. During combat, catch weaken creatures to add them. With loads of creatures, level-ups, unique skills and a fuse system, create hundreds of synergies and your own demon-hunting squad. Explore the town’s secret areas, strengthen your physical abilities at the gym, gain pocket money working at the grocery store, make resourceful friends or do some relaxing gardening. You decide what is the most useful for your adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Set your expectations with this game.The gameplay will be 90% story for a long time and 10% actual combat gameplay.  So if you're not into cheeseball anime stories, then don't bother.  If you ARE then you'll have fun with this game.I'm also tired of the co-op just being side missions and not being fully integrated into the gameplay experience.  Japanese games have a long way to go on this front and unfortunately it's too much progression as a solo player to REALLY be a good co-op game.I'm enjoying the experience given to me. _childDocuments_.review: Some may compare this to Armored Core. In my opinion, it's more apt to compare this to Phantasy Star Online.There's a lot to like here if you're into the Super Robot genre. The customization is decent, the art style is great, and there's a decent variety of Super Moves.The problem people might have with this game come down to the game design, though. As some have noted, it's not good enough as a dedicated co-op game. Much of it is single-player with story-telling in a similar vein to a normal JRPG, just with manga paneling and visual novel sensibilities thrown in. There's no actual roleplaying in it since you as a player don't make any choices.For multiplayer there is a PvP mode on top of a co-op mode, along with a live service element of Daily Login rewards and even Seasons like in other ARPGs. The netcode for these modes isn't terrible but it's not great either. The gameplay is also pretty unbalanced in the beginning and it can be difficult to get one's bearings, but the gameplay is also so easy for much of the playthrough that it can lead to frustrations. This is recommended only to people who understand that this is a fun action RPG with a big emphasis on story presentation and showing off the fun that comes with Super Robot tropes. This is not recommended to anyone who wants a highly polished Armored Core 6 competitor or an otherwise complicated mech game, because this game is not that.

_childDocuments_.review: While this is the third installment in the Megaton Musashi series, it'd be more apt to think of this as another expansion to the original Megaton Musashi released in 2021. This game contains all the content present in Megaton Musashi and Megaton Musashi X and adds plenty of its own content; as a result, Megaton Musashi Wired has hundreds of hours of content for you to sink your teeth into. The story is really compelling; you'll quickly find yourself hooked, looking forward to every story beat. However, I do have to admit the last few chapters feel rushed and aren't as good as the rest of the story, *especially* the last two chapters. Regardless, I really enjoyed the story; it's one of my favorites from Level-5. The gameplay is incredibly fun and addicting. There are a plethora of mechanics to work with, and the customization has quite some depth to it, though it can be overwhelming at first. Story missions won't pose much of a challenge, but the Dreadnought Missions will, especially in the endgame.Lastly, I'd like to talk about the live-service elements present in the game, which you may have heard about from other reviews. While the game does have log-in bonuses and a battle pass, they are not intrusive to the experience. In Wired, they only contain additional materials that you can already grind for; they do  contain exclusive content like weapons, Rogue parts, or Pilot skins. Additionally, the paid battle pass is a one-time purchase only available through the deluxe edition; you don't have to repurchase the battle pass whenever a new one comes out. The log-in bonus and battle pass are really just remnants of Megaton Musashi X's free-to-play roots. While I'd prefer if these live-service elements weren't in Wired, I ultimately don't mind their implementation here.Overall, Megaton Musashi Wired is an amazing mecha hack-and-slash action RPG from Level-5. I highly recommend playing it, even if you're not a mecha fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome Back, Level 5L5 Does Evangelion. the last of humanity lives blissfully unaware that outside their sheltered carefully curated lives in a safe heaven, the world is a wasteland where giant robots fend off the alien invasion that almost wiped us out and re-terraformed Earth to suit their needs.A team of youngsters with the ideal reflexes and neurological capabilities is assembled to go outisde and pilot the new generation of giant robots called  Megatons.The story unfolds in an open 2D sidescrolling rpg city while the combat gameplay is a full 3D (but not super expensive AAA, remeber, L5 is a AA dev that mostly comes from handheld games) mecha figther thats actually pretty fun. It invites comparisons to 13 Sentinels, another game I loved, but that drops the ball on the gameplay since the devs ran out of money and you dont really pilot the robots, you see them as dots on a radar (I'm still mad about that). But they made up for it with 10/10 art and a brilliant story. Which, yeah, this doesnt really match in those aspects but its clearly not attempting to be a Vanillaware title. The art and story we have here are actually pretty good too. So odious comparisons aside, both are great for different reasons.  So yeah, those vestiges of a diferent kind of monetization and the fact that the scale of the combat feels a bit on the toyish side like Gundam Alliance SD rather than say AC6. I liked it as an arcady, charming robot action game, with a sidescrolling neat anime story on top. But Armored Core this is not.

_childDocuments_.review: I am really on the fence about recommending this game or not as I probably would have skipped on buying it if I knew ahead of time, Pros; - Mech design and customization; (Why do mechs need pupils in their eyes?) - Wide variation of weapons. - Speed of the mechs furring game play. - Adding in 4 mechs from different franchises was really pretty dam cool.Cons;- The story is just a roller coaster between interesting and boring. The ending felt so rushed and should have started 5 chapters sooner and in the end it really put me off with the game. - ALL the missions are the same, go to a section of the map, beat X enemies,  continue a few more times till you get to the boss and beat him.- Having parts of the story play durring the game and if you stop to read it, you can get hit by the enemies. Would have been better to pause the battle to read what was going on. -  Having to enter cockpit mode to try and activate your super move is a pain in the ass. I do hope the developers work on some changes to the game, and perhaps offer up some DLC that changes the mission type. I never saw the anime the game is from, but there was a lot there that reminded me of the old school mech / super robo anime shows I grew up with. There are other mech titles that are able to pull off the execution between game play and story a lot better (sorry to say). The rushed ending.... I do feel a bit cheated as I did play a good amount of time, and then it was over and first thing I thought was "That was it?" So, with those things being said, if they buyer is aware of these things... then I would recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm in the middle of a completionist run of this that I'm realizing I may never actually finish. If you like games with a ton to do and with very high numbers popping up on screen, this is the one for you.My list of cons will seem longer than my list of pros but it's because ultimately the game is FUN, and I recommend it based on that. It's a fun, well-made, glitch-free (in my experience) way to spend time and I think people should try it. I got this without ever having played any mecha-fighting games, Steam was like "hey you might not like this, none of your library tells us you would", and I took a chance and I'm super glad I did - hence this being my current hyperfixation.Pros:- Robot fighting is dope as ♥♥♥♥, if you're not a little weenie- Borderlands-levels of loot drop, if that's something that satisfies you- Story is engaging enough, if that's what you're playing for- Deep upgrade/customization systems, if you're not worried about being overwhelmed- Lots of items in the overworld to collect, if you like seeing that little "0/16" in the menu turn into "16/16"- Fully voice acted, although I can't understand a single word of it so I don't really know if it's acted well. I assume it is.- There's just so much ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ content, dude. If you're one of those people who figures "oh, a $60 game should last me at least 60 hours", then this one is gonna beat the hell out of you. I remember reading a review of this that mentioned "oh yeah you could get a couple hundred hours out of this", and it makes sense now. I'm 43 hours deep and can tell I haven't even made a dent in what the game has to offer.Cons: - That amount of content is honestly excessive and could probably do with the fat being trimmed a bit. For those of you who have played Xenoblade, you're familiar with items showing up in the overworld as vague sparkles with no indication of what the item is until you pick it up. It must be a JRPG trope because they do that here too, and it's for sure in excess. Most of those sparkles, which change depending on the time of day and location, are items that side stories are locked behind. These side stories flesh out some of the side characters but also sorta spoil  - The game is SUPER cutscene heavy. The main gameplay loop is fun as ♥♥♥♥, so every cutscene I need to skip just gets annoying. You can get the gist of what's going on based on what you aren't allowed to skip anyway, so you might as well save yourself the time. Honestly there's probably tens of hours to be wasted actually sitting through all of the cutscenes I've gotten so far, and again, I'm nowhere near through the game. The story is fine, it just personally drives me up the wall when you sit through 5 minutes of talking, then get 30 seconds to actually play before another cutscene starts.- Similar to the cutscene issue, this game does that thing where sometimes, because of the plot, enemies you could one-shot are immune to damage until an arbitrary conversation happens between your characters that "reveals what they're weak to", which is inevitably the same thing you were just doing that, for no real reason, wasn't working. This also happens to line up with the huge power curves your characters go through, so if it's supposed to make the enemies seem menacing it doesn't work because I know I could dust them if the game wasn't quite literally holding me back from doing so. I really want to get every achievement for this game but with how deep the customization is and how much content there is, I'm worried about getting a bit burnt out. I definitely recommend this game to anyone who's simply looking for a fun game, especially if you're getting it during the Summer Sale like I did, but just be ready for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ wild amount of content. Props to the devs for pumping this game full of things to do, and without it being a broken package like so many games are when they're released. It's a good game, it's really fun, just give it a go.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a JRPG that can be a bit slow in the beginning, which made me stop playing for a while, but I eventually came back and finished it.The combat system is quite casual, allowing you to complete the game by repeatedly pressing the same button. The story, crafted by Level 5, is simple and straightforward, with some predictable elements. It feels like you're watching a mecha anime series, which adds to its charm. The pacing, conflicts, and character backgrounds made me love the main character.One of the best parts of the game is the OST, which kept me wanting to continue playing. The music adds a lot to the overall experience and helps maintain interest during the slower sections.I particularly enjoyed the boss fights, with all the dodging, guarding, and big moves. It was a fun and relaxing experience, but I should mention that I didn't touch any of the farm missions or side missions.Overall, despite its slow start and simple mechanics, this game offers an engaging story, memorable characters, and a fantastic soundtrack that together create a rewarding and enjoyable experience.

_childDocuments_.review: In short a fun game mecha builder that overstays its welcome somewhere around chapter 20, Gundam Breaker with Super Robots, I absolutely recommend this game to fans of specifically "super robots", anyone who enjoys customisation in their games and those who enjoy collection based grinding, just maybe gloss over the story.I really enjoyed this game for what it was, and in the early game collecting parts powering them up and creating something cool was a really enjoyable, even the story was while kinda silly and nonsensical at times was enjoyable that was until chapter 20.For some reason upon chapter 20 the story just takes a hard turn into ridiculous, the grinding stops being fun and it feels like it drags by chapter 23 you're wishing you stopped playing around chapter 19 with every other story mission stopping before you defeat the enemy denying you any satisfaction, you end up defeating the enemies so fast that they cant complete there exposition and enter a god mode where you cannot harm them which again takes away any tension when you've beat the enemy to within an inch of their lives and the crew you're with starts talking about how impossible the fight is, this was always apparent but around the last chapters becomes much more noticeable.Some side gripes, the translation suffers from the usual translator adding personality to lines that dont need it "Ossan" into "Boomer" rather than "Old Man" or something and I thought I had a stroke when "HUH!?!" was translated to "Holy Bologna", honestly I may have as at that point I was skipping story. As for the good; Mecha building, you can build a mech with the strongest parts and then "Holocast" another mech on top meaning you do not need to worry about powering up specific parts and can just snazz up your machine over whatever your strongest parts may be, the materials to do so are very generously handed to you so you can really have a blast with it, with the addition of the motherboard and mods customisation is key to enjoying the game and if you arent spending time agonising over which mods to use or what colour you want your holocast to be you're playing the game wrong.Super moves and animations, the animations are fantastic aided by the cool as hell weapons that come in so many variations adding more to the customisation, I ended up using rule of cool to pick out most of my super attacks but if you really wanted to "lore" up your mech giving them specific attacks and bonuses you absolutely can and I know a few people (myself included) who the idea of making custom mechs with head cannon lore and attacks to reflect that just tickles a special part of their brain. Remember just because every mech in your hangar IS a Musashi-R doesn't mean it has to look like it.8/10 Solely for the game play and customisation, Solid

_childDocuments_.review: This came out of the blue; I knew the Switch version in Japanese, but never thought that it would be ported to Steam in English.The game is really enjoyable if you like mecha games and visual novels based on anime usual tropes. As bonus there are a lot of classic Go Nagai robots in the game to collect, which is awesome as there are probably 3-4 games in total that have those in it in a playable form, beside the Super robot wars games (which are turn based, not action games).The game premise is simple: you have an anime, you make a game out of it following the story, and transpose the action in a mix of 2.5D graphics where you interact with people in this fictional city, and alternate that with actual missions where you pilot your mecha. The story itself is OK; I played just the first few hours and it is all I would expect from an anime based game, that is not a gundam game.Walking around and talking to the other people in the city is not like Persona games, but it does its job. The style and graphics are quite nice and way better than the Switch version. There are stores to visit, places to meet other characters and so on, so it has its reason to exist. Then you hop in your mech and you do missions; which is basically what you would expect from a simple action game in the genre. If you ever played games like Gundam Breaker, you will feel at home: it is like a simplified version of Armored core where you get parts for your mech, swap them, increase stats and do missions to get better parts. All with that classic anime flavor with super moves, rocket punch and mega laser beams as special weapons.You have 3 melee and 3 ranged weapons to use; and each weapon may have an element (fire, ice, lightning and so on), which affect enemies differently; so while the hack and slash part is pretty simple (dodge, boost, attack as classic gundam games); you need to have some wits in setting up the correct loadout before a mission, and swap weapons accordingly to do decent damage.From what I can see, you can replay side missions and main missions as much as you want, so there is quite a lot of content here, even after finishing the main story. You can also play online with other players in co-op (up to 3 players); or have PVP in the arena, if that is your thing. It is not the type of game you will play for ages, but if you like anime and super robots, and watched the original anime, it will entertain you for a whileThe good thing is that there are not that many microtransactions; everything is basically in the game except some extra mecha parts; but if you buy the game now you get a pre-order bonus which is a major upgrade to the starter mecha; so if you want to make the game super easy, you can use these parts... Or not; as you can swap any parts to make your own mecha (torso, both arms and both legs). Customization is absurd, as you can add augments to each part, and slot extra bonuses in these augments, which are per part and can be swapped at any mission loadout screen.Then you have your "motherboard" where you add chips you get by playing the game; which also augment your mecha... Basically 90% of the progression is in the parts you get, as your level does not affect the damage output or any other factor at all, except the best reward you get in a mission, as you cannot get a part for your mech that is above your current level.Overall I give this game a 8 out of 10 mainly because these are games you would see 10-15 years on Ps3, and they don't make games like this anymore... If you remove the nostalgia and the anime part (which by the way is present in the game as animated scenes; very well done), the game is above average at 6 out of 10; and you may want to wait for a sale maybe.

Its like LEVEL5 didn't want to put loading screens into the game because they'd be ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ everywhere because this game is like badly optimized PS2 game with loading screens EVERYWHERE. $100 of just cosmetic DLC, a log-in reward system, an in game battle pass (wtf?). The game showers you in items, but its just a boring, repetitive grind game. This could of been a really awesome game, but its made it like mobile shovel ware. I don't even think I'm mad. _childDocuments_.review: TLDR, Japanified Armored Core 6. High recommend, even for the $50 price tag, the deluxe is mostly cosmetic.Before I go into this review, I've gotta get this straight:I came into this game only having seen gameplay of the Megaton battles and the mech designs. So, as a Gundam fan, I was already hooked.I did not realize that I would suddenly be taped to my chair and persuaded into a cheesy sitcom anime storyline complete with a moral dilemma that actually felt really interesting.Above all else, if you're similar with games Level5 has done before, like LBX on 3DS, you'll know story is something they do well. With a happy artstyle, it's quite refreshing of a mech game in comparison to everything else out there. Edit: There is a LOT of story here. Believe me, I had expected the story to end or possibly leave at a cliffhanger earlier on, but the plot is well articulated and expansive. An easy way to get lost in it, especially with the characters and motives which you can really feel for.Upgrade paths are bloody everywhere. While weapon variation could use a bit of work, each one has a bit of a pro-con route, and by upgrading the motherboard route you can unlock new moves, DMC5 style. From a stronger charge punch to literal taser hand, its a great game on the battle-side as well.I'll update this once I get into the PVP and Co-Op aspect.Edit: Servers are quite stable for the game, and the Co-Op is a wonderful way to grind up higher level parts. That being said, there is still the "extremely op guy carrying" and vice versa, so if you want good runs, try partying with friends.PVP is a beast to tackle. See, parts you get in main game cant be used in PVP (AKA Colosseum), instead you must get Colosseum parts to play. A bit strange, but balanced.My applause to Level5 once again.

_childDocuments_.review: It's an enjoyable game, however, it really lacks substance plot-wise and it has several major flaws.While I am not familiar with the anime, the plot is quite dry, heavily drawn from Evangelion (even in details such as the music-based synchronising scene, e.g.) but lacking the depth and the detail the latter has. Scenes just cut to the chase with no real character development, if any. Things start picking up around Chapter 10 (12hrs in the game) but it's still no golden globe worthy script, which is comical considering the amount of cutscenes the game throws at you (and sometimes annoyingly mid-fight). It could be that it's definitely based on a Shonen manga, but geez when things like Evangelion / Yu-Gi-Oh exist it's inexcusable. It's annoying that so many plot elements could have been fleshed out so much, yet they are simply abandoned.Gameplay is fast and nice, but could be better. Maps are unsurprising, very similar to each other and usually it's a big corridor with barriers where you have to kill enemies in order to progress. To switch things up, it's a big circle where you need to defeat all enemies. That's it. I am hoping (and I've heard apparently) that difficulty will spike up soon. After 12 hours of playing, no real challenge has been thrown at me yet: bosses tend to be squishy even with builds you can only access early game, and when they are not, they're relatively static HP sponges. No mechanic outside hit, dodge, hit, dodge, maybe burst, maybe special attacks. Builds seem to offer a lot of variety, but in the end you either go ranged, melee or special attack focused (then back to the other two till the gauge recharges). Every mission rewards you with a generous loot, though it's hardly useful in the end; sorting through it is a pain as the game organises it in quite clunky ways. Motherboard / Circuit development / mods seem quite broad as well on paper, but are subsequently annihilated by a "recommended" setting given the sheer variety of loot you can get from every "hunt". As of now, without recommended settings you are basically left building your mech alongside mods with sometimes no immediate indication on what does what, and it would require you a considerable amount of time for a negligible improvement in damage / QoL. Builds can be varied, but it's mostly damage (ranged, elemental, melee), "debuff", special moves, etc.In fact, user experience is definitely not the best, considering that something simple such as colouring your mech requires you to singularly edit every part in ANOTHER section than the CUSTOMIZATION one where the pieces are assembled. PvP is dead or mostly matchmaking is not reliable at all (and you can get penalised for disconnections, which 99% of the time are entirely the game's fault). I assume the poor marketing effort Level 5 has made has also contributed in this situation. PvE is okay, though there's no tangible scaling that makes challenges harder, so it tends not to be as rewarding as it should be.The game is charming nonetheless, as any Level 5 title is. I think they were dreaming of a game like this since the days of Yellow Drops Moon Factory in Dark Cloud, but it is definitely lacking in so many areas and it shows. There is currently no reason to buy this at full price (at the time of writing £40 on steam & PSN, to £57.99!!!! for negligible DX content) unless you are a die-hard fan of Megaton Musashi. At a similar price, games like CRYMACHINA perform better while having the same flaws but a stronger art direction overall.This could have safely been a late PS2 game, and that is both the charm and the burden of this game. If you want to grab it, do it now or never at £20.

_childDocuments_.review: The story and even the setting are hot garbge. But the gameplay is probably some of the most solid work Level-5 has ever done. _childDocuments_.review: I'm not able to recommend this game, because it obviously wants to be an anime and falls apart about in the last 5-10 hours. But if you're still reading, that means you are looking into *why* I'm not recommending it, and perhaps wondering why I have 50  hours in it anyways. The closest analogy for the main gameplay I have is "Phantasy Star Online (take your pick of episodes) mixed with action RPG loot mechanics". You walk down a corridor, enemies spawn, you beat them up, you pick up the items they drop, repeat. Sometimes instead of little enemies you get big enemies. Really, there's nothing here that stands out as great gameplay, but it is fast and generally fun (if mindless) with mech customisation as your upgrade system and anime moves as your special moves.But there's a problem - this game is adapting a bunch of anime into a story, and also trying to make that fun. The story fails at this task. It's basically a visual novel. But you're stuck living the anime plot. You will never play the visual novel segments and feel satisfied that you know what's going on. So there will be things that just seem to *happen*, and you're forced to wonder if this poor pacing is part of the anime too, or if it's because of the adaptation. The stakes and the overall plot come unravelled as more and more things just *happen* without enough, or any, explanation. The last 5-10 hours are a turning point where I can only describe the quality as "we ran out of money and our contract hinges on adapting the full anime". Major threats are introduced, hyped up, then immediately ignored in favour of another threat. You might get to fight a threat once, but it's probably going to be resolved off screen.Another flaw is its insistence on sticking to the anime's shonen formula. Characters refuse to let you do any fight in one go, instead breaking up missions with the usual mecha/anime "we need to unlock a new move/powerup/etc to defeat this enemy" stuff.  Once or twice, this could be okay. But this is very consistent throughout, unfortunately. I often wished I could just finish a boss fight without getting 2 or 3 cutscenes. For those of you familiar with PSO, you might also be wondering if the gameplay has inherited any flaws from that game series. Unfortunately, yes - there are multiple difficult levels, and "completion" revolves around completing *all* of them. The higher up you go, the tougher enemies are, obviously, but at a certain point you end up with enemies just one-shot-killing you. Their damage scales up much more quickly than your survivability. You can increase the difficulty of a mission by one level, and go from "way too easy" to "almost impossible". Finally, the game is chock full of live-service game mechanics, like log in rewards, a premium pass, tons of achievements... It's also a full priced game. I know this is increasingly common these days due to the need for continuous revenue, but it breaks up the gameplay flow. Unfortunately dealing with the influx of junk items, because this has action RPG loot mechanics, also breaks up the flow (perhaps worse since you need to compare items and stats that are not always intuitive, and some descriptions are so long you have to wait for them to scroll across the screen), so the live service mechanics are somewhat less intrusive than it feels at first glance. Phantasy Star Online 2 exists now, is free to play (as far as I can recall), and it will give you many of the same vibes as the core gameplay of this game. Just, you won't be using a giant mech, referencing a bunch of mecha anime and/or mecha anime tropes, or piloting licensed mechs.

_childDocuments_.review: (I recieved this game as a gift from my girlfriend) There were reviews the day this game went live going "Hino doesn't miss" and those irk me greatly as a former Yokai Watch fan. The thing one has to understand with level5 games is that Akhiro Hino is a total hack and has built a career on launching phenomenal new IPs with his company he founded before somehow finding a way to yank failure out of the jaws of success. Megaton Musashi Wired is the third game in the series, following Megaton Musashi and Megaton Musashi X, both of which are part of this game (the reason you unlock new game + when you do is that you just beat Megaton Musashi), and you can really feel the standard level5 mismanagement once you reach the actually new Megaton Musashi Wired content. The game just completely giving up and putting in an entire episode of the anime with no pause button or anything in lieu of gameplay is absolutely egregious, the new Light Frame robots that Wired introduces are functionally a complete afterthought with no meaningful distinction on why you would play them, especially with the sheer loss in build customization due to lack of cross compatibility between rogue types, the final act continually introduces new threats before giving you extremely underwhelming fights where the only way to see what could have been is to go play dreadnought mode instead because the story mode just doesnt trust you with doing anything resembling a fight with gameplay mechanics, and ultimately finishes off with a real half-assed ending that resolves nothing and just tells you to go come back if they ever do an update for this game.The gameplay is engaging and fun all the way through, I quite enjoy the actual in depth mechanical fights you get in dreadnought mode, but the story surrounding it and the lack of effort put into the games actual new content compared to past releases really is just par for the course level5. I had to watch Yokai Watch rot under this same kind of half-assed release strategy and mismanagement back in the 2010s, so I'm at least dulled to it, but I really think just enjoying a game's combat engine is not quite enough for me to say anyone should buy it right now. Like, I'm personally enjoying it and am going to keep playing until I stop, being free of the bad story and having all the missions at my disposal to just play in a more monster hunter style definitely helps this game, but don't buy this at full price lmaoAlso, don't even try to play the pvp, it takes so long to queue for a game you might as well just go do anything else with your life.In closing: This is the third game in a Level5 series and tbh Akihiro Hino is about on pace for mismanaging an IP and reducing it to trash with that fact out in the open.

_childDocuments_.review: This was one of the best story driven game I've experienced in recent years.I thought the game would have a meh story with some fun super robot combat that I could experience for a few hours. 99 Hours in and I was floored by the constant changes, twists, and new mechanics delivered through the story.The story, though cliche anime in execution, was one of the best stories I've experienced in mecha games. _childDocuments_.review: Unexpectedly awesome.A shame it hasn't gotten more love. Though Space Opera Super Robot is rather niche I guess.From what I deduce the game seems based on 2 seasons of an anime I had never heard off.It's both it's strength and it's weakness.More on that later.Basically you run around locations with your character (anime chars) in a functional anime-inspired graphical style that works well though is hardly super impressive.It grew on me though and it allows the anime clips and the gameplay slide into each other nicely.The Japanese voice acting is good.Essentially there are 25 chapters.A first story arc based on the first anime season.A second story arc based on the second anime season.And then 'wired' being 2 chapters rushing to tie a lot of plotpoints up.Effectively but not that satisfyingly.Technically there is a sort of to be continued. But it's not that too big a plotpoint is left hanging.There is a lot of busy work when running around as a pilot.Talking to people, silly anime trope sidequests (goofy or slice of life frequently)And a ton of collectibles.Combat has a wide variety of missions you slowly unlock:- Story.- Resource harvesting- Huge 'world boss' encounter missionsEtc.All missions have many levels of difficulty.You customise your robot (your Rogue as the game calls it) with loot you find in the world (powerlevels, traits, elements, quality levels etc) in typical Diablo fashion. Your pilots also develop skills.And there is technology and abilities to unlock as well.I recommend doing some chapters of the story, grinding in between.But don't go overboard as i did early on as you can become quite overpowered quickly.The strength that the anime brings is: frequent use of gorgeous clips of the anime, fleshed out characters and designs.The weakness is that it also limits your choices and the visuals of the robots somewhat. But there is still a lot of cosmetics to unlock and a ton of playstyles to unlock. The anime basis (it seems to follow the storyline well) also means some anime goofyness can be a bit over the top. It also means some characters are underdevelopped. The caste is huge in this epic space opera - post apocalyptic Super Robot setting but for the most part characters have satisfying arcs and plot elements across the board.The 'wired' part of the plotline is as mentioned rather rushed introducing the 'arc' of a pivotal character that's a baby for most of the storyline and speedrunning it to a conclusion.Party comp (up to 3 Rogues and their pilot(s) ) leads to variety.Although I don't plan to do so at this time you can grind like crazy in an endgame situation.There is so much to unlock. And that's on top of a satisfyingly lengthy storyline.The battlepass edition is worth it if you plan to go all in on end game.If i ever revisit it, i'll use New Game + for this one.Definitely a memorable experience with memorable mecha combat and characters I ended up liking more than I though i would.A massive grump like me is hard to get to care for romance and the likes but I did end up invested in the main couple. And I greatly enjoyed the boomer captain's mentor relationship with all these uppity kids!Super Robot designs were unique but cool.Wouldn't mind seeing them expand this one with an addon.

_childDocuments_.review: I have yet to finish the game (I'm on Chapter 8 at the time of writing) but I wanted to give this game a review since it was seemingly stealth dropped on Steam with little to no advertising, and I want to help it find more people.This game is the dictionary definition of "better than the sum of its parts".The action gameplay is simple and straightforward while still being satisfying. It's similar to Gundam Breaker, Warriors games,  with flashy special moves and cut-in images to really sell the impact. On top of that, you have a variety of systems to advance and upgrade each of the mecha if you really want to invest and min-max, make big number go up, but the game also has auto-equip features to help streamline the process. I honestly haven't felt the need to sit down and sort through my inventory to get the most out of my mecha, but I'm still in what feels like the early game.The game is paced pretty well, giving you just enough story in between missions to keep you interested, and not too much that it gets in the way. The story, in of itself, is decent and involving, if a bit predictable. The cast has their archetypes (Hot-headed shounen protag, tough-guy rival/sidekick, brainy genius with a dry sense of humor, etc) but they all have just enough depth to prevent them from being boring, and their interactions with one another is where they really shine.The presentation of the game has a ton of budget behind it, which really stands out. There's several fully-animated cutscenes in the first hour alone, and more in later chapters. Every line of dialogue is voiced, even by incidental NPC characters. Even during the in-engine cutscenes, there's cut-in images with little animations that look incredibly high-quality, and I haven't seen them re-used as of yet. And sure, there are textures on the 3D environments that can look a little drab, but they never bothered me or got in the way of the experience. If anything, it feels like an enhanced port of a cult classic JRPG from the PS3 era, but, like, in a good way.I definitely recommend checking this game out if you like mecha at all, and/or want a smooth RPG to play on downtime. It's basically a playable mecha anime packed with fun details.Additionally, I switch between playing this on PC and Steam Deck and it works wonderfully on both.

_childDocuments_.review: Don't let the ugly character sprites turn you off, the story is actually really good and worth paying attention to (which is good, considering it actually takes up a lot of the play-time before you finish it).As far as gameplay, there's a lot to do here if you enjoy tinkering and optimizing, and a lot of hours of content to do. A bit wary of there being a battle pass in a paid game, but it doesn't seem particularly intrusive.As far as the mechs go, they definitely lean more into the super robot side of the genre, with nonsensical but cool-looking designs and bright colors. It's reminiscent of Custom Robo, Gurren Lagann, some of Gundam, hell, they even literally have Getter Robo and Mazinger Z parts. If you like those, you'll like these.Music is pretty good, but holy hell, what were they thinking with the opening song? There are several vocal tracks that play throughout the story (that I can only assume were *made for* the game because they keep saying "Musashi") that are waaay better than whatever the opening is.Overall been very good so far, will update the review if my opinion changes.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR - You will spend more time on loading screens than gameplay.Supposedly this gets better later on, but the campaign of the game drags out like the longest tutorial of all time. The VN story interrupts you every single time you get a flow going, including MID FIGHT. There is a specific sequence of missions that should have just been one continuous mission, but instead is broken up into tiny chunks where you have to go through menus to start a mission again. Every time I've gotten to sit down and actually play the GAME part of this nauseatingly bad VN-with-a-game-attached the missions have been trivial and over within a few minutes. If it's going to be this easy, at least give me some dynasty-warriors level of enemy spam for me to mow through, but it's usually a few generic mooks at a time and double digits at best.Onto the actual gameplay - Someone recommended this on the SD gundam battle alliance discussion page. That game is not overly complex, but it has this one beat in terms of mechanical depth. This game has some really cool tools in your arsenal, but you obliterate most things relatively quickly. And the element system is a completely artificial time-waster that forces you into menus. Effectively, elements are just one of five colors over each enemy and weapon - that is all the difference they make. Each mission has a set element or two you should bring, and if you do, every enemy in that mission will get obliterated in a couple hits - if you don't, it will take five times as many hits. Have fun going through a bunch of loading screens to change all your gear before every mission, IDIOT. You want to use X weapon type? You don't have Y color. A bazooka will do less damage per shot than a machine gun, because it has the wrong arbitrary icon color, IDIOT. ♥♥♥♥ you for playing. This is where things get really obnoxious. That "mission chain" that is just an excuse to break up one normal length mission into multiple VN segments with a tiny bit of gameplay in between? Each segment has a different element. Play for two minutes. Kill ten enemies. 5 minutes of VN, 3 minutes of menus and re-equipping. Repeat, but a bossfight (that was cleared in 47 seconds). The vast majority of my time "playing" this "game" has had nothing to do with the actual gameplay. I get that this game has an anime tie-in. That does not excuse anime episode pacing, where you get 2 minutes of action for 20 minutes of talking. The story isn't even the worst part. It's bad, but loops around to "so bad it's funny". The worst part is the structure. In the first hour you will have to move from area to area for a few lines of dialogue each time, when it all could have been wrapped into a single continuous scene. You spend more time on loading screens than the dialogue, and said dialogue can't even be progressed through at a reasonable speed. The game has a loading time for text - you can't mash through as fast as you want, there's a significant delay for each new line. You do get a "skip the whole scene" button, but even if you did that, since every scene is broken up into ten different areas, you have to click through a bunch of ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and skip repeatedly.I just want to play the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game. My combined time actually in gameplay is less than 10% of the time I've had the game running.

Most of my time has been spent in cutscenes and walking around town. I put a good amount of time into Gundam Breaker 3 and SD Gundam Alliance and interested to see how this stacks up to them.Edit: Currently almost at 40 hours and I can say this is better than any Gundam Breaker game or the SD games. _childDocuments_.review: If DAEMON X MACHINA or Armored Core lets you live out the fantasy of becoming a "real robot" ace pilot, then Megaton Musashi W lets you live out the fantasy of becoming a "super robot" pilot mowing through enemies with super moves. It's great mecha action fun.Core gameplay feels somewhat Musou-like where you get to battle waves of enemies, then a large one usually at the end of each stage. The controls feel great, and combat is fast-paced. It feels pretty amazing, honestly. While the flow of each stage can get a bit repetitive, the different weapons to choose from mix up combat enough that it doesn't get stale. Really helps that the effects and animations look really cool. There's lots of customization options too.It's the non-combat parts that kind of drag parts of the experience down for me, since the story is a bit of hit-or-miss. It's ambitious for sure, with a pretty large cast of pilots and characters, and I get that they're trying to deliver the experience of a robot anime show. (The story mostly follows the plot of the Megaton Musashi anime, too.)But sometimes the amount of menus and story content I have to go through between the missions feels a bit too much when all I want to do is go to the next mission and bash some mooks, because that's where the game really shines. I miss DAEMON x MACHINA's more streamlined approach where you'll spend more time in the actual missions and most of the story is told through them.There's also online 3v3 PVP, and I wasn't expecting it to be this much fun. I get why they feature it in the PR now. It's really fun, and I can see the potential for it to be something more. Perhaps an "Gundam EXVS at home"? It's just that unfortunately queueing for matches take longer than I would like (up to a minute or more) and that's for the designated time slots where you get increased rewards. Outside of that, I've had 30 minutes of waiting trying to find a casual, unranked match to no success. Which is a shame, so I do really hope that this game gets more players. If you like the thrill of mecha combat and are looking for some fast-paced action, or want to play through a season's worth of a mecha anime's story, then I recommend this. Despite some hiccups and design decisions I'm not too fond of, it's still quite well-made and I appreciate that they're making a mech game like this in 2024.

_childDocuments_.review: Yes *IF* on sale for 50% off or more (like now). Otherwise, absolutely not.It's alright. If you're going to play this, it's probably just so you can mash robot parts together and distract yourself for a few hours at a time. Nothing wrong with that, but $50 is a steep asking price since every mission is exactly the same, occasionally with some different set dressing. First, things I like, cause it's short and only justified by the 50% off sale:-- The cat didn't die (well, not yet anyway)-- GRENDIZER BABY (and others)-- If you like grinding for materials and unlocking a ♥♥♥♥-ton of upgrades, you're gonna be thoroughly distracted for a while-- Some sweet super movesAnd now the dislikes:-- Japanese developers remain unable to resist the urge to force anything more than ten feet from you from animating at 30 FPS. For the love of God, knock it off. The arenas are so tiny this is clearly just the result of laziness in porting the game from consoles... it's not that demanding on any halfway-decent system.-- Took the "let's just remove all honorifics" route for localizing. I know this is asking a lot of your average localizer, but come on guys. Mecha is one of the most Japanese things to ever exist. Please hire people that give a ♥♥♥♥ about preserving that.-- Daily login bonuses, a battle pass, currency-gated missions, $100+ of almost entirely cosmetic DLC. No, it doesn't matter that the DLC is cosmetic. I remember a time when you could earn those things by accomplishing something in game and didn't have to fork over even MORE money than the game is actually worth. -- The story... is there. It just exists for a thin excuse to give you giant robot fights. Mind you, I say this as someone who happily consumes seasonal isekai anime slop all year round and asks for more, so it's INCREDIBLY bland in my eyes. Also have a VERY hard time sympathizing with the "We should just be able to coexist!!!!" princess subplot when the aliens quite literally killed 99.9% of humanity.-- The 2D animation sucks-- Base Musashi head looks stupid (looks like it has a goofy little mouth)Honestly, it's just mindless robot smashing and grinding for moar stats. If you don't like mecha, you might not get anything out of this. And if you DO like mecha... you've probably played much better. Needless to say, at anywhere near full price, this would be a STRONG not recommend.

_childDocuments_.review: Have you ever wanted to play a video game that is 90% cutscenes?Did you want your missions that take 5 minutes tops to complete to be broken up MID-MISSION by multiple lengthy cutscenes?Have you ever had the desire to play a game with MASSES of content locked behind nearly 30 chapters of storyline which by the time you're nearly done, you lose all will to continue playing?Then look no further.You, too, can enjoy a mindless hack and slash action game, where the real meat of the game is simply at the end of a hallway, guarded by cutscene after cutscene after cutscene.You will walk across town, cutscene.You will be directed to walk further, cutscene, cutscene.You finally start using fast travel, anime cutscene, regular cutscene.To finally get a mission, which is then stopped 30 seconds in by a cutscene.And the story isn't particularly good either, yet you are burdened by it. You're shackled together, and even though you may skip the cutscenes, it will still take up MORE time than you would actually in a mission playing the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ game.You may be wanting to buy this simply for mech customisation. I did too.Unfortunately, it boils down to "make number go big" and equip your 3 favourite melee and 3 favourite gun types out of 4-5 types each, and go about your mission. The bodies don't make any particular difference so you go for looks. The amount of gear that gets thrown at you doesn't matter either, since all you do is equip a legendary, and upgrade that throughout the game to keep up with your rank, and trash the rest.Unlocking things on the skill tree is a grind. The motherboard customisation to fine tune your mech could be cool if it mattered outside of needing something hyper specific for a side mission (which you won't see before wanting to gouge your eyes out out of boredom)The combat itself is ok. Beating up enemies and managing your meter to pull off a set of cool moves would feel better if you had more opportunities to use them at key moments. It feels like this should have been a Dynasty Warriors type of game, rather than what it is.This game is probably at its best when you finally face smaller enemy mech bosses rather than the fodder in between fights, and infinitely better than the giant towering bosses where you simply attack their feet.If you're in this for the story, just watch the anime or the slew of cutscenes on youtube.If you're interested in the gameplay, there are probably better games for it. Just be warned that you will have to wade through a lot of ♥♥♥♥ to get to something reasonably fun.As it is, I wouldn't recommend it. Not for full price

_childDocuments_.review: I'm going to give this a very cautious thumbs up, there's a lot of issues with this game. Some can be fixed. It's a good game, story's a bit typical for an anime. No issue there if you know what you're getting. Main character is what you expect. Scrawny, short, spikey hair, able to take down several school yard bullies then a group of cyborgs (which so far only appear once) with nothing but a lead pipe and his bare fists. Super powers? No he's just that tough apparently. The story doesn't have to make sense. I'm fine with that. It's fun, dumb fun. My issue is with the tutorials and pacing. I'm five hours in, every moment i take a step, open a menu, customize my mech, talk to someone, sneeze, blink, there's an immediately deluge of pop ups telling me every mechanic, function, and hint regarding the game. This has to be one of the worst examples of help I've ever seen in a game at least in recent memory. Do you enjoy pressing a button and going through 20 popup boxes explaining how to start a mission? That's what this game does. Non-Stop. Want to do know mods do to a mech? Don't worry the game will tell you. Sure, you could probably figure it out yourself. But no it's going to tell you, whether you like it or not. Most games will have a central guide, or database, something you can access if you're stuck on a mechanic or need a bit of help or instruction. This game doesn't trust the player with that, it has the compulsive NEED to throw everything and the kitchen sink at you. If it's not that then it's cutscenes, this game LOVES to stop everything and send an explosive amount of exposition at you. Worst thing is it's at the worst possible times. Why are you sending me cutscenes IN A MISSION!? Not just at the start, when I'm actively FIGHTING enemies!?  When I'm moving around the map!? Why do you have the same stage layout for every single mission!? It's always go fight a few generic enemies, smack into invisible walls, encounter boss. Have the same ten second cutscene for the boss's appearance which nine times out of ten is the same enemy you've already fought but bigger with a different color scheme. Why!? Why are you stopping me from enjoying the game? I can't turn it off. I can skip it, but you have to hold a button down for five seconds to do so. So you're watching part of a cutscene even if you don't want to. One particular boss gets interrupted with a five minute cutscene half way through the fight, You don't do this, you don't interrupt the gameplay like that. It's infuriating. I'm actually cautious over it, knowing I can trigger a cutscene at any moment. Expect loading times per cutscene too, you're going to see that progress bar on the screen a lot. I lost investment in the storyline halfway because of this.I'm venting, I'm venting in frustration. Between this game's constant need to stop you there's fun here. A LOT of fun. Shooting enemies down using various weapons, customizing a giant war machine against an alien menace, using some of the most over the top ridiculous super abilities I've ever seen. Like a mech able to project a giant flaming fist across the battlefield at mach ten kind of ridiculous. It's insanity and it's a blast in multiplayer. Hell the story is engaging in a lot of areas too. I don't understand how a game can have all this, then leash the player against the wall with tutorials. Then sideswipe them with exposition dumps.

_childDocuments_.review: The monetization of this game is dreadful. It's monetized like a free-to-play game with all of these day-1 DLCs and has a battle pass with premium and regular tiers. Utterly dreadful, and it's a shame Level 5 would do this to their game and its players.Now that we've gotten the bad part of this game out of the way, ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ there is so much game in this game. You're never aching for something to do, there's always something to do or something to find. You're also not pressured to engage with the season pass, as rewards for completing a mission are extremely plentiful, with an almost looter-shooter level of dopamine drop when you see your winnings at the end of a mission. No matter what you do, you're progressing in *some* way, but you're encouraged to challenge yourself to grind for better gear.And that grind is not a boring one, as the Megaton-class robots are both quick and powerful despite their Godzilla-esque stature. You never feel like you're moving too slow or that it will take forever to get from one end of the level to another, all the while using absurdly huge weapons to mow down enemies. One problem that's plagued many mech-customization games--including Level 5's previous robot title, LBX--is that many of them have all these different parts in wildly different styles and colors, but without any kind of transmog system. Megaton Musashi's transmog system, while less than ideal and taking some getting used to, is a big step in the right direction. Now if only you could transmog weapons.With such a cartoonish mech design you wouldn't expect this game to have a good story, but you'd be wrong. The visual novel-styled story is one that really makes the world feel alive because we have so many different characters that all have their own motivations and desires. It's a difficult balance to have so many important characters while not feeling scatterbrained in your narrative, and I think Megaton Musashi executes this with a skill and grace that I haven't seen before.Overall, this game is so good and there is so much of it that it's started to ruin my life a little. Why do chores when I could just play this game a little more? Why go to work, or date my girlfriend when I could be playing more of this game? The games that make you ask yourself these questions are the BEST games, not because they've manipulated you with season passes or predatory microtransactions or because of the sunk cost fallacy, but because the game is just that fun. I give this game a Megaton out of 10

_childDocuments_.review: Oooops Forgot to mention that this game is infact not for children. Highly recommend.  Its a pretty good robot killing alien robot and sometimes other things game with a great story.  Without farming for things the story runs around 18-20 hours and then there is post game content for getting more cool mechs.  There are some things I found issue with.  I utterly hate the UI design for some of the screens, they really like cutting to cutscene during several bossfights, they also like going "Heres a new thing, now Survive 30 seconds against a boss that can 2 shot you while the characters scream out that they are doing the thing" and then you can just straight up miss if the boss stuns you at the end of that sequence.  The story towards the end feels rushed because it very much so is, certain things get dropped and the semi final villian is so clearly evil i started skipping his dialogue because it was clear where things were going.  Thats mostly it for the bad.  Quite enjoyed the story and gameplay but holy crap getting swatted around sucks while the boss is invulnerable.  So the game drip feeds mechanics as you play through it, topping out with a number of different mission types, game modes and a variety of paths to upgrade your mech.  You find parts to customize your Rogue(mech), upgrade those parts, slam mods onto them,  build your mechs motherboard which is where you load specific stat increases and your special moves, your Kabuki(Big super) and other upgrades that I'm still trying to figure out how this whole thing works as I've ignored it most of the game.  Then you have the Motherboard lab where you spend all the crunchy alien bits you have collected to build new upgrades, special moves, Kabuki supers, Passive unlocks for weapon styles.  Ontop of this you have your Pilot who can have access to 5 skills, and each pilot has 10 of these and I have about 11 pilots right now and I'm sure there are more.  Most of this isn't that important in the story mode until literally the last 2-3 fights.  If you half way pay attention to these mechanics you will overpower the story at normal difficulty, by the end I was fighting most of the story missions on Megaton or Master.  The two highest difficulties I have access to(Not sure if theres another one).  Theres a variety of ways to fight and ways to push that way of fighting to scary levels.  Sadly Mechs are a bit scaled power level wise.  THe earliest mechs you have will never be as strong as later acquired mechs even with different rarity scaling.  So finding one you love and keeping it in fighting shape is hard but theres almost always an upgraded version down the line somewhere. Theres too many special moves for me to talk about, if you can't find something you like I don't know what to tell you.

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game. Megaton Musashi invokes the feelings of Super Robot anime shows with the threat of an alien invasion over a supposedly peaceful town. The first few chapters are tutorial heavy teaching you where to go and certain gameplay mechanics from fighting to exploration. The exploration segments are nicely down with 2D anime backgrounds with freedom of movement. Not just from left to right, but also up and down the background. That kind of exploration is rare and I appreciated the fidelity of the town.Battles open up where you go to a battlefield, move around, knock down some small mechs, and then take down a boss. Even in your starting gear, you are grossly overpowered that most of them would go down in one hit, which really emphasizes why your super robots, Rogues, are stronger than the regular giant robots your fellow NPCs use before they were overwhelmed and gunned down. The setting is bleak with most of humanity almost instinct on a cold war with the invaders, but as soon as I got into fighting, I more or less lost myself in the fun of fighting.Its a shame that not many people know about this, because advertisement was more or less nil, and it comes with a bit of a cadveat. It feels like a MOBA gacha game. You are given rewards out of the wazoo for daily log-ins, achievements, online, BATTLE PASSES, even password entries and version updates. Such rewards range from weapons and parts of tiered levels (1 star common to 5 star legendary), to items that unlock your skill tree to further customize your Rogues.Megaton Musashi W: Wired throws a LOT of information at you very fast. Tutorials with up to ten mini pages, and even forced actions where you apply changed parts, mods, or other features. It even forces you to set up balanced options. On the one hand, I appreciate this way to tell players there's a way to avoid meticulous planning so early on, but it feels too soon to bring up among other ideas to juggle at once.As a single player experience, it really shines and you feel awesome and heroic. But as a multiplayer kind of community, it's not very active. I was lucky to only get one match in and that was during a promotion of getting bonus rewards. I'm just glad MMWW doesn't ask you to pay extra for rewards and you can earn everything through gameplay, as the loop is addictive and really sets off dopamine getting rewards like in Monster Hunter-lite games.
