_childDocuments_.review: Build upon the very first cd/rom puzzlegame of its time (1993), this was truly a enjoyable and fun time spent both gaming and thinking back to  when my dad and i solved the original game for the very first time,  he would have loved this game soo much :), folks if you love puzzles then this is must to have, with its eerie setting this is certain to give you a good time :) Bravo to Vertigo Games for put a new life to this classic retro puzzle.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I took 6 hours to finish this game, but this were 6 very cool hours. Started with relatively easy puzzles and a light story. The puzzles and the story get stronger you longer you play. I had several goosebumps moments.The knuckle integration is o.k. but can be improved, but I get used to.Would I buy this game for the full 30€? Probably not, but when you got an discount on this game, this is a good investment.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Very good VR game, the mysterious atmosphere and soundtrack is well crafted, puzzles are well balanced and increasingly challenging, specially towards the end, the story and the quality of the graphics and design create an immersive kind of gothic experience. Controls and interaction with my HP Reverb G2 headset worked as supposed to. I only wished the game was a bit longer... I would recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It's a very decent VR puzzle game, I'd say great even. The doll puzzle and final puzzle are the only ones where I used game's hint system, cause one felt tedious, the other felt boring and unfun. Other than that - the game is definitely beautiful and has a fantastic atmosphere. Also the way they scanned real people to be displayed in-game a-la the original but in 3d, cause you obviously can move around, while isn't perfect, sure is incredibly impressive and works great to keep that haunting atmosphere without breaking it by displaying lifeless 3d dolls.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This is a fun, if at time frustrating, VR remake of 7th Guest. It nails the atmosphere of the mansion and its fun to explore the rooms. Cut scenes capture the feel of the 90's very well. Most of the puzzles are very well done with the exception of the final one which honestly I would recommend just saving 10 coins to skip. It does have some of the usual fiddly VR control issues, but overall it was a fun experience and I would recommend it during a Steam sale.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Pretty cool.    It has a creepy atmosphere.The puzzles are enjoyable for the most part. However there were a few I found more boring or tedious than fun or interesting, but I liked the vast majority. Nothing is too difficult either.    The visuals and immersion are great. I really like the 3D scans of real actors and their kind of campy performances. I found them very enjoyable to watch.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played The 7th Guest a LONG time ago. I think I still have the box and install CDs somewhere. Was very excited to see a VR version of the game. It's been so long that I don't remember the game, but apparently this is only partly the same as the original. This is a very simple puzzle mystery game, with a silly story, but it's fun enough.I'm very impressed with the live action character modeling. There are some minor glitches, but for the most part, they look very life like and it's cool to be able to walk around a live action model and see different angles. You can't typically do that with live action. In a game like Obduction, the live action scenes are just movies placed through a portal in a door so you can't see around them. The story is told in little snippets after solving puzzles. The acting isn't great, and the story is silly, but it's fun.The puzzles are simple enough and I rarely got stuck, and when I did, it wasn't for long. The lantern turning areas back in time and looking brand new was really cool. This effect is really neat when you slowly pan it over dead flowers.There really aren't any VR gimmicks in it. You can pick things up, open doors and drawers, that's about it. One thing that was a nice touch was that you could turn things or open cracked doors just by using your hand, without grabbing on. The game has some minor issues involving the hands. They don't always interact with items well. I also would occasionally get stuck in the middle of a room. Or a door would instantly close after being opened. Nothing game breaking, but frustrating at times.The game took me 6 hours to beat, so an average length VR game. I'm 99% in game without any backtracking or trying. 78 achievements. Not interested in getting 100% on either. Given the length of the game, I'd say it's not worth the full price, but on sale, if you like puzzle games, it's worth it.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, good story. The tasks were suitably difficult, and there was also the opportunity to get hints if necessary. It took a little over 7h to play through. I bought it with discount, and compared to that, it's definitely worth the price, possibly even at the standard price. There weren't many bugs, sometimes using your hands (e.g. opening doors) was a bit awkward, at least at first.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this using the Quest 3 and am impressed. The presentation is very good with nice atmosphere. They use full motion video combined with 3D animation that makes the sequences with people look almost lifelike. The puzzles are challenging enough so far and seem to be getting more so as I go on. Overall, if you like a puzzle game with high production values (similar to the The Room VR), then you'll like this. I would not call this scary as there haven't been any jump scares so far, it's just creepy and atmospheric.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't play the original, but I am thoroughly enjoying the 7th Guest VRThe visuals are stunning, and the attention to detail is remarkable especially when using the lamp, everything illuminated appears changed to reverse the decay and rot of age. But the standout feature for me is the inclusion of Full Motion Video actors, which add a unique charm.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Great VR puzzle game. But its NOT the same as the original. This one is better - a lot better, And yes, I own and have played the original point and click scummvm game from the 1990's.  I even have the original game on CD somewhere. (yes, thats CD, not DVD, and yes I bought it when it first  came out. And yes, I really am that old). Sure, same name, and same concept, but new puzzles, new dialogue, and new characters. Its not a VR remaster - its a re-imagining. My only issue with it is the controls are clunky. Right trigger is the lamp, left trigger is the ouiji board - but gripping/interacting with the environment is squeeze the grip. Sensible on paper, or when you say it, but in practice, its a nightmare. (pun intended). I would have preferred the right A button be the lamp (toggle), left A be the ouiji (toggle) - the the triggers interact (and/or the grip) with the environment. Since the majority of the  game will be picking things up, and pushing buttons, the controls feel awkward. Never mind. Its still a fun game, and I'm only a few hours in. :)
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This game actually caught me by surpise. I thought i would just get a nice reahash of a game that has it's best game days long behind it. But this game is so much more!For starters, the presentation is absolutely stellar. The Mansion itself looks great and beliveable, eevealing and fixing hidden stuff with the ghost lantern is a nice twist and telling the story with 3D scans of real actors is pure genius. Sure there might be artifacts around their bodies but since they only appear as ghosts in the game this only adds to the illusion. I imagine this is not any less impressive than the FMV cutscenes were 30 years ago in the original.All of the puzzles were completely overhauled (read: better) although they do have some references to the old puzzles here and there. Some of the Puzzles truly do profit from VR mechanics but I am not gonna lie, some of the puzzles, especially the board game puzzles, made me wish to control the game with mouse and keyboard instead. But the puzzles never overstay their welcome so that is fine. I also appriciate that there is a hint system in the game as it beats awkwardly googeling solitions on your smartphone when you're stuck, however I wish it wouldn't go from 0 to 100 in the matter of seconds. The first hint vaguley explains what you have to do in a puzzle with a short rhyme, the second hint straight up tells you what to do and maybe gives you a nudge into the right direction but the third hint just straight up solves the puzzle. I wish the hint system would guide you towards the solution more naturally like the Professor Layton games do. The 7th guest is without a doubt one of the best VR games I have played so far. If you like the concept of escape rooms don't miss out on this game!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Such an amazing visual experience was this, the puzzles were challenging and absolutely fun. You get immersed into this beautiful environment that feels so realistic, this feels like a really thought through game with how everything connects and how each room feels like a sense of how many people have gone through this. I felt like I was really in a Disney room with how everything played out. Amazing experience, I wished I could replay this endlessly.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Price is being quite steep, but I think it's worth it (yet better wait for sale). In my opinion one of the best VR games available, It's very well made, utilizes FMV in 3D, I don't think I have seen it being used in VR games before.Took me about 7 hours to beat, stuck only twice as pointers were a bit blurry, but overall I feel quite satisfied with the game.Quite sad you can't revisit the mansion after beating the game, but I hope this will be introduced in future patches.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the original CD-I game and while this game was a lot easier, I feel it is a great modern take on the original. I did find the controls a little finicky at time but it didn't spoil the experience too much. It was great that they kept the musical themes from the original and they did a great job at updating them too.I didn't manage to unlocked all the achievements on my first play-through but I'll return to the game in a few months (after my memory has faded a little) and update this review if needed.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I've only just started, so I'll update later on with more, but so far I'm astounded by the amount of fun I'm having with this! The original 7th Guest is like a half-remembered dream from my childhood- a positive experience, but a vague one. I know that it helped shape my taste in horror and gaming, so I was prepared to have a fun little time with the VR game, and enjoy it as a curiosity.But whoa, even if I'd never heard of this game before, it would have had me hooked. The ambiance is positively sumptuous, and I'm astounded by how well they've implemented the live-action actors. I'm not too far in, so the puzzles are still easy, but the tactile sense of interacting with Stauf's mechanical gadgets is very charming and satisfying. The lamp mechanic interacts well with all the paintings to give that old "click-to-interact" vibe you'd see in early 90's adventure games. The assorted creepy moments and laughs from them are playful, and there are enough of them and they can be viewed quickly enough so that everyone's likely to find a few favorites.It can't have been easy translating such a cheesy, very 90's style of comedy and horror for modern audiences, but I feel like the heart and joy is still here, even if there's such a thick coat of fresh paint on it. My immediate impression is that this could well be the gold standard for a remake: people who know what they're doing, bringing their marvelous and keen eyes to something older, giving us all a new way to enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Very fun game and throw back to the original game.   No puzzle is exactly like the first game.  Closest is the chess game, but unlike the original, there is only one solution.  Don't want to give any spoilers so I won't go into too much detail.  Just that two pieces must be placed in specific spots (marked).One big change for me is the spirit board in the OG game could accidentally solve a puzzle.  The spirit board will give you hints to a puzzle, but on the third (I believe) look at the board, it would just say "Puzzle solved".  So if you wanted to re-read a clue, you missed out on solving.  In THIS game, you can re-read clues.  Most of the time it's stuff you already figured out, but to get it to solve the puzzle you must spend a coin.  Coins are found all over the house and I think there are enough to solve all the puzzles (never used one in first play through).Graphics were great, as well as the music.  Played on a Meta Quest 3 via Steam Link (wireless).  I had very little issue.  One puzzle didn't register as complete, but just logged out and back in and it reset.For those with phobias:  There are quite a few spiders lurking around.  You shouldn't need go near them if you don't want to.  Worst bits is the bathroom puzzles, and there is one guarding a coin in a backroom.  You don't need the coin (unless you are going for the achievement).  Bathroom isn't too bad (don't have a phobia tho).  Other is there are a lot of creepy dolls.  That should be expected being that Stauf is an evil toy maker.  There is one room where the puzzle is focused on dolls.  There are no jump scares.Just finished my first play through and missed 2 achievements.  Will play through again to get those last two.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I have no experience with this franchise, so I went in with no expectations. The game looks stunning on PCVR. There is an occasional hiccup when the audio cuts out but the game is still running, and I somehow missed a cut scene during one of these, but I don't feel like the cut scenes are essential to finishing the game, just a nice icing on top of the puzzles. One complaint I have is the hint system. Very early on I needed help and used all the hints. If you need the final hint, the one that costs a Stauf coin, the puzzle will just solve itself and not show you the solution. That was irritating, and I haven't used a coin since. Some puzzles are too easy. Most are pretty run of the mill for puzzle games, i.e. moving pieces around a board in one way or another. I was afraid the game would be too scary, but it's very like The Room: A Dark Matter VR, creepy atmosphere but nothing jumps out at you. The stereoscopic animations are something I've never seen in VR and look gorgeous. For the most part game interactions work well (sometimes a little janky trying to pull on something, which is normal to me for VR). I'm playing via Quest Pro on a 3060 Ti, so not a top of the line setup, and the game runs mostly smoothly.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Always wanted to play the original, but I am glad I got to experience this game via the VR version. The puzzles generally work well in VR, though some have awkward interactions. I love the creepy atmosphere - thanks to the great graphics and sound design. The cherry on top are the endearing characters that appear via volumetric cut scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: "Curses!Damn, next one will be harder!"That was quite fun for me;It's light in spookiness, easy in puzzles, nice in environment, a bit repetitive in assets;- nice graphics, even if not that really high res textures (besides view outside the mansion windows)- surprisingly good captured real-actors volumetric footage (even if noticably simplified from close-up)- I liked the variety of puzzles, but few were hard to get idea what to do (and pillow one in Julia's room even hard to find)- nice ambiance of the haunted mansion- good fun with the paintings- controversial end-puzzle, but it was fairly okeish for me- occasional cockroach and arachnophobia alert!- relaxing jazz music, that you want to listen irl- 9 hours in relaxed paceFor me it's 8/10, I would recommend for everybody
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: A really fun reimagining of one of the most historically significant PC games of the 90s. The puzzles are a bit kinder this time around, though sometimes the rules and objectives of certain puzzles can be a little unclear. I saw a lot of complaints about the final puzzle and I can definitely see some people bouncing off of it, but I didn't think it was too bad. Walking around the Stauf mansion in full VR is worth the price of admission alone if you've got a lot of nostalgia for this game
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played this way back in the day when it was first released on PC and for its time it was so much fun. So, when it came out on VR, I was very excited, but I was not expecting much. Maybe walking around the mansion and playing through some great puzzles with the same video clips from the original. Also, I loved the puzzles in the first one. Some of them were extraordinarily difficult for me so I wasn't looking forward to having to relive that frustration again. But to be able to see the mansion and everything in 3D, I thought might be worth it. I'm so glad I took a chance on this one. This game has completely blown me away. It does have the same underlying story but the developers have outdone themselves. Being able to step foot inside Faust's mansion and walk room from room and play through the puzzles was so much fun. There are few games that really immerse you in the atmosphere as well as this one does. Everything has been rebuilt. Nothing has been taken from the old assets. Everything is new, including new puzzles! The music and sound design is great and really sets the mood of the entire game. The graphics and visualizations are so much fun and creepy. You really feel like you are there, walking through the Faust mansion. The puzzles are challenging but solvable. Some are easier than others but if you just spend the time, you will get through the puzzles. Let's face it, the game IS the puzzles. This title is done so well though that the atmosphere quickly becomes the reason you find yourself playing. The acting is well done and adds very well to the story and again, the atmosphere :) I cannot recommend this game highly enough.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Nicely done in VR.+: See all other positive comments. Yay.-: Game is stuttering with a HP reverb G2 headset. Other users confirm that this is an issue between game & reverb G2 headset. (I still managed to finish the game, but had in real life to succeed some fortitude saves on my stomach)How to handle the stuttering: Lowering some graphics settings helped. Setting the pixel density beneath 100% increased the stuttering, setting it back to 100% was better.According to other users every time you start the game switching antialiasing off and on again should do it.Lowering some settings / switching them on and off helps.(It runs on a high end PC optimized for VR
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: seeing this game had been released was my main reason for picking up a meta quest 2, I had been on the fence about getting back into VR more seriously and didn't want the wires from my Rift. this did not disappoint, while sometimes the controls acted up I was thorougly engrossed the entire time i played it. still need to go back in and find a few coins but finished the story last night and do see myself walking around in here more. the last game wasn't exactly my cup of tea but I apprecite the effort that went into this and the game as a whole and I loved my whole time in there.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: A great remake of a classic horror puzzler. There is a sense of wonder and dread contained within the story as it unfolds. The horror is subtle yet chilling. Puzzle's are intuitive and fun; this vr version has made each puzzle more interactive and takes full advantage of motion controls. It is perfectly playable from a seated position. I have also been playing this beautifully on a quest 2 tethered to steam.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This is exactly the game i've dreamed of back in the 90's when the game originally came out !I feel like I know this place. It's mood is impressive and also weirdly familiar. There are mysteries and puzzles which are a great pleasure to beat... This old creepy mansion was a very good investment, especially with VR. Guest ghosts are particularly well integrated... This is an iconic game very well reimagined... a must-play for every VR enthusiast.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: OK so I was a MASSIVE fan of the original game, and as a re-imagining, this hit all the right boxes for me...mostly. The recreation of the mansion was flawless. They have made changes to it, but they're all for the better. The puzzles have changed this time round too. They weren't very difficult (With some exceptions) to complete, and some came with nice nods to the original game. The graphics have had a nice upgrade, and the characters were great to see in real 3D too.Now, I wish I could leave it there, happy to give it a positive. It will remain a positive but I have to address the elephant in the room, in the shape of VR controls. For like 90% of the game, they worked fine, but for some puzzle manipulation, the controls were at times very janky. Hard to select pieces, incorrectly pressing buttons, and poor touch recognition seemed to pop up from time to time. Not enough to completely ruin the experience, but were hard to ignore. Also, the end of game puzzle didn't rely on problem solving, rather brute force to complete. I shan't give details on the puzzle, suffice to say the finale deserved better.SO OVERALL: Would I recommend it? Yes! Even with the few negatives, the game as a whole was great fun. The creators were clearly fans of the original and this game provided a very good re-imagining of the old 90's experience.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The 7th Guest VR is a reimagining of the original 7th guest game, this much is obviously said. What isn't obvious is how much care was put into this game. While some may be disappointed that it isn't a 1:1 remake only in vr, and let me be honest there were parts of the game that did disappoint me, generally speaking the changes are made for the better. Generally. The script for the game is unquestionably improved by.. well using the original as a outline and then giving everyone better lines and direction. Look I loved the original but watching the FMV's now is.. sorta painful how bad they were at times. The puzzles of the original are almost all gone, although some of the puzzles reference the old ones or are new spins on them, but generally speaking each room has multiple puzzles in it rather than a single one and the originals simply would not translate well to VR space. Trying to rearrange 27 cans in a shelf in VR would likely be a nightmare and likewise would trying to trace a line with your finger through a martian maze. The house itself has had its layout changed around to be a little more in line with what the actual bounds of the house have been displayed as. No more weirdly jutting out rooms or confusing room attachments. Sadly this also meant some of the more out there elements were removed. No ghostly shortcuts like diving down a pool table and the basement maze was totally ripped out for better or worse.  That said the new puzzles are not without their issues. Several of are very difficult to navigate in VR due to not being able to lean over or see around them easily. Some are simply too cryptic. I still don't know what exactly the rules were for the ABCDE puzzle I simply farted around until i solved it. The Doll room puzzle was so maddening that I think a lot of people probably just used the auto-solve feature for it. And the final puzzle true to the original has a really annoying RNG element to it that I was fortunate ended up favoring me. Yes there is an auto solver in the game, it does sort of punish you for using it by locking you out of an achivement however.   Still problems aside I recommend the game to anyone who liked the original and want to enjoy a shortish 3-5 hour VR puzzle game of which it feels like there are vanishingly few of. The house feels so much more alive, the puzzles more head scratching, the FMV's are now replaced with volumetic 3d recordings allowing you to wander around and see them from different angles while retaining that unnatural feeling that the original games FMV had.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Fun puzzle game in VR set in a cheesy-horror-but-really-not-scary-manaion.The basic game structure is a series of rooms, each with its own self-contained puzzles. The puzzles are all logical and fair and are easy-to-moderate in difficulty. The VR interactions are mostly fine with just a hint of jank here and there.Unlike traditional narrative foccused adventure games the puzzles have at most a weak connection to the plot. The plot itself plays out in a technically impressive series of cheesy performances shows on volumetric video inside the game world.Would recommend to puzzles lovers.Played the game using Quest 3 + Steam Link over WiFi.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Wow, I HIGHLY recommend 7th Guest VR if you're into puzzle VR games. Not only is it a candidate for best VR Puzzle game on my lists, but this has worked its way into my top 10 Overall VR games.I went into this expecting kind of a typical escape room/puzzle sim, but this went well above my expectations. Having played & completed all three I Expect You To Dies, plus various other Escape Room/Puzzle VR games (like Escape from the 80s/90s), in addition to the more similar in fashion Myst, Obduction, and Firmament (and all in VR -- and all of which I enjoyed thoroughly), The 7th Guest VR easily earns a spot in the top 3; perhaps bested only by Wanderer.What really makes this game shine is how the dev team managed to nail so many vital aspects with epic cohesion.For example, the fact that they did 360 recordings of all the ghost 'cutscenes' was a VERY nice touch. Being able to walk around them while their scenes played out was great. I feel like it's one of those things that works so well, most people may not even notice the work that went into it.The audio & music were very well done, and truly pulled the atmosphere together. Again, one of those things that if you're not looking for it, you don't even notice it because it just pulls you into the scene. And absent it, the game would still be great, but when it all comes together... masterpiece.I'm always interested to see how VR teams work with UI/UX, and I must say, the Ouija board map/menu was amazingly done and fits well with the theme.But what really put it over the top for me, though, was the setting design. The dev team that worked on all the textures, paintings, and "feel" of the estate deserve an award for this. Not only did the entire estate have a great spooky atmosphere; but the entire thing was also recreated to be lighter & clean, as shown through the flashlight or when a room's puzzles are complete. The contrast and the way that it forces you to immerse yourself with arm movements (having to shine the light for clues) is a great subtle way to increase immersion; and really worked for me.Not even joking that if this game had 0 puzzles and plot/cutscenes, I'd still happily drop $5 just to be able to walk around the haunted house and shine the light around to see "what it use to look like". And I'm not one to usually like spooky houses or creepy things. Honestly, I tend to lean more towards futuristic/space-sim type environments.I didn't pursue the side-quest/100%/achievement awards, and just did the main story, which took me about 8 hours to complete. Well worth the price, for me. Played on an HP Reverb G2, RTX 2080, and had no issues whatsoever.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I never played the original from the 90s (i played a lot of Myst-likes though), so i can't compare this remake with the original. But i like The 7th Guest VR a lot. It's not perfect (graphically the contrast is a bit too low and the controls could be a little more precise sometimes), but overall it was a nice atmospheric puzzle adventure with overall nice graphics, sound design and some slightly janky 90s full motion video adventure feeling (don't mean that in a negative way, i loved a lot of those games). Puzzles (with one exception where i didn't understand the solution) were pretty fair and well designed, although mostly not too innovative. Some chess puzzles, combination puzzles, finding hidden hints with the lamp etc. When you get stuck you can use the ingame help system (which i did in one case).Feels like a mix of Myst and The Room with some Agatha Christie/Edgar Wallace vibes. If you like some of that you probably like this one as well. Not a masterpiece in game design, but a pretty solid adventure games.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome VR game. Very immersive environment with fun (and not too difficult) puzzles tailored perfeclty to VR controls and movement. Played on a Quest 2 through the Steam Link app without too many hiccups (one crash, and 2 desyncs where I lost head tracking and controller input; unsure if it is due to Steam Link or the game).
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The 7th Guest VR is everything VR is supposed to be and should be.I dislike puzzle games ... a lot.However ... this gem of a VR game forced me to reconsider.I loved Alex, cherish Hubris and many other action and sim VR related titles but I always thought ... nothing like this, no, not a puzzle game !?What made me to buy this anyway were the countless raving comments on YouYube and gaming websites.BTW I could always ask ... for a refund if I bought this on Steam anyway.But now I sure will not have to do this ... this is a keeper and The 7th Guest VR is a game that anyone can use to show VR newbies what VR can mean for gaming !I hope we will see more of this excellence ... we need these wonderful titles to prove PCVR is here to stay.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Solid puzzle game. Not really a horror title, but it does have moments that can be mildly unsettling. It comes close to being a children's game if not for one or two specific cutscenes and painting reveals.+ Overall solid cast of characters+ Collectible coins to be used (or not) for puzzles and hints+ A hint system altogether, completely optional+ Puzzles are alright in difficulty. They will probably give you a couple head scratches, but not for long. No moon logic whatsoever+ Cool time crossover via the lantern (obtained right at the beginning of the game) when shining it on objects inside the mansion+ As stated, not a horror game. But because I see the label and it being mentioned (the horror aspect), please note that there are NO JUMP SCARES. It's a good day- Annoying bugs where sometimes your lantern mysteriously goes missing. Only way to get it back it to restart the game entirely.I don't know if I would put this in a _must play_ category, but it was definitely a fun adventure. Took me ~6 hours to complete it.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The 7th Guest VR should be a part of everyone's VR library. This was honestly a fantastic retelling of an old classic and an experience that I felt has - despite the original still having a place in my heart - really improved upon the original. The live-action acting and environments dedicated to particular characters filled in the gaps that were missing with the original and their reasons for getting involved in the story. I was pleasantly surprised by some of the creative ideas that went into the puzzles, particularly by the ones which took on full use of the VR space. I never found myself bored or felt like the challenge wasn't there. Well done, Vertigo!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: As someone new to the series, I found this chilling puzzle game to be a gripping experience. The transition to virtual reality elevates the immersive horror and brain-teasing challenges within the Stauf mansion. Despite not having played the original 90s version, the game's well-crafted puzzles and immersive storytelling in VR made it a captivating journey.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: When a beloved game from your childhood is remade, this is about the best result you could hope for! It's clear the original was beloved by the devs as well, and they did a great job honoring the legacy while making it their own. Any complaints I could make feel like nitpicks compared to the enjoyment I got from exploring Stauf's mansion again. Perhaps the puzzles were a bit on the easy side, but then I just couldn't stop playing either.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: This is an outstanding re imagining of this title!  It is very respectful of the original and the team that worked very hard on it.  The VR elements are outstanding with controls being super smooth and very responsive and fun.  The graphics are top notch.  I didn't have a single crash or hiccup.  The story has been revamped to be like the original but more engaging.  Better characterization.  Great scenes!  I also really enjoyed the puzzles!  And it was very fun to explore.  There is one odd thing that I do not know is a glitch.  IF it says 15/17 rooms cleared it is OK to do the final.  When you finish the game and go back to your save you will see 17/17 rooms.  The coins were challenging.  I had like ... 5 I think? .. that took me longer to discover.  I didn't have any trouble getting all the story elements as I played the game.  I did not get all the achievements but that is OK.This was just a lot of fun and this team worked very hard to make it work as the ORIGINAL did, but better AND in VR!  It was not dumbed down.  I mean they kept it tied to the 1920s like the original did, so kept it of that period kind of story and characters.  They tweaked the characters just enough,  they did the most with the actress and made her better more DEVIOUS.I had such a BLAST playing this game!!  Thank you to the TEAM, and for their respect for both the original team and us the players!  I am not sure how they would revamp the sequel unless they completely redid it from the ground up.  The proposed 3rd entry could be fun to try to do in this format instead!  Also there is the fan game The 13th Doll I think it is that could be fun.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I played this via Rift Link on my Quest 2.  I thought it was very good, nothing stupidly obtuse or unfair (shaking fists at original's Microscope puzzle BS).  Looked great, I was a real treat to be able to walk through the House.  The lamp was a nice mechanic as well.  I really liked that most of the background music was remixed from the original so certain music beats I remembered and they even used the original 2 songs.  Definitely something I'll replay again after a while to try to pick up the achievements I missed.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Well done, quality pcvr game. I played the original flat game so long ago I had forgotten all of it, so this was basically a new game to me. Environments, graphics, sound, acting, story-line - all very well done, and the puzzles were original and varied. Difficulty of the puzzles varied as well. I just needed to use the hints to solve the drinking game, which seemed to defy all logic.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I really liked this game.  I was looking for a good puzzle game for VR and this fit the bill.  This game was fun and the puzzles weren't too challenging.  It's very fun to explore the mansion and shine your light on the paintings and see them change.  It's not a scary game, but some elements in the game could be creepy to children under 12.  I hope more games like this are released for VR.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Having played the original game on CD-ROM when it first came out, this is a decent remake.However the original atmosphere, music, and villain (Henry Stauf) were all way more unsettling. Even some of the puzzles were way harder. So it's unfortunately a bit watered down, kid friendly, and tame... Probably by design to appeal to a wider audience. Regardless of that this is one of the best VR games of 2023, and a really solid VR puzzle game.And while I've thoroughly enjoyed this remake, I really do miss the haunting, macabre vibes of the original.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: What an amazing game. The original game got me to but a computer for the first time back in 1995, and if not HL:ALYX, this would be the best VR game (and game) I have ever played.Seeing the mansion from this point of view was amazing. The graphics were very good and some of the detail like candle shadow moves on the walls and several other details was awesome. Seeing live characters in the game and the voice acting was very good too. The mansion design matches the original game and it maintains the core story, but this is mostly different puzzles from the original game (some are similar). The thought put into alot of these puzzles using VR was excellent. And most of the puzzles are very solvable with a little bit of thinking put forth. Some are very tough though and there was a glitch ,which has since been fixed, in the doll room that the heads quit attaching, so I had to use auto-solve feature on that one (you can get hints and have it auto-solve for you if you want, but that kind of defeats the purpose of the game). The final puzzle battling Stauff was pretty cool and fun.The only other complaint I have is the controls can be a little challenging. You are constantly grabbing an item or clicking puzzle stuff which can make it take longer to solve. So that drove me crazy. Otherwise game ran very smoothly. If you are going for the achievements, that could be challenging as I was missing 9 coins and somehow missed 1 record and memory. With the glitch being fixed can get the others since I won't need to use a coin to auto-solve any puzzle.Very impressed with this game. Had so much playing and hope they release another 7TH Guest game. If you have a VR and want a good puzzle game, this is it. Great game.Have ya played it yet?? lol
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: So this is a very interesting game to review and I want it to be known that while I ultimately choose to recommend this game I can completely understand if someone chooses not to.  Let's get the negatives out of the way first.So I personally have never played the original 7th Guest game this is based off of but the game definitely feels ported to VR, and not in a good way.  While the game does start off by giving you a lot of options on how you want to play (choosing between teleport or sliding for movement and sitting / standing for body position) none of it feels fleshed out well.  While teleport can get you close to the right area, it often struggles to place you directly in front of the object you want it to.  Which makes things like opening doors, or standing directly in front of a puzzle or object difficult.  This makes sliding absolutely necessary in the game.Likewise while the game offers you a seated experience, there were several times in the game where I had to stand up in order to see some collectibles and properly look at the puzzle.  The game also lacks pretty much any tutorial, instead being completely hands-off with the player for the most part.  Now while I can respect that in game design, telling your player what the controls are, especially for VR games, is vitally important.  VR games have not yet reached a standard control scheme yet and lord forbid this is someone's first VR game, they would probably struggle a lot.  The point is I shouldn't have to go into my options menu to figure out what the basic controls are.And some of them I still don't know, like it's still unclear to me how you grab some objects from a distance.  I know you can do it because I've done it accidentally plenty of times but doing it on purpose proved very difficult.  Speaking of UI issues, while it's nice that the game allows you to skip puzzles you find difficult the UI should DEFINITELY WARN the player that's what they're selecting.  I thought I was selecting another hint for said puzzle, not to skip it completely.  Also if you're going to skip the puzzle you should tell the player what the solution even was.  Also while they've said they patched issues in the doll/nursery room when I played I ran into a major glitch that stopped me from putting the doll heads onto the headless dolls.If that happens to you put the headless doll into the guillotine and cut, this seems to reset the objects variable back to the correct headless setting and allows you to put heads on the doll.The final annoyance is with moving objects.  Several objects have things written on the back of them but you're unable to just turn objects upside down or backwards and instead they will return to their default forward facing direction which forces you to have to awkwardly turn your wrist all the way and read stuff at an awkward angle.  Another problem is that other than holding onjects, the game has no inventory system, like you can't store objects in a bag you carry around or just float them in the air next to where you believe they might go.  While this isn't a major problem it does make solving some puzzles a little annoying as you have to leave items were they are and go grab them once you finished clearing up space for them.So with all that being said you must think I hate this game, but no.  While the U/I is rough and their are plenty of bugs, I actually still love this game.  That's what's frustrating.  Even compared to real life escape rooms this has to be THE BEST Escape room games I have ever played.  The puzzles are different but all feel logical, and while some took a minute to figure out they were all very fair and never had me rolling my eyes going "well that's a leap in logic," or "how was I supposed to figure that out".  I must admit the first two rooms can be a little jarring since the game doesn't tell you really ANYTHING.It's "here is an empty room, figure it out" and it's left up to the player to work out what even are the puzzles in the room.  With that said the game does give a feel voice-over hints here and there to help nudge players in the right direction.  But once you get used to it it's not bad at all and I would HIGHLY recommend this game to any escape room fan.  The story is also pretty good, with great acting from live actors and a decent plot.  It's clear they're going for an old-school cheesy horror movie vibe and they pull it off for the most part without it becoming cringy to watch.  The atmosphere is also really well done, with the lighting, and details in the environment, and choice of music all combining together to make for a great experience.So overall I would recommend this game, it's just in their future games I hope they clear up these U/I and control issues.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Big fan of the 7th Guest. Played the original when it was new in my friend's dad's computer room. Read the book (there's a book). Played the semi-official fan game 13th Doll, both character paths. When I first saw they were changing some things for this I was coming in skeptical, but overall I'm pleased with how it all came together. Puzzles all seemed reasonable. Writing and story felt well balanced between feeling like the original without repelling a more modern player. 3D video-ish capture worked well for how they're using it. Would recommend to fans of the original, it's different enough that you're not repeating anything, but close enough that it doesn't feel overly changed for its own sake.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Wonderful puzzle game that might seem like a horror game at first but it's more like an Agatha Christie novel; it reminded me of 'And Then There Were None', actually. In essence it is like an Escape room game where you solve puzzle after puzzle and get some bits of story after solving each room. I had a fantastic time with it, I never played the original so there's no nostalgia factor for me but after playing this I've been watching gameplay videos of the 90's game just out of curiosity and what a fantastic remake/reimagining have they done.The Room VR used to be my favorite game of this kind but The 7th Guest has become the new king. Now please, bring us The 11th Guest too.THE GOOD- Beautiful graphics, atmosphere and design- Lots of puzzles, completely different and varied- All puzzles are perfectly logical, no abstract or abbsurd puzzles here- Interesting story that adds a little touch of mystery to the mix- Volumetric capture effects for the real characters is superbly done- Pretty good length that will vary for each person depending on how good you are at solving puzzles. For an idiot like me it was close to 10 hours (not using any coins to solve any puzzles)- Smooth locomotion and teleport options (or both at the same time) to please everyone- The final minigame was great, I'd love to have it as an extra mode or somethingTHE BAD- Almost every time you solve  a puzzle you need to physically move closer to them since it always keep a distance from you which sometimes is a litte uncomfortable. Not a big deal, really, but it could be adjusted a little to make it perfect.THE UGLY- For very experienced players, most of the puzzles will probably be on the easy side which might be a negative for them. Personally I thought they had the right difficulty, I got stuck a couple of times but it was very fluid most of the game which I really liked and enjoyed.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: It’s a nice looking game with some interesting puzzles, the controls are a little janky, the sitting function isn’t functional as you need to stand to reach. It’s kinda spooky but no jump scares or any mysterious creatures lurking in the shadows. I’m patiently waiting for an update so fingers crossed.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent game! Very faithful to the dedication shown in the earlier games (7th Guest and 11th Hour). The graphics are fantastic and the atmosphere is dark and foreboding. The puzzles are fun, but some updates could improve the handling of objects (fine point manipulation where it is easy to touch other things unintentionally).I would also like it if there were some secret passages added to the game.I would like to request some consideration to add DLC for rooms that are not in the game that were in earlier titles. For example, the art gallery and the science lab. Perhaps some new outdoor material could be added. Also, perhaps MP3 music files as well for listening enjoyment.8/10.  I am a very pleased long time 7th Guest fan.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Really good, one of best VR games you can play. Simple, well realized, knows what it is and delivers on its premise.The time changing lamp gimmick never gets old, its such a cool effect that you will spend a lot of time flashing it at random stuff to see how it reacts. The 3d hologram actor recordings are one of the coolest thing i saw in VR.Could be longer, expect 6-8 hours assuming you dont get stuck on any puzzles.Only problem is last puzzle has some luck involved in it, would be fine, if not for how long the animations take, they really needed to speed up the last puzzle animations.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished it. 7 hours and probably one hour of that was spent trying to figure out how to get around a game breaking bug and replaying some parts after crashes. I was on the fence about whether to recommend it or not but overall it was a positive and worthwhile experience. Even though I was a PC gamer when the original came out I never played it as I wasn't a fan of pre rendered slide show games. It's a nice looking game overall. Some things are really beautifully done while some things are pretty bad looking and probably not better than the Quest port.It's got some entertaining acting and decent looking volumetric video. Puzzles range from mostly way too easy to a few that were decently challenging.  Some mini games were really fun for me, especially the end game. It has some cool game mechanics that take advantage of VR.A multiplayer co op mode could be interesting.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: I truly enjoy this game. I didn't think it would be my sort of game but wow. I am loving the story line and the puzzles. I must admit some are a struggle but that's what makes it fun. This is such a new concept in VR gaming for me and I am enjoying my struggle; still plenty to do. I will give this game 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: this is a great tribute to the original.  The atmosphere is incredibly well done.  The fact that they've managed to include the FMV like the original had, but have done it in a completely new way, somehow projecting the video onto 3D models of the characters, you can actually walk AROUND the FMV in VR.  It's really impressive!   The acting is just as cheesy, but in a really good way, as the original.  The puzzles so far have been very satisfying, and exploring the house in VR is just a real pleasure!  So glad they've created this amazing game!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Played this in turns with my partner, we both loved it. It feels like you're walking in a VR version of the haunted mansion in Disneyland so definitely spooky but not scary. Some quirks I wanted to share:Most puzzles are fun, but almost none of them use the VR medium that much compared to some other puzzle VR games.We only got stuck on two rooms. And I feel dumb writing how we got stuck but we really couldn't figure it out!:Played with Index / 4080 / R9 5950XThe controls are alright, just like most VR games (Alyx ruined my VR expectations) doors are hard to open and stuff can be hard to interact with.There are a couple of things that break immersion like But generally an excellent VR puzzle game definitely recommend
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Great game! The story was very engaging, and the puzzles were very satisfying to solve. I only have one gripe.Minor spoiler warning:The clues for the dolls seemed to indicate that some of them needed to be dead (with X's for eyes). After spending the only coin I spent the whole game for the auto solve, I found out that that was not the case.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: The 7th Guest was one of my favorite games from the 90s, I had it on the Philips CD-i. The experience of exploring Staufs mansion left you with your jaw dropping. I have to say, my jaw dropped again for this VR remake. The mansion has never looked so good. You can almost smell the dust and cob webs as you explore the mansion once again.The game is not only supporting great graphics and sounds, but amazing puzzles as well. The puzzles are new and fresh, but still remind you of the old ones. Is the game perfect, no. I did have issues with garbing and placing some items. I got stuck in a few places in the game, (stuck in walls, table), and had to restart the game a few times because the puzzles would not reset. It was nothing that would make me stop playing the game. I played through and finished the game on the Quest 3 in around 6 hrs. That was with no hints from the spirit board. I am about 3 hrs in on the Steam copy, and only a few rooms into the game this time. The game is the exact same, I am just spending more time examining the mansion and finding all the Stauf coins. In terms of replay, once you have solved all the puzzles and found all the coins all that is left for playing again is speed runs and looking at all the painting and other details throughout the mansion.If you played this game in the past, or always wanted to, this is a fantastic 7th Guest experience and should not be missed. The story will keep you wanting to learn more about Henry Stauf and the mysteries that unfolded within his house, and the puzzles should make any fans of the puzzle game genre happy.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Headset used for beating the game: Pico 4the mad man's game. Imagined. It is what they advertise, a puzzle game set in an old mansion.Just like the old game you explore the mansion of Henry Stauf. A Toymaker who's toys are a toy for life. During the game you'll go through puzzle room after puzzle room. usually solving a few puzzles which lead to restoring the room to it's old glory. The puzzles are generally really well done, not counting one clear outlier all the puzzles were clever, fun and nice intertwined in the rooms. Although the difficulty is lower than the original game, it uses so many fun and good idea's in the rooms that i didn't even think about that until i was done.The cutscenes are again done by using FMV (full motion video) but with an amazing twist. all the video's are taken in 360, meaning that you can walk around the ghosts while their story plays out.The mansion itself is also filled with small and big details for fans of the original game. maybe it's small things like names of achievements, or a puzzle which uses elements of the original puzzle which was found in the same location.The game played well with the pico 4, although the game was sometimes a bit shaky, this has been addressed by the devs as a technical issue with openVR/openXR, which i need to look into, more information about this is in the discussions tab. i also had to reach foreward and upward quite far sometimes, making me hit the slanted ceiling of my room a couple of times. this should only be kept in mind if you play this game in a smaller room.overall, This game is fun for both fans and newcomers alike.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely amazing game.  Faithful to the original and even has the two original vocal songs including the ending song.  Yes, I sang along.  The puzzles are different, which I am thankful for, but fit the game and are probably a little easier than the originals... or I was really young and smooth brained when I first played.  Still has the original concept that you need to figure out the rules of the games yourself, but there are more hints in the rooms, as well as they brought back the 2 hints plus auto solve feature from the original if you are struggling, but honestly with the length of the game being what it is you are better off taking your time if you are having trouble and work it out.  Even if you need to take a break and walk away for a bit.  I'm really glad they used real recorded scenes to tell the story just like the original, as well.  I do have some gripes.  First, the game plays much better standing.  I did stand for about half, but really did need to sit through part of it.  Age will do that to you.  When sitting, you can get fairly close to puzzles, but just not close enough at times and I ended up having to lean WAY over in my seat.  This is where standing works better for being "over top" of the puzzles as I think they were designed for.  Second was for some puzzles the controls are truly awful.  Your hand has no chill with grabbing and will snap to seemingly whatever it wants at times when you need to grab small pieces that are close together.  I also experienced a little jank.  One instance was very nearly game breaking when something I opened swung and clipped over and past a switch it was not meant to, preventing something else I needed to open from being able to be opened.  I had a double handed slap fight with it for a bit and eventually fixed it.  There is also a room with a guillotine.  If you are having trouble getting things to fit together, even if it makes no sense... consider using the guillotine.  It seems some flags are getting set that something is already connected even when there is not.  Is that vague enough to not be a spoiler but still useful?  I hope so.  That glitch was driving me mad for a good 10-15 minutes.Anyway, easy 9/10 for me.  The issues I had weren't that bad and honestly, I had a big dopey grin on my face the last 2 days beating this.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved the original, and it was the first game I got with my Packard Bell CD-ROM computer back in the day. The puzzles have been completely overhauled and work great with the tactile nature of VR.I only have one gripe, and it's the frequency of hints given by the child guide. I wish there was a slider for "hint volume" or something, as I currently just have voice volume at 0 and read subtitles only when I'm watching the cutscenes or am not solving a puzzle.

_childDocuments_.review: Finished the game in about 8,5 hours on my quest 2.The graphics are good en de game is very immersive. Audio is good as well. The live action cutscenes are really nicely done.I solved all puzzles and most of them are well designed. I had problems with one of them in the nursery because the vr controls got in the way and it bugged out. So had to use the auto solve on that one. So expect some control problems with some interactions being to close together  or not having the precision you would like.I enjoyed the mystery and the story a lot.There are plenty of lore to find including audio logs and other background information to the narrative and I really enjoyed that aspect. There is a hint system and auto resolve but I would advise you not to use it as the puzzles are not that difficult but it is always nice to have.The ending was a little bit disappointing, I won’t spoil anything but it was really out of place in contrast with the normal design and it was not really that enjoyable because it is a lot of RNG.Still the game is highly recommended if your are looking for a very immersive puzzle experience.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of the original I have to say that Vertigo Games did an outstanding job of porting this to VR. That said I can recommend this to anyone who enjoys rich atmosphere, compelling character driven story and lots of puzzles to solve.The only downside is the lack of WMR support. You will need to run the game with the Steam VR runtime which messes with the controller position in my Reverb G2.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Update: I went from positive to negative to positive on this game because a specific room was very buggy and not letting me progress, but the devs patched it, and I can now get further in the game.Orig. review: I'm a little over 2 hours into this and enjoying it. I never played the original game, so it's all new to me. At first, outside the mansion, I was thinking the graphics looked pretty Questified, but it looked better and more detailed inside the mansion. So far, it hasn't been scary at all, just mildly creepy. I was looking forward to the volumetric 3D video of the actors, but, for some reason, it's not as impressive as I had hoped. It might be because they're all semi-transparent and also because the game usually won't let you get very close to them. The main game element is the puzzles, which are good (not too easy, not too hard). My initial gameplay video is below.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Great VR games are few and far between. I think this one really stands out. The 3D FMV is extremely impressive, and manages to evoke old PC games like the original while also feeling new. Writing has been good so far but remains as campy as what I remember from the original. The music and sound design add to the atmosphere, making the game spooky, but not scary.  Game has performed well on my Nvidia 3080 at 144hz on Index.  The puzzle interactions are solid, not amazing. It definitely seems suited more for room-scale/standing in VR.  Overall I think this is an awesome achievement. Holy cow, someone made a new 7th Guest!  In VR! And it's great!
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review: Solid BUY, very polished, clean, and runs well on a 3070.WOW. Nostalgia overload. They did a great job bring this flat game from 30 years ago to life in VR. New puzzles, same creepy music and vibes. Not much for jump scares as the original didn't have it as well, it was slow paced mystery / escape / puzzle mansion. The puzzles start of easy and starting to get a bit harder. Everything so far is very intuitive and translates well in VR. I've played many other puzzles games and get stuck cause I didn't understand how far they take the physics in VR. I think even without nostalgia, newcomers, the next generation will still enjoy it if your into mysteries and puzzles. Almost 2 hours in and I'm on my 4th room. Not sure how many there are, but this is one to savor and take your time. Look at everything twice, once the old version, then use your light to restore it to the past. If you miss any of the sequences, you can play them again with your light. Same with the music box that has some story. Cons:Only issue I found is if you bring things to close to your head your vision goes black. Kinda happened at the start when I was rowing. Would be good for the devs to make the object disappear instead of making your whole screen black. Was a bit immersion breaking. This is sometimes set by default with collisions on VR rigs in Unity. I know VRIF has it. Should be easy to turn off. 1 minor thing when you get close to the ghost they disappear, seems you have to stand 5-6 feet away. Not sure if you can change that, would be cool to be closer to them.
_childDocuments_.name: The 7th Guest VR

_childDocuments_.review:
Experience the most spine-tingling VR mystery adventure of your life. The classic game that chilled you to the bone in the 90s has been brought back to life, with cutting-edge VR technology that delivers an atmospheric story like no other.

Six guests have been welcomed to the foreboding mansion. But something sinister is at play. The wealthy recluse and toymaker, Henry Stauf, hides in the shadows, and there is a dark power here, shrouded in mysteries. Who is the 7th Guest? What does Henry want with them? And who will live to tell the tale?

As you explore the eerie mansion, the puzzles become increasingly challenging, and there are dangers lurking around every corner, with every shadow, creak, and flicker of light adding to the haunting tension.

Unlock new rooms and uncover hidden secrets, all while trying to keep your wits about you against the eerie horrors.The 7th Guest VR is the ultimate adventure for fans of mystery-puzzle games and those seeking a new and terrifying VR experience.

_childDocuments_.review: I've mostly been playing the PS5 version and I have a bit over 8 hours in that so my sentiments are based on that but truth be told at first, like maybe my first two hours or so the game wasn't clicking with me, I liked the movie, cartoon, etc. and I like Heart&Slash, I had a lot to be excited about pre-release but when it was finally in my hands combat felt strangely limited and restricted and I felt so defeated because I liked everything else, but once I started getting midway through the skill tree and started really paying attention to the demonstration vids and looking at my move-lists, It really started to come together and now I've been having a blast with this game, the one I was hoping for before release.The Persona inspired elements of the game are greater than expected and a big part of the games charm, the time management, presentation and social links are pretty much pulled straight from those games while the social links don't have the same level of nuance, the stories told within them are simple, heartwarming and/or have great dialogue bits, there's one with Michelangelo that homages the classic NES Turtles game, in a really fun way, you can tell the people behind this were not just fans of Mutant Mayhem but the Turtles in general.The 3D Platforming aspect while subdued in comparison to the Hack & Slash and Persona stuff, is still very much involved and feels like all the best parts of the 2007 TMNT movie game's movement without the drawbacks, and there are cases where the movement and platforming really get to shine, in the pizza delivery challenges which are set up like obstacle courses and very much designed to encourage flow and speed-running, for the first time in a long time we've got a TMNT game utilizing the ninja aspect of them for more than just fighting.The combat is probably the most important part of this game for most, and I'm seeing comparisons to Yakuza and the TMNT 03 games and to those people feel how you want to I've played both of those, but honestly this is a character action game, its got its own flair and feel overall, but it blatantly is inspired by Devil May Cry, right down to enemies getting their own introduction scenes, to the slow-mo zoom on the finishing blow dealt in an encounter, to straight up lifting the style meter mechanic and I mean wholesale the ranking will stagnate if you continue to use the same attacks over and over again you're encouraged to mix it up, XP is pretty much red orbs, each of the turtles not only fights differently within their moves but they all have their own mini-mechanics pretty much ensuring that they are to be approached differently, We've had two other great TMNT games before this, Shredder's Revenge and Splintered Fate, but my biggest qualms with those is how Identical each character feels to control, I'm happy to report this game doesn't have that design choice and for me that'll do wonders for replayability. But it took a while to click, there's no jump cancelling and while you can guard or roll cancel some moves you can't do it for all of them. The game's enemies actually attack at a pretty frantic pace so for me its a little odd for your attacks to typically feel more like a commitment, I was so fixated on this early on and it took a while for me to get comfortable but please stick with it, the longer you play this game the more new features, side activities, mechanics etc. get introduced in addition to the skill-trees and move-lists getting quite deep and opening up your options tenfold, there are a number of people jumping to review this barely 1 or 2 hours in, and I'm saying it myself I wasn't won over early on but the game really does start taking off as you play.I should just address the game as it is, and not the sentiments I've seen thrown around on this discussion board but there's a lot of weird takes regarding identity politics, or a lack of online co-op, or something insane in between, while the latter would have been nice, the developer has never made an online game and If it came down to investing resources into the games various features and mechanics or cutting back on them to implement an online function that to be honest isn't all that suitable for this game, as it's really story/narrative driven and there would be a ton of time passed outside of the action bits where a second player doesn't get to do anything, I understand opting for the former, not to mention most character action games are single player anyway, that they squeezed in 2 players at all is kind of a feat in itself.There is just a strange amount of people trying to get their dream TMNT out of a $39.99 AA release with it's own unique ideas and people aren't judging it for what it is, rather they're judging it for what they want out of some hypothetical ninja turtles game.I think this game more than justifies its asking price, it is roughly 12-15 hours in length and that is without completion, 4 characters to master if you're the type to dig deep in these games, a cool dynamic difficulty mechanic that introduces itself a few hours in, and even fun little bonuses, like unlocking really cool alternate costumes for each character, and you can decorate the lair with graffiti you find in stages there's a shocking amount to see and do in it and there's going to be an extra mode released soon enough that will no doubt bolster it's replay value even further.It's not perfect the game takes a minute at least for me to really come together, took well over 2 hours for me to start liking it wholesale, the camera not often but early in the game and in rare cases there are encounters where it feels like its there for enemies to utilize it against you, there's a couple goofy instances of collision jank, and unfortunately their are some bugs I have the game essentially soft lock itself 2 or 3 times, forcing me to reset a level or an activity, but these issues aren't really enough to get me to not recommend it, and hopefully we see some patches for bugfixes and QoL add ons.This game is a clear labor of love I feel like I had to say my piece on it with how things are going atm despite preferring to wait until I've finished it, if you like TMNT and you're contemplating it but not sure because of the price or anything go for it, game is completely aware of it's price tag and does everything and more to justify it. This is the best 3D TMNT game to date and one of their best game outings in general, and probably the first genuinely good game out of Outright Games(no offense) Would love to see more like it some day.

_childDocuments_.review: It`s clear that cheap games based on a movie license cannot be taken seriously, they are usually made as if just for show,For "Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles" this is also relevant, but only partly, Firstly, it is curious how quickly they began to develop the universe of the new film (in the summer, a good series was also released), and, naturally, the main pillar is the cel-shaded visuals copied from Spider-Verse cartoon,But TMNTU also stands out for its fairly good, smooth combat mechanic, a fairly diverse number of techniques, combinations, rolls that you want to repeat over and over again, "AHEARTFULOFGAMES" was hired for the development, responsible for a tiny indie beatemup, and apparently they approached the matter with all their heart, if you play some old projects about the carriers of the shells of the 2000s or even 2010s - all the mechanics there were much more crooked than in "Mutants Unleashed", believe me,Also here Arenas and transitions between them use platforming, but it's too little to make a revolution in the genre, and somewhere it's inconvenient because of the fixed camera, if you're hoping for a full-fledged level like Tony Hawk with sliding along the railings, then, alas, all the maps are small boxes, and btw with a lot of backtracking, but this isn`t particularly noticeable, since the beginning and end of the map often change places,In short, my main thought about the game is that the combat system is literally constricted here, the target audience for the publisher is children, so they left no chance to reveal the potential, the enemies are too easy, so much so that you will get rank S in 99.9% of cases, without even having time to warm up your fingers, there is, of course, a small progressionespecially when mobs that shoot lasers appear, but you are unlikely to endure 5 tedious hours for the sake of a little difficulty at the end. Even with the bosses, things are uneven, the first one is very difficult, and the last one is click-killing in a minute, in terms of mechanics it's standard dodges from circular damage and a lot of hp, nothing special,And in short.. there's another fundamental problem: someone came up with the idea to stretch such a simple game, putting it in the shell of some Japan-RPG.. Like time after time we have to start missions from our sewer hub, or before the task go to the gym or office.. like a place where our friends are waiting for us, which opens up a new level of upgrades for one of the turtles just for dialogues, like in a visual novel ) And here there is also a day and night system and restrictions on completion by days. There are a couple more things like in the arcade you can take a modifier for 1 run to increase damage or for additional life (when you die, you return to the map), you can go through optional missions to find infected enemies.. which then for some reason will open up infected everywhere. There is also a pizzeria, where several unsuccessful platform levels for speed are available, and at home there are dojo challenges.. damn, there is also a smartphone there, you can read notes with it and scan the area for some goodies that are not used anywhere, as well as coins and cassettes, found on the main levels - In general, all this is so unnecessary, it kills the pace of the fighting game if anyone forgot..These cutscenes-dialogues about nothing with anthropomorphic animals from films begin to seem endless, fortunately they add the ability to skip them, but even so, the soul is exhausted by the minute-long loading between 3-minute levels. The content of the story also doesn`t affect the films, there everything is at the level of experiences of secondary characters like Bebop and Rocksteady disappointed in people, became bad, but we convinced them and "changed their shoes".. well, and some villain scientist spreads a virus at the end.. and I won't remind you about cheap animations, everything is clear here,And with aaall this, the game is not without the usual bugs, the most critical - because of which I cannot recommend the Cooperative game mode for 2 players (for which the camera is not adapted) - this is if you cross the checkpoint script before your friend, then you will immediately be separated by an invisible wall, because of which you will have to go back in order to then go forward together, and the passage back will again be frozen by the "wall" - who did this for what reason..🏆 In general, if you are a fan of Turtles and have a huge supply of patience, then it is definitely worth a try, after all, this is Beat ’em up an outdated genre, usually offer nothing but a dull slaughters, and mechanically it`s done cool, you won’t want to let go of the joystick buttons once you start (of course, it’s better play with it).
