_childDocuments_.review: To begin with, this is one of, if not the best indie title I’ve ever had the pleasure of playing. From a base perspective: environment, sound design, story, and gameplay are all phenomenal and will leave you wanting to finish the game. On a further level, this is the first game I’ve played that actually understands what goes into making a psychological horror game - what makes games like silent hill 2 and SOMA, well, what both the games are; what their legacies have created. Mouthwashing stands toe to toe with these giants and delivers a fantastic experience all while being an indie title. It is games like this that perpetuates the constant rise we are seeing in indie titles today and how they are the next step for gaming. A non-spoiler summary of the story is that five crew members are stranded in space aboard a freight ship as they struggle to ration out the remaining resources - physical and emotional resources alike. However, the story is also much more than that. **Spoilers** Overall, the game is fantastic and I recommend anyone who enjoys horror to play it, because it’s just that good. Even if you’re a horror fan that doesn’t care deeply for story, this game has plenty of regular horror elements that will keep you intrigued all the same. I look forward to seeing what this developer comes out with next.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a game with deep meaningful characters, an original story, beautiful graphics and an incredible OST; with a story so great I can't compare to any other media I've seen-movie, book or game, then Mouthwashing is a go-to game for you. I played once alone, cried and then introduced the game to my friends who all agreed they felt the same way I did. Without spoiling anything- I cared so much about all of the characters, they felt very fleshed out and real, the twists, the scary moments, the imagery and metaphors felt like nothing I have ever played before. _childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing. One of the best single video games I've ever played. ...up to a point.Most of this game is a masterclass in how to make an unsettling psychological horror. It uses a disjointed, nonlinear timeline and trippy, horrifying visuals to make you unsure of what's real. The characters are fleshed out enough that you start to genuinely care about them (or hate them.) The way it builds the tension and mystery keeps you anxious. You don't ever necessarily feel like you're in danger, but the narrative is enough to set you on edge.The last 25% of the game goes overboard with the surreal imagery until it stops feeling like it serves a point and begins to feel like repetition for the sake of having more strange visuals. The point gets hammered home so hard it feels like the developers were scared people wouldn't "get it."They also made the baffling decision to add some irritating maze/chase/combat sequences towards the end, which only take away from the atmosphere. Once you get taken out of the game by a frustrating puzzle or a death and notice the mechanics, it's harder to pull you back in.I still really liked it, but I was left with a tinge of disappointment. It could have been an all-time great if it had ended stronger. Still, it was memorable and affecting, and I'm absolutely looking forward to more from the developer!
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I'll admit, I thought that this was gonna be sort of a gag game at first, all I heard at first was "spaceship stranded and all they have to survive on is mouthwash". I was not expecting to find a game that ultimately was a huge meditation on dead-end jobs, being a burnout, and surviving SA and the trauma that comes with it. This game is something else. It's heavy. And if you've had any strong experiences in your past that come to mind when you hear those words, or if medical horror really hits hard for you, just be mindful that this game might be a rough experience for you if you aren't mentally prepared for it. It's *extremely* worth experiencing, I can promise you that. It's...just a lot to mull over.

_childDocuments_.review: Score: 9.8/10 (EIP.gg's highest this year)Mouthwashing is a near-perfect modern horror masterpiece. Deeply psychological, intensely stylish, incredibly nostalgic, shockingly powerful, and -- of course -- absolutely terrifying, there is essentially nothing to complain about in Mouthwashing. Compressed into a tight two-and-a-half hours, the cinematic ambitions of Mouthwashing are on full display, without sacrificing gameplay or visual flair.See my full review here: But, also, like... _childDocuments_.review: If you read nothing else, read this: Play this game right now. Don't go digging for more information, don't spoil yourself. Go in as blind as you possibly can. It'll make you a new person. My buddy gifted me this game because I saw some fanart of Daisuke and wanted to know what media he was from. I didn't know anything but his name when I started playing.Gameplay wise, this is a masterpiece. The puzzles were a challenge, but not to the point of being infuriating. The graphics are so charming, and they make the Horrors easier to stomach in a way. I couldn't imagine this game in 4K high-def; That'd mess it all up. And the writing? Out of this world. I've never felt more sick to my stomach playing a game in my life, and I've played some insane things in my time. This is a twenty car pile-up that you can't stop. It's knowing you're going to vomit and not being able to make it to a bathroom in time. It's watching a hunter circle its prey for hours and hours on end, wearing it down. There aren't real villains here. Everyone has a motivation, a reason, a good and a bad. You can't root for one of them without rooting for all of them. And you can only watch as they crumble apart. You go insane with them, in a way. You don't really have a choice.So yeah, play this game. It deserves every single bit of attention and praise that it's getting.

_childDocuments_.review: This is so good. The soundtrack is amazing, there were times where I had to just sit there and take it all in. I loved the dream(?) sequences, especially the one where you fall off the ship and get to see the sky growing brighter--that was so beautiful, it gave me this weird but great feeling that I will now crave from every game ever. The game looks amazing, the visual style is great--again, there were so many times where I just had to sit there and take in the visuals. I loved all of the fun details of the ship--it feels so lived-in, I can really see these characters actually living there. I also loved the transitions between scenes, how the screen freezes and melts into the next scene--small touches like that really add to the overall feel. Nothing makes me happier than seeing a dev team really love what they're doing. It's easy to see that this project was handled with so much love and care, and it shows in the final product.One critique I do have is the pacing at the end. It kept feeling like each section would be the last, so when the game continued from one "wrapping up" segment to the next, it felt like it was dragging along a bit. I find that to be a real shame, because there weren't any sections that I felt were bad on their own, just the way they were strung together towards the end felt off to me. I don't think it was even close to game ruining, though, just something to think about on your next game(which I will absolutely be buying btw!!). All in all, I really loved this game, and all of its characters. It felt very satisfying seeing the story come together in this non-linear format. Usually, I'm not a huge fan of non-linear storylines, but you guys really nailed it! I'm so excited to see what your team makes in the future, and I will absolutely be adding every song on the soundtrack to my playlist.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing obviously has a lot of passion, effort, and creativity put into it and it shows.  This is by no means a bad game.  Can I say I enjoyed it... not really.  I'm usually a big fan of psychological horror.  And this game is very cerebral with a number of disturbing elements.  But none of it really resonated with me and (aside from a couple moments) I never felt actual fear or palpable dread.Gameplay is very simplistic and follows a cycle of talk to person, find item, do thing.  Occasionally there will be a puzzle or something else to mix things up.  In a broad sense, the game feels very much like a walking sim or a point and click.  There's not much going on here and that's kind of the point.  To be completely honest, the I found the moments where the game broke from this loop to be the most tedious sections of the game.The story is very character-driven and is presented in a non-linear format.  I've seen a couple other reviews critique this part of the game, but I kind of liked it.  It does make the story a little difficult to follow, but it gives the more important plot points a lot more impact.Mouthwashing feels like a game I would have liked a whole lot more had I watched someone else play it.  It feels more like an interactive movie than an actual game.  And because of this, it's just not that fun to play.  Again, this is not a bad game, it just wasn't my cup of tea.

_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is down right sickening wrapped in a flawless execution. Even the smallest detail shows that there's no hope left for this crew since the beginning. The characters are what fascinate me the most, with how each of them retains remarkable flaws of their own yet still manages to form interesting dynamic. None of them shine as the generic "good guy", even Curly has done some wrongs in his part.It's the kind of game that keeps you on your toes even though there's no proper threat to be seen. _childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is an amazing experience. Short and sweet that left me with this feeling of disgust and despair that few games have. It doesn't sound appealing, but that's because the story being told isn't appealing at all. It's incredibly sinister and profoundly sad, but portrays itself with a seriousness and sincerity that isn't easy to achieve without bordering on being edgy or bad taste. The gameplay itself is simple with the most complex parts being a shooting-gallery-esque section towards the end, but for the most part you'll be walking around interacting with set-pieces akin to a point-n-click. But since the story is so well written and tightly paced, a simple objective like "go here, get this" turns into a stress inducing task. Towards the end of the game i was having mixed feelings about the story, since it really started to feel like the narrative was irredeemably evil with the amount of cartoonish narcissism that was being presented alongside the horrifying conclusions that were shown for the characters, but it ended up clicking for me after that final scene. I don't have many gripes with Mouuthwashing aside from some really minor once. I will admit that the "Analog horror" elements that were presented in Mouthwashing are a bit played out in horror media, but that's not to say it took me out of the experience. The puzzle sections were fine but there were some moments that really dragged on. Overall, Mouthwashing is great. It's incredible characters and tightly written dialogue are the real reasons to play, with the gameplay being more of a vehicle to get you to the next story beat. It's messages are clear and thought provoking, and it makes me want to talk about this game and its philosophy more than most other games with a similar tone. It's sad, occasionally heartwarming, constantly dreadful, and consistently thought provoking. Everyone should give this a shot.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing: A Deeply Disturbing Psychological ThrillerIntroductionIndie games often push boundaries, providing players with experiences far beyond mainstream expectations. "Mouthwashing" is a prime example of this, blending psychological tension with unsettling themes in a way that leaves a lasting impact. While not for the faint of heart, this game offers an artistic and emotionally intense narrative that challenges the player’s preconceived notions. It may not suit everyone due to its disturbing content, but for those well-versed in the genre, it stands out as a unique and thought-provoking title.Story and ThemesAt its core, "Mouthwashing" veers more into psychological thriller territory than traditional horror. As you progress, the game forces you to confront uncomfortable situations, both mentally and within the game’s narrative. The harsh and jarring messages scattered throughout the story critique societal issues and delve deep into individual psychological struggles. The thematic richness and emotional weight of the game give it significant artistic value, making it more than just another horror experience.GameplayWhile "Mouthwashing" is labeled as a horror game, the sense of fear takes a backseat to a persistent feeling of tension. The gameplay resembles that of a walking simulator, focusing less on intricate mechanics and more on delivering a narrative-driven experience. Players are encouraged to explore the minds and emotions of the characters rather than the physical environment. The limited interactivity suits the genre well, though it may leave some players desiring more traditional horror elements. However, it succeeds in immersing the player in its tense, foreboding atmosphere.Characters and AtmosphereOne of the game’s standout features is its character development. Each character's distinct behaviors and decisions reflect their psychological depth, encouraging players to engage with them on an emotional level. This leads to moments of genuine empathy, as the game gently pushes you to understand and even sympathize with the characters’ inner struggles. The focus on character-driven discovery, rather than environmental exploration, provides a unique form of satisfaction, setting "Mouthwashing" apart from other narrative-driven games.Disturbing Elements and Artistic Messages"Mouthwashing" does not shy away from deeply unsettling imagery and situations. Throughout the game, you’ll encounter scenes that are as disturbing as they are symbolic. These elements may not appeal to every player, but they serve to highlight the game's powerful artistic vision. The developers may not have reinvented the genre, but their bold storytelling and thematic choices elevate the game to a higher level of artistic achievement.ConclusionAt roughly two and a half hours, "Mouthwashing" offers a brief yet impactful experience. It transcends traditional horror, opting instead for a psychological thriller with a deep, meaningful narrative. Its emotional intensity, combined with thought-provoking character development, makes it a standout title in its genre. However, its disturbing content and slow, methodical pacing may not appeal to everyone. For those who appreciate innovative indie horror games with artistic ambition, "Mouthwashing" is certainly worth your time.-Sado

_childDocuments_.review: I have mixed feelings about this game and I have sort of a love-hate relationship with it, because on one hand the style and the horror aspects of the game are really great, but the gameplay and the story are definitely on the weaker side. In my opinion, this game is drastically overpraised for what it actually offers, so I'm giving this a thumbs-down here, primarily to balance the scale a little bit.From a gameplay perspective, this game barely even counts as a walking simulator let alone as an adventure game -- with the exception of one or two creepy scenes in the second half of the game it could just as well be an animated movie, escpecially since the entire game is absolutely linear without giving you any choices whatsoever. The "puzzles" are so shallow that they're not even worth mentioning. As far as the story is concerned, I think that there's a lot of wasted potential here, especially since the plot was quite promising for the first half of the game, but it then went down the obscure road in the second half and became so opaque that one can barely make any sense out of it.On the positive side, both the low-poly style visual design as well as the audio design are amazing. As far as the horror elements are concerned, this game does a pretty good job by going down a Silent-Hill-like-ish route, but it never really scared me or creeped me out and other (recent) games have done an ever better job here.Buy if you like the visual style from the screenshots and you're interested in some classic creepy horror, but stay away if you expect a consistent story and proper gameplay mechanis other than walking.

_childDocuments_.review: This is truly a work of art. The people that worked on this deserve endless praise for their dedication to producing an excellent narrative. Uncertain if there's a visionary behind the team or if this team is simply excellent all working together. I hope I can see your work in the future. Please continue making and creating, you truly have a gift for story telling.I don't usually even play games with this style of gameplay, but they really did it flawlessly. The controller mapping works perfectly too without any issues on my PC-Xbox controller.I love the resurgence of this graphical style, it works very well with the themes too as it leaves more to the imagination, we can often horrify ourselves better than the most visceral high-fidelity gore can anyway. It's a perfect mash of inspirations from all sorts of great art that ultimately synthesizes into a unique, beautiful homage rather than a cheap rip-off.The POV strangely transports us into the character themselves, thinking we are them and at least in my experience affecting how I played and engaged with the story. Which could lead to interesting twists and turns as the story unfolds. To me, this is the ultimate type of role-playing, not me with infinite choices, but me inhabiting the story of another for a time. I was transported outside of my normal life and lived for a beautifully short time as a member of this crew. Despite being in a very small, confined area with limited number of interact-able objects, they manage to tell a brilliant story with the set itself with time skips and a relatively smaller amount of exposition which is just gorgeously written (in the English version, I hope the translations do it justice).This type of story (including movies, books, etc) comes around only every once in a while. You owe it to yourself to experience it. Despite being a single linear story it even has decent replay value. Like a classic film, this one will age like a fine wine and one day this will be featured in whatever the equivalent of a current university "film studies" course will be.

_childDocuments_.review: MOUTHWASHINGSPOILER-FREE - I recommend going into this blind!Compared to its competition, "Mouthwashing" is well worth the price-tag if you're an experienced movie watcher / gamer looking for a tightly-wound sci-fi psych-horror / tragedy to occupy a weekend. Key Words : Surreal,  Tightly Wound, Character-DrivenDisclaimers : Strangely Of Our Time?Surreal : The imagery and scares in this game fully take advantage of the PSX aesthetics and digital medium. Spaces involute and symbols concatenate onto themselves until they become incoherent. This is a good picture of a mind breaking down, of memories intermixing and becoming something more terrifying than truth or fiction. This game is downright eerie. It's lovely in how it reincorporates and magnifies symbols until they are grotesque, dominating caricatures of themselves.Tightly-Wound: Both a plus and a minus. On the plus: This game does not waste your time. Every moment is meaningful, and there is nothing padded.On the minus: This game is about 3-5 hours long. At $14, you're basically buying a B-movie on Amazon to watch over and over.  Matinee in modern theater terms... but this B-movie is worth a rewatch or two. I doubt most people will see much replay value once they complete the main content unless it really resonates with them.Overall: You're paying for a interactive movie. This one happens to be worth watching.Strangely of Our Time? : It's set aboard a space ship governed by a dystopian corporate overlord. Perhaps this only applies to modern audiences (C.2024) but I've sort of seen enough of certain gameplay/horror gimmicks. We're oppressed by corporate overlords - what has changed? That's not horror....Or the scares: When I turn back, the hallway is different? The weird aesthetic where fleshy bits start to cover the walls like Dead Space? Moral ambiguity and black-as-pitch moral conclusions? This all seems like what Zoomers expect out of horror. I liked it, and it sort of worked, but it all felt in the boundaries of what to expect from a game these days...Character-Driven: What redeems "Mouthwashing" is ultimately its characters. However brief the game is, there are intricate and well-written relationships between each of the characters, and inside each of the characters themselves. You'll learn to care for and like each one of the people stranded on the Tulpar, though you may not love or forgive them. In the end, you'll at least understand them all. That's all I wanted out of this game, and it delivered.Conclusion:  I recommend it, though if your wallet is tight, I understand that $14 is a lot to ask given the length compared to a free AlphaBetaGamer Youtube video every 3 days for free. It's really worth the time if you can afford it, though - even 4 or 5 hours is worth the modern attention span. I personally loved it.

_childDocuments_.review: I would love to give this game a good review but i just cant. Let me start this review by discussing what i liked about it. I would also like to preface that this is MY OPINION. if you had a good experiance playing it than good for you! I am just expressing MY opinion on MY experiance with the game To start, the most notable thing about this game is the PS1 era inspires graphics mixed with the point and click style exploration games from the same era. The story is a unique take on  the "lost in space" genre of story telling without the presence of a scary monster. The soundtrack is also amazing. From the  ambient sounds to the music heard during certain parts of the game are all very fitting. Unfortunately this is where the praise ends.The actual story of Mouthwashing is very mediocre at best. I never truly felt connected enough to the characters to actually care about what was happening to them. The story progression is very quick not allowing time to connect to the characters or the setting of the game. Continuing on about the story. It is very all over the place. Never taking part in one exsisting moment for more than maybe 10 minutes of gameplay. The setting of the game is very tiny and extremely linear not allowing for much exploration. The exploration that is granted isnt very rewarding usually just being empty rooms with nothing to interact with or anything to tell us more about the world we are in. After my playthrough i had to watch numerous videos on the lore of the game and still felt unsatisfied with the lore. Probably because i wasnt given enough time to really connect with anyone or anything. This game is maybe a 45 minute playthrough, but there is just sooo much BS that is there probably to pad runtime. I can count on 2 hands the amount of times i felt the game was padding for runtime. The puzzles in the game are not at all difficult and take maybe 10 seconds to figure out. Now sure maybe the puzzles arent the center focus of the game, but the story isnt offering up much either. I have a runtime of 2 hours purely for the shear amounts of padding in this game. Another thing id like to discuss is the dialog. It just feels very bland and meh. After reading all these positive reviews i was expecting some amount of deep lore, character development, and world building. None of which i got. This game never made me feel uneasy, scared, stressed, sad, happy, etc. I had no emotions playing this game. I can tell that there was a lot of thought and care that went into making this game, but i just didnt feel that love or care. The replayablility of this game is none. Once you beat the game once the enjoyment kinda ends there. Which is sad to say. The story will always be the same every playthrough without the element of surprise of whats to come next. The story just feels all over the place taking place at what feels like random points in time. This game was kind of annoying to play. I genuinely wish i could  recommend this game. (Edit): I would also like to mention that point and click games rely heavily on exploration, dialog, and story telling due to the lack of actual gameplay. I feel this game falls short in all 3 categories.TLDR; Decent story, nostalgic graphics, other than that did not enjoy my playthrough and cant recommend

_childDocuments_.review: I am not a horror or even really narrative game enjoyer. In spite of this, I was on the edge of my seat while playing Mouthwashing, and the game left me thinking for hours, even days after. The game has a memorable cast of characters, by the end of the game you have a very good insight into what motivates them and makes them tick. The graphics are intentionally retro, reminiscent of PS1 games, however they are used very effectively to generate tension and apprehension throughout the game. Coupled with excellent sound design, the atmosphere of the game is both bleak and terrifying.There is limited actual gameplay (it's a point and click walking simulator for 90% of the game) and it is, in many sections, more like an interactive movie. However, that interactivity drives much of the story. Rather than merely watching the events of the game take place, you are in the driver's seat. You are powerless to stop the various tragedies of the story, you can only press on as it unfolds. While there is nothing you as the player can do to alter the fate of the Tulpar and her crew, you still feel responsible.Take responsibility.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILER WARNING (i am so sorry everyone, ive just seen the comments)What a beautifully horrific experience.When it comes to depicting sexual assault in media, so many tend to glorify it, to show the act for shock, make it some sort of revenge story for the victim, showcasing it was necessary for character development. But Mouthwashing does none of that. Anya is a terrific character, not falling into the tropes of revenge hungry or timid and shy, but simply a woman who is trying to survive. Who is aware of the situation she is in, of the man who could snap at anytime and tries to act accordingly. Despite what Jimmy and perhaps the rest of the crew thinks, she's smart. She's one step ahead, hiding the gun from Jimmy because she has seen him at his worst, keeping Curly alive with scraps of medicine.And without showing the assault happen, we see how this has affected her. The noises Curly makes reminding her of what happened, seeing someone choke and struggle to move due to lack of autonomy. Her attitude around Jimmy, carefully planning out what to say as to not set him off. And of course, the baby. The baby she does not want, trying to figure out ways to get rid off it. Alcohol (mouthwash) can't guarantee termination. waiting is not an option at all, and so she takes care of it by killing herself too, because she could not see any other way. That is a reality for many women. And that is pure horror.And of course, the discussion around rape culture. How (predominantly) men will protect their rapist friends for whatever reason (they don't believe the victim, deep inside their friend is still a good person etc), and we see how protecting an abusers leads to more harm down the line, even to their own "friends." And when you protected them, and now you are the one being harmed (by said friend or someone else entirely), whose to say you'll be saved? Be believed? They'll use the same talking points you did "I can fix this", "I'll talk to him", and now you have no one. But all of that could have been avoided. If you had taken responsibility in the first place.I ranted a tad sorry but this game is so amazing I don't think anything i say will do it justice.

_childDocuments_.review: Before anything else: it's at least three hours long, and worth  one replay. Gameplay is simple puzzles and navigation, but the narrative's a good one you'll doubtless find relatable if you're someone who's experienced or been exposed to any level of ♥♥♥♥ Life Syndrome. Even off sale, it's $13USD, which is about how much a movie ticket is anyway, and "at least three hours" is a long-ass movie. Definitely worth the price of admission.Anyway, if you're the type of person who likes gross games about flesh and humanity and horror and stuff, you'll probably like Mouthwashing.A slightly more detailed review follows:Aesthetically, it executes the "dithering-heavy vintage style" that some games have been doing lately quite well. Text you're not supposed to be reading outside of menus can be a little difficult to parse from some angles, but I never got sick of looking at the visuals. They manage to be quite expressive with texturework on the lower-poly models.Gameplay-wise, it's basically a visual novel with walkabout segments and the level/set design that goes along with that; Wrong Organ peppered details all over the place, so take your time and really comb your fingers through the viscera. As mentioned in the "it's worth it" at the top, gameplay also involves some simple puzzles and tense moments of timing; as far as I saw, you can't brick your run. (Though that might've been fun if it were possible.)Narratively, it's nonlinear and jumps from time point to time point, but each jump is marked by gigantic text and a sting so if you've lost track of where you are, that's sort of on you. There's a few twists in the narrative that I hadn't seen coming; one of them in particular comes to mind as a total perspective-changer, so if you want to play the game, go into it blind.Horror/Vibes-wise, it's claustrophobic atmosphere, interpersonal nightmare scenarios, the knowledge that this crowded bus stop bench's worth of people are  doomed in a  sense, gore/body horror, segments that call to mind the Invisible Water Monster from Amnesia (a positive comparison), and some tension-shaking jump scares.I didn't really care for the Mascot Horror, but it didn't get in the way of enjoying everything else about it. I just feel a little bit like "Cute Cartoon Mascot for Corporation" is well-trod ground in horror media these days, and the game's otherwise blisteringly, bloodily singular-feeling in other respects.

_childDocuments_.review: Using Mouthwash has become more than just a part of my oral hygiene routine; it’s a ritual of self-care that feels almost transcendent. The vibrant, refreshing flavor invites a moment of mindfulness, transforming a mundane task into a refreshing experience that awakens the senses.In our fast-paced lives, we often overlook the simple pleasures. Yet, each swish of this mouthwash serves as a gentle reminder to breathe deeply and appreciate the freshness that follows. It’s almost meditative—like a little pause in the chaos of the day.But then, oh, the true magic happens! It effectively combats bad breath, allowing me to engage with others confidently. _childDocuments_.review: Mouthwash, mouth rinse, oral rinse, or mouth bath is a liquid which is held in the mouth passively or swirled around the mouth by contraction of the perioral muscles and/or movement of the head, and may be gargled, where the head is tilted back and the liquid bubbled at the back of the mouth.Usually mouthwashes are antiseptic solutions intended to reduce the microbial load in the mouth, although other mouthwashes might be given for other reasons such as for their analgesic, anti-inflammatory or anti-fungal action. Additionally, some rinses act as saliva substitutes to neutralize acid and keep the mouth moist in xerostomia (dry mouth). Cosmetic mouthrinses temporarily control or reduce bad breath and leave the mouth with a pleasant taste.Rinsing with water or mouthwash after brushing with a fluoride toothpaste can reduce the availability of salivary fluoride. This can lower the anti-cavity re-mineralization and antibacterial effects of fluoride. Fluoridated mouthwash may mitigate this effect or in high concentrations increase available fluoride, but is not as cost-effective as leaving the fluoride toothpaste on the teeth after brushing. A group of experts discussing post brushing rinsing in 2012 found that although there was clear guidance given in many public health advice publications to "spit, avoid rinsing with water/excessive rinsing with water" they believed there was a limited evidence base for best practice.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like something people shouldn't be allowed to see (in a good way.)Watching this group of people fall apart in this claustrophobic space, watching each other tear themselves apart, collapsing under the weight of their situation... It arises fear I didn't know I could feel. The kind that lingers in the back of your mind, past the jump scares and gore. It's story, non-linear in nature, had me guessing about the structure of its timeline repeatedly, and it just genuinely intrigued me in a way most games fail to.Without getting too deep into spoilers, this game does non-linear storytelling really ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ good. I like how we hop from point to point at a seemingly random pace, but it gives us just enough information to put the pieces of the puzzle together. That mystery element made me confused at first, but had me discussing with friends and piecing together elements in our heads, creating new and possibly unintentional horror for us.I don't know if I really like or really hate (in a good way) the horror in this game, probably a mixture of both. The repulsive sound design and grotesque textures really give this game an atmosphere like no other. I've played quite a few PSX games, but none have hooked me with their visuals nearly as much as this one. The horror in this game is more than just your typical horror experience. The weight of my actions, especially in the second hour of the game, really started to make me want to put the game down. "I don't want to do this." It's really great when a game really makes you think about your decisions and their consequences, and it's even better when the game derives horror from our own actions, or actions we could have prevented. The monster designs here are really cool too, and one of them in particular made me jump in real life while trying to avoid it. I want to say that I wish the game was longer, but I feel like this game is almost better being a short experience. I got about 2 hours out of a single play through, and while I definitely have plans to play again soon to scout out achievements/secrets, it's still a crazy good experience that will stick with me for a long time.TL;DR: this game is way scarier than I had expected, and it's well worth the price and your time. Please check it out.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're reading this review before you buy, wait for it to be on sale because I cannot recommend buying this game above $8.Going into this game I was pretty excited. I had played the demo for it not too long ago and bought it pretty soon after it came out. I then quickly realized this game is really just a walking simulator: talk to character, get thing for character, talk to character again, repeat. The few times where the game actually has actual gameplay are just tedious.The story is told in a non-linear way. That's fine since the story isn't very difficult to follow. The problem is that inbetween story sections there are these nightmare sections that don't really add anything and I can assume only serve as padding or show spooky visuals that aren't really scary. They actually remind me a lot of the sections in the show evangelion that don't really do anything and just serve as padding because the studio was actively running out of money. Thankfully the story itself is actually good and the only reason I beat the game.The presentation of the game is nothing new at this point. The game has ps2 graphics which are fine and done well enough to be serviceable. Mouthwashing doesn't do anything particularly new with them however.In conclusion, the team has writing chops no doubt and they shine in Mouthwashing. I cannot however seriously recommend you buy it at its current price since all Mouthwashing has is a good story. Wait for a sale or better yet watch a letsplay.

_childDocuments_.review: The good:Visually the game is great. It's also quite spooky and doesn't rely on jumpscares at all. The story is entertaining and the way it is told is very mysterious and engaging. It's definitely fun to explore.The bad:The game has many parts that seem to be blatantly designed to extend playtime and nothing else. Namely with vague quests, ridiculously long hallways (not just done as a one time spOOky long hallway but several times). One sequence where you are chased by an invisible monster also takes way too long (a good 10 minutes or so) and just becomes tedious and boring as opposed to scary as a result. And the story doesn't make a whole lot of sense when put under scrutiny. Most of the story needs to be explained with "The character is just crazy! That's why he did those things!" rather than the character's actions actually making sense. I won't go into details as I don't want to spoil. Also, it's a spooky story, not really a horror game. If you're looking to actually get scared at a horror game you should probably look elsewhere.The game definitely isn't bad, it's qualitatively good, but the issues above kept me from enjoying it and I would not recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: While this game has a lot of good going on, and is definitely better than many low-budget horror games, I can't help but feel it didn't hit the exact spot it could've for a more impactful story, and for well... more pain, more hurting, as it wants to do so much (It hopes this hurts). it's a decent experience, but at the end of the game I felt a bit disappointed from what I expected. It feels a little unfinished, or rushed overall, especially for its price. Maybe because the team was either out of resources, or something else, I wouldn't know. I don't recommend it for this price currently, wait rather for a good sale. We follow the story of a stranded crew aboard the Tulpar, one of the last human-manned cargo ship of the Pony Express company. We get to witness, and, well (and this is kinda important to the story) their last days together. somewhat one of the game's strongest points behind the visuals, dialogue, and SFX, is a story that is fragmented "achronologically" (with flash backs & forward, while also switching to straight up hallucinations). This makes it more complicated to figure out what is going on, which is good for the sake of making the player confused like the crew is. This kinda forces 2 runs of the game to really understand everything and the details too.  My biggest complain is a lack of introductory phase for the game here. The little you get of the story and characters is good, but too fast-paced to really "feel" the dread and pain everyone is going through. The first time I just kind of phased through it a bit like the fever dream it is. If I would've cared more about the characters, their more meaningful and philosophical dialogue that we get could've been way more significant, and I would have been definitely more invested... and hurt. At the point it currently is, the characters are really just tools to deliver the story's themes and messages, and I think they could've been a little more than that... An idea I had would've been for example a section before the "crash", which is a chronologically-led segment that would introduce more softly the drama of the game and its characters, to ground the players in something more concrete, and that would allow for a stronger shock when things go down. The game could've also added maybe a fake drama for its "huis-clos" aspect, of something weird going on in the ship, maybe a fake "monster aboard"-to-amp-up-the-paranoia situation that twists after to what the game is really about. I feel this could've also matched well with the theme of "our worst moments don't define us, right?" when talking about monsters... are just amazing, there's a real sense of cinematography, photography, and so on. I have no comment other than bravo for that, this is what makes me like the game so much. The lines delivered hit really well, while staying mostly true to its characters. Props to SFX too! Also I really liked the monsters designs, too bad the gameplay linked to them is where the true horror is... is kind of almost inexistant, and it's where the ludonarration (ie. where gameplay is an extension of story and themes, in other words it makes sense to choose that gameplay over another for the content) feels a little off. While the fact that this story is delivered through a game makes sense for a good part about its theme of "taking responsibility", and the player is forced to makes the characters' "choices" or actions, and thus, taking responsibility (and the suffering) in their place; a good part of the walking around, monster encounters, and such just don't make much sense with what the game is about. I feel it could've been fleshed out a little more and made more relevant. But also straight up just some parts that are relevant to the game feel also a bit uninspired, like your repetitive gore-filled-corridors, or walls with eyes and such.I could talk more about the story and what I've thought of it, I think it's pretty good with how it handles its themes and such. And it makes me really want to put the pieces together chronologically with everything that happens, but I'm sure someone else will do that. Also CURLY DID NOTHING WRONG. And F*CK YOU, JIMMY.Thank you for reading all that. Let me know what you think too. Do you agree?

_childDocuments_.review: I had high expectations after the joys of How Fish Is Made. I could not have expected.... this. I don't know if it's the hyper-surreal-amazing trip a lot of the other reviews claim for it, but it IS compelling & uses the fact that it's a video game well. The tension in a linear game (& any game really) is that player choice is within a strict framework; there are things you must do to progress the story. I found myself dreading actions, but if I wanted to see the game, I had to do them. This is a side tangent, but this is why I've never understood complaints about games being "too linear." Games aren't a substitute for the infinite possibilities of reality; they're a game-framework where the pleasure comes from learning how to properly interface to progress. A game with infinite choices is a completely blank sudoku puzzle & that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ boring. Anyway, I say all that to say: Mouthwashing gets that right. It couldn't be a movie because the player has to do awful things if they want to experience the story & I find that an amazing tension as I felt genuine self-conflict about my actions here. So, if you can stomach some rather gruesome stuff & are game for an intense story (think: The Lighthouse but 5 people instead of 2), this is a must.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is an experience unlike any other I dare say. I've enjoyed so many horror experiences over the years. Decades even. I think only a few things could compare to it. S.O.M.A. comes to mind but the more I digest of the game(Which I just finished playing a few hours ago), I think this is more. The horror you experience is incredible. I wouldn't say there are jump scares, but there are times where I was freaked the ♥♥♥♥ out. This is a deep dive in how horrible humanity can be. This is set in the future, you're on a space ship in space, but the troubles that come could happen anywhere. When everything goes wrong, and wrong, and wrong it seems as though there is no hope. We are entitled to the lies we tell ourselves that it will all be okay. We avoid the truth, and we refuse to face responsibility for our actions or our inaction. To do is just as damning than to do not. This isn't a game for those that are easily affected. Though, I dare say those that encounter those dark moments when Depression is the only monster in our lives, you might find yourself having a dark chuckle a few times, while embracing the truth of it all.Normally I'm a game that enjoys a game's length equal to the price, but this one. Don't sleep on it. Go in blind. Stream to friends or don't. It will be nice to have other minds along with you for this ride. It's incredible. While I am still processing what happened, I'm glad to have played it. A lot of people seek horror for the fear of it, the excitement, the wanting to feel alive without the danger of death. All these reasons are good ones for playing Mouthwashing, but sometimes to see the light of life, you need to see the depths of the darkness. Sink right into it.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing takes players into a psychological space horror set on the doomed freighter spaceship Tulpar, where a routine mission spirals into a slow-burn nightmare. The crew, comprised of Captain Curly, co-pilot Jimmy, medic Anya, mechanic Swansea, and last-minute intern Daisuke, are stranded following a crash on an asteroid. With the captain incapacitated and supplies dwindling, an unlikely and tension-filled power struggle ensues. And when they open their precious cargo.... a shipment of mouthwash... the desperate circumstances begin to unravel relationships and reveal dark truths among the crew. But while Mouthwashing offers strong character writing, the game itself ultimately falls flat for me in several areas.At first glance, the game seems promising with its eerie, tension-filled premise. Its minimalist, retro-inspired graphics help set the tone for sure, capturing that claustrophobic, isolated feeling in space where every decision could mean survival or ruin. Yet, despite the retro appeal, the visual design isn't particularly novel, leaving an impression of "style over substance." For those who enjoy this type of atmosphere, it can provide an unsettling ambiance, but players accustomed to genre-defining titles might find it lacks a true WOW factor. It’s good, but doesn’t really push any boundaries.The real draw to Mouthwashing is the characters. Wrong Organ has clearly put thought into their backstories, personalities, and moral complexities, creating a cast with enough depth to make the survival horror plot feel grounded in real human fear and conflict. Jimmy, the acting captain, particularly shines with a personality that draws you in, even if it’s far from likeable. His choices, flaws, and dark descent are intriguing to watch unfold, and there’s a certain subtlety to the character interactions that makes them feel genuine, even amidst the horrific setting.That said, Mouthwashing’s gameplay is limited and lacks real tension-building mechanics, making it feel less like a survival horror game and more like an interactive story. As a result, the game doesn't offer the kind of engaging strategic decisions or tense exploration moments that I expected. Rather than being an immersive experience, it feels more like a static stage where characters perform their lines, without enough challenge or interactivity to support the atmosphere.This game comes with a LOT of hype from fans who praise its dark narrative and retro look, but I found those elements more "interesting" than "incredible." Mouthwashing does excel at telling a quick self-contained story, and those looking for something short and darkly intriguing might appreciate it. But I would caution new players: take the buzz with a grain of salt and avoid expecting anything groundbreaking. You’re unlikely to experience jaw-dropping revelations or high-stakes tension here. This isn’t a story where the plot grips you so much as the characters do.A final note about the fandom: I've noticed a pattern of fixation on certain characters, often reducing them to simple archetypes while ignoring the deeper, sometimes uncomfortable questions about their actions and motivations. Unfortunately, there seems to be a lack of nuance in these interpretations which can detract from meaningful discussion around the story's themes. It can be frustrating to see such a limited analysis from fans, especially for a game that actually has some complex layered character writing if you take the time to unpack it.In summary... Mouthwashing has well-developed characters and a unique story, but it doesn’t break new ground. If you’re looking for a compelling survival horror experience, you might leave disappointed. The writing keeps it from being a complete miss, but the lack of impactful gameplay combined with an overhyped reputation, left me wanting more. Ultimately, I’d recommend this for a casual playthrough if you’re curious, but I wouldn’t call it a must-play in the genre.Overall: Not recommended. Approach with an open mind, and you may still find something to enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugh, here we are again wishing for a 'mixed feelings' button. If I were to have to sum up my feelings about 'Mouthwashing' in 4 words for the 4 hours it takes to play through the game, they would have to be "stunning start, flames out". The setup for the game is so compelling - the time jumps, the changes of viewpoint as you play different characters, the excellent audio and strong visual style - that I was really set to give Wrong Organ my full attention after the disappointment that was 'How Fish Is Made', their debut title which despite ultimately leaving me cold showed a huge amount of promise in its grasp of unsettling aesthetics and body horror. And for a while, it really delivers.Sadly the final hour or so of 'Mouthwashing' saw my interest and patience fall off a cliff. There's some cheap videogame tricks and tropes which I've come to think of as 'Blooberisms': spatial distortions, endless corridors, turning around to find things different... if you've played many games by Bloober Team then you know the drill. They have a very limited bag of tricks and they overuse them heavily (I suspect they only did so well on the Silent Hill 2 remake because they were closely supervised) and lots of them show up here. The intrigue of what actually happened to the crew of the Tulpar and how things will turn out gets lost as the game bogs down in a lot of vapid psychedelia and the kind of adolescent miserablism that put 'How Fish Is Made' into the unfortunate 'profound or pretentious?' box. As with the various NPC fish in that game, some characters in 'Mouthwashing' will often drop into streams of dialogue that feel less like they flesh out the nature of the cast and more as deliveries of the writer's nebulously morose personal philosophy. I've nothing against games being depressing, dark or bleak, but it needs a deft touch to avoid coming across as emo moping or edgelord nihilism. A friend who also played through wondered if they were missing some hidden subtext, but on reflection I would have to say no, there is none. It's a game in the same vein as a movie like 'Martyrs' - its relentless bleakness might seem like it's saying something about the human condition, but it's actually as existentially meaningful as black nail polish.

_childDocuments_.review: mouthwashing is a surreal story about what it means to be human and what it means to be alive. this game plays with chronology in such a beautiful way, you will be left on the edge of your seat for the entire three hour run time. im going to try and keep this review short and spoiler-free because i truly think this game is best experienced in one sitting with no outside knowledge.mouthwashing is a non-linear lynchian story game about the members of the Tulpar ship, and their descent into madness as their ship suffers damage following a crash and their resources dwindle. at first, i thought this game was very cut and dry; im a big fan of story games that, on a second playthrough, make you realise the foreshadowing and contextualise the game in a completely different light. knowing what has happened and what will happen to a character can change the way you see their actions and change the way you overall view them. after my first playthrough, i initially thought that the story was rigid; characters were clear in their personalities, twists didnt change the way i would think about characters, and it felt like i didnt miss a single detail. but on a second and then third playthrough, as well as deep analysis, im so pleased to say that i was entirely wrong. these characters are beautifully tragic and perfectly flawed (even you, jimmy), and i feel like with every closer look, im more and more suprised about the true depth this game, its world and its characters have. i promise you that this game is more than worth its full price, and will easily give you several replays worth of time. i can see myself revisiting this game every few months.i feel less inclined to speak about the music and art direction, but even as someone who is untrained in these areas, theyre both incredibly stunning. this game really made me fall in love with ps1 style horror, a genre i previously thought was pretty tacky and talentless. this game uses the restriction of low polygon count to create something eerily nostalgic and claustrophobic for a time period ive never lived through and a fear i dont have. and the music is just as impressive, with a few catchy beats spread throughout (that main menu theme is something else...) its primarily ambient music, its so well produced and fits so snugly into a scene you dont even realise its playingto put a long review short, this game is incredible. it makes me thrilled to see it garner the attention that it deserves, and i promise you, the price tag is more than worth it. while some people may hear a 3-hour length game as slightly disappointing, i promise you this game doesnt waste a second with anything it doesnt need to push the story forward, ultimately leaving you with far more questions than answers, a chill down your spine, and characters you will laugh and cry with.

_childDocuments_.review: I absolutely hate giving mouthwashing a negative recommendation but I can't give it a far more appropriate mixed review. This is a game with so much heart and such an excellent grasp of what makes sci-fi tick that it's physically painful to criticise it as harshly as I'm about to. It's without a doubt one of the prettiest games I've played this year and it manages to maintain its top-tier atmosphere from start to finish. In only 2-ish hours the cast is somehow more interesting and striking than the majority of "character driven" narratives. With these in mind, I hope you can understand how the incredibly moving and poignant story that's buried under piles of played out, repetitive trite means I cannot in good conscience give a thumbs up.It is impossible to understate how badly mouthwashing fumbles the single best foundation for a horror game I've ever seen. What would be through-lines or a simple background themes in a better game are, one after the other, turned into bats the writers bash your head in with. Mouthwashing offers the unique experience of the single dumbest double entendre turning from far too stupid to actually be intentional to the main theme of the entire thing. It feels like it desperately wants to examine responsibility from several angles, almost all of which are either botched, hilariously misplaced or, most commonly, under-explored to the point of turning into lip-service. However i can't fault it too much for the latter, as it is a small 2-hour indie game......Considering the runtime, the amount of padding present is a marvel of modern game design. You could genuinely compare the filler ratio of mouthwashing to naruto shippuden. It's gorgeous filler, don't get me wrong, I was genuinely awe-struck at some of the set-pieces. The problems begin and end with such extravagant scenes being present in such an otherwise underdeveloped story. In the exact same vein, the sparse but consistently under-cooked "gameplay" sections could be removed and nothing of value would have been lost. Every single step mouthwashing takes away from a simple point & click game or a walking simulator is to its detriment and shifts focus away from where the dev team shines the brightest.The potential ren.py version of this game will haunt my dreams for months. I'll have forgotten about the real thing by next week.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is one of the most deeply disturbing games I have personally ever played. It gives a very interesting approach to writing a psychological horror story. I appreciate how human the characters feel. Curly wants whats best for everyone but unintentionally makes things worse for some, Anya is struggling as she goes through abuse, Daisuke wants to see the good in things despite suffering himself, Swansea wants to help Daisuke but he has such a harsh attitude, Jimmy is a disgusting human who takes his anger out on everyone else on the ship and uses physical violence when angry (He's also Anya's abuser). These are all people you'd find in real life, weather you like it or not, I appreciate how the characters don't feel stiff and actually have so much depth. I recommend this game to anyone looking for an amazing story, unique graphics, and anyone who enjoys psychological horror because man was this game a roller coaster of emotions, but instead of going up, it just kept going down.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is one of the best games I've ever played, period. I'm not one to write very serious reviews, but for this game, I'm making an exception.This game has an incredibly heartwrenching and multilayered story that stayed with me for a while. Honestly, I still keep thinking about it, even though it's been weeks since I finished my first playthrough. The amount of symbolism and foreshadowing cannot be caught in one go. It made me think and theorize, and to this day I still occasionally make connections to certain events and characters that I didn't notice previously. The story is told in a non-linear manner, but it's not too hard to follow, and kept me on my toes the entire time. Each time one chapter ended and the game jumped to another point in the timeline, I was eagerly waiting to see how things unfolded, and just how bad can it really get.Mouthwashing has a fantastic atmosphere too. The spaceship the story takes place in is incredibly cramped and claustrophobic, there's no natural light, and the music and general sound design is immaculate. Definitely best played with headphones in my opinion. The environments and characters don't look realistic, but that's part of the charm. The PS1-esque models are amazing and make this game stand out among the rest. Curly's design is so raw and distressing despite the graphics, and really made me feel bad for him. His sound design is rather disturbing as well, which I really like.Despite being a horror game, Mouthwashing doesn't rely on jumpscares for the horror, it instead comes from the terrifying situation the crew of the Tulpar are trapped in. There is no alien monster to run from, no fighting for survival, only the realization that the people you thought you could trust can turn into vile, twisted monsters out of desperation and jealousy. It's a very tragic and hopeless story, and also terribly human.Considering that the game is only roughly 2 hours long, the developers and writers did an extremely good job making sure that nothing overstays its welcome and nearly every line the characters say has some meaning behind it. Within these 2 hours, the game managed to make me care for the characters, and understand their motivations and personality. Everyone feels realistic, none of them are some sort of comic book type heroes that can overcome any obstacle. These are just ordinary people that could be your friends, your coworkers, your family members, and none of them are perfect, just like in real life.I urge you, if you have a little bit of time to spare, give this game a shot. It is incredibly good, and one of the best indie horror games of recent times.

The visuals are warped, surreal, and somehow laced with queer undertones—rainbows bleed into sinister hues, the men are just so hot omg, glitter turns to dullness, and the toothbrushes seems to wink at you. As a very obviously queer gamer, I felt oddly seen in the game’s blend of flamboyant absurdity and creeping horror. I mean we all know this is an LGBTQ+ paradise of a game. It’s as if the game knows the gay drama we live for and twists it into a dazzlingly terrifying reflection of self-care gone wrong. MouthWashing is a fever dream, and I love every terrifyingly fabulous moment.

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing (2024) Review“Pain is how we know we're still living.”Mouthwashing is a mesmerizing, terrifying, and intimate horror drama. The title may seem initially strange, but that's a part of its magic. Its terror thrives on oddity and insanity, while its humanity shines through its deftly written main cast. Additionally, the atmosphere is powerfully uncomfortable and maintains the ability to change the mood from chill to scary with the snap of a finger. Clearly, Mouthwashing is a fascinating three hour horror drama.The story revolves around the crew of the Tulpar, who are left stranded after its unfortunate crash on an asteroid. Much of Mouthwashing’s drama and horror centers around its five crew members. All their personalities and backstories are fleshed out, perfectly placed for the carnage to come. As a result of the cast’s adequate development, the story is able to create friction between these characters. All of them have their own goals and they clash like ice and fire. This is where the true terror of Mouthwashing lies, God and the Devil’s great battlefield, the human heart.The themes of Mouthwashing are also satisfyingly handled. Indeed, there is a lot to unpack here, from insanity, responsibility, and the plight of the working class. All of them are tackled with the maturity needed for this kind of story, being used sufficiently to invoke inner anxieties within the player. Besides, what’s scarier than working a 9-5 job without the promise of salvation from capitalism? The source of its dread is immediately recognizable and irrefutably relatable.The gameplays is minimal and could be described more as a walking simulator. Granted, there is an item menu reminiscent of Silent Hill, but this is no survival horror game. The player will be tasked to walk from one room to the next, talking to the crew and solving puzzles to save the day. You get to do birthday parties and maintenance repairs. The gameplay isn’t groundbreaking, but it works really well.The graphics are also fantastic, they play into the horror mood pretty well. It has PS1 graphics and may feel nostalgic to those attached to that time.  Since the game has minimal interaction, the power of its horror relies heavily on the visuals. Hence, Mouthwashing has much visual splendor, scaring its players with abstract and creepy imagery that will stick with me for a while.Thought provoking and dreadful, Mouthwashing is an essential classic horror story that preys on the fears of the modern working man. It has the visuals and atmosphere of a Silent Hill game accompanied with the thoughtfulness of many great horror writers. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: ***ORIGINAL REVIEW AFTER FIRST PLAYTHRU***This was a difficult one to review. I have been looking forward to this game for a long time, and it is clear a lot of love and effort has gone into the game. However to say it left me disappointed is an understatement. There are some genuinely creepy elements, the aesthetic and sound work are top notch, but the gameplay itself is slow and uninspired and the story has, in my opinion, been over hyped. Telling a straightforward story non-sequentially does not make the resultant story more interesting. It just makes it harder to follow. The game also has very few horror elements (there are a handful of jump scares,  ) and some of the more egregious examples present, detract from the overall experience - A large part of the horror comes from hallucinations  Some of these hallucinations are genuinely disturbing, whilst others were flat out boring and did little to push the story along. And this is why it gets a thumbs down from me. It appeared to me that sections were heavily padded to push the runtime over 2 hours and thus fall out of the Steam refund policy. A single play through is going to clock in a little over 2 hours. Given I was on the fence to recommend, this padding drags out uninteresting parts of the game, and hits the pacing as a result.  I would have felt more comfortable recommending a tighter game. As it is I couldn't and wouldn't recommend this game to anyone. You won't find much unless you are a huge fan of psychological horror, and even then you have to look hard to find that. If you are scared of eyeballs, maybe go for it.***UPDATED***This game has lived rent free in my head for the last few days. I've chopped and changed my mind on certain plot points and am still not entirely convinced regarding anything with 100% certainty, but have come away with a view that makes sense for me.I stand by the points regarding padding and the "game" itself. But the story is worth the price of admission. Any story that keeps me up til late, a number of nights in a row must have something going for it. So I've updated my review to recommend. I'M TAKING RESPONSIBILITY

_childDocuments_.review: The strengths of Mouthwashing is that it doesn't babysit its players. Explicit imagery is mostly absent and besides just one scene is never shown. The game cuts to black screen and let's player imagine the scene for themselves, with only the sounds to guide them. Mouthwashing features nice artstyle, but its graphics are not its strongest part. Even if they were, the decision to not show brutality feels much more tasteful as the game doesn't rely on shock factor as a cheap selling point. As it comes to the story, the game does the same and leaves parts to be figured out. Some dialogues are omitted and you can understand the meaning with the context alone.Unfortunately, it is how this style of directing becomes one of Mouthwashing's weaknesses also. After playing the game for 2 times now I felt like there were things we don't get to hear about. In the Q&A Wrong Organ did mention some peculiar facts about their characters, and these facts are actually important for character development: like Anya failing to get into medical school  (we only get to know that she didn't study there) or Daisuke actually hating his internship (Daisuke states many times that he likes it here, and his actions never prove otherwise). These things should've been left in the game.On smaller scale, it felt weird when characters would be talking, then screen would cut to black and them we get to learn what just happened from context. It's like minute pieces of dialogues being torn out for no apparent reason, as if one or two sentences would bore player so much they would stop playing.On bigger scale, Mouthwashing suggests a lot. I am dumb to hints, so I didn't figure out that - apparently - one of the characters was . The game leaves you with only bits of information but I had a hard time connecting them.  fits here very well and explains a lot of characters' behavior, but the suggestion is very vague. After watching a few playthroughs I know it's not just me who missed it. I am conflicted as to what to conclude: it's either that the story just isn't clear enough or I am dumb. Really, what's the value of hiding the plot from the player? What does it achieve?It's a pity that a lot of horror moments for some reason revolve around a pony mascot. Characters working for Pony Express company has nothing to do with the themes of Mouthwashing. It just feels cheap when horror with such heavy themes and implications wastes time on "oh no, I've gone mad and now cartoon horse scares me". Mouthwashing slightly touches upon capitalism and how all characters are affected by , but the story doesn't elaborate on it in any meaningful way. It sucks, but it is not a tragedy. And if it is, I never was given a reason to care as much as Jimmy who spouts his frustrations onto captain Curly.Because the game switches timelines, some inconsistencies follow: like the sanity of Curly.  I also don't understand why one of the crew would prioritize getting paid to survival, initially calling that idea to search for resources in cargo room stupid and more dangerous than dying. It is especially weird when it already took them 2 whole months to start considering opening the cargo room in the first place.  These inconsistencies really affect the believability of the story.I was also disappointed we got to see Curly's face. I think it would be so much more impactful if we didn't and the only picture of him we would have in our minds is him completely mutilated. I think it would've left a sour taste in my mouth after playing.So far it seems like I didn't enjoy the game, but that's not true. I liked Mouthwashing and for someone's second game it is simply astonishing. They managed to create an engaging cinematic experience. With non-linear narrative player always jumps between different time-lines and always wonders what happened in between and what did they miss. Some people call this style Tarantino-eaque, but I think they're downplaying his work that way. That way of storytelling is just interesting, but there isn't anything extraordinary but the fact of 2 timelines that meet at one point in time.Visual style of Moutheashing is also interesting. Cartoonish, but detailed in faces - the most important part here.Personally, I was sold on game's music. Can't say a lot. Main theme is just right.And then there's the big question. Do our weakest moments make us a monster? The game is trying to solve it in an interesting way. Normally, with all the problems the story of this game has I would leave a negative review but I liked Mouthwashing strong enough not to do so. It truly deserves better.
