_childDocuments_.review: Everything about this game is great. The graphics, the storytelling, and the characters. One of the best aspects of the game is that it can be interpreted in many different ways, and the characters are so multifaceted that you can decide how wrong or right you think some characters' actions are. This game leaves a lot of room for thought and speculation without being confusing. Would Recommend.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is an extremely dark narrative driven game about a group of five crew-mates who are stranded in space after one of them crashes the ship.If you like games with an emphasis on the story while the gameplay takes a backseat, I think you'll enjoy this game a lot. The characters are extremely well written, the situation they find themselves in is frightening and the story is told in a way that allows you to intuitively piece everything together if you pay attention.Whilst the game is short (it takes a little over two hours to see the end of the story), it *will* leave you with a sense of dread that won't go away any time soon. If you're in the mood to play something that handles heavy themes, I heavily recommend this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This game was absolutely phenomenal. Met all my expectations.10/10!now that all that boring stuff is over, let me say what makes mouthwashing so good.1. The horror is amazing. Only like 3 cheap jump scares and the rest is atmosphere and good game design.2. The characters are absolutely amazing! All of them have beautiful personalities and it makes them so memorable and real.3. The game design is just overall great, it’s beautiful and simple, you can see the art style everywhere and it doesn’t really get old or boring.4. It’s only 10 quid.5. The twist is GODLY. ABSOLUTELY AMAZING. I’m quite perceptive, and I didn’t even expect it!6. The game is just amazing. It doesn’t pull any weird stuff like intergalactic aliens or super powers, it’s just so real. All of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game about 4 people in a ship locked in with a monster.Its a horrific story that just kept me captivated the entire time, the only issue i have with the game is around near the late game  despite that i'd call the game a 9/10. Its a story that is going to stick with me for a long... LONG while
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I've been seeing this game around the internet for a while but had no idea what it's about, other then curly and something to do with mouthwash, so i decided to try it out not knowing anything really. I finished this game the day i started and the more in more i played i got sucked into the story and realizing how dark this game really is, this game has to be the most disturbing and yet beautiful way to describe depravity and the horrors of human nature, I've never stared at my screen with such despair and discomfort before, this game is a true masterpiece and is one of the best psychological horrors I've ever played, i hope this hurts.definitely recommended, if you want a gameplay that will stick with you for a while, for better or for worse
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is like stepping into a psychological car wash where the soap is existential dread, and the dryer is existential dread… but louder. It’s gross, it’s stressful, and it has all the subtlety of Kubrick meeting Star Trek in a dimly lit, slightly nauseating corner of space. And yet, somehow, it’s one of the best games I’ve played.Imagine the writers of The Shining and Star Trek: TNG getting locked in a room and asked to create a story about "being a good captain." What they came up with is an experience that’s more tension than terror and somehow leaves you both horrified and vaguely inspired. The tight, bleak story beats and its heartwarming message—buried somewhere deep under layers of unsettling visuals—are worth every second of its short, intense 2.5-hour runtime.It’s best to go into this with as little info as possible. Just a heads-up: don’t eat during gameplay (trust me on this). Grab it, clear an evening, and prepare to be mildly traumatized in the best possible way
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: really great! the story, the graphics, the writing, the music, etc, were all incredible! my only complaint was the horror-run-from-spooky-guy sections felt tedious. while i couldnt really connect to the themes i thought they were very interesting. this was a really good use of video games a medium for a story. i don't have much else to say, go buy it! only ~2hrs long so not a big commitment
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: my goty and not even close. perfect sound design amazing writing not a single bad aspect of this game. horrifying too! must play if you are into horror, and/or if you like good writing. indie horror has been almost exclusively terrible since the birth of the mascot horror genre, but with a publishing powerhouse like critical reflex, and an amazing devteam such as wrong organ, we are genuinely so back.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: An incredible game that highlights the deterioration of a person's humanity (or shows the true colours of a person) in an increasingly morbid situation. The characters were all very interesting in their own ways and the game uses non-linear storytelling in a startling yet fun format. That format allows the game to leave a lot of the story up to interpretation which can make players feel at unease in the best way.Most of the game is very narratively driven, but there are some parts with puzzle and thriller elements. They were a nice change of pace, without distracting from the main gameplay experience.Overall!! I'd highly recommend this game to anyone looking for a short but intriguing horror game.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing has altered my brain's chemistry.This game is like if modern psychological horror was actually good. I 100% recommend playing this with no spoilers or knowledge going in. I wishlisted it awhile ago since I just love all horror but my expectations were absolutely blown away. I don't usually write long reviews or anything because I have issues with articulating my feelings correctly but anyone reading this HAS to play it.  The writing for the characters is just absolutely amazing and I felt real care and empathy for every single one of them. 10/10 game, the monologue in utility made me tear up.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I knew these guys can make a good game after playing their previous little gem. But Mouthwashing has exceeded all of my expectations and then some!I genuinely think this is the best indie horror of 2024. Maybe even the last few years.I can't think of one thing that I dislike about it, so I'll just give it a well deserved 10/10
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I am a little ♥♥♥♥♥ and hardly ever actually play horror games but this game looked so appealing to me so a bought it at full price and I'm glad I did. One of the best things I've played in a while, the story is so amazing and every single part of this game feels so well thought out. Short but so amazing. 10/10 ♥♥♥♥ YOU JIMMY
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This horror game does an amazing job at filling you with dread. The story is told out of order as you slowly piece together what happened. I love the small details of each character and how they're dynamics work together. Nobody in the ship is perfect, but "I have to believe that our worst moments don't make us monsters."
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Me and Jesse's cousin went to the Chevron after work to grab a couple sixers and some beefy jerk. The man behind the counter said he'd like to see ID. I handed one of a guy who sorta looked like me. He frowned and asked me what was my address. I knew the street, but I couldn't quite get the rest. I said I'd lost my real ID and that we would pay him double. We swore we weren't cops and that he wouldn't get in trouble. He smiled and said "I'm sorry, but it's already 12:04. And the state says it's too late to sell alcohol anymore". Sadly we went to put back the beer, but then a bottle caught my eye and I got an idea. Then this happened.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Spoiler free review:Good things about Mouthwashing:-Interesting story, good suspense and mystery (until you figure out or see the twist, more details in second part)-Obviously people will look at is game length and can think its too short, but imo its perfect movie length and it tells its story that time-No screamers, huge respect to dev for that-Great sound design, carries horror aspect really hard-Visuals conveyed whats going on at each stage really wellNot so good things:-Few later sections (which come in a row one after another) while kinda made sense, didnt really fit into the game. They are well done, but i feel like they could have been removed and nothing would have been lost. But again, respect to dev for experimenting and trying to do something -Story turns out to be slightly disappointing, ending makes sense at least and fits the gameOverall still recommend to anyone who wants well done  intriguing horror mystery game
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended to me by a friend, with a playtime of just under 2 hours. I originally thought the $13 price was a bit too much.Beautiful and haunting; left me emotionally distraught in some places. There are moments of pure horror, both traditional and psychological; the realizations you come to as you get deeper into the game really hurt.I would advise avoiding this game if you are sensitive to the subjects of:I do not regret my purchase for this game, as long as the dev team gets the money to make more amazing stuff like this, they can take my entire wallet.Looking forward to seeing more stuff from the team.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: Gameplay poor, story good, not scary, did not hurt me  Based on the demo, I thought this would be a game about people slowly starving to death while consuming mouthwash. It wasn't. That's irrelevant to the quality of the game, but it was disappointing. Went in with very high expectations after the demo, reading rave reviews, and playing the masterpiece that was How Fish Is Made. Unfortunately, the game wasn't scary at all and elicited little emotion; even judging it as a story-based linear walking sim, it lacked in both surreal and psychological horror. In contast, How Fish Is Made immediately nailed me with dread. Most of the actual gameplay parts of the game were boring although a couple mini games were absolutely unique. The end of the game really dragged on and I (probably) see what they were going for, but it was very tedious. At that point it was already past the two hour mark so extending the gameplay was unnecessary. However, they spent just enough time developing the story, which is succinct and very clear. The characters are well-developed and charming. There is an excellent balance between hallucinations and reality, the concrete and the surreal. The voice acting is FANTASTIC and the audio detailed.Despite what I said I still played it 2.5 times. The .5 was spent in the Japanese and Korean versions and the translations were good. Chapter select is also a bonus!  A lot of other people liked it, so give it a try I guess. I hope it hurts.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: i have never written a steam review in my entire life. i chose to play this because i wanted to treat myself during this hurricane. this was the best decision i've ever made. play this game.this game is only three hours long but has the nuance and quality of a way longer, way more expensive game.it wears its inspirations on its sleeve and is incredibly creative. it builds on existing horror ideas in strange, exciting ways.the characters and writing in this game will stick with you for a long, long time.why? because these are people you've met before: people struggling under the weight of capitalism. angry, tired, depressed, relapsing, surviving, and dying. and you've worked with them.and now you get to decide their fate, in space. you have no choice.please play this game. you won't regret it.i hope this hurts.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This game is a gem. The horror premise is BONE CHILLING and deep. I found myself staring at my screen in total shock, my brain in overdrive attempting to decipher mouthwashing in an attempt to save the characters I'd become so attached to. That's another thing this game does INSANELY well. Though you only spend three hours with them, you become emotionally invested in your fellow crew members in just a few short minutes. They each have their own unique personalities and pasts, which make mouthwashing that much more immersive. I have an interesting relationship with this game. It disturbs and terrifies me like no other game before, yet I love it to bits. In conclusion, what are you waiting for? BUY THIS GAME.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: fantastic game, fantastic narrative...best played in 1-2 playthroughs so as not to disrupt ever-growing creepy feeling of uneasiness which this game has mastered.  The ending is delightful and the well-worth the completion of the game.  I loved "how fish is made" and i love "mouthwashing" - i look forward to future developments from these talented story-weaving game-designers.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to experience The Donner Party in space - desperation, hard decisions, hopelessness, a bit of gameplay and a chance of survival ... that's not what this is. The first 20 minutes make you think that's the genre you're getting into, going around the ship trying to eek out another day's worth of supplies, but soon it veers HARD in another direction. You spend most of the rest of it walking through a long string of hallucinations, decent into madness, yada yada, "and when I came to, a bunch of major plot points had resolved and now you get to guess what happened from subtext", that sort of thing. It's extremely well crafted if that is your cup of tea.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I played Penumbra and waited for Amnesia to come out. Played it and loved it, got spooked a lot. Oh there's a story to the game and all. This game is streets ahead of Amnesia. This story has been done before, but complicated with current problems and told in a MUCH more interesting way. Sometimes finding items can be frustrating but only because I was expecting it to be like other horror games and make me waste time instead of progressing story. Play it and get to the sweet sweet outro music.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is definitely one of those games that will stick with you. It's incredibly rare for me to feel such an emotional connection to a steam game, but here I am!!! Mouthwashing is genuinely one of the (if not the best) games i've ever played. This story is genuinely chilling, it gives me that disgusting pit in my chest if I think about it for too long. The characters are enjoyable and have distinct identities despite the game being so short, Anya being a personal favorite. Anya's story is heart wrenching. Mouthwashing takes the topic of SA incredibly seriously, and as a survivor, I found myself relating to Anya in several ways throughout the entire game. Mouthwashing is a gorgeous, well crafted, and beautifully thought out game. The metaphors, the visuals, the story, the characters, and the gameplay are so engaging, it gives the game a sense of solidity. This is not your average steam horror game. I absolutely loved mouthwashing and will be playing it over and over for years!!!
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: I recently purchased the Mouthwashing game after discovering it on social media, and I'm absolutely blown away by the experience. The game's horror-thriller storyline about tragic fate of the Tulpar crew members trapped in their spaceship is lost in space. I think this game's storyline is both captivating and masterful, I highly recommend this game, rating it 10 out of 10. It's the Best Indie Game ever in 2024!! The game has left me so inspired and I'm thinking about making fan artwork based on Mouthwashing game one day.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing has an absolutely fascinating story, with extremely compelling and interesting characters. It grips you all the way through, despite the tedious mechanics. (The minigames between main story segments and general controls were clunky and unintuitive, at least to someone who doesn't spend a ton of time with video games.) Overall, highly recommend for the story, if you can stand some flashing lights and clunky mechanics.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is of the type of game I normally loathe. I loved every second of it immensely. Not once was I startled, but I was deeply uneasy the entire time. Beyond bleak, beyond atmospheric, incredibly well-written. My only complaint is that it is that the price is on the higher end for something like this, but honestly I enjoyed it so much that I personally didn't mind. Approach it as a short-but-sweet interactive horror movie and you will have a fantastic time.Also I guessed the cargo hold keycode on my very first try. Never trust a retro game with immersive sim lore
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing... What can i say about it?Well, the game is primarily a story driven game, and that story is wonderful and extremely morbid. Besides that and the fact that the soundtrack helps complement the mood of the game i can't really say much else, this game is a trip from start to finish. Go in blind, you will be shocked. Play this darn good game if you love horror, you will enjoy it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Mouthwashing is, simply put, a game that will grab you. It will hold you. And, as the game itself says, it will hurt. I truly don't want to say much, cause I went in about as blindly as I could, and walked away with it still deeply ingrained in my thoughts. I'll be thinkin about this one for a while.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Its an exceptionally dark fusion of PT with elements of Tacoma's plot, and maybe How Fish Are Made by Wrong Organ as well in some ways, and then pepper in the fused aesthetics and the actual culture of a Walmart with Mike Klubnika's work.In terms of story (the most important part in this case) I'd call it "the feeling you get when your job asks you to work overnight on Christmas so that they don't get snowed in, and it doesn't snow, and your boss went home early, then fires you the next day" but also "trapped at work with your friends, for a thousand years, and you learn way too much about them, but also you realize a bit too much about yourself as well, and that you've let your Jungian shadow self fully consume you." - something like that.If you're looking at the play time and thinking "not enough bang for my buck" - this is top quality as long as your willing to read. It is a masterpiece and a... FRESH BREATH of air in a market over-saturated with copy paste time wasters. FRESH BREATH BECAUSE- If your wondering if this hurts, yes it does. It hurts. Like that pain when you chug some mouthwash and realize you have to keep that on your already floss-sliced gums for a whole half a minute, but again - extend that to a millennia.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: A phenomenal example of non-linear storytelling, environmental and indirect storytelling, and the expression of theme and story through every little detail of this beautifully made game. Deeply disturbing, completely enthralling and the kind of story that keeps you wondering and piecing things together until the end, and still after! Definitely recommend this game to anybody who can handle the themes of it.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly this was a really fresh horror experience that doesn't focus on the horror of some fantastic monster but on the horror of human evil. It had such great visual direction and the way the narrative unfolded itself got me hooked. It's a really excellent game that touches upon some truly uncomfortable topics that still need to confronted.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the most disturbing, creative, and surreal games I have ever played. It feels like a long, interactive movie, the quality of writing and cinematography is up there with the best movies I have ever seen. If you yearn for a masterful psychological horror that will make you want to vomit in unease by the end, yet leave so much to think about, do NOT let the short playtime shy you away from this game, it is an 11/10.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: This game does a fantastic job of making you feel as uncomfortable in the short amount of time that its gives. I was excited to see what they could fully do after their first game and damn they did a amazing job. Horrific and sad story and given to you in such a scary way. Definitely deserves the tag of Psychological Horror because damn I felt stressed the entire time playing this game. Great build up, atmosphere, characters and overall feel. Fantastic work and a damn solid experience for the price, look forward to whatever else is on the horizon for this studio.Oh, alsoTAKE RESPONSIBILITY
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: Its not hard to see why the reviews of this game are Overwhelmingly Positive, it deserves it.Easily accessible, great atmosphere, fun to talk about. That being said, from a technical side of things I found the experience... lacking. Spoilers:The achievements require replaying a game that is starkly lacking in replayability. There is no player agency, we are just along for the ride. So adding achievements that are meta (Yimpy, 360, Good Ending) and arbitrarily hidden employee cards actively distract from the story at hand.SOMA, a game with (some) agency, had its achievements pop throughout the story no matter what path you chose, this avoids the pitfall of distracting achievements + needing to replay the game with a guide open to make sure you snag cards during the right sequence. It relies heavily on tropes for its scares, I wish it focused more on the horror of humanity and less on the horror of sexy horse centipedes.
_childDocuments_.name: Mouthwashing

_childDocuments_.review: The five crew members of The Tulpar are stranded in the empty reaches of space, shrouded in perpetual sunset. God is not watching.

name: Expeditions: A MudRunner Game
detailed_description: Editions Expeditions: A MudRunner Game - Year 1 Edition You will receive the following content when the game launches: • The base game • The Year 1 Content Pass • The Cotco Canyon truck Expeditions: A MudRunner Game - Supreme Edition You will receive the following content when the game launches: • The base game • The Year 1 Content Pass • The Cotco Canyon truck • The Pioneer Pack, including an alternate version of 4 different trucks About the Game From Arizona to the Carpathians, chart through expansive open worlds in search of hidden treasures and forgotten ruins. Expeditions: A MudRunner Game is a groundbreaking off-road simulation crafted by Saber Interactive, creators of the critically acclaimed SnowRunner. Lead research missions as you drive a variety of all-terrain vehicles, using high-tech tools and managing your camp and crew to ensure your success in the wild. Embark on ever-rewarding scientific expeditions as you adapt to nature's challenges. Unravel the mysteries of uncharted lands, whether you're alone behind the wheel of your vehicle, or with fellow travelers in the online co-op mode for up to 4 players. Expeditions: A MudRunner Game builds on the legacy of Saber Interactive’s off-road simulations with its advanced physics-based gameplay systems, perfectly encapsulating the feel of driving through the wilderness. Whether you’re a long-time player of MudRunner games or a newcomer, you are in for a thrilling scientific adventure. Success depends on preparation. Plan your missions carefully and hire a team of Specialists to improve your skills in the field. With the drone and metal detector, scout your itinerary and locate points of interest. Invest the profits from each expedition to expand your home bases by building support structures to gain useful supplies and summon new vehicles. Equip your vehicles with state-of-the-art technologies and cutting-edge gadgets to ensure success in the wild. Use the winch and portable anchors to perform intricate maneuvers, and traverse treacherous rivers with the echo sounder. Choose strategically, as the tools at your disposal can make or break an expedition. Winch: Get your vehicle unstuck from the mud or rappel down steep cliffs Jackscrew: Turn your vehicle back on its wheels after accidental flips Echo sounder: Avoid sinking by probing the depth of the water around your vehicle And much more… Customize your vehicles in the garage, choosing between nimbler scout vehicles, off-road machines or large trucks. Tailor your approach for light and fast exploration or slower, equipment-heavy trucking. Successful expeditions allow you to invest in new accessories, such as storage extensions, spare parts, and measuring tools. From arid deserts to rugged forests and steep mountains, explore vast, uncharted lands brimming with hidden wonders and forgotten ruins. Archaeological sites, dinosaur fossils and natural curiosities can be found in numbers across Arizona and the Carpathians, and each discovery can be the key to groundbreaking scientific breakthroughs.

name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft
detailed_description: Discover Lara Croft’s Original Adventures, Lovingly Restored Play the Original Three Tomb Raider Adventures: For the first time ever, play the complete experience with all expansions and secret levels on modern platforms in this definitive collection. Included Game Titles Tomb Raider I + Unfinished Business Tomb Raider II + Golden Mask Tomb Raider III + The Lost Artifact Key Features Solve Ancient Mysteries : Uncover treasures of the ancient world by solving puzzles and unraveling mysteries lost to the ravages of time. _childDocuments_.review: Folks, this is NOT Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy: The Definitive Edition.What this is, is the best way to experience the first three classic Tomb Raider games in all their glory, without the jank of getting them to work well on modern hardware.-It's the OG 3 Tomb Raider games. The Original 5 games are the best the entire franchise has to offer.-It includes the very difficult to acquire DX/Gold editions, which feature additional levels as bonus content.-The graphical improvements to lighting, dept of objects, textures, etc really make the game look a lot better. I've been actively comparing and contrasting the modes, and it is night and day how great it looks, despite just being a rework of the classic games.-It owns up to some of the more derogatory themes these games featured, while not changing anything.-It runs butter smooth-Ultravide support-Works with OpenLara (a modding tool for the classic games)-The Modern Control scheme they were trying to market on? Yeah, not great.I was expecting at least a little bit of effort from them, but instead what we got was a half-assed addition. It actually takes away a lot of control of Lara and makes setting up jumps much harder. I'm not asking for much here. Just the ability to side jump, backflip, and backstep on demand, without having to have the pistols out, which has a split second delay that makes doing simple things like backstepping to grab a ledge on your way down MUCH more difficult than it needs to be.I reverted back to tank and won't lose any sleep over it, but I was REALLY hoping I could finally convince friend of mine to play, who had just refused to because of the tank controls.-The elephant in the room is that this isn't exactly a Spyro Reignited or Crash N-Sane level of remaster. It's not a full on remake designed to play as closely to the originals as possible. That isn't necessarily bad, especially given it's fairly cheap compared to those, but I know some will use it as a means to downplay the otherwise outstanding quality this game possesses.----------------------Overall, definitely giving it a recommend, but if you were holding off because you wanted better controls, I'd wait for some patches and mods that work to improve it.These games aren't just pieces of my childhood to me. They were one of the few games my parents, who hate most things gaming, actually played and enjoyed themselves. It helped bring my family together, albeit briefly, during a rough spot in my childhood. It's more than just nostalgia to me, and I greatly enjoy these games, even to this day, because of it. Here's hoping 4 and 5 get remastered as well.

_childDocuments_.review: Tldr; So far, it's good if you wanna play once to relive nostalgia. But it's terrible if you actually want to trophy hunt.Some good bits:- Copy to copy gameplay: Levels, controls, enemies AI, etc.- Ability to switch between old and new graphics at any time, even main menu- Choice of tank or modern controls- Texture updates made some areas more realistic, like actually *seeing* outside of the windows.- Three games with expansions in a single package.- NG+ is interesting featureThe bad:- Hunting trophies makes the game design instantly worse with bugged or impossible to pop trophies.  - Save counter does not reset.- Camera is a POS sometimes. I don't need to look at new Lara's face at every opportunity, and switching to OG graphics to see where I'm going should not fix for that- When using modern control scheme, don't breath on your controller unless you're holding walk.  - Pickups in new graphics can be near impossible to see.- (For TR1) No level select follow completion (which was a feature for OG completion).

_childDocuments_.review: Review for Tomb Raider 1:----------------------------I remember playing the original game on my first self-built PC (486 CPU @100MHz and 16MB RAM), so this remaster was an amazing nostalgic trip for me. The modern controls didn't work for me, but I got used to the tank controls somewhere in the second level. The camera can be extremely frustrating as soon as you're close to a wall, but the level design is brilliant and even today a blast to explore. Only exception for me is the mine level, which has too much needless backtracking and instant-death traps. Also my compliments to the devs for the excellent remaster. It runs and plays great on the Steam Deck.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a very lovingly made revamp of the Tomb Raider franchise's golden years. Going back and re-experiencing classic Tomb Raider has really made me realize why this franchise became a worldwide phenomena, and why Lara became such an iconic character in pop culture.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: The remastered version of Tomb Raider feels like a nostalgic trip back to 1996, capturing the essence of the original game while breathing new life into it. The updated graphics are stunning, with modern enhancements that bring the environments and characters to life in ways that were unimaginable back in the day. For fans of the original game, it's a delightful journey down memory lane, rekindling the excitement and wonder of exploring Lara Croft's world for the first time.Beyond the nostalgia, the remastered version offers plenty of fun and entertainment. The gameplay mechanics have been refined and polished, making for a smoother and more enjoyable experience overall. Whether you're solving puzzles, navigating treacherous terrain, or engaging in intense combat, there's always something exciting to do.One of the standout features of the remaster is the replay value it offers. With updated graphics, improved controls, and additional content, it's a game that you'll want to revisit time and time again. Whether you're aiming for 100% completion, seeking out hidden secrets, or simply reliving your favorite moments, there's no shortage of reasons to dive back in.Furthermore, the remaster includes a variety of achievements and challenges to keep you engaged and motivated. From completing levels within a certain time limit to finding all the hidden collectibles, there's plenty to strive for beyond just finishing the main storyline. These achievements add an extra layer of challenge and reward for players who are looking to fully immerse themselves in the world of Tomb Raider.Overall, I wholeheartedly recommend this remastered version of Tomb Raider to both longtime fans and newcomers alike. It's a fantastic blend of nostalgia and modern gaming, offering hours of fun, stunning visuals, and plenty of replay value at an unbeatable price.

_childDocuments_.review: There are many ways of alienating an existing player base with a remake or remaster, but this collection managed to do several of them: insulting players and the original developers as "inexcusable" racists in a trigger warning (first thing you see when starting the game), removing content that was in the originals to begin with, censoring and changing the games further post-release. This release angered a lot of people, unnecessarily, but at least Saber/Aspyr reversed, with the third patch, some of the censorship which was added post release.This whole affair left players with a very bad taste in their mouth, but it speaks well of the publisher if they listened to complaints and corrected course.So, how good is this collection of classic Lara Croft games? Mildly disappointing. This release is indeed faithful to the original experience, at least in terms of gameplay. A couple of changes I'm not a fan of: health bar in bosses, and action object indicators which make the puzzles easier but these can, at least, be switched off in the options. Not the bosses bars, though.I'd have preferred to see more graphical options to better exploit the capabilities of your card, because what's in the package is the bare minimum. No configurable antialiasing, or filters of any kind. Look for anything like video options in the settings menu, and you'll find nothing. Textures and models are kind of bland and they don't improve that much the visual appearance of the originals, save for being high res. Neither do they keep a close resemblance to the old textures in the aesthetic level. The games feature a different visual style than they used to have, but I can't really say that the change is for the better; some of the atmosphere has been lost in the translation. Many players seem to switch to the original textures for this reason, which is an option included in the game. But playing with pixelated graphics kind of defeats the purpose of buying this collection... not to mention that the classic texture mode, for some reason, limits your display to 30 FPS. And they actually feel like less.Its hard for me to recommend "Tomb Raider remastered". I feel that it doesn't improve on the originals, but neither is faithful enough to them in certain cosmetic and UI elements... it is more of a middle of the road compromise which will satisfy nobody, not the purists, not the people expecting a modernized version. And a couple of elements still remain censored despite initial claims on the contrary. Overall, this is a far too lazy and low budget effort to earn a recommendation from me. My advice is to skip it and keep playing the originals instead.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of Lara since 1990-something, I was pretty excited to hear about the remaster for Tomb Raider. I really enjoyed Anniversary which was a modern take but new from the ground up. Now we can have even nicer graphics but that one two step you remember before diving to your death. You can buy the originals on steam but "works" out of the box is a strong word. This game does 0 handholding and players unfamiliar with 90s games might struggle. For others, it will resurface muscle memory not seen in decades. You swan dove onto pavement? Reload. T-Rex ate me? Reload. Your last save was four levels ago? Have fun redoing it. The on the fly switching between original and updated graphics is a lovely touch. Modern enough to feel good while still embracing the tile life that was the original games.The only thing I wish they would have re-done was the video sequences. Happy birthday Lara Croft and make sure to hold the "action" button alas a spine-crushing fall.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: I waited for this remaster for 20 years and this product is exactly what I dreamed about. Core Design Tomb Raider series were my favorite, they reminds me times when games were much more about fun and less about being realistic and graphically flawless.The guys from Aspyr did awesome job here which was not easy because core Tomb Raider fans had quite a high expectations of it. A lot of things could go wrong but fortunately this was not the case.I already finished all 3 games including expansions packs, All hallows and Nightmare in Vegas bonus levels. After beating this adventure again I can say I was thrilled about the graphics improvements, how overall atmosphere was enhanced but the old concepts still carefully kept in place. The option to switch between new and original graphics is very cool and brings a lot of nostalgia.This piece is definitely a must for old Tomb Raider fans. However new players who never played old Tomb Raider games can have mixed feelings since game concepts could be quite odd in comparison with modern games.Anyway 10/10 from me, this is how honest remaster should look like.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Lara's back.And you can finally control her character the way a 3D character is supposed to be controlled.Yeah I said it; tank controls suck.Instead of focusing on stupid cinematics and trying to be a movie these games actually focus on gameplay.Yeah I said it; the Tomb Raider reboots suck.Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft is a collection of the 3 original Tomb Raider games updated for modern platforms with some modern QOL features.You can play with old controls or new controls.You can play with old graphics or new graphics.You can play as triangle tits Lara or round tits Lara.

In due course!=========================OLD REVIEW FOR THE RECORD=========================There is something  fishy going on with the update system behind the scenes. The Epic Games version is evidently the more complete release. This and other platforms are clearly unfinished and what we have received is a pre-release build of the game. Not to mention the absolute radio silence from CD and Aspyr regarding exactly what went wrong or what we can expect. Dodgy business is going down, I couldn't be surer of that.It's 2024. It's time the gaming industry answers to its consumers.Until I am satisfied that there isn't anything dodgy going on and this platform receives the same updates as other storefronts, I am not recommending this title and I implore others to do the same so we can get answers for why a product we have purchased is clearly inferior to another version already available elsewhere.

_childDocuments_.review: The original games have been remastered because they are classics. The TR franchise and in particular the first tomb raider influenced so many of today's modern games. The 90s originals,  mostly limited to ageing consoles and secret corners of the internet modding community, are simply not convenient to play easily on modern consoles and PCs for mainstream consumers. The remasters have solved that.There is a whole generation who can now enjoy and experience where modern gaming began. Tomb Raider was arguably the first commercially successful main stream game, puzzle adventure, with a fully realised and animated 3d character controllable by players.The remasters preserve the original titles in a sympathetic way to the original games, enabling them to have continued life with the advances made in modern graphics. To be able to flip back and forth comparing the old graphics to the reworked graphics is a nice addition.The limitations of game design and technology at the time influenced heavily what could be achieved with graphics and so the blocked puzzle adventure style was born. However the games early design puzzles and game play in many ways remain superior to modern game content. The three titles in the remaster contain mind bending problem solving, jump scares and content that to this day remain enduring entertainment.The developers have shone a bright light on the original Tomb Raider legacy for modern gaming platforms and preserved these classics in almost their original form. New players and fans will able to continue enjoying the games, played as intended within the deliberate limitations that preserve the clever game play, the puzzles, the speed-run challenges, the deaths, the frustrations and smiles that the originals brought to players and have continued to do so for die hard fans, in ways that many modern games do not.A remake was attempted with the Anniversary game but it never really captured the thrills and frustrations of the originals. Graphically it was arguably superior in visual design by comparison, in some levels, but the modern controls did not capture the enjoyable limitations of the original game, its forced style of graphics and game play mechanics, that elevated the character of the originals to classics of their time.A lot of work has gone into these remasters of I, II and III to faithfully realise and capture the imaginative concepts of the original games with subtle additions and improvements to the set. The early Tomb Raiders deserve their place in modern gaming history and the careful design decisions and huge amount of work by the developers that have gone into the remasters, enable today's gaming generation to enjoy their magic again, as they were originally loved and loathed by previous generations.

_childDocuments_.review: All three versions of tomb raider, core/edios, crystal dynamics, and square enix, have their distinctions, and are all vastly different experiences unto themselves. Younger gamers, aka “modern gamers” may in fact hate this release, as even with its fresh repaint, it’s just the original pc/psx releases that look a helluva lot better; all the wonk included. I’m old. I played these games at release back in the 90’s. For me and folks my age they hold a lot of atmosphere and weight and emotion for us. But they aren’t the products of the modern game industry with 1000’s of devs all working on them, the original game was made by 10 people. And while the product of that was amazing in the 90’s, it shows today. TR1 is old. It feels old. Painting it doesn’t change that. TR2 is still wonderful, but also still old. (Full disclosure: I have launched TR3 yet)If you want to play some psx era video games with 100% accurate controls, this is a great way to do it. But if you want a better experience, I’d send you towards “tomb raider anniversary” as it’s a remake of the original, that’s better all around.I like that this version allows for instantaneously switching between the new skins and original. It allows you to see how much work they put into it. Some areas look completely different. The “modern controls” seem to completely break the game tho. They don’t work at all with the math of the level design, nor the basic functionality of the game. Just keep it on tank controls and lean how to play it. Music is still fantastic.Random old guy thoughts follow:There is a major difference between the Core/Eidos Lara and the modern Square enix Lara.  The 90’s Lara is female James Bond. She’s heartless, brutal, and not afraid to merc anyone or anything. You get this told to you via very short, disjointed cutscenes. 99% of these games are mazes and puzzles. No awesome cinematic angles, no emotional damage, no epic story. Just puzzle, shoot occasionally, maze, repeat. These are games as they used to be. For better or worse. Don’t get me wrong, I absolutely LOVE the square Enix boot of Lara. Some of the best games I’ve ever played. But I do miss her Bond persona a lot. I’d like them to split that universe into like the 616 and ultimate universe from back in the day. Give us a modern version of the original Lara , including her questionable choices.

_childDocuments_.review: Ugggh. I so wanted to love this game. I've been playing Tomb Raider since it first appeared in the late 90's. I've played every version since the original. When I heard about the Remastered version I was so excited. It sounded like they took the modern controls from Tomb Raider Legend, and Tomb Raider Anniversary, and applied them to the original game. Finally, I thought I would be able to play the original series with controls that were less frustrating, and with graphics that were greatly improved.Yes, the graphics are much better, and I love how the developers improved the appearance of the game while still staying true to the original design. However, the controls are a mess. The modern controls make it nearly impossible to shoot enemies, and you'd be surprised by how many times you get stuck trying to complete a simple task. I'm sorry, but this is NOT the modern control system of the newer games. I play this for several hours, and I'm still struggling to make Laura do what I want.There is a general rule that applies to most video games: If your character dies, and you blame yourself for making the mistake that caused the death, then it's a good game. However, if you blame the video game for the mistake, or the bad control implementation for the mistake, then it's not a good game. Using that criteria, this is not a good game. Sometimes I'll be trying to get away from bats or wolves, and they keep munching on me because only 1 out of 5 bullets is hitting them. Other times I'm stuck at the surface of a small pool of water, unable to dive to a greater depth. This is not an easy game to play. I'm constantly blaming THE GAME for stupid mistakes, and not myself.Then there are a bunch of little frustrations. For example, try to quit the game. I'll bet you can't figure it out. Or, try to make Laura run fast using the dash key. Or, try to grab onto a ledge after a jump. These, and many other maneuvers aren't possible without doing web searches. The solutions are easy to find after a quick search, but why are we forced to figure them out on our own?I think Tomb Raider Remastered has one purpose: It's to preserve the game, and to make it playable on modern hardware. It's more of an experiment than a game. I'm sorry, but I just can't imagine playing this all the way through. It'll be far too frustrating.Here is my advice: If you want to play the original Tomb Raider with better graphics, purchase Tomb Raider Anniversary. It's a much better game, and when you make mistakes, you'll blame yourself rather than blaming the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Now THIS is how to remaster a game (or 3 games, in this case).I LOVE Tomb Raider. Specially those first 3 games. To me, the series kinda went downhill after TR5. And it was almost ruined by the 2013 reboot.TR1, 2 and 3 are, to me, the best games in the series, and while they are still playable nowdays with tweaks. But when I heard about those reboots, I was VERY happy, but also a little worried.Now that I payed it, I can say that this is EXACTLY what I wanted: modern reboots of my 3 favorite TR games, with better graphics (but without looking like a full remake), the same tank controls as before (you CAN also use the modern controls if you want. I prefer tank controls myself) and the exact same games, only with a new coat of paint, new textures, new character models and new weather effects.The new character model for Lara is great, looking exactly how I expected her to look back in the MS-DOS era (but didn't back then due to limitations). Plus, they added some new effects, like snow falling in some open areas in the first level. Fog now looks better, same for shadows.Is this a perfect reboot? Nah. Some things ARE off, like some bugs and how some textures seem blurrier than others. But honestly? This is like playing the originals, but without having to deal with Open Lara, Dosbox or OS incompatibilities. So yes, it was worth every cent. ^^.BTW, if you played the originals of PC like me, I'm happy to say that this remaster, while based on the PC version for the most part, includes the music from the PS1 and Saturn versions. For the ones that don't know, the PC version didn't have the short music that plays at some points, having only the ambiance tracks. The console versions had both ambiance tracks and musical cues. This remaster also has them. And I love it!

_childDocuments_.review: I grew up on the original three Tomb Raider Titles and I loved them to death... But eventually my Playstation died and and there weren't new systems being made anymore and in fact I upgraded to the Playstation 2. Which wasn't bad but eventually the Playstation 2 went the way of it's original system save? I've also bought the X-Box and Gamecube too! But one day? I looked at ALL my consoles and figured out HOW MUCH CASH I BLEW on all of them. EXPENSIVE and I can't afford this type of expense anymore but PC? Yes the system is generally twice as expensive to start with but perk? You buy a new PC when you old one dies? You simply transfer all your old games to the new PC. PC towers also have their own set of headaches but? Their flexibility makes them worth it. But Tomb Raider was one of the few Playstation games I couldn't emulate successfully on the PC no matter what emulator I used. Something game breaking always glitched IF the game would run at all.So I was actually excited to buy this remastered version and better yet? Seems to be running flawlessly. It's almost actually painful to watch the original graphics on a Hi-Def TV! LOL. More importantly? The gameplay itself hasn't been touched and the camera going wonky occasionally in Tomb Raider? Remember this was one of the FIRST EARLY games to play in third person as the vast majority of the time? Camera works just fine.I loved the first Tomb Raider, the second one was kind of hum ho and the final third one? WAS THE BEST easily! These classic games are easily worth $10 a pop, granted a lot of people whom never played the original Tomb Raider? Going to HATE the controls but the game was actually DESIGNED around them too. Some jumps HAVE TO BE MADE PERFECT or YOU WILL DIE. A standing jump and a running jump definitely define how far you CAN jump and it takes Lara exactly of square to hit running speed and also when you pull back? She hops EXACTLY one square back so you can get the perfect running space needed.Well enough going down memory lane, there's a REASON Tomb Raider was so good back in it's day and with the graphics touch up to roughly today's standards? It's not an eye sore either. But if you are into games where you need instant gratification? Avoid this game like the plague. This game is about exploring and figuring out how to get from point a to b with a decent story tied to it. The creatures are more jump scares than anything else as it usually is the levels themselves that are the MOST dangerous to you. Granted, definitely don't try wrestling with a bear either! LOL. Don't know why but ALL animals hate Lara and all the people she meets? Want her dead too! But great game just the same.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomb Raider 1 and 2 were some of the first video games I remember seeing as a child. My dad used to play them and Doom on our PS1 and let me watch. Probably not the best parenting, but I was very entertained. I tried to play TR1 and 2 only a few years ago on my PC and I managed it, but it was struggle of tweaks and mods to get them to run well. With this release I can play TR1 2 and 3 with no issues at all, and the extra content included. You are also able to swap seamlessly between remastered graphics and original graphics, and you have the option for a more modern control scheme, but personally I can't play with it.I really hope they remaster the rest of the original Tomb Rider games even though I'm not familiar with any of them.

_childDocuments_.review: I think Aspyr did a good job remastering what people wanted from this game. I think that still makes it a heavy chore and burden of an experience if you aren't nostalgic for it or a huge fan.I would say the controls hinder the experience, but the game was designed completely around these controls. If the game was faster, smoother and more responsive the titles would be muuuch shorter to play through and way easier.Simple tasks in other games are multi-button interactions that require a lot of general interaction with your controller. The fact that you are mostly fighting the controls and handling Lara is by design because the environments, zones, and gameplay are all very simple. Having the controls jammed in your face front and center are meant to distract you from auto aiming/shooting weapons, enemies that charge at you for touch attack, and zones that are really boil down to a couple of platforms or moving out of the way.While I don't recommend the game, I respect its vision and intention on what it accomplished at its time of launch and what it brings to a modern generation.The levels are pretty tight and become quicker to play once you really warm up to the controls. The game doesn't waste your time in anywhere except its controls. I cannot stress enough this is by design and "remastering" or changing these controls too much would really remove the only real charm these games have.I've given it a good go but I don't think I personally can stomach anymore of it. The whole experience is incredibly dated, more so than it's counterparts of the era. The controls of the classic Tomb Raiders are both its gift and curse and are truly the deciding point on whether or not you'll be playing these games.

_childDocuments_.review: I am 24 years old.My ex-husband and I have a daughter together, and we adopted our son together. Both are now 4 years old.When we were going through our separation, I felt lost and unhappy. I was self-destructive. One day, I was so angry with everything spiraling out of control that I punched a concrete wall in a moment of overwhelming emotion. This resulted in breaking my fifth metacarpal in my right hand—the hand I worked with, played games with, and used to carry my children to bed—the hand I desperately needed to ensure I could continue providing.Upon learning the severity of the self-inflicted damage, I became almost suicidal. Keep in mind that just a few months before this, I was the happiest man, with no history of depression or anxiety. I had never experienced anger outbursts, nor was I the type to break down and cry, but I was in a tough situation that truly prevented me from seeing the light on the other side.With nothing better to do, I looked for a game I could play WITH ONE HAND while recovering. Somehow, I stumbled upon this game and read some of the comments. I decided it was worth a try... I must admit I didn't beat the game, nor did I play as much as some of you. In fact, I may have played this game for only a day or two. That being said, after doing so, I had a new joy and hope for life. I managed to leave behind the pain and suffering that had been thrust upon me. I could experience the joy and happiness of other people. I relaxed for 5 ♥♥♥♥ minutes listening to this music, long enough to realize that I would be okay.After realizing this, I turned off the game and went back to work. My hand hurt a lot, but I was motivated. I stopped feeling so sorry for myself and became the father I needed to be at that moment, not the weak girl I was behaving like.Today, I am close friends with the father of my children. We don't fight, argue, or say hurtful things to each other. We are parents and friends.Now I have 3 children. My third child is, wait, ALSO 4 YEARS OLD. The man I am with was going through a very similar situation at the time of my separation, and we just unexpectedly stumbled into each other's lives. We have been dating for a year and are very happy together.Moral of the story: you never know what life has in store for you, and if I had given up when all odds were against me, I wouldn't be where I am today. This silly little game helped me realize that.Thank you.

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster of the original Tomb Raider trilogy is so faithful to the source material it's actually a bit surprising. There are a number of features that have practically been left untouched, including the original sounds and fonts. Even the cut scene animations are virtually unchanged— character models still do the silly head-bobbing thing when they talk even though their mouths are fully animated. However, there are definitely reasons to get the remasters instead of just playing the old games, so I'll list those below.Things I like about the remasters:- The lighting effects overall have vastly been improved, especially in Tomb Raider 1. The Tomb of Qualopec doesn't hurt my eyes quite so bad anymore.- Some sky effects have been added to certain areas of Tomb Raider 1, including the Lost Valley and Coliseum levels. This is a good thing in my opinion.- Some quality of life features have been added to the game, including a modern control scheme and action indicators (!) that tell you if something can be interacted with.- You can lock the butler in the freezer. And he actually freezes.A few shortcomings (as of the time of this review):- There are more than a few texture glitches and oddities that haven't been fixed yet, most notoriously the random paintings that appear in some underwater sections.- The game tends to freeze for a second or two when music cues are triggered. Not game breaking in any capacity, but the lag can be frustrating sometimes. Of course, it might just be my computer, but the game runs just fine at any other time.- The pre-rendered cut scenes were upscaled and not very well. The on-screen text especially has a grainy texture and was not cleaned up at all. Not particularly important, but just an FYI that they do not represent the quality of the remasters.Overall, though, I'd say the remastered Tomb Raider is definitely worth checking out. If you haven't watched any gameplay and are undecided about it, I'd recommend doing that first before buying.PS: If you're a newbie, this is just a reminder that the original games came out in the late 90s and have some content, including racial and ethnic stereotyping, that would be considered unacceptable by today's standards. This content was not removed, and Aspyr acknowledges it in one of the game's start-up messages.

_childDocuments_.review: You know what! I take back my negative review. The games aren't bad at all. I was bad. I thought the controls were bad. Then I realised I could change them to my preference. I do still have to switch back and forth between the classic tank controls and the modern controls. But it's not really game breaking. The only thing that still irritates me a little is the fact that there's no quicksave. I have to remember to manually save. And there's a counter that tells you how many times you've saved. Completely unnecessary if you ask me. The gameplay is actually both challenging and action packed. I've had to really use my ol' brain to solve some of the puzzles. There are hours and hours of gameplay. Re-play-value? Not so much. But you'll take so long getting through some of these levels, you'll know every nook and cranny of every level at the time you've beaten the game. And the memories last a life time. I still remember the layout of some of the levels from when I was a little whimp watching my cousin play these games....Aaaahhh.... those were the days...Uhmm where was I..? Oh! The review!  Right! Initially I was very frustrated because I didn't know what to do and even if I watched walkthroughs, my hand and eye-coordination aren't really what they used to be since I've gotten a bit older. 10 years ago I would have just breezed through it, no problem. But I guess these games have helped me reconnect a little bit with my younger self in a way. I now have affirmation that I still got it. Kind of like in Batman Beyond when old Bruce Wayne can still throw a bat-a-rang through his window with perfect aim, to shut off his alarm system!

_childDocuments_.review: I really really REALLY Love Tomb raider (i owned the Originals back in PS1 times), and got VERY excited about this announcment. The game looks cool - i wouldnt call it a remaster its more of a skin overlay -  It is nice to get an upgrade of the old lara and keep everything as faithful as possible to the OG (it's literally the same game but with nicer models and textures/overlay)and I cant help but feel nostalgic with the OG music and voice actingThere were 2 main things that made me not recomend this and actually ask for a refund: - Controls - as it is this time, it is PAINFUL to play with these controllers . the TANK controlers allow for all original animations but are also quite sluggish in controlling the camera and make moving the character a struggle, and the updated controls work better but remove some of the movements we should do.  I've spent sometime in reddit, youtube and google and there was really no solution for it. it just made me hate playing it.-This does not feel like a remaster, so it's not really worth the price. The cutscenes are exactly the same a the OG game, but have been AI upscalled, which means, they are just... less blurry (which I dont really understand, at least this could have been redone), and somehow dont match the experience you have while playing the game. Because we are upscalling some games that are nearly 30 years old, some of the objects are bulky and the platforms arent as polished. Tomb Raider Anniversary feels more of a remaster than this (entering the remake territory) and its already 15 years old...Simply not worth the price point as is. asked for a refund and will wait until it is heavily discounted or more fixes on control are announced.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Love that this is a faithful remaster with no changes other than a new graphical layer on top of the original. This is exactly what fans have wanted for years! Play with tank controls (on by default), the games were built for it and plays better with them. If you're playing with a keyboard, you might want to remap the keys, since these games were originally made before WASD was the dominant control scheme. If you're playing with a controller, use the D-pad for movement instead of the joystick for the best experience. When saving your game, make sure you go to the right within the "game" option. It defaults to the Load screen and it's pretty easy to accidentally load an old save rather than saving. You can overwrite a previous save without any warning, so it's best to be paying attention when saving/loading. Exiting the game is also found in that "game" option, just another "page" to the right past the Save screen.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: A classic series that has some of the most iconic moments in gaming history. These games really captured my imagination as a kid, serving as an embodiment of the Indian Jones fantasy. It is a brilliant gaming experience, with every level being a puzzle to unlock. Sure, it does get frustrating and sometimes repetitive, but it beats the hell out of so many modern games that it's not even funny.All I really wanted was decent controller support so that I do not have to dust off my old consoles. This remaster has mostly delivered on this, though the camera issues can be annoying to say the least. It remains a touchy game, but that's part of the experience. I have not tried the new control system, and probably won't because tank movement is my comfort zone. New graphics and embellishments are nice, though they actually make some things more difficult to see (eg rusty keys are almost invisible). The fresh coat of paint revitalises the experience without compromising the aesthetics of the original games.

_childDocuments_.review: Tomb Raider II'm going to rubbish this game for the same reason James May rubbishes old cars to the chagrin of Richard Hammond. It's a fairly faithful representation of the older games that I can't help but feel could have been much cheaper especially with active modding communities. Just a brush up to run, cheap price, and let the fans make what they want. DOOM style.I think games like this should be kept for historical purposes but the antiquated controls and homicidal camera make for an afternoon remembering why we moved on. You might suggest this to a younger generation who loves Fromsoft type agony but even they might roll their eyes at the last boss which turned out to be the camera all along. I can't really recommend this despite the feelings of nostalgia. I've moved on and replaying it just makes me remember why I put it down all those years ago. I remember playing Tomb Raider Anniversary and thinking it was a remake that was well done because it moved on from the older style while keeping the general story and play.If you enjoy the older levels of torture then this is a rare gem and you should totally get it but chances are you already have it running with mods and there's not much here to tempt you into paying again.

_childDocuments_.review: These games are everything I've ever wanted. Tomb Raider is my favourite game ever, the old ones. I never really connected as much with the new ones because for me they lost the essence of the game, which was exploring, figuring out what you had to do and where you had to go. I just wanted the same game with better graphics. You can tell that the people who worked on this are real Tomb Raider fans, they did a fantastic job and I hope they adapt the remaining ones. _childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This is the definitive version of classic Tomb Raider! A lot of love, care and attention to detail has been given to these 3 amazing games which stand the test of time impeccably. There's nothing like them and hasn't been since. Besides the gorgeous and faithful graphical overhaul they added 2 great Qol options for new players. The interaction indicator which takes out the guesswork on certain mechanics and the photo mode which serves as a "scanner" for the level for when you get stuck and don't really know what to do next. Of course their use is completely optional. No comment on the "modern" controls option. I'll argue these games didn't even need the optionIf you're a fan of the original games you should absolutely buy this! If you're new to classic TR then also go for it and find out why we fell in love with them in the late 90s. I really hope they do Last Revelation/Chronicles next so we can have the complete classic Core Design saga.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Welcome back and happy birthday to the real Lara Croft. It's a great port of 3 great games, that actually hold up really well today in terms of level design and puzzles. The modern visuals keep the art style mostly intact, with a few liberties taken here and there that some I enjoy, others I'm a little put off by (I.E. pretty much any character model besides Lara) As for the controls, there is a modern control scheme, but I HIGHLY recommend either sticking with the tank controls as a veteran, or at least giving them a go and actually attempting to learn them. the modern controls are decent, but the looser movement doesn't really gel with the tight grid based platforming the game demands, not to mention it actually restricts you from back flipping or side flipping unless you have a weapon drawn. The free camera is also kind of awful in tight spots. Just play with tank controls as the game was intended, it's not perfect, but it just works better with the way the games are designed. (Play Lara's House as a newcomer because she will literally walk you through it). These games are also challenging and get progressively more so from game to game. 1 isn't really too bad and ramps up a bit towards the end, 2 takes a similar difficulty to the end of the 1st game and keeps running, and 3 is a masochistic fever dream. I recommend playing them in order
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Would definitely recommend this remastered trilogy to any fans of the franchise and newcomers. I have really enjoyed the attention to details the developers have executed on. textures and models from the original have received beautiful HD enhancements without compromising integrity of the original assets. I find myself switching between the original and remastered looks throughout my game play, taking extra time within each level just to appreciate and marvel at the care and attention the developers gave this game. Lara looks great fully fleshed out in her new 3D model; fully modeled fingers and toes, HD clothing textures and even new facial expressions while she is shooting or talking. I especially love the care the developers put into the environments fully fleshing them out like how they were originally meant to. I'm specifically talking about adding sky boxes in areas where there would've been an empty black roof, or adding cutouts in areas that would understandably need lighting but doing it in a way that makes sense in the environment.  This remaster has fully re-ignited my love not only for this game but other 3D platformers of this time.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This really takes me back. this version of the game, you win both ways, new audience, and old school audience like myself. As it has an option to switch back and forth between the remastered graphics, and the old school polygon graphics.Some achievements are buggy, and misleading, but other than that, an amazing version of the games. And it even added the 3 expansion packs as well.Just be warned, if you ever played the original Unfinished Business, the order of the levels won't be the same. It's now the Atlantis levels first, then Egypt. I think the reason they did this, is to make it in canon-logical order, as the Atlantis set of levels are set after the fight with Natla, and Egypt is set months after the events of Atlantis.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Modern players going into this will be like Alfred Molina in Raiders of The Lost Ark, eager to get things done as quickly as possible and careless.At the time I'm writing this, I only have about an hour and a half of playtime. It took me a bit to get used to the modern control scheme since I was so used to the tank controls, but it's working great for me now. I've seen a few reviews on YouTube in which the journalists couldn't aim at enemies and ran in circles with guns in hand like headless cockroaches; I thought, "oh no, I won't be able to shoot very well with the modern scheme," but that wasn't the case since I was able to figure out pretty quickly how to incorporate rolling into combat and always keep the aim on enemies.Do Lara's obstacle course in her home and adapt to the new controls because it pays off in the end.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Long time fan and player of the TR games.(Ive only played the first game for a few hours at the point of writing this review.)The graphical update is welcomed and pricing is reasonable, so I would recommend.There are some good Quality of life changes, like being able to save on the fly, and naitive ultrawide monitor support.Surprisingly though, there is no RayTracing - hopefully this will be added in future.I am hoping that The Last Revelation and Chronicles get the same treatment soon too.Minor issues:The main menu has no exit option, meaning youve got to close the game from steam, AltF4 or via Task Manager.Im also not bothered, but the invert controls option isnt currently working.My one grievance:It blows my mind that even with a revamped control scheme they have not fixed the issues with performing a running jump from a standstil. I die more due to not being able to jump on command than I do to the actual enemies.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This is a remaster done right, for the most part. Video footage on YouTube doesn't really do this remastered trilogy justice. The redone character models, high-resolution textures, and new lighting do a great job of preserving the original art direction of these games while making them look considerably more pretty than before. The image quality is superb and the unlocked frame rate makes these games feel a lot smoother than ever before.However, it isn't all perfect. I  recommend using modern controls. It's nice that these are an option but I can't say they've been implemented too well here. In some ways, they completely trivialize the challenge of these games, as Lara can turn on a dime, but other times can be incredibly finicky and unreliable. The tank controls may feel awkward at first if you've never played these games before, but it's what they're designed for. Plus, part of the fun of these games is mastering the controls.The complete lack of graphics options is baffling. I understand that these games can run on basically everything, but the ability to manually change the resolution, toggle Vsync, post-processing, etc. would be greatly appreciated. Thankfully, I'm satisfied with the result I get out of the box, but I'm otherwise not a fan of this.Anyway, I'd say this collection is worth the price. I don't know if this is the best remaster I've experienced, but this is at about the standard your average remaster should be.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: Remarkable Remaster. Worth every single penny.You can tell this was made with love to the original content, you have the option to change the graphics settings on the fly, with the new graphics or the old 1996 ones.  You can also change the tank controles ( OG ones ) to the new "Modern controles", and many other quality of life changes added that do not taint the old gameplay or aesthetic.

_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: This collection is single-handed the best ways to play the first 3 tomb raider games. Immediate controller support, crisp framerate, great clarity options for item pickups. The only criticism I can give of the game is that the modern control settings are a little poorly optimized in certain areas in levels where the camera will want to fight with you not unlike the PS2 era games. Ignoring that though, its' got everything you need to enjoy the original and classic experience of the games without compromise.

_childDocuments_.review: It's all right. I think the controls are the biggest con. That and I keep getting frame hitching even though I'm using Digital Foundry's recommended fix for Nvidia cards. _childDocuments_.review: A brilliant graphical update to what are, in my opinion, the best Tomb Raider games. There's been no real changes to the gameplay, asides from a few quality-of-life improvements and the odd game-breaking bug fixed (most of the other bugs have been left in, with a few achievements for finding them!), and the graphical improvements can be turned off with the F1 key - which is oddly not shown in the controls, nor is F3 for Photo Mode - making this the best way to enjoy classic Tomb Raider on modern systems.For half the price of most games, you get three full games and their expansions, giving the average gamer around 50 hours of playtime, making this an absolute bargain! It is also a fascinating insight into early mass-market 3D adventure games, and the gameplay still holds up to modern standards. For those complaining about the lack of a rewind function, just do what I do, and have done since the original releases in the 1990s, which is spam F5 to quicksave and F9 to quickload. There's no limit to how many times you can save, and you can have multiple slots as well. Plus, Stella's Tomb Raider site has save files and walkthroughs in case you really get stuck.It would also be nice to have a level select function once you have completed the game, though you can just download save files, use the level skip cheat, or create a new save in a different slot at the start of each level.Update 7th March - I have found a few issues with Tomb Raider III, including a wall that you can swim through in the Nevada level (this wall isn't present in the old graphics), as well as sounds for boulders and spike walls becoming very high pitched and quiet after the first India level. There is also an overall issue with the increased draw distance making it possible to occasionally see behind the scenery, though this is only a very minor issue.Hopefully, these are things that the developer will patch out, as they do seem to be working on a big patch at the moment.
