_childDocuments_.review: I had my reservations about these as my memory of Tomb Raider games is that they were projects that sat on my shelf unfinished while games like Metal Gear Solid, Final Fantasy VII, Gran Turismo, Time Crisis, Circuit Breakers, and even Medal of Honour got all the screen-time. In fact, I don't think I ever finished Tomb Raider 1, definitely dropped 2 early and never even bought 3. I played a little of 4 and 5 on Dreamcast, skipped 6 due to poor press, and only started to love the idea of Tomb Raider with the Legend and Anniversary reboots.I hope you'll forgive the preamble - I feel it's relevant to lay out that I'm not a huge fan of Tomb Raider, before I then go on to say that these games are amazing.Why?It all comes down to the control system. The first Tomb Raider I enjoyed was the one that got rid of tank controls - that's not a coincidence. Looking back at the gaming landscape of the time, a change in default control schemes was occurring in the industry. In spite of Tomb Raider's appeal and popularity, the damned tank controls felt like a creative choice that was taken out of adherence to brand formula rather than for playability. Tomb Raider shared tank controls with a bunch of other very hard games like Nightmare Creatures, Deathtrap Dungeon, and of course Resident Evil. All felt like their difficulty came about in part due to the tank controls. Tank controls are immersion shattering in many ways, like for instance when wanting to backpedal from danger. In Lara's case, she'll need to spend 2 seconds turning 180° on the spot before she can run away from an approaching tiger or rockslide. When combating enemies the most common cause of massive damage or death comes from getting snarled up on a wall and giving your enemy a bunch of free hits, or plunging off a ledge while running away. The problem is that if you imagine the abilities of a nimble, athletic protagonist, you'd undoubtedly end up with a list closer to Mario's that Lara Croft's, yet Lara's moves suggests gymnastics, with rolls and tumbles, swan dives, and even a handstand. The deliberate and stilted tank controls just don't feel right given the character's identity as a gymnast who should be flowing and agile.Sales of analogue controllers were picking up at the time of Tomb Raider 2's release, and it was becoming clear that sports and racing games alone would drive adoption, but in addition, the fluid free-movement systems were becoming more popular in platformers and action games too. Analogue schemes allowed for faster and more precise movement than digital controllers using tank controls allowed so it was only natural that developers and players would gravitate to these schemes. Yet in spite of this innovation, Lara had her fingers in her ears singing 'la-la-la' while her contemporaries were running literal circles around her. As more and more franchises moved to a free movement scheme, Tomb Raider's tank controls felt more and more stale with every instalment. Analogue controls did start to appear in later games but the controls remained a hybrid of free and tank schemes, and for that, awkward.To tell you why Tomb Raider is great with tank controls I'm going to have to invoke Dark Souls.What makes Dark Souls difficult is the weight in the movement of your character. There have been many games where a relatively unknown protagonist hacks their way through skeletons, monsters and dragons on their way to toppling the strongest foes in the land, but few where the first basic enemies you encounter take more effort to overcome than the last group of elite knights before the final boss. Dark Souls is often described as having weight, meaning your actions in the game are deliberate, slow, and need to be considered carefully. You can't just stomp your way through enemies; each one needs to have their defences picked apart and exploited deliberately. Once Dark Souls' combat clicks, there's this wonderful sensation that occurs where you become aware of your mental tally changing; where you'd previously come off worse most of the time, now it's 1:2, then 1:1, then 2:1, then 5:1, then 20:1. Eventually, you're surprised when an enemy gets the better of you because your level of mastery has improved that much.Tomb Raider shares that sensation with it's movement and combat. To say levels use a grid-based system is underselling the complexity. It's true that from a bird's eye view, but from third person where you'll be spending the game, you'll be attempting jumps at a variety of elevations and angles. Lara can jump a standard 3 tile gap if both platforms are level, but what if your destination is higher like chest height, head height, or higher than that even? What if your destination is not directly opposite, but slightly off to the side, or a lot off to the side? If it's sloped will you be able to grab it? What if you want to drop from one ledge to another, will you be able to grab the other if it's a good bit below you? What if you want to jump over an obstruction like a jagged rock to land on a beyond, will Lara make it if the rock is stumpy, waist high, chest high, taller?Gradually you get to know the answers to all the above questions. Eventually you reach a level of familiarity where you can sight-read new terrain and kinda-intuitively know how to approach it. This level of mastery isn't possible in free movement games as you don't have that level of precision with free controls. Tank controls are very precise, meaning you can set up Lara in very predictable ways. Every time you intend Lara to jump a gap you know how to do, she'll do it in exactly the same way every time without any variance in execution. Contrast this with the free movement system of a game like Tomb Raider: Legend, a game with snap points to help you jump in the right direction, automatic grab points that suck Lara onto ledges, and a dedicated recovery button on the controller for all the times Lara don't quite land straight in spite of all the other assistance, maybe you can see why there is totally different feeling to mastery of tank controls. In Legend, skill comes from execution; in OG Tomb Raider with tank controls, skill comes from preparation.Combat is a mixed bag. Most of the enemy encounters in the first game are against melee chargers, which means Lara will be spending most of her time going backwards and standing out of reach. Later games introduce ranged enemies where the real fun begins as outranging them is not usually possible. Like with movement, combat has a decent skill ceiling where it's possible to develop much better strategies for dealing with enemies than standing and shooting or backpedalling whilst chewing health packs. Both melee and ranged opponents have facings, and getting behind them yields lots of lovely damage while you chase them around, but getting into the rhythm of fighting this way requires quite a bit of practice and patience. It is entirely possible to get very good at tank control combat, and immensely satisfying to pick apart enemy defences, just as it is in Dark Souls. It's not timing but speed and orientation that matter in Tomb Raider's combat; any ability or change in movement that can alter where Lara is heading has the potential to keep Lara out of harms way and disadvantage her enemies. Contrast this with Legend again, where combat revolves around using cover, distance and speed of movement to mitigate damage and all enemies continually face Lara irrespective of how much she tries to circle behind them, so you see why the limitations of tank controls and the skilful exploitation of those limits help create the conditions for mastery that's just not possible in games where player and enemies can turn on a dime.Limitation breed creativity.In short, Tomb Raider was a victim of 90s fashion. It's safe to tank.

_childDocuments_.review: Although this package should be a welcome remaster package, the price tag for such a poor work which includes trick advertising regarding "modern' controls, cannot be justified. The graphics look very good and make playing the games much better than the originals. From visual perspective, there is nothing to complain about, it looks great. But the old frustrating gameplay mechanics have not been fixed (it is indeed hard to fix this with a simple remaster). And the fact that they included "modern" controls to this package is what attracted me to buying the package at the huge price it was sold at (25-30 euros). But these modern controls, although they do work, do not work together with the whole interface and level designs which have remained the exact same as the old games. It becomes even more frustrating, because they do not match together and make playing the games even harder and even impossible to surpass some parts of the levels. For this alone, I do not recommend buying the package, only if it's price lowers itself to 5-10 euros.

_childDocuments_.review: Made with love and care! This is the "dark souls" of platform gaming. There may be "modern controls" but newer players should know that these games were notorious for their difficulty, especially Tomb raider 3.If you're a new player please experiment with controls! The game is based on an old grid/cube system and you might find the Classic controls work better. The Walk button is your best friend for lining up jumps and to avoid falling off ledges.  Modern controls work pretty well apart from in combat. I found it difficult to dodge and jump with guns out in modern controls. Also, there are some camera glitches in modern controls to, but they rarely happen. I prefer Classic controls because thats the way the game was intended to be played. Everything is spot on though. Amazing glow up, and they kept in almost everything from the OGs. So you have many options!I have since played more with the modern controls, and despite many people disliking them, they aren't bad at all once you get used to them. The biggest offender is the camera, but this can be bypassed by tapping the "look" button to reset the camera..

_childDocuments_.review: LOVE IT LOVE IT LOVE IT! Whenever remastered versions of games are being made (especially nowadays), you often times hear a lot of people complain "Why did they change this" or "Oh man, I wish they would've kept this in the game" or things like that. Well.. in this case right here you don't have that. Because this Remastered collection is SO true to the original and Aspyr did an absolutely fantastic job here (afaik they even involved fans who did a lot of stuff around these games over the year)! They kept all the levels, their designs, enemies, audio (+ the bonus ones) completely intact, while focusing on just making everything look a lot nicer. <3 They also tweaked some minor yet useful things (for example you don't have to stand on the exact pixel of an item in TR1 anymore to pick it up), making the experience feel smoother, added the option for modern controls (although I highly recommend the original ones still) and a cute little photo mode on top - bc why not. :D Oh and last but not least OFC the awesome ability to switch between Remaster and Original.There are a few small moments that could be fixed in a patch later on  - for example some corners, pits, etc in TR1 being just a little "too dark" to navigate and in a few places water and mud textures could indicate a little extra movement (for example at the first waterfall the water looks still although it's a current). But those are just very minor things, everything else is as GREAT as a Pyramid and I adore this collection! ^^That being said, as an oldschool Tomb Raider player I'm taking my hat off to the Aspyr team and I'd like to hug them if I could. Oh well, maybe one day. :'D Anyway, clear recommendation guys, you can't do anything wrong by getting this! Trust me.ps: Also Crystal Dynamics, we despise you. You're not worthy. :)Thanks for reading.

_childDocuments_.review: It is great to see the original Lara back after all these years, looking better than she ever did in the version that came out in the 90s. There is no map, there are no hints, there is no auto-save feature, and Lara will not wonder out loud in a helpful way if the game notices that you are stuck. This is very much the kind of game where you have to figure it out, and if you don't, tough luck. There is no shame in looking for a good guide too keep handy while playing if you have trouble, but keep in mind that this is not an easy trilogy.If you (newer players) are okay with this, go right ahead and pick this up. Tomb Raider was an absolute milestone in both gaming technology-wise as well as from a social standpoint. Lara was the original 3D female protagonist thjat won over the hearts of so many gamers, men and women alike. The OG Tomb Raider games will forever be an important part of videogame history.

_childDocuments_.review: I love the original tank controls, but one thing missing in Tomb Raider 2 (the one I mainly played back in the day and still do on my PS3) is how you had two buttons for precise walking: R1 would allow you to walk forward/backward and use the left and right directions to rotate and walk, and R2 would allow you to either walk forward/backward or strafe left/right.What they've done here in this remaster is put those functions in a single button, namely R1: to walk and rotate, you must first take a step forward, and then start turning. If you simply press left while holding R1, you will start strafing, as if you were holding R2 back in the PS1.This is counter to my muscle memory from the PS1, where I could both walk forward and rotate while still holding R1. In this new version, I must let go of R1 if I want to rotate in place, which is weird and confusing, and creates the risk of Lara starting to run forward if I'm using the analog stick instead of the d-pad.Another thing that is missing is the ability to use PlayStation button icons. Frankly, it is unacceptable for games to be releasing in 2024 without this option.I wish the developers would fix these issues before my refund window closes, because I really want to play these games.In most other regards, this is a beautiful port.

_childDocuments_.review: The definitive version and best way to play these three classic games.- The three full games, plus their respective expansions not previously available on Steam or any console. All included in one launcher.- Huge graphic overhaul that improves all textures, lightning/FX, and even straight updates 3D models for all characters, items, and some scenario elements. All while staying reasonably faithful to the originals' aesthetic and keeping all scenario structure intact in order to not compromise gameplay.- New Game Plus: An additional much harder difficulty that makes enemies and traps more deadly, while limiting healing resources and also bringing back the Save Crystals feature from PS1 TR1 and 3.- Added replay value with achievements encouraging different kinds of playthroughs.- A few new moves added from later TR games to make the gameplay more fluent. Now you can mid-air and underwater roll in TR1, and TR3 got two new moves to make crawling sections faster.- You can switch between remastered and original graphics anytime to compare how the visuals changed.- QoL such as Photo mode (which can be also used as a scouting tool if you wish) and modern controls as an alternative for those not very fond of the original tank controls.- No graphics customization settings. The games use your monitor resolution, but if you want to change things for whatever reason, it's not possible at least from inside the game.- Original graphics are capped at 30 FPS, so not very pleasant if you actually want to play that way.- The games were designed to work with tank controls, and it shows. If you're a newcomer expecting modern controls to make your life much easier, well, think twice. I personally use tank controls, but from what people say modern controls are far from working perfectly with these games.This review is based on the current build of the game as of May 15th (Patch 2, updated a month ago on April 11th), so I won't mention certain issues from the previous builds that have already been fixed or improved.

_childDocuments_.review: Now this is iconic and the only true Lara. Glad that this triangular sex-symbol of my generation is back in 2024. Tomb Raider II was one of my first games. Played all of them dozens of times. Last time replayed them few years ago. Unfortunately Remaster is full of hits and misses, but overal I'd call it acceptable. Lets's start with the brief overview.What's good?- It absolutely the same game from Core Design. Literally.- Lara looks really good.- Both airbags are at place.- Iconic dual-pistol are at place as well.- You can make a handstand and lock Winstone inside the fridge as before.- You can switch between OG and Remastered visuals with F1 any time.- All 3 games with their add-ons in one place.- Photo mode.- Tons of achievements.- New game+What's bad?- It was handled by Crystal Dynamics.- Lighting. It's a joke.- Random fps drops at certain levels.- A lot of visual bugs and glitching textures. A lot.- Minor censorship and virtue signalling.- Very lazy retexturing in lots of locations, mostly in add-ons.What's controversial?- Modern controls.- Visuals. They are good until they aren't.Ok. Now let's discuss some points that need explanations, excluding obvious ones. My biggest claim here is the lighting. While it's not terrible on it's own, but compared to OG it's totally screwed up. Remember GTA Trilogy [vomits] The Definitive edition? Everything was too damn dark there. TR has the opposite problem - everything is too damn bright here. Everything. TR was rather grim game with lot's of dark rooms and dim light. Here, no matter where you are, in caves, dungeons or sewers, etc - everything is brigh as in some ballroom. You can easily see it when you switch between OG and Remastered visuals. Also, this made flares totally useless. It was a common thing in OG to use one here of there even if you are a veteran of TR series. Here? - chances are that you won't burn even a single one. Now about visuals. Just as I said above. For the most part they look good... untill you encounter the situation where they cause troubles. It is not uncommon issue here when items just blend in with the terrain. Yeah, imagine this paradox, everything is bright, but it is still possbile to miss stuff. I replayed OG TRs dozens of times, remember locations literally of every key, medkit and ammo clip and these new visuals managed to confuse me. There were situations when I enter the room and was like: 'strange, a key/switch was supposed to be here, wher... ah here it it.' Obviously, Crystal Dynamics didn't play their own Remaster enough. I assume they noticed this issue too late, and instead of fixing it, they just added so called 'crutch'. Now everytime to come close to any point of interaction (medkit, switch, movable box), you get big ""!"" on your screen, lol. Absolutely ridiculous but this is how it is. Also, some locations are just not good. Floating islands in TR2, for example, in remaster are just meh. Totally lack any taste and style compared to OG.Technical condition? Overall - good. But at some levels, for example at Opera (yeah, I started with TR2) I had random fps drops to 20. At certain levels, if you start running into closed doors, it may drop fps so hard, that game will freeze for a second or too. Also, flipping or missing textures here or there. 2 at the Deck, 1 at Catacombs, a lot of Xian Temple and so on. It's funny, because you can switch back to OG and see that texture is there, then you switch to Remastered - invisible wall, haha. As to controls, there are classic (tank controls) and modern ones. I play with old ones and they work perfectly. I do not bother with new ones, but I heard that they have some issues. I can't help you with new ones, but if what, just remember that the game was created with tank controls in mind, so don't be afraid to switch back to classic ones.I mentioned achievs as an advantage not because it is something great on it's own, but because here they will really stimulate you to replay the game differently and choose various interesting options. Keep in mind, gameplaywise nothing new was added. It just proves one more what a titanic work was done by Core Design decades ago, if after so many years you can squeeze so much content out of it.In the end - I still strongly recommend the game. Well, mostly because it is still THAT game. It seems like Crystal Dynamics are just intentionally rage baiting us by doubtful statements and by doing/undoing censorship just to sabotage their own game. If they condemn something in these games, obviously, they hate OG TR and OG Lara. Don't give them such joy.

_childDocuments_.review: The reason i bought TR 123 Remastered was merely to replace the old games and to avoid playing TR1 inside DosBox or PS1 emulator.So any "remastered" feature that comes along is just an extra for me, i don't really care if the modern controls are broken as the bad reviews say so.But in my few hours of playtesting i have noticed a few things which is worth mentioning for hardcore classic players:-There is no settings to adjust brightness at all, classic mode feels a bit too bright in well lit areas, and a few dark areas you no longer need to use a flare to see anything.-There is no settings to adjust the framerate, remastered mode has very smooth framerate, but switching to classic mode brings the framerate down to very choppy, which never existed in the originals PS1 or PC versions.-The remaster mode has nice sound reverbs added which is very cool, but as soon as you toggle to classic mode, all that glamorous reverb goes away because "classic nostalgia does not deserve any enhancements", i wish i could manually toggle the reverb i don't like this being exclusive for the remaster mode only.-Classic mode water distortion effect no longer exists, which was a huge impression at the time, remaster mode does not have it either.-The inventory menu background texture is just black in all 3 remasters and TR1 and 3 classic, only TR2 classic mode the texture is correct which is that elegant red carpet waving effect.This remaster is really well done and is a really good way to bring new players to the classics.But me as a veteran hardcore gamer with 2 decades of experience with the old TR games i'm not really impressed by the HD graphics, my expectations was to see a well polished port to substitute the old executables, but those points i mentioned above are kinda triggering me so i can't fully recommend this remaster until they fix those.If you really don't care about classic mode, then i do recommend, this remaster is good enough and has no major flaws.But if you are like me and expect the remaster to 100% replace the old PS1 and PC versions, then not really (unless they fix those issues i mentioned above).Now a small surprise for those of you who have read to the end, i have also noticed that in TR3 you can actually crouch roll from a sprint, which is a TR4 move... and also roll off a ledge when facing forward while crouching, which is a TR5 move... maybe this is just an easter egg, or perhaps an accidental proof that they are really planning in remastering TR4 and TR5 as well.

_childDocuments_.review: The first  is one of my all-time favorites, no question about it, and I loved all the subsequent installments made by Core Design (yes, even  and ), so, not surprisingly, I couldn’t wait to get my hands on this collection of remasters.What a blast from the past this was for me! I felt like a teenager who got his very own PC again, launching ‘tomb.exe’ in MS-DOS for the first time, and then getting lost in Lara’s adventures for hours and hours. If you ask me,  was and still is a genre-defining masterpiece, the mother of all 3D action-adventure-platformers, and  and  are just as great, even if they didn’t revolutionize this genre as their predecessor did (to be fair, no one expected the developers to do that again with every entry in the franchise). Of course, old-school tank controls are not easy to get used to nowadays, I get it, and sometimes the camera angles make it impossible to see what’s directly ahead of us – but thankfully, we can save as often as we want to (imagine those poor console gamers back in the day who couldn’t…), and there’s a handy new photo mode which lets you scout ahead. And yeah, you can also switch to modern controls now, but I  wouldn’t recommend that, trust me. Classic  games are all about super-precise jumping and careful walking on high ledges, which are both quite difficult to pull off with modern controls (at least they were for me).The new graphics are absolutely gorgeous, and I loved how you can switch between the original and the remastered versions. I never imagined I could ever rewatch the cutscenes from these games with all characters’ lips moving! It’s a shame that the FMV scenes remained the same, they look especially outdated now compared to the rest, but hey, at least this way they’re as classic as they can get.Whether you played this trilogy before or not, I think this a must-buy for every gamer who’s not afraid of a little challenge… Actually, let me rephrase that: this a must-buy for every gamer who’s not afraid of an insane challenge with almost no handholding, dangers lurking at every corner, crazy huge levels, and puzzles that feel like torture. Yep, that’s classic  in a nutshell! What’s not to love here?

_childDocuments_.review: I do not for the life of me understand the awfulness which is this remaster, or why soooo many people have given it a positive review. When it comes to graphics and the looks of the game, sure it looks great. But the controls are so beyond atrocious they ruin the experience for me less than three hours in. A remaster is supposed to be more than just an upgrade on looks or else you certainly hope it would. And while Tomb Raider features 'modern controls' the entirety of the functionality of Laura is nearly unplayable. I have spent  over and hour trying to 'climb' past a basic series of jumping platforms that rise to another level. What would equal the most basic and fundamental game play movements that should take all of thirty seconds. Has been an infuriating escapade in lackluster design and overhaul. What am I talking about?1. Laura is unable to shift position or step forward without an animation launching her three feet in that direction. It is IMPOSSIBLE to shift her direction without causing her to move in a way that completely ruins the basic movement you're trying to achieve. Prepare to fall off platforms shifting positions over and over again.2. Even with modern controls Laura moves like a tank. It is impossible to take the most basic step forward, reverse, move to the side or have any basic functionality. It's like her legs are made from literal tread and you have to shift her accordingly. 3. The camera is wildly uncooperative and will never work with you, only against you. Prepare to jump from platform to platform without any field of view or knowledge of where you're even looking at. Adding yet another impossible layer to the most basic platforming abilities. 4. Fighting more than one enemy at a time is a controlling catastrophe. I hope you enjoy having a mid-air seizure as your arms flare around without any control of where you're actually aiming. Surrounded by four wolves and a cave bear? Good luck looser. Your pistols might as well be spray paint cans for all the accuracy you'll have.5. Switching to modern controls removes your ability to save and jump backwards. Seriously, with tank controls enabled and using an Xbox controller, because god help you with a mouse and keyboard. If you try to jump instantly forwards and then backwards, it actually feels good. It's precise and quick with the jumping. But switch to modern control and instead of jumping backwards. The camera shifts Laura's entire body around, forcing her to do nothing more than jump forward in the opposite direction. Then with tank controls hitting R3 opens up the options menu and instantly flips to the 'save page' allowing you a respite from the torturous controls and platforming. Upon switching to modern controls you will notice that the ability to save has been removed entirely and has now been replaced with a 'Load game' screen. Literally the opposite of what you want. So after completing the hell of which was basic platforming, the game flipped me off when i tried to save, only to realize the modern controls made me load the save before, loosing all my progress. Oh there is also no ability to quite the game. After several minutes of hitting every button and scrolling through every menu screen there was no option to quit the game and no option to save the garbage either. If the other two games (that I haven't played) weren't included. It would easily be the fastest refund ever for me.

_childDocuments_.review: I think this remaster plays it very safe. It doesn't change anything, just enhances what was already there. I don't think it's worth £25. Maybe £20, probably £15. Worth picking up if you're curious about the originals. Then again, TR1 is 99p on sale. Graphically it's about as good as a remaster can get without drastically changing the game. The player and object models are very well done across the board. I can tell that there is a lot of respect and appreciation for the originals from Aspyr here, and at the end of the day this is just enhancing what was already there. The 60fps makes combat smoother, and the ability for Lara to mid-air roll in TR1 is a subtle but appreciated addition. (she couldnt in the original, not until TR2)The menu's are good, though 2 and 3 lara look a little odd (her eyes off center?). Maybe i'm just used to the original. Having played tank controls on PC for the originals before, I can't say I've had any issues.I agree that I, like other's just expected something more. There's no bugfixes, no significant additions or new features; I really have just been marketed the same games i've been playing for 20+ years, but they have a fresh coat of paint. Despite that, I'm enjoying the new experience, seeing how each level has been altered. New sounds would've been nice, or extended soundtracks. But mainly, I wish we had new FMVs. The old FMVs are timeless but out of place now, despite AI upscaling. They are in my opinion some of the best parts of the originals but they've been left untouched. Also where are controls displayed? F1 for Switching between old/new graphics and F3 for photomode. Had to look these up. Also quick equip for weapons, meds, and flares aren't shown anywhere (its 1-9). Bonuses:- Compass in TR1 isnt uselss any more!- TR4 style pickup overlay so you can see what you're grabbing- Texture Bump maps and height maps everywhere. They hit more than miss, but I can tell they weren't done by hand- Lighting is very good in some parts, and worse in others- New raptors look hella goofy- AI upscaled textures are actually very good. - Specular effects on textures are nice.

_childDocuments_.review: Looks really good so far.It's the good old TR games with good old badass Lara. No modern day woke influenced whiney crap, just the way it's supposed to be.Graphics look pretty good and it runs smooth. Makes it kinda hard to switch back to the old graphics where it is locked at 30FPS but it is awesome that you can do so with just the press of one button. Really neat to be able to see the difference between the old games and this remaster on the fly.Controls are fine. In my opinion, it plays far better with the old tank controls but if you are an impatient Gen-Z kid with skill issues and low adaptability then there's also the modern control scheme for you. It makes it a lot harder to set up some tricky jumps correctly though and sometimes the camera can be an issue in this mode so all in all it just makes the game harder. I think they still need to tweak it a little bit... add a button to do the short back-jump  which you NEED to do the long jumps in the game for example.Other than that, this is a great way of experiencing the superb old TR games again. Completing them takes quite some time too so you get a lot of playtime for your money here.Recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing these remasters since they released earlier this year has been a legitimately wonderful and fun experience. To see the games I grew up with and enjoyed so much in childhood given a faithful remaster that can be enjoyed more freely by OG fans of the series like myself or potential new players, is a really good feeling. _childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: It's the same game as the original 3 with all the original DLC's that you wouldn't find on the PS1. Maybe it's the nostalgia talking, but they hold up well! By today's standards you might dismiss the platforming system as simplistic, but this also means that once you get the hang of it, you know exactly what Lara is capable of doing, and jumps are easy to judge before you commit thanks to the grid-based system. This plays surprisingly well great on modern controllers despite not being built for analog, and there's a modern movement scheme to really hammer it home (though I'm sticking with the ol' tank controls). Protip, you can hold down the menu button and use any action button to equip different weapons or use flares without rooting through your inventory.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played the classic Tomb Raiders I-III at least three times each and they are among my most beloved gaming experiences. If you're like me, I think you'll like this remaster. It brings many light-touch improvements, while still letting you experience the originals in all their jagged, pixelly beauty.A key recommendation: the F1 key will switch between old-style graphics and new-style, instantaneously. You can switch multiple times per room and see the differences. This is a bold choice by the developers, and one I respect a lot - anything that's lost in translation becomes way more obvious if you adopt this habit. It also means if all you want is a way to play the classic tomb raiders at a smooth frame rate and screen resolution, you've got them all in one package here; in old-style graphics mode, I don't think I would be able to tell there's any difference from the original game.So far I've only played through the TR2 mansion and the Venice/Bartolli's Hideout/Opera House levels. The graphical overhauls are very carefully-done. The textures are heavily inspired by the originals; they have tried to work out what they were aiming for and realise it more fully. Ladders, doors, and panels have a 3D look to them while behaving exactly the same. Rents in the wallpaper are lovingly recreated. If I have a complaint it's that they have made the lighting more forgiving, to the extent that many things that were INTENDED to be difficult to see (certain gold dragons for instance) are now trivial. Sometimes instead of pulling a flair I've just switched to new-style graphics. It's hard to be too bitter about this though when the original game is frustratingly dingy (perhaps to avoid over-taxing the engine).I've stuck to tank controls and they work exactly as my muscle-memory expects them to, so I can't comment on the new-style controls.Overall, I think this might be my preferred way to experience the classic Tomb Raiders from here on out. I don't exaggerate when I say I can see myself playing this remaster for decades to come. I've had great joy seeing the games I love given a fresh coat of paint, with the care and thought they deserve.

_childDocuments_.review: A faithful remaster that wants you feeling as if you're playing the original as you remember, not feeling nostalgic for it or noticing the drastic changes, which there aren't any. There are subtle level design changes, mostly regarding lighting and the sky, which actually make a lot more sense, especially with a longer view distance.The graphics are nice enough, but sometimes the odd geometry of the maps stands out. System Shock Remake had the same jarring effect. It's difficult to strike a balance between remastering the graphics without re-imagining too much. It would have been nice to see a greater effort into remaking the pre-rendered cut-scenes between levels, rather than simply upscale them, maybe this isn't possible?The controls on the other hand are abysmal, as they were at the time. The modern controls are worse again thanks to the automatic camera which will flip the controls back to tank so long as it's operating. This is infuriating and makes the final missions of TR1 almost impossible to complete and excruciating at best... this needs to be fixed. Buy this because you want the convenience of one package that can switch between old and new at the press of a button without any need to tinker with mods or files.
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say, this is the only true Lara Croft which has been around since 1996. Crystal Dynamics can take their poundland version and stick her up their a$$m as The Real Queen is back with updated (yet still keeping her classic form) look designed by incredibly talented Konrad Majewski! But this remaster includes more fans that worked on this three game collection! Being a long Lara Croft and Tomb Raider fan since when she was first introduced to the world I can't express how happy I am with this! Sure it might not be for everyone, especially MODERN AUDIENCE or other SJW activists but they can always go back to disney+ and continue to watch WIsh, because this game is for hardcore veterans. I haven't experienced any major bugs (few flickering textures on occasion but nothing serious), the remastered mode is a bit dark in many places because those games were never designed with baked lighting in mind and this mode uses exactly that so there are many dark places and since there are no video options you can't really adjust the game's brightness which can be sometimes problematic. It's not a huge issue esp. when you can easily switch to old graphics mode (use F1 on keayboard) so those dark areas become bright again but nonetheless it would be good if Aspyr could address this small inconvenience. Another thing which some people have (including me unfortunately) is the photo mode not working. I press F3 and nothing happens, as if I didn't press anything, so I hope this get's resolved with the patch as well. The modern controls aren't that useful with this game to be honest and I would recommend using old tank controls, might be a bit tricky for new comers but once you get used to them, you'll see that this is how those games are supposed to be played.To sum up, The Queen is back looking better then ever!
_childDocuments_.name: Tomb Raider I-III Remastered Starring Lara Croft

_childDocuments_.review: What a time we live in! Never thought I would see the day that the classics were treated to remasters and I am not disappointed! My expectations have been exceeded and what stands out the most is that the game feels like it has been a labour of love made by people who are fans themselves. If you look closely at all of the details, there has been so much thought put into how they have breathed new life into the games and added to them in ways that improves the originals whilst maintaining the exact same charm as the originals. I highly recommend frequently swapping between classic and remaster so that you can see the changes they've made (like new ceiling details to the temples, mountain flowers on cave walls and fish mosaic tiles in the mansion pool to only name a few!) I've played for 8 hours today and I've still not had enough! I can't wait to continue. I hope a new generation of players can experience what the real spirit of Tomb Raider was about and meet the true Lara for the first time! Amazing effort!

You can tell they really went through and polished them with love and care for the original source material. I love the new additions to lighting. It really shows when you go into a room and switch between both graphic modes. Great Job to everyone who helped make this a reality. I will be purchasing the 4-6 Remaster as soon as it comes out :)

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played these games in over 20 years, but the second one in particular is one of my favourite games from my childhood, so I'm glad they've finally been remastered.Pros & Cons:+ It's great to have all 3 titles fully remastered in one collection. With the DLC campaigns. For the price, it's an absolute bargain.+ Being able to switch instantly between old and new graphics is great and, unlike in other games I've played with this option, I'm finding myself using it a lot.+ They've faithfully retained the little things that make the originals so nostalgic, from the music, to the menus, to Lara's look, and the survival horror-like atmosphere. They haven't tried to impose their own vision on something they didn't create (this drives me mad in game remasters/remakes and tv/film adaptations); they've handled it with respect.+ There are quite a few little optional upgrades that you can toggle on and off in the settings, like subtitles, context sensitive action prompts, enemy health bars, etc.| The visual upgrade isn't going to blow you away, largely because it's a faithful remaster in terms of gameplay, which means any visual overhaul is limited by the geometry used almost 30 years ago. That said, the graphics do look better in-game than in screenshots, and above all it's great to be able to play these games on HD monitors without it making your eyes bleed.- The modern controls are a missed opportunity. Not all moves are available using modern controls, while other moves like backwards jumping and side jumping require you to have weapons out, but this is never explained anywhere in-game, and it's counter-intuitive. I wish they'd come up with a middle ground option of old school jump abilities mixed with modern camera and character movement. I quickly defaulted back to tank controls and haven't looked back since.- The cinematic cut scenes haven't been properly remastered, only the in-engine ones :(If you played any of these games all those years ago and have some nostalgia for them, this is definitely worth a purchase. Newcomers without any emotional attachment to them, however, will find the visuals dated (even with the remaster) and the gameplay probably quite frustrating because of a mix of precision-based platforming and tricky old-school controls. So if you grew up on modern Tomb Raider or games like Uncharted, don't come into these expecting them to be like that at all!

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, a really solid remaster. The graphics are absolutely stunning and Aspyr have been incredibly faithful to the originals. They have also added some much needed QoL updates to some of the movements in 1 and 3 and they only serve to improve the game and not take away from it. I haven't used modern controls because I've always preferred tank controls so I can't speak on that. I'm also super happy that they've made the save system better because it makes the games (3 especially) much less tedious and repetitive and punishing. What's also awesome is that once you've beaten each game, you can do a new game+ mode which honours the classic save system if you want a challenge which is so awesome. One thing I will say that really bugs me is that you can't replay certain levels once you've beaten them. I would love to play the Temple of Xian from 2 again because I really enjoy that level and the visuals in the remaster are incredible but in order for me to do that I would need to play through the whole game again (as it is at the end of the game) just to play it. I know that you can go into the game files and restore a certain backup but that's just a tedious work around to a feature that was present in the original games but not present at the time of me writing this. Overall tho, I'm super happy with this and could not recommend this enough to anyone who  enjoys the franchise and wants to see where it all started.

name: Vampire Therapist
detailed_description: Vampire Therapist is a narrative adventure / therapy simulator in the vein (get it) of What We Do in the Shadows, Young Frankenstein, My Dinner with André , and Horrible Histories where you play as a reformed bloodsucker helping other vampires find inner peace. This isn't your typical visual novel — featuring a fangtastic cast (such as Matthew Mercer, Sarah Grayson, and Cyrus Nemati), Vampire Therapist teaches real therapy concepts with a story that explores what it means to live, die, live again, and maybe even how to feel alive. Because even vampires deserve to love themselves. Step into the boots of Sam, a reformed Wild West gunslinger turned vampire therapist. After centuries of bloodshed, Sam teams up with a 3000-year-old blood-sucking mentor in a moody German nightclub, to guide fellow vampires through the twists and turns of their immortal existence — offering them a chance at self-acceptance in a world that feels ever more alien. From self-loathing vampires who’ve witnessed millennia of human folly to agoraphobic social media addicts, and even those grappling with the trauma of seeing too many awful streaming series (we’ve all been there), Sam’s got his work cut out for him. With each session, Sam will challenge cognitive distortions using real-life therapy techniques to help his clients reconnect with reality — even if reality has left them behind. You can’t fix the world, but maybe you can help other vampires accept it. That is, if you can accept yourself first. What Critics Are Saying: 'It's simultaneously earnest and winningly ridiculous...a labor of love, and an original one at that.' — The Spectator 'Vampire Therapist is shaking a lot of things up in one very elegant bag.' — Rock Paper Shotgun 'Every single character was memorable, and the thought of even more quirky clients for Sam to treat is exciting.' — GameRant 'I came away from Vampire Therapist actively wanting to emotionally improve and be kinder to myself' - GamesRadar Real Therapy Concepts: You’ll learn and apply real cognitive behavioral therapy concepts vetted by licensed therapists. By challenging client statements that contain “cognitive distortions”, you’ll help vampires see where their thoughts don’t match reality. A Comedic Look Through History: Meet emotionally damaged vampires from ancient Greece, Renaissance Italy, Tudor England, and the Bronze Age. An All-Star Voice Cast:  Featuring Matthew Mercer ( Critical Role, Baldur's Gate 3 ), Francesca Meaux ( Hades ), Sarah Grayson ( Gone Home, Hades II ), Kylie Clark, and the game's creator, Cyrus Nemati ( Hades, Pyre ). Unique Setting: Vampire Therapist merges cozy self-introspection with a dark European goth vibe. In fact, the whole thing takes above a goth club in Germany filled with willing necks to bite. Minigames: Learn mindfulness meditation, safely and consensually bite sexy necks! NOTE: Please read the content warning thoroughly before purchase. The game deals with mature and challenging themes that are not for the faint of heart.

_childDocuments_.review: target audience reached, it's me, i'm the target audience, an experience that somehow strikes a balance between silly vampire antics and painfully relatable humanity. i cackled, i cried, i will be thinking about this game for months if not yearsthis cast of characters has it all. a former outlaw who deep down is just a horse girl, two goths looking for a third, a misanthrope twitch streamer, that one theater kid who peaked in high school, a scientist trying to invent vampire veganism, a priest who listens to metal, the scariest art teacher you will ever meet,,the first visual novel i've played that feels worthy of being called a  in terms of narrative depth, yknow? you really get to dive into the life story of each of the four clientsjust stellar voice acting, especially in moments of Big Feelings. please give them all the awards immediatelyengages with therapeutic concepts in way that's both accessible and meaningful. i learned things as a therapy veteran but people without prior experience could also jump right in. genuinely, unironically, it is so helpful to practice untangling cognitive distortions in this gamified waythe sound design is the cherry on top. the vibe is: you are gently talking someone through their existential crisis while a fireplace crackles in the background, and at the same time, you can hear the ABBA remix they're blasting at the club downstairsmind the content warnings, things do get heavy, but generally: PLEASE PLAY THIS GAME i desperately need there to be a vampire therapist 2

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't completed the game yet (I'm about to see my third client for the second time), but I feel already compelled to leave a positive review because, so far, the game really deserves it.This looks like "Dream Daddy", but it definitely plays more like "Ace Attorney". It's not a dating game, you are a therapist and as such you are here to help your clients with their psychological problems, not to get in their pants. That doesn't mean the game doesn't shy away from discussing sex (on the contrary, it does that A LOT), but it has nothing to do with your goal. Like I said, it's a lot like "Ace Attorney". Instead of going through crime scenes and throwing evidence into your opponents' faces at court, you learn new cognitive distortions like "Labeling", "Overgeneralization", etc. and throw THOSE into your clients' faces when you catch them coming up during your therapy sessions. For the first 3-4 hours or so, the game gives you a fixed set of those distortions to work with. In later sessions, you get to pick your own set of 5 cognitive distortions so that it's possible for the player to focus on the ones that fit the client (by the second therapy session, you already have a good idea what each of them is wrestling with).The gameplay is simple, and like with "Ace Attorney", there's no real way to "fail" the game. If you get it wrong, you just try again, it's not possible to "mislead" a client. Which is GOOD in my opinion, I mean, it's also not possible to actually "mess up" the cases in "Ace Attorney" either and no one is really complaining about THAT one (I really prefer the developers of these games to focus on enhancing the story, not develop ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ "what if" scenarios which only serve to make you feel bad about messing up as a lawyer/therapist/[insert profession]). There are achievements for getting streaks of right assessments without making mistakes, that's nice. I somehow went through the first three sessions without a single mistake, seeing those achievements pop up felt pretty nice though I know it's just a bonus and the game wouldn't torture me for picking the wrong answer.The voice acting is absolutely superb and makes me actually take my time and listen to the full dialogue. That's a big accomplishment, usually I tend to just read and quickly click forward in VNs. The protagonist, his mentor, the clients, etc. - everyone sounds great and speak in a distinctive and interesting way that make you want to keep listening to them. Sam especially really grew on me.Speaking of Sam, he's QUITE the surprise! Reading about a game like "Vampire Therapist", you wouldn't expect your protagonist to end up being a freaking COWBOY VAMPIRE, sitting in LEIPZIP, doing THERAPY. But yet, here we are. And you know what? ALL of it makes sense. I kid you not! It really doesn't take long for the game to accept that this IS a thing and that Sam is not only a legit therapist, but to make the player curios about his story. Listening to him, you'd think that he's quite the simple guy, but, of course, like with his clients, there's more to him than meets the eye. Really dig that! The two German goths feel a bit like a hate crime at first (haha), but a) they already started to grew on me (ok, listening to IT people talk about their SQL problems in a heavy German accent IS kinda funny) and b) the developer is also German, so they'll get a free-pass. For anyone trying out the demo: I urge you to play at least the first therapy session before you make your judgment. The intro into the game is just a little wild, but once the therapy work starts, it really takes off! If you'll excuse me, I have to get back into my coffin for mortals called bed, getting some rest so that I can keep playing this jewel in the morning.

So there's some moments I don't choose the correct fallacy because that's not part of my therapy but it's still great. Going to enjoy finishing this game. My only downside is 100% a me thing.... I don't know how to manually save.

_childDocuments_.review: is a cleverly written, engaging, dare I say fang-tastic visual novel about helping vampires overcome their emotional hang-ups. The approach is humorous and witty, blending real life cognitive therapy elements into the narrative. It does not shy away from real life sensitive issues but treats them with respect and a touch of dark humour. You play as Sam, a cowboy from the Wild West. Sam himself is a vampire, but tired of the blood-thirsty existence that comes with being an immortal dead and he  a more positive way to live his life and travels to Germany where he meets the ancient vampire named Andromachos or Andy for short. Andy takes on Sam as a therapist-in-training. So your clients are obviously vampires. You meet many interesting and unique characters, well fleshed out and written who go through their own personal arcs as they proceed through therapy. The cast of characters range from historical figures to modern day streamers. The game at times is quite humorous and does not shy away from sexual humour and playful dark banter. One part I had a good laugh at is how Andy described Marcus Aurelius (the Roman Emperor), as Marky.  The roasts in this game are epic…”If I cannot consume high-quality blood, I might as well drink blood from Florida”. Settings include screen mode, resolution options, graphic options, text options and audio controls.* In order to save you have to hit ESC and then save.  However there is a way to view a history log,  press L to see the dialogue in text form. As you play the game you will be presented with choices like most visual novels. However this one mixes the fun of vampires and actual well-researched classic cognitive behavioural therapy (CBT) elements into the gameplay. As a therapist-in-training you will talk with people, construct a treatment plan and evaluate their progress. There are four main clients you will interact with. Dr. Drayne, Isabella d’Este, Edmund and Meddy. As you treat and talk to them you will uncover cognitive distortions (they appear as choices on the bottom of the screen) that become choices you can make to move the story forward in the right direction. There are no real wrong answers as Andy will cut in if you chose wrong and urge you to try again. There are some mini games. One is drinking blood (just match your cursor or “fangs” over the vein in the person's neck and a meditation mini-game. They are included to mix things up and while the vein mini-game is fun I really did not enjoy the meditation game, I found the floating text to be not as responsive as I would have liked.All the characters in the novel are not only voiced but voiced by some really great talent. Talent that makes the vampires . It is also developed by a talented voice actor,  who is known for his roles in the super popular game Hades (he voices Ares, Dionysus and Theseus). Amongst other greats such as Kit Chen, Kylie Clark, Sarah Grayson, Francesca Meaux and Matthew Mercer. Visually the game is great to look at. Unique characters with all their own styles. Hand drawn and vibrant. I need to shout out the artists that contributed; Ruth Bosch, Kim Schumacher, Sibylle Hell, Barbara Langa & Darcy Grimm. One of the things I love the most in visual novel games is CG’s (computer graphics) or as I call them  artworks. Sadly this game does not have any which is such a shame. The artwork is so well crafted that I would have loved to see some special arts of the main characters.  This game despite being highly unique and full of dark humour is really one that leaves you thinking. The concepts of cognitive behavioural therapy can benefit us all. We all are inclined to indulge in one or more of the cognitive distortions presented.  It is a novel that makes you think, feel and realize maybe we are too harsh on ourselves at times, harsh on others or our view on the world as a whole. Keep in mind this game is not influenced by the choices you make and you, realistically, can not fail which could be seen as a negative if the game was going for more of a darker twist. If you ended up not bettering a client but the opposite. But that would change the dynamic of the story and I think the whole point of this game is to teach, enlighten and entertain while keeping it overall in a positive place. I will be honest, those looking to just be purely entertained will not find this game engaging. It is a game that takes the therapist aspect more seriously than maybe it should, especially in the second half of the game where the concepts of CBT get more complex. Each client has 3 sessions each, so before each section more concepts are added, honestly making the game at times feel more like studying by having to keep referencing the in-game journal, than fun. So this game will be for some and not so much for others. I enjoyed my time with the novel. I do wish there was a bit more choice & consequence and maybe pulling back on the clinical terms and elements. 🩸
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Played this game with my husband for a date night, and it honestly has been surprisingly great for our relationship? We originally picked it up just because it seemed silly, but it actually describes CBT concepts really well and in a way that is easy to follow. Both of us were able to recognize what cognitive distortions we tend to use in our day-to-day by which ones we struggled to recognize in game. He struggled with emotional reasoning and personalization, while I struggled with black-and-white thinking and discounting the positive.This led to an actually deep and meaningful conversations on areas we could grow and how these distortions affect our relationship?????Came for Vampires. Stayed for the Therapy.

_childDocuments_.review: As an Licensed Professional Counselor, this game is an amazing guide to Cognitive Behavior Therapy (CBT) and other common orientations that are used in helping to stop the distortions that we have. This game teaches the CBT model and other therapeutic lessons in a sensitive but creatively engaging way, and of course all while being a lovable cowboy vampire! Can't recommend this game enough, I have had clients play it in between sessions.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: As a counselor this is an interesting game. The story telling is fun and the use of CBT principles is really interesting. I think if you are a geek therapist and you work from a CBT lens, this would be a great game to do with your client in session or give as a way to practice identifying cognitive distortions between sessions as they work on building insight into their own behavior. You can tell they consulted with a counselor when making this game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: So I actually work as a therapist, having obtained my license less than a year ago, they state in the game that this was made alongside licensed therapists and that tracks. In fact, this was actually a nice refresher of some concepts to the point that I actively think playing this game could be beneficial to new clinicians. It  also has great voice actors and art so you know its a great ride.The core game play comes in the form of challenging cognitive distortions, but the joy of it comes from the stories being told, watching your clients learn and grow into the version of themselves they wanted to be. Just as much as the main character learns to find the joy in hearing those stories and playing his bit part in their happier ending, I also recognized myself in that journey. I should hope that therapists the world over learn to find their joy in the work in the same manner, and can only recommend that if you enjoy stories and want to learn a bit all the while then pick it up. You may just learn a thing or two about yourself while you play.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: My background going into this is an intro level familiarity with VNs and a Bachelors in science of Psychology.Vampire therapist is a well written, excellently voice acted and highly compelling visual novel that tackles the idea of immoral beings struggling with centuries of emotional damage. It features an amazing cast and no one if phoning it in, for the dialog along VT is worth a play.Now as a psychologist I often find myself curious how well a game about psychology actually represents it and I'm happy to report I feel VT actually does a very good job.Now in session you probably would overtly state what sort of logical fallacy the patient was making but the empathy and earnest desire to help people, without judgment or condemnation, is the goal of any good counselor. Additionally, I appreciate them taking the time to point out that you shouldn't casually psychoanalyze your friends outside of session. Too often these days I see psychology applied to social and business stations to exploit people. Examples being so called “subtle manipulation” to get what you want out of people or “loot box” mechanics. Thus, touching on the ethical aspects of psychology and it's application are nice to see in a game focused on it.The only thing I'd say they got wrong was a bit of history on the nature of introspection. At one point it's said that “people haven't really been thinking about how they think very long” or something to that effect. The truth is, the Greeks often used self reflection and introspection in their phylsopy, in fact the Greeks went as far as to theorize that there were chemicals within our bodies that helped to regulate our moods. Fun fact: That's where the world melancholy comes from! As an aside, I don't normally reply to other reviews but I wanted to say that in my Psychology studies here in America, it was in fact greatly encouraged that you undergo therapy your self at least a few times, to understand what it's like to be on the other side of the equation, so that you can have genuine sympathy and understanding for what the patient is feeling or experiencing. On a more personal note, I would be somewhat skeptical of any counselor who has never known what it's like to be a client.Over all I'd give Vampire therapist an A+ as a game about psychology, it borderlines on being a teaching tool but doesn't loose track of the story or come off as “textbooky.”If you like sexy vampires, psychology and/or VNs with great VO work, this is a def pick up for you!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: It's is what it says: Vampire therapy, but i do wish there was a little more to do outside of the therapy...? I like Sam as a character and hopefully there's more story content for him. It plays like Ace Attorney, you pick up CBT terms and apply them where you need to in sessions - not particularly hard, and the clients you meet are usually fun to interact with. Another thing to note is that there is no fail state, if you use the wrong term the game tells you "thats wrong".Huge plus is that the entire thing is voice acted.My minor nitpick being that in the very first hour of gameplay two characters hit on you and you deny them four times in a row before being forced by the game to go along with their advances into a mini game- it felt like a weird choice given how the rest of the game works. Personally it did not bother me but I can imagine there might be someone put off by that game design decision.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Once I saw the name of the game and that the main character is a vampire cowboy, I knew I'd have to play it. Vampire Therapist is a generally charming game. I enjoyed the core gameplay and voice-acting, and I'd recommend it with some reservations (particularly one huge one at the end).I do wish that Sam's cowboy terms for cognitive distortions hadn't been immediately discarded. His examples are fun and evocative, and using terms like "High Noon Mind" and "Saloon Thinking" got me re-examining CBT concepts I'd long since internalized and otherwise tend to mentally gloss over in text. In comparison, "Nosferatu Thinking" is... cute? It's a joke but not a very evocative term, and for the first few sessions in the game I had to keep stopping to remember what it was supposed to mean.I  the blood-drinking mini-game though, and I wish it had been left out entirely. The teeth never actually line up with the vein you're supposed to bite, and I was never really sure why I succeeded sometimes and failed others. Overall, the experience is just irritating. In comparison, though the meditation mini-game is counterintuitive enough that I got stuck there for a while when it first appeared, I could consistently get through it easily enough after figuring out what it wanted me to do.You can also watch old black-and-white movies in Sam's coffin, for some reason. I really have nothing to say about the coffin TV besides that I'm confused about why it exists.The main reservation I have about the game is also the one part I'm genuinely angry about. The game provides some content warnings at the start, but it doesn't forewarn you then or at the time when it occurs that the last bit of gameplay is stopping a character's suicide attempt. There's also no way to prevent or skip over that section of the game. A game built in consultation with therapists and focused on mental health should know better than to spring that on players, and there's really no excuse for that massive oversight. There isn't even the token inclusion of a suicide hotline in the credits like most modern games that include onscreen attempts. This alone makes me wish there was a "maybe" review option instead of just "yes" or "no."As is, though I'd recommend the game in general, I absolutely would not do that without also spoiling that portion.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: The emotional intelligence of this game is ASTRONOMICAL! I love the way it approaches different mental health issues and cognitive distortions. While I don't recommend using a game to replace a professional, Vampire Therapist helps give different and new perspective on how to deal with these issues and distortions. It also reminds me that a step in the right direction, no matter how small, is still a step in the right direction.This game is beautifully made and I hope everyone gets a chance to enjoy it. Do be aware of the content warnings because some of the subject matter can be on the heavier side, but the story is lovely. I can't recommend it enough!

_childDocuments_.review: Lundy Bancroft is a counsellor who specialises in abusers, and a very good author. He warns that abusers and predators who receive generalized therapy can become more dangerous, and their therapy can 'inoculate' them against more specialized therapy later on.Vampire Therapist is unintentionally extremely good at portraying this, in its accurate and thorough portrayal of talk therapy. Its writing is well researched, it shows the severe holes in the practice between the lines, but avoids addressing this problem directly. I highly recommend this game, but I cannot do it in good conscience without a warning of what this game is avoiding.This kind of therapy is very good for identifying negative thought patterns, and for building an internal sense of self esteem.  It is very good for working with patients as they are, in a non-judgemental fashion. Because of this it often can't, or won't, present positive values to patients or teach them replacement skillsets or social expectations. So instead of making predators and abusers less of that, therapy can make them far more effective in their behaviours because they can use what they've learned in therapy as a weapon, and because it teaches them how to feel far more confident and unashamed in their antisocial behaviours without actually preventing those behaviours. Doing my best to not use spoilers, because I do recommend this game, I will limit myself to saying that the game has at least two storylines which show a heavy emphasis on the patient's emotional wellbeing with near total disregard to how dangerous they are to the people around them, and in one case a patient is celebrated for becoming more predatory in self-acceptance. This is not weak writing, but an accurate representation of this treatment in practice, and why getting the right *kind* of help is as important as getting help at all.Play Vampire Therapist, but keep this question in mind; "Does helping this patient hurt other people?"
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Interesting idea, poor execution. The comedy of an extremely American cowboy ending up in Leipzig with modern kinksters *is* funny, as is the premise of vampire therapy, but the dialogue is badly structured — you repeatedly end up with four options you must exhaust before progressing. This would only be annoying if one of those dialogues wasn't about sex and consent, where you are approached by two people who ask you to buy them a drink — where you, first, can't accept and are forced to refuse *four* times, and then the story puts you on rails to accept anyway; you then end up in the 'kink room' and play a stupid biting minigame. Baffling. I hope these elements are reworked, because it's promising otherwise, but as it is... no thanks.

_childDocuments_.review: At the end of my session with my Vampire Therapist, I would say I felt better overall (hence the brilliant blue thumb of approval), but unable to achieve full mindfulness.- Excellent VO performances. The voice talent carry this game.- Authentic characters expressed through natural writing.- Learn techniques to identify your own thought patterns!- Shoddy mini-games. Biting game feels like filler. Meditation game has bad conveyance (what am I supposed to do?).- The game is wrong about the "correct" Cognitive Distortion sometimes.- The above point is not my Cognitive Distortion either. Yes, I need therapy, but not over this! Let's talk about YOUR mother instead and see how you like it!!- Polish issues: Animation jitters. Script and VOs sometimes out of sync. Some outtakes still present in the wrong distortion choices. - The writing hiccups when transitioning to the spot the distortion sections (Lots of "That's neat, but let's continue . . ." kind of breaks)- Dialogue dips deeply into sappy, saccharine speeches - Summarily distracting (a lot alike abrupt alliteration). - They run the "Americans can't handle sex" joke into the ground. Firstly, this game taught me that's an Over-generalization. Secondly, as a citizen of Californication and a weeb with a Hidive subscription, this joke fell particularly flat.- Theater fans who enjoy passionate performances.- Fans of stories featuring characters with strong personalities, alien perspectives and intriguing histories.- Anyone who wants to dive into the thought patterns of ancient predators who could  while away their immortality writing Hallmark greeting cards and fortune cookie affirmations.Again, I want to stress that I liked this game, but I found myself constantly distracted. Sometimes those distractions came from without, via polish quirks and gameplay gaffs. Sometimes from within, via my fixation on writing that would cause my teeth to ache due to its sugary overtones. Perhaps a less curmudgeon-y, less finicky gamer would sink into this game's euphoric dialogues without feeling the sharp bite of dissonance prick them out of the moment. If you're a cynical bastard like I am (Labeling, I know), or can't switch off the part of your brain that's always spotting bloopers and ruining the movie for you and your couch buddies (and you're not in my "Recommend To" category), this might be a pass for you. Anyone else still reading this will likely enjoy their exceptionally voiced therapy sessions (hopefully subsidized with one of those schmancy non-American health plans).Now on the other hand, if you're all about those cynical bastard takes, or find something about my review style that speaks to you,

_childDocuments_.review: This is a highly intelligent game.  Not in the sense that it is pretentious.  A few of the characters you meet in the game ARE pretentious.But your main character is just a down to earth cowboy vampire who happens to be good at being a therapist to the undead.I found this game to be mentally stimulating, and even challenging.  Now this game is unpunishing - if you make a wrong decision, you don't get a game over, or a strike against you.  You simply try again, until you get the right answer.  But, you WANT to get the right answer the first time.  See, this game introduces very complex abstract concepts, and allows you to apply them to these troubled vampires, as they open up to you about their problems.  The goal is to get them to see past their own cognitive dissonance, and to see the truth of the situation they are in.  The truth of the matter is, their un-life isn't as bad as they make it out to be, and they are unnecessarily adding a lot of stress to themselves by holding themselves to unrealistic standards.I've only played this game for 3.7 hours at time of writing, but I myself am already learning a lot, about cognitive distortions, and, more importantly, about myself.  For I myself tend to view the world in very black and white terms, and that is a cognitive distortion that this game has helped me realize about myself.  For $15.00, that's a hell of a bargain.But the benefits of this game do not stop there.  This is, truly, a very gripping game.  It is more like a visual novel, with prompting similar at times to Phoenix Wright (when the court demands that you give the correct answer), but I truly felt that each vampire I interviewed, very much felt like a boss battle.  A fight.  Not in the sense that you are going against them, per se, but rather their distorted view of reality.  And it is exhausting.  I felt after each interview, I myself in the real world needed a break.  That is how deep each conversation gets.  It's almost emotionally draining, to talk to these vampires, because their personalities can be very abrasive, and the voice acting is so good and convincing, that this really does feel like having a difficult conversation with a patient, or a friend.  With the hardship of talking to these people, comes the very real reward that one feels when one successfully convinces a vampire that perhaps their view of reality is a little too extreme, and they should re-assess in order to fit in accordance to reality, not in spite of it.Yes, this game is very, VERY rewarding....as mentioned before, the voice acting is entirely on-point.  The art style is endearing, and the character designs are unique and vibrant, to match the characters' eccentric natures.  At no point did I feel bored.  These vampires keep you on your toes.  Buy this game.  Do yourself a favor, and get it.  When you talk to these vampires, you may just learn a little bit about yourself, as I have.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: i got this in a bundle together with a game I really enjoyed and i am so glad for that, otherwise i would've been very disappointed. your choices don't matter at all, not during therapy sessions, nor when approached by people to go to the kink room. If my therapist spoke so much during our limited session time i'd find a new therapist.Game play aside, something about this game seems to be very poorly optimized - even with graphics at the lowest setting, my computer gets hot and loud very quickly, which I've never encountered when playing literally any other visual novel type game, and even with much more challenging open world games is rarely an issue.

_childDocuments_.review: This one I absolutely recommend. I'm not normally someone who is easily taken into visual novels, but this one is special. It teaches you the basics of cognitive behavioral therapy you can immediately use for yourself, while being a vampire story that aspires to the idea vampires can aspire to more than they are. In practice the gameplay is like a much easier Ace Attorney, even after you get to the point you need to pick loadouts per session, but it's deeply rewarding and introspective. The voice acting is incredible. It's a must play for anyone wanting to start unpacking their own personal issues and has any affection for vampires whatsoever. Ever wanted to see a Red Dead Redemption protagonist become a vampire and watch public domain Three Stooges shorts from the comfort of his own coffin? That's a recommended by itself. This one deserves attention and love, even if just for suggesting What We Do in the Shadows inspired characters get some overdue therapy.

_childDocuments_.review: I love this game, absolutely a hidden gem. <3 But be aware, this is not a visual novel choices-matter game, its more of a find what therapy terms a patient is doing while they talk to you.It's basically is teaching you how to spot cognitive distortions and basic cognitive behavioral therapy (Polarized Thinking, Labeling, "Should" Statements, Control Fallacy, etc.)Doesn't sound like a fun game? Think again, you are learning by therapizing existential questions and issues that vampires have after death. Apparently they consulted with real therapists making this game and it shows, its sooo good. I played the demo of this during nextfest and was hooked.The voice acting is phenomenal, the stories of each vampire just draw you in, and I love the quippy humor inserted in the mix. As a lover of deep existential questions in video games, I am very much the target audience for this type of game. Also I love that the protag is a COWBOY vampire and that somehow works. xDOne of the most unique games I've played.10/10 no notes

_childDocuments_.review: I really like this game. Structurally it's a visual novel, but with an interested mechanics thrown in – .
