_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Therapist follows a cowboy vampire named Sam who has been alive for over 200 years. He has done some terrible things in his past, but after spending 90 years wandering the wilderness finding himself and coming to some realizations, he had the urge to help his fellow vampires. After learning how to use the internet just enough to email people, he came into contact with a 3,000 year old vampire known as Andromachos. Andromachos invites Sam to his club in Europe and, after proving himself to his employees, is able to meet Andromachos himself. It turns out the revelations Sam had were cognitive distortions he was able to figure out entirely by himself, which Andromachos was pretty impressed by. He teaches Sam the correct terms (rip Sam’s original names for them), tests him, and tells him that he will take Sam under his wing if Sam agrees to receive therapy as well. Much to Sam’s surprise, Sam will also have four vampire clients of his own, one per week with them returning every month.Thus, starts the game’s narrative loop. Sam will have a therapy session with Andromachos, where you get to hear his struggles and backstory, and learn more cognitive distortions to use. Then you’ll have sessions with your four clients as their therapist. You’ll get some basic information on them and what they’re coming in for, but it soon becomes apparent that there’s more to it. Despite being vampires who died in different time periods, they are actually pretty relatable with the problems they end up having. There’s Dr. Drayne a researcher struggling with addiction, a previously powerful matriarch named Isabella d’Este who feels her life/unlife was meaningless, Edmund Kean a Shakespearean actor who wants to return to the stage but has anger at the mere thought of getting criticized, and Meddy who is basically a vampire influencer who is struggling with the increasing demands of her followers. These guys are all pretty unique and interesting to talk to and learn about. There’s also some side characters you’ll interact with as well, with Crimson being the one you learn about the most.Gameplay is pretty simple here. Aside from the occasional dialogue choice, you’ll be tasked with identifying the cognitive distortion your client is exhibiting using the five that’s listed (which, once you learn more than five, are ones you end up picking yourself before the session). Don’t worry, there’s no fail state here so if you pick wrong you just get a hint on what the answer is and asked to pick again until you get it right. There’s also two minigames, which I found pretty okay. The first has you line up an icon of fangs to a human’s veins to drink blood (though it does get a bit harder with those that wear collars) and another where you meditate by breathing in and out and hovering your cursor over the words. I didn’t mind the inclusion of these minigames, but they are a bit annoying when you’re replaying to get missing achievements.Sam also has a journal where he puts all the cognitive distortion definitions in his own writing style, with cowboy-centry examples, session summaries for his clients, and journal entries for what he did during the time skips.No game is perfect and Vampire Therapist is no exception. Some of these are personal annoyances and some of these aren’t and I’ll just list them out:I was not expecting this to be fully voiced. All the voice actors did a wonderful job and really brought the characters to life. Each voice actor fit their character really well and I especially loved Meddy’s and Sam’s voice actors and the direction they were given. The music is also pretty good, giving it that club feel while also it perfectly balancing between being good background music and being too annoying to listen to constantly.Vampire Therapist definitely met my expectations that I developed after playing the demo. There are some aspects that I got annoyed by, but this is a great, solid, game that I’m so glad I played. Vampire Therapist managed to implement the real concepts of cognitive distortions in a way that was fun to learn and use. The writing style is great, and adding the wonderful voice acting brings more life to all the characters, and all the characters were all written very well. The game does a great job in bringing us along on their therapy journey, giving us their backstories naturally, and shows how each of them change over time. I honestly could not bring myself to end a play session until I did everyone’s session for that “month” and could barely stay away from the game for long. Not to mention that you play as a cowboy vampire!I’d say if you’re interested in playing a visual novel where you’re a therapist, uses real cognitive behavioral therapy concepts, and fine with it only focusing on the therapy; you’ll most likely like Vampire Therapist. The game is actually priced perfectly and is worth playing if you’re interested in what this game is offering. Though, you might get disappointing if you’re expecting to get scenes that aren’t focused on being a therapist and you’ll of course not like Vampire Therapist if you’re not at all interested in the premise.

_childDocuments_.review: This game takes the concepts of cognitive behavorial therapy and thought distortions and says "You know how people can learn them? COWBOY VAMPIRES." And amazingly, it works! You learn about them by playing as Sam, a cowboy vampire therapist in training, and seeing clients of the night. Cyrus, you have made a wonderful game where you learn how to identify the distortions and fight them, whilst maintaining a sense of humor and genre savvy jokes. I tip my hat to you, good sir!

_childDocuments_.review: Really clever, thought-provoking, funny, and unusual. Slipped in among the interesting, entertaining, and sometimes _sehr sexy_ characters are real-life psychological concepts. As the game progresses, you learn and practice more concepts, all the while getting sucked into the characters' stories. (Isabella d'Este is especially compelling -- her backstory is rich and the voice acting is AMAZING.) Each character has a distinct set of thought patterns, which makes each session feel like a different experience.  It's also extremely funny, if British-American is your bag. Buckets of wit, but also some goofy gags (hello, 3 Stooges). I saw a minor bugs in the launch version, but hitting the menu fixed them. Totally worth it; this game is something special.

_childDocuments_.review: Playing Vampire Therapist has opened my eyes to an entirely unexpected gaming experience. What truly captivates me is how it masterfully weaves legitimate therapeutic techniques and psychological terminology into a narrative centered around vampires. The game delves deep into their struggles with loss, emotional trauma, and the fascinating tension between morality and immortality that develops as these beings age through centuries.What sets this game apart is its refreshing take on vampire mythology. The characters are wonderfully crafted, balancing profound depth with moments of genuine humor that catch you off guard in the best possible way. I particularly appreciate how the game challenges traditional vampire tropes, presenting these immortal beings through various lenses and showing them grappling with challenges that feel surprisingly – almost uncomfortably – human.For anyone seeking an unconventional vampire story, this game delivers something special. It's a quirky yet thoughtful exploration of immortal beings facing very mortal problems, all while offering fascinating insights into therapeutic practices. _childDocuments_.review: Yee-naw, that ain't what I'm talking about! I hate to be harsh, as there's clearly a lot of love put into this game, but... yeah, between the choice of an ultra-stereotypical accented cowboy as the protagonist, the limited player agency, and the fact this is more like a quiz edutainment game than anything really killed my interest fast.I was so excited for this one! It looked exceptionally promising! And instead I found myself glossing over as Sam kept being encouraged to speak more, and more, and more, even though a therapist's job is, above all else, to listen. Yet most of your listening is instead about trying to figure which button at the bottom to press to continue the conversation, with no real risk of failure. It really sucks too because Andy, the head vampire therapist, is super charming, and the majority of the cast are bolstered by very talented vocal performances. The art is well done. This isn't a case of lack of skill, just... some utterly baffling creative decisions.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Two sessions in and I can safely say I wish this had come out sooner, as it'd have made my studying for Psych back in college much easier if I could de-stress like this. It's by far not meant to be used to treat yourself, but it provides an external lens that might just highlight a couple things in you.It's ultimately your average VN affair, but the approach of being a therapist gives it a 'pleasant' hook: the draw of helping others. I've had a few moments just among the first two clients where I had to pause and go 'Holy hell I've said about that much myself' and then found myself wanting to help them out even more. Like I said, this won't fix you, but at the very least it may help you identify a few things to speak about with a proper professional, or at the very least try to adjust yourself in the interim.Besides all of that, the art has been quite nice. It's easy to get a vibe for your clients just off of their portraits, and the character designs have been rather fun. Sam's just an overall enjoyable MC, and Andy is  as your guide. Voice acting is quality as well. Overall for a 15 dollar price tag this is a steal in my limited VN experience, especially considering the baseline exposure to basic psychotherapy.EDIT: One visit each with 4 different clients and my opinion remains the same. There are some startlingly relatable scenarios in play for centuries-old bone bags. And it's not all sunshine and rainbows either, which I enjoy. I expected the pushback, and it was realistic. If I remember to update again as I keep playing through, I will, but the extra hour/extra exposure has just reaffirmed how much I enjoy it.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the game, I’m updating my review. This game is everything I didn’t know I needed. I adore the characters so freaking much and the ending, without giving too much away, left me fighting off a case of the sniffles. Despite being a fairly short game, 12 hours give or take, I quickly grew attached to the characters because they were all very well written and the conversations felt realistic and organic, a thing which is kind of lacking nowadays. The music and sound were very well done, and while I hate the term ‘cozy’ in relation to a game, the setting for this was. It was relaxing, and I often found myself playing later in the evening when I wanted to wind down. I also enjoyed that the game caused me to take a look at myself as well; I even ended up mentioning the game to my therapist, and we had a few chats based on this game made me think about. However, that isn’t to say it’s ALL good. The game is, as I said, fairly short. Because of this, things happen quickly. There’s a lot of ‘behind the scenes’ relationship building between everyone that would have been nice to see firsthand. Stretching things out a bit would have also helped with the distortion concepts. Some of them were quite complex and hard to grasp, even with Andromachos’s examples. In the late game, I noticed quite a few spelling and grammar mistakes, small things like a missing comma or switched letters. There also doesn’t seem to be any replay ability to this and there is no real way to ‘lose’ or fail. Everyone gets their happy (mostly) ending. Now I could be wrong about that, but that’s how it appears. Lastly, the neck biting mini game. I’ll be honest. I hate it with a passion. I’m color blind and couldn’t really see the veins from the skin, let alone the two different veins, a fact which was made ever harder by the speed of the teeth. Maybe a progress bar with a little green ‘click when the slider is in here’ spot would have been better. Over all this game is amazing, and that teaser at the end, for a part two was just cruel because I WANT to get to know these characters better, want to spend time with them and I want to talk to them and hang out in the games world.

_childDocuments_.review: A friend recommended me to play the demo of this game, and I was immediately hooked. Bought the full-release version soon after it came out. The voice-acting and visuals have so much thought put into them, and the dialogue makes it very clear to me how much effort was put into making this game conscious of how therapy works in the real world. The concept is also dripping with personality. I've truly never seen anything like it. I also personally love how forgiving the gameplay is and how you're allowed to make mistakes without worrying too much about "losing", which allows the player to focus on growth. While this game might not me for everyone (as it is very dialogue-heavy and may be too forgiving for some), it has helped me take a step back during my own therapy journey and, in some ways, has helped me recognize some cognitive distortions within myself.

_childDocuments_.review: This was a really interesting story. I personally found the stories and characters fascinating and compelling. I also really enjoyed the interspersed vampire jokes acting as comic relief for often quite heavy subject matter.I started playing this with my partner but she quickly got bored and I continued alone, so it's not for everyone, but I found the details of cognitive distortions very interesting.Note that this is a VN, it's not really a game; there's interactivity in that you occasionally steer the conversations with choices, and you're invited to identify the cognitive distortions being displayed by the vampires as you talk to them, but that's about the limit of the gameplay.I'd recommend this if you're interested in stories about vampire psychology.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost never leave reviews but felt somewhat obligated to write this one. Despite the fact that I thoroughly enjoyed this game and am giving it a thumbs up, I am only really leaving this review to say that it absolutely will NOT appeal to everyone, and there are some things that should be made 100% clear to you before you decide to buy it.Most importantly, this is probably the most on rails visual novel I have ever played. You are moving from point A to B in the story no matter what happens, with no input on the proceedings whatsoever. Not only that, there are no fail states either; you cannot lose at Vampire Therapist and you are not punished for wrong answers in therapy sessions (you are rewarded for repeated successes with achievements though, for what it's worth.) I saw a negative review that summed this issue up quite well by calling it a quiz edutainment game more than anything else. It's not that the game doesn't have more to offer than that in terms of character or narrative, but that is absolutely the core gameplay loop of Vampire Therapist and needless to say this all ends up hurting replayability.Another small issue with the game that ties back to my first point is that because the game is so incredibly on rails your playtime is going to depend almost entirely on your reading speed. This is not necessarily a bad thing, but I think most people who play this kind of game can generally read at a fairly decent pace so you might not end up taking very long to complete all of the content. You can see this in some of the positive steam reviews for the game with some people having evidently completed it in four hours or less. This is most apparent with the two free DLCs, which despite being said to take approximately 30 minutes each are not very difficult to read through in five to ten.Lastly, in my very subjective opinion, the humor is also somewhat hit and miss. It is absolutely capable of being a very funny game, but that is not a rule. Most egregious in my opinion are a few jokes that end up dating the game, usually bits that refer to some kind of specific event from recent years in our time period. The game is small enough in scope that I imagine not many people will be playing it ten years from now, but if someone does something like that will absolutely feel very dated. Again, this is the most subjective part of the review by far, though. I probably made the game sound pretty bad with these three points, so let me be clear in saying that I still very much enjoyed it. It is well written, usually funny, has a cast of interesting characters who all have enjoyable, complex personalities, and probably most importantly clearly has a lot of love put into it. Even though there are certainly elements that I did not entirely appreciate, that is not to say that there is nothing good about Vampire Therapist.If all of the negatives that I listed out do not sound objectionably bad to you, I would recommend giving this a try.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I was expecting something more lighthearted and comical when I picked up this game, something along the lines of "Analyze this". I suppose that is what sprung to my mind when I read the title "Vampire Therapist". Though it does contain elements of lightheartedness and humor, this game deals with some heavier stuff than that. Not being what I expected does not equate to being bad though, so I recommend giving this game a try.Going a little further into details:You play as Samuel, a 200ish year old American cowboy vampire, who has had a revelation after spending 90 years wandering in the wilderness. He wants to help other vampires deal with the negative thinking (i.e. cognitive distortions) that keeps them from achieving personal growth, in other words he wants to become a therapist. For this, he travels to Leipzig, Germany, to meet Andromechos, an ancient several thousand year old Vampire, who becomes his mentor. While Adromechos takes Samuel into therapy, to help him deal with his own congnitive distortions, Samuel takes on 4 clients. A scientist, who has an addiction problem. A rennaisance noblewoman, who believes her existence has lost its meaning. An actor, who feels unappreciated by his critics and audience, and an internet celebrity, who feels stressed out by the demands of her followers. All of them also vampires.Through a series of sessions, you attempt to identify your own and your clients cognitive distortions, by clicking the correct option, with Adromechos offering advice when you get it wrong. As the game progresses, the difficulty increases, as more distortions are introduced and explained to you, and you must select which to focus on prior to each session. Other than some very simple gameified neck biting, and mildly entertaining cutscenes, that is pretty much it.I found it somewhat entertaining and challenging, and recommend giving it a try. The neck biting felt like an unnecessary and somewhat pointless hurdle between sessions to me, and unless you are a perfectionist and/or achievement hunter, I don't think this game offers much replayability.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so good I scarcely have the words for it. The passion that went into this is on full display, and I am stunned by the amount of research that must have gone into it. All the topics are explored respectfully without being pretentious, and the empathy and kindness it treats its characters with is a breath of fresh air.

_childDocuments_.review: Sometimes a game comes around with a concept so seemingly tailor-made for your artistic sensibilities that it seems too good to be true. Vampire Therapist lives up to its concept and then some. The writing is high quality, with each character having a distinct, recognizable voice, and their actors bring their dialogue to life beautifully. Speaking of the characters, I was instantly invested in their stories and wellbeing. I was literally clapping and cheering at certain points! It's definitely more of a reading experience than a gameplay experience, but the gameplay does a good job of enhancing the story by making the player think carefully about what the characters are saying, even if making an incorrect choice doesn't result in penalty most of the time. I'm not usually one to take notes for games, but I found myself naturally jotting down which cognitive distortions the clients used most often, or thoughts about what might be causing a certain reaction. This is the kind of game that makes me want to write something about it, and that's the highest praise I can give.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything it promises to be, and more. It's funny, moving, thoughtful, and sometimes even sexy. The art is really good, and the voice acting is superb (no surprises here, considering the cast, but still worth mentioning). I loved the references I spotted. I got a few minor bugs, but nothing I couldn't fix by going back to the main menu. I got really attached to Sam, the protagonist, but all the characters are intriguing, likable and relatable in a way or another, and I enjoyed learning more about them through each meeting and trying to guide them on a path of self-discovery and self-forgiveness. Truthfully, the game helped me realize how often I myself fall prey to these cognitive distortions, and why they're not helpful. It doesn't replace actual therapy, but being able to catch myself (or other people) doing it and identifying them is pretty neat. I guess we all need a Sam in our lives.The only thing I'm still confused about are the meditation parts. I don't know how I got that perfect focus achievement, I never figured what I was supposed to do during those parts (Sam's random thoughts were pretty funny, though). Other than that, it's a really accessible game, it never punishes you for getting an answer wrong, and you can at any point remind yourself of the cognitive distortions you've learned about by opening your journal. All in all, a refreshing and well-intentioned game about vampires and therapy. Here's to hoping for a "Vampire therapist 2"!

_childDocuments_.review: I am a psychology honours student with a history of self-loathing, and this game is one of the big highlights of my gaming year. Voice acting for something like this can be difficult, but I felt that the cast hit all the beats just right, and they're backed up by such great stories, both on their own and together. _childDocuments_.review: Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) is a psycho-social intervention that aims to reduce symptoms of various mental health conditions, primarily depression and anxiety disorders. Cognitive behavioral therapy focuses on challenging and changing cognitive distortions (such as thoughts, beliefs, and attitudes) and their associated behaviors to improve emotional regulation and develop personal coping strategies that target solving current problems. Though it was originally designed to treat depression, its uses have been expanded to include many issues and the treatment of many mental health and other conditions, including anxiety, substance use disorders, marital problems, ADHD, and eating disorders. CBT includes a number of cognitive or behavioral psychotherapies that treat defined psychopathologies using evidence-based techniques and strategies.

_childDocuments_.review: I was utterly let down by this game.  What first seemed to be a uniquely creative experience quickly devolved into a soap-box piece.  I love vampires, and I love the concepts of cognitive based therapy.  How could this go wrong?  The voice acting was also charming in the game.   So how could it go wrong?  It becomes a long winded diatribe against a certain portion of society, and that takes away from the story of "Vampire Therapy" to the point my immersion and humor was ruined!  When I realized I was just hearing someone's personal ideological rant from each character, rather than a story born of unique characters, I had to put it aside for wasting my time.The first instance was this long winded exchange that the great flood is a myth.  (It had no context to any of the characters either, as in, there was no character traumatized by the flood.)  It was out of place with the context of the discussion and odd.  Archaeology shows us sediment layers and fossil groups that prove Earth endured a major flood event, its why there is a great flood story in almost every culture's religion and records.  Whether you are Atheist, Agnostic, Muslim or Christian, science has shown us for a long time now that there was a great flood in Earth's history...  So while I would've accepted this rant if one of the characters was traumatized by the flood, it was entirely out of context and also ignorant of science.  Why are these age old vampires in the game not aware of that, and why the long winded rant against it out of sync with any subject matter the characters were engaged in?  I shrugged it off and played on. Then from that point, it only became more and more clear....   Jokes about Jesus and anal sex.  Jokes about farting in a chair that Jesus made.  Amongst other out of context, endless diatribes.  But it wasn't like it was just coming from one character who had an issue with Christianity or Jesus, it was coming from several characters, none of whom had an issue with Jesus!  So...  wtf?  Okay, well, traditionally speaking the very origin stories of vampires were that they hung out in catacombs and protected churches in exchange for protection during the day when they slept.  Then we have Dracula, an orthodox turned catholic crusader who repelled the Ottoman invasion.  So...  it wasn't humor or therapy that this endless exchanges were coming from, and it was odd that the game moved from the delicious concepts of Vampire Therapy to this anti-Jesus tirade.  And then, suddenly, came the tirade against the United States' personal liberty and the competition of Capitalism.  Again, this was not born out of what happened to one of the characters for the sake of therapy - it had nothing to do with the poor choices one of the characters made, yet it was inserted and then after sitting through it, there was one loose statement trying to tie it in to the trauma of the characters and I'm sorry, it fails!  It is obvious that "Vampire Therapy" was being loosely and illogically used as an excuse to force-fit ideological rants (not thoughtful discussions) into the game.  I wonder if the person who wrote this experienced the mass starvation tied to the history of nations run by communist dictatorships.  So, yeah, the game started off charming, but quickly devolved into an anti-Jesus Christ, pro-communist rant that Did. Not. Stop.  When you hear the same words and the same lines come out of several characters, those aren't genuine characters, that's bad writing.  And when you realize you're just reading someone's ignorant first year college essay instead of playing an entertaining game with genuine characters, I check out.  I uninstalled this garbage and deleted it from my library.  People who want to create 'games' only to self insert their rabid rants need to advertise correctly that the game is about that rather than try to sell it as "humorous and thoughtful discourse."

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10. Art.Vampire Therapist is a one-of-a-kind game that blends supernatural drama with real-world psychology. You’re a therapist using Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to help vampire clients deal with centuries of baggage — from guilt and loneliness to existential dread. _childDocuments_.review: I don't remember when I added this game to my wishlist but I got it for my birthday and I was super excited to play it. I've always been a psychology/therapy enthusiast. Finding out there was a somewhat accurate game about being a therapist to vampires was like a dream I didn’t know I wanted to have.The game uses real therapy concepts like cognitive behavior therapy, vetted by licensed professionals. So you know that what our characters are saying (at least the technical stuff) is real! It's like Therapist Simulator- Vampire Edition. I'd totally buy that one too. Besides therapy aspects, the game also has a lot of comedic elements. It's considered dark humor, but to me its just humor really. With that same comedic lens, it looks at some alternate historic depictions - could be characters and event or both and also the depiction of vampires.  It's a vampire game after all. But remember this, even vampires need consent! They can also learn too! I love that this is one of the things mentioned in this game since it has been historically depicted that vampires don't care. This gives vampires a little bit more humanity and respect towards others.  While still in the subject of how the game plays, even if it is a visual novel- it has mini-games! You can see how beautifully I mess up these games in my video. In clearer terms, I suck- pun intended. The game also features a stellar cast of voice actors you may even recognize some! During game play, I kept thinking, I know that voice. Once the credit rolled and I saw "Matthew Mercer" I screamed "I knew it!!"  at my monitor. It was very awesome to hear some actors I've heard in other games before. Now….Important stuff:⚠️⚠️Trigger Warning: Please read the content warning at the start of the game and on the Steam Store Page before continuing. ⚠️⚠️The game deals with some mature and challenging themes given that it uses real therapy practices, concepts and situations. Think in a very broad spectrum, all the situations people may go to therapy for. These may be included in the game. Please read the content warning on the Store Page and at the start of the game.You can watch my play-through on my YouTube Channel:  You'll also find more reviews and recommendations on my Steam Curator Page, My Instagram and YouTube Channel. _childDocuments_.review: I bloody love this game, pun intended obviously. _childDocuments_.review: A deeply analytical game on what it's like to be a vampire and the mental health problems that could come with it. The characters are well fleshed out and all highly unique. This is the kind of visual novel game that will lead you to making introspective critiques of yourself and the environment you live in. The game also taught me quite a bit about psychology as an academic subject. My only real complaint about the game is a weakness of the visual novel genre. Sometimes the game is looking for a specific cognitive distortion and I don't agree with the answer the game says is right. I think it might be because certain statements have more than one cognitive distortion, but for the sake of gameplay and the visual novel genre only one can be right. To be fair though, any game that can pull me in this much is absolutely a game worth playing.

_childDocuments_.review: This visual novel seems to be very linear, but it proved to be an excellent educational experience into exploring various cognitive distortions, with examples that were framed in a compelling narrative that made me tear up several times. There are numerous allusions to real people and history that spurred me to want to learn more about the real world as well. I was not expecting the mixed media elements, and I thought it was novel to be able to watch TV as Sam. The game does not shy away from being political at times, which might irritate some people, but I think that's unavoidable to some degree in telling a story that is grounded in presenting the human condition. I find myself invested in all of the characters we've encountered, and I'm very excited about the prospect of seeing a sequel.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who is a fan of vampires, story driven games and the practice of psychology, this game ticks so many boxes for me.  Add on top gorgeous backgrounds, well drawn characters, a bopping soundtrack, excellent voice acting and a great variety of in-game mechanics focused on feeding and meditation to drive the story forward, you can't go wrong with this game if you're looking for a cosy, interactive and well-made game to help flex your empathetic muscles, and learn a few tips and therapeutic tricks.I was very grateful of the mindful trigger warnings, and any players can take note of same should they not be in a place to experience such things yet.The entire design of the characters and the atmosphere were just stunning, and I felt quite proud to have helped the clients the way that I did.  The stakes were often times raised and I felt so compelled to continue to help Sam be the best vampire therapist.It is a lovely gem of a game and there should absolutely be a sequel as I am not ready to say goodbye to this world and characters just yet.

_childDocuments_.review: I LOVED this game! I'm already looking forward to the second one. A friend reccommended this to me before it even came out because it fits so well with my interests. I wish there were more video games incorporating psychotherapy and psychology, honestly! You really don't have to be into psychology to enjoy this though. If you're like me and you love WWDITS, vampires, and games like Ace Attorney, you'll definitely be interested in this. The story, dialogue, and characters were really well-written and moving. _childDocuments_.review: Very interesting game. The concept was enough for me to wishlist it, and I enjoyed playing through it. The fun character writing and psych concepts stuck in my mind enough for me to finish the game despite taking a couple breaks. Being a therapist made me nervous. I was first concerned with how many distortions I was labeling wrong: the definitions seemed broad enough that multiple distortions could apply to the same statement but the game wanted one. I had an easier time towards the end of the game where the system accepted multiple answers. The next concern I had involved the horse neigh, which wouldn't happen during every session for me and I relied on it to give me the dopamine hit of being a good therapist. I also overthought what distortions I should pick before the sessions. It was a satisfying experience. I enjoyed how the story resolved itself, and after the credits rolled I felt that I had learned something useful.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I loved my time with Vampire Therapist. It was funny, silly, sweet, sad and most of all, heartfelt. The characters are all complex and interesting, and I got so attached to my clients that it was genuinely bittersweet to reach the end of the game. The voice work, writing and art are all fantastic. I've found myself using a little bit of what the game taught me in real life - I'll catch my own thoughts with "Oh, is that Nosferatu thinking?" or "Huh! That sounds like catastrophizing." It's nice to have a little vampire cowboy in my head helping me a little sometimes, lol. There are a few very minor bugs & quirks here and there. A few mismatched dialogues, a couple of editing issues on voice lines, and some interesting save/load interactions. Nothing game-breaking and nothing bad enough to affect my enjoyment. I'm sure anything notable will be fixed in future updates. I can tell how much love went into the game, and it sincerely deserves to be loved in return. That may be a Fairness Fallacy, but I'll keep believing in it, haha. I really hope to see another Vampire Therapist game in the future!!

_childDocuments_.review: I recommended this game to my therapist. I also would recommend this for anyone that is interested in psychology/mental health, as well as people who are going to therapy in real life. Took me about 6 hours to complete, not in one sitting though, it's alot of reading and trying to figure out correct responses. But it's well-written and relaxing to play.- The art style.- The overall vibe of the game.- Non-intense gameplay (yes, I know, visual novels aren't intense, but I do appreciate not having an intense game to play).- The overall story.- Covers mental health topics with respect.- The terms used for the cognitive distortions are actual terms I have heard in therapy.- Well-written and interesting main character.- Andy is also well-written and likeable.- Between sessions with clients, to take a mental break from that reading, there's some more chill dialogue, as well as optional poetry reading and whole episodes of older shows.>> I was pleasantly surprised that I could sit through an entire episode of The Three Stooges and actually laughed quite a few times, although the last episode they included in the game wasn't very funny in my opinion. Then again, I grew up with alot of 1930's, 1940's, 1980's, and 2000's movies/shows, so it's just a personal interest.- Should have had more clarification for the player on what to do during the meditation sessions. I was stuck in the first one for quite a while before I figured out what I needed to do. (Edit: this has now been added since I first made this review, glad to see they are actively making improvements.)- Wish you didn't have to restart the section of dialogue when you miss an identification of a cognitive distortion.- Some of the subtitles for the dialogue don't match.- Alot of the clients aren't that interesting to me.- Wish it was optional to do the vampire-biting sections, and have a choice to have a drink instead.- There's alot of talk about sex (yes I'm also American). Not the most comfortable topic for me, and I would definitely recommend playing this with a headphone or headset.-I will play this again. And I like how there is a hint of a potential sequel at the end of the game. I will definitely play the second one if they make it.

_childDocuments_.review: The game is challenging for a visual novel, but incredibly forgiving. Which is good, because the cognitive distortions can often be very hard to recognize, much like in real life. Each character you meet is unique, fun to talk to, and has very intricate details to them (both story and design-wise). The game has somehow managed to take nearly every vampire trope and archetype and shove it into a clown car, and honestly kudos to them because that's no easy feat with how diverse vampires alone have become.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: So for reference I have beaten the entire game (7.3 hours), and am a therapist in real life myself, a Cognitive-Behavioral Therapist as well, like the game seems to base itself on. As such I am extremely biased so keep that in mind.This game is so good, so amazing, as both a teaching tool and as a shockingly realistic portrayal of what effective CBT therapy is, that I am heavily considering assigning it as homework to clients as a teaching tool (and will be requesting my own personal therapist, an older gentleman, play himself to potentially pass it along to -his- clients as well). The characters are genuine and sincere (and oftentimes annoying as hell, as humans tend to be), the voice acting is top notch (either A+ tier impressionists or they found genuinely skilled voice actors from all parts of the world), the writing is funny and insightful, and the insight and genuine mastery of psychological principals are humbling. -I- learned things, and at a minimum, even as a therapist explicitly trained in these things, it was an excellent review.I'm not sure if it will be for everyone, but it is clearly made with such love and care and passion, clearly with the intention to do good in the world rather than to make a million dollars, that it is breathtaking. I feel like it's one of those games that I will think about for years. Especially that final part, which without giving too many spoilers, really highlights the "unique to therapists" problem of thinking we already know enough that we can't fall into the same traps that our clients fall into, and thus how important it is for even therapists to have therapists. Truly beautiful.This is a game filled with love, and compassion, and acceptance, and healing, and growth. It reminds us that the most frustrating, upsetting, annoying, hurtful, and even "evil" people in this world are in the end deeply human, and flawed, and oftentimes hurting. It's also charming as hell, as only an "awww shucks" cowboy can be. Beyond excellent, 10/10, "literally recommended this to my mom who doesn't even play videogames" seal of quality.Edit note: So a few of the negative reviews have pointed out being "railroaded" into choices, particularly in regards to the activities your character participates in. While these are true statements I want to point out this is a visual novel and not an RPG, you are not "playing a character", you are following along with what the main character, a 200 year old cowboy vampire who may have tastes, morals, and desires different from you, would do. So if he makes a choice you yourself don't like or wouldn't want to do, that's perfectly valid, but to that end I ask people to keep in mind that he is acting according to what -he- would do. I would also state that there is (in my opinion) nothing explicit that he ever does/"you" have to do, so if that is a barrier for you/causes you discomfort, I would also state that exploring difficult people and concepts and alternative viewpoints from a wide variety of people is indeed the point. I would state wholeheartedly that what the game has to offer/teach is worth the discomfort it may inspire in some people.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: A funny, thoughtful, sexy, and compassionate visual novel. If you love character analysis, complex and layered characters, and vampires then you'll love this game. My hats off to the developer for this being their first game! I thoroughly enjoyed all the writing and art; a spectacular first outting for any developer. I now eagerly await any sequel! :D
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: This game is everything that I am nerdy about. Vampires, cowboys, history, psychology. It's a really good tool for boiling down therapy concepts. It tells a great story that I simply cannot put down! The art is beautiful and the voice acting is amazing. Give this game a shot, I think you'll fall in love too! I will warn everyone that there does need to be a trigger warning for some suicidal ideation. Just be prepared, it's not too heavy or very center to the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: A great game that's helped me look inward! The different characters are fun to interact with, and the writing's got a great range of light-hearted humor with its more serious/dramatic moments. The mini-games take some getting used to, but they're nice breathers from the rest of the visual novel elements.
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: An absolutely delightful game - although if I'm being honest there isn't much 'game' there per se, it plays a lot more like a Visual Novel where guessing the correct cognitive distortion grants you more dialogue.That being said, what Vampire Therapist does well, it does VERY well: the characters are very compellingly portrayed, both in their gorgeous visual art and top-notch voice acting that helps bring them to (un)life. While charming and funny, often using light-hearted jabs at various national and historical stereotypes (because remember, vampires are immortal), the game does also have its more serious moments that stop that the characters from being complete caricatures - after all, it's hard to give a character therapy if their trauma doesn't feel real. Ironically, the more vampiric the characters act, the more they reveal that they are actually very human, which I suppose is the point.From a technical standpoint the game is a little bit buggy, although not in a way that stopped me from enjoying the experience: the curtain transitions are VERY choppy, and I noticed that sometimes when I saved while on the screen in which you choose cognitive distortions for your next session, loading back into that save would result in a placeholder menu with no patient data loaded in, plus some other minor things like loading when an image was being displayed might show the wrong image. However, these were very minor gripes thanks to the game's autosave (or checkpoint) system; the actual dialogue, character images and voice acting all played as they should.Wait... SHOULD?!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I have been waiting for this game since I found out about it! _childDocuments_.review: Played the first couple hours together with my roommate, have to say this is genuinely one of the most fun games either of us have played in a while! Incredible) Really great balance in terms of difficulty for selecting each distortion - prompted some really fun discussions between us! Maybe the first time I've seen a really accurate depiction of what it's like to be in a therapy session - there is joy and lightness and pain and sadness and sometimes, yes, you do have to explain to your therapist the difference between RPG and FPS games. _childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: In the midst of the ever ongoing vampire craze, this is a pretty unique take on the creatures of the night and their surprisingly ordinary problems. If you love narrative games with a bit of a twist on the age-old formula, gorgeous character artwork and a generous helping of (sometimes cringey but good-natured) humour, this will be right up your alley. I didn't expect the game to remain so genuine throughout, considering you meet some whacky characters right out the bat (ha!). It manages to get a couple of complex concepts across while still being entertaining. Every patient has their personal history to explore and figure out a way to live with that in modern times with all its trials and tribulations. The results are funny yet heartfelt and emphasize compassion as a core message - I can honestly say it was a refreshing and enjoyable ride. Last but not least, always a joy to see some more games toeing the line between serious game and a fun time, as well as being produced in Germany. :) Doubly so as it is very queer-friendly. Diversity win!
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: Vampire Therapist is an excellent game that feels like the start of something big and I'd recommend it to all fans of visual novels who like games that push the VN formula a little further. You will also learn a lot about therapy and about yourself while playing without even realising it's happening. Also, there are cowboys AND vampires, so that's pretty ideal!My only question now is when's the sequel happening?
_childDocuments_.name: Vampire Therapist

_childDocuments_.review: I delight in playing Vampire Therapist almost as much as it delights in poking fun at Americans' discomfort around foreign languages and intimate matters. This game's writing is sharp, its voice acting on point, and its message genuinely heartfelt and helpful. The occasional typo and the audio being cut short in one or two spots are my only real complaints. Even if this game pokes at some sore points and highlights harmful patterns in my own thinking, I'm happy I found it and will recommend it to everyone I can.

I haven't gotten to any of the endings yet though. Overall I'm really happy with this game. If I were rating I'd give it a 4.5/5That said, I have a few recommendations for the dev/s: -Please allow us to access the journal when we are choosing which distortions the client might exhibit before the session. It will help us to better deliberate on which distortions we should pick.-Add an auto advance button for dialogue.-add a message log for past message.

_childDocuments_.review: If you like sexy vampires, clever banter, and improved mental health, this is the game for you.You play as Sam Walls, a 200-year-old cowboy vampire, who seeks out Andromachos, a powerful ancient vampire (and goth club owner), for advice on helping other vampires overcome harmful patterns of thinking. As you conduct frank and funny therapy sessions with some delightfully messy vampire patients, you learn to identify real concepts from behavioral psychology. Superbly voice acted and wittily written, Vampire Therapist just sticks with you, in the best possible way. I catch myself watching my own words and thought patterns even after I've put the game down. I also look at people's juicy arteries differently. (Props to the neck biting mini game!)I played an early version of the build and busted a gut laughing out loud. Now I've started over, playing the game in its full campy, sexy glory, and I can't get over its utter charm and originality. Full disclosure: I know the creator!

_childDocuments_.review: I have a rule against day one purchases, but this is absolutely broke that rule with the writing, voice acting, and comedy gold! It's probably the only game that could say "CBT" as both Cognitive Behavioral Therapy & ♥♥♥♥ and Ball Torture in the same breathe and still make complete thematic sense. The protagonist Val and his childhood friend Hinna, the newly appointed Alm of Fire, set off on a journey to the Mana Tree. The music in field areas feature interactive music, heightening the mood for adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: This feels like sitting in front of the SNES playing Mana in the 90s. The music. The colorful intro. The characters. Everything about it, is pure Mana. Child-like wonder and the power of friendship. I hope they port the other Mana games over to Steam. These games are instant buys. There was one summer where every day, I'd ride my bike down to a friends house to play Secret of Mana with him. Furiously pedaling, hoping against hope that he didn't progress the story any since the previous night. This game takes me back to that time. Where are you now friend? We have a new Mana Tree to save.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: After a long wait, the new installment of the Mana series is here. I enjoyed the combat and personally feel it is the most distinctive feature of Visions of Mana. It’s fast-paced and has a ton of depth with the class systems. I spent a lot of time experimenting with different classes yet somehow they all managed to synergize with your team in meaningful ways, making it hard for me to just stick with one class. There are a lot of fun minigames that test your knowledge of the game's mechanics, which is a nice incentive to learn and make full use of the little advantages some elements and classes have instead of just over-leveling one.The story is pretty simple in the early acts but does an excellent job of establishing the cast of charming characters and likable protagonists, but I do feel the later stages suffer from pacing issues and repetitive content. Despite this, the overall experience and narrative thus far remain emotionally satisfying. The game's vibrant high fantasy art style is beautiful to immerse yourself in, though I noticed some occasional visual bugs and framerate drops when a lot of effects appear on screen.There isn't much else to say, it's an amazing return for the series with innovative mechanics, extremely rewarding combat, and adorable characters that make it a strong contender for fans and newcomers alike. Despite consecutive mediocre and disappointing releases the past year, Square Enix finally delivered!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's a damn shame the studio already got shut down. NetEase is a very scummy company, but we pretty much all know this by now. As counter-intuitive as it may sound, giving this game the positive press it deserves will probably convince Square to rehire the devs as a new studio, since it's clear NetEase is washing their hands of this game.This is a great game, it feels exactly like Trials of Mana (3D), in all of the good ways that make me love that game. I hope the developers get re-hired by Xeen or another Square adjacent studio to keep at it. This game still has minor performance issues, but there's still a chance someone else will patch the game because it's UE5. Geometry pop-in is pretty bad, although Trials had the same issue, and someone made a basic mod to fix that.Game is still kinda easy, again, just like Trials of Mana, but that's also likely to be fixed by mods, again, just like Trials. Although Trials got an update adding some nicely brutal NG+ difficulties.I will say, if you enjoy this game, give Falcom's Ys series a look (specifically the Team-Based games), or Ni No Kuni 2, those games don't get enough attention, and have a very similar game feel and aesthetic.EDIT: I had an internet outage for multiple days, long story, but this game kept me company, Steam didn't record the time because of the outage. and I have one more thing to say about it.The level curve is much better balanced than Trials, unlike Trials, overlevelling is incredibly hard to do unintentionally, which is great because I ended up overlevelling and steamrolling the endgame of Trials trying to get ??? seeds early, before I realized that the game has a failsafe to get every 3rd class item through the ??? seeds assured via chests, which I'm fairly sure wasn't a thing in Trials' 2D version..In this game, the level requirements increase just enough to deter grinding without making it impossible to get an extra level or two, which is the sweet spot for experience curves. That being said, without grinding, the encounters are still very manageable even underlevelled, and gear matters more than level, and you get enough lucre to buy basic gear. Unlike Trials, you're not encouraged to get a huge stack of money before you're supposed to for a cheevo and never have to grind money ever again.EDIT EDIT: Basically just thought about this while checking in with the current reviews, I don't really agree with the complaints about lack of advancement, in terms of skills, there's still a lot of thresholds of growth for each class. Every class is actually multi-tiered, and you learn both universal skills and passives. There's no visual progression between classes' skill tiers, however I think earning new skills through earning new classes or gaining the items to unlock new tiers, still adds a satisfying sense of progression.I mean, sure, there's not anything with as big of an impact as class changing in Trials/SD3 Remake, but there is SOME depth to be had. However, I'm willing to point out that a fair amount of the complaints people seem to have with exploration are also problems I personally have with Trials that weren't addressed here, I just considered them minor to what was done right in both games.People seem to be quickly jumping to say this game is worse than Trials Remake, as if Trials Remake was some sort of respected ARPG classic, when Trials itself was actually pretty divisive on launch and really didn't do well critically. Original Trials fans were extremely split on it's changes, it was considered slop on release by more hardcore ARPG fans, and only got it's reputation over time thanks to people like Vinesauce who loved Trials, rightfully so, I think it's a fantastic lovingly-made and well-executed remake of a classic. I do think journos are overcompensating for their cold reception towards Trials Remake, but there are a lot of genuine improvements over Trials Remake.I personally struggle to find an area this game regressed in, other than that there's not much meaningful permanent gameplay choices regarding character builds. This game is almost too respec friendly to the point where building feels pointless. But also Trials had the exact opposite problem where it's extremely hard to actually reverse class choice to the point where it doesn't feel like a legitimate option.But, and this is a very big but, I would argue, being too respec friendly is a much better problem to have, than being overly restrictive. Overly restrictive progression has the problem of inducing choice paralysis, and encouraging restarts from people who think they botched their progression. I think my many abandoned XCOM files showcase what perfectionism in RPG progression can do to people. However, a balance is ideal, at the end of the day, but I'd err on the side of free-form character development.

I thought it was stale, boring and slow, but since I played other mana games growing up and Trials of Mana, I preordered the deluxe edition from sheer nostalgia and because I'm a sucker for JRPGs. _childDocuments_.review: Will update the review when I complete the game but here are my thoughts as a big mana fan so far.This game really makes me happy, it makes me smile, it feels like a 90s SNES arpg brought to life in a 2024 arpg presentation. My biggest issue is the price point so far, the game is really Double A which I love but it is prices like a Triple A title which might make some people disappointed. It's a really cozy, really fun game that doesn't need itself to be a crazy action game or another soulslike. Another aspect is how kid friendly the game is, I grew up on the mana titles and they were kid friendly enough while still keeping some really tragic stories and this tradition seems to continuing to this day, in fact even though it's a big 3D game now the controls feel really good and I can definitely see myself giving this to my kids, this is the kind of games nostalgia is born from.Now the bad news, the studio that made this game has been shut down the day of the games release. It's a really tragic tale, one of money. We probably don't know all the details yet, but so far it seems that china was investing a lot of money into japanese games, one of the result of this investment was Visions of Mana and its studio. Now that Black Myth Wukong is a major success, chinese companies have pulled fundings from japanese games and will invest more in domestic entertainment.This might be the last mana game but I really think they went out with a bang, with a game that has more soul and passion than any Triple A you will find recently.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I had waited to buy this game. It says Square Enix on steam for the publisher and dev but this game was actually handled by NetEase with their developpers Ouka Studios. A single day after launching the game, NetEase fired most of the dev team and basically plan to shut Ouka Studios down. This is not a practice I want to reward and I wish I learned about it before getting past the refund window.This game is not bad, there's a fun combat system and the story is ok albeit a bit weird with how everyone  On hard mode it hasn't actually been challenging so far which is a bit disappointing, but what really gets to me is that every zone and town is a collectathon hellscape. They went so heavy with it that the illusion of exploration is gone for me, you just see these shiny things littering the whole place and you've got to go pick them up because a lot of them are important. This turns a small zone that would've taken you 5 minutes to get through with a couple short fights into a half hour of going into every corner of the map systematically.TLDR: Combat is fun, story is a bit weird, zones are collectathon hellscapes, hard mode isn't really hard so far, and the real NetEase are scum and killed the dev studio a day after launch.

_childDocuments_.review: It's been forever since I played an expansive RPG like that I genuinely love in every aspect. The characters are charming (even the main protagonist with a sword and anime hair, which I never ever like usually), the story so far has some interesting twists and turns that I genuinely did not see coming, the combat is extremely fun and the class customisation is actually quite deep thanks to how varied each character's classes are and the ability system. _childDocuments_.review: OMG!  This is by far the finest attempt out of literally hundreds I've tried to play to recreate what made Squaresoft games amazing back in the 90s.  I can completely understand why anyone under 40 feels this game is undercooked and tedious.  This game isn't for you kids.  Its for old grumpy dudes like me who used to level up their Final Fantasy 3 party while on the phone with their high school girlfriend.  Nothing I have played in the past 20 years has felt to me this much like a real 90s game.But in the modern context, it is very nice to see a Japanese Action RPG that doesn't live and die based on whether Team Ninja or Tose felt like trying this time or not.  Ouka is bargain basement company that spanked a homerun on this one as far as I'm concerned.  The scenery is wonderful.  The action is sufficient and fun without being overly stressful.  It actually brings to mind the early "Tales of" games more than anything else.

_childDocuments_.review: Do not let the bright colors and happy vibe fool you. This is one of the saddest games I have played recently. Though the characters and environment is stunning and eye-catching, it's an easy distraction from the dark undertones of the game. While the story isn't SUPER complicated like some JRPGs, it does follow some major plot lines like the previous games. For example, going to the Mana tree, fighting Benevodons, and so on. While it does have "call backs" and easter eggs to previous games in the series, it is a stand alone story. The story may seem simple, but it has deep emotional moments that will make you want to cry, scream, or just say WTF.This game is a true callback to JRPG classics. Though I'm new to the Mana series (I only played trials prior to this), I can see this is a step in the right direction for these games. The combat is smooth, fun, and dynamic. Each character has their own class for each Elemental vessel, all different from one another. I had a lot of fun mixing and matching my party members and their classes. I do with the party size for battles was 5, but I know 3 is a Mana series staple.The environment in this game is hands down one of the best. I always saw the mana series have a heavy emphasis on nature and plants, and this game delivers. It's worth exploring to see everything and take in the endless beauty.I was worried at first that the characters would fall flat, but as new characters join your party and interact with story NPCs their personalities shine through and allow for some humor despite the dark undertones of the story.I've beaten the game at roughly 35 hours, and while I did some exploring, there is still plenty of content to enjoy and even a New Game+ option.Overall, if you are an action JRPG fan, give this one a go. You won't be disappointed!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: A great and really cute game.Would I recommend it?Totally.Does it have issues?Totally.Trying to 100% the game (which I did just now) is pure pain and I recommend to only do it if you hate yourself.Not because of the difficulty or challenge the game can provide. There is only 1 Achivement locked behind a difficulty mode (which it allows you to change at any moment). But if you beat the boss on Normal and overwrite your save while having no backup in a different slot, then good luck doing Newgame+ up to the postgame for that.What IS an issue. Are the sidequests. There are way too many for my taste. Quality over quantity is my preference. There are 100+ Side Quests and they are tedious, shallow, worthless and a pain to complete.DO NOT FORCE YOURSELF TO DO THEM RIGHT AWAY! You can just accept them and not bother with them until you feel like it. Side Quests start appearing based on your Mainstory progress for the most part. Sure there are some Side Quests that have pre-requisites, but there are only very few.Just enjoy the game for the story, the graphics, the characters and the gameplay. And if you still wish to 100% it. Go ahead.8.5/10 is my score if I exclude the Side quests.6.0/10 if I deduct the pain it caused me to stretch my 60 hour playtime by 20-30 hours.It could have been a cozy 30-40 hours playthrough. But instead I feel like I wasted so much time doing these Side Quests.

_childDocuments_.review: In a world where regular human sacrifices are needed to keep the very foundation of nature from breaking apart, how does society behave? With astonishing positivity, turns out. This curious exploration of grief and loss through a storybook full of charming characters and bright, airy music is punctuated with flashy combat and mechanics that may not reinvent the wheel but certainly give it a shine.

_childDocuments_.review: I was a huge fan of the SNES Secret of Mana, and must have played it 5 or 6 times. While it had it's issues, the story telling was top and notch and the game was exciting and pulled you into another universe. I was searching for a new game to play and came upon this, which surprised me. I had no idea they were making another Mana game, and it came as a surprise.Unfortunately, the game doesn't do it for me. My experience may not be everyone's experience, but let me explain why I felt the way I did.Because of my previous experience playing Secret of Mana, I had expectations for this. The gameplay was good, the graphics were ok for 2024, the voice acting was below average, but I could overlook all of those problems. The glaring issue was the variety  and story.Secret of Mana had an amazing story. It was full of emotional twists and turns, betrayal, threats, and lore. Although being told on a 16 bit system, they stretched storage capacity to the max of the time to bring to life a world that was fun, intriguing, curious, and satisfying. Visions of mana fails to deliver spectacularly.  The story is flimsy, the characters annoying, the villain is god awful, and the back story non-existent. I remember going into every door I could find in SoM, looking for treasure and surprises. In this remake, with 64 bit computing, almost infinite storage space, and gigabytes of ram, there are like 4 doors you can enter. There's loading screens everywhere interrupting the game play. The side quests are a nightmare to track and you'll end up with like 40 of them in your journal, and have no idea where to go. The in game map sucks. Which is fine, because I wasn't excited visiting ANY of the areas. SoM had variety, you had a sunken continent, labyrinths, modern trains and areas, a MANA FORTRESS, the Mana tree, amazing music and a rich story for every place you visited. I remember going to the gold city and being awed, but none hit my like the sunken continent. The desolate ice forest and the exciting desert, and who can forget the lunar palace? Every time you progressed, you were given a rich story and a sense of purpose.Take all of that stuff out of Visions of Mana. You go from task to task, star to star without any compelling reason to do so. The main villain is so bland I didn't care if you beat it or not. I honestly didn't care about anyone in the world. I guess one of the characters you meet is an academic who is supposed to be the "lore" master, but he doesn't have anything useful to say other than he wants to study everything he sees. He offers next to no useful insight.I'm disappointed, to say the least. I play games for the story telling aspect. This one feel way short of the bar set by SoM and ToM. It's cute, and pretty, but empty. I can't recommend it to anyone.

_childDocuments_.review: Ouka studio deserved better than what they got. That said, Visions of Mana is a great love letter to the series and a worthy addition. It's a good incentive to go back and re-explore places you've already been to get more loot and upgrades. Just a wonderful game all around.Seriously, Ouka deserved better than being shut down as soon as this game released.

_childDocuments_.review: Right away, let me say: if you enjoyed previous Mana titles, then you'll probably enjoy this game; stop looking for reasons you might not enjoy it and just buy it. However, if you're not already a fan of the series, or don't already intend to join the fandom, then steer clear of this mess.I find most positive reviews focus mainly on the game's visuals, and I agree that the game is visually pleasing and chock full of that distinctive Mana style and charm. The story and writing is fairly decent, but hampered by a translation that decided to do its own thing and leaves characters feeling a bit disconnected from the themes of the main story at times. The gameplay is simple, repetitive, and ultimately more than a bit grindy (even at Normal difficulty); and feels more like an online RPG from the early 2010's (such as Aura Kingdom) rather than a single-player experience. (That might explain why it has anti-cheat/anti-tampering software bundle with it too.)Movement throughout the whole game felt pretty awkward. For some reason there's no feeling of momentum, so jumping from a full-on sprint instantly slows your horizontal movement to the same speed you would be going if you'd made a standing jump; and if your character does a forward roll after a jump there's a pause before the character accelerates instantly to whatever speed the character was moving prior to the jump. I suspect the character animations were all developed independently and the inconsistent moments are the splice points where the models transition from one animation sequence to the other. This feels pretty bad in a game with lots of exploration and jumping.The awkward movement and animations also affects combat. There's no real combo system but, rather, normal and special attacks just repeat the same sequence of animations over and over without variation or blending. The only mix-up you can add is using a dash to animation cancel and work in a different attack. This leaves the game with the feel of being developed by somebody who wanted a fighting-game style of combat (with combos, animation canceling, and special effects) but didn't have the knowledge or the tools and gave up partway.Add in all the invisible walls and surfaces you can't stand on that make the game open world-ISH, sprinkle in a bunch of objects everywhere you can get stuck on or in, staircases you have to jump up because the character doesn't properly walk up them, a map that's surprisingly easy to fall through, combat you can get stuck in when enemies become uninteractable or THEY fall through the map, and ... at some point it's undeniable the game was poorly constructed and needs to be played with some care. (Free tip: class strikes auto-hit all enemies in combat with the characters, so you can use one to end  most glitched fights.) These sorts of things don't happen constantly, but they happen often enough for me to specifically mention as a warning about quality and playability.Finally, the English translation is neatly done with fun characters, strong voice acting, and decent pacing (would be great pacing but sometimes English lines are cut off early if your character sprints around). There are times, however, that character motivations seem out of sync with the main story. I felt like the English version of the game made the characters feel older and more mature through word choice and nuance used when discussing emotional topics (like mid to late 20's), but then the same characters make decisions and perform actions consistent with a much younger person since that's what the characters act like in the Japanese version.I attribute this largely to forcing a perspective of sacrifice onto a story that seems more about social roles. Right away the English version of the game refers to the sacrificial duty of Alms where the Japanese version describes the important social function of Mikos. Real world: alms are objects being given up as a social good while a miko is a traditional role that comes with duties of entreating, placating, and sealing spirits and gods (broad strokes, I know). So the English version of the game breaks down about halfway through when the characters seemingly bail out of sacrificing themselves for no good reason and instead fly around the world sealing away the Benevedons and incidentally dealing with each character's personal issues. Meanwhile, this all makes sense from the way the Japanese version frames and builds up the story. Furthermore, some of the story elements make more sense from the perspective of examining social roles: a boy and girl trying to move beyond being childhood friends while also taking up adult responsibilities, a girl whose injury makes her unfit for the thing she dreams of being, etc.And, of course, there's the dumb "why did they do this" stuff. Like changing one of the Merchant Sisters' names from Francois to Francine. Or turning the eloquent and well-mannered queen into a quirky tomboy with a penchant for alliteration and rhyme when speaking. And "re-imagining" lines from "That's our princess" (or "To be expected of a princess") into "That's what you can expect from being cooped up in a castle". The Westernization is strong with this one, so avoid it if this sort of thing bothers you.

_childDocuments_.review: Pros:It's pretty.The music is pleasant.The plot is very classic JRPG. Collect all the things, then go to the end.The combat is probably what you'd expect from a Mana game.Cons:Exploration is a chore. Every treasure chest and POI is marked on the map.You don't advance classes anymore. You just switch them out whenever you want. There are no choices to be made. You just get every skill.Gear is pointless. You just buy everything in the shop because they're always just +3 attack every time you get to a new vendor.The story telling is just insulting with how childish it is. I think even kids would say it's a baby game.None of the characters really have any personality. They're all just very shallow anime tropes.One of the characters is an actual baby. I have to skip all his dialogue.The menus are clunky. Navigating them takes too much time and button presses.Collecting chests feels like a mind-numbingly boring chore.
