_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I wish there was a middleground for recommending. What i mean is, I would recommend it on sale. Not at full price.It was good. Not great and far from bad. The characters really started to grate on me with their non-stop and repetitive voice lines. "Grrrizzly!" If you know, you know. And that's just the tip of the iceberg.On top of that, there are icons that don't appear on the maps until you land in that specific area, and icons linger when they're not supposed to. Specifically sidequests. As a completionist, this drove me absolutey bonkers. So bonkers, I ended up foregoing the last few achievements. It doesn't help they are hidden achievements, and there isn't one for completing every sidequest.There are a variety of bugs, largely minor, and nothing really game breaking. As for difficulty, hard mode is more like normal, normal is easy, and easy is basically just a long interactive movie. Combat is pretty fun, and building your characters is pretty free with 9 classes to choose from and can be switched at any time outside of battle. Graphics are pretty nice. It's very similar to Genshin Impact. I wouldn't hold out for any updates either to address the aforementioned problems, as from what I understand, Square Enix dismantled the developers immediately upon this games release, leaving it up to modders.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If you want a good mix of classic JRPG feels and Modern JRPG romp-a-bout this is definitely worth checking out. Never played a Mana game before but it was a damn good time. The game looks gorgeous, the plot is pretty good anime ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, and the combat (with a few specific exceptions) is a lot of fun. my only critique is in the boss fights occasional tendency to be INCREDIBLY ANNOYINGLY DIFFICULT (without rhyme or reason) and also the design in NOT being able to 1) swap out your team mates during a fight (since some fights you cannot escape) 2) not being able to swap out equipped elemental vessels on active players during a fight and 3) having limited use on restorative items during a fight even if you have plenty of stock in your inventory. These systems, I think, are used as a callback to earlier Mana games (but not sure) and only serve to make for tedium instead of actually fun or challenging gameplay, in my opinion. Similarly the save function uses the old school "save-at-a-save-point" which is just stupid these days. Just let me save my game and stop playing when I want instead of getting exhausted/hangry/late-for-whatever because I haven't found a save place and don't want to lose 2 hours of progress. It claims to have an autosave but there was never any clear indication of when it activated and I was not about to lose hours of progress on trusting it.  With that being said, this game was overall very fun and charming and really captured that old-school nostalgia and feel of the SNES / late 90s hand held era of 16 bit top-down JRPGs but still presenting a modern game. Its not perfect but its damn good. If Nintendo were to make a Pokemon game entry a quarter this good, my inner 10-year-old would be over the moon.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

Gives you that feeling of immersion right from beginning and draws you more and more into the world as you continue your adventure. _childDocuments_.review: (Total IMHO)Positive:World is really lush, intense, colors are cranked to eleven, everything is done with care. Looks like first 2D Mana, only carefully put into 3d. I really, really like it, and I've seen a lot of JRPGs in my time.Traversal is fine, there is even a limited fast travel, not Sea of Stars in this regard, though.Neutral:Music is unremarkable.Character designs... um. They are designed like they were supposed to be 2d, they are simultaneously primitive and over-the-top visually.Negative (hooo, boy):Character lack depth SEVERELY. Everyone is cliched, everyone, and those are a fun cliches. Rock in a field has more personal growth than any single one of them. It's really annoying, considering a REAL good visual execution.Story is a big cliche as well. If you wait for a twist — forget it. It is on a rails, and even fails to tearjek properly.It looks like Square traded soul of their games for graphics. It should be good for sales, yes. For playing — not as much.Summary: nice screensaver.

_childDocuments_.review: "Visions of Mana" is an artistic triumph. The combat and Vessel system are not only fun but also deeply engaging to manage. The world-building is top-tier, creating an immersive experience. While the game is rated "T," it feels like it should be rated "E," as it seems designed for a younger audience. The plot is straightforward, yet the dark themes and the world's rules add depth, making you question whether you're fighting for the right cause or upholding a questionable practice.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall a very enjoyable and warmhearted experience.+pleasant characters+beautiful music+nice environments with beautiful landscapes and lots of variety+combat has enough things going on to not be boring, balancing seemed a little off at timesI mostly liked the story. Its a mix of naive adventurers and then some heavier concepts sometimes mixed inbut it mostly stays pretty lighthearted I would say. My playthrough took about 40 hours even though I skipped a bunch of the side stuff (most side stuff was fetchquests and collect stuff on map). They gave one early companion a heavy accent in the english voices so I switched to japanese voices pretty early on. You can switch between difficulties whenever you want and theres no real penalty to it afaik, some bosses on hard later on seemed to require maybe somewhat specific builds so I turned back to normal sometimes.

_childDocuments_.review: Played 9 hours so far, have gotten 2 of the class change items, i still got a long way to go.However, i loved what i played so far. I've played all Mana games, starting with the first one Final Fantasy Adventure/Mystiq Quest GB. So far what i've played, its everything i wanted this to be. All the classic Mana enemies are back.Combat is great. Lessons have been learned from Genshin Impact, but they did make it Mana. Combat encounters are spaced pretty well to.Exploration is great, this is older style design with maps instead of open world. The exploration feels a lot like Xenoblade, but then with smaller maps. Thats good since xenoblade maps are a tad to big imho. Also theres no farming random map items like in xenoblade. Instead you get a bunch of items, which often can give new skills to so its really worth exploring.I adore the artstyle, its so good. The mana series always been way more connected with nature and thats is back. Music so far has been fine. Really liked the panflute in the wind village.The only real downside so far is the plot, pretty standard anime plot. But thats standard for the Mana series hah.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The story does what it needs to do; The characters are classical tropes, perfect for this day and age. Sure some people may feel like "I'm character X and I must do what X does" can feel stilted; but trust me, its much better than a character with no themes, ever changing ethics and zero human-like responses. The characters interact with one another and their perspectives change as you progress.The plot is somewhat simple, but it SHOULD keep you feeling unease with the situation as a whole. This was intentional. By design, it will make you uncomfortable from the very start. Bear with it, It'll pay off.Graphics look great, but some seemingly important textures and meshes look unloaded. I love the changes they made to the look of the 3D characters; they maintained their iconic art-style, but made the characters more expressive. The only thing that looks out of place is the water shader they used (seriously, two normal maps and a specular highlighting map, does not make believable looking water Wind Waker did it better, and thats two decades old!.). Otherwise the game looks as pretty as the trailers make it seem. The exploration and side-quests are rewarding. I found myself enjoying map traversal. Key points are already highlighted on the map. (brain-dead, I know, but it'll make being a completionist much less time consuming). Once you've collected everything, the open areas feel quite empty, especially given that enemies only spawn in if you're nearby.The combat is as good as the previous mana game.  Its nothing too complicated; time freezes when you open your spellcast/items wheel. You get two types of attacks, and specials that regenerate as you attack/receive damage. If you're losing, its probably because you're not Trying out different elemental forms/other characters.  The game is simply too easy for most veterans.Progression feels great, build crafting is better and much more intuitive.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Very good game with chilling atmosphere with a hint of challenge.Story : Protag convoy journey to the Mana tree. Looks a bit bland but... their goal is to d*e... for the sake of the world. That's a bit dark and keep me going for the ending.Visual : Colourful, many environment with a HUGE map!!. You can spend an hour on every new map to find every nook and cranny (a hidden item to get). Characters cute in their style.There are a lot of returning character/ boss/ NPC from Mana series. Newcomer can enjoy it because it doesn't link to anything. But veteran will point at screen and yell "I know him!" (which happen a lottt)With open world, you can find lv50+ monster while you are lv10... but if you somehow kill it with low level it will be very pleasant moment for you.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a fan of the classic games and this is a great return for the series (hopefully a sign of more to come). Everything works well, I loved the exploration/collection, it felt like everything I was finding/earning was useful and there was no junk. Was perhaps a little easy at first but I find I need to up the difficulty on most JRPGs these days (I know it needs to be accessible to all audiences, and I found Hard worked fine for my interests). Combat really started to shine once you get various classes and I had to really pay attention in the special encounters/bosses. All in all I was really pleasantly surprised how well they nailed their vision for this game, pun intended, and as someone who hates collecting things, I loved how optional it was here and yet I *wanted* to find it all (especially the Dudbear Syrup, I was shocked how fervent I was to find every last drop).

_childDocuments_.review: This is a game I went into with high hopes, it left me excited when it was announced but after playing the demo left me feeling a bit uneasy.After playing the main game however I really did enjoy my time seeing the world and experiencing the journey to the Mana tree the first time.  If you are a completionist however, this game hits a brick wall the moment you unlock flying in chapter 7...There are about 120 side quests in this game and 80% of them are thrown at you at the beginning of chapter 7, there is no fast travel between continents, every time you want to fly you will be watching an animation of them using the item, waiting for a loading screen, watching another animation of the flying beginning, flying to the area, and waiting for another loading screen, then spending time running to where you need to go, this will take up most of your play time.Couple this with tracking only available for one quest at a time, not having the ability to check or change your quest tracking while flying, being given access to about 60 quests at one time so your list is overwhelmingly massive.  it does not respect your time.It doesn't help either that enemies will not scale, and most of the quests do not even level you or give experience unless they require killing monsters.If you are a completionist and do them though even on the hardest difficulty there is zero challenge and you will out level everything.  The game is training you to do the same busy work over and over again, until you get to the final 2 challenging bosses, which are obsurd difficulty spikes you will not be prepared for because the game did nothing in the past 30 hours to prepare you.I managed to get every achievement in this game and really wanted to love it.  However, I can confidently say I hated this game.

_childDocuments_.review: It started as a captivating adventure with a strong storyline and engaging characters. The early and middle parts of the game offer great exploration and world-building, and I genuinely felt invested in the characters’ journeys.However, be prepared for some unexpected narrative twists that can drastically change the tone and direction of the story midway through the game. A key character’s fate takes a surprising turn that some players may find frustrating, especially if you were expecting a more traditional resolution. The main character’s journey takes a darker path afterward, which may not be to everyone’s taste.If you enjoy games that take bold risks with their story and are okay with some unresolved plotlines, this might still be a game for you. But if you prefer a more straightforward heroic tale, you might want to proceed with caution.

_childDocuments_.review: Another awful RPG to complete for the sake of brought it with full price. I couldn’t let my hard earn money went to waste, this is the motivation that I haven’t abandoned this game, not the game is actually fun.Again, game is an art form to interact with users, not a-one-sided input like movies. Designing a world with cute characters, monsters, environment with great voice acting, it’s what a cartoon would possibly make audiences like it, but hardly enough even to reach 50% the possibility to be a success in a video game. A better gameplay is required and far more important to accomplish the other half of the job which VoM has done terribly.If you don’t even realized in battle, the camera angle should always facing your locked target rather than asking players busy adjusting it, why not make a turn based combat instead? Now these days, you can simply insert QTEs to make a turn based RPG still feeling intense to play, better than making a half barked action game who’s nowhere any good in terms of combat competing common great titles in the market that aren’t even difficult to see. My gut was telling me more than once, VoM would be a much better game if the combat were turn based. Focus on making the battles being strategic were more a wise choice rather than trying to believe you can copy the brilliant model that FF XVI has achieved. It’s using a short sword trying to slain a giant while ignoring magic is what your strongest attribute lies. The result isn’t hard to imagine.The pace of game progression is also kinda of a problem. I believe, because of the clunky combat, sometimes, scenarios feel incredibly hard while fighting some certain enemies, then the next chapter, suddenly everything is too easy to acknowledge it’s the same game. This is what I meant ‘progression problem’. A good ARPG from what I’ve played, difficulties are suppose to match the progression of the story, not jumping up and down in every minute. This is not what you make players feeling exciting. In other words, the overall level designs are questionable.The story so far, unfortunately is bad too. To avoid spoilers, let’ say, they kinda of telling your the ending in the very beginning of this game. So unless the story has a big turn over, the ending is doomed to be what it’s told. Devs made their story telling harder to be a terrific one by using this approach, not my place to judge, it’s their choices. And so far, I am in Ch.4, the story was nothing amazing but chaotic. Can’ t tell you the detail, but I honestly have no idea how the story gonna unfold amazingly afterwards. If the story also fails, VoM would be literally nothing to praise for, a title better skip at all cost. God, now I have to pray this doesn’t happen.Sign...I see there are many staffs involving developing this game, are my own people. I don’t want sound too harsh on them. But Mana series is your own IP, Square. You should treat them with more care. Because the quality of this game in general so far will make me stop buying another one in the future. Full price is even more a fantasy in your dreams SE, I am sorry.This game is no more than 10 USD, if you have to buy it no matter what. But If I were you who is deciding buy a new RPG to play, Romancing SaGa 2: Revenge of the Seven is what you should look for and invest your money if you must, not this game. My statement above will sound more persuading if you have chance to play both games’ demos. Do not trust the statement saying ‘ the demo didn’t represent the game properly, the full game is better.’ Yes, it does. The impression of a demo leaves you, is what you get in the full game. I’ve learnt this the hard way.

_childDocuments_.review: This heartwarming and breathtaking adventure is a great example of how the games should be made nowadays. No microtransactions, no annoying online services, no built-in shops with skins/characters/missions etc. – sounds like unrealistic gamer’s heaven, huh? Greedy developers keep telling us about rising expenses, necessity to integrate online services, obligatory depiction of racial, ethnic and sexual diversity, release of tons of DLCs that had been previously cut off the game and so on, but this game is a different story. It’s a solid and involving adventure that makes you dive into the fictional world for ours in a row. Frankly speaking, I’ve already started to forget this kind of complete, cozy and pleasing experiences. If you played the Demo and still not sure whether to buy this game or not, the answer is simple – it’s worth every dollar spent. Despite having some issues while playing Demo, my configuration allowed me to beat the game without any issues. The only glitch I’ve encountered was one of the story-related NPC spawned half under the ground. However, once I reentered the hub, NPC has respawned perfectly well, and I could complete the current quest. Some people keep saying that they’re still experiencing game-breaking bugs, performance issues and crushes. Well, there might be some, but I’ve never encountered them in the first place. Maybe thanks to my totally red (AMD-based) configuration. Since I enjoyed Trials of Mana (Remake) a lot, I’ve been excepting the same from Visions of Mana. And you know what? My expectations were exceeded in more than a dozen of ways. Alright, let get to the proper evaluation of the game:-	The visuals. They are just stunning and breathtaking. Stylish top-notch game design is seen in every single aspect of the visuals. Every corner of the semi-open world is filled with details, animations and picturesque views. Animations are eye-catching and smooth;-	The plot. Seemingly simple Mana series-like plot keeps developing and twisting all over the game. It rises serious problems and makes the player think about such serios issues as life and death, self-sacrifice and self-denial, servitude and treason, life after death, necessity of the reward for heroism, etc. The only downside is the main antagonist and his perplexed motivation, but he is still better than antagonistі of the 99% of games. Moreover, the game follows strict rules of the Mana World, such as... Spoilers! inability to simply ressurect a dead character in WoW-like fasion End of Spoiler!;-	Combat and game mechanics. Real-time combat model seems a bit chaotic and complex at first, but once mastered it gets enjoyable and fun. Numerous classes available to the main characters, as well as skill seeds and elemental vessels provide for almost infinite combinations of combat tactics;-	Characters. Each character is a personality with their own motivation, background and a number of side stories to beat. Their outlook changes during the game and it’s interesting to follow their paths.-       Open world. This iteration of the Mana series features semi-open world. It's fun to explore it, search for treasure chests, rare items and local champion monsters. If you get tired of walking here and there, the game also offers a convinient fast travel system that lets you come back to already visited locations and special mana tree-like spots that also serve as the checkpoints. I strongly recommend playing this game, even if you might experience some tech issues. Such adventures are rarely offered to us, modern players. Despite hilarious tradition of selling 8-9 hours long movie-like glittering blockbusters, this game offers 25-30 hours of solid experience in one playthrough (not to mention new game+ option). Pity that the studio was consumed and dispersed by one of the Chinese giants… Seems like this is the price of releasing on of the best games of this year…

_childDocuments_.review: It looks pretty with colourful, imaginative and various sceneries. Runs smoothly with no crashes, too! The class system based on the artifacts you are using is engaging to tinker around with and I kept switching characters around. The story is lighthearted and yet takes itself seriously - this is good. The AI controlled allies smartly use the correct abilities depending on the weaknesses of your enemies and you can also adjust their behaviour in various ways.Yet this game eventually made me lose interest as combat with random minor enemies is over in a few seconds with you juggling them to infinity all the time unless they are one of the very rare ones with crowd control abilities - then you just safely clear them with your artifacts anyway. You never get to see enemies doing anything unless they are "elite" ones, which get cleared by your G screen wipe attacks, same goes for the shrine and tower challenges. This has never changed over the course of the game until I eventually quit. Overall: Boring.

_childDocuments_.review: Visions Of Mana-------------------------------------------A magical experience.Building upon the Mana series’ storied legacy, they’ve delivered a game that feels like a love letter to fans.Mana has never looked so good, with visuals that are colorfull.Visions of Mana is a art piece, brimming with charm.From start to finish, it captures the heart of the series effortlessly.The world is a visual marvel, each area a lush and a colorful dreamscape.Environments are crafted with care, begging players to explore every nook and cranny.The lore weaves a rich story, pulling us deeper into the enchanting world of Mana.Gameplay is a delight, smooth and responsive, with combat that feels just right.Character abilities are Great, providing depth and variety in every encounter.However, some battles can feel a bit too easy.These minor balance issues, though present, don't detract much from the overall experience.The soundtrack is simply solid, a symphony of melodies that uplift every moment.Each tune perfectly captures the mood, from exploration to intense battles.The music alone is worth the journey, a true highlight of the game.Visions of Mana is a must-play for fans and newcomers alike.It sets the series with a beautiful presentation and engaging gameplay.Square Enix and Ouka Studios have delivered a gem, an adventure that feels both nostalgic and new.Dive into this beautifull world.Visions of Mana is a brilliant addition to the Mana legacy.A shining example of the series’ enduring charm.Enjoy the game !!!

_childDocuments_.review: As a Tales of series fans this game is something that ticked a lot of my checkboxes. Inside the Mana series alone, I say this will be their best entry in both gameplay and story. It is the direct honest answer of 'What if Mana series actually evolve from Trials of Mana?'The bad:- They need to optimize the system for sure because when the game become busy (Undine Elemental Break + Lumina Vessel + Jin Vessel) the frame drops were crazy it is funny. I guess the game can't catch up with how the enemy just melt from the beat-up.- I didn't find it a 'bad' in particular because I've been used to Mana 1 but the world setting is either you love it or you hate it, no in between. A world where 8 Alm Sacrifice are needed every 4 years once is going to upset the keyboard warrior and people who were used to Trials world where sacrifice is done by the spiritual side of the world. I think it is nice how grim and hard the world is despite the cute design. Just think of it like Grimm Brothers' but with Disney color pallette.- Despite having a skin system for armor, they didn't provide with skin. I buy Deluxe and I got old title costume but you see, I expected that we can change the armor skin with other Class' skin not for my paid one.- The Cutscene is locked in 30 FPS but it can be skipped with two hit of F11. I didn't care about it in particular but it does feels jarring at time since my FPS at common goes around ~120 FPS. - Sub Quest. I think the Sub-quest amount in itself isn't that bad and it keep me running around doing all sort of things. But 90% of them didn't do anything more than a fetch-quest or extermination quest so the world didn't grow bigger. The one with actual cutscene attached to them were nice but the rest? They have existential crisis.- The Pikul isn't as useful as promoted since we can teleport to the Meridian and important spot within few seconds. There are some obvious reason but the place you can use Pikul is limited so it just isn't that important.- Around 4 seconds wait on the result screen. It didn't bother me most of the time but when a chest is close, waiting for the result screen to end is such a pain.The good:- The CharactersI was mildly surprised that everyone is such a ball of sunshine mid-way. My fav character ended up being Julie thanks to how he and Careena did the heavy lifting on lighting up the mood. Val is your classic JRPG heroes and in the midst of all JRPG heroes trying to be edgy and 'modern' in this time and age, Val as a Classic Hero is a breath of fresh air. He is a simple guy loving Hinna and after certain point in chapter 3 I think he actually tried to act cheerful at the very least. I'm just glad he get his good end in the end. For the rest of party members, to put it simply they are good people and are trying to be good folks. Careena is selfish but you kinda understand where she gets to that point when her parents and the villagers are toxic environment. She and Julie would make a great comedy duo so I hope the two would travel together after. Morley looked like he is the brain and the level-headed part of the group but he is actually 'young' and funny. His exchange with Ashe is so funny. Palmena shares my sentiment on Morley because she is portrayed as the Queen and she is one, but she has a childish part of her and it brings up a smile when she starts going on about theater and novel. Hinna and Ashe need more screen time albeit for the earlier it isn't like she can get into the screen.- StoryIt is a classic Mana story but longer and with more comedy. If you think ToM's story is a repeat but just with different PoV, then you'll feel the volume increase. The story shines in its simplicity because trying to tackle something heavy is a recipe of a disaster. You pick up Alm to go to Mana Tree as sacrifice, beat up bad guys then even badder bad guys appear then you learn what happened in the past. It is simple, orthodox, and while it sounds boring in text, when you actually play it you might feel that it is the comfort you want from the harsh real world. I love the story of everyone in the world across time and space getting together to save the world.- Graphics and Map I didn't expect much on a AA game but it is surprisingly good for what it is. I do wish they implement Photo mode because there are some place I would like to take screenshot on. I think Visions have the most beautiful Sanctuary of Mana for sure.- GameplayIf you ever play Tales game, then that's what you'll get. Mana is simpler though but Visions is going there. I have some complain on aerial combat back in other series since despite having aerial enemy, the aerial combat is trash. Can't explain it with word and the Demo is ♥♥♥♥ so just try Tales of Arise Demo and that's how it feels in Visions of Mana.Tips:If anyone having trouble with leveling, they give you ample amount of EXP and Lucre increase item. _childDocuments_.review: Quite a good game, and one that brings a long legacy of Mana games to a new generation admirably.The graphics were stellar, vibrant and thematically appropriate for the saturated cartoon world they portray.  The music and voice acting were all on point as well - it's a lot like watching a well-written anime series, but with a lighthearted action game to play between episodes.The combat is simple, but there's enough depth to it to keep action RPG fans interested throughout the story and into the post-game.  I finished the post-game and still had room to grow my characters further.My only complaint is that the pacing of the quests isn't always great - there are a lot of sidequests and you can't be sure whether each sidequest might unlock a subsequent quest with a great reward, so you spend a lot of time running after boar livers and spider fangs.  It does give you something to do and a reason to revisit areas you've already cleared, but didn't feel particularly impactful or fulfilling to complete.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so much more than I thought I was getting. I haven’t played any of the Mana remakes, but I grew up with the Super Nintendo originals and played them sooooo many times.I was iffy about the game because I’m older now and it seemed a little childish. And it can be, but after reminding myself to put my brain in old school Super Nintendo mode, I started really enjoying it. The semi-open world is scattered with treasure chests and other little collectibles reminiscent of older platformers, things just floating around for you to pick up. The characters are light hearted and voice acted well. Early on you meet a dragonoid character who has a thick country accent and that took me a moment to adjust to… but overall I really like the voice acting.I was expecting kind of a more barebones action RPG, so I’ve been surprised at the depth of character customization. Each character has many different ways you can use them, including classes and (very basic) ability trees for each element you’ll unlock. They aren’t great at avoiding attacks (they have died a handful of times in hard mode) but are competent enough and you can adjust how often they use their skills/what enemies they focus on.So far I would say my only complaints are that NPCs all look the same, and sometimes cutscenes can pop up a little too frequently for me. Overall I really enjoy it and I’m pleasantly surprised at its depth.

_childDocuments_.review: Senkei Densetsu 2 and 3 are two of the most nostalgic and meaningful games in my life.This game is nothing but a passionless cashgrab done by Square to capitalize on us.The game's story is so horrendously written, voiced, and directed; but its worst mistake is its massive emphasis on it: You CANNOT spend more than 15 mins of gameplay without being interrupted by a long cutscene. None of the Mana games had any kind of memorable story, but never did they emphasize it. Their stories were simply a backdrop to the fun hack-slash gameplay; however, Visions of Mana strangely makes the mistake of putting a MASSIVE emphasis on its horrible story. But to make it even worse, the game, exploration, and combat just absolutely drag outside of the story, so rarely expect to have any fun playing this game.Also, if you wanna play in the highest difficulty, then simply accept you will be playing it with 1 party member. Your  companions will REFUSE to dodge any mechanics from any enemies and will absolutely get blasted instantly; leaving you to fend by yourself and making the fights MUCH longer. If the developers really did not want to make this game have Co-op, then at least make all party members be as competent in battle as the player; this is absolutely ridiculous! Who playtested this?!I tried, I really did. Now in about the halfway point, I am giving up.If this game was sold for half the price, I would maybe recommend it to us Mana fans simply to see areas, races, and creatures we might recognize; but otherwise, if you are having an itch for a good Mana game, then just pick up the Trials of Mana remake, Legend of Mana remaster, or the Collection of Mana on PS4/Switch. HECK, EVEN PICK UP THE SECRET OF MANA REMAKE; I am NOT joking, that remake is a far better overall experience than this.With the studio shutting down, this simply proves my theory that this was a game simply done to meet a quota.As one of my most anticipated AAA games this year, I cannot express how disappointed I am in this. A current-gen AAA Mana game with the love and care FF16 got would be a DREAM come true; too bad the dream stays existing when I sleep instead of when I wake.Save your money.

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana is easily the best Mana game I've played since Legend of Mana, and I am a huge fan of the series. It expands on ideas that the Trials of Mana remake touched upon but could not fully flesh out (as a remake of a SNES game). The game's Job/Class system is extremely fun, with everyone getting neat magical girl cutscenes when they unlock new classes. Additionally, the world is stunningly beautiful, visually. It fully encapsulates the feelings the world of Legend of Mana gave me as a child, but now in a beautiful 3D artstyle. Honestly, I'm just going to gush about how much I love this game at this point. For those who tried the demo and were not fans of the combat speed, it absolutely does grow more complex and faster-paced as you unlock new classes and their abilities. Each character has unique weapons which are shared among multiple classes, and their skills typically overlap. This gives you access to new combos, new spells, buffs, attacks, etc.In general, I cannot recommend this game enough to those who already love the Mana series. If you are new, this is a gorgeous, imaginative Action-JRPG that is nothing if not insanely charming.

_childDocuments_.review: Combat in my opinion is a lot of fun. Dodging requires watching the opponent and moving in the right direction rather than just spamming dodge. And the flow of attacks feels so smooth that this is probably one of the best gameplay games I've ever played. The amount of customization is also surprisingly high for how your character plays and what abilities they learn, it's a very impressive system. However ; it's also a pretty big flaw, and you could potentially spend 10, or 20 minutes looking up what each class does for each character and experimenting with what works and what does. It wasn't until late in the game I finally realized abilities from other classes could be used in your current class which might of helped me much earlier in the game.Story can get pretty cheesy and weird, but overall it didn't make me cringe (too hard). There were some moments I didn't see coming and was surprised a few times. There were some big story moments I've unfortunately did see coming without getting into details, but overall the mystery behind the scenes of what's happening was fine. As for the characters, it's a bit of a hit or miss, I didn't personally dislike any character, but overall I did like the cast with the exceptions of a few wierdness. The soundtrack of the game is just incredible in my opinion is some of the best especially when in battles against massive enemies giving the feel of an epic battle followed by a calming music in small village, I enjoyed it from start to finish.Overall grade: AThe game Isn't perfect despite me giving it a High score, as it certainly has a number of flaws that can't be ignored, but this is one of the few games I've come close to 100%, and at this point I plan to do just that. I'm happy with my purchase, just be warned that even though I love this game (especially considering I loved secret and trials of mana) it doesn't mean everyone will enjoy it, but I hope this review helps.

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana is a game that truly allows the entry level gamer who wants to play an RPG but doesn't want to burden themselves with all the nuanced details like character motivations, complex story arcs, and over the top character development and stat chasing.  Visions takes the things that fans love about RPGs and simplifies them to create an accessible and overall joyful experience.  I've always wondered, in my later years why so many developers focus on adult gamers as opposed to catering to the younger fans who like me at their age, was invested in so many things that pushed my imagination.  Seems most games these days are only concerned with revenue and pushing the edge tech-wise.  Visions is a game that I feel is an engaging step for young fans and also a nostalgic trope for fans who are familiar with the series.  The combat from my perspective is hectic and often times confusing, but for a younger person, I am sure they'd feel like they were handing out punishment left and right with reckless abandon.  I love the dialogue and banter between the characters.  Nothing is so over your head that you lose track of why you're doing what you're doing.  The point is clear and simple and it's really fun to see these characters journey together.  I recommend this game for all ages, but I think this is something that a young gamer, with a vivid imagination and sense for adventure would absolutely enjoy.  It may not be a classic to me, but I am sure for the younger generation, Visions of Mana will be a title that they talk about for years to come.

_childDocuments_.review: For anyone seeking a true escape from real life, Vision of Mana is your game. Its return to form classic fantasy adventure with a merry band of friends on a grand journey. The colorful world clashes with the mature themes of the story and more than once it got to me emotionally.The battle system can be fine tuned to your liking. I personally set my party members to be a bit more passive and less frequent use of magic to make battles less chaotic.The weakest part of the story is the sidequest and collection aspect. Personally i would recommend people to ignore these parts unless you can't get enough of them.Vision of Mana is a incredible entry into the Mana Series.

_childDocuments_.review: 1st: The full game runs way better than the PC demo did. There is no traversal stutter and no shader compilation stutter in the full game. It runs buttery smooth and I've got it at a locked 120 fps with 4K dlss max settings.This game is relaxing and an absolute joy to play and explore. Exploring feels wonderful and at times, magical like the old games Secret of Mana and Seiken Densetsu 3 it descended from. Combat took me a little time before I fully enjoyed it, but once I got locked in I'm having a blast with the variety of characters, classes, and weapon variety. The only downside is some occasional voice acting that sounds childish and annoying. The music doesn't quite live up to the classics (Secret of Mana and Seiken Densetsu 3) but all of it is good and there are a plenty of really great and catchy tunes throughout. The story isn't anything that will blow you away, but it I find it very enjoyable as the turn of events often happen in a creative way or a different way then you'll be expecting. The main character Val is optimistic and kind to a fault. He may seem a bit one note at first, but I think they play around with such a straightforward personality in really fun ways.I'm 40 hours in and might come back if I have any more details to add after I beat the game.Visions of Mana is a rare game I just want to keep playing for hours and hours. It's easily in my top 5 games this year along with FFVII Rebirth, Astrobot, and Minishoot Adventures.

_childDocuments_.review: I truly cannot understand why I enjoy this game at all. It falls short in every possible way.A skilltree so heavily locked by progression where you can only skill along a single row with only minor things in it.A story so badly written, the developers seem to have forgotten what they wrote 5 seconds before.A map so badly thought out you could think they just gave information about the game to an AI and told it to use anything, giving no regard to lore or logic.The shops literally spoiler you what weapons you unlock in the future, but not letting you actually buy it before you unlock it. And while at first it's something minor and you get the class shortly after seeing it, later you get shown a weapon for a class you unlock 3 whole towns later and it's the exact same weapon everytime. And if you think that's where shops stop being stupid, just no. One of those towns sells you stuff worse than what you got in the one before and immediately tells you, you are not even supposed to be here for "story reasons".And now to the core problem of the game: The combat is outdated, clunky and unbalanced.Movesets are as simple as it gets (even though some really look nice and unique), with one minor change depending on the class.If an enemy is slightly above or below you, it is very likely that you just miss.Every attack glues you in place, so yeah, there is a chance you miss with the follow-up attack of a combo despite hitting the first one.And the worst is how much the balancing of the game jumps around. One moment you die in two hits and it takes a whole minute to fight a single group of normal enemies, the next the highest damage you receive is 1/8 of your hp and the fight is over in seconds. A bit later suddenly you can clear every fight with one button press in seconds and once again the next thing you remember is an enemy immune to a third of your characters and the the ones that still deal damage the enemy can barely tickle it.I could probably go on for a while with the general feel of the movement, the open world that forces you to get 90% of collectibles if you wanna feel atleast somewhat strong or the incredibly badly thought through menus.Am I gonna keep playing the game? Probably. Am I gonna keep enjoying it? Not sure. Is this game worth 60 bucks? Definitely not. Maybe half of it.

_childDocuments_.review: As somebody who's been playing Mana games since Final Fantasy Adventure, I'm pleased to say that Visions of Mana is a delightful new entry in the series. It has the same whimsical sense of fantasy and adventure with a serious undertone as all of the other games. I was worried that all the obvious visual references to older games might just be fanservice, but no, the developers who made this game clearly understood why people loved the previous games and sought to recapture that in a completely new title.The graphics are obviously gorgeous, the soundtrack is great, and the characters are likable. The story is good, too; I've seen several people put off by the game's high concept being that you're guiding a group of people to sacrifice their souls, and... c'mon, you know there's going to be a few plot twists along the way. I'll admit it got me to tear up at least once.It's also a game that just keeps getting better as it goes along.  I'll admit that the beginning of the game feels very restrictive; you have few options in combat, and it's easy to feel like you're just being herded from one cutscene to the next.  But over the course of the game, you keep unlocking more classes and more elemental vessels that add more options to combat, and you keep getting more travel options, and the dungeons and bosses keep getting more creative. A lot of games front-load their best content to try to hook the player, but then end up being unremarkable for the rest of the game; VoM saves its best stuff so you won't be disappointed at the end.But as much as I've enjoyed it, I've got a couple of issues. One is that its performance seems a bit unoptimized; it's playable on a Steam Deck but it's pretty choppy, and you won't get consistent 60 FPS on even the lowest graphical options.  It struggles to even keep a consistent 60 FPS @ 4K on a RTX 3070.  And while the game does look great, it doesn't seem like it's  much more graphically demanding than other games that perform much better.There's also, if anything,  side quests.  There are some genuinely interesting and fun side quests, like one where a woman whose father left her when she was young but has been sending landscape paintings to her, and you help her track down the locations where he made the paintings while she comes to understand him.  On the other hand, for every quest like that, there are ten dudes who just want you to kill some crabs.  It feels like obvious filler; they could've cut out half the quests in this game and it would've been better for it.But in the end, that's faint criticism.  This is a great game, and easy for me to recommend to anybody who wants a colorful action RPG.

_childDocuments_.review: Recommended: Yes!Grade: B+Goods:- Lovely and colorful world - Class outfits and designs are A+- Combat synergy, when locked in, is very satisfying- Pretty good voice acting; characters look and feel distinct- Main Story Quest does not overstay its welcome- Party builds have a lot of varietyBads:- Tutorial heavy; Somewhat hand-holdy when doing main quest objectives- Sidequest pacing could have been much better- AI behavior is sometimes questionable and can lead to some fake difficulty spikes- Combat can feel button-mashy at times- Combat effects can sometimes be blinding or disorienting- New Game+ doesn't have much of a purpose beyond breaking the game as much as possible (no extra achieve mints or encounters for doing so)- Being a teenager saving the world might be off-putting for older players (original Secret of Mana fans are now in their 40s)Uglies:- Fast Travel is clunky.  Coupled with poor sidequest pacing, it leads to tons of load time and waiting.- Whoever designed the Black Rabite fight is the epitome of evilWrite-up:Beautiful game and beautiful world.  Soulguard Val sets out on a journey to escort Hinna, the Alm of Fire, to the Mana Tree as a sort of pilgrimage.  Along the way he picks up other Alms of the seven other Elements as all eight of them are needed to effectively sacrifice themselves for the greater good.  As with all adventure games, everyone is exactly who they say they are and everything will turn out just fine.I greatly enjoyed this game.  Everything is bright and colorful; the environments are well designed, unique, and loaded with detail.  Character and monster designs are on point and any Mana fan will enjoy seeing classics like Mushbooms and Rabites rendered in the Unreal engine.  Even though everything's very cartoony, there is a feeling of realness and weight to the actors.  The story is a little paint-by-numbers but doesn't overstay its welcome.  There is a little bit of childishness to everything which might turn off older players.  As a 40 year old myself, it felt a little strange to return to this series I've grown up with only to play as an early teenager for most of the runtime.  I could definitely feel myself being not-the-target audience for this one.  It's fine, but for some might take a little getting used to.  The English Voice Acting holds up pretty well; Square's direction tends to feel out of place in a lot of their voice work, but I think it's pretty comfortable.  It also might need an adjustment period for some, but there's always the Japanese voices for folks who prefer that.Combat is pretty fun and not terribly punishing, although somewhat button-mashy.  However, some encounters, particularly with bosses, the AI struggles to stay alive in the higher difficulties.  They simply don't know how to respond to a giant laserbeams headed their way sometimes, which can lead to some pretty harrowing encounters if you go in unprepared.  Thankfully, recovering from a wipe isn't a major set back and changing strategies is very flexible.Mechanically, the game allows you to play as 5 characters that can choose among 8 classes, each corresponding to one of the game's 8 elements, or as a 9th freelancer class that has no immediate specialization.  You can customize your characters abilities to taste and the fun here is getting your party composition synergy down so you can plow through whatever content the game has on offer.  It's a slow start, but as you work through the game and more unlockables appear, it becomes very satisfying to assemble your A-Team.

_childDocuments_.review: So I decided to try out Visions of Mana. My expectations were not high following the trash that was the Secret of Mana remake back in the late teens. Given that the English voice actors could not even pronounce the word "Mana" correctly, I had to switch them to Japanese immediately and even then I had serious concerns that I had been burned in a pre-order once again.Instead what I have found is one of the most incredible gaming experiences I have had in literally years. From the opening gun this game works its butt off to impress. The world is lush and beautiful, colors are vivid and contrast for the sake of showing off what this game intends to be about. Visuals are exciting to look at, characters stand out and are interesting, engaging. Gameplay is fun and fast-paced. It's like a 90s Disney Storybook world come to life.While I've only been playing for about 7 hours or so, I can already see that there's a surprising depth to this game, to its character systems, and I compare this to the way that Starfield presented from day one: broken, ugly, slow, bad music, failing its promises, with lackluster boring visuals, bland and lifeless worlds, uninteresting plot, ugly characters, lifelessness, heartlessness, soullessness, tastelessness, and the only conclusion I can come to is that at this time, there is no real hope for the American AAA gaming industry.If you look at Concord, Star Wars Outlaws, almost any major release that has come out of the US over the course of the past two years, it all has this diversity equity inclusion garbage that makes for terrible, bland, pointless, self-congratulatory and utterly dull gaming experiences.For the several hundred hours that I unfortunately sank into Starfield not even 1 little bit of the music stands out to me and I don't remember any of the characters names. Meanwhile, even just the menu music of VoM stirs emotions I haven't felt in years.I just don't think the future of AAA games is in the United states anymore.Realistically though, given how many great overseas studios there are now, Western AAA games don't have to be our games anymore. Western AAA games are over.

_childDocuments_.review: I wish I could give this game a better review. And to be clear - There is a lot to like in Visions of Mana. If Steam had a neutral option, I would choose it. It is a decent time, if you have more patience than I do. But after 30 hours, and realizing I had another 20 ahead of me most likely, I realized there are games that respect my time more. The breaking point was finishing a chapter just for 25+ fetch-quests to pop up at once, all of which required me having to slog to different places of the map to collect them, and most of the quests involved going to different areas to complete and then return to. Given how much traveling in this game is a chore, I just turned the game off then and there. The major issues are...1. Exploration - I can see what they were going for, but failed to do. From the very first explorable area, there are "elemental crystals" and treasure chests you can only get by getting all of the elemental vessels. They obviously wanted to give you a reason to come back to previous areas, but since the monsters do not improve/change it just means you have two choices: Deny yourself Elemental Points, Items, and money for a bit to get all vessels (around the halfway point of the game, by my estimate) before coming back to get everything; or constantly come back to these maps each and every time you get a new vessel. The maps are also big for the sake of being big, with tons of empty space.2. Side quests - Not interesting, not fun. Most are just "go here, kill X, return for money". They pop up sometimes with no warning, and frequently in villages you haven't been at in 10+ hours, so you have to keep checking the maps. Later side-quests, which made my frustrations boil over, wanted me to get the quest, travel to a completely different part of the world (sometimes multiple different parts), do some menial fetch task, and return.3. Fast Travel - You can only fast travel between points on the same continent/island. And by 30 hours in, with more continents or islands to find, there were already 5 I'd been to. How do you travel BETWEEN continents/islands? Either use an item to summon a mount, which takes 30+ seconds to actually get done with its animation just to board, and then manually navigate over to the other continent/island. It sucks. Add that in with side quests asking you to travel between multiple continents and it just becomes padding and busy work. 4. Combat - Combat is perfectly serviceable... at first. But after 30 hours I was doing the same exact thing I was doing at hour 3. Maybe the later skills in the game really changed things up, but I was not putting in more time to find out. Sure, each character has "nine" classes. But really they each have 3 classes (weapons), and each class has 3 different elements. The only thing that determines their moveset is their weapon (with some special attack exceptions). And even still, most weapons just break down to light-combo, heavy-combo, and one or two mix-ins like launching an enemy. And some classes are just worthless, while some are so overpowered that you are choosing to actively hamper yourself by not using them (like moonblade). 5. Story - There is a decently interesting story in here, somewhere. But it's so slow, many times predictable, and even when it is moving along its not interesting enough to justify the time investment. The characters are just kind of there, existing. I was never really invested in their plight. Val is a Marty-Stu. Hinna is pure. Careena is a country gal with sass. Morley is refined. Palamena is a noble bookworm. Julei is a smarmy child. You have seen these characters 20 times before. And better.Overall, it's not a terrible game. The story is okay when it is moving, the characters are inoffensive, the combat is serviceable, the locales are beautiful, and the audio is mostly good. But the game simply does not respect your time or evolve in an interesting enough way to keep me invested. It's a shame too, because this game was the unintentional swansong of the developer, so I wanted to love it.

_childDocuments_.review: As a fan of games like Kingdom Hearts, I was immediately drawn to the game's stunning visuals and captivating music. The world is a sight to behold—each landscape feels vibrant and alive, making exploration a joy from start to finish.Though I hadn’t played any of the previous Mana games, Visions of Mana has definitely made me a fan going forward. The ability to switch between characters seamlessly keeps the gameplay dynamic and engaging. Each character has its own unique abilities, and the game gives you the freedom to build and customize your classes, adding layers of depth and personalization. This feature is especially rewarding for players who enjoy crafting a playstyle that suits them.The atmosphere within the game is truly remarkable. From the beautifully composed soundtrack to the richly detailed environments, every element works together to pull you into this magical world. Whether you're fighting through a dungeon, exploring a peaceful village, or tackling challenging bosses, the game never loses its charm.Visions of Mana strikes a perfect balance between story-driven moments and intense, action-packed combat. The mechanics are smooth, the controls intuitive, and the overall experience is just as rewarding for newcomers to the series as it is for longtime fans.If you love exploring vast, breathtaking worlds, experimenting with character builds, and immersing yourself in a game with a powerful atmosphere, Visions of Mana is an experience you won’t want to miss. I can confidently say that this game is a must-play and earns a perfect 10 out of 10. Highly recommended for any action RPG fan!

Also doesn't work right after a battle.- Switching characters to Palamena with the scyth weapon causing her to run around with the weapon out and it look so dumb, its a bug and should be rested when running, attacking again works around the issue.- Sound effects for attacking is very unattractive in comparison to trials of mana.- Visual effects are too much, hard to see what's going on.- 30 fps cutscenes, with a fan made workaround just shows the devs don't care about any patches, prove me wrong.- Overall performance, poor, especially in the elemental arena, that skybox is full of complex shaders, even on low graphics the GPU on a 3070 will consume 100%, who tested this game??- Graphics are blurry out of the box, oh my god umplayable, luckily I know my way around some simple engine.ini fixes to address it, what are the devs doing?? ie: r.DefaultFeature.AntiAliasing=2r.TemporalAASamples=8r.TemporalAACurrentFrameWeight=0.1r.Tonemapper.Sharpen=1- Class special attacks, there's like 1 attack and trials of mana had 4?? Dissapointing.  Also the transition coming out of them is not fluid, another white screen effect which no one wants, Trials of mana did it HEAPS better.- Voiceovers, distorted at some points, like the volume was too high, especially noticed with Palamena.- Autosave, damm it's bad. _childDocuments_.review: Beautiful game, fun game-play (even if a little simplistic), fun characters mostly.That's the only positives I have for this game. Now onto the negatives (minor spoilers at best):* Controls fight you tooth and nail to listen to you when you want to use items in battle. I've twice had issues where I cannot use items at all during the fight (bug), leading to frustrating restarts. You also have to standing perfectly still to use items in battle or else your character just stands there like an idiot. I even had a few instances where it bugged out completely and I couldn't even attack (different bug) - had to restart.* There are no auto-saves at all, so if you fail due to you know, bugs like not being able to use items in game, you damn well better have saved recently else you gotta do a bit of it over again (it does auto-save whenever you enter an area but that's it).* AI seems brain-dead STUPID when it comes to flying enemies. On several occasions, I am wondering why I am struggling against enemies I am 15 levels stronger than and its because I find my AI companions just running back and forth not doing a damn thing (everything set to be offensive battle strat).* Half the characters are pretty good, and the other half I cannot stand. Alm of Wind and Darkness can go jump off a cliff as I cannot stand them.* Exploration is nigh-meaningless as everything except the lil cactus dudes is highlighted on the map for you. This would have been nice as an end-game feature, instead of given to you immediately.* Playing on normal difficulty, the difficulty spikes are all around.* Status effects. They are all extremely debilitating and if all 3 of you get hit by something, you just gotta stand there and die. I remember some tutorial saying spam buttons to get out but it's never worked for me.* Speaking of tutorials, it throws so many at you towards the start of the game its annoying. Another tutorial says to double tap left bumper to auto-run to your next destination - that never worked for me either lol.* Collecting chests or talking to anyone is very *precise*. You basically have to stop in front of it in order to perform the action, cant just run up and press it like pretty much any other game.* Invisible walls galore. If you ain't on the path, it blocks you basically. See something that looks like you can jump on? Nope, invisible wall.* Your dog companion (to travel faster) is pretty useless. A lot of actions will kick you off him, he throws you off whenever he touched any water (even puddles) but other times he can roam water just fine. There's no consistency.* Unless you're constantly boosting, grinding seems pretty weak so you're just progressing the story - feels like a 'fake' RPG in that sense. It does get better, especially if you do all the side content.* You're extremely weak up until you get your 3rd main character to help in battles. The first boss in the game took me like 10 minutes because I did no damage. Then you go insane damage.* Story is rather predictable - it has one twist that is easily seen coming somewhat early on and the rest of the story is pretty mid. Due to the numerous frustrating issues I was having with the game, I fully tapped out of the story By Chapter 6 and after witnessing my allies doing nothing against a flying enemy *again*, I had enough and uninstalled - I wanted to finish the game but that was the final straw for me.* Several story elements make no damn sense except to progress the plot (bad guy gets away? When you're in a cave? and he can barely run? Your bird companion doesn't want to move a rock and go to the area behind it but after you move it, all good it will go with you!??? etc)* Had 2 crashes, which wouldn't be so bad if the game auto saved more often.Overall, the game is quite fun and nice to look at, but has a lot of frustrating mechanics and bugs that irritated me to death to where I cannot stomach finishing it anymore. I do not recall Trials of Mana being like this, so play that instead.

Solid 7-8 out of 10. Feels more nightmarish than a Souls game in the first half. Wouldn't recommend since it has no bonuses. Regular enemies each can 1-2 shot you. What's worse than Souls is that you're dragging along 2 teammates with horrendous dodging AI. It's like playing with 2 younger siblings who can barely hold their controllers. From 20-70% story progress, I'm always 2 levels lower than enemies, which made it way more difficult. Getting past that, my characters stopped dying in 1-2 hit, but rather 2-5 hits; revive items and skills became easy to get. I could start killing things 10-12 levels above me with revive spams and overleveled my team from that.It absolutely irks me that there's a Moon element alongside Dark and Light. The kicker is that the strongest and arguably coolest fighter has the worst hair in the entire game, and his strongest class/element is Moon type. Besides that, you can find a character or team that represents YOU well. Not having multiplayer mode is a CRIME, but I guess there are game-pausing features that they'd need to figure out3 chars max, no need for dedicated healer since you can spam up to 9x healing (small to large) and 9 revive items per battle. Support role is great to have. Magic skills are limited, mostly to cause effects or change elements of your melee attacks. Melee skills are limited. If you push it, you can make a ranged/support character melee, but there are only 2-3 most viable combos (by far) that make sense to spam. - Val: main boi, required for his buffs if you spam melee and/or need elemental shield. Slower melee and can be annoying; extremely limited offense magic blasts. Best elements: Wind (BIG buffs), Light (tank and low taunt)- Careena: tsundere, flexible buff/debuffer, fills supporter slot for ANY team. Workable melee with fire element. Best elements: idk any would be good, Fire for main melee if you like.- Morley: deep voice nyan, CRIT boiiiiiiii. Best elements: Moon for 70% crit chance, grab other effects for debuff on crit; other elements are gimmicks.- Palmena: HOT ice queen, an actual queen, squishy (HP and thighs), offense-wise is purely magic skills, limited melee but cool basic combos later on (still weak combos though). Best elements: Earth according to guides, maxes her magic stat and provides dmg reduction, Water for thighs and cast speed- Julei: sarcastic shouta old hermit, dedicated healer and supporter. I don't play him cuz defensively it's cheese and excessive. Anyone can cast heal and regen, especially regen and that's enough. Great/excessive pick for support slot. Best elements: Wood (team wise revive; useful if both the other 2 chars died lmao), Light (heal, class, self revive to prevent game over, revive everyone once per battle so that's twice the out-of-jail cards(?))Classes are tied to elements. 8 classes for each of the 5 characters = 40 classes. But the downside is you can only pick 3 out of 5 characters at any time. I just wish they made 2 support slots. It is what it is. Each element has an inclination towards a role regardless of who you play.- Moon: crit, time-control (coolest effect honestly), supporting effects, maybe some HP drains I can't remember- Fire: burn, ATK boost- Water/Ice: freeze (strong), MATK boost, some cleanse, HP regen (very nice)- Wind: main char's best class, unlocked early on, due to elemental imbue and later on teamwide elemental shields/imbues and buffs upon them. Other chars get some regens and mostly aoe buffs and debuffs- Earth: somehow the magic caster's best class, can petrify maybe. Others can raise DEF- Wood: poison and summon oriented. Summons are almost one-off attacks with a variety of elements. Chars can get revive and maybe cleanse skills- Light: healing and MDEF boosts, tanking and support options, dmg spreading ultimate- Dark: silence, grouping ultimate, stat boosts on low HP, enemy buff dispels, self cleanseElemental debuffs can be applied at a 80% bonus rate, so very easy to use later on. Stat debuffs benefit the whole team (for 3 members so not that much). Stat buffs are better against single bosses, some broken dmg-immune ones don't last longs, elemental shields and imbues last long; disappear on death.Class Passives don't stay with you if you change to another class, at least until endgame as far as I know (it's an incentive to stay with a class) Class Active skills you can retain when mix and match, which I thought was the BEST regarding customization. AI teammates (and you) and hold up to 8 active skills in battle if I remember correctly; so set up wisely. The active character can also bind up to 4 skills to hotkeys; these won't be auto-cast by AI.are just stat sticks. You can change the weapon skin as long as the desired weapon isn't sold.provide options to use active skills from any classes and any character, which is nice. The downside of using other classes's skills is you are not benefiting from whatever passives that indirectly boost those skills.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a modern Mana game that deserves to be called a Mana game. They tried going 3D twice with the 3D remaster and Trials. _childDocuments_.review: This is a truly astonishing example of just how a bad story can ruin a beautiful and fun game.Before we begin, I am an English teacher. I completely respect that lots of people enjoy stories at face value, without intentionally considering the story's themes. If you are one of those people who will see the story as something that can ultimately be skipped in service of gameplay, my review will not be applicable to your experience.That said, I'm truly curious if the cultural divide between the United States and Japan is so deep that we don't even seek the same fundamental morals in our themes. I don't understand how someone could even successfully write this story unless their entire personality is the consequence of decades of generational trauma.This game's world is one in which the inhabitants enjoy the protection of magical forces from the Tree of Mana, but in order to do so, must make human sacrifices to that tree. The story begins with a woman being chosen as the sacrifice of her village--a woman who is not even a native of that village, who never had to be there, and who therefore owes them nothing twice over. She seems ultimately willing to do so. It is her lover who refuses to let her go, ultimately damning their entire village to destruction.So we've done two pretty disgusting things right off the freaking bat, here. Number one, we've effectively established the planet itself as the villain. The tone is clear. The monsters it summons to try and stop the pair are clear. The transformation of the girl into stone just as they are about to escape is about as clear of a "screw you" from the planet as anything can be. But, somehow, the Earth itself is not the villain. No, it's the people who would criticize those who blindly sacrifice one another for the planet. Those are the villains.And then there's problem number two. Do you know what this woman did the whole time her boyfriend was refusing to let her change her mind and help her people? She was damn-near bent over backwards so that her breasts could be the focal point of every scene as she blandly "ummed" and "uhhed" instead of taking any control of her situation.So the first woman the story introduces is freakin fridged by this world's god, and not even to inspire a hero to kill him as the villian, but instead as a gesture to ensure no one else rises up against this tradition of ritualistic suicide.Like, I'm sure this game is a real banger. Its so pretty, and it looks like the kind of game that would really restore my childhood RPG feels. But I'm not a child. I can read.Tl;dr It isn't "Dark." It's bleak, hopeless, and thematically toxic.Edit: I looked up the remainder of the plot and willingly spoiled it for myself to see if it was going to redeem itself. In my eyes, it doesn't. But I'd hate for any of you to mistake my review as a review of the first 40 minutes. I already told you I adored the gameplay, but the story was really ruining it for me. So, I spoiled the story to see if I could make it through. I cannot.Those of you who are criticizing me for making a judgement too soon, if I had in fact only played the first 40 minutes and made no other research on my own, you'd be entirely valid in your opinions. Likewise, I empathize with your frustration. You are not wrong to have felt this way about my review.However, I am also not wrong to be repulsed by the game.

_childDocuments_.review: Review: Visions of ManaRating: 8/10Visions of Mana is a captivating entry in the action RPG genre that expertly combines a beautiful, hand-painted art style with an immersive fantasy world. The game’s storyline dives into a rich lore of mystical creatures, elemental spirits, and ancient conflicts, making each quest feel like a step deeper into an enchanting saga.One of the strongest aspects of Visions of Mana is its world-building. The environments are meticulously crafted, from lush, sprawling forests to haunting ruins, each locale packed with details that make exploration a pleasure. The dynamic weather and day-night cycles also enhance the immersion, adding atmosphere to each environment and influencing gameplay in subtle ways.Combat in Visions of Mana is fluid and satisfying, balancing fast-paced action with strategic elements. The ability to summon elemental spirits offers a unique twist, allowing players to adapt their style on the fly and exploit enemy weaknesses. It’s rewarding and keeps battles fresh, though the game could benefit from slightly more diverse enemy types.Character progression is well-paced, with a customizable skill tree that lets players shape their character’s abilities to fit different playstyles. However, some players may find the grind for resources a bit repetitive, especially when it comes to crafting powerful gear.While the main storyline is compelling, the side quests are hit-or-miss. Some offer intriguing lore or unique challenges, while others feel like standard fetch quests. That said, the game's charm and emotional resonance shine through, particularly in key narrative moments and character interactions.Overall, Visions of Mana is a beautiful, engaging RPG that may not be perfect but still offers an enjoyable and memorable journey through a lush, magical world. Fans of fantasy and adventure will find plenty to love, and it’s an easy recommendation for anyone looking for a deep, atmospheric RPG experience.If you’re a fan of world-building, elemental magic, and heartfelt storytelling, Visions of Mana is well worth the adventure!

_childDocuments_.review: Pros: Furries. Furries everywhere.Cons: Game is fine, but really suffers the comparison with the earlier Trial of Mana remake, which is just all-around a much better game. The main antagonist here is really badly written and doesn't add much to the overall arch of the characters; and while there are a few truly good moments in the plot, they are very few and far between and don't really make up for the rather bland rest of it. I feels like two different people wrote the script and didn't talk to each other: there's the heroes' plot and the main villain plot, and they don't really interact, so you're left with a bunch of half-explored strands that never really amount to anything. The side quests are nothing more than an afterthought, boring and unrewarding. You'll quickly learn to ignore them.Again, the game is fine. I played though the story once and I had a good time. But I don't think I'll touch this ever again.Play if you're a Mana fan. If not, play Trial of Mana, become a Mana fan, and maybe come back here if you want more.

I realize their is a ignorant negative review that remarked something on textures being from 2015, unfortunately that reviewer is poorly educated, and does not understand art. Voice acting is a bit basic that is true, story however so far seems pretty good, though I wish the main protag wasnt so oblivious. I am sure interested modders will release something soon to unlock the Cutscene FPS and maybe better A.I behavior for mobs.  Until then I recommend waiting on playing this game, so you can get a enhanced experience thru mod support. It is afterall, one of the main reasons we play on PC to begin with. Controller support is fine.  Their are players who are having trouble playing with whatever controller they wish to use, like Switch Pros or PS5 controllers.  Thing is these particular players are generally basic, when it comes to PC gaming, and continues to fail to understand that games on PC will configure their games on the assumption of Xbox style controllers being used first, and that any compatibility for other controllers are either a afterthought, or not thought of at all. _childDocuments_.review: As a longtime enjoyer of the Mana series going back to Secret of Mana I was really hyped for this game. That was probably my first mistake. This game has a lot of potential that I feel wasn't realized with that I've experienced so far. At this point I have completed my first playthrough of the main story on 'Hard' difficulty and unless the extra chapter has a lot of content to make up for all the hanging plot threads I can't recommend this game despite its pretty good combat. For those that played the remake Trials of Mana the combat system is almost identical with just the addition of elemental vessels/breaks which range from useful to overpowered depending on the enemies. The remake of a number of classic bosses in the new style was interesting at first but felt like they didn't make use of the fracturing weakspot mechanic or otherwise have reactive boss mechanics like they tease in the prologue.If you are looking for difficulty, as far as I can tell hard mode just makes things more bullet spongy, and with the exception of 2 minor bosses I didn't wipe a single time. I'm not a particularly good player and I didn't take the time to farm or optimize my builds/items/comp so I can't rate this game highly for challenge.What really killed the game for me in the end was the story however. While at first I thought they were going for a darker tone with the sacrifice of the souls to the Mana Tree it rapidly became clear that the story was focused almost entirely on juxtaposed love stories. Now this could have been done well if you made the 'villain's story a bit more deep to flesh out how he became the villain rather than treating the character as a one-dimensional plot device. The number of inexplicable power-ups that in the setting make 0 sense for the main enemy of this game is incredible. Some may say that its just the power of emotions taken to an extreme but when you are playing through it in-game it feels very contrived. Frankly speaking the game lacks any example of a good evil character or even a joke evil character that both of the previous games that I played had. It feels like at several points in the game that there might be the existence of a 'hand behind the curtain' type of enemy that engineered some of the tragedies that occurred within the world (like with Etaern) or even what appears to be the corruption of the main enemy however nothing actually comes of this and I'm left scratching my head and guessing I just read too much into things.In any case I feel like I'm rambling so the TLDR is:Decent combat/art/worldGood performanceWeak writingTerrible antagonistLess boss/enemy varietyMore chore content familiar to other open world style games.Low baseline challenge (extreme mode not tested yet)Again really wanted to like this game more but left feeling unsatisfied in the end.
