_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: The game is surprisingly good. Everything is very detailed and smooth. I feel like the team put a lot of effort into this game. The dubbing is good, the graphics, the gameplay, the story, the art, the characters, the environment, everything was well done. There are some things that could improve, like the world could have more interactions, entering houses, climbing mountains, but other than that, it is a pretty good relaxing game.~Story 9/10~Gameplay 8.5/10~Sound 6.5/10~Music 9/10~Dubbing 10/10~Characters 9/10~Performance 8.5/10~Environment 8/10~Fun 9/10Final score 8.6
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Great game, easy to pick up and play. Visions of Mana has a nice blend of an old school RPG with an updated combat system. I found this game relaxing, cozy, and fun to play compared to most of what is out there these days. Here is a list of some of things I liked and disliked about Visions of Mana.Pros:- Fun and engaging combat system with just enough challenge mixed in to spice it up.- Does not waste your time; it's easy to fast travel around and explore.- You are rewarded for exploring and seeking out all the treasures and it does not feel forced.- The class system and customizable options are fun to play around with.- Cool story without a woke agenda and characters.- No micro-transactions or in-game store.Cons:- Morley's haircut is just appalling, lol.- Some of the classes are underwhelming with a large discrepancy between usefulness.- There are a lot of cut-scenes that do drag on at times; this could be a pro if you are a story driven player.- Some of the zones are a collect-a-thon with treasures and items.- NetEase is scum and killed the studio that made the game.- Can be too easy if you are a skilled gamer.I highly recommend this game, especially if you are the type of person that likes RPG's from the 90's and 2000's.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I Think Square Enix brought a lot of elements together from some greatly loved titles for this one! The action rpg elements make me nostalgic of the early Kingdom Hearts games, and I find myself hungry to explore every nook and cranny of maps. The exploration is rewarding!! I'm enjoying the hard difficulty which is giving a decent challenge to a souls lover. The equipment features are original and Versatile, i don't think you will end up with any useless or uninteresting party development. And finally the story has feelygood elements and a deep darkness that hooks the player. Kingdom hearts fans will feel right at home, but will never see any dumb "disney skills". The formula is improving here, This is how action rpg's should be done.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it, it brings back wonderful memories from my childhood. The developers really put a lot of effort into this and polished it up wonderfully. It's nice to finally buy a AAA game that was ready for release on day one and not suffer performance bugs. This is easily becoming one of my favorite games. Thank you to all who made this game possible!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic, Beautiful, Engaging.This is a perfect starting game for people curious about JRPGs, but thanks to the hard mode, an engaging action RPG.The story is slightly more intellectual than previous entries, but it's still nothing original. Your preference is subjective but it's more in line with traditional fantasy stories. Unlike other Japanese games, it doesn't overwhelm you with vocabulary. It's a cozy story that could put some people to sleep.The gameplay is a more unshackled version of Trials of Mana. Once a few upgrades are obtained, Combos become more fluid. Ability slots allow you to chose stat boosts, or abilities a party member wouldn't normally learn.The visuals of the game are stunning, extraordinarily vibrant landscapes everywhere. The character designs are creative too.it's definitely a more on the "pretty" or "cute" spectrum. This might turn a few people off, even more so with the extra dialogue. It would be understandable to find the cutsie overjoy of characters repeating the same lines in the field after collecting basic items.This is a longer entry in the franchise. Which has its ups and downs. Thankfully the pacing is acceptable, it might take you twenty or more hours to get your final squad member.I recommend this to fans of FF7 Remake. Fans of Tales of Arise. People who like mashing buttons for attacks. And I recommend it to people who like  simple but dynamic options. As well as anyone that just wants a colorful, epic tale with lovable characters. Unlike Trials of Mana, which was a modest but bold remake. This pulls off what current day triple A games should arrive for in terms of value. And the value is here. But so is the charm. People have said "it's 7/10 but that's still amazing." No. This game is excelling at almost everything it's trying to do.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: While it does have some issues as a pc port, this game has been a great time so far.  I've only played the trials remake prior to this, and enjoyed that also. Overall compared to that I'd say this is a pretty significant step up, and while it might not have quite the same charm in simplicity they've done about a good a job as they could to keep that while also making things a bit more modern. Still relatively early in but here are some positives and negatives I've noticed.- Great visuals- Runs well (see later notes for more detail)- Story has had more meat than I expected going in compared to trials, not revolutionary but pretty good so far- The class system gives a decent amount of freedom- The artifacts in and out of combat have been enjoyable- Good soundtrack- While the game looks great, there's a pretty disappointing lack of PC customization options- Some cutscenes are capped at 30fps by default- Combat is fairly simple, if you like trials it's not going to dissapoint you but if you're coming in expecting in depth combo systems/twitch doge and pary this is not that at all- Large zones/semi-open world, it's done well enough not necessarily bad but be aware if you aren't a fan of that style of zoneAs of writing, you can use cheat engine to fix the cutscene cap issue. You can find steps in the discussions section. You can also find a few mods to increase some of the graphical settings past stock without much performance impact I've noticed. Also, you can force DLSS instead of FSR which I recommend if you have a compatible setup, again just look in the discussion board. After setting this stuff up pretty much all the issues with the port are resolved and everything looks and runs great. On a 3080 and 5600x this is running a solid 100-120fps at 4k with balanced dlss (and the higher settings mod paks).
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Visions of Mana is truly amazing, really gives off that classic 90s Sqauresoft vibe. Multiclassing is really fun, I created a lady with a scythe and ice magic and she's really fun to play as. The story is really good and is keeping me hooked. The combat feels snappy and to the point, though on hard mode enemies felt a bit too tanky for my liking. The music is really enjoyable, I've stopped to take in the music and scenery countless times now. The game truly feels like a Mana game too, not like Tales of Arise where they completely shifted the format.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If you need a challenging action RPG I would recommend buying it. The game offers lots of customization options thanks to the elemental board. There are lots of things to do and find in the world. My playing time was around 30 hours for the first playthrough. There is a New Game Plus mode with more Content and secret Bosses. get to the Bacon!
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is so delightful. It feels like a relic of childhood, while also having grown up alongside those of us who were enchanted by the series as kids. It's just magic. It's so tragic that the studio got shut down on release day and I hope that somehow we can see more from them. Despite that, I know this game is reaching the people it needs to, and I'm thankful for Ouka's hard work and love of the series.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Is this the best game in the Mana series? Absolutely. Is it an excellent game overall? There was potential, but it’s not quite there.Pros:- In its own style, the aesthetics of the environment are very enjoyable. The colours stand out well, and the cities almost make you want to live in them. The game's semi-open world field also allows for exploration that leads to several breathtaking scenery. The various mounts are, of course, very practical and fun to ride.- The gameplay doesn't disappoint, though we're not into great sophistication either. The class system is perhaps the best aspect of the game. Instead of forcing players to choose a specific build, they can simply combine the skills of several classes at once, while choosing their main branch and switch it without significant penalties. The build possibilities based on 8 different elemental spirits are therefore numerous, as are the different fighting styles that come with them. - The puzzlelike main dungeons are very fun to beat. There’s a little Zelda vibe in their design, but a little bit more simplistic. It makes everything more dynamic and stylish. Not to forget the bosses are quite visually impressive and sometimes hard to beat.- The game has its several super challenges: supermini bosses, super bosses, options to choose several difficulty levels, etc. To get through high difficulty, you'll need to master all the combat mechanics as well as often refer to the Pokédex style bestiary.Cons:- This is a baby game. The storytelling is very, very childish, and the sprites of both playable and non-playable characters lack a lot of maturity, in my opinion. I know it's a Mana game and all that fits in with the initial style of the series, but more maturity wouldn't have hurt for older players.- In combat, the camera is your worst enemy. You'll understand. Also, when you’re fighting, if your character is the least bit unsteady and you ask him to cast a spell or use an item, he won't do anything. In other words, your character must be perfectly stable before you ask him to make an action, and it’s even worse when you don’t control this character. A pain in the Butt Hole when you’re getting severely overwhelmed.- The game never immerses you in a vibrant plot. At some point, there's a triggering event that makes things interesting, but it never leads to a very ‘’wow’’ turn of events. In short, the game's storytelling is as beige as its events, and that's not to mention a lip sync and acting that will make you often cringe.- The music is good, but we’re not in the masterpiece zone.I'd recommend Visions of Mana to those who have already played and enjoyed the other classics in the same series. If you're a fan of Secret of Mana, Trials of Mana (Seiken Densetsu 2) and Legends of Mana, you'll enjoy Visions of Mana. Also, wait until the game is on sale. Otherwise, I'd simply say that the game lacks polish and maturity. It's a shame, since its foundations are very good. In short, Visions of Mana won't make history, but it's still worth completing once, at least if you’re the nostalgic type.(A generous) 8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I am a GenX old guy who played Secret of Mana when it was new on the SNES, and it always stuck out with me for how amazing it was (except for the ending where you fight your own dragon that you were just flying on? wtf was that about?)... And I must say that this game so far is really fun, and gives some of us oldies nostalgia with things like the bright color palate and monsters I somehow remember after 30 years. I really love how they did the spell casting where it kind of freezes time giving you a moment to think - as opposed to some games that hurry you to make a choice. The ring system is perfect for the battles... And the story is actually pretty good so far. Granted I am only 5 hours in as I write this and I am not sure why everyone seems so excited to basically off themselves as Alms to a tree... but ok. Really great fun so far.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: While it doesn't follow the tiered class system from Trials of Mana, this game introduces a fresh take on character progression that really shines. The new class system may not be as structured, but it’s a welcome change that adds a lot of replayability. Switching classes is now much more accessible, and the game’s skill tree-like system allows for a lot of experimentation with character builds, making each playthrough feel unique.The story, however, is a bit of a mixed bag. I appreciate the attempt at a darker tone, which is a bold direction for the Mana series, but it doesn’t quite hit the mark for me. It feels somewhat out of place compared to the usual vibe of the series, but it’s not a deal-breaker.The world has definitely expanded, offering a larger playground filled with treasures and side quests that encourage exploration. The bigger world is a strong point, making the adventure feel more epic and engaging.Overall, this is a solid entry in the Mana series. I’d recommend it to long-time fans and anyone looking for a casual hack-and-slash experience with some interesting character-switching mechanics. It may not be perfect, but it’s a great game to dive into, whether you're a fan of the series or just looking for something fun to play.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is more meant for those who have been around the mana series long enough to know the references and the lore. Its a great game with a lot of different options to customize your characters, the story is enjoyable so far and im only half way through.People will say nothing about this game is original.  And that's fine, in the same way meals are not original, its ultimately how its cooked, and this game is cooked really well.  There are a few minor gripes I have like wishing for more melee skills or bringing back the skill system from trials.  Or not tying the class down to 1 weapon type per class. Those are minor, im enjoying the rest of the game very well.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I've been waiting for a game like this for a long time. It's top tier JRPG goodness with fantastic graphics to boot. The English voices were a bit annoying at first but they're growing on me, the only downside that I am still disappointed about is the lack of good facial expressions on the characters. Love how it is almost Kingdom Hearts-like in the combat though and I just can't get over how nice the world looks. Very much enjoying it and I would recommend it if you are a fan of JRPG's and/or beautiful imaginative worlds.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, I recently already reviewed this game and recommended it but I have to redo this after finishing it.The ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ STUTTERING. It's in the beginning, then it stops and then after chapter six, it comes back and it hits even harder. I used a mod to up the performance of the game but nope, it's not changing much. I don't have a benchmark-pc but I certainly don't have a bad computer. Why can I run Elden Ring in good graphics, Enshrouded and the likes but not Visions of Mana without the stuttering out of hell? Tweaked on the settings, also no change. Just endless stuttering. It's annoying in fights and horrible in cutscenes.Shame on this unoptimized mess.Now to the story. Went in with the expectation of something more mature, something that really hits since this is THE new Mana Game everyone was waiting for (and my entry in this series) and...welp, got disappointed. I never played a game this corny and cheesy. Sure, we are all honored to safe the world but you can't tell me not a single soul except that gaian-boy is against throwing their loved ones practically in front of a train?! In such a world, where every four years, people are sacrificed, I'd suspect there'd be more people hiding in the wilds or living away from the faeries eyes to not go through that emotional damage. Also:  Everyone is just so incredibly happy all the time and the few moments where negative emotions are displayed are either If you are 12-16 years old or a die-hard fan, you probably will enjoy this game a lot. The voice acting is on point and really great, the world looks amazing and there is stuff to do (although I find the rewards for some things ridiculous and not worth all the effort - looking at you, cactus.)The travelling system got teleported from hell into this game. Eventually, you can travel freely everywhere but to travel to spots on another continent, you need to move to your mount, travel to a spot on the other continent to freely teleport there and if you need to go back, you once again need to sit through that cutscene, move over to the other continent before being able to teleport again. That's just a waste of time and annoying.Corny story. Already said enough about that.But what I can't mention often enough is the bad stuttering in this game. There are even mods out for it! Wanting sixty dollars for a game this badly optimized and forcing modders to take care of the mess is downright cocky but hey, it's square enix so nothing f*** new. Can't believe I'm always falling for this. So no, I'm not recommending this game. Not while it's such a stuttering mess. I'm not not recommending this game due to story or anything else because that's just my taste and this game didn't hit it but the stuttering is a big, big no-go.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This game is the first game in years to truly make me feel like I'm a kid again. Its good, simple, lighthearted fun in a beautiful, colorful world. The combat is fast and fluid, customization aplenty, and characters that I sincerely care about. The soothing soundtrack compliments the various landscapes and just relaxes you as you play. So far I'd give it a solid 9/10
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say about this game? I'm not a Mana fan, I'm more of a gritty/dark fantasy vibe guy, but I have played Trials of Mana and really enjoyed it. I thought to myself: this game is really fun, but it still feels a bit cheap... I would love for the next mainline game to have a bigger budget and scope than Trials. Oh boy, how pleased I am with this one!Visions is like Trials on HEAVY steroids. It's gorgeous, it feels massive, the music is beautiful, the exploration is AWESOME and don't even get me started on the combat! There are so many classes to try on each of the characters, that I just can't wait to unlock a new element and see what it unlocks in terms of combat and exploration. On the hard difficulty it feels challenging in all the right ways (apart from the timed elemental trials, some of these can feel a bit unbalanced, at least in the earlier portion of the game).The only real "complaint" I have with it, is the same I have with these types of traditional high fantasy jrpgs: the world just doesn't have what it takes to immerse me in the story. It feels very happy-go-lucky and upbeat, and when it tries to create drama it just doesn't feel like it have any weight to it. That being said, I already made my peace with it even before I bought it, and the story itself isn't bad on it's own. I just prefer more mature and nuanced storytelling/worldbuilding. Also, be aware that the opening hours are on the slow side and even if the dialogues never extended their welcome for me, I would prefer if the game just let me explore, fight and admire it's beauty with less interruptions.To summarize, here is what you will get with this EXCELLENT game:º Gorgeous graphics (and really good optimization)º Expansive areas to explore, with meaningful exploration that rewards going off the beaten pathº Excellent and responsive combat with a good amount of challenge (on hard mode)º Great and varied boss fightsº Great variety in how to customize your characters and their classesº Gorgeous musicº Ok characters in an ok story that has a bit of a slow startº Seriously, just go buy this gem
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a worthy successor of the Mana series.The engine and gameplay are immediately recognizable if you played Trials of Mana. This is very much that, with a much more freedom-based class system and much larger exploration areas. I would not call this an "open world" game - its just a game with larger zones.Recommended.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's probably a rough 7.5/10 at best. I'm not terribly far in yet, but the base gameplay is just "ok". The zones are decently large and there aren't an overabundance of invisible walls (though they do exist even within the traversable bits). Combat is fun enough and not very difficult on normal settings. Bosses are mostly dodge red and wail on things. Standard and fine too. Graphics are a bit disappointing on max and chances are you'll want to use third party mods to get the best performance.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It is excellent.The game has a lot of systems and I think it was hard for the demo to teach them well. In the actual game, things take more time so you get used to it little by little.It is designed like old school action rpgs, but with all the modern quality of life and presentation than you would except. As a result, there aren't many games like this. It's colorful, whimsical, you can either rush or spend time in areas, it's up to you. Visuals are great, music is great, the story is much more interesting than I thought it was gonna be, and gameplay is actually pretty fun, love the exploration, and combat once you get some abilities and use shortcuts etc.. it's solid.Seems like a natural evolution of Trials of Mana, with a bigger budget. They did fix most of the stutters from the demo, it seems like mods may be required to force 60 fps cutscenes and draw distance, but besides that, no issues with the PC port. Runs good looks good.I just wish Eowen was a playable character ...edit :Still peak. Extremely comfy game. Don't hesitate to check out the ingame guide in the start menu, it explains a lot of things that had flown over my head ! From lore to battle systems.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure if I'm sold on the characters or story in this yet, it's pretty early in, but I am very impressed with the level design of these first couple zones. Reminds me of playing some of the old school platforming games like Spyro or Jak and Daxter or something like that. Lots of verticality and jumping around for collectibles like weapons and armor, which is nothing out of the ordinary, but I didn't expect it here, and I didn't expect it to be so well done. If the rest of the zones in this game are as well done as the first open zone in this, this game is gonna to please a lot of fans. ....I really hope the story and characters don't get in the way of what might be a pretty good Mana entry, we'll see.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Growing up with Seiken Densetu 3 as one of my favorite games of all time, this game gives me so much nostalgia. Simple easy to follow story, beautiful characters, good combat animation and above all fun gameplay are here. Highly recommend for trial of mana fans.The only con I find is 30 fps cap for cut scenes.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite game franchise from the first installment that came during my childhood to the latest released it has continued to be held dear and near my heart. It is incredibly beautiful to see how much it has grown and developed over the years. It makes me extremely happy to see all the hard work and dedication the team has put on each new installment. This one feels like a love letter to all the players who experienced the game since the start. Every little detail of the game you can really see they carved it with love and respect for the older games which can't be said for a lot of older franchised that are made today. I was worried that their creative vision might get tainted, but the team held their ground from what I can see thus far and have read from the team. I hope that the team will continue to create and share their master pieces with us. I will follow in whatever endeavor it may lead them. I wished the game would've had a Switch release, but I understand why it couldn't which is why I ended up with 2 copies of the game the Collector's Edition and Deluxe Edition <3.Ps. In the odd chance he'll read this. HACCAN I love you. What an absolute unit. A king amongst man <3
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: - The combat isn't amazing, but it feels fluid and works well.- The collect-a-thon isn't very grindy for a JRPG (This may be a positive or negative depending on you).- The graphics are good in their own stylized sort of way. It works.- The story is NOT just a typical happy-go-lucky generic JRPG plot; anyone complaining that it is has not played very far; I think the plot that unfolds is actually one of the game's strong points. It's pretty interesting.It's a good game, I'd say as a JRPG it's in the same realm of quality as Ni No Kuni 2 or FF16; but it's no masterpiece like some of the better Final Fantasy games or Dragon Quest 11.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Was skeptical because the demo wasn't that great. Starting at the actual beginning gives much more depth to the characters and plot. Have had no stutters and have played past the demo mark at this point. Everything feels great so far and if you like action jrpgs or the mana series, then this game is great. Will update review after i beat the game but just wanted to note that my experience with the full game is vastly superior to the lack luster demo. Biggest and only con so far is 30 fps cutscenes and hitting f11 to bypass it is annoying. Hopefully a mod fixes that later.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: It's pretty much 2020 Trials of Mana but improved in every way. ToM had been my favorite game since its release despite the fact that I never play the original game before. Its biggest downside was ludicrously shallow story, as expect of a remake of 25 year old game.I'm still very early in the game but Visions if Mana so far has a pretty decent story. And by far the most enjoyable explorations I have in a video game. It's kinda insane how many games even nowadays don't allow you to jump over a fence. VoM on the other hand allow you go take almost every path you want. The game gives you double jump right away which itself worth celebrating.Shame the studio got shut down the day it releases.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Most of my Mana experience is with Secret of Mana, SNES Trials of Mana, and Legend of Mana on PS1.  This game, so far, is a great action RPG with a fun class system akin to Trials (or Seiken Densetsu 3).  Combat is action packed and overworld offers a few unique objectives so far to make it fun.  I'm playing on hard mode, and a few hours in it definitely starts to feel like a fun difficulty to make you use the battle system elements to full advantage. Story is a bit basic jPRG so far, but it's enough to keep you going.Only real cons are the voice acting (english) is a bit amateurish, and the overworld jumping seems to ignore any momentum  you have from sprinting.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Do you know how long it's been since I have actually enjoyed a single player game?  Far too long, that's how long!  I've loved every game out of the Mana series and I have been waiting for this game for a while now and I'm so happy it's finally here.  You get that old school Secret of Mana feel to the game in a 3D world!  At least I do.If you have liked other Mana games, I would highly recommend this one too.  I'm not very far but I'm enjoying roaming the maps and exploring.  I hope they add some fun DLC content for this, being able to customize your look is awesome.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it already.  Voice acting + lip syncing is rough like Trials of Mana, but I can easily overlook that.  I'm honestly happier with the janky voices than I was with FF7R's.  The prologue is mercifully short.  Exploration is fun -- I'm spending more time than I anticipated just looking around, taking in the scenery, trying to climb everything, and finding treasure chests and items lying around.  Battles are fun.  The relationship between the two lead characters is sweet.  The world looks pretty.  Everything feels exciting and fresh.  I'm excited to keep going.

_childDocuments_.review: I wanted to play to test the performance.  I played in 4k on high graphics with no stutters or odd graphics. My controller worked immediately and the entire time. _childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: and we got a winnera) the game is pretty, like realy pretty to look at. it is not just the color palette, it is pretty much everything. the textures, the particle effects; the world is full of little details you realy wouldn't expect coming from the pre-quel.there is little petals floating through the air, gust of wind blowing dust, critters beeing critters; incredible athmospheric lighting effects and always animated (and alive feeling) flora and fauna.heck the attention to detail even goes so far as to have ambient sound effects for butterflies.this game is a piece of art.heck even the menues are nice to look at.nevermind the pre-rendered or ingame cutscenes.beeing it animations, coloring, art-design: 10/10and it just keeps on growing; everytime you think this couldn't get prettier it wows you again.now my rig is by today's standart not quite up-to-par anymore, but running everything on max, 1080 to 1440p (hughe screen/TV) with Vsync turned on i have 0 frame drops (only certain ingame cutscenes seem to be rendered at a lower frame rate), 0 glitches or bugs i noted. this is running on 3070, 32GB, i5 and on a SSD.b) the OST is fantastic (again); mixing and remixing the classical OST while offering some fitting new tracks; the same goes for the ambient sounds. snow crackles, planks plank, flies buzz and the see crushes it's waves. the VO (english) is for the overwhelming part great (again); there is a metric ton of VO (pretty much only random villageresques and shop-like dialogue ain't voiced). c) the writing and general story presentation is a hughe leap foreward from what the pre-quel offered...which is something i realy didn't expect. there is a lot more world building and context to everything going on. much of the dialogue has again it's very own unique, quirky style. this time around i feel like also the cast got somewhat more attention. even party-members i initialy though to become annyoin (i'm old and zynical) quickly grew on me. but this is always going to be a matter of taste. it is still very upbeat and light-hearted, mixing the traveling adventure the series is known for, with some more intricate themes, but never getting to the point of beeing annyoingly edgy or dark (or fan-servicy).d) and most important: the gameplay is spot on. you have again this almost job-system, where depending on what element you equip you change classes; this time around you gather a currency (through leveling normaly, doing little side-challenges or gathering stuff) to unlock abilities and you again need special items to unlock higher tiered skills. mixed ontop is the ability-seed system: think FF's materia; each character having slots where you can equip said seeds (like equipment) and switch around any- and everytime you want. these offer what you'd expect: classical stat boni, to active and passive skills, etc. .then there is the elemental vessels which serve both as traversal tools (kinda like a metroidvania) and hefty incombat attacks (like the moon-element slows enemies, wind is a damage attack) which also net you mana.at to this gear, items, all sorts of classes and spells/abilities, buffs and debuffs, active party-members which are actualy usefull this time around and often very different playing and feeling classes depending on the character you equip with a specific element (like moon will turn Van into a lance-tank, shieldbash-included while Morley becomes a thief/assasin like nightblade focused around crits and quick hits for example).e) outside of combat the game has also seen a hughe amount of love. the areas feel much more organic this time around, with miles better and more interesting level-design. there are collectibles (different "currency-items" for special traders), little challenges, metroidvania-like-unlocks and treasure hidden all over the place, aswell as re-spawning trash mob packs (and special mini-bosses).and this is still skipping on quite some features.tbh. if you like action-rpgs, the series, or action-combat jrpgs/rpgs this is a must have without a doubt.even trying to think about some negatives the best i can come up with is that mounting and dismounting could be a tad faster and more fluid (yes, there are mounts).as someone who grew up with the series in 2D and actualy kinda liked the 3D pre-quel despite some rough edges, i already expected to like Visions, but in all honesty: this game has blown me away. might be an easy GOTY for me. it is fun, it is upbeat and uplifting, it is probably suited for minors (although there are some hard topics touched upon) and more min/maxing gamers alike. there is quite some depth to the combat and rpg mechanics, the exploration is drop-dead-gorgeous, the music just slaps and the dialogue, OST, visuals, writing and pacing and athmosphere are like taking a vacation from our often pretty brutal and harsh (or annyoin) reality.10/10, well done Square Enix
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: If you want some of that classic Mana vibe on a much larger scale with very much not reinventing the wheel this is for you. I say not reinventing the wheel as an intentional dig at the Final Fantasy series for their inability to stop reinventing the formula that gave it success.  Look to the Dragon Quest series which has been consistent from the start Square Enix. That is what will make the Mana series great moving forward. Continue this way. Doesn't need to be a monster budget necessarily. The Trials of Mana was awesome because it stayed true to the original but translated it to 3D. Do the same with Chrono Trigger (hell the main character in Visions of Mana looks very much like Crono) and Final Fantasy 6 using either the Visions of Mana engine or even the Trials of Mana engine. Not every game has to be compicated and reinvented similar to the FInal Fantasy 7 remake (which was great on its own but we don't need a monster budget for every game).
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Beat the game edit:This is one of the best games I've played in the past 2 years, and I've played other SE games like FF16, FF7Rebirth, FF14 Dawntrail, etc.  The story is great, the character development is awesome, and the class system is fun.A few technical things: I had an issue with the camera panning down randomly despite changing my settings.  Also, I'm not a huge fan of the cartoony art style.  However, those issues are easily glossed over as this is the best Mana experience I've had since Secret of Mana.  The world is open to exploration, the action RGP elements are part same part innovative, and the music is top notch.All in all, 9.5/10 game.  Definitely pick it up, and don't wait for a sale if you're a fan of the Mana series.  It's worth it.Early Review: I'm ~3 hours into this game and really enjoying it.  I've gotten my first extra party member, and my first elemental vessel.  This feels like a modern Secret of Mana; you get to explore, kill monsters, and use elemental abilities.  It's a lot of fun so far.  If the rest of the game continues like this, it will be an above average score for me.As far as game-play goes, this is way better than the demo.  I've had 0 lag spikes or stuttering.  The combat makes more sense because you go through tutorials.  The camera defaults to auto-moving, but I updated that in the settings and not it's great.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: So far the game has been amazing!- Exploration is fun and rewarding- Combat is interesting but still too early to fully say as I am far from having all the spirit vessels- Story for far is nothing to ride home about but its not bad either, I am enjoying itThe game's performance so far has been stellar, all cut scenes are locked at 30 FPS but exploration and combat is locked at 60 FPS. No lags, no crashes, no breaking bugs.I use a Xbox Series X controller and had no problems with support, completely working.If you like RPGs, here's a solid one.=========== UPDATE ===========So, after playing it for over 70h and doing everything that had to be done, I still recommend this game. The story as I sad before is not the best one out there but it is ok, and although I thought chapter 10 a bit out of place the battle system on this game is very fun and I like the freedom it gives me to find my own play style.The sound track on this game is a banger, specially the sproutling village.A big problem I found with the game is that the more on end game I got the more fatal crashes from UE4 I was getting, usually I would expect those to be fixed within the first week or close to release but with the current studio state idk if they gonna get fixed at all. I had crashes happen mid battle, forcing me to redo some bosses, had a crash on the cut-scene right after final boss which made me redo the battle with the final boss and let alone the many other crashes along the game that made me save after any major progress.8/10, I had fun.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: TL;DR- I really enjoyed the game from start to finish, solid pacing, fun combat/characters/world but Wish the NG+ was actually interesting. I just love me some Mana games man, they are super comfy & this one kept me engaged & active the whole play through, I only wish it had better or more interesting replayability.8/10 if I had to give a rating, where as I gave Trials of Mana 9-9.5/10 personally. So take that information as you will.Just finished Visions of Mana after 64.5 hours on Hard Difficulty. Both full main story & post game stuffs(don't disclose)Was a very enjoyable romp through another Mana game that was most welcome & as always these games take me back to when I was a kid.Some takeaways from the full experience:-The Story is easy to digest & enjoyable as long as you are just along for the ride, it's got it's sets of twists & turns & mystery that it sets up & slowly discloses throughout the game, so the pacing felt good.-The Combat: It feels slower & less responsive & more clunky at times in comparison to The Trials of Mana remake of which this will heavily be compared to by many people. However it's more a system that once you adjust to it & it *clicks* you get it & start flying through combat scenarios at a nice pace, the only problem there is the end of battle menu takes a looong time to finally close out so you can interact with things in the world.-Since we're in the Combat portion, how about itemization for gear: There is no crafting/forging/upgrading new gear, you either find it in a chest or buy it from a merchant or earn certain weapons from  boss fights. Then once you find the new shiny thing you replace old shiny thing & move on, no skills from equipment or anything like that, just flat numbers.That being said, you can use different weapons you own as skins for any other like weapons so whatever you do DON'T SELL YOUR WEAPONS or else you'll lose the ability to use it as a skin & will have to buy it again.Skills: The skill system is spread between the elemental class system & the seeds you equip into slots to give yourself either passive stats or access to certain skills you would otherwise not have access to for certain characters. Later on the Passive Class skill system gets much more interesting but that's a late game thing & has to do with basically building your own class, but won't divulge more than that to avoid spoilers. On that note....-The Class system: A neat design that forces you to swap characters around to the different elements but also lets you take abilities you've unlocked from other classes & use them across all classes you have unlocked, from there it becomes which Elemental Spirit vessel you prefer to use. Personally my favorite combination is a Dark, Light & Water Vessel team; try it it's fun!-Graphics: they are just like Trials of Mana, very vibrant, comforting to look at & easy on the eyes, not much else to say, if you like anime style games then this is just that.-Performance: So for the most part I played the game at 120fps & it held pretty steady except for a few Boss fights that have a lot of arena based effects going on (HEAVY DARKNESS in the arena boss fight) that absolutely TANKED my FPS down to literally 2fps which forced me to pause mid combat & wait a few moments to un pause & let it settle itself back out, so there are clearly some unoptimized areas of the game that need addressed. There are a handful of other situations similar usually during boss fights & some other fights when you get a lot of spells going off simultaneously.Also Cutscenes at 30fps SHOULD NOT BE A THING. If you hit F11 to change your screen it will actually adjust & let the cutscenes play at proper fps, no reason why they had to limit it here, I expect there will be if not already mods to fix that by the time of this review.-Controller: I used a DualShock 4 controller & the game played fine except for when you accidentally even lightly touch the touch pad your character & camera will WHIP a complete 180, and it happened VERY often which almost caused several falls off of ledges, ect & lost time since there's no fall damage so not a big deal ultimately but very annoying for me which was probably the most annoying thing overall to deal with.-NewGame Plus: It exists & it does nothing special that I could tell except allow you to adjust to another tier higher difficulty in Expert, however the game literally just resets the world, same 100 lucre in the same chests, same piece of candy from that same yellow light item, same level 1 enemies at the beginning of the game, only plus side is allowing you to get more resources for class ability unlocks & remaining character unlocks that you may not have felt it worth grinding the Nicollo coins for during the initial run, that will make sense as you get later into the game.
_childDocuments_.name: Visions of Mana

_childDocuments_.review: Early game, Feels like the Trials of Mana remake with a budget and thankfully. Better VO Direction. name: Dark and Deep
detailed_description: I created Dark and Deep because I wanted to bring a totally new visual aesthetic to the horror genre. There is not a game that looks like mine. My art process is unique, bringing the illustrations of 19th Century Artist, Gustave Doré into a new dimension. My Journey Making this Game I have had a lifelong obsession with conspiracies and mythology. I made Dark and Deep to share my love for the strange and ancient with the horror game community. Through the 4-6hr playtime of Dark and Deep, you will be intrigued, unsettled, and mystified by the blend of strange storytelling and meaningful mechanics I have devised for you. DARK and DEEP You play as Samuel Judge, a loyal fan of the mysterious conspiracy podcast, 'Dark and Deep' . Plunged into a shadowy and dangerous landscape, you must survive... and you are not alone. Use magical picture frames to fight hidden creatures and reveal important objects. The frames are windows into a terrifying world, but also tools to banish the darkness. Unveil the conspiracy before the shadows swallow you. Listen to the podcast. Experience the unraveling as your favorite conspiracy podcast comes too close to home. Become embroiled in a dramatic tale of intrigue and betrayal where the real and surreal collide. Solve physics puzzles using powerful ancient machines of cryptic origin. Manipulate gravity and clear a path through the deadly fog. Use precious embers of light in the darkness to show your way. But beware… The creatures in the shadows want nothing more than to steal your light. Dark and Deep features a totally unique aesthetic, which uses the art of 19th century master artist, Gustave Doré as the textures for much of the game. Doré was legendary for his detailed black and white illustrations of mythological and historical scenes. Dark and Deep uses his aesthetic to tell a surreal cosmic horror story where the boundaries of sanity and reality are bent and broken. - Unveil hidden secrets and lurking enemies with a collection of mystical frames given to you by a mysterious observer. - Battle what lurks in the shadows using your frames and ancient supernatural machines discovered in the world. Don’t let what hides in the deadly darkness steal away your light. - Survive in a cryptic and surreal world filled with dangerous inhabitants and challenging puzzles. Click to join my DISCORD to share theories and leave suggestions

about_the_game: About Abyss Online Embark on an epic adventure in Abyss Online , the newest PVP MMORPG releasing in 2024 . Dive into a vast open-world teeming with possibilities, where a player-driven economy and intense PVP battles shape your destiny. Early Access Disclaimer Abyss Online is currently in Early Access and is under active development. While not yet feature-complete, we're continuously expanding the game with new content and systems. Please note that major updates may require game resets. Your feedback is invaluable in shaping the future of Abyss Online. Key Features Expansive Open World Explore diverse landscapes from bustling towns to untamed wilderness. Player-Driven Economy Influence the market through gathering, crafting, and trading. Intense PVP Combat Engage in arena battles against other players and rise to the top. Evolving World Encounter dynamic events and challenges that react to player actions. Early Access Highlights Starter Zone Exploration Begin your journey in a rich starter zone filled with resources and secrets. Gathering and Crafting Collect materials to craft weapons, armor, and tools essential for survival. Mob Camps and Combat Test your skills against challenging mobs and earn valuable loot. Community-Driven Development Participate in shaping the game by providing feedback and suggestions. Planned Features Dynamic Building Mechanics Construct and customize structures in the open world. New Regions and Biomes Unlock new areas with unique environments and creatures. Enhanced Quest System Experience deeper storytelling and engaging missions. Advanced PVP Mechanics Introducing guild wars, territory control, and ranked arenas. Expanded Crafting and Skills More crafting options and skill trees for character customization. Join Our Community Become a part of the Abyss Online community! Share your experiences, discuss strategies, and collaborate with fellow adventurers. Your insights help us create a game that evolves with its players. Discord: Join our Discord server Social Media: Follow us on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram. Stay Updated Wishlist and Follow Abyss Online Add the game to your wishlist and follow us on Steam to receive the latest updates and announcements. Experience the next generation of PVP MMORPGs with Abyss Online. Your adventure awaits!

_childDocuments_.review: This is not an MMO. This isn't even a "game" at time of writing. The EA blurb states:  I'd love to know what development, if any, actually occurred during this time period, because this feels like someone's game jam project that was put together in a weekend with some free assets, not something aspiring to be an MMO. I'm not a good enough writer to summarize just how under-developed and not worth your money this game is. You are dropped into the world with no guidance, no tutorials, a painful UI/UX, a non-functioning combat system, some random enemies you can't even attack (but can attack you), and some farmer selling you farming supplies. I understand it's Early Access, and I've bought many an EA game throughout the years, but this "game" should not be asking for people's money until there's an actual game-loop and something tangible to play test. I've already requested a refund.

_childDocuments_.review: It is interesting to see this game get so much hate. It is in EARLY ACCESS, which is something that most people these days do not seem to understand. Sure, there are some "early access" games that come out that are nearing their completion (this may even be the trend these days), but those games also typically have huge teams and not much more to look forward to.It is by no means an exaggeration to say that the developers of Abyss Online are more passionate and committed than any other game devs. People just need to give them time to cook. Back in the day, gamers were patient and this was never even an issue. The game is currently in a playable state, and can be fun if you are not a moron or a six year old. Give it a shot. Join the discord and interact with the dev team. Be a little patient to see the growth happen. Don't fade it until it becomes mainstream, as you will most likely regret it in when early access players are given the most exclusive vanity in the game. Keep up the good work team.

name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess
detailed_description: A new tale of the Kami awaits... Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess is a unique Japanese-inspired, single player Kagura Action Strategy game. The game takes place on a mountain covered by defilement. During the day, purify the villages and prepare yourself for sundown. During the night, protect the Maiden against the hordes of the Seethe. Repeat the day and night cycle until you cleanse the mountain of defilement and return peace to the land. Unique Japanese-inspired World The setting is Mt. Kafuku—a mountain covered in defilement. The game offers a taste of Japanese culture, including Kagura dance, masks, as well as the music that plays in the background. The Seethe The Seethe emerge from the Torii Gates to the other world when the sun sets. This enemy, which has a variety of different abilities, attacks at night under the cover of darkness, targeting the Maiden. The director's ideas and attention to detail have been packed into the design that presents the setting of this game. Exhilarating Sword Dance Action The main character, Soh, wields a sword to protect the Maiden of the mountain, Yoshiro, as she confronts the Seethe. Do not be intimidated by the enemy's array of attacks, and slay them with dance-like sword attacks! A Fusion of Action and Strategy . Soh's battles are not fought alone, but with the help of villagers who have been bestowed roles. What placements and roles will be most effective? Where will the villagers fight? And which enemies will Soh focus on? Constant changes during battle will test your strategy and tactics. Purify the Torii Gates of the Defilement . If you can survive the Seethe attacks until dawn and lead Yoshiro to a Torii Gate while the sun is still up, you can purify it with her Kagura dance. Restore peace to the mountain villages!

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to have the experience of playing an obscure PS2 game you never heard of and found as a rental in the back of a Blockbuster and spent an awesome weekend playing it and wondering why more people don't know about it, this is it. The setting is gorgeous and inspired, the characters seldom speak but are charming none the less, and the tower defense with villagers is a solid game play loop reinforced by rebuilding villages and finding new equipment for your character, unlocking new classes for your villagers, and permanent upgrades for those classes.When people say they wish they made good games anymore this is what they're talking about. This is the antithesis of modern video game slop.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

_childDocuments_.review: Have to give it a thumbs up just because it defies modern yapfest storytelling. The game tells you what's going on in a simple but very well made cutscene, says "okay now go do it", and you're off. Cutscenes are just to introduce new concepts and nothing more. There's barely even any words said, and they don't need to be said. Gameplay is solid, doesn't hold your hand any more than it needs to, and the art direction is top-notch. Capcom really cooked with this gem, I hope it gains traction. Tired of AAA moviegames. Other reviewers are saying this feels like a PS2 game and I have to agree, and that's probably the highest praise I could give a game.EDIT: Figured I should update the review now that I've 100%'d this game.First off let me say this: It is not common for me to 100% a game. I consider Persona 5 and Library of Ruina to both be some of my favorite games of all time- games that I would award a solid 10/10. I haven't 100%'d them.I'm someone who regrettably gets bored of games quickly and honestly? I leave many games unfinished in my backlog. But this game kept compelling me to come back, to finish the story, despite there being almost no words said. I was so deeply invested that I carried on through optional objectives that are frustrating as hell, I save scummed, I thought about giving up, but I kept coming back.Kunitsu-Gami is a hauntingly beautiful game. Everything about it exudes a dreamlike, ethereal sensation. It makes you really feel like you've been taken to another world, with mystical creatures and masked villagers. The fact that Yoshiro's face is the only one you see for the entire game  is a fantastic choice imo, as it really serves that dreamlike feeling splendidly. As humans we are used to seeing faces everywhere, it's in our DNA. So when a story is completely bereft of them, it makes it all feel so much more surreal. The gameplay is fun as hell. I have seen it described as "Pikmin but you're playing as Bayonetta" and I think that fits. For the first portion of the game before you unlock Soh's upgrade tree, it certainly can feel a bit dull and repetitive. But once you start unlocking more and more abilities and villagers, the gameplay becomes thrilling and such a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ joy to play. The music, the animations, the sound design, it's all spot-on. Capcom is further cementing they're the kings of action games with this one. Everything about this game feels so unreal. It's unreal to me that a game could release in 2024 that has such a high emphasis on the gameplay, which trusts in the player's intelligence and doesn't say any more than it has to. This honestly is in the top 10 for my games of the decade.
_childDocuments_.name: Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess

Projects built on artistic passion and strange ideas that make something truly unique, interesting, and if your lucky fun as well. Calling it a tower defense game is actually reductive. _childDocuments_.review: Game of the year for me right now. Beautiful pieces of media. I was on the fence because of the price, but I'd say its worth the money. This is one of the few games where I actually  to complete new game plus, because its so much fun to play.I thought the soundtrack was worth mentioning too. I was expecting some traditional Japanese string instruments, based on the game's aesthetic, but there's a good bit of variety here. The boss fights in particular ranged from metal guitar riffs to funky experimental jazz saxophone. This game feels like Capcom back in their Playstation 1 and 2 era, when they made games like Okami and Viewtiful Joe. I hope they do more of this.Edit 11/27/2024 - Can't believe this game got completely snubbed at the game awards!

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game and doing a New Game+ run (iworth it and fun to do since you carry everything you had previously and there's a few new things to experience) and completing it to 100% the only thing to add to the initial review would be that I really hope that Capcom hits all their internal targets/milestones on what would be needed for this game to be considered a success and thus to see a sequel to Kunitsu-Gami and also I hope that they keep betting on other new unique and innovative projects as is the case of this one, even if they have to be much smaller in terms of scope or execution (plus to add to the wishlist something on the Okami or Onimusha IPs!).Everyone on the team that was part of this project should be really proud on being able to contribute to such an amazing piece of art.Early review but this game is an absolute gem in all aspects that hopefully won't get overlooked to turn into just an unknown cult hit and instead has the deserved attention right from the release with a slow build up as time passes so that we can get more games in this vein. The game really feels as something out of the "PS1/2 gaming Era", where game companies still tried to innovate and bring something new with each game release - if you are even just middling interested in the game, give the demo a try since as many other people, with myself included, it might change your mind on it for the better or further reinforce your interest in it.Great visual art style with some innovative character and world design based on Japanese Folklore with graphics and effects that although are nothing to write home about they are well executed enough to do justice to the game accompanied with a perfect sound design and traditional music, plus containing also small cut-scenes between levels that tell this simple old-as-time and good-versus-evil but still compelling story with absolutely no dialogue.The gameplay which is the key aspect of the game, has the perfect mix of tactical phases by doing some planning on where to position your units with which roles while juggling resources and then moving around fighting with Soh (your samurai character) when suddenly all hell breaks loose and you are trying to save all your fronts and need to act quickly.■   where you have a selected few units that you can position around and choose their roles depending on the layout of the land and enemies that you will face (at a surface level can be similar to games such as Orcs Must Die/Sanctum/Dungeon Defenders but think more on Warhammer 40K Dawn of War II or something like the campaign missions in Age of Mythology where you have just a few heroes that you need to position them in some key position with some moving around to be able to win the levels rather than brute forcing with a huge number of units or have static Towers doing all the work);■   where you are just going around attacking the enemies in a empty front that you need to hold or to run to catch the ones that have escaped your troops with some simple but visually and satisfying combos - plus you also have boss encounters where it varies greatly on what might be the opponent and thus what can be the best strategy to win the fight (e.g. you might be alone, the boss might be flying most of the time);■   as you progress through the game you will liberate bases and in between the levels you will be able to revisit them to use as a base camp to manage the upgrades for your units, equip new talismans for Soh (your character) and also have some choices of which areas you wish your villagers to repair to get some specific resources back when they finish it (in the end you get all of them done so it's just a matter of getting a specific thing sooner rather than later).

_childDocuments_.review: Wildly, this game heavily incorporates interpretative dancing into almost all aspects of the gameplay. Why I say "wildly" is because the gameplay loop is a mix between Pikmin and Okami. It's a tower defense with RTS and hack-n-slash elements.Here is where the dancing comes into play- there is hardly any spoken dialogue and every action the characters make are exaggerated and theatrical, and the combat consists primarily of moves inspired by Japanese folk dance. Dance is at the core of this game's identity. BUT, not in a way that feels overly snobbish or boring, it's kept me engaged, curious, and oddly satisfied.The game is a bit rough around the edges in some places, and definitely a bit slower than I'd like at spots, but it's an impressive effort for a new IP from what I'd imagine is a relatively small to mid-sized team within Capcom. It's an experimental and creative game that deserves more attention and support- definitely check this out if you're the kind of person who laments how boring and samey AAA games get.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't even like tower defense games but this one really hooked me. The hack and slash combat starts out fairly weak since you don't have access to your skill tree yet, but once you get there then the game really opens up. You get access to a parry which looks and sounds amazing and staggers anyone nearby, you get a counterattack that you can use after guarding that does a ton of damage, you even get a dark souls-esque riposte when you stun enemies by depleting their resist gauge that one-shots everything short of one large enemy and the bosses. Oh, you also get access to a different fighting style which does a lot more damage than the starting one, but it's slower so I don't really like it.You've got special attacks in the form of Tsuba guards which let you do super flashy attacks on a fairly long cooldown that typically decimate entire groups of enemies or do serve some utility function, like you've got one that kills you but revives nearby villagers and one that teleports you to the priestess who is the main defense target of this game, you even get a massive ♥♥♥♥-off lighting wave that has the longest cooldown in the game but it obliterates anything in its path including bosses AND it looks cool as ♥♥♥♥. You can't die btw, if you die you just go into a spirit form and lose your ability to attack but you can still command and give roles to villagers, after your health bar refills you automatically get sent back into your body and can keep fighting.Your towers in this game come in the form of villagers, they start out without any abilities but you can spend crystals to give them a role which is basically this game's version of a tower type. Each role serves a distinct purpose, nothing here is made obsolete by any other role which I really liked, you're gonna be using the starter roles all the way through the whole game because they're the cheapest and when upgraded can defend key points well enough that you won't need to be in 3 places at the same time. You move your villagers around through a fairly intuitive interface and you can move them at any moment, whether it's the middle of a wave or the beginning of your prep phase, no one is locked into any one position unless you explicitly tell them to (or you get hit by the big scary debuff man whose sole purpose is to prevent you from commanding your villagers, he's not very common though.)Most levels have you spending crystals to carve a path through the ground for the priestess to move through, it's on rails and once she reaches the end of the level you just interact with the end door and you win. Those crystals are also used for roles though so you gotta kinda balance them a bit, not too difficult though.I got %100 in this game about an hour ago and I'm sad there isn't any more to play but it was well worth the $50. I really liked the part where my villagers fortnite danced in front of the torii gate and it died.

_childDocuments_.review: A very focused arcadey game with awesome aestheticsThis game is great in that it has a vision, and it executes that vision extremely neatly. There's no bloat here, and the game has an impressive grasp on which areas it has to focus. It has an interesting mix of tower defense/pikmin/hack and slash combat, which kind of had me remembering Little King's Story. Pacing is amazing, and it is easy to get into a flow of mission - upgrades - boss - upgrades - mission - etc. Missions are also very arcade like, in the sense that you jump into one, get it done in about half an hour, and cool down in the upgrade hub for a bit. The art direction is also a highlight. Everything looks like a small handicrafted diorama, and characters do huge, choreographed moves for their attacks that look like traditional japanese dances.A great soundtrack tops this off, in particular the boss themes, which get pretty wild. One of them goes full on jazz fusion at one point, and it rocks.The writing, while minimal, also does a good job in setting the tone - mystical, atemporal japanese fareAll in all, while it might be somewhat expensive for what are 13~20 hours of game, this is a premium experience, and I feel it's worth the price to take a look.

_childDocuments_.review: A beautiful Japanese escort game.  The whole game is heavily stylized, inspired by traditional Japanese art, especially the theatre. I was shocked to learn that stages of the game were physically modelled as miniatures and scanned. Even costumes for characters and sweets were based on real objects. The result is undeniably atmospheric and extremely beatiful.  The traditional theater is also referenced by human characters moving in a fluid dance-like fashion and wearing masks that denote their role. The music is excellent and mixes traditional and modern styles. It is also very diverse: from contemplative slow songs during exploration to fast eerie remixes playing during boss-fights.  The gameplay is basically a mix of escort missions and boss fights. In a standard mission there is a day/night cycle. The day is time for preparation, exploration and resource gathering. The night is spent defending the priestess by fighting (in 3rd person), using special abilities and managing supporting villagers. This formula is changed in special missions (static defence until resources are gathered, naval fights) and boss arenas. Villages cleared of corruption can be repaired over time, getting more lively and gathering more resources to take into missions.  The story is shown, not told (as characters generally do not speak) and is based on folk tales and eastern religions. More flavor is added by little descriptions of individual villagers, monsters and even sweet treats. The true ending is reached only after New Game+ and additional tough boss fight.  This game is practically exuding Japanese culture - paintings, theatre, music, religion and folklore... It is well worth to watch "Making of" videos. And a traditional puppet theater show, made just for this game. Because the authors really went all in.

_childDocuments_.review: I have positive experience with the game so far so here is my review and it will change once I am finishedGraphics is not this game strong suit but the art style is so pretty like Okami.The music is pretty great and uses traditional Japanese instruments just like OkamiThe gameplay of this game is not a hack n slash but an action game with some tower defense elements, the Villagers are the "towers" that you can move at any time you want and change before and during waves. The game does a good job with the Tutorial bits by slowly introducing units after you complete a stage or a boss with 11 total units you can get throughout  the game. Before the waves you can get a carpenter that builds up defenses and use orbs to make units while making a path to the corrupt Tori gates. When the sun sets the maiden will stop and you have to defend that position from enemy waves until the sun comes up.  Also you can control where she stops so you can have a better position to defend from. Now here is your character role on the battlefield, he is a general that you can move around and attack enemy units so if there is a problematic enemy you can rush and dispatch it while your Villager units handles anything that got past you. but you aren't invincible so retreat behind your units when things get hairy.  The main character can also  apply 2 passive buffs  and one ultimate that you can use to increase your chance of victory and with more slots that you can unlock later.There is bossfights in this game so your maiden gives you 200 orbs to spend on units and 3 free health potions to use on yourself or your units, not every bossfight is the same so consider your unit choice and loadout.The difficulty is pretty challenging since you have to adjust to the situation whenever you see an annoying enemy type and there will be times that you can't fight as your character so unit composition and position is highly important in this game.The story is told through one cutscene and the rest are told by gestures during other cutscenes so there is very little voice acting in this game which can be a deal breaker to some people if they expect the entire story being told through voice acting. There is also lore you can collect about the enemies, the Villagers and the world itself.That is my review and if you are on the fence on buying this game try the demo, it has 4 levels with 3 being the tutorial levels while the last one gives you the taste of the gameOne thing to note at the time of writing this review there is a bug that crashes your game but it can resolved by lowering the Tree detail setting to 120%

_childDocuments_.review: I strongly recommend Kunitsu-Gami: Path of the Goddess. It was a delight to play from start to finish. The lovingly rendered sweets, ukiyo-e art, props, clothes and models give a beautiful coat of paint to an amazingly designed and incredibly refreshing game.Kunitsu-Gami's gameplay is somewhat similar to Pikmin, Brutal Legend and Orcs Must Die, in what must now be a burgeoning "Dandori" genre. You assign job/classes to villagers that you save during the day so that at night, they may protect a Priestess in an "Escort the Payload" format. You yourself are a cool samurai type and can order them to different positions on the map to engage enemies tactically. This could have easily gone south, but the levels are incredibly well-balanced to challenge your tactical skills and on-the-fly decision making without making it feel too overwhelming to new players. There are even level gimmicks that keep the formula fresh, never detract from the experience (yes, even the swamp level), and that impressively get expanded upon with new ideas to mix up the pace. There is also a day/night cycle that gives you room to explore, familiarize, prepare and plan around the stage for when the fight begins at night, adding an excellent gameplay loop that services the meat and potatoes combat. Oh, and despite not having voice acting for almost all cutscenes, it was able to tell a compelling and moving story nonetheless.I love Kunitsu-Gami. I love how tightly the levels are designed, I love how pretty the game is. I love how refreshing everything feels. I strongly recommend Kunitsu-Gami. A worthy GOTY 2024 contender. There's a barefoot maiden and a swamp level so I know some of you Miyazaki fans will love this game for sure.

_childDocuments_.review: [Original review based on ~25 hours of playtime, final edited review based on ~50 hours playtime. Completed all stages and side-objectives for both the first cycle and New Game+ w/ 100% achievements]In a year with Unicorn Overlord, Shadow of the Erdtree, FF14 Dawntrail, Granblue Fantasy Relink, Hades II, P3 Reload, FF7 Rebirth, Like A Dragon Infinite Wealth, SMTV Vengeance, etc etc etc (all of them excellent)….never in a million years did I expect a strange little tower-defense action game to come along and take ALL my spare time and attention.I won’t go into gameplay details as a demo is available and other reviews have already touched on a lot, but the overall experience is phenomenal: music, art design, progression and upgrades, difficulty, amount of content, gameplay, direction, story and writing, thoughtfulness w/ controls, UI, and graphics options - all *excellent*. It has a really unique vibe that teeters back and forth between being cool, silly, horrifying, zen, super intense, and very sweet / genuine…as a whole I don’t think I’ve ever played anything else quite like it. Hands-down the most creative thing I’ve seen come out of Capcom since Ōkami.It’s not an insanely difficult strategy title, but I would never call it easy or mindless. Level to level I’ve been constantly kept on my toes while adapting to new situations and enemy types, there’s an awesome amount of variety in how the stages “work”, what units you need to prioritize, and some seriously great boss battles and set pieces. Everything hits just right.Being a brand new property in a VERY niche style and genre, I do wish Capcom had actually promoted this + priced it at $40 to appeal to more people, but personally I couldn’t be happier with my purchase. I’ve seen a lot of comments such as “it’s like a PS2 8/10 game”, but I think that’s severely underselling it - whereas “things like this don’t get made anymore” feels scarily spot-on. Even if it’s outside of the usual type of game you enjoy, please try the demo and consider supporting Kunitsu-Gami. It’s beyond worth it and I’d love to see more companies take chances on non-AAA games.--------------------Final edit and note post New Game+ / 100% achievements = sad to shelf this game for now, but extremely satisfied with my time spent. All my original thoughts held through till the very end, I couldn't put it down until I had done everything. New Game+ makes every stage handle a little differently, enemy types are changed up and there's a lot more coming your way with each wave. It's a blast to play around with the more upgraded units and see how your own strategy has improved since the first run. Each stage also gets two new side objectives to complete, and certain ones definitely make you step up your game / can take a few attempts + some patience to get through. Finally, there is one extra "super boss" at the very end to really test your skills, and it's a great trial to wrap everything up with.--------------------Kunitsu-Gami gets my highest recommendation. It’s weird and truly wonderful, I’m overjoyed it exists, and will be shoving it in the faces of friends / plugging it every chance I get in online comment sections for years to come. I hope you enjoy it!

_childDocuments_.review: Unique, captivating, and satisfyingly fun, Kunitsu-Gami defies categorization. This is a shining example of a triple-A producer empowering a team of talented, creative people to takes risks in pursuit of an artistic vision. This game was lovingly crafted, and it shows. The gameplay is a mix of elements that, on their own, could make for a repetitive or even boring experience, but when combined create a feedback loop that kept me saying "one more..." The pacing is excellent, as each level builds on previous levels with new enemies, abilities, and strategic considerations. What starts out feeling almost too easy quickly becomes challenging and deeply engaging.The beautiful, artistic representations of feudal Japanese costumes, settings, choreography, and martial arts is a spectacle; a jubilant celebration of Japanese culture and folklore. There are so many fine details to enjoy uncovering. Every aspect of the interface has something decorative to appreciate, to the point that it's almost overwhelming at first. The enemy design is some of the most imaginative I've ever seen - bizarre, grotesque, colorful and stylish, anything but derivative or rote, and that alone is refreshing and genuinely entertaining.Its fun factor and high degree of replayability make this game worth the price of admission, but it's the incredible attention to detail, the visionary artistic sensibility, and the willingness to try weird new ideas that make it truly special. I hope more people discover and enjoy this game, and I hope that other publishers take note and follow suit. Kunitsu-Gami is a reminder that great games start with fun and unique experiences, not cosmetic skins and monetization loops disguised as gameplay.
