_childDocuments_.review: My expectations were already high for this game from the trailers. Somehow they managed to surpass those expectations. A solid remaster of an already great game, and an excellent new second campaign that ended up being one of the most enjoyable experiences I've had in my 20+ years of playing Sonic games.For the Sonic Generations remaster, it's... Sonic Generations again. There's a couple changes here and there (most notably the rewritten and redubbed cutscenes), but for the most part, it's the same game it was 13 years ago. Whether or not that's a good thing is up to you, and it certainly makes it hard to justify buying again if you already own the original, but after how disastrous Sonic Colors Ultimate was, re-releasing the same game might've been the safer bet. For what it's worth, outside of having to manually set VSync through my graphics driver instead of in-game to fix some stuttering and load time issues (please fix the in-game frame limiter ASAP), it's a solid version of the game that even managed to fix some long-standing bugs with the original PC port. Though, again, a $50 price tag with the new-found addition of Sega's long-time favorite Denuvo would be hard to justify for owners of the original port. Let's be honest, though... you're not buying this for the Sonic half.You're buying this for Shadow Generations. And oh my... they delivered. They absolutely delivered here. This is one of the most well-designed, polished, finely-tuned and, most importantly, fun Sonic experiences I've ever had. Sonic Team clearly listened to all the feedback they received from Frontiers, and they acted on  of it. The visuals are easily the best of any Sonic game to date, and are exactly what I'd wanted from Sonic over the past decade, with beautiful environments, smooth animations and detailed facial expressions. The controls are far more responsive than any other boost title, lying between Generations fast-paced boost controls and Frontiers' more responsive turning, along with help from newly-added 120fps support (a first for any new 3D Sonic game). The level design is on par with (and possibly even exceeding) Sonic Generations, with plenty of alternate routes that interact brilliantly with the new Doom Powers you unlock throughout the game. The new 3D White Space is an excellent addition that polishes a lot of the rougher aspects from Frontiers' open-zone exploration while keeping so many of the aspects that made that game fun. Bosses are some of the best in any 3D Sonic game and are a blast to both experience and master. The story, arguably the weakest aspect of the original Sonic Generations, is also one of the series' strongest and finally remembers why people love Shadow as a character to begin with. There's also a good amount of content after completing the main story, with new challenges to unlock, harder variants on the main bosses, and collectibles aplenty to find and unlock for the Collection Room. Even though it's a relatively short experience like its Sonic counterpart, every second of it was an absolute blast.If you already own the original Sonic Generations, I'd recommend waiting for a sale (which shouldn't be long, given previous releases). But if not, I'd say go ahead and jump in. This is a perfect place to start if you're new to the franchise, and long-time fans should be very pleased with the new content. Keep up the momentum, Sonic Team, and whatever you do...  abandon this formula. Like Frontiers, you're finally on the right track again. Just keep building on what you have.

_childDocuments_.review: Overall, I'd say this is a really great package. A legendary mix of a solid port, and a solid new experience. More specifics:The main new meat of this package... and oh boy is it something.Story-wise.. As someone who's a fan of the more heartfelt action and drama of the tone more commonly in 2000s Sonic games... This was refreshing. I don't think it really overdoes itself either. If you consider yourself invested in Shadow, I'd say they did him justice.Game-wise... Oh man we are so back. It's nice to have more Unleashed & Sonic Generations style stage design again... after the kinds of stage design I felt we were stuck with in Lost World, Forces, and the cyberspace stages in Frontiers (as much as I do like Frontiers)... It's a breath of fresh air. Whatever team they have working on this one... . Nothing's too short and underwhelming, or overly buggy, or anything. It's just right imo. Also, gotta say, I think they picked some real interesting stages and bosses to rep.That being said, don't let me overhype you. This is all just my opinion, and Shadow Generations is not some revolutionary package. Nor is it that long. It's maybe about as long as the other half of this package, if not a bit shorter. However, if this were sold on its own, and you really like Sonic games, I'd say this is easily worth $20, maybe even $30!Between Shadow Generations, and the things I like about Frontiers, this definitely feels like a new, brighter age for the franchise. I'm hoping they can keep it coming.However, if I had to have some asks, I'd like to see these quality of life adjustments going forward:Admittedly, Sonic Generations hasn't changed too much. If you already have the original, and you're hinging on this to have some big change ups to make full price worth it... lol, noThat being said, there ARE improvements (and some downsides). Here's a quick summary:A lot of the dialogue was rewritten, and re-recorded. Additionally, there's new flourishes to various cutscenes. This doesn't dramatically change the game. Most of it offers additional fan service or adjusted context. Personally, I thought most new lines were sidegrades, with a couple being worse, and some being a bit preferred.Additionally, this version is  still compatible with mods for the old version... It's just a matter of fans getting a new mod loader working.Also, bindings are adjusted by default. ie, boosting is now on one of the triggers, like Shadow Generations and Sonic Frontiers.By the way, if you were hoping for a next-next-gen upgrade of the visuals for 9th gen, don't expect it. It seems to still have the same 7th gen visuals it did more or less. Looking closely in some spots, things are still fairly low poly, or blurry. THAT BEING SAID, I do not see this is as a downside. This wasn't something I needed, and I believe that Sonic Generations still holds up  thanks to its strong and detailed art direction. Updating the visuals risks bloating the file size even more, and also risks slightly losing the art style's integrity.There are some performance snags, likely thanks to the Denuvo DRMSonic Generations is personally one of my favorite games in the series, and I highly recommend picking this up if you haven't played it before. However, to folks that have run the course before... yeah, it's still the same old Generations at its heart... It doesn't really do anything to change what I see as personal negatives, such as a kind of nothing-burger story, or an underwhelming final boss. I'm just glad this didn't turn out like Sonic Origins, or, worse yet, Sonic Adventure DX and Sonic Colors Ultimate.

_childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing, I've completed Shadow Generations, and have passed the first major boss of Sonic Generations.Mechanically, both games are good. Sonic Generations plays the way it did in the original release in the PS3 era, includes the Casino Night DLC, and has an extra collectable element: There are now lost Chao in each stage, three of them per act. Not sure what they give you.Shadow Generations is short but sweet. It brings back two stages from SA2 that Generations skipped over, A stage from Sonic heroes, A stage from Sonic 06, and two stages from adventures that happen after Generations in the timeline. Shadow gets a suite of new powers that fit gameplay rather well, and has a double jump Sonic doesn't have right out the gate. Strangely enough, his Act 2s are in the Classic Sonic style, though there is no real reasoning for this besides "It's more Sonic Generations."As I've said. Mechanically the game is sound, and what one should have come to expect from modern Sonic games.I'll stop beating around the bush, and address the big problem: Changed dialogue and censorship.I don't care about "changing things to fit a modern audience", as long as the writing is good. The problem is where this writing has actively taken away from the personalities of the characters I've come to love since I was a child. Knuckles was always a hothead who would take jabs at Sonic when he had the chance, while still being one of the Hedgehog's fiercest allies. Amy would never pass up a chance to steal a cuddle with Sonic, much to the Blue Blur's dismay. But even besides that, some of the dialogue just doesn't hit the way it used to. I won't spoil, but the character writing has been changed across the board. I expected some small changes, as Shadow isn't just standing around waiting to challenge you anymore, and is off doing his own thing. I expected some writing changes to reflect that. The story hasn't changed. All the same beats are hit, and everything plays out the way it did originally. What has changed is how characters bring up plot points and talk about what's happening in Generation's few cutscenes, as well as when you talk to them within the White Space.Overall, if you wanted Sonic Generations having a modern release for current hardware, and having a few hours more of it in the form of Shadow Generations, This release will have you covered. I suggest, however, if you played the original, that you skip the cutscenes in Sonic Generations this time around. The original version had better writing.

_childDocuments_.review: I will not lie, I just played base Sonic Generations literally just a few months ago so I didn't really care about the Sonic Generations part of this game. You know why I am here, I know why you are here, it's for Shadow Generations. Its peak, genuinely the best Sonic game I've ever played. When the only complaint I have is that I wish it was longer, than you know you've made an amazing game. I've been critical of Sonic, especially recently. Frontiers was an okay game with amazing concepts but with an lacklustre execution. Shadow Generations is what Sonic Frontiers tried to be. An open zone hub that contains boost-gameplay levels in self contain "Cyber-spaces"/Zones. Except this time, both of these aspects were handled perfectly.The White Space is a really good showcase for an more open level design in Sonic. Having tons of collectables and allowing the player to just relax and have a small break between the constant high energy that the zones have. It teaches the player how to use the new mechanics really well and is a good establishment to the game's story.The Zones are what steal the show though, being in my personal opinion, the best boost levels ever in a Sonic game. I've seen some complaints with Shadow's jump losing momentum and his base speed being overall slower than Sonic Gens. But I actually think this is to a benefit to the level design. As you are more capable of making smaller turns & are encouraged to experiment more with interacting with the levels. Boosting in Sonic felt like a clutch, something that was just too convenient to use and discouraged slower platforming and broke the pacing of the game. In Shadow Gens, boosting is now an reward, as you can not keep spamming boost otherwise you will run out of it REALLY quickly. You're encouraged to use it in certain areas, time it and to save the boost to get past tough obstacles. Shadow Gens feels like the perfect blend of formulas of the Sonic Adventure and Boost gameplay, and I dearly hope we can see this effect future Sonic Games going forward.

_childDocuments_.review: First of all, I want to tell everyone that this game is pretty much a remaster of the Original Sonic Generations. The game is like a two game in 1 type of deal. You cannot get Shadow Generations on its own. The game is very fun and talks about the Origin of Shadow the Hedgehog in addition to all the events going on in the Original Sonic Generations. (Along the way, you understand the "Shadow vs Sonic" Rival battle in "Sonic Generations" with some cut-scenes vs replaying that from Shadow's Point of View. )Shadow Generations is short. You can beat the game in under 10 hours without getting all the collectibles. The Power ups for Shadow are really cool, but the "Doom Wing" is very difficult to control. Also take note while using a PC controller such as an XBOX one, the controls can be a bit taking time to get used to.  I really enjoyed the campaign for Shadow as the game does highlight some of Shadow's Origin points and has a good story-line. The game is really fun and you immediately start with Space Colony Ark, -- Really is just a remaster of Final Chase with some new redesign. Radical Highway is also from SA2 also has a remaster/edited version where the level has Shadow flying and nothing really like the same as the "Original" SA2 level. Music is also remixed and fun to enjoy as well. I do recommend this game to others despite the controls getting some used to. I also want to make note that the tutorials are helpful, but on two of them it took several tries to get it right to move on if your hands are small such as mine. I was able to play this due to the Pre-order Digital Deluxe edition.  You also understand Gerald's and Maria's POV as well in Shadow Generations. The game is really fun and I do recommend this to others despite the controls being difficult at times, the power ups are cool and the last one is hard to control and takes time to get used to as it depletes your rings just like Shadow turning into Super Shadow in the end of SA2.(SA2 - Sonic Adventure 2/SA2-B is Sonic Adventure 2: Battle) The game does play positive tribute to previous games of Shadow. Especially with the level selection for this campaign. Very much a positive experience for me and I do consider replaying this to get 100% completion some other day, but overall I recommend it. If you're a new player to the franchise, this will not disappoint. If you are a returning player, Shadow Generations has the same appeal as Sonic Gens with the whole 2D/3D shift on levels. If you want to play older games to get an understanding of levels between the two, you'd have to play Sonic 1-SA2 and then Sonic (2006), Shadow the Hedgehog to understand the Black Arms, and other games.)  But, you don't have to play those in any particular order to get the gist of Shadow Generations. The only thing I'd change in Shadow's campaign was to make the game side longer in some way. But, overall I'm happy I got to enjoy this thanks to the Steam Digital Deluxe pre-order on my part, and I hope everyone else enjoy's Shadow's Origin like I do.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, I was questioning whether I should purchase this game(these games?) or not. The package consists of Shadow Generations, an eye-catching game that's perhaps the most excellent Sonic-related project we've seen come out of SEGA for years with a unique and refreshing take on the franchise and the"remaster" of beloved game Sonic Generations, a game that most Sonic fans still remain playing to this date, with some questionable choices made (which I'll get to later). However, for now I want to start on a positive note with Shadow Generations.SHADOW GENERATIONS:The memory of how awe I was in when the announcement trailer came out for this spectacle remains engraved in my brain, and I'd like to say that this game maintained that initial excitement and "hype" that I had from that day consistently. The story is very well-written by Ian Flynn (and did not lack the most essential part to any Ian Flynn story -> the references), and although the story felt a bit rushed in some aspects of the game (mostly towards the end), I observed the character arc for Shadow was satisfying, and made the protagonist feel... fulfilled. Shadow was finally able to abandon the shadow of his past (see what I did there?) and one of his most desired wishes, to get a second chance with Maria, was granted to him in beautifully written interactions between the two. It was certainly enjoyable watching Shadow getting rid of Black Doom for once and for all (hopefully), and I cannot await what future is in mind for him. Now, time for me to move on to the gameplay. Firstly, it was absolutely astonishing seeing all abilities from previous games with Shadow returning into this one. 'Chaos Control', 'Chaos Spear', 'Chaos Attack' (in the form of Doom Blast) with the other three abilities, 'Doom Wing', 'Doom Surf', and 'Doom Morph' (my least-favorite) were implemented excellently into the game, with each move-set being utilized in literally every corner of it(although some of it was pretty inconsistent), and it took away what has been the main focus of most Sonic games of the boost-era, boost through the enemies and get to the goal. Secondly, the 'White Space Hub World' that drew its origins from critically-acclaimed game Sonic Frontiers, was mostly tedious. Although I did enjoy the freedom of movement I gained while moving through the space, getting the collectibles was a monotonous and at times - nerve-wracking, and the lack of an interactive map made it even worse. However, I 100% all of them through the means of various online YouTube guides, and if you're dedicated enough, I'm sure you can too. Lastly, the details in this game were finely-tuned and most of the kinks were all ironed out. For example, once 'Chaos Control' activates, everything slows down, the enemies, the projectiles they may hurl at you, the music, and even the chaos spears, and if you attempt to 'Doom Blast' the hideous bead-eyed 'Black Arms' enemies, or let the eagles kidnap you to a different location in Kingdom Valley, the power-up simply deactivates. In conclusion, Shadow Generations was a well thought-out and executed game which crowns it as perhaps the best Sonic game of all time (under SA2 and others, of course), and I wish good luck to all of Sonic Team's future endeavors. SONIC GENERATIONS:The beloved game full of nostalgia released for Sonic's 25th Anniversary has been "remastered". Now, there isn't much to say about the original game that hasn't been said. Although the story's game was horrendous and full of plot holes, I can agree that the game provided a delightful experience to us Sonic fans by taking trips down memory lane with places from all of Sonic's history present throughout the entire game and giving us a new yet recognizable playable option - Classic Sonic. Although there was a scarce number of 18 Acts, the Challenge Acts, the bosses, and the rival fights filled in the gaps. Nevertheless, I want to focus mainly on what the remaster changed (which it really didn't). Firstly, the new "Chao Rescue" system implemented in every level of the game gave players of the original game an incentive to go back and replay these levels, and what did we get from unnecessary collecting all of the 54 Chao through extra hours of gameplay? Nothing. No new soundtracks, artwork, or other collectibles. Secondly, SEGA seemed to have realized that the story of the original game lacked any definite narrative, so who do they get to do the job? Ian Flynn. Now, I have nothing against this man, and some of the re-writes were somewhat tolerable this time around, but some were... inexplicable. For example, when Classic Sonic rescues Knuckles from his slumber, instead of Knuckles asking if Sonic got fatter, he asks, "Where's the rest of my island," then Sonic looks down at his stomach as if he regrets eating the island but is yet hungry for more. However, the blame for this should be pointed towards Sonic Team for not re-animating some of the cutscenes to get the characters' mouth to sync and to fix random expressions of some of the characters with some of the new dialogue. I believe the rest of the game's flaws are self-explanatory (such as the fact the "remaster" has some bugs from Version 1.0 of the original Generations) and don't need to be included in my lengthy and tiring review. Overall, the game was solid.Rating of Sonic Gens: 8/10Rating of Sonic Gens "Remaster": 7.5/10Rating of Shadow Gens: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has 100% both games I'll try to make this relatively quick and concise:SONIC GENERATIONS This is the fan favorite game people know and love from way back when for the most part. As far as additions go, there are the chao hidden in each level which are a fantastic way to further expand replayability (arguably this game's strongest aspect), and the drop dash which... Is a bit of a hit or miss. Don't get me wrong it works great for classic sonic but for modern I found it to be a bit of a nuisance since he wasn't exactly designed with it in mind. Although that might just be due to my old habits from the original version. Either way it's certainly not a deal breaker.The most major difference in this version is the rewriting of the cutscenes which I personally liked but some people admittedly found the writing dissatisfying. With that said, this game is definitely worth the hype gameplay wise, especially if you didn't get to experience it before... And it's not even the main attraction!SHADOW GENERATIONSI really don't have much to say, this is honestly the best sonic game we've ever gotten. The boost format has finally reached it's absolute peak with fast paced, creative level design allowing for a plethora of different routes and skips on both 2d and 3d levels. The new doom mechanics have all been excellent additions to spice things up (yes even the doom morph, it's harder to learn than the rest but mastering it feels extremely rewarding).Even the missions felt amazing to blast through in this one which is a definite plus considering almost all of them are necessary for story completion.Additionally, the open hub world and it's hidden collectibles add some very much appreciated replayability as well as a playground for the players to mess around with, essentially serving as a mini sonic frontiers.Lastly, the story while not exactly genre definiting did what it had to do and more in a spectacular fashion bringing back much needed depth to characters that were stripped of it for over a decade.This package is undoubtedly worth it's surprisingly lower than standard price tag, even more so  if you engage with the post game content.Really the only complaint I have about this game is that it ends and I really hope sega can release some more level packs for both generations games further down the line.

_childDocuments_.review: Ok so i have beaten the shadow generations story and have done 100% the shadow generations story. I will be giving my review on that part first. If you don't want spoilers, PLEASE DON'T READ AHEAD! ONLY WARNING I'M GOING TO GIVE.----------------------------------------------------------------Shadow generations i found was quite a joy to play through and was such a refreshing play style. it takes the old formula of generations and gives it a fresh coat of paint with new abilities. First we will be talking about the basic move set for shadow within the game.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------- -His boost feels fast from time to time but can slow down in some sections. -His chaos spear in a boost game really changes how you approach some enemies instead of homing attacking which keeps the player alert instead of blindly homing attacking. -Chaos snap (Homing attack) feels a little on the slow side but benefits the player due to vanishing through objects that can hurt you-Sidestep feels very bad and does not always allow the player to move out of a single lane but does the job by double pressing. New Abilities----------------- -Doom Spears: These are upgraded chaos spears and allow you to lock onto more then a single enemy to cause a stun and is needed for boss fights, overall you will be using this ability a lot when dealing with multiple enemies or targets like balloons. -Doom Blast: Doom blast is for when the game offers split pathways only or to deal with large numbers of enemies. This will be mainly used in 1 boss fight and the rest is for the split pathways. -Doom Surf this is for riding anything with water and is huge main mechanic. Unfortunately this is where things start to take a turn as this ability is super hard to control and is very difficult to use due to having bad controls. -Doom Morph: This allows shadow to climb walls and use his body to swing of objects. This ability however is even worse then the Doom Surf and is even harder to control because of bad physics and camera angles.-Doom Wings: This ability is the best one out of the bunch as it allows shadow to fly, grants small durability buffs from being hit and refills the boost gauge entirely, but this power uses rings to stay active. Ratings on shadows Move set - I personally think this move set creativity is a 9/10 but due to Doom Surf and Doom Morph play ability, I'm going to have to rate the Move set a 7/10 --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Graphics: the graphics of shadow generations is great and i feel the Cutscenes were done even better then frontiers! Maria and Gerald had a complete redesign and they look even better then their Sonic Adventure 2 counterparts. for shadow however, he lacks animations needed to make him feel fast like Sonic Adventure 2 which is a huge important thing when it comes to speedy characters. his speed build up animations o his boost animation just don't look all great and his spinball animation is reused from other sonic games like forces and frontiers. For the graphics im going to give it a 10/10 and for the animations im going to say 6.5/10  Level design: The levels are suppose to take inspiration from shadows past adventures, and honestly they do this very well. the design in the level to indicate the easter eggs and the size of the levels are amazing. The music to the levels have been completely redone and sound even better then the originals. When i sat and played the levels i really got a boost from how exciting the levels can be. I would rate the level design a 10/10 and wish to see more like this in the future. Open zone: To me, the open zone feels very empty with it being a white void and it doesn't feel full like when you are within a level. the white background looks very bland and dull so for this I'm giving it a 4/10. To make open world/zone everything has to have colour and needs to be interesting to look at for the player to play more. and to me, everything within that open zone looks identical and the same.Story: the story i think was very good for shadow, it helps him move on from his past and to say his goodbye to his loved ones which i feel wraps up his backstory very well. Shadow can now live on in piece and become something new with what he experienced. We also have a reason behind his name, we also have some deep end lore about shadows journey as well. I'm giving this story a 9.5/10.Overall rating for Shadow Generations: I have played every sonic game ever made and this one really hits differently when you play it. the gameplay is a good difference, the story is correct, so many easter eggs and i think that leaves me with a solid 9/10.----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Sonic generations i have played around 1/3 of it and i have some very bad thoughts on this remaster unfortunately. First of all,  the games advertisement says that they remastered generations to be ported to console. Now i assumed for PC players we would be able to configure our graphics, FPS etc. But to start, the upscale does not really make much of a difference other then using a basic sharpness option in most modern games which it does a very poor job of. Second of all the generations "remaster" can only go up to 60 FPS unlike Shadow generations which can achieve 120 FPS. Now you may ask why this might be such a problem? well because of the latest specs of PC gaming we now have up to 120HZ monitors with 1440p graphics cards. when you play a game like sonic generations that goes to 60 FPS and has motion blur with a sharpness effect, it really ruins the image quality in-game.The game also has a slight Imput delay due to running at 60 FPS which can cause problems later down the line. Third of all is the cut scenes in this "remaster". the cut scenes have been up scaled and some have slightly changed. However, the lip sync with the new voice acting does not line up at ALL. the cut scenes only run at locked 30 FPS. and the dialog has been changed for the worse and some voice actors have been replaced (E.g. rouge's entire voice actor, tails pitch in the voice etc). Lines from the original have been removed and some of the lore in generations has been changed from the original to accommodate the new Shadow Generations. some changes are good in favour of the Shadow Generations, however character lines that have been removed have changed entire personalities and ruins the aspect of that character, -My Review for Sonic generations "remaster" - Honestly, if you have the original, go play that version instead. and if you cant do that, wait until modding comes out to fix up the original generations correctly as this "remaster" in my opinion is even worse then colours. the graphics are not remade at all, the fps over is bad as it drops frequently, the quality of the game when moving fast is bad, the input delay is bad, the story is now even worse, some cutscenes have only been upgraded in quality and its not great. Overall review on Sonic x Shadow generations: i would only buy this game for the shadow generations and only if its on discount by 20% at least. but the overall bundle of both games packed into one for 25 bucks each is around 7/10.

_childDocuments_.review: The best 3D Sonic game do far. Somehow they took a great Sonic game from a little over a decade ago, touched it up nicely, then gave us a brand new second half with the most exhilarating level design I think this series has ever had even when comparing it to Sonic Unleashed & Sonic Adventure 2.Sonic Generations scores a solid 8.5 with me. The physics & controls have been touched up a bit from the original version and the dialogue has been completely rewritten, not only to better connect it to Shadow's half, but to flesh it out better in general. Shadows, textures, framerate & rendering in general is superb even on Steam Deck.Shadow Generations scores a perfect 10 with me for taking the very best of Sonic & flipping it on it's head not only with levels as hard as they are exciting, but with new powers & remixed bosses that have been overhauled incredibly well. You'll find a fantastic blend of speed & even a good amount of combat that feels somewhat inspired by other great SEGA games like Bayonetta. Shadow's story has also been brought back into focus and is properly expanded upon for the first time in many years which was a real treat as a long time fan, wrapping up with perhaps the most bittersweet yet satisfying ending of the whole series so far.The music is the best it's ever been, you'll hear plenty of iconic music from various levels throughout the series history either remixed quite nicely or presented in their original mixes as unlockables. Regardless of if you're new to the series, returning to it after many years or if you've been a consistent fan since you started, there's plenty to love about this game. Sonic X Shadow Generations is the best value for a 3D Sonic game and deserves a spot up there with the greats like Sonic Mania Plus, Sonic The Hedgehog 2 & the Sonic Adventure series.

_childDocuments_.review: This is SonicTeam's best work in a decade and a half. Some of the most solid level design, interesting setpieces, a fun hub, and most clever mechanics we've seen from Sonic, all rolled into an admittedly short package. This is just the Shadow half I'm talking about, of course, but Sonic Generations has been talked to death and feels almost entirely unchanged here so if it's your kind of thing, you already know it. I'd love to see this kind of character-focused side story stuff going forward, or short of that, these more bite-sized, $30 games instead of full-priced bloated packages, as fun as Frontiers was to play the first time. Replayability has always been Sonic's greatest strength, and the stages in Shadow Generations are as replayable as they come (for the most part) given the time-dominant scoring system.If I could throw out a hope for the future, I'd be willing to pay for more stages as dlc, and I feel like there's a relevant game left unrepresented here that could offer a lot of fun to a game with some of the greatest potential in the franchise as-is. Frankly even just two more zones would have felt more like a complete package at launch. Mad Matrix and Black Comet, maybe?

_childDocuments_.review: Two years ago, Sonic Frontiers launches and marks the return of 3D Sonic with a flawed but fun experience that had a lot of potential. Fast forward 2 years later, and we now have the release of Sonic X Shadow Generations, a bundle of a brand new game (Shadow Generations) and the remaster of Sonic Generations which originally released in 2011. Let's start with Sonic Generations. For starters, the game is MOSTLY untouched. However, some of the game's cutscenes have been redubbed and  rewritten to fit modern Sonic continuity. This change didn't bother me though, as Generations never had much of a story to begin with. The controls have also been updated and feel a lot smoother, which did take some time getting used to. Other than that, it's Sonic Generations.Now the real meat of this bundle: Shadow Generations.Holy ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥, this game may be one of the best 3D Sonic's ever, up there with SA1/SA2/Unleashed and the original Generations. The level design is excellent for starters. Sonic Team went for quality over quantity with the 3D stages here and they are very fun to replay. The open zone (White Space) is also excellent. You can tell Sonic Team looked at all the criticism of Sonic Frontiers's open zone level design and fixed those issues. White Space level design feels baked in with the environment and feels very organic and not out of place and there is little to no pop-in either.The Doom Powers also feel very fun to use in the open zone and in the levels as well. My favorite Doom Power would probably be the Doom Wings, as they add lots of repeatability to the stages (there are separate times on the leaderboards with and without the Doom Wings).The story in this game is also great. Ian Flynn's writing has improved greatly from his writing in Sonic Frontiers and the ending of the game brought a tear to my eye; it was fanastic and served as a great epilogue to Shadow's origin story; Xenoblade 3: Future Redeemed/P3 FES style. Cutscenes also have great animation as well.Sonic X Shadow Generations is a fantastic way to get into the Sonic series, and a wholeheartedly recommend it to newcomers or people wanting to get into 3D Sonic. Sonic Frontiers was a step in the right direction but this IS the right direction. Keep going Sonic Team and push forward as the Sonic series has still more untapped potential. Don't stop.10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is easily one of the best games in the franchise. Each stage has two acts, both of which are incredibly well-designed and full of insane challenges. I’m not usually a fan of 2D sections, but the 2.5D perspective in this game really helps with visibility, letting you see what’s ahead. Shadow's speed is perfectly balanced in these sections—you can boost without being punished harshly, while still needing to react quickly to shortcuts. Huge win in terms of gameplay design.The bosses? Absolutely insane. Each one is super cool, with unique mechanics that made every battle stand out. The way they incorporated the Doom abilities into each boss fight was next-level and kept things fresh, making each encounter feel distinct and thrilling.I completed every act challenge with an S rank, collecting every item along the way. The challenges are actually challenging, and finding all the collectibles is fun rather than a chore. Every stage offers different routes, with hidden paths leading to keys and collectibles, adding a lot of replayability.The abilities are handled perfectly, feeling essential in many stages and adding depth to the gameplay. The hub world also offers tons of content, and even after all this time, I’m still not done with it. The reappearance of several beloved characters, each with a great introduction and charming cutscenes, is a fantastic nostalgic touch.Overall, Shadow Generations delivers in every aspect. I can’t wait to see more games like this. Absolute banger, 10/10.

_childDocuments_.review: I've never felt more validated for being a Ride or Die for Shadow The Hedgehog (05) than after playing this.Shadow Generations builds on some of the gameplay ideas introduced in Frontiers & puts it into a more focused lens. With traditional 3D & 2.5D levels for Shadow, as well as introducing tons of new gameplay mechanics exclusive to him via his Doom powers. Sonic Team have clearly taken some of the lessons from Frontiers "Open Zone" format & applied it to the hub world. The hub world is not as large as the islands in Frontiers, however it is incredibly fun to traverse, as well as being much denser & filled with things to do & find. Shadow Generations has arguably some of the best gameplay & level design in the entire franchise. Along with a good story that helps flesh out & develop Shadow while getting first time fans up to speed on his story. Shadows characterisation & gameplay is literally the best it's ever been here & hopefully Sonic Team takes note of this for the future.This game is a love letter to Shadow fans. From the collectables that help build on the lore with Gerald, Maria, the ARK & the creation of Shadow. To the story that roots itself firmly in the history of Shadows Journey through SA2, Sonic Heroes, Shadow 05, Sonic 06 & even Sonic Forces. Everything that fans love about this character & his lore/story is here on full display proudly, & I couldn't be happier.Sonic Generations is mostly the same package with some minor upgrades here & there such as control options for classic or modern controls & a few visual tweaks. It also has the added collectable Chao in the main stages, which adds a nice extra layer of content, especially for completionists. Overall Sonic Generations is still the same great game it was back in 2011, with a couple of old issues here or there from the original release that stop it from being an all timer. Mainly the final boss that is arguably one of the worst in the series & is probably the only major negative for the game.Both of these games make a final product that is both a genuinely great starting point for newcomers to the series & a fresh experience for older fans with Shadow Generations. Which could honestly be one of the highest highs the franchise has seen in a while.Between Sonic Frontiers & now this game, I can't wait to see where Sonic Team goes next with the franchise. Especially for Shadow.

_childDocuments_.review: This truly is Shadow's game. As much as I would've liked an exclusively Shadow game with a longer playtime, I do seriously enjoy this game and it is a must-play for anyone who is a fan of the Sonic series. I'll split the review into two as there are technically two entire games here.[Shadow Generations]First and foremost it has fantastic level design which reminds me of Sonic Adventure 2's designs. Amazingly paced and I was always discovering more hidden routes to find the box keys and to improve my times. I can say with full confidence that I never lost interest in the game and have even 100%'d it because I enjoyed it that much. The game's Doom Sphere 'hard mode' is actually very enjoyable and I attribute that to it actually feeling challenging yet rewarding once you master the movement and the fun ways you can use Chaos Control. The hard mode also doesn't just add unfair obstacles to fake a higher difficulty which I've seen in previous Sonic games so that's always great to see. The stages, like Sonic Generations, are fairly easy to S-Rank but Shadow Generations adds a different layer of difficulty to them as you can choose to forgo access to the Doom Wings in the stages which, in stages that assume you have them, offers a fun challenge to try and S-Rank them using the paths that you would otherwise be flying over completely. The story for the game is fantastic and I love the lore drops in the collectibles. I will not spoil anything here but just know that Ian Flynn and Sonic Team absolutely put their best effort into making a genuinely enjoyable story for Shadow that fans of Sonic can appreciate to its fullest. The controls are extremely intuitive and there is a lot of response in how Shadow moves. He can stop fast, doesn't feel like he's on ice and sliding around, good acceleration, jumping preserves speed by default (iykyk), and lightly tapping my joystick doesn't send him into a wall. I love how aerial boosting feels like a sort of smaller jump that gives you speed. The movement feels very rewarding to learn and there is a lot of room for skill expression and stage knowledge in the game. Boosting also doesn't just feel like a win button because Shadow's stages have a lot of fast-paced platforming and feels like how any Sonic game should feel; fast, intuitive, rewarding to master, and cool. Honestly takes all the best parts of the improved Frontiers movement and none of the bad things! The soundtrack, as standard for Sonic games, is insanely good. Maybe it's nostalgia, maybe it's genuinely just THAT good but I cannot put into words the excitement I felt hearing tracks from Sonic Adventure 2 and Sonic '06 again as I'm going through stages at break-neck speeds. Having Chaos Control right out the gate is an amazing thing and I have always wanted to properly use it in a game (and now I can!) I love how Chaos Control is not merely used as a simple time-stop gimmick but actually allows for some alternative, and sometimes mandatory, faster routes. The challenge stages especially highlight this ultimate power's capabilities in both combat and platforming.TLDR;- Amazing level design- Fantastic story- Best a hedgehog has controlled in 3D- Soundtrack is ALWAYS a banger- CHAOS CONTROL !- Movie Shadow skin incoming :>[Sonic Generations]I can't really say too much more than people have said about it in the past. However, I will say that revisiting this AFTER playing Shadow Generations is a huge shock. You can physically feel the differences in the Hedgehog Engines and they're very annoying to deal with. I had to make my joystick less sensitive because I forgot how floaty Sonic felt and there is skill that takes up a slot on your skill loadout that makes stopping much faster no matter what speed you have and that makes it feel like how it should by default. Shadow definitely spoiled me with the movement and ability to finely control directions. I had also forgotten that, despite separating Sonic Generations into Modern (3D) and Classic Sonic (2D), that a fairly substantial portion of Modern Sonic's stages are also in 2D or 2.5D perspective; some parts allow for side-stepping, some are just 2D. It's very weird honestly and is kind of jarring especially because it can, in some cases, kill all momentum you were carrying over throughout the level which is mildly annoying. It feels like they plucked Modern Sonic and put him in Classic's stage for a moment. The stages are absolutely, insanely easy especially compared to even the easiest of stages from Shadow Generations. I was hoping we could get a slight change to score calculations in the remaster but it doesn't seem to be the case. I will say that I felt kind of baited from the promotional art and even the main menu art featuring the different Chao. I knew we weren't going to be getting a Chao Garden, I swear SEGA refuses to do anything like it anymore, but I was hoping for some sort of interactions at least rather than cameos in cutscenes and them being extra collectibles to a game I thought had enough of them between the music notes and red rings. The soundtrack is good though, same as the original but I wasn't expecting much of a change there.TLDR;- Game is basically the same as the original with slight alterations (mostly just weird obscure things that I think is weird to change)- Controls are a bit floaty sometimes, very obvious after playing Shadow Generations- Soundtrack is a banger, as always !- Extra Chao collectibles are a bit weird but I'm glad to see them again at all- Level design is weaker than Shadow Generations but the levels were made like 11 years ago- Drifting still feels as cool as it did when I was younger[Final Thoughts]Honestly, if you've played Sonic Generations before and done everything there in the past I would say you can probably just play Shadow Generations or revisit Sonic Generations for nostalgia reasons. Personally, I've played the game to death on both PC (though not 100%'d on PC, unlike my Xbox 360) and Xbox and, while I will still be playing through the rest of Sonic Generations, I don't think you're missing out on much if you decide not to (assuming you've played it before)(Obligatory "I received this product as a birthday gift")

_childDocuments_.review: For everyone who's a bit of a weirdo for going "UHHHGG THEY'RE CENSORING THE GAME HHNNNGG IAN FLYNN YOU BASTARDDDDD", Remember that the OG is still available to buy and play. You don't have to play this if you don't want to, stop being dorkasses.For the people who are actually paying attention, here's some cold hard facts for you. Sonic Generations is here in it's entirety. It's still one of the best games Sonic has had to date, and one or two line changes, one or two animation changes, and one or two vocal performance changes isn't going to change that. But it's not a remaster. You're getting a near identical version to the original that is now available in the Sonic Legacy Bundle for 20 bucks. It runs the same that it did in 2011, with exception to load times which are a touch rougher, and it comes with the Casino Night dlc on top of that without needing to buy the deluxe edition. It even comes with a new set of collectible Chao, which is at least SOMETHING to push you to to play through that game again, even if it simultaneously acts as a reason why you can't just port a save from the OG generations to this one. I see what you're doing SEGA, I'm a little cross by it.What you're ALSO getting here is Shadow Generations, a sort of "Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury" type of situation. The original game is there, but Shadow Generations is it's own fully fledged game here too, complete with the near identical level count as the original game, but with some super beautiful cutscenes, some lovely collectibles that're entirely or mostly Shadow focused, and some stellar levels based around returning stages from the 3DS version of Sonic Generations or completely new levels from games that came out after Generations did in 2011. With plenty of meat on that game's bones, it's certainly nice to play through if you're a ride or die Shadow the Hedgehog fan. Hell, there'll eventually be DLC coming out based around Sonic The Movie 3 which will make the stage count equal between both games in this compilation, so a nice bonus.All in all:- If you've never played Sonic Generations, firstly how, that game has been hyper cheap for a decade now, but secondly this is a pretty good pick up. 50 Bucks for two meaty games with a lot to collect and mess around with? Great deal.- If you *have* played Sonic Generations though, if you have it sitting in your steam library like I do, and even if you really like it, Your Mileage May Vary. I love it, it's satisfying, and knowing I bought it exclusively for the Shadow content I'm still comfortable with saying it's worth $50 for that experience. $60 considering I bought the deluxe edition and played it early. I love the game,  I'm gonna enjoy 100%ing it and getting all the achievements in both games.- If you're not a huge Shadow fan and don't see the point in picking it up, that's fine too. Leave it be. I completely understand why, it's a lot of money to drop on 2 games especially when one of those two games is wrapped in a nostalgic visage of "2011 Havoc Engine Quirks". But at least consider picking it up whenever it goes on sale. The Sonic side might be showing it's age a fair bit, but the Shadow side is a fresh, modern, squeaky clean experience that will give you the gift of Maria being murdered for sport again and again and again. Oh, and the actual game is pretty good too.

A very solid engine that hadn't crashed on me once, looks great, and ran exceptionally well with minimal graphical configuration on my part.(Also the Shadow Generations portion features probably the most gratutious and detailed butt-shots in all of Sonic games in one specific cutscene. _childDocuments_.review: Tl;dr: If you like Sonic gameplay both in 2D and 3D, play this. If you like Shadow the Hedgehog (the character), absolutely play this. It is a really good game, I swear. Once again, the Generations game is an absolute gem. (From Edit 3:) If the Sonic part one day stopped working for me, I would not even care if it meant Shadow Generations would still be playable. Shadow's side is just THAT MUCH FUN. I reiterate myself, ABSOLUTELY play this game if you like 3D and 2D Sonic & especially if you like Shadow. You will most likely not be disappointed.I love Shadow the Hedgehog, man. Biased review, because I bought the preorder deluxe lol, but I'll try my best.From the 110 minutes I played in Shadow's portion: S ranks are pretty manageable, or I am just way too good rn. 2D challenges are so-so, I would rather have more 3D ones. I suppose it's fine though. At least the ones I played were pretty short though, so no biggie there. Collectibles are usually easy to spot or require just a little bit of looking around, nothing too difficult. Story seems a bit fast paced, but I am also at the start, so I will hold off on giving that a proper rating. The intermission map is much better than what OG Sonic Generations had.I feel Sonic Frontiers controls are in place, might be wrong. That means that 2D is slower, with emphasis on remembering the layout and jumping (and using Shadow's abilites) well. 3D is pretty nice though, like really chill. Controls are easy to change though & there's an option to use legacy Sonic Generations control scheme.Graphics are very pretty, though nothing to put in a "RTX demo" kind of material. Game is actually really smooth on 60 FPS all the time, except the 30 FPS cutscenes, which I don't mind, but it is a little funny. Audio is also a banger.Collectibles have so far been a joy. Everything is beautiful.Issues: So far only had an audio bug which was fine after restarting my PC: Kinda weird, but didn't happen later.Edit: So, I finished Shadow Generations! It was amazing. Difficulty went up with more Doom Powers to use and yeah, S ranks aren't so easy after all. The ending boss too, so much spectacle, but not the easiest! Only real trouble was the Doom Morph power up - it felt a bit finnicky, though it did get its job done and is pretty cool otherwise.Story was Generations-esque - short, pretty fast-paced, repeated beats from older games, but it was sensible enough thanks to its simplicity - though the ending scene made me cry a little. It is very nice. Only bummer is that some CGs have this weird aspect ratio, so everything is just slightly stretched horizontally. Dunno why.The hub world is honestly absolutely amazing, holy hell, it's so good to roam in itPerformance was always absolutely fine.I am giving this a 9/10, maybe 8.5/10 if I had a bad mood, which I don't, because I got to play as Shadow again!Edit 3: Nah, I think the 9/10 is solid by now. Really fun game and movement with Shadow. Just a very very enjoyable experience.Sonic side is just Sonic Gens with minor changes, the rewritten dialogue I could honestly care less about, though it is unnecessary. And going from Shadow to Sonic made me realize this: I much prefer Shadow over Sonic in this game. Shadow's double jump is just preferrable, his Chaos Control is just awesome. Sonic goes faster, his gameplay is more about speed, while Shadow is about playing a stage gracefully, if that makes any sense. Sonic Gens is like an 8/10. Definitely felt worse after Shadow Gens, but that was to be expected, since the team has advanced their craft. Shadow's challenges are fewer, but don't feel too inflated, unlike what I felt in Sonic Gens (especially since you need to clear just one challenge there, while Shadow needs to clear two for one key).So, I won't be editing this anymore, but I'll say this: I'd buy the game just for the Shadow part only, it is THAT good. Sonic Gens remaster is the one who feels like a DLC to me. Sonic Team made an amazing game with Shadow Generations, they should keep it as one of the best they ever made.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is as delightful as it was when it first launched, this is just a minor remaster of the game but at least it runs great and looks fine. I still don't like this insistence on 60 frames being the limit for so many games, but there's likely engine limitations with Sonic Generations preventing it from achieving frames as gloriously fast as our favorite blue blur. If you have a high refresh rate monitor that is G-Sync or FreeSync compatible, make sure it is on and the game will look and feel just fine at 60, turn off v-sync of course.The addition of an entirely new campaign with Shadow is impressive and has much better PC options, it makes this a solid package. The Shadow campaign is next level in quality and fun. It makes me wonder why we can't just get more new Sonic games just like it.One of my favorite things about Sonic Generations is just how addictive and fun it is to try to perfect all the challenge missions. Then there's the tight controls and exquisite level design. The levels have brisk pacing and you can't go wrong with that. I was trying to figure out what was wrong with some other recent 3D Sonic games, like Sonic Colors, which I really disliked, and it was just floaty bad controls and bland level design that overstayed its welcome. Sonic is at its best when the levels are carefully crafted to reward speed, reaction time, and have great setpieces. The same for any 2D Sonic game, and the same for any 3D Sonic game.Sonic is back and letting us know that... hey, he did, can, and will have good games!

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is my new favorite Sonic game. Sonic Team has finally made a game that is, on every level, a step up from the best entries in the series. The game is polished and Shadow feels great to control, and I was surprised how much fun simply traversing the world is in this game. Every stage has amazing level design, there are so many pathways and shortcuts, and each is more challenging and complex than recent games' stages. It's the first true step up from Sonic Generations on those fronts. The game is visually stunning, with fluid animations, gorgeous lighting, quality reflections, and a cinematic flair. It's the first true step up from Unleashed in that regard. The open zone of the hub world, while relatively small in comparison to Frontiers' open zones, feels visually more in line with Sonic than its predecessor, and the platforming challenges in the zone are more interesting and feel less out of place, with objects like rails and platforms fitting the style of their environment rather than clashing with a more realistic environment as seen in Frontiers. The boost stages are also far longer and more complex than cyberspace stages were, with varying paths and shortcuts. Shadow Generations even manages to have a narrative that is more emotional and interesting than Frontiers', and that's saying something when Frontiers was the first game in a long time to take itself seriously and deliver a genuine narrative. It's a step up from Frontiers in these areas. I'm sure you can recognize a pattern here, but Shadow Generations doesn't just thrive by refining aspects of prior games, as it also succeeds in the new ideas it presents. Shadow's doom powers are intuitive and compliment the usual gameplay without overstaying their welcome or feeling forced. Each feels relatively easy to learn, and a couple of them are also a bit hard to master, rewarding players who take the time to learn these mechanics. None of these abilities feel as though they obstruct normal gameplay or as if they can be used to bypass everything. Each ability has strengths and weaknesses, and are most useful in specific moments rather than being overpowered cheat codes or useless padding. A skilled player will learn how to most effectively flow between these abilities and regular gameplay, and it feels incredibly rewarding. Shadow Generations is, without a doubt, my favorite Sonic game. I'm still in shock that Sonic Team has managed to, in one game, outdo their best work and deliver an incredibly polished, fun experience. Even if you've played Sonic Generations before, or if you don't care about it, I highly recommend this title for Shadow Generations alone. You'll be hard pressed to find a better deal than what Sega offers here, combining a remaster of one of the most beloved Sonic titles alongside a brand new masterpiece of a Shadow game. Bravo Sonic Team, you've reached a new peak.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though I've only played a small amount of the Sonic Generations included in this game, mainly because I've already completed the original, I can say that Shadow Generations of this game is really good. Without going into spoilers, the levels were fun to play, some of Shadow's new abilities were pretty neat, the bosses were pretty creative (especially the final boss), and the soundtrack was an absolute banger as always. And for those curious,  I gave both Sonic Generations and Shadow Generations a quick test on my Steam Deck and they both worked great. Though be aware for Sonic Generations, you can't use the D-Pad to control Classic Sonic in his stages, though this might change in a future patch.Really the only two things I dislike about Shadow Generations involves what you get when getting the digital deluxe. First off, the mini soundtrack you get doesn't include any of the new songs included in Shadow's campaign. There are some Shadow-related music featured, but not any of the new remixes. This is odd when you consider that Sonic Frontiers also had a mini soundtrack and that included some of the songs featured in the game (even if it wasn't all of them). It was pretty disappointing to not see anything new in this game's mini soundtrack, then again I might have missed something and if so, that's news to me.The second thing I didn't like that much was the Terios skin for Shadow. While the design itself is fine, what really threw me off was how equipping the skin doesn't change specific animations for Shadow. I'm primarily referring to his running and boosting animations and how weird they look when equipping the skin. Unlike Shadow where he wears roller skates, (no wait sorry "Air Shoes" as Shadow calls them), Terios' design doesn't have him wear anything that could justify him using Shadow's skating animations. This is definitely more of a personal preference, but I can dismiss stuff like this because it's just a cosmetic and doesn't change how the character controls... Also yea Terios' quills do look weird, but I don't mind them that much.Overall, this is a very solid game and if you didn't try the original Sonic Generations either, I'd say this is worth getting given that, at least to my knowledge, there are barely any differences between the original steam release and this version.

_childDocuments_.review: This game is honestly incredible, I fully recommend this game to anybody who liked the original generations, likes sonic frontiers, or is new to sonic, it will get you up to speed for the most part (the other games referenced are NOT required reading). My only gripe is the addition of the drop dash, specifically because you can only turn it off for classic sonic, while certain modern sonic stages really suffer from its inclusion.I am going to talk slightly spoilery now so if you dont want spoilers stop here and buy the gameI really love that they changed the dialogue in the remastered cutscenes, the story is actually coherent now, with a lot less plotholes (like tails not knowing what chemical plant is), they could have adjusted the animation a little to fit better but that is a minor nitpick (also they swapped out tail's "You always do" and Im sad). Also the Shadow generations add on is insanely good, he controls a lot like sonic does in frontiers but the level design really complements it, I also love that they have a level from every game shadow appears in (and frontiers), you even get to fight Mephiles, and since he was erased from the timeline, Shadow doesnt know who Mephiles is, at this point Im just gushing about how fanservicey this addition is but like, its a lot of fun, if you havent played and are still reading please, buy this game and experience it for yourself, it is even better than I thought it would be, and generations is my personal favourite sonic game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just finished this game and for the first time in a long time, it has left me feeling hopeful for Sonic games again!The love, effort and care that went into this game legit makes me so happy!I'll be mainly talking about Shadow Generations.The Sonic Generations half of the game is more or less the same, so i'll only talk about the changesSonic Generations=================+ The new dialog in my opinion is great! It feels a lot more natural compared to the original.+ The Chao collecting is a nice little addition and its nice to see them hanging around the stage gate when you beat it. And having hints to where they are is nice, especially since some are hidden inside stuff and could be seen as annoying.+ Classic Sonic having a Drop Dash is always a plus! sure it's not as OP as the Spin Dash, but i think it's a nice if you want a secondary way to get quick speed but not go too fast.- Modern Sonics Drop Dash, while cool, feels kinda clunky and doesn't feel that useful, especially since it only works after using an air dash, not on its own or even after a homing attack.- While i like the changes made to the writing, some voice lines i feel require a second take or better direction, as they don't always feel nice to listen to. Charmy and Cream especially don't really sound good to me at all. (No offense to the Actresses)- I'm not expecting big changes for Cutscenes, i just feel some scenes/shots could use some needed adjustments for the animation and timing to fit the new dialog, especially since they've shown they can do it.Shadow Generations==================+ The Story, The Voice Acting, The Animation. i LOVE it! The characters are written like actual characters in an actual story. It makes me happy that sonic is capable of this now.+ The level design is great! feels like a good mix between Boost Gameplay and Adventure Styled Platforming. idk if this was intentional, but it feels like i run out of boost more often, which i feel encourages me to not use it all the time and only use it when needed.- Stage Dialog Mixing: There's times where it's really hard to tell what characters are saying during bosses and stages, requiring to either have subtitles or change audio settings- Shadows second to last Upgrade; Overall Thoughts================There's probably more, but i'll probably come back and edit this later after i complete the game and once my thoughts settle in.For the Sonic Generations Side of things, i like it. For me, I don't think it'll replace the original game in terms of replayibility, but that'll depends on what mods the community comes up with.As for Shadow Generations. its the best thing to come out of sonic in years and i'm finally happy to see Sonic going in a better direction.I'll admit and say i haven't played Sonic Forces, so i can't say what i think of that game entirely. but even so, it felt like ever since then, it felt like sonic was focusing less on quality and fun and the writing was no longer interested with older fans in mind. (Possibly with Sega at fault.)I was fully convinced that if the next main game following Forces was the same thing gameplay and writing wise, i knew Sonic was never gonna get any better, to the point i was ready to quit any future modern sonic releases.Thank god this finally changed with Sonic Frontiers. It showed promise for better things, and Shadow Generations delivered. I'm hoping this marks the beginning of a better Sonic age.Keep on rocking Sonic Team, Please keep on improving.

_childDocuments_.review: Alright, I'm going to give you a fair review from a fan who abandoned the franchise for many many years.  I haven't played through all of the game yet, please keep that in mind.TL;DR:  It's a good game, shadow is king fight me, some graphics and performance gripes on Sonic's half, does not effect shadow's game-play.  Shadow bumps the score to...  Yes.  Yes it is.  You can feel the speed, the wins don't feel easy and feel earned.Alright I gotta say it.  I love how they are portraying Shadow in this game.  And even more-so, I love the game-play mechanics he has.  You can truly feel like the "ultimate life-form" when you play as him.  The music is banging, the level design is peak, the mechanics are awesome and responsive, and honestly it's so much more fun than the sonic side.  Which, honestly, is a little sad that they couldn't make all of the game-play as fun as that half. Yes.  It does.  For some reason, however, the Sonic half seems to have some frame loss (particularly at balloon challenges).  I do run a modern high-end PC, so this issue is from the game itself.    (I am running a basic Logitech F310 game controller).  The game mechanics are really good.  I do feel like for the first few levels I did feel some kind of lane locking (?) that appeared to go away after a few acts.  I could be wrong there.  Modern sonic specifically has some issues with the lock-on.  It can get really frustrating at times, but not horribly. Yes, most of the time it looks good.  In fact, during game-play it looks amazing.  I do have one mild gripe.  The textures on the models aren't that great.  I can see the pixels, and I was surprised that this was the quality for the "high" graphics setting.  But, you only notice this when you are in an up-close shot of a cut-scene.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is a HUGE surprise for me, I'm loving this game a lot more than I expected to and it's a really nice take on the Boost formula. I highly recommend buying this bundle for Shadow, forget the Sonic Generations Remaster.The remaster is barely different from its counterpart and the main selling point is the new dialogue, as the story has been partially rewritten to be less "cheesy". But it's now full of out of place references and HEAVILY flat and stilted voice acting. I have no clue why the voice acting quality is so low for the remaster, it feels as if they got a group of impressionists to record the lines so they could save the budget, because Roger's Sonic voice in particular sounds really off.Long story short, I still highly recommend buying this game for the Shadow side, and Sonic Generations is still a really good game so its a nice side piece. Shadow's comeback has been legendary so far.

_childDocuments_.review: i was expecting a bit more from this game than what we have at the moment (actual updated models, textures, visuals and such - mainly thinking something like HE2/Sonic Frontiers assets) but despite that, i really liked it in a way of revisiting the game slightly updated and bundled with what matters the most (Shadow Generations)sure that the changes on existing models and voice acting/dialog changes were unnecessary but outside of that revisiting the game was really fun, and the addition to a new game mode made exploration and treasure hunting a new nostalgia for the oldies of the franchisethe DLCs could have also been way better worked on since the skins dont include Super transformations, or cutscenes which is a bummer, yet its still a nice step for SEGA/Sonic Team to overlook those details and upgrade in their next titlewe all needed this game - its visuals, its difficulty, the little yet big details, the story/plot.. makes this game to good that i cant stop praising it. i personally was expecting it would be a lot more like HE1/Sonic Generations in terms of engine and controls, but it gave a better name to that with HE2 and its power. theres always a lot to do in this game that can make someone busy, specially if youre a thirsty one for S Ranks and Perfect Clears. bringing back old characters from SA2/SH (Adventure Era) and ShTH/06 (Dark Era) was also the greatest decision someone could ever made; proving theres always space for improvement on character design and development despite bosses not being entirely real or (probably) irrelevant to the franchise in generalTerio's DLC was a bit controversial at first but regardless its a great addon to the game that also makes old fanatics to scream of surprise. it was a charismatic move from SEGA/Sonic Team to the people who loved Shadow's earliest designsthis is the way SEGA. this is the game people wanted - not because of the simple parts of the gameplay but for the rich story and challenges we have to face.

_childDocuments_.review: Definitely became one of my top favorite games, especially since it's about my favorite character in video game history. The story was compelling, the soundtrack is BANGING, and the gameplay throughout the stages feels smooth as butter. Speaking of stages, they have all been so fun to blast through, not too short, and not too long either. Plus, the addition of the doom powers really adds more variety to the stages, basically showing you potential shortcuts to get an easy S rank. This really does feel like a huge dedication to the Ultimate Life Form himself, truly the biggest highlight of his year. As for the Sonic Generations half, it's still the classic game I know and love since I was a kid, with some extra little bits and changes to add to the fun. Speeding through the stages like muscle memory. Took my time to 100% this game on both sides, because I sure did have a fun time with a stupid smile on my face. How could I not when it's about Shadow the Hedgehog? The spotlight is his, and he will fight like he always has, as the Ultimate Life Form.I already can't wait for future installments if they keep this up, especially with the story. Here's to the Fearless Year of Shadow!

_childDocuments_.review: IMPORTANT NOTE: The "OST" included with the deluxe version is not the OST for the game itself, just a bunch of random sonic songs from throughout the series, you don't even get to download them. Really SEGA? Come on.Sonic generations is as good as ever, with some slightly rewritten and redubbed cutscenes to make it fit better with shadow generations and the current sonic canon. Shadow generations itself is FANTASTIC. Every stage is really good, the music remixes are on point, and the story (while less in depth than i was expecting) is still very enjoyable. I'd say its still worth getting even if you've already played the original game, but if you REALLY don't want to re-purchase a game you already played, shadow generations on its own might not be *quite* enough to be worth the full 50$. _childDocuments_.review: Sonics story is basically exactly like the console generations, and might even just be an updated version of the steam port with a few small tweaks and the addition of Chao collectables in every level, and the controversial censorship. Frankly, I don't even think they re-rendered the cutscenes at all. Compared to Shadows cutscenes, they look sloppy and lower quality. Sonics levels are the same as they were in the older generations. And the reason I say it feels just like the updated steam port, because WHEN YOU SELECT SONIC GENS IN THE MENU, it opens up a whole new window and closes the previous one. Personally I wasn't as upset about this because I never got to play the console version, but for someone who's looking for a full revamp of the original, its kind of the same thing. HOWEVERShadows story is absolutely amazing. I haven't even finished it yet but just with what I've played so far its by far the main game that's actually worth the 50 dollars (60 if your a digital deluxe user.) Sure, they definitely couldave picked better levels to remake for Shadow, but even the remakes of these levels (that ive played so far) Have been absolutely amazing. The music is great, and the new features Shadow unlocks is so refereshing. The 3D experience in white space with Shadow Generations just feels like a nice cup of ice cold water compared to how 2D and restricting Sonic Generations is.So ultimately, yes. get this game. For Shadow <3333. Dont get this game expecting a complete remaster of Sonic Generations, because you might be a bit disappointed, due to the rewrites and censorship (which I will not discuss. thats for you to decide how you feel regarding it.) Nothing feels new and exiting with that game. Shadow Generations is worth every penny though, even if its not the longest game in the world. Thats why I havent beaten it yet, because its so amazing I just wanna savor every last drop of content I get. In my opinion I feel like they shouldave just cut sonics part out entirely, and dedicated all their work to Shadow Gens.

_childDocuments_.review: So I have very different opinions on Shadow Generations and Sonic Generations, and will be reviewing them separately here. As a package, Shadow Generations HEAVILY carried for me. Even with that, I still would recommend waiting for a sale as there isn't enough content in Shadow Generations alone to justify the $50 for me at least.Shadow generations is phenomenal. The movement feels responsive and the 3D Shadow Stages are the best a Sonic game has played IMO. You really feel fast as ♥♥♥♥ when playing as Shadow. The level selection is a bit disappointing. The levels from Forces and Frontiers feel like wasted spots as there is not a single stage from Shadow's own game (give us Westopolis you cowards.) I would rather sacrifice the 2D Shadow Stages (very mid compared to the 3D ones) for more 3D levels. I would have liked to see something like White Jungle from SA2, Westopolis from Shadow the Hedgehog, or maybe some of the other 06 stages- Kingdom Valley is amazing in Generations. Another complaint I have is some of the doom powers are very, very wonky feeling. Specifically the Doom Surf and Doom Morph. You can get used to those though. There's a lot of neat callbacks to older games, and the lore added is pretty cool. Having Cubot and the other robot in Shadow's whitespace feels very odd given that the others all have some significance to Shadow or act as a foil to him in Big's case. Shadow gets some cool dialogue from the white space characters, so it would have been nice to have someone else interesting (aka Emerl) instead of the dumb and dumber robots... This is all trivial because Shadow's movement feels amazing and these levels are some of the best designed the series has ever had. They remind me of SA2 or SA1 sonic levels with a fair amount of exploration, while also being designed to use the boost formula mechanics of later games. Even the worst designed level in Shadow's section (Sunset Heights from Forces) is much better than it's original game, or even most of 3D Sonic stages in Generations. In my opinion, Shadow Generation's is the only reason to buy this. If I had the choice to buy it without Sonic Generations I would have.For Sonic Generations, I have not been enjoying this at all compared to Shadow Generations. I played Shadow first, so 3D Sonic feels clunky and slow by comparison. The 2D Sonic levels work fine as they are pretty standard 2D Sonic levels, but I find myself wrestling with the controls and physics with Sonic's 3D levels a lot more than I ever did with Shadow's. Not to mention, 3D Sonic levels feel very limited compared to 3D Shadow levels, so I always end up disappointed playing the Sonic ones. The Sonic ones feel like 2D sonic levels with the occasional 2.5D or 3D segment. and that 3D segment always feels inferior to what Shadow's side has to offer. 3D Sonic just feels too slow and restricted after playing Shadow Generations, so it's hard for  me to appreciate it in this package. That being said, if you like the style of gameplay it has you might enjoy it a lot more than I did.

_childDocuments_.review: When SEGA annouced they were making this game, I wasn't really looking forward to it. To me it seemed like a cheap way to sell old game for a ridiculous price tag with a sprinkle of new content. Holy smokes was I far from the truth.This brought me back to when I first played Sonic Generations as a kid. It was my first contact with Sonic the Hedgehog franchise and I loved every single bit of it. Even these days, I religiously replay the game until there's nothing left to collect or beat. I kept chasing that feeling of being able to experience it for the first time. While playing the Shadow campaign of this game, it absolutely delivered on that. It's fun just like it's predecessor, if not even better. One thing I gotta mention is that the hub (or the "white") world is very very reminescent of how Sonic Frontiers treated it's sandbox open world gameplay, except it's clustered and tightened to one smaller area. While it may sound like a bad thing, it's not. It is the perfected concept of what was Frontiers supposed to be and how I wanted it to feel.The way they handled the Sonic part of this game is also great. I can't really get into that remastered feeling of the gameplay since Generations always looked this beautiful to me, but I adore the feeling of spotting any slight little changes. The chao collection let's me replay all the levels while giving me something fresh to look out for. I know that it's just a minor gimmick, but I love it nonetheless. Overall, Sonic X Shadow Generations is a great game for old and new players alike. SEGA built upon a working concept and made it even better. 10/10, it's a great time to be a Sonic fan.
