_childDocuments_.review: Sonic X Shadow Generations features the original game Sonic Generations and all its DLC as a remaster and a new Shadow game which serves as a new Generations game.Sonic Generations:This remaster holds up to the same graphical quality we see in Shadow Generations and includes new content. Sonic Generations features both Classic 2D gameplay with Classic Sonic as well as Modern 3D gameplay with Modern Sonic. You explore each level recognised from previous Sonic titles with the gameplay styles of both Sonics. It's really cool to see all these levels with modern graphics as well as experiencing 2D Sonic levels in 3D, and 3D Sonic levels in 2D. Each level contains other challenge minigames. There are rival battles and boss battles to challenge as well. One of these rival battles includes Shadow. Eventually you can explore all levels as Classic Super Sonic and as Modern Super Sonic. The DLC from the original game included here has the Casino Night pinball minigame. A very fun and creative spin on pinball featuring Sonic as the ball and a slot machine mechanic. The new content in this remaster encourages you to find and collect many types of Chao found in the Modern levels.Shadow Generations:As Sonic Generations was already considered by most to be one of the best Sonic games, and peoples' love for Shadow, this game serves as just that. Shadow Generations features Shadow being brought into the same time stasis as Sonic. Shadow must conquer more recognisable stages from his past and his future - including levels from Forces and Frontiers - the same as the Sonics did. While Shadow is the only playable character in his story, he is not alone when it comes to facing both 3D and 2D levels. Though unlike Sonics', the hubworld in Shadow Generations is sort of an open area you can explore. Shadow also has new abilities for intreging gameplay use, called Doom Powers. This features Doom Spears, a multi-strike Chaos Spear, Doom Blast, an attack that can send certain enemies flying, Doom Surf, a water-treading ability, Doom Morph, a squid-like creature that allows Shadow to travel along special surfaces and swing, and Doom Wings, a power that allows Shadow to glide. At a certain part, Shadow's interaction with Sonic is reflected to intertwine the stories. This game also includes the same amount of bosses yet a shorter amount of stages. Each boss battle is crazier than the last, with my favourite being the second. Overall, the animations and visuals are very well made. You can tell the jump in graphical quality from Forces to Shadow Generations.Overall both games have incredible music and visuals. There are already plenty of mods for Shadow Generations to try out and there will be more for Sonic Generations in the future.That being said, I don't think this game is better than Sonic Frontiers. It has a lot going for it, but there is a lack of content as a new title. Shadow Generations has six stages while Sonic has nine. The open area also is quite small. While it is made to seem big when it is first revealed and nice to witness the potential of Shadow in an open area, it doesn't feel big when you start moving around. You can get from one side of the map to the other in less than a minute. Frontiers overall has more replayability. And I might be the only one thinking this but I appreciated the boost system from Frontiers much more than Generations. I would put this game at #2, being better than Mania, Forces, and Superstars, but short of Frontiers. I think if they can combine the themes, gameplay elements, and visual effects from this game with an open world adventure like Frontiers, they could make the perfect game.Highly recommended to anyone who likes the original Sonic Generations or Shadow the Hedgehog. This is definitely one of the best Sonic games.

_childDocuments_.review: This game simply puts a tear in my eye. Not only did you bring back the gameplay to a level comparable to Generations and Unleashed, Shadow Generations even IMPROVES on them in some aspects. Mainly being that Shadow controls so well both while boosting and not boosting, this makes all of the platforming a joy to do. (In Generations and Unleashed Sonic can feel like he is running on ice while accelerating) The second improvement is the level design, (I KNOW, IT'S CRAZY BUT THEY DID IT) it's just straight up better than Sonic Generations. The levels are much longer with a lot more open environments with a beautiful abundance of multiple paths to take. (It just feels excellent to replay all of the levels because of this and is never repetitive) Unleashed is still better when it comes to obstacle placement and fast reaction timing though. Then there's the open zone part of this game. It simply does what Frontiers tried to do but much better. The world feels so much more engaging than Frontiers instead of being a lot of automated platforming and big empty fields of grass. The texture/object pop-in is also reduced compared to Frontiers. (They basically took all of the right lessons, WAY TO GO SEGA)I also want to bring up the boss battles. They are outright fantastic. 3D Sonic bosses tend to be sort of simple with the mechanic just being dodge some obstacles, get close enough to the boss and homing attack. But Shadow Generations takes inspiration from the Frontiers titan fights and combines it with the regular formula, and the result is awesome. The only things I don't like about this game is nr. 1 the homing attack, (But only the version Shadow does while attacking an enemy) it's not as fluid as Unleashed or Generations. But no way near as bad as Frontiers thankfully. (The Frontiers homing attack is super slow and takes away all of your momentum).The other thing I don't like is the EDM Dubstep music. Seriously what is up with this? It does not fit in and is very annoying to listen to. Might be a matter of subjective view, but I think Sonic and organic Rock goes together hand in hand much better as it matches the attitude of Sonic and Shadow.VERDICT: Sonic Team managed to create a truly quality game with Shadow Generations. It honors the Sonic IP with respect and the player's time and money too. If they keep this up we are in for an exciting foreseeable future. (I can't wait for the Keanu Reeves movie DLC!) The only thing that worries me is that Kishimoto is directing the next mainline game. He did not take part in making this. Which is probably why this is actually a good Sonic game.But as they say nowadays, WE ARE SO BACK!!!

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic's side is not changed too much. They added a dropdash which seems pretty useless on Modern Sonic due to the button mapping of it, while on Classic Sonic it actually does improve flow. There are also new hidden chaos in the stages for you to find which can be pretty fun. Sadly the final boss didn't change at all. The new dialogue they added is also really rough and the voice acting is even rougher on this side. The story is filled with unnecessary changes and they also removed a lot of the charm and character of Amy Rose.The Shadow side of this bundle is an incredible experience. Controls are amazing, level design is fast, open and flows very well. The Doom abilities are all very nice and I really like how Doom Morph/Squid challenges you. Also the story is well-written and explains Shadow's history while also developing his character a little bit. The voice acting on this side is really good compared to Sonic's. Shadow's campaign is one of the greatest and most polished Sonic games out there. It's one of the rare Sonic games that doesn't fall off towards the end, but instead always get's better and better. This game makes me wanting more, but in a good way.

_childDocuments_.review: Having just finished the final boss, I wanted to write this while everything is fresh in my mind. This game (Shadow Generations) has easily made it into my top 3 Sonic games of all time. With peak level design and story that adds character development for Shadow, It's very easy to recommend this game to any sonic fan of any level. My one gripe is that its over before you want it to be. Obviously we all want more shadow and I'm hoping that Sega will include our favorite hedgehog in more future projects as a main character. but for now, this suffices my cravings for a new story starring the Ultimate Life-form.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: I own both versions of “Sonic Generations”. With that being said, this release is phenomenal with minor hiccups. Shadow's campaign is a joy to play and the story is appropriately bittersweet. I enjoyed every moment of it. Sonic's campaign might divide some fans in terms of story and other writing changes. I personally think that the changes are unnecessary and it shows in the cutscenes. The presentation seems rushed in Sonic's cutscenes; the animation does not match the voice performance. Sonic's cutscenes are a downgrade while Shadow’s are expressive and lively. Odd.Another issue I had was the performance. It's such a shame that a re-release with minor changes (primarily Sonics' gameplay) comes with a noticeable dip in frame rate compared to the original which was released 13 years ago. Make sure you have decent specs before purchasing. If you are planning to purchase this game just to play Shadow’s story, I recommend you wait until the game is about 50% off. BUT, If you have never owned the original “Sonic Generations” before this, then I believe it’s worth a full purchase. ...I would also advise avoiding the online discourse about the changes from political “grifters”.  Just watch some comparison cutscenes on Youtube if you want to see the differences.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best Sonic games ever if not the best. _childDocuments_.review: Sonic Team and Sega finally made a good Sonic game for the first time in...well, a long time. _childDocuments_.review: This game is VERY good.Base Sonic Generations was already a really good game; granted now, there're a few more graphical issues & bugs in this re-release, but nothing like Colour's Ultimate. They're not game-breaking, just a tad annoying-- easily be patched out. The rewritten cutscenes, though a point of contention, really add to the little story existing Generations had. Plus, some of these characters haven't been in a game in the last few years, so having Sonic interact with them more is always welcome. Though I do wish that the animations got touched up more than they did.Anyhow.Shadow Generations; honestly, one of the best Sonic games in the last few games, and a contender for one of the best Sonic games of all time.The story is neat. It reaffirms any Sonic fans from the early 2000's with characters like Mephiles, or more notably Black Doom. Also reintroducing characters like Gerald and Maria helps to give Shadow more a character than just edgy Sonic, which is always nice.The gameplay in Shadow Generations is, in my opinion, much better than Sonic in Generations. The level designs have so many more branching paths, Shadow controls more like Sonic does in Frontiers but more polished, and really levels just have a nice flow to them.His stages are split into 2 Acts, one 3D and one 2D.Honestly, I've never been a big fan of Modern Sonic 2D stages, but Shadow Generations fixes that. I don't know what happened after Frontiers, but it's clear Sonic Team locked in with this game.Even the Open Hub they made for Shadow is just fun to run around in; and the pop-in, though blatant in Frontiers, is minimal. If there's any, it's cleverly hidden, so props to Sonic Team all around.Bosses are cool. The spectacle they started in Frontiers has been carried over and expanded on, and by God have they made so much better. Speaking of spectacle; the Cutscenes in Shadow Generations are phenomenal. Best in the series hands down. Seeing these characters so expressive is great; they really have built on Frontiers massively for Shadow Generations and I'm so glad.Though the campaign is short, levels are so fun to replay. It's a must for any Sonic fan.

_childDocuments_.review: Admittedly, I came into this game with low expectations. The pre-order was 100% worth the wait, and I believe this game is a must play for both veteran and new Sonic fans.

_childDocuments_.review: I was pretty hyped for this game in the run up till its release, and while I am disappointed by one or two things about Shadow Gens. It lives up to my expectations and overall is a fantastic Sonic game that in some aspects makes it a better game then generations. Story while short is very good, seeing a modern day Shadow interact with Maria and Gerald before the events of SA2 is heartwarming and at times heartbreaking. Gameplay while a little slower and stiffer then Frontiers is still really good. Levels are fun with a good amount of multiple pathways. Boss fights for me are a mixed bag, they're fun but a little too easy imo, they last a little longer in hard mode but there isn't a whole lot that changes with the hard mode version. As for the Sonic Generations remaster, it is very similar to the original, the biggest change is that the entire script is rewritten. For the most part I am ok with the new script but there are a few moments where I prefer the original script (examples being the cutscnes with modern sonic and tails after green hill and chemical plant). Gameplay is exactly the same as the orignal with the stellar level design you know and love. Albeit the controls of boost Sonic haven't aged all that well, he feels very stiff when not boosting and when hes in the air.Overall I'd say the package as a whole is worth the asking price as you get 2 great games for the price of one. Hoping that Frontiers 2 takes what this game did great and runs with it.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow just wow, I loved sonic Generations when it first released back in 2011 and one thing i always wanted was a remaster for current gen, when they announced it was returning and this time with Shadow and his own story i was so hyped to be getting more game play and then the announcement of the Sonic movie 3 pack was just the cherry on top, only slight gripe i have is the Shadow campaign felt a bit short i managed to beat it in 3 and a half hours however that being said there is a lot of extra stuff to unlock in the campaign itself, i have noticed a bit of stuttering but it is rare and doesn't always happen the cutscenes and game play for the main game look more improved as well which is really nice to see, i highly recommend this for any sonic fan, heck even if you aren't a big sonic fan it is a great game, i'd give it a 8.5/10 would have been 9 but again Shadows campaign felt short.

_childDocuments_.review: \Absolutely Fantastic Level Design, which is already piggybacking on some of the best level designs in history from the original Generations- One Stage choice especially surprised me since I didn't think Sonic Team would even dare step back into bitter territory, but they surpassed what they once had before in such a fantastic way. The new Frontiers-esque overworld is pretty dang great. It took what was initially bland and odd and put it into a fitting liminal space that only worked to its advantage, keeping it all in one small hub world to really make it fit properly. I think my one critique is that- well, it had a story- but it's super linear, and by the halfway point, you know where everything is going for the most part. But granted, if you want more Shadow, that's exactly what you'll get, and this only raises my hopes that whatever they choose to do next for a Sonic game really follows in this games' footsteps since it was insanely well constructed. Legitimately take a look at some of the in-level transition cutscenes alone make me confident that we'll have an absolute banger of a next game with Sonic as the protagonist once more. Well worth paying full price for as a remastered version of (debatebly) the best Sonic game ever made, and the newest side story absolutely sweetens the deal tenfold to where I will undoubtably 100% this game just because it's such a blast.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic X Shadow Generations is everything I could ask for in a Sonic game. Remastering a already fantastic game with new dialogue and small additions makes the already admired 2011 game even better. Don't even get me started on the Shadow Generations side OH BOY. Not only is the story so fantastic, with Shadow confronting Maria and properly saying goodbye to her, but the GAME PLAY OF THE ACTUAL SHADOW GENS HALF HOLY MOLY. All the levels in Shadow Generations are flawless, with stages such as Space Colony Ark, Kingdom Valley, and Chaos Island making a return in this gem of a game. The boss battles are no exception, some of the most hype bosses I've ever played in a Sonic game. The Metal Overlord fight is a great example, and is just such an awesome fight. Overall, Sonic X Shadow Generations is a collection of two of the greatest games to grace the Sonic franchise. WE WON GUYS WE WON WOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOOO!Final Rating: 100/10

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is a really good game and damn I wish it was longer. I'm glad Shadow got a huge spotlight cast on him this year, he's a really good character. Flynn wrote the game pretty damn well if you ask me. Gameplay wise the new powers are sick as hell, and the stages and remixes are stupid fun. I actually ended up liking the 2D stages a lot. Sonic Team clearly has a good direction they want to take for the Frontiers sequel. I'm very hopeful for what comes next.As for Sonic Generations, the rewritten story is alright. It's better than OG Gens, but the replacement animations for the cutscenes look off. It's still nice to see the once pre-rendered cutscenes fully done in-game (ex: the cutscene after finish GHZ Act 1). Loading times are increased from OG Gens, don't really know why. And the redub sounds pretty good, glad to see Roger is back doing the old Sonic voice direction rather than the Frontiers one.All in all this duo pack of games is very well put together. I still think OG Gens is worth picking up still even though you have to get it via a bundle now. I don't really see this version of the game getting any huge mods or things like Unleashed Project getting ported to this version, despite all the improvements to the game's engine. But for $50 USD, you get a Sonic game known for being good, and a new Shadow game that is actually great.Rating: 8/10

_childDocuments_.review: I've had absolutely 0 zero in the Sonic franchise up until now, and bought this on a whim because I saw the title image by chance and thought it looked interesting, and the overall review rating of "overwhelmingly positive" seemed bizarre, because I'd thought Sonic games were generally ridiculed for one reason or another.I don't think I have, at any point in my life, been so terribly bad at something and yet enjoyed it so much. I'm a fairly uptight person, and I now believe this game should be used as exposure therapy to people who are too tightly wound up. I cannot for the life of me get my head around what is going on in the game at any point. It's chaotic, wildly ridiculous, and everything happens way too fast to process what's happening moment-to-moment. Normally that would irritate me because I'd want to swiftly learn everything and do really well at it. Instead, I end up giggling like a moron and loving every moment of it. The level design (though I gather it's all largely inspired by previous Sonic games?) feels engaging, and though I do occasionally end up dying for seemingly unfair reasons, it doesn't damper how much joy the game brings me.This game has honestly changed my personality for the better, in that I feel more comfortable and happy approaching things I don't understand or just aren't good at. Somehow the way this game works has broken a part of my personality I didn't like: a stubborn impatience when facing things I'm not naturally good at.

_childDocuments_.review: ★★★★★ - Amazing 11.4 Hours 4.4 Hours	• Game consists of a remix\remake of iconic classic and modern 2D and 3D iconic levels all throughout the Sonic and Shadow games.	• Controls are responsive, but some of Modern Sonic and Shadow’s abilities have a steep learning curve.	• Boss fights are dynamic, and end just before they start to feel repetitive.	• Majority of levels have the best feeling of speed and flow that I've felt in any Sonic game in the Franchise.	• The Shadow DLC is a short but great enhancement of everything that Sonic Generations did right. 	• The story is focused on a time frozen multiverse collision, a simple but engaging premise.	• Dialogue captures each character’s personality well, with Shadow’s dry edgy melodrama contrasting Sonic’s unwavering optimism.	• Vibrant visuals with detailed environments that transition smoothly between zones.	• Character design and animations are well polished.	• Music is a standout feature, remixing iconic Sonic tracks with high-energy.	• Sound effects are satisfying, but voice acting can be repetitive and hit-or-miss depending on how much you restart a mission. 	• Strongly suggest playing Sonic Generations before playing Shadow Generations if you haven't already.	• Use a controller for optimal gameplay—keyboard controls feel less intuitive.	• Make sure to set time to explore each level and all its challenges thoroughly. Collectibles and aiming for S rank on levels add replayability and lengthens the time. Focusing on just the main missions, you will miss out on great gameplay.

_childDocuments_.review: Since most of us are here for Shadow Generations, that's what I'll focus on.In short, you get one of, if not  best Sonic game ever, for a grand total of $50, with a free copy of Sonic Generations with a few extra bells and whistles.Shadow Generations takes what made Sonic Generations so good - the polished, fun and well-designed levels (except for Planet Wisp), smooth, easy-to-get-used-to and diverse gameplay and egregiously good soundtrack - and builds upon it like no other Sonic sequel has before, ever since S3&K.The game itself doesn't have a huge amount of zones, but it makes up for it tenfold with the sheer length of the acts (which are long enough to make the purchase worth it and not long enough to make the game boring and tedious), the amount of alternate pathways and endgame replayability thanks to the addition of the Doom powers.Speaking of which, the Doom powers feel more like an organic expansion of Shadow's moveset rather than annoying afterthought gimmicks. They're polished and well-implemented, and flow naturally with the level design. You unlock them gradually and can use all of them at once - you don't need to manually equip and replace any of them. You can, however, disable them in act select before you start a stage (only works while replaying the stages).Challenge stages are also present and, in my opinion, are also an improvement compared to Sonic Generations' challenges. Though, unlike Sonic Generations, you must complete all of them in order to be able to complete the game. The post-challenge bell note chases are also a lot more engaging, which isn't really that important, but still is a nice improvement.In both story and challenge stages, there are three medallions in each; They act as an alternative Sonic Generations' red rings and are used as keys for chests in the white space, which unlock collectibles - artworks, soundtracks and story recaps of Shadow's previous game appearances. You can also gradually unlock a digital version of Gerald Robotnik's journal and view it along with the rest of collectibles in the collection room (accessible through the pause menu in the white space).Speaking of the white space - It's now in 3D, with massive amounts of explorable areas. It can be compared to Sonic Frontiers' open zone gameplay, but much more polished. It gradually expands, giving you more and more space to explore and traverse in many different ways, including all of the Doom powers. The white space also contains various extra challenges which also grant you collectibles.While there isn't much story in this game, it still plays quite an important role. Although it's not as long and complex as, for example, Sonic Adventure 2's or Sonic '06's, but it does a great job portraying Shadow's inner struggles and how his past still haunts him, no matter how much he has tried to leave it behind. In tandem with the Dark Beginnings animated mini-series, which you can find on Youtube, it makes for a great and emotional story - one that Shadow has needed for all this time.Regarding player controls, they are very responsive and, as expected, can be fully customized in the settings, including alternate KB/M bindings. Though, you cannot use some specific keys, such as either of the Shift keys. By default, the homing attack is bound to a separate button, but you can choose legacy controls to bind it to the jump button. Air dash is replaced by double jump, and drop dash is absent.There are three different control modes for Shadow: Act 1 (3D), Act 2 (2D) and white space (3D).Act 1's controls are great - an undeniable improvement compared to Sonic Generations. On controller, as far as I'm aware, there are no issues whatsoever. On KBM, however, there's one issue that can be a bit of a pace breaker. Attempting to turn/change direction with WASD while not boosting will reset your speed to the base speed - same as when you just start moving. However, you'll quickly get used to avoiding this issue, and it is only really a problem while you're getting used to the game and in one specific challenge stage. Even with this little drawback, the controls feel great.Act 2's 2D controls are simply 3D controls limited to a 2D plain. Classic Sonic with the Modern moveset and physics.White space controls are perfect - free camera controls, mouse steering and seamless turning, complete freedom of movement.If you bought the Deluxe edition, you'll receive a digital artbook and soundtrack, as well as some extra soundtracks to select in-game, as well as an optional skin for shadow - Terios, based off one of his concept designs. Said skin only replaces Shadow's model - animations, VFX and skills are identical.The Sonic Generations part shouldn't be ignored either - as one of the best Sonic games of all time, it is a must-play. Despite not much having changed compared to the initial release, I can still confidently say that this is the definitive way to play this game. This time, it's a proper PC port with fully customizable controls and up-to-date settings. Some dialogues have been rewritten and re-voiced (although not re-animated), but otherwise, the game mostly remains the same - aside from the addition of collectible Chao spread throughout the levels. There is, however, no Chao garden in the game, but you can view the Chao in the collection room.In conclusion, Sonic x Shadow generations is as close to a perfect package as it gets. You get two great games for less than a full price tag, with great replayability and barely any cons. The only complaint I could possibly have towards Shadow Generations is that it's just so good that it leaves you wanting more. 10/10, if you're considering getting this game(s), absolutely do it.Now be real, you can't tell me that Shadow with those wings isn't the rawest ♥♥♥♥ ever

_childDocuments_.review: This review will mainly be about the Shadow portion and I won't spoil. The Sonic portion got some control changes, slightly rewritten story, and a dropdash.It exponentially exceeded my expectations. When I first loaded in, I expected 4 zones, 2 acts each, a couple bosses, and a mid final boss. I was EXTREMELY wrong. The story was great and a pretty solid length (although not as long as Frontiers or Unleashed but a little longer than Colors) on top of side missions and more challenges after you beat the game. The animations got a huge upgrade as well. Controls amazingly and the gimmick is fun but a little weird to control sometimes. Runs great as well and good to see a Sonic game get native 120 FPS support. I enjoyed every stage and they don't feel linear like Forces stages and have several different paths, although they were somewhat easy until the late stages but not too easy. Very excited for the movie DLC in December.

_childDocuments_.review: It's no secret that anyone buying this game will do so for the sake of playing Shadow Generations over Sonic Generations. That's probably for the best, as the Shadow campaign is much more lore-heavy and provides a breadth of new experiences that Sonic fans (and especially fans of the red-and-black renegade) will love. However, this game collection suffers from a number of issues that may end up limiting your enjoyment of the product as a whole. Still worth buying for sure because of how much content is in it, but you may have your hopes dashed a bit with what you're expecting.Positives:-Shadow Generations campaign is all-new, action-packed, and plays quite a bit like Sonic Frontiers with more refined controls.-Sonic Generations is pretty much intact... for better and for worse.-Fans of lore will enjoy the extra bits of backstory given to Shadow.-As expected, both games are loaded with content between artwork, music, and character biographies that stimulate the imagination.-You can tell by the voice acting, cinematic cutscenes, and the loads of content that a lot of love went into Shadow Generations and the developers' efforts to expand Shadow's backstory. It also feels like a breath of fresh air to play a Sonic game where Sonic himself is NOT the main character for the first time in years.-Nostalgia mixed with nuance on Shadow's end makes the game a welcome addition to your library.-Gerald's Journal was a thrill to read through for that extra bit of context into the Space Colony ARK and the events leading up to Shadow's origin story.All that being said, we also need to take a look at what this collection is lacking, and how it may impact people's decisions to buy the game at its current price tag of 50 USD. Be prepared, because there's a lot of missed opportunities here.Negatives (Sonic Generations):-Sonic Generations has the same clunky, godawful controls as it did in its original release. For both Sonics. Many unfair deaths or restarts were made because of how bad this game's controls are. Classic Sonic's physics and spin dash are still the worst. Modern Sonic's boost tends to be unreliable because of how differently it works here than in Frontiers. This does NOT transfer well to Shadow Generations.-In fact, they changed nothing of importance about Sonic Generations at all. Except for the unnecessary changes to the characters' dialogue, which ends up ruining a couple of interactions entirely.-No more Extra Life system, which diminishes the challenge factor by a mile. Also, they left in a particular Skill in Sonic Generations that is now useless and doesn't even need to be bought to get the Mad Skillz achievement.-There is ZERO reference or tie-in to Shadow Generations from the Sonic side of things. For a game that had a major selling point of the stories intertwining with each other, they offered nothing on this side of the collection. Again, Sonic Generations here is almost the exact same as the original release... which is now no longer available to buy in the Steam Store. So, this now HAS to be your experience with Sonic Generations if you didn't get the original version before.-They added the Sonic Mania Drop Dash, but didn't add any Sonic Mania music. They didn't add ANYTHING else new worth note to the game when they very well could've. Also, in my experience, the Drop Dash sucks. For both Sonics.-One thing they DID add... that turned out to be totally useless, was the 'Find all the Chao' gimmick, where they just hid a bunch of Chao in EVERY act of EVERY stage, three at a time. And you get NOTHING for finding them all. Not even a lousy achievement. Yeah, it's nice to see the Chao make a return, but you can't do anything with them but watch them float around once you're done searching for them.Negatives (Shadow Generations):-Shadow Generations' campaign is too short and relies heavily on playing through challenge stages and looking around an honestly bland, tiny, and lifeless hubworld for collectibles to pad for extra play time.-The "tie-in" to Sonic's side of things from Shadow's perspective is only a couple of cutscenes and Rouge of all characters being the only other character to appear in both games. So, no Sonic boss fight in which you play as Shadow.-The collectibles. A bunch of them DON'T APPEAR ON THE MAP, which makes looking for them a massive chore if you're going to 100% the game. Speaking of which...-The map. You can't interact with it to mark points of interest or even scroll around to get a decent look at anything.-Oftentimes, the game does not give you a full explanation of how Shadow's Doom powers work, forcing you to suffer occasional cheap deaths as you learn about them.-Doom Powers can be pretty gimmicky and end up only serving one or two purposes before being rendered useless because the stages don't do enough to incorporate them.-Shadow feels sluggish most times and his boost does not always give a meaningful speed increase. This is a problem shared by Sonic Frontiers. Given that this game runs on the Frontiers engine, it's all but expected.-Not a SINGLE stage you play through in this game is from Shadow the Hedgehog (2005), yet they have nearly every song from that game in here. As well as that game's main villain. Make it make sense. -There are only six stages in total. Without spoiling too much... TWO are from Sonic Adventure 2, One is from Sonic Heroes, One is from Sonic 06, One is from Sonic Forces, and one is bafflingly from Sonic Frontiers. Two of these six stages are from games that took place lorewise AFTER Sonic Generations, and the game barely gives an explanation as to why this is. And don't expect it to mean anything that the Frontiers and Forces stages are here.-The usual Modern Sonic-era problem of the main stages being way too linear with little room for exploration or ingenuity is still here.-Bosses are formulaic and far too easy, even on Hard mode. You just play through a bunch of quick-time events while occasionally being able to damage the boss between those events. Matter of fact, the Challenge stages you're forced to play through just to progress the game aren't that much of a challenge either. They're too quick and any enjoyment you get from the creative stage alterations is hampered when you find the goal ring in less than 30 seconds.-There is a singular hubworld side quest that doesn't involve challenge stages... and it's a MASSIVE waste of time. All for a joke that ends up not being funny. It's optional, thank goodness, but why is it even here?-Ending (NO SPOILERS) can be a bit of a tearjerker, but it's also... underwhelming at the same time.All in all, this is a decent collection and another solid addition to any Sonic fan's collection. Especially because of all the music and artwork jammed into both games. If you're NOT a Sonic fan going into this, however... Ya MAY want to ask for this game as a holiday gift instead of spending the money upfront. Perhaps this game could get better with DLC for Shadow Generations other than the movie tie-in level, but that will remain to be seen as of this review. I recommend buying this game collection, yes, but I do so with much trepidation because of how little substance the collection actually has once you get past the flash.

_childDocuments_.review: Easily the best Sonic game to release since the original Sonic Generations in 2011. Sonic Generations was already a good game and they didn't change much. If you liked Generations before, you'll like it here. They made some interesting changes to the cutscenes, for better and for worse, but Sonic Gens didn't have much of a story anyway so it doesn't matter much. The new chao rescue is a neat addition, but are a bit tedious to find. The chao can be hidden in some really obscure spots and are easy to miss so you'll have to really stop and look around to find them.Shadow Generations feels like an improvement in every way, building off of the original Sonic Gens formula with the lessons learned from Frontiers. The level design is on par with the Sonic Gens but the controls are so much tighter and more responsive! Shadow's doom powers only enhance the gameplay and add new ways to traverse the levels. Far better than anything like the Wisps from Colors, which were already pretty good. The open zone hub is also fantastic. It's an absolute joy to traverse and I spent hours wandering around trying to collect everything.Basically, everything here is great! If you haven't played Sonic Generations yet, I highly recommend picking this up. If you have played it, it's still worth buying for Shadow Generations alone, even if it's a bit short.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been seeing the hype up for this game for months and decided that I wanted to play it 3 days earlier than official release. Now I didn't start off with the Shadow portion first and I decided to play through original Generations first. It's still a pretty good game and it holds up well despite being nearly 13 years old. I hate the classic Sonic levels and the final boss is terrible but it's still a good game for sure. Shadow Generations on the other hand I was just blown away with how good it is, the levels throughout the whole game are super well made (especially Sunset Heights and Kingdom Valley), the use of Chaos Control and the doom abilities made levels so much fun. The bosses were sick, the movement and controls are great too I never had a real issue with both, and the animation quality in cut scenes and levels... I couldn't even tell if they were in game or CGI half the time it looked so clean. The story as well was very good (for a Sonic game at least, Ian Flynn wrote it so that's probably why). The hub world is sick too, lots to explore, lots of collectables which I'm far from getting all of them, the collection room. They cooked so hard, this is what peak looks like. And no real performance drops either. I was running it max settings 120FPS 1440p and couldn't really see visible drops in performance (i5-12400F, RX 6750XT), which is great nowadays since some games are just not optimised well at all. Overall I give it either a 9 or 10/10, I can't decide on what to give it. Either way it is probably the best Sonic game in god knows how long. Also the movie DLC looks pretty nice so can't wait to give that a go in December.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations:A good remaster for a game that was already excellent, with lightly rewritten dialogue and cutscenes that benefit going beyond the original bare-bones story from the 2011 release.Shadow Generations:We're so back, a great standalone game with deceptively expansive levels offering multiple routes and secrets that reward repeat playthroughs using new abilities exclusive to Shadow, the best boss fights the series has to offer, and the most stunning in-game cutscenes to date for Sonic games. The whole experience oozes with care and refinement, especially regarding the writing, character interactions, and voice acting. (Seek out the Gerald Robotnik journal entries, simply amazing storytelling and lore to chew on and theorize whats to come for the future)This is the game you would recommend to newcomers and longtime fans. This is the production value that'll set a new standard going forward for the series. A two-for-one deal under full price that offers fulfilling gameplay experiences and tons of replayability.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow's campaigin is a lot of fun while it lasts. Even though the runtime is short you could sink a ton of time into finding all the collectibles and replaying stages to improve your rank. I did find some of the stage choices odd though. There are 6 stages in the game and there isn't a single one from Shadow the Hedgehog? Like how? It's not like that game had any shortage of neat levels from Westopolis, Digital Circuit, Gun Fortress, Sky Troops, Final Haunt, etc.  I feel like the campaign would have felt complete if they had 7 stages with the additional one being a Shadow the Hedgehog stage. My other criticisms are that pretty much all of the boss fights felt overly scripted even though they were still fun to fight. There were just a lot of instances of the game telling you exactly which button to press or exactly which move to do.Lastly, the doom morph ability just didn't feel good to use. Thankfully you get it later in the campaign so earlier stages don't utilize it but when it is used later it just feels slow and clunky. All in all this is the best feeling modern-style Sonic game in a long time. Between this and Frontiers I feel like Sega is on the right path. I am only critical because I care about the franchise and want it to be the best it can be.

_childDocuments_.review: Though the base game technically has more stages, Shadow's campaign is more than qualified to be considered a full-fledged speed platforming experience with vastly superior level design, visuals, and overall presentation versus Sonic Frontiers. Though it can't compete with the sheer size and scale of Frontiers, it does seem to improve upon the "open zone" design and actually has fully realized levels (finally).It's not as blistering fast as the base game, but it's uniquely "Shadow", offering different kinds of play-styles and tons of ideas that are executed surprisingly well. The story is pretty light (and only fans will really pick up on the tiny details sprinkled about), but it's meaningful for those who have followed Shadow for a long time, waiting for his character to be done right.Honestly an impressive feat from Sonic Team, they nailed it. Fun set-pieces, solid level design all-around, and lots of replayability. Gets me even more hopeful and excited for the direction of future Sonic games. Shadow's campaign really just sweetens the deal of this remaster, which is definitely worth getting if you never got the chance to play the base game. Though if you want a nitpick, it's probably that there are moments where the hub world and 2D levels can feel a bit too cluttered, but maybe that's because I've been looking at the barren emptiness of Frontiers for a while now.

_childDocuments_.review: SHADOW GENERATIONS-I enjoyed the game quite a bit! It feels like everything that was wrong with Frontiers was addressed here and is an amazing experience. The character writing was really well done and the level design was great too! Unlike the original Sonic Generations, Shadow Generations does not feel bloated at all, with every stage act and challenge act all feeling polished and enjoyable. It never felt like a grind to go and beat every level. The gameplay loop feels much more polished this time around, with EVERYTHING feeling better than what was considered one of the best Sonic games of all time when it came out.However, if I had to voice complaints I do have a few. I feel that the controls for Doom Morph are hard to learn. It's unclear how specifically the grapple works, and there are not any good spots to test it out and learn the specifics. Once I searched online for tips it all clicked, but it was a very frustrating experience trying to figure it out on my own. Another frustrating experience is the journey of collecting the last few collectables. While the chests show up on the map and in the world even after being collected, the rocket parts disappear completely making it unclear where you haven't looked yet. The strategy for finding the last few are to use a video guide and check all EIGHTY locations in a row until you stumble across the one you haven't found yet. The lack of an ability to pan the map while zoomed in doesn't help eitherSo to wrap it up, Shadow Generations is amazing as a standalone product and improves upon everything that it was inspired by. AND it comes WITH Sonic Generations. While I haven't played the Sonic Generations part of the game yet (and have heard there are more than a few bugs that were not present in the original), the proposed changes all felt like they'd be a net positive that reinforce the good parts of the game's core gameplay loop. Hopefully the bugs I've heard about are either only exaggerated or will be fixed in the future.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: A remaster of Generations was not particularly needed, aside from the awkward way it runs on PC, but it was a fun game with some great music so hearing it was coming back wasn't a bad thing. However, the Shadow half makes this more than worth it. The level design is done in a way that is punishing but fair with a lot of branching path for those with lightning reflexes. The overworld, to me, feels like they jammed all of Frontiers into a Mario 64 Peach's castle and I'm here for it. The new powers are weird... but fun to use and don't feel left behind ever - they all keep getting use beyond their initial reveals so that's really nice. And the music is outstanding, but I mean, obviously. It's Sega, what did you expect?The story, though, is an absolute joy. Original Generations was serviceable, and once again, Shadow's side brings it to a new level. I don't want to spoil it, but it's very touching and has quickly become a favorite. The game is pretty short, but what's there is very solid, which is good because while the story might not take a ton of time, the replayability factor is through the roof. There is so much to do for those who want to 100% everything, or for those who are too bad at games for stuff like that, it's still fun to explore and try new challenges. Or even just pop on Doom Mode and hang out in an apocalypse nightmare, you know, whatever!The controls for the remastered side are still a little on the jankier end. I'm not an expert, but I feel like maybe that wasn't touched up so much. It runs fine, but I found myself getting a little frustrated with some of the movements. Shadow's side has a ton of improvements there, but even then you should expect the occasional surprise you jumped off a cliff ending. Huge improvement from the former, though!If you are new to the series, this isn't a bad place to start! You get a sampling of the whole series to this point in time, but some of the story might not be as fleshed out as it could. It's tough for me to tell, but I think they have enough there you can follow along. For long time fans, what am I even addressing you for? Get it! It's peak! Seriously!! This might be the best "Sonic" game. I don't know. I'm still processing my experience. But it might be!

_childDocuments_.review: The Sonic side of things remains effectively the same as Sonic Generations, and that was a good game. The only difference is now there's extra collectibles in each Act in the form of Lost Chao.The Shadow side of things is incredible. The campaign is about equivalent in length to Sonic's, the hub world is much larger (and 3D), and as a gameplay experience it's frankly just better (to be expected given it's much newer). Everything's taken many steps forward:* The animations are dynamic, smooth, and well choreographed. The Radical Highway Doom stuff is something I'm amazed they were able to make look as good as it did.* The level design is much better. 2D sections in particular do a sort of 2.5D view to help you see further ahead, which is much appreciated. Though you're moving fast, alternate paths are still easy to see and react to.* Shadow feels great to play as, probably the smoothest gameplay I've had in a Sonic game. There's very little jank, and most of the time what you want to happen, happens.It is a little unfortunate though, as going from Shadow's back to old Sonic Generations's gameplay does make it feel more dated and frustrating. But that's to be expected from a 10 year old game, advancements are a good thing.

_childDocuments_.review: Review with spoilers.This game is what I came to this franchise for. It feels weird to be a Sonic fan and *truly* think a game is exactly what you wanted. Literally every Sonic game before had some "catch" or "bad part" but this one lacks said thing in the new portion of the game. How they managed to finally do this is beyond me.Where do I even begin? The stages are finally long again! After so many years of 3D stages in boost games that barely scratched the two minute mark playing 4 minute 3D acts that have both challenge, unique fun gimmicks and actually good level design feels surreal.This level design is very open at times, with so many routes and hidden paths that it honestly seems like they brought the best from Sonic Unleashed HD Daytime, Og Generations and the Sonic adventure games/Sonic Heroes. These stages are some of my favorite in the franchise. I haven't loved boost this much since Jungle joyride or Skyscraper scamper. I was worried the doom powers would make the gameplay worse of feel slower. Boy was I wrong. All they do is add to a levels greatness. I will admit though the last one (Doom Wing) while cool is not my cup of tea and am glad is optional (not a big fan of flying over stages) but the others are very good.You'd think the 2D acts would be the "catch" or something but no???? They are so fun and well designed too! Their design feels more linear but it favours challenge, keeping the pace and good movement over some massive open 2D area, which sounds "bad" on paper but Is so well executed thay these ended up being some of my favorite 2D levels in the franchise, right next to the OG Gens classic acts or Mania, but for more proper comparison the it's on par with the best Sonic Rush adventure stages or Colors DS stages.The challenge actsrange from really nice to ok at worst. Wish at least some were optional but it's fine since they are fun.The bosses are on the same level, reaching the heights of my favorites in the whole franchise. Not a dull moment. This game has my favorite Sonic boss of all time now, and many that come close.The seudo open zone/hub world is pretty fun too, it takes the best of Frontiers open zone and adds on it. I 100% the Shadow part of this game already and collecting everything was a great experience, so many secrets and things to see/challenges to complete.Maybe there's more I could meatride this game for that I haven't said here but I can't stress enough this is my favorite Sonic game as of now. I can look at this game and actually put it near my actual favorite games (Mario Odyssey, the Maroo Galaxies, Team Fortress 2, Doom 2016 to name a few).So glad Sonic team finally got their ♥♥♥♥ together :).The remaster of the og is fine, nothing too special but it's fine. Wished they did something about that snoozefest of a final boss but oh well, everything else is a banger. The new chao are basically more red rings and I appreciate an excuse to explore these open levels more.My only actual issue with the Shadows portion is the story. On the one hand they seem to have finally made Shadow truly amazing again as a character (Sonic Forces, Sonic Prime, latests comics and Murder of Sonic showed some hope) and I can finally say he's back to the level he was in 06 or Archie. On the other hand while the story has beautiful moments it relegates alot of dialogue into optional talks with the npcs and heaps of things feel unexplained. The story feels so rushed and it seems like it's missing so many cutscenes and moments. Omega doesn't do anything really, Black Doom needed way more scenes to explain stuff and the "We are one in the same" thing barely felt explored, which is something this games story seems to suffer from a lot, rushing and not exploring things. There doesn't seem to be proper payoff to lots of things that are brought up. But hey at least that ending was beautiful and borderline tear jerking. It's a skeleton of a good story at base level. It could have been so much more and that's disappointing.I do like the rewrites in the og gens though that's cool (Classic Sonic ate Angel island) to patch up the problems the characters used to have back then. But ofc the story is still super D tier. They turned a D into a D+.Sonic fan or no Sonic fan do get this game. This is where Sonic peaked so far, and it's not even Sonic it's Shadow because he is much cooler than Sonic unfortunately...

_childDocuments_.review: Since I've fully 100%ed the game, I felt I should give the game a review. The best way I can describe this game is "I can't believe they bundled Sonic Generations with the best Sonic game ever made". So far, anyway.I mean, Sonic Generations... is Sonic Generations, but with better dialogue here and there, and the Drop Dash is here too. It's a game I already really enjoyed, and I enjoyed revisiting it just as much. Shadow Generations, on the other hand, quickly has made this 2-in-1 deal my favorite Sonic game of all time. There is SO much to love here, that frankly I would be here ALL day talking about it, so I'll try my best to keep it brief.The story is great, while I think the pacing is a little quick and could've used a bit of extra time to breathe, that's frankly a minor nitpick in this overall great story. It's not as grandiose or interesting lore-wise as Sonic Frontiers's story, but it's a delight nonetheless, and fans of Shadow's character will love it for sure like I have.Like with any game though the most important thing is the gameplay, and this game has an Open Zone-esque White Space to explore, which is really fun with plenty of collectables and side challenges to complete which you can really sink your time into if you want, but of course there's the main levels, and the bosses. On the levels, GOD these have to be some of the best 3D Boost stages the series has to offer so far, they are incredible! So many alternate paths (especially in the final level, I still have yet to see every single path myself), they're pretty lengthy being about 5 minutes on average, but they're fun throughout that entire runtime. And don't misunderstand me, the 2D stages are awesome as well, while not as long or with as many branching paths, they're fast paced and really fun to run through, too! And the bosses... I almost don't want to say anything and just tell you to experience them yourself, they're AWESOME! While not as epic or blood pumping action filled as the Titans from Frontiers, they're really fun to fight, and the optional Hard Modes are no joke, either!The last topic I should bring up is, as you can probably see in the icons in this review, somewhere, I played the entirety of the game on Steam Deck. And it works great! Really smooth experience in both games, although some really dense areas in Shadow Generations caused the framerate to drop a bit (a particular section in Chaos Island comes to mind that just makes the game chug), but it never became unplayable or anything, and felt really smooth.Overall, if you haven't played Sonic Generations, then this game is a mustbuy. If you're a Sonic fan, you already have this game and loved it, be serious with me now. And even if you have played the original Sonic Generations, this is a fun way to re-experience it, along with an incredible new campaign.

_childDocuments_.review: For those with low attention spans: 9/10, Great Levels, Great Bosses, Amazing Animations, Decent Story, Ok-ish music.Shadow Generations. For newcomers, Im only going to be talking about the Shadow side, as Ive played the original Generations many times, and have nothing to say. This game. THIS GAME. Is one of the best Sonic games ever made. Sonic Team knocked it of the park. Amazing animations, phenomenal level design, the doom powers are splendid (got me speaking like a british person that's how you know its good.) A rather simple, but well written story about Shadow confronting his trauma. I can understand how that could leave a lot to be desired for some people though, not me, I loved it. The animations in this game are CRAZY, this is not only the best animated sonic game, but one of the best animated games of 2024. Props to the animators.The levels are mostly great, there are a few fumbles (Rail Canyon 2, Space Colony Arc 2), but they're fun, challenging, and very replayable. They allow for a ton of experimentation with chaos control and the new doom powers (which are all fun, except doom morph, I think doom morph controls poorly). The bosses. Oh man. Not going to get into spoilers, but the bosses are all BANGERS. Especially the 2nd one.  Ost is very hit or miss, which is a little sad.Overall, I'd give this game a 9/10. As a long time Sonic fan, I couldn't be happier. My boys are back.

_childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is awesome!!!!!!!This is the evolution of boost-style Sonic game that I have been waiting for since the original Sonic Generations. The game mechanics, stage design, and cinematics are all significantly improved. The Doom powers do add a lot of colors to the gameplay (no pun intended). The stages have just the right pace and length. The bosses are very satisfying to beat. They got the atmosphere right and did a good job re-telling the story of Shadow. After finishing the main campaign, you really want to re-visit the stages to try out different tricks and get the collectibles.For those who want to know the length of the game before you buy it: The Shadow campaign has five zones, each contains two main acts and four challenge acts. Along the way you fight three bosses. After beating the third boss, you get access to ten optional challenge acts and the grand finale, which contains two main acts and the final boss. The hub world is an open zone that is about half the size of a Sonic Frontiers island, filled with plenty of collectibles and map challenges.I haven't tried the Sonic campaign yet, but looks like it is pretty much the same experience as the original version, with some minor tweaks here and there. If you did not play the original version, you should find it a lot of fun too. (The only exception is the final boss... It is a pity that they did not take the chance to fix it.)All in all, you have the best two boost-style Sonic games in one package. It's a great package to have in your library.

_childDocuments_.review: I really didn't know what to review this game, since 'ok' isn't an option. But I thought I'd give it a shot anyways, since I have strong thoughts on it despite my mixed feelings. Spoilers ahead.Firstly, the Generations remake is more just a pc port of a pc port. It's lost bugs and gained them, and it's slightly choppy. But the story is slightly better, and all the lines are rerecorded which is trippy as hell, but ultimately a plus I think. You can really hear Ian Flynn's influence in it, a lot subtler than usual despite it's bluntness. A lot of 'this is for my friends', and that's fine. But honestly the changes aren't really that interesting, nor good, they're just there.Planet Wisp Act 2 is still terrible, and the final boss is still ass, that didn't change. But the rest of the game being really fun hasn't either. Both Sonics have the drop dash, and it works for Classic and sucks for Modern. Want to Air Dash but are close to the ground? Roll into a pit. Want jump higher, so you hold the button down? Drop dash into a pit when you land! It's real clunky and annoying, but honestly it didn't rear its head to much.But Sonic Generations is just that, Sonic Generations. New chao collectibles, a drop dash, and that's it as far as I can tell. It's a good game, with a huge drop off at the end, as it always has been.Now, Shadow Generations.... wow, what a doozy. First of all, it has one of the greatest starts of any Sonic game I've ever played. I've never been more excited and happy while playing a game since when I was a kid, honestly. It was amazing. It held up strong for the first few stages. The story starts great, and the writing is a bit on the nose, but still fun. The first three stages were really good!I really want to state here just how good the first half of the game is. It is utterly fantastic, and that's awesome. But... oh boy.Gimmicks are to Sonic what meth is to that one guy under the bridge who speaks in eldritch tongues I can't comprehend. And these 'Doom Powers' are all absolute ass. The chaos spear is fun and fast paced, but the surfboard and... oh, the squid... Shadow the Fish-hog is aaawful to control. But the surfboard is like... okay? It feels super weird, and it's used a LOT.Shadow Generations goes HARD with its gimmicks, and it doesn't give. Each gimmick gets a boss fight, you don't get to do one as just 'Shadow' which really sucks. Biolizard is super fun, but it has an over-reliance on the Chaos Spear, but it was still awesome. Metal Overlord, while ♥♥♥♥♥♥' cool to see, was ENTIRELY on the surfboard. And... oh my god, Mephiles, I love you so much my boy, but your fight was THE SQUID NOOOOO NOT THE SQUID PLEASE GOD ♥♥♥♥ WHY THE SQUIDPoint is, each gimmick isn't just a 'power-up'. Nah, it's an entire different character sometimes. A bogged down, sluggish and clunky different character. It just sucks that these cool moments were bogged down with such ♥♥♥♥♥♥ gimmicks.But that's not my biggest problem with Shadow Generations. That problem is... re-use. It re-uses assets and levels. AGAIN. "Green Hill Again?" No, much worse. Two of the five stages are... FROM GAMES SHADOW WASN'T IMPORTANT IN, AND WERE SUPER RECENT. AND ONE OF THEM IS FROM FRONTIERS, WHICH HE WASN'T EVEN IN AT ALL.What the ♥♥♥♥ were they thinking? I know, and you should too. Money, money, money.Shame on you SEGA, but what's even worse.Shadow Generations, the celebration of Shadow the Hedgehog... HAS NO LEVELS FROM SHADOW THE HEDGEHOG!Are you ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ kidding me SEGA? Levels from SONIC FORCES, and SONIC FRONTIERS where SHADOW WASN'T PLAYABLE AT ALL!!! And it was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Chaos Island! You took levels from games where they reused levels from Generations, the cycle continues! It's terrible! And the music just ♥♥♥♥♥ itself when you get to those levels. From cool remixes, kind of Eurobeat-esque in a way, to terrible dubstep that grates on your ears. It really falls off HARD at the Forces level. Then Metal Overlord shows up, and it's like "Yo, sick! It's that guy!" The boss fight kinda sucks, but Crush 40 plays in the background so it's okay. "Man, that Forces Level kinda sucked. Why was it there? Anyway, glad to see we're back on track." Nope. Instead, there aren't even two more levels before the next boss, it's JUST FRONTIERS.But MAN, I was so excited to see that purple goop all over the place. Mephiles is in the game, and I'm very miffed and unsure about my feelings on that. But we'll come back to this.So, we've had The Ark (Final Rush/Chase), Bullet Station, Kingdom Valley, Sunset Heights (♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ City Escape again, mind you.), and Chaos Island (kill me). Black Doom is popping off, what's the final level? They're saving the Shadow the Hedgehog level for last, let's go! It's gotta be Final Haunt, right? Or maybe The Doom? Something really representative of Shadow the Hedgehog (the videogame, the one Black Doom is from).Radical Highway. It's Radical Highway. Which was already in 2 or 3 levels throughout the game.So what I think happened is, they got halfway through the making Shadow Generations and realised something."We just spent loads of time on the Gens Remake, we have no budget or time left! What do we do?" "Oh man, what about those Radical Highway parts in The Ark? Just use those!" "But the game is so short, we have no time left and only three levels ready!""Uh, oh! Shadow was in Forces, right? Use one of those!""But we have another boss after that part!""Oh ♥♥♥♥... uhm, oh! Use the Frontiers one! The one they didn't like, the '2D Island'! Make it 3D""You got it boss!"Seriously, I think they realised they didn't have time to finish it. So they slapped a half-hearted second half of the game together. They say in the game "Oh, you haven't visited those places? Probably means you do in the future" in the same way they make excuses for Sonic visiting Green Hill again in Frontiers. It's just so gross. You're meant to be celebrating Shadow the Hedgehog. Put a level from his game in, it's literally the one thing that you SHOULD have done. It's the bare minimum.Radical Highway, they fully unlock your 'Doom Wings' or whatever, and you're incentivised to skip the entire level with them. It sucks, is boring and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sucks. Then the final boss is pretty much entirely flying with the wings. Yeah, a cool orchestral and rock mix of All Hail Shadow is blaring, and the music changes as the fight does, and that's cool. And Neo Devil Doom's design is cool. But the fight sucks, and the fact that it sucks sucks.Anyway, the gameplay is ass whenever a gimmick kicks in, we're used to this. But the story makes no sense either, when you think about it.So, Black Doom is trying to bring back the Black Arms thanks to the time whatever the ♥♥♥♥ is going on. Fine. Why is Mephiles not doing that? He says "I just want to exist!" Which, first of all, he is the MIND of the GOD OF TIME AND SPACE. Why would the GOD OF TIME AND SPACE not be capitalising on the fact that TIME AND SPACE is broke so he's back? He's a manipulator, and he should absolutely be doing what Black Doom is doing. In fact...How the ♥♥♥♥ is Black Doom using the time break to ♥♥♥♥ with everything? At the end of the game Gerald says that now that Black Doom is gone White Space can't hold up anymore. What? Black Doom... never could do that? His power only ever related to the Black Arms, and he used Chaos Control when he had the seven chaos emeralds to warp the comet to Earth. That's it.Did they think the Snapcube Fandub was canon or some ♥♥♥♥? I'm so confused.OK so I've run out of characters, didn't know there was a limit here. Basically, started great, attached to a remake of a game that didn't need a remake that meant they didn't have time or budget to finish the new game. Shadow Gens starts strong, halfway through it plummets and sucks so hard it sucks to even think how much it sucks.Buy it if you want to, I don't know if you should though.

_childDocuments_.review: What can I say that hasn't already been said about this game?If I had to start somewhere, let's begin with Shadow's portion of the game because that's the main attraction here. Shadow's campaign is a refinement of what worked in Sonic Frontiers but follows the structure of Sonic Generations. You must go through two acts of each level, complete challenge gates, and defeat the boss from said area. All while exploring a 3D hub world whose size pales in comparison to the Starfall Islands of Frontiers, it is much more interesting to go through due to the game's strong art direction. The levels are a massive improvement from the last two mainline games in every aspect. They are longer, control better, and offer more routes to explore, giving players more incentive to replay levels. The bosses are once again memorable and fun to play. Boss fights have hit or miss for most Sonic games, but starting with Frontiers has been a highlight. One aspect I enjoy is that they ramped up the difficulty in this game when going for S Ranks, although it's pretty erratic. Some levels are easy to S Rank, and others are really difficult. Oh yeah, the story is pretty heartwarming, seeing Shadow come to peace with his past after trying to forget about it at the end of Shadow '05. While being a smaller-scale project than Frontiers, Shadow's half of this package is worth the price of admission by itself, and I urge you to play it, but would recommend getting it on sale if the short runtime makes or breaks it for you.If you liked Sonic Generations before, I'm happy to report that it's the exact same gameplay-wise, aside from finding three Chao in every level. To my knowledge, collecting all of them doesn't give you anything outside of an achievement, essentially a lesser form of Red Rings. It's completely optional, so it doesn't affect the experience. Now it's time to tackle the elephant in the room: the altered cutscenes. Every cutscene in this game has been rewritten, and... it's inoffensive. The rewrite doesn't change anything about the game's story, making me wonder what the point of changing it even was. The delivery of some lines sounds like they were rushed to fit the runtime of certain scenes but overall it's alright. But it's not like the story matters in Generations anyway. It mainly acts as an excuse to run through these levels again. While being a downgrade from before, it shouldn't affect your enjoyment of this game. Visually... this release doesn't do anything to improve it's presentation. It's nice to have FMVs not look like a blurry mess, but the textures could have been upscaled. Luckily, this game has a strong art direction, so I can forgive it. At the very least, they didn't butcher the game's art style like Colors Ultimate did. And... yeah, this game is one of the best in the series and is packaged with a new fan-favorite. I strongly recommend this game. It's a good entry point to the series and is a classic.

_childDocuments_.review: is surprising. Announced as apart of a  Remaster, I wasn't sure what to expect. Was this a couple Generations levels, but you're Shadow? How long is it? Is it a nice bonus to a much bigger game, a la Bowser's Fury to Super Mario 3D World? What IS it?Well, it's definitely its own game. It's not on the same engine as  proper, and it feels and plays significantly different too. In revisiting the concept of giving Shadow his own game, Sonic Team tackled their past mistakes eloquently, righting wrongs in regards to how to make this idea work. This new  game doesn't just work, it's genuinely polished, fun, and the right amount of challenge. A fantastic game that is both a love letter to anyone who was once a kid with a Gamecube, as well as a game that stands proud and tall against the best action-platformers you can play today. Even if you've never played the games this particular one is referencing, if you want to play a high-speed platformer that rewards finesse, creativity and mastery, it cannot be recommended enough.At the time of this review, I completed the main story, but still have much more to do. I can't wait to hop back in, get my S-Ranks and unlocks, and continue having fun. A smile on my face. Again, love it.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Okay, let's cut the crap here. This is a review of  Sonic Generations is almost 13 years, and if you want to play it, this is the best way. It runs great, plays great and looks better than ever before. Both Sonic's now have the drop dash, for some reason. Some new challenges, some dialog changes. That's about it. OK, time for the real deal.Shadow Generations has, objectively, some of the best level design and gameplay implementation in any Sonic game. Level design has been evolved from base Gens, opening up multiple pathways and skips at almost every turn. Most of these pathways can be accessed through Shadows new Doom powers, all of which, except one (Morph), are a joy to use. The 3D stages feature all the bells and whistles you'd expect, flashy action pieces, high speed platforming and fun new gimmicks every time. That said, there really aren't that many levels. Sonic Team has clearly chosen to put great effort into these select few stages and deliver longer and more meaty levels as a tradeoff. It is up to you to decide if this was a good decision. Having 100% Sonic Forces, I say yes.Bosses are also great and deliver the sceptical you would expect. These also sacrifice numbers for run time, however.Gameplay, predictably, weakens in ACT 2. While still good, playing these fully 2D stages continues to be a real bummer after the treat that is an ACT 1. I understand that it is harder and more expensive to create fully 3D stages, but you start to dread them almost as much as you do in the regular Gens by the end.Now seemingly using Hedgehog Engine 2 and Sonic Frontiers as a base, Shadow Gens is the best looking Sonic game, bar perhaps Unleashed. Every environment is rendered to perfection and cleverly updates level assets to match modern expectations. This is maybe best seen in Kingdom Valley, now given a much clearly visual direction compared to 06. And Sunset Heights is a particular highlight, finally accomplishing the destruction and action Sonic Team... attempted, in Forces. Special shoutout to the Black Doom transitions in most ACT 1's, they are all amazing. Anyway, it looks amazing.I played Shadow Generations on a NVIDIA RTX 3050, a AMD Ryzen 5 4500 6 Core CPU and 8gb of RAM with all settings set to HIGH or above.I experienced a perfect 60fps throughout, with no noticeable framedrops in any scenario. 'Nuff said.Predictably, Shadow Gens sounds amazing.  every music remix sounds great. Space Colony Ark and Kingdom Valley in particular is stellar. Sound effects are crisp and sound exactly how they should. It's not all perfect though, Chaos Island Act 1 is a real stinker, and in my opinion,  the voice acting throughout is notably poor. Gerald just being Mike Pollok again is a bit a cheap out.I've long stopped bothering to care about stories in the Sonic videogames. Any exploration of interesting ideas of concepts can be found exclusively in the Comics (Shoutout IDW Metal Virus Arc). As the name of the game might suggest, this new story follows Shadow's journey through the events of Sonic Generations. I'm not going to go into to much detail (neither does the game), but the story does, frankly, nothing to evolve Shadow as a character. He doesn't get enough time interacting with Maria to facilitate it. That said, the story is serviceable. Just don't expect no Sonic Adventure 2 (unless you expect to just  in which case, the game is sure to shove that games lore down your neck, don't worry).It's not often you can unequivocally recommend a Sonic the Hedgehog game, it's always "a step in the right direction" or "a bold idea executed wrong". This game is neither. Shadow Generations takes a bold new approach in the Sonic franchise, and is just more of the good stuff. I experienced zero glitches, zero grinding, zero artificial roadblocks and zero moments of frustration. It's a short game, yes, but a damn good one from start to finish. It's clear throughout that Sonic Team is no longer set on "reinventing" Sonic. Frontiers gave them the blueprint of what a good Sonic experience could be, and this is the evolution of that game.

_childDocuments_.review: I'll enable comments because I need a laugh and want to see who agrees or has good counter-points for some of what I am going to say here.I wish there was a neutral option here because I don’t think it is a terrible game, I just don’t think it was worth the asking price or the greatest Sonic ever made.  (I'm also going to leave out a lot I want to say not to spoil things.)Shadow is back and has his own campaign.  Yes, we finally get to have something focused on Shadow and he deserves it!The GoodGame looks beautiful!Great performance (then again my computer is a beast.)Rarely had camera issues.  (A common issue plaguing 3D Sonic games.)Radical Highway is back and honestly, one of Shadow’s best levels ever.  It also has quite a few twists in store for us!The music is awesome.  I really loved the music in this game.  But no surprise since most Sonic games have an awesome soundtrack!The BossesI actually really enjoyed the bosses for the most-part.  10/10 would go back and re-fight again!The NeutralLevel designsSome parts of the level design annoyed the heck out of me, however, I do like that they had braching paths throughout the level.  This allows you to find collectibles hidden on different paths and have a slightly different experience in each level if you go back and replay them.  I am a fan of this.Why is it neutral?  Well they give you chaos control and seem to constantly try to stiff arm you into using it.  Many times it isn't necessary, but sometimes it kind of is and it feels too forced.  I understand wanting to stress the new gimmick (a cool one at that) but don't shove it down my throat.  Ironically, I found myself wanting to use Chaos Control at times when they blocked you from being able to use it.  I am probably going to be the odd one out here, but that was MY experience with it.The Over WorldThe over world is cool and there are things to explore, but I prefer the simpler 2D oversold Sonic's campaign gets.  At times getting to certain points can be a tad annoying and it felt like doing the awkward puzzles in frontiers... which I didn't care for.  That being said, it is cool exploring the map and if you are into collecting and finding hidden nuts, bolts, and chests, you have ample opportunity to do so.  It just didn't do it for me.  Collecting the music notes also did not do it for me.  They are even worse in a 3D space.The BadMovementShadow feels slow a lot of the time, unless you are being boosted or grinding.  He just starts off sluggish to me.  But then you get this random burst of speed, as if he has a turbo engine and it just kicked in.  This can throw you off on platforming areas.Slippery ShoesMy experience with inertia is that shadow felt like he had oil on his shoes at times.  If you got that turbo boost of speed, he will just slide.  Not great if you are going for precision platforming.  The game is still playable, but it was something I had a bit of a sore spot for me at a few points in the game.Okay now I am going to talk about some of the changes they made to Sonic's Campaign...  Some of the issues I think were made bigger than they are, and to a degree I think some of the criticism is deserved.Yes some scenes where Amy is all over sonic were changed.  However, there are still scenes where she tries to hug sonic and is clearly showing affection for him.  It isn't like the washed her character completely like they did in Frontiers.The knuckles one where he talks to old school sonic makes no sense with the changes they made.  The dialogue AND the cut scene should have been changed IMO.  That was a stupid oversight on their part.  Speaking of stupid oversight... The scene where Amy is holding cupcakes doesn't even look like she belongs there.  Go back and watch the cut scene.  They did a half-assed job with it.  They should have just not had that scene to begin with.Rouge being censored.  It is a small change but it also isn't in a way.  When rouge was introduced in Sonic Adventure 2 she was made to fit a certain trope.  An "attractive" spy character that is willing to use her feminine wiles to get what she wants...  Like most things the west gets, certain things are watered down.  So yes, her showing off some of her assets is literally part of her character, and honestly, she doesn't look any worse than half what you would see going out in public...  I see people whose normal attire looks waaaay more suggestive than anything they ever made Rouge wear...  It just seems silly to me that we have to cover a little bit of cleavage and her back (which doesn't make sense functionally due to her wings.)People grew up with these characters as they were made.  There are long-term fans that love old school portrayals of these characters.  Of course those folks are going to have issues when these characters are significantly changed.  Especially, in the greater context of what has been happening with games in recent history.  Of course people will be on their guard and defend what they like.On a final note, someone promised to give me 1 dollar per clown award I receive so feel free to hate on this review.  You will be making me rich!
