_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic game.Sonic Generations is one of my favorite games, and seeing it come back with more is great. It does, however, feel like the new port is a bit buggier than the original. I got stuck on a lot more things than I remember.They made lives an option which is really cool. Then there's the drop dash.For Classic Sonic, it's a skill that is automatically applied to your skill set. You can turn it off. YOU CAN NOT TURN IT OFF ON MODERN SONIC. IT ALSO CHARGES IF YOU HOLD A, THE JUMP BUTTON, AFTER JUMPING. This basically leads to you holding the jump button, , and then charging the drop dash for under a second and getting a fully charged spin dash off the side of the stage. There is NO WAY to rebind the control either, so if you stay on legacy controls you're just stuck with it.They've also cut out a bunch of the random stage achievements which is a bit sad but I also didn't want to do them for a third time so I don't mind too much.Almost none of the gameplay improvements from Shadow's campaign made it into this port either. The game opens up a new executable when you choose sonic on the main menu, so I have to assume it's just running a modified version of the old game.All of that being said, the game still very good and worth playing. Definitely one of the best Sonic games to exist. Hope the modding scene is able to move some things over to the new version.I really liked the new story content that came with Shadow. Not only is he peak fiction, but they also made a lot of improvements to the engine and gameplay that make the experience a lot more seamless than regular Generations. Retrying has almost no load time and also keeps the music playing rather than restarting the track. A small touch but it means a lot to me personally.The cinematic and graphical presentation is also fantastic. It's got that sonic flair without it detracting from the gameplay in most cases.The levels are very fun and the movement is great, which makes most of the challenges are satisfying to S rank. I've seen people do some crazy stuff with the chaos spear ability stalling you in the air for example. This game is also way way harder then base Generations. S rank is determined by time alone, rather than just being A Rank without dying. For example, a mechanic you unlock later pretty much doubles the amount of S Ranks you have to go for as well, and the time requirement on the last level doesn't change between these modes, so you need to play perfectly to get the S.The collactible unlocks are really cool. Glad we get to see a lot of shadow related stuff. There's a lot more than I thought there could be.The overworld also has fast travel, which I didn't realize I needed until I used it. Incredible addition.I do have a few issues, namely in the overworld challenges and a specific instance of some boss fights.Some of the overworld timer challenges are a real pain to actually complete. It really just speaks to the fact that this is way harder than base Generations, but I had a lot of trouble trying to get some of these done. The challenge is nice, but the walk back across the entire hub world, even with the fast travel, when you make a mistake makes it take way longer than just having a reset button in the pause menu and makes the grind drag on.To my knowledge, the collectable locations aren't tracked in any way around the map, so all you really have to go off of is the number of the artworks you get. not to mention that there are a bunch of small items  that just add to a number, so you really don't know which ones you missed, even if you were to look up a guide.My last issue lies with a specific attack that two of the bosses have. If you've played it, you most likely know the one. I'm probably just bad, but the telegraphing really really does not help when trying to dodge this attack. It looks like it marks an area, but sometimes it's safe there and other times it isn't. I'm pretty sure that it's not actually marking the spot and just alerting you to the attack. That being said, the depth perception in the fight doesn't really line up with where the attack is going to be, so it's really a toss up as to if you're going to get hit or not.Pair this with the achievement to not get hit at all by the final boss, and said boss using this attack on the last phase with , and it really wastes your time and infuriated me. Only took 45 minutes though :))))Despite the flaws, the game is fantastic and definitely worth playing. There is so much in here to do and most of it is good Sonic fun. Edgy Cringey music, enemies that are just barely in the way that mess you up, and most of all going fast. Really can't recommend this one enough.

_childDocuments_.review: Wow! Finally after 13 years, a fantastic Sonic game! Other games since Generations (2011) have ranged from poor to ok to interesting, but I can finally safely say that this game is PHENOMENAL which I haven't felt from a Sonic product since 2011. It also doesn't rest on Sonic's foundation, it pushes the gameplay to new heights with all kinds of new moves and abilities and mechanics! I am so happy that they got a new director and team together for this project. It has everything I wanted out of a Sonic game. Fresh mechanics, expansive and layered (multiple paths) level design, great music, a touching story, and I CAN'T WAIT to replay these stages over and over and over again just like with Adventure 2, Unleashed, and Generations. I haven't been this excited to experience a Sonic game since 2011. Thank you so much to the team behind this game for making this possible, I have been waiting so long for a Sonic game to be proud of. From the bottom of my heart, thank you!

_childDocuments_.review: MINOR SPOILERS AHEAD, READER BEWARE! (If you care Sonic X Shadow Generations is a game I've been actively excited about. Having grown up playing the original generations, I was really looking forward to playing this game.And BOY did it not disappoint! The Sonic side of the game plays EXACTLY as I remember. It felt just as good to play and is an incredible remaster of a beloved game. Personally I do not have much problem with the rewritten dialogue. (Some cases I actually prefer it over the old dialogue). BUT the original story isn't what I was most excited for.The Shadow story might possibly be one of the greatest pieces of Sonic Media I have ever gotten my hands on. Tied directly with Frontiers. Shadow controls beautifully, and the small tweaks to his gameplay combined with the additional gameplay elements make him different enough to where it doesn't feel like I'm just playing as a Sonic Reskin. The story was REALLY good despite how short it was too, and I found myself excited to revisit some of these old locations from previous games. I remember getting particularly excited about seeing the inclusion of Forces and Frontiers stages, along with the addition of Kingdom Valley. (I have a soft spot for Forces in particular despite the game itself being somewhat mid.)Without getting too deep into story spoilers, the story itself made me feel so many different things. All varying emotions, but all I would count as positive. (Why must you shatter my heart, Ian Flynn? I wasn't emotionally ready for feels. D:)Sonic Team has knocked it out of the park and delivered a game truly worth price! And it makes me proud to be a Sonic Fan! 10/10!

_childDocuments_.review: Like all the other reviews, it looks great but it falls flat in a few areas that just kills me. Firstly, I hate the open world/over world concept (or at least the execution. I found that it was really difficult to find my way around and everything felt really tedious. The extra missions were fine up until I got to the forces and frontiers stages, I'm pretty sure that shadow isn't even in frontiers but I didn't play it. But the frontier stage was god awful, incredibly frustrating and forced me to use the worst ability in the game that controls terribly. The doom morph ability is just bad.How is there not a single stage from the original Shadow game?? That makes no sense, replace the forces or (preferably) frontiers stage with Westopolis or Sky troops, or hell maybe even Eggmans carnival stage, i don't care but just have something. I think the game is fine if you're not an avid fan of Shadow, most people won't care that frontiers has a level in here, most people won't feel like the controls are that bad. But so many times during my play through, I would just get frustrated because Shadow would homing attack something that I wasn't even close to, or it the squid jerks into the next dimension because I clipped a wall. I feel as though this game is made artificially difficult because of the controls and mechanics. This just isn't what I was expecting/hoping for and am now dissapointed.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Team knocked it outta the park. No spoilers in this review, as it is mostly about Shadow Generations.The music is phenomenal. If you at all care about the plot or continuity of Sonic games or Shadow as a character, this game more than does it justice. Progression itself doesn't feel too challenging or too easy, all in all a very satisfying experience. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: Final Review For SHADOW GENERATIONS: Right off the bat the presentation is stunning, every cut scene is so insanely well animated and is so detailed and smooth, such a happy surprise too see things how they should be. The colors, animation, art-style changes and the music is all top notch this time around like ALL of it. There is so much polish in all the animations in Shadow generations, there is so much attention to detail I never thought I'd see in a sonic game again. I cannot stress this enough, THIS GAME LOOKS AMAZING. The cutscenes are absolutely stunning and amazing, I cant put it into words how good they are!The controls/how it plays: Its what you'd expect, its sonic frontiers but smoother and more refined. So its very pleasant to skate around and play with the movement. Its fun and rewarding like before. I can say this game controls great and plays very well. You can customize how it plays like frontiers so you can change what you want which is always a plus. The only control issue I had was the doom powers, they were a bit hard to control, some more than other but overall I have not had any issues so far. Soundtrack: You can already guess lmao, i dont even need to say anythingStory: Im still progressing but I like it so far! A return to previous story parts and is fleshing out the inbetween parts that happened to shadow while sonic was doing his thing in the 2010's...EDIT: I finished the story and It was super fun and exciting, It was so nice seeing some characters back in modern day! I dont wanna spoil anything so PLAY IT. Gameplay: The hub world takes inspiration for Sonic Generations and Sonic Frontiers and combining the two for fun areas so explore with nooks and crannies for goodies along the way. Its fun to explore and fun to move, so its good. The stages are your typical boost formula stages but finally expanded to feel less one lane like some previous titles so there are many ways to go, so its not like your usual song and dance that you are so used too, look around you might find a new path. Theres way more replay-ability due to the level design being improved and greatly expanded. So its like the cyberspace stages in frontiers but a bit longer and better thought out. Gameplay loop is very funLevel design: This is by far the best boost formula levels in the series, I cannot give anymore praise in the quality and replay-ability. They are on par or even surpassing Sonic Unleashes day time stages, THEY ARE THAT GOOD. The improvement from forces to frontiers and now to this, They got it down now. Boss Battles: They are so good, so cinematic and thrilling, super fun to fight them. They are about as good as frontiers boss fights, not as epic but they are still VERY good.Complaints: IT IS TOO SHORT, I WANT MORE and I find the doom powers not super fun to control personally. A cool addition but I didnt enjoy them that much.Conclusion: This  review has gone on long enough so the point is that the game blew my expectations outta da water with its stunning presentation and game-play improvements from sonic frontiers. If you like sonic frontiers and generations you will be very pleased with this game. This is the best sonic gameThis is the right direction.9/10

_childDocuments_.review: TL/DR: Shadow's campaign is amazing, but pretty short, if that's all you're here for, wait for it to go on sale, because otherwise it's base Generations with more dialouge. _childDocuments_.review: At the time of writing this review, I have about 3 hours on the game (2 on the original Generations portion and 1 hour on the new Shadow stuff). So far, it's been phenomenal. The Shadow material is so well-crafted, from gameplay to presentation. The voice acting on Shadow is surprisingly stellar and the animations are so fluid and lively, packed with incredible audio design and some of the most intricate level design the series has seen so far, and it's undeniable that you'll find a great time here.The original Generations portion is familiar and safe, especially if you've played it before, but I've still been having a lot of fun exploring these remastered levels to find the newly added chao's littered throughout the stages. I did run into a few visual bugs on the OG Generations portion; however, the Shadow stuff has been seamless - no game-breaking bugs so far.I woke up at midnight to play this game, and it's currently 5 AM as I'm writing this. I have work in a couple hours, but I couldn't resist the urge to get up and play it as soon as it came out. So far it's been absolutely incredible, and the stuff I was most excited for (the Shadow material) is shaping up to be some of this series' best efforts at making the spectacle, speedy platforming experience that this franchise is known for. Absolutely recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is already a good game, and the remaster here only improves it (having the drop-dash for the classic sonic stages feels very nice and new collectibles are always welcome).Shadow Generations though, which is for most people the real selling point of this package, has probably turned out to be the single best Sonic title of all time. The Level Design is near perfect, taking everything that Sonic Generations did and expanding upon it. Shadow controls perfectly (the best controls of any game in the sonic series) and his new unique gimmicks expand upon the boost gameplay formula in interesting ways. The white space hub area here takes the ideas of the open zone from Frontiers but does it much better, with a condensed space filled with things to do and see as a nice distraction between the incredible main stages. Challenge acts are also here, but unlike in Sonic Generations these are actually fun and replayable speedrun stages (the design of some of them almost feel like miniaturised versions of unleashed DLC levels). This game is everything a boost game should be and more.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is Sonic Generations, an infallible classic (besides the classic sonic levels being somewhat wonky)Shadow Generations though is utterly amazing. Easily at the same level as Sonic Mania in terms of sheer quality. The level design is super solid, I have experienced no bugs, the controls feel AMAZINGLY tight, the graphics look outstanding, the animations look shockingly good.Definitely worth every cent.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: As someone that was fairly underwhelmed with Sonic Frontiers, I am so pleased to say that Shadow Generations might be one of, if not, the best 3D sonic games of all time. They really did it... they nailed it. It's not without its issues (second half feels a bit less polished than the first half, including even the music), and I think they could have done better to make the story more cohesive and satisfying, but WOW. The sauce is back.
_childDocuments_.name: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS

_childDocuments_.review: On the Generations side of things complaints are minimal. The script changes mostly feel a tad unnecessary and the modern version of the drop dash feels like a fairly pointless addition in practice, but the chao hunting is a fun addition, the game runs very well, and Generations was already a very good entry in the series. Very solid overall there.The main event is absolutely the Shadow content. Very tight level design that feels incredibly satisfying to navigate and optimize on repeat playthroughs with some of the best visuals this series has ever produced in the form of its reality-warping sections. Controls feel fast and responsive, and the abilities gained overtime function as fun tools to add some depth to levels. My only real issue is that I wanted more levels to play, but combining this excellent game with Generations (which is also too short in my opinion) makes for great experience with lots of bonus content for those willing to seek it out. One of Sonic Team's standout releases, excellent through and through.

_childDocuments_.review: This review is just from the shadow part of gens.The PROS:Shadow animations are amazing, they gave him so much more life in his expressions,the gameplay feels very much like generations so if you enjoyed that u will enjoy this,the levels are long, so it really feels like you get your moneys worth.The doom powers are fun to play with and add a unique element into the game.The CONS:Anyone who has seen the trailers, there isn't anything much new in the game. you pretty much get what u see. There is not any more levels/doom powers than what you have seen.coming from frontiers (which is insanely difficult) on to play this, everything felt too easy and there was little challenge. (you do unlock hard mode after completing it, but this should of been an option from the start)The writing falls flat, giving very minimal conclusions.The last boss is just a rehash of previous boss and level mechanics.I would recommend it for people who want to replay gens with a little shadow on the side, or newcomers to the series.

_childDocuments_.review: EDIT: The original review is at the bottom. I want to keep it there because the OG. stuff about Sonic Generations stands true. I just finished Shadow Generations. I loved it. The only issues I had with it is that I do not care for open world games (I loved the stages in Frontiers, did not care for the open world) and that the last level was just too much. That being said, It was definitely a solid 9 or 10 experience. It is NOT worth £50 though, unless you do not already own SONIC Generations. [or if you really want Sonic Generations again.]Preface: I haven't played SHADOW Generations yet because I wanted to check out Sonic's side first. Though I heard it's short (around 4 hours), it seems like Shadow Generations is decent but not worth the price. Also, I absolutely love Sonic or else I would not be writing this. I grew up with Sonic, I'm a diehard fan. SEGA knew that folks like me would pre-order the game, expecting changes to the original Sonic Generations. Not sure why I thought SEGA would put in any effort for this. I've played up to Speed Highway and here are the two massive changes they've done! (sarcasm)Dialogue has been re-recorded, and the direction/lines have changed. SEGA had an issue with Sonic and Tails' original conversation about Green Hill Zone & Chemical Plant, apparently. Tails no longer makes comments about the anxiety-inducing water in Chemical Plant zone; both characters instantly know where they are now. While there's a nice reference to Sonic CD's Time Stones, the rest of the dialogue feels off.Some cutscenes have been changed... barely. Now you see Robotnik being taken by the Time Eater instead of just hearing his voice call for help.That's it. Those are all the changes I could find. None of the boss fights are different. Metal Sonic is still a 3? 4? hit joke, the Death Egg Robot is still the same fight. Nothing new. At all. Launching Sonic Generations just boots up the original game. Clicking 'exit game' closes the entire thing. It doesn't take you back to the game select screen because it shuts down the original program to launch Generations instead. This is a scam. Don't pay for it now. Wait until Christmas, please.

_childDocuments_.review: Absolutely love this game. I was feeling burnt out on the boost style of Sonic games, between Force's lackluster level design and enjoying Frontiers' open zones more than the Cyberspace levels. But this game surprised me. It has some of the best boost-style levels the series has ever seen. The animation and presentation are both huge steps up for the series, too. I really hope this mix of actual, well-made levels and fun open zone hubs sticks around. It's a winning formula!Also Sonic Generations is here too.Jokes aside, the Sonic half of the game holds up really well. And if you've got a Steam Deck, this version runs so much better out of the box. The previous PC version needed mods to run well on Deck, and installing said mods on Deck was an absolute pain. I wish more had been done to actually remaster it, but the game still holds up. Having both this and Shadow Generations makes this one of the best Sonic games on the market. Highly recommend it!

_childDocuments_.review: Sonic Generations is still as good as it was before. Not much had change with it beside some small stuff like collectible chao or drop dash added for both modern and classic Sonic.Shadow Generations is simply amazing. The best 3d level design and overall gameplay. Shadow controls amazing compared to the predecessor, Sonic Frontiers, where I thought Sonic controls were extremely janky. Shadow's Doom powers are great and a better addition than something like the Wisps power ups seen in a few Sonic games. Level choices are good except for the fact that Shadow's own game doesn't get level for some reason.While I did like Chaos Island, it was a strange choice for a stage as it is obviously reused asset and Shadow wasn't even in Sonic Frontiers. Whereas something like Westopolis or Sky Troops would be better fit than Chaos Island. Still, all the levels have multiple paths and agency to make the player actually interact with the stage. Unlike something like Sonic Forces where the game plays itself. With Kingdom Valley being my favorite stage.The overworld is also amazing as I think this overworld is much better than what is seen in Sonic Frontiers. _childDocuments_.review: - The following is in review of the Shadow Generations portion of this title.An okay release. Assuming this is the result of it been ported to a newer version of the engine. The Shadow portion runs at 120FPS. With the exception of some of the transitional action scenes, which are at 30FPS. All that said, I never once saw either of them dip below their max frame-rates.Presentation is great, although boss fights feel like I'm in a on-rails interactive movie with no room to fail, with more focus on triggering flashy fight scenes than it was on the game-play itself.I will fill this review out more when I have the time.Runs out of the box on Linux.

_childDocuments_.review: SONIC X SHADOW GENERATIONS is an unpleasant case of tie-in sale. The base game isn't bad so to say, but it holds itself almost solely on fan service (it won't be half as appealing if you haven't played other entries), the final boss is pathetic and the few improvements introduced by this new version feel lazy and buggy. _childDocuments_.review: Finally, after such a long time, we have a new boost game that feels great. This game already is great enough for repackaging Generations, which has been preserved very well, keeping the game mostly intact, with a few quality-of-life improvements, and a rewritten story, which I am mixed on, but appreciate the effort. And shut up about the small edits to Rouge's model and Amy's bio + cutscene animations. Y'all ain't doin' anyone a favor. But the Shadow portion of this is the main "thing" and it is GREAT. It takes the physics from Frontiers and refines them to be their best. The Doom Powers, while still being a gimmick, are very fun to use and flow seamlessly with gameplay, and they only help, especially the Doom Wing. The level design is amazing, feeling fast and lasting the perfect time, around 3-4 minutes. And the story is written very well, and while I won't provide spoilers, it's some of the best in the series. The open world is also great, being inspired by Sonic Frontiers, with tons of collectibles that can be fun to collect. And finally, the game(s) look BEAUTIFUL. While I do believe there is a bit too much of an "aura" around characters in Shadow Generations, It still looks great, making good use of HE2 (Hedgehog Engine 2, the game's graphics engine), having great lighting and beautiful environments. TL;DR, buy the game. It's GOOD.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm loving it.Edit: I'll add (addition:) under the segments for the new stuff. I have completed Shadow Generations and gotten every collectable, all S ranks on normal and challenge stages, no hit the final boss, did the hard mode bosses w/ S rank, and got all hub challenges with a GREAT completion (gotten by have at least 10 seconds to spare when completing them).The abilities engage the player in the levels to utilize them and abuse them correctly to find alternate paths and easier ways to get through sections of the levels. The star platinum style time stop is very good in this regard, turning an object that damages you even when boosting into a platform that allows you to get to a higher route or just a 4 second time save.Addition: the extra morphs that are unlocked add another level of both difficulty and engaging gameplay. When beating the final boss you can activate Doom Mode, it just adds more challenge stages, new hub challenges, and hard mode bosses. The hub challenges REALLY put the knowledge of the hub and your abilities/morphs to get those GREAT finishers. One boss was a real test. Biolizard is mostly the same, just you need to beat him hitless, and same for Mephiles. As for Metal Overlord, it is a true test to your knowledge of the beginning section and movement to get those direct hits with the ramps. For S rank it really makes you good at the fight. Same goes with beating the final boss hitless for the achievement.There are sadly 2D stages, BUT they are very short in comparison to the 4-8 minute (depending on pace and stage) 3D ones. They are just as good as the 3D ones, and they really don't impede on the journey through the game.The hub on the other hand isn't 2D, and is actually a sizeable 3D area to explore as you unlock the transformations and abilities. It definitely is a better try at what they went for in Frontiers, and I'm very happy they didn't just dust the interesting concept under the rug and are actually TRYING to get better with the concept. (I'm a huge fan of Sunset Overdrive, and this is one step closer to getting half of its awesomeness)The red rings are replaced with tokens between 3 categories(think similar to the sun and moon medallions from Unleashed) artwork, music, and lore. These tokens are used in the hub to unlock the chests with the corresponding icon. They aren't tricky to find in the levels, but there has been one that kicked my butt trying to find. (it was in rail canyon at the VERY END, right after the twisty rails at the end when you fall down, keep boosting forward, it is on the roof of the goal ring area).Addition:The pain does not end here. In the open hub the chests and ship parts really get further as you try searching for them. There is NO help besides guides and pure luck crossing paths with them. There's an amazing guide in the steam guides for the chests. There is a video for the ship parts, but it really is annoying to watch, but it's the only one at the moment. I'd say the map shows you all the unopened chests after beating the game, and there'd be a setting you can turn on for a compass pointing to a rocket part. Those are the only ideas I've got to make it less of a pain in the butt to find.Music good as always, makes me enjoy songs I didn't listen to all that much (biolizard's theme in particular), it gets the blood flowing and really gets you into the game.Story and lore stuff is good. Like how they did in Frontiers how they took the previous games and brought them into a new context they did the same here giving a new understanding of the previous titles that Shadow was in.(also I realized that Big the Cat really hasn't met many other characters really, IDK why this was a surprise when the two meet here as he says "your name is Shadow, right?").Addition: The power scaling mfs will have a field day discussing this story.

_childDocuments_.review: Basically if you're into Sonic games I think this is a no brainer. I personally however cannot recommend this game.I have previously played the start of Generations but couldn't get into it due to the art style. I don't think 3D works for 2D levels at all for both Sonic and Shadow.I've seen a lot of reviews praising the art style but I cannot disagree more. I am a huge fan of the character of Shadow as well as the original game, but this campaign just looks hideous to me.In terms of gameplay the 3D Shadow levels are definitely the most fun I've had playing a Sonic game and are very good, however the 2D levels felt very simple and again I can't stand how they look. Additionally the "Doom Morph" ability did not feel good to me at all, but I've seen some people saying it's "hard to master", so perhaps this is just a skill issue for me.The whole Shadow campaign took 4 hours for me to complete. I have not 100% it, Running around a small hub world looking for collectibles is not a way I want to spend my time but I've seen some people praising this.The story as well has nothing going on. There is one plot point and it's resolved in the game, you can't really expect more for such a short game I suppose. It's so strange to me to see people praising this game's writing. What writing? Truly, there is nothing going on here.There's 4 boss fights in the Shadow campaign all of which are essentially impossible to lose with 1 or 2 mechanics going on. They require essentially nothing of the player. I've seen praise for these as well but they just felt lazy and disappointing to me.In terms of environments there's 6 different ones for the whole of the Shadow campaign, one of which is from Forces (no one wants to see this) and the other is from Frontiers (Shadow wasn't even in this and it looks so hideous). Absolutely insane to have 33% of environments in such a short game be like this, when there's so many from the original "Shadow the Hedgehog" and SA2 alone.Also when Shadow boosts he just flies around instead of skating, I truly don't understand this decision, skating is his thing.It's a Sonic game so voice acting dips quite often too, but is generally better than I've seen before.This game is another case of me just not understanding what it is Sonic fans enjoy. I don't know what has warranted these overwhelmingly positive reviews at the current time. Just seeing some decent Shadow levels for the first time in over a decade? I cannot see this appealing to someone who isn't caught in the weird vortex of Sonic obsession.

_childDocuments_.review: The best and most complete Sonic package since Adventure 2. Sonic Generations is just as good as it was. I loved Frontiers, but there were so many minor issues that added up and stopped me from entirely enjoying it, but this game has none of that baggage. They took all the best elements from Frontiers and packed them into a condensed game in the form of Shadow Generations. Almost every level (especially the fully 3D ones) in this game is some of the most enjoyable Sonic gameplay I've had, Kingdom Valley being an absolute highlight. The hub world is also really fun, although I think 100%ing can be a little tedious. It's a more focused and concentrated rendition of the open zone formula. The bosses are great spectacles, although are still not that impressive gameplay-wise. The story is very solid. The remixes are awesome. Honestly, the only issue with the game is just that I wish there was more of it. As it stands it's really short and I hope they continue to add DLC stages like the upcoming Movie tie-in even though I doubt that will happen. If they keep this level of polish and quality on the Frontiers scale and foundation for the next mainline title, it might just be the best Sonic game to date. Good luck, Sonic Team.

_childDocuments_.review: I would recommend this peak game to everyone in an instant! As a diehard Sonic fan since my childhood, I was sad what had happened to the franchise in the past. And even though Frontiers was definitely a step in the right direction, it just didn’t click with me. But from the day Sega announced this game I was hyped – and boy! Sonic Team DELIVERED! It was a blast playing this game. Maybe most of my positive feelings come simply from the fact that Shadow is back as a playable character in his actual own campaign! But I cherished every second of Shadow Generations. The fast gameplay, all the mechanics, the level design, the music – sure, these are already known levels and already known boss fights. But in my opinion the developers did a great job at remaking them into something new and exciting. In the end the star for me personally was the story. Without wanting to spoil anything – THIS is the care and love for the story and characters I missed for so long. The only negative thing I can think about for Shadow Gens is the length – but this is just because I had a great time and wished for more content to explore.Sonic Generations is still a good game, which I always enjoyed. Was the remaster necessary? Not really, in my opinion the original game is still fantastic for modern standards. It definitely looks great and I appreciate most of the changes they have done for the dialogue (although the old cutscenes mixed with the new dialogue feel off at some point). This game will always be good in my opinion, but after playing Shadow Generations … well for me there is just no comparison between those two. For me I wouldn’t have needed the Remastered version of original Generations. I only bought the game for the sake of Shadow Generations anyway, no reason to lie about that. But I would buy it again every day for the same price just for Shadows campaign alone, that’s just how good it was for me. The hype, the marketing, everything built up to this fantastic game. I have bet Shadow Gens in about 8 hours and I took a lot of time exploring and trying to get S-ranks. I am not done yet and I am sure I will continue to have more wonderful hours of great gameplay or just racing through the creative hub world trying to get all the collectibles. In conclusion: The best Sonic game I have ever played, period! This truly is a great time to be a Sonic fan and I hope this game continues to get positive reviews and sells good. If Sega and Sonic Team continue to follow this path, then I think the future for the franchise is very bright and I will be happy to be around to see what they can do! Buy this game, enjoy it and all I have left to say is – all hail Shadow!

_childDocuments_.review: 20/10. Very biased because Shadow has been one of my favorites for a very long time, but the game is trule incredible. All the bosses are incredibly fun, most of the soundtrack is amazing (one of the later ones is a huge miss, but the rest of the amazing soundtrack more than make up for it, plus you can just changes that stages bgm!) To top it all off, a fun overworld between stages with mini platforming challenges that let you play with all of Shadows new abilities to their full extent, while collecting fun lore pieces and artworks to the side. and that's just the Shadow Generations side!Everyone knows Sonic Generations is one of the best in the franchise, and if you didn't now you do. Now it finally has a fully functioning PC port with none of the headaches of the first time launch of the old port! _childDocuments_.review: An excellent updated version of Sonic Generations, one of the best 'modern' Sonic games (though it's over a decade old), plus a full campaign as Shadow the Edgelord. I'll be honest, I liked Sonic's half much more than Shadow's, but that's probably the nostalgia factor working on me. Sonic's levels are a lot more memorable and visually interesting; Shadow simply doesn't have the history or iconic soundtracks to work with that Sonic does. That said, Shadow's content makes up for this by being a bit more refined, having better boss fights and using some incredible dimension-shifting set pieces. It's also a touch harder than Sonic's content. I appreciate how the devs managed to make Shadow feel distinct from Sonic, with meatier enemy-smashing, teleport attacks, unique abilities and moves to unlock, and not least his power of Chaos Control. Activating this will turn missiles into temporary platforms, which can be used to reach collectibles and different pathways. You'll need your timing to be on point if you want to earn those S-ranks.One thing about Shadow's campaign that I kind of disliked: the treasure hunting in the hub world. If you're looking for everything, you'll probably need a guide at some point, because it gets so dull flying around the map trying to find it yourself.Overall, this is one of a select few games I've purchased on release, without waiting for the price to drop, and I don't regret it. Absolutely recommended for any Sonic fans or Sonic-curious people, especially if Generations passed you by.

_childDocuments_.review: Note: I haven't touched a sonic game in ages, haven't played Frontiers. I've played all other Sonic platformers except the dumbass Apple Arcade one. I really wanted to like this one.I gave into the hype and played this to inject some fresh Sonic Autism into my ADHD veins. And honestly? It's not too bad. I think my only problems are issues with generations in general: The momentum-free speed-setting grind rails, the complete lack of momentum in general in favor of pressing the "reach max speed button" just doesn't feel right. I played and enjoyed Gens when it came out, but the game design is really old at this point, and I wish they'd evolve the movement besides just boost.I feel like 3d Sonic is usually a fairly simple concept, but this time around they've used a lot of the face buttons to give Shadow cool abilities. I'm mixed on how this makes it harder to steer, though. Quick step left and right while boosting is done by sort of clawing your bumper while boosting with right trigger, which doesn't feel good. When turning without quick step, Shadow seems content to do a weird large arc instead of a sudden turn or worse, do a lengthy "hard stop" animation. This lack of fundamental platformer control is reflected in the level design, which features primarily long corridors that don't encourage turning at all, or "open-world" design where it feels more like a chore to get around than anything. There are some moments of platforming freedom, but they're mostly fighting against the "on-rails" philosophy of the Gens game design.As for new moves: Chaos Control would be cool, but the sound design isn't very satisfying. I remember Riders Zero Gravity! They can go hard with sound design if they want to! But instead, it distorts the very excellent music and most of the time I just forgot to use it. Chaos Spear was basically useless, didn't love taking my thumb off the joystick to use it. The wings: Man, I was disappointed. I thought we'd get some new movement options, but all it did was modify my boost arc for one early level, and then they get taken away. Maybe they come back later, I don't know. It really felt like missed opportunities, because these aren't tools that allow you to platform better, they're more like dressed-up quicktime events. This includes the enemy kick button, which is just Laser from Colors but easier, and while it's still as much of a quicktime event as everything else, it does feel really good to use.Overall, to newcomers to the series, it's probably fine. It's got solid setpiece moments and it's a good time generally. Shadow's pretty cool. I only don't recommend it because the controls feel clunky when compared to some of the clunkiest games in the series, the gameplay boils down to "Homing attack at the thing while mashing RT to go fast" and "Forced to do slow platforming with weird, floaty controls". It doesn't really feel like a fast platformer, more like an on-rails reaction simulator that occasionally has platforming. Even the loops (the things that have always been on-rails and are generally exciting in previous entries) feel bad when the camera just zooms out to show them instead of tucking near shadow to give you a sense of speed. If the intended mood is to make the player feel like they're going fast, then you're killing it by stopping to show shadow do a cool move without your input.If you've read this far, thanks. At the risk of being elitist: You should play Sonic Adventure 2 instead. It's a 3d platformer. It actually *controls* like a platformer. It has Shadow. It has a metagame with virtual pets. I straight up went back and played through Hero story to get my Sonic fix after bouncing off this game, and it's still way better than this, sorry. Maybe this one is better if you get super good at tryharding the movement and doing speedrun tricks. All I can say is it's definitely not as fun casually as SA2, and that game is 20 years old.

_childDocuments_.review: No more "A step in the right direction". They actually did it.Shadow Generations is a triumph. A really, REALLY good Sonic-style platformer that iterates on both the skillful, multi-pathed platforming of Generations, and the addictive open-zone style of Frontiers. The main levels all bang, and the Doom Powers are a great additional wrinkle for Shadow's moveset (though Doom Morph took me a minute to understand, but once it clicks it's good.) For the first time in a while, I was replaying these stages over and over, trying to find new paths and cut down on my times. It's fun. REALLY fun!Heck, this is even the first game in the series where all the bosses are good! They scale back the scope of Frontiers' Titans for more focused spectacle, while allowing much more mechanical complexity so it doesn't feel mindless in the slightest. The story's good and heartbreaking, reflecting on the past while weaving it into something new, and the visuals are a frankly unbelievable leap from Frontiers. My only real complaint is that I wanted more of it.Now more than ever, I'm glad Sonic Team proved me right: the base of what we have in the open-zone format is fantastic, and iterating on it will only bring good things. Looking forward to the next mainline entry, I wanna see this level of quality on original level visuals! (Though I won't lie, it was very nice seeing these biomes again.)(Oh also there's a Sonic Generations rerelease in here too. It's fine, it rounds out the package nicely. Sonic Gens is a good game, and they avoid a Colors Ultimate situation with it. The script rewrites are strange but I don't mind them. Overall, really good bang for your buck, especially if you never played Sonic Generations.)

Shadow controls very smoothly and responsively, making it fun to play, whereas in the older Sonic games the handling feels a lot "heavier" and more sluggish. The levels themselves are really well designed. They're substantially long and also substantially varied, with a number of different paths to take, lots of eye candy and cool things to discover.If you also got high refresh rate screen, this game can run at 120 FPS natively, which puts all the older games to shame with their 60/30 FPS caps. _childDocuments_.review: Shadow Generations is the game I've always wished for, ever since I got my hands on Shadow 05 back when I was a kid. It is the most polished, well optimized and well animated entry in the franchise. Also, they've done justice to Shadow the Hedgehog as a series, I can't think of a single moment I disliked the way he was characterized here. The story can get pretty deep and dark, especially if you find all the collectibles and read Gerald's journal, and when you know what is bound to happen to such an adorable character as Maria. Also, loved all the references to past games and the reused tracks, I literally recognize all of them and can pinpoint in which cutscenes they are exactly used in previous installments. All of my favorite bosses from the franchise are all part of the same game, with Mephiles and Devil Doom being by far the best for me. The presentation in these is perfect, and the overall level design is amazing. The Doom Powers are the best gimmick seen in a Sonic game, too.TBA

_childDocuments_.review: This has been my first "modern" Sonic experience since playing adventure 2 decades ago.I returned to the franchise thanks to Sonic mania and origins, so I learned to appreciate 2d sonic.So this was my first boost era sonic, and my first 3d sonic in a while (mingled with good old classic Sonic, who by now I'm used to it).Well.I got all the achievements because I enjoyed the game that much.The sonic campaign is was fun and lighthearted. This remaster was announced just when I planned to play the original generations as my jump to modern Sonic. Searching for the collectables was fun, revisiting old levels in 3d and 2d was fun (green hill and city escape being favorites of mine), the only part I didn't like was the final boss tbh. And a certain side quest involving a crocodile and musical notes.But the real treat, of course, was Shadow's part of the game. I've always loved his character and I had seen him undergo a bit of flanderization over the years, which made me sad.Based on what I've experienced from the sidelines during my years of not really playing Sonic until now, I think Shadow has not been this well written in years. His campaign was interesting, heartrending and I liked that his controls were different enough from Sonic, that jumping from one campaign to another always required a bit of readjustment. I loved being able to use all of his skills freely in the overworld and I enjoyed all the extra challenges, even if the rocket parts were a pain to collect. After unblocking all the achievements, I was even sad there was nothing else to unlock! Might do more than one playthrough, here and there, in different languages (I've played in Italian and btw, the Italian dub of both campaigns is fantastic!)All in all, 10/10. Game of the year 2024 for me. I will definitely recommend it to anybody who wants to approach sonic and to longtime fans who haven't played this yet. A delight from start to finish. Even the slowest or most flawed parts get overshadowed by everything else.Utter perfection.

_childDocuments_.review: I will focus mainly on Shadow Generations portion of this package since its the main selling point and because Shadow is one of the most important characters in all fiction to me. It is recommended that you check out Sonic X Shadow Generations: Dark Beginnings animation that's on youtube and not in the game for some reason before playing.There was a point in time where I lost all hope for this series. Having my favorite characters become a parody of what they used to be, stories that were afraid of taking themselves seriously and embracing what they were, self deprecating humor that showed to me they were embarrassed of what made me love the series in the first place... When Sonic Frontiers released my hope hasn't just been rekindled, it was in flames, and I am happy to say the fire keeps burning in my heart with Shadow Generations.  The game itself took me 5 hours to finish which I fully expected and is okay since there's still bunch of collectables to find and leaderboards to conquer until hackers reach the goal ring in 0 seconds or something. I enjoyed the story and moments that were there, but the ending felt so sudden. It feels like its missing on a conclusion, after credits scene or something and no, original Generations doesn't make up for it. Shadow finally gets a second proper gaming experience dedicated to him and him alone. This time you have a fully explorable hubworld that you can interact with, along with very lengthy main levels that are bursting with visual spectacle and branching paths. For the first time since Sonic 06, Shadow feels different to control and play compared to Sonic, they finally decided to get creative. Speaking of which, there are also new powers Shadow gets, and they're all fun to play except for one which I'll mention later.Boy oh boy the spectacle in bosses was so enjoyable to witness. Aside from Frontiers and now this, there has never been this level of ass whooping and I am all for it. Going full anime, Asura's Wrath style with Shadow is something I always fantasized and now it became a reality. I enjoyed every single fight this game threw at me and I want more.- Trailers showed everything, there's no surprise to be had here minus the dialogue between characters. - Why is Dark Beginnings not included? Why does Playstation get extended cuts while the rest of us have to use Youtube for it? What the hell guys?- Some remixes really don't land, luckily you can pick what song you want in whatever stage you're playing. - Squid. I hate the way it controls, it ruined so many of my good runs, I hate the hook mechanic it has, I don't want to git gud at using it, get it the hell out of here.- The repetitive structure of Generations lives on as you can't go stage to stage but instead have to do side content to obtain keys and it kinda ruins the pacing. These levels aren't bad mind you, I just wish it was optional. Give Shadow more games, please? He deserves them.

_childDocuments_.review: So I think since this is essentially two games bundled together, it would be best to review the Sonic and Shadow chapters separately.I'll be honest, the Shadow Generations portion is the main reason you WANT to have this game in your library. Incredible story, incredible gameplay, and incredible graphics. There were parts of the game where I was floored that the effects were being rendered in-game, and wasn't just a pre-rendered video. I feel like this is the game where Sega finally nailed the design of human characters in Sonic, and I hope this means future games will show more human/mobian interactions in their society. Shadow's input response is incredible. He moves perfectly to the buttons I press. That also means you need to make sure not to panic press every button. A lot of the levels that Shadow's story calls back to play way better here than in the games that they originally featured in. They made  actually good. The Open Zone in this game is an improvement on Frontiers. You still have plenty of freedom of movement, but the space is better used as you're not stuck in the middle of nowhere with nothing to do. The story is probably my favorite part of the game. Shadow's story is predictable, but in a good way, because you know where it's going, as well as the emotions that you'll be feeling by the end. And the ending was perfectly delivered. I would also highly recommend watching the Dark Beginnings episode Trilogy on YouTube before playing Shadow's story, as it bridges everything together, while also setting the mood of what you're getting into. If you've never played the original, and didn't get a chance to buy the original PC version on Steam, don't worry. Playing this will give you more or less the same experience. A fun mashup of Sonic levels from previous games in the series. Each level has two acts: Act one plays out like a classic 2D Sonic Platformer, while the second act plays out in 3D with it's own playstyle. Get to the goals as fast as you can, but remember to watch your step! It's a good introduction to both 2D and 3D Sonic game mechanics if you're new to the franchise. If you've already bought and played the original Sonic Generations, there's not really much different in this remaster, aside from some cleaned up graphics, cleaned up voice lines, and some input changes. A lot of it was just some quick polishing while making sure that the game itself was pretty much exactly as it was in the original. They didn't even patch some of the bugs that I swear were in the original. While that's great for people who want the OG Sonic Generations experience, it does make for a stark contrast compared to the Shadow Story, who's gameplay and graphics are so smooth that you feel like you're playing a much older and clunkier game when you switch to Sonic's story. Because you are. It'll even open Sonic's story in a separate executable than the main game. I experienced that personally when screen-sharing the game to friends in Discord. When it changed executable, it interrupted my screenshare, and I had to restart it. This doesn't make Sonic's part of the game bad, just that it's showing it's age, which makes sense as it originally came out in 2011. That being said, there are reasons to play Sonic's story, if anything, just to spot the differences between this version, and the original. Some cutscenes were altered to better fit the new script, but most of the animations remain the same, for better or for worse:  Overall, Sonic Generations does have some jank, but that's expected out of older games. It still remains one of the best Sonic titles of the 2010s. Full of charm and love for the series, iconic levels and iconic music, including great remixes of the classics.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm just going to say it, this game is a SOLID 9/10, and I instantly fell in love, and it became my favorite Sonic game. Sonic GenerationsIf you love Sonic Generations, then the remaster is here for you with some redone cutscenes. These cutscene changes include some animation changes and voice lines were MOSTLY redone and rewritten to provide continuity to the games and to give the story a bit more of a serious tone, while still keeping that goofy charm the original had in some of the cutscenes. The remaster also comes with new controls that can also be changed in the menu with the old controls the original had. I played with the newer controls throughout my entire playthrough, and I didn't have many issues with it! The game also comes with the edition of chao that you collect throughout Sonic's campaign, and they function as red star rings of sorts. Shadow GenerationsNow, THIS is the most interesting part of this package. Shadow Generations is an entirely new campaign, centering Shadow as the main protagonist of the adventure. If you loved the quality of Sonic Frontier's character animations, then you're going to LOVE Shadow Generation's character animations, just due to how expressive and lively they are, especially with Shadow. The gameplay takes a very creative turn, letting you use Shadow's chaos powers in unique ways to get around obstacles. There's also the addition of the Doom Powers, which I've had SO much fun using throughout the game. There was not a dull moment with this game. And, oh, I cannot forget the story! While the story is simple in concept, it provides an emotional story following Shadow and his traumatic past during the events of Sonic Generations, and it ended up becoming one of my favorite Sonic stories (Even though it's really Shadow's story LOL). While Sonic fans already know what happened to Shadow in his past, this campaign takes an interesting spin on things, keeping this already known story very fresh and appealing. And for newcomers looking to jump into Shadow's story either to get to know more about him or to prepare for the third Sonic movie, then this game is perfect for you! If you're considering purchasing this game and you can, I do recommend it, especially for Shadow's fantastic story and incredibly fun gameplay. And there's Sonic's campaign for some extra fun :)Edit: I nominated this game for a lot of awards on Steam! It deserves them.

_childDocuments_.review: When I make this review, I'm speaking specifically about Shadow Generations, as it's the actual new game here, and oh my god did the Sonic team absolutely COOK! This is some of the most fluid and fast-paced gameplay I've ever had the pleasure of experiencing.I will say I was not the biggest Sonic fan beforehand, but over the last few months I've been getting back into the Sonic franchise, and have been very excited and very hyped for this game, learning Shadow's lore and rewatching the Dark Beginnings prologue over and over again. I may be a ♥♥♥♥♥ for this, but the ending left me tearing up, it's just something so sentimental, something so sad yet so beautiful for a Sonic game. My only complaint is that the game could've been a little longer (4 hours including me screwing around and being stupid) but I expected it to be on the shorter side since it was a 2nd campaign to Sonic Generations.I can't believe I'm saying this so many years after my first Sonic phase ended, but I'll say it now, we're so back!!Edit: Forgot to mention; THE SOUNDTRACK IS FIRE!! And I also wanted to go a bit more in depth on the levels themselves. They do an amazing job at being these long set pieces that just look so DAMN cool (And ofc, they're callbacks to older levels and areas related to Shadow), and trying to speed through the levels as fast as possible is such a blast.Each level has many, many separate branches and paths for you as the player to take, which require you to use the new doom powers alongside your own skill to reach, and it makes the first playthrough of each level so exhilarating as you speed your way through, trying to find possible alternative paths to go faster!Speaking of the doom powers, they add quite a lot of variety to the gameplay, to the point where it's no longer just a "Hold forward, jump and press X" game, and that will definitely make me replay this game again because of how well done and unique these abilities are!Again, just want to reiterate that this is peak fiction, and that the Sonic franchise is BACK!!

_childDocuments_.review: Before starting this review I should say that my favorite 3D sonic game ever was the original Sonic GenerationsAs someone who has PLAYED that game a lot I think I can have a pretty good stance of a review of this game. First off, this game is called Sonic x Shadow Generations, this is not one game, but two. If you have NOT played the original sonic generations, you should buy this. Literally a no brainer, two of the best 3d sonic games ever in one package.Now for people who HAVE played generations before. I still believe this game is worth picking up even if you have zero plans on ever touching the original sonic generations within it. I haven't even finished Shadows campaign and I already have 5 hours logged on this game. I can confidently beat the ORIGINAL game in 5 hours. Granted, I am taking my time with shadows story, but gosh is it hard not to!!The HUB world in this game, oh my gosh. It's literally amazing, the entire hub area is like one giant open world. If you've played Bowser's Fury on the nintendo switch, it's comparable to that. I just have so much fun running around and performing my abilites doing cool stuff that I forget I can play the actual levels too sometimes hahaShadow plays fundamentally different from Sonic. He has new moves and new abilities. I have never in all my years of being a sonic fan felt this in control in game. It's seriously crazy, some sections might have you be able to take a higher path by use chaos control, or by using doom spears, or by electing to glide on the water or etc etc etc. In sonic generations you take the top path often by jumping at the right time! Not a terrible way of doing things but i think that shadow generations just absolutely crushes the original in terms of how you navigate the different paths.Oh BY THE WAY. These zones are soooooo open. I feel like there's so much room to breath, and so many different options for taking different routes in these zones. It's seriously so coolThis game is cinematic as all hell also! Nearly every single act has some crazy dynamic ♥♥♥♥ shadow will be skating around or destroying or dodging etc etc etcI don't know where the sonic team that put out sonic forces is now, but the team that made this must have taken them out back like they took out old yeller cuz it's unrecognizable from that game.Shadow Generations is the most complex sonic game I have ever played and I mean that in the best way possible. _childDocuments_.review: I have beaten Shadow's story and I've played some of Sonic's campaign and I've realized it's almost exactly the same as the last game with only a few minor dialogue changes, and I checked other people's reviews to ensure that there were no major changes whatsoever, so I'm just going to put my review out there now.We're going to start with the new stuff: Shadow's story.It's great! It's in my opinion the best 3D Sonic content we've ever gotten, and yet it has almost nothing to do with the blue blur. It looks fantastic, it plays super well, and it actually treats Shadow like a character and not like an edge lord who loves killing people because it's fun. The level design is phenomenal in this game. Every level feels incredibly unique and creative in ways that we haven't seen in any Sonic game before, making me hopeful that whatever comes next continues to add new and interesting features to their levels. The bosses are all great too, with a lot of differentiation in how they play, taking advantage of all of Shadow's abilities. Speaking of new and interesting features, Shadow's new abilities are awesome. Every single one of them plays well, is incredibly fun to use, and just looks really cool. This is the best way to differentiate him from Sonic, by having him be able to do stuff like this. I'm very sad that there's a chance this will be his only outing where he uses any of these abilities, because I want to see how they evolve as he appears in more and more games. The story and performances are all solid, Kirk Thornton is at his best with Shadow here, and while the story is good, it's also nothing to write home about. I like the character conclusion Shadow gets in the game, as it really does feel like he's finally gotten closure on something that's been haunting him his entire existence. Here's to hoping that conclusion will give him a bit of a warmer personality in future games. Not warm enough where it changes who he is entirely, but enough to where it's noticeable that this experience has made him a better person.I'd say my only real problem with Shadow's section of the game is that I want more of it. I really hope they hear the love from the fans and decide to give Shadow another game all to himself at some point in the future, because if it's anything like this, I will be there day one.Moving onto Sonic Generations...It's Sonic Generations. The game is great. I don't have much to say, it's still some of the best 3D Sonic stuff we've gotten.However, I wish they did more than slightly upgrade the graphics. Even with the slight update, Sonic's part of the game could use a graphical remaster, it doesn't even have to be anything crazy, just giving the models better textures is all that they need to do. Just look at Shadow, his model is just the Sonic Forces model with new textures and it looks great. The graphical difference makes the switch so jarring, especially because Sonic gets an upgraded look in the Shadow segments, but he doesn't in his own segments. The animations could use some work too with how fluid Shadow's are. Also, given that the bosses are the same as the original game, I wish they tweaked them a little bit to make them more fun, especially the final boss. I hate that boss. Overall, Sonic X Shadow Generations is awesome. If the next Sonic game has the quality of Shadow's sections, it will easily be one of the best games the franchise has ever produced, just as this one is. There has never been a better time to be a Sonic fan. Can't wait for the movie pack in December.Final Rating: 8.5/10(Sonic Section: 8/10 for a lack of upgrades. Shadow Section: 9/10.)

_childDocuments_.review: (Spoiler Free review)I have just finished playing the Sonic generations story of the game, and just began the Shadow Generations story of the game, here are my thoughts.Sonic generations: This part remains essentially unchanged, except for some quality of life changes. Such as red star ring counter, infinite resets, Graphical enhancement, dialogue changes, and the drop dash from sonic mania returning with BOTH playable Sonics. This part of the game is very fun and nostalgic, if this is your first sonic game you will really enjoy what this part of the game has to offer. Simple enjoyable fun with many mini side missions and cool bosses and fun stages that will really make you feel the speed Sonic travels at.Shadow generations: I have played this part of the story for only 2 hours, and this is already my favorite boost formula Sonic/shadow game. This game does everything right, controls are great, music is a heavenly delight upon your ears, and the cutscenes are stages are just jaw dropping good. This part of the game is a MAJOR improvement of other games such as Sonic generations and it really shows both graphically and gameplay wise. You WILL enjoy this part of the game. Not only do you get to enjoy these fast paced great stages, you also get an open world. Yes, an Open world. In this Open world you can talk to characters, find collectible chest than can be unlocked through collectible coins via stages and used in the gallery room, fun mini stage sections, find parts, etc. It is VERY fun to just explore this White space in the form of an open world. Now these stages in Shadow generations, are the most fun ive had with a Sonic game, (and I have 1.2k hours on Sonic Frontiers). the first stage is hands down one of the best Sonic stages. Its welcoming to beginners, and teaches u the fundamentals of this part of the story. After you find new routes, it becomes SO FUN!! Ive already played about 25 minutes of just the first stage. This part of the game requires you to play smarter if you want a better time. Using chaos control to stop time and obstacles, chaos spear to stun enemies, and so much more that makes the game play very enticing and jus pure joy. The music is pure bliss, and if you don't know much about shadow as a character, dont you worry. There is a cutscene explaining Shadows dark past, and you can find shadows story collectibles to further explain his journey up until now.My rating for this game is a 9.5/10, I simply just had such a fun time playing this, and a couple of friends of mine simply had fun just watching it. It is worth the money, you are getting 2 games with 1 being worth more. I highly recommend this game, as it's really fun, not TOO long, and replayable, so even when you finish the game, there's still more things waiting for you!

_childDocuments_.review: Who would've thought that the best 3D sonic game would be a Shadow game?The controls feel responsive, tight, and smooth all at the same time.Levels are decently long, but don't overstay their welcome, with plenty of branching paths.The small open world hub is perfectly sized for the game's length, allowing enough space to find collectables hidden around the world, but it isn't too big that finding all of them is impossible.But man, for me the highlight has to be the boss fights, which is shocking to say for a sonic game (aside from frontiers) without spoiling too much, most boss fights lean heavily into a gimmick, which sounds bad, but the way it's implemented actually works incredibly well.The Sonic Generations portion is also as good as the original, with minimal changes, and the Chao rescue from Sonic Advance 3, which was a fine addition, promoting playing levels in ways you normally wouldn't, such as purposefully taking the lower, slower path to find a Chao.While the highlight is Shadow Generations, revisiting the modern classic of Sonic Generations is never a bad time.At time of writing I have about 30 hours (played some offline on steam deck so it doesnt log properly) and have 100% completed both Sonic and Shadow generations, and I can only say:When your only complaint about a game is that there isn't enough of it? _childDocuments_.review: I'm sad the original Generations is not 120 fps like Shadow Generations. It needed it, as playing the new updated version of Generations feels so much worse. I feel a lot of hitches too, it isn't as stable as I remember it. It's a minor thing I suppose, but the most jarring thing for me have been the updated physics. Something is definitely off, because I've played so many hours of the original Generations, blast through the original levels, yet I make weird little mistakes with the remastered Generations that I never would before. It feels a little off, but not so much that it kills the experience. I just need to get used to the new physics. The rewritten dialogue is fine, although a bit wonky since they didn't update the animations to match. I don't really notice the graphical updates much personally. It might be a little prettier? but in the same way one might struggle to see the difference between "Medium" and "High" settings in any other game. The improvements are there, but the game doesn't look any different really.As for Shadow Generations, they nailed it. Wow, it feels ultra smooth, 120 fps, no hitches, and the levels are bangers. I'm seriously impressed, and this half alone was worth rebuying Generations. I think what I enjoyed the most so far, is that the level design sacrifices the speed that Generations levels provide, and trades them off for path variety. There's so, so SO many different routes to take sprinkled throughout every level, that it genuinely feels like what 2D Sonic levels in 3D ought to be. I find myself having a lot of fun exploring the new levels because of this. Sure, blasting through levels at insane speeds is addicting in its own way, but it becomes a memory puzzle that once you master, never changes or improves really. Which is fine, I replay Gen levels for the exhilaration of speeding through the levels anyway, not to find new routes. But wow, Shadow's levels feel incredibly well designed, I was worried we'd get the garbage design we did from Forces, or the somewhat improved but mostly stolen design from Frontiers, but no, these levels are fantastic, slower(but still decently fast), and just so great to explore and try many different paths/routes. I think they found a great middle ground with the boost gameplay, and giving you a chance to have control of your character and explore like Heroes or Adventure 2.It's great. If you don't have Generations, this is worth getting to experience that, and an awesome new second half.Edit: I've beaten Shadow Generations, and I'll say.. technically it took as much time as Sonic Gen would've, but that's because of a few reasons. 1. The levels on average are longer than Sonic Gen's Act 2(Modern Sonic) stages. 2. The open world hub isn't very big but it's still 3D explorable like in Frontiers.3. You're forced to do much more challenge stages to get keys to unlock the bosses.That being said, the game has less levels than Sonic Generations. Six total zones, with Seven total 3D Modern stages and 5 2D modern stages. To me, the lack of zones is less content. I kept hearing it had the same amount of Sonic Gen, but it doesn't. I guess they kinda made up for it with the hub world but.. eh? I like stages. Still, it was fun, and the levels are awesome and varied in how you go through them. The bosses are all much better than Sonic Gen bosses, imo. They're pretty fun.

name: FINAL FANTASY XVI
detailed_description: FINAL FANTASY XVI COMPLETE EDITION The COMPLETE EDITION is a bundle containing the following: Game Content: - FINAL FANTASY XVI Base Game - 'Echoes of the Fallen' DLC - 'The Rising Tide' DLC (The products included in this bundle are both available for separate purchase, as well as contained in other bundles. Please be careful to avoid making duplicate purchases.) Redeemable Weapons & Items: - Buster Sword - Curtana - 'Away (1987)' Orchestrion Roll - 'Torn from the Heavens' Orchestrion Roll - 'Through the Maelstrom' Orchestrion Roll FINAL FANTASY XVI Expansion Pass The Expansion Pass set includes FINAL FANTASY XVI DLC “Echoes of the Fallen” and “The Rising Tide” at a discounted price. *To enjoy this DLC content, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Items included in this Expansion Pass are also sold separately. Please be sure that you do not already own either of these DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI Echoes of the Fallen As the sun sets over the land of Valisthea, strange, dark crystals begin to circulate on the black market. Could they be the sinister fruit of a long-slumbering Mothercrystal—one the world never knew existed? Setting out in search of answers, Clive and company encounter a group of suspicious traders. Their trail leads them to a long-abandoned Fallen tower known as the Sagespire and the terrible secrets that await within... New Story Quest Unlock Conditions The new quest will become available after unlocking Origin as a destination on the world map and completing the quests 'Where There's a Will' and 'Priceless.' Special Bonuses - Buster Sword Wield Cloud Strife's iconic weapon from FINAL FANTASY VII. - 'Away (1987)' Orchestrion Roll Liven up the hideaway with a new background music track. *To enjoy this DLC, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Some bundles include this DLC with the base game. Please be sure that you do not already own this DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI The Rising Tide An unmarked letter arrives at the hideaway containing a request most curious: the Dominant of Leviathan, long lost Eikon of Water, is in need of rescue. To heed this call, Clive and his companions must journey to Mysidia—a hidden land under a blue sky—where they will uncover the tragic history of a forgotten people. New Story Quest Unlock Conditions The new quest will become available after unlocking Origin as a destination on the world map and completing the quests 'Where There's a Will' and 'Priceless.' Special Bonuses - Curtana Signature weapon used by the Warrior of Light in FINAL FANTASY XIV, reimagined for FINAL FANTASY XVI. - 'Torn from the Heavens' Orchestrion Roll - 'Through the Maelstrom' Orchestrion Roll Liven up the hideaway with new background music tracks. *To enjoy this DLC, you must have the FINAL FANTASY XVI base game installed. An internet connection is also required in order to update the base game to the latest version. *Some bundles include this DLC with the base game. Please be sure that you do not already own this DLC before purchasing. FINAL FANTASY XVI DEMO Play the opening section of FINAL FANTASY XVI. Save data can be carried over to the full version of the game. After completing the opening section of the story, players can enjoy FINAL FANTASY XVI’s amazing action gameplay in the “Eikonic Challenge” mode made specially for this demo. *Some content in this demo may vary from the final game. *It is not possible to save or load game data for the Eikonic Challenge mode. Data from this mode cannot be carried over to the release version of the game. About the Game The first fully fledged Action RPG in the mainline Final Fantasy series. An epic dark fantasy world where the fate of the land is decided by the mighty Eikons and the Dominants who wield them. This is the tale of Clive Rosfield, a warrior granted the title “First Shield of Rosaria” and sworn to protect his younger brother Joshua, the dominant of the Phoenix. Before long, Clive will be caught up in a great tragedy and swear revenge on the Dark Eikon Ifrit, a mysterious entity that brings calamity in its wake. Titanic Clashes - When rival Dominants come head to head, epic battles between their Eikons ensue! Eikonic Action - Clive utilizes the powers of multiple Eikons in breakneck battle! From Strength to Strength A plethora of powerful swordplay techniques and Eikonic abilities lie within Clive's remit—and it is up to you to decide which ones you wish to learn or upgrade. If you're having trouble choosing, upgrades can be unlocked automatically. Story-focused mode is recommended for those players who are less comfortable with action games and wish to focus more on the game's story elements. In this mode, Clive will automatically evade some attacks, and epic Eikonic combos can be triggered with simple button presses. Action-focused mode, where Clive's every action is controlled by the player, is available for those who are confident in their skill—or want to test it. ■Content included with this product - FINAL FANTASY XVI Base Game - “Onion Sword” weapon (Available for redemption from the System tab in the Main Menu upon reaching the main scenario quest 'A Chance Encounter.')

_childDocuments_.review: I'm giving this game a 3/5.The introduction aspect of this game is straight up amazing. However, as time goes by there are a few things that've stood out that I think anyone who buys the game should be aware of.1, The game is dark. Visually speaking. It hurts my eyes to play this game for squinting even when the settings are maxed. 2. There isn't a "comprehensive" equipment screen. You've got one build but for how your abilities can be used and its straight up  because the controller is limited and not how powerful the character should be.3. You will feel like a 10th grade ethics teacher. The characters give the same hack of a speech every fifteen minutes of game time. It's seriously padding out the play time. It's like Squarenix asked Chat GPT to give the same speech with the same keywords from fifty different characters. It's really, really bad writing. Super bad.4. There is nothing in this game that is the slightest bit interesting except the main story line at 17 hours in. I wish I did less of the side stories with the exception of the mount quest that happens in the beginning of the third act. 5. You collect a lot of gil to buy music. No. Not kidding. If you are any good you will literally never need gil for anything but music. 6. Would buy for the first time again at half price. Wishing I had kept an eye on the time for a refund for full price.
