_childDocuments_.review: 6/10One of the times I would really love a better review system in steam!The game is not bad, the story is amazing BUT...Positive: The story feels a lot more mature than previous FF games, the characters feel a bit more realistic.Graphics are pretty good and the game runs very smooth. No problems in my playthrough!Bonus positiv: Torgal, the best boi!Now the negative points:The game is FAR too easy, even if you stop upgrading your weapon mid game and don't use any trinkets it's easy! After just a few battles you already know when to dodge most enemy attacks. All Eikons have at least some strong and usefull abilities. Exploring the world is just bad! The world is empty, filled with the same 5 types of enemies everywhere and there is absolutely NOTHING to explore! The only things you find at some places are just a few of the currency or more random upgrade materials of which you already have a ton because you never need it. Side quests are extremely boring and just bad fillers. Slay the enemies at x, bring y back to the quest giver. Also the game is filled with thousands of cutscenes for main and side quests which especially for side quests quickly become very annoying! There are basically 0 rpg elements and no customization. Even weapons are boring. You have your 5 types of boring swords you can buy and upgrade at all tiems and one questline to craft the "strongest" weapon in the game, which again is just a boring linear side quest of run from A to B, slay the enemies at C, return back to A.... Eikon battles are "flashy" but extremely boring and again... EASYIn total the game feels like a movie with short breaks of run from A to B and slay the same 2 enemies again and again. Out of my 47 hours I would say it was at least 15 hours of cutscenes if not even more...I would only recommend the game if it's on sale for at least 50%It's completely linear, weak combat, no difficulty, no rewarding exploration and a good story. You basically buy a movie filled with some filler quests.

_childDocuments_.review: Review Update: It turns out that this game likes its inbuilt dynamic resolution setting. When this setting is activated, it'll use DLSS/FSR/XeSS (depending on your card I guess) dynamically on demand. All you have to do is leave it on and it'll do its magic while stil keeping the game looking great and steady 60 FPS (I capped at 60) without the abrupt variations I was having before when I had this specific setting off. Seriously, they did a very good job at the way it works without compromising graphic fidelity. I am now using the High preset, but people with a card better than mine could run it on Ultra probably. I have an RTX 3070. Something to note is that you won't be able to alternate between Quality, Balanced, Performance and Ultra Performance modes because the option will be greyed out on Auto despite using upscaling. The  game will decide how to handle it and will deliver very smooth gameplay. Just choose a preset according to your hardware. I have a Ryzen 5800X, RTX 3070 and 32GB RAM @3200 and the High preset delivers smooth 60 FPS at all time. I run the game at 1440p.I also recommend leaving RivaTuner at 0 for this game and only use the ingame cap to avoid messing up the way the dynamic resolution works in this title. Set the Vsync to 120Hz and cap the framerate at 60 ingame while using Nvidia Reflex for really responsive and smooth gameplay.Regarding the game itself, I don't need to add much. It's a great game with great characters, story and music and setting. The tone is very dark, grim and mature, which deviates greatly from what we are used from Final Fantasy games. A very welcoming change. Don't let nostalgic haters tell you otherwise. The combat is incredibly fun if you like action combat there is room for a lot of flashiness and flow if you put your mind to master it and it's very satisfying to masterfully defeat enemies. Or if you prefer to play it as a story game mode, there are accessories which will almost play the game for you as long as you keep mashing the attack buttons.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------Outdated.09/18/2024 - Massive bait at the current time of this review. Game has some serious performance issues with incredibly inconsistent framerate and ♥♥♥♥♥♥ frametime no matter what you do. If you have an average card like me (3070), you can try DLSS quality or performance, settings all on low or high, and it'll still run bad. At this point we hope SE does something about this atrocious performance and fix this bad port.Yet again, another great game pissed by a bad port.

_childDocuments_.review: I've beaten this game multiple times on PS5. It is a marvel that it exists. Every single decision, from gameplay, to design, to thematic ideas, feels as if it was tailor made for me specifically. The protagonist, Clive, looks like an average of my last three DnD characters, and his story/arc mirrors them all in various INCREDIBLY SPECIFIC ways. I am almost convinced that we live in a simulation, because if you took my mind and used my preferences to make a videogame from scratch, this game is likely the end result. "I want Devil May Cry freeflow combat!" Okay, done, that's the foundation, we hired their combat director. "Protagonist should use spells AND swords." Yep, for sure, also some of the spells ARE swords and you have like every element ever. "Story should be about brotherhood and liberty and fate." Yeah of course also childhood friend romance "Dark fantasy but not too dark." I MEAN LITERALLY EVERYTHING IS HOW I WANT WE CAN KEEP GOING DOWN THE LIST DON'T GET ME STARTED ON THE 181 SONG SOUNDTRACK YOU GET THE IDEAThe demo is free and contains the first 1-2 hours of the game, and will carry over your save data. You'll know if you want to play the game or not afterwards. The sequence is amazing and the full game has many more like it, it is not a one off experience, it fires on those cylinders constantly. Everyone I have shown the demo to (several friends, roommates, parents, etc.) all wanted to watch me play the full game and some of them did. The devs managed to merge narrative with game play in ways that astounded me, but even if you aren't the best at character action games you'll pull off some crazy stuff, the systems are vast if you wanna experiment but are also totally fine staying shallow if you'd rather, and expanded the story in such unique ways that I didn't think was possible.There are likely valid criticisms of this game, I could probably stop and name several myself, but I do not care, because to me, it is perfect. I do not often find myself writing steam reviews. I would much rather articulate myself to my friends and family; giving recommendations to people I personally know rather than strangers on the internet. With that being said, please give this game a shot. It did AMAZING critically but sold poorly due to the PS5 exclusivity. It would be an absolute travesty if a game as great as this went quietly into the night. I hope my enthusiasm and words can encourage you to at least try and demo, and if I get one person to love this game half as much as I do, I consider this review a success. Hell, even if I don't, just writing about my love for it may be enough for me."For thirteen years killing was all I knew, so obsessed with death that I never stopped to consider the lives of those around me. Lives that, I see now, were scarcely worth living. Be they Bearers or beggars, most but march blindly to their end, never realizing that they, too, deserve a choice... And I dare not turn a blind eye to their suffering any longer." - Clive Rosfield, protagonist of FFXVI, a character that shall never leave my heart and mind.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI is a masterfully-created game full of action, adventure and RPG elements that coalesce to create an experience like no other.The game is visually stunning, especially in some of the story's big moments. The graphics are certainly up-to-date and look absolutely wonderful.In terms of combat, it's a gradually-unfolding library of abilities and options that doesn't stop pouring more and more depth out to the player, which I can safely assume doesn't stop throughout the course of the game's entire story. I haven't finished the game, being only 24 hours into it, but I can safely say that the way things are structured lets you know that you'll never be at a loss for more new powers and attacks to use. I  would say the combat in this game strays from the usual of this franchise, and the developers opted for real-time button-masher slice-and-dice type of combat instead of the turn-based JRPG combat. Some similarities I can safely make are the God of War franchise and the Devil May Cry franchise, where you have a vast array of skills you can chain together in intense, fast-paced slash-and-dash combat. As I mentioned before, the combat capabilities of both Clive and his companions increases constantly throughout the game's main story campaign, starting off somewhat limited and slower-paced, with not much potential for chaining abilities or juggling an enemy with combos. However, later during the game, many options are presented to you and you can craft your own array of powers to channel depending on what you like best.There is a skill tree, although it is much more simplistic and very surface-level compared to other games in the genre. I find this to be a positive, as I would much rather spend my time playing the game than stuck in the menus trying to navigate a digital library of damage and armor numbers.The story is absolutely enthralling, with a lovable cast of characters each with their own personalities and personal stories. Clive is a wonderful protagonist with an incredible voice actor and a perfectly-structured list of motivations that shifts in a very sensible and relatable way throughout the game's story. You get to see the entire tale unfold right from the beginning and even from other characters' perspectives at times.I would draw a comparison between this and George R.R Martin's Game of Thrones, as the political aspects of the world's nations and interactions between their powerful figures, their plots and their schemes, intertwines with the fantastical nature of FFXVI's realm to create a very, very immersive story.This is only my second Final Fantasy game, having only played FF15 before this. I can easily say that this time around, the game's story and worldbuilding is on an entirely different level of maturity. It is darker, grittier, and more brutal, and the game does a great job expressing this in its cutscenes, the carefully-designed environments, and the dialogue of the characters. There is even an NPC that comes up during the main story, which educates the protagonist on the state of the world, really delivering more information and lore to the player as part of a collection of entertaining cutscenes.This game's boss fights are some of the most epic and memorable I've seen in any video game. There are amazing massive-scale fights that feel almost addictive, and really spark a flame of that power fantasy for the player. I can't say any more without spoilers, but if you're looking for some visually-stunning large-scale boss fights, you can't do much better than this game, save for maybe the God of War franchise or Shadow of the Colossus.As for performance, I am running this on an i9 with a 3060ti and 32gb ram. The game runs very smoothly often times for me, with a bit of roughness on day 1 of PC release. My computer restarted a few times when playing this game, but that issue has faded away entirely. Over the course of my 24 hours of gameplay, I've experienced only 1 or 2 second-long brief patches of FPS loss, which did not happen very often. Maybe once or twice per session, during the particularly weighty moments where there was alot to see on-screen.The only problems with this game are as follows:I find the pacing to be rather slow between the big main story moments. It's fine and dandy to run around doing normal things every once in a while, but sometimes it drags out a tiny bit and it feels a little like a chore. Despite this, the game's story uses the time it is given by the slow pacing to further flesh out the characters. Turning the bad into good, I suppose - I like it :)Loot - the game throws out new weapons, armor pieces and accesories at you, which have their own numbers and effects that can be pretty interesting. However, there isn't really any time during the game where you'd defeat an enemy and your jaw would drop because you got a rare piece of loot, that kind of joy isn't made available by this game, unfortunately. The weapons do change the visuals of Clive's sword, but mechanically, all they change is a number. It would've been nice to see some of the weapons or armor pieces being a little bit more involved in combat than simply changing around the number of damage you do in a hit, or how much HP you have, and such.There is little in the way of customization. At some point in the game, you do gain the ability to change Clive and his companions' appearance, by selecting one of some outfits that are made available to you. I find this extremely limited, and I'd love the ability to change around individual pieces of Clive's armor. That's alot to ask for, so I'd settle for just a few more outfits to be made available in the game. FF15 was the same way, but that one had quite a few more options than FF16.That's all I can say for this game. I can see myself playing it all the way through and I'm super excited for everything that comes next :)That being said, my rating for this game is a solid 9/10. If you're a fan of hacking and slashing through enemies, navigating a fantastical world with carefully-designed environments, and being immersed in a wonderful and interpersonal story, FFXVI is the game for you

_childDocuments_.review: A wonderful fantasy adventure with a focus on storytelling and characters!Strikingly beautiful visuals and vistas, fun action-packed combat with lots of abilities and boss fights - each fight feels like a highly choreographed cinematic spectacle, except you're in control.Stellar, truly incredible voice acting and music. _childDocuments_.review: Its mostly cutscenes, not much gaming. Recommending because it's still enjoyable as a game, but there's a lot of things lacking that could've been expanded on or improved. I feel like even 15 had more exciting lore to it even if it felt unfinished as a whole. This is just my opinion and thoughts so it's not very organized. TL;DR: generic plot with flashy combat. Lacks combat variation, character development, equipment variation, music variation. Interesting Eikon designs and weapon designs. Basic FF story-line of defying gods/fate, felt like a mash between 13 and what 15 probably could've been. I couldn't stop thinking about how Clive and Jill are probably what Noctis and Lunafreya should've been. But while they had more story in their relationship that made it more believable that they were a couple compared to 15,  it was still lacking in interactions that could've made it more meaningful. Most of Clive's companions lacked meaningful interactions, as they're all mostly in the infirmary or sent off somewhere. The story itself, to me, started off strong and interesting but kind of died off the longer it went on, it was just insanely predictable and generic. IMO ambiguous endings are just lazy writing as well. To me the game felt more story heavy vs combat focused, and it lacked in both. I did enjoy the game play, combat mechanics and the music, the main characters are very likable. It's visually stunning, especially the eikon designs. However, the amount of abilities you have are kind of limited...there's no variety, without using eikon abilities you just swing your sword. And you can obliterate everything with your eikon abilities, because of this I not only never really needed to simply attack, but I've also forgot I had the ability to throw fireballs for a majority of the game. I was also bit disappointed by Odin's abilities  that you get to use vs what I expected it would be with how insanely powerful he was shown to be. I feel like that could've been used as the base attack combos and they could've had something else for the eikon ability.A whole lot of gil but nothing really to use it on, Very limited amount of equipment, although I did appreciate the sword designs.The music that plays during each boss battle is the same, I feel like it would've been best used for the first fight or the very last. Speaking of boss battles, every single one had this cinematic QTE fight but it's just 2 buttons, your attack and your dodge. It's cool once in a while, maybe if they added more variation or impact, but it became dull after a while.I didn't bother with sidequests because of the one's I've done they seem to be mainly fetch quests. The game was like, semi open world? But it was dead, kind of like 15. Made me wish Clive or the chocobo walked faster.I started 16 with no expectations, wasn't really excited about it or really looking forward to it, so I'm not literally disappointed by the game or anything but it's not something I would play more than once.

_childDocuments_.review: This was my personal GOTY last year so this will be longer than most reviews I done in the past.Happy to see it on PC and be able to go on this journey again.CONS:1. Combat system becomes stale in the late game when you settle into your build. Doesn't help that there is no debuffs or elemental damage mechanics between Clive and the enemies. It just boils down to use ability, dodge, wait for cool down, and repeat. Occasionally use potions or limit break if you mess up.2. Most side quests suck. There are a few throughout the game that are good and the side quests that unlock right before the finale are absolutely S tier but the rest were just glorified errands.3. The story begins dark and a lot like Game of Thrones but eventually becomes a traditional Final Fantasy. I like this but the problem is how jarring it is because how quick it changes after the buhamat fight leading into Odin and final chapters.4. If you want to enjoy the game in Ultrawide or other small fixes then you have to install a mod, it's really simple and YT will help but it's annoying that SE still can't release a fully functional PC port.PROS:1. Music is Godly.2. Visuals is Godly.3. Voice acting is Godly, shout out to Ben Starr as Clive. Such great casting all around.4. Eikon, or summons if your a classic FF player, fights are a spectacle and a perfect blend of over the top action with story beats that lead up to the fight.Extra: I'm surprised it released as a $50 game. That and the DLC prices are worthy of their price, but I won't hold it against you if you wait for a sale. (As of 20sept2024, on GOG there is a 15% discount)FINAL (FANTASY) VERDICT:Objectively this is a 8/10 or 9 if you apply the mod and know what your going into. But my heart says 11/10. Like Elden Ring, Nier, & Wukong, I suffered post game depression when I finished the game for the first time xD immediately going to YT to watch others play and listen to the games music.I hope you give the demo a try if your even a little interested!

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing music, emotional story, compelling world and characters, and entertaining combat system.This game is one of my favorites I've ever played. The graphics are gorgeous and the voice acting is phenomenal. The gameplay is very DMC spectacle hack and slash, with lots of fun techniques you can mix and match depending on your playstyle. The fights feel rewarding, with different ways to stagger enemies, and boost your own abilities, as well as satisfying parry and dodge mechanics. While the combat system is fun, if you don't like heavily story based, cinematic games, this is not one for you. There are a lot of cutscenes, especially at the beginning of the game, and some of them get long. Personally, I enjoy them a lot, they're very artful, entertaining, and serve to give a lot of character insight and development that would very likely be less effective through other means. All in all, while FFXVI differs a lot gameplay wise from other entries in the franchise, this is by far one of the most thematically "Final Fantasy" final fantasy games to date. Everything feels epic and larger than life, and they really immerse you in the world they've created.

_childDocuments_.review: After almost 70+ hours and completing both DLC, Final Fantasy XVI is a great action, adventure game filled with great characters to accompany with you along your journey with amazing, fun combat. Not a perfect game by any means, however. I do have a few issues such as repetitive side quests, some pacing issues, and the absence of RPG elements. Again,  (even though the game-play changes every installment past FF X). Pretty much what you see in game-play videos, it's literally Devil May Cry meets Final Fantasy. If you're a DMC fan, you'll probably enjoy this game. As for FF fans, it is a departure from the traditional FF games, but I still think you'll have a lot of fun with it once you get settled with three Eikons.  I feel at times I didn't even try and still won.  I think SE/Creative Studio III listened to feedback from the base game and really upped the difficulty in the two expansions. I actually felt I was challenged in those two expansions and had fun with it.  Story is good overall. Love the tone of it with being more "mature" and dark. Maybe not the best story out of all the FF games, since there is some pacing issues where some characters are not "fleshed out" as they should be and some story elements not being explained well where you can get lost and confused. There is a feature called active time lore where you can pause and see some background information on characters, setting, etc. related to the current cutscene you are watching that can explain it to you; a bit handy at times. The main villain was okay in my opinion. The dominant villains who held the eikon's power were more interesting.  10/10. Don't think I need to go any further. Just listen to it on Spotify or Youtube Music and you'll know why almost every FF16 fan obsess over it.  I have mixed feelings with side quests. One half they can be good if you are invested in the world and its characters. On the other, it is reptitive and a grind fest. With the game coming from the team behind FF14, the quests are structured from MMO games. 'Go here', 'kill/fetch/talk/etc.), come back to the initial NPC, complete, and repeat. Maybe it is my fault since I did try to force myself to do as many as I can before I do the main quests. But how it is presented does at times bore me and make me feel exhausted. With that said, there are times I do get engaged with the characters when they reveal their dark pasts in this troubling world . I just think unless you are invested in the world of FF16, you can skip them. The important side quests are with the '+' icons where they can give you new equipment to craft, increase your inventory slots, and potion potency.  The game isn't open world but similar to FF12 where they have a batch of handcrafted maps; you can say its an "open-area" game more or less. While the areas have purpose, there isn't much exploration. There aren't any big cities for you to get lost and explore or secret mines or dungeons (besides the ones related to the main quests). I believe this is due to hardware limitations and/or ran out resources and time during development.  Performance and graphics can vary. There are times it looks magnificent and there are times it just looks mushy and frames would drop significantly. I want to think there is just too much detail at times the game can handle with NPCs and buildings that SE didn't bother making the capitol cities explorable knowing it would require a lot of system resources. Game play at least was smooth to me. Otherwise, it's a good PC port.Despite all of the issues, I still got past it and had an amazing experience with Final Fantasy XVI and I consider of my favorite FFs so far.

_childDocuments_.review: So without spoilers: Music: 11/10 the music was so well crafted that it enhanced the experience of every encounter and it made me feel so many emotionsStory: 9.5/10 The beginning was a fantastic introduction to any game I've ever played, it did kinda fall off a little at the end but it was still such a beautiful story, one of the best that I've played however I haven't played many final fantasy games so take from that what you will, as someone who reads a lot I definitely enjoyed the story despite some of the hiccups/ambiguities that plague it. Characters: 10/10 the game did a fantastic job of getting you invested in the characters, I loved, and hated with such strong emotions Combat: 7/10 I like the combat but it feels a little clunky at times despite having a consistent 200 fps while running the game, the combos that you can make and the feel of the combat is good though, if you like a devil may cry type of combat then you would like it. Visuals 10/10: The game is beautiful, the screenshots that you can take are full of potential, the beauty of the world and character models is just chefs kiss, if you love stunning visuals and want to make many cool desktop backgrounds this is definitely a good choice. Gameplay/RPG elements 4/10: ngl I wasn't the biggest fan of this, there wasn't a lot of loot, item upgrading felt pointless, and many things that were just there just to be there or just a lack of things that would make some of the best rpgs. The world isn't open world which is fine but it is pretty restrictive on where you can go unlike ff15, to me the world felt kinda dead but I think that's what they were going for, spoilers if I explain what I mean by that. the next part is a pseudo spoiler so please skip this if you don't want to get an idea of what the ending is like:  Overall I give this game an 8.6/10 if you want a story that will make you feel a myriad of emotions while having decent combat that makes you feel as if you're kicking ass, then I recommend it, personally though I would probably wait for a sale as there are probably much better games for your dollar. But the dollar aside, I enjoyed the game and was definitely worth the years I spent waiting for this to come to pc.

_childDocuments_.review: PERFORMANCE: Dunno if the updates have helped, but at least for me on my pc (13900k and RTX4080), the game is running splendidly, around 80 fps at 4k, and then turn on Frame Gen, and i get 120fps or more at 4k max settings. I would recommend taking a minute to install the FFXVIfix mod to fix any strange hiccups with cut-scenes and to unlock some extra settings. GAMEPLAY: Now performance aside, this is a REALLY good game the combat is a somewhat more streamlined version of Devil May Cry 5, it might be a bit sad that there is only one playable character, but with how the game goes its something you can get passed, the giant monster fights are EPIC BEYOND EPIC! seriously worth the price of admission, the story is great, the dialogue is really good, and graphics are beautiful. so really the only mild complaints is that other than some optional quests and fights, the game is rather linear so while the world is rich you might be left wanting for some more adventuring. OVERALL: I think this game and FF7 Rebirth are a return to form for the FF franchise despite the game play differences, the dialog is good again, the story is fleshed out, the fights are epic, and the characters are likable (and unlikable if they are meant to be) this particular entry is fairly grim with themes of slavery and a land that's formed around exploiting others for convenience or religion. not to mention a pretty high death count relative the series for named characters. also pro tip while many of the side quests are rather mundane, a few of them are pretty good, and none of them take too long. so give em a go. 8.5/10

_childDocuments_.review: Amazing story, keeps you on the edge as well as providing joyful and happy moments. I enjoyed the story across the whole game. Absolutely worth giving it a try, you probably won't regret it. I was playing on story mode, combat felt not very good at first, but got much better through the game. Has some space for build-diversity and gives you a choice of a playstyle. _childDocuments_.review: Solid action gameplay and impressive (at times epic) presentation. The RPG elements are reduntant, the cutscenes are ample and boring, and the side quests are a chore.Overall, the tedium of this game (that also probably inflated its budget way beyond necessary) can be skipped, so I won't hold it too much against it. I had fun.Also, all the usual suspects of the Final Fantasy franchise are of course here as always, and it's cool to see them adapted in a fresh way.As far as technical issues go, I only experienced the game getting laggy a couple of times towards the end, which was solved by restarting the game.

_childDocuments_.review: The game does two thing right, boss fights and music. From Dragoons and Ninjas to Eikons each fight was fun and engaging and Soken never misses with his music (we'll just ignore that one song in Dawntrail). Unfortunately it suffers from the CBU III curse. If you've played Final Fantasy 14 then you're familiar with it. The whole Talk to NPC A who sends you to NPC B who then sends you to NPC C who then sends you back to NPC A, then you get to travel to a spot and MAYBE you'll fight 5 monsters who go down in one combo (This is actually becoming more prevalent in newer FF games although Rebirth kinda eased up on it). I'd say wait for a sale before buying this game.

_childDocuments_.review: The very definition of wasted potential. The cool moments are really cool but the moments in between are a massive drag. It has all the ingredients to be a god tier game but is held back by sterile game design that offers the player little freedom to do anything outside of what the developer wants you to do and ends up more feeling like an interactive movie than a video game. Suffers from many of the same design problems that they do in FFXIV like god awful filler quests during the main story, half baked characters that get no development, and unimaginative encounter design that just consists of throwing trash mobs at you a few times followed by a boss. Still a cool experience but I think has little replay value.

_childDocuments_.review: I know I am only about 14 hours in at the time of writing this, but I absolutely love this game. I love to play these type of games and get fully engrosed in the story, starting to care for the characters and the world. I also really love Clive, he is not this stoic "doesn't-speak-much-and-just-looks-menacing" but he has character, he has empathy, he is caring and his voice actor did an amazing job capturing the hurt he went through, you can hear the absolute anguish in his voice in some scenes that just had me hold back some tears. Overall I love this game and would recommend, if you are not much of a story-typ of person than maybe look for another game. _childDocuments_.review: A beautiful game with an intriguing storyline. I normally dislike games that are heavily on rails and prefer more open world games, but this game builds a nice balance between the two. No grinding, both a story mode and an action mode, and the people that rebuilt the controls for keyboard/mouse did a great job.  This is an excellent port.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: I really enjoyed Final Fantasy XVI. The story was INCREDIBLE, and the ending was so good that it's going to stay with me for a while.The music was perfect and the boss fights were mostly great, and I noticed the combat had a similar feel to DMC. After finding out that the combat director for this game also worked on DMC5, it made sense why the fights felt so good.This was my first Final Fantasy game, and I decided to try it because it was different from the previous ones that never really caught my interest. Now that I've played it, I'm definitely going to check out other games in the series.On the downside, the side quests were pretty repetitive and got annoying over time. It felt like you were stuck in a loop of talking to NPCs and running errands. Also, the game wasn't well-optimized for PC. I had lags, freezes and slow startup times.Despite the issues, it was worth playing, especially for the story and cinematic experience. It felt like watching a movie.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: Fantastic story and great game play. Long time Final Fantasy fan here, and this definitely takes a spot in my top 5. Without going too in depth with a write up, I'll leave it at a 9/10 story and 8/10 gameplay. I plan on playing the DLC now that I've completed the story once through. (I didn't do much for side quests as I don't have much time to game these days) I only wish that Square Enix had released this on PC much earlier. I refuse to buy another console for a single title release.Edit: Now that I've reviewed some of the communities reviews, I've found that with what left most unsatisfied, actually made the game more enjoyable for myself. I'm also incredibly surprised that many of you still think FF's are turn based. LOLOpen World: I dislike the overuse of "open world" games and with how FF16 flowed, I felt like it was a breath of fresh air. I could experience the story at the core without dealing with any fluff or wasted time traveling back and forth across previously explored areas. Why waste time developing an open world when most quick travel anyway? They did a fantastic job making the world feel large without integrating open world. I couldn't be happier with the outcome. Side Quests: Another awesome point is that the side quests are quite literally side quests. You aren't required to complete them. I don't care that a fisherman needs help finding rare bait to catch fish to feed his family. I want a straight to the point story and Square did a great job making that happen without forcing you to run endless quests for the level grind. Yes, some of the main story quests do have you do a few simple material gathering, but what RPG doesn't? They kept it short and sweet.Acting: The voice acting and even character models were incredible. I played on max graphic settings which I feel is a must for this game. If you aren't, you are going to miss out on a good bit of detail. With that being said...Visuals: The visuals are absolutely amazing. (Again, playing on a brand new PC at max graphic settings 4070Ti I9 14k etc) There are no laggy or stuttering bits. The game runs incredible assuming that you have a PC that can handle it. Your 1070 won't cut it this time. They say the minimum is a 1070 with an I5 but what they really mean is an I7 with 2080. Even that might not be enough to run max settings and get the full seamless experience.Story Development: The story starts out small and increases in scale as you progress. If you've ever watched Gurren Lagann, you will see a similar scale progression in FF16. I found this incredible. Yes, there are some slow points in the story. No, it's not 100% action packed. But if you have the patience to appreciate the dialog, character development, and the time to sit through cutscenes, you will most likely enjoy the story. It's not a Call of Duty. It's not Devil May Cry. It's Final Fantasy, and Square Enix kept it classic for this one. I for one greatly appreciate the consistency.

_childDocuments_.review: Honestly, after XV, I was a bit wary about what the company would release after, but playing this has alleviated those concerns. While some will forever want either turn based or ATB combat, I'm perfectly fine with action style fighting, especially since this doesn't seem to have bugs during combat, that I've found. The story feels fleshed out and complete, and not in any way rushed. And honestly, I'm happier with a less open world setting. Doesn't feel like I'm running around an empty sandbox, but it also doesn't feel like driving down a one way street. I do wish there were more opportunities to do the Eikon battles, but understand from a story perspective why they wouldn't have more of these. And I can probably satisfy myself by going into stage replay for this.Won't give a rating, but I do think if you like RPGs, this is worth playing.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who was a fan of the old turn based Final Fantasy games, a part of me wanted to pass on this just to discourage them from going in the action combat direction. But ultimately I decided that was kind of a lost cause, and decided to buy it anyway. What Final Fantasy XVI ended up being to me was an RPG with some rough spots, but ultimately ended up being an incredible experience. I will say up from that this game is not for everyone, so I'll start with the negatives. If you're the kind of person who skips cutscenes and wants to be hitting buttons as often as possible, you'll probably be frustrated with this one. The combat loop is pretty satisfying when you do get to it, but I wouldn't really consider it that special. It's just decent action combat in an RPG, with some decent boss fights. Some of the side quests get pretty tedious, and if you're a completionist, or the kind of person who likes to do these kinds of quests to have more time in the game, some of them can really drag. I also can imagine people having PC performance issues with this one. I used this game to test a new midline 1440p build in 2024, and while the game ran fine for me, I could see people with older hardware having a tough time.What really carries this game is the cinematics, story, characters, and worldbuilding. This is easily one of my favorite Final Fantasy stories to date, and I think I enjoy it more than the Shadowbringers expansion of FF14, FF10, and FF9 (my favorite FF stories before.) I was quite invested early on, and the main story did a great job of making it feel like the world was worth diving into. It tackles some uncomfortable themes, but does it in a way that's ultimately compelling and adds to the experience.This game ended up being something pretty special, and considering the price point, is definitely worth giving a look. Going forward this will be the game I compare other narrative focused RPGs to.

_childDocuments_.review: While the story of this game is very rich and immersive, I would recommend waiting for an optimization patch before truly investing yourself into this game. My PC meets all the recommended requirements but after every "fix" found on youtube and reddit, the game is playable for about 15 minutes before the frames completely drop again. I can restart my pc, try a new "fix" get 144fps for about 15 minutes until I change areas or start a boss fight before the frames crash again. It completely ruins the immersion of the game. Very unfortunate as the story and game play are both wonderful. Highly recommend the game, just don't ruin your initial experience until they optimize the game better.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has played every main FF title and most of the spin-off titles, I have to say that this one did NOT disappoint! Yes it is different in many ways from the traditional formula and I personally found that to be refreshing! One of my favourite changes is the pace of the game: no slogging through huge dungeon areas with repetitive environments! It's in and out of one area and onto the next!Voice acting was SOLID the whole way through! The amount of spoken dialogue is insane. The music is some of THE best in any RPG out there, as can be expected of a Final Fantasy title.The environment itself is so well detailed. Even upwards of 70 hours in, I still found myself stopping to look around and admire everything! Look up at the sky to see birds gliding off into the sunset, look into a stream to see fish swimming around (and there's no fishing in this game, they're just there for cosmetics). The Rising Tide DLC being the most beautiful parts of the game I thought.It's EXTREMELY well optimised for PC which is great! I did have to download a quick fix mod for the cut-scenes to run at 60FPS but other than that, it just works well as is. Rising TIde DLC was doing some odd light flickering here and there but nothing terrible.When I play games for more than 60 hours, I can get pretty burnt out sometimes. Not with this title! I attribute that to the previously mentioned pace of the game as well as the fact that the fighting in battles felt great! I never once felt like I had to grind for levels or even that I had to fight everything along the way.If I had to choose something to nitpick, it would have to be the whole equipment and currency integration. You can forge and upgrade equipment and find some (rarely) in treasure chests along the way but each piece of equipment is only marginally better than the one before it to the point that you could easily just not forge anything at all and survive simply on the Eikon weapons you unlock after boss battles throughout main story missions. I didn't change up my accessories at all in between 8 hours in to 65 hours in and I was doing just fine power-wise. Gil... what is it good for? Absolutely nothing! Except for purchasing the wildly expensive music records and the odd potion or two if needed.FULLY recommend this title!

_childDocuments_.review: Beautifulest things first: the presentation is sublime, it's one of the best looking games released to date. The world is gorgeously detailed, the effects are a complete pleasantry to the eyes, the cutscenes are very well composed, the characters look amazing, and the battles, the big battles, are the most cinema in gaming.Playing this game is a joy, for the most part. With a different take on gameplay, only a bit similar to Final Fantasy XV's, Final Fantasy XVI feels like a Final Fantasy take on the hack n' slash genre with souls vibes, it's the most fun I have had for quite a long time. Standard battles are already fun, even more so with how many abilities you can learn and equip, but the boss battles are its own beast; timing your attacks, your dodges, parries, learning your opponent's moves, and making the most out of your magic, it makes you feel like a dominant. Adding to the epicness of it all, the Final Fantasy's all time trademark, the soundtrack, the gorgeous tracks that not only fit perfectly in the game world but are also a callback to the history of Final Fantasy, as an innuendo from previous titles and as a celebration of them, which completely turns this experience into something special.Final Fantasy XVI tells a story of magic, a story about humans with a predestined fate, a story of war, of loss, of hope. The story is enticing and overall exciting, and the characters are quite interesting, being able to see their relationships evolve and their growth as the story progresses, it makes it so much more emotional. Although some moments feel like filler (few of them and quite spaced out), the pacing is much improved from previous efforts (looking at you, Final Fantasy XV), and it's presented as a living tale, as if you were in a movie, sometimes watching the amazing cutscenes, some other times playing what feels like a great looking cutscene.There are some caveats to the experience, with the less animated cutscenes feeling much less polished and some dialogues looking a bit weird, and, most of all, the lack of RPG mechanics in this RPG, with only a handful of items and equipment and not much of a reason to try leveling up. Although there are some nice additions which, while unexpected, are very much welcome, making the lore and overall story more accessible and helping those who may forget some details (or those who may come back to the game later).Regarding the PC experience, this is a very demanding game which provides a very inconsistent experience throughout the different areas (with some running fine and others very poorly). The settings don't make much of a difference in regards to the framerate, but they can help alleviate some "symptoms" if the hardware is not quite up to the task, such as minor stutters while loading the areas or the fps drops in highly populated areas. Using dynamic resolution is recommended to have a mostly fine experience while retaining the graphical fidelity of the game, even more so with a graphics card compatible with DLSS.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: Preliminary review on "mid-tier" PC (RTX 3070/i5-13600K) It is a much smoother experience compared to the demo but it remains a port of a PS5 game that the PS5 itself struggled to run well.I got a stutter-free experience getting to the town of Lostwing (2-3 hours in) on the game's recommended settings with dynamic resolution and DLSS so the shader compilation seems to work. Cutscenes are 30 FPS and there is a mod to unlock them, but they're 20% more demanding than regular gameplay, so I decided to keep it 30 because my GPU can't handle it at 60 FPS.I got a 60 FPS experience 95% of the time, you will get drops when it comes to towns with NPCs and effects like volumetric fog. Fights with multiple enemies will also get me around the 50s, but one-on-one fights and bosses are a solid 60 FPS for me. Frame Generation will take care of these drops, but I also didn't mess with the other settings to see if I could gain performance elsewhere. Any GPUs above mine should be able to get a solid 60 throughout.All in all, it's pretty much behaving like the PS5 version, it's demanding where it was demanding on PS5, but I get much better performance and image quality so I don't think I'll go back on the PS5 now. No more walking around at 40 FPS in performance mode, and 720p resolution during combat.The game is gorgeous especially at night time, I recommend enabling HDR because the game was made for it, and if you don't have HDR, crank up the brightness to a 7 or 8 to see better.You get a practice room in the game and I recommend trying it out at least to get a handle on magic burst (pressing timed magic button between each sword slashes). There is an option there to show burst timing, which will flash red any time you can do it, and there is a timing for virtually every move you make, such as perfect dodging (try doing melee then magic after a dodge, I didn't know about it until way later lol). I also recommend getting your base ability kit like stomp, and mastered charged blade and magic. These moves allow you to chain things together so fluidly and you will work towards getting better at it from the jump.So far, it's pretty good, better than other Square ports but not as fancy as FF15 with all its options. For some reason Square is terrified to include a hard mode from the start, so I recommend to challenge yourself to not use potions and/or to downgrade your equipment if you find it too easy. Waiting for a difficulty mod to fully jump back in. I recommend reading other reviews to get a bigger picture too

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10 Main Story with some 6/10-ass side content. Side quests are a long and drawn out series of cutscenes with little substance and even less rewards. Hunts are fun but literally all of them are reskinned enemies which is disappointing to say the least.Main story is incredibly good however and has some of the best setpieces and fights in the whole series. Music is top notch and combat is slick and satisfying. Base game's a little on the easy side and I wish they'd let you play the Hard mode on default instead of making you finish a playthrough to unlock it but it's whatever. Runs like a dream on a 4070 ti at 1440p, had some minor stuttering with DLSS3 on but fortunately the FSR3 implementation here is actually really good so I'd recommend that as an alternative if you've got a card that can use it.But yeah definitely recommend just doing the main quest and maybe a handful of side quests and calling it there. 100%ing the game is kind of super boring and doesn't feel satisfying at all. Still a very cool and good videos game tho.

_childDocuments_.review: As a FF veteran I have found this 'game' severely lacking.It is NOT a game, but a minimally interactive movie.  In the first 3 hours of 'play' there is about 15 minutes of cut scenes for every 3 minutes of interaction.And in the next 5 hours, it is about 50 / 50.  Usually just running down a path.The guardian force battles are 99% cinematic and little more than pressing 'X' on demand.There is no real decisions for the player to make.  You go where they tell you.  Side quests only available at certain stages.  And run in circles in a valley hoping to farm APs to buy skills.If you like being *told* a story, this game is perfect.But if you want to be PART of the story, then run away.  Run fast.And this is the crucial difference between this FF and all others.  I don't feel like the story/fantasy is unfolding around your game play, it is simply being recited.  I would happily return.Really only playing because it hurts wasting the money, and not for enjoyment.
_childDocuments_.name: FINAL FANTASY XVI

_childDocuments_.review: The game is definitely a slow burner, looks decent enough, but the combat is quite dull. It wants to be an action game but doesn't have the fluidity (or the difficulty) to be challenging in any real way. It looks flashy, but there's not much more to it than that.In many ways, I don't think there have been any meaningful lessons learned from FF15 (or previous games), either. Both in terms of story and combat. There's a general feeling of an incomplete combat system, and it's so weird that those two games suffer from generally the exact same problems. There's a lot of hand-holding too. And I mean a lot.It is also a game that has a significant amount of side reading required to understand who is who, what is what, and why all those things matter. If you're going into the game cold like I did, you really need to get to the hideout, unlock the library, and then spend some time trying to understand all the puzzle pieces.Overall, the style and presentation is also puzzling. It very much has a veneer of Final Fantasy 14, but somehow doesn't quite have the same charm. There's no sound when levelling up or completing a quest, making it feel incomplete and out of place in this universe. There's voice acting, except when you're doing side quests, where you get the first introductory line and then just classic grunts etc. Which is fine and all, but this is meant to be Square Enix's poster child, the cream of the crop - I don't expect corner cutting here. Again, it weirdly feels like I'm playing FF14 offline with an action combat mod (that's not very good).In some aspects, this game feels like it came out in 2014 - not 2024. It feels like an older game, far older than it actually is.And if I've upset you so far, wait for this next one.It reminds me of Final Fantasy 13.And I finished all three of those games!There's a lot, and I mean a lot, of what boils down to an endless amount of hallways. In a big forest? Actually just a hallway. In the open plains? Hallway. Desert? Hallway. Castle? Hallway. Okay, fine on that last one, but it gets old pretty fast. The movement also feels eerily similar to FF13 too, it's this strange floaty sensation where it feels like there's no weight to anything. Jumping is especially comical. Can't believe that made it to the final production.And don't get me started on the quick time events - this is another reason as to why the game feels way older than it is. They feel so out of place and awkward. Additionally, there's some very clear moments that are designed specifically for the PS5 controller and its original exclusivity. You're not just pressing X to open a door, son, you've gotta press X and then 'force resist' the R2 trigger. This would be fine in moderation, but there's a point where it feels like they're hitting a PlayStation quota.Another mark against this game is the absolute brain-dead AI. Both in terms of your party, and the enemies. Your party will stand around whilst you've staggered an enemy, doing nothing. The enemy will also stand around as you smash their allies, almost if they're stuntmen waiting their turn in a movie. Kind of hilarious that they even give you items that trivialize all combat, too (I immediately discarded them). I wish there was a very hard mode or something to give it a sense of challenge... or, you know, a completely reworked combat system.Performance is kind of a mixed bag. It's mostly fine (RTX 3080) at 4K, but there's definitely room for improvements, which I expect to be released in the next few weeks.Overall, I think this is a decent buy on sale. If you're kind of mixed on whether to get it or not, I'd strongly suggest Black Myth Wukong over this if you want a brand-new action game, and wait for the likely winter sale reduction. A 10-20% price reduction would probably be a good buying point.If I could leave a mixed review rather than a negative one, I would. I think it's just fine, but for Square Enix/Final Fantasy you kind of hope for something more epic. At this point, I think their subteams are actually their best teams, i.e. Team Asano and so on, producing Octopath Traveler and similar games.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally a playable release of FF XVI!Tried to play this on PS5, but it was unbearable, both performance mode and quality mode just ran poor and looked worse.Finally, albeit on a 4090, I can reach decently high frame rates, at max details using frame gen and DLAA.Sadly DLAA seems to cause some blur on the plains where there are a very thick layer of grass that moves, that aside it looks perfect.Combat system is ok at first and get's fun once you unlock enough "powers" (let's call them that to avoid spoilers), if you played the demo you know what I mean, however, to be fair, it takes a long while before you get to that stage.World looks awesome, as you'd expect from a Final Fantasy.Your objective and what you do sort of changes during the story but overall I think it evolves nicely at least up to the point I got to on PS5.The only thing that I kind of find weirdly disappointing is how the soundtrack abruptly cuts after you defeat an enemy or a boss. I mean, the music in itself is great, it's just the switching between tracks that kinda kills it for me.It Nier Automata did an awesome job of switching OSTs this game is kinda subpar. But hey, no game can be perfect I guess.Loading is blazing fast on an NVME, I mean, I've always had an NVME, but this game in particular is extremely fast, from a cold boot into a vast area it takes about 3 seconds to load, no pop-in afterwards.To travel location to location often it takes even less than that. Not sure if it's due to the magic of direct storage or what they're doing, but this is faster that Demon's Souls Remake load times on PS5.Glad it's finally on PC and I must say, so far I'm very satisfied with the port, haven't encountered a bug or any issues yet.

_childDocuments_.review: Would recommend as an "interactive movie", not so much as a "game".I recognize and accept FF16's mainstream popularity and acclaim, however, as a diehard fan of the series, I have never been more disappointed by a mainline title.Disclaimer: Keep in mind I am only reviewing New Game (Action mode) til ending with DLC.Whatever happened to the 'fantasy' in "Final Fantasy"? Why is the theme getting more realistic and 'modernized' devoid of creativity/originality?I realize there are still monsters, magic, and chocobos, even the fact that previous titles have also taken much inspiration from real medieval history, but Final Fantasy used to be so much more unique and fun. Heck we don't even have a functional airship in this one.World setting and theme aside, what about customization?Pretty much everyone only uses swords in this FF.Crafting (if you can even call it that) is so linear I don't even see the point of belts and bracelets nor the useless surplus of materials.Only thing worth getting from vendors are accesories and orchestrion rolls. Can you believe it? ORCHESTRION ROLLS that literally serve NO PURPOSE besides being a gil sink, if I want to listen to music I go to YT.Abilities that you can spend points on to level? Except you're limited to 6 so extra points are rendered useless, not to mention there are only a few abilities worth equipping your precious slots.Why design so many accesories with minor ability buffs when you can only equip 3 at any given time, when instead it would've made more sense to make us spend extra AP on them?Side quests are also boring, but I guess it's what you'd expect from team FFXIV. Don't get me wrong, I appreciate lore and story but using dialogue as a medium throughout most of these side quests gets real tiring - especially with this level of language (really, can we stop trying to be too fancy with words).Last but not least, my biggest gripe with FF16 is its difficulty.I wish we could've had difficulty on the level of FF mode AT LEAST, from the start.Seriously, action mode was already SO. DAMN. EASY. AND FORGIVING. by the time you reach end game with your full kit, bosses have long became just another chore to unlock the next cutscene.Really guys, not only do you give us a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ of potion capacity but you even refill them to FULL after a single death? There's literally no punishment?Also what's with the non-centered camera???I wish we can have another PS1 Final Fantasy...

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI: A great tale of a character's journey.But I do like to judge it in 2 different fronts: Story-wise and Gameplay-wise.First, and most importantly, Story-wise. I say Story is the most important because it's the major point in the game, and what will make you want to finish the game besides some shortcommings.It's great, but it's selfish.What do I mean by this? It's an absurdly great and epic tale of a character Journey. And I mean a single character: Clive.The game focus heavily on Clive, and Clive alone. Are there other nice characters? Yeah.Are there some nice moments with them? Yes.But due to the game's lack of a party system, you don't feel that typical party connection you feel with other Final fantasy games. You don't feel attached to many other characters besides Clive and maybe one or another. Mostly because not only you don't play with them, but they can also constantly leave and join your "party" depending on where you are in the story.This makes you focus on your attention mostly on Clive. But I'll say it, Clive more than compensates for that. It's an amazing character with one of the best Final Fantasy journeys I've played.Now, gameplay-wise. I'll be far more critical.It's fun... for a couple hours.But the gameplay loop can become really repetitive, due to how simplistic the combat is.In a Nutshell, you mash Square+Triangle+Square+Triangle+Square+Triangle+.... and ocasionally use eikon skills and dodge atacks. That's literally it.It's ok. It's quite satisfactory for the first hours, but the gameplay loop can become quite tedious after a while, especially because it's a really long game.Mostly because the Eikon skills are "boring".The biggest difference lies in the basic skill: one has a dodge, one has a block, one has a grab...But the combat skills are too samey. "Your Damage skill number 1, 2 and 3". The difference usually being if it focus on damage or stagger.And the open world can be really empty and tedious. A vast and pretty map, with nothing but the same bugs, plants and wolfs you find all the time. The only difference is that you can ocasionally find a hunt-mark, a.k.a. boss battle, with a different enemy for a change. You gain nothing from exploring the world. The only RPG aspect in the game is your level up system. And nothing more. There are no build paths, class system or anything like it. You are completly stuck with one kind of gameplay with no branches at all. Your itens are literally: Sword, belt and wrist. Do the itens give anything different? Defense and Health. Just pick the one with higher value and that's it.I feel like the gameplay part of the game, although not bad per se, feels  really repetitive and lackluster, and lacked some serious polishing.It simply feels good *enough* for you to play 30/40 hours of it and finish the game.So, do I recommend the game? Yeah. It is a nice game. A amazing story with a "okayish" gameplay system. Honestly, I think this game deserved better.But still, even though I might sound a bit negative, I did have fun and I did enjoy it. But... don't pay full price. Wait maybe for a nice promo, or share the game with your steam-family friends.

_childDocuments_.review: Story line: 9/10Final Fantasy XVI offers a captivating narrative set in the war-torn land of Valisthea. The story follows Clive Rosfield as he navigates themes of duty, sacrifice, and revenge amid political intrigue over the powerful Mothercrystals. The character development is strong, and while the pacing can be uneven at times, the deep lore and emotional engagements keep players invested in the unfolding drama.User Interface: 8/10The user interface is sleek and user-friendly, allowing easy navigation through menus and HUD elements that don’t clutter the screen. However, some sub menus could use better organization, making it occasionally cumbersome to find specific items or skills.Battle System: 9/10The combat system is a standout feature, blending fast-paced action with strategic depth. Players can engage in fluid combos and switch between Eikon abilities, offering a dynamic experience that encourages experimentation. The challenge level is well-balanced, making battles exhilarating and rewarding.Final ThoughtsIn conclusion, after 17 hours, Final Fantasy XVI impresses with its engaging story line, intuitive interface, and thrilling battle system. While minor improvements could be made to the menu organization, the overall experience is compelling. This game is a must-play for fans of the series and newcomers alike.

_childDocuments_.review: If you want to be enthralled in a beautiful cinematic narrative, Final Fantasy is perfect for you. Whether you are a veteran gamer or newcomer, the game can be played how you want with modes that fit.The story is great, its not perfect and it does seem to slow down at moments, but its great and worth playing through. The english voice cast does a fantastic job all around.Gameplay is as varied as you want it to be. You unlock new abilities as you progress and its on you to try what you like best. As others have said, this game is about story first and foremost. You wont find deep character customization or crafting here, its all pretty linear. I played this on a 3070 GPU. There were times when i loaded into different places where the game would stutter. This was easily fixed by saving, exiting to title screen and loading back in. This wasen't much of an issue as the games load times are extremely quick. Overall the game is an 8/10. Would reccommend at full price if you love epic video game tales.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced combat that makes you feel like a god once you mix-and-match your perfect set of Eikonic abilities, real grabber of a story, and top-notch cinematics and visuals. Unfortunately, there's no ultrawide monitor support either which I was expecting to see on the PC release, and the base difficulty of the game personally speaking is a bit lacking. There are mods to up the difficulty a wee-bit before you reach NG+, but otherwise it's hard to not love this game and the oddly-exciting lore between Bearers, Dominants and looking forward to a world of change.Try the demo. - If you hate a game with cutscenes and deep stories, go find another game.  Regardless of what you think it is, this is an amazing Final Fantasy game, and I'd buy it a third time.

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI is an amazing game.  Buy it.  Play it.  In typical Final Fantasy fashion the relationship that you build with the characters after your roughly 40 hour journey through this game (if you stick to knocking out the main story and nothing else) you really get to know and like the characters.  Or really dislike the bad guys.  There are some really crazy and messed up people.  My friends and I joke that this game sometimes goes full anime at times and when it does it is some of the greatest scenes in video games.  I'm the type that likes to explore everywhere, collect as much as possible, and do every possible thing in the game.  I am only short on a few things at around 100 hours of game play.The combat in this game is tons of fun!  It is fast, engaging, over the top.  Sometimes you have so much going on that you can see a damn thing.  Sometimes frustrating, but it is all the over the top action scenes you saw during cut scenes of the turn base games is just the combat in this one.The music in this game is absolutely beautiful!  Composed by none other than Masayoshi Soken (the man is a legend within the FFXIV community.  Go check out LAHEE.).  There are some very special fights in this game and the music hits perfectly every time!It isn't a flawless game.  I have a few frustrations with how some parts were handled.  Parts I wish they polished a bit more.  Side quests are the biggest thing that comes to mind which feel like they would fit better in an MMO.DLC:I forked over the extra $10 to get both DLC.Echos of the Fallen is awesome!  People complained that it was short (~4 hours?).  It was tons of fun so I didn't personally mind.  The characters that are introduced, the extra layer of lore, and one of the best fights in the game.  It is straight to the point and is great.The Rising Ride on the other hand...  Visually great.  I was happy to have more game, but I personally didn't care for the story.  I think they intentionally wanted it to be its own thing but it feels out of place for the setting of this world.  It added a lot of fun extra stuff to the combat which is nice.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t sure whether I should pick up this FF game, although I’ve played nearly all the others, because I have a strong preference for turn-based RPGs, and this was completely action based.   So, I played the (free) demo and was hooked.  This game nails it in every respect.   The story was good and the voice acting and soundtrack superb.  The game looked and played beautifully even on my aged but still venerable 1080 Ti.   There were a few times during my 69 hours of play (I’m a completionist) that the game froze and had to be restarted, but the auto-saves worked surprisingly well and I lost little progress when this happened.   (There is also a manual save option.)     The fights against the common, and not-so-common, riff raff are good, but the boss fights are incredible; you feel like 2 Gods (or at least 2 Kaijus) are duking it out.   Some of the fights – Bahamut comes to mind - were very intense but you never feel overwhelmed as the level progression is implemented nicely. Unlike some earlier FF games, you don’t need to grind out levels to reach a place where you can win a boss fight.  The normal progression of the game does that for you.  There is a skill tree of sorts, but it is limited to learning, upgrading and mastering spells of your Eikons.If you are even a bit of a fan of CARPGs, this title is a must have.

_childDocuments_.review: FF16 a departure from earlier entries with a focus on real-time action combat and a massive sense of scale. It is a polarizing experience, where die-hard fans of past games may not enjoy this style of combat. This is a formula which the FF franchise has been slowly moving towards, and with this game, it feels like it has finally been realized. Although not as dynamic and transformative as other games in the genre, fights are flashy, controls are incredibly tight, and boss battles are thrilling in every way. That being said, the game is relatively easy, with the combat sort of being a delivery system for the story. However, I really don’t see this as a negative, since the story is very gripping, and I always looked forward to the cutscenes and what was happening in the over arching narrative. One thing I must mention is the “Active Time Lore” system, which lets you pause any cutscene you are currently watching and lets the player read about topics that are mentioned in that scene. These topics change as the story advances and as grows and as you learn more about the world of Valisthea. This is an amazing system that keeps you immersed in the world, and I can only hope that other franchises take note of. Overall, Final Fantasy 16 is a masterpiece of a game, with wonderful combat, superb writing, and VO casting that rivals the greats. This is the best FF game I’ve played since FFX, and I hope Square Enix takes what they’ve learned and make FF17 even better. An absolute 10/10 game, and an experience I will remember forever.

In these times i wish steam had a Mixed option for reviewsThe Game has Awful pacing issues. The main quest itself is interesting, the story of the game is interesting. But the way they sectioned off everything is so unfun it makes you want to stop playing. Especially towards the 50% point of the storyThe Game does this thing where it separates the interesting bit of story and gameplay with 1 hour of boring side fetch quests. Example : You fight big giant monster in an epic fight for an Hour, then for the next 3 missions you are force into boring fetch quest missions. Go talk to person A then go Talk to Person B who is 20 feet away then go talk to person C , then go Back to person A . Then go fight 4 random guys on path and boom mission done.The Game tries to be an  ARPG , RPG , MMORPG and just an action game at the same time. It ends up doing everything poorly. Theres not enough RPG elements to make it an RPG, so it just ends up feeling like leftovers. The Quest design and world environments feels straight out pulled from FF14 wich makes it feel like an MMO , But its not one. Also not an ARPG like FF7 Remake. More of a hack and slash like Devil May CryThe Game is also so easy that even boss fights feel like a chore. I played on the Action mode and i don't know why but theres no hard option. You need to finish the game a first time to unlock '' Final Fantasy '' mode. Kinda goes back to the MMO quest design. Just giving you 3-5 basic enemies and going '' Here have fun '' When i completed entire fights by using 1 ability. Then at some point even boss fights feel like a chore , because they aren't hard ( appart from the few last bosses)I died exactly 3 times in 34 hours. 2 of these deaths are in the last 3 boss fight of the gameThen theres performances issues, I have an RX6600 with an AMD ryzen 5 3600. Wich runs the game fine. Until it dosent. Random frame drops. Sometimes the frame-rate would be at 120, then cutscene happens and after that my game starts lagging and goes down to a sluggish 20 FPS. _childDocuments_.review: Beyond the narrative, this game really doesn't feel like a Final Fantasy game, even with the recurring elements present such as the Eikons, Chocobos, etc. That in itself doesn't present a problem, aside from its use as a mainline title. But for some I know this might be a turn off.While playing I certainly had a lot of thoughts, so I'll try my best to put them into a scuffed review for now.Tldr;Pros:-Great music and scenery in DLC and final segment;-Incredible quality graphics;-Overall good performance;-Stellar voice acting (second only to Xenoblade Chronicles franchise imo);-Well written and paced story;-Believable characters that are well written;-Good character design;-Some cool and flashy cinema.Cons:-Music placement is often badly placed and can take away from some very serious scenes;-A lot of ugly/bland environments for much of the game;-So much focus on cinema that the combat suffers;-Introduces a lot of names and places at once, drops them and expects you to recall them much later in order to follow events and conversations;-Early eikon battles overstay their welcome;-Side quests while trying to be meaningful are just busy work with endlessly pointless dialogue tacked on;-Equipment upgrades don't feel interesting;-Accessories feel pointless;-Lacks replayability.Music:Music was weird to me; one the one hand, there were some amazing pieces, especially later on and in the Rising Tides DLC. But on the other hand, for the vast majority of the game, the music fell flat, often not fitting. For example, avoiding spoilers, there's a very serious scene that really sets the tone and direction of the story for the rest of the game that for myself was around 10 hours in. This very serious event had the goofiest music imaginable playing in the background which, for me, took away from the scene massively. And it didn't stop there; this kind of thing happened regularly, as well as a lot of the background/ambient music for general exploration often just feeling like it didn't fit for me. This is certainly an odd change as Final Fantasy music is among some of the best used in games in my opinion.The latter section of the game, however, truly delivered on this front, in my opinion.Graphics:It's clear from the moment you boot up the game: this game is first and foremost a cinematic game. That is to say, a lot of works was put into graphical fidelity and it honestly looks great, especially during the eikonic battles that were the main feature marketed toward us during development. Issues arise, however, in that the world often despite this looks ugly; like there was no attempt to create beautiful scenery for much of the game, instead opting to put that effort into flashy designs for eikons and battles. Of course, there is technically a lore reason that you can fall back on as an excuse, but for me it was very noticeable even when said excuse would not fit. The RIsing Tide DLC does fix this and has some of the most stunning scenery I've ever seen in a video game at this level of graphics.Gameplay:Honestly, the battle system overstays its welcome; Eikon battles initially feel gimmicky although eventually evolve into something much more exciting and interesting. It's difficult to talk about combat properly without spoiling how it progresses, but regular combat takes far too long to ever really build up; Clive doesn't really get access to enough abilities to play your own way until late in the game and even then it feels like you're limited to specific abilities because of their stats and cooldowns. Not only that, but combat simply becomes a chore later on when boss enemies are sponges that attack relentlessly, sometimes not even leaving a big enough window to use one of the few abilities that are meant for staggering. And on top of this, it felt like  I was better off just running through the regular trash mobs half of the time.Again, though, this game has a big focus on cinema and it shows in the combat. That, however, is to its detriment. There are almost always so many particles on the screen at one time that you simply can't see what is there, meaning it is frequently difficult to read an enemy's actions and respond accordingly. For an action game, this was an absolutely abysmal decision.Story:From literally the first trailer, I was hooked on the story and the game's opening did nothing to change this. This game's story is incredibly well written and the overall pacing of it is very well done. Most past Final Fantasy games have had big ideas but were unable to execute on them properly - usually characters would make decisions that made no sense just to progress the narrative. Here, however, every person's motives and actions make sense for which I applaud Square Enix.  Voice acting:Wow. Just Wow. Especially by the leading case, this is some of the most phenomenal video game voice acting work I've ever known. To me, it's second only to the Xenoblade Chronicles franchise.It took me by surprise just how many more colloquial accents were chosen for the English voice cast. And the  apparent attention to detail was amazing too; during the DLC, you meet characters from the northeast all with accents hailing from the same region of England, in the northeast. As someone from the region myself, it was quite a nice change to hear such solid vocal work from here.Side content:This is another area that really fell short of the mark. There was a solid attempt to make the side quests interesting by using them in order to develop the arcs of characters introduced during the main story, but just about every quest felt like endless busy work. At first, the quests felt like a nice little break between emotionally charged main plot moments, but as more areas opened up the number of quests that appeared at once, all very similar to each other, was massive to a point that I can see some people being burnt out by the sheer amount of time wasted when completing these quests.In addition to this issue, often the dialogue in these quests can have a very typical JRPG problem of there simply being too much pointless speaking. And for most quests, the rewards don't really do much for the player - thankfully quests that give new upgrades of new crafting recipes will be obvious due to the symbols used on the map and journal.Miscellaneous:-A lot of the names of places in the game were incredibly hard to follow for a long time; their contexts are introduced in an instant and then often disappear for 10s of hours at a time with an expectation that the player recalls a random minute detail so that events make sense.-Character designs for the main cast are mostly solid, although admittedly one or two I felt were just one off side characters due to their generic looks. I actually quite like this change since not every character needs to look interesting if they're well enough written as they were in this case.-I play with a 3070 and had very little issue performance wise; the first time I entered a ruin area the frames lagged for that playthrough until I left the location, however after this most cases of frame drops were minor and short lived.-Weapon and armour upgrades are too incremental to feel worth working for and the damage ceiling never really increases with new abilities or skills earned.-Accessories are meaningless.-Due to the cinema over gameplay nature and overall length of XVI, I can't see this game having replayability for many people. Which is a first for mainline FF games and very rare when it comes to JRPGs.

_childDocuments_.review: Feels like an exhibition rather than a game.  There are a lot of Final Fantasy tropes in the game, but they exist for fan service.  There are virtually no RPG elements, as the game is story-based with fairly meaningless battles in-between.  There are almost no new new items to get.  There are a ton of resources to collect, for pretty meaningless upgrades to the protagonist's weapon and one piece of armor...There is a really good "Final Fantasy" story surrounded by gorgeous visuals, and some good action game-play here.I got bored with the action in a few hours.  It feels like a Soul's Like for an hour or two, and then just gets amazingly easy and pointless.  The story was pretty cliche.  There is nothing to work towards, even basic stuff like weapon and armor upgrades are pretty meaningless.If you like Final Fantasy narratives about crystals and Gods, go for it. If you want an RPG wherein you build up a character, upgrade gear... - stay away.  This is 90% narrative, and pretty corny at that.  The other 10 percent is collecting for non-impactful upgrades.
