_childDocuments_.review: This is a difficult one, but unfortunately this is the first and the only FF series game I cannot recommend.What make FF great is a good dramatic story and remarkable characters - none of these can be found in this game:* Story - generic, extremely predictable, soft, like a tale for small children...* Characters - none of them are remarkable, all are plain and 1-dimensional without any real development. The  main protagonist of this game is the first spinless loser in FF series* Side quests - waste of time in terms of both narrative and rewards, enough to can say that common side quests in average MMO RPG are way betterAs for other game mechanics - this is the most shallow FF game ever in all aspects:* Combat - you literally may spam-click 1 button for basic attack + evade when needed till the end of the story and you will be just fine. A few available skills just add some diversity so you will not get bored to death* Exploration - Almost non-existent and even those scraps of exploration left comparing to previous games in FF series are completely pointless* Crafting system - just plain increase of damage at set intervals to match increase in mobs level so you will not notice any difference in combat at all. No variety at all.* Builds - non-existent, those few spells you have are not required at all and are there just to add minor variety to boring combat.This game is a total disappointment. It feels like a B-class fan-fiction game in FF setting. Playable, but you will miss nothing if you skip this one or pick it on sale when you get bored.

_childDocuments_.review: ~60-65 hours to finish the story + all side content (both DLCs included)~75-80 hours to 100% Great story, good action-orientated game play, but horrendous pacing. Sometimes you'll sit through a 10-minute-long cut scene only to walk down a hall to watch yet another very long cut scene. It is criminal how often you put down your controller, because every micro emotion must be given at least 10 seconds of scene time to be fully expressed. Thankfully, most cut scenes outside boss fights can be skipped, which allowed me to maintain my sanity during new-game+.I wouldn’t pay full price, but there is a lot of fun to be had, around $30 - $40 with DLC included.

_childDocuments_.review: An absolute masterclass in character writing and character moments. _childDocuments_.review: Brilliant characters, story, lore and world building, my new favourite Final Fantasy in that regard. Looks fantastic and outright stunning alot of the time. Combat is very fun and if you make the effort to really combine different Eikon abilities it can be very rewarding. Early side quests can seem mundane yes, their payoff for story and lore building is well worth it though and comes into play later in the game where the side quests are amazing. Thoroughly enjoyed the DLC too and you will love it even more (also the main game) if you're also a XIV player.

_childDocuments_.review: The Pros-Best story in a Final Fantasy game since FFX.-Masterfully crafted combat system. Tons of cool skills to use. Amazing boss fights! Kaiju!!!-It looks absolutely phenomenal. Especially in combat and during the kaiju fights.-Voice acting is amazing. Music also.The Cons-Sadly the game is very very easy. Crafting system feels like an afterthought.I was in the camp of people who were bummed about FFXVI being more of an action game than an RPG. I kept an open mind and tried the demo and boy am I glad I did. It doesn't try to do much but it excels at the things it does.Overall it's a beautiful story with a great emotional hook unlike recent FF games. _childDocuments_.review: Let's get the good out of the way.  The game is gorgeous, especially in its environments but also in character models, special effects, and overall presentation.  I didn't encounter any performance issues or frequent crashes, though I can't speak for lower-end systems.  I was continually impressed by the fast load times; changing maps is nearly instant, as is initial load-in when starting the game.  Amazing work by the team.The music is standard Soken; serviceable when it needs to be, standout when it needs to be. Not much to say here, if you like Soken's extensive body of work from FF14 this will be familiar territory.  The combat is smooth and well-polished, with a wide variety of eikonic abilities.  Each Eikon lends itself to different approaches to gameplay, so being able to mix and match them helps make the somewhat simplistic combat feel fun and engaging.  Clive feels good to control in combat.  That said, I do feel like the game is a bit too easy on Action mode.  I was playing as a completionist and before the DLCs, I probably saw the game-over screen less than a dozen times, even including all the optional hunts.  Players should note that there's a "Final Fantasy" mode that unlocks after completing the story once, which is supposed to be harder.  There are also optional challenge modes that restrict certain things and make combat harder, so that's there to offer a lot of potential gameplay to those who want a tougher challenge.The writing is where more of my criticisms start.  Before I sound too harsh, it's worth mentioning that, especially for people weary from FF stories falling apart with ridiculous complexity by the end, this one is very straightforward and easy to follow.  An average player can play through the entire story and have a clear idea of what's going on just from listening to the dialogue and watching the cutscenes.  If that's somehow not enough, the plethora of plot comprehension aids (the Lore Codex, the character-relationship lookup, and the world events pages), make understanding what's going on and who people are incredibly easy.  I almost feel like these awesome features were wasted on this story, as I at least felt like it was so simple it hardly needed such rigorous explanation, but it's there nonetheless if anyone gets confused.  Sidequests are, again, pretty similar to what you'd expect from FF14.  Which means that some of them are alright, if a bit dry, and others are very rote "interact with 3 shiny spots in the vineyard and then talk to the questgiver again" sorts of timewasters.  I don't mind them in an MMO but in a single-player game they feel like a waste of time.  I'd rather they weren't there at all or were more interesting. Sidequests are unfortunately also where the presentation breaks down a little as well.  On the one hand, maybe this is how the team was able to avoid going over budget or over schedule, but longtime players of FF 14 will start to recognize the FF14-isms in the way the sidequest dialogues are blocked out; the way people walk into frame, the simplistic ways the camera moves, the way characters sort of move in a sequence and rarely if ever simultaneously.  It's hard to avoid the comparisons with FF14, once you notice it you start seeing it everywhere, which again, isn't necessarily a bad thing, but it does feel like a step back from the cinematography and sometimes artistry of FF15.  The main story for the most part is free of these problems, where the team clearly spent much more time working on the presentation.  The main story strongest in the first 2/3rds of the game. In the last third the plot starts to feel like it's continually retreading the same ground over and over while it waits for you to finish killing the rest of the people on your list, but that doesn't stop you from growling arguments at the villain every time you meet.  I want to emphasize though that the story isn't -bad-, it's just not exceptional.  All in all, it's very passable, and it's possible that it might resonate with some people who aren't as critical as I am. The eikon fights are neat, but I found they grow a bit stale the more you see of them.  It was a fun experiment but I hope they don't come back as a main feature again. I think they work better as a one-off thing like in FF15. A small word on the DLC: both are great, although fairly short.  Writing, presentation, and gameplay in a both sections are above average, and you get some nice rewards.  Nothing but good things to say about the DLCs, shame there weren't more. In a time where gaming backlogs only seem to ever grow longer and games fight more and more for players time, it's nice to be able to say that FFXVI respects your time and doesn't drag out the playthrough with frustrating mechanics and RNG.  Yeah, I'm talking about you, FF12. At the time of review I've essentially done a 100% playthrough on Action difficulty in 100 hours, and I definitely could have done it faster if I wanted to.  Completing the game entirely should be possible with another lap of the game, though i'll likely skip the sidequests the next time around.Overall 16 is a good game, it has good momentum and doesn't waste your time.  It's overflowing with quality of life features and is definitely the most accessible, beautiful, comprehensible game in the series so far.  I'm glad CU3 got a chance to make a mainline game, and I'm very curious where the series will go from here.

_childDocuments_.review: Finally beat the game and all the hunts after 65 hours. I played it with a 14700K and 4080 Super in 4K and it was a fantastic experience. No issues, no crashes. My favorite Final Fantasy to date. The combat system is really fun, but takes a while to feel fluid and cohesive. Once it gets going though you won't want to set it down. Dodges and parries are super satisfying, and combining all your newly acquired abilities makes you want to continue further and unlock more. The story is where this shines. A Final Fantasy take on Game of Thrones of sorts. Very political, war, the greed of man, and humanity. You have to mentally piece together all the different factions and nations but it all starts to make sense the more you play. There's an npc that summarizes the story so far, so you can catch up if you've been away from the game or want to keep up if things didn't make sense.Clive is a bad-ass protagonist one of the best in FF. Keep an open mind and enjoy the ride. "We fight, we survive, we endure, we don't need a reason"

_childDocuments_.review: Performance significantly impacts the enjoyment of the game and requiring 4000 series cards with access to all those frame gen and upscaling technologies to enjoy 60 frames is perplexing considering the quality of visuals. What's especially predatory and dishonest is that they spent time to optimize the areas included in the demo and for them to maintain  60+ frames on DLSS on capable cards. Once you buy the release version and step into other areas, the reality hits. Extremely deceptive practice. Not recommending until substantial (lol, not gonna happen) optimization efforts and removal of denuvo. To include denuvo in a game that requires all the nvidia gimmicks exclusive to newer models is utterly anti-consumer. As of now it is required to use an official mod which removes frame rate caps from cutscenes and generally helps keeping the game with a steady frame rate and less stuttery. It is an amazing and spectacular game. A throwback to simpler time but in no way the visuals justify the ludicrous system requirements.  I do not understand how can a game that blurry and lacking in detail with graphics comparable with nearly ten year old games can run at 30 frames with dlss upscaling on 2080, as old as it may be. I can even get 60 frames without upscalers in hogwarts legacy now! REMOVE DENUVO, that thing is a 20 fps hit alone. Jedi survivor is finally playable on something else than 4000 series cards without it. Even bioware decided not to include it in new dragon age with how bad their devs are being unable to optimize the game.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're a real final fantasy fan pick it up, but if you want a nice game to play and relax with i suggest looking elsewhere. The game alternates between running like butter to running like my fat ass. I'd say its in areas with lots of assets for your processor to deal with but i've seen maps with 0 entities lag worse than areas with 30+ enemies in a large expanded map all while launching nuke like abilities. _childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 16 is a 7 out of 10 game.The best part is the boss fight, when you transform into a giant monster and fight another giant monster, it’s really cool. It’s so cool, there are few games that can compare to FF16 in terms of epicness.Story is mature and sophisticated, you can clearly see the inspiration from Game Of Thrones, in a good way. But I don’t like the ending, it feels contrived, it seems Final Fantasy must has a sad ending.But that’s it, the good parts of FF16.The bad: Combat, unsatisfying, boring, repetitive. I actually like the action game combat, I think turn-based RPGs are boring. But FF16’s combat feels like FF14 MMO-RPG with free normal attack. It doesn’t have the smoothness of an action game, I don’t know how to say it, just not right.Side missions, COMPLETELY GARBAGE. Basically all fetch quests.And when you talk to NPC, the animation of the character is like a 20 year old game. Very stiff and robotic, let alone facial animation, non-exist. I don’t think there is any motion capture outside of cut scenes where characters actually act like humans.It took me 73 hours to unlock all achievements, which is impressive, but I don't enjoy playing the hardest difficulty in New Game+, because of the boring combat and insanely high HP enemies. I just want to rush through the New game+ and be done with it. And as soon as I unlocked all achievements, I deleted  the game,  I don’t want to play again.All in all, 7/10 game. There are many epic moments in this game, but those epic moments can’t compensate for the bad stuff. FF16 isn’t a bad game, but an OK game.

_childDocuments_.review: Cons:Bad performance/optimization.Predictable story (I have been able to guess how things were going to go with a pretty high degree of accuracy throughout the story so far.)A lot of the major plot points just seem derivative and generic.Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene> Boss Battle>Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Cut scene>Visit hideout to upgrade 1-6 pieces of equipment>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene>Cut scene>Linear combat stage>Cut scene> Boss Battle... etc.No party management to speak of. Can't choose party members, or change their gear/skills/etc.Super linear gameplay, even for Final Fantasy standards. Even gear progression is pretty linear. Just go to the forge every so often, craft newest belt+bracer+weapon, then upgrade it. No brainpower necessary.You also have 3 accessory slots that you either use for the "story mode" items to make the game easier, boost the effectiveness of a certain attack skill, or boost some other stat to a mild degree. So there's some strategy there, but it's bare minimum.Pros:Some of the fights look cool.Action/fighting is pretty snappy and responsive. You can pet the dog.(Edit: Like many other hack and slash games, you can ultimately turn your brain off and mindlessly engage in the combat. Which I suppose is a 'Pro' if you're looking for a Devil May Cry alternative, and a 'Con' if you are looking for a JRPG.  As such, if I'm ever in the mood to do some mindless hack and slash, I'll be putting some more hours into this.Basically, if you REALLY want something akin to DMC, and are an action game fanatic, then I actually WOULD recommend this game. _childDocuments_.review: easily one of my favorite final fantasies of all time, as a long-time fan since childhood. this review comes after two 100% playthroughs (one on ps5, one on pc) and half a third playthrough on ff mode trying to collect all the no damage medals.i understand people's gripes with the game, of course. the sidequests can ruin the pacing at times (though many are great), the combat can be repetitive especially on the first playthrough's difficulty, and the production quality of cutscenes can vary wildly from triple-a blockbuster to budget indie game. but the highs are so high and the gameplay loop is so damn fun that i can't help but love it regardless. clive rosfield is an incredible protagonist and the story they tell of free will, acceptance and tragedy is one that shouldn't be slept on. it's one that hasn't left my mind since the day i completed it, and the more i think on every beat the more i grow to appreciate the narrative as a whole, especially the overarching antagonist.the combat system is as complex as you want it to be. can you just get through spamming "ultimates" (the big, flashy moves for each eikon that stop time and do a ton of damage)? yes! can you also do bayonetta-esque combos in the right hands? yes! and on harder difficulties such as ultimaniac, learning the intricacies of what's on offer is necessary to find success. it's the definition of easy to learn, hard to master. the one issue i have with it is that people will naturally take the path of least resistance with the ultimates and never try the ng+ difficulties which punish you for doing so. there should be more consequence for diamond dust and tsunami spam. tl;dr - ffxvi is a fantastic game that is as complex as you want it to be. though it has its low moments which many discuss in their own reviews, it's such a thrill ride all the way through that everyone should at least give it a shot. especially for 50$!

_childDocuments_.review: PERFORMANCE ISSUES : read this first.Before fiddling with graphics settings, make sure the demo/game is installed on a SSD drive (along with the necessary USB3 cables, plugs, and drivers to not hinder data transmission). It's in the hardware requirements for a reason. If you do not, you will suffer from out of sync/choppy/freezing cutscenes regardless of your computing prowess. Reminder : an SSD drive is ~5 times as fast as a physical one.This is the reason for the disparity in performance reviews, with some being unable to run their game smoothly enough despite their alienware but using external hard drives for lack of space on C: after installing 36 games, like me. If the graphic card doesnt receive the data fast enough, it cannot create miracles.Only after that, if you still have issues, can you consider other tweaks, like disabling overlays (from steam, graphics software, and discord) and lowering graphic settings (like disabling that horrible blur). I personally recommend lowering screen resolution first and foremost, from 4K to 1980x1080, it eases the burden on your graphics card by 4 times, allowing you to keep in-game options/settings as high and detailed as possible ; or you can pick middleground with 2560x1440.Do note that you will likely need some free space on your C: (internal SSD) for memory swap purposes during game play. Cauz I did : quitting the game just now freed 15 Go, despite my game being installed on D:.

_childDocuments_.review: Fast-paced, action RPG system that emphasizes real-time battles, combos, and flashy Eikon summons. Set in the dark, medieval world of Valisthea, the game follows Clive Rosfield, who embarks on a personal journey of revenge and redemption.The story delves deep into themes of political intrigue, power struggles, and the fate of nations, with a darker tone compared to previous Final Fantasy games. The graphics and visuals are stunning, particularly during large-scale Eikon battles, which offer cinematic action sequences.However, some fans of the series may find the lack of party-based gameplay and RPG depth to be a drawback. The game focuses more on combat and spectacle than exploration or character customization. It has a more linear structure than the open-world setups seen in past titles, and side quests are generally not as engaging.

_childDocuments_.review: Unfortunately, the epitome of "meh".There's a lot of poor design choices that ultimately hinder this experience, and it just shows how boxed in this particular dev team is because of how many of these design choices are also in FFXIV.Pacing is atrocious because for some reason basic exposition that should be done in 2 minutes is somehow lengthened to  hour long segments because of the obsession with mundane fetch quest design. There are parts of the main story where I was actually getting into it, and immediately the momentum is killed because I now have to spend the next hour doing fetch quests to help build a stupid bridge.This game has genuinely the worst side quests I have ever seen in an "RPG". It is actually insulting how they're literally just there to pad your playtime.The combat is fine. It really doesn't evolve at all throughout the game and there is no challenge in any of the combat encounters, even the hunts. It's just super watered down Devil May Cry. I get that the game doesn't aim to be challenging, but maybe at least have a difficulty option for those who want a challenge? I'm not playing through this 40 hour long game twice to do New Game + and sit through the story again.The "RPG Mechanics" are also insulting. There is no actual gear system, but they do shove a loot system down your throat that may as well have been designed by an unpaid intern. It's just stat increases with no effects, no visual changes aside from your sword. The obsession with sprinkling literal 1 gil loot in the environment is also just bizarre. In 2024, from a AAA company, that is a joke.The music and voice acting are good, and I think a few of the characters were decently written, but that's not anywhere near enough for me to recommend a $50 video game.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr: 10/10 probably my number one FF rnI am a diehard Final Fantasy fan. I absolutely love the series and this game is like a love letter to it. It is an amazing experience and shows that the series is heading in a great direction. I won't talk about the other recent games because I don't want to compare and detract from either of the amazing works we've received recently. CBU3 really made this game feel like a cinematic experience through and through. I bought my PS5 specifically for this game and I was not disappointed (as unfortunate as it is, was unable to secure the limited pre-order to get statues); and, clearly I liked as it as I put 170 hours into this game on PS5 alone (only 7.5 here on Steam *so far*) and also immediately pre-ordered the Complete Edition the day it was announced on PC. I am anxiously waiting for more mods to customize the game in a way that I would personally like more.The shift to a more serious Final Fantasy as well as truer ARPG mechanics felt right here. There is still some improvement to be made (hence my mentioning of PC mod support) as the true RPG mechanics were a little lackluster and the ARPG mechanics felt like an earlier Devil May Cry game. I know that they've almost got the formula down because it taste so sweet as it is so far. In addition to that, the side quests could use some work; they felt like quests from FFXIV which, like most MMOs, have a bread and butter formula they use. The main question, however, is "what is the main attraction?" Simple answer: Clive.The story for this game is amazing and you feel truly there with the characters, as Clive-- from adolescence to Wyvern to [REDACTED] the [REDACTED]. I felt every emotion, every footstep, every touch, every embrace, every clash, every shout, every piece of Clive is embedded into you as you play as him-- he smiles, you feel that; he furrows his brow, you feel that; he cries, you feel that. And, no emotion seems wrong for him, nothing he says is ever "off"; as he evolves as a character and changes over time, it is still Clive. It is genius how well they made Clive so realistic and human; which goes for all the characters in the story (minus, like, one specific character). And with Clive comes the story-- the synergy between everything that's happening and him is diabolically good. This man is what I would call as the epitome of Final Fantasy main characters. Jokingly I like to say he's like Cloud's cooler older brother; you hang out with Cloud who is super cool and anime and all that but you hear about his older brother Clive who's out doing some cool ♥♥♥♥ and living the phrase "let's make today a movie, bruh". (I know I said I wouldn't reference another Final Fantasy but this was for a funny reprieve.) Humor aside, Clive really is an amazing main character and I hope they take more from him. He's the star of the game through and through; even with other amazing characters, he still shines above all. He also says the thing at the end!The world building is amazing. You have so many ways to learn more about the world and how the setting is just constantly affected by the story and how the culmination of it all is shown. The lore for this game is pretty expansive so shout out to homeboy Tomes for keeping those archives updated! While we got a plethora of lore for Eikons and those revolving around them, there's a ton lore that is there as well. Add on to that the expansive DLC and how it's easily just incorporated into the story, and you have a wondrous story to experience. The way everything interconnects and how the story is woven seems almost like it's a farewell, send-off letter for the series and truly I hope that is not the case. I hope that I open the envelope with this love letter to the series just to find out that there are much more amazing works in store for us.Also, I was once a Benedikta Harman simp but became a reformed man-- I now simp for one of the best and most well written Final Fantasy ladies in the series: Jill Warrick.All in all, I give this game a solid 10 out of 10. While, yes, there are a few gripes with the game, they are not enough to detract a single point from the game. I eagerly look forward to seeing what else is in store for the series, and if there were a way to make a sequel to this game then that would be rad.

_childDocuments_.review: I think the game is really great, it has good soundtrack, combat and story. The only negative thing is that some side quests are a bit repetitive and the dialogues from the side quests can be a bit boring (either a hit or miss but at least you don't always have to do them if you just want to enjoy the main story). Either way I still managed to finish all the side-quests and I still find myself relaxing while enduring the long dialogues and finishing them.The story is also quite dark and gritty than I expected, which I really enjoyed. It felt mature and very different for a Final Fantasy game. I still haven't played the DLCs which I plan to do so on my second play-through. Overall the game isn't hard at all, you don't have to stress or worry much while playing the game (except while experiencing the story). The game also reminds me of Devil May Cry from the action style combat and also monster hunter, which feels like a combination of the two. And also, you get to actually find & hunt monsters for bounties around different locations throughout the game and I quite enjoyed that part of the game as well. I suggest getting the game to those who want to experience a game with good story since the best part and focus is the story and don't mind some grind with repetitive combat. The game itself is also heavy in cut-scenes (feels like a movie and game in one) and I definitely did not regret buying, especially considering how many hours I put into this game and how much i enjoyed the exploration, combat, lore and story.I thought it was quite of a wonderful experience and having the chance to get to play FFXVI from the start to finish, getting to see how the story progresses (even some side quests) and getting to meet new characters, which I thought were nicely portrayed (voice lines, design, how they fit into the story or introduced/revealed, etc.), especially their character development. The story definitely hits hard emotionally overall but I think the game is awesome just the way it is despite the side quests which could've been better if maybe cut a bit short or simpler. Another annoying thing is that the side quests involves with a lot of walking back and forth and even have different quests going to the same place again in a short period of time.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: A would be exceptional game is ruined by a set of bad decisions. This should be my favourite final fantasy game, and yet I cannot recommend it. In what it's so great at, it merely serves to make what it fails at more painful and unacceptable given the fact that they keep making the same mistakes and failings (which is what they are) over and over again with every entry. This is not a matter of creative direction, but bad choices. It's a choice to implement Denuvo, which is proven to result in a negative experience for paying consumers all while NOT protecting long-term sales (which has been proven in study after study, game after game) in terms of latency, lost frames, and offline and Linux playability. This is always based on the fallacy of piracy = lost sale, even though it does not translate into people that were going to buy the game.ITS A CHOICE, to have brilliant options for those that need or want easy or mindless gameplay, to have a mechanically good and vast array of dodges, counters, projectile blocks, skill and timing-based abilities yet put ZERO effort into catering to users that want to have a challenging or engaging experience that actually uses or needs them. It's a choice not to give people harder difficulties from the get-go; to cater to these users with level caps, more punishing time windows, item disablement, achievements, or recognition for these players that make it worthwhile, they CAN cater to both of these groups and make the game accessible while levergating what they have to make it good for those that want something with more challenge. Yet they choose not to, damaging the quality of the game for all but a small amount of people that want easy gameplay instead of just catering to both group which they can do. It's a choice not to implement ultrawide; people do not expect perfection. When a modder with zero programming knowledge can implement a solid solution in a few hours, THERE IS ZERO excuses for a port with 1+ year of development time not to have this option.Its choice to have creative business unit  3 left without aid from other studios despite their limited experience outside of MMORPG's (In terms of recent developments i am aware of what they have done outside of this including the director) side quests entirely out of place in a triple game. RPG elements are worthless and should not be implemented. Endless materials people cannot and will not use because there is no point as the best items are given through just playing the game. These failings could have been fixed by having the studio do what they were good at and NOT what they could not do or handle. Those dismissing this as merley having an issue with change of direction are WRONG; the action is good; its a great system thats being hampered; if they wanted full action, why are they implementing systems that cannot actually be leveraged? It's just a misstep and a failing the gameplay is the perfect exmaple, so much abilities to counter, block, ect yet you do not need to leverage this because they wont add difficulty options from the start. The world is vastly empty. and never used or touched; some of the most detailed and brilliant areas I have ever seen in any game were wasted. Again, more evidence; they needed more time and help. They have made amazing artwork, stories, and worlds but have filled them with endless worthless fetch quests that will put you to sleep; it's a massive step back from even FF15, which had many brilliant and worthwhile optional fights, while the Bounty Hunts are a boring afterthought with limited and basic rehashed movesets and animations with small changes. The story is great, well formulated with quality in its narratives, characters, and interactions. The soundtrack is the best I have ever heard, even from Soken; there is SO MUCH right; the setting is well implemented, respected, and honoured; it's brilliant; I never found the game to be "EDGY." Every interaction seems in place and relevant; active time lore is great.I just can't advise this game at the price, because while it's good, it's badly let down by the same bad choices that mar and damage every entry. It draws me as it's so close to being exceptional and its ruined every time.

_childDocuments_.review: 3 hours in this and 2 and half in the Demo, So far the story is hitting all the right notes.Story- So far great and I find myself enjoying the characters even if they seem a little buzzkill and series but the writting drops little tidbits and rifts of humor that land well and give depth to the characters and enemies even.Sound- Ambient sound is beautiful without coming across as to much or to little, music is SO good and the pacing of it from scene to scene is mixed very well and the BOSS MUSIC... I can't praise this enough.Graphics- Are a combination of absolutely stunning and straight up bad BUT even then the bad doesn't matter as it's "good enough" The models are top notch with the environments textures looking a little muddied if your looking close but as your playing nothing pops out as "off" and generally is still very pretty.Gameplay- I'm split here a little bit so far the story is very straightforward with no real point to explore and seems to push you from one battle to the next using hallways and boss rooms. I'm not entirely turned off by this hand holding as you get to experience the story quicker leading to my next small issue. This game plays more like an 3rd Person Action game with leveling seemingly an add on that also doesn't feel like it makes a ton of difference along with the equipment you use having fixed stats and unlockes (which is fine) when you have options but here as soon as one weapon becomes useless another takes it place you never really feel like you have options for equipment. Also max level being 50... really... Overall- 4/5 as it stands (will come back later and update on completion) I'm happy I picked up the game and if your an action lover like God of War this is more in common with that than its roots that it came from and that both makes me happy as I don't have time to grind 100+ hour games anymore but same time I miss the RPG mechanics that the franchise was known for. Final Fantasy hasn't for a long time now made a game where you feel so over powered using the leveling system and ops for more action-y style combat. Pick this up if your a huge fan, if your on the fence stay on it and pick it up on a sale.

_childDocuments_.review: I don't ever write reviews, much less a serious one. However, having put in a near 100 hours into this game, completing both the Main Story and DLC's story, as well as completing nearly all of the side content, I felt almost compelled to write this review. Compare to the previous Final Fantasy games, Final Fantasy 16 makes way for a more dark and heavy-hitting story, showcasing various cases of Inequality, Mistreatment, and Hardship. In the first 5 hours of the game, you start to see what our main character, , has to endure in , and see what the world of Final Fantasy 16 really is. Progressing through the game, you get to see the violence and tension that exist between . Along side with the treatment of a specific group of people, showcasing the dependency that humanity has on the , with how dark this Final Fantasy game is compared to its predecessors, CBU3 did not shy away from portraying the violence that exist.And under all of this, is a more sinister plot that is waiting to be unraveled. Final Fantasy 16 offers a diverse cast, each with a compelling story that is waiting to be unearthed. Each of the characters will have an influence on not only the MC that'll lead into who he will become, but also on you. Majority of the cast are very memorable and beloved, especially the side characters, such as . One of the things that makes me love the cast, is that they all feel HUMAN, Throughout the game, you'll get to see how the characters change in behavior, ideals, and beliefs, especially members of the main cast. You get to see how much details CBU3 had put into making the characters feel human and authentic. Previous Final Fantasy games always have a great cast, but FF16 stands on its own for how compelling each characters are, and with the plot of the story, it make these character shine even more.The MC himself is the most compelling character I have seen so far in any game I've played this year because of what drives him to do what he does and it's for  His willingness to "destroy" the society he lives in so that others can  is something I haven't seen in recent games. If Asura's Wrath and Devil May Cry had a love child, Final Fantasy 16 is that child. The combat is straightforward yet with the variety of abilities that the game has to offer, you can make find something that suits your preferred play-style. I was so surprised with a few of the boss fights that I genuinely thought I was playing Asura's Wrath, and I love it. And just like Asura's Wrath, FF16 have Quick Time Events, thankfully those only happen at a pivotal point of a major boss fight. so you don't have to worry about feeling like you are watching a movie.And while you can't control your party members, you don't have to worry, for they prioritize small enemies, leaving you to only deal with the bigger enemies. And the party members have have their unique set of abilities that distinguish them from each other. Let it be known that the Final Fantasy series never once had an bad soundtrack, and with the great Masayoshi Soken, composer for Final Fantasy 14, behind the wheel, Final Fantasy 16 might have the best soundtrack of the series. Soken's work turned the game from a movie you get to play into an Opera, with each track highlight a specific part of the game, representing specific characters, and making you feel you CAN overcome whatever the world throws at you.The soundtrack itself is diverse, containing gentle piano pieces as you explore the game, powerful orchestras during major fights, a GREEK CHOIR to highlight specific feelings , and ELECTRONIC Music. Side Quest, Dungeons, Challenges, DLC stories, this game as it all. You never feel like there isn't anything to do, because anywhere you go, their is always something hidden away just waiting to be discovered. The Side quests is a nice change a pace from the heavy fighting of the main story, as it gives you a chance to wind down and helps with the character development of the main cast and those around you. The Dungeons and Challenges are a great way to test yourself in combat and see where you stand. And with NG+, you can to see how far you've got when fighting a new set of enemies that weren't there when you first started the game.The DLCs help in giving you something new to do and answered questions that never were answered, it was a nice touch that the game need to further improve the world of the game I bought the Complete Edition of the game and it was worth every pennies. If i had some way to forget everything about this game just so I can play it all over again, and experience what i felt, I would do it in a heartbeat.The only thing I wish for this game is a second part, a Final Fantasy XVI-2. It's wishful thinking, but seeing how much was put into the world of the game, some loose ends that needs to be taken care of, and questions left unanswered, I want Square Enix and CBU3 to continue the story of Final Fantasy 16.This game was worth the wait, to final get my hands on this game and experience its amazing story, I'm glad i can mark this off my list of games to play.

_childDocuments_.review: Even without performance issues the game is just awkward.It's this weird hybrid of action game and RPG that does neither particularly well, which is weird coming from a company that did KH and FF7R. KH at least always plays well, 7R had fun combat with a fun hard mode.Pacing of the story is completely atrocious, after every peak they take out all of the momentum like they want to make sure you're not having too much fun. I like the cast in general, the minor characters have a lot of personality. Side quests are so mind numbing it gives me physical pain. "Go collect 3 flowers" over and over. The overworld/map feels too close to an MMO, I was just warping around like an idiot and nothing felt cohesive.I don't like giving thumbs down to games I completed but this just isn't it. I thought after 13 and 15 surely it has to get better again but they somehow made a game that barely even functions with its mechanics. Why the ♥♥♥♥ is gear and crafting a thing? Why is Gil a thing if all I can buy is Orchestrion rolls? Abilities are fun at first but eventually it gets stale. Counter moves are very satisfying, the big hitters have these mini-cutscenes which last a little bit too long after a while. Elements have no function, there are no buffs, debuffs or synergies. The Rising Tide DLC gave Leviathan a nice gimmick. Why not change Clives weapon along with the Eikon? Why limit myself to 2 Abilities per Eikon? Why are accessories so boring? -6s Cooldown redaction, % increase in damage? Rising Tide introduced some accessories that alter some of the Eikons abilities and that's the stuff I was hoping to find in the base game. I also much rather have abilities tied to a resource I can manage rather than Cooldowns, that type of design doesn't do it for me. The game had an overall good story premise which then ♥♥♥♥♥ itself through the halfway point. Why hide so much lore behind ♥♥♥♥♥♥ fetch quests that offer nothing? At not a single point did this game feel like an actual journey. 10/10 Set pieces but that's it. A lot of speeches/monologues also feel redundant. I heard this characters reasoning already, I don't need it to be reiterated over and over.I really hope CBU3 never gets to do a single player game again on their own. A lot of the FFXIV "DNA" is in this game and that's for better and for worse. They know how to do spectacle, some tracks in the OST are really good and characters are likable. The game took 40ish hours to finish with all side quests and side content and I much rather it would have taken 20. I will not touch NG+ or Echoes of the Fallen.I'm absolutely butthurt, buttblasted, upset with borderline buyers remorse. It's what I deserve for trying not to spoil myself on anything regarding this game

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of the best Final Fantasy games of all time and definitely the best one since FFX.Buy this game. Its a great mix of Lord Of The Rings and Game Of Thrones in terms of world building and plot and Devil May Cry in terms of game play/combat. The music is great, but even though it's maybe not the best or as catchy as past FF games I still find it hauntingly beautiful and some of the music feels like a warm breezy day laying in the grass among fire lilies while dragonflies dance in the sun rays.This game is unlike any FF game that has been released before it, but still manages to feel all familiar. The world is beautiful and the characters are amazing. I'm not too big on the main character I like his backstory and abilities, but I can't get past the fact that hes literally one of the ugliest MC's FF has ever had it might be the fact that he slightly resembles a dog to me and I just don't like his face also his Imperial outfit is atrocious. In terms of party members I love this rendition of [REDACTED] its honestly my favorite version of him/her hes such a bad ass and just a really honest character. I also think Jill is really cool and love how shes there from the beginning helps that shes also extremely pretty and has one of the best outfits in FF history! There's also Torgal the dog he's such a nice addition. FFXV also had a dog(s), but they didn't really do much and weren't incorporated into the game play. The story is great and the world building is incredibly deep with so much lore added into the game that really enriches the game very similar to Mass Effect, but maybe not as grand of scale. And while the side quests are mundane the story centered around those quests are actually really good and makes finishing them well worth it, I find many of them deepen the story, world, and characters so even if they're not the best game play wise the stories they bring are done very well and worth experiencing.This is quite possibly one of the greatest games of the generation. If not one of the greatest games of all time. As you progress through the game you are constantly unlocking new things  The fact that the game manages to touch on social issues like slavery or intolerance while still managing to be a great high fantasy game puts it above similar titles that are at the end of the day just fantasy fluff. Even though the game play switch to a DMC style might throw off some long time fans because it's is so different game play wise I strongly encourage you to buy this game its incredibly good and really something special that I think all FF fans will appreciate. This is truly a "Final Fantasy for fans and first timers". 10/10(mini rant)Every single Final Fantasy game that has been released in the past decade and a half has been a near disappointment and almost everything Square Enix has put out in the past 2 decades has been literal rage bait bad, but this, this is good. Square Enix is 2 for 2 with Final Fantasy Remake and FFXVI if Life Is Strange Double Exposure turns out to be good then they will be back on my good side.Final edit:  This game is a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ masterpiece a literal masterclass of it's own. Video games like this don't come around often it is literally up there with one of the greatest video games of all time. I don't see a FF game topping this one in a long time. It's that good. I'll go so far as to say this is the best AAA game of the generation, the best that were going to get. It is truly lightning in a bottle for this gen of gaming.

_childDocuments_.review: -There's a loot system for crafting, but most of it is meaningless. -There are notorious monsters but they mostly play the same.-There's an interesting skill system, but I only used the same 6 skills for the whole game because there's no element damage/protection and you can use anything on anyone. Some later ones are good but I wish they had cut most of them. -You can fast forward the dialogue in some cutscenes but in others you're forced to listen through the whole thing or skip it entirely.-Clive runs at two different speeds outside or inside town and so you're stuck at a snail place in these areas, which truly is baffling to me.-Eikon battles are quite cool.-The writing is actually decent when they don't lore dump a 5 minutes cutscene about some war you don't care much about.-Voice acting is really good and so most of the dialogue.-Some of the battles are quite fun if you like dodging attacks and countering.-Great music and visualsAt the end of the day I'm glad I played this game. _childDocuments_.review: I paid $70 for the DLC and have spent 55 hours in the game currently. I can only spend a few hours a day playing, minus on the weekends when I can go a little crazier.That said I have yet to finish the game but I am getting closer to the end. 55 hours includes doing all the current side quests that I've unlocked so far, Hunts that I've unlocked so far, and a couple of the Worldmap Trials. I can say that I've gotten my moneys worth of entertainment this far.That said I do think there are a lot of things this game missed out out on opportunity wise. Burning Blade being the only charge-able sword attack when you have multiple elements at your disposal makes no sense. It should have been adaptable. Perhaps even going Semi-primed / LB.There is a lot missing in terms of battle structure. You don't really have any of the trademark FF spells like Cure, Poison, Stop, Protect etc. Enemies can use them however. One of the Dogs abilities states he can Heal allies which makes me think they had bigger plans that just weren't ever realized because Allies are basically just there. They don't provide much support and you cant play as them nor see their HPs so I don't know what their real purpose is other than to be there for the story.I'm seeing a few mods come out that tackle some of the other issues like weapons being just stat sticks and basic gear with very little bonus or boosts to make a difference. I'm hoping more modders come out and pave the way for aggressive allies, too and maybe a way to sword-channel different aspected elements to damage enemies. Even if it's just the color of the glowing effect I think it's the way it should have been.I also wish there were more costumes since we all know Glamour is the real end-game, Yoshida. There are only two outfits for each character which is very small but alas here's to hoping Modders enjoy the game enough to push these things out.All in all I'll definitely be trying a New Game+ with the higher difficulty and of course finishing the DLC content first but not without Mods to make sure I have all Eikons unlocked early on. I also want to complete the Worldmap Eikon Trials since I've only beaten two of the presumably 6. They have been quite the challenge. I would also attempt the Arcade Mode/Trials but I haven't seen any mention through the game of Rewards, just Time-based challenges to beat your own score which I couldn't give a rats ass about. If I ever learn there's cool gear or st00f to be had I might give it a go but right now it's just there.

_childDocuments_.review: I almost passed on this one, thinking "last I loved a FF game was FFX" and most reviews I saw were luke warm for this entry. I'm glad I gave the demo a shot; it made me buy the game about half way in and FFXVI is now sky rocketing into being a contender for the spot of my favourite FF (still too early to say though). The old FF RPG style is long gone, this is an action game with RPG elements, but it still drips of that final fantasy vibe.The atmosphere have a more mature tone where heavy topics, such as slavery, are ingrained in the world. The dialogue and the decisions being made are leaning more to the realistic fantasy side - they are nuanced and often relatable.The combat is silky smooth and really nails those dopamine hits with timed combos, dodges and parries - it reminds me of Devil May Cry. You have ways around it if you don't enjoy the action parts so much: you can choose story mode and equip rings that automate your selected pain point (not recommended imo).The set pieces, world building and boss fights... ermagerd, it's a unique and spectacular experience - my jaw have dropped many times. Try the demo and you'll know what I mean within 15 minutes, and if you keep playing and watch the culmination... just chef's kiss.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/5/24 - The most recent patch was supposed to fix crashing bugs a lot of people experienced. Played for an hour today and got a crash to desktop during a very important moment in a cutscene. This bug didn't have the Japanese text like the previous one, but a crash is a crash.Update: I can no longer recommend this game. After getting 14+ hours in, the game is frequently crashing with a Japanese error message. I'm getting about 3 crashes per ten minutes and previously I'd only had 1 crash in the first 10 hours or so. It seems to especially like crashing during side quest dialog. I've restarted my PC, drivers are already updated, and everything else on my PC runs fine without any crashes. Nothing has changed on my PC setup since the day I installed this and I haven't even installed any other software. I'm surprised they haven't already released a patch by now based on all the other people who seem to be having the same issue.Review: Many hours of top-tier greatness with epic moments, but at least as many hours of bewilderingly low quality gameplay and frequently meandering dialogue.Score: 7/10 	• I played 180 hours on PS5 and platinumed / 100%ed the game.	• The first 7-10 hours is almost a consistently great time.	• It's still worth playing through the rest of the main story, despite multiple extended periods of 'how could something this lame make it past quality control?' It really destroys the pacing and is a likely reason many players will just not feel like coming back to the game when there are so many other great video game experiences out there.	• There is plenty of fantastic dialogue in the main story, but there is also a lot of vapid and empty dialogue dressed up in flowery rants with awkward medieval dialect all over the place, just like in FFXIV. This can make it hard to keep paying attention until I suddenly realize they're talking about something interesting now but I missed part of what they said earlier.	• The voice acting is generally great and the main characters VA is top-tier. Ben Starr as Clive especially knocks it out of the park.	• The new weapons and gear upgrades are so trivial and mundane, that it feels nearly meaningless. Some of the swords do look cool though, and it's great they added an option to display any weapon you've collected instead of what's equipped.	• It also doesn't feel like you earned any gear upgrades because the vast majority of rare crafting materials are dropped by mandatory bosses so you'll have more than enough gil/materials to buy the new gear when it becomes available.	• There is no sense of interesting choice when it comes to equipping your character or making purchases. 	• Weapon choice would have been more engaging if only some weapons had high damage / low stagger and some had low damage / high stagger. But 99% of the weapons have the exact same number for the two.	• The vast majority of crafting materials and pickups in the environments come across as junk you don't need. 	• Exploration feels like time wasted instead of feeling rewarding.	• The concept of good level design is pretty much absent. There are two 'dungeon-style' areas that are kind of decent in my opinion: The opening swamp area and Caer Norvent castle - conveniently both featured in the demo.	• Environments and dungeons are not very engaging, although a few locations feature some fairly epic environmental destruction that happens automatically as you continue forward. 	• You interact with dungeons in 2 ways besides jogging through them: Opening doors /gates on the main path and fighting arena style groups of enemies.	• After about halfway through the game, almost all of the non-boss and mini-boss enemies are the same mobs you've been fighting the first 20 or so hours of the game. You're going to start seeing dozens (hundreds overall) of the same enemies and attack patterns you've already killed hundreds of times, but with more health, defense, and attack.	• Combat encourages a repetitive routine instead of presenting opportunities where you'd be thinking of a solution to a challenge like the FF7R series does. 	• Using the block / counter ability freshens things up for a little while, but a few hundred of the same enemies later, and it becomes just like the routine you use without them, except it also takes up one or more of the 6 Eikon ability slots	• I don't believe that the game needed to have status effects to make things more fun, but elemental weaknesses could have gone a long way to make things much more interesting, especially if you could instantly restart the battle to change loadouts like in FF7R or better yet, change loadouts mid-battle. For people who don't want the battle paused or interrupted for something like a 'decision,' they could just fight with what they already had equipped as long as the elemental weakness just gave an advantage, but wasn't really needed to win.	• 'Decisions' in battle tend to feel pretty trivial because the most effective routine is pretty obvious. Deciding whether to use some Eikon abilities before a boss is staggered or on weak enemies is about as thought provoking as it gets while in battle.	• Torgal is an awesome companion, but the 3 commands you can give him nearly feel like a waste of buttons that could have been used for something more interesting. Can anyone genuinely tell me that they still really enjoyed using a precision 'Sic' or 'Ravage' for the 200th time, dozens of hours into the game?	• For anyone who loves spending hours mastering a particular combination of moves and abilities to perfection but doesn't mind doing it against a lot of the same encounters, I can see the combat being much more appealing for you.	• If you play the game just an hour or two at a time, a few times a week, then the repetitive aspects of the game will likely be much less of a problem.	• The lack of playable party members is certainly disappointing, but I think even this downside could have been alleviated if there was more for Clive to do than his available routines.	• I think the cooldown system for Eikon abilities might be a big part of the problem. Powerful Eikon abilities could instead cost mp that regenerates slowly but could be more quickly restored with valuable, expensive and occasionally rare ethers. Some of Clive's moves could restore mp more quickly to create a give and take dynamic.	• How about if bosses had a 3rd gauge showing how much mp they have. Once it reaches zero, you know you're don't have to worry about their strongest attacks for a while. Then a new mechanic would be that the boss has to reach a spot in the arena to restore their mp or you have to do something to prevent them from regaining mp. That could liven things up a bit (not the exact same thing on every boss though lol.)	• Despite these flaws that seem pretty detrimental, I still feel like there is a solid 20 hours of excellent content in this game.	• There is plenty of really great music. 	• For every outstanding song, there is another song that's good enough, but definitely not something I'd intentionally go and listen to.	• The environments look really nice and are very high quality. Some of them do have monochrome color palettes though, which probably won't bother everyone, but is something I generally dislike.	• The characterization, moments, and interactions in the earlier parts of the game are really well done and memorable. That becomes increasingly more rare once you reach the latter half of the game. Playing Final Fantasy XVI is like going on several thrilling roller coasters, including the time spent waiting in line between each one.

_childDocuments_.review: Before I wrote a not recommended because of the PC port issues I was having.Having now finished the game, that is now a no because this game, frankly, is not worth your money nor your time. It has an excellent combat system, but it undermines itself with awful level design, absolutely rushed plot, awful side content and really very minor redeeming qualities. The setpieces are cool, fighting is fun, but this game has no identity, as all of its redeemable elements are done better elsewhere. Want similar combat? Play DMC, want similar setpieces with QTEs? Play Asuras Wrath. Want a mature medieval fantasy with swords, blood, political intrigue and a badass protagonist? Witcher 3. There is nothing this game does that makes it stand out.It's sad - I love Final Fantasy, but now, Final Fantasy wants so desparately to be everything else it's not.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm running a Strix 1070, i7 8700K at 4 Ghz, 32 gigs of ram, installed on samsung 970 evo m.2 It runs pretty impressively on a mix of mid and low settings, I'm getting a fair 40-60 FPS in open world/town/battles, locked 30 in cutscenes on 1080p ingame res, on 1440p monitor res; in game res difference is about 9 frames between 1080 and 1440. Considering the fact I'm still running a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ 1070 and still able to both play and enjoy this, makes me pretty happy. My gpu is out here sayin I'm tired boss and I'm telling that ♥♥♥♥♥, too damn bad, we finna do right by Joshua. This even runs on my steam deck on all low settings pinging 28-50 fps. This game is not badly optimized, it's simply a product of its time and actually exceptionally optimized. The game itself? It's a straight banger.Big FFIX vibes, big respect to Yoshi P pushing the marker on violence/traumatic and mature themes. _childDocuments_.review: Gorgeous graphics. Spoilers aside, early cutscenes of a certain Eikon had me captivated with the beautiful rendering of its feathers.Combat is reminiscent of The Witcher 3 and Devil May Cry games, with customization options to formulate your own style. The Eikon combat sequences have you taking control of familiar Final Fantasy summons, towering over the battlefield and shattering the landscape with their iconic elemental abilities. A combination of cinematic active time events and real-time combat will have you on the edge of your seat, riddled in goosebumps. Without elaborating any further due to spoilers, later Eikon vs. Eikon battles get really, really good.Amazing story, with a widely varying and memorable cast. The sidequests are a breath of fresh air and a very welcome change to your plain, grindy "fetch x of random item." Each has a short, unique storyline of its own that builds up your understanding of the culture of the game's world. I don't usually take the time to do sidequests, but I find myself eager to start each one in FFXVI. There's also a fast travel option to warp directly to the NPC to turn in your sidequest, which you can ignore/disable if you want.The game is developed by Creative Business Unit III, the same team that developed FFXIV.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Beat game at 66 hours doing I'd say about 75% of the side quests, all the hunts but one (need to go back and finish up Savrog) and ended at level 45. Everything I said below still stands. Excellent action game, and it "feels" like a Final Fantasy - especially in the story beats. The front half of the game is very reminicent of IV. Still, some more enemy variety in the back half of the game would have been nice, and the middle of the game lags a bit. The enjoyment of the gameplay really comes down to how much you like the combat loop and getting better and more efficient. The game DOES NOT punish you for losing in the traditional sense. Got my money's worth and then some. I'll come back to finish up the DLC. Original Thoughts: Incredible, action-packed RPG. The "stylish action" heavy gameplay and huge, cinematic battles won't be to everyone's tastes. If you're looking for a traditional JRPG experience with tons of menu diving, this isn't it. If you're looking for a deep job system, you won't find it here either. Instead, you have an excellent action RPG that is more Devil May Cry than Secret of Mana. Basically, play the demo and if you like the combat loop (what little you actually play in the demo) then you'll be golden. The pacing picks up tremendously after the demo - there's just a lot of world building and set up at the outset. Sure, sure, native Ultrawide and 60FPS cut scene support would have been nice but it was an easy fix with the mod. The mod for the demo works just fine on the base game as well and it is a game changer for in-engine cut scenes. While the game is well optimized, it is still one of the more demanding games even for my super beefy rig. I can run most modern AAA games without any of the AI driven enhancement support and hit a solid 4k/60. Even with a 4090, super fast CPU, yadda yadda I still had to turn on DLSS3 in Quality mode and enable VRS to hit a smooth 60 at all times. The 60fps cut scenes are wonderful, but they are demanding. Frame gen and the low latency options tend to make the game feel sluggish, imo, but those can further get your performance higher if you prefer. Overall, great port. Played over 10 hours on PS5 and sat the game down to wait for the PC release. Glad I waited to finish the game on Steam. It's incredible so far. Enjoy.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: - Good music 9/10- Great voice acting 10/10- Story 6/10- Core gameplay 7/10- RPG ?/?- Overall a 7,5/10____________________________________!POTENTIAL SPOILERS AHEAD!- The music was pretty good, there is a great mix for every region and boss. The combat music got repetitve after a while. I would prefer 3-4 different tracks, maybe even change it based on the region.- I played this game in german and the voice acting was awesome. It made me a part of the world.- The story and gamepacing are lackluster. You get this NPC with side quests and in the first half he dosen't  have any quests - at least it felt like that - while you get a ton right before the final boss and it takes you around 2-3 hours of basically walking back and forth. The ending was predictable and left a really bad taste. I hope a future DLC/Addon will improve some of the following aspects.- You also get your 3rd power after like 18-20 hours of gameplay. This should've been changed. Give it earlier to the player. The accessory system should've been implemented as a skill upgrade where you can choose to get either more dmg or a shorter cooldown. Dodging feels pretty good and rewarding after you get the berserker ring while parrying feels underwhelming. Its hard to time or the attacks are bad telegraphed. Some Eikons you get really late in the game when you already established and found a skill set that works for you. Upgrading other weapons besides the main "story weapon" feels pointless.- This game misses a lot of rpg elements. There are no status effects, no slow, no stun, nothing. The game always decides your party for you, you don't make any decisions. You also can't improve your party members by giving them armor or weapons or choosing skills or playstyles for them. You're most of the time with Torgal + Jill or Joshua or both. You also can't play as anyone else besides Joshua at 2 specific moments during the game. (while there was a good oportunity to play as Cid or Jill or other characters...) Leveling up feels underwhelming. You're just improving all of your stats, you can't specifically invest in physical or magical playstyles by upgrading your attributes. Something that also made little sense to me is, that you're the eikon of Ifrit and should be able to use Ifrit skills all the time despite choosing other eikon abilities. One last Point that I wanted to make is to give every eikon a different weapon type with a different playstyle or make the charged attack change based on the eikon with different effects. "Your magic changes to a different type whem using this eikon" - just saying... - Oh and where is the iconic job system in Final Fantasy 16???- Purple sky syndrom -> its okay for the first few hours but made me feel sick and I hesitated to continue playing the game. Maybe reduce the intensity after 2-3 Story missions.__________________________________________The DLC's improved my experience by a big margin. I really liked the dungeon DLC. It had a great final boss and the accessories were a great addition. The second DLC had a great story overall. The eikons specific accessories that you find should be implemented as an upgrade to the coresponding skills.I also would change the time when you unlock these two DLC's. There are already a lot of quests right before the final battle. IMO the dungeon DLC should unlock after the timeskip as some kind of a flashback to show what Clive did in these 5 years.

_childDocuments_.review: Questionable. 7/10 overall, at best. Parts of a 10/10 game are here, but they're squished between a 6/10 game that takes up 90% of the runtime, and that's not accounting for the literal 11 hours of main story cutscenes.FFXVI has...Epic highs in the form of climactic boss fights, music, voice acting, and some emotionally resonant plot and character moments.General mids in the form of... - the simplistic, limiting battle system; - 11 hours of main story quest cutscenes that often go on for far too long - a dour, bleak, and depressing world that only grows more so as the plot moves forward- open-zone environments that look pretty yet generic while being largely devoid of reason to explore- linear dungeons that look incredible, but feel particularly predictable and straightforwardAnd a ton of lows in the form of...- trash mobs fights being 95% of the gameplay, as none are threats that require more than half a brain cell to be active at a given time as you run through your combat rotation- FFXIV's influence at its worst via its exact quest structure (Main Story Quests and sidequests) and low production quality sidequest animations (there's a clear difference between the animations used in these instances and when they actually bothered to animate the characters)- padding between set pieces and moments of interest. If you're up for a fast-paced narrative, this ain't it- repetition in general. You've seen all the game has to offer after the 2nd boss fight; there's just more of ittely, FFXVI doesn't feel like a Final Fantasy game beyond the usual trappings of FF (summons; chocobos; magic). Whether you'll like it or not depends on how much patience you have for the slow-paced plot and the lows between the climactic highs, as the game experiments with leaving behind party systems and RPG elements while sacrificing complexity to optimize for accessibility. As far as gameplay goes, FFXVI opts for style over substance even as it comes nowhere close to being an equivalent action game to, say, Bayonetta or Devil May Cry V, and that is sure to chafe at many who appreciate past FF entries.Overall: FFXVI is okay, but it tested my patience and I fully understand why others don't like it and didn't finish it.

_childDocuments_.review: I’ve only put about 6 hours into Final Fantasy XVI, but it’s already shaping up to be one of the most intense and engaging FF games I’ve played. The story, visuals, and combat have definitely pulled me in, and I’m excited to see where it goes from here.Pros So Far:Story Hooks Right from the Start: The darker, mature story is immediately gripping. Clive is an interesting lead, and I’m already invested in his journey and the world around him. The game doesn't hold back with the themes, and it’s refreshing to see this new direction for Final Fantasy.Incredible Visuals and Presentation: Everything looks amazing. The landscapes, the character designs, the cinematics—it all blends together so well, and I feel like I’m watching a high-quality fantasy show while I play.Fast-Paced Combat: The real-time combat is a blast. I’m getting used to the combos and Eikonic powers, and it feels great when you pull off those powerful moves. They’ve really gone all-in on action, and I’m enjoying every fight so far.Cons So Far:Very Linear So Far: It feels pretty focused on the main story path, with not much room for exploring yet. I don’t mind it for now because the story is so strong, but it’s worth knowing if you’re looking for a big open-world vibe.Side Quests Feel Basic: I’ve done a few side quests, and while they’re fine for a break from the main story, they don’t feel as deep or essential so far. Hopefully, they pick up a bit as I go along.Not Much in Terms of Customization: It’s pretty straightforward with gear and abilities, which is great for getting right into the action, but if you’re used to heavy RPG mechanics, you might find it a bit streamlined.Overall, I’m loving the experience so far. Even just 6 hours in, Final Fantasy XVI is shaping up to be a game that’s bold, cinematic, and totally worth diving into. Can’t wait to see how it all unfolds!

_childDocuments_.review: Post Game Edit: I have now beaten the game. I don't want to go on a tirade, I'll just say this. This game aimed to to get a B rating, and it got it. It aimed no higher, took no risks, it was not brave or bold or special. It exists as an above average game that did not try to be great and it did just that. This is not a Final Fantasy.___________________________________I've been an FF fan for over 20 years and am about 1/4th of the way through the game, after the return to Rosaria/Phoenix Gate. Don't know how it ends, but I see where it's going. This game is really good, but not great. I put this game at about 7th place (14, 6, 9, 7, 10, 12, -16-, 8), I put it over 8 mostly due to gameplay.GameplayTL;DR A good action-rpg held back by long stretches of being drip fed adequate MMO-like quests, new abilities and good boss fights. This game feels like a Dragon's Dogma world, with an MMO-like structure mixed with pretty good Kingdom Hearts combat on top.- Very good integration of Devil May Cry like combat with RPG elements (but it does not hold a candle to DMC5)- Combat can be repetitive, especially with the slow exp rate and long stretches between getting new Eikons. I recommend testing out different ability mixes often by resetting points in skills to keep things fresh.- The sidequests have been mostly superfluous fetch/rescue quests usually with monetary not very valuable rewards that have only been passable to me because of some very small story rewards that add to the setting a little. There are mercifully few of them so far.- The bosses are the highlight of this game- I like how they added noticeable area attacks like in FF14 that you can anticipate while fighting midbosses and bosses. It's one of my favorite parts of FF14's combat.- I personally don't like QTEs but they are here and at least add a cinematic quality to bosses- You can feel how slow the game is sometimes like the; tutorials for simple things (yes you can turn them off, but they also turn off tutorials for necessary/new info), strange door opening QTEs and the oddly slow quest transitions. Yet the loading screens are pretty quick.Story (light spoilers)TL;DR The worst thing I can say about this game's story so far is "missed opportunities". I came in thinking I'd get an FFT or 12 or 14 styled deep plot with a big setting and if not a large at least a colorful cast. Everything story-wise is just adequate, above par, save the setting itself which is very fascinating. It's like a primer for FF14.- Characters - They're fine if not flat. Clive's main trait is his vengeance/guilt and brooding on dark aspects of his life and I desperately wish there's more to him later which seems to be sparking where I am. The Cid of this game is up there as one of the most charismatic Cids of the franchise. Jill's fine, a nice supportive young woman to take in Clive's dark. The supporting cast is inoffensive to decent.- Plot - A mostly straightforward revenge plot in the midst of deep political struggle sparked by resource problems that develops into more later as you deal with each nation's intertwining issues.- Setting - Fascinating. The world of Valisthea is not as detailed as most FF worlds, but I can tell it will open up more as things get more dire with mysteries like the ruins and Aether. The spreading Blight is a threat they make apparent to pull you in. The dependence on the Mothercrystals for blessings and power is intriguing. The flip on Bearers (mages) being slaves is fresh and gave me Dragon Age vibes. Though the theme of slavery comes across as convenient with how often you meet people against it personally but are told discrimination's a deep problem. The function of Dominants for the world and Clive's power's relationship to them is a good mystery.- Towns - None are memorable; they feel a bit better than Dragon's Dogma with at least some interesting elements like a nice field or crashed airship as a town square and more character with the little things like seeing how magic works in normal society or talks of local/current events. Each usually has one to three strong supporting characters.- Dialogue - This one hurts the most. The voice actors are really good, but the script is shallow. The characters don't talk about absolutely nothing, but it gets close. There are so many opportunities to add context and subtext in interactions between characters parting, reuniting, catching up on what's happened, the setting, using things that have been brought up to motivate or harm, etc. I'm not asking for more conversation, I'm asking for what's there to be deeper. Really examine the dialogue and acting in Vagrant Story, FF12, FFT and FF14 to see what I mean about giving you context and subtext. Just the opening of Vagrant Story and 12 (plus directorial choices) should give you what you need to see how well dialogue and setup can be made in a semi-action game's opening even with a relatively simple plot.- Pacing - In the end this game feels like it was intended to be long form, but had to be made short form. It uses slow plot beats and quests mixed with fast actiony moments that create a little dissonance. Yet that's the most confusing part is how slow it feels even though I know it's shorter than most FFs, and the lack of subtext does not help. I wish it were either longer with more dialogue depth, or shorter with less attempts at having depth, it's in a strange in-between.- Art Design - Good. The world is mostly classical medieval in look, but this game is missing that FF charm of outlandishly designed places and people. That is not true for the main characters, Eikons, enemies and ancient relics though; those are all well designed with complex clothes/looks that aren't too hard too complicated like some FFs can be. There's a hard cut separation between the simple medieval look and the fantastical magitech and character designs that has its own charm. The most prominent design motif is the "Repetitious, incomplete circle" seen mostly in ruins, very thematic.- Music - Great. Soken's work for FF14 is far better due to years of work on that game's expansive OST with many hits and misses, but this game's OST is still great. The area music adds a lot to Valisthea's semi-realistic medieval fantasy, wonder and culture. His use of leit motif is always excellent and helps connect ideas, themes, characters and groups to moments. Sometimes I swear I you can almost feel how a plot point is going to change or come up just because you heard its melody elsewhere. When you're in an ancient mystical forest or a military fortress infiltration the music makes you feel it. My favorite thing about the music is that the transition from areal music to battle music is seamless and uses the same melodies as the area to keep you in the feeling of that area while fighting; like FF13-2, Nier, KH3, etc. does.- Some early mysteries/setup/buildup are not hinted at well with scenes and bread crumbs to figure them out for yourself. For instance Clive's 13 year timeskip is only talked about, not shown. We don't get to see his striving, struggles and killing which makes its mention later a little hollow. Also the opening feels like the "pancakes" moment of a certain other rpg. And the scenes at the end of the return to Phoenix Gate confuse me, not in terms of plot and mystery, but more motivation and how the characters understand what's going on or not.I get the feeling this game is very back-loaded. As in the highlights, strong points and heavy lifting are going to be in the last 3rd. Despite my problems there's a slow, progressive buildup that I just wish had a better filling out. This game has a good strong start, but due to the poor dialogue and semi-repetitive combat after the second dungeon up to the return to Rosaria I have not been enjoying it as much as I'd like. Yet I still think this is a very good game.If I had to give it a number right now it's somewhere around a 7/10.
