_childDocuments_.review: Update: after 2 patches frame rate issues still persist.I'd love to give this game a medium voting but considering the high praise this game receives and does not deserve, I feel obliged to give a negative rather than a positive rating.The good:- likeable protagonist- overarching story feels promising- gameplay and fighting is funThe bad:- the much critizised performance issues. I tried all the mods and am running everything at the lowest settings (my rig: GTX 3070, Intel i9 9900KF 3.6GHz, 32gb Memory). I have huge frame drops especially in combat and cut scenes. Running any other modern game on high settings was never an issue.- nearly all dialogues feel shallow. There is no depth or bigger meaning to what is being said and it just comes across as superficial. Characters seem to have a past but you never learn more details, they just act as if something happened between them but you learn no concrete details. - Characters make stupid decisions like staying behind to cover a retreat when they are incognito at the moment and could simply leave without being noticed altogether. - The people who are dominants (meaning they are able to transform into one of the godlike creatures) are everywhere. They don't feel like a rarity but basically every character with more screen time than 30 minutes seems to be a dominant. It feels unnatural.- I wonder why people go to war at all. Every faction seems to have 1 to 2 dominants. Why bother sending your foot soldiers who die in masses as soon as the other dominant arrives when you could just fight it out with the dominants solely?- Every dominant seems to have healing powers of a certain degree as soon as they turn into these gods. It negatively impacts the tension when the big god fights happen.- All the leaders appear to be simply evil or fans of war with no deeper reason. Just for the fun of it. I often feel like there is no depth to most of the characters. Jill as another example seems to have been with our protagonist for a very long time and they seem to have a connection but I do not know anything about her. She is just always there. Reading two lines of background story in the wiki gave me more understanding of her than playing the game for over 20 hours. - Side quests and "filler" main quests (that kind of get in the way on your path to actual bigger and interesting goals) are with little depth. It is not comparable with the unique mission design of a "Witcher 3" where twists and surprises motivated you intrinsically to move forward and learn more. It is always as expected: Go from point a to b, maybe kill something and return. It feels like finishing a to do list.Conclusion:It is a solid game and does deserve a rating of 7/10 depending on your expectations. But It definitely does not deserve the high praise it receives.I like the game and will play it to the end. I hope for positive surprises in the overarching story line and do enjoy the combat (despite the frame rate issue).

_childDocuments_.review: Main story: Seemingly dull for the first half with slow pace paired with overwhelmingly boring sidequests. due to 'world building' purpose. QTE system is too simplistic with only 2 buttons. Torgal battle mechanic is unnecessary; dealing insignificant damage. Honestly, 'Final Fantasy' difficulty fixes some of these issues but it's locked behind NG+.Mind you, the final boss was ASS easy in normal mode. I legit machine-gunned him to death using single leviathan ability, without having the chance to change my eikon due to back-to-back battles.Weapon & Armor: It's as if they didn't know how to implement blacksmith system properly.a) there is barely a weapon/armor to craft with no unique stats to be considered except +15 STR for new weapon.b) overabundance of materials and money in your inventory. (even if you avoid mobs most of the time)Music: Very good OSTs.  Characters: Jill- Can be more expressive. It felt like she's an android with very little emotion 90% of the time. Some non-spoiler knowledge about the world of the game that makes it easier to understand going into it blind that you'll learn in the first half an hour (Like actually) but possibly not register because you don't know what's important yet:- Nations are generally built around "Mothercrystals". _childDocuments_.review: TLDR: This game for me personally is a C rank on a tier list or a 7/10. Its a step in the right direction, but is weighed down heavily by some poor design choices. Would I recommend this game? Yes, but I'm not going to go out of my way to recommend it. Let me get into a more in depth review. This is from the perspective of someone who has played every mainline FF game (not including the 2nd games and spin offs within those series, like say ff7 crisis core.)First thing I wanna point out: I am fan of Yoshi P's work and team. He turned FF14 into a legendary MMO and I can not express that this man is dedicated to his craft. With that being said, im going to reference this as one of my biggest issues with the game.STORY:I would say that the story is quite excellent! Aside from some minor small things I have against it, I think the theme of this FF game has to do with free will if I had to make my own assumption. I very much enjoy this games CID, and seeing how FF5 is my all time favorite game in the series, I was beyond happy to see the amount of love and joy put into the writing and references from that game into this one. PACING: God Awful. This game has some of the worst pacing ive ever seen in a modern single player game. The issue here is the design philosophy that was applied. Yoshi P and his team have tried to apply the ff14 design elements in this game were as those elements are amazing and work great in an MMO environment. Here you run into major problems and god awful pacing that just amounts to doing the same quest over and over with a small reskin here and there.Here is what I mean. Without any spoilers: your going to need to go a city and fast. The story puts in a sense of urgency into the players mind and you feel the tension with that going through you. Here is a big problem that keeps happening: when you enter a new area, just like in ff14 the developers want the player to experience it by doing a handful of quests and side objectives to familiarize themselves with the land. While im not against this design philosophy, what I am against is this: If were urgently needing to get from point a to b, why would you have the player stop what their doing? Just to do some 5 pointless fetch quests, fight the same monsters, and for what? For some side characters that have no major story relevance outside this one area? This would be fine in an MMO setting, but not here.They could have easily just broken up these things with some fun side mini games like: cards, chocobo racing, even a damn gambling section would have at least made things a lot less aggravating. GAMEPLAY:I would say its quite fine and fun, however is the issue with scaling and certain enemies. You combine this with the boring side quests and fetch quests, you end up loosing your mind realizing that if this games combat system wasn't fun, it would be outright unplayable. So because the system is fun to experiment and mess around with, it saves the game from out right just being a miserable experience. Mid boss battles feel like they tend to drag even longer than some of the major boss fights. The boss fights are easily the best part of this entire game. SOUNDTRACK:This honestly might be my favorite ff sound track ever. Soken never misses and the heart and soul that went into composing these tracks. I find myself listening to them every day when I go to the gym to work out.Last few thoughts:There was a lot of debate on wether this game felt like a Final Fantasy game, coming off the train wreck of FF15, I wouldn't be surprised if a lot of fans felt disillusioned. I know Yoshi P and his team are experts at turning around failing series, I would just be flat out honest and say this: Even tho in my opinion his team missed the mark and failed to deliver a truly amazing single player final fantasy, they did take a massive step in the right direction. I trust that yoshi P and his team will take the thoughts and feedback of the players into mind if and when they decide to try again and make FF17. To me that could easily be the best game they would ever produce as in my past 10 years of playing all the ff games and playing ff14, one thing is for certain: Yoshi P always delivers and improves when he knows he needs to. Thanks for reading this review! I hope I didn't sound to negative, its a good game but its not amazing ether. Its biggest problems outweigh its strongest moments.

_childDocuments_.review: Edit after completing the game:A masterfully woven tapestry of loss, sacrifice, love, tyranny, gods, hardship, redemption, and perseverance. Ignore what I say below about the story deviating into nonsense territory. They thread the needle so well and keep the story engaging, emotional, and important throughout. My only issue with the game is now that I've completed it I will miss these characters and guiding them through their struggle dearly. Up there with Final Fantasy 6 and 4 in terms of greatness. This game deserves all the praise and accolades it gets and then some. I wish more people would play it. Resume first impressions review:While completely upending the formula for Final Fantasy -- 16 feels more like the SNES Final Fantasy 4 than any game in the series. For fans of that unsung classic, this is a very good thing. It mixes the best parts of mature storytelling with the least anime story (at least for the first half -- until you get to the mystical nonsense later in the game) in ages. People who have stuck with the series through 13 on know what I mean. It's just nonsensical garbage -- this story feels grounded and not a single character speaks in an annoying squeaky child's voice. It's just wonderful.Combat slaps, and once you start unlocking new builds and powers you can really flex on enemies in fun and satisfying ways. I'm on a 4090 and Ryzen 9 7950X so obviously I'm not having any performance  issues, and the widescreen mod still allows for achievements, so if you're on a 21:9, install it. It's worth it. So is this game -- for $50 you're getting a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ steal for this fantastic game.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best action games of this generations, but to call it an RPG is generous at best. There is no branching main story, no exciting side quests, and barely any build variety. What we have here is a competent action combat that stands in the middle of the triangle formed by Dark Souls DMC and God of War, bringing some ideas from each but not really adhering to either formulas. It's really good, if somewhat easy. But what brings me here, and what is the reason you would and should buy Final Fantasy XVI, is the story, particularily the boss fights. Because boys, this is an absolute MUST SEE. This is the kind of absolutely epic nonesense story that we all have dreamt our favourite Anime/Cartoons could produce but just didn't have the technology pr budget.Graphics: 9/10 Music 10/10Gameplay: 8/10Writing: 8/10Lore 10/10Boss fights: 2 out of 2 cut off Kupka handsNow to address the only really big issue with the Steam version of the game: I revised my review from negative to positive in light of the recent patch which seems to have fixed the performance leak.That said, the game still runs like absolute ass on PC. It absolute unoptimized and there is no indicator of the graphically intensive locations. Some places just tank FPS for seemingly no reason. So keep that in mind. Unless you have a strong high end GPU perferably of the recent generation, you can forget anything higher than shaky 30FPS.

_childDocuments_.review: This game deserved to be GOTYSo that in and of itself is my TLDR review. However, for those looking for more, let me first start off with how I came to play this game to begin with. I had pre-ordered Dragon Age: The Veilguard, and refunded the pre-order. Had used money I had earmarked for my dog Joby...who died at 10 weeks. My father was in the hospital, and I wanted something to distract me - something story driven. Veilguard wouldn't be out soon enough, so I looked at what new was already out. Final Fantasy has always been hit or miss for me. I adored FFIX, but despise FFXI've beaten the original FF7, but barely made it past the beginning area in FF15So to say I was iffy about this game is an understatement. Especially since the change to action combat, and that I had heard it was pretty much on rails. Still, I watched a youtube video by the "Before you buy" guys. Falcon, eagle, whatever his name is. Anyways, he described the game as Final Fantasy's attempt at Game of Thrones, which intrigued me. Had they finally went a more ...mature route? So that was my getting here. For the last month I've gotten a few hours in here, a few there, and during which my father died. However, each day I looked forward to seeing more and more of Clive Rosfield, who, in my appraisal, is the best voice-acted character since Geralt of Rivia. Not only that, he's believable and well written. The story itself was a JOY to experience. I'd say the story was better than that of Witcher 3, and I loved Witcher 3. Only reason I'd say it's BETTER is because it flows so much smoother than that of the Witcher games. Yes, the game is on rails a lot of the time, but that isn't a bad thing here. Side quests exist, and later on become important, but there are always just enough to give you a break between main story entries and then it's back on. The pacing feels like Mass Effect 2, but again, even better. Oh and Square don't hold back either. They do go mature and without being overtly gory or relying on nudity. Not that I mind either, but to see a game stand on it's feet without them, and still feel like it's keyed to adults - that I am amazed by in the current market. FFIX was my first FF game and will always be my sentimental favorite, but if I am to be honest, I'd say this game has become my favorite in the series and has made it onto my top 5 of all time favorite RPGs, period. The combat feels somewhat similar to Monster Hunter and Soulslike games, just in terms of timing your dodges or your parries. You've abilities that slow down or stop time which do help, and all of it is very flashy and very satisfying in a "I'm a dragon ball z fan, here is a big bang or kamehameha" kind of way. But I wasn't in this for the finish because of the combat. I was here for the story. I had to see what came next, and I had to experience it first hand, not see it spoiled. When a story is able to grip you in that way...it has love and care put into it by the writer(s).This game is worth buying if you love a good story. It will be one you remember long after you've finished it. 9.9/10 What would have made it a 10 is if a certain outlaw had made an appearance at the very end. Those who know, know.

_childDocuments_.review: 4/10The music, sound design, and voice acting are incredible, and the game itself is visually stunning. The large-scale mecha-kaiju battles (though more cinematic than interactive) are thrilling to watch. Unfortunately, the rest of the game falls flat.The gameplay feels like a stripped-down version of mechanics we’ve seen done better elsewhere. Even classic turn-based RPGs offer more freedom and fluidity than what’s found here. Final Fantasy XV delivered a more satisfying combat experience, and it doesn't come close to the level of Devil May Cry V—even the fourth installment. There’s zero choice in gear, no stats to customize, and companions feel identical and uninspired.So maybe the story saves it? Unfortunately, no. It feels like someone tried to blend the worst parts of Game of Thrones with Marvel-style dialogue. The characters lack depth, coming across as hollow or puppet-like, with only one or two exceptions. You finish the game feeling like they’re action figures with voices, lacking any defining traits.For a game aiming for a mature tone, the only “mature” aspect is the repetitive use of a single slur, which quickly loses any impact. Where Game of Thrones (which the game feels most inspired by) offers complex characters, schemes, and motivations, this game offers nothing beyond partial nudity and cursing, never venturing deeper than a puddle.I love the Final Fantasy series and always will, but this entry feels like a step down—even compared to Final Fantasy XV.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay....I've finished the main story and figured I'd give my take as a decades old FF fan.  Been playing since the original release of ff7, so...there is my age for you.Let me start by saying that I do not feel this should have been a main FF franchise entry and is more deserving of a title as an offshoot of the main FF franchise.  I'll keep this short and sweet, so here are my cons:Cons:- Does not feel like a journey.  You revisit places ALOT- Solo player experience, and "party" members are just AI with no meaningful damage output unless against trash mobs- The story felt dragged out, and there really wasn't depth to the characters or villain(s).  Near the end it felt like it was really dragging and nothing was really happening.  I'm particular annoyed at Jill and how she is pretty much a blank slate the entire game, and this blank slate "follows" you the majority of the game and there isn't a real connection between her and Clive that's shown until later in the game which you see coming form a mile away and it's annoyingly hinted at during the game's progression.  Even after her goal is met, she is still kinda just a meh character- Side quests get boring fast and imo is a poor way to develop story.  Some of that content should've been built into the main story quests to flesh out world building/environment (I've done all but 3 side quests in the game).  - Combat gets way, waaaay too easy as you progress- QTEs- Performance can take a hit in some areas- Feels like anime bros made this game- Hugo Kupka fight's tone vs. the rest of the gamePros:- Combat feels good.  But as mentioned in my cons becomes pointless later in the game.  ESPECIALLY after you get your last eikon which just takes off so much damage and wipes mobs in an instant- Cinematic battles.  I'm torn here as some of those battles should have been more interactive, but they nailed the spectacle aspect of them and enjoyed watching those- Hunt Board.  I actually enjoyed this as it brought enemy variety, although some were just altered enemies of those you already faced.  Still a good way to battle different types of enemies.- Music is top tierI can't recommend this game as a FINAL FANTASY game.  For me, these games used to be about traveling with a party, each party member being unique, each party member involved in combat, the feeling of going on a journey in the game and seeing/exploring lively cities and not run down villages all the time (no big cities you explore), leveling up a character and building them (RPG aspect), SECRETS....SECRETS....SECRETS (items, weapons, etc.).  Nothing is waiting for you if you try to explore.  No secret eikons, no secret weapons....everything is tied to a quest.  I've played ff14 a good amount, and it's clear that team was behind this given camera shots are straight out of ff14 story scenes at times, and they make nods here and there to 14.  The little music and camera shot when you accept a side quest I honestly felt like I was playing 14 in that little moment...just shows much this game was influenced by 14.  Which leads me to believe I think this game may have struggled if they didn't tie the FF name to it.What I would highly recommend to the developers is that if you want to keep this play style, bring some time of a true party system back in like in ff7 remake, but preferably ones where you can choose ALL THE TIME which characters you want in the party.  In this game I should have been able to switch to Jill as a playable character during a fight with her own unique moveset....maybe certain characters have advantages against certain enemy types or something.....I feel they used the eikon switching to supplement that feeling of just playing with one single person in a FF game, but that gets old and after King B's eikon the game goes to super easy mode....so there are obvious balance issues and the combat system needed work. During most of the game play I felt starved for a story and connections, and that's a big part of why I liked these games.  The sessions with Vivian were just exposition dumps that I never really followed the political aspect of the world, but even then there wasn't a whole log going on there.  Again, most of the story Jill is a blank slate.....Clive's appearance and vibe is just that of a super edge lord, and there isn't a big amount of enemy variety.So all in all, play the game if you want.  But dont expect a traditional FF experience.  Things are clearly changing but I think we need to make sure they know what we don't like, and don't take this series for granted thinking people will just buy it because it has the FF name attached to it.  At the end of the day this isn't a FF game.  Is it good enough to buy...play the demo first.  If that grabs you then sure go ahead.  But outside of that if the demo is kind of meh....don't buy this game because you will for sure be disappointed as you progress through it's content.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Beautiful game with smooth combat that should not be called Final Fantasy because they have left abandoned nearly everything genre defining and special about the FF series.Good: the graphics are beautiful both cgi and gameplay, the  music is varied and good, the story is cohesive and enjoyable, and the combat, though completely new and different to the series, is smooth.Bad:  *The game is no longer what I would consider an open world environment. The world is tiny and not explorable in the true sense of the word. You don't interact with the environment, there are NO HIDDEN items or areas I have discoivered as of yet @ 40ish hours in. You walk from point A to point B on these tiny maps designed to be straight roads(hand holding).*There is NO  character development, NONE. You have zero need to gear for special situations like resists or special combat tactics because they have been removed! You can no longer find 1000's of pieces of gear from monsters, hidden chests or areas, etc becauset it no longer exists! You are given every little upgrade as part of the main quest with very few examples found in side quests( a lot of which being useless by the time they are achievable) so I am up to a dozen? weapons I can use and they are all exactly the same with exception only of their skin. No special's talents, boosts, stats, different weapon types, etc. Stats have just been reduced to attack and defense essentially(hand holding to the extreme).*The new combat system , while very smoothly implemented, is just boring after your first few fights because you realize you can basically stand in one place and hit attack or evade, that's it! Your eikons don't actually matter, their elements don't matter, your gear doesn't matter because there is no complexity or difficulty to the fights any longer.*While the CGIs are great, there is no longer any choice of what you want to do or where to go to do it! The entire game is linearly mapped out for you with no RPG type choices of consequence built in. The side quests are absolutely boring. There really aren't a lot of REAL sidequests either when you compare to older games or other games of the genre. Most of the sidequests are literal "hey teleport here, run 200ft, kill this monster(don't worry zero challenge) and the game teleports you back to turn it in in exchange for....some gold. No prizes, special items, gear upgrades, nothing because they have removed the need for anything special in the game! The Main quests are not much better. There is a bug as of this writing they have yet to fix to my knowledge. IF your screen times out during a CGI the game crashes. Why is this important? Because the main quests go like this most of the time: Teleport to new place, watch 10 minutes of CGI(amazing looking, cool) but try not to forget to play with your mouse or controller during this time when you are SUPPOSED to be enjoying the CGI, then take control for 10 minutes to fight the EXACT same fight over and over about 8 times, 10 more minutes of CGI(controller, screen timeout, crash, etc)then kill the boss, 10 more minutes of CGI and done! It is extremely boring aside from the lovely CGI's. THis is supposed to be an RPG though right? *The game is no longer an RPG. It is a Story with a little combat in between, combat that a 5 year old could complete because all complexity and difficulty has been thrown away, all of it! The entire game is a Hand Holding event with lots of pretty picture, no choices, no development, no suprises, it's all gone. I personally will no longer be purchasing anything close to FF16 that Sony produces in the future. It's a great game but it is NOT an open-world RPG as they claim. It is an casual story game whatever you call that.

_childDocuments_.review: There is a ton that I could say about this game. From its musical score to the combat and skill expression, to the narrative body as a whole. This is a game for both fans of the series and newcomers wanting to get a taste of what the Final Fantasy universe is like and all of the joy it can bring. And this title certainly delivers. Despite a few flaws here and there and perhaps -a controversial topic- the preference of the uncapped frame rate mod, this is a title worth picking up~The sensation of combat feels akin to that of Devil May Cry where you have multiple abilities and can string combos together. Mastering such abilities allows for further customization and skill expression and the enemies you're using these combos against pack a punch too. Worthy of that of a protagonist in this game. Coming off of FF15 and the remake of FF7, the combat has a lot to draw similarities to, and all combine to make the fun action sequences all the more thrilling. From bosses to regular enemies, it feels great. Slow at first as your skills are limited at the beginning, but as you grow and explore the more you unlock and the stronger you become.Gods, where do I even begin? The writing is fantastic, the characters are relatable in terms of personalities, and each of them have their own personal goals and challenges that they're facing. Even as we grow in the story, these characters evolve and change around us as well due to the story and the things that we encounter within. It can feel like the pacing may be long for some (Average completion time is around 30-ish hours and a little less if you're speed running the game) but most games in the franchise are long. Its what makes these RPG's what they are.With a New Game+ mode and a unique difficulty that is only an option there, this game is as easy or as hard as you make it out to be. The quests do a good job leveling you up to where you need to be to handle just about anything the game can throw at you. And the DLC content is also a challenge too! I never felt stuck unless I "accidentally" went to challenge a boss that was around 15-20 levels above me. *cough cough fighting a dragon cough couch*I haven't played a solo game in a long time. With so many multiplayer games out there and so much to try and keep up with, its good to have a game that will be here when you get here rather than a live service or online game where keeping up is always key. After a long day of classes or even doubling a shift at work, I coudl always come back home and enjoy the story and gameplay that is Final Fantasy 15. If I were to give one complaint, its just the side quests lengths/quantity. There are a lot and can pile up quick if you let them linger on without touching them. You will laugh, you will cry, you will have relatable moments and feel sympathy for characters. You'll cheer for victories, feel defeats when you fall, and have moments of triumph when you hear that fan fair theme play. (Du du du dun, dun dun dun da dun) This game is fantastic from start to finish. And for the price of a average AAA title, you get a full game AND the DLC's. And I believe thats a win. Went into this game blind ever since it was announced, and i'm so glad I waited for it to arrive on pc."No matter how bitter the truth that awaits me, I will press on."10/10. Would, and will be, playing again.

_childDocuments_.review: I didn't really know what to expect when people described this game as "linear" or "Devil May Cry-like," which left me a bit worried because I wasn't a particularly big fan of DMC or Bayonetta, however, I think this game does a good job of keeping things moving in such a way that I don't have any issues with it so far. In fact, I was kinda surprised how easy it was to get sucked in to the whole thing. As someone who tends to prefer more open games with a bit more of an RPG focus, I was a bit surprised how much I enjoyed moving from place to place quickly without having to do any obligatory "roam around an area and level up with nonsense fights" kind of stuff.If for some reason it feels like a slog, I'll update with a negative review, but for now, it's really a surprisingly solid experience thus far.UPDATE MANY HOURS LATER: So now that I've had a lot more time with the game, I can really appreciate its approach to the world and how it balances "linearity" and "open world" ideas. In a lot of ways, it feels like XV now because various stages are reused and begin to give the game more of an open-world feeling. The nice part is that there's quite a bit of variation because each of the "stages" is large enough to house quite a bit without feeling like I'm constantly walking across an enormous expanse. Also, the gameplay mechanics do get deeper and more compelling with time, even if they're not the deepest RPG mechanics.The story is strong for a Final Fantasy game and is easily one of the most interesting ones we've had in years.As someone who preordered Metaphor and FFXVI at the same time, I feel like I'm going to get the perfect balance of both new and traditional JRPG goodness in recent years.

_childDocuments_.review: The thing that will determine whether you'd enjoy this game or not depends on how you define Final Fantasy as a series. If you're coming into this expecting a sprawling RPG with tons of depth and customization to explore, you'll be disappointed. Final Fantasy XVI is much closer to a linear action-adventure game, where there are not a lot of RPG systems interactions to be found. What you'll find in this game is an incredible action game with an amazing sense of scale and wonder, packed in an epic story that is presented excellently with stellar voice acting, scene direction, and a heart-pounding soundtrack. There is a sense of focus and vision that you can feel throughout the whole experience that we have not seen in this series since the classics, and in my opinion that is every bit as "Final Fantasy" as you can get. As for the PC port itself, this is a pretty demanding game. I've already made peace with the fact that I can only experience the game at 30fps and no upscaling with my current setup. The game is still very much playable and enjoyable as I did not notice any other major technical issues. Nevertheless, you will need some pretty beefy hardware to push this game to its best. My PC currently rocks an i7 10700f, an RTX 3060 12GB and 32GB of DDR4 RAM. I play the game at maxxed out settings in 1080p 30fps with no upscalling. Lossless Scaling can give me a pretty solid 60fps experience with frame generation.

_childDocuments_.review: To preface, I started my FF journey with FF15 which to this day is probably still my favourite FF game (Yes yes I know crucify me) and moved on to 13, 13-2, Pixel Remasters 1-2, and then OG 7. None of the FFs after 15 really hit me as much as 15 did but I still enjoyed playing them. I won't lie, my drive to finish the entire series was kind of burning out...until I played FF16 when PC released.Story wise, top notch. I enjoyed the entire story, side quests were really good (most of them, at least) and don't get me started about the characters. Jill is top notch and I would steal her from Clive if I could but here we are 🤷. I've always played with JP voices but decided to give ENG a try since it was written first and wanted the lips to sync. Was very pleasantly surprised. VAs did a great job, especially Joshua and Dion. Music was chef's kiss, found some new favourite songs (My Star, The Worm Mounts, Holos).HOWEVER, nothing's perfect and there's still things I didn't like in FF16.The biggest thing being combat. It's not insanely bad or anything it just feels very...basic? I feel like it could've been just more rewarding and wished there was actual melee combos instead of using Eikon abilities to basically carry the fight and the 4-hit combo.The gearing system also felt really lackluster. Wished there were different weapon types and a more sophisticated crafting system. Crafting and upgrading weapons felt really underwhelming. Couldn't even really tell the difference with each new sword and upgrade since 90% of every fight involved using Eikons. It's just a cosmetic honestly.But overall, FF16 is definitely up there in one of my favourite games of all time. Not overtaking FF15 but the closet to doing so, at least. It really feels like my motivation to play every FF is reignited. Time to play FF7 Remake now.TLDR; Game very good👍Make me play rest of FF

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy 16 is an epic journey with a compelling main cast, gorgeous environments, tight action combat, engaging main story, and meticulously thought out lore. All of that is unfortunately undercut by low-effort padding* and glaring pacing issues**,  which first rear their head after the game's superb opening hours and only get progressively worse. I still loved the game, and I totally recommend it for the amazing highs, but it's a very uneven experience that would've benefitted from a more condensed approach and a better qualified dialogue editor (if the game even had one to begin with).   * Most (not all) of the diversions and side quests are mind-numbing filler too mundane for your character to be tasked with in the first place.  ** The dialogue tends to get pointlessly long-winded, killing all sense of urgency because characters keep standing and rambling without actually adding anything substantial minutes after it was time to get moving

_childDocuments_.review: I am a huge fan of the original final fantasy games (1-10) and I did give the newer ones a try. XII was a worthwhile experience despite the weak story. XIII had amazing graphics for its time, but weak story and characters. 15 was .....unique, and had memorable characters.Now let's talk about 16. There was a lot of hype about this game because of its relatively mature theme compared to earlier games. I tried it out with high expectations and.....was unfortunately disappointed. Disappointing. I didn't complete the game, and that itself speaks volumes about how unimpressed I was with the plot. Moreover, I feel the writers didn't really do a good job with some of the scripted events in the story. There will be times when a perfectly healthy/capable/powerful character just stands by helplessly while her companions are in trouble. And her only contribution in that life or death event is to scream out her companion's name occasionally despite actually doing anything. If you've watched Naruto, then I'm referring to the "Sakura" effect from early in the series. You'll see this happen frequently with the female character in your party.Satisfactory. No complaints here.The voice acting is convincing and professional for the main characters.This is pretty important in all games. Sometimes we are able to convince ourselves to sacrifice story for gameplay and vice versa. If you want people to stick with a game till the end, it needs to have either really good gameplay or really good story. We rarely get both. So I was hoping the gameplay would be the main selling point here as the story was nothing great. And oh boy was I disappointed. As others might have mentioned by now, this game is 80% cutscenes and 20% gameplay. And even the 20% gameplay includes several quicktime events during fights. You'll grow from being intrigued by these QTEs to being annoyed by them later. Even opening doors has you do a very unnecessary "hold F", which adds nothing but tedium to the game. Fights aside, even the questing can be very boring. I admit the main story quests were able to captivate me most of the time. But the side quests (and there are a lot of them) mostly involve walking from point A to point B and pressing F on a person/object, then going from point B to point C and pressing F, and then pressing F at several other locations. It is mindless, uninspired, and boring. I grew tired of this very fast.Despite all my complaints and the fact that I dropped the game at somewhere around the halfway mark, I'd still recommend buying this on sale and playing it if you're really bored while waiting for the next installment in the series. It has its flaws but I wouldn't call it a "bad game". But maybe my standards have dropped in recent years.....

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI, the latest installment in the beloved franchise, takes players on an unforgettable adventure through the enchanting world of Valisthea. From its gripping narrative to its immersive gameplay and stunning visuals, FFXVI delivers an experience that both captivates and impresses.The story of Final Fantasy XVI revolves around the tale of Clive Rosfield, a protagonist driven by a compelling dual purpose. As players embark on Clive's journey, they are immediately drawn into a realm fraught with political strife and ancient conflicts. The narrative unfolds with intricacy, weaving together elements of revenge, redemption, and the destiny of nations. With morally grey choices and complex character relationships, the storyline keeps players engaged and eager to uncover the secrets of Valisthea.Combat in FFXVI takes a departure from the turn-based mechanics of past entries, introducing a real-time system that is both dynamic and exhilarating. The seamless transitions between exploration and battles create a sense of immersion, allowing players to feel fully engrossed in the world. The ability to switch between characters with distinct play styles adds strategic depth and keeps combat encounters fresh and engaging.Visually, Final Fantasy XVI is a feast for the eyes. The graphics showcase a meticulous attention to detail, bringing the world of Valisthea to life with breathtaking environments, intricately designed cities, and character models that exhibit a level of realism rarely seen in the series. The darker and more mature art style complements the narrative tone, immersing players in a visually striking and atmospheric world.Behind the scenes, the development team, led by the talented Naoki Yoshida and Hiroshi Takai, has crafted an experience that honors the Final Fantasy legacy while pushing the boundaries of innovation. The result is a game that stays true to the series' roots while offering fresh and exciting elements that both longtime fans and newcomers will appreciate.Final Fantasy XVI is a triumphant addition to the acclaimed franchise. With its captivating story, thrilling combat system, and breathtaking visuals, it successfully transports players to a fantastical realm filled with adventure and intrigue. FFXVI proves that the Final Fantasy series continues to evolve and delight, promising an experience that will leave a lasting impression on players.

_childDocuments_.review: Due note before reading, I am playing on the very minimal, if not even below minimal specs.I am running on a nitro 5 gaming laptop with a GTX1650, 10th gen i5 CPU, and 16gb of ramThat out of the way, this game might just be my favorite game I have ever played. The story has brought me to tears on more than one occasion, and made me laugh more times than I can count, and every character feels like a real person, and I am not even half way done.I will say, if you don't like death, or blood, or people dying not being a big deal, you might not like this game. Death is a part of the game in the sense that it happens, but you need to move on and keep going. Sure there are the moments where you mourn specific people, but for the most part death happens fast. In my opinion, this is not a bad thing, because when you are in a life and death situation, you NEED to keep going.On the gameplay side of things, it feels like a mix of devil may cry meets witcher 3. In my personal opinion, I would love if all future FF games continued with similar systems, but I know a lot of FF fans dislike that this is an action game.Now as I said, I am running minimal specs, but I get frame drops at times so bad that I get 15fps, and I have issues with cutscenes dropping FPS when specific characters come on screen, to the point some sounds go out of sync. Although this isn't the best, the rest of the game being so good, I push past it. Most Dungeons and cutscenes within run at smooth framerates anyways. (I will also state I am running 720p fullscreen, because I could not get more than 15 fps in most areas with borderless 1080p, but again minimal specs.)All in all, in my personal opinion, if you have the money, and the system specs required, I recommend playing. I haven't stopped playing except to sleep and do IRL errands.

_childDocuments_.review: Visual masterpiece with hack-and-slash mechanics emphasizing reaction time over strategy or character build (i.e. little to no drawbacks for using fire-attuned attacks against fire-based creatures). One of the greatest stories that's come out of the FF franchise in recent iterations, but the inability to select difficulties results in a play-through that is not challenging enough to be engaging. While being able to switch through elemental stances to string together combinations for major damage is fun - it gets monotonous after the first few hours of unlocking a new affinity. Once you find a repetition that works, you'll end up using it over and over with few alterations based on the monsters or characters you are battling. This doesn't feel FF, to me. This is an opinion coming from someone that has played every FF game - and while the story is a grandiose mixture of politics and fantasy featuring the elemental deities we've all come to know, fear, and love throughout the FF franchise (Ifrit, Shiva, etc.), it fails to deliver the same level of dread as it felt when Seymour summoned Anima - or the joy of any number of other FF protagonists enlisting the aid of their aeons/eikons in the midst of a pitched battle. The cinematic-to-gameplay ratio in FF XVI is heavily tilted toward cinematics - more-so than almost any other in franchise history. Within a given hour of playtime, I feel it isn't too much of an exaggeration to say you have about 15-20 minutes of controlling the character to 40-45 minutes of watching the story unfold. The leveling system is not very rewarding. It lacks that feeling of satisfaction when you finally unlock Firaga, Full-Heal, Armor Break - or any other skill that you've faced enemies using earlier in the story and finally get to use yourself. It also fails to deliver on any sort of rewarding, fun side-game like FFX's Blitzball, Chocobo racing, or any other type that's been used in the past. Finally, its item and gear system is laughably simplistic to the point of being almost meaningless, and combined with how exceedingly easy the battles are, it is almost more fun to use under-leveled weapons so there is some semblance of a challenge.While its darker, more mature dialogue and storyline are a great departure from FF's general 'group of friends going on an adventure fighting against a singular big bad' approach, the inability to make any meaningful choices on the skills, build, or selection of who is in your party at a given moment takes away from what I've always enjoyed most about FF games - the strategy of bringing the right person for the right job. All that being said - I will still recommend this game just barely because of what it does right. It is a great story, the combat has its moments, and the voice acting is top-notch. Just be aware - this is not what many FF franchise fans, like myself, will expect, completely outside of the turn-based or real-time combat system that most people are complaining about. This is a guided Netflix show with Devil May Cry combat and a nod to FF icons.

_childDocuments_.review: Hello everyone! o/ Hope your day goes well!Final Fantasy 16 has been a PS5 exclusive for quite a while and recently has gotten a PC port due to Square Enix's efforts of going multiplatform.It is important to mention that I have already played the game on the PS5 but got it again on PC for the better experienceWithout further ado, Let's take a look at the PC version of FF16 and the game by itselfIt's not a secret that each Final Fantasy game is very different by its own. that also comes at the genre that it represents and FF16 is a perfect example of this. the FF community often does look at XVI as a FF game but with Devil May Cry gameplay and feel attached to it and I think it's a very accurate point of view. However, that doesn't mean that the game is flawed and instead I will be looking at the game with its own merits insteadThe story of the game is all focused around Clive Rosefield from start to finish with the game also giving us all of the details about during the main story right away. Making it easy to form a connection and relation while also introducing more characters and background stories which all seem to be connected very to the main point without taking our focus away or messing around with it. in terms of emotions and stakes, We are talking a roller coaster with that as the game constantly plays around that aspect which keeps the player constantly engaged and curious. every moment of the story is well designed and only made me more hooked to the realm of Valisthea. I strongly recommend getting the DLCs too as they do add more context towards the ending of the story while introducing more on their ownSo gameplay.. As I mentioned, This is a Devil May Cry but with FF theme on it which isn't a bad thing and I personally approve of but old timers might be disappointed with the lack of RPG elements as XVI did reduce that aspect to the very bare minimum compared to previous entiries.Combat is great and if I had to use a word to describe it then that will be "satisfying". Visually and feeling wise its great but the game shares a similar problem to FFXIV that the game by at its normal difficulty is very easy that the game is few steps away from including an autoplay feature. to truly experience and enjoy the combat then you have to go through New Game+ for that or otherwise it will feel as a visual novel/interactive movie to say the least due to the insane amount of cutscenes that the game has. It's very clear that CBU3 did use XIV as their baseline for the quest design and how the game represents itselfGraphics and port? It was a PS5 exclusive at first so it did aim at high standards within that aspect and the game does look amazing across all fronts and if anything. It's say that XVI has mastered the act of presentation wellHowever that also brings us to performance which weren't great on the PS5 already with constant slowdowns and FPS going down to as low as 15 or less and the problem keeps on going with PC as well. the performance of the game are rather incredibly inconsistent for no real reason. frame rate goes down for no real reason while in some scenes its more than perfect with all of the visual effects.Sometimes the game does have small micro shutters out of nowhere which can go through the entire game until you restart the computer (and no, even when VRAM, RAM or CPU aren't maxed out). Not to mention the lack of Ultrawide support or the game limiting the FPS to 30 in cutscenes. If you decide to play the game, I suggest looking at FFXVIFix which is a mod that does correct some of the shortcomings of the portWhat are my overall thoughts on FF16 and should you buy it? FF16 has been an amazing experience to me during the play-through of both platforms and genuinely I enjoyed the game and maxed all of the value I could get out of it. It's a great game by its own right and I would suggest people to at least try out the demo to see if it's for their liking. However, the port is plain and simple. Bad... and I do hope that the game will get more patches to improve the experienceAs far as my rating goes? FF16 by itself is a 8/10 game and I would recommend it. Just be aware that the port does have issues and a lot of them.

_childDocuments_.review: The Game is a stark contrast from FFXV in pretty much all ways.The world is more of a centralised hub system where you are free to visit the different maps as you unlock (and as the story allows) and a fair few are rather large but the exploration is fairly unrewarded.FFXVI has about 4 good things going for it:The narrative is fairly good, albeit not too original a premise.The cinematic clashes are phenomenal. The Eikon clashes are a really cool to watch.The Music is really great. Not Nier: Automata, but still very good.And Cid.Now, it has a few points worth mentioning that are not so great:The combat is weird. It is very weird. It is extremely simply, very flashy, and attacks flow very smoothly from one to another...but something keeps nagging at me. A "is this it?" feeling.I first thought it was because the combat mechanics are too simple. you have a sword attack, a ranged attack,3 special abilities related to your EIkon (of which you can have 3 and swap very smoothly in combat), the ability to jump, and some perfect timing features such as a perfect dodge, block, parry and timing certain special moves. After I noted all these abilities I realised that it's quite a lot. As someone who loves Soulsborne games, it certainly has more features than my standard souls build.Yet the Souls' gameplay felt more compelling.And after A LOT of thinking i realised that it's because in a Soulslike, your actions feel impactful. To parry someone is a high risk move but the reward has a huge payoff. When you dodge an attack, its because you have to or you die in like 3 hits. In other games with a perfect dodge feature, you typically get a slow time feature where you can deal a lot of damage to your enemies before having to dodge like crazy again.FFXVI doesn't have this. It's not a rewarding combat system.Don't get me wrong though, the fluidity of combat is some of the best I've seen. There is only one official combo set but the combat is designed that you can effectively make your own. You can mix attacks and do follow-up with certain attacks that actually behave as a scripted combo. e.g. Around 30ish hours in I found out that following up a dash attack with a ranged attack blasts enemies with bigger explosive that knocks them prone and allows you to follow up with what is effectively a headstomp.You teleport infront of a flying enemy, blast them to the ground, immediately follow up with a charged range attack that knocks them back into the air and repeat the whole process.The issues is...it lacks impact. That headstomp from earlier rarely kills any enemies later on in the game even if you are over leveled, and the whole reverse juggling airborn enemies can only be repeated twice. So the option to spice up the combat mechanics are there, but you actively have to put effort in to find them, and even when you do it's pretty lack luster.Another example is the perfect parry mechanic. You can parry(to my knowledge so far) ANY attack in the game if you time it right. But your reward is a brief bit of slow time (which to enemies which are just damage sponges is pretty meaningless) in which IF you use a special ability it speeds up the cool down for it but only for the duration of the time left before slowed time deactivates, and even then its not by a significant amount.What I'm trying to say is...the combat is flashy.Very Flashy. But that's it. It's like a watered down bayonetta.A really watered down bayonetta.But is it terrible? Meh. It's just mid. painfully mid.Another issue I've been having is crashes. I'm not sure why, and I have a very high end laptop and the settings shouldn't be pushing it too hard, but it does crash and only during cutscenes.This is a major issue, because the cutscenes are SO LONG. The story is pretty engaging so it's not too bad the first time, but crashing through what feels like a 8 minute long cutscene only to have to watch it all again is just frustrating...As for the other game mechanics?Well, you only unlock a bunch of them like halfway through the story.Hunts are an example of this. And most of your abilities are story locked as well. Which is not inherently bad. I just think its worth noting (especially for combat reasons) that you don't start with much but a gritty story, a relatively ok main character and a really fun mentor character.TLDRCid carries the game. Charon is also pretty fun.

_childDocuments_.review: The performance of this game is abysmal.I have a 3080ti and a 5800x, and even the lowest settings get extremely choppy FPS in the bigger areas (Which you conveniently won't get to until you're well past the 2 hour refund mark)Even ignoring that, the cutscenes are locked to 30 fps.This is just a piss poor port.Edit after more hours:So the performance got a bit better, but this is just a bad Final Fantasy game.Let me be clear: The story is good. The story is the best thing about it. If you like political intrigue, you'll like the story.But every Final Fantasy after 7 (and some before) had something to draw you into the world gameplay-wise. 7 had chocobo breeding, golden saucer, etc. 8 had Triple Triad, 9 had the card game and mini games. 10 had Blitzball. Hell, even 15 had cooking and fishing, and a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ customizable car.16 has nothing. 16 has generic fetch side quests, kill x enemies, etc. 16 has combat, story, combat, story, combat story. 16 has cutscene primal fights with Quick Time Events. They're awesome to watch, and some of the combat is cool. But it's generic, and boring, and that's all there is in the game.And worse yet: Naoki Yoshida decided to make even basic enemies take several minutes of pure non-step beating on them to actually kill them. I installed a mod to increase the MC's damage by 150%, and reduced enemy health by 30%, and it still takes too long to kill some of the enemies. It's insane. This game stands for what not to do with your combat: Artificially jack up enemy HP numbers just to prolong the playtime.It's insane how bad this game is after you get past the pretty scenery/graphics, and the characters and story. It's basically a visual novel with a little more pzazz.If you're someone who can absolutely fall in love with the good things this game has, then you will enjoy it. I'm not saying you won't. But most people are going to want more from a Final Fantasy game. I want to be IN the world and feel like a part of it, with more activities than just combat.

The story and characters are bland, uninspired, checklist-driven more than anything. Any kind of human-like ambiguity, gets resolved easily because plot tends to happen to it. The story simply doesn't let the characters out of their leashes. The characters don't have room to breathe, to be other than their past and their duties and whatever the ♥♥♥♥ they are. The quests are also repetitive, and a chore to complete. Go there fight these monsters, go there search for this item. This game is deep, if puddle is deep. If you want a quality RPG with great world building, story, characters and quests, I suggest play The Witcher 3, this one just isn't worth it.

_childDocuments_.review: By Square Enix standards, this is a pretty good port. There are lots of graphical settings and it takes advantage of all the upscaling tech from the various GPU manufacturers. If you've got substantial hardware, then you'll definitely see a noticeable improvement over the PS5 version. It is missing Ultrawide and uncapped FPS cutscenes, however. Though the folks over at Nexus Mods have already remedied that so download that fix before you even get started if those things are important to you. As for the game itself, I'll give a brief review. Although at time of writing you may see a small amount of hours, I have completed this game on PS5 and even went so far as to obtain Platinum (not overly difficult admittedly). The game is fantastic. It has all the rich story telling elements and character depth you'd expect from a Final Fantasy game. The villain is quite mysterious and keeps you wanting to play more to find out more about them. The Active Time Lore mechanic of the game allows you to pause at any time, during cutscenes or general gameplay, and learn more about the world, characters, key phrases you might have heard, and more. Lore junkies will love it. Admittedly, the final fantasy franchise has not always done well in explaining its story and some games, like XIII, horribly hide the most interesting parts of the story behind datalogs. Active Time Lore eliminates the barrier to entry of digging through menus to find out more about the world and dishes it out clean and concisely.The combat is unlike anything fans of the franchise have seen before. If you've played Devil May Cry, you'll feel right at home with the combat of this game. What Final Fantasy has always done well is taking an established gameplay style and perfecting it. It's fluid, dynamic, though at times formulaic. Do yourself a favor and challenge yourself. Hard mode makes this game quite interesting, but even on the 1st playthrough, experiment with different abilities and combos. In a game like this, it can be easy to fall into a singular way of playing for the entire playthrough. Eikon battles are huge cinematic setpieces that are sure to leave you haw dropped. Each one is unique. While not particularly challenging, that's okay because clearly they are trying more to put on a show and game over screens would get in the way of that.The music is just what you'd expect from Final Fantasy, it even won a Game of the Year award for it, so wear headphones or crank those speakers up!Graphically the game is a masterpiece. Most cutscenes in this game are rendered in game, and you'll have a fairly hard time distinguishing them unless you're a keen observer. It's quite impressive what they've done with this engine.Overall, this is a fantastic game and well worth your $50. The DLC are great as well , particularly Rising Tides. The Echoes of the Fallen DLC is mainly an excuse for a badass boss battle, but otherwise not entirely compelling on its own. You save $10 by buying the bundle so might as well go for it. Though if it is too steep for your budget, the base game is satisfying enough on its own. Perhaps next spring during Square Enix's sale (I think it usually happens in March), you can snatch the DLC for a discount.PS: This game does support Direct Storage. So if you have a PCIE Gen 4 NVME SSD, be sure to install this game on there for ultra fast loading.

_childDocuments_.review: This game feels like a love story. I was extremely excited for 16 when it was first announced. I haven't had such excitement for a game since KH3 release, so much so that I bought a PS5 just for FFXVI. I have zero regrets and I will happily spend money again to own it on my PC. FFX was my #1 Final Fantasy game for years but now 16 holds that place for me.  I fell in love with the story, world, characters and I can never get over the amazing soundtrack provided by Soken. Here are my thoughts with the game playing this prior on PS5. The story is overall fantastic and grand. This game is cutscene heavy, so if that is something that bothers you, you might not enjoy this. The story itself is very engaging but I would say there is some pacing issues. Not enough to taint the experience in my opinion. The cast and voice acting are a 10/10 only wishing on some more spotlight time for a few characters. The side quests can be fun and offer great world building. But I would say they can lack a bit in gameplay engagement. A good comparison would be like doing quests in ff14. Essentially a "go to this spot, do a thing, go back to quest giver" I still very much enjoyed most of them.The gameplay itself is so fun. You are meant to experiment with your eikons and abilites, coming up with combos that work for you. It's very satisfying once you get it down. I had the most fun when timing the titan blocks and shiva dodge. The eikon battles can honestly be described as epic. With the most stunning visuals and jaw dropping events. Most of what I wished for is for regular battles to have more variety with enemies and for more difficult enemies from the get go instead of getting only getting the option in new game+.The music, god the music. I'm a huge fan of ff14 so knowing Soken would work on the ost had me more than excited and I loved every single track in this game. Had it on repeat for practically a year since release, and now that the DLC ost is officially out, I will expect to have that on repeat for a good while.There is a lot of love put into this game and I can't wait to watch my friends play it and go through everything again in my own playthrough on my own time.

_childDocuments_.review: Never wrote a review before. Suh dudes/dudettes!The story in this game hits a lot of phenomenal notes, Without revealing important plot or spoiling anything. (Keep in mind, I did not look up any guides and still I found it broken).Aesthetics: (10/10)Unreal how Square Enix produces this quality. To this day. I played FFX (My first FF) and that game was mind blowing in it's time. Now on FFXVI I feel the same realistic graphic quality that completely blows me away in many scenic instances.PERFORMANCE:  (7.5/10)Tricky subject, it has only been recently ported. I didn't struggle much. While I look at lots of bad reviews and notice, lots of people give this game a 1 star because they are having issues. Worst case, I see issues in frames on boss fights. sometimes on cutscenes, But, there are resources out to help (mods and settings). PROS:ChocobosCidFantastic StoryTorgalI said Torgal, what else do you needCONS:PC port isn't always going to be clean. _childDocuments_.review: This is my favorite modern Final Fantasy currently.You might think my choice to not recommend is a mistake. It isn't.When I can experience the game, I enjoy the more serious, slower, 'politics' based narrative. The combat feels fantastic, especially when you've learned how to chain together various combinations and abilities. The 'Spectacle' in this Spectacle Fighter is worthy of the name with dramatic boss fights, over-the-top combat set pieces, and 'Dragon Ball' level ridiculous summon abilities. Somehow it is both mature, brooding and dark while also being cartoonish, ridiculous and satisfying. It's a wacky mix and I'm all for it.However, this game basically requires DLSS to function reliably, and if you don't have a GPU that was made in the last 2 years, you're going to have a bad time. Whats worse, this game doesn't need DLSS, it was just optimized terribly. There are memory leaks, an overeliance on CPU and an inability to utilize the GPU like other modern games do. For some reason, alt-tabbing out of Fullscreen causes the visuals to lock on the last frame while still running underneath, almost as if there are multiple instances of the game running. I can't say if this is a Denuvo thing as other games with it do not experience this behavior.I want to believe that the devs will 'eventually' sort out these optimization issues as I continue to experience this game in 1 hour chunks before it inevitably crashes. I've even contacted their support out of a genuine desire to help them address these problems, but their responses have been "verify game files, try redownloading the game, make sure you have the latest drivers installed", stuff that anyone would have done before reaching out to support.I shouldn't need to get a brand new mid-tier or higher card just to play a game released on PS5 without crashing.

_childDocuments_.review: First things first:   Despite the games massive filesizes, I regularly see subpar texture work and there is no Raytracing. At highest settings the game is pretty but nothing revolutionary. As such, there is NO REASON for it to be this taxing. I'm seeing a 7800X3D and a 4080 being brought to their knees (with fast ram to spare and running from an NVME drive) to sometimes sub 60 fps at 1440p ultra. On a game with NO RAYTRACING. What the heck, Square. Second: The game has three pillars for my money. Story, combat and spectacle. And so far only the third is holding its weightThe plot so far is engaging enough (it's no FF 6 or 9) but in keeping with the tradition of 15, it's hampered to hell and forth by dismal pacing. At least they didnt chop bits off of it and put them in media outside the game this time. However the story wastes its opening on a battle we will see in better context later, then jumps to what should have been the intro, diverts from it to introduce antagonists and their politics, then jumps back in time, then forth again, then into a super implausible double childhood reunion Dickensian coincidence...Look, I get it. You have to deliver a lot of exposition to set the stage but frankly you fumbled harded than Skyrim. The game makes you think the tutorial is finally over after the Title Drop but HOURS after that you are Sidenote: I really like the Acitve Time Lore and how much effort when into editing it for almost every line during a cutscene. The in game wikia is also cool since it uses several to the point articles and invites you to pile on Tabs from the "See More" section, much like a real life Wiki dive you get lost in.Next problems, however:The combat. It seems to be based on Forspoken's system of collecting sets of powers to spam in real time as you swap sets you acquire from big bosses.However it inherits Forspoken's problem of making the combat feel super dull until you get the first boss' power set, and introduces new ones.Unlike Forspoken, your character isnt nimble at all. You are slow as ♥♥♥♥. You have a magic dash but IT GIVES NO IFRAMES AND CANT BE USED FOR DODGING.  You dodge with a crappy slow sidestep. You cant even roll. Parrying is a joke. It has no dedicated button, you have to line you animation with an enemies and hope the planets magically aligned to give you one. You cant block either. Since the game assumes powers spamming will be constant almost every enemy is either a push over or has too much health. The combat does get more fun when you become powerful enough to overcome the spongy nature of enemies. But you will mostly be mashing and stunlocking with the occational dodge or jump-to-dodge. There's barely any build variety and your full set of actions is so limited its all about waiting for the powers to charge to spam.Im playing in Action Mode by the way. I wanted to give the combat a chance on its terms. Its mediocreNuiscances pile up with UX and the overworld, thousand papercuts style:YOU ARE SO. EFFIN. SLOW. There is no run button. You hold a direction and after an eternity you start dashing. Your default moving speed is dismal and running doesnt help that much. You cant double jump or climb or crouch. It's one of those games where any enviromental movement interaction is predetermined and everything else is an invisible wall.Did I mention there is no Parry button? i'm still mad at that oneThe game constantly stops to show a fullscreen Title Card for every quest that starts. Just put it on the side ffs. Some cutscenes are locked to 30 fps and its really jarring when it constantly jumps framerates back and forth since only some parts of a whole sequence are considered "Detailed Cutscenes" and locked to 30.You cant give orders to any party member except the dog, nor change their looks or gear.The sidequests are filler garbage.The spectacle sequences of the fights are smeared by fullscreen distortion effects when I need to mash. Just put the prompt by itself instead of flashing crap all over and let me see the animations you worked so hard on clearlyI probbaly will keep at it now that I'm past the worse, but

_childDocuments_.review: Final Fantasy XVI is a masterpiece that seamlessly blends epic storytelling, stunning visuals, and thrilling combat to push the series into bold new territory. _childDocuments_.review: Performance issues aside, Final Fantasy XVI is an incredible experience from start to finish. The high points of this game punch holes through the atmosphere and makes all the tedious in-betweens almost a non-issue.The Good:Firstly, I still have a 1080ti as of this review. The game does have performance issues, but so far it's been fully playable and is not riddled with bugs, crashing, or any other fatal flaws that inherently prevent me from playing the game. If you can stomach some low dips in frame rate, I assure you you will have a great time. Visually, this game is beautiful. The world is incredibly detailed and character models are expertly crafted. The voice acting is stellar and every actor has done an incredible job bringing these characters to life. Every character is interesting, believable and a treat to get to know throughout the story. The story is a well crafted, heart string pulling, engaging plot that had me gripped and wanting to know what happens next the whole way. These characters and this story are up there with the greats of the genre. The combat is flashy, fun, and an absolute blast filled with high octane action and freedom of expression with many different abilities and play styles. The set pieces and boss fights are out of this world in scale and sheer insanity. If I had a game with the boss fights alone I would say my money was well spent. Lastly, the OST has to be hands-down one of the greatest OSTs I've ever heard. I do not often listen to a game's OST outside of playing it, but FFXVI has broken the barrier of the game and landed in my personal music library. I loved this game so much, I bought it a second time on Steam.The Bad:My main gripes were the same ones echoed from the PS5 release. Side quests are fairly lack luster, doing menial tasks like kill X enemies, grab Y items and bring them back to quest giver Z. NPCs ramble on forever practically repeating themselves when just a few lines of dialogue would suffice. Exploration is fairly limited, giving these vast areas to explore but ultimately feeling pretty bare with not much going on. The difficulty, at least on first playthrough, I thought was fairly tame and a lot of times I was wishing the game would ramp up in difficulty and kick my behind a little but it never did. You have to finish the game before a harder difficulty is select able. I rather would have selected the more difficult play through from the start if I could. The lack of a party system is quite disappointing. If you've played FFVII Remake or Rebirth and enjoyed that, it is a bit of a downer coming to this and only having control over Clive and maybe a little bit of Torgal. There are performance issues with the game that for some is a deciding factor on whether or not to play the game and I am disappointed the game has released in this state. Hopefully Square can make some hefty performance updates to help the matters. It would be amazing to see this steam deck verified someday. I'll give it two ratings that display my personal and critical stances on this game. Personal: 10/10. This game is killer and the way I feel playing this game and watching the story unfold again is pure joy and I would put this game in every gamer's hands if I could.Critical: 9/10. The sidequests and lack of proper RPG mechanics are a bit of a bummer and I can't quite get it up to masterpiece status.

_childDocuments_.review: Gonna write an early review and will update this later, to give my impressions so far:TL;DRCombat 8 | Gameplay 7 | RPG Elements 4 | Story 7 | English Voice Acting 6 | Visuals 9 | Music 10I would rate this game a solid 7.5/10, which isn't bad at all, it just isn't a masterpiece in my opinion.Don't go into this expecting an RPG with deep character progression, view this more like Final Fantasy goes God Of War and then you'll definitely enjoy it.Long version:Combat is fun, it's definitely a lot more slow and tactical than pure hack&slash (like if you just brainlessly spam attacks you're inevitably gonna lose and die), it's very different from either FFVII Remake and FFXV. But I personally like it this way, it's a lot less messy and less all over the place, a lot more controlled and clean and it does make it more satisfying to eventually win the big fights. Overall I would say the combat is on the easier side, but some specific battles are definitely big difficulty spikes, so that keeps the flow interesting.The actual combat mechanics and system (Eikon system) seems messy at first and takes some getting used to, especially weaving combos while swapping Eikons in the middle of it can feel a little clunky, but after you get a flow going with it and get used to it, it starts feeling a lot more fluid and satisfying. The upgrading system ('RPG' system I guess is what people call it) is unfortunately very simple and straight-lined. So if you're looking for deep character progression and choices, this isn't the game for you, this is definitely more for the people that like solid action games as opposed to people that like deep RPGs with 1000 character choices. Equipment system is almost non-existent.Story so far is good, generally the English voice acting is fine, especially between main characters during main events.But I will say that the banter between side characters during less important events sometimes really make me raise my eyebrows with how cheap and terrible the voice acting is. So quite a bit of inconsistency there for sure.Main characters are very likeable, I love Cid and Tolga, Clive is okay.Side quests so far are forgettable, but at least they're very short and quick.Graphics and musical score are exactly what you would expect from Squeenix and Final Fantasy: absolutely top notch.

Again. WILD. that this game has been so positively reviewed.

name: 7 Days to Die
detailed_description: HOW LONG WILL YOU SURVIVE? With over 18 million copies sold, 7 Days has defined the survival genre, with unrivaled crafting and world-building content. Set in a brutally unforgiving post-apocalyptic world overrun by the undead, 7 Days is an open-world game that is a unique combination of first-person shooter, survival horror, tower defense, and role-playing games. It presents combat, crafting, looting, mining, exploration, and character growth, in a way that has seen a rapturous response from fans worldwide. Play the definitive zombie survival sandbox RPG that came first. Navezgane awaits! GAME FEATURES Explore - Huge, unique and rich environments, offering the freedom to play the game any way you want, featuring 5 unique biomes and worlds up to 100 square kilometers in size. Craft – Handcraft and repair weapons, clothes, armor, tools, vehicles, and more with over 500 recipes. Learn more powerful recipes by finding schematics. Build – Design your fort to include traps, electric power, auto turrets, automated doors, gadgets and defensive positions to survive the undead in a fully destructible and moldable world. Cooperate or Compete – Work together to build settlements or against each other raiding other player’s bases, it’s really up to you in a wasteland where zombies and outlaws rule the land. Create – Unleash your creativity with access to over 800 in-game items, and over 1,300 unique building blocks and a painting system that offers infinite possibilities. Improve – Increase your skills with a multitude of perks under 5 main attributes. Gain additional skills by reading over 100 books. 7 Days to Die is the only true survival RPG. Choose – Play the campaign world, or dive back in a randomly-generated world with cities, towns, lakes, mountains, valleys, roads, caves and over 700 unique locations. Combat – Encounter nearly 60 unique zombie archetypes including special infected with unique behaviors and attacks progressing in difficulty to provide an infinite challenge. Survive – Experience real hardcore survival mechanics with nearly 50 buffs, boosts and ailments that will impact the gameplay in ways that can both challenge and aid in your survival. Destroy – Buildings and terrain formations can collapse under their own weight from structural damage or poor building design with real structural stability. Loot – Scavenge the world for the best weapons, tools, and armor with 6 quality ranges providing thousands of permutations. Augment items with a multitude of mods. Quest – Meet several Trader NPCs who buy and sell goods and offer quest jobs for rewards. Enjoy many unique quest types supported by over 700 locations. Customize – Create your own character and customize your character further in-game with a huge selection of clothing and armor you can craft or loot in the world. Drive – Enjoy the badass vehicle system where you find all the parts, learn the recipes, craft and customize your own bicycle, minibike, motorcycle, 4x4 or gyrocopters and ride with friends. Farm or Hunt – Plant and grow gardens for sustainable resources or head out into the wilderness and hunt over a dozen unique wild animals.

You will NOT find what you expect here. You won't be building massive castles to isolate yourself from the horde. You will NOT be looting dangerous places for the possibility of super good rewards. And the game will most likely be COMPLETELY different from what you saw online, or what you played year ago. Why?Below are some examples.Players looking for military bases and gun factories to find guns right away?Let's make it so you will literally find only bows IN A MILITARY BUNKER if you're not high enough lvl.Players building massive fortified bases with walls etc?Let's make it so zombies home in perfectly on the weakest part of it.Players using a ton of traps in mazes etc?Lets make traps break after killing like 3 zombies. And lets make it so zombies just tunnel through walls if the maze is too long.Players making underground bases?Lets make it so zombies can dig all the way down magically knowing exactly where you are.Players using helicopter on horde night to fly around escaping horde?Let's put in SUPERMAN VULTURES THAT HAVE SUPER SPEED AND SHOOT PROJECTILES into the game.The game keeps changing almost entirely in every single update, just to stop people from playing the game how they want.
