_childDocuments_.review: My friend and me like to play zombies/survival/crafting games, and I gotta say that when I bought 2 copies of this game I wasn't expecting much, barely more than one of these games we sometimes buy and are bored of after a few days. Well I can tell you I was wrong.We started playing 7D2D on november 2014, the game was then on alpha 9 and it was already a great gaming experience, at the time where I'm writing this review the game is on alpha 12.4 and received huge improvements which make it even more enjoyable. The game is broadly very good, the crafting system is solid, scavenging and fighting for your survival is hard, but often rewarding and the feeling of accomplishment when you finally manage to have good tools/weapons and a tough fortress is simply pleasurable. I'm not very picky when it comes to talk about graphics so I'll subjectively say that, even tho it'll never overshadow engines like the CryEngine for instance, 7D2D is not an ugly game at all, I even happen to find the game really beautiful sometimes, mostly when I'm going through woods or clearings.There are of course some flaws and bugs, most of them appearing after every major update, but the devs often fix them very quickly. Talking about the devs, they are very attentive to feedbacks and keep the communication with the community really open, which obviously leads to faster bug fixes and advancement through the updates.My friend and I are coming back on the game every major update to try all the new features, items and other stuff, that makes it never getting boring. For instance, the major addition of alpha 12 is a craftable minibike, it makes the game so different once you managed to get one. We got one each and are having a hell load of fun with it. Being so mobile is truly enjoyable and driving over zombies minding their own business (or innocent pigs and rabbits >.>) is even more.If you like zombie survival and crafting games then I highly recommand you to give it a shot, 7D2D is definitely worth its price, even as a pre-release game.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Days to Die has pivoted from 2 of its four defining gameplay characteristics with the introduction of Alpha 17.  The severe reduction of block resistance to zombie damage has removed much of the tower defense aspects and shifted the player focus to exploiting AI pathing vulnerabilities.   The integration of a new graphic designer to the team while dramatically improving the aesthetics has reduced the open world immersion by shifting to stealth gameplay and away from realistic immersive aspects.  (Examples:  Zombies in nearly every closet rather than logically placed.  All buildings are designed only with obstruction of player view rather than realistic building design.)In addition:The revamped skill system now ties attribute requirements directly to skills which feels like a step backward.The introduction of a rudimentary quest system while promising in concept has backfired in its reduction of a need for open-world exploration.Summary:  If you are looking for a stealth game with some survival elements, 7dtd is a good choice.  However, if you are looking for an open-world, crafting, tower defense game within a zombie apocalypse this is no longer the droids you are looking for.

_childDocuments_.review: I played this game a lot since Alpha 15, I mean A LOT. The fun pimps have done a great job and made it better with every alpha. _childDocuments_.review: My first impression was lackluster. I expected another half-hearted pseudo-sandbox with pushover survival mechanics. My expectations were way off mark. 1) 7DtD has one of the most comprehensive crafting sysmtes I seen, even in building within the world, with many tools that provide a variety of benefits and a plethora of resources differing by biome that alter the way you manage your survival. The world is fully detructible, being able to dig and mine (with some decent physics) as well as destroying parts of the landscape (or cityscape), thrown in with many gatherable items for survival purposes.2) Survival itself is key and is directly tied into game play. Managing your hunger and thirst will determine not only how long you will live, but more nuanced features, like stamina and wellness. There are many resources available to satisfy both survival mechanics, but you have to manage them well to maximize their effectiveness, and you have to gather them without dying.3) Zombies are no joke. Even during the day time, if you're hammering on zombies with your crossbow, all it takes is for one not-so-noticeable zombie to flank you, and you're dead. Taking hits from zombies can detriment you in several ways, including bleeding, infection, and being temporarily stunned.At its stage in development, this game is already basically a fully-fledged game, and it only continues to get better with bugfixes and additional content. 10/10

_childDocuments_.review: This is one of those games where you will need to give it some time. Honestly, while the game has gotten better over its many patches and alpha updates it still will look horrible on most computers. The normal human will look and think "err, my eyes! What ... errr". But don't be put off. Overall, this game is 7-8/10.Before going into anymore detail, I've played this game for around ... 800 hours as of writing and have played since alpha 5 or something (old ... very old). I've played mostly PvP but I've also played a healthy amount of PvE and CoOp.My computer specs: i7 3.7ghz 8core CPU, 980 Nvida graphics, 16MB (good speed which I cannot remember) RAM, installed on a SSD. (5 months old)So, the good:1. You can spend hours ... and I mean hours loving this game. From when you get in and start raiding your first NPC town while mumbling "♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ ♥♥♥♥ its nearly night! (when they run) to the trantilising moment when you finish off a gigantic base. This game is close to a MMO but its fast past not horribly grindy (though it has bits)2. The PvE. Its good! Yer sure the zombies are a little dumb, but they are getting clever and they are zombies! I expect them to run into walls. You are gunna die, you are gunna run and you may even scream if you're like me and the bees (Why are bees in this game!!!). Assuming you don't join a overpopulated server the zombies are all over the place and they can creap up on you without too much trouble. At night its worse, if you're like me and you don't sit in a base dropping axes (you don't wanna know) then you will be out at night a lot and the zombies can outrun you (until higher levels) they hurt like hell and they are tanky as bricks sometimes. 3. The skill system. Its skill system is second to none ... well kk that isn't true but its good.  You gain exp from most activities (hint: killing zombies is the best now) The exp you make will become levels as any normal system at which time you get 5 skill points to spend. There are hundreds of skills and this is where most of what makes you a "stronger player" will happen. Do you level up a skill that makes you be able to run for longer, get better loot from scavenging or hit harder with a club? One makes you less likely to die while trying to escape, one makes you more likely to find something to shoot with and the last means you can kill your attacker as if this were season 7 of the walking dead!4. The PvP. Where the game shines and dimes the most! PvP is what this game was built for in manys eyes. Tactically stalking, scouting and then raiding somones base is fun, scary and rage worthy if it goes wrong! Defending is also fun and can often be mind games with the enemy.Now the bad:1. The lag. Sigh ... sigh ... sigh, yes ... this game has all the above and A LOT more good stuff, but damn does it lag. This can be solved moslty by good server admins and a 3rd party system (which most servers used) called CBSM which can be used to limit and kick players with high ping (high being 150+ ish). You get use to it after awhile, but don't expect this game to be smooth. What to expect: Generally lagging gameplay, skips here and there, "that didn't hit me game", "Goodbye bike", "That zombies just teleported"2. The glitches. The general theme of the "bad" is bugs and glitches. Mostly the same as the above ... This game can be one hell of a gltich fest. "I just died from nothing", "Where did my gun go?" , "Where did I go?", "What is this fps lag?", "Why can I not build here?", "What is that ... omg , thattts not right ... zombie ... err". ... You get the picture. This game has many a bug. 3. The cheaters. This one isn't too bad, but there is a bit of cheating in this game. Mostly glitch releated. Duping of items is beyond easy and many do it. Sometimes its hard to blame people but most of the time its plain cheating. "kk well my bike just zoomed off into the nothingless bit .... I'm gunna cheat it back" VS "This server looks fun! Lets zoom around it like superman and kill everyone in 1 shot before blowing up their bases"4. The developers. Yerp, while they are making a good game I would be lying if I said they don't have some issues. Most of the playerbase plays this game on servers of 15+ people and enjoy doing so. However, the developers have openly stated they want the game to be played on a max of 12 people and seem to care little about lag and fps issues in regards to higher population.To their credit though, the updates are not all too spread out and often come with many new/improved items and mechanics of the game. They seem very detached from the game they're making but ultimatly seem (somehow) still good at doing it.TL;DRGreat game that you can sink many worthwhile hours into with good first-time scares which you as a player learn to adapt to. Good PvP, PvE and CoOp but can sufer from horrible lag and gliches.

_childDocuments_.review: If you're wondering why there's always so much chaos in the reviews for this game, it's pretty simple.  You see, awhile back (like Alpha 6), this game was pretty casual.   4 years ago it looked like crap, but by god there was a shotgun in every purse and a horde of GPS zombies who knew exactly where you were every night.  They were fully capable of ripping out a building from underneath you, but couldn't figure out how to get to you if you simply knocked out a few blocks of a staircase.   And for quite awhile, things stayed largely the same.  Hell, some of that sh*t is STILL the same.Now, suppose you were working on a game of your own with a team.   It was your project, your job, your hopes and dreams.  You played it day in, and day out.  You knew everything about it, and when changes were made you knew about those, too.  At some point, after hundreds, and then thousands of hours, it wouldn't matter how you modified the game - it was never going to be a challenge.  But you'd try anyway.  In a feverish, desperate attempt to make the game interesting, you delved into the black arts of mathematical sorcery, questionable tilted mechanics, pure nonsense, and even verifiable cheapness.  And soon, as other people played your mangled masterpiece, some arose who knew almost as much about it as you did.  Certainly THEY would know where to go from here?  After all, some communal back-and-forth is what early access is all about, and who better to get it from than those who may or may not even play any other games besides yours?  Many versions passed by.  At some point, the playerbase was split into two camps.  People like the above who continually thought the game was too easy, and, y'know, non-masochists who bought the game for a good time.  One group who, as an incorrect assumption, would make the game invariably "better", and the other group who actually represented continued economic appeal.  And so, the war started for this little title, and still rages to this day.  You have people with hundreds and thousands of hours into this game who wonder why it's always too easy in a painfully oblivious manner, and newbies who wander in, get slammed, complain and get shoved out the door as casuals.  You also have a tertiary group who, although correct, cannot help but smugly point out (usually to the casuals) that you can edit the game's files yourself, with it never really occurring to them that needing to do so is asymptomatic of the game's many problems.  My two cents?  The Fun Pimps spent way too many versions in the diehard camps, and have been trying to balance the game the other way while adding content ever since.  Versions tend to lean back and forth to one camp or the other, sometimes even alternating.  New material gets added, gets exploited by old pros, gets weird asynchronous fluff attached to it to make it more difficult, and then either rots as part of an archaic system or is just removed altogether while the doe-eyed newbies never know what the f*ck is going on.  The diehards or newbies who would become as such are most of the people who still play, so they hold the greater statistical relevance, are the most vocal with a moblike presence on the forums, have the most things of relevancy to say, and should not for developmental reasons be forgotten.  Everyone else who tries to break into the game represents all new players who know nothing about it, have very little that's relevant to say beyond initial impressions as an unbiased base of opinion, and therefore cannot for economic reasons be forgotten. The ironic part of all of this is the game has never had true difficulty.  There have been pieces here and there.  Some are still in it, some are gone.  This is what keeps diehards from ever being satisfied with the game, and the garbage artificial difficulty thrown into it that SEEMS like actual difficulty is what prevents a lot of new players from falling in love with it.  Adapting to the game isn't so much about learning an honest and progressive difficulty as it is getting used to and accepting its weird little nonsensical proclivities that have spewed forth from the rotted corpse of millenia of hours lost.  Draw a circle of blood around the goat's head or gtfo, noob.     And that's it.  I'm not going to say this game should have been finished by now, or nearly so.  Game development is hard.  I'm not going to say which group in the playerbase I lean towards more.  I won't say anything about where I think the game should go, other than I'm a big fan of options and slider bars.  Mostly because I think this back-and-forth will just keep going.  I will say though that all I've REALLY wanted is for zombies to stop f*cking spawning on top of me for at least TWO YEARS now, and I still don't have it.  Make of that what you will.

I can’t recommend anyone buy it in its current state.If you look at the reviews you will see most negative reviewers played this game for hundreds of hours. The game is riddled with terrible AI, horrible game breaking bugs, and horrible multiplayer desync making PVP and PVE gameplay nearly impossible for anyone but the host. The developers seem to be on a yearly or longer patch cycle and have terrible communication with their customers. They contradict themselves constantly and can come across as very arrogant and condescending. Any dissent or constructive criticism on their forums is met with bans and post removals.Early access or being a new developer is no excuse for leaving their game in such a poor state. I would strongly recommend buying this game only if it was deeply discounted and only with the intention of playing a bit till you get frustrated and quit. As it stands the bugs and issues will eventually frustrate you and turn you away. Maybe keep it on your wishlist and see what state it is in when it finally goes live. My guess sometime in 2022.Their development choices are easily reflect in the reviews, going from mostly positive to mixed. If they keep this up I wouldn't be suprised if it starts dipping into mostly negative.

_childDocuments_.review: *UPDATE 11/28/2022*Yeah, haven't really played this in a long time. At the time of this review, the game was in a much earlier state. it seems that 7DTD is still in "early access", which should tell you everything you need to know. To be honest, I have no idea how this game is now. don't trust this review. I guess just enjoy my 17 year old self's story telling and catch a snippet of one of my exaggerated core gaming memories.Three friends and I spawn in the wasteland biome.Thought we could make a shelter out of this apartment complex.Was going well at first.Gathered many supplies.Fortified the door.Was supposed to be temporary, started turning into something permanent.Everything was going well.they broke down the door...Everything went to hell.They started pouring through the stairwell.Dogs everywhere.The only way out was down.Started running down and dodging walkers.We got separated in half.Two of my friends made it out.My other friend and I were still stuck inside.Figured we'd spend the last night, hiding.The moaning of walkers never stopped.Morning came..It was time.We had to go.My friend and I continued to drill down passed the horde.Got desperate.I jumped out the second floor.Broke my legs.They were everywhere.Managed to limp through the horde.Met up with my other three friendsDon't look back..We crossed the river into a forest.Started off with a small shack.Turned it into a four house village.We had a wall, a trench around it.We had something.We never did forget about what happened that day in the wasteland.That right there, is just a small story (that wasn't even in full detail) of what 7 Days to Die is like. Very few may say that "Oh, it's just another zombie survival game" or "Oh, it's just a DayZ knockoff". Well, I'm here to tell you that this is not the case at all. I own H1Z1, DayZ, and 7dtd. I have to say that this is the best one. Why?1. The developers are actually going in the right path.2. Loot system is pretty awesome.3. Crafting system is also pretty awesome, may take a bit to get used to. But, still awesome.4. Instead of just piling blocks and making a box-house, there are actually physics to the building system. Like, in some cases, you actually have to put support. Otherwise that sniper tower or that neat house will collapse on you. Which has happened to my friends. It's kind of satisfying to watch, but damn you're mad if it's your structure.5. The different variety in enemies is cool! Right now, you have: bees, dogs, and zombies; and other different kind of zombies to add to that.6. Speaking of zombies. This game's zombies have something that DayZ doesn't have. You know... They actually pose a threat and can move in numbers. There are moments when you see that police station surrounded by a horde of zombies and you think to yourself "No, I'm good", because they actually threaten you. The fact that they sprint at night by default (settings can be changed) also adds a thrill to the game. To a point in which you don't even want to leave your shelter at night because you can hear a spider zombie calling a nearby horde. Hordes also happen randomly at anytime and anywhere. This is also unheard of in DayZ. You never see a horde in that game. Also, as the days go on, the zombies start to get a little tougher. You start to feel that the apocalypse is worsening. Zombies are also smart.7. There's nothing more satisfying than fortifying your base to prepare for the undead. This game does a very good job at that. You can do almost whatever your mind imagines.. Wanna put a trench that surrounds your base and put spikes at the bottom of it? Do it. Want to salvage land mines from an overrun military base and use them as your own? Do it. Want to build a huge wall around your base? Do it. However, don't think that just putting a wall around your base will help. Zombies will rip through it and actually dig under the wall. We've seen this done in our server before, and it's frustrating, but it's so awesome having to constantly keep maintanence on your base and look for new ways to prevent them and to see your weak spots.These are just some of my points, and you wanna know the awesome thing? This right here, is just an alpha.. A ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.. Alpha, and the developers have already come this far. As I type this, the alpha11 update is imminent and should be released any day now. This is said to be the biggest update this game has seen. This game is going nowhere but up.Unfortunately, I can't tell you about the PvP, because my friends and I just normally play on a private PvE server and survive together. I have no idea how well PvP works. If I ever play PvP, I'll tell you how it goes.

_childDocuments_.review: I never do reviews, this is my first.  7daystodie is a brilliant game. I write this review as of alpha11 and while the new patch is only a few days and a tad buggy, the devs have already hotfixed some of the bugs and i have every faith the others will be fixed in the next few days.  Even this the bugs Alpha 11 is very playable. I have 835 hours invested in this game as of writing this review. Yes I LOVE IT!!! ... honestly the price is well worth it.  People come into a game like this for different reasons, my husband loves fps and loves the zombie hunting elements of this game. I have always sucked at that sort of thing so i focus on the crafting/building elements. My kill counts are always very low ...but just because i don't like to do to much killing doens't mean i don't enjoy the game as it would with so many zombie survival games out there. I focus on crafting the things we need to survive and building a safe place to lay our head at night and trust me there is enough to do in that respect alone to keep me busy without me needing to run around with a gun.  You can easily play this game as a pure survival, sneaking and hiding avoiding zombies as much as possible while you scavenge enough food/drink and build yourself and impenitrable bunker to ward off even the most mighty of enivitable hordes which will eventually come looking for you. (and trust me they can be terrifying.... i have literally logged off too scared to play untill my husband joined me)  Or you can play it almost like a fps ... living moment to moment scavenging for supplies while blasting the hell outta zombies with the multitude of weapons the game has.  The weapon system is great, all the weapons feel different, they have different usage. Some are better for up close and then theres your hunting/rifles and snipers for distance. It's rare to find a game with the right mix of elements to keep me and my husband both happy, because we are both very different gamers.  This game has managed to keep us both hooked for over 800 hours so kudo's to the pimps it's not an easy thing to do.

_childDocuments_.review: I've played this game plenty enough to both love it and truly hate it. The concept is brilliant, and if they ever actually finish the game it will be a masterpiece. BUT, and it's a big but, it has been almost a decade and every update they send out destroys any playable progress you make. And more importantly than that, as I've spent hours today rebuilding a world in creative mode, you can't ever build truly what you want. Creative mode broke for me, destroying days of progress and sending me back to a blank world all because I drove five seconds away from my base, literally just enough to turn around, to test the truck with my gate system. No matter how much you love the game, its building system, or the concept, your creations and love won't last. It is a man-child of a game stuck permanently in its own broken adolescence. It will never be worth the money or time investment as it will never, via ever erased and rebuilt skill trees or constantly obselete constructions, allow you to build something awesome and enjoy it without breaking as you should be able to. This game will always update over your creations with equally broken content and it will never, as it seems, grow any closer to becoming anything more than a broken alpha video game concept.

_childDocuments_.review: It pains me to do this, it really does. I have nearly 4,000 hours in this game. Yes you read that correctly, I suffered from a chronic illness that immobilized me, as a former workaholic it was easy to do. I could actually move, build, and go on adventures, it was an awesome release... until now. I doubt I'll ever hit the 4k hour mark because, quite frankly, it's not fun anymore. And that is not because I lost interest, I would LOVE to keep playing. But over the past few years of development the gameplay itself, the sense of immersion and adventure, has suffered, greatly. It does indeed look better, much better, but it's lost it's mojo.What changed that caused this? A ton of little things really. Removal of Learning By Doing being a huge one, actions no longer mean anything. Instead of fixing exploits, like other games do, they just replaced ALL of it with RNG based magazines. Lame, mods found a compromise by mixing it up at least. Skill improves with use, but crafting up needs mags, that works well enough. But the vanilla just doesn't get it. They removed E for picking things up, now you have to punch crops to get them, also dumb. Farming, also ruined, used to be fun, organic, and useful. But one thing that seriously ruins each new game almost immediately is loot containers becoming static unusable objects once looted. Like wtf, at least give us an option. I hate looting now, and they force you to do more of it. Ugh.I used to take over existing buildings and fix them up, loved to do it, because who in the F would build a house from scratch in a world full of empty buildings. And I love building, so usually I'd make a horder base at least. But with fixer-upper buildings one of my fav things was getting to the point where I made a generator and wired up it's existing lights to work. It was a huge milestone in each playthrough... can't anymore. Again, wtf. How do you dev a game backwards like this.I didn't even mention the new armor system because I can't suffer through a playthrough long enough to get to that point. Especially being FORCED to deal with Rekt, can't stand that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and we have no choice, progression is so overly linked to them now, it no longer feels like a sandbox, I no longer feel independent.Wrapping it up, again I hate doing this, I have gotten far more than my moneys worth, no doubt, and I deeply appreciate what this game once was. But now I cannot in good faith recommend the polished turd it has become. I am hoping mods will save it, I really am. Regardless I owe a deep Thank You to the Fun Pimps for giving me way over 3k hours of good times, alas those times have ended.

_childDocuments_.review: Ambitious and addictive, but terrifying for all the wrong reasons.I'm a big fan of zombie games, crafting, open-world survival... 7 Days to Die was a dangerous combination in that regard.  The developers took the creative aspect of Minecraft and tried to make it "grown-up" in a pseudo-realistic zombie setting.  They pulled it off in a refreshing but incredibly sloppy way.Before I go further, I'll point out that I have about 100 hours in this game as of writing and I'll probably play it still, so obviously I enjoyed a lot of it.  The open-world aspect combined with leveled items, customization, and minibikes is extremely addictive after you get past the steep learning curve (but before you get fatigued by the bugs).Anyway, if you like those things, you'll like the game.  You already knew that.  Let's talk about all the things that are wrong with this game - developers PLEASE get out your notepads now: - Athletics and combatThis isn't a huge complaint, but a lot of the combat and movement feels stilted and artificial, like the game really is just Minecraft bugging out under a facade of extra polygons.  It'd be greatly improved by minor parkour elements (a way to climb some obstacles and fences would be great). - The hot mess of unoptimizationMy laptop isn't top of the line, but it's pretty new and is capable of running games like Portal, Starcraft II, and Skyrim without major lag and stutter.  On the very, very lowest settings, where trees disappear and reappear at an arms length away, and hills turn into instant mashed potatoes from about ten feet away, I get about 20 fps and noticeable lag when turning or moving.  I have low expectations for graphics, but 7DtD is absurdly bad. - VehiclesThe only vehicle in the game is a miniature motorbike.  That's cool and all, but a normal bicycle would be vastly superior in a zombie apocalypse.  Would it be too easy and effective?  Too difficult to implement?  I don't know why it hasn't been done.  Drivable cars would also be nice, but I'm not holding my breath.bike - The worst audio of any video game I've ever playedHarsh?  Sure, but true.  I can forgive the annoying, immersion breaking "spooky noises" that happen at night and during certain biomes.  What I can't forgive is the awful, horrible, terrible, no-good balance when the zombies make noise.  The voices themselves are okay enough.  The volume is ridiculous - a gunshot should crack through the night, echo off the sides of buildings and leave a ringing in the ears, whereas a telltale breathy moan gives away the zombie shuffling slowly behind you.  Instead, we have gunshots that sound like a Call of Duty soundboard on downers and zombies whose horrifically loud grunts should come with the warning "zombies aren't anywhere near as close as they appear.  Or maybe they are.  You can't tell because they all sound the same and they're all way too loud."Okay, that may sound like a bit too much whinging, but it really grinds my gears.  Directionality is poor, and abysmal when the zombies are actually close to you.  Worse still, there's no recognition of obstacles at all - a zombie inside a wooden store should sound quite muffled compared to a zombie outside of it.  No difference.  But it gets much more ridiculous - even in a concrete bunker with 30 feet of dirt over your head, if a zombie walks by aboveground, you'll be startled out of your beauty sleep by another canned moan that sounds like it's right in your f***ing face. - MiscZombies glitch through doors, ladders, and sometimes walls.Lumberjack and biker zombies are just obnoxiously tanky and a chore to fight.  The former is not okay because they're the only zombies in the winter biomes.  Also, f**k zombie dogs and vultures.  I hate those glitchy monstrosities with a passion, but that's arguably just a personal problem. - EndOverall, I still have to respect this game for being so ambitious and coming together as a cohesive whole, patchwork though it may be.  It's given me hours of entertainment, but it's still severely suffering from some major issues that remain unresolved.  The devs recently released a large overhaul update with all sorts of new places and things - this was nice.  Some code optimization and audio fixes, however, would have been a much better use of time.

_childDocuments_.review: 7DTD is an incredibly fun post-apocalyptic survival game with zombies. It has a Minecraft-esque building mechanic with RPG elements, lots of loot, blueprints, and weapon types for creative killing.This is an early access review and will be updated as the game progresses.Survival Game with a post apocalyptic zombie theme.Mouse and keyboard in first person perspective (third person in vehicles).Character creator allows you to choose sex and name and has basic sliders to change face, hair, and body. You spawn on the map in a random biome with very little to your name - 2 bottles of water, a can of chilli and a few other items.  You immediately launch into a very useful tutorial where you end up gathering resources and crafting some clothes, weapons, and basic building blocks.  You are then set loose to scavenge, kill zombies, build a base, etc.  There are always zombies in the game (they scale with your difficulty level so the game eases you in). During the day, you can run circles around the zombies, but at night they become Usain Bolts. Every 7th night, there is a blood moon when the zombies go ballistic.  They sense you through walls and will literally tear down your base to get at you.  At the time of writing, I have over 1500 hours in this game. It's loads of fun with friends or solo. It's my wife's favourite game of all time. I would highly recommend this - well worth the price.If you found my review helpful and want to support me (at no extra cost to you), please consider buying the game through this link: Or come say hi on my stream:

_childDocuments_.review: It's a great game when you first start. Plenty to explore and see. After about 100 hours the game starts to take a toll. Between the horrific UI, the poor aiming and hit box mechanics it grows to be frustrating. Fun Pimps doesn't know what they want to do with this title. Seems like they're too concerned with updating character models, updating the maps and weapons and skills etc but not touching on performance, stability and sharpness of the game. I started playing this game 7 years ago, and to this day they still haven't updated any graphical or performance enhancements to make the game run better, look better on higher end PC's. The game still plays like a 1990's Tomb Raider title, but Tomb Raider at least had smooth performance for its time. This was a game I loved for many years, but have slowly started to hate it seeing as it takes Fun Pimps almost a year to put out a major update and every time it's just band-aid fixes and mostly model updates, map changes, mechanics. Let's not even talk about the poor decision to release it on consoles when the game isn't even a game yet. Fun Pimps have had plenty of years to at least fix the graphical problems on high end PC's and adjust the controls so the game moves and feels like a real modern zombie survival. Night of the Dead did better and that's still a freshly developed game. What was my top favorite game of all time in the zombie category is just collecting dust knowing it'll never be more than it is now.Edit: 1.0 has lived up to a lot of expectations. There's still a lot to do, but it's in a really good place now.

_childDocuments_.review: 7 days to die is one of the best post apocalyptic zombie survival genre in the market. The gameplay focuses on realistic approach on surviving, planning and building while dealing with the hordes of zombies.Some of the game feature are object degradation, death penalty, supply drop, zombie behavior in a day & night cycle and many more that adds spice to the survival experience.Pros:-affordable price of the game-16 player online co-op, shared/split screen co-op-cross platform multiplayer-realistic character injury, illness & treatment-realistic character wellness (thirst, hunger, temperature etc.)Cons:-worse optimization-lack of human npc-lackluster lategame-lackluster sidequest-tedious crafting-tedious grind

_childDocuments_.review: Summary:  You awaken, virtually naked, to a dangerous survival world inhabited by the living dead.  In the default setting during the day the dead are George A. Romero zombies, slow but relentless.   At night they become Dawn of the Dead (remake) zombies, fast hunters.  To live you must break down bits of the world for raw materials, craft, loot and club your way to fabricating a base from which you can last through the night and gain experience enough to build a facility that will last through the 7th night.  Some are dwarves digging into the ground, but I a prefer to be the kid building cement treehouses (I call them rooks) and seeing if I can keep them being collapsed.  With the new 7-day horde limit setting, which I set as the max of 64, I don't think that will be possible since I am always alone but I will soon see as the 7th night is moving in.Alpha 16; Experimental - I really like the improvements given in this release, one of the struggles I have with open world environments is the limited array of critters in the ecosystem.  An additinal flying critter, a bit more variety from the land based fauna and the different types of attack hordes are a very nice addition.  I particularly liked the platoon of Army guys that attacked on the 6th day escorted by three guys in hazmat suits.The creators are working their way up to including bandits and real quests and this recent addition was a good sized move forward to that aim by increasing the variety of city/town footprints and the changes to the trading posts.  I always close the doors when leaving a trading post because I assume in some release in the future if I do the poor lonely guy (always a guy so far) will get overrun cause I left his unbreachable wall open.  I have  to say it does look like it will be a while before other living npc humans (besides the trader) will be added.The new skill/point system makes it easier to get to the level of a workbench but the reduced amount of materials and the addition of bad mechanic makes the harvesting a lot slower.  I'm o.k. with that as I don't need to grind as much to get skill points, and before it was too easy to get 5000 stacks of wood and stone in A15.  The ability to actually get mechanical parts from a dead car is much much better.  Not getting enough parts for a workbench until day 20 was often a drag.But the best part for me will always be the refinements to the procedural world generation.  The towns are starting to look more like towns found in a typical modern country and the terrain has fewer errors like ultra steep walls and hanging houses.So yes, I like this game  much for the endless supply of zombies to beat on, the improved variety of critters and the varied terrain to exploer.  It makes a great diversion after a rough day of work or, more recently, a break from studies.

Surprisingly i never thought my wife could enjoy zombie slasher. She does though. And she does it extremely well for an amateur. _childDocuments_.review: I used to love this game too. I played it before I owned it. Graphics like Minecraft back then but I still loved it and recommended it to everyone. I bought about 5 copies total by now. I am leaving a negative review but I am still playing it occasionally, hoping the negatives get better.The patches started out with mostly improvements. Graphical improvements, started looking better. Added more things that were interesting and worked well. Electricity, electric traps, lights. You gained skills by using them. Ability to craft guns and farm, build elaborate bases to defend against the hordes. Mines, trip wires, spike traps, barbed wire, automated turrets,  vehicles.The patches then started improving some things, usually superficial things like graphics, but removing things that worked and people liked. No longer gained skills by using them. Spike traps and other defenses generally stopped working due to AI changes making zombies smart enough to pile on and charge through layers of spike traps in single file, detecting the weakest part of the walls to get to you. They added perks which sounds good, but retracted the ability to gain skills by using them. Then they gated the perks with heavy investments into attributes that lock out other perks and force you into using only 3 weapon types per attribute. IE, if you spec into perception you can use "rifles" (not automatic rifles), explosives, or spears. Perception is also the attribute that allows you to gather more materials with wrenches, and to get better loot. If you want to max loot rewards, you basically have to use those weapons, or waste your points. This is one of several cheap difficulty raising changes that artificially lengthen the time of each game.These are all basically minor issues, as the main direction of the game seems to keep drifting that way. They want to force you to have jump scares and cheap hits to make it "more exciting", while the forum moderators and devs just tell you how they "never have that problem", and to "git gud". If you don't like a new mechanic they tell you to play on easiest difficulty as its the only way to turn it off. You explain that it's not too hard, as you are playing on harder than normal difficulty and haven't died, and they continue to belittle your thoughts and are dedicated to ignoring your opinion. They have already sold the game to us and apparently don't care about our opinion anymore. They are openly changing the game to attract new players that will pay money for a different kind of game while throwing all of us dedicated players to the wolves. I never wanted to leave a negative review, I don't recall ever reviewing a game at all but... they forced my hand.  Definitely be aware before buying... and I will update if things change enough to warrant it.

_childDocuments_.review: Firstly I want to say I’m really enjoying this gameSecondly I WOULD tell what is good about it. But I rather tell you a story.Once upon a time, in a hell hole, far, far away there was a nameless man who could punch insanely quickly and break bushes with his fists.He plopped into existence on a remote server. With nothing more than his starting items and a zombie mauling his face due to server latency.His journey started light heartedly. He came across a body of a dismembered fellow citizen, he politely inquired if the citizen would be requiring that wrench on his persons any longer. The man took the gentleman’s silence as a “yes, please good sir! I cannot bear to have it in my locale any longer!”The man then starting using the head of the wrench to mate with the faces of walking dead - It was the start of a beautiful relationship and symbiosis between two sentient objects. Man and wrench.After some through mating with skulls; the wrench began to tire, the man acknowledged his silent partner’s weary state and left her (My lawyers say the wrench must be a she due to gender neutrality) in his inventory to rest.The man travelled onwards, admiring the fly tippers that had plagued the lander with their rubbish tipping on public highways. “Are there no gentlemen left anymore?” the man asked himself. His companion would retort, is she were not so tired.The man after many minutes of walking the man was ambushed by 4 gentlemen, all armed with firearms pointed at him.The gentlemen asked in the most gentlemanly fashion:- That man pondered for a while, this could be a trap. What he was more worried about is that following 4 burley white men into the bushes late at night could ruin his reputation as a stand up and decent gentlemen.Weighing the risks he agreed politely.The 5 gentlemen travelled down the road, for what seemed like many hours (20 minutes) until they came across a small town, partially build in the middle of a plains area.For the next few days the man and his fellow gentlemen laughed, sang, and drank the polluted water from the river merrily. And as a result were plagued by the ungentlemanly affliction of diarrhoea.Many days passed of incontinence and building.Then, a large pack of ruffians assaulted the town’s walls.The more nimble ruffians simply vaulted over the walls  while the slower Ruffians pounded on the walls and demanded an audience with us.The ungentlemanly behaviour…The pounding on the walls…The way they attacked us like feral beasts…The way they were dressed and many of them unclothed…Being a gentleman I knew this could only mean one thing. The walls fell, many died from being driven indoors and (presumably) forced to sample their heathen food.I did what I could, but there were too many Frenchmen to repel. I came down from my tower, firing my rifle as fast as I could at the hordes of unwashed Frenchmen. I could have sworn one was wielding a baguette.I was forced inside, I fired my rifle with the most British and gentlemanly fury I could muster.The Frenchmen piled up by the door. But there was too many.I then barricaded myself inside – buying myself only time.In my last efforts, I took out my tired companion. I bashed and bashed and bashed the wall in front of me, breaking through enough to escape.On the final swing my friend broke into pieces.I heard her speak to me, broken on the floor…I ran outside, jumped over the fence and off to freedom.In a nutshell 7D2D is what early access games should be. It has a good range of features to keep you entertained while updates come out. The devs were friendly and helped me with a FoV problem I had with the game (I suffer from acute simulation sickness).What put me off is seeing people and curators endorse the game as “like minecraft”There is much I still have to explore and it honestly is one of the best survival games I have ever played. Compared to a game such as DayZ everyone seems rather friendly. Which is much better than other zombie world based games like Dayz (not making many comparisons, for obvious reasons) because not many people seem to shoot me on sight. Which was refreshing.Once you get access to guns everyone loves you (totally unrelated I’m sure). Definitely worth a pickup. I can’t find much wrong with it. The only problems are purely cosmetic and don't break the game. Which is nice because every build seems to be very stable, aside from the few bugs that do get fixed rapidly.The only major complaint I have is that the range of melee weapons and a zombie’s reach feels misleading, if a reticule turned green when in range and red when out of melee range I would be happy with this. But it's hard to judge range and distance, espically when you are like me and you modded the FoV files because you suffer from motion sickness.Aside from that, completely worth the money - nice to see someone finally did the genre justice.The only warning I will give however is that this game is pretty damn taxing, not on your hardware, but on you;-1) The ambiance will quickly start messing with your mind (really good, props to the sound artists) and it's easy to give up because of it being "too hard"2) Thankfully 7D2D isn't hard just because it has to be or it feels it must be. It's hard because it is. And thats what counts.

_childDocuments_.review: This is the epitome of "what could have been" in gaming. You want a FPS survival crafter shooter with RPG elements? 7D2D has that, as well as a super neat tower defense style gameplay with every 7 days a horde comes and you need to defend with the RPG elements you've chosen which will dictate how you defend along with what you have built with the survival/crafting aspect. Literally, that all sounds amazing...But its been in early access for almost a decade now, with new alpha updates every few months. Alpha... updates, a decade later, how is that possible with 12 million copies sold? They clearly took the money and essentially ran, leaving a skeleton crew to do bug fixes and add a new zombie or crafting options once a year to keep selling copies. The game is still a buggy unoptimized mess with some of the worst combat and movement mechanics in any games ive ever seen. The guns overall feel bad, but nowhere near as bad as melee feels in this game. Holy smokes is melee in this game just... god awful, you can absolutely learn to use it and make it work, but it is the most clunky awkward melee system i've ever encountered. Movement? It's somehow even worse than the combat/melee systems in this game. You are more or less a stick figure with legs that barely move. You dont really bend at all, when you jump you just kinda bounce upwards. If you want to be able to have the bottom of your feet land on the platform while essentially standing straight up. There's no mantling, vaulting, sliding, etc. It's an incredibly basic movement system and combat system for a game that has had this much time and money in it. Not to mention the vehicle movement in this game, lol, or bugs... so many bugs.So the question im sure you're asking is, why a negative scathing review for a game I have 250+ hours in? For the same reason this has a Very Positive score even though everybody who plays this can more or less admit that these are problems. The idea of the game is amazing, and nobody else does it. Where else can you create and build a customized character with the RPG elements in this game, to build a shelter and defend against a mass horde of zombies in an FPS setting? None, and that sucks cause any decent dev team could in a year or two with generic Unreal assets throw together a game with what this game offers, but substantially better game mechanics and probably less buggy. So this is a negative review because of squandered resources and little to no actual updates and real content being dropped in almost a decade.

_childDocuments_.review: Long story short: The Walking Dead and Minecraft have a mexican standoff over who has the best water physics.7 Days To Die is an indie, first-person open-world zombie survival game with gameplay elements in the likes of Minecraft. To elaborate, you can dig and build in the same way; square by square. Yet, the game shares similarities to, say, PUBG/Rust; large, open world with a lot of nothing in between points of interest with strong emphasis on PVP. However, the PVP part is optional, so you can go solo or with friends.You spawn in a random location on the map. After a brief tutorial all you have to do is survive. Eat, drink and heal yourself. Yep, that's it. Due to the lack of any story or endgame content, how you do it is entirely up to you and when you decide to quit is your call too. In short, it's currently very role-play-friendly as the lack of concrete objective will require a lot of imagination from you.As you wander, you'll collect items and use them to craft better things. Killing zombies, looting containers and farming ressources will give you XP. When you level up, you gain a skill point which can be used to increase 5 different sub-class, but you can choose whatever you want at any time. By investing points in Intelligence, you can unlock more crafting modules used to make other non-common material like a Forge to smelt metals or a Chemistry Bench to make drugs and alcohol, etc.After a few hours, you get comfortable and start building a home or fortify a pre-built home you picked for yourself. You invest in the "Build Vehicle" skill, craft yourself a bike and do loot runs. You can raid any structure you want, wether it's a small home or a big factory. In-game days pass, you hoard stuff and you get more confident. But then...Then something happens. There's one huge hint in the game's title about what happens. After 7 days, your day counter turns red. At dusk, the sky turns red, roaring and flashing with thunder. Then, at 10pm, night falls and the Bloodmoon Horde comes for you. From 10pm to 4am, you will be besieged by a horde of running zombies. Like you'd expect, zombies will destroy your door, your windows and even your walls in attempts to reach you and eat you up.A little side note on the zombie destroying walls... The way I understand it is that Z's try to destroy blocks so they can make a "stairway" to you, in any possible way they can. The AI, as I heard, is not fully ironed out, so Z's will almost always go for the weakest part of your base to get to you. The shortest way, the better. But there's a another catch to that: structural integrity. See, unlike Minecraft, there's no "floating cube/land/structure" BS here. If your home's structural integrity isn't as great as the blocks it's trying to support, your house will collapse. All blocks and how the world was modeled works this way, which is really cool. If you take refuge in a cheap, run-down home during bloodmoons, it's highly likely your base will fall apart within the first hour of the night. So, Bloodmoons are no jokes here. I was VERY unprepared on my first bloodmoon and paid the price as the paragraph above implies... heheh... When the second bloodmoon came, I stopped everything I was doing at 19pm and prepared heavily, tacticaly placing crude traps and gearing up with the best guns I had. With each passing bloodmoons, the layout of my house changed drastically. Each horde invasions helped me re-invent my defenses and kept things fresh.There's only 2 logical outcome to survive these bloodmoons. First method is smart use of traps and defending by yourself as best as you can. The other outcome is to run away, preferably on a vehicle. See, it doesn't matter how much you kill, the moment one zombie dies or despawn, another one will respawn in the horizon and run after you with laser-guided prescision.There's a lot of difficulty options in the world menu. You can prevent zombies from running, reduce the number of zombies during bloodmoons, reduce the damage done by zombies on built blocks and more. I played on Normal difficulty all along, never tweaked the difficulty. I actually praise the oppressive and aggressive nature of bloodmoons or the "surprise running sleepers" which is the opposite of the usual "easy slo-mo Walkers". It makes you think and rethink all the time. Lone zombies and sometimes small hordes will orbit around you randomly. It's these factor that makes this zombie game quite nice.I also have to praise how exploring building was tailored. Most of the time, there's usually a defined entrance and exit. Most doors are locked and you must snake your way across, passing by each rooms in the process. Sometimes you have to enter through the roof and jump down in the house from the attic, or maybe jump in a basement to reach the upper floors since everything above was locked. There's also a lot of secrets hidden behind paintings and out-of-place wall tiles. Then there's the "sleeper zombies" I mentioned above. These zombies are not randomly generated, they are pre-set and are sleeping on the floor. The moment you make too much noise, you can wake up the whole house and trap yourself inside.So, exploring buildings is far from boring. You can see the devs put in some effort in that section. Each complex building feel unique and the layout is never the same. Simple buildings have been copied and pasted, but you raid these in about 30 seconds and I haven't seen that much duplicates. Raiding a complex building will take at least 5-10min and are filled with surprises. Raiding a big complex building, like a Factory, might require 2 trips since you'll run out of inventory space before you've looted 1/3 of the place. So yeah, great, elaborate exploration and hoarding. You have that here.Now that I've covered the Good, let's have a look at the Bad and the Ugly.Poor optimization: This game uses the Unity engine and I knew right from the start, before I even pushed the Buy button, that there was going to be FPS drops and an overall ugly look. I wasn't wrong. I was kinda disappointed when I had to crank down the Overall setting to Medium to get decent fps. Setting it to High is sorta ok, but it stutters when loading chunks and navigating cities is a stuttery, low fps nightmare. This game cannot have faster vehicles because the engine fails to load terrain if you go too fast...Poor Sounds in general: It feels like every walls in this game is made of cardboard paper. I can be in the 2nd basement of a house and zombies on the ground above will be heard moaning as if they were right next to me. It seems only the distance between you and the enemies make a difference in the sound's volume. No dampening, or echo or whatnot. Very, very raw sound design.Slightly unforgiving aiming mechanic: If the pixel inside the middle of your crosshair is not touching the enemy when you attack, your attack won't count. This results in a lot of missed melee swings or gunshots whenever zombies decide to bob their head a little or change voxel pathfinding at the last moment. It's raw and it's frustrating at times.Slightly overdone skill-walls: Most popular one is how you need 7/10 Intelligence to unlock all the cool stuff like vehicles, workbench, forge, etc. But rushing these will compromise everything else like HP, Stamina and fighting power. Yet noone is talking about how Disease Resist or Increase Swim Speed are redundant skills NOBODY would want to spend points into and should just be integrated into the main stat it's under. More Fortidude equals more Disease Resits, etc. You need so much skill points that even going past level 100 will feel like less than half of what you could max. I have 230 hours in this game and I can say I'd probably need 100 more to max out all skills. Useless, mindless grind long after you reached godlike status.(continued in comments because Steam sucks)

_childDocuments_.review: 7D2D has always looked like a great  for a game. But each new update has just made that beginning longer and more tedious. The latest update has finally convinced me that 7D2D really isn't going anywhere. With Alpha 13 it now takes me , with a really good Stone Axe, to get through  of a boarded-up door. That's 100 chops to get through one door. And  doors are now boarded-up, even ones  a house. (Who boards up the door to their own bathroom??) But it doesn't really matter, because there's no good loot behind those doors anyway. No chance of something useful - like maybe an iron axe. More likely some empty tin cans, or more parts for a Hunting Rifle I won't be able to assemble for another 20 hours or so.I'll be lucky to live that long. There are dogs everywhere, and they're pretty much un-killable. When I  kill an animal (dog, pig or deer),  Also, air conditioners don't give up Steel Pipes any more - which means no way to make a Grill, and therefore no way to cook food. So I'm rapidly starving. I'm also overheating all the time, over 100 degrees standing outdoors in a normal woodland biome. So I'm going through 10 water or more in a single day. That means more trips to the river, more boiling to purify the water, more chopping wood for fuel. Also, items wear out really fast now, so you'll be spending most of your time repairing and re-making the same gear over and over and over again.This is after almost 8 hours of play on Alpha 13, with most of my stats well up from their starting points.  with difficulty reduced one notch from the default. So when, exactly, does the  part start?Each successive 'big, big update' to 7D2D has turned out to be mostly about better visuals, more tweaks to an already perfectly-adequate UI, and, above all, more ways of making the game agonizingly, screen-punchingly slow and difficult. Instead of extending the game with new content, TFP is just stretching what's already there, thinner and thinner. What they've got now, is a game that's both tedious and pointless. Grind your way up the skill tree as far as you like, and you'll find there's still never any actual progression in the gameplay. No advanced tactics. No grand strategy. No storyline. No fascinating new locations to discover. Just more of the same simplistic gameplay: see a zombie, kill a zombie. Build a fort and watch the zombies rip it apart in one night.This is a game so linear and mindless that it could be played  an actual zombie.So why have I spent so much time playing 7D2D? Two reasons. First, because it actually  to be a lot more fun. Back when it was simpler and not quite so mind-numbingly grind-y. Second, because I was sustained by . The hope that by the time I inevitably got bored - yet again - the  patch would give me somewhere to go, something to do that I'd never done before. But after literally   of waiting, I have now officially lost that hope. I've crafted thousands of blocks, hunted down hundreds of crafting blueprints, fended off endless hordes of zombie dogs. And there's still no point to it all. Only now it's  more difficult and  less fun that it was back in the early days. I probably would have recommended 72D2 a year ago. Today, in December 2015, I can't. It's been 'improved' and 'upgraded' until it's become hopelessly broken. Don't bother with it until you see some signs of real evolution in the gameplay. And some  reduction in the grind factor.: I've been informed that to get hides, you have to chop the animal with a bladed weapon. It works. Changes like this ought to be documented by the developers... nothing like a good 'readme' file. Reading the "How Alpha 13 Works (Basics)" thread, I've learned how to level up my crafting skills in a hurry. Basically, just keep making the same stuff over and over and over. It works, and it makes the difficulty a lot more manageable. But it's also kind of the definition of 'grind.'There's a no-man's land in game design, between 'too easy' and 'too difficult.' The way to fill in that gap is with 'interesting.' TFP obviously don't understand this. They won't let players build an impregnable base, because they fear that would end the zombie threat permanently. They don't realize that the solution to the problem isn't simply to make the game tougher, it's to make it more interesting, to allow gameplay to evolve. When you've built the impregnable base, the game doesn't , or become trivial - it moves to a higher level. Until they realize this, 7D2D will always be an exercise in futility.

_childDocuments_.review: Update: 2020The Fun Pimps have now implemented a way to become a tester like they said they would. The game has continued to be updated and still more updates in the future. Game is still solid and customer relations has improved. The work the devs did never deserved 0/10 but I viewed "Game 10/10" as a nod to their work, and "devs 0/10" as a nod customer relations and their opinion of their community. Not sure where the future of this game is going, but for now I can still tentatively change from not recommended to recommended.I'm sorry but I just can not support this anymore. I've got over a thousand hours, bought in during kickstarter, bought 5 copies for friends along the way, and loved every second of it. To be clear the game itself is great, probably my favorite of all time, and has so much more potential. The Devs have sadly decided not to support pvp or greater than 8 players multiplayer. But that's not what I'm upset about today. This was a KICKSTARTER game, now in EARLY ACCESS, that has an EXPERIMENTAL opt-in only even EARLIER EARLY ACCESS, that now is giving streamers and not KICKSTARTERS access to the game to "build hype" on an EARLY ACCESS game because the streamers have supported the devs. The developers are claiming that they are giving this special treatment to streamers so that they can find more bugs to fix, and that they cant give the game out to the supporters because there could be show stopping bugs... First if there was show stopping bugs you were worried about you wouldnt be streaming those to the public, second if you want to find more bugs youd let more people play it so you can have more testers, this is simply a terrible decision by the developers. The developers do not believe that kickstarters supported the development of this game by buying the game before it was even on steam... In addition Joel "madmole" Huenink, one of the developers, has taken to insulting forums members who bring up kickstarters having supported their game by saying they have not earned it. "Quote Originally Posted by madmole I have the utmost respect for our customers. If someone wants to get access before experimental, then earn it. Its as simple as that. You can earn that by applying to be a tester, or stream our game for a long time building a reputable channel around it, or apply for a job here, etc. But crying, complaining and bickering won't get you much IRL, or anything here.""Streamers have promoted the game and earned it. What have you done? If you want to play a buggy pre-experimental build sign up to become a tester and earn it.""If someone wants to get access before experimental, then earn it." This is a ridiculous thing to say to the people who kickstarted your dream Joel I am dumbstruck that you could possibly believe this let alone think it was a good pr decision. we funded your dream because we thought it was our dream game together, now its just your cash grab.TLDR: Great game as is, huge potential, terrible, terrible customer relations.Game 10/10Devs 0/10Update: Alpha 17 looks interesting I'll update this review when it comes out.Update: 2020The Fun Pimps have now implemented a way to become a tester like they said they would. The game has continued to be updated and still more updates in the future. Game is still solid and customer relations has improved. The work the devs did never deserved 0/10 but I viewed "Game 10/10" as a nod to their work, and "devs 0/10" as a nod customer relations and their opinion of their community. _childDocuments_.review: A friend got this game for me, I looked at the title, looked at the screenshots and groaned. "Not another 'zombicide game' trying to say it's a 'survival game'." But he got it for me, and it woud be rude to not atleast give it another shot. I'm rather glad I did.I started play in a -private game- with my friend, set to the medium difficulty. Day one was a mess, I figured I was playing another left4dead 'survival' game which was all about killing as many zombies as one humanly can before wandering to the next area. Well, after breaking a few weapons on zombies and getting no reward outside of what lint was in the zombie's pockets, I knew I was wrong, and night had begun to set in. My friend luckily -had- played before and warned me that things got a lot different at night, so we managed to make it through with no deaths, but many close calls.50 days in, I'm more than hooked. Survival is the key- Food, water, scavving, repairs and building at day. Shelter, security and stealth at night. Crafting damn near anything in a Alpha game, from multiple layers of cobblestone walls outside of what used to be a log cabin. Each peice taken the long crafting process of finding rocks, chopping them down into stone and then turning into cobblestone. More? We built a second story for storing items. More? Two layers of spiked pits surrounding our 'cabin' with only a ♥♥♥♥♥ for us living people to cross. More? Another story, turned into a rooftop farm of corn, blueberries and potatos.Nights can get rough at the "Spillway Estate" as we have now dubbed our fortress, we try to keep quiet throughout the nights, limiting player activity to things that dont make sound, or carry foods on our person that generate smell. ( Yes, that's a thing!) A chest near the front door full of easy repaired and built weapons. Pistols, a shotgun and some ammo for it, fresh from the forge! when things get really bad- The newly crafted fallback point, a basement/bunker. Metal walls , floor, and roof, only one entry which is blocked in times of emergencies. Beds, emergency food and water (or tea!) supplies stored next to some of our most powerful weapons. ( Chainsaws, landmines, a rocket launcher, and a whole lot of shotgun ammo! )To sum it all up, it has a few minor bugs, but it's in alpha, and they generally get fixed up rather swiftly! Worth the money, great with friends- Especially when you notch up the difficulty and find yourself hiding for your life in a closet with nothing but a stick to protect yourself!Lots of potentiel, and fun as is.

_childDocuments_.review: I really don't understand why so many people are bashing the new update. Personally, I think it improved the game quite a lot, and most of the criticisms I've seen are either a unelaborative "They changed it now it sucks!!!" or sprinkled with actual lies or contradictions, or just attacking the devs in general instead of reviewing the actual game, so I'm going to go through the major complaints I've seen so far, and say why I personally don't think it's as bad as many people are making it out to be."They added vehicles but cut the map size in half, so they aren't as useful": They actually over DOUBLED the map size in the new update, from 16km to 36 km, so vehicles are still useful. Not to mention that the stamina system people keep criticizing should actually make them a god send."They prevented people from just building what they want outright and made it so you have to grind for levels now, and their new leveling system is boring and tedious": While the new level system is a bit of a mixed bag, (I still like it however, I just wish the still had base skills to go along with the new more specialized perks) the game always had a barrier to letting you craft higher grade stuff since the beginning, they just replaced a (potentially) slightly faster RNG system with the schematics to more reliable leveling. They essentially swapped out RNG for XP, and while it's still annoying in many ways, (especially with some of the level requirements being in the 70's for certain perks) RNG could also be tedious. Instead of checking 5 working stiffs to get either too many or no schematics to make a minibike, you now have to clear out 5 working stiffs to get enough xp to get there. Not to mention that while rare, the RNG system could actually lock off content in a certain playthrough if favor didn't go your way; I once checked every library in my game world in A16 and never acquired a single minibike or scrap armor schematic my entire playthrough. At the very least, it's now a sure thing at some point, even if it takes a while, and feels more rewarding when you reach that goal instead of just lucking out while searching a garbage bag."The new stamina and health system is obnoxious and prevents you from playing the game practically": I will concede that stamina drains much faster than it should, and they should probably change the numbers around a bit, but everything else seems pretty ok to me. Better recipes and more animals in the world to hunt also offset this penalty a bit, I have master chef and we cleared out the boar farm early on for meat, and now I can keep my entire party of 5 going singlehandedly for another 2 weeks at least, and this will only get better as I level up and we start dipping into farming. It makes hunters and farmers much more valuable now, since in A16 a single piece of grilled meat and a jar of water was enough to sustain a person for around 3 days, and since food has no spoil timer, you'd quickly rack up a stockpile and then never have to worry about that aspect of the game ever again. Now it actually matters throughout the entire playthrough since you have to eat constantly to keep your stamina up, and food depletes much faster overall. More tedious, yes, but it makes previously lackluster classes much more important in keeping everyone alive."Guns are super common now, and because loot is no longer as rare as it was, the only reason to go into buildings now is for XP farming zombies.": I actually do not understand this one. I am playing a game right now with 5 other people, all of which have looted around 5 entire buildings worth, along with the entire boar/corn farm POI, as well as 2 supply drops, and we have maybe 4 level 1 pistols, 2 level 2 hunting rifles, and 1 level 1 smg, with a shotgun here or there. Definitely more common for sure, but by no means actually "common." And this was with 3 points into the looter perk. Maybe we got ♥♥♥♥ with the RNG, or they got really lucky, but this isn't even to mention that unless these people were finding 200 rounds of ammo with each gun and were finding level 4+ guns in these stashes early on, (which I know for a fact they weren't) looting is still a big necessity to actually find mods, better guns, or ammo to keep those guns functional. And while this system makes guns feel slightly less of an accomplishment, was the old RNG system of finding 4+ parts to a single gun and the book that much better? You know what it felt like to have 50 ♥♥♥♥♥♥ receivers, grips, and parts for a pistol, but no barrel, so they just sat in a safe doing nothing? That was also obnoxious, and if you think this new system is still worse than that, go right ahead, but don't act like the old way was lightyears better."Zombies got massive damage buffs to buildings, making builders much worse than they were.": My group was able to survive the first two 7 day waves (with 64 enemies and on nomad difficulty) plus countless smaller ones by going into an information center in the middle of the woods, upgrading the door to iron, and putting a simple wall of 3 wooden spike traps around the perimeter, and the zombies were never able to breach the walls or doors yet, so I don't know what mega hoards and/or crappy bases you guys are putting up, but decent defenses are still a must for higher waves. But even if they chew through bases slightly faster than before, I like that it still encourages a more active defense approach than just letting you sit underground in a slightly reinforced bunker every time a wave came.Overall this update can still use some work, (which the devs promised they would do after the holidays) but the only major complaints I have so far are these:Max stamina drops pretty damn fast, and until you get higher level food recipes it can be a chore to get it back.The new skills system is pretty fun and immersive, but only if you have a party of at least 3 people playing together. I can see how solo players will struggle to get their feet off the ground, with the lack of sharing XP and all.Some of the level requirements for perks seem a bit too high, like the level 40 requirement to finally start making iron tools, let alone actually using them efficiently.I wish they still had base skills to go along with perks and attributes instead of going down the Fallout 4 path of just boiling it down into perks, but even still, I think the addition of attributes was a great idea, and the system works for the most part.Other than these 4 complaints, I personally feel that the update as a whole was an improvement, and people who personally don't like it have some good points and give some criticisms, but those that claim that alpha 17 gutted and ruined the entire game to the point of no return are committing egregious hyperbole. Give it some time, I'm sure it will be improved further, just like every other major update this game ever had.

_childDocuments_.review: 10/10  for this Early Access Project.  Excellent Survival, Exploration, and Building!This game has been in development for a long time and has lots of content. Many POIs to explore and loot.  Lots of missions and quests. And lots and lots of Zombies!  You really never stop defending your base, they are always coming for you.  And every 7 days there's Horde Night, when they come outta the walls till 4 in the morning.  Horde Night is a very cool feature that keeps you busy through the week as you repair and upgrade your home base.  Most players use a "Horde Base"- a sacrificial structure with long hallways to form a kill zone.  You can build from scratch, or take over an existing structure and modify it for Horde Night.  The Zombies will attack wherever you are on Horde Night and leave your main base alone.  Mostly.Steam Forums and Discord are very active, pretty much 24/7.  There is a great community to help out if you get stuck.The Menu and setup options are stellar.  For non-combat types like me, the game can be dialed in with ease.  Enemies' strength and speed can be set so that there are attacks and challenges at your desired intensity.   This is cool because Creative Mode can seem cold and boring in survival games.  Even Horde Night can be turned off entirely.  These options can be changed anytime without starting over.The building system is unique and awesome.  I am a builder and this is my favorite feature in 7dtd.  Most survival games have some type of base building, but in so many it seems an afterthought.  There's nothing worse than building up a large base, only to discover there is no outside corner or some specialty shape to complete the design.  Sure, there are still a few more items that could be added- I can always make a list of needed block shapes, but 7dtd has a definite commitment to builders and it shows!There is a structural integrity requirement.  You can only cantilever out so far with your structure before it will collapse.  The system is quite forgiving and works well.Survival mode building seems very realistic.  Pretty much everything in the world can be broken down and recycled for use or for sale to traders.  There are no autominers or any automated resource gathering.  This game is grind-a-liscious!  You do it all, or have some friends join you in Co-Op mode.  There is no jetpack or flying-  for tall structures you will need to build scaffolding and nerd-pole up using blocks.  The basic building blocks can be easily picked up when you are finished with the scaffolding and no loss of materials.  Once you upgrade the blocks to their finished state, they must be hacked away with tools and you will lose some materials.  Don't fall off your your structures- fall damage is serious, but can be mitigated with perks, armor, and character upgrades.Performance wise, 7dtd is very good.  This was my only beef until recently.  The last update had optimizations that have the game running very well now.  In this game, nearly everything can be destroyed, modified, or picked up.  Everything moves and that makes for a heavy load on the computer. With that in mind, I normally build a huge base and have lots of inventory.  FPS drops to the 30's at times, but the game never crashes or locks up.  Indeed, I have not found a game -breaking bug yet!All in all, 7dtd is a wonderful project.  Don't worry about how long it takes to finish it, or when the game will be done.   Early Access is like going to College, you never want it to end!Highly Recommended!

_childDocuments_.review: 7 Days to die is an interesting game. It's been in "Alpha"-stage for years and the development of the game progresses very slowly. Surprisingly enough, even in this "early" stage the game works better and seems more complete than several similar games that are supposed to have reached "Beta".Anyway... in this sandbox game you start off at a default or random map and explore the world, slaughter zombies and the wildlife, collect materials, build bases, traps, farms, vehicles and go for treasure hunting. Lots of things to do. The map features a destroyed world. Ruined villages, burned down forests, the remains of civilisation everywhere. Very atmospheric. It features different biomes and even various, beautiful weather effects like snow, rain and fog. When it's foggy you can't see far and when the snow covers everything in white, it's hard to distinguish individual things on the ground.The base building part lets you build complete fortresses out of nothing and reshape the world to form it the way you want. There's a decent amount of different enemies you can face. On top of that, as you progress in the game and time passes on, new and more dangerous enemies and versions will spawn. Just when you thought you had seen it all the game keeps surprising you and it does a good job in keeping things interesting.I'm playing the default map for the first time, have seen only about 1/3 of the world and already spent over 100 hours in the game. So I see a lot of potential in "7 days to die".
