_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster? Zombie Mayhem Meets Modern Gaming! (ฅ'ω'ฅ)Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster brings back the iconic zombie-slaughtering mayhem, now rebuilt using the powerful RE Engine. The game takes place in the chaotic Willamette mall, where Frank West, a determined journalist, must uncover the truth behind a zombie outbreak while battling hordes of the undead. With improved graphics, modern controls, and a host of quality-of-life upgrades, this remaster aims to enhance everything that made the original special, while smoothing out some of the rougher edges.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster preserves the sandbox-style zombie-slaying fun of the original while adding some much-needed modern conveniences. The improved graphics are the most obvious enhancement—textures are sharper, environments more detailed, and the sheer number of zombies on-screen is impressive, adding to the game's chaotic atmosphere. Character models, particularly Frank's, look fantastic, and his wardrobe options feel more varied and responsive than before.The game also overhauls the control system, making combat smoother and more intuitive. The dodge mechanic is now far more useful and survivability has increased due to revamped controls that allow more freedom when using the vast array of improvised weapons. The inclusion of auto-saves, alongside updated UI and controls, reduces the frustration found in the original game, especially during high-tension moments where any misstep could lead to disaster.One of the most notable improvements is the vastly better survivor AI. In the original, escorting survivors was a major source of frustration, as they often got stuck or overwhelmed by zombies. This time, survivors are far more capable of defending themselves and following Frank's lead, making rescue missions much more enjoyable. However, the AI isn't foolproof and still suffers from occasional quirks, such as inconsistent pathfinding and combat decisions.Despite these improvements, not everything is perfect. Technical issues persist, with random crashes and frame drops occurring frequently in areas crowded with zombies, breaking immersion and potentially losing progress. The Infinity Mode, a fan-favorite, has been rendered almost unplayable due to frequent crashes after hours of gameplay, making it impossible to complete in its current state.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is a visual and mechanical upgrade to a beloved classic that delivers on its promise of zombie-slaying chaos while improving many of the original's frustrating elements. However, lingering technical issues and some questionable design choices prevent it from being the definitive version. For newcomers, this remaster is the best way to experience Frank West’s bloody mall adventure, while returning players will appreciate the smoother controls and quality-of-life improvements—if they can overlook the game's technical flaws.If you enjoyed this review and want to stay updated on the latest game remasters, be sure to follow our  for more deep dives into gaming classics! Keep an eye out for our next review on the best zombie games to play in 2024! ヽ(´• ω •`)ノ

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR : This remaster is good, but not without flaws. The Remaster is good, but I don't know to whom I should recommend it. If you like an easier game, play this one. If you want an harder experience, the OG might be more up your speed.The good: they added improvements that bring some good QOL and makes some part of the game less tedious. The graphics are pretty nice. I like the RE Engine, but it was weird to see Dead Rising looking a bit like Resident Evil, but it nearly never bothered me. I liked that they added a lot of voicelines and the hability to skip through dialogue ingame (like when Otis calls). The new voice actors did a good job I think. At first I didn't know what to think, but after like 2 hours the voices grew on me (except for Steven, the voice actor didn't catch the crazyness of the character like the original VA). The performances of the game were mostly fine. The survivor AI is less dumb (not smart, but less dumb. Aaron is still annoying, but less). I like the challenge tab when you pause the game. In fact, I really enjoyed the new UI.The bad: I'm not too sure what they did, but the special forces are so annoying to fight now. I think it's a design choice, but if you fight 2 or more, you can get stun-locked and therefore die because they shoot a bit too quickly (it's especially annoying in Infinity Mode). I think if they added a bit more time between shots it would fix the problem. I said the performance were mostly fine. They are not fine in the maintenance tunnels (it lags a bit, zombies spawn on you because the game can't render them quickly enough) and during Infinity Mode. The last one is especially annoying because it's a save mode, meaning you die you lose all progress. I don't like that when you change area (Paradise Plaza to Entrance Plaza for example) they do not show you how much time is left. It doesn't make the game harder, but I feel it takes away the tension of the timer because it's not in your face anymore.The I don't know what to think: Some changes seem to have been made half-way through, Now Frank can move while aiming, but if he shoots while aiming he stops. However, Frank can shoot while running if he doesn't aim with the gun. Why can't you move while shooting+aiming then? The changes to th survivors are nice, but I don't think they are useful. They can be mad at you or like you depending on what you give them for example. If they like you, they will do more and help you more. That's nice but why? I played the OG Dead Rising on Xbox 360 and on PC and I never wanted to keep survivors around, you're better alone I think. I don't think it's bad but I don't really see the point. I think they made the game a bit too easy.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising: Deluxe Remaster is a faithful remake of the Original 2006 XBox launch title. You play as Frank West, wartime photo journalist. After receiving a tip of events in the town of Willamette, Colorado. You have 72 hours (6 real-time) to solve the mystery behind the Willamette incident and how it connects to Santa Cabeza.If you liked the original Dead Rising and believed all it needed where some touch ups, you will be happy with Capcom's re-release. It took the core heart and soul of DR and sanded the rough edges while retaining that since of difficulty and urgency. That said: some of the difficulty is lost with the improved control scheme. In regards to the controversy of the removal of the "Erotica" category, Larry's model change, and Cliff's Dialogue: I can confidentially say that it doesn't take away from the core package as a whole. These changes are silly, but don't negatively affect the player experience. This is only a problem for content purists. Speaking of content purists: This game does change things and is NOT the same experience as the 2006 release. If you want the game with all its janky, difficult charm, I earnestly recommend sticking to the 2016 re-release or the original 2006 Console release. On a 100 point scale, I rank this game a 95 out of 100. Wonderful work Capcom. I hope to see Dead Rising 2 get this deluxe treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Dead Rising when I was quite young, and somehow even more imbecilic than I am now. I managed to beat it, but the experience was quite an abrasive one; my child mind couldn't grip the idea that following routes outside of quest markers could be optimal, or that guns wouldn't be the best solution for every possible scenario. It was a game I ultimately walked away from not understanding neither the love surrounding it nor even its most basic structural design. Having played this remaster, I safely and definitively say I was wrong. This game rules, and almost all of its best bits trace back to that original release, and many of its weaknesses are contingent on this iteration. A title that encourages creativity, environmental awareness, and arcadey replayfulness supercharged to the max is a welcome delight in the modern era of gaming. Throwing cardboard boxes at a zombie to stun them, then running up and suplexing them into half a dozen other zombies never once failed to make me smile. The athletic abilities you unlock for Frank are almost all handily useful, and just simply fun to employ. The final stretch of the game is relatively far less imaginative, with its most obvious desire to showcase a strength in rendering hundreds of zombies having been long outdone by the march of time, but that, and that alone, is the only sore point I could nail down in the original design document. For this release specifically, I don't like Erotica's removal, I don't like the absurd speed with which you can level, I love the changes to survivor AI and responsiveness, the graphical overhaul was almost always an improvement- sans lighting- and the modern control scheme worked quite a treat for me. I considered DRDR well worth the $50 I paid for, almost specifically for its reserved length, but the fact that it's so replayable means that value will only get drawn from me again and again. It gets a very strong recommendation from me if you also dislike modern design's focus on accessibility over all.

_childDocuments_.review: If Capcom go on to do more Dead Rising like they have done with this? I'll 100% be there for it.I consider myself a pretty big fan of Dead Rising so when Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster was first shown off, I laughed, got excited and concerned all at the same time. Entirely rebuilt on the RE Engine? Sweet! No TJ Rotolo? (Frank's original VA) I don't like the sound of that. But as time went on and Capcom showed some more footage, excitement took over and I pre-ordered and now after a few playthroughs and close to 100%'ing the game I can safely say I don't regret it one bit and would do it again for Dead Rising 2.DRDR is a weird one to me because it's the only game that comes to mind where I actually can't place where I'd put it in terms of 'Remaster' and 'Remake'. Because it IS essentially the 2006 version converted to a modern engine. All the bells and whistles of the RE Engine while still maintaining the same old story, characters, animations, cutscenes etc.However, that is not the say there hasn't been some changes which seem to have taken a spotlight on the overall talk of the game. A huge spotlight has been cast on the 'negative' changes which I think is a shame because personally I think the positive changes greatly overshadow these.The biggest I've seen is the removal of the 'erotica' photo category that would grant you extra points if you snapped a photo containing things like cleavage or upskirt of Jessie or Cheryl's sexy poses during her side quest. While I always saw the erotica category as something that added to the comical side of the game, I also don't REALLY care all that much that it's now not present. As far as I can tell, the extra points you would have earned are still covered as I think it still accounts for that and these changes didn't alter Jessie's appearance or remove Cheryl's sexy photoshooting quest meaning really all that I can tell that's changed is there are no more pink circles to mark the areas? The other two of note are the changes to Cheryl's dress and the shirt with the nude woman that Frank can wear have now been changed which have already started to see mods restore.Now, in terms of positive changes there are tones of them. Some DR1 purists might not enjoy all of them but I personally am happy with them. Some of the big changes I have noticed are the game now including an optional modernised control scheme (no more accidental dodge rolling!), all dialogue is now completely voice acted, new camera features, PP sticker tracker which I believe wasn't in the first game?, better survivor AI that can assist Frank in finding collectibles and useful items (a lot like the pawns in Dragon's Dogma 2), some small map changes like stairs added to the vent on the rooftop to prevent survivors from getting stuck and an overhaul to the overall theme of Paradise Plaza, some changes to Infinity Mode to make surviving longer a bit easier, the ability to advance time to keep the player in the action rather than stood around waiting needlessly and a better day/night cycle making the mall feel almost welcoming in the day compared to the dark and scary silence at night. There is also an autosave feature which may make the consequences of the players riskier actions less severe but I do appreciate the idea of not having to play catch up every now and then because of the death of either myself or a survivor.And for arguably the biggest change. The voice acting. I think this one is entirely down to the individual. I think TJ Rotolo's performance in the original was one of the biggest factors in what made Frank West such an iconic character. But that isn't to say the new voice actor (Jas Patrick) is bad. Initially I found it quite strange not hearing TJ's voice coming from Frank but it quickly grew on me and I found that it was a refreshing new rendition that also managed to kept Frank feeling like Frank. An example for me was the infamous "I've covered wars, you know." line. I was eager to see how the new voice held up and I was pleasantly surprised to hear it delivered better than I had hoped. As for everyone else, I think they sound great. They still sound how I remember them and fit great. My one and only issue with the game so far is the performance. Although I imagine these will get ironed out soon, I feel it is only right to mention on a 4070 Super and 5800X3D, fps is great but there are in some cases micro-stutters that I believe might be due to the amount of zombies in one given location. They haven't stopped me from playing the game but have in some cases threw me off a little. Stability-wise, the game also needs a patch or two. I have lost 2 attempts at the 7-Day Survivor challenge due to a crash after alt-tabbing a few times and the other was moving between locations under the effect of Quickstep/Fleetfoot. Normally I would be okay with a rare hiccup like that due to it now having an autosave feature but as that challenge doesn't, I think it's very important that is fixed immediately.To bring my yapping to a conclusion. Overall, I think this is an easy one for Dead Rising fans to decide on when it comes to whether or not it is worth it. If you're not a huge fan, have already played it or didn't like some of the clunky/arcade-y feel, be aware that although I feel this version is a lot more accessible, it is same game at it's core.I think it's great that Dead Rising is getting some attention again and I only hope that continues. I would have never thought that we would see Dead Rising on the RE Engine and I pray that one day we see Dead Rising 2 and all of it's additional content get the same treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising is a game I've been playing for over 11 years. when I was 8 years old my father brought home a copy of dead rising 1 and left 4 dead 2 for the 360. And after that my perspective and appreciation for games was forever changed, I've gone back to get all achievements on all subsequent releases of of dr1 from its xbox one, pc, ps4 port and I can just never get tired even after a decade. so when this Deluxe Remaster was announced I waws ecstatic and spent everyday anticipating its release so now that its here how do I feel? I absolutely love but at the same time I have my flaws with it but it's to be expected as the original is my 2nd favourite game of all time.When playing through DRDR my first concern and notice was the voice actors, I'm a pretty open minded person when it comes to remakes or remasters of games as I don't mind seeing things spruced up as i'll always have the original so how do I feel about the changes?VOICE ACTING:it's a hit or miss in my opinion, Keep in mind that i've been playing the original for a decade so adjusting to these new voices would be hard, A lot of them just sound mediocre compared to the original but never bad. I will say though that a few I enjoyed more then the original Larry, Isabela, Carlito. All sounded better then the original in my opinion and Larry especially, Brent Mukai does a phenomenal job for Larry and made me appreciate him more then the original. Also the main man Frank West, Jas Patrick does a pretty good performance, He doesn't replace TJ but he does a damn good job trying to fill in the legend TJ. His performance in the meat plant when Carlito is dying is amazing and I loved it. and his performance during overtime mode was decent, Jas is also very passionate about the series and that's always great to see from a voice actor. PS otis is also goated DIFFICULTY: Now this is a mixed bag for me. A lot of people say its easier but its much more deeper then that, Levelling up is indeed easier and some books give you crazy abilities (unlocking all special moves no matter what level you are) Dead risings difficulty always felt very artificial to me as all the complaints about difficulty in the original could be chalked up to BS mechanics. Survivor Ai, clunky controls, Otis, unclear directions with certain missions, certain psychos. so what does DRDR do?. Well psychos are actually harder now i'd argue, in the original they had no damagecap which resulted in people melting them in seconds. DRDR now has it so psychos can only take a certain amount of damage then after they barely lose health. I welcome this change as psychos in the original were a complete cakewalk other then say Cletus, who could still be cheesed if you have a long range weapon. Special forces are also no joke and will light you up in seconds, they do not care and will fire until you're dead.  Survivor AI is drastically improved now, I've witnessed the worst of the AI in the original and experimented a lot with them to see their limits and comparing it to DRDR is night and day not once did they ever get stuck or stop to randomly to attack a zombie. They will follow frank wherever now.MISCELLANEOUS ohh boy.. One of my favourite additions to this game has to be the extra voice acting for the survivors and psychos as its such a nice detail and breathes in so much life into them now. when you escort survivors now they will occasionally talk to each other and I find it so charming lol. I had a playthrough where I was escorting Kindell and the movieland survivors. And when one of the survivors were grabbed Kindell freed them and said "Have no fear, for I am here" I know it's nothing major but I love the survivors in dead rising 1 and seeing them have interactions like that is just so damn cool. Another cool addition is psycho's now talk during the fights and some of there dialogue is great and I feel further adds onto their characters. A couple of my favourites are cliff mentioning he hears his dead comrades calling out to him, Isabela telling frank to stop looking at her a$$ and Kent telling frank to go back to shooting p0rn0s. It's such minor additions but they add more soul to the psychos In my opinion compared to the original. And another cool detail is that all the survivors now have their own unique models when they are zombiefied its such an amazing attention to detailTHE BIG BAD WOKE:I'm sure everyone knows with the changes and I'm going to preface that censorship is an objective bad no matter DRDR i’d say is 97% the same as the original (not counting the new features and additions) the posts going around about the removals are justified to some extent.. (Larry change I believe is for better) the issue I have personally is with the people saying that they completely butchered the game and that it is inferior in every way when that is not true and a complete over exaggeration. The removal of erotica while yes it sucks as it removes a feature. Is a very minuet and niche detail that was purely for gags, Keiji Inafune has a history of adding perv elements to his game as jokes and it’s the same for dead rising, the theory about it being subtextual commentary on journalism is a pure head canon by people that I didn’t even know was a thing until erotica was removed. Dead risings themes are about satirical consumerism and the American government, as they are directly stated in the games story. Anything else is headcanon material. I will say though the removal of erotica is a detriment to a character like Kent as it removes the factor to show just how he deranged he is and anyone saying the change is good is being ridiculous.Finally regarding the games wackiness and s3xual themes, are still kept in. Jo is still kept the exact same, cheryl’s request and her very risky dialogue towards frank is still kept intact. And I’ve noticed a few new dialogue additions, during the Isabela fight she tells frank to go stare at another persons ass instead of hers, while also calling him a yankee, another example is when fighting kent he’ll tell frank that he should go back to shooting p0rn0’s which actually gave me a good laugh and felt like something inline with dead risings wackiness and s3xuality.FINALE:Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster was a very enjoyable experience as a diehard fan. I feel like it's a great remaster of Dr1 but it doesn't replace the original as it still has a few things that it does better then DRDR. But it compliments the Original in A lot aspects while brushing up and tweaking the game to be more palatable for newcomers of the series. While also adding a lot cool details for veteran fans such as beta assets being added, new magazines, new weapons etc. Seeing one of my favourite games Finally touched up after wanting a RE engine remake of dr1 for years feels like a dream come true. Although I will preface the game is very buggy atm for others, and some things are missing detail that the original had which im hoping will be patched.

_childDocuments_.review: I finished 72 Hour Mode...My takeaway from all this: the devs love the first game but totally miss the point. The entirety of the 72 Hour Mode was a tension-filled romp through the Willamette Parkview Mall with only a bit of time in-between to relax. You were battling the clock as much as you were zombies. You were in a blitz a majority of the time, going at insane lengths to get to where you needed to be at any cost. You planned a lot in your head, almost meticulously. You balanced your inventory, your read the map, you remembered a nice shortcut to cut time and limit your engagements against zombies, you were ready. Here, you can just run right through without much thought. Yes, there are some difficult bits still but with how powerful they make the player early on and throughout, it almost becomes a stroll through the game, not the crazed mad dash it had become. Every second mattered, every decision you made cost you time, the most valuable resource in the game and taking just a second off made the difference. Every time you went to another part of the mall, the clock showed up right in front of your face. The countdown started as soon as you stepped onto the rooftop of Willamette Parkview Mall. By the time you survived your first encounter with the undead, the clock went down to 71 Hours. Already an hour burnt.It's disappointing not to feel the adrenaline as much. The original game made you feel as though you were going through the experience. You had Scoops to cover, people to rescue, weapons to gather, food to eat and carry; everything is against you and you have to make due. Even at your most powerful, zombies are dangerous. Time is your worst enemy. Your decision making made much more of an impact. Instead, here, it feels less punishing and much more forgiving. Time almost feels generous. 72 Hour Mode here didn't bite as much as I wanted it to. I wanted to be down to the wire, challenged. I wanted to be in a mad dash through the Mall, being smart with my decision making and route-taking. I wanted to feel like I had to take a risk just to make it to the bathroom. I wanted to feel like my journey to the North Plaza was dangerous. I wanted the race to retrieve the time bombs to be just as nail-biting and dangerous as it was in the original. Now, it's as easy as ever as to find them and complete a mission that felt simplified when it didn't need to be.I'm moving onto Overtime Mode soon but, so far... this game isn't the definitive Dead Rising experience. If you want to experience the intensity of fighting the clock, the undead and psychopathic survivors in a scrap to the finish, play 2016 re-release first. It's $10. It's intense. It's the Dead Rising game we wanted DR4 to be. It's what DRDR had to be... It isn't. It's not without fun, but it's not the Deluxe Remaster it's advertised to be. The vast array of weird glitches that range from slight annoyance to game breaking, the gameplay that's been made even easier, weird design changes and choices for the remake etc. I've covered my journey in detail in the Discussions. I plan on playing Overtime Mode and Infinity Mode. But, for those wondering if this game is the Deluxe Remaster we've been waiting for. It isn't. It's a nice game to add to your DR collection but it doesn't seem to fully understand its roots besides the details on the surface level. We have yet to wait for a true DR title that goes back to its roots, essence and all.

_childDocuments_.review: If you've never played a Dead Rising game before, buy it and play it - I highly recommend you experience this type of game and it's mechanics, all the things that make the original game great are present in their entirety here, and Dead Rising is a really fun and unique experience - even if the amazing RE engine isn't quite as 'charming' and oldschool as the original game.If you've played the original, read onnnnn:---------A very genuine remaster of an all time classic. Be aware the difference between a remaster like this and a reMAKE like Capcom's resi 2/3/4 - DRDR holds true to the original mechanics and gameplay far more than the RE remakes do.As a die-hard fan of the original Dead Rising, to play a near identical copy of it with the new RE Engine's lighting and shadows is just everything I dreamed it could look like 20 years ago. It straight up feels like the original with a lot of QOL updates and good lighting/shadows. Most importantly the SURVIVOR AI IS WORKING NOW!I almost wish the AI was as dreadful as the original game, purely for the immense challenge of getting the achievements like Transmissionary and Saint, but ultimately I imagine the OG game now feels unplayable with the new improved survivor AI it's that well improved.There's a few things that aren't great, erotic photo types are gone but the sub-quests referring to them exist (yet a third quest IS changed to a new photo type? weird). Also of course the original voice actor for Frank wasn't brought back which is such a shame, but the new VA does the job well, kudos too as it's an iconic role to try take up.The new content is good, there's not a tonne which honestly I think is a good thing - a handful of interesting and useful books to upgrade Frank, a few new weapons to play with including the rocket launcher which is a capcom classic. The DLCs look good, they're cosmetics to support Capcom and the team who worked on Dead Rising so pick them up if you enjoy.Highly recommend, especially if you have never played a Dead Rising Game before.

_childDocuments_.review: The Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster offers a polished, modernized version of the 2006 cult classic, with significant updates that enhance both visuals and gameplay. Powered by the RE Engine, it features improved graphics, bringing the zombie-filled shopping mall to life with more detailed environments and characters. The controls have been streamlined, making combat smoother and less frustrating. Frank West, the protagonist, can now move while aiming, and the survivor AI has been improved, though it still has occasional hiccups.Fans will appreciate the ability to choose between classic and modern control schemes, offering flexibility in how the game is played. New features like autosave and a refined weapon durability system reduce some of the original’s tedious aspects. However, the game retains its zany charm and over-the-top boss fights, and nostalgia. the updated AI and control improvements make the game more accessible without losing its original appeal.a decent and faithful remake that offer appeal to the O.G of the original and newcomers alike.I give it a solid 8/10 on the coffee creme chart.

_childDocuments_.review: This is overall a great way to experience dead rising 1, but there are a few caveats I personally wouldn't call these deal-breakers though.Pros:-Visuals (duh)-Better controls-Weapon durability is more easily visible-Survivor AI has been reworked and are much more co-operative, with some added mechanics for extra flavour-Can fast-forward the timer in the safe room- You can move while shooting- Several books have been reworked to be more useful- Can change clothes in the safe room as long as you’ve picked up these clothes in the shop beforehand, you also aren’t locked into an animation when picking up clothes- All survivor interactions (and Otis) have voice acting now- Otis is a lot less annoying- Thomas can be spared, albeit he can't be rescued- The mini-chainsaws have been nerfed, which helps to slightly counterbalance how much easier the game is now.- All of the licensed music has been preservedCons:- There’s no longer an indicator for when survivors are able to enter a new area- A lot of censorship, and the erotica tag for photos has been removed- The voice acting is worse across the board- No option of a classic mode with reduced PP gain and disabled auto-saving.Listing cons like this may make them seem worse than they actually are, but overall I do recommend this remake. I imagine mods will fix a number of these issues.

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who has been quite the Dead Rising fan since the original, It feels like I've been waiting forever for something to come around, after the disaster that DR4 was for the series I was thinking it might never return, then we got news of the remake, honestly going in I was concerned, but mostly, those fears didn't come to be.First the few negatives: Although most of the new voice cast is grand, the odd person sounds bad but seems more like a voice direction issue (On that front, although he's not THEE Frank West, the new dude does a grand job, just takes a little getting used to at first)The game has poor optimisation on it's settings, despite my specs being far and away above what the recommendations are, it needed me to turn down graphics by quite a bit (a common issue I've seen browsing discussions) and I'm sure Denuvo is having an affect on all of us as it normally does.A few crashes here and there, although mostly ONLY when the graphics were not adjusted for myself, once I toned it down it only crashed a single time and I had been playing for about 6 hours straight, so I can't fully blame it happening.Now onto the positives:Despite the graphic issues, the game still looks wonderful, the cast, suriviors, zombies & world all look great, the RE engine is very much a good thing for Capcom!Combat is updated enough to feel great but still keep a small bit of the OG Dead Rising "clunkiness", loads of weapons to pick from, with even the Rocket Launcher, that was cut from the OG getting in.The voice cast! Although as stated that we have a few bad apples, on the overall, they do great! all lines are now properly voice acted, you can skip through to save any hassle from Zombies trying to force convos to restart and it all just helps add to the experience.The story is mostly untouched and is what the OG was, most lines are the exact same, with the odd change for censorship here or there (get over it, it's not big stuff) leading to it feeling like a trip down memory lane, even if it turns out I forgot bits of the story or thought they happened in DR2.The updated endless mode is much better, allowing you to suspend your run, although you still need to do 7 in-game days, you can make a save that quits you out the game, allowing you to return when you have time, no more leaving your machine on overnight or trying to do a 14 hour IRL straight run!Overall, DRDR is a grand revisit to the Willamette Mall and our favourite War Journalist, hopefully Capcom patch the few bugs and annoyances and this will then become a perfect entry point for new fans & a modern feeling experience for us old folk.

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing the original dead rising for 14 years. I've spent almost 25 hours with this game (maxed out Frank, completed main story and infinity mode, still working on finishing the achievements). Here's my review.This remaster is great. It has its problems, but the good outweighs the bad.Accessibility is one of the best new features of this game. However, it also comes at a cost. The game is much easier. Leveling up is a much quicker process, moving while aiming broke a few of the fights, and the new control scheme is much more intuitive. The ability to now skip time has been a god send for, not just the main game - but, the infinity mode. No longer do you have to spend 14 hours of real time to complete it. The loss of challenge is a balancing issue which could be fixed via patch. As it stands, the sense of helplessness and hopelessness you get from being miles away from a bathroom after a boss fight with no healing items is gone. There are a lot of new features that are great. There is a lot more camera customization. You can get a bunch of brand new upgrades to dig into the photography mechanic. The AI has drastically improved with new survivor mechanics that, while I didn't pay much attention to, were still cool. Every NPC is now voiced which adds a new level of immersion. Graphically the game looks fantastic. Costume selection has been streamlined and it's less of a hassle to try on new clothing pieces. I also appreciated that the original soundtrack stayed in tact. There's probably more, but generally speaking the quality of life changes have been a god send for a veteran of this game.This game does have its issues. While Frank West's voice and look grew on me, I can't say the same for a lot of the cast. Many of the models look about the same, yet the voice cast is completely different from 2006. The main voice that sticks out is Brad. His VA sounds like a 19 year old trying to do their best Samuel Jackson impression. It's rough. There were times where this game dropped frames on me during intensive moments but otherwise I didn't have many technical issues. They changed some of the dialogue for seemingly no reason. Frank no longer says "what in the world" when watching the security camera near the beginning of the game, all of the detail is taken from Clint's dialogue as he no longer is specifically a Vietnam vet (we know he is, but 'communist' is replace with 'mole' and his entire PTSD attack is way too vague to be believable now), and they white washed the butcher. _childDocuments_.review: I'm loving most of the changes and improvements they've made with this remake so far, but there's a few glaring problems that compel me not to recommend it to anyone at its current state or price point:1. A ton of ambient sound is broken or missing. Zombies make absolutely no noises unless you're very close to them. There's no echo or reverb in the mall--especially during cutscenes. The Wonderland Plaza rollercoaster makes zero sounds unless you're right in front of the ride entrance. The list goes on, and it really drains the atmosphere and immersion out of the game, making everything just completely lifeless and a lot less fun. It seems like this is an issue lots of people are having across all platforms, and it was something plenty of YouTubers discussed when they got their hands on the preview build of the game a month ago. The fact that it's still like this leads me to believe it was a creative choice and not a technical problem, and if so, this is a huge blunder.2. The game is way too easy.PP gain (haha) is out of control. Perfectly framed stickers now give out five times the amount of experience that they used to, and photography in general just gives you way too many points. Having only rescued the two tutorial survivors and messed around in Paradise Plaza, I was able to reach level 12 before the first boss fight (out of 50 total levels!)With this much experience being handed out, players will have no incentive to ever restart the game with a leveled character. Worse, they will have no mechanical reason to rescue survivors--which is a real shame, because the improvements to survivors are all fantastic. I wish I could say the same about the zombie AI, but I can't. It seems like they've been tuned to become less aggressive, and in some cases, will outright ignore the player that's standing inches from their faces.3. Technical problems.Some stuttering. Lots of texture and LOD pop-in during cutscenes. Zombies stuck inside trees or pillars. Zombie pop-in is really bad in several areas, and it just feels like there's significantly less zombies on screen at a time compared to the original. If the awful sound design is simply broken, then that belongs here too. Perhaps it can be blamed on Denuvo, or maybe it's just launch day jitters. Either way, there's enough problems here that it's worth mentioning.If Capcom fixes these problems, I would recommend the game in good conscience--and I really wish I could! Because, with these issues aside, there's so many fantastic quality-of-life improvements and new additions that this could be the definitive way to play Dead Rising in the way that Resident Evil 1's remake is the de facto RE1 experience.

_childDocuments_.review: Is this game fun? Yes.Is this game good? Yes.Is this Dead Rising? Yes.Is it better than the last Dead Rising game? Oh definitely.Then why is this review negative? Well... If steam had a "neutral" option, I would've chose that for this review. This is Dead Rising. It's that same Dead Rising we played on the Xbox 360, and later here on PC with the original remastered release. Sure some things here have been changed and at least one very core feature removed, but don't get it wrong. This is Dead Rising down to every little intricate detail. It even has the same bugs as the original. Don't believe me? Go into day six of infinity mode and try to enter the Food Court and see what happens. I had fun with this game. I had fun showing it off to all my friends and talking about all the little cool things you can do in it. It is a fun game... but. It's the same exact game as the one currently available here on Steam for $9.99. I understand this is a "Deluxe Remaster" and not a "Remake" but I didn't expect this to be a 97% carbon copy for $49.99. I only have 3 major gripes about this game and you just heard me talk about my first one. The second is the "light" censorship present in this version. I've heard that the Erotica tag for photos was removed because of a couple of new laws in Japan. If this is truly the case, I understand. The Psycho, Larry Chiang, was made to resemble more a normal guy than the original's. I can see the reasoning for that as well, his character in the original was a laughably racist stereotype. The last one however is the one I have the most problem with, Clint. Clint is portrayed as a Vietnam War Veteran suffering a PTSD Flashback after seeing his granddaughter be eaten by zombies. As such he believes that everyone, including Frank, is "Viet Cong" and "Filthy Communist". This was changed to "Mole" and "Filthy Animal" in this remaster. This, in my opinion as someone who is the son of a Vietnam War Veteran and was one of their caretakers, is distasteful. It downplays on the emotions that these men feel, and felt by plowing over it with verbal AstroTurf. You might say they did that as to not offend anyone of Vietnamese descent... I don't care. This one is the most far-fetched censorship out of them all, and it leaves a bitter taste in my mouth. I think now I should move on to the final criticism I have for DRDR before people begin to think that one thing influenced this review. My final criticism is the voice acting. Holy. God. This is some of the worst voice acting I've heard in a while. Out of all the main characters Brad is by very very VERY far the worst. It's so bad that it is beyond laughable bad. He sounds like the voice that everyone makes when they're trying to mock someone with an authoritative tone. Jessie, Isabela, and Carlito are all different levels of average to good, but oh my god did the VA for Brad phone this one in. Now Frank's... I was really hesitant and went into the game with a negative opinion for Frank's new VA, but in complete honesty. I really like the new VA for Frank. This new guy sounds like he is really putting the effort into properly portraying Frank in this remaster, and it grows on you as you make your way through the game. I respect and admire the effort, good job.So we're at the end. Thanks for reading all this if you did. There is a lot more I could talk about, like the quality of life changes. For example, you only need 5 queens instead of 10 like in the original. The amount of PP you get is much higher than the original, which in turn makes the whole game way less stressful. I think I'm gonna leave it at those two, and finish writing this review. So what is my final verdict? It's alright... buy it on sale, or something idk. I'm gonna go play Space Marine 2 now.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is an incredible faithful reconstruction of the original title.  Almost everything that made the original good is present & accounted for here.  From the arcade fun of finding the variety of weapons in the mall, to entertaining & terrifying psychopaths scattered about.  Aspects of the setting have been fleshed out more in this title, with many areas of the mall feeling more alive than the original.  The RE Engine has been utilized to a horrifying degree as the undead look more realistically gruesome than before.  The visuals received an improvement all around, & it actually shows the best with the little details throughout the mall.  PP stickers are now more visible, making it possible to hunt them down without utilizing a guide.  On top of that, all survivors have their own audio rather than just text boxes, with a few even having cues that alert the player to their presence.  On audio, the game's entire soundtrack is still here.  Control wise, the only noticeable change is the ability to move while aiming, a welcome feature that makes the gunplay a little more useful.  They even added scrapped elements from the original title this time around.  The AI has undergone the biggest change, not only with survivors.  Yes, survivors now follow orders & play around zombies far better than before, but enemy AI also interacts better as well with the special forces soldiers becoming a challenging enemy to overcome.  The best addition for repeated playthroughs has to be the new ability to fast forward time at any save point.  This is even available in infinity mode, making a waiting slog into a more frantic survivor hunt.  Unfortunately, a few of the voice acting roles feel worse than the original.  Considering the original only had voice acting for a select few, this is an issue due to them appearing in many of the game's cutscenes.  On that note, along with a follow up from the game's soundtrack, the original cast was not brought back for this title, & many musicians stated the tracks were used without them being contacted (contracts & all that, but it's still something that should be mentioned).  Visually, there's some noticeable pop in for all zombies in the distance, something that does take one out of the experience whenever it happens.  Frank's movement in this game feels a little stiffer than the original.  In order to balance out the new gun controls, it feels like guns fire slower, especially the real mega buster (which now has a charged shot to attempt to make up for it).  Amusingly enough, with exception to the psychopaths & soldiers, the entire game feels easier thanks to all the changes.  It's interesting looking at both this & the original release, because the lists are very similar.  Many achievements have had their grind reduced, such as Transmissionary dropping from all calls to only 30.  Several middle of the road & severely grind based achievements have been removed & replaced with a few task based ones instead.  Noticeably, Zombie Annihilator (previously Genocider) & 7 Day survivor are still here, but all of the achievement based rewards are there as well, giving incentive to go for them.  All of the improvements & removal of most heavy grind achievements makes this list far easier to go for, though still requiring a few playthroughs to net them all.  Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is exactly what should be wanted from a title like this.  Everything from the previous game is still present & accounted for (unless you're someone seethingly upset that the erotica option was removed from taking pictures).  The change in the voice actor team & behind the scenes audio stuff will turn a few people off, & it's reasonable to be.  Overall, the game stands out, & deserves a recommendation in my book.

_childDocuments_.review: As a massive Dead Rising 1 fan who's been playing the first game well over 15 years now. The aiming feels much better now and far more streamlined to newer releases now. Survivor AI though still feels rough. The only change that I can see personally is that they don't get targeted or grappled nearly as much as they used to.  They still feel pretty dumb 80% of the time so I guess it's a slight upgrade.Graphics look fantastic however, the RE Engine truly brings this game to life as a whole. Every area has gotten a pretty face lift and looks great!One of the biggest issues by far is pop in. I don't know if its just my PC/Specs but it felt like every 20 or so feet zombies were popping in like crazy. It felt jarring every time it happened. In much denser areas it's not as bad but open ones? It looks horrible.Now lets get the biggest issue out and about. The voice and dialogue changes. I know its been a huge talked about aspect of the remaster and while some changes didn't make much sense. *Like the change where Frank doesn't say "What in the world?" anymore.* To Cliffs changes too. I don't have the biggest issues with these. While it does suck to see them get changed it wasn't a massive deal breaker by any means. Most of the original lines have stayed in the game and I'd go as far to say nearly 99% have been kept while adding extra ones. Speaking of extra voice lines, every character now has voice lines. Even Otis! It's such a nice change and breathes new life into the game. It's all around a lovely touch.But so far I enjoyed my time with the game itself despite the some of the issues. It's a great way to play one of the greatest games from the 360 era and even better for long time fans!7.5/10

A couple of new additions such as a new weapon, and about 6~ new books which allow you to use more weapons, or even make your survivors more durable and aggressive.An interesting mechanic where you can now fast forward time to get those harder achievements where it previously required you to play 3 days straight, lol; or even just skip downtime in between cases.Overall, as a hardcore fan of the franchise, and of the OG game specifically, I'd give this a perfect 5/7!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay so, as a big fan of the original I do like a lot of the quality of life improvements that have been made to make it feel a little less jank, it's not jank-free, it's still got some issues, but it's a better user experience overall in game-play in comparison to the original, so points for that. What I do take points off for is a lot of the odd changes they've made, Larry is a weird one where I feel they may have gone a bit too far in the opposite direction, I feel like there could've been a better redesign that would've fit better in the middle when comparing the original to the remaster because both are quite drastically different, it's weird because it makes me like neither of the representations of him and instead wish for a better one that isn't so one way or the other. Moving on from Larry, Cliff's changes I also didn't like but it's not a huge deal, but seriously, if you're that scared of calling the player a "filthy communist" maybe just change that line for the regions it affects? Doubly so, we're literally talking about a Vietnam War veteran going through post-traumatic stress disorder due to the events unfolding, it was kind of fine the way it was and neutered in the remaster to I guess pander to anyone who likes communism? I don't know. Another issue I have is the performances, I feel people are missing out on the original voice performances which were fantastic, I'm not going to rag on the new voice actors chosen for this remaster because they did a fine job, but the issue is that the performances in the original were already so good that it's hard to top them, so trying would just kind of be a lost cause, I appreciate the new life the new performances bring to the remaster, but I feel they fall a bit flat at times and lack the direction that the original had in that regard, they're not bad, but like I said; it's just hard to top something that was really good to begin with, especially when we were at a time where voice acting was still a bit of a toss-up, where-as now it really shouldn't be, yet we still get blunders regardless. Erotica photography genre has been removed entirely, I'm fine with it but I find it funny that they kept a side-mission that is literally made for the Erotica photography genre with little to no changes other than slapping a PP moment on the character in question to make up for the lack of prestige points you'd normally get from the Erotica genre. Other than that you've got new bugs that are specific to this version, I've noticed a lot of zombies getting stuck in geometry more than the original and also sometimes phasing through doors you've closed which is really annoying when you think you're safe but the horde just pushes a zombie through a closed door due to the amount of zombies all clustered together and pushing each other in attempts to reach you despite you being in another room entirely. I get FPS drops consistently in the same areas (RTX 2080 Ti btw, I know it's not the most powerful card in the world but it should be fine for this game I feel?) so I'm really holding out for a patch although I haven't seen one at all and was kinda expecting one by now. Survivor AI luckily is MUCH better than the original, where the original felt like you were truly babysitting, in this version I feel a bit more confident in the survivors, but only a bit since they're not THAT smart, just smarter than their original counter-parts in most scenarios. This is a nitpick but the cultists and them pointing at their head rather than praying and they gave Sean a cute little headband to signify him being the cult leader and why the cultists point at their head now instead of pray, I guess they didn't want to feel like they were insulting other religions? Why care enough about this to change it I do not know, go look at Far Cry 5 and how much they shove religion in your face then come back to this being confused as to why Capcom was scared to insinuate cult behaviour with religion. This game also has the fabled yellow paint that same people love and some people hated about Resident Evil 4 Remake and other titles, I don't really care, if anything I find it funny because I've witnessed people completely miss it regardless of it's integration so I feel like it's utterly pointless. I'm kind of running out of steam for this review so I'm gonna try and wrap it up here; the new magazines are cool but some of them I feel really didn't need to be added because they add next to nothing or make the already easy game even easier, the cut weapon they brought back is neat but also a little pointless at the end of the day, infinity mode is infinitely easier so yay to those who appreciate that and boo from those who did the original and feel the newcomers must also suffer lol, uhhhh overall great game, hope this review helped in some way, still a big fan of the original and prefer it in a lot of ways and I hope we get something for Dead Rising 2, preferably with less cuts, censorship and more content (God would I love if they bundled Case Zero, 2, Case West and Off the Record into one big neat package with a little bow on it considering both Case Zero and Case West are still stuck on the Xbox until the day they die)

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster is, at the moment, very rushed feeling. So much so that I felt the need to list all the grievances I have with it in hopes of them being noticed and fixed by Capcom, or modders down the line. Before I get into that stupid long list though, I should mention that this game is still incredibly fun. It's still mostly Dead Rising 1, and that alone makes it a great time.When compared to the original 2006 version, however, there are just too many problems -- either from bugs or weird decisions -- that I can't recommend it at full price. Getting the original at 1/6th of the price is a much better deal, with a much more cohesive experience.So with all that being said, here's a giant list of all the weirdness I've encountered thus far, in no particular order:--------------------------------------------------------------------In the beginning chopper scene, you can see objects spawning in on the side of the screen if you have the camera zoomed all the way out. This doesn't make a very good first impressionTutorial images show an unfinished build of the game, missing lighting and assets. This makes for a very *bad* first impressionFrank can be grabbed while attacking, meaning you get grabbed a lot more, especially when trying to use slower weapons like the sledgehammerYou can no longer jump on boxes to break them, likely due to the fact that objects can now be pushed by walking into themAlso due to the ability to push objects, the hunk of meat is now insanely powerful, as zombies will continually kick it away from them while trying to pick it up, resulting in large groups swarming around it for a long time, moving with it as it gets kicked until one of them finally gets itThey added yellow paint in the food court for Carlito's fight that's both unnecessary and also persists for the entire duration of the game despite only being useful in that one instanceKicking trash cans no longer breaks them consistentlyFrank no longer plays his fatigued animation after being attackedFrank feels much floatier than the original gameZombies constantly despawn or pop inPP is awarded way too generously (I got to level 6 in the very first encounter before the safe room was locked, with up to 6,000 PP in a single image. I went back to the original and the highest I could get here was 800 (without stickers in the mix)Speaking of PP Stickers, they now glow bright yellow, and are called out by survivors, making them painfully obvious and removing a lot of the fun of searching for them as you explore the mall (They're also barely worth it when you can get the same amount of PP they give you in two photos easily)Frank can't get blood on him from zombiesBlood splatter happens immediately, instead of being delayed to simulate the travel time of the liquid as it was beforeThe skateboard is like 3x too big for some reason, and feels 3x as fast (seriously, what the hell)Ambient sounds are missing, most noticably the low zombie growl that's supposed to constantly play. This makes areas feel incredibly empty, which isn't helped by the lack of zombiesVoice acting is worse than the original in nearly every instance, and things like reverb are missing from the voice lines. Also, I will forever be salty about no TJ RotoloThe boxes showing the survivors on your HUD are now just dots, making it more difficult to tell when they're in danger or stuck; especially since they constantly bump into each other and make sounds like they're being grabbed because of itCop zombies being able to shoot means your movement is constantly interrupted by random gunshots hitting you. I imagine this is why it was removed from the original game.Mirrors *only* function in bathrooms, with any other mirrors still present only using cubemaps and screenspace reflections, and some (like the gym one) being outright removedGates were added in-between areas for some reason, making the mall feel even more disconnected than beforeSome textures are just poorly upscaled, or didn't receive proper care (like the door behind Jessie reading "NATAlieS GateO FimPrisOnmentK FimPrisOnmentK NATAlieS GateO", when in the original game it was just too blurry to make out)You can now take 100 photos before having to recharge instead of 30, making it easy to abuse the camera (they tried adding a progressively longer cooldown if you spam it, but with the amount of PP awarded it really doesn't matter)Aligning the servbot head is now a pain, as it's harder to make contact with and spins way further from a single punchErotica was removed, but none of the sexualized angles in cutscenes were changed, nor was the side quest in which Cheryl requests Frank take literal erotica pictures of her (the picture is just considered "drama" or "no genre" now)Item health is now not only visible at all times, but is also overly generous. (Seriously, the regular Chainsaws now last for ages without books and allow you to just clear a path through like three areas)Lots of small details are now worse, like the belt on the treadmill no longer giving the illusion of spinning properly, and moving you back in "steps" when you stand still on it instead of smoothly sliding you offThe dialogue from survivors while exploring with them is awful, and they say the weirdest things, including mentioning posting on "social media" despite the game taking place in 2006Frank's character model is not only unappealing to look at, but is wider than the original by quite a good bit while still using the same rig, resulting in some animations looking strange or being less readableLighting in cutscenes feels very poorly done, which is weird since the lighting in the mall itself looks great. The maintenance room in particular suffers from gross dim bathroom lightingFrank doesn't hold the transceiver properly, his fingers clip through it while he makes a closed fistThe game sometimes stutters when you enter a new area as it loads all the objectsIn general the character models don't look great, especially in comparison to the mallThe Chuck Greene pre-order skin (that I can't get due to not pre-ordering) has errors all over it, including the word "Racing" missing on the back, the "4" being on both of his shoulders instead of one with a logo on the other, and having the number be the wrong color as wellFor me in particular, I killed the convicts, then loaded my game to before I did so and killed them again. The first time I was awarded the prisoner outfit, the second time I was not, and I can no longer seem to obtain it in my playthroughThey didn't change the scoop chances with saved survivors being immediately lost if you enter and exit the safe room, which I find odd as that seems like one of the biggest QoL changes you could make (next to tweaking the AI)The cult's new "eye" pose is kinda cool, but the lack of animation transitions to/from it make it looks like an unfinished mod. It's also just a weird idle animation. Having them pray makes much more sense.Frank goes like a full 6 feet up in the air before dropping back down when he does the knee drop now and it looks insane----------------------------------------------------------------------------------And that's all the stuff I've found so far. Haven't beaten the game yet, but I'd imagine that covers most of the important (and some nitpicky) stuff. Like I said, I'm still enjoying the hell out of the game, and it's worth noting I haven't mentioned a lot of the *good* QoL stuff they added (like survivors not dropping their weapons after you give them food)I just felt it was worth mentioning that while this game is fun, it has a plethora of issues that, until they're addressed, make this the worse version of Dead Rising on PC by a good bit. I very much hope that the team that put this together is able to continue polishing it until it's at least equal to the original, but if not then we at least have a great framework for modders to work with.

_childDocuments_.review: So this is my comprehensive review of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster after a little over 13-14 hours of gameplay and all achievements unlocked aside from the 5 and 7 day survivor achievements which I am working on now. I will likely talk about the story a little bit so expect spoilers. Not sure why I should care about spoilers as the story itself is going on 20 years old, but I might as well put it out there to avoid some complaining.- GraphicsSo the game has been updated with the RE engine and has been given a serious touch up in the graphics department. The changes are VERY noticeable in the mall itself and especially in Leisure Park. Foliage as far as the eye can see in the park, and lots of smaller details added into the whole mall to really bring the Willamette Parkview Mall to life. I think it is a very impressive update to the original's already good looking setting. My one complaints would be with 2 things: the gore and the character's face models. Now let me say that the gore looks absolutely amazing. Blood looks super real and it is an absolute mess after slaughter. My complaint is that blood doesn't really get onto Frank at all. You'd think after taking a battle axe I found in an antique shop to 50 zombies or so, that I'd get some blood on me. Nope, my outfit is just as clean as it was before I even jumped out of the helicopter. Blood on your character is something that literally EVERY other entry in the series had, including the atrocity that was Dead Rising 4. Maybe this is something that can be added in a future update (assuming they do anything else with this game). As for the character face models, it's very much a mixed bag. There's a lot of detail added into all of the faces that make them look more real, but they still seem...ugly compared to the admittedly already ugly-looking faces the original Dead Rising had. It's hard to explain. To me, Frank especially looks much older than he was in the original. Whether this was intentional or not, I don't know. But it just doesn't click with me very well. Not the biggest deal though, and it doesn't take away from all of the graphical fidelity added to the rest of the game.- GameplayGameplay, for the most part, is still just as solid as in the original. Zombies are still super fun to take...whatever you can find to. That's the beauty of Dead Rising, if you can pick it up, you can use it as a weapon, and that very much still holds true to this game. There have even been some improvements to gameplay, like the option to fast forward time at safe places to get rid of some of the downtime people would run into with the original. It's not required by any means, and if people still prefer waiting out the time doing...whatever, they can just avoid the option. There have been a few tweaks to difficulty overall with a few aspects, but I will touch on those more later in the review.- AudioAudio is probably the thing that was altered the least out of everything from the original game. All of the original music from the OST of Dead Rising to the added in tracks for Pyschopath fights are still present in this version of the game. The developers even added a streamer mode so that streamers and content creators can safely play through the game without worry about copyright strikes. Very welcome change! Now personally, the original Dead Rising tracks were never really my favorite in gaming. However, that is definitely a personal preference. The soundtrack is still very well done!- DifficultySo based on what I've seen from other reviewers, this section has been a pretty controversial set of changes from the original. The game has definitely seen some changes, mostly QoL that make the game significantly more accessible for players. Now, a lot of people say that the original game was "so much harder" than this version. I'm going to have to respectfully disagree. The original Dead Rising definitely had a lot more outdated game mechanics to it that made the game more...frustrating to play in my opinion. The survivor AI is a particular stand out one to me. In the original game, survivor NPC AI would CONSTANTLY get stuck on objects, zombies, and each other. Often times, this would lead to you having to babysit them incredibly close and kill every zombie in the immediate area or you risk them getting swarmed super easily and promptly killed. This would cost you valuable PP (the XP for this game) and the Saint achievement if you were going for that. The survivor AI in the remaster has seen a serious improvement. They are not by any means easy mode though. In my first playthrough, I had a couple of occasions where they would run into each other and make a lot of noise, or would get hit by one zombie and go into, what I can only describe as a rage, and start attacking every zombie around them and you would have to kill the zombies yourself to stop this rage. This is reminiscent to what they would do in the original game, however to a much lesser extent. Now, while survivors are definitely more intelligent in this game and receive less friendly fire damage from you (thank god), they are much more squishy to zombie attacks. I had a survivor get stuck in a relatively small swarm of zombies for only roughly 10-15 seconds, and they had almost died on me and costing me my Saint run. That being said, it is definitely and improvement overall and I got the Saint achievement first run from level 0 which is a lot harder in the original.Infinity mode is another thing that was changed a little. They added a change for zombies to drop random items whether it be weapons or even small food items. However, this is a very small chance for food and it is not usually going to save you from dying. However, the ability to save in infinity mode is SO nice. I despised having to do my original 7 day run in one go for 14 hours which most of which is spent waiting. This wasn't fun, or even satisfying when I did do it. And yes, you can skip time in infinity mode too which is also super nice. Just keep an eye on your health bar. - GrindThe grind honestly felt about the same overall. However, the first few levels seemed to come INCREDIBLY fast. I got to level 15 before I even finished the first case. However, it levels out around level 20 where you have to get a lot PP in order to level up. So it took me about the same amount of time to hit level 50 as the original. I imagine the first few levels were for newer players which is okay if you ask me.- StoryThe story is the same, so I'll take this time to give my opinion on the voice actor changes. There is no doubt that the acting is a step down from the original game. However, I don't think it is quite as bad as people make it out to be. Nobody will be winning any Emmys for this but it's not horrendous like people say. Even Frank's new voice actor grew on me a little more as I progressed. However, I do miss old voice actor, TJ Storm a lot. That one was a hard change.- Game TimeI managed to get all but the Infinity mode achievements in roughly 14 hours. A lot of achievements have changed or were removed and are easier to get. Got mixed feelings on that.- PriceHonestly, I'd wait for a sale. $50 is pretty steep for an 18 year old game with a graphical update.- BugsI ran into a quite a few shuddering problems and a 3 crashes in my first run. Nothing game breaking but hopefully these get smoothed out with updates. Final Rating & Conclusion: It's a very solid remake/remaster of Dead Rising. For the most part, it respects everything the original game did while adding nice QoL changes to make the game more accessible for new players. It's definitely the best way to play Dead Rising now in my opinion. However, I still think people should check out the original and judge that for themselves.* 7/10 *

_childDocuments_.review: Excellent remaster, or remake rather. Before I get to the review, a bit of a PSA on the performance.I was a bit put off by the performance initially, and I think many people will be as well. RE Engine, if you're not familiar, is a bit weird with its graphics setting. While I don't know what the VRAM allocation setting actually does, setting it too high causes horrific stutters, hard locks, low FPS, and severe object pop in. Remember that VRAM fluctuates based on what is going on on screen. If you're on, say a 8GB RTX 4060, and you set all the graphics options to max and the menu is reading 4.51GB of with DLSS Quality, that does not mean you have 3.5GB of free space and can set the textures to High (3GB). Too much VRAM being used will caused massive instability. For reference, I'm on a 10GB RTX 3080 and, without DLSS, the menu VRAM use was at 5.01GB. Setting the VRAM on my rig to High (4GB) gave me so many performance issues. Once I set it to High (2GB) it was fine. It's generally a good idea to always try and leave 20% of your VRAM open for fluctuations. Since the game doesn't tell you, you'll have to do just a little bit of simple math to work that out.Now, onto the review.Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is partly a remaster, and partly a remake maybe leaning more towards the remake side. Although it's genuinely hard to say because a lot in a lot of ways it feels like a port with all of the original's little quirks, jank, and nuances that made the 2006 release so damn charming. But on the other hand you can tell its built from the ground up on an entirely new engine. I have to give kudos to the developers for being able to replicate that because, in a lot of ways, that really is part of what made Dead Rising 1 such a cult classic and replicating mistakes on purpose is no easy feat. This does mean that, despite the QoL improvements made to the gameplay, the game is still quite frustrating at times which many people will find to be a good thing.Some of the OG jankness I noticed includes:As far the removed content goes, I'm sorry, but if you're the kind of loser that is so up in arms because you can't take creepshots of women for points, maybe you should try getting a girlfriend and real problems? The game's cutscenes still feature Frank ogling at women.  Jessica's cleavage is still very much in plain view, purposely, at all times and there's even the shot from Frank's POV where he stares at her ass first before looking at her face. You all are crying censorship over nothing. Please, just grow up. The yuppies who yap at you through YouTube do not have your best interest at heart. They are manufacturing outrage for you to get mad at in order to garner views, grift for your attention, and some are even funded by the Russian government for the sake of spreading an agenda. The wokies are not after your games. The changes made to Larry is not censorship. Get over yourselves.The new actors are a little jarring at first, especially Frank, but as you see the remake's cutscenes unfold this new VA offers the same if not better delivery on a lot of Frank's iconic lines. The visual overhaul is gorgeous in a lot of ways, but can lack in some. I think my biggest gripe is the game's lighting. Sometimes it looks really good. Sometimes it looks really washed out. I was worried the shooting while moving would made the game too easy but, thankfully, it's actually really not that all that different from the original. You can only move while aiming, not while actively shooting, so you have to still sit still to actually fire off rounds continuously. The AI improvements to the survivors is actually pretty solid overall. They're not the smartest, still, but if you beeline through zombies they're capable of keeping up without taking any damage or only taking a very minuscule amount of damage. There's still a bit of babysitting you have to do, but it's definitely  frustrating than it was in the original.My only real big complaint is leveling up. It does feel like it goes by too quickly. I've only just finished the first Psychopath, and all the survivors before 6AM on the first day and I'm already level 15. I think Capcom needs to dial back the leveling by about half and this remaster would be perfect.One addition I really like is that now all interactions outside of cutscenes are fully voiced, even Otis's dislogue. And these survivors can now make call outs pointing out various points of interest, helpful hints, and even pointing out effective weaponry nearby as you're escorting them back to the saferoom.Overall, this remaster/remake/whatever you want to call it is a perfect way to enjoy the classic that started it all. The combat is the same, the physics and jank are the same, everything feels new but familiar at the same time and it's quite comforting.

One being the boss fights while i do admit they are definitely harder than the original guns make them so much easier, i mean maybe too easy. Kent is an ass, if you don't get there in time and have to fight him chained up. Just reload the save.  in short, you want to zoom through fights then load up on guns. You want a decent challenge then use melee weapons. Soldiers are insanely overpowered and i know they are supposed to be but i cant help feel like they need fine tuned slightly because trying to go anywhere with multiple of them is near impossible. The stun lock its just too much, i had 4 soldiers destroy my health on lvl 45 in seconds and i could not run, jump or roll away at all. I 2 shot the military helicopter with the sniper. _childDocuments_.review: There were so many QOL changes and improvements I just wasn't expecting, and I love it!If you liked Dead Rising 1, you'll love Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster... UNLESS you let nostalgia dictate every emotion you have, and always say things like "The orginal is ALWAYS better than the remake". No sir, everything has an opportunity for improvement, and these devs saw that :) Pros--Fast forwarding time, in 72hr and infinity mode, is so perfect-Skateboards were improved in almost every way -Motorcycles can go room to room, now.-AI aren't completely braindead anymore-The new magazines they added gives more game play options.-PP stickers and zombie kills give a lot more exp now, so you actually use your camera to level up now.-Walking while aiming, and gunslinger mags actually make gun builds more enjoyable-Rolling is a nice combat feature now since you become invulnerable in the beginning of the animation. Fighting bosses kinda feels like a very easy souls game since you can dodge attack based on enemy motions. I don't remember ever using the roll in DR1 since it didn't really help, and you couldn't predict attacks from animations being too fast.-Changing from a locker in the safe house is awesome!-Everyone has a voice actor, so no more reading dialogue to break the immersion.-Survivor tips have been surprisingly helpful in the first playthroughCons- -Brads voice sucked. Hard lol. He sounds like he was recording from his moms basement and didn't want to wake up her from a nap.-Stun locks from special forces are insane.It only takes 2 to get you in a nasty stunlock for at LEAST half your HP.-AI fixation on targets is annoying. They won't stop attacking their targets until it dies, and won't just through zombies anymore.-Tank fight at the end was WAY too easy. Tank has never even made an attempt to attack in any playthroughs, and the fight lasts about 15 seconds, now.Pro OR con?-For my fellow achievement hunters, for better or worse, achievements have become a LOT easier to manage. You don't have to kill 1000 zombies barehanded anymore, replay the whole game if you missed just a single call from Otis, or try one of every food in the game lmao.-The  game is being labeled as 'woke' now? I guess from making some dialogue less offensive and removing erotica. I personally don't understand WHY they changed it, but the changes aren't bad. It sounds like these changes offended more people then the original ever offended lmao-You can SPARE Thomas now. It'd be cool to be able to bring him back to the safe house but this still works, I guess.(I'll try to keep updating the list as I remember some of the other changes.)

The gym equipment doesn't work, So you cant get PP from the exercise bike or treadmill, i didn't bother with the punching bag but it did move when i hit it so maybe??If they patch this game up i could see this being a good jumping off point for people who haven't played the previous games. Then maybe moving on up to the original for an increase in difficulty. If they give this game the necessary polish it could really pull people back into these games except 4. 4 is awful.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I've been playing this alongside the original on the Steam Deck, since this one runs pretty badly on Deck. It's a great remake, but the OG still does some things better. The maintenance tunnels, for example, have far more zombies in the original game, and the driving physics in the remake are somehow even wonkier. Hitting shopping carts can sometimes result in your car getting stuck in ways that just does not happen in the OG. If you don't want to pay this much for a remake, I think that's fair, because the OG is still really very good (and playable), especially on Deck where it gets a consistently high frame rate and is very smooth as a result. The remake is easier if that matters to you.

_childDocuments_.review: For a so called "Deluxe Remaster" its way different from its 2006/2016 counterpart, for a zombie game marked as "mature" it sure has alot of censorship.
