_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: So To preface this, I played 2, OTR, 3 and (unfortunately) 4 but I just never got into 1 as it just didn't feel comfortable after going from newer games mechanics and QOL features.This remaster remedies them and builds upon the other gamesAI, As said in another review, is good now. They will help you out, save other survivors and point out secrets such as PP stickers and caches. Protip, Do the halo strat and give them nearly unloaded firearms to maximise their effectiveness.The controls are now smooth and are rebindable in the new control scheme, although you can access the old control scheme if you prefer.The only downside I've found right now, besides frank's original VA not being here and some questionable choices when it comes to censorship, is the optimisation is currently awful. That's the only thing however!A solid way to play Deadrising 1 if you don't want to play the original due to age or QOL issues!
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This game is phenomenal. I grew up playing Dead Rising, and while the original has its charm (and is still available, if you'd rather experience that), the graphical updates, refinement of the controls and new contents wholly justifies this new experience.Dead Rising brings a unique formula to zombie-killing, relying mostly on scavenged weapons and environmental objects to survive. It also has a fixed time limit, which is surprisingly generous but still adds urgency that really builds the story atmosphere, with more quests and areas unlocking as time progresses.Please support this reboot if you want this series to return, I'd love to have Dead Rising 2, Dead Rising: Off The Record and potentially some new entries coming.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is how you remake a game. I know Im going to love this, so Im leaving my positive now, and will come back for a full review after I complete the main game! (Graphics update below)Graphics: So far I have encountered only two little hitches during the opening act when the zombies first get in the mall, and out in the park, where the grass has caused a frame drop of about 10 FPS, which quickly stabilizes. The game is on par graphically with other games that run on the RE Engine (Think RE2 Remake, RE7, RE8, etc.) There are a few little pop-ins with shadows on zombies that are further out, but it really can be noticed is you are looking for it.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: Saying "Dead Rising is back" would be wrong, because Dead Rising never left.This game gives you both the option to use modernized controls and classic controls. I played with classic controls, and true enough, I did not have the luxury of aiming while moving, lol.But playing through the game, I was INCREDIBLY impressed with how true to the original the deluxe remaster is while simultaneously feeling better and smoother. There's lots of quality-of-life stuff added, but in no way do they take away from the difficulty. There's tiny additions sprinkled about like new skill magazines which are fun!That's not to say there aren't changes. Obviously there's the graphics, which look great. I LOVE the updated character and zombie models. However, I don't think the visuals are an objective upgrade from the original. I prefer the colour grading in the original game, and the stylistic choice of having intentional frame drops in cutscenes during dramatic moments was unfortunately done away with in favour of simple slow-mo.But man, playing through this was so much fun, just like the original. It's nice to play a game that encourages you to interact with its rules and quirks. There's not a lot of games where using a hockey stick to shoot around corners to outsnipe a sniper is one of the more viable methods.When it simply comes to *playing* it, definitely go for the deluxe remaster over the original. However, when taking *everything* into consideration, I honestly think both the original and the deluxe remaster are worth playing. Dead Rising is simply that good.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is almost a perfect remake. Yes it censors some small elements, which should be criticized, but I can live with it. It fixes so much that I had issue with in the original game, and I love it. 9/10.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a 1:1 remake of the original. As someone who loves the 360 original and the 2016 PC port, this is about as faithful as you could ask for.The only big difference is the lack of returning voice talent. I find it strange that they made shot for shot remakes of the original cutscenes while giving the entire cast new voices. Why not take the chance to rework the scenes a bit? If not that, why not just use the original voices or give us an option to? They clearly still exist in the 2016 game. That all said, it's worth noting that EVERY line in the game is now voiced, including Otis on the radio and all the other survivors. It's a nice bit of polish the original lacked, but the survivors getting to spout off about things while escorting them is mostly unwelcome. This character just sobbed to me about how she watched her daughter be eaten by zombies, but then halfway back to the Security Room she says 'lol at least i have something that will finally go viral on social media!'.The game is also slightly censored, notably in the way 'Erotica' is no longer factored into photos taken. Most of the points I got from that classification were incidental anyways, so the game doesn't really feel lacking without it. Otherwise, the graphics, gameplay and quality of life, atmosphere and overall fun factor is at it's best here. It's hard not to recommend it to fans of the original or someone wanting an offbeat open world adventure.

_childDocuments_.review: Haven't played this since i was a kid, but i had a lot of fun reviving the memories. _childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I am gonna be honest, this game is just a better looking dead rising with some QoL updates. Nothing more & nothing less, do not go into this game thinking it has been entirely reworked & remade like Resident evil remakes. Capcom warned people but it always best to reiterate for those out of the loop.That out of the way, if you like dead rising and you haven't played it in awhile it still as fun as you remember. Moves are still wacky, the mall is still a cool place to explore; katana is on the awning in pleasure plaza, battle ax is still at the antique shop, and Uzi still in the fountain. Biggest change I can find is that they have removed the "erotica" genre when taking photos. It didn't bother me but it might bother some. For the most part the game is pretty much one to one with the original.This version does feels a little easier with the new control scheme and using skills is a whole alot easier this time around.  They have kept intact the timer mechanic so it is still a mad dash to get that perfect run to save every survivor. Unlimited mode is also still intact; so if you were wondering, yes it is still there.If you are a mega fan of the series or new to the game series in general, go ahead and get it; you won't be disappointed. If you replayed the game recently, are expecting a different story this time around, or felt like the original was boring\not your thing, then it might be better to wait for a sale for now.

_childDocuments_.review: A very faithful remaster to the original 2006 game, it's clear that a lot of time and dedication was put into this game. There is some changes to the game. However they are very minimal and understandable as Capcom want's to appeal to other markets then just the american one this time. [Larry's new design looks very good] The Gameplay story is exactly the same as the original with no alterations made to it. The game is more easy going in the beginning then the original however certain twists in the game can trick up even the most veteran of players and the game gets a lot harder then it previously did in the endgame stage even for higher levels giving it a more fun experienceIf your a big fan of the classic version its 100% worth checking out this one.

_childDocuments_.review: As a teenager i was so desperate to play dead rising, I had a ps3 growing up and was extremely salty that I couldn't play it. It wouldn't be until dead rising 2 that I could finally experience the franchise and I loved it but it wouldn't be until the release of halo 4 that I'd get my hands on a xbox 360 and whilst halo 4 was disappointing I at least finally got to play dead rising. Fast forward to 2024 and I'm playing dead rising all over again thanks to this shiny new remaster, after many years playing the og it was nice to step back into Willamette with a fresh coat of paint. I would love to say this is now the definitive version to play and it nearly is! But it does unfortunately come with some caveats. Let's split this up first we'll talk about the game itself then talk about the remaster itself, so what is dead rising? It's a zombie survival game that's heavily inspired by dawn of the dead as in you are stuck in a shopping centre (sorry mall, I'm from the UK so it feels weird to call it that.) And you have to survive 3 days. The fun of the game comes from both the zombies themselves and also a time mechanic in which you have 3 days which tick down in real time whilst having to uncover the plot around the zombie outbreak. Think of majoras mask but without time travel. The ticking clock elements are both fantastic and stressful but the game heavily emphasises repeat playthroughs and the game is short enough that it's not annoying to do so. It pains me that the franchise turned away from this mechanic as it's integral to the stress and tension and without it we get games like dead rising 3/4 which are shallow, boring messes which are too focused on zombie killing, this is a perfect time to talk about the zombies, they are slow and stupid but in packs they are deadly especially early game, the fun comes not so much from killing them (that is fun.) But finding unique ways to traverse them be that using the shopping centres many products or just using Frank's brute force. Dead rising is really well made, it's a small open world which is fantastically hand crafted and has some of the best attention to detail in a game, from secrets to hidden game mechanics this game is packed to the brim without being overstuffed, it's a crying shame that dead rising peaked at the first entry and while yes dead rising 2 is also fantastic I can't help but be disappointed in the direction this franchise took. Without even talking about the new additions from the remaster, yes this is 1000% a recommendation. I love this game so much and if you're new or returning then you won't be disappointed. Let's talk remasterThe good- Fast forwarding time is such a nice qol change that I think all dead rising games would benefit from this, makes replaying the game so much more manageable - new control scheme is really nice. I never had that much of a problem with the original but mapping the special moves into RB and a face button is so much better, I can rip out intestines with ease!- user interface and readability of cases is much better, not that it wasn't good in the original but it is better here.- I don't hate otis! You can continue playing normally whilst using the radio - everyone is fully voiced! All npcs that used to be text is now voiced! Frank speaking Japanese was a highlight - moving whilst shooting, subtle but very much appreciated - extra magazines have been added!- cool new dlc costumes - multiple save slots! The mixed - graphics are decent but some character models look rough and frank looks a bit off, I found some cut scenes had some messed up textures- voice acting was always going to be an issue considering how iconic his voice was but to be honest I liked new frank and almost all the new voices fit really well! It's Brad who takes the biggest hit unfortunately he's really bad in this game - PP is earned way too easily, I finished my first playthrough at level 48 with the best ending and it wasn't hard at all. I'm not saying I want them to be hard but I'm upset this has really discouraged repeated playthroughs to learn and level up which was a big deal for me as a youth, having to earn experience to come back and beat the game was so much fun but now you can basically get a perfect run with no issue first try The bad - they made some changes to censor certain more questionable parts of the game, I don't mind that they removed erotica as a sub genre for taking pictures as snapping upskirts of zombies is just gross and if you're someone who's really bothered by that then I question you as a person. Same with making the butcher not an Asian stereotype. What I do mind is changing Cliffs dialogue, it somewhat ruins what is one of the more morally complex bosses in the game. - to preface I have a rtx 4070 yet I still had stuttering and crowd density especially in the tunnels is nerfed, I really wasn't expecting this game to have stuttering but it really bothered me more than normal.In conclusion dead rising is still a fantastic game, even if this remake doesn't outright replace the original it does make going back difficult. This is easily in my top 5 zombie games and is an abosule classic, if you're old or new you'll love this game.FANTASTIC/10

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Rising is a game that holds so much love in my heart since I first watched my brothers play it in 2008 on the Xbox 360 and eventually played it myself. When I first heard about Capcom making this deluxe remaster I was a bit skeptical but then became more excited and bought the preorder bonus. Safe to say, I do not regret my decision at all and this is an amazing remaster. Every minute I played this game I had a smile on my face. This remaster is not perfect though. Some of the voice acting is a downgrade from the original, odd dialogue changes, glaring pop ins from zombies (especially in the beginning), frame drops, and my game crashed about four times while playing. Difficulty wise I do find the game a lot easier than the original but others may disagree. My biggest gripe though is the zombie density in the maintenance tunnels. In the original, the maintenance tunnels were PACKED, but in this game there's not a lot. Overall, despite my complaints, this game was extremely fun and felt like playing DR again like I did in 2008. I hope Capcom can fix some of the above mentioned issues to turn this remake into a "Fantastic" to a "Perfect". Also it's become apparent that right-wing grifters have tried to taint this games reputation by saying that Capcom is "woke" and is censoring stuff because modern audiences are dumb or whatever. While yes there is some censorship, it is very minor and does not change the overall gameplay. Plus, most of the complaints are from people who were hardly Dead Rising fans, never played the game, or repeating talking points without doing any research. Please do not let these people sway your view and check out the game yourself as any true Dead Rising fan would understand these few changes do not affect the gameplay at all.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster was a giant surprise this year developed by Capcom and NeoBard as a quite literal remaster/remake to one of my favorite games of all time. I believed that I missed when they were having the Capcom showcase this summer (for which I remember them announcing Resident Evil 7 for the phone??) but I certainly remember my feelings when I first heard about the remaster: cautiously optimistic. This is one of, if not my favorite, games of all time and as such when anyone says “Remaster” it could mean one of three things: absolute dumpster fire (aka Kingpin: Reloaded), bare minimum (most remasters out there) or could be absolute gold (like the Nightdive Remasters) and as such, I knew there was a ⅔ of a chance to which this could absolutely blow fat d i c k. My hopes for there being more for the Dead Rising franchise went limp under the absolute clusterf u c k of Dead Rising 4 (review for that below) and as such, I figured that playing Chop Till' You Drop on the Wii and 4 would be the last that I would play of Dead Rising for quite some time. Over the months I would see inside developer previews of the game but I didn’t really tune in much then but would still remain semi-optimistic, so much that I PRE-ORDERED the digital copy to play Day 1 (which I didn’t do anyways cause I got so busy so no more of that) and since the failure of Dead Rising 4 I don’t really pre-order games unless I go into it for collectible purposes (aka every Playstation Exclusive ever except Concord and certain others). This is also in spite of the many criticisms that I’ve heard/seen (and agreed on some) for the game like the lack of TJ Rotolo as Frank West, how goofy some of the character models look, and the removal of certain things (will get into later). Recently over the past month I’ve played it on and off as a sort of “chill out and vibe” game after I beat Batman: Arkham Origins and just in time for the Halloween season, I decided to beat this game and review it.(For the rest of the review, go here:  )The gameplay for the remaster remains largely the same, though with a few changes to certain mechanics as well. Starting with the actual camera (since Frank is a photographer), you can actually choose to turn on and off the flash or create dutch camera angles. Some of these upgrades of course you’ll have to find around the mall as an added little collectible, but I think that it’s pretty damn cool that they added that in. However, on the flip side, they removed the Erotica points system in photography too. What’s that? In the original game you can take photos of things and there will be an added category depending on what's in the pic (Funny is putting stupid helmets, Brutality for the really violent scenes, Erotica for the more perverted photos, etc). They removed Erotica entirely so anytime you take a pic of someone posing in a seductive manner (like Cheryl in one of her quests), it’s replaced with the Drama category. I personally don’t hate this but I don’t enjoy it; this I can understand that nowadays things are a lot different to things back twenty years ago, but I also wanted as much of the original in there as humanly possible. This also affects a side quest in the sense that Kent, a psychotic photographer, wanted you to show him your best Erotic picture in the original and it basically gave him a characterization as an unhinged freak. In the remaster, it feels a bit less unhinged but I also suppose it didn’t really affect it too much anyways considering he still tries to infect a guy later.The actual combat itself feels fine for the most part, it still feels the same and/or better due to several layout changes but admittedly I felt that it lost a bit of the “oomph” that the original Dead Rising had, at least at the beginning. In fact, a whole lot of the game feels a lot easier with the combat: the beginning boss with Carlito used to take a whole lot more in the original while in this version? A lot easier. Later on while the Special Forces invaded, I took down a helicopter with two assault rifle shots while it took a lot more in the original. Now I also had a skill book with me (for which they added a whole bunch of new ones) that increased firepower, but even in the original I didn’t feel like it did this. According to the TVTropes page, your fists do three times the damage from the original; like there are changes like this that make the game fundamentally way easier than the original ever did. Hell, about the only complaint I really have with the difficulty here is that the Small Chainsaw you get from Adam was nerfed a decent bit and it disappoints me. Links: (Dead Rising 1 review) (Dead Rising: Chop Til You Chop Review) (Dead Rising 4 review)       (Down below there’s a new Remaster section)

_childDocuments_.review: This remaster was one of the things I needed that I did not know I needed. Nostalgia overload, being that Dead Rising, the original was one of the very first games I was ever introduced to by my older brother. I can definitely say I fell in love with zombie games because of Dead Rising, and I am not at all opposed to the series by any of the later release, I really enjoyed them all but Dead Rising 1 and 2/OTR were definitely my favorites.Very satisfied with how it came out, I have no complaints, only experienced minor bugs with lighting at times and some 'wonky' survivor AI but it is much better and polished than the original game's survivor AI, so I wouldn't really even feel it appropriate to slam on the AI, because it is leagues better now. The most I experienced is just that sometimes the survivors would get caught up on each other and do this weird like stagger/stutter animations but they would quickly adjust and start moving normally. The military soldiers, also, seemed a little strong at first because they do a LOT of damage and can stun lock you if you are not careful, but with a proper strategy I figured out a way to take care of them, so that's not necessarily a problem, especially because they are intended to be one of the stronger groups of enemies (especially in pairs or groups.)Boss fights seemed a little too easy, but maybe it's just because I have experience and prior game knowledge of what items work well to make bosses easy, and that just adds to the authenticity of the game, because even in the remaster old strategies are still viable.The urbanization of the game, HUD, controls and everything was done perfectly, and is much better than the original in all ways possible.The graphics are great, very visually appealing and immersive.I do not have anything bad to say about this game, if you are a fan of zombie games or a long time Dead Rising fan like myself, please make sure you give this one a shot. I've own all of the Dead Rising games across console and PC and can definitely say if any of them are worth a shot, this one is it. I would like to finish off my review by saying that I believe they should use this same formula and take the time to remaster 2/OTR and make it a all-in-one sort of deal, even if it means it'll be $69.99, take my money. I would much rather they remaster the ones that did the series justice rather than possibly releasing a Dead Rising 5 and having another Dead Rising 4 situation on our hands, where some enjoy it but the vast majority do not, stick to the script guys, learn from the success of this game, and it's remaster and maybe then, it will be justifiable to come out with a 5th title. Dead Rising 3/4 obviously do not need a remaster as they are still somewhat up to date with technology and whatnot.Thank you very much to the development team of this remaster, you guys gave us Dead Rising fans a gift none of us were expecting but that all of us I am sure appreciate very deeply.I just finished the main story and overtime, but I will not be putting the game down any time soon, I have a new spare time hobby, slaughtering zombies as one of the most iconic zombie themed game's protagonist, FRANK WEST BABY!

_childDocuments_.review: Dont listen to the negative reviews. Yes this game has some flaws that in my opinion can be easily fixed but if you liked the original Dead Rising you will love this. _childDocuments_.review: I want to start off by saying I've NEVER played any other Dead Rising games in the franchise, this is my first entry. I've heard of it before, but it wasn't much of a buzz to me back then. For what it's worth, I'm a die-hard fan of Resident Evil - I've played all mainline games front and back. After playing the RE4 Remake, I found there was nothing else that was as enjoyable until this game dropped OUT OF NOWHERE. I can't say much about the discrepancies, I know people have their gripes with the changes Capcom has made to the game in comparison to the original - I don't really understand them, but I'd imagine it's how us Resident Evil fans felt when Capcom did what they did to Chris, or the many times they made changes for no reason at all.That out of the way, I now want to say that: never in my 2 decades of living and gaming have I sunk 54 hours into the game after JUST picking it up.This review isn't for the die-hard Dead Rising fan, but this is MOST DEFINITELY for the average Jane or Joe surfing steam for a nice game to pick up in today's unfathomably over saturated and under achieving market.Its for the "Aw man, why don't they don't make games like they used to" folks - this DOES it.I want to say that any resentment for the game from die-hard fans is probably valid - I plan to play the old ones too to see how they hold up, but SHOULDN'T rob people the insane experience this has given me so far.I'm SO proud that this is my entry to the franchise. Capcom did this game abundantly well, and I don't think I'll ever retract this statement. I always thought the zombie survival game genre was dead, I've never looked back until now. There is a STUPID AMOUNT OF FUN in this game, it's still UNBELIEVABLY replayable. I've never had this much fun since Left 4 Dead and Resident Evil.P.S: I know I'm the last to talk - seeing as I've never played the other ones. But I'm unbelievably happy with this version of Frank West, he's just awesome.P.S^2: I've seen the videos about the censorship. I understand people have their frustrations with it, but I want to clarify once and for all: THEY DON'T retract ANY enjoyment from the game - and you can 100% pick up on the references the original insinuates without any direct mention, so it's perfectly fine.

_childDocuments_.review: It's Dead Rising improved imo.  Somehow just as fun as it always was. I got it just to check out and I've already put in 9 hours and I'm having a blast. There isn't much original to say. I loved Dead Rising at launch and I revisit it every 5 years or so since then.  I just want to address some of the talking points about this release.1) Censorship - I understand being annoyed by censorship in a game, but the things they took out are negligible in my opinion. I don't care all that much about the photo mode to begin with. It's pretty boring and shallow.  So for me the removal of erotic photos does nothing.  I do think it's probably the most uncalled for removal though, considering its a comedic game from the perspective of a sleazy photo journalist.    The race change on the butcher feels unnecessary, but also doesn't make that big of a deal to me. I didn't find the original to be exceptionally racist or anything, especially considering all of the characters are kind of parody or caricatures to begin with, but I like the new aesthetic for the butcher so it's fine with me considering the original didn't blow my socks off or anything. He's kind of a throw away boss fight that never shined to begin with.  The stuff about Viet Cong being removed feels like a right move. Not because it's offensive, but because this is a remaster made for new players to some degree and the joke or parody just doesn't feel all that relevant anymore. I'd have even been okay with them changing the character to an Iraq vet considering this.  Honestly I think considering that's about all of the censorship there's not much to cry about.  It's still a pervy, gory, trashy horror show full of grotesque schizo obese villains, and hot skanky survivors(exaggerating to make a point. That point being the game could still be seen as offensive).  Graphics - Not much for me to complain about here. There are a few new character models like Carlito that look a little plastic to me, but overall it's an improvement and looks about as good as I'd expect a modern remaster of a game this old to look. Some people are divided on the textures, I really don't mind. Some things could be improved like the glass shattering effects, some questionable FPS drops in new environments(really doesn't impact gameplay for me), and reflections.  I'm liking the polish for the most part though.  It's very true to the original while being improved.Voice acting - Brad and Carlito aside I actually love all of the new voie actors. I don't like new Frank any more than the old one, but I also don't like him any less. I think he's great and still feels like the character I love.  Remaster or Remake - Definitely remaster, no doubt, the title says it, and by definition it's exactly that. Not sure how they implimented the old game engine, but it's clear some things were ported over.  As for whether it was necessary. I'm not sure. I'm happy to have great remaster, but I gladly would've taken a complete remake.  I loved all 3 of the recent Resident Evil Remakes and they all felt much more dramatic than this. Would've loved to see something on the same level as RE4.  Gameplay - Its improved where it needs to be and the same otherwise.  I feel like I'm playing the exact same game, but the survivor AI is better, the aiming is better with guns, and moving feels smoother.  They also added stairs to the entrance to the safehouse which was much needed. Really the AI improvement is game changing though. The survivors felt like a real burden in the original to the degree that I'd often just kill them, but now I'm actually changing my play style and trying to save as many as possible.  I've even found them handy in battle and I've brought back groups as large as 7 people. That's mostly all I have to say.  I hope to see a remake of this or Dead Rising 2 some day with totally modern game physics, controls, and mechanics, but I'm just as happy to see this happen.  I do think the price is steep. Had I not felt splurgy I would've waited and I have a hard time recommending this for $50 or even $40 to a friend, especially one with no nostalgia for the game.  The most I'd recommend it at is $30 and I really think $20-$25 is a fair asking price for a remaster today.  I'll be on the lookout for DR2. Hoping for even bigger visual and gameplay improvements for that one if it happens.  Thanks Capcom for making this a refreshing experience again in 2024. Just please stop robbing wallets. SF6 dlc still has me really sour.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster isn't perfect, but keeps the complete Dead Rising package by being a faithful remake of the original game. At first I was worried that the story would be changed, however no major story beats had been changed (Unless you're weird and count Larry being made white a major story change) to the point I'm genuinely shocked at how well the story has aged well over these years.Gameplay wise, the game's a bit buggy. Zombies can spawn in walls, pillars, and sometimes even on top of nothing. However, a huge part of what makes these games fun is the jank that follows. The Zombies are an obstacle you have to cut, shoot, or even smash through to get from point A to B. Them getting stuck? Consider that one less obstacle. I did find myself getting grabbed almost way to easily however, even if I was on a skateboard a zombie would grab me the first frame it could. However, that could just be a skill issue.Graphical wise, and I never really complain about this as I find it not much of a matter as artstyle is a subjective and personal issue, but I don't think I needed to see every pore on Frank's face. Or anyone else's faces to that matter. There was a graphical glitch that gave pseudo-cel shading style that I thought was somewhat intentional that actually added a good bit to the textures. The lighting having the darkest color at a majority of the time being a blueish hue really helped me alot, as I personally struggle with seeing in the dark in video games, and is something I wish more games would do. I will say, the classic Frank and Chuck Greene costume being the original models was a funny thing to note. These low-poly low-resolution textured models in such a Hi-definition game genuinely made me laugh.Overall, I'd have to give this game an 8/9. My favorite highlight was how well the controls felt on a controller, as well as how expressive and animated the Psychopaths are.

_childDocuments_.review: Almost a perfect game to me. I would still consider this game pretty much a 10/10 or even a 9.5/10 since it is the same amount of quality as the Resident Evil 4 Remake.I completed the game and got 42/50 achievements on my first playthrough in 12 hours, and played one more for the 6 remaining achievements and one more for infinity mode. My Snuff Shot J achievement was glitched out and I had to get it on my second playthrough.Literally everything about this game is exactly the same as the original masterpiece 2006/2016 rerelease except...- Achievements are for the most part the same except it removed some for easier ones, or just changed the conditions for some of them like Transmissionary being much easier now.- Little censorship such as dialogue for Cliff Hudson (The Hatchet Man) and the Chinese Butcher psychopath. Along with that censorship was the removal of Erotica completely as a photo genre.- Yellow spray paint for like one section in the food court for one of the easiest bosses in the game- Some additional dialogue and cutscenes, and even secret dialogue that was not in the original game- Better Survivor/Follower AI, Harder Special Forces AI, Harder Psychopath AI (Kent the Photographer is way harder now)- Harder to grind or collect kills in the Maintenance Tunnel for the 53,594 because zombies do not spawn fast or consistently throughout the tunnel and you need to let them load in or there will only be a few of them- Food Court no longer crashes your game on Infinity Mode and you can now get food and weapon drops from zombies. Plus you can save the game (which I should have done on my first playthrough where it crashed on Day 7 right before getting the achievement)I do like aesthetics of the OG release and some gameplay mechanics and AI just because it made the game much harder, but the remaster was pretty much the same thing and more polished, and I would still replay this game many more times.Despite all that, I would still strongly recommend this version to play, even if I do like the original so much.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm not sure what's happening with remasters lately. First of all, I understand this game is running on a brand new engine so it can't be the exact same experience as the original. However, something about this remaster feels clunky. I have no problem getting the game to run at whatever frame cap I set with graphics at max. The game looks great, but something is definitely off with the in game audio. I am personally not a fan of the new Frank voice, but that's a matter of personal preference. Leveling up through PP bonuses is completely broken. It's far too easy to become OP early on in the game just by taking pictures, whether that is intentional or not. I hope that gets patched as it makes the game much easier than it should be. This game as a whole seems more forgiving than it originally was. At least the option for the classic controls is still there. One annoying and consistent bug I encountered was in changing clothes at a store. After the initial switch I was not able to switch back or change to a different item in the store. Instead the game would just swap between a return and change prompt. I should mention this was after using the OG Frank DLC skin which would unfortunately also swap the model to new Frank. There also seems to be less places to change clothes than in the original game. I'm not sure if the visual facelift and censorship has given this now 18 year old game new life especially since the original is still for sale on here and ripe with a community of modders. Still I'm glad to see the series is getting the right kind of attention again from Capcom after DR4 and an abandoned DR5 seemed to kill the series. If you haven't played the series before, this modernized deluxe remaster is a great place to start, but wait for a sale and for the bugs to be ironed out. If you're playing this as a fan of the original game like myself, you may be disappointed.

_childDocuments_.review: I've bought this game day-one, completed this game to 100%, gotten every unlockable, and done every achievement. Here's my honest thoughts about the game. If you're expecting the level of difficulty that the 2006 version had, don't. You're not going to get it. This game is easier than the original, there's no way of sugarcoating it - but it's still a fun experience by itself. The remaster adds quality-of-life changes that make your playthrough easier to just pick up and play, while at the same time giving you utilities that you wouldn't have normally. If you want a higher difficulty, play the 2006 version - it's worth your time.For example, you can now fast-forward time to wait for certain scoops or survivors. You get a view of Frank's watch as you do, and this significantly cuts down the amount of time spent in one playthrough of the game, therefore making it much less time-consuming. You can get the entire game done by cutting it into three complete playthroughs, and it's worth it to do all three. They're all pretty fun experiences, since Capcom finally fixed the Survivor AI.More on the technical side of things, you can customize the graphics to fit your performance or if you want the game to look prettier - this is a given, but it's a godsend for certain areas of the game that will lag out of nowhere. Is this remaster worth buying? Yeah. If you like Dead Rising but don't want it to be as difficult as the 2006 version for whatever reason, with some quality-of-life changes and additional items, go for it.

_childDocuments_.review: Awesome "Remake/Remaster", There's tons here to love if you're a Dead Rising fan, I'm a huge fan of the original and not really concerned about being a purist, but there's a couple of things that need addressed before I would consider this the definitive version.The Good:- Everyone is voice acted, Escorts now point out points of interest and use common sense navigating the horde, Franks new VO is actually really good, he gives off that sleazy, selfish reporter that the dialog in the original had you believe, but the performance didn't quite match it. I am glad to see that all the little tricks, cheesing and methods have not changed. It has a better graphical quality, few bits have changed for the better. The survivors are now no longer dribbling morons and will also give you info along the way. Added an auto save at certain points which the OG never had and people hated. This game stands the test if time well and so many funny things to do, things to see.

_childDocuments_.review: + Insanely gorgeous remaster and improved AI. + Also has improved zombie features like police zombies being able to randomly fire their gun.- Voice acting is really hit or miss. The lines are delivered poorly and the charcters seem soulless. Compare OG Brad VA to new Brad VA. - Combat is still the same but certain elements are missing. It's missing the heavy feel of pushing multiple zombies off you and certain items miss the weighty feeling when using it.- Preformance stutters sometimes.- SIGNIFICANTLY LESS ZOMBIES ON SCREEN THAN BEFORE?????Personal niche: I really don't enjoy that npcs have dialogue and enjoyed reading the text more. _childDocuments_.review: and now we watch as every single recent review copy and paste the same opinion after watching a crowbcat video!it's a good remake, I don't agree on the price and the lack of any meaningful new content to accommodate it, but I'm glad that I played it. the difficulty is relatively toned down - I think changes to the dodge roll system, new aiming mechanics and the fact that you can still jump spam through every swarm may have made the game noticeably easier, along with how much your PP is boosted/how fast you level up. the new voice acting is very hit or miss, but there are mods to help correct that if need be. the original game is also available on steam if that's the experience you're looking for.as a result, replayability is down overall for this one, but endless mode has always been a big draw after clearing it anyway.all in all, an enjoyable remake and a fun time, but with some predictable issues that aren't unique to capcom's streak of RE remakes. wait til it goes on sale, and please form your own opinion that isn't completely coloured by someone else.

_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original 2006 game on my Xbox 360 about 10 years ago. Ever since then, I have been obsessed with the game. I could even say it's my favorite game. This remaster feels like I am playing the game for the first time again, but at its full potential. Every second of the game is fun and never feels like a chore. The new quality-of-life improvements only further add to the game's pros. The only cons I have are the occasional minor glitches. But I highly recommend this game to any old fans or people who like zombie games.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: As a long time Dead Rising fan: This is as close to how (and why) remakes should be done, with some quirks.First off, if you've never played Dead Rising I 100% recommend this as the starting point now. You can always check out the original after the fact (as of writing it's still available)Pros:RE Engine made this game look PRETTY. Everything looks great hear, the posters, the zombies, the mall, almost all of the character models (looking at you Frank). The lighting is spectacular.Survivor AI has been upgrade ALMOST too much. I don't need to spam the call button every step I take toward the security room and the addition of stairs leading up to the vent is *chef's kiss*They kept the core of the game play intact, but polished with modern tools not available in 2006 and they've provided the option for classic controls and modern controls. I haven't bothered switching to the OG controls because the modern controls are so smooth.One of the most impressive parts of the OG is the sound design and this is a glow up I didn't even know I needed. Cons:There have been a few moments of me skipping dialogue and getting ahead of myself and ruining a survivor prompt. I can't tell if this is a bug that could be triggered in the OG, but it's a bit frustrating.Frank has been aged up visually but nothing in the narrative indicates that this is not supposed to be the same nearly 30 year old man. He now looks just shy of 50. He literally looks closer to his OG Dead Rising model in DR4. Fortunately the OG cosmetic is available. So far every other model has been upgraded very well.This isn't necessarily a con, but it feels like XP gain is cranked to 1000x. In the OG it took a good handful of playthroughs to max out your level. In this it only takes barely 2 playthroughs. While great for increasing the pacing as the story and quests get more busy, it does feel like it makes the game TOO easy in some regards. Regardless the cons that I have are negligible and honestly subjective. I would love not only DR2 remastered in the same fashion but a Resident Evil Outbreak style game would also be great fun. Definitely worth the pick up.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: You cannot get the original look for Frank West from 2006 unless you pre-ordered the game, there is no way to purchase it right now, and that is super frustrating.  What is even worse is you can see those 3 pre-order only outfits in-game but it does not let you buy them right now, as of September 2024.I had no clue there was a pre-order bonus for the game because I hate the default look of Frank in this remaster, he looks horrible.  They also did not get TJ for the voice and that bothers me the most.  I would have preferred if they had just left the voices from the original game because I would bet they'd sound better even if it was of lower audio quality.  This feels like babies first Dead Rising, it looks fine for people who want updated graphics but the textures and characters look horribly ugly.  The RE Engine didn't fit this game at all.The only good thing I can say about the art style or graphics is the environments.Also the game is super unstable.  With a 3070 Ti Ftw3 Ultra, 16 Gb's of RAM, 5800X CPU, Asus Prime x470 Pro motherboard the game crashes constantly and has bad framerate.The game runs but as soon as I change the Screen Resolution from the 1080p it defaulted to 1440p native resolution, the game constantly crashes, over and over and over.  It may have been because my dualsense controller was plugging in via usb-c because when I unplugged it the game stopped carshing.Capcom, fix your f**king games, Jesus Christ you guys make horrid PC ports every time.  They're always missing features or ultrawide or fov sliders, they are never feature complete.The game is working for me for now but it was crashing a lot when I first started it up.  This version has a lot of QoL features but the characters look so terrible compared to the original, the voice acting is bleh, and the game runs bad.  If I could keep the originals graphics and audio, and just get the QoL features and better textures/resolution, it would have been a perfect remaster.  But instead they basically remade the game, but call it a 'remaster', with no way to go back to the original look and sound.  That bothers me and its overpriced.I want to say that all of the digital deluxe outfits look terrible too, there is not a single one that I want to use because none look good or cool.  The one that I like (the 2006 version of Frank West, which if it included the original voice actor TJ would have been amazing) is pre-order only.  I wish I could refund this but I made the mistake of purchasing the digital deluxe on Humble Bundle because it had 15-20% off the digital deluxe, but no refunds.OH!  And there's Denuvo!  That is probably what is causing the terrible stuttering and performance drops but Capcom doesn't care.  The only good thing Capcom has done lately is release the Marvel Vs Capcom 2 Collection but I am sure that wasn't all Capcom.  Just a few passionate people in their company.Edit to address people:Folks always bring up hours played and achievements like it matters to them.I have 100% completed Dead Rising OG at least 3 times on the original Xbox 360 when the game first came out, using a 360 VGA converter cable to a CRT monitor, I am old.  I remember doing the week long survivor achievement like 3 times in a row because my console kept getting that bug that would freeze your game at the 15th and final hour of playing.  I know this game a little TOO well.  Dead Rising 1 is one of my favorite games of all time, and ironically I never finished Dead Rising 2, 3, or 4.  I don't think they did this "remaster" justice for such a fantastic game.  It feels lazy, like they just used a modern engine and ported the game over, not bothering to give the game the spirit it once had with a good look or voice acting or anything else.You know how I know that?  They went the cheap route and didn't include TJ Rotolo due to Union BS because it would cost them too much money, instead of making the fans happy and being genuine, they did what they could to make a quick buck.  Sometimes Capcom does well like with the Marvel Vs Capcom Collection, but most of the time they are lazy and once they release a game on PC, they almost never go back and fix the port or correct problems.  RE7 sat around for years without the promised VR mode on PC, no Ultrawide support.. but had an FOV slider.  Almost out of spite in Resident Evil 8 Village they added Ultrawide support, but had no FOV slider or way to remove Vignetting, making UW almost unusable without third party fan made programs to fix it.  Capcom is inept sometimes.  I didn't have high hopes for this remaster and they proved they just don't care so long as they make money.I think their inclusion of Denuvo just proves they do not give a F about you.  I could almost guarantee the performance problems and stuttering I am experiencing is due to Denuvo.

_childDocuments_.review: They thought the original was too difficult for the current audience and removed any way for you to find stuff out on your own.- You have exit arrows EVERYWHERE, so there's no need for you to figure out where to go.- There's a minimap on the top of your screen that literally tells you where to go.- The Carlito fight has big bright yellow arrows directing you where to go in order to fight him correctly with the text "THIS WAY" like they think the people playing are braindead which is also immersion breaking because why else would they be there?- The leveling system has been reworked for you to not have to struggle for long so you level super quickly.- You no longer have to figure out what interesting things you can take picture of that may have PP stickers, you could not miss them now if you tried because theres a big yellow circle begging you to take a picture of it.- The bosses are now super easy to kill, a few shotgun blasts and it's over, not like the original at all.If you want a game that insults your intelligence and holds your hand like you are aren't capable of playing the game the way it was originally intended then play this game, otherwise play the original.

_childDocuments_.review: Very good remake, it fixed alot of the issues present in the original like the AI having terrible path finding, for the most part anyways, you can speed up the time insteadof waiting with nothing to do until some side stuff pops up, modern controls which are well made for keyboard and mouse users like myself more visual fidelity with modern effects to make an old game feel aesthetically refreshing.It's not all sunshine and rainbows as the game has a few things that I dont like or find it to be a downgrade over the original.The voice acting though not bad I think it's inferior to the original I wish there was an option to switch between old voice actors and the new ones, please both crowds ya know? Performance is weird, this is before any patch but the game made me restart my computer 2 times because the game once blacked my whole screen and the other time was the opposite it was full on white and I could not get it to normal unless I rebooted my pc, I dont have a beast gaming rig but I played on the medium settings with consistent 60fps so I dont know why the game would crap out my graphics/display like thatAlso in some weird instances where it had no zombies the frame rate would drop to single digits but it happened only once or twice. Overall good remake but it has a few performance glitches which Im sure will be ironed out once the updates roll out.

_childDocuments_.review: Sadly Capcom is continuing the streak of releasing unoptimized games. Should have been more careful after DD2's disastrous state, but unlike that game(which only just recently received an actual performance patch, and even then it seems inconclusive in terms of its gains) I'm not going to give them the benefit of the doubt or time to fix. Ship a broken product and i'll just refund. What an absolute shame.Fwiw; The game was pretty much a prettier(in some ways, some textures just didn't seem like they were made for the same game and stood out) version of the original. Some controversy in some of the removed/changes features with certain psychos or the erotic photos not being a thing, but didn't bother me at all personally and most people are likely just overstating their importance because of political climates. It was stupid easy for the 2.5h I played, that outside of the performance issues would've been my only gripe or complaint.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This ain't it chief.The game as a whole is just not great, the OG is by miles better.Visually it's kind of a cluster♥♥♥♥, with great lighting and reflections, updated to look like what you would expect from current tech, but other details are poor. Shadows and effects such as smoke and fire look extremely bad with low draw distance, textures are mostly blurry or low res except the floors and the zombies themselves which do look great, but things like clothing and objects barely seem touched. What this does is give the game an uncanny feel as you have realistic lighting and reflections along the terrible effects and textures. Every graphical option is set to the max available mind you, so unless I have something bugged within the game I just don't see why would I choose this over the OG, at least the OG was visually consistent according to its limitations.Animations are not great either, I know the OG and even DR 2 and 3 were clunky and stiff, however, here most attacks send the zombies flying in a weird angle, even if you punch them. As I recall and noticed from playing DR 2 this past week, even that game had varied and somewhat more grounded animations, funny, yes but then again not uncanny as they are in this remaster. Hell even when you jump Frank floats for a good 2-3 seconds in the air for no reason.What frustrates me the most is that Capcom had been putting out great remakes with Resident Evil, I can't fault any of them, but this one feels cheap, like no time or detailing was put into it. It rubs me the wrong way as if most of the work was done by AI, and looking at the inconsistencies it might very well have been an AI putting this remaster together. This is nowhere near the quality of the recent RE remakes. Even more baffling is why there was time to remove parts of the original game and change characters for people who won't even buy your game, but there wasn't to polish the textures, the animations, you know, ♥♥♥♥ that we are going to look at for the entirety of it?If this is the kind of effort Capcom is going to put from now on, don't even bother remaking or remastering anything else, let the other franchises rest in peace.Edit: While continuing to endure it, I noticed a few more things worth mentioning. While using 1440p resolution, I upped the texture resolution slider in the game options to 200%, textures look slightly better but still blurry enough to be unacceptable, for instance the first time you get out of the vents, the vent door texture still looks like ♥♥♥♥.The depth of field effect is also terrible, instead of providing a proper sense of depth, it just blurries everything that is about 4 to 5 steps away from you, if I wanted to feel like my sight is going bad, I would just stop wearing glasses instead.Zombies cast shadows only when they feel like it. Some do cast, some others don't cast a shadow regardless of how far or close to them I am, some others only cast a shadow of their head, so the shadow looks like there is just a head floating around. Overall my only feeling about the game right now is disappointment.

_childDocuments_.review: I love Deadrising 1, and I feel this is a competent remaster. Despite the new and sometimes pitiful voice acting, and Frank looking like what an Alien assumes a human male looks like, the QOL changes are so noticeable and increase the accessibility and fun of the game quite a bit. I see a lot of people praising the new survivor AI, and if I'm being honest, I barely noticed, I think the issues with the original games survivor AI are greatly overstated. The game still maintains a lot of the charm, and I cannot deny the gameplay is polished beautifully. Gone Guru is still playing in the courtyard so I would've given it a 10/10 no matter what.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is gonna sound pretty trite, but yes, this is fun, because the original Dead Rising is a masterpeice of a zombie game, and this is an *almost* faithful recreation of that, 1-to-1 with some of the best lighting I've seen in a remaster, hell, even any game, for a seriously long time.I'm not political, and I don't care about the censorship as much as other people, do I think the removals are stupid?, yes, the commie voicelines are harmless, and add to the pshycopath's story, and the erotica genre being removed from photography is even moreso, considering they kept the sidequest where you take erotic pictures of a woman anyway, and they kept the achivement centered around having 8 women in your party.Other than that, It's a great remaster, I give it a 7/10 I would give it an 8 if they didn't overtune the damage the Special Forces did, and the amount the stunlock you, if this happens to be a bug, and they change it, I'll edit the review.Should you buy it?, for 60$?, probably not, unless you're desperate for the QoL changes, and absolutely despise older graphics, the old game holds up incredibly well, with a well-preforming pc port available for a quarter of the price on steam already. If it's on sale though?, it's most definitely worth buying if you love the game and wanna see Willamete rendered beautifully.

_childDocuments_.review: The original Dead Rising is my favorite game, so I had some pretty high expectations for this remaster. I want to start off saying the graphics are amazing, their was some obvious care put into the way the game looked. With added set pieces to make the mall look more alive, to retroactively adding cut content back into the game like the rocket launcher and the police zombies shooting their guns. Being able to skip time is a god send for infinity mode and something I never realized I needed until I had it. They kept the original animations for the zombies and survivors so the charm of the original is still there. I noticed a few issues with zombies glitching into the walls when I went into the maintenance tunnel to get the 53 thousand kills but other than that the game was visually stunning. There's some obvious issues with lag and crashes but i'm not sure if that's an issue on my end or the games. They did take out the erotica photo category, but if i'm being honest it was kinda weird and I'm not missing it. I do miss cliff mentioning Vietnam, but it was still clear to me he was a veteran. Larry definitely needed a remodel, I can see how some people would be upset at the change with wanting the game to be as pure to the original as possible, but og Larry was a walking stereotype. Obviously I miss the original voice actor for Frank but I didn't feel like anyone of the new actors did a bad job, some did worse, some did better, it's just how it goes. I'd recommend this game to anyone looking for a fun zombie sandbox with a compelling story that doesn't take it self too seriously.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: A very well crafted remake/remaster of the original classic, Dead Rising. I'm very pleasantly surprised I have (mostly) good things to say. I do feel the game is easier, but it's not boring it's more convenient than anything. The censorship does exist, but it's honestly very bizarre as there's only a handful of dialog changes but some other "risque" content is left fully intact. I would love to see a patch to remove the censorship but I highly doubt it, but it's also so minimal that it barely matters. It's inconsistent but it should not affect your decision to purchase as it really amounts to nothing.I loved having everything be exactly where it was, it kept a lot of the soul in tact for me and the ability to speed up time has increased the replay-ability in one of the most re-playable games ever, that I am going to have a hard time going back to the original. Totally recommend, I loved it, best Capcom remake since RE2.

_childDocuments_.review: 💗Amazing. An Enhanced Dead Rising Experience. That’s how I would describe this Remastered edition. Feels like it’s between a Remastered and a Remake of the game. I’m a long time DR fan so it won’t be a first impression but a review, there’s also one little thing I didn’t like that I’m gonna mention later :) I’ve been playing the original Dead Rising till these days, since its debut in 2006. I was younger, 18 years have passed, and as a long time DR fan who played them all, I never stopped playing DR1 from time to time. On xbox360, ps4, and steam. Got platinum as well. When I first heard about this remastered, I wasn’t too fond of. I thought it was just a graphics remaster and didn’t feel the urge to get it. Also the little “censors” they had to make didn’t make me excited to get it as well. I gave it a try anyway, got it and beat it in 13 hours. It really got to my heart!❤️ It’s not just the graphics, but they made the characters more human, added dialogues, refined the story, dubbed everything (for non-english speakers like me 🇮🇹,  but also added extra dubbing to all the characters unlike the original), and put a bow on it by adding more contents and MAKING THE AI work 😍🙈Yes, everyone, the AI finally works well. I managed to do 50 survivors on my first run starting from level 1. The AI was one of the biggest difficulties in DR1, which made the game very challenging. It never bother me tho cause it’s one of its peculiarities as Dead Rising is much of a strategy game when dealing with missions & time. The graphics are really beautiful, feels finally like a current gen game, the characters new design is well made, they look so real with their mannerism and facial expressions, also the dialogues feel more real & like they’re actually expressing their emotions. Madonna back in 2006 was a puppet 😆 The gameplay is better, the AI is better, the automatic saves are a Life saver! Now you get to track when your weapons are damaged in the bar, survivors get to talk to you and they give tips and react. There are plenty of enhancements packed with a beautiful graphic, new musics and the usual story that we all love, redefined to the best. Obviously don’t expect AAA graphics, it’s re engine but it’s still a bit rudimentary, this game is not intended to be an AAA. Everything is current to today’s graphic definitions and well polished. They made a good complete job 👏🏻 To the thing I didn’t like, most know that they had to change one character and the backstory of another character as well. Didn’t get why they removed the hot (se*y) photo genre? Didn’t get that choice but it’s a small little thing. I may understand the other two changes. Pay attention to the military cause they’re too difficult now. Game is a little buggy but can be optimized, never crashed for me. The original is still gold, but playing this one makes the experience more enjoyable and complete. DR1 will remain the good a little harder old school.Hooray for DEAD RISING ❤️ Waiting for more! ❤️

_childDocuments_.review: I gotta admit this is an absolute GODSEND of a remaster. I have played the original Dead Rising, and this version delivers not only the classic story I absolutely love but improves upon the original gameplay by so much. The ability to side strafe while aiming doesn't sound like a big deal until you weave out of the way of a big ol Hummer. The camera got a huge buff, making taking pictures actually viable for level-ups. They also introduced camera add-ons allowing you to upgrade the camera giving you more camera.... who doesn't love more camera. The graphical improvements are obvious, don't need to talk about that. I don't understand why people are complaining about CAPCOM removing stuff like erotica and the big Asian guy. I felt like they weren't needed to begin with, so it never felt like anything was lost.Bottom line this game feels like it was made by actual Dead Rising fans. The amount of viable effort put into this remaster is astonishing and should not be over looked.I'm giving this a Smokin' Sexy Style!! out of Smokin' Sexy Style!!... definitely not cause Dante is holding a gun to my head.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom finally did it they made a good remake, took 'em four tries but they go there in the end.Inside memes aside its fine, I like it but I'm a big fan or Dead Rising especially the first one, few things feel and look wonky and I'm pretty sure the convicts are bugged in my current run few audio issues as well, unlike the Dead Space remake I wouldn't say theres no need to play the original this is a good way of playing it but the 2006 (or 2016 one for pc) is still worth it.7.5-8/10
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: The game can feel a bit rough around the edges, and a bit ''undercooked'' in some areas, but I feel like it's mostly part to  using the RE engine with a 2006 video game design - but I think it's nothing some patches could fix.It still got that original Dead Rising charm, and although it is a shame the game is not completely 1:1, this game also has some surprises in store for players who are familiar with the original.I don't think the changes from  the original are that much of a big deal, even though I would have preferred that all elements of the original were still there like the erotica  category, it doesn't take away from  the fun of the game, or the message it provides. And again, they added some neat new details that make up  for it - meaning this game doesn't substitute the original, but offers  a fresh new experience alongside a familiar story and setting for those that were waiting for another title in this amazing franchise.At the end of the day, it's more Dead Rising, you should support it!P..S: I am suffering from some random crashes  whenever I transition to a new area, and one of those crashes just ended my 5 days infinity mode  run towards the 7 days. I hope these crashes are fixed soon.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: This is a good remaster don't get me wrong but it's too easy. I don't know if it's the fact I've had numerous playthroughs on 3 consoles and PC but this feels like those players who want an easy mode on souls game. I can blow through this game with no issue survivors being fixed. It was a good edition but leveling up is a joke being almost lvl 35 half way through the game was shocking to me. Call me selfish but being tested was part of the OG's design and progression it wasn't supposed to be easy just like old RE but they have made this game to be streamer friendly making it easy and nothing that's too risky which causes fans like me to be left in the dust and not able to show players a real survivor experience. _childDocuments_.review: If you've never played the original version, I'd recommend playing this one.  It has several quality of life changes that make gameplay, and several achievements, more player-friendly.  The graphics aren't the best, but they are significantly improved over the original.  It's also fully voiced, unlike the original.  It also stays true to the original in many regards that matter, mostly improving on what was already provided by the original.  The original, despite its flaws, was great- and this version is even better.  That being said, if you have played the original before, I'd recommend waiting for this version to go on sale before buying.  While it is greatly improved over the original, I don't necessarily think it is worth the ridiculous price of $49.99-$59.99 (depending on the edition you choose) to players who've likely already been exposed to the same story and gameplay before several times in the original.I do have some criticisms, though:1) Gore is limited to just the zombies.  In the Wii version (Dead Rising: Chop 'Til You Drop), you could dismember human enemies.  Sadly, this was not included in this remaster.2) Survivor AI, while being improved, is still incredibly awful.3) It didn't personally bother me, but there is a bit of censorship.  Outfits on some female survivors have been adjusted to be less suggestive, the erotica category for pictures has been removed, the Butcher had a race change from being Asian to Caucasian, Cliff's dialogue has been changed slightly (he refers to frank as a mole instead of a communist, for example), etc.  Like I said, it didn't bother me all that much, but I am throwing it out there anyway because it has stirred up the community a bit.4) The special forces will still stun-lock you, which can be really annoying (especially when going for the 5 day/7 day survivor achievements).  It's not even so much a challenge as it is just annoying.I'm sure there are other things to critique, but those are the only things that really stood out to me at the time of this review.  TL;DR: Overall, great remaster.  I'd definitely recommend it if you haven't played the original, though I might suggest waiting for a sale if you have played the original.

Lots of additions to the game give you too many hints. You level up way faster, removing a lot of the challenge. Any management you had to do in the original game to survive is pretty much gone or just made pointless. Moving place to place is now way faster so you never feel like you're tight on time, removing more tension. Zombies, which are the most common enemy in the game, are less aggressive and way less of an obstacle, making the main threat not threatening at all. The path finding for the NPCs is at times just as bad as they were in the 2006 version. Often times escorted survivors and enemies get stuck on props easily. The auto saves make manual saves in save areas redundant and also makes it easy to undo any punishment the game had, like getting captured. The only thing this game really has to boast is its new graphics and even that is unpolished. Anyone with dark hair now looks like they have gray hair because of how weird the lighting reflects off it. This game feels cheaply produced and it's pretty obvious seeing how it's outsourced to a Chinese developer and how this game was not even marketed that much. I would say, just play the 2006 version that's still available on Steam.

_childDocuments_.review: Not bad! The Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is a solid Remaster/Remake of the original Dead Rising that was released back in 2006. It offers a host of QoL changes that make the overall experience more enjoyable while also simplifying some elements of the original to help ease more casual gamers into the series. However, it doesn't come without its issues.The original Dead Rising isn't a tough game but it required you to have a sense of time management and patience when it came to completing cases and escorting survivors. DRDR felt like it was a lot more lenient when it came to giving me time to complete cases, psychopaths, and survivor missions. Even leveling up in this was a breeze in comparison to the original. Before even reaching the first Carlito fight I was already level 10. By the end of my first playthrough, I was level 48 and had managed to save about 42 survivors without a guide. The Deluxe Remaster includes a few new books that help dumb down the difficulty of the original. Early on you can find a book that increases firearm damage and one that increases survivor's health along with a book that gives you access to late-game skill moves. While you're not required to pick them up, they do help simplify the experience. Survivor locations, clothing locations, pp stickers, and case times are all the same and remain unaltered from the original. Doing my clean-up runs of the game for the rest of the achievements was nice given all of the old guides for the original game still apply to the Deluxe Remaster. I won't delve into the censorship changes but, the changes made were silly and unnecessary. The Cliff psychopath being changed from a Vietnam veteran to a "random war" veteran is the biggest change that I didn't like given he's one of my favorite psychopaths in the series. The removal of erotica is even sillier when you get to the end and realize they kept in a side mission that requires you to take "erotic" shots of one of the female survivors posing for you.The models in this game look phenomenal... aside from Frank. I don't like the older appearance of Frank in this game. The receding hairline this early on in this series and the amount of wrinkles he has makes him look drastically older than he should. I don't think he should be some young pretty boy but, he definitely should look a lot younger when it comes to the Willamette zombie outbreak. Characters like Isabela, Jessie, Brad, Carlito, and all the psychopaths (especially Adam the Clown) look like they were ripped straight from pre-game renders and concept art from the original game. Voices, for the most part, are serviceable. The inclusion of having all dialogue outside of cutscenes fully voiced is one of my favorite additions to the game and helps you get a bit more immersed. Frank and Brad were the only voices that kinda bugged me and a few psychopaths. Frank's new voice, wasn't my favorite at first, by the end, he'd grown on me but still was by no means Frank West to me. Something about his inflections doesn't hit the same for me. He came across as just a generic reporter man. TJ Rotolo's delivery had a gritty, seasoned reporter feel, which fit Frank’s background perfectly. Rotolo’s voice had a slightly cynical edge that matched the character’s sarcastic sense of humor, giving Frank West a unique charm. Frank West, in TJ's performance, had a distinct, iconic voice that contributed to his memorability, something that was lost with the recasting in the remaster. As for the rest, Isabela, Jessie, and Carlito don't sound all that different from the original. If you didn't tell me they recast Adam The Clown in DRDR, I would have fully believed it was still John Kassir the Crypt Keeper, the new VA was spot on. Overall, visuals look great while voice acting could have been better.Infinity Mode this time around was A LOT more enjoyable. I attempted the original "7-Day Survivor" achievement once, stayed up an entire night, got to day 6 and my game crashed. I've never tried it again until this Deluxe Remaster came out. With the ability to fast forward time, have survivors and psychopaths marked on your map to easily find food, and the inclusion of a few books that increase how much health you can receive from eating, this was a surprisingly fun achievement and didn't suck up 14 hours of my life! Infinity Mode was fun for the 4ish or 5ish hours it took me to complete and the addition of being able to save mid-mode made it a lot more managable. If you're an achievement hunter, all of the achievements were fun. If you're looking to get all 50 achievements, go for it!There isn't really much to be said about the Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster that I find notable in mentioning. Sure the QoL changes are nice, the added voice lines, and the simplified achievements that don't suck up hours of your life, are all nice but it feels like a lot more was sacrificed to achieve said changes. A lot of the charm of the original is still there while at the same time, it felt like something was missing still. The Deluxe Remaster is an 8/10. Dead Rising wasn't a game I thought needed a remake/remaster as much as other Capcom classics. The original Dead Rising in my opinion still holds up well, but, even after all is said and done, this will now probably be the one I revisit when wanting to play the first game given the graphical and gameplay QoL changes made. Capcom, if you're reading my review, I just want ya'll to know that whoever is modeling your female characters. Please, give them a raise. Isabela is absolutely stunning in this game. I mean I kid you not I had steam blowing out of my ears, my tongue unrolled like a carpet onto the floor, my mouth was agape, my eyes bulged out of my skull, and I went "AWOOGA AWOOGA  AWOOGA" every time she was on screen. No cap, give them a raise. God Bless them.

_childDocuments_.review: 27 hours for 100% completion over 3 72 Hr Mode Playthroughs (1 for full completion, 1 for Zombie Annihilator, and 1 for Grateful Eight and Misc Achievos), 1 Overtime Mode, and 1 Infinite Mode Playthrough. Not having as much nostalgia for the original since I played the original not too long before this came out, but this is all in comparison to the original.ConsZombies grab way too oftenSpec Ops Soldiers lost all their stun lockable-ness in the original and in fact made it extremely easy for you to get forever stunned by them which makes them a pain to fightRIP my boi Mini ChainsawsContinuing the trend of every new Frank design being worse than the last, but everyone else's redesign is fineVoice Acting on the other hand is SIGNIFICANTLY WORSE. Jessie Isabella and Carlito's VA's were pretty good, but Frank and Brad's were BAAAAAD. New survivor voices are mostly fine and psycho's are good as well, but WHERE DID STEVE BLUM GO.Makes some dumb dialogue changes (Hatchet Man no longer Vietnam Vet, Kent asking for a funny shot but the game still has all the weird shots in the story)And that's about it. Game is alot easier than the original which can be seen as a con but this is a really solid spot for new players to jump in and give the series a go since the difficulty is still a bit higher than DR2 onward, but the difficulty chasm is way smaller.ProsDurability meter on all your items VERY NICERE Engine really does alot of work here and makes the game look really really good while running great most of the timeSurvivor AI is WAYYYYYY better, making that Saint run relatively easy to do on a first runthroughMannequin Torso continues to be my beloved and feels even stronger than it did in the originalFast forward time option keeps 7 Day Survivor's difficulty without all the waiting in a safe spot and eating the food you've stockpiledOverall doesn't fully supersede the original, but if you're looking for a decent entry into the series with a lot of nice modern QoL changes it's worth the money.
