_childDocuments_.review: So here is what I have to say about this game, Buckle up because this is a long one.I've played all the way through Dead Rising 1 again recently before the release of the Deluxe Remaster and had an amazing time revisiting it, it's one of my all time favorite games ever and I'm super happy with it still to this day, Obvious gripes people have with it are the time limit and the survivor A.I. which by ♥♥♥♥ was it not always great in the original. However this remaster is pretty much exactly as I was expecting it to be and to put it short, I believe it is worth it if you are a Dead Rising fan, if you are just curious, I'd wait for a future sale.I had no issues with the voice acting at all, I think everyone does a passable job as the character they play as, Except for Cliff, I'm not impressed there especially replacing the "Vietcong" line with "It's because you're a mole" who the hell out there was offended that he said "Vietcong"? Other than that I was happy with it overall. I've crashed 3 times, twice when I apparently Paused my game at the wrong time, and once when my game loaded after killing a Psychopath, but the Autosaves are pretty lenient and do a great job not ruining a play session by having having to load a save an hour back so I can't complain to much about the crashing other than it was a minor annoyance. What DID annoy me however was the fact that "Erotica" is now just straight up missing now. Why? It's nothing to do with it being hot to me, hell if I want to go that far I'll just head to some adult sites, but it was a pivital part of the game mainly due to two missions, now one is replace by "Getting the funniest shot" and another one is just for Player Points and nothing extra besides that, by a survivor who also unfortunately gets censored having a less revealing outfit, I know what you're thinking "But how is that such a bad thing that she is censored you sexist pig" Well what do you think they are gonna do in Dead Rising 2 if they remaster that? You remember where it takes place right? Fortune City, which is a play on Las Vegas, there are revealing outfits everywhere and sexual stuff everywhere, a remaster for DR2 if they censor it is going to mess the game up pretty bad. Other than those two gripes I have with it, I think it is a really fun game, It's essentially Dead Rising with a fresh coat of paint making it look SO MUCH BETTER and having Quality of Life improvements such as being able to move and shoot... despite the fact that once you shoot you stay still, Auto Saving, being able to advance time forward in case you are just waiting on cases or more calls for survivors, Clothing Items being saved and stored in a locker where you can change into clothes you wore in the mall already along with if you got any of the DLC or grabbed the Deluxe Edition, and the mall musics that you get with it are essentially just Capcom songs that are just nice little tracks to walk around the mall to. The Psychopaths music THANKFULLY is untouched here, unless you enable streamer mode. There are definitely some bugs in it, I've seen enemies getting spawned and stuck in walls. But It is a nice addition to the Dead Rising collection, and as a fan, I'm glad to see it getting more love and brought back to it's roots, Dead Rising 4 scared me because I thought that pile of garbage was going to be the last one that ever gets made, Maybe now Capcom will see that we miss this series, Now if they DO decide to remaster Dead Rising 2, DO NOT CENSOR IT! And please keep it's multiplayer components both the Coop and the Terror is Reality. Thank You Capcom for this revisit to an old classic.

_childDocuments_.review: After finishing the game I fully recommend Deluxe Remaster. It is mechanically improved over the original in every meaningful way. Being able to move while aiming, having autosaves, and the much better survivor AI make a big impact on how enjoyable the entire experience is. I didn't have trouble with performance issues or crashes like other reviews mention, my setup is a 5700X3D CPU, 6800XT GPU, and 32GB of RAM.The new voices are definitely not bad, and at moments I found they had better direction for the VAs than the original game. The only negative is Brad's new voice not being as good as his original. He just doesn't have the same cool attitude or emotional impact, but every other voice is just as good as the original cast and sometimes better. I really enjoyed Jessie's and Adam the Clown's performances for this game. We also have Dave Fennoy coming in to finally give Otis a voice, and it makes him instantly lovable.I would definitely recommend this game to both long time Dead Rising fans and newcomers. This is the best way to get into the series, or re-experience this classic.

_childDocuments_.review: I have always loved this game and I can honestly say that this is a faithful remaster that improved Dead Rising where it needed improvements the most. Without changing the core game play too much, Capcom learned how to improve on their escort missions with the Resident Evil 4 Remaster and they made the clunky survivors better in this Deluxe Remaster. Sure it's not perfect but for long time fans of this game, it's a breath of fresh air.In this game, Frank West is still that slightly off-kilter freelance reporter that covered war stories, ya know? They replaced the original voice actor but he grows on you (or infects you like a virus?) as you play through the game. Frank's abilities and leveling up progression has been untouched and it feels as perfect as it did when this game released with the Xbox 360 in 2005. With the added ease of the improvement on the escorting of survivors, I find myself having more time between missions. I have more time to get lost in dispatching the undead and Psychos alike.This game came out at the beginning of when zombies began to solidify themselves in American pop culture. Zombies became a central part of Horror movies and The Walking Dead kept people wanting more! People who watched these shows or movies wanted to feel what it would be like if a normal person was dropped in a Zombie Apocalypse. Resident Evil, Dead Space, and the like are amazing games but they showed us how highly trained individuals with powerful weapons would fare in this scenario How would the common man fare against zombies? Someone like you or me wouldn't be a member of S.T.A.R.S. and we wouldn't know how to make a plasma cutter with scraps laying around a derelict space station. Frank West had no training, he wasn't this hero who wanted to save the world, and every move in his repertoire is taken from popular wrestling shows like WWE. Frank West works with the tools and knowledge available to everyone. He makes do with the zero training he has and makes it so fun that it hasn't lost it's appeal in almost 20 years!!If you are a fan of zombies, this is a must have in your video game library. This is a timeless game that you will come back to when you want to experience a zombie Apocalypse from your point of view. Anyone can get into this game with no prior knowledge but I highly recommend you pick up some of the reading material scattered across Willamette Parkview Mall before you look for laughs in Wonderland Plaza. There are 3 magazines that will make your 72 hour bout in Willamette easier after you CUT your way through the line at the Space Ride.

_childDocuments_.review: Okay I'm still playing the game, but lets do a quick review. I have a ♥♥♥♥ ton of hours on Dead Rising 1. I'm a huge Dead Rising fan, so is this game up to my standards? Yeah its the second best Dead Rising game we have out right now. Simple as that. I'm mixed on if I prefer the OG Dead Rising or the Remake (yes its a remake, I know they say remaster).There are things the original does that is better, but there are a lot of things that the remake does even better. Of course there are thing that this remake does that is worse, but also just a bunch of weird things. Overall its a 8/10 in its current state, a 9/10 if it gets the polish it needs to be perfect. There's just sadly a bunch of little annoying glitches and lack of polish that add up. It's not HORRIBLE OR ANYTHING, but like maybe wait a lil before buying the game. Capcom has been updating this game even during the beta testing the past couple of months. So most likely we will see more polish / bug fixes sooner rather than later.Overall this a fun game that I remember from 2006. Yeah no one can beat TJ as Frank, but the new guy does a way better job than 'hank' Also people are being weird about 'censorship' and throwing the world around like its about to die. Cliff still comes off as a war vet. Larry Chang is Chinese America (idk why people are calling him white) It was done due to the high tensions between Japan and China rn (prolly why they changed cliff's line) Along with that Erotica was removed. Um, not for like any stupid 'woke western' reasons or anything. But Japan currently has a huge counter culture against up-skirt photos. There are trains dedicated for women, you cannot turn off the shutter on any Japanese phones, and its a major political issues in Japan... You -can- still take up-skirt, and booby shots if you want. You just won't get PP for them. I know I said short review but, there's a lot of weird and stupid controversy around this game. Clearly Capcom did a simple remake of Dead Rising to test the waters with the franchise again. After all Dead Rising 4 failing is why Capcom Vancouver died. So they're going back to their original roots to see what people like and what people don't. Its why they didn't change a lot about this game. So if you're a Dead Rising fan of any sort, or like want more games from Capcom rather than just Resident Evil and Monster Hunter, consider picking up this game and helping Dead Rising out to prove to Capcom we want more games like this.

_childDocuments_.review: SPOILERS AHEAD!~THE GOOD!The game is a perfectly fine way to experience the story. The only changes I could notice are Frank's What In The World (not the biggest complaint, facial model and animations make up for it, no longer has to state his thoughts when we can read it on his face.) Clint's Communism line (likely altered for better sales in China) and Kent's erotica subplot. (By the way, the erotica mission with the female survivor is still in the game.)ADDRESSING CHANGES!Most of these changes only result in minor adjustments to character backgrounds.For instance, Kent is no longer portrayed as a peeping creep, which makes his later death more illogical. (But did I mention the erotica mission with the female survivor is still in the game?)Now, Clint is still a war veteran, though of an unnamed war. This isn't too bothersome, as the Vietnam name-drop isn't essential to his character. What will always be essential are his lines about his daughter, which remain intact.*NEW*Military now can use and also drop Rocket Launchers in The Park, which is welcomed and having a new achievement dedicated to it is neat as well.Thomas can now be spared, if you take out his brother and father first, adds a lot of emotion compared to the OG, where you could only wish to save him while you slashed him down with your Level - 3 Mini ChainsawSUMMARY!Overall, the game is much more fluid in terms of movement, visuals, animation, and so on.The few issues that did frustrate me, like my items disappearing in certain very specific areas where the collision mesh didn't exist, weren't enough to make the game feel not worth playing.UNNEEDED CHANGES!Why change some of the damage values for weapons? Some old strats don't work, I understand Capcom wanted to encourage new strats, but this was really, really dumb for returning players.I can completely agree that Erotica is both a useless change and a needed one, the thing is Erotica didn't serve any purpose in the game other than legit 2 missions, and just being a creep by yourself in your room while gaming. Did it NEED to be removed? No. But is it game-altering? No. So it's not a big deal, and anyone that has an issue with it's removal is gonna mod the game to have fat tidz anyways. So get over it.Why the yellow paint? The game and Brad himself clearly tells you how to defeat Carlito in the Food Court. Ridiculous change.Why is Snuff Shot J unlocked after arriving in the Security Room and not upon Picture Taking? This is basically a free achievement now if you just arrive, whereas you could end up missing this if you weren't paying attention to your trophies and/or challenge list.PS.Will add more as I play, maybe. Or if you anyone who sees this wants to make a valid critique I'll consider it too. - DDopemane

_childDocuments_.review: Update: Getting 100% of the achievements was fun, EVEN INFINITY MODE! Just goes to show how well the quality-of-life changes have taken this game. I will say though, difficulty-wise it's much easier compared to the OG. Most of the time I just don't worry about escorting survivors, they're incredibly efficient on their own, and most follow you very closely. Quality-of-Life changes are very appreciated, but I think Psychopath battles needed a bit more difficulty or added elements to make up for how easily you can dodge, or even just tank hits like nothing.Overall though, there are more positives compared to negatives, and it's a great stepping-stone for future Dead Rising remasters/remakes. I'll wait patiently for Off the Record Remake, PLEASE CAPCOM!

_childDocuments_.review: Just finished the game recently.I think this is a great upgrade to Dead Rising, great graphics, a good modern control scheme, auto save, fast-forward, improved AI for better(survivor escorts) and for worse(the convicts), and the game basically being 1:1 with the og outside of some changes.My only complaints is that the VA work is a bit mixed compared to the og, and on Steam Deck it runs well outside of when you look down big areas like the entrance plaza hallway, where the fps just tanks to ~20 (also do NOT set the game to max graphics on Steam Deck unless you like 1fps).I don't think the censorship that some people got upset about was that big of a deal, from what I can tell few things were changed and the changes made weren't that bad and don't really go against the fan base. Cliff is a bit unfortunate since Dead Rising doesn't strive away from politics, but I think you can still figure out he's talking about 'nam. I don't care about Erotica being removed because I doubt many people actually took Erotica pics outside of the Kent missions and maybe their personal Jessie folder, and honestly Kent's "sexiest shot" being replaced with his "funniest shot" is more funny than it is unfortunate. Of course this is my own opinion and this isn't me saying "I love censorship!" I just don't think this instance is that confusing or annoying compared to when some other games do it.This honestly is just Dead Rising with a modern fresh coat of paint with changes being more for the better than for the worse. _childDocuments_.review: If you've played the original, you've played this. Its not like the Resident Evil 4 Remaster where it feels like a completely different game. _childDocuments_.review: This Remaster is easily a solid 8/10. I've formulated my thoughts in the style of the Good, the Bad, and the Ugly. Let's begin!The Good: As remasters go, this is an excellent one. The quality of life improvements to both story and gameplay are very welcome. Censorship smensorship. The changes in this game that everyone was dreading were completely minimal and didn't take anything away from the experience. That being said, I do not like censorship in games, or in general, but this stuff was not oppressive or "woke" at all. The atmosphere and visuals are amazing with new re-imagined areas and much more detail everywhere you look. A few examples of some "good" aspects for me were the new locker system for both clothing and DLC costume, the PP sticker checklist, the mini-chainsaw still being amazing, Gone Guru (nuff said), the Skateboarding, the improved Survivor AI, and so much more! Overall, the game was really, really excellent.The Bad: The only thing I will say about my list of complains, albeit short, is they are mostly subjective. First off, there used to be a speed storage glitch in the original game, but it was sadly fixed, which is totally expected. It might've not even been an intentional fix. The DLC Costumes are a bit over the top at times, especially the choice of some of them, however not everyone has those, so I understand the subjectiveness of that point. That's mostly what I have to say about the bad.As far as the Ugly goes, I only have one major thing to complain about here, and that is the military soldiers. My god, are they broken. I am not going to let this one aspect completely tank my review because they are only in the game for a short period of time, but I am serious when I say I think they need a Nerf or CapCom has to "fix" them a bit. They are incredibly difficult to escape if there are more than two, and in most situations, you are facing 3+ minimum. I am hearing about a very effective hand-to-hand combo strat to deal with them easily, but I don't think you should have to abuse anything to get an upper hand on a basic enemy type. The soldiers were difficult and devastating in the original, but not nearly as bad as this one. The stunlock and rapid health drain is crazy to deal with.Overall, this game was an excellent remaster, and I really enjoyed playing through it. I still have more to experience with Overtime and Infinity Modes, but I am very pleased with what I have played so far!

_childDocuments_.review: Despite some performance issues and making the game easier in some ways this is a very close to being a direct upgrade to the original Dead Rising. Other fantastic additions include being able to change into any clothes you've previously worn from the safe room and voice acting for all survivors.I will say that streamlining the game to this point has taken this from a fairly daunting and time consuming 100% to something I pretty much did in a weekend and some change in just under 30 hours. Granted I have a lot of experience with the game and do know what I'm doing as I have 100%'d it on the 360 and revisited the 2016 port.For first time players this is a strong recommend, this is a classic that has been modernized in all the right ways, and yet kept things the same when they needed to be to have the integrity of what makes dead rising a unique experience. Existing fans will also find this a treat to revisit, well, at least I did. There are some nitpicks and nostalgia factors that I still prefer the original for but overall this is mostly the better version of the game at this point. Here's hoping to the dead rising franchise having a prosperous future.

_childDocuments_.review: While I'm not a huge fan of the new voice acting, on the whole this is a phenomenal way to re-experience the original game. The new visuals are gorgeous and the game thankfully runs well on my low-mid range PC at 1440p, and while that would have been worth the price of admission just on its own, there's a few new changes that make this version worth grabbing. Survivor AI has been greatly improved, there's new camera functions to mess around with, side quests and dialog are now fully voice acted like in Dead Rising 3, there's welcome QoL improvements like being able to move/shoot and track multiple quests at once, and there's even new books that bring fun tweaks to combat.I'm not sure if this would replace the original as that still looks and plays great at high refresh rates, and its still better suited to game on handhelds like the Steam Deck. But DRDR is still a very nice companion to the original that really breathes life back into this series, here's hoping that this ends up being a new start for it.

_childDocuments_.review: I loved this game and series during my childhood and Capcom did not disappoint with this remaster. The new features are exceptional and make the game feel modern, while keeping that classic fun and janky style of the 2006 classic. The NPC ai improvements are huge and the small quality of life additions to add some convenience to the game (time skipping, autosave) are game changing.The game looks and runs great in the RE engine and it plays better with more modern controls and some much needed remapping (the original dodge was a double tap of the left analog stick that often triggered by accident and was annoying as hell, it's so much better placing it on the B / O button. These types of changes are small, but add a lot to the new experience if you played the original.Die hard fans of the original were disappointed with some instances of dialogue censorship and voice acting changes, but personally you won't even notice the stuff they altered if you're a new player, it's not a big deal at all. I get that the argument of censorship is real and it's not right to change the experience when you're simply remastering something, but this game is far from having the worst case of it. It's very minimal in the grand scope of the entire game. The new voice acting is quite good and I really enjoyed Frank's performance.This is the approach they need to stick with for the future of Dead Rising: KEEP IT SIMPLE AND KEEP IT FUN. I'm so happy they returned to this franchise and gave it some love because it's one of those IPs that really needed to come back. I hope we get some more Dead Rising sequels / remasters to coincide with the upcoming Resident Evil, Monster Hunter, and Street Fighter releases. Capcom is bringing back the good ol' days of gaming!

_childDocuments_.review: As someone who played this game a bit as a kid, I still remember it somewhat fondly. Capcom has done a phenomenal job with the remake, capturing much of what made the original special. However, there are a few issues that I can't overlook.For starters, the improved graphics are a massive step up from what we saw in the early 2000s. The game looks absolutely stunning, especially when you hit a zombie and see the blood splatter in vivid detail.Gameplay has been streamlined as well. No more restarting at your last save if you die, you can pick up exactly where you left off. While this feature adds convenience, it might frustrate some of the more hardcore players looking for a tougher challenge.A cool feature that was added is the ability to switch between the original and updated controls. For those who prefer the more sluggish, nostalgic movement, it's still available. At the same time, newer players can enjoy modernised controls, like being able to move while shooting. In the classic mode, you're restricted when shooting or throwing objects, which adds a nice touch for fans of the original gameplay style.Many of you will be glad to hear that survivors have finally been made more useful. While they can still be a bit useless at times, they now actively try to assist you rather than just standing around like rocks. So far, with the exception of one, nearly all the survivors have made genuine efforts to keep me alive, a vast improvement over the originalThe story remains unchanged, staying true to the original, the psychos are far more terrifying this time around. Thanks to the new graphics, they've been made significantly creepier, adding a fresh layer of horror to their encounters.  This time around, from what I remember, there definitely seems to be fewer zombies compared to the original, which was a bit disappointing. I was hoping Capcom would take a bigger leap and increase the zombie count, but unfortunately, it feels like there are fewer this time.Unfortunately, the boss fights haven't been updated, so all the frustrating mechanics from the original are still there. Psychos like Steven Chapman nearly killed me multiple times with his shotgun, firing at me from across the entire store, which makes no sense.It also feels like zombies can grab you more frequently, which can get really frustrating, especially when it seems like they shouldn’t be able to reach you.And then there's Otis, still the most annoying character ever. During my fight with Carlito, he called me roughly 50 times, and hearing that constant 'beep, beep, beep' while trying to focus was infuriating. There really should be a way to mute him. Sure, I can answer him while fighting now, but come on, Otis, I get it, some survivors are dead!And finally, the worst change by far is Frank’s voice. The new actor sounds awful—like he's AI-generated, emotionless, and bored. In the original, Frank’s journey from 'I’m here for pictures' to becoming the savior of Willamette was amazing to witness. Now, he just sounds robotic, completely stripping away the personality that made his character so memorable. You should have brought T.J Rotolo back.    >Better Graphics> More refined while staying true to the original> you can choose between Newer movement or classic movement> Survivors are more useful  > Frank's new voice is terrible> Otis is still annoying> Psycho fights are still tedious (shotguns can still kill you from miles away) >  fewer zombies than the original > zombies can grab you far more frequently and from bizarre angles  If you get the Licker outfit, make sure to use it during cut scenes, it’s absolutely hilarious!

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is good but not great, and in terms of gameplay minus a few things is a faithful remaster (for better AND for worse). If you are expecting a vastly improved game, you will be disappointed. More details below. First off, there are Quality of Life features that debuted in later titles that would have been fantastic additions here. For example, there is no indicator whether or not a survivor will see and follow you into a new area (wherein the later titles place a little icon above their pictures). You can now move while aiming which is a nice feature, but it is still extremely slow, and only marginally an upgrade. Capcom also decided to speed up the leveling process, which some may dislike. Personally, I was able to complete the game and save all survivors in one play-through and ended at level 47, easily could have reached level 50 if I had not fast forwarded during the last day. Are the survivor AI improved? Yes and no. They no longer get stuck quite as easily, but there were a few closer calls than I would have liked. I did not however, have a nightmare time trying to escort the Movieland Survivors through the cult (a notorious spot for the AI). Next, the visuals. The visuals are greatly improved across the board. There is however, some noticeable pop-in, particularly in the Central Park and in the introduction scene with the Helicopter ride. The pop-in is not game breaking, but it is a little janky/distracting. Zombies also regularly clip through objects even in cutscenes, again not a big deal, but some would rather see that fixed in a Remaster that is supposed to be the definitive version of the game to play. Audio wise, the new voices are fine. Some are better, some are about the same, and a few are worse. None of the voices were so bad that I felt the experience was actively being hindered. The soundtrack is still very good. Bugs & Crashes: I did not have any crashes on my run of the game, but I have seen others mentioning crashes. It is worth noting that I am reviewing this a week after launch, so perhaps some quick patches have made the crashes less frequent. There are two common complaints that you will see regarding enemy AI that I wanted to address here. 1). Zombies grab too frequently? Some have complained that they are getting grabbed way too often by zeds. This however is fairly accurate to the original release, as i-frames during attack animations and "momentum" from your character weren't as prominent until Dead Rising 2. It can be a bit difficult to adjust at the beginning, but getting grabbed was simply more prominent here in the first game. 2). The Soldier AI is too accurate? This I have experienced in my run of the game. In overtime when the soldiers are patrolling the mall, they are far more accurate and deadly. If you run into two soldiers and don't stealth, knock them down, or have a heavy MG or rocket launcher, you will have a bad time. They are extremely proficient at stun-locking you, and will continue hit you over and over again. If you love Dead Rising, this is worth picking up at full price. I personally had a ton of fun (some of which is definitely just nostalgia) running through the game again. If you are not familiar with the original, or perhaps only played the later titles, this may be worth waiting for a 25% or greater discount. Looking forward to (hopefully) a Dead Rising 2 Remaster in the future.

_childDocuments_.review: Its the same great game from 2006, just with a few added bells and whistles. As is the case with Capcom's recent remakes, the game is both easier and harder than the original. Its difficult to describe. A lot of the more frustrating elements from the original game have been either removed entirely or toned down to make them more tolerable (survivor AI being chief among them). The bosses and military soldiers towards the end of the game are a lot tougher now and will kill you very quickly if not properly prepared.The ability to fast-forward the in-game clock is honestly such a game changer. It adds to the fast pace the game has and once you know what you're doing, it cuts out a bunch of downtime. I do have some minor gripes with the game, mainly the sound design in some areas (voice work is fine. guns sound strangely weak when compared to the original game). There were also a handful of odd visual bugs I kept noticing as I played, but nothing to really ruin the experience.One of the greatest zombie games of all time has straight up just been made better and I cannot applaud Capcom enough for it. I only hope Dead Rising 2 gets similar treatment down the road.

_childDocuments_.review: I wasn’t planning to buy the Dead Rising remaster, especially not at launch, but something inside me wanted to give it a try. And unexpectedly for myself, I ended up playing a game I hadn’t been waiting for at all. I haven’t played the original, but I’ve heard from friends and others that the remaster had some content cut and some censorship added in certain places. It sounds sad, but I find it hard to feel strongly negative about it because I never tried the original and decided to jump straight into the remaster.I want to say that I liked it — it turned out to be fun, absurd, and stylish. I enjoyed the leveling and skill acquisition mechanics, the variety of weapons, the photography, and the concept that time is always passing. You’re given 72 hours to do everything, and some rescue missions are very time-limited, making them truly challenging. There aren’t many bosses in the game, but they are funny and memorable. I managed to save exactly half of the people I could, as I didn’t want to save scum and just accepted it when someone died during the escape to the safe room.I also liked that the game allows you to fail the main story quests (though here I did reload). I enjoyed the game a lot, but judging by the weak sales, Capcom won’t be releasing new remasters for Dead Rising anytime soon, if at all. Perhaps they should have lowered the price for this specific remaster, but I’m not sure that would have changed the overall sales picture for the game (Dragon’s Dogma says hi).

_childDocuments_.review: A soulless watered down remake that doesn't live up to the essence of the original game. Still boggles my mind on how the devs were able to mess up and censor most of the zombie's mechanics and gore, which are arguably the most integral part of a game... a sandbox game that takes place in a ZOMBIE-infested mall, but whatever. Even the difficulty has been toned down significantly which makes the game feel too easy and ultimately less enjoyable.On a better note, I personally don't mind the new VA cast. Frank's new VA ultimately grew on me, along with the talented performances behind the psychopaths and main characters, so I have no complaints in that department. Overall, get this remake on sale for $20 or less. OR, better yet, play the original game where the devs actually cared about what they were presenting towards their audience. This remake needed wayyyy more time in the oven, but I think its too late for it now either way.TLDR: I feel like the vfx artists were sleeping during the production of this game lmao

_childDocuments_.review: Specs:-CPU: Intel Core i7-11700K - 8 cores - 3.6GHz (5.0GHz)-GPU: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3080 Ti FE 12GB-1440p Ultrawide MonitorUltrawide Users:Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster has full ultrawide support from Day 1, something still few and far between for modern games for some reason. Personally, the vignette that comes standard with the RE Engine feels especially oppressive on ultrawide, so I'd highly recommend REFramework for the best experience possible.I took a Capcom survey around Christmas time last year, where the studio asked a bunch of questions about their franchises and what gamers feel about the current selection, and even what they want to see for the future. I think I was in a minority when I wrote that I would love a full remake/remaster of Dead Rising, a real contender for my favorite IP under Capcom's belt. Imagine my surprise 6 months later when they announce the exact thing I wanted! And coming out just a few months later! So, is it everything I wanted it to be, and more importantly, everything it needs to be?Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (DRDR) takes the "soul" of the 2006 release and packages it up to modern audiences without losing a single important detail. From the reusing of a majority of animations, to keeping the same story beats and plot points of the original, the overall experience is a great one. It's a strange feeling to start playing a brand new game and to already be going through it as though I've beaten it a thousand times, but I think that really attests to how much of the original game is still here almost 2 decades later.Bringing DRDR to the RE Engine is something I never knew I needed, but seeing Resident Evil 2/3/4 Remake-quality level zombies in Willamette's shopping mall is incredible! Despite the vast number of zombies on screen, if you slow down and actually observe them on a singular level, you can make out the same deformities, blemishes, and injuries you would see playing as Leon or Jill in Raccoon City. Zombie models are unquestionably repeated, but that's no different from the 2006 version, so those who are returning to the game all these years later probably won't feel amiss at all. The world around you doesn't miss this treatment either, with incredible detail given to Frank's surroundings, with new lighting effects and objects placed in every scene of the mall, really bringing the whole package together. It's been a long time since Dead Rising was able to give me a bit of dread with just its environments!Mechanically, this might as well be the same game! All the small little tips and tricks from the original are still present, making any skills you learned from playing the original work just as well in this version! But that's not to say this was purely a copy+paste job by Capcom's team. Many QoL features have been added to the experience, such as a brand-new control scheme for actually moving while aiming, multiple new features for your camera, and a clothing collection in the safe room that keeps every single clothing item you've put on once for future customization. No more running back to Entrance Plaza for a pair of shoes! Combat also feels identical, with a ton of fighting animations feeling like the original with small differences here and there. But new content doesn't stop at QoL, and certainly not just DLC, but the dev team has added multiple new magazines that drastically change certain mechanics, even making some joke items very lethal! There's even  and new attacks from zombies, as well as having Frank's learnable skills now bound to buttons, allowing you to execute them at your leisure!Now, is there a catch? Well, sort of, actually. I'm not sure whether it's optimization, limits of the engine, or my own setup, but initial boot of a save file or new game certainly comes with jitters and stutters, but smooth out after a few minutes tops (at least for me). There's also the occasional zombie-clipping, with zombies ending up in places that are impossible to get to, such as inside a window display or a column. I've also noticed that some enemies will have a "cooldown" of some kind when getting hit by attacks, which was present in the first game, but has been turned up to a degree that leaves me questioning. For example, a survivor died to a psychopath that was tasing them that I was physically unable to stop despite dealing 75% of their health bar in damage while it was happening, which frankly didn't feel fair. But these instances are few and far between, so they felt more like one-offs rather than things that impact the whole experience.I also feel like I should give my 2 cents on complaints I've been seeing around the internet about DRDR, because us gamers sure do love to complain.Listen, I love TJ Rotolo as much as the next guy, but the original game was 18 years ago! Honestly, there's half a chance that a large portion of the original cast don't do VA work anymore, or may not even be alive. Thinking we could get a big family reunion almost 2 decades later is a bit much.Yes, a specific psychopath won't call you Vietcong anymore, and you can't get free PP just by taking pictures of Jessie's chest, but if we can be perfectly honest with ourselves, these aren't the features of the original we needed, it was everything else! I can't even confirm if any of the original dev team worked on DRDR, but even if it was the exact same team, we should expect some touch-ups after all this time.This is a video game. In 2024. You're gonna find yellow paint in your 2024 video game.Jokes aside, and if we're willing to be honest, none of these things are deal breakers. Not to mention this is an RE Engine game, there's going to be mods that likely fix all your grievances. Overall, this is a fantastic experience and well worth the full price. Don't agree? That's fine! Capcom still has you covered. At the time of this review (9/21/2024), the original is still on Steam for a full price of $10. That's less than lunch! There's no way you can't find a way to enjoy Dead Rising if it's something you're genuinely interested it, and I feel DRDR is the best way to do it!

This game is a classic that has stood the test of time - the improvements to the AI are a welcome addition and the additional unlocks are brilliant. _childDocuments_.review: the game is fun. it is just dead rising 1. the issue is that there seems to be a few missing elements or things that feel not fully finished in the game.the biggest standout for me is the lack of zombie ambient sound. you can sit in a courtyard full of 1000's of zombies, and it's just complete silence. in the original game you would hear the zombies mumbling and grunting all around you. now it's just dead silence? it seems completely off and not really sure how it got to the full release like this.another thing is you can just straight up walk through zombies. frank will just phase through them as if they didn't even exist. the feel of walking through crowds of zombies seems completely messed up in this remaster. lastly, the game's performance is just not really all that good. i have a 3080 TI and a 7800 x3d. game installed on an SSD. i have one of the best PCs money can buy and the game just doesn't hold a steady framerate in many scenarios. moving throughout the game world seems to produce numerous stutters and FPS slowdowns. it's honestly a shame as i am a huge fan of the original ever since its release. it feels like this game needs a relatively decent post release patch to bring it up to the level of the original.i'm still going to play through the game and enjoy my time with it, but it definitely needs some further fixes to make it worth buying over the original.

_childDocuments_.review: I'm a big fan of the 2006 original, and for good reason! It's an absolute classic and, for the time, a really innovating game in the semi open-world zombie games genre. So, how does the remaster hold up? Pretty good actually! The story is the same as the original, sadly Frank's OG voice actor didn't reprise his role for the remaster, but I don't mind that much. The main complaint I got is that the game is way less clunky, which makes it very easy, mainly the survivors don't struggle so much anymore in escort side missions, which takes away a lot of the challenge from the original. The difficulty spike at the end portion of the game is ridiculous tho, you can get stun locked very easily and that can make the experience pretty frustrating, but nothing a well-timed dodge roll can't fix!In conclusion, it's a fun, modern day introduction to the Dead Rising franchise, I wouldn't rank it above the original, but it's an excellent way to experience the game!

_childDocuments_.review: I wanna start this off by saying I'm probably going to refund this game. This remake did not personally strike a chord with me, and overall I felt very apathetic to a lot of the design changes. It just was not a vibe for me. It's not a particularly bad remake, and for anyone interested, I would pick up the original on Steam in case Capcom decides to delist it. I don't think they have any particular reason to, but you never know.Sound design for weapons, and impacts got heavily nerfed. Anything from Throwing CD's or plates at zombies, or even pounding them with a sledgehammer. Weapons just sound so weak and pitiful, a lot of weapon feel and sounds like they are made out of cardboard or plastic. The new dialogue feels wooden, and not in a charming way, more in like a every line of dialogue they just went with the first take, and called it a wrap. Character movement and jumping around as just feels floaty, and overall just off.Of course it launched with Denuvo DRM, and there is traversal stutter (that is immediately noticeable when you decide to use skateboards in particular). I don't know if the traversal stutter is due to shader compilation stutter, but that does seem to be a very common problem in newer games. And there is no shader compiling on startup, so I'm kind of assuming that's what the problem is.So much of the original games charm, or what made it stand out, has been changed or altered in destructive ways for my taste. The new voice cast isn't even particularly bad, it's just mainly the soulless line delivery. It's like they couldn't be bothered.Most character models are pretty faithful to the originals, which sort of creates an uncanny valley effect with most characters, where in the original they had a very stylized look, and implementing this together with RE Engine's ultra-photorealistic aesthetic creates this very ugly, and uncanny look that I'm honestly just not a fan of.I really wanted this remake to be the ultimate way to play the original Dead Rising, but in most ways it does not feel that way. It's not particularly bad, but then again I don't think anything will ever be as bad as Dead Rising 4 was. It makes me extremely happy to see that Capcom is not giving up on this franchise. But overall this remake just, isn't it. At least for me. I just feel so mixed on it overall. Wanting to love it, but feeling so disappointed with a lot of the changes made.The most egregious is the change to one of the psychopaths (Psychopaths in Dead Rising are boss encounters, that are usually crazy survivors you meet in different locations). One of them in the original is supposed to be a Vietnam War Veteran, suffering from PTSD.Now with the change that has been made to his dialogue, he could be just a veteran of *any* war. It is an absolutely ridiculous change.Overall RE Engine is an incredibly well optimized engine, but I'm genuinely so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ sick of Capcom shipping every new game release with Denuvo DRM, so for at least the first 6 months it has overall worse performance. Until they eventually strip the DRM out of the game, and then it starts running like it should have at launch. (We seen this with Resident Evil Remake 2, 3, and I don't personally know if it was a problem with 4).Shader compilation stutter may also be an issue, as there is no shader compiling on startup. And I'm not going to lie I am borderline sick of games not launching with shader compilation on startup. When is this just going to be a standard feature to launch with your game. This should be standard on PC by now.Overall as someone who was a massive fan of the two original Dead Rising games, this remake has me feeling mixed and sort of put off. As a newcomer, it's probably worth a buy at least at a 30% discount or more once they fix the performance issues. Myself this remake is not for me, and I don't have interest in picking it up again.

I do wish the difficulty of the original was still here, You can literally be lvl 10+ from the helicopter ride at the beginning and you can easily hit lvl 50 in your first playthrough without really meaning too. _childDocuments_.review: I was just reading a few of the negative reviews for this game and was laughing to myself. They made a few good points, particularly about the removal of a Chinese character and the erotic photography - I do agree with this they were unnecessary changes. Does it affect the gameplay in any way? NO. So let's get over it and move on.This is one of the best remastered games I've ever played. I've only played just over 4 hours and it bought back some great memories. I was 16 years old and had to save my money to buy an Xbox just to play this and my god was it worth it. Today I downloaded the remaster and completely re-lived the fun I had 18 years ago.I only have a mid range pc with a 3070 and the game runs great. I haven't had any crashes at all. Someone else posted a negative review here saying it crashed 15 times in 12 hours. There must be something wrong with his pc because my pc is old and it has been running absolutely fine.The survivors work a little better now. However I did encounter 1 bug. The Chinese guys in the book store were loosely running around and I was unable to interact with them. I tried leaving the area and coming back but it did not fix. Eventually they just died. The bosses are great. Definitely one of the highlights of the game. Anyone who played the original knows why. However I did encounter another bug. The prisoners outside for some reason I had to defeat them twice. I've returned to the area a few more times and they appear to be permanently dead now.The voice acting is poor at times. It's cheesy. It probably will bother you if you never played the original. So yeah, aside from a few bugs and some poor voice acting this game is an absolute blast. If you didn't play the original but love zombie games (or the Dawn of the Dead movies) you will likely enjoy this game.

_childDocuments_.review: I played the original Dead Rising way back in the day. As much as I loved its unique premise and over-the-top tone, some gameplay quirks and control woes kept me from fully enjoying the title.Fast-forward to 2024, and DRDR addresses pretty much all of the concerns I had with the 360 release. Better survivor AI, more intuitive controls, and other QoL tweaks help make Dead Rising a slightly more forgiving but still challenging and thrilling romp through one of gaming's most unforgettable locales.

The survivors are much more self sufficient which takes a way a lot of the tedium, but they still have some charming crunchiness to their AI. The game runs well, looks good, and it feels like i'm playing it for the first time again!

_childDocuments_.review: It's a total overhaul like the RE2, 3, and 4 remakes. It looks really good, that engine Capcom uses for these games is *chef's kiss* I could stand for a few less pores showing, it's a bit overboard.I didn't think I would care at all about the new Frank voice, I'm an easy audience. It just doesn't match the character design to me though. Your milage may vary. The sounds otherwise are pretty good, nothing amazing. I'm using an Arctis headset with Atmos enabled and I really haven't noticed noticed any 3d sound despite it being in the options.The psycho fights I've had were very easy compared to the original. It does feel like the mall fills up quicker though.The photography is still fun. I don't think I can catch a pic of a zombie I just bashed as they fall. I may just not have the hand dexterity I had 20 years ago when it came out.One thing to know for new players that haven't ever played the original, it's totally normal, fine, and even expected for you to restart with your upgrades when you get stuck. Sure you'll start back from the intro, but you'll have learned some of the mall navigation and have better stats and skills. Restart until you feel comfortable enough to not get eaten alive. Lots of whiners about horniness and racist stereotypes. They add nothing to the original except make anyone but straight white guys feel put off. Incels gonna incel though I suppose.Finally the bugs. It's a buggy game, that seems to have come in as hot as Outlaws, another current buggy game by a huge publisher. I found that turning off LOD altogether and lowering the texture size to 2gigs was the best fit for quality and frame rates for me. I noticed no real difference between 2gigs and 8gigs. After that, no more issues. Prior to that I had crashes, bad hitching in scene transitions and terrible framerates pretty often. One size doesn't fit all, so keep your playtime under the Steam return policy if you're unable to unfix the jank. All in all, it's a great remake and after a patch or two it should get better in general. I also noticed that the GeForce Experience app doesn't support the game currently so you'll need to adjust and test to dial it in.

_childDocuments_.review: I was obsessed with this game when the original came out. I watched every trailer and read entire strategy guides online. I never got a chance to play it though. Then suddenly this comes out and I decided to give it a try. I don't think it is as good as childhood me thought it was, but it is still fun.One thing really surprised me though. I always pictured this as an open world sandbox where you messed around killing zombies with tons of wacky weapons. The game can be that way if you want it to be, but if you are trying to complete the story (especially if you also want to save everyone) then it is a very different game. At that point you stick to a couple boring but effective weapons and spend most of your time sprinting around the mall ignoring the zombies while a bunch of idiots trail along behind you and you try to stop them from doing anything stupid.I think a big strength of this game is that there are a ton of different ways to play, and the game works whichever one you do. You can do what I did and try to complete all the missions, you can do the main story and ignore the side missions for a less stressful experience, or you could just ignore the story entirely and run around killing zombies for three days then peace out on the helicopter. Heck, if you want to, you could just sit in the security room for three days and then leave without killing a single zombie. These are all a perfectly valid ways to play the game and will give you different endings depending on what you do. That said, while sitting in the security room is probably the most reasonable thing to do if you were actually in that situation, I don't think the game would be worth your money if that was what you chose to do.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR: It's a good remake, feels exactly like the original just looking much nicer and with a few more QOL features. The changes a lot of people complained about for a while until they found another game that made them mad are blown way out of proportion.The thing that most people and fake "concerned gamers" complain about on Twitter is the content that was altered between the original and now. In practice, after completing 72 hour mode, the differences from the original are really not intrusive or obvious at all. One or two lines of dialogue were changed and the "erotic" photo category no longer exists. I suspect this is because Japan has historically had issues with gross old men taking creepshots of women in public and that Capcom (a Japanese studio) looked back on this with the context of the modern day and thought "maybe this isn't such a good feature". I really didn't miss its inclusion and I'm glad I no longer get told by the game that my photo that contained a zombie that was wearing a low cut dress was sexy.The only omission I actually care about is that Capcom didn't even try to contact TJ Rotolo to reprise his role as Frank West, but the silver lining is the new actor puts in a solid performance that really tries to mimic Rotolo as best he can.As for *actual* issues, it's crashed more than a few times. Sometimes, randomly, it will crash on ALT+TAB, but usually it won't. I also noticed it was a lot more unstable if the Discord voice overlay was active. I blame Denuvo for a majority of the crashes, though. If that's what's stopping you from picking it up, I've heard that Capcom tends to remove Denuvo after a certain sales target has been reached, so you can wait for that.

_childDocuments_.review: they added a bunch of quality of life stuff and made it easier to track things for some of the achievements. survivors are also less stupid, they will also just tell you where PP stickers are and weapons and whatnot while you are carrying them. also they throw more PP at you in general, mostly based around photo pp being so much higher than the original game, so you can get most of the levels in 1 run instead of only getting to like 35 and having to do a 2nd run to get to 50. they changed some buttons on modern control scheme to be easier, like you just press b to dodge instead of double tap a direction. they also just have more voice acting in general; everyone is either a sidegrade or slightly better, usually similar performances to the original cast with some exceptions (kindell sounds hard now instead of being goofy's voice actor and sounding hokey). they also added a blender to the safe room for some reason, guess you can blend quick step right away with the apples and coffee creamer.they fixed enemy ai and added more health to bosses, so there's less exploits and boss fights are harder. sometimes they added new moves. some cars are more maneuverable, but the red car is has normal acceleration instead of just being super fast. skateboards are very tanky, starting with like 12 hits instead of 3, and they are faster by a lot, but you cant steer as tightly as you could in the og game. they changed the order of some scoops around and on one hand, it might make things less stressful and easier by spreading them out more evenly, but also it's kinda weird if you've played before, you also could fight a harder boss earlier than usual.performance has been acceptable: I get some minor lag for like 2 seconds on loading into a new area, then it goes to normal. the underground section is a bit wonky though. people are trying to say there's less zombies, but it seems like the same amount to me, and I've played the 2016 port a lot for speedruns; it mostly seems the same everywhere except maybe the tunnels, where it might be slightly less. overall, it's neat. if you want to play dead rising again, yeah go for it. the other version is still great too. so far it's not mind blowingly different or anything or super improved that you have to get this version, but it's better looking and has more audio and some quality of life stuff. _childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster could have gone wrong, in many ways but luckily the creators of this remaster admire the original as much as it's fans do. The inclusion of so many of the game's positives without basically any of the annoyances of the original mean that it's a game that is essentially Dead Rising 1 but more of what you love and almost spotless of what you don't. It's a great stepping on point for series newcomers or people who have never tried the original and a great romp if you're a veteran. I'll be reviewing this from my own personal standpoint as a returning player, you might not get some of this as a newbie.Dead Rising was infamous for it's difficulty at certain spikes during the game and while some can be mitigated some were serious pain points either left completely out of your control, due to the eccentricities of it's control scheme, the first person camera aiming when using ranged weapons and a mix of all of the above in regards to the game's boss fights. All have been dealt with. Aiming in Dead Rising 1 is no longer a complete pain in the ass, it took us 18 years folks but we finally did it! You can even auto aim if you aren't directly aiming, which acts as a good way of giving you some space from you and some annoying zombies. The control scheme has been revamped and it's a generally much more approachable game from that standpoint. You can opt for classic controls if you really want that, which for veterans with muscle memory.. it's appreciated but i found the newer controls better than the originals even if it took brainhacking my mind to do so.  Holy god, i need to talk about survivors. They aren't perfect but we've finally done it boys. They actively do not constantly get into trouble or constantly do the most hairbrained things imaginable. They aren't a complete nightmare to ferry around the mall, unless you make it that way. 8 Survivors and a tight corridor come to mind. I have never been so happy to set a set of stairs in my entire life as i had when i stepped out the saferoom as a veteran of the first. There is a new mechanic with character affinity and their AI working better with some weapons as opposed to others but it's very barebones and the can give some unintentionally hilarious dialogue when they try to point out something useful as you're swamped in a zombie horde. Yeah, i think i'll live without getting that 5k pp bonus photo shoot you just mentioned while we're surrounded by ZOMBIES TRYING TO RIP US APART. Nevertheless, the changes to survivors is appreciated like capcom offered me a cold glass of water on a hot day.Boss Fights in Dead Rising 1 were just simply ballbusters unless you came prepared with good weapons and with forward knowledge or had simply been through the raw pain of beating them before. They have been slightly nerfed, at least some of them have and progressively get more difficult as you get through the game. Probably a good idea of onboarding players  instead of throwing them at early game bosses that usually were the bane of early players existences. A single boss has had a significant redesign and frankly, it's actually leagues better than the original game. If you're a vet, you'll know who when you run up on them.The original game has seriously shown it's age in recent years and while we got a re-release that did give some of the older graphics a bit more life. It does look dated. Deluxe Remaster gives it a massive new breath of life, some areas have a flair that wasn't there before. The game just looks way way better and at the fidelity you can expect from a game nowadays. You can probably nitpick a few things here or there but they are so inconsequential to the overall experience that i think you would have to actively look for them in order to actually notice them. This applies also to the voice acting. I'm going to be honest, i love TJ rotolo's voice acting as Frank West in the originals and his VA's absence is seriously felt here but his replacement Jas Patrick does a fantastic job of projecting the tone of the original. There were seriously times i thought it would be messed up here or there but the performance is a great emulation of rotolos. I warmed up to it quick and i went in pretty unsure off the back of the announcement trailer. The rest of the cast is the same, you can really tell they trained their performances on the original performances. The smaller more subtle inflections are taken into account in the new VA work. The whole game is also voiced, random ass NPC 231? He's not relegated to the phantom zone of text box with no dialogue. He actually has a voice now, i cannot tell you how much my mind melted to hear old man Otis Washington actually speak on the transceiver after being stuck to a text box FOR 18 YEARS!Right, do you have any legitimate critique mr.freakingoutaboutstairs? Yep. An enemy type later in the game. They are a lot more deadly than the original, take them seriously. And use that first person mode and a machine gun like your life depends on it. If you're fighting more than 2, prepare for a bad time. *SPOILER* Mode is too easy and it's solely down to how often and easy it is to find a certain resource as opposed to the original. That's all i'll add to that for risking spoilers.The game has crashing issues, i crashed maybe a total of 3 times but the game aggressively autosaves and i barely lost any progress so that's kinda a boon. I wouldn't recommend the game on weaker hardware right now and if you're paranoid about that maybe wait for awhile so these crashes can be patched out currently.Overall, Capcom has once again knocked it out of the park in regards to it's remasters and i've already established this is perfect for first timers. However there are a few critiques that this Remaster doesn't have a lot of offer a veteran of the series. I disagree, the changes made here are significant and directly effect pacing. Being able to skip time alone kills huge stretches of just.. killing time in the original. I cannot tell you the magic of finding the exact same weapon spawn from 18 years ago, remembered by whoever put it there or wanting to know what Otis Washington would sound like or STAIRS, I DON'T HAVE TO WAIT FOR EVERY SURVIVOR TO SINGLE FILE CLIMB UP A LEDGE. As a fan of the original, it's like christmas morning and i still highly recommend it if you're looking for a replay. You'll get to experience things in a unique way that newcomers will just simply not be able to appreciate and for a good reason. In terms of value, i understand if it's pushing it a little for some people but to me the price was about worth it for what i got out of it as a returning player but you'll get more bang for your buck as a newbie. Highly recommended.

_childDocuments_.review: Putting this up front: The difficulty has gotten easier, but the game as a whole is not easy. The psychopaths feel just as difficult as the OG, which I played and beat for the 30th time a few months ago. The easier bits are survivors not getting caught in hordes or stuck on spots at random, this is something that massively inflated the OGs difficulty. Zombies still grapple you, the game still has challenge to it, but the inflated difficulty is gone. THEY FIXED THE SURVIVOR AI, the survivors no longer aimlessly get stuck on absolutely nothing and can navigate extensively without issue. I have so far saved over 10 survivors and none have gotten stuck or placed themselves in a situation causing their demise.So far it has been great, a zombie pop-ins are the only complaint I have, besides that it is a woke paradise where Carlito has been changed to a white man named Carl and it's super LGBTQIA+ accessible. In all seriousness, Dead Rising holds a special place in my heart and I can even recall the exact day I got the game and my 360. While I enjoy the VA for the original Frank more, so far this has been a much smoother experience with gameplay tweaks QoL that make it worth it, graphics are very stylish, it's nice to have all lines voice acted, and so far it has been really solid.Denuovo is a meh thing, I haven't noticed many dips on my 2070 super RTX and the only performance issue is zombie pop-ins, which I feel used to in this franchise, but it would be nice to fix it. Performance side for me is fine, but I see a lot complaining so maybe it needs a few patches.Afyer beating the game and getting the Ture Ending, I do think this is the best way to play the game, there's some issues, some unnecessary changes, and some changes I wish they made, but it is still a great way to play the game. Pop-ins are bad, clipping is bad, performance is a little spotty, these are things I hope are fixed.

_childDocuments_.review: This is for the 1.0 release.  I thoroughly enjoyed this release, sure it has a few issues here and there, but this is one game I never expected to get the remake treatment.  The original game got an excellent port to PC a few years back and now only costs a whopping $10 so really this release is trying to please 2 crowds, fans of the OG and newcomers that would use this as a jumping in point for the series.  I myself played the original 360 release many times over through the years as well as the previously mentioned PC release and consider them excellent if not a little quirky games.  DRDR takes the original release and cleans up alot of the "jank" the OG has.  Controls:The new control scheme in particular is a massive improvement over the original, having a dedicated button for rolling and much more consistent inputs for Frank's wrestling moves.  Having a dedicated button to switch through targeted nearby items is a great addition too.  The only thing I can really say is a downgrade as far as the controls are concerned is inventory navigation, the original control scheme made it very easy to switch through items while simultaneously weaving the crowds, where as DRDR puts inventory controls on the D-Pad, necessitating you to move your hand off of the movement stick.  Seems minor but comes into play pretty frequently.  Visuals: Graphically this release looks properly modern with all the good and bad that usually indicates.  Across the board I'd say model quality and effects look very good.  Like the original game, the main cast definitely look the best, with all of the different survivor models looking a bit rougher.  I found it a little hard to look at this redesigned Frank when I first started playing but he kinda grew on me.  I think he fits the new voice actor well.  Texture work is a bit inconsistent, sometimes it looks great, sometimes it looks like an intern handled it.  Lighting in particular DRDR struggles with.  Nights just look gray and washed out, and usually right before dawn it can get unnaturally dark.  Days generally look pretty, and some well placed ambient lights add to the atmosphere.  The original game definitely has way better looking nights that keep a creepy atmosphere.  Also why is the skateboard model like 4X larger than the original game?  It looks horrible and I'm not sure how that passed QA.Bugs / Stability:Straight up, I encountered WAY too many crashes for a 1.0 release.  In roughly 30 hours I 100%'d the game and crashed ~15 times.  Luckily this game implements a new auto-save feature whenever you travel between areas, and I only ever crashed while going through an area transition loading screen so I never lost any progress.  I'm on a mobile GPU, a 2080 Super Max-Q and with a mix of ultra/high settings I kept a consistent 60 everywhere except the maintenance tunnels, it kinda chugs in there for me, not sure if everyone has that issue.  My first convict fight, they crashed into a tree then flew across the park at 100mph bouncing across the walls.  I've yet to have that happen again but it did kinda kill my immersion.    I've seen some other reviews saying infinity mode is unplayable due to crashes and I'm not sure where that is coming from as I completed my 7 day survivor run in 1 sitting with 0 crashes.Balance / Difficulty:There is really no debating this, DRDR is much easier than the original game.  With the ability to move while shooting and much more consistent movement controls, you can obliterate every boss with barely any effort.  Many weapons were rebalanced to make them more useful and across the board it felt like every weapon had much more durability.  I actually checked my challenge progression and I had only broken 6 weapons by the time I first completed 72 hour mode.  The infamous survivor AI of the original has been greatly improved, so much so I never had one even come close to death.Menus / Time ManagementDRDR does a fantastic job of cleaning up all the menus, navigating the map, checking challenge stats, seeing what survivors you've missed, all very easy to find and concisely conveyed.  A new fast forward mechanic is available at all save points that lets you skip filler time (which you will probably have a lot of considering the difficulty.)  It does kinda make Infinity mode a joke but hey, I already did my time with the original, so whatever.Little AdditionsDRDR adds a few new features to the mix which are greatly appreciated.  Camera upgrades, a dozen or so new (and actually pretty fun) magazines, new interactions with psychos, the survivor moodlet system, all of these are fantastic additions.  Cop zombies shooting at me got a bit annoying but still a cool originally cut feature to bring back.THE VOICE ACTINGAlright, I didn't hate any of the new voice acting.  Except Brad.  Brad's VA sounds so intensely bored and uninvolved it really hurts every cutscene he's in (WHICH IS MOST OF THEM.)  Frank's new voice actor could never replace TJ as the voice of Frank in my mind, but I think he does a quality job.OverallI wouldn't be upset if a newcomer told me they wanted to play DR1 for the first time and they played this.  It really does feel like the same game at it's core and is very polished aside from the stability issues.  $40 seems a BIT steep for what is essentially a 20 year old (and pretty short at that) game, but I wasn't upset with my purchase.Schizoid babble over
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: [No story spoilers, but, maybe other kinds so be cautious if you want to go in fresh]TL:DR - Yeah, if you really love the original's story and game play, you should feel right at home IF you NEED a reason to hop into Willamette 2.0. Otherwise the original is still there (and cheaper) with all it's wonderful charm right in tact.   Taking into account how much time I've spent with the original across multiple platforms, I have a lot to say about the original, both good and bad. To me it is a special game (my first solo purchase!) and possibly my favorite series in any game media. It is not, and never has been, a 10/10 game, objectively. Regardless I've had a 10/10 experience with the original for over 10 years now (and honestly the 2nd or OTR pick whatever.)    This "Deluxe Remaster" is mildly involved in bringing some beta/ alpha mechanics and designs, and removing some, that a lot of people have grown to love. Erotica is gone, but I never really interacted with it outside it's required usage because I only ever interacted with the camera when it was useful to my situation (PP Stickers, brutality/ horror/ drama/ outtake/ ~erotica~,  and the legendary no genre shots,) so this did not bother me much. The camera angles during some cut-scenes are seemingly "closer to the action" and while that is fine for the wide panned out shots, it is not for the close up personal ones. Heads get cut off and well I would appreciate an FOV slider I'll say that much. Personally I think the graphics (when bugs and errors are not present) are fine, the volumetric lighting is a cool edition but nighttime lacks that "video game" kinda vibe with the more realistic lighting.  Characters feel "just as" expressive as the original because they kind of weren't as finely animated (hair follicles/ body language/ eye/ mouth/ head movement) and now they do. (Irrelevant)   The voice acting is removable, should I ever get tired of hearing it, and overall is fine, but it would be great if some characters had better direction on their delivery.  TJ Rotolo made Frank work really well, too well even, so of course the new guy pales in comparison but he still did a good job of giving Frank a new breath of life, if only just this once. The most notable downgrades are Brad and Adam because the original VA's really put their damn feet in it. Nobody really got "upgraded" unless they didn't have a voice in the first place.   All of the areas now have gates attached to their loading zones, traversing the mall is UBER FAST now like skateboards are faster than the dang cars. Weapons have status bars, the durability of items has been adjusted and the animations have been adjusted for a more hit and run style of game play which means you do have to think just a touch more about your weapon arc and damage. Melee combos are easier to pull off in the modern control scheme, and after a few button swaps my brain adjusted just fine and I felt no loss in skill compared to the original (which to be honest was only challenging until I learned of the mini chainsaws.) Juice blenders have 1 more function and you can just make a quickste... "Fleetfoot" in the safe room.  You may also do a little "timeskip" if you want, it's just in the game now.Survivor AI is slightly more dependable, but once you've done a saint play through you should know the way to keep them safe every time regardless of if you give them supplies or not.  Some survivor interactions has been altered and none of it really effects the main story, just interpersonal dialogue. The comments YOUR survivors make will be more like "very unavoidable hints" and you may feel as if you're playing LAD 7/8 with how often they make them. The Boss fights AKA the Psychopaths/ Maniacs/ etc. are somewhat more challenging overall, and scale in a more linear fashion compared to the original. I was using abilities I never really wanted to before because it was just fun to pull of a good combo with snappier controls. It wasn't impossible to use abilities in the original, but they at least feel a bit more intuitive now. They removed some terminology and MASSIVELY redesigned a certain boss-fight, but I'm not really qualified to comment on that, nor do I want to use it as a wedge to insert politics into this game about exposing a massive government conspiracy while putting funny horse masks on zombies and dressing up in whatever outfit I want to so the cut-scenes look funny. (you can still ogle the pretty girls, son, you just don't get the pink circle.)   The game is just as difficult to get off the ground as ever if you really don't know how to level your Frank. Running the cycle I've always run in the beginning (as many PP stickers in the entrance/ paradise as I can and the plates/ treadmills etc) and while you do gain levels really quickly, bosses scale differently, and don't (easily) die in one shot. I'd recommend just playing casually your first time and seeing how far you can go before you reset if you even want to.   As a long time fan I really hope this is the breath of life that Dead Rising needs to maybe get a new game, with a new cast just doing what Dead Rising does best. This remake deserves the chance to stand on it's own legs via game-play merit alone. I recognize this is a long shot, but a true remaster like this also felt like a long shot for over a decade now. All in all this delivers almost everything I can ask for, and what it didn't, I can probably get with mod support, should mod makers be so kind and creative as they are known to be. No it's not a 10/10 because Dead Rising never was a 10/10. This remake was never going to change that no matter how successful it was. I enjoyed my time, if you don't like what they've done, then enjoy the OG to your heart's content.    The changes to infinity mode are actually really fun. Survivors and Bosses seem to spawn at random, certain NPC's and zombies will give you random drops from time to time. They cut the experience down by a LANDSLIDE as the skip time option is available, but no saving. Only built in suspending. A far cry from what Capcom asked of you on the 360/ PC ports (14 hours or more of your machine being on and running if there's no rest mode option and even then, the port crashes at certain points so you have to route around that.) Though if you don't want to use the timeskip, and you'd like to sit around in the Mall for 14 hours, go on ahead. It's a good way to get some challenges done without a hard time restriction. Just HP. It feels MUCH harder to not die in this mode, especially around the 3 day mark. I did not experience any crashes (except for my own skill issue) in the 6 Days and 18ish hours I survived for.   I'm glad I can give a genuine recommendation  (I have before, warts and all) this game to my friends and family now because I don't have to do the whole "well it's a bit tough and jank but it's got a lot of really cool ideas" song and dance because they have auto-save and some stairs by the vent. Not everyone is going to like this game, not everyone has to. I do, and I think this Remaster does a good job at being Dead Rising, not a perfect job, but a pretty damn good one.

_childDocuments_.review: Even though the graphics might make you think this is a remake, it's more in-between a remaster and a remake. The game feels exactly the same as the 2006 version, just with enhanced visuals and some QoL features such as auto-saving, moving while aiming (which honestly trivializes boss fights now, since they didn't change anything else about the encounters), and a compass replacing the arrow that now allows you track multiple objectives at once instead of only one. This game runs on the RE Engine which has produced some great visuals in the RE2-4 remakes but it doesn't look as near as impressive here. Maybe that was a design decision or consequence of being an 18 year old game basically copy and pasted into a new engine, not sure. The only reason I bring this up is that this game doesn't look near as impressive as RE4R, which had RT and this doesn't, yet it stresses my PC's temps much more (CPU runs about 10-15⁰C hotter), possibly due to Denuvo DRM. I didn't follow much about this game prior to launch other than it's announcement so maybe this on me, but I will say I was expecting a bit more. It has a "budget" price of $50, which is $10 less than the Resident Evil 2 remake cost in 2019, and that was a complete overhaul and brand new game. I wasn't expecting anything that drastic but overall, this is the same game that released in 2006 with some much needed QoL fixes. If you've already played through the original and want to do so again but in a more convenient way, I'd say this a good way to do that, since at it's core, the game will provide you lots of entertainment and replay value; just don't go in expecting some brand new game that plays entirely different: This is still Dead Rising 1, just with a new coat of paint.
