_childDocuments_.review: Some mixed feelings, partially due to some heavy bias towards the original, but overall I feel this is a good remaster. Lots of positive changes, though also a some negative ones, with many negatives being a matter of personal opinion.Overall though, when playing with classic controls, it managed to preserve the experience of playing the original game for the most part. I had a blast playing through the game again, and there were some great QoL changes that will likely make the game a lot more approachable to new players.There are way too many little changes to go over, but the things that stood out most to me were the difficulty and infinity mode changes.In terms of difficulty, they made the game as a whole a lot easier. Levelling happens much faster, and escorting survivors is significantly easier (Maybe even a bit too easy). Some psychopaths also seemed to have balance changes, making some easier and others harder, which is also a welcome change. My biggest issues are some of the changes to Infinity Mode though. It really took the wind out of my sails when I realized how much easier 7 Day Survivor became due to the ability to fast forward time at save points (which is a new mechanic in 72 hour mode as well, but I appreciate a lot more there). The survivor/psychopath locations being randomized at set intervals each day is a good change as well, though having their locations marked on the map kind of spoils the fun of that. Being able to suspend your session for infinity mode is really nice though as it can be a bit daunting to set aside roughly 14 hours in a single day just to attempt 7 Day Survivor mode in the original.I'd recommend turning some settings such as Survivor's being able to give you hints off though, as they'll tell you hidden item locations, which can take away some of the mystique you feel when finding little hidden places in each area on your own. I don't see myself coming back to the remaster very much and will probably just go back to the original game again whenever I want to replay Dead Rising, but I definitely really enjoyed playing this and felt it was worth my time.

_childDocuments_.review: As an avid fan of the Dead Rising series, I'd be hard pressed to recommend this over the original release version.That being said, if you've already played the original and are looking for something with a new coat of paint, some tweaks and QOL improvements then this might be for you, though I'm sure the latest Crowbcat has me agreeing there were definitely corners cut and unnecessary changes made.The addition of the time skip mechanic is okay, not something I think should be available from the start as I think it would make a first time player miss out on some of the content of the game. Traversing the mall during the downtime between cases, finding new survivors or just mowing down the undead with whatever was to hand was. All in all, I would recommend this really only to people who have played the original release and want an updated; graphically and game play wise, version of Dead rising. However, to a new player I would wholeheartedly recommend the original release. Though it may feel a little outdated, you simply cannot replicate the feel it has. P.S. wait for a sale, this game ain't worth the price tag they got on it.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising is one of those zombies games where you can just pop it on, enjoy walking around and throwing random objects at zombies.  Coming back to the deluxe remaster i realise that it wasn't just my nostalgia but the game itself holds up incredibly well. Now obviously it has had a "remaster" which drastically improves upon things you've already read like AI or aiming but a lot of the charm is still there. The characters are still goofy even with new voice actors and now with every character having a voice outside of "FRANK" really goes a long way. However that said I wish they didn't give so many hints all the time. Like if I'm fighting a boss just to have "Frank you're a photographer? Maybe you should photography that" - No I'm good some psychopath is trying to kill you. Oh and the lighting is amazing, particularly the flashlights on the rifles really give it a resident evil feel. I know some people have voiced their complaints around the censorship of the game, but to be honest it hasn't really impacted the game. The only thing that was slightly mishandled was a boss fight including a PTSD psychopath. They removed references to the Vietnam war and replaced with with something generic. While I don't mind the removal it might have been better to tie it in with something to do with a plot element (i won't spoil here) but I don't think it's the end of the world. I also have to say that the cut content return was a treat and really adds to the overall experience without negating the legacy of this game. Overall I think this is a solid package and anyone who is either a fan of DR already, fan of zombies or just want a sandbox to play around in should try dead rising. It was a hit in 2006, classic in 2016 and now a legendary classic in 2024. If Capcom wants to I would 100% love to see Dead Rising 2 and it's and all of it's expansions  come out as a remaster. It took me 19 hours to 100% baring in mind that I have already done this in the 2016 release back on console. 7 Day survivor is actually fun now. It took around 3 hours of play time but you are constantly moving with the new time mechanic which is still optional to engage with.

_childDocuments_.review: I won't say the game's perfect, but it still holds up decently well as a "remake". I know it won't capture the same magic and "perfection" we all praised the original game for. I'm just as bummed out as the next guy about the fact that Frank's OG voice actor was not involved. I love the rocket launcher addition (albeit it ironically feels underpowered at times) and the new blender magazine that allows you to create weapons. Plus I may be one of the few folks out there that didn't necessarily mind the new redesign of Larry Chiang. My biggest concern lies in the fact that zombie spawning is odd and buggy, which is very noticeable in areas such as the Maintenance Tunnels, where you can see zombies fading into the distance when revisiting a cleared-out portion or two. Another glitch I came across once was in the Wonderland Plaza section, where I could repeatedly kill a cop zombie and it would immediately respawn above its former carcass, which easily led to an infinite pile of pistols and bodies. Some minor other issues I have are the fact that during infinite mode, some psychopaths/survivors spawn already defeated/dead when entering their area for no particular reason. I also don't really like how the SMG and Spec Ops rifle fire rates are a lot slower compared to how they were in the video games. So far, those, plus the zombie spawning issues, had stuck out to me the most in terms of issues. If the developers are willing, I think this game will do a lot better overtime if or when they start doing patches and updates. Hopefully, this can also provide opportunities to bring in more content and perhaps address the censorship that a lot of people got pissed about (maybe as a dialogue option?). Though I'm probably being way too optimistic, so I can only hope things can patch up overtime with this game's current issues.  ...By the way, some of you guys keep using that word, "Woke". I do not think It means what you think it means.

_childDocuments_.review: tl;dr - Fine remaster/remake of the original.I don't really like them removing/changing some OG content for "reasons" (I'm not going into the whole DEI debate, the Internet can duke it out), but dang it, did they fix the survivor AI and infinity mode. Doing a perfect run, or even getting all achievements is no longer a dreadful chore, which can be a good or "bad" thing depending who you are.Survivors no longer self-implode the second you take your eyes off them. Fast forward feature also means that you no longer need to wait for hours just to make progress in infinity mode.There are also other QoL improvements as well. For starters, you wouldn't want to rip Otis in two anymore since getting attacked (or doing anything really) no longer cuts you off the ratio. All dialogues are all voiced and more importantly, can be skipped. This drastically improves replayability for folks who wanna bother with the escort quests.If there's one thing I want to criticize heavily is the dodgy performance in the maintenance tunnel. Despite nerfing the zombie count there *significantly*, the framerate and pacing is really weird over there. I'm rocking a 4090 so this is somewhat unacceptable in my eyes.Glitches and bugs are a thing tho I'd imagine they will get smoothed out with updates. Please don't be like in the OG where you *promised* to release a patch for the SDTV readability issue, only then to say "screw it" and tell people to buy a HDTV instead :)))))

_childDocuments_.review: Where Capcom's Resident Evil 2 Remake felt like it was trying to introduce the game to new people, DRDR feels like it isn't trying to garner a new audience or rejuvenate the franchise.Despite the game running on a whole new engine with a new voice cast, the game feels shockingly similar to its 2006 counterpart, so much so that I'm not sure if it's worth the price tag for people (like me) who are intimately familiar with the original.I was sure that - at least - a lot of the original's jankiness and balancing issues would be fixed, but to my surprise, the chainsaw-three-magazine combo is still here and as strong as ever, and the AI is still as dumb as ever (At least in my first playthrough. Even in the original, AI behaviour is very inconsistent).In terms of the changes it does make, the ones that stand out the most are the myriad quality of life changes, including, but not limited to:*The ability to skip time (although it can occasionally affect the pacing negatively.)*Having full control of Frank during radio transmissions*Blender in the security room*Multiple missions can be tracked at once*Skills are simpler to useA big change I've left out is the autosave system and that's because I think it actually harms the game. I'm not opposed to an autosave in DR, but this one feels overly aggressive in the way it saves the game after every single zone transition. This removes a lot of the tension in your treks through the mall as you almost always have a save to revert to from just a few minutes earlier (given how many zone transitions are throughout the mall) if anything goes wrong. I think what confuses me most is that there isn't an option to turn autosaving off for those who don't want to use it.To touch on the new voice cast, I think it's a downgrade in every capacity. At best, you get somebody doing a very good impression of the original character. At worst, you get a performance with the emotional range of Siri. Whether these issues are due to the actors themselves or the direction they were given, I'm not sure, but they're present regardless. There's also the censoring in this version. Most prominently, the 'erotica' photography genre has been removed, and a character's line about communism has been removed.To those with zero media literacy, this is the woke mob in full force ruining a video game. For others, it's the game removing outdated elements. For me, I find it a tad bothersome because I considered these to be aspects of the game's social commentary - the former, a commentary on the male gaze and the objectification of women, particularly as it pertains to the p*rn industry (admittedly, there are much better and more tactful ways of handling this kind of commentary), and the latter, a commentary on the bogey-man-like mentality most Americans harbour towards communism. Whether or not these were the intended interpretations, I'm not sure, but they certainly fall in line with the game's other themes (American consumerism being the big one).TL;DR /// Here's my verdict:If you're a fan of the original, you'll most likely enjoy DRDR given how closely its genetic makeup matches the 2006 classic. You'll most certainly appreciate the plethora of QoL improvements the game makes, although some changes (such as the new voice cast) might not be so appreciated. If you're new to the franchise, there's absolutely nothing wrong with starting here, but personally, unless you absolutely need modern visuals and some improved accessibility, I would recommend the 2016 remaster for the original voice acting alone.It's obvious why they chose to market this as a 'deluxe remaster' rather than a full on remake - it mostly is the same (great) game.

_childDocuments_.review: I just wrapped up 100% completing the game, so I'll keep this very short and simple: Then you'll appreciate all of the great quality of life features, including the ability to fast forward time, vastly improved survivor AI, new unlockables, restored cut content, and more! It might not be worth full price, but I'd say you're the intended audience for this game. And if you ever had a dreaded Xbox 360 Red Ring happen in your attempt to achieve 7 Day Survivor, I've got great news: The new fast forward feature works in that as well, along with the ability to suspend save! Then you'll love the improved controls and really grow to love all of the above changes. Some of the jank is still there, but it's the kind of jank you grow to appreciate after a while of playing. Then while I'll definitely say this is currently the best way to play it, there are some things here and there that got lost in translation (Some of them intentional), so while I do recommend you give this a playthrough, I'd also suggest playing the original right afterwards so you too can appreciate all of the new changes. The new voice cast is more hit than miss, and while Frank's new actor really grew on me the longer I played it (But just as David Hayter will always be Snake, TJ will always be Frank West), Stephen and Brad and definite downgrades. I'm also not one to harp on the other changes made, as they seem to be more for selling the game in other countries than anything else. You can still buy and play the original game if they do personally bother you, though.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster is an effective way of introducing new fans to the series while welcoming old fans with a fresh start after the series' long hiatus and a couple bad apples.It includes many quality-of-life improvements to the original including a wardrobe in the security room, allowing you to try on any item you've found in the mall; survivors with fully voice-acted lines and improved AI, an autosave feature (which proved to be very useful for me by the time the military arrived), and even some new items such as the Rocket Launcher, which was planned to be in the original game but scrapped.Despite these enhancements, the groundwork and clunky mechanics from the 2006 game are still present in many places. Small areas such as the grocery store, theater, and warehouse still have to be rendered separately as opposed to being connected to their greater regions. Survivors have slightly improved AI but are still prone to jumping into danger and getting killed immediately. Zombies still spawn in the warehouse elevator every time you use it, something that the devs felt was vital enough to keep in the game.To conclude, Deluxe Remaster holds many of the same issues as the original, but it delivers an experience that the franchise has been missing for so long, and it leaves me optimistic that someday a remaster of Dead Rising 2 will occur.

_childDocuments_.review: Here is my honest review of the game:- The game is ABSOLUTELY fantastic! As far as remasters go this is definitely one of the best I have ever played. The amount of quality of life changes made in this version is astounding. I was worried that time skipping would make the game too easy but to my surprise the way the game is made the fact you can time skip really doesn't change much in the grand scheme of things and definitely made infinity mode an actually fun mode to play not having to wait 14 real hours.- PP stickers having picture clues makes them so much easier to find and that's not a bad thing as a don't have to look up a 30 minute guide on how to find them all and can actually look for myself.- The achievement challenges are an amazing addition as well actually giving an incentive to 100% the game (Which I myself did within 3 days of release lol) as well as of course adding the closet where you can keep all the clothes you find and earn throughout the mall which is much better than running around the entire mall to assemble your favorite outfit.- The voice acting is good despite everyone's complaints, the only real reason I can think that people hate on it so much is because the love the original's voice acting which I personally agree is a lot better but that doesn't make the remakes voice acting "bad" by any means (though I am personally not a fan of Brad's voice in this version).My complaints about this remake:- Leveling is much too easy in this version.. I found myself at a much higher level in this version than the original at some points making the game feel a lot easier and hurting the replayability a bit.- Another complaint is of course the censorship.. and while I understand why the changes were made I do think that it did take away from the personality of the game a small amount.- The final (small) complaint I have is that the dlc costs an extra 10 bucks because I didn't buy the deluxe edition which a lot of companies seem to do but I still dislike, I don't think the extra costumes are worth another 20 bucks so I will sadly have to wait for a sale.BUT all in all I love this remaster and I really REALLY hope that capcom see's all these positives reviews left (I was worried it would get review bombed but thankfully not) and consider making a remake for the second game, I'd love to play it with a friend!

_childDocuments_.review: Okay. So. Dead Rising is VERY special to me and a lot of others. I personally, am In LOVE with this. HOWEVER. Here are my talking points.Voice Acting:It's. Acceptable. Barely. Truth be told, we knew this was going to be a downgrade from the iconic characters we know and love. I CAN say, I came to not mind New York Frank. The new side voices are actually really great, like Otis and the survivors. Brad remained a huge miss for me but with a few more replays, maybe I will connect more. Gameplay:It's outstanding. The best in the franchise hands down. There's been a clear re balance here. Everything is more quick. Damage intake and outtake is much higher and slightly jarring. Definitely still as rewarding though, I found. The challenge is here and while easier in my opinion than the original, it's welcomed and a different type of fun. It lets you play how you want. FINALLY. Don't like the new autosave system? Don't use it! Don't want to sit and wait for the next story scoop? Fast forward time! Costumes and collectibles? All in one place, dawg. Save and exit in Infinity Mode? Play how you want. It's. Faaaaaaantastic. Although Frank doesn't even say that anymore. WHY doesn't Frank say this anymore? It's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ iconic.The  Ahem. "Changes". Do I miss the Erotica tag? Honestly. Yes. Call me a gamer, but I do feel like we didn't need to take it out. Just maybe don't highlight it and I feel like everyone could have won. Not a big deal. Just personal opinion. Cliff's new dialogue, while it works, did throw off the vibe of the fight for me. I don't see anything wrong with the stereotypical American anti- communist PTSD trope. The changes made with Larry the butcher are fineeee. I guessssss. I diddd find it hypocritical that "someone" found the Chinese butcher too offensive but then in the same scene rip on fat Americans for eating too much meat. I will still refer to this version as "DEI Rising", but It is NOW in good faith. I do love the game and adopt it as a meme more than being upset about anything. There is a new rocket launcher weapon which I had a blast with and the new megabuster-while feeling slower, packs way more of a punch. Update:Bro. They added an easy difficulty. They think we're idiots. Gettin more and more disillusioned by this version the more it seems they are out of depth with what the player base actually wants. Getting DR4 coddling vibes again. How about a mode to turn off zombie boxes in Infinity mode? or anything fans are actually asking for? Thanks.Overall. If anyone is even reading this review, they're probably a fan of the original and can form these opinions themselves.

_childDocuments_.review: Another great game updated for modern hardware with a few quality of life improvements tossed in to even out the package. If you're the sort who wished the Resident Evil Remakes were more 1:1 in trying to preserve the original gameplay and mechanics then this is definitely what you want to be looking at. This does include some of the jank from the original too when it comes to animations, getting stun locked, and things like that but that's also part of the unique charm to the series which helps it stand out among a rather crowded zombie market these days. I will say it is a little pricey for what is on offer here. I feel like $40 at release would have been better in-line with what you get given that there's nothing really new, content wise, being added here. The original story returns along with Overtime and Infinite Mode as well as the multiple game runs to keep leveling up Frank while trying to save all the survivors. Performance wise it runs incredibly well for me pretty much staying locked 120 with some dips down to the 90's/80's in more open areas when first loading in. There is some pop-in in places like the park and maintenance tunnels too as the RE Engine is really being pushed here in terms of zombie count and all that. Still nothing that ruins the experience or leaves you wanting for more zombies. Had no problem racking up thousands upon thousands of kill during a single run. Only had one crash early on during the Father/Sons sniper fight. Picked up a rifle, game froze for a moment, and then just closed. Autosave put me right back at the start of the fight so didn't really lose anything, just a bit annoying. Outside of that zero issues from start to finish. I have heard Infinite Mode has some bugs but I haven't spent a great deal of time with it at the time of writing this review. If I do encounter any issues I'll update this with the necessary information. Really hoping we see Dead Rising 2 get this treatment.

_childDocuments_.review: (Quick Note: I'm writing this after I completed my first playthrough of the story mode.)A well done "remake" of the original. The graphics, mainly pertaining to the facial animations of the main cast, really do help sell their emotions during cutscenes. The gameplay, with it's small tweaks and additions, really did make it fun to go through Willamette Mall once again!A nice new addition, was the way they handled clothing! Having clothing you put on be saved to the lockers in the Security Room, and having certain clothes tied to achievements, makes me want to keep playing! I want to go through all the achievements, just to see what clothes they unlock. However, I do miss some of the suit recolors we had, right at the start of the original game. I wish they were still there...perhaps a few might be tied to achievements this time around?The new voice actors did a solid performance, though I'd still prefer to have the original VAs again (whether it's the actual audio from the OG game, or a re-record with the old VAs.) I especially enjoyed that every survivor you came across, had a voice this time around. It really did make me care more about them, than I did in the original. Especially because they're no longer annoying to escort! xD The smarter AI for survivors was VERY VERY APPRECIATED... I got used to Jas Patrick's voice for Frank West rather quickly! If we do get future Dead Rising games that include Frank, I would still prefer if TJ Rotolo could return to playing the character. Also, if there can be an update to this game, where they bring back TJ and possibly the rest of the old cast, that'd be FANTASTIC!Honestly, I think the two new VAs that stood out the most, were Tiana Camacho as Isabela Keyes, & Kevin Andrew Rivera as Adam MacIntyre! Tiana felt right in the role, & Kevin's sounded so close to the original performance! I'm amazed how well they pulled it off.I'm gonna get more playthroughs in, and I hope newcomers to the franchise do pick this up! If this game sells well, I really do hope it means that we can get actual sequels, and/or a "deluxe remaster" of all of Dead Rising 2 (DR2, DR2 OTR, Case Zero, & Case West)! If we do get DR2 again, please try to get some of the original main cast in this time!Again, I hope this game sells well, and thank you Capcom for attempting to faithfully revive this franchise! Let's hope it works! <3

_childDocuments_.review: It seems as though using ReShade causes the game to crash repeatedly which is why I had hard time getting past the beginning section. Other than that, this is a great remake that keeps the core gameplay intact, and although it takes some liberties with certain story elements (particularly psychos), I am having a really enjoyable time revisiting such a classic. Voice acting differences can be a bit jarring, mainly because so many of us have become accustomed to the original, but it honestly isn't as bad as people are making it out to be (the addition of Otis having a voice, and voiced by Dave Fennoy no less is a big win). The only thing I hope is that this can in some way revitalize the IP and start getting the Resident Evil treatment in the future, so long as they don't half-ass it or remove any semblance of what made the original games so special.

_childDocuments_.review: Capcom has set the gold standard for remakes with their latest reimagining of the legendary *Dead Rising*. This beloved classic, originally released in 2006, has received a fresh coat of paint and a slew of new gameplay features that make it a must-play for both veterans and newcomers alike.One of the most exciting aspects of this remaster is the opportunity to experience the stunning visuals powered by the RE Engine in the new version. The thrill of wielding that iconic Rocket Launcher feels even more satisfying this time around, bringing a sense of realism that enhances the overall experience.However, it's essential to clarify that this is a remaster, not a full remake. While the game has its fair share of technical hiccups—bugs that can occasionally detract from the fun—the core gameplay remains as exhilarating as it was in 2006. For those willing to overlook these issues, *Dead Rising* retains its charm and intensity.One of the standout improvements is the new control scheme. Players can opt for the classic controls reminiscent of the original or take advantage of the updated layout inspired by *Resident Evil*, which makes for a smoother and more intuitive gaming experience. This thoughtful addition opens the door for new players to jump in without feeling overwhelmed.Yet, not all changes hit the mark. The game suffers from a lack of ambience and sound effects at times, leaving certain areas feeling a bit empty and soulless. However, the most significant upgrades lie in the AI improvements. Gone are the days of frustratingly incompetent characters; the new and improved AI enhances the overall experience, making objectives feel less tedious and more engaging. Otis, in particular, is less of a nuisance, allowing players to enjoy the game’s flow without unnecessary interruptions.While some old dialogue and character interactions have been altered, the remaster successfully strikes a balance between nostalgia and modernization. It’s a thrilling time to be a *Dead Rising* fan, as this version breathes new life into the classic formula while honoring what made the original special.In summary, *Dead Rising Remaster* is a fantastic homage to its predecessor, and I highly recommend it for both long-time fans and those new to the franchise. Despite its bugs and occasional sound issues, the fun factor remains high, and it's clear that Capcom has put considerable effort into enhancing this iconic title. Whether you’re reliving the past or discovering it for the first time, this game promises a wild ride through the zombie apocalypse. Don’t miss out!

_childDocuments_.review: Damn, I just typed out this really long review and then hit "Add Comments," erasing the whole thing. Here's my second rushed attempt.--TL;DR If you haven't played the original, this isn't a half-bad game. I don't think it's worth $50 or $60, but I could be persuaded with some light debating; the acting may be better in this game than in any game I've played since. But if you've played the original, apart from some quality of life improvements, you'll find that it's not a "remaster" it's a money grab, hyped up as revisiting the original in the series, but is actually a re-branding as a more generally acceptable title in the way of content and difficulty. --Here's the thing. This game is not a simple remaster. Capcom has changed some aspects of the game that make it worse than the original and frankly make it a bad game in general. In the trailer, it looks like they've added some content to the cut scenes, but they haven't. They added an intro. It's not worth even mentioning, in my opinion, except to deceive people into thinking they added new content. If anything, they removed a lot from the game, maybe changing it to lower the parental rating. I'm not sure.Here's what I'd consider improvements: Lighting, mood, model textures, aiming system, quality of life change to achievements, and some of the new costumes are amusing.My list of complaints is much longer. It's not even about the differences between the original game and this one; it's about how this game doesn't feel complete and falls short of being a modern AAA game, but with the matching price tag. For brevity, let me keep it to the top 3.1. The game is so much easier. In the first game, you had to plan out game saves and slog through restarts, and leveling up meant you might learn a skill that literally changed the game, almost making you want to start over again just so you could experience how awesome it is to roll away from being attacked. Meanwhile, in the remaster, I got to level 50 on my first playthrough and was only ever killed by Kent when he chains you to the statue. The game is now so easy that you probably won't spend the time on the game. When I buy a modern AAA game, I pay between $0.25 to $1 for an hour of gameplay when the game costs between $60 and $120. In this game (I could have every achievement by now if it weren't for game crashes), I'm pretty much done at hour 40 because it's so easy. And I imagine the average player is going to get half of that. So you'll probably pay $1.50 to $3.25 for an hour of gameplay. Not that making it more difficult makes it somehow worth your money, but the experience of having to struggle, earn, strategize, lose and then win is just not there. It's a breeze. There's no incentive to explore or experiment.2. You don't really have to help the survivors survive. They mostly manage on their own. There are even some books to help you out in the remaster. In the original, you had to repeatedly help them make it from point A to B until you got them through. You had to get to know the 50+ survivors. Were they going to dominate with a hunting knife? Could they be trusted with a gun? Would they help others? Are they more prone to getting injured? Can they take a lot of damage? Do you need to hold their hand more often, or are they better at surviving than you'll ever be? There was a lot of immersion in the original version because of this system. This was the game. To see it cast aside and to have paid them to do it is like a slap in the face.On an aside, why can't I point across the level for the survivors, but I can shoot bad guys to death who don't even know I exist? And what is this prestige system? It does nothing. I spent some time trying to figure it out, but it's all just a waste of time. And if you're going to rebuild this system, why not tell me when everyone is close enough that they'll go to the next area? This exists in later Dead Rising games. I just don't get it. Saving the other people is now the worst it's ever been in the series in the newest game of the series.3. Close combat is broken. This may be my biggest complaint. The close combat in the original game was spot on. It was organic, and you'd get a feel for how fast, far and recoverable an attack was, and you could rely on it. I didn't realize how great of a mechanic this was. In the original, it may have been revolutionary. In this game, the fact that it's so unreliable makes it aggravating. I'll load up on guns rather than take the katana (my favorite weapon in the original) because I keep getting hit in a situation I shouldn't, or I miss, or the camera will spin the wrong way, or Frank will swing the wrong way, or zombies will spawn behind me, or it won't kill/knock over one zombie who then grabs me, or maybe I get grabbed three times in a row without being able to attack back or escape by two completely random zombies out in the open. I'm spending more time learning where the guns are and using them instead of picking up a bench and clobbering the zombies like this series is begging me to do because it's unpredictable and not fun.If you're still reading, thank you. But here's the last thing. This game crashes like crazy. I've not had a game crash on my like this in a long time. I can't even get to day 5 in the infinite mode because the game crashes so much. Mostly when loading between levels but during a couple of boss battles. Also, I haven't had a game crash Windows since Windows 98, and this game did it once, which was impressive. I got the blue screen of death, which I forgot existed.

I have encountered multiple bugs which range from re-spawning one of the convicts upon entering the park each time, to Jo's captured survivors just not appearing (apart from Kay).Also, several times I've been walking along when suddenly I get hit by an invisible enemy again and again until death. While that can be kind of funny, I think I'd prefer to have a properly functioning remaster instead.Beyond that, the sound design is not good. _childDocuments_.review: A Fresh Coat of Blood – Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster ReviewOverall Rating: 8.5/10Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster brings Frank West’s wild zombie escapade back to life with upgraded graphics, quality-of-life improvements, and a few new surprises for fans of the original. Capcom has taken this iconic 2006 classic and given it the polished, modern feel it deserves without losing the chaotic charm that made it so beloved. While the remaster maintains the original’s focus on creativity and open-world freedom, some dated mechanics hold it back slightly from achieving perfection in the remaster space.Visuals and Graphics : 9/10The Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster gives the game a stunning visual update, taking full advantage of modern hardware. The textures are noticeably sharper, with detailed character models and dynamic lighting that breathe life into the bustling, zombie-filled Willamette Parkview Mall. Frank’s camera now captures even more detail, letting players appreciate the upgraded environment and the sheer madness of zombie hordes. The increased frame rate also means the action runs more smoothly, and the new lighting effects make the mall feel both more alive and more threatening than ever.The graphical overhaul is impressive, and the enhanced visuals make exploring the mall a more immersive experience, highlighting the wild, unpredictable nature of the zombie outbreak and the gritty industrial backdrop of the mall itself.Gameplay and Combat : 8/10The remaster preserves Dead Rising's signature blend of horror, humor, and creativity, with the combo weapons system updated to be more accessible and less cumbersome. The freedom to experiment with everyday objects—from benches to mannequins and garden tools—is as fun and absurd as ever. The game’s weapon variety remains a joy to explore, allowing players to experiment with everything from chainsaws to golf clubs in taking down hordes of zombies in increasingly bizarre ways.Capcom has made some quality-of-life improvements, like smoother aiming controls and more forgiving hit detection, which help the game feel less clunky by modern standards. The save system has also been reworked, allowing for more flexible saving options, a welcome change from the original game’s stricter mechanics. While the classic time-sensitive structure remains, the remaster includes a more relaxed “Sandbox Mode” for players who prefer exploring the mall without the constant pressure of a ticking clock.Story and Characters : 6/10The story of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster remains true to the original, following photojournalist Frank West as he documents the zombie outbreak in Willamette. The narrative is mostly unchanged, sticking to its mix of horror and satire, with Frank’s deadpan humor shining as he navigates the chaos.That said, the character interactions and voice acting retain the charm of the original but may feel a bit dated. Frank’s cheesy one-liners and exaggerated dialogue add to the game’s dark humor, though some scenes lack the polish and emotional depth players may expect from a modern game. Still, fans will appreciate the iconic moments and hilarious exchanges that have become part of Dead Rising’s legacy.Sound and Music : 8/10The sound design has been improved to enhance immersion, with clearer audio effects and re-recorded lines that add a crispness to the experience. Zombie moans, weapon sounds, and mall ambiance all contribute to a more immersive experience, helping the remaster feel both modern and true to its roots. The updated soundtrack blends tense themes with more whimsical, jazzy tracks, providing a unique tone that bridges horror and dark humor.Replayability and New Features : 10/10Replayability has always been a strength of Dead Rising, and the Deluxe Remaster stays true to that legacy with both the main story and Sandbox Mode offering players plenty to do. The remaster also introduces new challenges and optional objectives, adding extra layers of challenge for players who want to fully explore and survive everything the mall has to offer.All DLC is bundled into the Digital Deluxe package with unique outfits and Background Music. These additions provide new ways to customize and experiment in the game, allowing players to approach the chaos of Willamette with a fresh sense of style and creativity.Conclusion : 8.5/10Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster successfully revitalizes a cult classic, merging nostalgic gameplay with modern enhancements that make it enjoyable for both returning fans and new players. The polished visuals, quality-of-life upgrades, and additional content make it the definitive way to experience Frank West’s unforgettable first encounter with the undead.While the core mechanics still feel slightly dated, and some character interactions may seem simplistic, these minor drawbacks don’t overshadow the thrill and humor at the heart of Dead Rising. It’s a bloody good time and a wonderful return to the chaotic, satirical world of zombie-infested Willamette. Whether you’re wielding unusual weapons or simply surviving against the odds, Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster offers a reimagined classic that’s more entertaining than ever.

_childDocuments_.review: TLDR; If you are debating whether to play this version or the original, play the original first. I'll talk about the positive and then the negative.For positives, this game plays a whole lot smoother and better than the previous version. The PC port of the original is fantastic but you can feel the clunky design that Dead Risings first version had, especially when it came to inputting special attacks. The AI is improved and functions more autonomously without need for 100% babysitting, especially when armed. This is actually probably one of the most important things in the game to get right, so I am glad they did it.There is also new content added, with nice things like new books like one for fist damage and extra skills, skateboarding tricks, probably some I missed as well. Challenges also now exist which add more cosmetics and give you intensives to try new things.The graphical quality is significantly improved as well, with modern day lighting quality that big budget games tend to have. Nothing stuck me as "amazing" but it all just looked good. The ability to move and shoot, as well as the bullets coming from the center of the screen and not from franks gun does lead itself to some cheese, more on that later. The new versions of the music are good, as well as the sound effects for most things felt fine. The new menus and UI, for the most part, are also an improvement and a lot of quality of life changes were made. Honestly, as far as gameplay goes, it all just felt good and that's a good thing. Another really nice touch is that every NPC is fully voice acted in this, which I really appreciate. But onto the negatives, lets start with that same point. The voice acting is an almost universal downgrade and many of the tones of moments were lost due to this. Many main characters lacked character due to these issues. While many of the main cast try to do a good job, you definitely notice the ones who don't when you play the original. While Franks voice is alright, he does a good job, but unfortunately he just doesn't really sound like Frank. The main offender is probably Brad, who's voice actor completely misses the mark in every moment that it would matter. This is generally the trend you'll notice throughout, where Brad is definitely saying the same lines, but without the intensity, passion or emotion. I found some better voice acting from some of the minor NPCs that you escort back to the safe room. The grocery store clerk was another good example, where the iconic screaming was just not present at all as the VA could not even match half of the intensity of the original.But that's not all, there were some unnecessary changes to things that are now censored. Now I actually don't have an issue with some of it. Larry the Butcher's original model and VA from the OG Dead Rising might be one of the most racist portrayals of a Chinese man I've ever seen and came from an era where Japan really didn't like China, which has since improved as time has gone on. I understand the censorship of this character, however I do kind of wish they were still noticeably Chinese. Other changes are the removal of the Erotica stat when taking photos, which on it's own is understandable even if I don't agree with it, but then in the police officer Jo psychopath fight, they kept all the erotic material in that, even the sexual assault implications, as well as many of the in-cutscene ass/chest shots. It seems rather odd to be picky and choosy about what material is acceptable in the same umbrella. The last censorship thing I noticed was the removal of the Vietnamese war veterans lines about the Vietcong and communists. I do not see any reason this should have been removed, it was unnecessary and I cannot imagine who would be offended by this. On top of it, it's removal was half-assed and the replacement is flat and comes across as much less impactful as a result. It just feels really strange to do that.Onto other issues, difficulty. The original game is rather hard, with aggressive lunge-heavy zombies and a very slow level up system. Survivor AI was especially challenging to manage which both added charm and added more frustration. The AI in this game is remarkably easier, but it also tends to remove some of the difficulty as a result and isn't replaced by something else. On top of that, you level up anywhere between 2x to 3x faster in the Remake. This resulted in me hitting Level 50, the max level, in the last few stretches of the game which was probably their intent. But in the original, you would likely have to do a second playthrough to get to level 50, with people probably reaching about 25 to 30 if they complete the entire game in one playthrough. On top of this, it makes the game even easier as I had access to very useful tools and a lot of health and inventory space right off the bat. This also compounded with speed upgrades, which made time management easier and made the PP gains easier as well, in a self fulfilling cycle. I don't think this is wrong, but the game was very easy as a result. The guns also trivialize the game, with the damage being especially strong if you pick up the new "firearm damage" skill book, combined with the ability to shoot around corners due to the bullets coming out of the center of the gun, instead of the gun itself. And even if you die a lot, new autosaves will generally save you.Some of the graphics did not get the same love as the original game. The gas station explosion in the beginning actually looks better in the original despite being an xbox 360 launch title, with heat waves and much more smoke and fire. The new explosion looks very very cheap by comparison. Brads disembowelment in the parking garage looked way less gruesome and way less impactful, with a lot of the horror of the moment being lost. The lighting especially ruins some of the moments with much more brightly lit environments when it shouldn't be. The mall was very dark, in a good way, at night.And lastly, the biggest issue of the remake so far and the one that will likely be fixed, is the crashing. My playthrough of Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster (which is a Remake) had actually crashed over 15 times in my 12 or so hour session. The crashes reduced when I deleted "Crash Handler" exe and dll from the games files. The fact this exists at all is embarrassing, but even without it, crashed plenty of times. Luckily the autosave at least managed to reduce progress lost when it occurred, but this is still unacceptable. Zombie pop-in was very high and framerates were uneven and a little poor, but mostly ran okay.To conclude the review, ill tldr it.This remake (despite being called a remaster) is very good where it counts as far as gameplay improvements and the like, but it does remove a bit too much from the original in terms of content and difficulty.The original is still on steam and still very good and I recommend playing that over this, despite all the nice things this has going for it, as I feel this version of the game is inferior to the original, but is a treat for returning players who won't mind the poor voice acting and easier difficulty. If you are debating whether to play this version or the original, play the original first.

_childDocuments_.review: A pretty faithful remaster/remake of the Xbox 360 classic.If you somehow haven't played Dead Rising already, it is a third-person hybrid of a survival horror and a beat-em-up that puts you in control of Frank West, a photojournalist who travels to rural Colorado to investigate an anonymous tip for the biggest news story of the century. This mysterious scoop sees him airdropped into a shopping mall in the middle of zombie-infested town, where he has three days to uncover the conspiracy on why the dead are rising...or die trying.- A simple but satisfying gameplay loop of scavenging the mall for supplies, killing huge hordes of zombies, defeating psychos, and rescuing wayward survivors. Frank starts off extremely weak but steadily ramps up into a proper zombie-destroying badass by level 50, giving this game one of the most satisfying power progressions I can recall in any game ever.- Playing into the solid power progression from point 1 is a wide array of hand-to-hand techniques you can unlock including things such as a lariat, an RKO, a suplex, two jump kicks, and even barehanded disembowelment. Although weapons are always helpful, you won't  them to deal with basic zombies once you are sufficiently leveled up.- The impressive scale of having dozens upon dozens of zombies on screen can't be overstated. It was cool back in 2006 on the Xbox 360 and it's cool now, especially with the upgraded graphics on offer from the RE Engine.- Although dismissed by some as baseless shock content, the human bosses (called psychopaths in game) you encounter are very well-done in my opinion. They are excellent examples of showing seemingly normal people who suddenly 'snapped' when confronted with the horrible trauma of a zombie outbreak. This also reinforces the subtle message that maybe the zombies aren't the only monsters in our midst.- Time in the game world advances as you play, albeit at an accelerated rate. Both story and side missions are time-sensitive and can be missed if you goof off, forcing you to wisely manage your time. This also prevents the gameplay from getting stale by shuttling you from objective to objective with breaks in the zombie-filled sandbox in between.- New auto-save feature removes a ton the frustration from the old version while preserving most of the challenge. It won't save you in every situation (such as if you auto-save with not enough time left to complete a particular scoop) but it can help with retrying boss fights.- Survivor AI, while not perfect, has been vastly improved compared to the Xbox 360 version. This is good, as you will get the lion's share of your XP for leveling up by escorting other survivors who are trapped in the mall to safety.- You can carry over Frank's power level to subsequent playthroughs. This is excellent if you happen to lock yourself into an undesirable outcome, you can restart the game with a big advantage to regain your lost progress.- Lots of cool little environmental details hidden in the mall reward you for exploring and experimenting. Such things include using ovens to cook frozen pizzas, using stoves to cook steaks, and using blenders to mix potions for temporary stat buffs.- Some of the writing is hit or miss. The game has some sort of social commentary against mass consumerism, but has a hard time selling it given how goofy some of the lines and their delivery are.- Although it's not really necessary to use, which is funny given how the main character is a journalist, there is also a photography system involving Frank's camera. Snapping suitably gory, funny, or dramatic photos will earn you bonus XP. There are also special locations/items you can film, such as statues and storefronts, that will also give you big bonus XP.- The erotic photo category has been removed from the photography system. I think removing it is dumb and was done to, ironically enough, appease journalists who aren't even going to buy the game, but it's not a huge deal as the system is superfluous to begin with.- There is a new system where each survivor has a set of favorite items and they will...trust you more...if you give them what they like? I don't know, I never used this system once and it never seemed to penalize me for ignoring it. As long as you don't pointlessly attack your followers they won't turn on you.- The balancing on the psychopath bosses ranges from being easy-ish to infuriating, especially for a clueless first time player who is starting at level 1. This does, however, make killing annoying bosses, such as the roaming trio of convicts, extremely memorable on the first time.- There is some definite issues with stun-locking and enemies that use firearms, the special forces commandos being the main perpetrators of this.- As stated above, you will get the lion's share of your XP from escorting random survivors around the mall to safety. This essentially means a huge chunk of the game is locked behind escort missions, which might be a deal breaker for some people. The survivor AI has been improved, but there are still instances where they will suicidally charge into hordes of zombies and cause extreme frustration.- There is some microstutter when entering crowded areas. Hopefully this can be patched out, as the game otherwise performs beautifully on my RTX 3070.Dead Rising was well-worth the day one purchase to me, and is an easy buy for anyone who happens to love chaotic sandbox games or zombies. Pick this one up if you want to relive the "ye olde zombie craze" of the late 2000's/early 2010's, this game is one of the first that started the trend and there is a good reason for it.

While escorting and not being eaten alive, they'll make comments about the area and may give tips. And with better pathing, I have a lot less trouble escorting them.My main two negatives so far are small ones. First, I noticed quickly that the loading screens are very minimalist, with only the time and a loading bar. This is fine and can actually dramatize the tense moments when you might be late to save somebody, but I prefer the photos and film reels of the original. The second is the modern controls, which are ALMOST perfect. However, I wish there were a way to use Dead Rising 2: OTR's camera controls (aim down sides + right bumper), because I'd love to use the bumpers to switch weapons, but don't want to deal with the original game's terrible roll input. (not hard, just annoying)Even with those small issues, I've gotten used to the D-pad for switching pretty quick, and all the new additions have me smiling and enjoying this return to Dead Rising 1. I hope this game will bring us to a new era of the series that sticks to the charm of the first and second game!

I would've loved to see some features from Dead Rising 2 implemented, such as alternate weapon attacks and icons notating when a survivor is able to transition to the next area but the quality of life changes present are still a nice touch. I am not entirely sure why they opted to get all fresh new voice actors when the dialogue in cutscenes is pretty much untouched, which translates to the same lines being repeated by new voices outside of changing Cliff's dialogue and some of Kent's. I do think Dead Rising has some really good bones, so I get wanting to keep a large majority in tact, but I think the original had room to improve and they didn't try to do so here.All-in-all, I do recommend the Deluxe Remaster, but I think Capcom played it a little too safe to the point where if you played the original the most you're getting here are new graphics and some QOL changes.

_childDocuments_.review: As far as remasters go, this is exactly what I would hope for. Absolutely faithful to the original but brought into present day. Dead Rising is one of my all time favourite games and the remaster makes it look and play so much better than the original. All the pain points, the janky interactions such as responding to Otis on the radio or escorting a survivor are tidied up and features such as using the camera are expanded upon with the option to pick up camera parts. The quality of life improvements like being able to change your outfit in the safe room and pass time at save points are very welcome as well. The downloadable content included with the digital deluxe edition is also a lot of fun, who doesn't want to walk around Willamette in a Nemesis costume whilst his BGM plays around the mall? 10/10 - fantastic remaster.

_childDocuments_.review: Normally I wait to write a review either when I beat a game or get all of the achievements. But with this being a remake and I've quite recently gotten all of the achievements in the OG Dead Rising. Currently as im making this review, I had just killed Adam the Clown and unlocked the shortcut The game runs well on max setting i rarely if at all ran into lag or massive frame drop in or out of the mall.  I did run into weird texture popping when in the helicopter, but when thst was over it was smooth with no popping. (Unless you want to count the zombies, but that i believe was in the original but I could be wrong)The new VA are fine nothing against any of them if you're someone new to the dead rising franchise thenits not a big deal. But if you've played the original back on the 360 or even the re-release then it'll throw you off. I would have loved an option to be able to switch between the new VA or the original, but im sure with this being on the RE engine we'll get a mod in no time. Also giving a voice to Otis and every single survivor amazing giving them all more personality.The UI is hit or miss for me, I don't like the way the inventory looks being so small and having boxes empty away on the side of it, I'd like to be able to use the original inventory but its whatever, also being able to have multiple quest selected is great.The AI ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ this is the greatest thing, I've never had a smoother time taking 4 survivors  across the park while being chased by the convicts ever before. This is by FAR the best thing about the remake having fixed AI and not having to baby the survivors the whole time.And last bosses which I feel like is the staple of dead Rising is still there with the original songs (at least for Adam and the Convicts) is still there, so you'll still hear "WELLLLLLL" every time you walk out to the park. Again I could be widely mistaken but even after killing all three convicts at least two of them would spawn back every time, always thinking it was the next day till they responded but I guess its free PP.Overall id say this is better in many ways but treat it like the RE4 remake id recommend playing both. The original still good behind all the jank, and should be played. (You know as long as they don't pull a Fromsoft and remove it from the store later on)

_childDocuments_.review: Hands down the best way to experience a classic game in the modern day.Since the moment I got my hands on it, I have been completely amazed. The game sticks to the original material extremely well, and has an incredible level of detail that was just not possible with the original hardware back in 2006.The graphics are spectacular, the survivor AI changes are spectacular, being able to move while aiming is SPECTACULAR. Even the modest changes to the camera like giving us filters, attachable parts, and adding tilt controls are all amazing additions that don't subtract from the original experience in the slightest.Playing through this remaster has revitalized my love for the original, and has genuinely restored my faith in CAPCOM to do good by this series and make up for the 4th game. This game is definitely worth it if you're a fan of the original, or even if you've never played a DR game before!I'm still working to 100% all of the achievements, but from what I've seen so far- this is by far worth your time and you won't be disappointed.
_childDocuments_.name: Dead Rising Deluxe Remaster

_childDocuments_.review: If there was a neutral option for review, I'd probably use it. So far, this remaster has done nothing to justify its existence.The graphical upgrades are cool for the mall itself (characters not so much) but some areas, like outside in the park during certain times of day look terrible and washed out as they did in the trailers. In fact, a lot of areas look really washed out, I imagine some LUT mods and reshades will start popping up soon if they haven't already. They somehow couldn't replicate the almost perfect mirror reflections from the original either which is alarming.Voice acting just doesn't hold a candle to the original. If you're a first-time DR player this wouldn't mean anything but for the ones who grew up on the original, I'm sure some will agree that a lot of the voices feel off and don't have the same effect.I also can't get over what they did to Frank. He looks like Munch from Oddworld and is built like a vending machine.The game is way too easy. The iconic prisoner bosses are somehow more idiotic than before. I also took the 50. cal from the prisoner's vehicle and used it alongside the firearm magazine to kill Adam the clown in 4 seconds (literally). He didn't even have a chance to move from his starting spot.Escorting survivors is better, they don't run head-first into a zombie's clutches anymore. The suggestions given by survivors while escorting feels out of place though, like Capcom sprinkled some Dragon's Dogma 2 on top.Zombies are also phasing in within view. Same goes for if you've just cleared an area, look away then look back again. Boom, zombies are back. Understandable for 2006, not really for 2024.Just a few things I've picked up on in the 2 hours I've played so far. Giving it a positive review for now because Dead Rising in itself in a fun game and newcomers to the franchise is always a good thing. There's just some strange design choices, particularly with the characters and voice acting that make me shake my head.

_childDocuments_.review: One of the best remasters/remakes out there, hands down. I think people complaining about it being too easy are just too used to the original Dead Rising, which is balls busting difficult and sometimes unforgiving to the player. I'm not gonna be upset that there is a more casual experience to enjoy, especially for people getting into the series. Automatic saving is a massive plus, AI that actually works is a plus, and little changes and details that overall make the experience far more smooth. Are some of the psychopaths, such as the prisoners, maybe a bit too easy? Sure, you can make that claim, but it doesn't bother me at all. Is the yellow paint in the beginning odd? Sure, but it's literally only in the food court, and it's pretty much not noticeable past that case. Is it easier to level up? Absolutely, but that doesn't change the flow of the game that much at all.And of course, the game itself is absolutely stunning. The textures look great, the models are great, and the overall atmosphere and vibe is incredible. The voice acting, which I was concerned about since the trailers, was ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ superb, and having all the survivors be able to talk to you is quite nice too. The voice acting somehow makes Aaron Swoop not hateable, though I think that's also because his AI, alongside everyone else, was massively improved. If you've never played a Dead Rising game, I'd absolutely recommend this remake, and then to try out the original. Both are fantastic, and worth your time exploring everything. It's good to see something great come out of this franchise again.

_childDocuments_.review: Dead Rising is EASILY my favorite Capcom game, hell, my favorite zombie game. I won't be leaving a review for the original on steam (It's got a lot of issues and just isn't the full OG Dead Rising Experience) But to say the least, amazing game. Now, on to DRDR. Amazing but flawed. More than anything, I was so excited to see Dead Rising built up from scratch in the RE Engine, and I can say they delivered. The game looks wonderful, the mall is beautiful and welcoming, the characters look amazing, and most item/weapon models are neat and improved. I PERSONALLY, think they did a wonderful job taking the mall from the original, and just making it prettier.The gameplay feels fresh, but still the same. I don't really have much to say about gameplay, it feels the same, while still feeling somewhat fresh. Though, a few things I was hoping they'd add to this. Moving while aiming is nice, but feels pointless when you have to stop to shoot?? And I know it was a long shot, but I was hoping for the item system from DR3, being able to pick up items while moving and use consumables felt so nice and always kept you on your feet, but It's not a huge issue to not see it here.AI is really improved, there's this new "Affinity" system which is kinda nice, you can see what weapons or food items Survivors prefer, and upon receiving them, they're more effective in combat. (Some survivors still got stuck on geometry though) Story is the same, I dunno. The hud is kinda ugly in my opinion it just feels like a prototype, but the pause menu and map are beautiful. I love the added challenge list and PP Sticker album, makes keeping track of stuff a lot easier. I'm a sucker for menus. The "Level Up" pop-up is really nice too.The costumes and outfits are really nice. Bringing the DR3 outfit locker mechanic was a great idea, I love collecting all the outfits around the mall and just switching to whatever I want whenever I want.There's a few new items also, nothing major. The Rocket Launcher is here after being cut from the OG, We got a couple new Books, and the camera has some Upgrades you can find too.Some items apparently have new move sets? I personally haven't noticed any of them yet though.I did, however, notice that it seems to me like some items just can't be picked up now?? Like, maybe it's just me, but I never found a store sign I could pick up like in the OG, which was odd.AND the only major bug I think I saw, was that the Cutscene for zombie Jessie never played for me, and thus I never got to find her in the Safehouse.Really, I do recommend this for die hard Dead Rising fans, a lot of the same Dead Rising jank is intact, while adding some new issues sadly, but I can't complain too much. Was this a cash grab by capcom? Yes, easily. But, it wasn't so poorly done that I feel like 0 love went into making this. I hope this sparks new life into the Franchise and we get more Dead Rising stories. Leave frank alone though, dudes been through enough, and DR4 did him DIRTY. Let's just forget that game all together, hopefully they use this Remaster/Remake to wipe the slate clean and fix some mistakes they made in later entries.

_childDocuments_.review: Very faithful remaster of a very fun game!Gameplay feels just like the original, with key improvements to movement and controls (rebinds, moving while shooting, etc). Lots of great QoL improvements (autosave, overhauled infinity mode, outfit storage, better survivor AI), kept the AMAZING soundtrack, and has a bunch of really fun new unlockables that do everything from add new minor mechanics, to giving a few pseudo "cheat codes", to making previously useless weapons not just relevant but flashy and powerful!There are new voice actors for everyone(?) so that all previously unvoiced lines could now be voiced. The new voices are sometimes a different flavour from the original, but they fit well and even the few that were a bigger shift have settled in for me. While I am a HUGE fan of the original voices still, the new ones are excellent as well once my ears had become accustomed to them from characters I had heard with different voices for almost 2 decades.As of writing the this review, there are a few performance hitches that can be *mostly* mitigated by tweaking how much VRAM is used for textures, but I do still get frame drops on and off (mainly in wonderland plaza and the courtyard). This didn't hamper my enjoyment of the game but as with most performance issues YMMV. There is supposedly a patch coming sometime soon which will hopefully fix this, but it is worth mentioning in the meantime. If you're a fan of the original, or if screwing around in a mall full of zombies seems fun, this is definitely a worthwhile buy!!-----Below is a response to the Gamer™ discourse around this release, if you somehow haven't seen it, it's really not relevant to the review so feel free to skip it. For anyone wanting *yet another* take on it, here goes-----Any cries of censorship in other reviews or the discussions should be taken with a grain of salt. All that has been changed is: a racist caricature was changed to no longer be offensive (while still preserving his character and race), a character suffering from PTSD no longer directly names the war he was traumatized by (it is still very clear which war it is, it is just not named), and the erotica photo category is removed (the risque photoshoot late in the game remains fully intact, it just labels photos taken as "no genre" instead of "erotica" while still giving you the points).First of all, if they were removing these from the original game it could be considered censorship, BUT this is a new release and a developers decision to make changes in an updated version is not censorship, it's just another design choice. Secondly, while removing the erotica genre seems a little silly considering the photoshoot still exists, all that was removed is pink circles appearing in some pictures. You can still *take the pictures* if you want to lmao. Finally, keep in mind this game was being developed around when post covid racial hate was at a high. Of course negative racial stereotypes and references to wars, even past ones, could be a sensitive issue! Updating the egregiously offensive character design is a welcome change, and obfuscating references to a war with a group of people being demonized unfairly is completely understandable. Anyone hung up on those edits should really consider why having those things remain in the game is so important to them.Besides, if it genuinely does bug you that they removed them, modders are already at work reverting the changes, so it's all a non-issue anyway.

_childDocuments_.review: Disclosure: My friend gifted me this game, so as I did not pay $30 myself, the sting of the sparse content doesn't bother me as much.You can tell the quality of a licensed game by how surface level references and character inclusions are tied in. For example; yet another TMNT game lacking Casey Jones. Seriously, not even as an assist power-up? You added two new levels in to this port but couldn't bother to get one of the main staples of TMNT?If you, like me, are a reclusive shut-in that never ventures outside, and also enjoy Ninja Turtles like any self-respecting manchild, the release of this former arcade cabinet-exclusive likely caught your interest. A 2017 arcade machine being ported to home devices seven years after the fact? Interesting.That aside, this is a by the numbers and fairly unpredictable, but enjoyable, beat-em-up. It's yet another brawler chasing the dragon that is Turtles in Time, and while it doesn't come close to meeting the goal it aims for, it's still a fun time. The story is barebones and follows as thus: Go fight through New York to get to Shredder. Why? Because it's an arcade game, dummy.The levels are standard side-scrolling fare with dozens of enemies leaping onto the screen from various angles, VERY often shooting at you from off-screen (I'm assuming this is a leftover from the arcade cabinet version where it was likely intended to screw you over to drain more quarters out of your wallet) -- as enemies filter in from all corners. It can get hectic, but thankfully you have ways to even the odds with frequent objects to grab and throw, explosive barrels to set off, special pick-ups that will cause you to spin around on the back of your shell as you 1-hit KO enemies for a short period of time, and even Ally Tokens that will spawn the likes of Metalhead and Leatherhead (AGAIN, seriously-- where the hell is Casey Jones? Or Splinter, for that matter?) which will do screen-clearing waves of attacks that kill any and everything currently on screen.Each level has two boss battles, some of which are peculiar deep cuts from the 2012 version of the series, and all voiced by the 2012 cast. The bosses all sound great, but the turtles themselves... well. You can tell they were called in to do voices on their days off, AND it sounds like they were ony allowed to do one take. I don't know if Greg Cipes was sick the day of this recording, but he sounds incredibly off as Mikey- AND irritating. The game has the most obnoxious, three repeating high-pitched wails from Mikey and Donnie that repeat ad nauseum any time you press the attack button. Seriously, for the love of God-- don't pick Mikey unless you have the game on mute. That aside, the turtles DO all have unique voice-lines for each boss, giving it just the slightest touch of novel effort that other TMNT beat-em-ups don't have.The visuals themselves are fine, but... flat? It's a strange mix. The turtle shells look incredible and have a glowing sheen on their shells, but other models seem... off. Shredder, for instance, looks like he's been fasting for several decades and is very lanky. Some stages look like they've jumped right off the screen of the 2012 series, while others are flat and lacking shadows or the tone that made the '12 series what it was. I'm not sure which is which as I've never played the original arcade cabinet.However, there are little touches that surprised me. When destroying one of the Krang robot suits, the Krang themselves will climb out of the suit and attemple to scuttle away. You can smack it to get extra points/Turtle Power (your own, less powerful screen-clearing super attack) or sometimes fling it towards the screen, Turtles in Time style. It caught my friend and I off guard and made us laugh when we managed to do so. On one level, the 80's Krang will destroy a wall and shoot electric beams through the giant gap into the arena, ripped straight from Turtles in Time. On the New York level, vans will burst onto the screen from the backdrop, swerving into the foreground as Krang robots pile out onto the street in frront of you. Another particularly cool moment is in the sewers where a subway car gets derailed right in front of you and crashes into a wall, only for the Xenomorph-esque squirrel mutants to kick the doors open and come piling out in a screeching fury. These are small touches, of which the game needs WAY more of, but they're still appreciated. (I'm also aware the aliens are called Utroms, but we're going with 2012 terminology.)There is no V-Sync as of this writing, so prepare for notable screen tearing. Aside from that, I had zero issue with performance, the game had no crashes or hitches. I played through Remote Play with a friend and we had a good time despite some of the oddities with the voice performances.The game took about 55~ minutes to beat with a friend on Normal. I plan to play through it at least a few more times over the coming weeks, but your mileage will absolutely vary. The content IS incredibly sparse, and it lacks any of Shredder's Revenge replay value.This is no Shredder's Revenge, but if you were always curious how the arcade cabinet played and you wanted to try it for yourself, this is a surprisingly competent game- just, seriously, don't expect anything on the level of Shredder's Revenge. It's not even close.Personal favorite moment: During the Karai miniboss, she teleports and taunts with a "Catch me if you can!" - before she finished her taunt, she got an explosive crate to the face and flopped over. Made my friend and I burst out laughing.
