_childDocuments_.review: TMNT Wrath of the Mutants. Now, this is a game where it's highly recommended you know what you're getting into before buying. Mainly, that this is a home port of the 2017 arcade game with some extra content. That being two new levels based on Dimension X and an Amusement Park. There are also some new bosses as well as other bosses that were swapped around. But does that make this port worth it? One way to find outGameplay: This game, like many TMNT beat 'em ups, takes inspiration from the old Konami beat 'em ups. Meaning you have stuff like screen throws and slam attacks. However, there are some unique things this game does like circle attacks that attack all around you, and a screen nuke called Turtle Power that is charged through dealing damage and finding powerups. Said powerups are another addition to separate itself from the 80s beat 'em ups, and include different abilities like more Turtle Power, Health increase, or weapons/assists from the series that do damage to enemies. However, there is also the shell powerup that is basically the Bomb Pizza from the old games. Besides that, it doesn't really get more complex than that, it's a surprisingly simple game. Almost too simple as combat can get repetitive at times, and all the turtles basically play the same, barring their screen nuke... Which is also just more visual flair. It's kinda disappointing that the Turtles don't even get their own stats. Still, the main appeal in these games is the multiplayer, so, I assume everything is more fun there.Another weird thing is that the difficulty is a weird middleground of easy and hard. Even though you do have selectable difficulties, you do get reminders that this was originally an arcade game, so you will often get stuff like enemies with huge reach, enemies with impossible reaction times, or sometimes the enemies will just delete your health bar. But there are also times where you just completely demolish the enemies, and the game already gives you plenty of lives and continues that refresh each stage, so even with these difficulties, you'll still have an easy time playing.That leaves the new stages, the Amusement Park and Dimension X. They're alright, they don't have the most intense gimmicks, but they were still pretty fun to play through. Overall, this game gets an alright 7/10 for gameplayGraphics, Presentation, and Sound: This part is weird. Since it was originally released in 2017, it's based on the 2012 series, so the character designs, locations, and other details are based on that version of the Turtles. This is the closest we will get to 2012 content in the modern age after Nick got obsessed with the 87 designs. Overall, the game does look fine for a 2017 arcade game in most parts, while other parts look... Bad. It's clear that this game didn't receive too many visual upgrades when it was being brought home, which is kind of disappointing. Although the new content does look nice and fits in perfectly with the original arcade stages, stuff like the ending scene that looks like complete crap, and oddly enough, isn't voiced at all. Despite them getting the original voice cast for this game. Speaking of, yes, they were able to get the original voice cast to voice the characters, but for some reason the Turtles themselves sound... Off. It seems that they weren't properly prepared when doing voices for the arcade release, and not much else for the home port (Although in the case of the home port, it was probably years since they did voices for these characters, although Rob Paulsen had the benefit of voicing 87 Raphael so his Donnie here sounded on brand). The rest of the characters sound fine, even if most of them were just reused from the arcade original, including Nolan North, Kevin Michael Richardson, and the late Gilbert Gotfried.Although staying on the sound, the game had issues with sound balancing. Despite the music sounding fine, it was way too quiet to properly hear, causing all the tunes to be less memorable than they should. Same with the sound effects, they're way too quiet and not punchy enough. They really needed more work on this part. 6/10Steam Deck Compatibility: Despite it being listed as unknown, this game worked on Steam Deck with 0 issues whatsoever. 10/10Replayability: After you beat the game, you get the option to replay on hard mode, but after that, nothing. I get it, this was meant to just be a port of the arcade game, but with basically nothing to work for, at best you would only replay this to play with friends, or to practice for a session on the actual arcade cabinet. Not even something as basic as a survival mode. That's... Sad. 2/10Final Thoughts: Again, you have to know what you're getting into with this. I feel if you know that this is a port of the 2017 arcade game, and it's something you're looking for, I'd say go for it. It helps that the game is a somewhat generous 30 bucks, and right now it's on sale. And since it's a GameMill game, it'll go on sale every 2 seconds. However, if you aren't interested in a near direct port with minimal additions to the original game, I'd say pass. Personally however, I found this a very fine game, so I think it deserves a fine rating of a 7/10 with a side of a plain cheese pizza. If nothing else, there is one undeniable fact on one thing this game does well: Preservation. Raw Thrills is absolutely horrible at making their games accessible. In the modern age, you really cannot rely on arcade exclusives, so we are really lucky that GameMill is porting their games over to console. Why GameMill? I dunno. But still, it's good that Raw Thrills' games are being properly preserved on consoles instead of being stuck on arcade jail. Now... Can we get Dirty Drivin' next? Or maybe Nicktoons Nitro if they're gonna keep doing Nick arcade games (Maybe with a fully voiced cast this time).If you're looking for other platforms to play this on, it's on every other modern platform: PS4, PS5, Switch, XBONE, and XBOX SeX/SeS including physical copies, so you won't have trouble finding it

_childDocuments_.review: I am enjoying this so far. Yes, the game is much shorter than Shredder's revenge but it doesn't have to - Wrath of the Mutants was initially an arcade game. I feel that a number of folks these days have never experienced an arcade game and expect games to take 10+ hours to be worth their money, except that most folks would not be spending 10+ hours at an arcade to play a game. Shorter games can be very entertaining, and this is a good example. This is also based on the 2012 cartoon series, not the more recent iterations.

_childDocuments_.review: This is a Steam Deck review.  At the time of this review, this game runs smoothly and easy to play on the handheld.  There’s no cloud saves in case you delete and redownload, but the content of the game isn’t heavy or needing to unlock much besides the last level or hard mode.The game plays like a 90’s TMNT game which is fine if that’s all you want.  That also means the controls are limited to move, jump, and attack.  And I wish it was just a jump.  The jump button also lunges at an opponent in proximity, which doesn’t help when an explosive is near.  Maybe there’s workarounds for this.  It’s pretty straightforward and doesn’t require a lot of time, so this is good in between things or other games.  Cathartic gaming at the end of a day.  This is really only for your hardcore TMNT base, or if you have a group that wants to play arcade beat em up ports.  This should be bought at a discount, around $5-20 - five dollars for every player you expect to play with you.

_childDocuments_.review: This is an enhanced version of a 2017 arcade game, with-- according to the description-- three extra stages and six extra boss fights. I never played the original arcade game, so I can't compare the two; however, it feels fairly seamless to me. I have no idea which are the new stages and which are the old, so nothing feels out of place.As for the game itself, it is about what you would expect. It is a side-scrolling beat 'em up that is obviously inspired by the older TMNT arcade games (available on Steam as part of the Cowabunga Collection). You can choose between the four turtles, and it has four-player local co-op as well. There are three difficulty levels, and finishing it on hard was challenging for me. That said, it is on the short side, and you will probably finish it on easy or normal in less than an hour. Getting the achievements adds some replayability, though.I'm glad to see this game getting another chance outside of the arcades. I enjoyed it, and recommend it.

_childDocuments_.review: I remember playing the original arcade game back in either 2017 or 2018 and I was hyped after seeing that the game was coming back better than ever on PC and other platforms. NYC, Sewer, and T.C.R.I. brought me back to the good old days while Dimension X and Amusement Park were perfect additions to the game. I could tell that the developers tried hard on this game and put heart into it. A lot of the other players got mad because the game took 1 hour to beat, in the game's defense, that's just how it was. The thing that made the older arcade game feel like it took forever to beat was the fact that you had put in more money for each time you ran out of continues, you don't have to do that anymore now that you've paid $29.99 for it here on whatever platform you're playing on which makes the game feel shorter despite the new levels. Although, it's not gonna feel like it took 1 hour to beat if you're playing on hard mode. Overall, I love this game and I don't care what other people think.Likes: The boss fights are fun and you might get some funny dialog from one of the turtles when the boss fight starts or when it ends. It has an excellent usage of other characters who can help you like Leatherhead, Metalhead, and Ice Cream Kitty. I'm surprised and glad that they were able to get all of the voice actors back just so that they could get some new lines from them. Dislikes: It's possible for the blue Foot Soldiers and the Kraang to shoot you off screen with their laser gun, it's hard to dodge the lasers when they're off screen, especially since you can't see them and know if they're about to shoot lasers at you or not. It's also hard to evade attacks, there are times where opponents can hit you without warning, enough time to react, or in other unfair ways like glitches for example; which is a becomes a big issue if you're playing in hard mode. During the Karai boss fight, I knocked Karai down and jumped next to her (because opponents getting up will kick you if you're in the way) and she got up while I was in mid air, and while I was next to her hitting her, she just suddenly stood still in a different position and it dealt damage even though she already got up like 3 seconds ago and she didn't even do anything to hit me. Things that I would do if I could change the game: I would make it so that you could evade attacks, have opponents attack with time for you to react, and also make it so that opponents getting up after being knocked down doesn't deal damage. I was kind of disappointed that Michelangelo didn't shout "Leatherhead" or "Ice Cream Kitty" when they came to help you, so I would've made Michelangelo shout one of those things depending on who came to help you. I would also make it so having more players would benefit you because there were some extra opponents when I was playing the game with my dad. Another thing that I would do is make it so that the Shredder boss fight and the Super Shredder boss fight weren't combined, I would make Karai and Shredder the only boss fights in "Shredder" and add a bonus level called "Owari" where you fight Shredder on the roof of the hidden mansion in the woods and each turtle is in their Owari outfit and you can only play it if you beat easy, normal, and hard mode (the difficulty would be optional no matter what mode you beat the game in). I hope that we get a sequel to this game; there are so many boss fights that we could get like Captain Mozar, Lord Dregg, Ho Chan, Savanti Romero, Oroku Saki (before he became Shredder), Hattori Tatsu, Newtralizer, Mom-Thing, Spider Bytez, etc. Thank you to whoever made this game available on more platforms so that we don't have to let the game drain our wallets at the arcade anymore (even though I'm still willing to play the older arcade again) and thank you for adding all of these cool levels, this game is awesome. My rating: 9/10

_childDocuments_.review: Great fun! So glad Raw Thrills made the effort to update and release commercially. My kids love it. It is simple, sharp and short. That’s exactly what you should expect from an arcade port, this isn’t a console game. Doesn’t try to be. Visuals are solid, and it has a unique spin on the series. If you want more depth/longevity go for Shredder’s Revenge. If you want straight up turtles arcade action, pick this up. Fans are spoilt for choice at the moment, keep ‘em coming!
